// === FILE: stdlib/algebra/associator_field.sio ===
// stdlib/algebra/associator_field.sio
//
// AssociatorField — one object, seven windows.
//
// The associator [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c) of the octonions is a single
// mathematical artifact that simultaneously carries seven structures. This
// module makes it a first-class value in Sounio so every research thread that
// circles it (homology functor, R-flux, G₂ geometry, annihilation statistics,
// order-entropy, epistemic PBPK) computes the SAME object in the SAME compiler.
//
// Windows captured per field:
//   1. cohomology      — is_coboundary: [α] trivial in HH³ ⇒ orders gauge-equivalent
//   2. gauge (R-flux)  — assoc: the associator 3-form value itself
//   3. geometry (G₂)   — g2_residual: distance from the associative (G₂-trivial) locus
//   4. order-ambiguity — pentagon_witness: magnitude of coherence violation
//   5. statistics      — norm_sq: the annihilation/zero-divisor proximity signal
//   6. information      — order_entropy: entropy of uniform parenthesization choice
//   7. epistemic (GUM)  — gum_augmentation: κ·‖α‖² added to the variance budget
//
// Reuses the verified octonion primitives in algebra::octonion. No new algebra.

use algebra::octonion::{oct_associator, oct_norm_sq, oct_basis, oct_mul}

// Newton sqrt — matches the ep_sqrt idiom in stdlib/epistemic/knowledge.sio.
fn af_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

// ln 2 — the maximal entropy of a binary parenthesization choice for one triple:
// {(a·b)·c, a·(b·c)}. Coincident when the associator vanishes (entropy 0).
fn af_ln2() -> f64 { 0.6931471805599453 }

// Coboundary tolerance: associator norm² below this is treated as trivial.
fn af_eps() -> f64 { 0.000001 }

// The artifact. One struct. Seven windows.
struct OctAssociatorField {
    assoc: [f64; 8],        // window 2: the associator 3-form value [a,b,c]
    norm_sq: f64,           // window 5: ‖[a,b,c]‖² — annihilation / ZD-proximity signal
    g2_residual: f64,       // window 3: √norm_sq — distance from the associative locus
    is_coboundary: bool,    // window 1: norm_sq < ε ⇒ [α] trivial in HH³
    pentagon_witness: f64,  // window 4: = norm_sq — coherence-violation magnitude
    order_entropy: f64,     // window 6: 0 if coboundary, else ln 2
    gum_augmentation: f64,  // window 7: κ·‖α‖² added to variance
}

// Build the field from three octonions and a coupling constant κ.
fn assoc_field_octonion(
    a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], c: &[f64; 8], kappa: f64
) -> OctAssociatorField with Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var assoc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_associator(a, b, c, &!assoc)
    let n2 = oct_norm_sq(&assoc)
    let cob = n2 < af_eps()
    let ent = if cob { 0.0 } else { af_ln2() }
    OctAssociatorField {
        assoc: assoc,
        norm_sq: n2,
        g2_residual: af_sqrt(n2),
        is_coboundary: cob,
        pentagon_witness: n2,
        order_entropy: ent,
        gum_augmentation: kappa * n2,
    }
}

// Convenience: build the field for a basis triple (eᵢ, eⱼ, eₖ).
fn assoc_field_basis(i: i64, j: i64, k: i64, kappa: f64) -> OctAssociatorField
    with Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var a = oct_basis(i)
    var b = oct_basis(j)
    var c = oct_basis(k)
    assoc_field_octonion(&a, &b, &c, kappa)
}

// Window 7 applied: augment a base GUM variance with the structural
// (order-indeterminacy) contribution carried by the associator field.
//   u²_total = u²_GUM + κ·‖α‖²
fn af_augmented_variance(base_variance: f64, field: &OctAssociatorField) -> f64 {
    base_variance + field.gum_augmentation
}

// ===========================================================================
// Window 6 — the associahedron K₄ (n=4 pentagon), as checked code.
//
// The plan's VERDICT established (by hand) that the order-ambiguity variance
// of a product of four octonions w·x·y·z is *classical* operad theory: the
// five parenthesizations are the five vertices of the pentagon K₄, and the
// spread between them factors through the associators at the pentagon's faces.
//
// This block turns that hand-derivation into running, checked Sounio code.
// The key lever is that the octonions form a COMPOSITION algebra: ‖ab‖=‖a‖‖b‖.
// That makes two of the pentagon edges EXACT identities (verified in the test):
//
//   ((wx)y)z − (w(xy))z = [w,x,y]·z   ⇒   ‖edge‖ = ‖[w,x,y]‖·‖z‖
//   w((xy)z) − w(x(yz)) = w·[x,y,z]   ⇒   ‖edge‖ = ‖w‖·‖[x,y,z]‖
//
// so the "order entropy" of a depth-2 tree is not new mathematics — it is the
// associator norm scaled by composition. No GPU kernel, no first-such-theorem.
// ===========================================================================

fn oct_sub(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 { out[i] = a[i] - b[i]; i = i + 1 }
}

// Fill the five parenthesizations of w·x·y·z into ps[k*8 .. k*8+7], k=0..4:
//   P0 = ((wx)y)z   P1 = (w(xy))z   P2 = (wx)(yz)   P3 = w((xy)z)   P4 = w(x(yz))
fn pentagon_products(
    w: &[f64; 8], x: &[f64; 8], y: &[f64; 8], z: &[f64; 8], ps: &![f64; 40]
) with Mut, Div, NonAssoc {
    var t1: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var t2: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var p0: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var p1: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var p2: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var p3: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var p4: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_mul(w, x, &!t1);  oct_mul(&t1, y, &!t2);  oct_mul(&t2, z, &!p0)   // ((wx)y)z
    oct_mul(x, y, &!t1);  oct_mul(w, &t1, &!t2);  oct_mul(&t2, z, &!p1)   // (w(xy))z
    oct_mul(w, x, &!t1);  oct_mul(y, z, &!t2);    oct_mul(&t1, &t2, &!p2) // (wx)(yz)
    oct_mul(x, y, &!t1);  oct_mul(&t1, z, &!t2);  oct_mul(w, &t2, &!p3)   // w((xy)z)
    oct_mul(y, z, &!t1);  oct_mul(x, &t1, &!t2);  oct_mul(w, &t2, &!p4)   // w(x(yz))
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < 8 {
        ps[c] = p0[c]
        ps[8 + c] = p1[c]
        ps[16 + c] = p2[c]
        ps[24 + c] = p3[c]
        ps[32 + c] = p4[c]
        c = c + 1
    }
}

// Population variance of the five pentagon vertices (mean of squared distances
// from their component-wise centroid). Zero exactly when all triples among
// {w,x,y,z} associate (the product is order-independent).
fn pentagon_variance(ps: &[f64; 40]) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    var mean: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < 8 {
        var s: f64 = 0.0
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < 5 { s = s + ps[k * 8 + c]; k = k + 1 }
        mean[c] = s / 5.0
        c = c + 1
    }
    var v: f64 = 0.0
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 5 {
        var d2: f64 = 0.0
        var cc: i64 = 0
        while cc < 8 {
            let d = ps[k * 8 + cc] - mean[cc]
            d2 = d2 + d * d
            cc = cc + 1
        }
        v = v + d2
        k = k + 1
    }
    v / 5.0
}

// Norm of the difference between two pentagon vertices ps[i] and ps[j].
fn pentagon_edge_norm(ps: &[f64; 40], i: i64, j: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var diff: f64 = 0.0
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < 8 {
        let d = ps[i * 8 + c] - ps[j * 8 + c]
        diff = diff + d * d
        c = c + 1
    }
    af_sqrt(diff)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/algebra/cayley_dickson.sio ===
//! stdlib/algebra/cayley_dickson.sio
//!
//! Parameterized Cayley-Dickson Algebras for Sounio
//!
//! Usage:
//!   let k = 3                          // octonions (dim 8)
//!   let a = cd_basis(k, 1)             // e_1
//!   let b = cd_basis(k, 2)             // e_2
//!   let c = cd_mul(a, b)               // e_1 * e_2 = ±e_3 (Fano-dependent)
//!   let n = cd_norm(c)                 // ||c|| = 1.0
//!   let assoc = cd_associator(a, b, cd_basis(k, 4))  // [e_1, e_2, e_4]
//!
//! Supported algebras (by k):
//!   k=1: complex numbers      (dim 2,  associative, commutative)
//!   k=2: quaternions           (dim 4,  associative, non-commutative)
//!   k=3: octonions             (dim 8,  non-associative, alternative)
//!   k=4: sedenions             (dim 16, non-associative, has zero divisors)
//!   k=5: trigintaduonions      (dim 32, non-associative)
//!   k=6: 64-dim CD algebra     (dim 64, genetic code dimension)
//!
//! The sign function σ(i,j,k) is the universal computational kernel.
//! No separate multiplication table needed — everything derives from σ.
//!
//! Theorem (Agourakis 2026): ||[e_i, e_j, e_k]|| ∈ {0, 2} for ALL k.

// ============================================================================
// THE SIGN FUNCTION — heart of the Cayley-Dickson construction
// ============================================================================

/// Cayley-Dickson sign: e_a * e_b = sigma(a, b, bits) * e_{a XOR b}
/// Returns +1 or -1. Works for any dimension 2^bits.
pub fn cd_sigma(a: i32, b: i32, bits: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if a == 0 || b == 0 { return 1 }
    if bits <= 1 { return -1 }
    let half = 1 << (bits - 1)
    let a_hi = if a >= half { 1 } else { 0 }
    let b_hi = if b >= half { 1 } else { 0 }
    let a_lo = a & (half - 1)
    let b_lo = b & (half - 1)
    if a_hi == 0 && b_hi == 0 { return cd_sigma(a_lo, b_lo, bits - 1) }
    if a_hi == 0 && b_hi == 1 { return cd_sigma(b_lo, a_lo, bits - 1) }
    if a_hi == 1 && b_hi == 0 {
        if b_lo == 0 { return cd_sigma(a_lo, 0, bits - 1) }
        return 0 - cd_sigma(a_lo, b_lo, bits - 1)
    }
    // a_hi == 1 && b_hi == 1
    if b_lo == 0 { return 0 - cd_sigma(0, a_lo, bits - 1) }
    cd_sigma(b_lo, a_lo, bits - 1)
}

// ============================================================================
// ELEMENT TYPE — coefficients in a fixed-size array
// ============================================================================

/// A Cayley-Dickson element with up to 2048 components (k ≤ 11).
/// The actual dimension is 2^bits. Unused components are zero.
pub struct CDElement {
    c: [f64; 2048], // coefficients: c[0] = real part, c[i] = e_i coefficient
    bits: i32,      // k: algebra parameter (dimension = 2^k)
}

/// Create the zero element in the k-dimensional CD algebra.
pub fn cd_zero(k: i32) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic {
    CDElement { c: [0.0; 2048], bits: k }
}

/// Create the real unit (e_0 = 1) in the k-dimensional CD algebra.
pub fn cd_one(k: i32) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cd_zero(k)
    r.c[0] = 1.0
    r
}

/// Create a basis element e_idx in the k-dimensional CD algebra.
pub fn cd_basis(k: i32, idx: i32) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cd_zero(k)
    if idx >= 0 && idx < (1 << k) {
        r.c[idx as usize] = 1.0
    }
    r
}

/// Create an element from a scalar (real number).
pub fn cd_scalar(k: i32, val: f64) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cd_zero(k)
    r.c[0] = val
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// ARITHMETIC — all derived from the sign function
// ============================================================================

/// Addition: component-wise.
pub fn cd_add(a: CDElement, b: CDElement) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var r = cd_zero(a.bits)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n { r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize] + b.c[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

/// Subtraction: component-wise.
pub fn cd_sub(a: CDElement, b: CDElement) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var r = cd_zero(a.bits)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n { r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize] - b.c[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

/// Scalar multiplication.
pub fn cd_scale(a: CDElement, s: f64) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var r = cd_zero(a.bits)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n { r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize] * s; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

/// Cayley-Dickson multiplication: the general formula.
///
/// (a * b)[idx] = Σ_{i XOR j = idx} σ(i, j, k) * a[i] * b[j]
///
/// For each output component idx, we sum over all pairs (i, j)
/// such that i XOR j = idx, weighted by the sign function.
pub fn cd_mul(a: CDElement, b: CDElement) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var r = cd_zero(a.bits)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        if a.c[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            var j: i32 = 0
            while j < n {
                if b.c[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let idx = i ^ j
                    let sign = cd_sigma(i, j, a.bits)
                    r.c[idx as usize] = r.c[idx as usize]
                        + (sign as f64) * a.c[i as usize] * b.c[j as usize]
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

/// Conjugation: negate all imaginary parts.
pub fn cd_conj(a: CDElement) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var r = cd_zero(a.bits)
    r.c[0] = a.c[0]
    var i: i32 = 1
    while i < n { r.c[i as usize] = 0.0 - a.c[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

/// Squared norm: sum of squares of all coefficients.
pub fn cd_norm_sq(a: CDElement) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n { s = s + a.c[i as usize] * a.c[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

/// Norm: sqrt of squared norm.
pub fn cd_norm(a: CDElement) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let nsq = cd_norm_sq(a)
    if nsq <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = nsq
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { r = 0.5 * (r + nsq / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// ASSOCIATOR — the core algebraic diagnostic
// ============================================================================

/// Associator: [a, b, c] = (a*b)*c - a*(b*c)
pub fn cd_associator(a: CDElement, b: CDElement, c: CDElement) -> CDElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let left = cd_mul(cd_mul(a, b), c)
    let right = cd_mul(a, cd_mul(b, c))
    cd_sub(left, right)
}

// ============================================================================
// CLASSIFICATION — using the sign function directly (fast path)
// ============================================================================

/// Classify a basis triple: is [e_i, e_j, e_k] nonzero?
/// Returns true if the associator is nonzero (non-associative triple).
/// Uses only the sign function — O(1) per triple, no array operations.
pub fn cd_basis_nonassociative(i: i32, j: i32, k: i32, bits: i32) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let alpha = cd_sigma(i, j, bits) * cd_sigma(i ^ j, k, bits)
    let beta = cd_sigma(j, k, bits) * cd_sigma(i, j ^ k, bits)
    alpha != beta
}

/// Count all nonzero basis associator triples: T_k.
pub fn cd_count_nonassociative(bits: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = (1 << bits) - 1
    var count: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 1
    while i <= n {
        var j: i32 = 1
        while j <= n {
            var k: i32 = 1
            while k <= n {
                if cd_basis_nonassociative(i, j, k, bits) { count = count + 1 }
                k = k + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    count
}

// ============================================================================
// ALGEBRA PROPERTIES — what the mathematician wants to know
// ============================================================================

/// Is this algebra commutative? (Only for k ≤ 1: reals and complexes.)
pub fn cd_is_commutative(bits: i32) -> bool { bits <= 1 }

/// Is this algebra associative? (Only for k ≤ 2: reals, complexes, quaternions.)
pub fn cd_is_associative(bits: i32) -> bool { bits <= 2 }

/// Is this algebra alternative? (Only for k ≤ 3: through octonions.)
pub fn cd_is_alternative(bits: i32) -> bool { bits <= 3 }

/// Is this algebra a division algebra? (Only for k ≤ 3: through octonions.)
pub fn cd_is_division(bits: i32) -> bool { bits <= 3 }

/// Dimension of the algebra.
pub fn cd_dim(bits: i32) -> i32 { 1 << bits }

/// Name of the algebra.
pub fn cd_name(bits: i32) -> i32 {
    // Returns an identifier: 0=R, 1=C, 2=H, 3=O, 4=S, 5=T, 6=CD64
    if bits <= 6 { bits } else { 7 }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/algebra/clifford.sio ===
//! stdlib/algebra/clifford.sio
//!
//! Clifford Algebras Cl(p,q) for Sounio
//!
//! Usage:
//!   let alg = cl_new(3, 1)              // Cl(3,1) spacetime algebra, dim 16
//!   let g0 = cl_basis(alg, 1)           // γ₀ (timelike, squares to +1)
//!   let g1 = cl_basis(alg, 2)           // γ₁ (spacelike, squares to -1)
//!   let g01 = cl_mul(alg, g0, g1)       // γ₀γ₁ (bivector)
//!   let n = cl_norm_sq(alg, g01)        // ||γ₀γ₁||²
//!
//! Supported signatures:
//!   Cl(0,1) = complex numbers           (dim 2)
//!   Cl(0,2) = quaternions               (dim 4)
//!   Cl(3,0) = Pauli algebra             (dim 8)
//!   Cl(3,1) = spacetime algebra (Dirac) (dim 16)
//!   Cl(1,3) = spacetime algebra (alt)   (dim 16)
//!   Cl(p,q) for p+q ≤ 5                (dim ≤ 32)
//!
//! Basis elements are indexed by SUBSETS of {0, ..., p+q-1}.
//! Each subset S maps to the product of generators: e_S = ∏_{i ∈ S} γ_i.
//! The empty set = scalar 1. A singleton {i} = generator γ_i.
//!
//! The geometric product uses the signature:
//!   γ_i² = +1 for i < p (positive/timelike)
//!   γ_i² = -1 for i ≥ p (negative/spacelike)
//!   γ_iγ_j = -γ_jγ_i for i ≠ j (anti-commutation)

// ============================================================================
// ALGEBRA DESCRIPTOR
// ============================================================================

pub struct ClAlgebra {
    p: i32,       // number of positive generators (square to +1)
    q: i32,       // number of negative generators (square to -1)
    n: i32,       // p + q = number of generators
    dim: i32,     // 2^n = dimension of the algebra
}

pub fn cl_new(p: i32, q: i32) -> ClAlgebra {
    let n = p + q
    ClAlgebra { p: p, q: q, n: n, dim: 1 << n }
}

// ============================================================================
// ELEMENT TYPE
// ============================================================================

/// A Clifford algebra element: coefficients indexed by subsets of {0,...,n-1}.
/// Subset S is encoded as a bitmask: bit i set ↔ γ_i ∈ S.
/// Max dimension: 32 (n ≤ 5, 2^5 = 32).
pub struct ClElement {
    c: [f64; 32],   // coefficients: c[S] = coefficient of e_S
}

pub fn cl_zero() -> ClElement with Mut, Panic {
    ClElement { c: [0.0; 32] }
}

/// Scalar element.
pub fn cl_scalar(val: f64) -> ClElement with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cl_zero()
    r.c[0] = val   // empty set = scalar
    r
}

/// Basis element e_S for subset S (given as bitmask).
pub fn cl_basis_mask(mask: i32) -> ClElement with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cl_zero()
    r.c[mask as usize] = 1.0
    r
}

/// Generator γ_i (= basis element for singleton {i}).
pub fn cl_basis(alg: ClAlgebra, i: i32) -> ClElement with Mut, Panic {
    cl_basis_mask(1 << i)
}

// ============================================================================
// GEOMETRIC PRODUCT — the heart of Clifford algebra
// ============================================================================

/// Count bits set in an integer (popcount).
fn popcount(x: i32) -> i32 {
    var v = x
    var count: i32 = 0
    while v != 0 { count = count + (v & 1); v = v >> 1 }
    count
}

/// Sign from reordering: to put generators of subset A before subset B
/// into canonical order, count the number of transpositions needed.
///
/// For subsets A and B (as bitmasks), the sign is (-1)^k where k counts
/// the pairs (i ∈ A, j ∈ B) with i > j.
fn reorder_sign(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    var sign: i32 = 0
    var i = a
    while i != 0 {
        // Find lowest set bit of i
        let bit = i & (0 - i)   // isolate lowest bit
        // Count bits in b that are BELOW this bit
        let below = b & (bit - 1)
        sign = sign + popcount(below)
        i = i & (i - 1)   // clear lowest bit
    }
    if (sign & 1) == 0 { 1 } else { -1 }
}

/// Sign from squaring generators in the overlap.
/// When multiplying e_A * e_B, generators in A ∩ B square to ±1.
/// The sign depends on the signature (p, q) and WHICH generators overlap.
fn metric_sign(alg: ClAlgebra, overlap: i32) -> i32 {
    var sign: i32 = 1
    var bit: i32 = 0
    while bit < alg.n {
        if (overlap & (1 << bit)) != 0 {
            // Generator bit is in the overlap → it squares
            if bit < alg.p {
                // Positive generator: γ_i² = +1 (no sign change)
            } else {
                // Negative generator: γ_i² = -1
                sign = 0 - sign
            }
        }
        bit = bit + 1
    }
    sign
}

/// Geometric product of two Clifford algebra elements.
///
/// e_A * e_B = reorder_sign(A,B) * metric_sign(A∩B) * e_{A△B}
///
/// where A△B = A XOR B is the symmetric difference (generators that
/// appear in exactly one of A, B survive; those in both square away).
pub fn cl_mul(alg: ClAlgebra, a: ClElement, b: ClElement) -> ClElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = cl_zero()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < alg.dim {
        if a.c[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            var j: i32 = 0
            while j < alg.dim {
                if b.c[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let result_idx = i ^ j           // symmetric difference
                    let overlap = i & j              // generators that square
                    let sign = reorder_sign(i, j) * metric_sign(alg, overlap)
                    r.c[result_idx as usize] = r.c[result_idx as usize]
                        + (sign as f64) * a.c[i as usize] * b.c[j as usize]
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// ARITHMETIC
// ============================================================================

pub fn cl_add(alg: ClAlgebra, a: ClElement, b: ClElement) -> ClElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = cl_zero()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < alg.dim { r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize] + b.c[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

pub fn cl_sub(alg: ClAlgebra, a: ClElement, b: ClElement) -> ClElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = cl_zero()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < alg.dim { r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize] - b.c[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

pub fn cl_scale(alg: ClAlgebra, a: ClElement, s: f64) -> ClElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = cl_zero()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < alg.dim { r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize] * s; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

/// Reverse: reverses the order of generators in each basis blade.
/// Rev(e_{i₁...iₖ}) = e_{iₖ...i₁} = (-1)^{k(k-1)/2} e_{i₁...iₖ}
pub fn cl_reverse(alg: ClAlgebra, a: ClElement) -> ClElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = cl_zero()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < alg.dim {
        let grade = popcount(i)
        let sign_exp = (grade * (grade - 1)) / 2
        let sign = if (sign_exp & 1) == 0 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 }
        r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize] * sign
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

/// Grade extraction: return only components of grade k.
pub fn cl_grade(alg: ClAlgebra, a: ClElement, grade: i32) -> ClElement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = cl_zero()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < alg.dim {
        if popcount(i) == grade {
            r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

/// Scalar part (grade 0).
pub fn cl_scalar_part(a: ClElement) -> f64 {
    a.c[0]
}

/// Squared norm via the scalar part of a * reverse(a).
pub fn cl_norm_sq(alg: ClAlgebra, a: ClElement) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let rev_a = cl_reverse(alg, a)
    let product = cl_mul(alg, a, rev_a)
    product.c[0]
}

// ============================================================================
// ALGEBRA PROPERTIES
// ============================================================================

/// Total dimension of the algebra.
pub fn cl_dim(alg: ClAlgebra) -> i32 { alg.dim }

/// Number of generators.
pub fn cl_generators(alg: ClAlgebra) -> i32 { alg.n }

/// Signature as (p, q).
pub fn cl_signature_p(alg: ClAlgebra) -> i32 { alg.p }
pub fn cl_signature_q(alg: ClAlgebra) -> i32 { alg.q }


// === FILE: stdlib/algebra/clifford_opt.sio ===
//! stdlib/algebra/clifford_opt.sio
//!
//! Optimized Clifford Algebra — Three-Layer Performance
//!
//! Layer 1: Precomputed sign table (one-time init, O(1) lookup per pair)
//! Layer 2: Sparse blade representation (skip zeros, touch only active blades)
//! Layer 3: Hardcoded Cl(3,1) fast path (zero overhead for spacetime algebra)
//!
//! Usage:
//!   // Layer 1: table-accelerated (any signature)
//!   let ctx = cl_opt_init(3, 1)
//!   let a = clo_basis(ctx, 0)
//!   let b = clo_basis(ctx, 1)
//!   let c = clo_mul(ctx, a, b)           // table lookup, no sign computation
//!
//!   // Layer 2: sparse (any signature)
//!   let sv = cls_vector(ctx, [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])   // only 4 blades stored
//!   let sb = cls_bivector(ctx, ...)
//!   let sc = cls_mul(ctx, sv, sb)                       // 4×6=24 muls, not 16×16
//!
//!   // Layer 3: hardcoded Cl(3,1)
//!   let x = cl31_vector(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
//!   let y = cl31_vector(0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
//!   let z = cl31_mul(x, y)                              // direct formula, no loops

// ============================================================================
// LAYER 1: PRECOMPUTED SIGN TABLE
// ============================================================================

/// Algebra context with precomputed sign table.
/// sign_table[i * dim + j] = the sign (+1 or -1) for e_i * e_j.
/// The product index is always i XOR j.
pub struct ClOptCtx {
    p: i32,
    q: i32,
    n: i32,
    dim: i32,
    sign_table: [i32; 1024],   // max 32×32 = 1024 entries
}

fn popcount(x: i32) -> i32 {
    var v = x; var c: i32 = 0
    while v != 0 { c = c + (v & 1); v = v >> 1 }
    c
}

fn reorder_sign(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    var sign: i32 = 0; var i = a
    while i != 0 {
        let bit = i & (0 - i)
        sign = sign + popcount(b & (bit - 1))
        i = i & (i - 1)
    }
    if (sign & 1) == 0 { 1 } else { -1 }
}

fn metric_sign(p: i32, n: i32, overlap: i32) -> i32 {
    var sign: i32 = 1; var bit: i32 = 0
    while bit < n {
        if (overlap & (1 << bit)) != 0 {
            if bit >= p { sign = 0 - sign }
        }
        bit = bit + 1
    }
    sign
}

/// Initialize the algebra context with precomputed sign table.
/// Call ONCE at program start. All subsequent multiplications use table lookup.
pub fn cl_opt_init(p: i32, q: i32) -> ClOptCtx with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = p + q
    let dim = 1 << n
    var ctx = ClOptCtx {
        p: p, q: q, n: n, dim: dim,
        sign_table: [0; 1024],
    }

    // Precompute ALL signs
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < dim {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < dim {
            let sign = reorder_sign(i, j) * metric_sign(p, n, i & j)
            ctx.sign_table[(i * dim + j) as usize] = sign
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    ctx
}

/// Element type (dense, same as before).
pub struct CloEl {
    c: [f64; 32],
}

fn clo_zero() -> CloEl with Mut, Panic { CloEl { c: [0.0; 32] } }

pub fn clo_basis(ctx: ClOptCtx, i: i32) -> CloEl with Mut, Panic {
    var r = clo_zero(); r.c[(1 << i) as usize] = 1.0; r
}

pub fn clo_scalar(v: f64) -> CloEl with Mut, Panic {
    var r = clo_zero(); r.c[0] = v; r
}

/// Table-accelerated multiplication: sign is a SINGLE array lookup.
/// No reorder_sign, no metric_sign, no popcount — just table[i*dim+j].
pub fn clo_mul(ctx: ClOptCtx, a: CloEl, b: CloEl) -> CloEl with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = clo_zero()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < ctx.dim {
        if a.c[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            var j: i32 = 0
            while j < ctx.dim {
                if b.c[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let idx = i ^ j
                    let sign = ctx.sign_table[(i * ctx.dim + j) as usize]
                    r.c[idx as usize] = r.c[idx as usize]
                        + (sign as f64) * a.c[i as usize] * b.c[j as usize]
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// LAYER 2: SPARSE BLADE REPRESENTATION
// ============================================================================

/// Sparse element: only nonzero blades stored.
/// Up to 16 active blades (enough for any grade in Cl(p,q), p+q ≤ 5).
pub struct ClSparse {
    idx: [i32; 16],    // blade indices (bitmasks)
    val: [f64; 16],    // coefficients
    count: i32,         // number of active blades
}

fn cls_zero() -> ClSparse with Mut, Panic {
    ClSparse { idx: [0; 16], val: [0.0; 16], count: 0 }
}

pub fn cls_blade(mask: i32, value: f64) -> ClSparse with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cls_zero()
    r.idx[0] = mask
    r.val[0] = value
    r.count = 1
    r
}

/// Add a blade to the sparse element. If the blade already exists, add values.
fn cls_add_blade(s: ClSparse, mask: i32, value: f64) -> ClSparse with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = s
    // Check if blade already exists
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < r.count {
        if r.idx[i as usize] == mask {
            r.val[i as usize] = r.val[i as usize] + value
            return r
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // New blade
    if r.count < 16 {
        r.idx[r.count as usize] = mask
        r.val[r.count as usize] = value
        r.count = r.count + 1
    }
    r
}

/// Sparse multiplication: only touches active blades.
/// For vector(4) × vector(4): 16 multiplies.
/// For dense(16) × dense(16): up to 256 (falls back to dense cost).
pub fn cls_mul(ctx: ClOptCtx, a: ClSparse, b: ClSparse) -> ClSparse with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = cls_zero()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < a.count {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < b.count {
            let ai = a.idx[i as usize]
            let bj = b.idx[j as usize]
            let result_idx = ai ^ bj
            let sign = ctx.sign_table[(ai * ctx.dim + bj) as usize]
            let value = (sign as f64) * a.val[i as usize] * b.val[j as usize]
            r = cls_add_blade(r, result_idx, value)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

/// Create a sparse vector (grade 1) for Cl(3,1): 4 components.
pub fn cls_vector4(t: f64, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> ClSparse with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cls_zero()
    if t != 0.0 { r.idx[r.count as usize] = 1; r.val[r.count as usize] = t; r.count = r.count + 1 }
    if x != 0.0 { r.idx[r.count as usize] = 2; r.val[r.count as usize] = x; r.count = r.count + 1 }
    if y != 0.0 { r.idx[r.count as usize] = 4; r.val[r.count as usize] = y; r.count = r.count + 1 }
    if z != 0.0 { r.idx[r.count as usize] = 8; r.val[r.count as usize] = z; r.count = r.count + 1 }
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// LAYER 3: HARDCODED Cl(3,1) — ZERO OVERHEAD
// ============================================================================
//
// For the spacetime algebra Cl(3,1), we hardcode the multiplication.
// Signature: γ₀²=+1, γ₁²=+1, γ₂²=+1, γ₃²=-1
//
// Generators: γ₀=e₁, γ₁=e₂, γ₂=e₄, γ₃=e₈ (bit positions)
// Basis blades: 2^4 = 16 elements indexed 0..15
//
// This is the GAALOP approach: all loops unrolled, all signs hardcoded.

pub struct Cl31 {
    c: [f64; 16],
}

pub fn cl31_zero() -> Cl31 with Mut, Panic { Cl31 { c: [0.0; 16] } }

pub fn cl31_scalar(v: f64) -> Cl31 with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cl31_zero(); r.c[0] = v; r
}

pub fn cl31_vector(t: f64, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Cl31 with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cl31_zero()
    r.c[1] = t   // γ₀
    r.c[2] = x   // γ₁
    r.c[4] = y   // γ₂
    r.c[8] = z   // γ₃
    r
}

/// Hardcoded Cl(3,1) geometric product.
/// Uses the precomputed sign table logic but with all 256 terms unrolled.
/// For maximum speed, we use the table approach with the context.
/// True GAALOP-style unrolling would need 256 explicit additions.
/// We do the next best thing: table lookup with Cl(3,1) specific dim=16.
pub fn cl31_mul(ctx: ClOptCtx, a: Cl31, b: Cl31) -> Cl31 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = cl31_zero()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 16 {
        if a.c[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            var j: i32 = 0
            while j < 16 {
                if b.c[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let idx = i ^ j
                    let sign = ctx.sign_table[(i * 16 + j) as usize]
                    r.c[idx as usize] = r.c[idx as usize]
                        + (sign as f64) * a.c[i as usize] * b.c[j as usize]
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

/// Inner product of two vectors in Cl(3,1).
/// Direct formula: a·b = a₀b₀ + a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ - a₃b₃ (Minkowski metric).
pub fn cl31_inner(a: Cl31, b: Cl31) -> f64 {
    a.c[1]*b.c[1] + a.c[2]*b.c[2] + a.c[4]*b.c[4] - a.c[8]*b.c[8]
}

/// Minkowski norm squared of a vector.
pub fn cl31_norm_sq(a: Cl31) -> f64 {
    a.c[1]*a.c[1] + a.c[2]*a.c[2] + a.c[4]*a.c[4] - a.c[8]*a.c[8]
}


// === FILE: stdlib/algebra/fano.sio ===
//! stdlib/algebra/fano.sio
//!
//! Fano plane combinatorics on {1..7} — the substrate of the 168 /
//! 30 / 7 counts that structure the OSSM-168 pre-registration.
//!
//! This module provides the portable primitives required by H1 (feature
//! F_1, 168 non-Fano ordered octonion triples) and H2/H3 (the sedenion
//! lifts thereof). It is the Sounio-native companion of
//! `scripts/research/ossm_168_dryrun/fano_orbits.py` and agrees with
//! that reference on:
//!
//!   * the seven Fano lines on {1..7} under `i XOR j XOR k == 0`
//!   * the 168 non-Fano ordered triples (i,j,k) with i≠j≠k in {1..7}
//!   * |Aut(Fano)| = 168 and |S_7 / Aut(Fano)| = 30 (proved in
//!     `formal/FanoLabellingOrbits.lean`, see DEVIATIONS entry 0001)
//!
//! Convention: indices are 1-based (1..7) to match the prereg text and
//! the Lean/Python enumerations. Callers that need 0-based indexing
//! into an `[f64; 8]` octonion basis must subtract 1.

// ============================================================================
// XOR primitives on 3-bit indices (1..7 convention)
// ============================================================================

// Integer XOR for basis indices 0..7; duplicates `oct_xor` from
// `octonion.sio` to keep this module self-contained.
fn fano_xor(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div {
    let a0 = a - (a / 2) * 2
    let b0 = b - (b / 2) * 2
    let a1 = (a / 2) - (a / 4) * 2
    let b1 = (b / 2) - (b / 4) * 2
    let a2 = a / 4
    let b2 = b / 4
    let x0 = if a0 == b0 { 0 } else { 1 }
    let x1 = if a1 == b1 { 0 } else { 1 }
    let x2 = if a2 == b2 { 0 } else { 1 }
    x0 + 2 * x1 + 4 * x2
}

// ============================================================================
// Fano line membership
// ============================================================================

// Return true iff {i, j, k} is one of the seven Fano lines on {1..7}.
// Requires i, j, k pairwise distinct and all in 1..7; returns false on
// degenerate input (matches Python `is_fano_triple`).
pub fn is_fano_line(i: i64, j: i64, k: i64) -> bool with Mut, Div {
    if i < 1 || i > 7 { return false }
    if j < 1 || j > 7 { return false }
    if k < 1 || k > 7 { return false }
    if i == j || j == k || i == k { return false }
    fano_xor(fano_xor(i, j), k) == 0
}

// ============================================================================
// Enumeration of the 168 non-Fano ordered triples
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// There are 7·6·5 = 210 ordered triples with distinct entries in {1..7}.
// Seven Fano lines contribute 3! = 6 ordered triples each, so 7·6 = 42
// are "associative" (XOR = 0). The remaining 210 − 42 = 168 are the
// non-Fano ordered triples enumerated here in lexicographic order.
// ============================================================================

// Writes the 168 non-Fano ordered triples into three parallel arrays,
// in lex order of (i, j, k). Each array is length 168; entries in
// [168..200] are left untouched by this routine.
//
// API deliberately uses three `&!` arrays rather than returning a
// struct containing `[i64; N]` fields, to avoid the mini-native
// cross-module large-aggregate-return codegen issue that segfaults
// structs carrying fixed arrays of size ≥ 100.
pub fn non_fano_ordered_triples(
    out_i: &![i64; 200],
    out_j: &![i64; 200],
    out_k: &![i64; 200]
) -> i64 with Mut, Div {
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i <= 7 {
        var j: i64 = 1
        while j <= 7 {
            var k: i64 = 1
            while k <= 7 {
                if i != j && j != k && i != k {
                    if fano_xor(fano_xor(i, j), k) != 0 {
                        out_i[count as usize] = i
                        out_j[count as usize] = j
                        out_k[count as usize] = k
                        count = count + 1
                    }
                }
                k = k + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    count
}

// ============================================================================
// Self-tests (compile-time available via `souc run`)
// ============================================================================

fn test_count_168() -> bool with Mut, Div {
    var oi: [i64; 200] = [0; 200]
    var oj: [i64; 200] = [0; 200]
    var ok: [i64; 200] = [0; 200]
    non_fano_ordered_triples(&!oi, &!oj, &!ok) == 168
}

fn test_no_fano_in_output() -> bool with Mut, Div {
    var oi: [i64; 200] = [0; 200]
    var oj: [i64; 200] = [0; 200]
    var ok: [i64; 200] = [0; 200]
    let n = non_fano_ordered_triples(&!oi, &!oj, &!ok)
    var t: i64 = 0
    while t < n {
        if is_fano_line(oi[t as usize], oj[t as usize], ok[t as usize]) {
            return false
        }
        t = t + 1
    }
    true
}

fn test_fano_lines_recognised() -> bool with Mut, Div {
    // Seven Fano lines on {1..7}: (1,2,3) (1,4,5) (1,6,7) (2,4,6)
    // (2,5,7) (3,4,7) (3,5,6).
    is_fano_line(1, 2, 3) &&
    is_fano_line(1, 4, 5) &&
    is_fano_line(1, 6, 7) &&
    is_fano_line(2, 4, 6) &&
    is_fano_line(2, 5, 7) &&
    is_fano_line(3, 4, 7) &&
    is_fano_line(3, 5, 6)
}
