fn tape_pow(tape: Tape, a: Var, n: f64) -> Tape {
    let idx = tape.size
    let val = pow_f64(a.val, n)
    let node = TapeNode { value: val, adjoint: 0.0, op: op_pow(), parent1: a.idx, parent2: 0 - 1, aux: n }
    let t = tape_set(tape, idx, node)
    return tape_with_size(t, idx + 1)
}

fn tape_relu(tape: Tape, a: Var) -> Tape {
    let idx = tape.size
    let val = if a.val > 0.0 { a.val } else { 0.0 }
    let node = TapeNode { value: val, adjoint: 0.0, op: op_relu(), parent1: a.idx, parent2: 0 - 1, aux: 0.0 }
    let t = tape_set(tape, idx, node)
    return tape_with_size(t, idx + 1)
}

fn tape_sigmoid(tape: Tape, a: Var) -> Tape {
    let idx = tape.size
    let val = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp_f64(0.0 - a.val))
    let node = TapeNode { value: val, adjoint: 0.0, op: op_sigmoid(), parent1: a.idx, parent2: 0 - 1, aux: 0.0 }
    let t = tape_set(tape, idx, node)
    return tape_with_size(t, idx + 1)
}

// ============================================================================
// BACKWARD PASS
// ============================================================================

// Helper: Add adjoint to parent2 for add operation
fn backward_add_p2(tape: Tape, p2_idx: i64, adj: f64) -> Tape {
    if p2_idx < 0 { return tape }
    let p2 = tape_get(tape, p2_idx)
    let p2_new = TapeNode { value: p2.value, adjoint: p2.adjoint + adj, op: p2.op, parent1: p2.parent1, parent2: p2.parent2, aux: p2.aux }
    return tape_set(tape, p2_idx, p2_new)
}

// Helper: Subtract adjoint from parent2 for sub operation
fn backward_sub_p2(tape: Tape, p2_idx: i64, adj: f64) -> Tape {
    if p2_idx < 0 { return tape }
    let p2 = tape_get(tape, p2_idx)
    let p2_new = TapeNode { value: p2.value, adjoint: p2.adjoint - adj, op: p2.op, parent1: p2.parent1, parent2: p2.parent2, aux: p2.aux }
    return tape_set(tape, p2_idx, p2_new)
}

// Helper: Add gradient for mul operation to both parents
fn backward_mul(tape: Tape, p1_idx: i64, p2_idx: i64, adj: f64) -> Tape {
    if p2_idx < 0 { return tape }
    let p1 = tape_get(tape, p1_idx)
    let p2 = tape_get(tape, p2_idx)

    if p1_idx == p2_idx {
        // Same variable: d/dx(x*x) = 2x
        let p1_new = TapeNode { value: p1.value, adjoint: p1.adjoint + adj * p1.value * 2.0, op: p1.op, parent1: p1.parent1, parent2: p1.parent2, aux: p1.aux }
        return tape_set(tape, p1_idx, p1_new)
    }

    // Different variables: d/da(a*b) = b, d/db(a*b) = a
    let p1_new = TapeNode { value: p1.value, adjoint: p1.adjoint + adj * p2.value, op: p1.op, parent1: p1.parent1, parent2: p1.parent2, aux: p1.aux }
    let tape2 = tape_set(tape, p1_idx, p1_new)
    let p2_new = TapeNode { value: p2.value, adjoint: p2.adjoint + adj * p1.value, op: p2.op, parent1: p2.parent1, parent2: p2.parent2, aux: p2.aux }
    return tape_set(tape2, p2_idx, p2_new)
}

// Helper: Add gradient for div operation to both parents
fn backward_div(tape: Tape, p1_idx: i64, p2_idx: i64, adj: f64) -> Tape {
    if p2_idx < 0 { return tape }
    let p1 = tape_get(tape, p1_idx)
    let p2 = tape_get(tape, p2_idx)
    // d/da(a/b) = 1/b, d/db(a/b) = -a/b²
    let p1_new = TapeNode { value: p1.value, adjoint: p1.adjoint + adj / p2.value, op: p1.op, parent1: p1.parent1, parent2: p1.parent2, aux: p1.aux }
    let tape2 = tape_set(tape, p1_idx, p1_new)
    let p2_new = TapeNode { value: p2.value, adjoint: p2.adjoint - adj * p1.value / (p2.value * p2.value), op: p2.op, parent1: p2.parent1, parent2: p2.parent2, aux: p2.aux }
    return tape_set(tape2, p2_idx, p2_new)
}

// Helper: Add gradient for unary op to parent
fn backward_unary(tape: Tape, p1_idx: i64, grad: f64) -> Tape {
    let p1 = tape_get(tape, p1_idx)
    let p1_new = TapeNode { value: p1.value, adjoint: p1.adjoint + grad, op: p1.op, parent1: p1.parent1, parent2: p1.parent2, aux: p1.aux }
    return tape_set(tape, p1_idx, p1_new)
}

// Propagate gradient from node to parents
// Refactored to avoid nested if blocks (Sounio compiler scoping bug workaround)
fn backward_node(tape: Tape, idx: i64) -> Tape {
    let node = tape_get(tape, idx)

    // Copy ALL needed values to local vars at function start
    let cur_adj = node.adjoint
    let cur_op = node.op
    let cur_p1_idx = node.parent1
    let cur_p2_idx = node.parent2
    let cur_aux = node.aux
    let cur_value = node.value

    // No parent means nothing to backprop
    if cur_p1_idx < 0 {
        return tape
    }

    // Get parent info
    let p1 = tape_get(tape, cur_p1_idx)
    let p1_value = p1.value

    // Dispatch to helper functions (no nested if blocks)
    if cur_op == op_add() {
        let t1 = backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, cur_adj)
        return backward_add_p2(t1, cur_p2_idx, cur_adj)
    }

    if cur_op == op_sub() {
        let t1 = backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, cur_adj)
        return backward_sub_p2(t1, cur_p2_idx, cur_adj)
    }

    if cur_op == op_mul() {
        return backward_mul(tape, cur_p1_idx, cur_p2_idx, cur_adj)
    }

    if cur_op == op_div() {
        return backward_div(tape, cur_p1_idx, cur_p2_idx, cur_adj)
    }

    if cur_op == op_neg() {
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, 0.0 - cur_adj)
    }

    if cur_op == op_sqrt() {
        // d/dx sqrt(x) = 1/(2*sqrt(x))
        let grad = cur_adj / (2.0 * cur_value)
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, grad)
    }

    if cur_op == op_exp() {
        // d/dx exp(x) = exp(x)
        let grad = cur_adj * cur_value
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, grad)
    }

    if cur_op == op_ln() {
        // d/dx ln(x) = 1/x
        let grad = cur_adj / p1_value
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, grad)
    }

    if cur_op == op_sin() {
        // d/dx sin(x) = cos(x)
        let grad = cur_adj * cos_f64(p1_value)
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, grad)
    }

    if cur_op == op_cos() {
        // d/dx cos(x) = -sin(x)
        let grad = 0.0 - cur_adj * sin_f64(p1_value)
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, grad)
    }

    if cur_op == op_tanh() {
        // d/dx tanh(x) = 1 - tanh²(x)
        let grad = cur_adj * (1.0 - cur_value * cur_value)
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, grad)
    }

    if cur_op == op_pow() {
        // d/dx x^n = n * x^(n-1)
        let n = cur_aux
        let grad = cur_adj * n * pow_f64(p1_value, n - 1.0)
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, grad)
    }

    if cur_op == op_relu() {
        // d/dx ReLU(x) = 1 if x > 0, else 0
        let grad = if p1_value > 0.0 { cur_adj } else { 0.0 }
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, grad)
    }

    if cur_op == op_sigmoid() {
        // d/dx σ(x) = σ(x)(1-σ(x))
        let grad = cur_adj * cur_value * (1.0 - cur_value)
        return backward_unary(tape, cur_p1_idx, grad)
    }

    // Unknown op - return unchanged
    return tape
}

// Run full backward pass from output node
fn backward(tape: Tape, output: Var) -> Tape {

    // Set output adjoint to 1
    let out_node = tape_get(tape, output.idx)
    let out_new = TapeNode { value: out_node.value, adjoint: 1.0, op: out_node.op, parent1: out_node.parent1, parent2: out_node.parent2, aux: out_node.aux }
    var t = tape_set(tape, output.idx, out_new)

    // Traverse in reverse order
    var i = output.idx
    while i >= 0 {
        t = backward_node(t, i)
        i = i - 1
    }

    return t
}

// Get gradient of a variable
fn get_grad(tape: Tape, v: Var) -> f64 {
    return tape_get(tape, v.idx).adjoint
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_tape_square() -> bool {
    // f(x) = x², df/dx = 2x
    // At x=3: f(3) = 9, df/dx = 6
    var tape = new_tape()
    tape = tape_new_var(tape, 3.0)
    let x = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_mul(tape, x, x)
    let y = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = backward(tape, y)

    let grad = get_grad(tape, x)
    let error = abs_f64(grad - 6.0)
    return error < 0.001
}

fn test_tape_chain() -> bool {
    // f(x) = sin(x²), df/dx = 2x·cos(x²)
    // At x=2: f(4) = sin(4) ≈ -0.7568, df/dx = 4·cos(4) ≈ -2.614
    var tape = new_tape()
    tape = tape_new_var(tape, 2.0)
    let x = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_mul(tape, x, x)
    let x2 = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_sin(tape, x2)
    let y = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = backward(tape, y)

    let grad = get_grad(tape, x)
    let expected = 4.0 * cos_f64(4.0)
    let error = abs_f64(grad - expected)
    return error < 0.01
}

fn test_tape_product() -> bool {
    // f(x,y) = x·y, df/dx = y, df/dy = x
    // At x=3, y=5: f = 15, df/dx = 5, df/dy = 3
    var tape = new_tape()
    tape = tape_new_var(tape, 3.0)
    let x = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_new_var(tape, 5.0)
    let y = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_mul(tape, x, y)
    let z = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = backward(tape, z)

    let grad_x = get_grad(tape, x)
    let grad_y = get_grad(tape, y)
    let err_x = abs_f64(grad_x - 5.0)
    let err_y = abs_f64(grad_y - 3.0)
    return err_x < 0.001 && err_y < 0.001
}

fn test_tape_exp() -> bool {
    // f(x) = exp(x), df/dx = exp(x)
    // At x=2: f = exp(2) ≈ 7.389, df/dx = exp(2)
    var tape = new_tape()
    tape = tape_new_var(tape, 2.0)
    let x = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_exp(tape, x)
    let y = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = backward(tape, y)

    let grad = get_grad(tape, x)
    let expected = exp_f64(2.0)
    let error = abs_f64(grad - expected)
    return error < 0.01
}

fn test_tape_sigmoid() -> bool {
    // f(x) = σ(x) = 1/(1+exp(-x)), df/dx = σ(x)(1-σ(x))
    // At x=0: σ(0) = 0.5, df/dx = 0.25
    var tape = new_tape()
    tape = tape_new_var(tape, 0.0)
    let x = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_sigmoid(tape, x)
    let y = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = backward(tape, y)

    let grad = get_grad(tape, x)
    let error = abs_f64(grad - 0.25)
    return error < 0.001
}

fn test_tape_division() -> bool {
    // f(x,y) = x/y, df/dx = 1/y, df/dy = -x/y²
    // At x=6, y=2: f = 3, df/dx = 0.5, df/dy = -1.5
    var tape = new_tape()
    tape = tape_new_var(tape, 6.0)
    let x = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_new_var(tape, 2.0)
    let y = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_div(tape, x, y)
    let z = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = backward(tape, z)

    let grad_x = get_grad(tape, x)
    let grad_y = get_grad(tape, y)
    let err_x = abs_f64(grad_x - 0.5)
    let err_y = abs_f64(grad_y - (0.0 - 1.5))
    return err_x < 0.001 && err_y < 0.001
}

fn test_tape_relu() -> bool {
    // f(x) = ReLU(x), df/dx = 1 if x>0 else 0
    // At x=3: f = 3, df/dx = 1
    // At x=-2: f = 0, df/dx = 0
    var tape1 = new_tape()
    tape1 = tape_new_var(tape1, 3.0)
    let x1 = tape_last_var(tape1)
    tape1 = tape_relu(tape1, x1)
    let y1 = tape_last_var(tape1)
    tape1 = backward(tape1, y1)
    let grad1 = get_grad(tape1, x1)

    var tape2 = new_tape()
    tape2 = tape_new_var(tape2, 0.0 - 2.0)
    let x2 = tape_last_var(tape2)
    tape2 = tape_relu(tape2, x2)
    let y2 = tape_last_var(tape2)
    tape2 = backward(tape2, y2)
    let grad2 = get_grad(tape2, x2)

    let err1 = abs_f64(grad1 - 1.0)
    let err2 = abs_f64(grad2 - 0.0)
    return err1 < 0.001 && err2 < 0.001
}

fn test_tape_neural_net() -> bool {
    // Simple 1-hidden-layer network: f(x) = tanh(w1·x + b1)·w2
    // At x=2, w1=0.5, b1=1, w2=3:
    //   h = tanh(0.5·2 + 1) = tanh(2) ≈ 0.964
    //   y = 0.964·3 ≈ 2.892
    // Gradients:
    //   dy/dw2 = h ≈ 0.964
    //   dy/db1 = w2·(1-h²) ≈ 3·(1-0.964²) ≈ 0.209
    //   dy/dx = w1·w2·(1-h²) ≈ 0.5·3·0.0707 ≈ 0.106

    var tape = new_tape()
    tape = tape_new_var(tape, 2.0)
    let x = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_const(tape, 0.5)
    let w1 = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_const(tape, 1.0)
    let b1 = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_const(tape, 3.0)
    let w2 = tape_last_var(tape)

    // h = w1·x + b1
    tape = tape_mul(tape, w1, x)
    let w1x = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_add(tape, w1x, b1)
    let h_in = tape_last_var(tape)
    tape = tape_tanh(tape, h_in)
    let h = tape_last_var(tape)

    // y = h·w2
    tape = tape_mul(tape, h, w2)
    let y = tape_last_var(tape)

    tape = backward(tape, y)

    let grad_w2 = get_grad(tape, w2)
    let grad_x = get_grad(tape, x)

    // Check dy/dw2 ≈ 0.964
    let h_val = tanh_f64(2.0)
    let err_w2 = abs_f64(grad_w2 - h_val)

    // Check dy/dx ≈ 0.106
    let expected_grad_x = 0.5 * 3.0 * (1.0 - h_val * h_val)
    let err_x = abs_f64(grad_x - expected_grad_x)

    return err_w2 < 0.01 && err_x < 0.01
}

fn run_tape_tests() -> i32 {
    var passed = 0
    if test_tape_square() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_tape_chain() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_tape_product() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_tape_exp() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_tape_sigmoid() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_tape_division() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_tape_relu() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_tape_neural_net() { passed = passed + 1 }
    return passed
}


// === FILE: stdlib/bayes/diagnostics.sio ===
// bayes/diagnostics.sio — MCMC Convergence Diagnostics
//
// Gelman-Rubin R-hat, Effective Sample Size, Geweke diagnostic.
//
// References:
// - Gelman & Rubin (1992): "Inference from iterative simulation using multiple sequences"
// - Geweke (1992): "Evaluating the accuracy of sampling-based approaches"
// - Vehtari et al. (2021): "Rank-normalization, folding, and localization" (split R-hat)

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn diag_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn diag_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

// ============================================================================
// GELMAN-RUBIN R-HAT
// ============================================================================
// chains is a flat array: chain[c] sample[s] at index c * chain_len + s
// n_chains: number of chains (max 8)
// chain_len: samples per chain
// R-hat near 1.0 indicates convergence; >1.1 suggests non-convergence.

pub fn bayes_rhat(chains: &[f64; 1024], n_chains: i32, chain_len: i32) -> f64 {
    if n_chains < 2 || chain_len < 2 {
        return 0.0 - 1.0
    }

    let m = n_chains as f64
    let n = chain_len as f64

    // Compute per-chain means
    var chain_means: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var c: i32 = 0
    while c < n_chains {
        var sum = 0.0
        var s: i32 = 0
        while s < chain_len {
            let idx = c * chain_len + s
            sum = sum + chains[idx as usize]
            s = s + 1
        }
        chain_means[c as usize] = sum / n
        c = c + 1
    }

    // Grand mean
    var grand_sum = 0.0
    c = 0
    while c < n_chains {
        grand_sum = grand_sum + chain_means[c as usize]
        c = c + 1
    }
    let grand_mean = grand_sum / m

    // Between-chain variance B
    var b_sum = 0.0
    c = 0
    while c < n_chains {
        let d = chain_means[c as usize] - grand_mean
        b_sum = b_sum + d * d
        c = c + 1
    }
    let big_b = n * b_sum / (m - 1.0)

    // Within-chain variance W (mean of per-chain variances)
    var w_sum = 0.0
    c = 0
    while c < n_chains {
        var svar = 0.0
        var s: i32 = 0
        while s < chain_len {
            let idx = c * chain_len + s
            let d = chains[idx as usize] - chain_means[c as usize]
            svar = svar + d * d
            s = s + 1
        }
        w_sum = w_sum + svar / (n - 1.0)
        c = c + 1
    }
    let big_w = w_sum / m

    // Pooled variance estimate
    let var_hat = (1.0 - 1.0 / n) * big_w + big_b / n

    if big_w <= 0.0 {
        return 0.0 - 1.0
    }

    // R-hat = sqrt(var_hat / W)
    diag_sqrt(var_hat / big_w)
}

// ============================================================================
// EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE (ESS)
// ============================================================================
// Uses autocorrelation-based ESS estimate.
// ESS = n / (1 + 2 * sum(autocorrelations))
// Truncates when autocorrelation goes negative.

pub fn bayes_ess(chain: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 {
    if n < 4 {
        return 0.0
    }

    // Compute mean
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + chain[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean = sum / (n as f64)

    // Compute variance (lag 0 autocorrelation)
    var var_sum = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let d = chain[i as usize] - mean
        var_sum = var_sum + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    let variance = var_sum / (n as f64)

    if variance <= 0.0 {
        return 0.0
    }

    // Sum autocorrelations at increasing lags, stop when negative
    var tau = 1.0
    let max_lag = n / 2
    var lag: i32 = 1
    while lag < max_lag {
        var ac = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n - lag {
            ac = ac + (chain[i as usize] - mean) * (chain[(i + lag) as usize] - mean)
            i = i + 1
        }
        let rho = ac / (variance * (n as f64))

        if rho < 0.0 {
            lag = max_lag  // break
        } else {
            tau = tau + 2.0 * rho
            lag = lag + 1
        }
    }

    if tau <= 0.0 {
        return (n as f64)
    }

    (n as f64) / tau
}

// ============================================================================
// GEWEKE DIAGNOSTIC
// ============================================================================
// Compares first 10% of chain to last 50% using a Z-test.
// |Z| < 1.96 suggests convergence at 5% significance.

pub fn bayes_geweke(chain: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 {
    if n < 20 {
        return 0.0
    }

    // First 10%
    let n_a = n / 10
    if n_a < 2 { return 0.0 }
    var sum_a = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_a {
        sum_a = sum_a + chain[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean_a = sum_a / (n_a as f64)

    var var_a = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_a {
        let d = chain[i as usize] - mean_a
        var_a = var_a + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    var_a = var_a / (n_a as f64)

    // Last 50%
    let n_b = n / 2
    if n_b < 2 { return 0.0 }
    let start_b = n - n_b
    var sum_b = 0.0
    i = start_b
    while i < n {
        sum_b = sum_b + chain[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean_b = sum_b / (n_b as f64)

    var var_b = 0.0
    i = start_b
    while i < n {
        let d = chain[i as usize] - mean_b
        var_b = var_b + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    var_b = var_b / (n_b as f64)

    // Z-score
    let denom = diag_sqrt(var_a / (n_a as f64) + var_b / (n_b as f64))
    if denom <= 0.0 {
        return 0.0
    }

    (mean_a - mean_b) / denom
}

// ============================================================================
// INLINE TESTS
// ============================================================================

//@ run-pass
fn test_rhat_identical_chains() -> i32 {
    // Identical chains should have R-hat = 1.0
    var chains: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 128 {
        let val = (i as f64) * 0.01
        chains[i as usize] = val          // chain 0
        chains[(128 + i) as usize] = val  // chain 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    let rhat = bayes_rhat(&chains, 2, 128)
    // For identical chains, R-hat should be very close to 1.0
    if diag_abs(rhat - 1.0) > 0.01 { return 1 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_ess_constant_chain() -> i32 {
    // Constant chain: variance = 0, ESS = 0
    var chain: [f64; 256] = [5.0; 256]
    let ess = bayes_ess(&chain, 100)
    if ess != 0.0 { return 1 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_geweke_constant_chain() -> i32 {
    var chain: [f64; 256] = [3.0; 256]
    let z = bayes_geweke(&chain, 100)
    // Constant chain: geweke should be 0
    if diag_abs(z) > 0.001 { return 1 }
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/bayes/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/bayes - Bayesian Inference

module bayes


// === FILE: stdlib/bayes/mcmc.sio ===
// stdlib/bayes/mcmc.sio — Metropolis-Hastings MCMC Sampler
//
// Bayesian posterior sampling with epistemic uncertainty tracking.
// Bridges posterior distributions to GUM-compliant measurement uncertainty.
//
// References:
// - Metropolis et al. (1953): "Equation of state calculations by fast computing machines"
// - Hastings (1970): "Monte Carlo sampling methods using Markov chains and their applications"
// - Gelman et al. (2013): "Bayesian Data Analysis", 3rd ed.
// - JCGM 100:2008 (GUM): Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement

use epistemic::gum::{GUMResult, gum_simple}

extern "C" {
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// Math helpers
// ============================================================================

fn mcmc_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn mcmc_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

fn mcmc_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// Cosine approximation — maps x to [0, 2π] then applies a Chebyshev-style approx
// by folding to [-π, π] and computing cos via higher-order Taylor or section.
// Accurate enough for Box-Muller (we only need |cos| ≤ 1).
fn mcmc_cos(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Reduce to [0, 2π]
    var t = x
    let two_pi = 2.0 * mcmc_pi()
    let pi = mcmc_pi()
    while t < 0.0 { t = t + two_pi }
    while t >= two_pi { t = t - two_pi }
    // Fold to [0, π], flip sign for second half
    var sign = 1.0
    if t > pi {
        t = two_pi - t
        // cos(2π - t) = cos(t), so no sign change here
    }
    // Further fold to [0, π/2], cos is even around π/2
    let half_pi = pi * 0.5
    if t > half_pi {
        t = pi - t
        sign = 0.0 - sign
    }
    // Now t in [0, π/2], use higher-order Taylor for accuracy
    // cos(t) = 1 - t²/2! + t⁴/4! - t⁶/6! + t⁸/8! - t¹⁰/10!
    let t2 = t * t
    let t4 = t2 * t2
    let t6 = t4 * t2
    let t8 = t4 * t4
    let t10 = t8 * t2
    let c = 1.0 - t2 / 2.0 + t4 / 24.0 - t6 / 720.0 + t8 / 40320.0 - t10 / 3628800.0
    sign * c
}

// ============================================================================
// MCMC CONFIGURATION
// ============================================================================

pub struct MCMCConfig {
    pub n_samples: i32,     // Number of posterior samples to collect
    pub n_burnin: i32,      // Burn-in (warmup) samples to discard
    pub step_size: f64,     // Proposal step size (std dev of normal proposal)
    pub model_id: i32,      // 0=normal_mean, 1=normal_variance, 2=linear_slope
}

pub fn mcmc_config_default(model_id: i32) -> MCMCConfig {
    MCMCConfig {
        n_samples: 1000,
        n_burnin: 200,
        step_size: 0.1,
        model_id: model_id,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// MCMC RESULT
// ============================================================================

pub struct MCMCResult {
    pub samples: [f64; 1024],   // Posterior samples (up to 1024)
    pub n_samples: i32,          // Actual number of samples collected
    pub acceptance_rate: f64,    // Fraction of proposals accepted
    pub mean: f64,               // Posterior mean
    pub std_dev: f64,            // Posterior standard deviation
    pub as_gum: GUMResult,       // Epistemic bridge: posterior -> GUMResult
}

// ============================================================================
// PSEUDO-RANDOM NUMBER GENERATION (LCG)
// ============================================================================
// LCG parameters from Numerical Recipes: a=1664525, c=1013904223, m=2^32
// Returns updated state for pure functional threading of random state.

struct LCGResult {
    value: f64,
    state: i64,
}

fn lcg_next(state: i64) -> i64 {
    let a: i64 = 1664525
    let c: i64 = 1013904223
    let m: i64 = 4294967296
    (a * state + c) % m
}

// Returns LCGResult{value=uniform[0,1], state=new_state}
fn lcg_uniform(state: i64) -> LCGResult {
    let next = lcg_next(state)
    let m: i64 = 4294967296
    let u = (next as f64) / (m as f64)
    LCGResult { value: u, state: next }
}

// Returns LCGResult{value=standard_normal, state=new_state} via Box-Muller transform
fn lcg_normal(state: i64) -> LCGResult with Div, Panic {
    let r1 = lcg_uniform(state)
    var u1 = r1.value
    let s1 = r1.state
    if u1 < 1.0e-10 { u1 = 1.0e-10 }
    let r2 = lcg_uniform(s1)
    let u2 = r2.value
    let s2 = r2.state
    let z = mcmc_sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * log(u1)) * mcmc_cos(2.0 * mcmc_pi() * u2)
    LCGResult { value: z, state: s2 }
}

// ============================================================================
// LOG-LIKELIHOOD FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// model_id=0: Normal mean inference, known variance=1
// log p(data | theta) = -0.5 * sum((x_i - theta)^2) (omitting constants)
fn log_lik_normal_mean(theta: f64, data: &[f64; 256], n_data: i32) -> f64 {
    var lsum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_data {
        let d = data[i as usize] - theta
        lsum = lsum - 0.5 * d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    lsum
}

// model_id=1: Normal variance inference, known mean=0
// log p(data | theta) = -n/2*log(theta) - sum(x_i^2)/(2*theta), theta>0
fn log_lik_normal_var(theta: f64, data: &[f64; 256], n_data: i32) -> f64 {
    if theta <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var lsum = 0.0 - (n_data as f64) * 0.5 * log(theta)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_data {
        lsum = lsum - data[i as usize] * data[i as usize] / (2.0 * theta)
        i = i + 1
    }
    lsum
}

// model_id=2: Linear slope inference, y = theta*x + noise (variance=1)
// log p(y | theta, x) = -0.5 * sum((y_i - theta*x_i)^2)
fn log_lik_linear_slope(theta: f64, x_data: &[f64; 256], y_data: &[f64; 256], n_data: i32) -> f64 {
    var lsum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_data {
        let resid = y_data[i as usize] - theta * x_data[i as usize]
        lsum = lsum - 0.5 * resid * resid
        i = i + 1
    }
    lsum
}

// Compute log-likelihood for normal_mean or normal_var models (single data array)
fn dispatch_log_lik(model_id: i32, theta: f64, data: &[f64; 256], n_data: i32) -> f64 {
    if model_id == 0 {
        return log_lik_normal_mean(theta, data, n_data)
    }
    if model_id == 1 {
        return log_lik_normal_var(theta, data, n_data)
    }
    // model_id=2 handled separately (needs x_data and y_data)
    log_lik_normal_mean(theta, data, n_data)
}

// ============================================================================
// POSTERIOR SUMMARY COMPUTATION
// ============================================================================

fn compute_posterior_mean(samples: &[f64; 1024], n: i32) -> f64 {
    if n == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var s = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        s = s + samples[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    s / (n as f64)
}

fn compute_posterior_std(samples: &[f64; 1024], n: i32, mean: f64) -> f64 {
    if n <= 1 { return 0.0 }
    var ss = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let d = samples[i as usize] - mean
        ss = ss + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    mcmc_sqrt(ss / ((n - 1) as f64))
}

// ============================================================================
// METROPOLIS-HASTINGS SAMPLER — single data array (model 0 or 1)
// ============================================================================

pub fn mcmc_run(config: MCMCConfig, data: &[f64; 256], n_data: i32, seed: i64) -> MCMCResult {
    var samples: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]

    // Initialize theta at data mean (faster convergence than starting at 0)
    var init_sum = 0.0
    var ii: i32 = 0
    while ii < n_data {
        init_sum = init_sum + data[ii as usize]
        ii = ii + 1
    }
    var rng_state = seed
    var theta = if n_data > 0 { init_sum / (n_data as f64) } else { 0.0 }
    var log_lik_cur = dispatch_log_lik(config.model_id, theta, data, n_data)

    var n_accepted: i32 = 0
    var n_total: i32 = 0

    // Burn-in phase
    var bi: i32 = 0
    while bi < config.n_burnin {
        let prop_r = lcg_normal(rng_state)
        let z = prop_r.value
        rng_state = prop_r.state

        let theta_new = theta + config.step_size * z
        let log_lik_new = dispatch_log_lik(config.model_id, theta_new, data, n_data)
        let log_alpha = log_lik_new - log_lik_cur

        let u_r = lcg_uniform(rng_state)
        let u = u_r.value
        rng_state = u_r.state

        let log_u = log(if u < 1.0e-30 { 1.0e-30 } else { u })
        if log_u < log_alpha {
            theta = theta_new
            log_lik_cur = log_lik_new
        }
        bi = bi + 1
    }

    // Collection phase
    let max_store: i32 = 1024
    var sample_idx: i32 = 0
    let to_collect = if config.n_samples < max_store { config.n_samples } else { max_store }

    var si: i32 = 0
    while si < to_collect {
        let prop_r = lcg_normal(rng_state)
        let z = prop_r.value
        rng_state = prop_r.state

        let theta_new = theta + config.step_size * z
        let log_lik_new = dispatch_log_lik(config.model_id, theta_new, data, n_data)
        let log_alpha = log_lik_new - log_lik_cur

        let u_r = lcg_uniform(rng_state)
        let u = u_r.value
        rng_state = u_r.state

        let log_u = log(if u < 1.0e-30 { 1.0e-30 } else { u })
        if log_u < log_alpha {
            theta = theta_new
            log_lik_cur = log_lik_new
            n_accepted = n_accepted + 1
        }
        n_total = n_total + 1

        samples[sample_idx as usize] = theta
        sample_idx = sample_idx + 1
        si = si + 1
    }

    let n_collected = sample_idx
    let acc_rate = if n_total > 0 { (n_accepted as f64) / (n_total as f64) } else { 0.0 }
    let post_mean = compute_posterior_mean(&samples, n_collected)
    let post_std = compute_posterior_std(&samples, n_collected, post_mean)
    let gum = gum_simple(post_mean, post_std)

    MCMCResult {
        samples: samples,
        n_samples: n_collected,
        acceptance_rate: acc_rate,
        mean: post_mean,
        std_dev: post_std,
        as_gum: gum,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// METROPOLIS-HASTINGS SAMPLER — linear slope model (model 2)
// ============================================================================

pub fn mcmc_run_linear(config: MCMCConfig, x_data: &[f64; 256], y_data: &[f64; 256], n_data: i32, seed: i64) -> MCMCResult {
    var samples: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]

    // Initialize theta at OLS slope estimate: sum(x*y) / sum(x^2)
    var sum_xy = 0.0
    var sum_xx = 0.0
    var li: i32 = 0
    while li < n_data {
        sum_xy = sum_xy + x_data[li as usize] * y_data[li as usize]
        sum_xx = sum_xx + x_data[li as usize] * x_data[li as usize]
        li = li + 1
    }
    var rng_state = seed
    var theta = if sum_xx > 1.0e-15 { sum_xy / sum_xx } else { 0.0 }
    var log_lik_cur = log_lik_linear_slope(theta, x_data, y_data, n_data)

    var n_accepted: i32 = 0
    var n_total: i32 = 0

    // Burn-in phase
    var bi: i32 = 0
    while bi < config.n_burnin {
        let prop_r = lcg_normal(rng_state)
        let z = prop_r.value
        rng_state = prop_r.state

        let theta_new = theta + config.step_size * z
        let log_lik_new = log_lik_linear_slope(theta_new, x_data, y_data, n_data)
        let log_alpha = log_lik_new - log_lik_cur

        let u_r = lcg_uniform(rng_state)
        let u = u_r.value
        rng_state = u_r.state

        let log_u = log(if u < 1.0e-30 { 1.0e-30 } else { u })
        if log_u < log_alpha {
            theta = theta_new
            log_lik_cur = log_lik_new
        }
        bi = bi + 1
    }

    // Collection phase
    let max_store: i32 = 1024
    var sample_idx: i32 = 0
    let to_collect = if config.n_samples < max_store { config.n_samples } else { max_store }

    var si: i32 = 0
    while si < to_collect {
        let prop_r = lcg_normal(rng_state)
        let z = prop_r.value
        rng_state = prop_r.state

        let theta_new = theta + config.step_size * z
        let log_lik_new = log_lik_linear_slope(theta_new, x_data, y_data, n_data)
        let log_alpha = log_lik_new - log_lik_cur

        let u_r = lcg_uniform(rng_state)
        let u = u_r.value
        rng_state = u_r.state

        let log_u = log(if u < 1.0e-30 { 1.0e-30 } else { u })
        if log_u < log_alpha {
            theta = theta_new
            log_lik_cur = log_lik_new
            n_accepted = n_accepted + 1
        }
        n_total = n_total + 1

        samples[sample_idx as usize] = theta
        sample_idx = sample_idx + 1
        si = si + 1
    }

    let n_collected = sample_idx
    let acc_rate = if n_total > 0 { (n_accepted as f64) / (n_total as f64) } else { 0.0 }
    let post_mean = compute_posterior_mean(&samples, n_collected)
    let post_std = compute_posterior_std(&samples, n_collected, post_mean)
    let gum = gum_simple(post_mean, post_std)

    MCMCResult {
        samples: samples,
        n_samples: n_collected,
        acceptance_rate: acc_rate,
        mean: post_mean,
        std_dev: post_std,
        as_gum: gum,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/bayes/prior.sio ===
// bayes::prior — Prior Distributions for Bayesian Inference
//
// Common prior distributions with log-probability evaluation.
// Designed for use with MCMC and variational inference.
//
// References:
// - Gelman et al. (2013): "Bayesian Data Analysis"
// - Stan Development Team: "Stan Prior Choice Recommendations"

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64;
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

// ============================================================================
// PRIOR RESULT TYPES
// ============================================================================

// Result of prior evaluation
struct PriorEval {
    log_prob: f64,      // Log-probability density
    valid: bool,        // Whether value is in support
}

fn prior_eval_new(lp: f64, valid: bool) -> PriorEval {
    PriorEval { log_prob: lp, valid: valid }
}

// Prior specification with hyperparameters
struct Prior {
    dist_type: i64,     // 0=Normal, 1=LogNormal, 2=Uniform, 3=Beta, 4=Gamma, 5=HalfNormal, 6=Exponential
    param1: f64,        // Mean/location/lower/alpha/shape
    param2: f64,        // Std/scale/upper/beta/rate
}

fn prior_new(dist_type: i64, p1: f64, p2: f64) -> Prior {
    Prior { dist_type: dist_type, param1: p1, param2: p2 }
}

// ============================================================================
// NORMAL PRIOR
// ============================================================================

// Normal(mu, sigma) prior
fn prior_normal(mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> Prior {
    prior_new(0, mu, sigma)
}

// Log-probability of Normal prior
fn log_prob_normal(x: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if sigma <= 0.0 {
        return prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
    }

    let z = (x - mu) / sigma
    let lp = -0.5 * log(2.0 * pi()) - log(sigma) - 0.5 * z * z
    prior_eval_new(lp, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// LOG-NORMAL PRIOR
// ============================================================================

// LogNormal(mu, sigma) prior - for positive parameters
fn prior_lognormal(mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> Prior {
    prior_new(1, mu, sigma)
}

// Log-probability of LogNormal prior
fn log_prob_lognormal(x: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if x <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0 {
        return prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
    }

    let log_x = log(x)
    let z = (log_x - mu) / sigma
    let lp = -0.5 * log(2.0 * pi()) - log(sigma) - log_x - 0.5 * z * z
    prior_eval_new(lp, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// UNIFORM PRIOR
// ============================================================================

// Uniform(lower, upper) prior
fn prior_uniform(lower: f64, upper: f64) -> Prior {
    prior_new(2, lower, upper)
}

// Log-probability of Uniform prior
fn log_prob_uniform(x: f64, lower: f64, upper: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if x < lower || x >= upper {
        return prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
    }

    let lp = -log(upper - lower)
    prior_eval_new(lp, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// BETA PRIOR
// ============================================================================

// Beta(alpha, beta) prior - for probabilities in [0, 1]
fn prior_beta(alpha: f64, beta: f64) -> Prior {
    prior_new(3, alpha, beta)
}

// Log-probability of Beta prior (simplified, no log-gamma)
fn log_prob_beta(x: f64, alpha: f64, beta: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if x <= 0.0 || x >= 1.0 || alpha <= 0.0 || beta <= 0.0 {
        return prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
    }

    // log(x^(a-1) * (1-x)^(b-1)) - log(B(a,b))
    // We omit the normalizing constant for MCMC purposes
    let lp = (alpha - 1.0) * log(x) + (beta - 1.0) * log(1.0 - x)
    prior_eval_new(lp, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// GAMMA PRIOR
// ============================================================================

// Gamma(shape, rate) prior - for positive parameters
fn prior_gamma(shape: f64, rate: f64) -> Prior {
    prior_new(4, shape, rate)
}

// Log-probability of Gamma prior (simplified)
fn log_prob_gamma(x: f64, shape: f64, rate: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if x <= 0.0 || shape <= 0.0 || rate <= 0.0 {
        return prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
    }

    // (shape - 1) * log(x) - rate * x + shape * log(rate) - log(Gamma(shape))
    // Omit normalizing constant
    let lp = (shape - 1.0) * log(x) - rate * x
    prior_eval_new(lp, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// HALF-NORMAL PRIOR
// ============================================================================

// HalfNormal(sigma) prior - for positive scale parameters
fn prior_half_normal(sigma: f64) -> Prior {
    prior_new(5, 0.0, sigma)
}

// Log-probability of HalfNormal prior
fn log_prob_half_normal(x: f64, sigma: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if x < 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0 {
        return prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
    }

    let z = x / sigma
    let lp = log(2.0) - 0.5 * log(2.0 * pi()) - log(sigma) - 0.5 * z * z
    prior_eval_new(lp, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPONENTIAL PRIOR
// ============================================================================

// Exponential(rate) prior - for positive waiting times
fn prior_exponential(rate: f64) -> Prior {
    prior_new(6, rate, 0.0)
}

// Log-probability of Exponential prior
fn log_prob_exponential(x: f64, rate: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if x < 0.0 || rate <= 0.0 {
        return prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
    }

    let lp = log(rate) - rate * x
    prior_eval_new(lp, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// CAUCHY PRIOR (HEAVY-TAILED)
// ============================================================================

// Cauchy(location, scale) prior - robust, heavy-tailed
fn prior_cauchy(location: f64, scale: f64) -> Prior {
    prior_new(7, location, scale)
}

// Log-probability of Cauchy prior
fn log_prob_cauchy(x: f64, location: f64, scale: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if scale <= 0.0 {
        return prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
    }

    let z = (x - location) / scale
    let lp = -log(pi()) - log(scale) - log(1.0 + z * z)
    prior_eval_new(lp, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// HALF-CAUCHY PRIOR
// ============================================================================

// HalfCauchy(scale) prior - for variance parameters (recommended by Gelman)
fn prior_half_cauchy(scale: f64) -> Prior {
    prior_new(8, 0.0, scale)
}

// Log-probability of HalfCauchy prior
fn log_prob_half_cauchy(x: f64, scale: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if x < 0.0 || scale <= 0.0 {
        return prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
    }

    let z = x / scale
    let lp = log(2.0) - log(pi()) - log(scale) - log(1.0 + z * z)
    prior_eval_new(lp, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// GENERIC PRIOR EVALUATION
// ============================================================================

// Evaluate log-probability of any prior at value x
fn prior_log_prob(prior: Prior, x: f64) -> PriorEval {
    if prior.dist_type == 0 {
        return log_prob_normal(x, prior.param1, prior.param2)
    }
    if prior.dist_type == 1 {
        return log_prob_lognormal(x, prior.param1, prior.param2)
    }
    if prior.dist_type == 2 {
        return log_prob_uniform(x, prior.param1, prior.param2)
    }
    if prior.dist_type == 3 {
        return log_prob_beta(x, prior.param1, prior.param2)
    }
    if prior.dist_type == 4 {
        return log_prob_gamma(x, prior.param1, prior.param2)
    }
    if prior.dist_type == 5 {
        return log_prob_half_normal(x, prior.param2)
    }
    if prior.dist_type == 6 {
        return log_prob_exponential(x, prior.param1)
    }
    if prior.dist_type == 7 {
        return log_prob_cauchy(x, prior.param1, prior.param2)
    }
    if prior.dist_type == 8 {
        return log_prob_half_cauchy(x, prior.param2)
    }
    // Unknown prior type
    prior_eval_new(-1e100, false)
}

// ============================================================================
// PRIOR RECOMMENDATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Weakly informative prior for regression coefficients
fn prior_weakly_informative_coef() -> Prior {
    // Normal(0, 2.5) as recommended by Stan
    prior_normal(0.0, 2.5)
}

// Weakly informative prior for intercepts
fn prior_weakly_informative_intercept() -> Prior {
    // Student-t approximated by Cauchy
    prior_cauchy(0.0, 10.0)
}

// Weakly informative prior for scale parameters
fn prior_weakly_informative_scale() -> Prior {
    // Half-Cauchy(0, 2.5) as recommended by Gelman
    prior_half_cauchy(2.5)
}

// Jeffreys prior for variance (improper, use with caution)
fn prior_jeffreys_variance() -> Prior {
    // Corresponds to p(sigma^2) prop to 1/sigma^2
    // Approximated as Gamma(0.001, 0.001)
    prior_gamma(0.001, 0.001)
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { -x } else { x }
}

fn test_normal_prior() -> bool {
    let prior = prior_normal(0.0, 1.0)
    let eval = prior_log_prob(prior, 0.0)

    // log(N(0|0,1)) = -0.5 * log(2*pi) ≈ -0.919
    eval.valid && abs_f64(eval.log_prob - (-0.919)) < 0.01
}

fn test_lognormal_prior() -> bool {
    let prior = prior_lognormal(0.0, 1.0)

    // Value must be positive
    let eval_neg = prior_log_prob(prior, -1.0)
    let eval_pos = prior_log_prob(prior, 1.0)

    !eval_neg.valid && eval_pos.valid
}

fn test_uniform_prior() -> bool {
    let prior = prior_uniform(0.0, 1.0)

    let eval_in = prior_log_prob(prior, 0.5)
    let eval_out = prior_log_prob(prior, 1.5)

    // log(U(0.5|0,1)) = log(1) = 0
    eval_in.valid && abs_f64(eval_in.log_prob) < 0.01 && !eval_out.valid
}

fn test_beta_prior() -> bool {
    let prior = prior_beta(2.0, 2.0)

    let eval = prior_log_prob(prior, 0.5)

    // Beta(2,2) is symmetric, mode at 0.5
    // log((0.5)^1 * (0.5)^1) = 2 * log(0.5) ≈ -1.39
    eval.valid && eval.log_prob > -2.0
}

fn test_half_normal_support() -> bool {
    let prior = prior_half_normal(1.0)

    let eval_neg = prior_log_prob(prior, -0.5)
    let eval_pos = prior_log_prob(prior, 0.5)

    !eval_neg.valid && eval_pos.valid
}


// === FILE: stdlib/bayes/vi.sio ===
// bayes/vi.sio — Variational Inference (Mean-Field Gaussian)
//
// ELBO maximization for approximate Bayesian inference.
// Uses mean-field Gaussian approximation with reparameterization trick.
//
// References:
// - Blei, Kucukelbir, McAuliffe (2017): "Variational Inference: A Review"
// - Kingma & Welling (2014): "Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes"
// - Kucukelbir et al. (2017): "Automatic Differentiation Variational Inference"

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn vi_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn vi_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn vi_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

// ============================================================================
// VI PARAMETERS — Mean-field Gaussian q(theta) = N(mu, sigma^2)
// ============================================================================

pub struct VIParams {
    mu: [f64; 16],       // Variational means
    sigma: [f64; 16],    // Variational standard deviations (>0)
    n_params: i32,       // Number of active parameters (max 16)
}

pub fn vi_params_new(n: i32) -> VIParams {
    var mu: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var sigma: [f64; 16] = [1.0; 16]
    VIParams { mu: mu, sigma: sigma, n_params: n }
}

// ============================================================================
// PSEUDO-RANDOM (LCG)
// ============================================================================

fn vi_lcg_next(state: i64) -> i64 {
    let a: i64 = 1664525
    let c: i64 = 1013904223
    let m: i64 = 4294967296
    (a * state + c) % m
}

fn vi_lcg_uniform(state: i64) -> (f64, i64) {
    let next = vi_lcg_next(state)
    let m: i64 = 4294967296
    let u = (next as f64) / (m as f64)
    (u, next)
}

// ============================================================================
// EVIDENCE LOWER BOUND (ELBO)
// ============================================================================
// ELBO = E_q[log p(data|theta)] - KL(q || prior)
//
// For mean-field Gaussian q and standard normal prior:
//   KL = sum_j [ -0.5 - log(sigma_j) + 0.5*(mu_j^2 + sigma_j^2) ]
//
// We approximate E_q[log p(data|theta)] using the variational mean.
// Assumes normal likelihood: data ~ N(theta[0], 1) for simplicity.

pub fn vi_elbo(params: VIParams, data: &[f64; 256], n_data: i32) -> f64 {
    // Expected log-likelihood at variational mean (plug-in approximation)
    // Assumes: data[i] ~ N(params.mu[0], 1)
    var ll = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_data {
        let d = data[i as usize] - params.mu[0]
        ll = ll - 0.5 * d * d
        i = i + 1
    }

    // KL divergence from q to standard normal prior N(0, 1)
    var kl = 0.0
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < params.n_params {
        let mu_j = params.mu[j as usize]
        var sig_j = params.sigma[j as usize]
        if sig_j < 1.0e-10 { sig_j = 1.0e-10 }
        kl = kl + 0.0 - 0.5 - log(sig_j) + 0.5 * (mu_j * mu_j + sig_j * sig_j)
        j = j + 1
    }

    ll - kl
}

// ============================================================================
// VARIATIONAL GRADIENT STEP
// ============================================================================
// Gradient of ELBO w.r.t. mu and sigma (analytical for Gaussian case).
//
// d ELBO / d mu[0] = sum_i (data[i] - mu[0]) - mu[0]  (likelihood gradient + prior gradient)
// d ELBO / d sigma[j] = 1/sigma[j] - sigma[j]  (entropy gradient + KL gradient)

pub fn vi_step(params: VIParams, data: &[f64; 256], n_data: i32, lr: f64) -> VIParams {
    var new_mu: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var new_sigma: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

    // Copy current values
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < 16 {
        new_mu[k as usize] = params.mu[k as usize]
        new_sigma[k as usize] = params.sigma[k as usize]
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Gradient for mu[0] (the mean parameter)
    var grad_mu0 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_data {
        grad_mu0 = grad_mu0 + (data[i as usize] - params.mu[0])
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Prior gradient: d/dmu[-0.5 * mu^2] = -mu
    grad_mu0 = grad_mu0 - params.mu[0]
    new_mu[0] = params.mu[0] + lr * grad_mu0

    // Gradient for sigma (entropy + KL)
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < params.n_params {
        var sig_j = params.sigma[j as usize]
        if sig_j < 1.0e-10 { sig_j = 1.0e-10 }
        // d ELBO / d sigma = 1/sigma - sigma
        let grad_sig = 1.0 / sig_j - sig_j
        var new_sig = sig_j + lr * grad_sig
        // Enforce positivity
        if new_sig < 1.0e-6 { new_sig = 1.0e-6 }
        new_sigma[j as usize] = new_sig
        j = j + 1
    }

    VIParams { mu: new_mu, sigma: new_sigma, n_params: params.n_params }
}

// ============================================================================
// INLINE TESTS
// ============================================================================

//@ run-pass
fn test_vi_params_new() -> i32 {
    let p = vi_params_new(3)
    if p.n_params != 3 { return 1 }
    if vi_abs(p.mu[0]) > 0.001 { return 2 }
    if vi_abs(p.sigma[0] - 1.0) > 0.001 { return 3 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_vi_elbo_computes() -> i32 {
    let p = vi_params_new(1)
    var data: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    data[0] = 1.0
    data[1] = 2.0
    data[2] = 1.5
    let elbo = vi_elbo(p, &data, 3)
    // ELBO should be finite and negative
    if elbo > 0.0 { return 1 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_vi_step_moves_toward_data() -> i32 {
    var p = vi_params_new(1)
    var data: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    // All data at 5.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 10 {
        data[i as usize] = 5.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    // After a step, mu[0] should move toward 5.0
    let p2 = vi_step(p, &data, 10, 0.01)
    if p2.mu[0] <= 0.0 { return 1 }  // should be positive, moving toward 5
    0
}
