// === FILE: stdlib/clinical/tacrolimus_oral_safety.sio ===
// stdlib/clinical/tacrolimus_oral_safety.sio
//
// Tacrolimus oral steady-state C24h-trough screening with Knightian
// uncertainty inputs.
//
// Pipeline:
//   PK params (Vc, CL, F_oral) --lift--> Knightian PBoxes
//   --1-compartment oral SS approximation (ka >> ke)--> Knightian C24h PBox
//   --within(target_lo, target_hi) support gate--> {WITHIN_BAND, REFUSE}
//
// This module is the F_oral-dominant analog of stdlib/clinical/vancomycin_pbpk.sio.
// It is the formal-export surface for `formal/lean4/SounioTacrolimusDosingSafety.lean`.
//
// References:
//   Jusko WJ et al. (1995) Clin Pharmacol Ther 57:281–290.  (popPK in
//     liver transplant, CL ≈ 0.4 L/h/kg.)
//   Kershner RP & Fitzsimmons WE (1996) Transplantation 62:920–926.
//     (Whole-blood concentration / efficacy + toxicity, oral F ≈ 0.25
//     CV ≈ 50%.)
//   Bekersky I et al. (1999) J Clin Pharmacol 39:1212–1216.  (Oral
//     absorption, ka ≈ 0.38 h⁻¹.)
//   Staatz CE & Tett SE (2004) Clin Pharmacokinet 43:623–653.  (Review
//     used as umbrella citation for Vd_ss ≈ 1300 L and TDM targets.)
//   Hesselink DA et al. (2014) Clin Pharmacokinet 53:123–139.  (CYP3A5
//     expressor pharmacogenetics, used by validation gate T6.)
//
// Therapeutic window (whole-blood C24h trough, Prograf US label, kidney
// transplant maintenance): 5–15 ng/mL. The narrower 5–10 ng/mL band is
// used for late maintenance and is parameterizable via `is_safe_tac_dose`.
//
// Clinical warning: this is a conservative compiler/stdlib example of
// Knightian interval propagation for trough screening. It is not an
// AUC-guided clinical dosing engine and must not be used as medical
// guidance.
//
// Refinement-type-style contracts (currently enforced at runtime):
//   weight_kg     in [30, 200]
//   crcl_ml_min   in (0, 200]
//   dose_mg       in (0, 20.0]      // oral daily limit (Prograf label)
//   interval_h    in [8, 24]
//   tdm_samples   >= 0
// Each violation produces a vacuous PBox with confidence 0 (REFUSE).
//
// Lean export: formal/lean4/SounioTacrolimusDosingSafety.lean (M3-stage,
// statement-only — same maturity as the vancomycin obligation).

use epistemic::knightian::*

// ============================================================================
// PK PARAMETERS — simplified IV-equivalent values for trough-screening with
// explicit F_oral as a separate variance axis.
//
// Identifiability note (important for the dissertation argument):
//   Standard oral popPK fits report V/F and CL/F (apparent values) because
//   F is non-identifiable from oral data alone. To expose F as a separate
//   uncertainty source — the dissertation contribution for this drug — we
//   adopt the IV-equivalent frame (V, CL, F as three independent inputs):
//
//       C_trough_ss(F, V, CL; D, τ) = F · D / V / (exp(CL·τ/V) − 1)
//
//   Population means calibrated so that 5 mg PO q12h (F=0.25) reproduces
//   the clinically observed whole-blood C12h trough of ~8 ng/mL (Prograf
//   label; Kershner 1996):
//       V_true = 3.6 L/kg     → 252 L for a 70 kg patient
//       CL_true = 0.144 L/h/kg → 10.1 L/h     (apparent t½ ≈ 17 h)
//       F = 0.25                                (Kershner 1996)
//   These are NOT directly Jusko 1995 apparent values; they are the
//   IV-equivalent factorisation V = (V/F)·F, CL = (CL/F)·F using V/F ≈
//   14 L/kg and CL/F ≈ 0.58 L/h/kg, i.e. the apparent fit divided by F.
//
//   The full 14-compartment Vd_ss ≈ 1300 L is exercised separately in
//   stdlib/darwin_pbpk/validation/tacrolimus_oral_pbpk.sio. This 1-comp
//   IV-equivalent model is the *trough-screening* approximation used by
//   the Knightian gate (matches the role of vp_default in vancomycin_pbpk).
//
// CrCl is retained as a refinement-input constraint per the project's
// uniform-screening convention, even though tacrolimus is < 1% renally
// cleared.
// ============================================================================

pub struct TacPKParams {
    vc_l: f64,              // IV-equivalent central volume (L)
    cl_l_per_h: f64,        // IV-equivalent whole-blood clearance (L/h)
    ka_per_h: f64,          // oral absorption rate constant (h⁻¹)
    f_oral: f64,            // oral bioavailability (dimensionless, [0,1])
}

pub fn tp_default(weight_kg: f64, crcl_ml_min: f64) -> TacPKParams {
    // V_true ≈ 3.6 L/kg (IV-equivalent factorisation of V/F ≈ 14 L/kg × F)
    let vc = 3.6 * weight_kg
    // CL_true ≈ 0.144 L/h/kg (IV-equivalent factorisation; gives apparent
    // terminal t½ ≈ 17 h, matching Kershner 1996)
    let cl = 0.144 * weight_kg
    // Refinement-input only — current model does not scale CL by CrCl.
    let _ = crcl_ml_min
    let ka = 0.38     // h⁻¹ (Bekersky 1999, fasted)
    let f  = 0.25     // Kershner 1996, CV ~50%
    TacPKParams { vc_l: vc, cl_l_per_h: cl, ka_per_h: ka, f_oral: f }
}

// ============================================================================
// LIFT params -> PBox with Knightian bands.
// Band widths shrink in tdm_samples (post-TDM Bayesian narrowing).
//
// Pre-TDM widths reflect literature popPK variability:
//   Vc:     ±15% (Staatz 2004)
//   CL:     ±25% (Jusko 1995; CYP3A4 IIV + CYP3A5 polymorphism)
//   F_oral: ±50% (Kershner 1996; food, formulation, P-gp IIV)
// ka is held fixed in the Fréchet enclosure because for ka >> ke the
// C24h trough is insensitive to ka (sensitivity ≈ 0 to leading order).
// ============================================================================

fn tp_band_vc(tdm_samples: i64) -> f64 {
    if tdm_samples >= 3 { return 0.07 }
    if tdm_samples >= 1 { return 0.10 }
    0.15
}

fn tp_band_cl(tdm_samples: i64) -> f64 {
    if tdm_samples >= 3 { return 0.10 }
    if tdm_samples >= 1 { return 0.15 }
    0.25
}

fn tp_band_f(tdm_samples: i64) -> f64 {
    // F_oral does not narrow much with TDM alone (TDM measures C, not F
    // directly; post-TDM the F·V combination is well-identified, but F by
    // itself remains uncertain). The post-TDM narrowing here represents
    // additional information from CYP3A5 genotyping or repeat-dose data
    // routinely collected alongside TDM in transplant clinics — see Staatz
    // 2004 §3.3 and Hesselink 2014.
    if tdm_samples >= 3 { return 0.25 }
    if tdm_samples >= 1 { return 0.40 }
    0.50
}

pub fn tp_vc_to_pbox(p: &TacPKParams, tdm_samples: i64) -> PBox {
    let frac = tp_band_vc(tdm_samples)
    let lo = (1.0 - frac) * p.vc_l
    let hi = (1.0 + frac) * p.vc_l
    let v = 0.0025 * p.vc_l * p.vc_l
    pb_new(lo, hi, v, 920)
}

pub fn tp_cl_to_pbox(p: &TacPKParams, tdm_samples: i64) -> PBox {
    let frac = tp_band_cl(tdm_samples)
    let lo = (1.0 - frac) * p.cl_l_per_h
    let hi = (1.0 + frac) * p.cl_l_per_h
    let v = 0.01 * p.cl_l_per_h * p.cl_l_per_h
    pb_new(lo, hi, v, 880)
}

pub fn tp_f_to_pbox(p: &TacPKParams, tdm_samples: i64) -> PBox with Mut {
    let frac = tp_band_f(tdm_samples)
    var lo = (1.0 - frac) * p.f_oral
    var hi = (1.0 + frac) * p.f_oral
    // Bioavailability is bounded in [0, 1]; clamp.
    if lo < 0.0 { lo = 0.0 }
    if hi > 1.0 { hi = 1.0 }
    let v = 0.04 * p.f_oral * p.f_oral
    pb_new(lo, hi, v, 700)
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPONENTIAL — range-reduced Taylor approximation. Identical mathematical
// content to stdlib/clinical/vancomycin_pbpk.sio::vp_exp_approx (Fréchet
// enclosure requires a numerically stable exp over the full ke·τ range).
// ============================================================================

fn tp_exp_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 { panic("negative exp domain") }
    if x > 64.0 { panic("exp domain outside trough-screening contract") }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var kf = x / ln2
    var k: i32 = 0
    if kf >= 0.0 { k = kf as i32 } else { k = (kf as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2
    var sum: f64 = 1.0
    var term: f64 = 1.0
    var n: i32 = 1
    while n < 28 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 {
        var i: i32 = 0
        while i < k {
            result = result * 2.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < (0 - k) {
            result = result / 2.0
            j = j + 1
        }
    }
    result
}

fn tp_expm1_pos(theta: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if theta <= 0.0 { panic("invalid theta") }
    if theta < 0.001 {
        let t2 = theta * theta
        let t3 = t2 * theta
        let t4 = t3 * theta
        let t5 = t4 * theta
        return theta + t2 / 2.0 + t3 / 6.0 + t4 / 24.0 + t5 / 120.0
    }
    tp_exp_approx(theta) - 1.0
}

// ============================================================================
// STEADY-STATE C24h TROUGH (1-compartment oral, ka >> ke approximation).
//
// For ka >> ke (tacrolimus: ka=0.38 h⁻¹, ke = CL/Vc ≈ 0.022 h⁻¹, ratio ≈ 17),
// the absorption phase is complete well before τ and the trough at time τ
// reduces to the IV-bolus steady-state Cmin scaled by F_oral:
//
//   C_trough_ss(F, Vc, CL; D, τ)
//      = F · D / (Vc · (exp(ke·τ) − 1))
//      = F · D / (Vc · (exp(CL·τ/Vc) − 1))
//
// This is exactly F times the vancomycin Cmin formula in
// stdlib/clinical/vancomycin_pbpk.sio. We inherit the hand-derived
// monotonicity of the inner Cmin term (vancomycin_pbpk.sio:158-165):
//
//   d(F·Cmin)/d(F)  = Cmin                                  > 0
//   d(F·Cmin)/d(D)  = F · Cmin / D                          > 0
//   d(F·Cmin)/d(Vc) = F · D · [e^θ(θ−1) + 1] / [Vc²(e^θ−1)²] > 0  ∀ θ > 0
//   d(F·Cmin)/d(CL) = −F · D · τ · e^θ / [Vc²(e^θ−1)²]      < 0
//
// Fréchet enclosure on the joint distribution of (F, Vc, CL):
//   C24h is INCREASING in F, INCREASING in Vc, DECREASING in CL.
//   → C24h_min at (F_lo, Vc_lo, CL_hi)
//   → C24h_max at (F_hi, Vc_hi, CL_lo)
// Independent of correlation between F, Vc, CL.
//
// Refs: Moore (1966); Williamson & Downs (1990); Ferson et al. (2003).
// The general 2-arg theorem (`pb_apply2_monotone_inc_dec`) extends to
// 3-arg monotone composition by associativity (compose F·g then g·Cmin).
// Lean obligation: formal/lean4/SounioTacrolimusDosingSafety.lean ::
// `tac_c24h_monotone_corners_enclose`.
// ============================================================================

fn tp_c_trough_ss_point(f: f64, vc: f64, cl: f64, dose: f64, tau: f64)
    -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    if f  < 0.0 { panic("invalid f_oral") }
    if f  > 1.0 { panic("invalid f_oral") }
    if vc <= 0.0 { panic("invalid vc") }
    if cl <= 0.0 { panic("invalid cl") }
    if dose <= 0.0 { panic("invalid dose") }
    if tau <= 0.0 { panic("invalid tau") }
    let theta = (cl * tau) / vc
    let denom = tp_expm1_pos(theta)
    if denom <= 0.0 { panic("invalid c24h denominator") }
    (f * dose / vc) / denom
}

// ============================================================================
// CONTRACT GATES (refinement-style runtime enforcement).
// Tacrolimus oral daily dose: Prograf label cap is ~0.2 mg/kg/day for adults
// (= 14 mg for a 70 kg patient). We use 20 mg as a hard outer bound; doses
// above this require ID/pediatric specialist override outside the screening
// pathway.
// ============================================================================

fn tp_dose_valid(dose: f64) -> bool { dose > 0.0 && dose <= 20.0 }
fn tp_tau_valid(tau: f64) -> bool { tau >= 8.0 && tau <= 24.0 }
fn tp_weight_valid(w: f64) -> bool { w >= 30.0 && w <= 200.0 }
fn tp_crcl_valid(c: f64) -> bool { c > 0.0 && c <= 200.0 }
fn tp_tdm_valid(t: i64) -> bool { t >= 0 }

// ============================================================================
// CONSTANT — convert mg to ng for output. C24h is reported in ng/mL,
// which is mg·1e6 / L. The dose-to-Vc ratio above is already in mg/L, so
// we apply the 1e6 ng/mg factor at the public-API boundary.
// ============================================================================

fn tp_mg_per_l_to_ng_per_ml(x: f64) -> f64 { x * 1000.0 }
//                                              ^ 1 mg/L = 1000 ng/mL

// ============================================================================
// PUBLIC API — predict_c_trough_knightian
// ============================================================================
// Returns a PBox over C24h trough in ng/mL. Vacuous (confidence 0) if any
// refinement-type contract fails.

pub fn predict_c_trough_knightian(
    weight_kg: f64,
    crcl_ml_min: f64,
    dose_mg: f64,
    interval_h: f64,
    tdm_samples: i64,
) -> PBox with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if !tp_dose_valid(dose_mg) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if !tp_tau_valid(interval_h) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if !tp_weight_valid(weight_kg) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if !tp_crcl_valid(crcl_ml_min) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if !tp_tdm_valid(tdm_samples) { return pb_vacuous() }

    let params = tp_default(weight_kg, crcl_ml_min)
    let vc_pb = tp_vc_to_pbox(&params, tdm_samples)
    let cl_pb = tp_cl_to_pbox(&params, tdm_samples)
    let f_pb  = tp_f_to_pbox(&params, tdm_samples)

    if pb_lo_mean(&vc_pb) <= 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_hi_mean(&vc_pb) <= 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_lo_mean(&cl_pb) <= 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_hi_mean(&cl_pb) <= 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_lo_mean(&f_pb)  <  0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_hi_mean(&f_pb)  <= 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_lo_mean(&vc_pb) > pb_hi_mean(&vc_pb) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_lo_mean(&cl_pb) > pb_hi_mean(&cl_pb) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_lo_mean(&f_pb)  > pb_hi_mean(&f_pb)  { return pb_vacuous() }

    // Fréchet outer enclosure on (F, Vc, CL).
    // C24h is INCREASING in F, INCREASING in Vc, DECREASING in CL ⇒
    //   C24h_min at (F_lo, Vc_lo, CL_hi);  C24h_max at (F_hi, Vc_hi, CL_lo).
    // Holds for ANY joint distribution of (F, Vc, CL) — see header.
    let c_lo_mg_l = tp_c_trough_ss_point(
        pb_lo_mean(&f_pb), pb_lo_mean(&vc_pb), pb_hi_mean(&cl_pb),
        dose_mg, interval_h,
    )
    let c_hi_mg_l = tp_c_trough_ss_point(
        pb_hi_mean(&f_pb), pb_hi_mean(&vc_pb), pb_lo_mean(&cl_pb),
        dose_mg, interval_h,
    )

    let gap = c_hi_mg_l - c_lo_mg_l
    if gap < 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }

    // Convert to ng/mL at the API boundary.
    let lo_ng = tp_mg_per_l_to_ng_per_ml(c_lo_mg_l)
    let hi_ng = tp_mg_per_l_to_ng_per_ml(c_hi_mg_l)

    // Support-only enclosure (vancomycin convention): leave variance
    // uncalibrated instead of inventing pseudo-statistics from an unknown
    // joint distribution.
    let v = 0.0
    // Preserve the weakest input confidence (3-way min over F, Vc, CL).
    let vc_conf = pb_confidence(&vc_pb)
    let cl_conf = pb_confidence(&cl_pb)
    let f_conf  = pb_confidence(&f_pb)
    var c1 = if vc_conf < cl_conf { vc_conf } else { cl_conf }
    if f_conf < c1 { c1 = f_conf }

    pb_new(lo_ng, hi_ng, v, c1)
}

// ============================================================================
// SAFETY GATE — conservative support-band therapeutic-window screen.
// Refuses if the *band* crosses either boundary OR confidence is below
// the structural provenance threshold.
// ============================================================================

pub fn is_safe_tac_dose(predicted_c24h: &PBox, target_lo_ng_ml: f64,
                        target_hi_ng_ml: f64, min_conf: i64) -> bool {
    if pb_confidence(predicted_c24h) <= 0 { return false }
    if !pb_is_credible(predicted_c24h, min_conf) { return false }
    pb_within(predicted_c24h, target_lo_ng_ml, target_hi_ng_ml)
}

// ============================================================================
// SELF-TEST main()
// ============================================================================
// Three scenarios:
//   1. Pre-TDM (0 samples) — wide band, refuse 4 mg q24h.
//   2. Post-TDM (3 samples) — narrow band, in target → recommend.
//   3. Contract violation — weight 15 kg (out of [30, 200]) → vacuous PBox.

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Standard adult kidney-transplant maintenance patient:
    // 70 kg, CrCl 80 mL/min, oral 7 mg q12h immediate-release Prograf,
    // target whole-blood trough C12h ∈ [5, 15] ng/mL (Prograf label).
    let pre = predict_c_trough_knightian(70.0, 80.0, 5.0, 12.0, 0)
    println(pb_lo_mean(&pre))
    println(pb_hi_mean(&pre))
    if is_safe_tac_dose(&pre, 5.0, 15.0, 700) {
        println("PRE_PRESCRIBE")
    } else {
        println("PRE_REFUSE")
    }

    let post = predict_c_trough_knightian(70.0, 80.0, 5.0, 12.0, 3)
    println(pb_lo_mean(&post))
    println(pb_hi_mean(&post))
    if is_safe_tac_dose(&post, 5.0, 15.0, 700) {
        println("POST_PRESCRIBE")
    } else {
        println("POST_REFUSE")
    }

    let bad = predict_c_trough_knightian(15.0, 80.0, 7.0, 12.0, 0)
    if pb_confidence(&bad) == 0 {
        println("CONTRACT_BLOCK")
    } else {
        println("CONTRACT_LEAK")
    }
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/clinical/vancomycin_pbpk.sio ===
// stdlib/clinical/vancomycin_pbpk.sio
//
// Vancomycin trough-screening approximation with Knightian-uncertainty inputs.
//
// Pipeline:
//   PK params (Vc, CL)  --lift-->  Knightian PBoxes
//   --1-compartment steady-state Cmin approximation--> Knightian Cmin PBox
//   --within(10, 20) support gate-->      {WITHIN_BAND, REFUSE}
//
// References:
//   Rybak MJ et al. Am J Health-Syst Pharm 2020;77:835. (ASHP guideline.)
//   Roberts JA et al. Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2011;55:2855.
//   Marsot et al. Clin Pharmacokinet 2012;51:1-13. (popPK review.)
//
// Clinical warning: this is a conservative compiler/stdlib example of
// Knightian interval propagation for trough screening. It is not an AUC-guided
// clinical dosing engine and must not be used as medical guidance.
//
// Refinement-type-style contracts (currently enforced at runtime):
//   dose_mg     in (0, 4000]
//   interval_h  in [4, 48]
//   weight_kg   in [30, 200]
//   crcl_ml_min in (0, 200]
//   tdm_samples >= 0
// Each violation produces a vacuous PBox with confidence 0 (REFUSE). The
// confidence field is compiler metadata for propagated inputs, not a calibrated
// clinical probability.
//
// Lean export: formal/proof_obligations/vancomycin_dosing_safety.lean

use epistemic::knightian::*

// ============================================================================
// PK PARAMETERS — simplified population values for trough-screening examples
// ============================================================================

pub struct VancoPKParams {
    vc_l: f64,          // central volume (L)
    cl_l_per_h: f64,    // total clearance (L/h)
    vp_l: f64,          // peripheral volume (L)
    q_l_per_h: f64,     // intercompartmental clearance (L/h)
}

pub fn vp_default(weight_kg: f64, crcl_ml_min: f64) -> VancoPKParams {
    // Vc ≈ 0.5 L/kg
    let vc = 0.5 * weight_kg
    // CL (L/h) ≈ 0.05 * CrCl (mL/min) — Cockcroft-Gault scaled
    let cl = 0.05 * crcl_ml_min
    // Retained for future two-compartment/AUC extension; not used by the
    // current trough-screening approximation.
    let vp = 0.5 * weight_kg
    // Retained for future two-compartment/AUC extension.
    let q = 7.0
    VancoPKParams { vc_l: vc, cl_l_per_h: cl, vp_l: vp, q_l_per_h: q }
}

// ============================================================================
// LIFT params -> PBox with Knightian bands.
// The bands reflect literature uncertainty in popPK estimates.
// ============================================================================

// Band widths parametric on number of TDM samples observed.
// 0 samples (pre-TDM):    Vc ±15%, CL ±25% (literature popPK)
// 1+ samples:             Vc ±10%, CL ±10% (Bayesian narrowing)
// 3+ samples:             Vc ±7%,  CL ±7%  (post-TDM convergence)
fn vp_band_vc(tdm_samples: i64) -> f64 {
    if tdm_samples >= 3 { return 0.07 }
    if tdm_samples >= 1 { return 0.10 }
    0.15
}

fn vp_band_cl(tdm_samples: i64) -> f64 {
    if tdm_samples >= 3 { return 0.07 }
    if tdm_samples >= 1 { return 0.10 }
    0.25
}

pub fn vp_vc_to_pbox(p: &VancoPKParams, tdm_samples: i64) -> PBox {
    let frac = vp_band_vc(tdm_samples)
    let lo = (1.0 - frac) * p.vc_l
    let hi = (1.0 + frac) * p.vc_l
    let v = 0.0025 * p.vc_l * p.vc_l
    pb_new(lo, hi, v, 920)
}

pub fn vp_cl_to_pbox(p: &VancoPKParams, tdm_samples: i64) -> PBox {
    let frac = vp_band_cl(tdm_samples)
    let lo = (1.0 - frac) * p.cl_l_per_h
    let hi = (1.0 + frac) * p.cl_l_per_h
    let v = 0.01 * p.cl_l_per_h * p.cl_l_per_h
    pb_new(lo, hi, v, 880)
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPONENTIAL — range-reduced Taylor approximation for steady-state formula.
// The Fréchet Cmin enclosure depends on corner ordering, so this must stay
// stable across the full physiological positive `ke·tau` range instead of relying on
// a low-order Maclaurin approximation around zero.
// ============================================================================

fn vp_exp_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 { panic("negative exp domain") }
    if x > 64.0 { panic("exp domain outside trough-screening contract") }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var kf = x / ln2
    var k: i32 = 0
    if kf >= 0.0 { k = kf as i32 } else { k = (kf as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2
    var sum: f64 = 1.0
    var term: f64 = 1.0
    var n: i32 = 1
    while n < 28 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 {
        var i: i32 = 0
        while i < k {
            result = result * 2.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < (0 - k) {
            result = result / 2.0
            j = j + 1
        }
    }
    result
}

fn vp_expm1_pos(theta: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if theta <= 0.0 { panic("invalid theta") }
    if theta < 0.001 {
        let t2 = theta * theta
        let t3 = t2 * theta
        let t4 = t3 * theta
        let t5 = t4 * theta
        return theta + t2 / 2.0 + t3 / 6.0 + t4 / 24.0 + t5 / 120.0
    }
    vp_exp_approx(theta) - 1.0
}

// ============================================================================
// STEADY-STATE Cmin (1-compartment approximation of slow phase).
//
// ke    = CL / Vc
// tau   = dosing interval (h)
// dose  = mg per interval
//
// Cmin_ss = (dose / Vc) * exp(-ke*tau) / (1 - exp(-ke*tau))
//
// We compute this on Knightian PBoxes by interval extension on the
// monotone subterms.
//
// Hand-derived monotonicity:
//
//   Let θ = ke·τ = (CL·τ)/Vc. Cmin = (D/Vc) / (e^θ - 1).
//
//   d Cmin / d CL = -(D·τ) e^θ / [Vc² (e^θ - 1)²]                  < 0
//   d Cmin / d Vc =  D · [e^θ (θ - 1) + 1] / [Vc² (e^θ - 1)²]      > 0  ∀ θ > 0
//
//   (h(θ) := e^θ(θ-1) + 1 has h(0)=0, h'(θ) = θ·e^θ > 0 ⇒ h(θ) > 0 ∀ θ > 0.)
//
// Therefore Cmin is INCREASING in Vc and DECREASING in CL.
// PBox image corners:
//   Cmin_min: (Vc_lo, CL_hi)
//   Cmin_max: (Vc_hi, CL_lo)
//
// Fréchet soundness statement:
//
//   Because Cmin is C¹ on the closed rectangle [Vc_lo, Vc_hi] × [CL_lo, CL_hi]
//   and strictly monotone in each argument with the signs above, the
//   Theorem in stdlib/epistemic/knightian.sio (`pb_apply2_monotone_inc_dec`)
//   gives an OUTER ENCLOSURE that holds for ANY joint distribution of
//   (Vc, CL), including arbitrary or unknown copula. Concretely:
//
//     [Cmin(Vc_lo, CL_hi), Cmin(Vc_hi, CL_lo)] ⊇ Cmin(Vc, CL)
//                                                      almost surely,
//
//   for any joint distribution of (Vc, CL) with marginal supports in
//   the rectangle. This addresses the consensus pushback recorded in
//   docs/research/knightian_operator_consensus_2026-04-30.md.
//
//   Refs: Moore (1966); Williamson & Downs (1990); Ferson et al. (2003).
//
// Implementation note: Sounio currently lacks closure literals, so we
// cannot pass `vp_cmin_point` curried with (dose, τ) to
// `pb_apply2_monotone_inc_dec`. The body below evaluates the same
// corner enumeration *inline*; the result is provably equal to what
// the wrapper would produce. The wrapper itself exists for other
// 2-arg monotone PBPK / engineering computations.
// ============================================================================

fn vp_cmin_point(vc: f64, cl: f64, dose: f64, tau: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if vc <= 0.0 { panic("invalid vc") }
    if cl <= 0.0 { panic("invalid cl") }
    if dose <= 0.0 { panic("invalid dose") }
    if tau <= 0.0 { panic("invalid tau") }
    let theta = (cl * tau) / vc
    let denom = vp_expm1_pos(theta)
    if denom <= 0.0 { panic("invalid cmin denominator") }
    (dose / vc) / denom
}

// ============================================================================
// CONTRACT GATES (refinement-style runtime enforcement).
// Each returns a vacuous PBox if any precondition fails.
// ============================================================================

fn vp_dose_valid(dose: f64) -> bool { dose > 0.0 && dose <= 4000.0 }
fn vp_tau_valid(tau: f64) -> bool { tau >= 4.0 && tau <= 48.0 }
fn vp_weight_valid(w: f64) -> bool { w >= 30.0 && w <= 200.0 }
fn vp_crcl_valid(c: f64) -> bool { c > 0.0 && c <= 200.0 }
fn vp_tdm_valid(t: i64) -> bool { t >= 0 }

// ============================================================================
// PUBLIC API — predict_cmin_knightian
// ============================================================================

pub fn predict_cmin_knightian(
    weight_kg: f64,
    crcl_ml_min: f64,
    dose_mg: f64,
    interval_h: f64,
    tdm_samples: i64,
) -> PBox with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if !vp_dose_valid(dose_mg) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if !vp_tau_valid(interval_h) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if !vp_weight_valid(weight_kg) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if !vp_crcl_valid(crcl_ml_min) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if !vp_tdm_valid(tdm_samples) { return pb_vacuous() }

    let params = vp_default(weight_kg, crcl_ml_min)
    let vc = vp_vc_to_pbox(&params, tdm_samples)
    let cl = vp_cl_to_pbox(&params, tdm_samples)
    if pb_lo_mean(&vc) <= 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_hi_mean(&vc) <= 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_lo_mean(&cl) <= 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_hi_mean(&cl) <= 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_lo_mean(&vc) > pb_hi_mean(&vc) { return pb_vacuous() }
    if pb_lo_mean(&cl) > pb_hi_mean(&cl) { return pb_vacuous() }

    // Fréchet outer enclosure (see header comment for full statement
    // and `pb_apply2_monotone_inc_dec` for the general theorem).
    // Cmin is INCREASING in Vc and DECREASING in CL ⇒
    //   Cmin_min at (Vc_lo, CL_hi); Cmin_max at (Vc_hi, CL_lo).
    // Independent of correlation between Vc and CL.
    let cmin_low = vp_cmin_point(pb_lo_mean(&vc), pb_hi_mean(&cl), dose_mg, interval_h)
    let cmin_high = vp_cmin_point(pb_hi_mean(&vc), pb_lo_mean(&cl), dose_mg, interval_h)

    let gap = cmin_high - cmin_low
    if gap < 0.0 { return pb_vacuous() }
    // Support-only enclosure: the meaningful output is [cmin_low, cmin_high].
    // Leave variance uncalibrated instead of inventing pseudo-statistics from
    // an unknown joint distribution.
    let v = 0.0

    // Structural metadata only: preserve the weaker input confidence. The
    // support-band gate below is what carries the conservative safety decision.
    let vc_conf = pb_confidence(&vc)
    let cl_conf = pb_confidence(&cl)
    let conf = if vc_conf < cl_conf { vc_conf } else { cl_conf }

    pb_new(cmin_low, cmin_high, v, conf)
}

// ============================================================================
// SAFETY GATE — conservative support-band therapeutic-window screen.
// Refuses if the *band* crosses either boundary. `min_conf` is retained for
// compatibility, but it is only a structural provenance threshold.
// ============================================================================

pub fn is_safe_dose(predicted_cmin: &PBox, target_lo: f64, target_hi: f64,
                    min_conf: i64) -> bool {
    if pb_confidence(predicted_cmin) <= 0 { return false }
    if !pb_is_credible(predicted_cmin, min_conf) { return false }
    pb_within(predicted_cmin, target_lo, target_hi)
}

// ============================================================================
// SELF-TEST main()
// ============================================================================

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Standard adult ICU patient: 78.5 kg, CrCl 65 mL/min,
    // dose 1000 mg q12h. Pre-TDM (0 samples) -> wide band -> REFUSE.
    let pre = predict_cmin_knightian(78.5, 65.0, 1000.0, 12.0, 0)
    println(pb_lo_mean(&pre))
    println(pb_hi_mean(&pre))
    if is_safe_dose(&pre, 10.0, 20.0, 800) {
        println("PRE_PRESCRIBE")
    } else {
        println("PRE_REFUSE")
    }

    // Same patient, post-TDM (3 samples) -> narrow band -> safe to prescribe
    let post = predict_cmin_knightian(78.5, 65.0, 1000.0, 12.0, 3)
    println(pb_lo_mean(&post))
    println(pb_hi_mean(&post))
    if is_safe_dose(&post, 10.0, 20.0, 800) {
        println("POST_PRESCRIBE")
    } else {
        println("POST_REFUSE")
    }

    // Contract violation: weight 15 kg out of [30, 200]
    let bad = predict_cmin_knightian(15.0, 65.0, 1000.0, 12.0, 0)
    if pb_confidence(&bad) == 0 {
        println("CONTRACT_BLOCK")
    } else {
        println("CONTRACT_LEAK")
    }
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/cmp/lib.sio ===
// stdlib/cmp/lib.sio — Comparison and ordering utilities
//
// Functions:
//   cmp_i64      — three-way comparison (-1/0/1) for i64
//   cmp_f64      — three-way comparison (-1/0/1) for f64 (epsilon 1e-15)
//   min_i64      — minimum of two i64 values
//   max_i64      — maximum of two i64 values
//   min_f64      — minimum of two f64 values
//   max_f64      — maximum of two f64 values
//   clamp_f64    — clamp f64 to [lo, hi]
//   clamp_i64    — clamp i64 to [lo, hi]
//   approx_eq    — f64 equality within tolerance
//   sign_f64     — returns -1.0, 0.0, or 1.0

fn abs_f64_cmp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    x
}

fn cmp_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i32 {
    if a < b { return -1 }
    if a > b { return 1 }
    0
}

fn cmp_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> i32 {
    let eps: f64 = 1e-15
    let diff = a - b
    if diff < 0.0 - eps { return -1 }
    if diff > eps { return 1 }
    0
}

fn min_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    b
}

fn max_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    b
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    b
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    b
}

fn clamp_f64(x: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < lo { return lo }
    if x > hi { return hi }
    x
}

fn clamp_i64(x: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 {
    if x < lo { return lo }
    if x > hi { return hi }
    x
}

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let diff = abs_f64_cmp(a - b)
    diff <= tol
}

fn sign_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return -1.0 }
    if x > 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    0.0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/collections/bitset.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL PASS

// stdlib/collections/bitset — Dense bit set
//
// BitSet: 65536 bits (1024 i64 words). O(1) set/clear/test.
// Supports union, intersection, xor, and popcount.

let BITSET_WORDS: i64 = 1024
let BITSET_MAX_BITS: i64 = 65536

pub struct BitSet {
    words: [i64; 1024],
}

impl BitSet {
    fn set(self: &!BitSet, bit: i64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
        if bit < 0 || bit >= BITSET_MAX_BITS { return }
        let word_idx = bit / 64
        let bit_idx = bit - word_idx * 64
        self.words[word_idx] = self.words[word_idx] | (1 << bit_idx)
    }

    fn clear_bit(self: &!BitSet, bit: i64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
        if bit < 0 || bit >= BITSET_MAX_BITS { return }
        let word_idx = bit / 64
        let bit_idx = bit - word_idx * 64
        let mask = 1 << bit_idx
        self.words[word_idx] = self.words[word_idx] & (0 - 1 - mask)
    }

    fn test(self: &BitSet, bit: i64) -> bool with Div, Panic {
        if bit < 0 || bit >= BITSET_MAX_BITS { return false }
        let word_idx = bit / 64
        let bit_idx = bit - word_idx * 64
        (self.words[word_idx] & (1 << bit_idx)) != 0
    }

    fn count(self: &BitSet) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
        var total: i64 = 0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < BITSET_WORDS {
            var w = self.words[i]
            // Brian Kernighan: w & (w-1) clears lowest set bit, avoids shift of negative i64
            while w != 0 {
                w = w & (w - 1)
                total = total + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        total
    }

    fn union_with(self: &!BitSet, other: &BitSet) with Mut, Div, Panic {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < BITSET_WORDS {
            self.words[i] = self.words[i] | other.words[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    fn intersect_with(self: &!BitSet, other: &BitSet) with Mut, Div, Panic {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < BITSET_WORDS {
            self.words[i] = self.words[i] & other.words[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    fn xor_with(self: &!BitSet, other: &BitSet) with Mut, Div, Panic {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < BITSET_WORDS {
            self.words[i] = self.words[i] ^ other.words[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    fn clear(self: &!BitSet) with Mut, Div, Panic {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < BITSET_WORDS {
            self.words[i] = 0
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    fn is_subset_of(self: &BitSet, other: &BitSet) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < BITSET_WORDS {
            if (self.words[i] & other.words[i]) != self.words[i] {
                return false
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        return true
    }

    fn equals(self: &BitSet, other: &BitSet) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < BITSET_WORDS {
            if self.words[i] != other.words[i] { return false }
            i = i + 1
        }
        return true
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

var CNT: [i64; 2] = [0; 2]

fn chk(label: i64, ok: i64) with IO, Mut {
    if ok == 1 {
        print("  PASS ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[0] = CNT[0] + 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[1] = CNT[1] + 1
    }
}

fn test_bitset() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var b = BitSet { words: [0; 1024] }

    // Initially empty
    chk(1, if b.test(0) { 0 } else { 1 })
    chk(2, if b.count() == 0 { 1 } else { 0 })

    // Set some bits
    b.set(0)
    b.set(1)
    b.set(63)
    b.set(64)
    b.set(65535)

    chk(3, if b.test(0) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(4, if b.test(1) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(5, if b.test(63) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(6, if b.test(64) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(7, if b.test(65535) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(8, if b.test(2) { 0 } else { 1 })
    chk(9, if b.count() == 5 { 1 } else { 0 })

    // Clear a bit
    b.clear_bit(1)
    chk(10, if b.test(1) { 0 } else { 1 })
    chk(11, if b.count() == 4 { 1 } else { 0 })

    // Union
    var c = BitSet { words: [0; 1024] }
    c.set(2)
    c.set(3)
    b.union_with(&c)
    chk(12, if b.test(2) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(13, if b.test(3) { 1 } else { 0 })

    // Intersection
    var d = BitSet { words: [0; 1024] }
    d.set(0)
    d.set(2)
    b.intersect_with(&d)
    chk(14, if b.test(0) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(15, if b.test(2) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(16, if b.test(63) { 0 } else { 1 })

    // XOR
    var e = BitSet { words: [0; 1024] }
    e.set(0)
    b.xor_with(&e)
    chk(17, if b.test(0) { 0 } else { 1 })
    chk(18, if b.test(2) { 1 } else { 0 })

    // Clear all
    b.clear()
    chk(19, if b.count() == 0 { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(20, if b.test(2) { 0 } else { 1 })

    // Subset
    var f = BitSet { words: [0; 1024] }
    f.set(5)
    f.set(10)
    var g = BitSet { words: [0; 1024] }
    g.set(5)
    chk(21, if g.is_subset_of(&f) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(22, if f.is_subset_of(&g) { 0 } else { 1 })

    // Equals
    var h = BitSet { words: [0; 1024] }
    h.set(5)
    chk(23, if g.equals(&h) { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(24, if g.equals(&f) { 0 } else { 1 })
}

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    CNT[0] = 0; CNT[1] = 0
    print("─── stdlib/collections/bitset tests ───\n")
    test_bitset()
    print("─── "); print(CNT[0]); print("/"); print(CNT[0]+CNT[1]); print(" PASS ───\n")
    if CNT[1] == 0 { print("ALL PASS\n"); 0 } else { 1 }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/collections/btree.sio ===
// stdlib/collections/btree — Flat-array B-tree (order 4)
//
// IntBTree: sorted i64 key → i64 value map.
// B-tree with branching factor 4, max 4096 nodes.
// Each node stores up to 3 keys and 3 values with 4 child pointers.
// All nodes stored in flat arrays (no pointers/allocation).

let BTREE_ORDER: i64 = 4
let BTREE_MAX_KEYS: i64 = 3
let BTREE_MAX_NODES: i64 = 4096
let BTREE_NIL: i64 = 0 - 1

struct IntBTree {
    // Per-node data: node i has keys[i*3..i*3+2], vals[i*3..i*3+2]
    node_keys: [i64; 12288],
    node_vals: [i64; 12288],
    node_children: [i64; 16384],
    node_key_count: [i64; 4096],
    node_is_leaf: [i64; 4096],
    node_count: i64,
    root: i64,
}

fn btree_node_key(tree: &IntBTree, node: i64, k: i64) -> i64 {
    tree.node_keys[node * BTREE_MAX_KEYS + k]
}

fn btree_node_val(tree: &IntBTree, node: i64, k: i64) -> i64 {
    tree.node_vals[node * BTREE_MAX_KEYS + k]
}

fn btree_node_child(tree: &IntBTree, node: i64, c: i64) -> i64 {
    tree.node_children[node * BTREE_ORDER + c]
}

fn btree_set_key(tree: &! IntBTree, node: i64, k: i64, val: i64) {
    tree.node_keys[node * BTREE_MAX_KEYS + k] = val
}

fn btree_set_val(tree: &! IntBTree, node: i64, k: i64, val: i64) {
    tree.node_vals[node * BTREE_MAX_KEYS + k] = val
}

fn btree_set_child(tree: &! IntBTree, node: i64, c: i64, child: i64) {
    tree.node_children[node * BTREE_ORDER + c] = child
}

fn btree_alloc_node(tree: &! IntBTree, is_leaf: i64) -> i64 {
    if tree.node_count >= BTREE_MAX_NODES { return BTREE_NIL }
    let id = tree.node_count
    tree.node_key_count[id] = 0
    tree.node_is_leaf[id] = is_leaf
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < BTREE_ORDER {
        btree_set_child(tree, id, c, BTREE_NIL)
        c = c + 1
    }
    tree.node_count = tree.node_count + 1
    id
}

impl IntBTree {
    fn new() -> IntBTree {
        var tree = IntBTree {
            node_keys: [0; 12288],
            node_vals: [0; 12288],
            node_children: [0; 16384],
            node_key_count: [0; 4096],
            node_is_leaf: [0; 4096],
            node_count: 0,
            root: BTREE_NIL,
        }
        tree
    }

    fn is_empty(self: &IntBTree) -> bool {
        self.root == BTREE_NIL
    }
}

fn btree_search_node(tree: &IntBTree, node: i64, key: i64) -> i64 {
    if node == BTREE_NIL { return 0 }
    let n = tree.node_key_count[node]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let k = btree_node_key(tree, node, i)
        if key == k { return btree_node_val(tree, node, i) }
        if key < k {
            return btree_search_node(tree, btree_node_child(tree, node, i), key)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return btree_search_node(tree, btree_node_child(tree, node, n), key)
}

fn btree_contains_node(tree: &IntBTree, node: i64, key: i64) -> bool {
    if node == BTREE_NIL { return false }
    let n = tree.node_key_count[node]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let k = btree_node_key(tree, node, i)
        if key == k { return true }
        if key < k {
            return btree_contains_node(tree, btree_node_child(tree, node, i), key)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return btree_contains_node(tree, btree_node_child(tree, node, n), key)
}

fn btree_search(tree: &IntBTree, key: i64) -> i64 {
    btree_search_node(tree, tree.root, key)
}

fn btree_contains(tree: &IntBTree, key: i64) -> bool {
    btree_contains_node(tree, tree.root, key)
}

// Simple insert into non-full leaf (for basic usage)
fn btree_insert_simple(tree: &! IntBTree, key: i64, val: i64) {
    if tree.root == BTREE_NIL {
        let r = btree_alloc_node(tree, 1)
        tree.root = r
        btree_set_key(tree, r, 0, key)
        btree_set_val(tree, r, 0, val)
        tree.node_key_count[r] = 1
        return
    }
    // Walk to leaf and insert (no splitting — works for < MAX_KEYS per node)
    var node = tree.root
    while tree.node_is_leaf[node] == 0 {
        let n = tree.node_key_count[node]
        var i: i64 = 0
        var found = false
        while i < n && !found {
            if key < btree_node_key(tree, node, i) {
                node = btree_node_child(tree, node, i)
                found = true
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        if !found {
            node = btree_node_child(tree, node, n)
        }
    }
    // Insert into leaf (sorted position)
    let n = tree.node_key_count[node]
    if n >= BTREE_MAX_KEYS { return }
    // Find position
    var pos: i64 = 0
    while pos < n && btree_node_key(tree, node, pos) < key {
        pos = pos + 1
    }
    // Check for duplicate
    if pos < n && btree_node_key(tree, node, pos) == key {
        btree_set_val(tree, node, pos, val)
        return
    }
    // Shift right
    var j = n
    while j > pos {
        btree_set_key(tree, node, j, btree_node_key(tree, node, j - 1))
        btree_set_val(tree, node, j, btree_node_val(tree, node, j - 1))
        j = j - 1
    }
    btree_set_key(tree, node, pos, key)
    btree_set_val(tree, node, pos, val)
    tree.node_key_count[node] = n + 1
}


// === FILE: stdlib/collections/deque.sio ===
// stdlib/collections/deque — Ring buffer double-ended queue
//
// IntDeque: i64 ring buffer, capacity 4096.
// push_front/push_back/pop_front/pop_back O(1).

let DEQUE_CAP: i64 = 4096

struct IntDeque {
    data: [i64; 4096],
    head: i64,
    tail: i64,
    count: i64,
}

impl IntDeque {
    fn new() -> IntDeque {
        IntDeque { data: [0; 4096], head: 0, tail: 0, count: 0 }
    }

    fn len(self: &IntDeque) -> i64 {
        self.count
    }

    fn is_empty(self: &IntDeque) -> bool {
        self.count == 0
    }

    fn is_full(self: &IntDeque) -> bool {
        self.count >= DEQUE_CAP
    }

    fn push_back(self: &! IntDeque, val: i64) {
        if self.count >= DEQUE_CAP { return }
        self.data[self.tail] = val
        self.tail = (self.tail + 1) % DEQUE_CAP
        self.count = self.count + 1
    }

    fn push_front(self: &! IntDeque, val: i64) {
        if self.count >= DEQUE_CAP { return }
        self.head = (self.head - 1 + DEQUE_CAP) % DEQUE_CAP
        self.data[self.head] = val
        self.count = self.count + 1
    }

    fn pop_front(self: &! IntDeque) -> i64 {
        if self.count == 0 { return 0 }
        let val = self.data[self.head]
        self.head = (self.head + 1) % DEQUE_CAP
        self.count = self.count - 1
        val
    }

    fn pop_back(self: &! IntDeque) -> i64 {
        if self.count == 0 { return 0 }
        self.tail = (self.tail - 1 + DEQUE_CAP) % DEQUE_CAP
        let val = self.data[self.tail]
        self.count = self.count - 1
        val
    }

    fn front(self: &IntDeque) -> i64 {
        if self.count == 0 { return 0 }
        self.data[self.head]
    }

    fn back(self: &IntDeque) -> i64 {
        if self.count == 0 { return 0 }
        let idx = (self.tail - 1 + DEQUE_CAP) % DEQUE_CAP
        self.data[idx]
    }

    fn get(self: &IntDeque, idx: i64) -> i64 {
        if idx < 0 || idx >= self.count { return 0 }
        let actual = (self.head + idx) % DEQUE_CAP
        self.data[actual]
    }

    fn clear(self: &! IntDeque) {
        self.head = 0
        self.tail = 0
        self.count = 0
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/collections/hashmap.sio ===
// stdlib/collections/hashmap — Open-addressing hash maps
//
// IntIntMap:   i64 → i64
// IntFloatMap: i64 → f64
//
// Hash: FNV-1a. Collision: linear probing. Capacity: 2048 slots.

let HASHMAP_CAP: i64 = 2048
let FNV_OFFSET: i64 = 0x00000100000001B3
let FNV_PRIME: i64 = 0x01000193

// ============================================================================
// Hash function
// ============================================================================

fn fnv1a_i64(key: i64) -> i64 {
    var hash: i64 = FNV_OFFSET
    var k = key
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let byte = k & 0xFF
        hash = (hash ^ byte) * FNV_PRIME
        k = k >> (8 as u8)
        i = i + 1
    }
    if hash < 0 { hash = 0 - hash }
    hash
}

// ============================================================================
// IntIntMap — i64 keys, i64 values
// ============================================================================

struct IntIntMap {
    keys: [i64; 2048],
    vals: [i64; 2048],
    used: [i64; 2048],
    iim_cnt: i64,
}

impl IntIntMap {
    fn new() -> IntIntMap {
        IntIntMap {
            keys: [0; 2048],
            vals: [0; 2048],
            used: [0; 2048],
            iim_cnt: 0,
        }
    }

    fn len(self: &IntIntMap) -> i64 {
        self.iim_cnt
    }

    fn is_empty(self: &IntIntMap) -> bool {
        self.iim_cnt == 0
    }

    fn insert(self: &! IntIntMap, key: i64, val: i64) {
        if self.iim_cnt >= HASHMAP_CAP - 1 { return }
        let h = fnv1a_i64(key)
        var idx = h % HASHMAP_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHMAP_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 {
                self.keys[idx] = key
                self.vals[idx] = val
                self.used[idx] = 1
                self.iim_cnt = self.iim_cnt + 1
                return
            }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                self.vals[idx] = val
                return
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHMAP_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
    }

    fn get(self: &IntIntMap, key: i64) -> i64 {
        let h = fnv1a_i64(key)
        var idx = h % HASHMAP_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHMAP_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 { return 0 }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                return self.vals[idx]
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHMAP_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return 0
    }

    fn contains(self: &IntIntMap, key: i64) -> bool {
        let h = fnv1a_i64(key)
        var idx = h % HASHMAP_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHMAP_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 { return false }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                return true
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHMAP_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn remove(self: &! IntIntMap, key: i64) -> bool {
        let h = fnv1a_i64(key)
        var idx = h % HASHMAP_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHMAP_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 { return false }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                self.used[idx] = 2
                self.iim_cnt = self.iim_cnt - 1
                return true
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHMAP_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn clear(self: &! IntIntMap) {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < HASHMAP_CAP {
            self.used[i] = 0
            i = i + 1
        }
        self.iim_cnt = 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// IntFloatMap — i64 keys, f64 values
// ============================================================================

struct IntFloatMap {
    keys: [i64; 2048],
    vals: [f64; 2048],

impl IntFloatMap {

        IntFloatMap {
            keys: [0; 2048],

        }
    }

    fn len(self: &IntFloatMap) -> i64 {

        self.ifm_cnt == 0
    }

    fn insert(self: &! IntFloatMap, key: i64, val: f64) {
        if self.ifm_cnt >= HASHMAP_CAP - 1 { return }
        let h = fnv1a_i64(key)
        var idx = h % HASHMAP_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHMAP_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 {
                self.keys[idx] = key
                self.vals[idx] = val
                self.used[idx] = 1
                self.ifm_cnt = self.ifm_cnt + 1
                return
            }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                self.vals[idx] = val
                return
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHMAP_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
    }

    fn get(self: &IntFloatMap, key: i64) -> f64 {
        let h = fnv1a_i64(key)
        var idx = h % HASHMAP_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHMAP_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 { return 0.0 }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                return self.vals[idx]
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHMAP_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return 0.0
    }

    fn contains(self: &IntFloatMap, key: i64) -> bool {
        let h = fnv1a_i64(key)
        var idx = h % HASHMAP_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHMAP_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 { return false }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                return true
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHMAP_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn remove(self: &! IntFloatMap, key: i64) -> bool {
        let h = fnv1a_i64(key)
        var idx = h % HASHMAP_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHMAP_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 { return false }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                self.used[idx] = 2
                self.ifm_cnt = self.ifm_cnt - 1
                return true
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHMAP_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn clear(self: &! IntFloatMap) {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < HASHMAP_CAP {
            self.used[i] = 0
            i = i + 1
        }
        self.ifm_cnt = 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// HashMap64 — i64 → f64, capacity 256, open-addressing with linear probing
// Standalone-function API (no impl block)
// ============================================================================

let HM64_CAP: i64 = 256

pub struct HashMap64 {
    keys:     [i64; 256],
    values:   [f64; 256],
    occupied: [i64; 256],   // 0=empty, 1=occupied, 2=tombstone
    count:    i64,
    capacity: i64,          // always 256
}

fn hash_i64(key: i64) -> i64 {
    let h = (key * 6364136223846793005) >> (33 as u8)
    let r = h & 255
    if r < 0 { 0 - r } else { r }
}

pub fn hashmap_new() -> HashMap64 {
    HashMap64 {
        keys:     [0; 256],
        values:   [0.0; 256],
        occupied: [0; 256],
        count:    0,
        capacity: 256,
    }
}

pub fn hashmap_insert(m: &! HashMap64, key: i64, value: f64) -> bool {
    if m.count >= HM64_CAP - 1 { return false }
    var idx = hash_i64(key)
    var probes: i64 = 0
    while probes < HM64_CAP {
        if m.occupied[idx] == 0 {
            m.keys[idx]     = key
            m.values[idx]   = value
            m.occupied[idx] = 1
            m.count = m.count + 1
            return true
        }
        if m.occupied[idx] == 1 && m.keys[idx] == key {
            m.values[idx] = value
            return true
        }
        idx = (idx + 1) & 255
        probes = probes + 1
    }
    false
}

pub fn hashmap_get(m: &HashMap64, key: i64) -> f64 {
    var idx = hash_i64(key)
    var probes: i64 = 0
    while probes < HM64_CAP {
        if m.occupied[idx] == 0 { return 0.0 }
        if m.occupied[idx] == 1 && m.keys[idx] == key {
            return m.values[idx]
        }
        idx = (idx + 1) & 255
        probes = probes + 1
    }
    0.0
}

pub fn hashmap_contains(m: &HashMap64, key: i64) -> bool {
    var idx = hash_i64(key)
    var probes: i64 = 0
    while probes < HM64_CAP {
        if m.occupied[idx] == 0 { return false }
        if m.occupied[idx] == 1 && m.keys[idx] == key { return true }
        idx = (idx + 1) & 255
        probes = probes + 1
    }
    false
}

pub fn hashmap_remove(m: &! HashMap64, key: i64) -> bool {
    var idx = hash_i64(key)
    var probes: i64 = 0
    while probes < HM64_CAP {
        if m.occupied[idx] == 0 { return false }
        if m.occupied[idx] == 1 && m.keys[idx] == key {
            m.occupied[idx] = 2
            m.count = m.count - 1
            return true
        }
        idx = (idx + 1) & 255
        probes = probes + 1
    }
    false
}

pub fn hashmap_count(m: &HashMap64) -> i64 {
    m.count
}


// === FILE: stdlib/collections/hashset.sio ===
// stdlib/collections/hashset — Integer hash set
//
// IntSet: set of i64 values, backed by open-addressing hash table.
// Capacity: 2048. Uses same FNV-1a hash as hashmap.

let HASHSET_CAP: i64 = 2048

fn hashset_fnv1a(key: i64) -> i64 {
    var hash: i64 = 0x00000100000001B3
    var k = key
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let byte = k & 0xFF
        hash = (hash ^ byte) * 0x01000193
        k = k >> 8
        i = i + 1
    }
    if hash < 0 { hash = 0 - hash }
    hash
}

struct IntSet {
    keys: [i64; 2048],
    used: [i64; 2048],
    count: i64,
}

impl IntSet {
    fn new() -> IntSet {
        IntSet {
            keys: [0; 2048],
            used: [0; 2048],
            count: 0,
        }
    }

    fn len(self: &IntSet) -> i64 {
        self.count
    }

    fn is_empty(self: &IntSet) -> bool {
        self.count == 0
    }

    fn insert(self: &! IntSet, key: i64) -> bool {
        if self.count >= HASHSET_CAP - 1 { return false }
        let h = hashset_fnv1a(key)
        var idx = h % HASHSET_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHSET_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 {
                self.keys[idx] = key
                self.used[idx] = 1
                self.count = self.count + 1
                return true
            }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                return false
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHSET_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn contains(self: &IntSet, key: i64) -> bool {
        let h = hashset_fnv1a(key)
        var idx = h % HASHSET_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHSET_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 { return false }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                return true
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHSET_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn remove(self: &! IntSet, key: i64) -> bool {
        let h = hashset_fnv1a(key)
        var idx = h % HASHSET_CAP
        if idx < 0 { idx = 0 - idx }
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < HASHSET_CAP {
            if self.used[idx] == 0 { return false }
            if self.used[idx] == 1 && self.keys[idx] == key {
                self.used[idx] = 2
                self.count = self.count - 1
                return true
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % HASHSET_CAP
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn clear(self: &! IntSet) {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < HASHSET_CAP {
            self.used[i] = 0
            i = i + 1
        }
        self.count = 0
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/collections/heap.sio ===
// stdlib/collections/heap — Binary min-heap
//
// IntHeap: min-heap of i64 values, capacity 4096.
// push O(log n), pop_min O(log n), peek_min O(1).

let HEAP_CAP: i64 = 4096

struct IntHeap {
    data: [i64; 4096],
    len: i64,
}

impl IntHeap {
    fn new() -> IntHeap {
        IntHeap { data: [0; 4096], len: 0 }
    }

    fn len(self: &IntHeap) -> i64 {
        self.len
    }

    fn is_empty(self: &IntHeap) -> bool {
        self.len == 0
    }

    fn peek_min(self: &IntHeap) -> i64 {
        if self.len > 0 { return self.data[0] }
        return 0
    }

    fn push(self: &! IntHeap, val: i64) {
        if self.len >= HEAP_CAP { return }
        self.data[self.len] = val
        self.len = self.len + 1
        // Swim up
        var i = self.len - 1
        while i > 0 {
            let parent = (i - 1) / 2
            if self.data[i] < self.data[parent] {
                let tmp = self.data[i]
                self.data[i] = self.data[parent]
                self.data[parent] = tmp
                i = parent
            } else {
                return
            }
        }
    }

    fn pop_min(self: &! IntHeap) -> i64 {
        if self.len == 0 { return 0 }
        let result = self.data[0]
        self.len = self.len - 1
        if self.len == 0 { return result }
        self.data[0] = self.data[self.len]
        // Sink down
        var i: i64 = 0
        var done = false
        while !done {
            let left = 2 * i + 1
            let right = 2 * i + 2
            var smallest = i
            if left < self.len && self.data[left] < self.data[smallest] {
                smallest = left
            }
            if right < self.len && self.data[right] < self.data[smallest] {
                smallest = right
            }
            if smallest == i {
                done = true
            } else {
                let tmp = self.data[i]
                self.data[i] = self.data[smallest]
                self.data[smallest] = tmp
                i = smallest
            }
        }
        result
    }

    fn clear(self: &! IntHeap) {
        self.len = 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FloatHeap — min-heap of f64 values
// ============================================================================

struct FloatHeap {
    data: [f64; 4096],
    len: i64,
}

impl FloatHeap {
    fn new() -> FloatHeap {
        FloatHeap { data: [0.0; 4096], len: 0 }
    }

    fn len(self: &FloatHeap) -> i64 {
        self.len
    }

    fn is_empty(self: &FloatHeap) -> bool {
        self.len == 0
    }

    fn peek_min(self: &FloatHeap) -> f64 {
        if self.len > 0 { return self.data[0] }
        return 0.0
    }

    fn push(self: &! FloatHeap, val: f64) {
        if self.len >= HEAP_CAP { return }
        self.data[self.len] = val
        self.len = self.len + 1
        var i = self.len - 1
        while i > 0 {
            let parent = (i - 1) / 2
            if self.data[i] < self.data[parent] {
                let tmp = self.data[i]
                self.data[i] = self.data[parent]
                self.data[parent] = tmp
                i = parent
            } else {
                return
            }
        }
    }

    fn pop_min(self: &! FloatHeap) -> f64 {
        if self.len == 0 { return 0.0 }
        let result = self.data[0]
        self.len = self.len - 1
        if self.len == 0 { return result }
        self.data[0] = self.data[self.len]
        var i: i64 = 0
        var done = false
        while !done {
            let left = 2 * i + 1
            let right = 2 * i + 2
            var smallest = i
            if left < self.len && self.data[left] < self.data[smallest] {
                smallest = left
            }
            if right < self.len && self.data[right] < self.data[smallest] {
                smallest = right
            }
            if smallest == i {
                done = true
            } else {
                let tmp = self.data[i]
                self.data[i] = self.data[smallest]
                self.data[smallest] = tmp
                i = smallest
            }
        }
        result
    }

    fn clear(self: &! FloatHeap) {
        self.len = 0
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/collections/heap_map.sio ===
// Heap-allocated dynamic open-addressing hash maps.
// Backed by heap_alloc / heap_free (mmap underneath).
// Usable in native mode only (not JIT).
//
// HeapIntIntMap: i64 → i64, FNV-1a, linear probing, load factor 0.75.
// Initial capacity: 64 slots, doubles on growth.
//
// Method API:
//   var m = HeapIntIntMap { keys: 0 as *mut i64, vals: 0 as *mut i64,
//                           used: 0 as *mut i64, count: 0, cap: 0 }
//   m.insert(42, 100)
//   let v = m.get(42)        // returns value or 0 if missing
//   let ok = m.contains(42)
//   m.remove(42)
//   print_int(m.len())
//   m.free()
//
// used[] values: 0=empty, 1=occupied, 2=deleted (tombstone)

let HEAP_MAP_INIT_CAP: i64 = 64
let HEAP_MAP_LOAD_NUM: i64 = 3  // load factor 3/4 = 0.75
let HEAP_MAP_LOAD_DEN: i64 = 4

// FNV-1a hash for i64 key (same as hashmap.sio)
fn heap_map_fnv1a(key: i64) -> i64 {
    var hash: i64 = 0x00000100000001B3
    var k = key
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let byte = k & 0xFF
        hash = (hash ^ byte) * 0x01000193
        k = k >> 8
        i = i + 1
    }
    if hash < 0 { hash = 0 - hash }
    return hash
}

// ============================================================
// HeapIntIntMap — dynamic i64 → i64 map
// ============================================================

pub struct HeapIntIntMap {
    keys: *mut i64,
    vals: *mut i64,
    used: *mut i64,
    count: i64,
    cap: i64,
}

impl HeapIntIntMap {

    fn _alloc_arrays(self: &!HeapIntIntMap, new_cap: i64) with Alloc, Mut {
        let bytes = new_cap * 8
        self.keys = heap_alloc(bytes) as *mut i64
        self.vals = heap_alloc(bytes) as *mut i64
        self.used = heap_alloc(bytes) as *mut i64
        // zero the used array (heap_alloc via mmap returns zeroed pages)
        self.cap = new_cap
    }

    fn _rehash(self: &!HeapIntIntMap) with Alloc, Mut {
        let old_cap = self.cap
        let old_keys = self.keys
        let old_vals = self.vals
        let old_used = self.used
        let new_cap = old_cap * 2

        // allocate new arrays
        let new_bytes = new_cap * 8
        let nk = heap_alloc(new_bytes) as *mut i64
        let nv = heap_alloc(new_bytes) as *mut i64
        let nu = heap_alloc(new_bytes) as *mut i64

        // re-insert all occupied entries into new arrays
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < old_cap {
            if read_i64(old_used, i) == 1 {
                let key = read_i64(old_keys, i)
                let val = read_i64(old_vals, i)
                let h = heap_map_fnv1a(key)
                var idx = h % new_cap
                var probes: i64 = 0
                while probes < new_cap {
                    if read_i64(nu, idx) == 0 {
                        write_i64(nk, idx, key)
                        write_i64(nv, idx, val)
                        write_i64(nu, idx, 1)
                        probes = new_cap  // break
                    }
                    idx = (idx + 1) % new_cap
                    probes = probes + 1
                }
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // free old arrays
        heap_free(old_keys as *mut i8)
        heap_free(old_vals as *mut i8)
        heap_free(old_used as *mut i8)

        self.keys = nk
        self.vals = nv
        self.used = nu
        self.cap = new_cap
    }

    fn insert(self: &!HeapIntIntMap, key: i64, val: i64) with Alloc, Mut {
        // initialize on first insert
        if self.cap == 0 {
            self._alloc_arrays(HEAP_MAP_INIT_CAP)
        }
        // grow if load factor exceeded
        if self.count * HEAP_MAP_LOAD_DEN >= self.cap * HEAP_MAP_LOAD_NUM {
            self._rehash()
        }
        let h = heap_map_fnv1a(key)
        var idx = h % self.cap
        var first_tomb: i64 = -1
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < self.cap {
            let u = read_i64(self.used, idx)
            if u == 0 {
                // empty slot — insert here (or at tombstone if we saw one)
                if first_tomb >= 0 { idx = first_tomb }
                write_i64(self.keys, idx, key)
                write_i64(self.vals, idx, val)
                write_i64(self.used, idx, 1)
                self.count = self.count + 1
                return
            }
            if u == 2 {
                // tombstone — remember first one
                if first_tomb < 0 { first_tomb = idx }
            }
            if u == 1 && read_i64(self.keys, idx) == key {
                // update existing
                write_i64(self.vals, idx, val)
                return
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % self.cap
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        // map full (shouldn't happen with load factor check)
        if first_tomb >= 0 {
            write_i64(self.keys, first_tomb, key)
            write_i64(self.vals, first_tomb, val)
            write_i64(self.used, first_tomb, 1)
            self.count = self.count + 1
        }
    }

    fn get(self: &HeapIntIntMap, key: i64) -> i64 {
        if self.cap == 0 { return 0 }
        let h = heap_map_fnv1a(key)
        var idx = h % self.cap
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < self.cap {
            let u = read_i64(self.used, idx)
            if u == 0 { return 0 }
            if u == 1 && read_i64(self.keys, idx) == key {
                return read_i64(self.vals, idx)
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % self.cap
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return 0
    }

    fn contains(self: &HeapIntIntMap, key: i64) -> bool {
        if self.cap == 0 { return false }
        let h = heap_map_fnv1a(key)
        var idx = h % self.cap
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < self.cap {
            let u = read_i64(self.used, idx)
            if u == 0 { return false }
            if u == 1 && read_i64(self.keys, idx) == key { return true }
            idx = (idx + 1) % self.cap
            probes = probes + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn remove(self: &!HeapIntIntMap, key: i64) with Mut {
        if self.cap == 0 { return }
        let h = heap_map_fnv1a(key)
        var idx = h % self.cap
        var probes: i64 = 0
        while probes < self.cap {
            let u = read_i64(self.used, idx)
            if u == 0 { return }
            if u == 1 && read_i64(self.keys, idx) == key {
                write_i64(self.used, idx, 2)  // tombstone
                self.count = self.count - 1
                return
            }
            idx = (idx + 1) % self.cap
            probes = probes + 1
        }
    }

    fn len(self: &HeapIntIntMap) -> i64 {
        self.count
    }

    fn cap(self: &HeapIntIntMap) -> i64 {
        self.cap
    }

    fn free(self: &!HeapIntIntMap) with Alloc, Mut {
        if self.cap > 0 {
            heap_free(self.keys as *mut i8)
            heap_free(self.vals as *mut i8)
            heap_free(self.used as *mut i8)
        }
        self.keys = 0 as *mut i64
        self.vals = 0 as *mut i64
        self.used = 0 as *mut i64
        self.count = 0
        self.cap = 0
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/collections/heap_vec.sio ===
// Heap-allocated growable vectors.
// Backed by heap_alloc / heap_realloc / heap_free (mmap/mremap underneath).
// Usable in native mode only (not JIT).
//
// Method API:
//   var v = HeapI64Vec { ptr: 0 as *mut i64, len: 0, cap: 0 }
//   v.push(42)
//   let x = v.get(0)
//   print_int(v.len())
//   v.free()
//
// IMPORTANT: Always use heap_alloc for the FIRST allocation.
// heap_realloc uses mremap which reads a header 8 bytes before the pointer —
// it must never be called with a null/initial pointer.

// ============================================
// HeapVec<T> - generic heap vector
// ============================================
struct HeapVec<T> {
    ptr: *mut i64,
    len: i64,
    cap: i64,
}

impl HeapVec<T> {
    fn new() -> HeapVec<T> {
        HeapVec { ptr: 0 as *mut i64, len: 0, cap: 0 }
    }
    fn with_capacity(cap: i64) -> HeapVec<T> with Alloc {
        let bytes = cap * 8
        let ptr = heap_alloc(bytes) as *mut i64
        HeapVec { ptr: ptr, len: 0, cap: cap }
    }
    fn push(self: &!HeapVec<T>, val: T) with Alloc, Mut {
        if self.len >= self.cap {
            let new_cap = if self.cap == 0 { 4 } else { self.cap * 2 }
            let new_bytes = new_cap * 8
            if self.cap == 0 {
                self.ptr = heap_alloc(new_bytes) as *mut i64
            } else {
                self.ptr = heap_realloc(self.ptr as *mut i8, new_bytes) as *mut i64
            }
            self.cap = new_cap
        }
        write_i64(self.ptr, self.len, val)
        self.len = self.len + 1
    }
    fn pop(self: &!HeapVec<T>) -> T with Mut {
        if self.len > 0 {
            self.len = self.len - 1
            return read_i64(self.ptr, self.len)
        }
        return 0
    }
    fn get(self: &HeapVec<T>, idx: i64) -> T {
        if idx >= 0 && idx < self.len {
            return read_i64(self.ptr, idx)
        }
        return 0
    }
    fn set(self: &!HeapVec<T>, idx: i64, val: T) with Mut {
        if idx >= 0 && idx < self.len {
            write_i64(self.ptr, idx, val)
        }
    }
    fn len(self: &HeapVec<T>) -> i64 {
        self.len
    }
    fn cap(self: &HeapVec<T>) -> i64 {
        self.cap
    }
    fn is_empty(self: &HeapVec<T>) -> bool {
        self.len == 0
    }
    fn clear(self: &!HeapVec<T>) with Mut {
        self.len = 0
    }
    fn contains(self: &HeapVec<T>, val: T) -> bool {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < self.len {
            if read_i64(self.ptr, i) == val { return true }
            i = i + 1
        }
        return false
    }
    fn sum(self: &HeapVec<T>) -> i64 {
        var s: i64 = 0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < self.len {
            s = s + read_i64(self.ptr, i)
            i = i + 1
        }
        return s
    }
    fn free(self: &!HeapVec<T>) with Alloc, Mut {
        if self.cap > 0 {
            heap_free(self.ptr as *mut i8)
        }
        self.ptr = 0 as *mut i64
        self.len = 0
        self.cap = 0
    }
}

        v.cap = new_cap
    }
    write_f64(v.ptr, v.len, val)
    v.len = v.len + 1
}

fn heap_f64_vec_pop(v: &! HeapF64Vec) -> f64 with Mut {
    if v.len > 0 {
        v.len = v.len - 1
        return read_f64(v.ptr, v.len)
    }
    return 0.0
}

fn heap_f64_vec_get(v: &HeapF64Vec, idx: i64) -> f64 {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < v.len {
        return read_f64(v.ptr, idx)
    }
    return 0.0
}

fn heap_f64_vec_set(v: &! HeapF64Vec, idx: i64, val: f64) with Mut {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < v.len {
        write_f64(v.ptr, idx, val)
    }
}

fn heap_f64_vec_len(v: &HeapF64Vec) -> i64 {
    v.len
}

fn heap_f64_vec_cap(v: &HeapF64Vec) -> i64 {
    v.cap
}

fn heap_f64_vec_free(v: &! HeapF64Vec) with Alloc {
    if v.cap > 0 {
        heap_free(v.ptr as *mut i8)
    }
    v.ptr = 0 as *mut f64
    v.len = 0
    v.cap = 0
}
