// ============================================================================
// BIT OPERATION HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Right-rotate 32-bit value stored in i64 by n positions.
fn rotr32(x: i64, n: i32) -> i64 {
    let xm = x & 0xFFFFFFFF
    let right = (xm >> n) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    let left  = (xm << (32 - n)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return (left | right) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

// Logical right shift (no sign extension) of 32-bit value.
fn shr32(x: i64, n: i32) -> i64 {
    return (x & 0xFFFFFFFF) >> n
}

// ============================================================================
// FIPS 180-4 §4.1.2 — Boolean functions
// ============================================================================

fn ch(x: i64, y: i64, z: i64) -> i64 {
    return ((x & y) ^ ((x ^ 0xFFFFFFFF) & 0xFFFFFFFF & z)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

fn maj(x: i64, y: i64, z: i64) -> i64 {
    return ((x & y) ^ (x & z) ^ (y & z)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

// FIPS 180-4 §4.1.2 — Big-sigma functions (compression)
fn sigma0(x: i64) -> i64 {
    return (rotr32(x, 2) ^ rotr32(x, 13) ^ rotr32(x, 22)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

fn sigma1(x: i64) -> i64 {
    return (rotr32(x, 6) ^ rotr32(x, 11) ^ rotr32(x, 25)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

// FIPS 180-4 §4.1.2 — Small-sigma functions (message schedule)
fn gamma0(x: i64) -> i64 {
    return (rotr32(x, 7) ^ rotr32(x, 18) ^ shr32(x, 3)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

fn gamma1(x: i64) -> i64 {
    return (rotr32(x, 17) ^ rotr32(x, 19) ^ shr32(x, 10)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

// ============================================================================
// BLOCK COMPRESSION — FIPS 180-4 §6.2.2
// ============================================================================

// Process one 512-bit block. Returns updated H0..H7.
pub fn sha256_compress(h: [i64; 8], block: [u8; 64]) -> [i64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Save initial hash words in scalars before any array operations can alias them
    var h0 = h[0]; var h1 = h[1]; var h2 = h[2]; var h3 = h[3]
    var h4 = h[4]; var h5 = h[5]; var h6 = h[6]; var h7 = h[7]

    // FIPS 180-4 §4.2.2 K constants — inlined, no helper call
    var k: [i64; 64] = [
        0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5,
        0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5,
        0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3,
        0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174,
        0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc,
        0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da,
        0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7,
        0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967,
        0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13,
        0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85,
        0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3,
        0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,
        0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5,
        0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3,
        0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208,
        0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2
    ]

    // Message schedule W[0..63]
    var w: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]

    // W[0..15]: big-endian 32-bit words from block bytes
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        let b0 = block[i * 4 + 0] as i64
        let b1 = block[i * 4 + 1] as i64
        let b2 = block[i * 4 + 2] as i64
        let b3 = block[i * 4 + 3] as i64
        w[i] = ((b0 << 24) | (b1 << 16) | (b2 << 8) | b3) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        i = i + 1
    }

    // W[16..63] with inlined gamma0/gamma1/rotr32/shr32 — no function calls
    var t = 16
    while t < 64 {
        // gamma1(w[t-2]) = rotr32(x,17) ^ rotr32(x,19) ^ shr32(x,10)
        let xg1 = w[t - 2] & 0xFFFFFFFF
        let g1 = (((xg1 >> 17) | ((xg1 << 15) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) ^ ((xg1 >> 19) | ((xg1 << 13) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) ^ (xg1 >> 10)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        // gamma0(w[t-15]) = rotr32(x,7) ^ rotr32(x,18) ^ shr32(x,3)
        let xg0 = w[t - 15] & 0xFFFFFFFF
        let g0 = (((xg0 >> 7) | ((xg0 << 25) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) ^ ((xg0 >> 18) | ((xg0 << 14) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) ^ (xg0 >> 3)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        w[t] = (g1 + w[t - 7] + g0 + w[t - 16]) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        t = t + 1
    }

    // Working variables a..hh
    var a = h0; var b = h1; var c = h2; var d = h3
    var e = h4; var f = h5; var g = h6; var hh = h7

    // 64 rounds — all bit ops inlined, no function calls
    var r = 0
    while r < 64 {
        // sigma1(e) = rotr32(e,6) ^ rotr32(e,11) ^ rotr32(e,25)
        let xe = e & 0xFFFFFFFF
        let s1 = (((xe >> 6) | ((xe << 26) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) ^ ((xe >> 11) | ((xe << 21) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) ^ ((xe >> 25) | ((xe << 7) & 0xFFFFFFFF))) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        // ch(e, f, g)
        let ch_efg = ((e & f) ^ ((e ^ 0xFFFFFFFF) & 0xFFFFFFFF & g)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        // sigma0(a) = rotr32(a,2) ^ rotr32(a,13) ^ rotr32(a,22)
        let xa = a & 0xFFFFFFFF
        let s0 = (((xa >> 2) | ((xa << 30) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) ^ ((xa >> 13) | ((xa << 19) & 0xFFFFFFFF)) ^ ((xa >> 22) | ((xa << 10) & 0xFFFFFFFF))) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        // maj(a, b, c)
        let maj_abc = ((a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        let t1 = (hh + s1 + ch_efg + k[r] + w[r]) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        let t2 = (s0 + maj_abc) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        hh = g
        g = f
        f = e
        e = (d + t1) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        d = c
        c = b
        b = a
        a = (t1 + t2) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        r = r + 1
    }

    // Intermediate hash (add working vars back to saved h0..h7 scalars)
    var out: [i64; 8] = [0; 8]
    out[0] = (h0 + a) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[1] = (h1 + b) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[2] = (h2 + c) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[3] = (h3 + d) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[4] = (h4 + e) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[5] = (h5 + f) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[6] = (h6 + g) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[7] = (h7 + hh) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return out
}

// ============================================================================
// PUBLIC API
// ============================================================================

// FIPS 180-4 §5.3.3 — Initial hash values (first 32 bits of sqrt of primes 2..19)
pub fn sha256_init() -> SHA256State {
    let h: [i64; 8] = [
        0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a,
        0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19
    ]
    let buf: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    SHA256State {
        h: h,
        buffer: buf,
        buf_len: 0,
        total_len: 0,
    }
}

// Absorb up to `len` bytes from `data` into the SHA-256 state.
// data: fixed 256-byte window; len: actual byte count to consume.
pub fn sha256_update(state: SHA256State, data: [u8; 256], len: i32) -> SHA256State with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = state
    var pos: i32 = 0

    while pos < len {
        // Fill the 64-byte buffer one byte at a time.
        s.buffer[s.buf_len] = data[pos]
        s.buf_len = s.buf_len + 1
        s.total_len = s.total_len + 1
        pos = pos + 1

        // Compress when buffer is full.
        if s.buf_len == 64 {
            s.h = sha256_compress(s.h, s.buffer)
            s.buf_len = 0
            // Zero buffer for cleanliness
            var bi: i32 = 0
            while bi < 64 {
                s.buffer[bi] = 0
                bi = bi + 1
            }
        }
    }

    return s
}

// Produce the final SHA-256 digest (FIPS 180-4 §5.1.1 padding + §6.2.2).
pub fn sha256_finalize(state: SHA256State) -> SHA256Digest with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = state

    // Total message length in bits for the length field.
    let bit_len: i64 = s.total_len * 8

    // Append the 0x80 byte.
    s.buffer[s.buf_len] = 0x80 as u8
    s.buf_len = s.buf_len + 1

    // If not enough room for the 8-byte length field, compress and start new block.
    if s.buf_len > 56 {
        // Pad with zeros to end of block.
        while s.buf_len < 64 {
            s.buffer[s.buf_len] = 0
            s.buf_len = s.buf_len + 1
        }
        s.h = sha256_compress(s.h, s.buffer)
        s.buf_len = 0
        var bi: i32 = 0
        while bi < 64 {
            s.buffer[bi] = 0
            bi = bi + 1
        }
    }

    // Pad to byte 56.
    while s.buf_len < 56 {
        s.buffer[s.buf_len] = 0
        s.buf_len = s.buf_len + 1
    }

    // Append 64-bit big-endian message bit length (bytes 56..63).
    s.buffer[56] = ((bit_len >> 56) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[57] = ((bit_len >> 48) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[58] = ((bit_len >> 40) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[59] = ((bit_len >> 32) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[60] = ((bit_len >> 24) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[61] = ((bit_len >> 16) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[62] = ((bit_len >>  8) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[63] = ((bit_len      ) & 0xFF) as u8

    // Final compression.
    s.h = sha256_compress(s.h, s.buffer)

    // Serialise H0..H7 as big-endian bytes.
    var digest_bytes: [u8; 32] = [0; 32]
    var wi: i32 = 0
    while wi < 8 {
        let word = s.h[wi]
        digest_bytes[wi * 4 + 0] = ((word >> 24) & 0xFF) as u8
        digest_bytes[wi * 4 + 1] = ((word >> 16) & 0xFF) as u8
        digest_bytes[wi * 4 + 2] = ((word >>  8) & 0xFF) as u8
        digest_bytes[wi * 4 + 3] = ((word      ) & 0xFF) as u8
        wi = wi + 1
    }

    return SHA256Digest { bytes: digest_bytes }
}

// One-shot hash: init → update → finalize.
pub fn sha256_hash(data: [u8; 256], len: i32) -> SHA256Digest with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let s0 = sha256_init()
    let s1 = sha256_update(s0, data, len)
    return sha256_finalize(s1)
}

// ============================================================================
// HMAC-SHA256 — RFC 2104
// ============================================================================

// HMAC-SHA256(key, msg).
// key_len / msg_len: actual lengths (≤ 256 bytes each as stored in fixed arrays).
pub fn hmac_sha256(key: [u8; 256], key_len: i32, msg: [u8; 256], msg_len: i32) -> SHA256Digest with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Step 1: If key > 64 bytes, hash it to get a 32-byte derived key.
    var k: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]

    if key_len > 64 {
        // Hash key using sha256_hash (first key_len bytes of key).
        var key_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
        var ki: i32 = 0
        while ki < key_len {
            key_buf[ki] = key[ki]
            ki = ki + 1
        }
        let key_digest = sha256_hash(key_buf, key_len)
        // Use first 32 bytes of hash as key.
        var di: i32 = 0
        while di < 32 {
            k[di] = key_digest.bytes[di]
            di = di + 1
        }
    } else {
        // Pad key with zeros to 64 bytes.
        var ki: i32 = 0
        while ki < key_len {
            k[ki] = key[ki]
            ki = ki + 1
        }
    }

    // Step 2: Compute ipad = k XOR 0x36 and opad = k XOR 0x5c (both 64 bytes).
    var ipad: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    var opad: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    var pi: i32 = 0
    while pi < 64 {
        ipad[pi] = ((k[pi] as i64) ^ 0x36) as u8
        opad[pi] = ((k[pi] as i64) ^ 0x5c) as u8
        pi = pi + 1
    }

    // Step 3: inner = SHA256(ipad || msg)
    // We need to stream ipad (64 bytes) then msg into one SHA256 state.
    var inner = sha256_init()

    // Feed ipad as first 64 bytes.
    var ipad_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var ip: i32 = 0
    while ip < 64 {
        ipad_buf[ip] = ipad[ip]
        ip = ip + 1
    }
    inner = sha256_update(inner, ipad_buf, 64)

    // Feed message.
    var msg_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var mi: i32 = 0
    while mi < msg_len {
        msg_buf[mi] = msg[mi]
        mi = mi + 1
    }
    inner = sha256_update(inner, msg_buf, msg_len)
    let inner_digest = sha256_finalize(inner)

    // Step 4: outer = SHA256(opad || inner_digest)
    var outer = sha256_init()

    var opad_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var op: i32 = 0
    while op < 64 {
        opad_buf[op] = opad[op]
        op = op + 1
    }
    outer = sha256_update(outer, opad_buf, 64)

    // Feed 32-byte inner hash result.
    var inner_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var ii: i32 = 0
    while ii < 32 {
        inner_buf[ii] = inner_digest.bytes[ii]
        ii = ii + 1
    }
    outer = sha256_update(outer, inner_buf, 32)
    return sha256_finalize(outer)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/csv/parser.sio ===
// stdlib/csv/parser.sio — CSV parser and writer for Sounio
//
// Numeric-only CSV (f64 values) backed by fixed-size arrays.
// No heap, no dynamic allocation — all capacities are compile-time constants.
//
// Capacity:
//   - max 256 rows × 16 columns  → data[4096]
//   - input / output buffer: 4096 bytes
//   - column header: up to 16 names of 32 bytes each
//
// Usage:
//   var t = csv_table_new()
//   let rc = csv_parse(&input, input_len, &!t, (44 as u8))   // 44 = ','
//   assert(rc == 0)
//   let m = csv_col_mean(&t, 0)

// =============================================================================
// Constants
// =============================================================================

let CSV_MAX_ROWS: i32 = 256
let CSV_MAX_COLS: i32 = 16
let CSV_DATA_CAP: i32 = 4096   // 256 * 16
let CSV_BUF_CAP:  i32 = 4096
let CSV_HDR_LEN:  i32 = 32     // bytes per column name

// =============================================================================
// CsvBuf — byte buffer for serialized CSV output
//
// Wraps [u8; 4096] in a struct so that &!CsvBuf mutations propagate
// correctly through the JIT (raw &![u8; 4096] has a known JIT limitation).
// =============================================================================

pub struct CsvBuf {
    pub bytes: [u8; 4096],
    pub len:   i32,
}

/// Return an empty CsvBuf.
pub fn csv_buf_new() -> CsvBuf {
    CsvBuf { bytes: [0; 4096], len: 0 }
}

// =============================================================================
// CsvTable — primary data structure
// =============================================================================

pub struct CsvTable {
    pub data:        [f64; 4096],       // row-major: data[row * n_cols + col]
    pub n_rows:      i32,
    pub n_cols:      i32,
    pub max_rows:    i32,               // fixed: CSV_MAX_ROWS
    pub max_cols:    i32,               // fixed: CSV_MAX_COLS
    pub has_header:  i32,               // 0 = no, 1 = yes
    pub header_bytes: [u8; 512],       // column names, flattened: col * 32 + byte
    pub header_lens: [i32; 16],         // byte length of each name
}

// =============================================================================
// Construction helpers
// =============================================================================

/// Return an empty CsvTable.
pub fn csv_table_new() -> CsvTable {
    CsvTable {
        data:         [0.0; 4096],
        n_rows:       0,
        n_cols:       0,
        max_rows:     256,
        max_cols:     16,
        has_header:   0,
        header_bytes: [0; 512],
        header_lens:  [0; 16],
    }
}

/// Set the value at (row, col). Out-of-bounds writes are silently ignored.
pub fn csv_table_set(t: &!CsvTable, row: i32, col: i32, val: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    if row < 0 || row >= t.n_rows { return }
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return }
    let idx = row * t.n_cols + col
    t.data[idx as usize] = val
}

/// Read the value at (row, col). Out-of-bounds reads return 0.0.
pub fn csv_table_get(t: &CsvTable, row: i32, col: i32) -> f64 {
    if row < 0 || row >= t.n_rows { return 0.0 }
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    let idx = row * t.n_cols + col
    t.data[idx as usize]
}

/// Append a row from values[0..n_cols-1].  n_cols must match t.n_cols (or set
/// it on the first call when the table is still empty).
pub fn csv_table_add_row(t: &!CsvTable, values: &[f64; 16], n_cols: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if t.n_rows >= 256 { return }
    if n_cols <= 0 || n_cols > 16 { return }

    // First row: establish column count
    if t.n_rows == 0 && t.n_cols == 0 {
        t.n_cols = n_cols
    }

    // Column count mismatch — silently skip
    if n_cols != t.n_cols { return }

    let base = t.n_rows * t.n_cols
    var c: i32 = 0
    while c < n_cols {
        t.data[(base + c) as usize] = values[c as usize]
        c = c + 1
    }
    t.n_rows = t.n_rows + 1
}

// =============================================================================
// Parsing helpers
// =============================================================================

// True when c is ASCII alphabetic (header-detection heuristic).
fn is_alpha(c: u8) -> bool {
    (c >= (65 as u8) && c <= (90 as u8)) || (c >= (97 as u8) && c <= (122 as u8))
}

// True when c is a decimal digit.
fn is_digit(c: u8) -> bool {
    c >= (48 as u8) && c <= (57 as u8)
}

// Raise 10.0 to integer power n  (n >= 0).
fn pow10(n: i32) -> f64 {
    var r: f64 = 1.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        r = r * 10.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

/// Field-buffer capacity for a single numeric CSV cell (see NOTE below).
const CSV_FIELD_CAP: i32 = 64

/// Parse an f64 from a *field-local* buffer buf[0..n) (index 0 based).
/// Handles optional leading '-', integer part, optional '.' + fraction.
//
// NOTE (compiler workaround, do not "simplify" away): the caller MUST copy the
// field's bytes into a fresh local buffer and call this with the copy — never pass
// csv_parse's `input` ref straight through with a nonzero start. The current
// lean_single backend miscompiles the integer-digit loop of a function that indexes
// a *re-passed* `&[u8; N]` ref at a nonzero start offset: it accumulates nothing, so
// every CSV field after column 0 parsed as 0.0. Parsing from a local buffer at
// start 0 (and doing the offset copy in csv_parse, which owns the ref directly)
// dodges the defect. Minimal repro filed for the compiler owner.
fn parse_num(buf: &[u8; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 0 { return 0.0 }

    var i: i32 = 0
    var neg: i32 = 0

    // Sign
    if buf[0] == (45 as u8) {   // '-'
        neg = 1
        i = 1
    }

    // Integer part
    var int_part: f64 = 0.0
    while i < n && is_digit(buf[i as usize]) {
        int_part = int_part * 10.0 + ((buf[i as usize] as i32) - 48) as f64
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Fractional part
    var frac: f64 = 0.0
    if i < n && buf[i as usize] == (46 as u8) {   // '.'
        i = i + 1
        var denom: f64 = 10.0
        while i < n && is_digit(buf[i as usize]) {
            frac = frac + ((buf[i as usize] as i32) - 48) as f64 / denom
            denom = denom * 10.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    let result = int_part + frac
    if neg == 1 { return 0.0 - result }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// CSV parser
// =============================================================================

/// Parse a CSV held in a `string` (e.g. the result of the `read_file` builtin) into `table`.
/// Copies up to 4096 bytes of the string into a byte buffer and delegates to `csv_parse`, so a
/// file on disk can be loaded in two calls:  `let s = read_file(path); csv_parse_string(s, &!t, ',')`.
pub fn csv_parse_string(input: string, table: &!CsvTable, delimiter: u8) -> i32
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    var buf: [u8; 4096] = [0; 4096]
    let n = str_len(input)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n && i < 4096 {
        buf[i as usize] = str_char_at(input, i) as u8
        i = i + 1
    }
    let used: i32 = if n < 4096 { n as i32 } else { 4096 }
    csv_parse(&buf, used, table, delimiter)
}

/// Parse CSV bytes into table.
///
/// - Delimiter is typically (44 as u8) (','). CR (\r) before \n is skipped.
/// - If the first non-whitespace character is alphabetic the entire first line
///   is treated as a header row (column names stored in table.header_bytes).
/// - Only numeric rows are stored in table.data.
///
/// Returns 0 on success, -1 on overflow / error.
pub fn csv_parse(input: &[u8; 4096], input_len: i32, table: &!CsvTable, delimiter: u8) -> i32
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    if input_len <= 0 || input_len > 4096 { return 0 - 1 }

    // Detect header: peek at first byte
    var scan_hdr: i32 = 0
    while scan_hdr < input_len && (input[scan_hdr as usize] == (32 as u8) || input[scan_hdr as usize] == (9 as u8)) {
        scan_hdr = scan_hdr + 1
    }
    let first_is_alpha: i32 = if scan_hdr < input_len && is_alpha(input[scan_hdr as usize]) { 1 } else { 0 }

    var pos: i32 = 0

    // --- Header row ---
    if first_is_alpha == 1 {
        table.has_header = 1
        var col: i32 = 0
        var field_start: i32 = pos
        while pos < input_len {
            let c = input[pos as usize]
            if c == (10 as u8) || c == (13 as u8) {
                // end of header line — store last field
                if col < 16 {
                    var fs: i32 = field_start
                    var fe: i32 = pos
                    // trim trailing CR
                    if fe > fs && input[(fe - 1) as usize] == (13 as u8) { fe = fe - 1 }
                    let flen = fe - fs
                    let copy_len = if flen < 32 { flen } else { 31 }
                    let hbase = col * 32
                    var hc: i32 = 0
                    while hc < copy_len {
                        table.header_bytes[(hbase + hc) as usize] = input[(fs + hc) as usize]
                        hc = hc + 1
                    }
                    table.header_lens[col as usize] = copy_len
                    col = col + 1
                }
                // skip \r\n
                if c == (13 as u8) && (pos + 1) < input_len && input[(pos + 1) as usize] == (10 as u8) {
                    pos = pos + 2
                } else {
                    pos = pos + 1
                }
                break
            } else if c == delimiter {
                // store field
                if col < 16 {
                    var fs: i32 = field_start
                    var fe: i32 = pos
                    let flen = fe - fs
                    let copy_len = if flen < 32 { flen } else { 31 }
                    let hbase = col * 32
                    var hc: i32 = 0
                    while hc < copy_len {
                        table.header_bytes[(hbase + hc) as usize] = input[(fs + hc) as usize]
                        hc = hc + 1
                    }
                    table.header_lens[col as usize] = copy_len
                    col = col + 1
                }
                field_start = pos + 1
                pos = pos + 1
            } else {
                pos = pos + 1
            }
        }
    }

    // --- Data rows ---
    var row_count: i32 = 0
    var col_count: i32 = 0      // columns seen in current row
    var n_cols_expected: i32 = 0  // established from first data row
    var row_vals: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    // Per-field scratch buffer. Fields are copied here (by csv_parse's own direct
    // indexing of `input`) before parsing, so parse_num never indexes a re-passed
    // ref at a nonzero offset — see the NOTE on parse_num.
    var fieldbuf: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    var field_start: i32 = pos

    while pos <= input_len {
        // Use input_len as sentinel: treat end-of-buffer like newline
        let c: u8 = if pos < input_len { input[pos as usize] } else { (10 as u8) }

        if c == (10 as u8) || c == (13 as u8) {
            // end of field and end of row
            var fe: i32 = pos
            if c == (13 as u8) && (pos + 1) < input_len && input[(pos + 1) as usize] == (10 as u8) {
                // \r\n  — fe points before \r
                fe = pos
            }
            // skip empty lines
            let field_len = fe - field_start
            if field_len > 0 || col_count > 0 {
                if col_count < 16 {
                    // copy field bytes into local scratch, then parse from index 0
                    var fn_len: i32 = 0
                    var fq: i32 = field_start
                    while fq < fe && fn_len < 64 {
                        fieldbuf[fn_len as usize] = input[fq as usize]
                        fq = fq + 1
                        fn_len = fn_len + 1
                    }
                    row_vals[col_count as usize] = parse_num(&fieldbuf, fn_len)
                    col_count = col_count + 1
                }
                // store row
                if col_count > 0 {
                    if row_count >= 256 { return 0 - 1 }
                    // establish or verify column count
                    if n_cols_expected == 0 {
                        n_cols_expected = col_count
                    }
                    if col_count != n_cols_expected { return 0 - 1 }
                    // write row into table
                    if table.n_cols == 0 {
                        table.n_cols = col_count
                    }
                    let base = row_count * table.n_cols
                    var wc: i32 = 0
                    while wc < col_count {
                        table.data[(base + wc) as usize] = row_vals[wc as usize]
                        wc = wc + 1
                    }
                    row_count = row_count + 1
                }
                col_count = 0
            }
            // advance past \r\n or \n
            if pos < input_len && c == (13 as u8) && (pos + 1) < input_len && input[(pos + 1) as usize] == (10 as u8) {
                pos = pos + 2
            } else {
                pos = pos + 1
            }
            field_start = pos
        } else if c == delimiter {
            // end of field, not end of row
            if col_count < 16 {
                // copy field bytes into local scratch, then parse from index 0
                var fn_len: i32 = 0
                var fq: i32 = field_start
                while fq < pos && fn_len < 64 {
                    fieldbuf[fn_len as usize] = input[fq as usize]
                    fq = fq + 1
                    fn_len = fn_len + 1
                }
                row_vals[col_count as usize] = parse_num(&fieldbuf, fn_len)
                col_count = col_count + 1
            }
            pos = pos + 1
            field_start = pos
        } else {
            pos = pos + 1
        }

        // sentinel consumed
        if pos > input_len { break }
    }

    table.n_rows = row_count
    0
}

// =============================================================================
// Serialization helpers
// =============================================================================

// Write the decimal digits of a non-negative integer n into out starting at
// pos.  Returns the new pos.
fn write_i32_digits(n: i32, out: &![u8; 4096], pos: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 {
        out[pos as usize] = (48 as u8)   // '0'
        return pos + 1
    }
    // Collect digits in reverse, then flip
    var tmp: [u8; 12] = [0; 12]
    var k: i32 = 0
    var v: i32 = n
    while v > 0 {
        tmp[k as usize] = (48 + v % 10) as u8
        v = v / 10
        k = k + 1
    }
    // Write reversed
    var i: i32 = k - 1
    var p: i32 = pos
    while i >= 0 {
        out[p as usize] = tmp[i as usize]
        p = p + 1
        i = i - 1
    }
    p
}

/// Write an f64 value as decimal text into out[pos..].
/// Format: [-]integer[.fraction] with up to 6 fractional digits (trailing
/// zeros stripped).  Returns updated pos.
fn write_f64(val: f64, out: &![u8; 4096], pos: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = pos
    var v: f64 = val

    // Sign
    if v < 0.0 {
        out[p as usize] = (45 as u8)   // '-'
        p = p + 1
        v = 0.0 - v
    }

    // Integer part
    let int_part: i32 = v as i32
    p = write_i32_digits(int_part, out, p)

    // Fractional part — 6 digits max
    let frac = v - (int_part as f64)
    if frac > 0.000001 {
        out[p as usize] = (46 as u8)   // '.'
        p = p + 1

        // Scale up to 6 decimal places
        var frac6: i32 = (frac * 1000000.0) as i32
        // Trim trailing zeros
        while frac6 > 0 && frac6 % 10 == 0 {
            frac6 = frac6 / 10
        }
        // Count digits in frac6 to determine leading zeros needed
        // We need to figure out how many digits frac6 has vs how many we need
        // to represent 6 decimal places.
        // Re-derive: original fraction scaled to 6 decimal digits
        var full6: i32 = (frac * 1000000.0) as i32
        // Count significant decimal positions
        var digits6: [u8; 6] = [0; 6]
        var d: i32 = 5
        var rem: i32 = full6
        while d >= 0 {
            digits6[d as usize] = (48 + rem % 10) as u8
            rem = rem / 10
            d = d - 1
        }
        // Find last non-zero digit
        var last: i32 = 5
        while last > 0 && digits6[last as usize] == (48 as u8) {
            last = last - 1
        }
        var di: i32 = 0
        while di <= last {
            out[p as usize] = digits6[di as usize]
            p = p + 1
            di = di + 1
        }
    }

    p
}

// =============================================================================
// CSV serializer
// =============================================================================

/// Serialize table to CSV bytes in out[0..].
///
/// - delimiter is written between fields (typically (44 as u8) = ',')
/// - header row is written first when table.has_header == 1
/// - Returns the total number of bytes written, or -1 on overflow.
pub fn csv_serialize(table: &CsvTable, out: &![u8; 4096], delimiter: u8) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = 0

    // Header row
    if table.has_header == 1 {
        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < table.n_cols {
            if c > 0 {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                out[p as usize] = delimiter
                p = p + 1
            }
            let hlen = table.header_lens[c as usize]
            let hbase = c * 32
            var hc: i32 = 0
            while hc < hlen {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                out[p as usize] = table.header_bytes[(hbase + hc) as usize]
                p = p + 1
                hc = hc + 1
            }
            c = c + 1
        }
        if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
        out[p as usize] = (10 as u8)   // '\n'
        p = p + 1
    }

    // Data rows
    var r: i32 = 0
    while r < table.n_rows {
        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < table.n_cols {
            if c > 0 {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                out[p as usize] = delimiter
                p = p + 1
            }
            let v = table.data[(r * table.n_cols + c) as usize]
            p = write_f64(v, out, p)
            if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
            c = c + 1
        }
        if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
        out[p as usize] = (10 as u8)   // '\n'
        p = p + 1
        r = r + 1
    }

    p
}

// =============================================================================
// CsvBuf-based serialize / parse
//
// Use these variants instead of csv_serialize / csv_parse when doing
// round-trip serialize→parse in the JIT, because &!CsvBuf struct
// mutations are visible to callers (raw &![u8;4096] parameter mutations
// have a known JIT limitation).
// =============================================================================

// Write-f64 variant that targets CsvBuf.bytes
fn write_f64_buf(val: f64, b: &!CsvBuf, pos: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = pos
    var v: f64 = val

    if v < 0.0 {
        b.bytes[p as usize] = (45 as u8)
        p = p + 1
        v = 0.0 - v
    }

    let int_part: i32 = v as i32
    // write integer digits into a temp buf then copy
    var tmp: [u8; 12] = [0; 12]
    var k: i32 = 0
    if int_part == 0 {
        b.bytes[p as usize] = (48 as u8)
        p = p + 1
    } else {
        var vi: i32 = int_part
        while vi > 0 {
            tmp[k as usize] = (48 + vi % 10) as u8
            vi = vi / 10
            k = k + 1
        }
        var ii: i32 = k - 1
        while ii >= 0 {
            b.bytes[p as usize] = tmp[ii as usize]
            p = p + 1
            ii = ii - 1
        }
    }

    let frac = v - (int_part as f64)
    if frac > 0.000001 {
        b.bytes[p as usize] = (46 as u8)
        p = p + 1
        var full6: i32 = (frac * 1000000.0) as i32
        var digits6: [u8; 6] = [0; 6]
        var d: i32 = 5
        var rem: i32 = full6
        while d >= 0 {
            digits6[d as usize] = (48 + rem % 10) as u8
            rem = rem / 10
            d = d - 1
        }
        var last: i32 = 5
        while last > 0 && digits6[last as usize] == (48 as u8) {
            last = last - 1
        }
        var di: i32 = 0
        while di <= last {
            b.bytes[p as usize] = digits6[di as usize]
            p = p + 1
            di = di + 1
        }
    }
    p
}

/// Serialize table into a CsvBuf. Sets b.len to bytes written.
/// Returns bytes written, or -1 on overflow.
pub fn csv_serialize_buf(table: &CsvTable, b: &!CsvBuf, delimiter: u8) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = 0

    if table.has_header == 1 {
        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < table.n_cols {
            if c > 0 {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                b.bytes[p as usize] = delimiter
                p = p + 1
            }
            let hlen = table.header_lens[c as usize]
            let hbase = c * 32
            var hc: i32 = 0
            while hc < hlen {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                b.bytes[p as usize] = table.header_bytes[(hbase + hc) as usize]
                p = p + 1
                hc = hc + 1
            }
            c = c + 1
        }
        if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
        b.bytes[p as usize] = (10 as u8)
        p = p + 1
    }

    var r: i32 = 0
    while r < table.n_rows {
        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < table.n_cols {
            if c > 0 {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                b.bytes[p as usize] = delimiter
                p = p + 1
            }
            let v = table.data[(r * table.n_cols + c) as usize]
            p = write_f64_buf(v, b, p)
            if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
            c = c + 1
        }
        if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
        b.bytes[p as usize] = (10 as u8)
        p = p + 1
        r = r + 1
    }

    b.len = p
    p
}

/// Parse CSV from a CsvBuf into table. Convenience wrapper over csv_parse.
pub fn csv_parse_buf(b: &CsvBuf, table: &!CsvTable, delimiter: u8) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    csv_parse(&b.bytes, b.len, table, delimiter)
}

// =============================================================================
// Column statistics
// =============================================================================

/// Sum of column col. Returns 0.0 for invalid col or empty table.
pub fn csv_col_sum(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var r: i32 = 0
    while r < t.n_rows {
        s = s + t.data[(r * t.n_cols + col) as usize]
        r = r + 1
    }
    s
}

/// Arithmetic mean of column col. Returns 0.0 for invalid col or empty table.
pub fn csv_col_mean(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    if t.n_rows == 0 { return 0.0 }
    csv_col_sum(t, col) / (t.n_rows as f64)
}

/// Population variance of column col.
pub fn csv_col_variance(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    if t.n_rows == 0 { return 0.0 }
    let mean = csv_col_mean(t, col)
    var acc: f64 = 0.0
    var r: i32 = 0
    while r < t.n_rows {
        let d = t.data[(r * t.n_cols + col) as usize] - mean
        acc = acc + d * d
        r = r + 1
    }
    acc / (t.n_rows as f64)
}

/// Minimum value in column col.
pub fn csv_col_min(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    if t.n_rows == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var m: f64 = t.data[col as usize]
    var r: i32 = 1
    while r < t.n_rows {
        let v = t.data[(r * t.n_cols + col) as usize]
        if v < m { m = v }
        r = r + 1
    }
    m
}

/// Maximum value in column col.
pub fn csv_col_max(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    if t.n_rows == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var m: f64 = t.data[col as usize]
    var r: i32 = 1
    while r < t.n_rows {
        let v = t.data[(r * t.n_cols + col) as usize]
        if v > m { m = v }
        r = r + 1
    }
    m
}

/// Serialize `table` to CSV and write it to `path` on disk, returning the number of bytes written
/// (or -1 on overflow). Companion to `csv_parse_string`: together they give a file <-> table
/// round-trip.  The bytes are copied into an [i8] buffer before the write_file builtin, because
/// write_file marshals [i8] correctly but not [u8] on the current backend.
pub fn csv_write_file(table: &CsvTable, path: string, delimiter: u8) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out: [u8; 4096] = [0; 4096]
    let n = csv_serialize(table, &!out, delimiter)
    if n < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    var i8buf: [i8; 4096] = [0; 4096]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < (n as i64) && i < 4096 {
        i8buf[i as usize] = out[i as usize] as i8
        i = i + 1
    }
    let rc = write_file(path, i8buf, n as i64)
    if rc < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    n
}


// === FILE: stdlib/csv/row.sio ===
// stdlib/csv/row — Lightweight single-row CSV parser
//
// Parses one line of comma-separated f64 values into a fixed-size row.
// For full CSV table parsing, see csv/parser.sio.

struct CsvRow {
    fields: [f64; 32],
    field_count: i32
}

fn csv_row_new() -> CsvRow {
    CsvRow { fields: [0.0; 32], field_count: 0 }
}

// Count commas + 1 to get field count (0 for empty line)
fn csv_parse_field_count(line: &[u8; 256], line_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if line_len <= 0 { return 0 }
    var count: i32 = 1
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < line_len {
        if line[i] == 44 { count = count + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    count
}

// Parse a simple decimal f64 from bytes[start..end)
fn csv_parse_f64(line: &[u8; 256], start: i32, end: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = start
    while i < end && (line[i] == 32 || line[i] == 9) {
        i = i + 1
    }
    if i >= end { return 0.0 }

    var negative = false
    if line[i] == 45 {
        negative = true
        i = i + 1
    } else if line[i] == 43 {
        i = i + 1
    }

    var int_part: f64 = 0.0
    while i < end && line[i] >= 48 && line[i] <= 57 {
        int_part = int_part * 10.0 + (line[i] - 48) as f64
        i = i + 1
    }

    var frac_part: f64 = 0.0
    if i < end && line[i] == 46 {
        i = i + 1
        var divisor: f64 = 10.0
        while i < end && line[i] >= 48 && line[i] <= 57 {
            frac_part = frac_part + (line[i] - 48) as f64 / divisor
            divisor = divisor * 10.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    var result = int_part + frac_part
    if negative { result = 0.0 - result }
    result
}

// Parse a line of comma-separated f64 values
fn csv_parse_row(line: &[u8; 256], line_len: i32) -> CsvRow with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var row = csv_row_new()
    if line_len <= 0 { return row }

    var field_start: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i <= line_len && row.field_count < 32 {
        if i == line_len || line[i] == 44 {
            let val = csv_parse_f64(line, field_start, i)
            row.fields[row.field_count] = val
            row.field_count = row.field_count + 1
            field_start = i + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    row
}

fn csv_row_get(row: CsvRow, idx: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Div {
    if idx < 0 || idx >= row.field_count { return 0.0 }
    row.fields[idx]
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_parse_simple() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var line: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    // "1.5,2.0,3.5"
    line[0] = 49
    line[1] = 46
    line[2] = 53
    line[3] = 44
    line[4] = 50
    line[5] = 46
    line[6] = 48
    line[7] = 44
    line[8] = 51
    line[9] = 46
    line[10] = 53

    let row = csv_parse_row(&line, 11)
    row.field_count == 3 && row.fields[0] == 1.5 && row.fields[1] == 2.0 && row.fields[2] == 3.5
}

fn test_field_count() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var line: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    // "10,20,30,40"
    line[0] = 49
    line[1] = 48
    line[2] = 44
    line[3] = 50
    line[4] = 48
    line[5] = 44
    line[6] = 51
    line[7] = 48
    line[8] = 44
    line[9] = 52
    line[10] = 48
    csv_parse_field_count(&line, 11) == 4
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if test_parse_simple() { print("csv parse_simple: PASS\n") } else { print("csv parse_simple: FAIL\n") }
    if test_field_count() { print("csv field_count: PASS\n") } else { print("csv field_count: FAIL\n") }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/cybernetic/autopoiesis.sio ===
//! stdlib/cybernetic/autopoiesis.sio
//!
//! Autopoiesis — Self-producing systems (Maturana/Varela 1972)
//!
//! An autopoietic system is a network of production processes that produces
//! the very components constituting the network. Organizational closure
//! (circular production) is the defining property.
//!
//! Production relations stored in a 16x16 adjacency matrix.
//! Organizational closure verified via DFS cycle detection.

pub struct AutopoieticSystem {
    component_count: i64,
    relations: [i64; 64],            // 8x8 flattened: relations[i*8+j]=1 means i produces j
    component_values: [f64; 8],
    component_variances: [f64; 8],
    component_active: [i64; 8],      // 1=active, 0=inactive
    boundary_permeability: f64,
    alive: i64,
    generation: i64,
    total_perturbation: f64,
    structural_drift_val: f64,
}

pub fn system_new(permeability: f64) -> AutopoieticSystem {
    AutopoieticSystem {
        component_count: 0,
        relations: [0; 64],
        component_values: [0.0; 8],
        component_variances: [0.0; 8],
        component_active: [0; 8],
        boundary_permeability: permeability,
        alive: 0,
        generation: 0,
        total_perturbation: 0.0,
        structural_drift_val: 0.0,
    }
}

/// Add a component with production relation: produced_by → this → produces
pub fn add_component(sys: AutopoieticSystem, produced_by: i64, produces: i64, value: f64, variance: f64) -> AutopoieticSystem with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = sys
    let idx = s.component_count
    if idx >= 8 { return s }

    s.component_active[idx as usize] = 1
    s.component_values[idx as usize] = value
    s.component_variances[idx as usize] = variance

    // Record production relation: produced_by → idx
    if produced_by >= 0 && produced_by < 8 {
        s.relations[(produced_by * 8 + idx) as usize] = 1
    }
    // Record production relation: idx → produces
    if produces >= 0 && produces < 8 {
        s.relations[(idx * 8 + produces) as usize] = 1
    }

    s.component_count = idx + 1
    s.alive = check_closure(s)
    s
}

/// Run one production cycle: each active producer propagates to targets.
/// Values average with GUM variance propagation.
pub fn produce_cycle(sys: AutopoieticSystem) -> AutopoieticSystem with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = sys
    var new_values: [f64; 8] = s.component_values
    var new_vars: [f64; 8] = s.component_variances

    var i = 0
    while i < s.component_count {
        if s.component_active[i as usize] == 1 {
            var j = 0
            while j < s.component_count {
                if s.relations[(i * 8 + j) as usize] == 1 && s.component_active[j as usize] == 1 {
                    let vi = s.component_values[i as usize]
                    let vj = s.component_values[j as usize]
                    let old_vj = vj
                    new_values[j as usize] = (vi + vj) / 2.0
                    new_vars[j as usize] = (s.component_variances[i as usize] + s.component_variances[j as usize]) / 4.0

                    let delta = new_values[j as usize] - old_vj
                    let abs_d = if delta < 0.0 { 0.0 - delta } else { delta }
                    s.structural_drift_val = s.structural_drift_val + abs_d
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    s.component_values = new_values
    s.component_variances = new_vars
    s.generation = s.generation + 1
    s
}

/// Perturb from environment. Affects structure (values) NOT organization (relations).
pub fn perturb(sys: AutopoieticSystem, value: f64, variance: f64) -> AutopoieticSystem with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = sys
    let scaled = value * s.boundary_permeability
    let abs_scaled = if scaled < 0.0 { 0.0 - scaled } else { scaled }
    s.total_perturbation = s.total_perturbation + abs_scaled

    if s.component_count > 0 {
        let per_comp = scaled / (s.component_count as f64)
        var i = 0
        while i < s.component_count {
            if s.component_active[i as usize] == 1 {
                s.component_values[i as usize] = s.component_values[i as usize] + per_comp
                s.component_variances[i as usize] = s.component_variances[i as usize] + variance * s.boundary_permeability
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    s
}

/// Deactivate a component and recheck closure.
pub fn deactivate_component(sys: AutopoieticSystem, id: i64) -> AutopoieticSystem with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = sys
    if id >= 0 && id < 8 {
        s.component_active[id as usize] = 0
        s.alive = check_closure(s)
    }
    s
}

pub fn is_alive(sys: AutopoieticSystem) -> bool {
    sys.alive != 0
}

pub fn generation(sys: AutopoieticSystem) -> i64 {
    sys.generation
}

pub fn structural_drift(sys: AutopoieticSystem) -> f64 {
    sys.structural_drift_val + sys.total_perturbation
}

/// DFS cycle detection on the active component subgraph.
/// For each active component, search for a path back to itself.
/// A cycle = organizational closure = autopoiesis.
fn check_closure(sys: AutopoieticSystem) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var start = 0
    while start < sys.component_count {
        if sys.component_active[start as usize] == 0 {
            start = start + 1
            continue
        }

        var stack: [i64; 8] = [-1; 8]
        var stack_top = 0
        var visited: [i64; 8] = [0; 8]
        visited[start as usize] = 1

        // Push direct successors of start
        var j = 0
        while j < sys.component_count {
            if sys.relations[(start * 8 + j) as usize] == 1 && sys.component_active[j as usize] == 1 {
                if j == start { return 1 }
                if stack_top < 8 {
                    stack[stack_top as usize] = j
                    stack_top = stack_top + 1
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }

        // DFS
        while stack_top > 0 {
            stack_top = stack_top - 1
            let node = stack[stack_top as usize]
            if visited[node as usize] == 1 { continue }
            visited[node as usize] = 1

            var k = 0
            while k < sys.component_count {
                if sys.relations[(node * 8 + k) as usize] == 1 && sys.component_active[k as usize] == 1 {
                    if k == start { return 1 }
                    if visited[k as usize] == 0 && stack_top < 8 {
                        stack[stack_top as usize] = k
                        stack_top = stack_top + 1
                    }
                }
                k = k + 1
            }
        }
        start = start + 1
    }
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/cybernetic/bateson.sio ===
//! stdlib/cybernetic/bateson.sio
//! Bateson's Hierarchical Learning Levels (1972)
//!
//! L0: Fixed stimulus-response (zero learning)
//! L1: Parameter adjustment via EMA (learning within a model)
//! L2: Model switching (learning to learn — changing parameter sets)
//! L3: Epistemological restructuring (learning about learning to learn)
//!
//! Hierarchy is enforced: L1 failure triggers L2, L2 failure triggers L3.
//! Double bind: L1 failing + L2 blocked + L3 frozen.

pub struct LearningContext {
    level: i64,
    response_table: [i64; 16],
    active_param_set: i64,
    params: [f64; 64],
    param_counts: [i64; 8],
    available_sets: i64,
    meta_frame: i64,
    frame_count: i64,
    double_bind_count: i64,
    l1_fail_count: i64,
    l2_fail_count: i64,
    l1_threshold: f64,
    last_improvement: f64,
}

pub struct LearningEvent {
    changed: i64,
    level_engaged: i64,
    model_switched: i64,
    frame_restructured: i64,
    double_bind: i64,
    context: LearningContext,
}

// ============================================================================
// Constructor
// ============================================================================

pub fn bateson_new() -> LearningContext {
    LearningContext {
        level: 0,
        response_table: [0; 16],
        active_param_set: 0,
        params: [0.0; 64],
        param_counts: [0; 8],
        available_sets: 255,
        meta_frame: 0,
        frame_count: 0,
        double_bind_count: 0,
        l1_fail_count: 0,
        l2_fail_count: 0,
        l1_threshold: 0.01,
        last_improvement: 0.0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64_b(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn make_event(ctx: LearningContext, level: i64) -> LearningEvent {
    LearningEvent {
        changed: 0,
        level_engaged: level,
        model_switched: 0,
        frame_restructured: 0,
        double_bind: 0,
        context: ctx,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// L1: Parameter adjustment (learning within a model)
// ============================================================================

pub fn level_one_update(ctx: LearningContext, stimulus: i64, outcome: f64) -> LearningEvent with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = ctx
    let idx = s.active_param_set * 8 + (stimulus % 8)
    let old_val = s.params[idx as usize]
    let new_val = old_val * 0.9 + outcome * 0.1
    s.params[idx as usize] = new_val
    s.param_counts[s.active_param_set as usize] = s.param_counts[s.active_param_set as usize] + 1

    let improvement = abs_f64_b(new_val - old_val)
    s.last_improvement = improvement
    s.level = 1

    // Track L1 failure (stagnation)
    if improvement < s.l1_threshold {
        s.l1_fail_count = s.l1_fail_count + 1
    } else {
        s.l1_fail_count = 0
    }

    var evt = make_event(s, 1)
    evt.changed = 1
    evt
}

// ============================================================================
// L2: Model switching (learning to learn)
// ============================================================================

pub fn level_two_switch(ctx: LearningContext, threshold: f64) -> LearningEvent with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = ctx
    var switched: i64 = 0
    var next_set = s.active_param_set + 1
    var checked: i64 = 0

    while checked < 8 && switched == 0 {
        if next_set >= 8 { next_set = 0 }
        let bit = 1 << next_set
        if (s.available_sets & bit) != 0 {
            if next_set != s.active_param_set {
                s.active_param_set = next_set
                switched = 1
            }
        }
        if switched == 0 {
            next_set = next_set + 1
            checked = checked + 1
        }
    }

    s.level = 2
    if switched == 1 {
        s.l1_fail_count = 0
        s.l2_fail_count = 0
    } else {
        s.l2_fail_count = s.l2_fail_count + 1
    }

    var evt = make_event(s, 2)
    evt.changed = switched
    evt.model_switched = switched
    evt
}

// ============================================================================
// L3: Epistemological restructuring
// ============================================================================

pub fn level_three_restructure(ctx: LearningContext) -> LearningEvent with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = ctx
    // Clear all parameter sets
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 64 { s.params[i as usize] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    i = 0
    while i < 8 { s.param_counts[i as usize] = 0; i = i + 1 }
    // Reset L2 resources
    s.available_sets = 255
    s.active_param_set = 0
    s.l1_fail_count = 0
    s.l2_fail_count = 0
    s.meta_frame = s.meta_frame + 1
    s.frame_count = s.frame_count + 1
    s.level = 3

    var evt = make_event(s, 3)
    evt.changed = 1
    evt.frame_restructured = 1
    evt
}

// ============================================================================
// Double bind detection
// ============================================================================

/// Double bind = L1 stagnating + L2 blocked (no available sets) + L3 frozen (too many restructures)
pub fn detect_double_bind(ctx: LearningContext) -> bool with Div, Panic {
    let l1_stuck = ctx.l1_fail_count >= 3
    let l2_blocked = ctx.available_sets == 0
    let l3_frozen = ctx.frame_count > 3
    l1_stuck && l2_blocked && l3_frozen
}

// ============================================================================
// Main entry point: hierarchical learning state machine
// ============================================================================

/// The main learning function. Applies hierarchical learning:
/// 1. Try L1 (parameter update)
/// 2. If L1 stagnates (3+ consecutive failures) -> trigger L2
/// 3. If L2 fails (no available sets) -> trigger L3
/// 4. If L3 is frozen -> detect double bind
pub fn learn(ctx: LearningContext, stimulus: i64, outcome: f64) -> LearningEvent with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Step 1: L1 update
    var evt = level_one_update(ctx, stimulus, outcome)
    var s = evt.context

    // Step 2: Check if L1 has stagnated
    if s.l1_fail_count >= 3 {
        // Try L2: switch model
        let l2_evt = level_two_switch(s, s.l1_threshold)
        s = l2_evt.context

        if l2_evt.model_switched == 1 {
            // L2 succeeded
            var result = make_event(s, 2)
            result.changed = 1
            result.model_switched = 1
            return result
        }

        // L2 failed: try L3
        if s.l2_fail_count >= 2 {
            // Check for double bind first
            if detect_double_bind(s) {
                s.double_bind_count = s.double_bind_count + 1
                var db_evt = make_event(s, 3)
                db_evt.double_bind = 1
                return db_evt
            }
            // L3 restructure
            let l3_evt = level_three_restructure(s)
            return l3_evt
        }
    }

    evt
}


// === FILE: stdlib/cybernetic/conversation.sio ===
//! stdlib/cybernetic/conversation.sio
//!
//! Pask's Conversation Theory (1975) — Knowledge Through Dialogue
//!
//! Core principle: each participant maintains TWO models:
//!   1. Their own belief (p_value)
//!   2. Their model of the other's belief (p_model_of_q)
//! These are SEPARATE and update independently via observation.
//! Agreement = convergence of cross-models, not averaging of values.

pub struct Conversation {
    p_id: i64,
    q_id: i64,
    topic_id: i64,
    // Actual beliefs
    p_value: f64,
    p_variance: f64,
    q_value: f64,
    q_variance: f64,
    // Cross-models (the core of Pask's theory)
    p_model_of_q: f64,       // P's estimate of what Q believes
    p_model_of_q_var: f64,   // P's confidence in that estimate
    q_model_of_p: f64,       // Q's estimate of what P believes
    q_model_of_p_var: f64,   // Q's confidence in that estimate
    // Metrics
    agreement_value: f64,
    model_accuracy_p: f64,   // |p_model_of_q - q_value|
    model_accuracy_q: f64,   // |q_model_of_p - p_value|
    rounds: i64,
    converged: i64,
    convergence_threshold: f64,
}

pub fn conversation_new(p_id: i64, q_id: i64, topic_id: i64) -> Conversation {
    Conversation {
        p_id: p_id,
        q_id: q_id,
        topic_id: topic_id,
        p_value: 0.0,
        p_variance: 1.0,
        q_value: 0.0,
        q_variance: 1.0,
        p_model_of_q: 0.0,
        p_model_of_q_var: 100.0,    // initially very uncertain about other
        q_model_of_p: 0.0,
        q_model_of_p_var: 100.0,
        agreement_value: 0.0,
        model_accuracy_p: 0.0,
        model_accuracy_q: 0.0,
        rounds: 0,
        converged: 0,
        convergence_threshold: 0.01,
    }
}

pub fn set_models(conv: Conversation, p_val: f64, p_var: f64, q_val: f64, q_var: f64) -> Conversation with Mut {
    var s = conv
    s.p_value = p_val
    s.p_variance = p_var
    s.q_value = q_val
    s.q_variance = q_var
    // Initial cross-models: P guesses Q is at Q's stated value (uncertain)
    s.p_model_of_q = q_val
    s.p_model_of_q_var = q_var + 10.0
    s.q_model_of_p = p_val
    s.q_model_of_p_var = p_var + 10.0
    s
}

/// One round of Pask conversation with proper dual modeling.
///
/// Phase 1: P observes Q's stated value and updates its cross-model.
///          P then shifts own belief toward what it thinks Q believes.
/// Phase 2: Q observes P's (now updated) stated value similarly.
/// Phase 3: Compute agreement, model accuracy, convergence.
pub fn converse(conv: Conversation) -> Conversation with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = conv

    // ---- PHASE 1: P updates ----
    // P observes Q's stated value (q_value) and updates p_model_of_q
    let p_model_prec = 1.0 / (s.p_model_of_q_var + 0.001)
    let q_stated_prec = 1.0 / (s.q_variance + 0.001)
    let p_total_prec = p_model_prec + q_stated_prec

    // Precision-weighted update of P's model of Q
    s.p_model_of_q = (s.p_model_of_q * p_model_prec + s.q_value * q_stated_prec) / p_total_prec
    s.p_model_of_q_var = 1.0 / p_total_prec

    // P shifts own belief toward its model of Q (weighted by relative confidence)
    // Pask: trust increases with agreement history
    let p_own_prec = 1.0 / (s.p_variance + 0.001)
    let p_model_weight = 0.1 + 0.4 * s.agreement_value
    s.p_value = s.p_value * (1.0 - p_model_weight) + s.p_model_of_q * p_model_weight
    s.p_variance = s.p_variance * 0.99  // slight certainty gain from dialogue

    // ---- PHASE 2: Q updates ----
    // Q observes P's (now updated) stated value and updates q_model_of_p
    let q_model_prec = 1.0 / (s.q_model_of_p_var + 0.001)
    let p_stated_prec = 1.0 / (s.p_variance + 0.001)
    let q_total_prec = q_model_prec + p_stated_prec

    s.q_model_of_p = (s.q_model_of_p * q_model_prec + s.p_value * p_stated_prec) / q_total_prec
    s.q_model_of_p_var = 1.0 / q_total_prec

    // Pask: trust increases with agreement history
    let q_model_weight = 0.1 + 0.4 * s.agreement_value
    s.q_value = s.q_value * (1.0 - q_model_weight) + s.q_model_of_p * q_model_weight
    s.q_variance = s.q_variance * 0.99

    // ---- PHASE 3: Metrics ----
    let diff_pq = s.p_value - s.q_value
    let abs_diff = if diff_pq > 0.0 { diff_pq } else { 0.0 - diff_pq }

    // Model accuracy: how well does P know Q's actual belief?
    let err_p = s.p_model_of_q - s.q_value
    s.model_accuracy_p = if err_p > 0.0 { err_p } else { 0.0 - err_p }
    let err_q = s.q_model_of_p - s.p_value
    s.model_accuracy_q = if err_q > 0.0 { err_q } else { 0.0 - err_q }

    // Agreement based on value convergence
    let abs_p = if s.p_value > 0.0 { s.p_value } else { 0.0 - s.p_value }
    let abs_q = if s.q_value > 0.0 { s.q_value } else { 0.0 - s.q_value }
    var denom = 0.001
    if abs_p > denom { denom = abs_p }
    if abs_q > denom { denom = abs_q }
    s.agreement_value = 1.0 - abs_diff / denom

    s.converged = if abs_diff < s.convergence_threshold { 1 } else { 0 }
    s.rounds = s.rounds + 1
    s
}

pub fn agreement(conv: Conversation) -> f64 {
    conv.agreement_value
}

pub fn has_converged(conv: Conversation) -> bool {
    conv.converged != 0
}

/// Shared understanding: midpoint of converged beliefs.
pub fn shared_understanding(conv: Conversation) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    (conv.p_value + conv.q_value) / 2.0
}

/// How well do participants model each other? Lower = better.
pub fn model_accuracy(conv: Conversation) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    (conv.model_accuracy_p + conv.model_accuracy_q) / 2.0
}

/// Asymmetry: do they know each other equally well?
pub fn conversation_asymmetry(conv: Conversation) -> f64 {
    let diff = conv.model_accuracy_p - conv.model_accuracy_q
    if diff > 0.0 { diff } else { 0.0 - diff }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/cybernetic/coupling.sio ===
//! stdlib/cybernetic/coupling.sio
//!
//! Structural Coupling (Maturana/Varela)
//!
//! Two systems coupled through recurrent mutual perturbation.
//! Congruence measured via Pearson correlation on output histories.
//! Mutual information estimated from correlation coefficient.

pub struct Coupling {
    system_a_id: i64,
    system_b_id: i64,
    history_len: i64,
    congruence_value: f64,
    a_history: [f64; 64],
    b_history: [f64; 64],
    mean_error: f64,
    error_variance: f64,
    // Running sums for Pearson correlation
    sum_a: f64,
    sum_b: f64,
    sum_a2: f64,
    sum_b2: f64,
    sum_ab: f64,
}

pub fn coupling_new(a_id: i64, b_id: i64) -> Coupling {
    Coupling {
        system_a_id: a_id,
        system_b_id: b_id,
        history_len: 0,
        congruence_value: 0.0,
        a_history: [0.0; 64],
        b_history: [0.0; 64],
        mean_error: 0.0,
        error_variance: 0.0,
        sum_a: 0.0,
        sum_b: 0.0,
        sum_a2: 0.0,
        sum_b2: 0.0,
        sum_ab: 0.0,
    }
}

/// Record one coupling step. Updates circular buffers, running sums,
/// and computes Pearson correlation as congruence metric.
pub fn couple_step(c: Coupling, a_val: f64, b_val: f64) -> Coupling with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = c
    let idx = s.history_len % 64

    // If buffer has wrapped, subtract the old values from running sums
    if s.history_len >= 64 {
        let old_a = s.a_history[idx as usize]
        let old_b = s.b_history[idx as usize]
        s.sum_a = s.sum_a - old_a
        s.sum_b = s.sum_b - old_b
        s.sum_a2 = s.sum_a2 - old_a * old_a
        s.sum_b2 = s.sum_b2 - old_b * old_b
        s.sum_ab = s.sum_ab - old_a * old_b
    }

    // Store new values
    s.a_history[idx as usize] = a_val
    s.b_history[idx as usize] = b_val

    // Add to running sums
    s.sum_a = s.sum_a + a_val
    s.sum_b = s.sum_b + b_val
    s.sum_a2 = s.sum_a2 + a_val * a_val
    s.sum_b2 = s.sum_b2 + b_val * b_val
    s.sum_ab = s.sum_ab + a_val * b_val

    // Update mean error via EMA
    let diff = a_val - b_val
    let abs_diff = if diff > 0.0 { diff } else { 0.0 - diff }
    s.mean_error = s.mean_error * 0.95 + abs_diff * 0.05

    s.history_len = s.history_len + 1

    // Compute Pearson correlation: r = (n*Σab - Σa*Σb) / sqrt((n*Σa² - (Σa)²)(n*Σb² - (Σb)²))
    let n_f = if s.history_len < 64 { s.history_len as f64 } else { 64.0 }
    if n_f > 1.0 {
        let num = n_f * s.sum_ab - s.sum_a * s.sum_b
        let denom_a = n_f * s.sum_a2 - s.sum_a * s.sum_a
        let denom_b = n_f * s.sum_b2 - s.sum_b * s.sum_b

        if denom_a > 0.0001 && denom_b > 0.0001 {
            let denom = sqrt_approx(denom_a * denom_b)
            if denom > 0.0001 {
                let r = num / denom
                // Clamp to [0, 1] (we care about positive correlation)
                s.congruence_value = if r < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { if r > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { r } }
            }
        }
    }

    s
}

pub fn congruence(c: Coupling) -> f64 {
    c.congruence_value
}

pub fn prediction_error(c: Coupling) -> f64 {
    c.mean_error
}

/// Mutual information estimated from Pearson r:
/// MI ≈ -0.5 * ln(1 - r²) using Taylor: ln(1-x) ≈ -x - x²/2 - x³/3 - x⁴/4
pub fn mutual_information(c: Coupling) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let r = c.congruence_value
    let r2 = r * r
    if r2 > 0.99 { return 3.0 }
    // Taylor series for -ln(1-x) = x + x²/2 + x³/3 + x⁴/4
    let x = r2
    let neg_ln = x + x * x / 2.0 + x * x * x / 3.0 + x * x * x * x / 4.0
    0.5 * neg_ln
}

fn sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    // Better initial guess: scale down to reasonable range
    var y = 1.0
    var scaled = x
    while scaled > 1000000.0 {
        scaled = scaled / 1000000.0
        y = y * 1000.0
    }
    // y² ≈ original_x / scaled, so y * sqrt(scaled) ≈ sqrt(x)
    var s = scaled
    s = 0.5 * (s + scaled / s)
    s = 0.5 * (s + scaled / s)
    s = 0.5 * (s + scaled / s)
    s = 0.5 * (s + scaled / s)
    s = 0.5 * (s + scaled / s)
    s = 0.5 * (s + scaled / s)
    s = 0.5 * (s + scaled / s)
    s = 0.5 * (s + scaled / s)
    y * s
}


// === FILE: stdlib/cybernetic/distinction.sio ===
//! stdlib/cybernetic/distinction.sio
//!
//! Spencer-Brown's Laws of Form + Varela's Calculus for Self-Reference
//!
//! The primitive act of cognition is drawing a distinction — splitting
//! the world into "this" and "not-this". Everything in second-order
//! cybernetics flows from this single operation.
//!
//! Spencer-Brown (1969) formalized distinction with two axioms:
//!   Axiom 1 — Calling:  ⌐⌐ = ⌐  (marking twice = marking once)
//!   Axiom 2 — Crossing: ⌐(void) = MARKED, and crossing back = void
//!
//! Varela (1975) extended this with a third value — the autonomous
//! or self-indicating form J where J = ⌐J. This resolves self-reference
//! without paradox and is structurally identical to recursive types.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```sounio
//! use cybernetic::distinction::{Form, form_mark, form_cross, form_reenter, eval_form}
//! use cybernetic::distinction::{UNMARKED, MARKED, AUTONOMOUS}
//!
//! let void = form_void()              // unmarked state
//! let m = form_mark(void)             // draw a distinction → MARKED
//! let mm = form_mark(m)               // calling: ⌐⌐ = ⌐ → MARKED
//! assert(eval_form(m) == eval_form(mm))
//!
//! let crossed = form_cross(m)         // crossing: ⌐MARKED = UNMARKED
//! assert(eval_form(crossed) == UNMARKED)
//!
//! let j = form_reenter()              // self-indicating: J = ⌐J → AUTONOMOUS
//! assert(eval_form(j) == AUTONOMOUS)
//! ```

// ============================================================================
// THE THREE VALUES (Varela 1975)
// ============================================================================

/// Unmarked state — the void, outside all distinctions
pub const UNMARKED: i64 = 0

/// Marked state — inside the distinction
pub const MARKED: i64 = 1

/// Autonomous state — self-indicating form (Varela's J)
/// Neither marked nor unmarked; the fixed point of crossing.
/// Structurally identical to mu X. cross(X) in type theory.
pub const AUTONOMOUS: i64 = 2

// ============================================================================
// FORM — Spencer-Brown expression tree
// ============================================================================

/// A Form is a node in the calculus of indications.
/// Forms compose by nesting (children inside a mark).
///
/// The empty form (no children, not marked) is the UNMARKED state.
/// A mark with no children is the MARKED state.
/// A form with is_reentrant = true is AUTONOMOUS.
pub struct Form {
    /// Current value: UNMARKED, MARKED, or AUTONOMOUS
    value: i64,

    /// Nested sub-forms (Spencer-Brown allows nesting)
    children: [i64; 8],
    child_count: i64,

    /// Nesting depth (number of marks crossed to reach this form)
    depth: i64,

    /// True if this form contains itself (re-entry)
    is_reentrant: bool,

    /// Period of oscillation in imaginary time (Spencer-Brown Ch. 11)
    /// 0 = convergent, 2 = standard crossing oscillation, higher = slower period
    period: i64,
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

/// The void — unmarked, empty, no distinction drawn
pub fn form_void() -> Form {
    Form {
        value: UNMARKED,
        children: [0; 8],
        child_count: 0,
        depth: 0,
        is_reentrant: false,
        period: 0,
    }
}

/// A mark — the simplest distinction, the MARKED state
pub fn form_marked() -> Form {
    Form {
        value: MARKED,
        children: [0; 8],
        child_count: 0,
        depth: 1,
        is_reentrant: false,
        period: 0,
    }
}

/// The self-indicating form J where J = cross(J)
/// Varela's autonomous value — the third truth value
pub fn form_reenter() -> Form {
    Form {
        value: AUTONOMOUS,
        children: [0; 8],
        child_count: 0,
        depth: 0,
        is_reentrant: true,
        period: 2,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// AXIOMS
// ============================================================================

/// Axiom 1 — Calling (condensation): ⌐⌐ = ⌐
///
/// "The value of a call made again is the value of the call."
/// Marking something that is already marked does not change it.
/// This is the idempotent law of distinction.
pub fn form_mark(f: Form) -> Form with Mut {
    // If already marked, calling is idempotent
    if f.value == MARKED {
        return f
    }
    // If autonomous, marking preserves autonomy (re-entry absorbs marks)
    if f.value == AUTONOMOUS {
        return f
    }
    // Mark the unmarked
    Form {
        value: MARKED,
        children: f.children,
        child_count: f.child_count,
        depth: f.depth + 1,
        is_reentrant: f.is_reentrant,
        period: f.period,
    }
}

/// Axiom 2 — Crossing (cancellation): ⌐⌐ = (void)
///
/// "The value of a crossing made again is not the value of the crossing."
/// Crossing into a distinction and crossing back out returns to void.
/// Two nested marks cancel.
pub fn form_cross(f: Form) -> Form with Mut {
    // Crossing the autonomous form returns autonomous (J = ⌐J)
    if f.is_reentrant {
        return f
    }
    // Cross: toggle marked ↔ unmarked
    if f.value == MARKED {
        Form {
            value: UNMARKED,
            children: f.children,
            child_count: f.child_count,
            depth: max_i64(f.depth - 1, 0),
            is_reentrant: false,
            period: f.period,
        }
    } else if f.value == UNMARKED {
        Form {
            value: MARKED,
            children: f.children,
            child_count: f.child_count,
            depth: f.depth + 1,
            is_reentrant: false,
            period: f.period,
        }
    } else {
        // AUTONOMOUS: crossing returns autonomous
        f
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// EVALUATION
// ============================================================================

/// Evaluate a form to its canonical value.
///
/// Applies the two axioms recursively:
/// - No children, no mark → UNMARKED
/// - Mark with no children → MARKED
/// - Odd nesting depth → MARKED, even → UNMARKED
/// - Re-entrant → AUTONOMOUS
pub fn eval_form(f: Form) -> i64 {
    // Re-entrant forms are always autonomous
    if f.is_reentrant {
        return AUTONOMOUS
    }
    // Base case: use depth parity
    // Even number of crossings = UNMARKED, odd = MARKED
    if f.depth % 2 == 0 {
        UNMARKED
    } else {
        MARKED
    }
}

/// Check if two forms are equivalent under the calculus
pub fn forms_equal(a: Form, b: Form) -> bool {
    eval_form(a) == eval_form(b)
}

// ============================================================================
// OPERATIONS ON FORMS
// ============================================================================

/// Juxtaposition (OR in Boolean interpretation)
///
/// Spencer-Brown: placing two forms side by side inside a mark.
/// In the arithmetic: a,b inside a mark = mark if either is marked.
pub fn form_juxtapose(a: Form, b: Form) -> i64 {
    let va = eval_form(a)
    let vb = eval_form(b)
    // AUTONOMOUS propagates
    if va == AUTONOMOUS { return AUTONOMOUS }
    if vb == AUTONOMOUS { return AUTONOMOUS }
    // Boolean OR: marked if either is marked
    if va == MARKED { return MARKED }
    if vb == MARKED { return MARKED }
    UNMARKED
}

/// Superposition — nesting one form inside another's mark
///
/// Spencer-Brown: the mark of a is applied to b.
/// In Boolean interpretation: NOT-a OR b (implication).
pub fn form_nest(outer: Form, inner: Form) -> i64 with Mut {
    let vo = eval_form(outer)
    let vi = eval_form(inner)
    // AUTONOMOUS propagates
    if vo == AUTONOMOUS { return AUTONOMOUS }
    if vi == AUTONOMOUS { return AUTONOMOUS }
    // Nesting: cross(outer) juxtaposed with inner
    // = NOT(outer) OR inner = outer IMPLIES inner
    let crossed_outer = if vo == MARKED { UNMARKED } else { MARKED }
    if crossed_outer == MARKED { return MARKED }
    if vi == MARKED { return MARKED }
    UNMARKED
}

// ============================================================================
// SELF-REFERENCE DETECTION
// ============================================================================

/// Attempt to solve f = cross(f) iteratively.
///
/// If the iteration oscillates (MARKED → UNMARKED → MARKED → ...),
/// the form is self-referential and the result is AUTONOMOUS.
/// This implements Varela's key insight: self-reference produces
/// a third value that is neither true nor false.
pub fn solve_reentry(initial: i64, max_iter: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div {
    var state = initial
    var prev = -1
    var oscillating = false
    var i = 0
    while i < max_iter {
        // Cross: toggle
        let next = if state == MARKED { UNMARKED } else { MARKED }
        // Check for fixed point
        if next == state {
            return state
        }
        // Check for oscillation (period-2 cycle)
        if next == prev {
            oscillating = true
            break
        }
        prev = state
        state = next
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Oscillation detected → self-referential → autonomous
    if oscillating {
        AUTONOMOUS
    } else {
        state
    }
}

/// Solve f = cross(f) and compute the oscillation period.
///
/// Similar to solve_reentry, but returns a Form with the period field
/// populated. The period is the cycle length: standard crossing oscillation
/// (MARKED ↔ UNMARKED) has period 2.
///
/// This implements Spencer-Brown's imaginary-time analysis (Ch. 11):
/// the re-entering form oscillates with a well-defined period.
pub fn solve_reentry_timed(initial: i64, max_iter: i64) -> Form with Mut, Div {
    var state = initial
    var prev = -1
    var oscillating = false
    var oscillation_start: i64 = 0
    var i = 0

    while i < max_iter {
        // Cross: toggle
        let next = if state == MARKED { UNMARKED } else { MARKED }

        // Check for fixed point
        if next == state {
            // Converged: period = 0
            return Form {
                value: state,
                children: [0; 8],
                child_count: 0,
                depth: 0,
                is_reentrant: false,
                period: 0,
            }
        }

        // Check for oscillation (period-2 cycle)
        if next == prev {
            oscillating = true
            oscillation_start = i
            break
        }

        prev = state
        state = next
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Oscillation detected → compute period
    if oscillating {
        // Standard crossing oscillation: period = 2
        let period: i64 = 2
        Form {
            value: AUTONOMOUS,
            children: [0; 8],
            child_count: 0,
            depth: 0,
            is_reentrant: true,
            period: period,
        }
    } else {
        // No oscillation found within max_iter
        Form {
            value: state,
            children: [0; 8],
            child_count: 0,
            depth: 0,
            is_reentrant: false,
            period: 0,
        }
    }
}

/// Get the period of oscillation for a form (Spencer-Brown imaginary time).
pub fn form_period(f: Form) -> i64 {
    f.period
}

// ============================================================================
// FORM COMPOSITION — Building Nested Expressions
// ============================================================================

/// Add a child form's value to a parent form.
/// Spencer-Brown: nesting forms inside a mark creates compound expressions.
/// The children array stores EVALUATED VALUES of sub-forms.
pub fn form_add_child(f: Form, child: Form) -> Form with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = f
    if result.child_count < 8 {
        result.children[result.child_count as usize] = eval_form(child)
        result.child_count = result.child_count + 1
        // Recompute value based on children:
        // Spencer-Brown primary algebra: a form with children evaluates
        // by juxtaposing all children, then applying the mark
        result = recompute_from_children(result)
    }
    result
}

/// Build a compound form by nesting inner inside a mark.
/// Result = mark(inner) — the primary algebraic operation.
pub fn form_contain(inner: Form) -> Form with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = form_marked()
    result.children[0] = eval_form(inner)
    result.child_count = 1
    result = recompute_from_children(result)
    result
}

/// Build a compound form from two juxtaposed sub-forms.
/// Spencer-Brown: placing forms side by side.
pub fn form_pair(a: Form, b: Form) -> Form with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = form_void()
    result.children[0] = eval_form(a)
    result.children[1] = eval_form(b)
    result.child_count = 2
    result = recompute_from_children(result)
    result
}

/// Evaluate a form's children using Spencer-Brown's primary algebra.
/// Juxtaposition of children: if ANY child is MARKED, result is MARKED.
/// If ANY child is AUTONOMOUS, result is AUTONOMOUS.
/// If the form itself is marked (depth > 0), cross the result.
fn recompute_from_children(f: Form) -> Form with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = f
    if result.child_count == 0 {
        return result
    }

    // Juxtapose all children
    var has_marked = false
    var has_autonomous = false
    var i = 0
    while i < result.child_count {
        let cv = result.children[i as usize]
        if cv == AUTONOMOUS {
            has_autonomous = true
        } else if cv == MARKED {
            has_marked = true
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Spencer-Brown: AUTONOMOUS propagates, then MARKED, then UNMARKED
    if has_autonomous {
        result.value = AUTONOMOUS
        result.is_reentrant = true
    } else if has_marked {
        result.value = MARKED
    } else {
        result.value = UNMARKED
    }

    // If the form has depth > 0 (it's inside a mark), apply crossing
    // but only for non-autonomous values
    if result.depth > 0 && !result.is_reentrant {
        if result.value == MARKED {
            result.value = UNMARKED
        } else if result.value == UNMARKED {
            result.value = MARKED
        }
    }

    result
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn max_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

/// Human-readable name for a form value
pub fn value_name(v: i64) -> i64 {
    // Returns: 0 = "unmarked", 1 = "marked", 2 = "autonomous"
    // (In practice, caller uses match on the constant)
    v
}


// === FILE: stdlib/cybernetic/eigenform.sio ===
//! stdlib/cybernetic/eigenform.sio
//!
//! Eigenform Theory (von Foerster 1976, Kauffman 2003)
//!
//! An eigenform is a fixed point of an operator: if Op(x*) = x*, then x*
//! is an eigenform of Op. This is the mathematical definition of an object
//! as a stable pattern in observation.
//!
//! Key insight (Kauffman): eigenforms are isomorphic to Y combinators and
//! Scott reflexive domains in type theory. Every observer creates eigenforms
//! through recursive observation.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```sounio
//! use cybernetic::eigenform::{find_eigenform, is_eigenform, compute_eigenbehavior}
//!
