// Probabilists' weights — integrate under φ(x) = (2π)^{-1/2} e^{-x²/2}.
// Obtained from the physicists' 8-pt Gauss-Hermite weights by
// dividing by sqrt(π); the weights sum to 1 by construction.
pub fn bbb_pce_gh_wt_0() -> f64 { 0.00011261453491 }
pub fn bbb_pce_gh_wt_1() -> f64 { 0.00963968330    }
pub fn bbb_pce_gh_wt_2() -> f64 { 0.11723990768    }
pub fn bbb_pce_gh_wt_3() -> f64 { 0.37301080711    }
pub fn bbb_pce_gh_wt_4() -> f64 { 0.37301080711    }
pub fn bbb_pce_gh_wt_5() -> f64 { 0.11723990768    }
pub fn bbb_pce_gh_wt_6() -> f64 { 0.00963968330    }
pub fn bbb_pce_gh_wt_7() -> f64 { 0.00011261453491 }

pub fn bbb_pce_node_at(k: i32) -> f64 {
    if k == 0 { return bbb_pce_gh_node_0() }
    if k == 1 { return bbb_pce_gh_node_1() }
    if k == 2 { return bbb_pce_gh_node_2() }
    if k == 3 { return bbb_pce_gh_node_3() }
    if k == 4 { return bbb_pce_gh_node_4() }
    if k == 5 { return bbb_pce_gh_node_5() }
    if k == 6 { return bbb_pce_gh_node_6() }
    bbb_pce_gh_node_7()
}

pub fn bbb_pce_wt_at(k: i32) -> f64 {
    if k == 0 { return bbb_pce_gh_wt_0() }
    if k == 1 { return bbb_pce_gh_wt_1() }
    if k == 2 { return bbb_pce_gh_wt_2() }
    if k == 3 { return bbb_pce_gh_wt_3() }
    if k == 4 { return bbb_pce_gh_wt_4() }
    if k == 5 { return bbb_pce_gh_wt_5() }
    if k == 6 { return bbb_pce_gh_wt_6() }
    bbb_pce_gh_wt_7()
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Probabilists' Hermite polynomials (He_n)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// He_0(x) = 1
// He_1(x) = x
// He_n(x) = x He_{n-1}(x) - (n-1) He_{n-2}(x)
// Orthogonal under <He_m, He_n>_N = m! δ_mn.

fn bbb_he_poly(n: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 { return 1.0 }
    if n == 1 { return x }
    var h_prev = 1.0
    var h_curr = x
    var k = 2
    while k <= n {
        let h_next = x * h_curr - ((k - 1) as f64) * h_prev
        h_prev = h_curr
        h_curr = h_next
        k = k + 1
    }
    h_curr
}

// Integer factorial (safe for n <= 4).
fn bbb_factorial(n: i32) -> f64 {
    if n <= 1 { return 1.0 }
    if n == 2 { return 2.0 }
    if n == 3 { return 6.0 }
    if n == 4 { return 24.0 }
    120.0   // n=5
}

fn bbb_pce_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 18 { y = (y + x / y) * 0.5; i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// PCE result container (order 4 — 5 coefficients)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub struct BBBPCE1D {
    // Input distribution (normal)
    input_mean: f64,
    input_std:  f64,
    // PCE coefficients (He basis)
    c0: f64,   // = E[Y]
    c1: f64,   // linear sensitivity (compare to GUM ∂Y/∂p * sigma)
    c2: f64,
    c3: f64,
    c4: f64,
    // Derived statistics
    mean:         f64,
    variance:     f64,
    stddev:       f64,
    nonlinearity_share: f64, // (c2^2 * 2! + c3^2 * 3! + c4^2 * 4!) / variance
    // Solver evaluations (for audit)
    n_nodes:      i32,
    node_x:       [f64; 8],    // physical-scale p_k
    node_y:       [f64; 8],    // Y_k = Kpuu_AUC at node k
}

fn bbb_pce_zero() -> BBBPCE1D {
    BBBPCE1D {
        input_mean: 0.0, input_std: 0.0,
        c0: 0.0, c1: 0.0, c2: 0.0, c3: 0.0, c4: 0.0,
        mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, stddev: 0.0, nonlinearity_share: 0.0,
        n_nodes: 0, node_x: [0.0; 8], node_y: [0.0; 8],
    }
}

// Build a 1-D PCE on kpuu_brain for the Kpuu_AUC endpoint.
//
//   input_mean, input_std:  prior mean and standard deviation of
//                            kpuu_brain (N(mean, std)).
//   floor:                   tiny lower bound to keep kpuu_brain
//                            positive if a node pulls below zero.
pub fn bbb_pce_build_kpuu_auc(
    sys_prm:     PBPKParams14,
    base_bbb:    BBBParams,
    input_mean:  f64,
    input_std:   f64,
    floor:       f64,
    dose_mg:     f64,
    checkpoints: [f64; 32],
    n_points:    i32,
    bbb_dt:      f64
) -> BBBPCE1D with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pce = bbb_pce_zero()
    pce.input_mean = input_mean
    pce.input_std  = input_std
    pce.n_nodes = 8

    // --- Solver evaluations at each Gauss-Hermite node ---
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < 8 {
        let kdx = k as usize
        let xi = bbb_pce_node_at(k)
        var p_k = input_mean + input_std * xi
        if p_k < floor { p_k = floor }

        var bbb = base_bbb
        bbb.kpuu_brain = p_k

        let trace = bbb_coupled_run(sys_prm, bbb, dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points, bbb_dt)
        let y_k = trace.kpuu_auc

        pce.node_x[kdx] = p_k
        pce.node_y[kdx] = y_k
        k = k + 1
    }

    // --- Coefficients c_n = sum_k w_k * Y_k * He_n(xi_k) / n! ---
    var sum0: f64 = 0.0
    var sum1: f64 = 0.0
    var sum2: f64 = 0.0
    var sum3: f64 = 0.0
    var sum4: f64 = 0.0
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < 8 {
        let jdx = j as usize
        let xi = bbb_pce_node_at(j)
        let w  = bbb_pce_wt_at(j)
        let y  = pce.node_y[jdx]
        sum0 = sum0 + w * y * bbb_he_poly(0, xi)
        sum1 = sum1 + w * y * bbb_he_poly(1, xi)
        sum2 = sum2 + w * y * bbb_he_poly(2, xi)
        sum3 = sum3 + w * y * bbb_he_poly(3, xi)
        sum4 = sum4 + w * y * bbb_he_poly(4, xi)
        j = j + 1
    }
    pce.c0 = sum0                       // /0! = 1
    pce.c1 = sum1                       // /1! = 1
    pce.c2 = sum2 / bbb_factorial(2)
    pce.c3 = sum3 / bbb_factorial(3)
    pce.c4 = sum4 / bbb_factorial(4)

    // --- Derived statistics ---
    let var1 = pce.c1 * pce.c1 * bbb_factorial(1)
    let var2 = pce.c2 * pce.c2 * bbb_factorial(2)
    let var3 = pce.c3 * pce.c3 * bbb_factorial(3)
    let var4 = pce.c4 * pce.c4 * bbb_factorial(4)
    let total = var1 + var2 + var3 + var4
    pce.mean     = pce.c0
    pce.variance = total
    pce.stddev   = bbb_pce_sqrt(total)
    pce.nonlinearity_share = if total > 0.0 { (var2 + var3 + var4) / total } else { 0.0 }

    pce
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Diagnostic print
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn bbb_pce_print(pce: BBBPCE1D) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("BBB PCE (1-D, order 4, He basis, 8-node Gauss-Hermite)")
    print("  input_mean          = "); print_f64(pce.input_mean); println("")
    print("  input_std           = "); print_f64(pce.input_std);  println("")
    println("  coefficients:")
    print("    c0  (mean)        = "); print_f64(pce.c0); println("")
    print("    c1  (linear)      = "); print_f64(pce.c1); println("")
    print("    c2  (quadratic)   = "); print_f64(pce.c2); println("")
    print("    c3  (cubic)       = "); print_f64(pce.c3); println("")
    print("    c4  (quartic)     = "); print_f64(pce.c4); println("")
    println("  statistics:")
    print("    E[Y]              = "); print_f64(pce.mean);     println("")
    print("    u_c (stddev)      = "); print_f64(pce.stddev);   println("")
    print("    nonlinearity share= "); print_f64(pce.nonlinearity_share); println("")
    println("  nodes (p_k, Y_k):")
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < 8 {
        let kdx = k as usize
        print("    p="); print_f64(pce.node_x[kdx])
        print("  Y="); print_f64(pce.node_y[kdx])
        println("")
        k = k + 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/bbb/bbb_pce2d.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/bbb/bbb_pce2d.sio — 2-D PCE + Sobol indices
//
// Tensor-product Gauss-Hermite PCE over the two transporter inputs
// (kpuu_brain, ps_bbb) — together 78.5% of the combined variance per
// the first-order GUM budget.  Order-2 bivariate He basis:
//
//   Ψ_00 = 1
//   Ψ_10 = He_1(ξ₁)         — kpuu_brain linear
//   Ψ_01 = He_1(ξ₂)         — ps_bbb linear
//   Ψ_20 = He_2(ξ₁)         — kpuu_brain quadratic
//   Ψ_11 = He_1(ξ₁) He_1(ξ₂) — interaction
//   Ψ_02 = He_2(ξ₂)         — ps_bbb quadratic
//
// Under probabilists' normalisation ⟨Ψ_αβ, Ψ_αβ⟩_N = α! β!, so the
// variance decomposition is
//
//   Var(Y)  = Σ_{α+β ≥ 1} c_αβ²  α!  β!
//
// and the Sobol indices follow directly:
//
//   V_1    = c_10² · 1 + c_20² · 2            (kpuu_brain alone)
//   V_2    = c_01² · 1 + c_02² · 2            (ps_bbb alone)
//   V_12   = c_11² · 1 · 1                    (pairwise interaction)
//
//   S_1  = V_1 / V_total,  S_2  = V_2 / V_total,  S_12 = V_12 / V_total
//   S_T1 = S_1 + S_12       (total-effect of kpuu_brain)
//   S_T2 = S_2 + S_12       (total-effect of ps_bbb)
//
// Cost: 8×8 = 64 coupled-solver evaluations.

use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_core::{BBBParams}
use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_coupled::{bbb_coupled_run}
use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_pce::*
use darwin_pbpk::tsit5_pbpk14::{PBPKParams14}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Bivariate He basis
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn pce2_he(n: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 { return 1.0 }
    if n == 1 { return x }
    if n == 2 { return x * x - 1.0 }
    // Higher orders only needed if we extend beyond total order 2.
    var h_prev = 1.0
    var h_curr = x
    var k = 2
    while k <= n {
        let h_next = x * h_curr - ((k - 1) as f64) * h_prev
        h_prev = h_curr
        h_curr = h_next
        k = k + 1
    }
    h_curr
}

fn pce2_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 18 { y = (y + x / y) * 0.5; i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2-D PCE result container
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub struct BBBPCE2D {
    // Input distributions (normal)
    mu1: f64,
    sd1: f64,
    mu2: f64,
    sd2: f64,
    // Six PCE coefficients on the order-2 bivariate He basis.
    c00: f64,
    c10: f64,    // kpuu_brain linear
    c01: f64,    // ps_bbb     linear
    c20: f64,    // kpuu_brain quadratic
    c11: f64,    // interaction
    c02: f64,    // ps_bbb     quadratic

    // Derived statistics.
    mean:     f64,
    variance: f64,
    stddev:   f64,

    // Sobol indices.
    v1:       f64,
    v2:       f64,
    v12:      f64,
    s1:       f64,      // first-order, kpuu_brain
    s2:       f64,      // first-order, ps_bbb
    s12:      f64,      // interaction share
    s_t1:     f64,      // total-effect, kpuu_brain = s1 + s12
    s_t2:     f64,      // total-effect, ps_bbb     = s2 + s12

    // Share captured by the linear (first-order He) terms alone —
    // complement to the higher-order + interaction terms.
    linear_share: f64,
}

fn bbb_pce2d_zero() -> BBBPCE2D {
    BBBPCE2D {
        mu1: 0.0, sd1: 0.0, mu2: 0.0, sd2: 0.0,
        c00: 0.0, c10: 0.0, c01: 0.0,
        c20: 0.0, c11: 0.0, c02: 0.0,
        mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, stddev: 0.0,
        v1: 0.0, v2: 0.0, v12: 0.0,
        s1: 0.0, s2: 0.0, s12: 0.0, s_t1: 0.0, s_t2: 0.0,
        linear_share: 0.0,
    }
}

// Build a 2-D PCE on (kpuu_brain, ps_bbb) for the Kpuu_AUC endpoint.
// floor1, floor2 prevent negative parameter draws from the outer
// Gauss-Hermite nodes.
pub fn bbb_pce2d_build_kpuu_auc(
    sys_prm:     PBPKParams14,
    base_bbb:    BBBParams,
    mu1: f64, sd1: f64, floor1: f64,
    mu2: f64, sd2: f64, floor2: f64,
    dose_mg:     f64,
    checkpoints: [f64; 32],
    n_points:    i32,
    bbb_dt:      f64
) -> BBBPCE2D with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pce = bbb_pce2d_zero()
    pce.mu1 = mu1; pce.sd1 = sd1
    pce.mu2 = mu2; pce.sd2 = sd2

    // Accumulate quadrature sums for each coefficient.
    var s_00 = 0.0
    var s_10 = 0.0
    var s_01 = 0.0
    var s_20 = 0.0
    var s_11 = 0.0
    var s_02 = 0.0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let xi1 = bbb_pce_node_at(i)
        let w1  = bbb_pce_wt_at(i)
        var p1 = mu1 + sd1 * xi1
        if p1 < floor1 { p1 = floor1 }

        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < 8 {
            let xi2 = bbb_pce_node_at(j)
            let w2  = bbb_pce_wt_at(j)
            var p2 = mu2 + sd2 * xi2
            if p2 < floor2 { p2 = floor2 }

            var bbb = base_bbb
            bbb.kpuu_brain = p1
            bbb.ps_bbb     = p2
            let trace = bbb_coupled_run(sys_prm, bbb, dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points, bbb_dt)
            let y = trace.kpuu_auc
            let w = w1 * w2

            s_00 = s_00 + w * y
            s_10 = s_10 + w * y * pce2_he(1, xi1)
            s_01 = s_01 + w * y * pce2_he(1, xi2)
            s_20 = s_20 + w * y * pce2_he(2, xi1)
            s_11 = s_11 + w * y * pce2_he(1, xi1) * pce2_he(1, xi2)
            s_02 = s_02 + w * y * pce2_he(2, xi2)

            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // c_αβ = s_αβ / (α! β!)  — under probabilists' norm ⟨Ψ_αβ, Ψ_αβ⟩ = α! β!.
    pce.c00 = s_00
    pce.c10 = s_10
    pce.c01 = s_01
    pce.c20 = s_20 / 2.0
    pce.c11 = s_11
    pce.c02 = s_02 / 2.0

    // --- Variance decomposition ---
    let v_10 = pce.c10 * pce.c10 * 1.0        // He_1⊗He_0: 1! · 0! = 1
    let v_20 = pce.c20 * pce.c20 * 2.0        // He_2⊗He_0: 2! · 0! = 2
    let v_01 = pce.c01 * pce.c01 * 1.0
    let v_02 = pce.c02 * pce.c02 * 2.0
    let v_11 = pce.c11 * pce.c11 * 1.0        // 1!·1! = 1
    let v_1  = v_10 + v_20
    let v_2  = v_01 + v_02
    let v_12 = v_11
    let total = v_1 + v_2 + v_12

    pce.mean     = pce.c00
    pce.variance = total
    pce.stddev   = pce2_sqrt(total)
    pce.v1  = v_1
    pce.v2  = v_2
    pce.v12 = v_12
    if total > 0.0 {
        pce.s1   = v_1 / total
        pce.s2   = v_2 / total
        pce.s12  = v_12 / total
        pce.s_t1 = pce.s1 + pce.s12
        pce.s_t2 = pce.s2 + pce.s12
        pce.linear_share = (v_10 + v_01) / total
    }

    pce
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Diagnostic print (human-readable)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn bbb_pce2d_print(pce: BBBPCE2D) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("BBB PCE (2-D, order 2, tensor He basis, 8×8 Gauss-Hermite)")
    print("  input 1 (kpuu_brain):  mu="); print_f64(pce.mu1)
    print("  sd="); print_f64(pce.sd1); println("")
    print("  input 2 (ps_bbb):      mu="); print_f64(pce.mu2)
    print("  sd="); print_f64(pce.sd2); println("")
    println("  coefficients:")
    print("    c00 (mean)         = "); print_f64(pce.c00); println("")
    print("    c10 (linear k_br)  = "); print_f64(pce.c10); println("")
    print("    c01 (linear ps_bbb)= "); print_f64(pce.c01); println("")
    print("    c20 (quadratic k)  = "); print_f64(pce.c20); println("")
    print("    c11 (interaction)  = "); print_f64(pce.c11); println("")
    print("    c02 (quadratic p)  = "); print_f64(pce.c02); println("")
    println("  statistics:")
    print("    E[Y]               = "); print_f64(pce.mean);      println("")
    print("    u_c (stddev)       = "); print_f64(pce.stddev);    println("")
    print("    linear-share       = "); print_f64(pce.linear_share); println("")
    println("  Sobol (variance-based):")
    print("    V_1  (kpuu_brain)  = "); print_f64(pce.v1);        println("")
    print("    V_2  (ps_bbb)      = "); print_f64(pce.v2);        println("")
    print("    V_12 (interaction) = "); print_f64(pce.v12);       println("")
    print("    S_1                = "); print_f64(pce.s1);        println("")
    print("    S_2                = "); print_f64(pce.s2);        println("")
    print("    S_12 (interaction) = "); print_f64(pce.s12);       println("")
    print("    S_T1 (total k_br)  = "); print_f64(pce.s_t1);      println("")
    print("    S_T2 (total ps)    = "); print_f64(pce.s_t2);      println("")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/bbb/bbb_priors.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/bbb/bbb_priors.sio — BBB parameter uncertainty priors
//
// Per-parameter uncertainty distributions for rapamycin BBB input
// parameters.  These priors feed directly into the GUM-through-ODE
// sensitivity harness (bbb_gum.sio).
//
// Each prior carries three numbers:
//   mean       — the literature-consensus central value
//   variance   — squared standard deviation, in the natural scale
//                of the parameter (NOT log-transformed; matches the
//                JCGM 100:2008 first-order propagation formula)
//   confidence — an [0, 1] epistemic quality score (NOT a Beta
//                posterior); high confidence means the literature
//                directly measures this parameter with converging
//                methods, low confidence means cross-species
//                extrapolation or a single primary source.
//
// The priors are ordered to match the indexing used by
// bbb_perturb_param(prm, idx, delta) in bbb_gum.sio:
//
//   0: ps_bbb       — BBB permeability-surface area
//   1: ps_mem       — cellular membrane permeability-surface area
//   2: kpuu_brain   — BBB steady-state unbound partition
//   3: kpuu_cell    — cellular steady-state unbound partition
//   4: fu_plasma    — plasma unbound fraction
//   5: fu_isf       — brain ISF unbound fraction
//   6: fu_icf       — brain ICF unbound fraction
//
// The first four are the TRANSPORTER / MEMBRANE parameters — these
// are what distinguish the dissertation-grade BBB model from the
// coarse Kp approach.  The last three are the PROTEIN BINDING
// parameters, which the dissertation cites as "measurement-dominated"
// (high-confidence wet-lab determinations).
//
// Expected GUM decomposition for rapamycin: ps_bbb and kpuu_brain
// dominate the Kpuu_AUC variance (transporter variability >>
// binding variability for this drug).

pub struct BBBPriors {
    n:          i32,
    mean:       [f64; 8],
    variance:   [f64; 8],
    confidence: [f64; 8],
}

pub fn bbb_rapamycin_priors() -> BBBPriors with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var v: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var c: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]

    // 0: ps_bbb — effective BBB permeability-surface area (L/h)
    // Central value 0.30 L/h captures the observed ~10-15 h brain
    // Cmax lag time for rapamycin.  Inter-species extrapolation and
    // inter-subject P-gp expression variability together give a
    // published CV of ~40% (Gaohua 2016; Shah & Betts 2012).
    // variance = (0.30 * 0.40)^2 = 0.0144
    // confidence = 0.45 (extrapolation-dominated)
    m[0] = 0.30;       v[0] = 0.0144;    c[0] = 0.45

    // 1: ps_mem — cellular membrane PS (L/h)
    // No direct rapamycin microdialysis data; we take 10 L/h from a
    // class-analogous macrolide.  CV estimated at 60% (generous).
    // variance = (10.0 * 0.60)^2 = 36.0
    // confidence = 0.25 (structural analogue only)
    m[1] = 10.0;       v[1] = 36.0;      c[1] = 0.25

    // 2: kpuu_brain — BBB steady-state unbound partition (-)
    // Mean 0.15 bracketed by Lampen 1998 rodent Kpuu post P-gp
    // correction and Laplanche 1994 human AUC ratios.
    // Literature spread 0.10-0.25 → SD ≈ 0.04, variance ≈ 0.0016
    // confidence = 0.60 (two primary sources, consistent)
    m[2] = 0.15;       v[2] = 0.0016;    c[2] = 0.60

    // 3: kpuu_cell — cellular steady-state unbound partition (-)
    // Typical neutral lipophilic drug; mean 2.0, broad prior.
    // variance = (2.0 * 0.50)^2 = 1.0
    // confidence = 0.30 (class estimate)
    m[3] = 2.0;        v[3] = 1.0;       c[3] = 0.30

    // 4: fu_plasma — plasma unbound fraction (-)
    // Schreiber 1991 in vitro equilibrium dialysis, well replicated.
    // CV ≈ 15%, variance = (0.08 * 0.15)^2 = 1.44e-4
    // confidence = 0.90 (well-characterized wet lab)
    m[4] = 0.08;       v[4] = 0.000144;  c[4] = 0.90

    // 5: fu_isf — brain ISF unbound fraction (-)
    // Class-typical value 0.02; CV 40% (microdialysis not directly
    // measured for rapamycin).
    // variance = (0.02 * 0.40)^2 = 6.4e-5
    // confidence = 0.35
    m[5] = 0.02;       v[5] = 0.000064;  c[5] = 0.35

    // 6: fu_icf — brain ICF unbound fraction (-)
    // Assumed equal to fu_isf absent direct data.  CV 40%.
    // variance = 6.4e-5
    // confidence = 0.25 (assumption, not measurement)
    m[6] = 0.02;       v[6] = 0.000064;  c[6] = 0.25

    BBBPriors { n: 7, mean: m, variance: v, confidence: c }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/bbb/bbb_rapamycin.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/bbb/bbb_rapamycin.sio — Rapamycin (sirolimus) BBB parameters
//
// All parameters are sourced from the open pharmacokinetic literature.
// Each value is documented with the primary source, the measurement
// method, and an uncertainty assessment (for downstream GUM-through-ODE
// propagation).
//
// Drug identity:
//   Rapamycin / sirolimus (MW 914.17 Da, LogP ≈ 6.0, macrolide, neutral)
//   P-glycoprotein (MDR1/ABCB1) substrate — confirmed in knockout mice
//   by Lampen et al. 1998.  Efflux at the BBB is the dominant driver
//   of its low CNS exposure.
//
// References (short form — full citations in docs/research/bbb_refs.md
// once the literature review is written up):
//   [1] Lampen A. et al. (1998) Pharm. Res. 15:1234 — brain:plasma
//       ratios in MDR1a/b(-/-) vs WT mice; Kpuu shift ~6x.
//   [2] Fridén M. et al. (2007) Drug Metab. Dispos. 35:1711 — Kpuu
//       framework for CNS drug distribution; brain microdialysis.
//   [3] Schreiber S.L. et al. (1991) J. Am. Chem. Soc. 113:7433 —
//       rapamycin plasma protein binding, fu = 0.08.
//   [4] Davies B. & Morris T. (1993) Pharm. Res. 10:1093 —
//       physiological blood flows and volumes (70 kg human).
//   [5] Guyton A.C. & Hall J.E., Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th
//       ed. (2020) — brain compartment volume fractions.
//   [6] Gaohua L. et al. (2016) Drug Metab. Pharmacokinet. 31:224 —
//       brain PBPK architecture / feed-forward coupling validation.
//   [7] Laplanche R. et al. (1994) Transplant. Proc. 26:3200 —
//       rapamycin brain:plasma AUC ratios in humans.

use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_core::{BBBParams}

pub fn bbb_rapamycin_params() -> BBBParams {
    BBBParams {
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // Compartment volumes (70 kg human, 1.4 kg brain)
        // [4] Davies & Morris 1993, [5] Guyton & Hall
        // Brain mass 1.4 kg → brain volume ~1.37 L (density ≈ 1.03 g/mL).
        // Vascular fraction ~3%, ISF fraction ~20%, ICF fraction ~75%.
        // Remaining ~2% is CSF in ventricles (not modelled separately).
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        v_vasc: 0.041,    // L   (~3% of 1.37 L)
        v_isf:  0.274,    // L   (~20%)
        v_icf:  1.028,    // L   (~75%)

        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // Cerebral blood flow [4] Davies & Morris 1993
        // Standard human value, physiological.
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        q_brain: 44.0,    // L/h

        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // Effective BBB permeability-surface area (L/h).
        //
        // For P-gp substrates, PS_bbb is a NET value encoding
        // (passive diffusion - active efflux).  Published rapamycin
        // brain:plasma AUC ratios in humans are 0.10-0.30 [7] and
        // Kpuu values in rodents after P-gp correction are 0.10-0.25
        // [1, 2].  We take PS_bbb = 0.30 L/h as a middle value that
        // reproduces the observed ~10-15h brain Cmax lag time post-IV
        // (clinical observation, cited in [7]).
        //
        // Uncertainty: 30% CV (driven by inter-species extrapolation
        // and inter-subject P-gp expression variability).
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        ps_bbb: 0.30,

        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // Effective cellular membrane PS (L/h).
        //
        // For lipophilic macrolides the cell membrane exchange is
        // fast (minutes-scale).  We take PS_mem = 10.0 L/h as an
        // effective value — the ICF sub-compartment equilibrates
        // with ISF within the first hour post-dosing.
        //
        // Uncertainty: 50% CV (no direct microdialysis data for
        // rapamycin ISF vs ICF).
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        ps_mem: 10.0,

        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // Unbound fractions (dimensionless)
        // [3] Schreiber 1991 for fu_plasma = 0.08 (in vitro dialysis).
        // Brain tissue binding is not well characterised for
        // rapamycin; we use fu_isf = fu_icf = 0.02 as a literature-
        // typical value for a lipophilic macrolide (LogP 6), matched
        // to the rapamycin-specific estimate in Liu et al. 2020.
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        fu_plasma: 0.08,
        fu_isf:    0.02,
        fu_icf:    0.02,

        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // Steady-state unbound partition ratios (Fridén 2007 framework)
        //
        // Kpuu_brain = 0.15: rapamycin is a confirmed P-gp substrate
        // [1]; net BBB transport is efflux-dominated.  This is the
        // PK endpoint that dictates CNS target engagement.
        //
        // Kpuu_cell = 2.0: moderate ICF accumulation, typical for
        // neutral lipophilic drugs binding to FKBP12 intracellularly.
        //
        // These are the key dissertation-grade numbers — every step
        // below is calibrated to reproduce them at t → infinity.
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        kpuu_brain: 0.15,
        kpuu_cell:  2.0,
    }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Steady-state analytical solutions (for validation and sanity checks)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// At t -> infinity under constant plasma concentration C_p, the
// unbound concentrations equilibrate as
//
//   C_vasc,u   =  C_plasma,u                 (perfusion-limited, Q >> PS)
//   C_isf,u    =  Kpuu_brain * C_plasma,u
//   C_icf,u    =  Kpuu_cell * C_isf,u  =  Kpuu_brain * Kpuu_cell * C_plasma,u
//
// These are the analytical targets that the RK4 integrator must
// reproduce in the Kpuu steady-state test.

pub fn bbb_rapamycin_ss_c_isf_u(c_plasma: f64) -> f64 {
    let prm = bbb_rapamycin_params()
    prm.kpuu_brain * prm.fu_plasma * c_plasma
}

pub fn bbb_rapamycin_ss_c_icf_u(c_plasma: f64) -> f64 {
    let prm = bbb_rapamycin_params()
    prm.kpuu_brain * prm.kpuu_cell * prm.fu_plasma * c_plasma
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/bbb/bbb_voi.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/bbb/bbb_voi.sio — Value-of-Information (VoI) ranking
//
// Dissertation contribution #5 — mechanises the experimental-design
// recommendation that falls out of combining the 7-D HDMR Sobol
// indices with the per-parameter confidence tags.
//
// Core question: "If I could run exactly one measurement to shrink
// the Kpuu_AUC uncertainty, which parameter would I target?"
//
// Definition:
//
//     VoI_i = S_i · (1 − confidence_i)
//
// where S_i is the first-order Sobol index from bbb_hdmr.sio (how
// much the i-th parameter contributes to the combined variance) and
// confidence_i ∈ [0, 1] is the prior evidence-quality tag from
// bbb_priors.sio.  VoI is dimensionless and scales with:
//   - variance share (high-share parameters are worth reducing)
//   - evidence gap      (low-confidence parameters give room to
//                        update).
//
// A parameter with high Sobol but high confidence (well-measured
// already) ranks LOW — further measurements would have diminishing
// returns.  A parameter with low Sobol ranks LOW regardless of
// confidence — its uncertainty does not propagate to the endpoint.
// Only the intersection (high share × weak prior) warrants
// experimental investment.
//
// This is the "expected-value-of-sample-information" (EVSI) framework
// from decision-theoretic PK (Claxton 1999; Kennedy 2000), specialised
// to first-order Sobol weighting.  Existing PK tools (Simcyp, NONMEM,
// PK-Sim) report neither Sobol nor confidence, so they cannot emit
// this ranking; Sounio's epistemic-type stack is purpose-built for it.

use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_hdmr::{BBBHDMRResult}
use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_priors::{BBBPriors}

pub struct BBBVoI {
    n_rows:        i32,
    param_idx:     [i32; 8],
    sobol:         [f64; 8],
    confidence:    [f64; 8],
    voi:           [f64; 8],
    rank:          [i32; 8],     // rank[k] = index in param_idx with k-th highest VoI
    top_idx:       i32,          // param_idx of the #1 recommendation
    top_voi:       f64,
    voi_total:     f64,
}

fn bbb_voi_zero() -> BBBVoI {
    BBBVoI {
        n_rows: 0,
        param_idx: [0; 8], sobol: [0.0; 8], confidence: [0.0; 8],
        voi: [0.0; 8], rank: [0; 8],
        top_idx: 0 - 1, top_voi: 0.0, voi_total: 0.0,
    }
}

// Compute VoI from an HDMR budget + the same priors that fed it.
pub fn bbb_voi_from_hdmr(
    hdmr:   BBBHDMRResult,
    priors: BBBPriors
) -> BBBVoI with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out = bbb_voi_zero()
    out.n_rows = hdmr.n_dims

    var total: f64 = 0.0
    var best_idx: i32 = 0 - 1
    var best_voi: f64 = 0.0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < hdmr.n_dims {
        let idx = i as usize
        let s = hdmr.sobol[idx]
        let c = priors.confidence[idx]
        let v = s * (1.0 - c)
        out.param_idx[idx]  = i
        out.sobol[idx]      = s
        out.confidence[idx] = c
        out.voi[idx]        = v
        total = total + v
        if v > best_voi { best_voi = v; best_idx = i }
        i = i + 1
    }

    out.voi_total = total
    out.top_idx   = best_idx
    out.top_voi   = best_voi

    // Rank by VoI descending (simple selection sort, n <= 7).
    var used: [bool; 8] = [false; 8]
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < hdmr.n_dims {
        var best_j: i32 = 0 - 1
        var best_v: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < hdmr.n_dims {
            let jdx = j as usize
            if used[jdx] == false && out.voi[jdx] >= best_v {
                best_v = out.voi[jdx]
                best_j = j
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if best_j >= 0 {
            out.rank[k as usize] = best_j
            used[best_j as usize] = true
        }
        k = k + 1
    }

    out
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Dissertation-ready report
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn bbb_voi_param_name(idx: i32) -> string {
    if idx == 0 { return "ps_bbb" }
    if idx == 1 { return "ps_mem" }
    if idx == 2 { return "kpuu_brain" }
    if idx == 3 { return "kpuu_cell" }
    if idx == 4 { return "fu_plasma" }
    if idx == 5 { return "fu_isf" }
    if idx == 6 { return "fu_icf" }
    "unknown"
}

pub fn bbb_voi_print(v: BBBVoI) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("BBB Value-of-Information ranking")
    println("  VoI_i = S_i × (1 − confidence_i)")
    print("  VoI_total  = "); print_f64(v.voi_total);  println("")
    if v.top_idx >= 0 {
        print("  top target = "); print(bbb_voi_param_name(v.top_idx))
        print(" (VoI = "); print_f64(v.top_voi); println(")")
    }
    println("")
    println("rank,param,sobol_S1,confidence,VoI")
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < v.n_rows {
        let kdx = k as usize
        let p = v.rank[kdx]
        let pdx = p as usize
        let rank_k = (k + 1) as i64
        print_i64(rank_k); print(",")
        print(bbb_voi_param_name(v.param_idx[pdx])); print(",")
        print_f64(v.sobol[pdx]);      print(",")
        print_f64(v.confidence[pdx]); print(",")
        print_f64(v.voi[pdx])
        println("")
        k = k + 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/bbb/scenario_gate.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/bbb/scenario_gate.sio — Scenario-level VoI-weighted gate
//
// Dissertation contribution #4 extension: the per-parameter gate in
// bbb_gate.sio refuses the prediction if ANY dominant driver falls
// below the confidence threshold. Clinicians and reviewers, however,
// reason at the scenario level — "is this IV-bolus / Cypher-stent /
// oral-SS prediction defensible as a whole?".
//
// The scenario gate collapses the per-parameter confidence vector
// into a single scenario-level score, weighted by the parameter's
// Value of Information (S_i × (1 − conf_i) from bbb_voi.sio). A
// scenario is ADMITTED iff its VoI-weighted confidence clears a
// threshold. This is compatible with the existing per-parameter
// gate: run both, require both to pass for "strong admit".
//
// Why VoI weighting (not uniform averaging)?
//   Parameters that dominate endpoint variance AND have weak priors
//   deserve more weight in the scenario verdict — they are the ones
//   that can sink the prediction. A high-confidence but low-Sobol
//   parameter should barely move the scenario score. VoI is exactly
//   that joint weight.
//
// Formula:
//
//     w_i        = VoI_i = S_i × (1 − conf_i)
//     conf_bar   = (Σ w_i × conf_i) / (Σ w_i)
//
// Degenerate case: if all parameters have conf = 1.0, every w_i = 0,
// we fall back to the unweighted mean (which is 1.0). Treated as
// ADMITTED.

use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_voi::{BBBVoI}

pub enum ScenarioKind {
    IVBolus,
    CypherStent,
    OralSteadyState,
}

pub struct ScenarioGateVerdict {
    kind:                   ScenarioKind,
    admitted:               bool,
    voi_weighted_conf:      f64,
    fallback_mean_conf:     f64,
    used_fallback:          bool,
    refuse_threshold:       f64,
    weakest_driver_idx:     i32,
    weakest_driver_voi:     f64,
    weakest_driver_conf:    f64,
}

fn scenario_name(k: ScenarioKind) -> string {
    match k {
        ScenarioKind::IVBolus         => "IV-bolus",
        ScenarioKind::CypherStent     => "Cypher-DES",
        ScenarioKind::OralSteadyState => "oral-SS",
    }
}

fn scenario_gate_zero(k: ScenarioKind, thr: f64) -> ScenarioGateVerdict {
    ScenarioGateVerdict {
        kind: k,
        admitted: false,
        voi_weighted_conf: 0.0,
        fallback_mean_conf: 0.0,
        used_fallback: false,
        refuse_threshold: thr,
        weakest_driver_idx: 0 - 1,
        weakest_driver_voi: 0.0,
        weakest_driver_conf: 1.0,
    }
}

pub fn gate_scenario(
    kind: ScenarioKind,
    voi: BBBVoI,
    refuse_threshold: f64
) -> ScenarioGateVerdict with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var v = scenario_gate_zero(kind, refuse_threshold)

    var sum_w: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_wc: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_c: f64 = 0.0
    var worst_voi: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0
    var worst_idx: i32 = 0 - 1
    var worst_conf: f64 = 1.0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < voi.n_rows {
        let idx = i as usize
        let w = voi.voi[idx]
        let c = voi.confidence[idx]
        sum_w  = sum_w + w
        sum_wc = sum_wc + w * c
        sum_c  = sum_c + c
        if w > worst_voi {
            worst_voi = w
            worst_idx = voi.param_idx[idx]
            worst_conf = c
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let n = voi.n_rows as f64
    let fallback = if n > 0.0 { sum_c / n } else { 1.0 }
    v.fallback_mean_conf = fallback

    if sum_w > 1.0e-12 {
        v.voi_weighted_conf = sum_wc / sum_w
        v.used_fallback = false
    } else {
        v.voi_weighted_conf = fallback
        v.used_fallback = true
    }

    v.weakest_driver_idx  = worst_idx
    v.weakest_driver_voi  = worst_voi
    v.weakest_driver_conf = worst_conf
    v.admitted = v.voi_weighted_conf >= refuse_threshold
    v
}

pub fn scenario_gate_print(v: ScenarioGateVerdict) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("Scenario gate: "); println(scenario_name(v.kind))
    print("  refuse_threshold      = "); print_f64(v.refuse_threshold); println("")
    print("  VoI-weighted conf     = "); print_f64(v.voi_weighted_conf); println("")
    if v.used_fallback {
        print("  (fallback mean conf)  = "); print_f64(v.fallback_mean_conf); println("")
        println("  note: Σ VoI ≈ 0 → all priors strong, fell back to mean")
    }
    print("  weakest-VoI param idx = "); print_f64(v.weakest_driver_idx as f64); println("")
    print("    its VoI             = "); print_f64(v.weakest_driver_voi); println("")
    print("    its confidence      = "); print_f64(v.weakest_driver_conf); println("")
    if v.admitted {
        println("  scenario verdict: ADMITTED")
    } else {
        println("  scenario verdict: REFUSED")
        println("    reason: VoI-weighted confidence below threshold —")
        println("    highest-VoI parameter is the best next measurement target")
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/brain_plasma_tac.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/brain_plasma_tac.sio — Canonical brain/plasma TAC workflow
//
// This module defines a stable brain/plasma trajectory surface on top of the
// validated 14-compartment Darwin PBPK kernel. The initial target is a fixed
// rapamycin reference workflow suitable for export into measurement tables.

use tsit5_pbpk14::*
use epistemic_pbpk14::{EpPrior14, ep14_rapamycin_params, ep14_rapamycin_priors}

pub struct BrainPlasmaTacTable {
    times_h: [f64; 16],
    blood_values: [f64; 16],
    blood_uncertainties: [f64; 16],
    brain_values: [f64; 16],
    brain_uncertainties: [f64; 16],
    n_points: i32,
    success: bool,
}

fn tac_empty() -> BrainPlasmaTacTable {
    BrainPlasmaTacTable {
        times_h: [0.0; 16],
        blood_values: [0.0; 16],
        blood_uncertainties: [0.0; 16],
        brain_values: [0.0; 16],
        brain_uncertainties: [0.0; 16],
        n_points: 0,
        success: false,
    }
}

fn tac_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

fn tac_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn tac_fdiff_h(mean: f64, variance: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let h_rel = 1.0e-6 * tac_abs(mean)
    let h_abs = 0.01 * tac_sqrt(variance)
    if h_rel > h_abs { h_rel } else { h_abs }
}

fn tac_perturb(prm: PBPKParams14, idx: i32, delta: f64) -> PBPKParams14 with Mut {
    var p = prm
    if idx == 0 { p.cl_hepatic = p.cl_hepatic + delta }
    if idx == 1 { p.cl_renal = p.cl_renal + delta }
    if idx == 2 { p.fu_plasma = p.fu_plasma + delta }
    if idx == 3 { p.kp_brain = p.kp_brain + delta }
    if idx == 4 { p.kp_liver = p.kp_liver + delta }
    if idx == 5 { p.kp_kidney = p.kp_kidney + delta }
    if idx == 6 { p.kp_adipose = p.kp_adipose + delta }
    p
}

pub fn brain_plasma_reference_times() -> [f64; 8] {
    [0.0, 0.25, 1.0, 4.0, 8.0, 24.0, 72.0, 168.0]
}

fn simulate_checkpoints(
    prm: PBPKParams14,
    dose_mg: f64,
    checkpoints: [f64; 16],
    n_points: i32
) -> BrainPlasmaTacTable with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Tail-phase TAC (checkpoints extend to 168h) requires tight
    // tolerances so the error norm stays sensitive to trace
    // rapamycin concentrations; default_ode_config's atol=1e-4
    // produces spurious non-monotone decay at t > ~24h.
    let cfg = tight_ode_config()
    var out = tac_empty()
    out.n_points = n_points

    let c0 = dose_mg / prm.v_blood
    var st = pbpk_state_zero()
    st.blood = c0

    var t = 0.0
    var dt = cfg.dt_init
    var nsteps: i64 = 0
    var nreject: i64 = 0
    var point_i: i32 = 0

    while point_i < n_points {
        let idx = point_i as usize
        let target = checkpoints[idx]

        while t < target && nsteps < cfg.max_steps {
            let dt_use = if t + dt > target { target - t } else { dt }
            let result = tsit5_step_pbpk(st, t, dt_use, prm)
            let err_norm = compute_error_norm_14(result.err, st, result.state_new, cfg.rtol, cfg.atol)

            if err_norm <= 1.0 {
                st = result.state_new
                t = t + dt_use
                nsteps = nsteps + 1
                dt = optimal_step_14(dt_use, err_norm, cfg.safety, cfg.max_growth, cfg.min_shrink)
            } else {
                nreject = nreject + 1
                dt = optimal_step_14(dt_use, err_norm, cfg.safety, cfg.max_growth, cfg.min_shrink)
            }

            if dt < cfg.dt_min { dt = cfg.dt_min }
            if dt > cfg.dt_max { dt = cfg.dt_max }

            if nreject > 10000 {
                return out
            }
        }

        if t + cfg.dt_min < target {
            return out
        }

        out.times_h[idx] = target
        out.blood_values[idx] = st.blood
        out.brain_values[idx] = st.brain
        point_i = point_i + 1
    }

    out.success = true
    out
}

pub fn simulate_brain_plasma_tac(
    prm: PBPKParams14,
    priors: EpPrior14,
    dose_mg: f64,
    checkpoints: [f64; 16],
    n_points: i32
) -> BrainPlasmaTacTable with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ref_table = simulate_checkpoints(prm, dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points)
    if ref_table.success == false {
        return ref_table
    }

    var out = ref_table
    var blood_var: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var brain_var: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

    var prior_i: i32 = 0
    while prior_i < priors.n {
        let idx = prior_i as usize
        let h = tac_fdiff_h(priors.mean[idx], priors.variance[idx])
        if h > 0.0 {
            let prm_p = tac_perturb(prm, prior_i, h)
            let pert_table = simulate_checkpoints(prm_p, dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points)
            if pert_table.success == false {
                out.success = false
                return out
            }

            var point_i: i32 = 0
            while point_i < n_points {
                let pidx = point_i as usize
                let dblood = (pert_table.blood_values[pidx] - ref_table.blood_values[pidx]) / h
                let dbrain = (pert_table.brain_values[pidx] - ref_table.brain_values[pidx]) / h
                blood_var[pidx] = blood_var[pidx] + dblood * dblood * priors.variance[idx]
                brain_var[pidx] = brain_var[pidx] + dbrain * dbrain * priors.variance[idx]
                point_i = point_i + 1
            }
        }
        prior_i = prior_i + 1
    }

    var point_j: i32 = 0
    while point_j < n_points {
        let jdx = point_j as usize
        out.blood_uncertainties[jdx] = tac_sqrt(blood_var[jdx])
        out.brain_uncertainties[jdx] = tac_sqrt(brain_var[jdx])
        point_j = point_j + 1
    }

    out.success = true
    out
}

pub fn rapamycin_brain_plasma_reference_tac() -> BrainPlasmaTacTable with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let prm = ep14_rapamycin_params()
    let priors = ep14_rapamycin_priors()
    let base_times = brain_plasma_reference_times()
    var checkpoints: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        checkpoints[i as usize] = base_times[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    simulate_brain_plasma_tac(prm, priors, 5.0, checkpoints, 8)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/compartments/brain.sio ===
// brain.sio — Darwin PBPK brain module
// Rewritten in Sounio syntax

fn dpbpk_brain_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 { term = term * x / (i as f64); result = result + term; i = i + 1 }
    result
}

fn dpbpk_brain_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn dpbpk_brain_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn dpbpk_brain_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn dpbpk_brain_clamp(x: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 { if x < lo { lo } else if x > hi { hi } else { x } }

struct Brain_State {
    concentration: f64,
    flow_in: f64,
    flow_out: f64,
    volume: f64,
    kp: f64,
}

fn brain_state_new(vol: f64, kp: f64) -> Brain_State {
    Brain_State { concentration: 0.0, flow_in: 0.0, flow_out: 0.0, volume: vol, kp: kp }
}

fn brain_compute_flux(c_arterial: f64, c_tissue: f64, kp: f64, blood_flow: f64) -> f64 {
    blood_flow * (c_arterial - c_tissue / kp)
}

fn brain_update(state: Brain_State, c_arterial: f64, blood_flow: f64, dt: f64) -> Brain_State with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let flux = brain_compute_flux(c_arterial, state.concentration, state.kp, blood_flow)
    var new_state = state
    new_state.concentration = state.concentration + dt * flux / state.volume
    if new_state.concentration < 0.0 { new_state.concentration = 0.0 }
    new_state.flow_in = dpbpk_brain_max(flux, 0.0)
    new_state.flow_out = dpbpk_brain_abs(dpbpk_brain_min(flux, 0.0))
    new_state
}

fn test_brain_flux_positive() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let flux = brain_compute_flux(10.0, 5.0, 2.0, 90.0)
    flux > 0.0
}

fn test_brain_zero_init() -> bool {
    let s = brain_state_new(1.5, 5.0)
    s.concentration == 0.0 && s.volume == 1.5
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/compartments/coronary_smc.sio ===
// stdlib/darwin_pbpk/compartments/coronary_smc.sio
// Coronary smooth-muscle sub-compartment — 5%-mass carve-out of heart.
//
// Background
// ----------
// The dissertation §4.5.3 claim is that the Cypher drug-eluting stent
// targets coronary smooth-muscle cells (SMCs) in the arterial media, NOT
// the bulk of myocardium. Whole-heart C_v is therefore a poor proxy for
// the drug exposure the SMCs actually see — locally elevated by direct
// stent contact (Higuchi diffusion from the polymer coating), then partly
// washed out by coronary perfusion.
//
// PBPK28 currently uses heart (organ index 4) as the coronary_smc proxy;
// this module implements the proper sub-compartment carve-out described
// in gap_report items `coronary_smc_status` and `cypher_flocal`. The
// PBPK28 parity gate (Sounio ↔ Node) continues to exercise the heart-
// proxy approximation pending JS engine adoption — §4.5.3 cites this
// module as the canonical formulation and the parity ref as the
// currently-validated approximation.
//
// Model
// -----
//   V_csmc       = 0.05 · V_heart   (5% mass carve-out, ~16.5 mL out of 330 mL)
//   Q_csmc       = (V_csmc/V_heart) · Q_heart  (volume-proportional perfusion)
//   Kp_csmc      = Kp_heart  (SMC partitioning ≈ myocardium average)
//   f_local      = 0.30  (Cypher stent: 30% of Higuchi flux deposits in SMC
//                         contact zone; 70% washes systemically via the
//                         capillary bed before reaching the SMC layer.
//                         Sehgal 1995 / Sousa 2001 estimate band.)
//
// ODE per timestep dt (perfusion-limited well-stirred + local Higuchi source):
//
//   dC_csmc/dt = (Q_csmc / V_csmc) · (C_blood − C_csmc / Kp_csmc)
//              + f_local · release_rate(t) / V_csmc
//
// The caller routes (1 − f_local) · release_rate(t) into the systemic
// blood ODE so total mass is conserved across the split.
//
// Stage G-ε-17. gap-report claims `coronary_smc_status` (this module),
// `cypher_flocal` (f_local parameter).

// ─── Parameter record ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
struct CoronarySmcParams {
    v_csmc:  f64,    // L, sub-compartment volume
    q_csmc:  f64,    // L/h, perfusion into sub-compartment
    kp_csmc: f64,    // tissue:blood partition coefficient
    f_local: f64,    // 0..1, fraction of Higuchi flux routed locally
}

// Rapamycin / Cypher stent default parameters.
//   V_heart = 0.33 L (ICRP standard man) → V_csmc = 0.0165 L
//   Q_heart = 16.0 L/h (coronary flow)   → Q_csmc =  0.80 L/h
//   Kp_csmc = 2.30 (inherits Kp_heart for rapamycin)
//   f_local = 0.30 (Cypher band — see header note)
fn coronary_smc_default_params() -> CoronarySmcParams {
    CoronarySmcParams {
        v_csmc:  0.0165,
        q_csmc:  0.80,
        kp_csmc: 2.30,
        f_local: 0.30,
    }
}

// Parameter ctor for non-default scenarios (sensitivity sweeps).
fn coronary_smc_params(v_csmc: f64, q_csmc: f64, kp_csmc: f64,
                       f_local: f64) -> CoronarySmcParams {
    CoronarySmcParams { v_csmc: v_csmc, q_csmc: q_csmc, kp_csmc: kp_csmc, f_local: f_local }
}

// ─── State record ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
struct CoronarySmcState {
    c:               f64,   // drug concentration in sub-compartment, mg/L
    deposited_mass:  f64,   // cumulative mg deposited locally (audit)
}

fn coronary_smc_state_zero() -> CoronarySmcState {
    CoronarySmcState { c: 0.0, deposited_mass: 0.0 }
}

// ─── Step kernel ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Explicit Euler half-step on the sub-compartment ODE with two source terms.
// Caller is responsible for:
//   (a) passing `c_blood` from the systemic compartment at the same instant,
//   (b) routing `coronary_smc_systemic_flux(p, rr)` into the blood ODE so
//       total drug mass is conserved.
fn coronary_smc_step(s: CoronarySmcState, p: CoronarySmcParams,
                     c_blood: f64, release_rate_mg_per_h: f64,
                     dt: f64) -> CoronarySmcState with Mut, Div {
    let perfusion  = (p.q_csmc / p.v_csmc) * (c_blood - s.c / p.kp_csmc)
    let local_flux = p.f_local * release_rate_mg_per_h / p.v_csmc
    let dcdt = perfusion + local_flux

    var r = s
    r.c = s.c + dt * dcdt
    if r.c < 0.0 { r.c = 0.0 }
    r.deposited_mass = s.deposited_mass + dt * p.f_local * release_rate_mg_per_h
    return r
}

// ─── Release-routing helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Local fraction routed into the SMC sub-compartment.
fn coronary_smc_local_flux(p: CoronarySmcParams,
                           release_rate_mg_per_h: f64) -> f64 {
    return p.f_local * release_rate_mg_per_h
}

// Systemic fraction routed into the blood ODE (1 − f_local). The caller
// adds (this / V_blood) to dC_blood/dt for mass conservation across the split.
fn coronary_smc_systemic_flux(p: CoronarySmcParams,
                              release_rate_mg_per_h: f64) -> f64 {
    return (1.0 - p.f_local) * release_rate_mg_per_h
}

// ─── Mass-balance audit ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// True iff |local + systemic − total_released| is below an absolute floor
// (1e-12 mg) or a 0.1 % relative threshold. The relative tolerance covers
// explicit-Euler truncation against the analytical Higuchi cumulative; pass
// an exact-integral driver (release_step_amount) to get to 1e-12 absolute.
fn coronary_smc_mass_balance_ok(s: CoronarySmcState, systemic_mass: f64,
                                total_released: f64) -> bool with Mut {
    let computed = s.deposited_mass + systemic_mass
    var diff = computed - total_released
    if diff < 0.0 { diff = 0.0 - diff }
    if total_released < 1.0e-9 { return diff < 1.0e-12 }
    return (diff / total_released) < 1.0e-3
}

// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/constants.sio ===
// stdlib/darwin_pbpk/constants.sio — Shared PBPK Constants
//
// Mathematical utilities and physiological constants for PBPK modeling.
//
// References:
// - ICRP Publication 89: Basic anatomical and physiological data (2002)
// - Brown et al. (1997) Physiological parameter values for PBPK models
// - Davies & Morris (1993) Physiological parameters in laboratory animals and humans

// ============================================================================
// MATHEMATICAL CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn dpbpk_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }
fn dpbpk_e() -> f64 { 2.71828182845904523536 }

// ============================================================================
// MATHEMATICAL FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn dpbpk_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn dpbpk_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn dpbpk_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn dpbpk_clamp(x: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < lo { lo } else if x > hi { hi } else { x }
}

fn dpbpk_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Taylor series with overflow/underflow protection
    if x > 700.0 { return dpbpk_exp(350.0) * dpbpk_exp(x - 350.0) }
    if x < -700.0 { return 0.0 }
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n: i64 = 1
    while n < 30 {
        term = term * x / n as f64
        result = result + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    result
}

fn dpbpk_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 15 {
        y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn dpbpk_log(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Natural log via Newton's method
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000.0 }
    var y = 0.0
    var xr = x
    while xr > 2.0 {
        xr = xr / 2.71828182845904523536
        y = y + 1.0
    }
    while xr < 0.5 {
        xr = xr * 2.71828182845904523536
        y = y - 1.0
    }
    y = y + (xr - 1.0)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 15 {
        let ey = dpbpk_exp(y)
        if ey > 0.0 {
            y = y + (x - ey) / ey
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn dpbpk_log10(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    dpbpk_log(x) / 2.302585092994046
}

fn dpbpk_pow(base: f64, exp_int: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if exp_int == 0 { return 1.0 }
    var result = 1.0
    var b = base
    var e = exp_int
    if e < 0 {
        b = 1.0 / b
        e = 0 - e
    }
    while e > 0 {
        if e % 2 == 1 {
            result = result * b
        }
        b = b * b
        e = e / 2
    }
    result
}

// Test: dpbpk_exp(0) = 1
fn test_dpbpk_exp_zero() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_exp(0.0) - 1.0) < 0.0001
}

// Test: dpbpk_exp(1) ≈ e
fn test_dpbpk_exp_one() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_exp(1.0) - 2.71828182845904523536) < 0.001
}

// Test: dpbpk_log(e) ≈ 1

    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_log(2.71828182845904523536) - 1.0) < 0.001
}

// Test: clamp works
fn test_dpbpk_clamp() -> bool {
    let a = dpbpk_clamp(5.0, 0.0, 3.0)
    let b = dpbpk_clamp(-1.0, 0.0, 3.0)
    let c = dpbpk_clamp(1.5, 0.0, 3.0)
    let ok1 = dpbpk_abs(a - 3.0) < 0.0001
    let ok2 = dpbpk_abs(b - 0.0) < 0.0001
    let ok3 = dpbpk_abs(c - 1.5) < 0.0001
    if ok1 { if ok2 { ok3 } else { false } } else { false }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/core/fractal_blood.sio ===
// fractal_blood.sio — Fractal Blood Dynamics for PBPK
// Implements CTRW framework for anomalous transport in vascular networks

fn dpbpk_fb_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn dpbpk_fb_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 { term = term * x / (i as f64); result = result + term; i = i + 1 }
    result
}

fn dpbpk_fb_ln(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var v = x
    var scale = 0.0
    while v > 2.0 { v = v / 2.718281828; scale = scale + 1.0 }
    while v < 0.5 { v = v * 2.718281828; scale = scale - 1.0 }
    let y = (v - 1.0) / (v + 1.0)
    let y2 = y * y
    2.0 * y * (1.0 + y2 / 3.0 + y2 * y2 / 5.0 + y2 * y2 * y2 / 7.0) + scale
}

fn dpbpk_fb_pow(base: f64, exp_v: f64) -> f64 {
    if base <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    dpbpk_fb_exp(exp_v * dpbpk_fb_ln(base))
}

fn FRACTAL_DIMENSION() -> f64 { 2.7 }
fn MURRAY_EXPONENT() -> f64 { 3.0 }
fn BLOOD_VISCOSITY() -> f64 { 0.0035 }
fn ANOMALOUS_EXPONENT_BLOOD() -> f64 { 0.85 }

struct FractalParams {
    fractal_dim: f64,
    anomalous_exponent: f64,
    spectral_dim: f64,
    hurst_exponent: f64,
}

fn fractal_params_new(d_f: f64, alpha: f64) -> FractalParams {
    FractalParams {
        fractal_dim: d_f,
        anomalous_exponent: alpha,
        spectral_dim: 2.0 * d_f / (d_f + 2.0),
        hurst_exponent: alpha / 2.0,
    }
}

fn fractal_params_default() -> FractalParams {
    fractal_params_new(FRACTAL_DIMENSION(), ANOMALOUS_EXPONENT_BLOOD())
}

struct VesselSegment {
    radius: f64,
    length: f64,
    flow_rate: f64,
    branching_level: i32,
}

// Gamma function approximation (Stirling)
fn fb_gamma(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    if x < 1.0 { return fb_gamma(x + 1.0) / x }
    // Stirling: Gamma(x) ~ sqrt(2pi/x) * (x/e)^x
    let pi = 3.14159265358979323846
    let e = 2.71828182845904523536
    dpbpk_fb_exp(0.5 * dpbpk_fb_ln(2.0 * pi / x) + x * dpbpk_fb_ln(x / e))
}

// Mittag-Leffler function E_alpha(z)
fn mittag_leffler_approx(alpha: f64, z: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if alpha == 1.0 { return dpbpk_fb_exp(z) }
    if dpbpk_fb_abs(z) < 0.0000000001 { return 1.0 }

    var sum = 0.0
    var term = 1.0
    var k = 0
    while k < 100 {
        sum = sum + term
        if dpbpk_fb_abs(term) < 0.0000000001 * dpbpk_fb_abs(sum) { return sum }
        let g = fb_gamma(alpha * ((k + 1) as f64) + 1.0)
        if g > 0.0 {
            term = term * z / g
        } else {
            return sum
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    sum
}

// Fractional concentration decay
fn fractional_decay(c0: f64, lambda: f64, t: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    c0 * mittag_leffler_approx(alpha, 0.0 - lambda * dpbpk_fb_pow(t, alpha))
}

// Murray's law branching
fn murray_child_radius(parent_radius: f64, n_children: i64) -> f64 {
    if n_children <= 0 { return parent_radius }
    let factor = dpbpk_fb_pow(n_children as f64, 0.0 - 1.0 / MURRAY_EXPONENT())
    parent_radius * factor
}

// Anomalous dispersion coefficient
fn anomalous_dispersion(d0: f64, t: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 {
    if t <= 0.0 { return d0 }
    d0 * dpbpk_fb_pow(t, alpha - 1.0)
}

// Tests
fn test_ml_exp_recovery() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let ml_val = mittag_leffler_approx(1.0, 1.0)
    let exp_val = dpbpk_fb_exp(1.0)
    dpbpk_fb_abs(ml_val - exp_val) < 0.001
}

fn test_ml_zero() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let val = mittag_leffler_approx(0.85, 0.0)
    dpbpk_fb_abs(val - 1.0) < 0.001
}

fn test_fractional_decay_t0() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let val = fractional_decay(100.0, 0.1, 0.0, 0.85)
    dpbpk_fb_abs(val - 100.0) < 0.001
}

fn test_murray_law() -> bool {
    let child_r = murray_child_radius(1.0, 2)
    child_r > 0.0 && child_r < 1.0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/core/ode_pbpk.sio ===
// ode_pbpk.sio — ODE solver for PBPK compartmental models
// Forward Euler integration for multi-compartment pharmacokinetics

fn ode_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn ode_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn ode_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 { term = term * x / (i as f64); result = result + term; i = i + 1 }
    result
}

struct PBPKState {
    c_plasma: f64,
    c_liver: f64,
    c_brain: f64,
    c_kidney: f64,
    c_muscle: f64,
    c_fat: f64,
    c_gut: f64,
    t: f64,
}

fn pbpk_state_zero() -> PBPKState {
    PBPKState { c_plasma: 0.0, c_liver: 0.0, c_brain: 0.0, c_kidney: 0.0, c_muscle: 0.0, c_fat: 0.0, c_gut: 0.0, t: 0.0 }
}

struct PBPKParams {
    q_liver: f64,
    q_brain: f64,
    q_kidney: f64,
    q_muscle: f64,
    q_fat: f64,
    q_gut: f64,
    v_plasma: f64,
    v_liver: f64,
    v_brain: f64,
    v_kidney: f64,
    v_muscle: f64,
    v_fat: f64,
    v_gut: f64,
    kp_liver: f64,
    kp_brain: f64,
    kp_kidney: f64,
    kp_muscle: f64,
    kp_fat: f64,
    kp_gut: f64,
    cl_hepatic: f64,
    cl_renal: f64,
}

fn pbpk_params_default() -> PBPKParams {
    PBPKParams { q_liver: 90.0, q_brain: 42.0, q_kidney: 72.0, q_muscle: 42.0, q_fat: 18.0, q_gut: 60.0, v_plasma: 3.0, v_liver: 1.5, v_brain: 1.4, v_kidney: 0.31, v_muscle: 35.0, v_fat: 14.0, v_gut: 1.2, kp_liver: 5.0, kp_brain: 1.5, kp_kidney: 3.0, kp_muscle: 2.0, kp_fat: 10.0, kp_gut: 3.0, cl_hepatic: 10.0, cl_renal: 5.0 }
}

fn pbpk_rhs(state: PBPKState, params: PBPKParams) -> PBPKState with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let cp = state.c_plasma
    var deriv = pbpk_state_zero()

    // Liver
    let flux_liver = params.q_liver * (cp - state.c_liver / params.kp_liver)
    deriv.c_liver = (flux_liver - params.cl_hepatic * state.c_liver / params.kp_liver) / params.v_liver

    // Brain
    let flux_brain = params.q_brain * (cp - state.c_brain / params.kp_brain)
    deriv.c_brain = flux_brain / params.v_brain

    // Kidney
    let flux_kidney = params.q_kidney * (cp - state.c_kidney / params.kp_kidney)
    deriv.c_kidney = (flux_kidney - params.cl_renal * state.c_kidney / params.kp_kidney) / params.v_kidney

    // Muscle
    let flux_muscle = params.q_muscle * (cp - state.c_muscle / params.kp_muscle)
    deriv.c_muscle = flux_muscle / params.v_muscle

    // Fat
    let flux_fat = params.q_fat * (cp - state.c_fat / params.kp_fat)
    deriv.c_fat = flux_fat / params.v_fat

    // Gut
    let flux_gut = params.q_gut * (cp - state.c_gut / params.kp_gut)
    deriv.c_gut = flux_gut / params.v_gut

    // Plasma: sum of return flows
    deriv.c_plasma = (0.0 - flux_liver - flux_brain - flux_kidney - flux_muscle - flux_fat - flux_gut) / params.v_plasma

    deriv
}

fn pbpk_euler_step(state: PBPKState, params: PBPKParams, dt: f64) -> PBPKState with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let deriv = pbpk_rhs(state, params)
    PBPKState {
        c_plasma: state.c_plasma + dt * deriv.c_plasma,
        c_liver: state.c_liver + dt * deriv.c_liver,
        c_brain: state.c_brain + dt * deriv.c_brain,
        c_kidney: state.c_kidney + dt * deriv.c_kidney,
        c_muscle: state.c_muscle + dt * deriv.c_muscle,
        c_fat: state.c_fat + dt * deriv.c_fat,
        c_gut: state.c_gut + dt * deriv.c_gut,
        t: state.t + dt,
    }
}

fn pbpk_simulate(dose: f64, params: PBPKParams, t_end: f64, dt: f64) -> PBPKState with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var state = pbpk_state_zero()
    state.c_plasma = dose / params.v_plasma
    while state.t < t_end {
        state = pbpk_euler_step(state, params, dt)
    }
    state
}

fn test_pbpk_iv_bolus() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let params = pbpk_params_default()
    let result = pbpk_simulate(100.0, params, 1.0, 0.01)
    result.c_plasma >= 0.0 && result.c_liver >= 0.0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/core/pbpk28_params.sio ===
// stdlib/darwin_pbpk/core/pbpk28_params.sio — PBPK28 state + parameter records
//
// The Stage G dissertation kernel: 14 organs × {vascular C_v, interstitial C_t}
// with a permeability-surface-area product PS coupling. Blood is organ 0;
// peripheral organs are indexed 1..13.
//
// State carries only the transport-layer values (Cv, Ct). TMDD layer
// (R_free, DR) and PD layer (A, N) live in separate records under
// `stdlib/darwin_pbpk/tmdd/` and `stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/` — composed by the
// scenario file.
//
// Parameters bundle the per-organ physiology (V_ref, vasc_frac, K_p, PS, Q)
// + a central clearance (cl_central; routes are drug-specific:
// rapamycin = hepatic CYP3A4, semaglutide = proteolytic). The drug profile
// constructors `pbpk28_params_rapamycin()` / `pbpk28_params_semaglutide()`
// populate the fixed-size arrays from literature values matching the JS
// engine `website/src/lib/pbpk28_core.mjs` and the parity refs.
//
// Stage G-ε-15. gap-report claims `organ_topology` (CONFIRMED),
// `peptide_extension_path` (PARTIAL — peptide K_p set lives in this file
// rather than a separate `core/peptide_partitioning.sio` module, which the
// dissertation §4.3.5 may want to relocate).

// ─── State record ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 14 organs × {C_v, C_t}, all mg/L. Blood is C_v[0] (C_t[0] unused).
pub struct PBPKState28 {
    cv: [f64; 14],
    ct: [f64; 14],
}

fn pbpk28_state_zero() -> PBPKState28 {
    PBPKState28 {
        cv: [0.0; 14],
        ct: [0.0; 14],
    }
}

// ─── Parameter record ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pub struct PBPKParams28 {
    v_ref:      [f64; 14],   // L, organ volume (ICRP standard man 70 kg)
    vasc_frac:  [f64; 14],   // V_v / V_total per organ (Brown 1997)
    kp:         [f64; 14],   // tissue:vascular partition coefficient at eq
    ps:         [f64; 14],   // mL/min·… permeability-surface-area product
    q:          [f64; 14],   // L/h, organ blood flow (70 kg adult)
    cl_central: f64,         // L/h; hepatic (rapamycin) or proteolytic (sema)
}

// ─── Rapamycin profile ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Lipophilic small molecule (MW 914 Da). High Kp in liver (5.4) / lung (3.1) /
// kidney (4.2) / heart (2.3) / gut (2.6) / spleen (2.1); low at BBB
// (Kp_brain = 0.10 — P-gp efflux per Lampen 1998). PS is large (membrane
// not rate-limiting). Hepatic CYP3A4 clearance 12.4 L/h (Ferron 1997).
fn pbpk28_params_rapamycin() -> PBPKParams28 {
    PBPKParams28 {
        v_ref:     [5.0, 1.8, 0.31, 1.45, 0.33, 1.1, 28.0, 20.0, 1.2, 3.6, 6.6, 0.18, 0.09, 3.7],
        vasc_frac: [1.000, 0.210, 0.160, 0.037, 0.262, 0.262, 0.040, 0.050, 0.024, 0.019, 0.041, 0.282, 0.180, 0.050],
        kp:        [1.00, 5.40, 4.20, 0.10, 2.30, 3.10, 0.50, 0.30, 2.60, 0.80, 0.20, 2.10, 1.80, 0.40],
        ps:        [0.0, 1800.0, 1110.0, 88.0, 160.0, 10500.0, 336.0, 40.0, 660.0, 126.0, 51.0, 150.0, 96.0, 78.0],
        q:         [350.0, 90.0, 74.0, 44.0, 16.0, 350.0, 42.0, 10.0, 55.0, 21.0, 17.0, 10.0, 8.0, 13.0],
        cl_central: 12.4,
    }
}

// ─── Semaglutide profile ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 4114 Da peptide. Low Kp everywhere (Kp < 1; vascular-confined). PS is much
// lower than rapamycin (steric exclusion at endothelium; BBB nearly
// impermeable PS=1). Proteolytic clearance 0.077 L/h (Overgaard 2019).
fn pbpk28_params_semaglutide() -> PBPKParams28 {
    PBPKParams28 {
        v_ref:     [5.0, 1.8, 0.31, 1.45, 0.33, 1.1, 28.0, 20.0, 1.2, 3.6, 6.6, 0.18, 0.09, 3.7],
        vasc_frac: [1.000, 0.210, 0.160, 0.037, 0.262, 0.262, 0.040, 0.050, 0.024, 0.019, 0.041, 0.282, 0.180, 0.050],
        kp:        [1.00, 0.50, 0.60, 0.05, 0.40, 0.30, 0.20, 0.10, 0.80, 0.30, 0.20, 0.40, 0.70, 0.30],
        ps:        [0.0, 50.0, 30.0, 1.0, 5.0, 100.0, 10.0, 2.0, 30.0, 5.0, 2.0, 10.0, 8.0, 5.0],
        q:         [350.0, 90.0, 74.0, 44.0, 16.0, 350.0, 42.0, 10.0, 55.0, 21.0, 17.0, 10.0, 8.0, 13.0],
        cl_central: 0.077,
    }
}

// ─── Total-mass utility ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Σ_i (V_v,i · C_v,i + V_t,i · C_t,i). Useful for the parity-gate's case-4
// mass-conservation invariant (12/12 samples monotonically decay under
// no-source bolus runs).
fn pbpk28_total_mass(s: PBPKState28, p: PBPKParams28) -> f64 with Mut {
    var total = 0.0
    // Blood: V_b · C_v[0]  (V_t,0 is zero).
    total = total + p.v_ref[0] * s.cv[0]
    var i = 1
    while i < 14 {
        let vi = p.v_ref[i]
        let vf = p.vasc_frac[i]
        let vv = vi * vf
        let vt = vi * (1.0 - vf)
        total = total + vv * s.cv[i] + vt * s.ct[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return total
}
