// Create default PBPK parameters for a 70kg male adult
fn create_default_pbpk_params() -> PBPKParams {
    return PBPKParams {
        // Default organ volumes (L) - based on ICRP reference adult male
        v_blood: 5.6,
        v_liver: 1.8,
        v_kidney: 0.31,
        v_brain: 1.45,
        v_heart: 0.33,
        v_lung: 1.17,
        v_muscle: 29.0,
        v_adipose: 14.5,
        v_gut: 1.65,
        v_skin: 3.3,
        v_bone: 4.9,
        v_spleen: 0.19,
        v_pancreas: 0.14,
        v_rest: 3.5,

        // Default blood flow rates (L/h) - based on cardiac output ~6.5 L/min
        q_blood: 390.0,
        q_liver: 97.2,   // 25% of CO (includes portal + hepatic artery)
        q_kidney: 74.1,  // 19% of CO
        q_brain: 46.8,   // 12% of CO
        q_heart: 15.6,   // 4% of CO
        q_lung: 390.0,   // 100% of CO (series circulation)
        q_muscle: 70.2,  // 18% of CO
        q_adipose: 19.5, // 5% of CO
        q_gut: 70.2,     // 18% of CO (includes portal)
        q_skin: 19.5,    // 5% of CO
        q_bone: 19.5,    // 5% of CO
        q_spleen: 11.7,  // 3% of CO
        q_pancreas: 3.9, // 1% of CO
        q_rest: 19.5,    // 5% of CO

        // Default clearance (L/h)
        clearance_hepatic: 10.0,
        clearance_renal: 5.0,

        // Default partition coefficients (typical for neutral lipophilic drug)
        kp_blood: 1.0,
        kp_liver: 3.0,
        kp_kidney: 2.5,
        kp_brain: 1.5,
        kp_heart: 2.0,
        kp_lung: 2.5,
        kp_muscle: 1.2,
        kp_adipose: 5.0,
        kp_gut: 2.5,
        kp_skin: 1.8,
        kp_bone: 0.5,
        kp_spleen: 2.5,
        kp_pancreas: 2.0,
        kp_rest: 1.5,

        // Default physiological parameters
        fu_plasma: 0.1,    // 10% unbound (typical for protein-bound drug)
        hematocrit: 0.45,  // 45% (normal adult)
        bp_ratio: 1.0,     // Equal distribution in blood and plasma
    };
}

// Create a patient profile with basic demographics
fn create_patient(age: f64, weight: f64@kg, sex: bool) -> PatientData {
    let height: f64;

    // Estimate height based on sex and typical BMI
    if sex {
        height = 175.0;  // Default male height (cm)
    } else {
        height = 162.0;  // Default female height (cm)
    }

    return PatientData {
        age: age,
        weight: weight,
        height: height,
        sex: sex,
        disease_state: HEALTHY,
    };
}

// Validate PBPK parameters for physiological plausibility
fn validate_pbpk_params(params: PBPKParams) -> bool {
    // Check organ volumes are positive
    if params.v_blood <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_liver <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_kidney <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_brain <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_heart <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_lung <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_muscle <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_adipose <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_gut <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_skin <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_bone <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_spleen <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_pancreas <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.v_rest <= 0.0 { return false; }

    // Check blood flows are positive
    if params.q_blood <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_liver <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_kidney <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_brain <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_heart <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_lung <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_muscle <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_adipose <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_gut <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_skin <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_bone <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_spleen <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_pancreas <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.q_rest <= 0.0 { return false; }

    // Check clearances are non-negative
    if params.clearance_hepatic < 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.clearance_renal < 0.0 { return false; }

    // Check partition coefficients are positive
    if params.kp_blood <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_liver <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_kidney <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_brain <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_heart <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_lung <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_muscle <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_adipose <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_gut <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_skin <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_bone <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_spleen <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_pancreas <= 0.0 { return false; }
    if params.kp_rest <= 0.0 { return false; }

    // Check fu_plasma is between 0 and 1
    if params.fu_plasma < 0.0 || params.fu_plasma > 1.0 { return false; }

    // Check hematocrit is between 0 and 1
    if params.hematocrit < 0.0 || params.hematocrit > 1.0 { return false; }

    // Check bp_ratio is positive
    if params.bp_ratio <= 0.0 { return false; }

    return true;
}

// Calculate total body volume from organ volumes
fn calculate_total_volume(params: PBPKParams) -> f64@L {
    return params.v_blood + params.v_liver + params.v_kidney +
           params.v_brain + params.v_heart + params.v_lung +
           params.v_muscle + params.v_adipose + params.v_gut +
           params.v_skin + params.v_bone + params.v_spleen +
           params.v_pancreas + params.v_rest;
}

// Calculate cardiac output from blood flows (excluding lung which is series)
fn calculate_cardiac_output(params: PBPKParams) -> f64@L_per_h {
    return params.q_liver + params.q_kidney + params.q_brain +
           params.q_heart + params.q_muscle + params.q_adipose +
           params.q_gut + params.q_skin + params.q_bone +
           params.q_spleen + params.q_pancreas + params.q_rest;
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/core/rodgers_rowland.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: PASS

// stdlib/darwin_pbpk/core/rodgers_rowland.sio
// Rodgers-Rowland (2006) mechanistic tissue:plasma partition coefficient
// prediction for neutral compounds with GUM uncertainty propagation.
//
// Reference: Rodgers T & Rowland M (2006) J Pharm Sci 95:1743-1764
//
// SCOPE: Neutral compounds only (rapamycin is a neutral macrolide, pKa N/A).
//
// VALIDATED RANGE: The R-R model was calibrated on drugs with logP < 4.
// For rapamycin (logP = 7.0), absolute Kp values are overestimated due to
// the linear lipid partitioning term dominating outside the model's domain
// (Poulin et al. 2011 Pharm Res 28:1562). This module therefore provides:
//   1. Raw R-R Kp predictions (documents systematic overestimation)
//   2. Dimensionless log-sensitivities ∂ln(Kp_i)/∂logP (valid across logP range)
//   3. GUM scaled uncertainties: sensitivities × literature Kp (for GUM budget)
//
// For GUM budget purposes, the sensitivity structure from R-R is applied to
// the literature Kp values (rapamycin.sio), consistent with JCGM 100:2008 §5.1.3.
//
// GUM formula (JCGM 100:2008 Eq 13):
//   u²(Kp_i) = [∂Kp_i/∂logP]² u²(logP) + [∂Kp_i/∂fu]² u²(fu)
//
// 14-compartment ordering (matching tsit5_pbpk14.sio):
//   0=blood, 1=liver, 2=kidney, 3=brain, 4=heart, 5=lung, 6=muscle,
//   7=adipose, 8=gut, 9=skin, 10=bone, 11=spleen, 12=pancreas, 13=other

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn rr_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 12 { y = (y + x / y) * 0.5; i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn rr_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// exp(x) — Taylor series, matches ppcr_neural_net_demo pattern
fn rr_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 20.0 { return rr_exp(x - 10.0) * rr_exp(10.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 0.0 }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i <= 20 {
        term = term * x / (i as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

// 10^x = exp(x * ln(10))
fn rr_pow10(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    rr_exp(x * 2.302585092994046)
}

// ============================================================================
// TISSUE COMPOSITION TABLE (R-R 2006, Table 1 + PK-Sim defaults)
// ============================================================================
// All fractions as volume fractions (dimensionless).
// Sources: Rodgers & Rowland (2006) Table 1 for most tissues;
//          PK-Sim Human Reference Values for adipose/bone/other.

fn rr_fw_e(i: i32) -> f64 {   // extracellular water
    if i == 0  { return 0.620 }   // blood
    if i == 1  { return 0.161 }   // liver
    if i == 2  { return 0.273 }   // kidney
    if i == 3  { return 0.092 }   // brain (Rodgers 2006 Table 1)
    if i == 4  { return 0.320 }   // heart
    if i == 5  { return 0.312 }   // lung
    if i == 6  { return 0.118 }   // muscle
    if i == 7  { return 0.135 }   // adipose
    if i == 8  { return 0.282 }   // gut
    if i == 9  { return 0.382 }   // skin
    if i == 10 { return 0.100 }   // bone
    if i == 11 { return 0.207 }   // spleen
    if i == 12 { return 0.125 }   // pancreas
    return 0.200                   // other
}

fn rr_fw_i(i: i32) -> f64 {   // intracellular water
    if i == 0  { return 0.038 }
    if i == 1  { return 0.573 }
    if i == 2  { return 0.483 }
    if i == 3  { return 0.678 }   // brain high intracellular (Rodgers 2006)
    if i == 4  { return 0.456 }
    if i == 5  { return 0.392 }
    if i == 6  { return 0.630 }
    if i == 7  { return 0.017 }   // adipose: mostly lipid, little water
    if i == 8  { return 0.475 }
    if i == 9  { return 0.291 }
    if i == 10 { return 0.346 }
    if i == 11 { return 0.579 }
    if i == 12 { return 0.631 }
    return 0.500
}

fn rr_fn_l(i: i32) -> f64 {   // neutral lipid fraction
    if i == 0  { return 0.0019 }
    if i == 1  { return 0.0140 }
    if i == 2  { return 0.0130 }
    if i == 3  { return 0.0390 }   // brain: significant myelin lipid
    if i == 4  { return 0.0140 }
    if i == 5  { return 0.0220 }
    if i == 6  { return 0.0100 }
    if i == 7  { return 0.8530 }   // adipose: dominant lipid depot
    if i == 8  { return 0.0380 }
    if i == 9  { return 0.0600 }
    if i == 10 { return 0.0170 }
    if i == 11 { return 0.0110 }
    if i == 12 { return 0.0200 }
    return 0.0200
}

fn rr_fn_ph(i: i32) -> f64 {  // phospholipid fraction
    if i == 0  { return 0.0019 }
    if i == 1  { return 0.0240 }
    if i == 2  { return 0.0120 }
    if i == 3  { return 0.0360 }   // brain: rich in phospholipid
    if i == 4  { return 0.0110 }
    if i == 5  { return 0.0130 }
    if i == 6  { return 0.0070 }
    if i == 7  { return 0.0020 }
    if i == 8  { return 0.0160 }
    if i == 9  { return 0.0040 }
    if i == 10 { return 0.0020 }
    if i == 11 { return 0.0110 }
    if i == 12 { return 0.0130 }
    return 0.0100
}

// ============================================================================
// OUTPUT STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

pub struct RRResult {
    // Raw R-R Kp values (may overestimate for logP > 4, see header)
    kp: [f64; 14],
    // Dimensionless log-sensitivity ∂ln(Kp_i)/∂logP for each tissue
    // Bounded by ln(10) ≈ 2.303 in the lipid-dominated regime (logP >> 4)
    log_sens: [f64; 14],
    // GUM uncertainty u(Kp_i) using raw R-R values
    kp_unc_raw: [f64; 14],
    logP: f64,
    fu_plasma: f64,
}

pub struct RRScaledUnc {
    // GUM uncertainty applied to literature Kp values:
    //   u(Kp_i) = sqrt( (log_sens_i * u_logP * Kp_lit_i)^2 + (Kp_lit_i/fu * u_fu)^2 )
    u_kp: [f64; 14],
    conf: f64,   // Evidence quality: 0.60 (R-R sensitivity + literature Kp)
}

// ============================================================================
// CORE COMPUTATION — Neutral Compound R-R (Eq. 6 in Rodgers 2006)
// ============================================================================
// For a neutral molecule (no ionization, fu_water = 1.0):
//   Kpu_i = fw_e_i + fw_i_i + P*(fn_L_i + 0.3*fn_P_i)   [unbound tissue:unbound plasma]
//   Kp_i  = Kpu_i / fu_plasma                             [total tissue:total plasma]
//
// Analytical GUM sensitivities:
//   ∂Kp/∂logP = P * ln(10) * (fn_L + 0.3*fn_P) / fu_plasma
//   ∂Kp/∂fu   = -Kp / fu_plasma
//   u²(Kp) = (∂Kp/∂logP)² u²(logP) + (∂Kp/∂fu)² u²(fu)

pub fn rr_neutral(
    logP: f64,
    fu_plasma: f64,
    u_logP: f64,
    u_fu: f64
) -> RRResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let P = rr_pow10(logP)
    let ln10 = 2.302585092994046

    var kp: [f64; 14] = [0.0; 14]
    var log_sens: [f64; 14] = [0.0; 14]
    var kp_unc_raw: [f64; 14] = [0.0; 14]

    var i = 0
    while i < 14 {
        let fw_e = rr_fw_e(i)
        let fw_i = rr_fw_i(i)
        let fn_l = rr_fn_l(i)
        let fn_ph = rr_fn_ph(i)

        // Lipid composite term (neutral lipid + 30% of phospholipid)
        let lipid_c = fn_l + 0.3 * fn_ph

        // Unbound tissue:unbound plasma ratio
        let kpu = fw_e + fw_i + P * lipid_c

        // Total tissue:total plasma (JCGM-compatible; accounts for plasma binding)
        let kp_i = kpu / fu_plasma
        kp[i] = kp_i

        // GUM sensitivity coefficients (analytical)
        let dkp_dlogP = P * ln10 * lipid_c / fu_plasma
        let dkp_dfu   = 0.0 - kp_i / fu_plasma

        // Combined GUM variance (JCGM 100:2008 Eq 13)
        let var_i = dkp_dlogP * dkp_dlogP * u_logP * u_logP
                  + dkp_dfu   * dkp_dfu   * u_fu   * u_fu
        kp_unc_raw[i] = rr_sqrt(var_i)

        // Log-sensitivity: ∂ln(Kp_i)/∂logP — bounded by ln(10) for logP >> 4
        if kp_i > 1.0e-12 {
            log_sens[i] = dkp_dlogP / kp_i
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    RRResult {
        kp: kp,
        log_sens: log_sens,
        kp_unc_raw: kp_unc_raw,
        logP: logP,
        fu_plasma: fu_plasma,
    }
}

// Convenience: rapamycin physicochemical inputs
//   logP = 7.0 (Vaidyanathan 2001), u_logP = 1.05 (CV = 15%)
//   fu_plasma = 0.08 (Schreiber 1991), u_fu = 0.02 (CV = 25%)
pub fn rr_rapamycin() -> RRResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    rr_neutral(7.0, 0.08, 1.05, 0.02)
}

// ============================================================================
// GUM SCALING: Apply R-R sensitivities to literature Kp values
// ============================================================================
// For logP > 4 compounds (rapamycin), absolute R-R Kp overestimates.
// The sensitivity STRUCTURE (relative tissue ordering, ∂ln Kp/∂logP) is
// preserved even outside the validated domain (Poulin 2011).
//
// Scaled GUM uncertainty for each tissue i:
//   u(Kp_i)² = (log_sens_i × u_logP × Kp_lit_i)² + (Kp_lit_i / fu × u_fu)²
//
// Confidence: 0.60 (R-R sensitivity applied to literature Kp — single calibration)

pub fn rr_scaled_uncertainty(
    rr: RRResult,
    kp_lit: [f64; 14],
    u_logP: f64,
    u_fu: f64
) -> RRScaledUnc with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var u_kp: [f64; 14] = [0.0; 14]
    var i = 0
    while i < 14 {
        let ls = rr.log_sens[i]
        let kp_i = kp_lit[i]
        let fu = rr.fu_plasma

        // logP contribution: u(Kp_i) from u_logP
        let term_logP = ls * u_logP * kp_i

        // fu contribution: u(Kp_i) from u_fu — ∂Kp/∂fu = -Kp/fu
        let term_fu = kp_i / fu * u_fu

        u_kp[i] = rr_sqrt(term_logP * term_logP + term_fu * term_fu)
        i = i + 1
    }
    RRScaledUnc { u_kp: u_kp, conf: 0.60 }
}

// ============================================================================
// RAPAMYCIN LITERATURE Kp VALUES (matching tsit5_pbpk14 ordering)
// ============================================================================
// Sources: Lampen 1998 (brain), Serkova 2000 (muscle, kidney),
//          Napoli 2001 (liver, lung), Ferron 1997 (adipose capped model)
pub fn rr_rapamycin_kp_literature() -> [f64; 14] with Mut {
    var kp: [f64; 14] = [0.0; 14]
    kp[0]  = 1.0    // blood (by definition, reference compartment)
    kp[1]  = 8.0    // liver   — high hepatic uptake (CYP3A4 site)
    kp[2]  = 4.0    // kidney
    kp[3]  = 0.08   // brain   — P-gp efflux limited
    kp[4]  = 3.5    // heart
    kp[5]  = 10.0   // lung
    kp[6]  = 3.5    // muscle
    kp[7]  = 0.3    // adipose — capped for 48h BBB-focus model
    kp[8]  = 5.0    // gut
    kp[9]  = 2.0    // skin
    kp[10] = 1.5    // bone
    kp[11] = 6.0    // spleen
    kp[12] = 4.0    // pancreas
    kp[13] = 0.5    // other
    kp
}

struct TissueComposition {

    f_ew: f64,
    f_iw: f64,
    f_neutral_lipid: f64,
    f_phospholipid: f64,
    f_acidic_phospholipid: f64,
    f_protein: f64,
    pH_iw: f64,
}

fn tissue_liver() -> TissueComposition {

}

fn tissue_brain() -> TissueComposition {
    TissueComposition { f_water: 0.770, f_ew: 0.092, f_iw: 0.678, f_neutral_lipid: 0.039, f_phospholipid: 0.036, f_acidic_phospholipid: 0.0059, f_protein: 0.048, pH_iw: 7.0 }
}

fn tissue_kidney() -> TissueComposition {
    TissueComposition { f_water: 0.783, f_ew: 0.209, f_iw: 0.483, f_neutral_lipid: 0.012, f_phospholipid: 0.024, f_acidic_phospholipid: 0.005, f_protein: 0.127, pH_iw: 7.0 }

// ============================================================================
// MAIN — Gate tests
// ============================================================================
// T1: Lipid-driven ordering: Kp_adipose > Kp_liver > Kp_brain (correct for
//     neutral lipophilic drugs regardless of absolute values)
// T2: GUM uncertainties non-zero for all 14 compartments
// T3: Log-sensitivities in valid range (0, ln(10)] for lipid-rich tissues
// T4: Scaled GUM uncertainties non-zero and finite

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let rr = rr_rapamycin()
    let kp_lit = rr_rapamycin_kp_literature()
    let scaled = rr_scaled_uncertainty(rr, kp_lit, 1.05, 0.02)

    var passed = 0
    var failed = 0

    // T1: Adipose (7) >> liver (1) in absolute R-R Kp (adipose fn_L=0.853 vs liver 0.014)
    //     Brain (3) > liver (1) because brain has higher lipid+phospholipid in R-R table
    //     (myelin-rich tissue; P-gp limitation not in R-R — accounted by literature Kp)
    let kp_adipose = rr.kp[7]
    let kp_liver   = rr.kp[1]
    let kp_brain   = rr.kp[3]
    if kp_adipose > kp_brain && kp_brain > kp_liver {
        println("T1 PASS: R-R ordering adipose > brain > liver (lipid-dominated neutral)")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("T1 FAIL: unexpected Kp ordering")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // T2: All 14 uncertainties non-zero
    var unc_ok = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < 14 {
        if rr.kp_unc_raw[i] > 0.0 { unc_ok = unc_ok + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if unc_ok == 14 {
        println("T2 PASS: GUM uncertainties non-zero (14/14 compartments)")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        print("T2 FAIL: only ")
        print_int(unc_ok)
        println("/14 compartments have non-zero GUM uncertainty")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // T3: Log-sensitivity of adipose and liver > 0 and ≤ ln(10)
    let ls_adipose = rr.log_sens[7]
    let ls_liver   = rr.log_sens[1]
    let ln10 = 2.302585
    if ls_adipose > 0.0 && ls_adipose <= ln10 + 0.01 && ls_liver > 0.0 {
        println("T3 PASS: log-sensitivities in valid range for lipid-rich tissues")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("T3 FAIL: log-sensitivity out of expected range")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // T4: Scaled GUM uncertainties non-zero for literature Kp
    var scaled_ok = 0
    var j = 0
    while j < 14 {
        if scaled.u_kp[j] > 0.0 { scaled_ok = scaled_ok + 1 }
        j = j + 1
    }
    if scaled_ok == 14 {
        println("T4 PASS: scaled GUM uncertainties non-zero (14/14)")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        print("T4 FAIL: only ")
        print_int(scaled_ok)
        println("/14 scaled uncertainties are non-zero")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    println("")
    print("R-R summary — rapamycin (logP=7.0, fu=0.08):")
    println("")
    print("  Kp_liver (lit=8.0)  u_Kp=")
    print(scaled.u_kp[1])
    println("")
    print("  Kp_brain (lit=0.08) u_Kp=")
    print(scaled.u_kp[3])
    println("")
    print("  Kp_adipose(lit=0.3) u_Kp=")
    print(scaled.u_kp[7])
    println("")
    print("  [NOTE] R-R raw Kp overestimates logP>4 drugs by design")
    println("")
    print("  log_sens_adipose=")
    print(rr.log_sens[7])
    print("  log_sens_liver=")
    print(rr.log_sens[1])
    print("  log_sens_brain=")
    print(rr.log_sens[3])
    println("")

    if failed == 0 {
        println("PASS")
        return 0
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        return 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/cumulants.sio ===
// stdlib/darwin_pbpk/cumulants.sio
//
// M5: fourth-order GUM cumulant budget for PBPK28.
//
// The implementation is intentionally direct and scalar.  It does not depend
// on the D.2 tensor tape because the PBPK28 AUC endpoint is already exposed as
// a deterministic scalar model; finite differences over that scalar are the
// smallest honest derivative extractor for this branch.

use darwin_pbpk::core::pbpk28_params::*
use darwin_pbpk::tsit5_pbpk28::*
use darwin_pbpk::theta_pbpk28::*
use darwin_pbpk::epistemic_pbpk28::{EpPrior28, ep28_rapamycin_params, ep28_rapamycin_priors}
use darwin_pbpk::epistemic_pbpk28_hessian::{Pbpk28HessianBudget, hessian_pbpk28_auc}

// ============================================================================
// BASIC NUMERICS
// ============================================================================

fn m5_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn m5_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn m5_finite(x: f64) -> bool {
    if x != x { return false }
    return m5_abs(x) < 1.0e14
}

pub fn m5_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

pub fn m5_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 999999.0 }
    var sx = x
    var scale: f64 = 0.0
    let e = 2.718281828459045
    while sx > 2.0 { sx = sx / e; scale = scale + 1.0 }
    while sx < 0.5 { sx = sx * e; scale = scale - 1.0 }
    let u = (sx - 1.0) / (sx + 1.0)
    let u2 = u * u
    let r = 2.0 * (u + u * u2 / 3.0
                     + u * u2 * u2 / 5.0
                     + u * u2 * u2 * u2 / 7.0
                     + u * u2 * u2 * u2 * u2 / 9.0
                     + u * u2 * u2 * u2 * u2 * u2 / 11.0)
    return r + scale
}

pub fn m5_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    let inv_ln2 = 1.4426950408889634
    let n_f = x * inv_ln2
    var n: i64 = n_f as i64
    if (n as f64) > n_f { n = n - 1 }
    let r = x - (n as f64) * ln2
    var t: f64 = 1.0
    var result: f64 = 1.0
    var k: i64 = 1
    while k < 24 {
        t = t * r / (k as f64)
        result = result + t
        k = k + 1
    }
    var factor: f64 = 1.0
    if n > 0 {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n { factor = factor * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    }
    if n < 0 {
        let neg_n = 0 - n
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < neg_n { factor = factor * 0.5; i = i + 1 }
    }
    return result * factor
}

// ============================================================================
// PEBAY/WEST ONLINE CENTRAL MOMENTS
// ============================================================================

pub struct CumulantState {
    n:  i64,
    m1: f64,
    m2: f64,
    m3: f64,
    m4: f64,
}

pub struct CumulantSummary {
    mean:     f64,
    variance: f64,
    kappa3:   f64,
    kappa4:   f64,
}

pub fn cumulant_init() -> CumulantState {
    CumulantState { n: 0, m1: 0.0, m2: 0.0, m3: 0.0, m4: 0.0 }
}

pub fn cumulant_update(state: CumulantState, x: f64) -> CumulantState with Div {
    let n1 = state.n
    let n = n1 + 1
    let nf = n as f64
    let n1f = n1 as f64
    let delta = x - state.m1
    let delta_n = delta / nf
    let delta_n2 = delta_n * delta_n
    let term1 = delta * delta_n * n1f
    let m1_new = state.m1 + delta_n
    let m4_new = state.m4
               + term1 * delta_n2 * (nf * nf - 3.0 * nf + 3.0)
               + 6.0 * delta_n2 * state.m2
               - 4.0 * delta_n * state.m3
    let m3_new = state.m3
               + term1 * delta_n * (nf - 2.0)
               - 3.0 * delta_n * state.m2
    let m2_new = state.m2 + term1
    CumulantState { n: n, m1: m1_new, m2: m2_new, m3: m3_new, m4: m4_new }
}

pub fn cumulant_finalize(state: CumulantState) -> CumulantSummary with Div {
    if state.n <= 0 {
        return CumulantSummary { mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, kappa3: 0.0, kappa4: 0.0 }
    }
    let nf = state.n as f64
    let variance = state.m2 / nf
    let k3 = state.m3 / nf
    let mu4 = state.m4 / nf
    let k4 = mu4 - 3.0 * variance * variance
    CumulantSummary { mean: state.m1, variance: variance, kappa3: k3, kappa4: k4 }
}

// ============================================================================
// LOGNORMAL CUMULANTS
// ============================================================================

pub struct LognormalCumulants {
    sigma2_log: f64,
    variance:   f64,
    kappa3:     f64,
    kappa4:     f64,
    central4:   f64,
}

pub fn lognormal_cumulants_from_mean_variance(mean: f64, variance: f64) -> LognormalCumulants with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if mean <= 0.0 || variance <= 0.0 {
        return LognormalCumulants { sigma2_log: 0.0, variance: 0.0, kappa3: 0.0, kappa4: 0.0, central4: 0.0 }
    }
    let cv2 = variance / (mean * mean)
    let s2 = m5_ln(1.0 + cv2)
    let e1 = m5_exp(s2)
    let e2 = m5_exp(2.0 * s2)
    let e3 = m5_exp(3.0 * s2)
    let e6 = m5_exp(6.0 * s2)
    let m3 = mean * mean * mean * (e3 - 3.0 * e1 + 2.0)
    let mu4 = mean * mean * mean * mean * (e6 - 4.0 * e3 + 6.0 * e1 - 3.0)
    let k4 = mu4 - 3.0 * variance * variance
    LognormalCumulants { sigma2_log: s2, variance: variance, kappa3: m3, kappa4: k4, central4: mu4 }
}

// ============================================================================
// DIRECT PBPK28 AUC MODEL AND FINITE DIFFERENCES
// ============================================================================

pub struct DerivativeBudget {
    d1:      [f64; 8],
    d2:      [f64; 8],
    d3:      [f64; 8],
    pub success: bool,
}

fn m5_derivatives_zero() -> DerivativeBudget {
    DerivativeBudget { d1: [0.0; 8], d2: [0.0; 8], d3: [0.0; 8], success: false }
}

fn m5_perturb(prm: PBPKParams28, idx: i32, delta: f64) -> PBPKParams28 with Mut, Div {
    var p = prm
    let fu_ref = 0.08
    if idx == 0 { p.cl_central = p.cl_central + delta }
    if idx == 1 { p.cl_central = p.cl_central + delta }
    if idx == 2 {
        if fu_ref > 0.0 {
            let scale = (fu_ref + delta) / fu_ref
            p.cl_central = p.cl_central * scale
        }
    }
    if idx == 3 { p.kp[3] = p.kp[3] + delta }
    if idx == 4 { p.kp[1] = p.kp[1] + delta }
    if idx == 5 { p.kp[2] = p.kp[2] + delta }
    if idx == 6 { p.kp[7] = p.kp[7] + delta }
    return p
}

// Bolus run at dt = 0.1 h: Rannacher-started clamp-free CN (theta_pbpk28).
// Shared by m5_simulate_auc and the mass-balance gate. Until 2026-09-26 this
// was pbpk28_full_cn_step (+52% AUC_blood floor bias at this dt).
pub fn m5_simulate_ledger(prm: PBPKParams28, dose_mg: f64, t_end: f64,
                          st: &!PBPKState28, led: &!PBPK28Ledger) -> bool with Mut, Div {
    return pbpk28_bolus_run_mut(prm, dose_mg, 0.1, t_end, 5000, st, led)
}

// A stencil AUC is usable iff finite and > 0 (0.0 is m5_simulate_auc's
// failure value).
fn m5_solve_ok(auc: f64) -> bool {
    return m5_finite(auc) && auc > 0.0
}

fn m5_simulate_auc(prm: PBPKParams28, dose_mg: f64, t_end: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var st = pbpk28_state_zero()
    var led = pbpk28_ledger_zero()
    if !m5_simulate_ledger(prm, dose_mg, t_end, &!st, &!led) { return 0.0 }
    let auc = led.auc[0]
    if !m5_finite(auc) { return 0.0 }
    return auc
}

fn m5_step(mean: f64, variance: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let h_rel = 1.0e-4 * m5_abs(mean)
    let h_abs = 0.02 * m5_sqrt(variance)
    m5_max(h_rel, h_abs)
}

pub fn extract_pbpk28_derivatives(
    base_prm: PBPKParams28,
    priors:   EpPrior28,
    dose_mg:  f64,
    t_end:    f64,
) -> DerivativeBudget with Mut, Div, Panic, Epistemic {
    let n = priors.n
    var out = m5_derivatives_zero()
    let f0 = m5_simulate_auc(base_prm, dose_mg, t_end)
    if f0 <= 0.0 || !m5_finite(f0) { return out }

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let h = m5_step(priors.kn[i].value, priors.kn[i].variance)
        if h > 0.0 {
            let f_p1 = m5_simulate_auc(m5_perturb(base_prm, i, h), dose_mg, t_end)
            let f_n1 = m5_simulate_auc(m5_perturb(base_prm, i, 0.0 - h), dose_mg, t_end)
            let f_p2 = m5_simulate_auc(m5_perturb(base_prm, i, 2.0 * h), dose_mg, t_end)
            let f_n2 = m5_simulate_auc(m5_perturb(base_prm, i, 0.0 - 2.0 * h), dose_mg, t_end)
            // m5_simulate_auc returns 0.0 for a rejected trajectory (see
            // pbpk28_bolus_run_mut); one rejected stencil solve fails the
            // whole budget rather than entering the quotients as 0.
            if !m5_solve_ok(f_p1) || !m5_solve_ok(f_n1) || !m5_solve_ok(f_p2) || !m5_solve_ok(f_n2) {
                return m5_derivatives_zero()
            }
            out.d1[i] = (0.0 - f_p2 + 8.0 * f_p1 - 8.0 * f_n1 + f_n2) / (12.0 * h)
            out.d2[i] = (0.0 - f_p2 + 16.0 * f_p1 - 30.0 * f0 + 16.0 * f_n1 - f_n2) / (12.0 * h * h)
            out.d3[i] = (f_p2 - 2.0 * f_p1 + 2.0 * f_n1 - f_n2) / (2.0 * h * h * h)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    out.success = true
    return out
}

// AUC = D/(CL*V) analytical validation helper, independent of PBPK runtime.
pub fn extract_auc_inverse_derivatives(dose: f64, cl: f64, v: f64, h: f64) -> DerivativeBudget with Div {
    var out = m5_derivatives_zero()
    let f0 = dose / (cl * v)
    let fp1 = dose / ((cl + h) * v)
    let fn1 = dose / ((cl - h) * v)
    let fp2 = dose / ((cl + 2.0 * h) * v)
    let fn2 = dose / ((cl - 2.0 * h) * v)
    out.d1[0] = (0.0 - fp2 + 8.0 * fp1 - 8.0 * fn1 + fn2) / (12.0 * h)
    out.d2[0] = (0.0 - fp2 + 16.0 * fp1 - 30.0 * f0 + 16.0 * fn1 - fn2) / (12.0 * h * h)
    out.d3[0] = (fp2 - 2.0 * fp1 + 2.0 * fn1 - fn2) / (2.0 * h * h * h)
    out.success = true
    return out
}

// ============================================================================
// FOURTH-ORDER VARIANCE BUDGET
// ============================================================================

pub struct VarianceBudget4th {
    u_1st:               f64,
    u_2nd_hessian:       f64,
    u_2nd_skewness:      f64,
    u_4th_kurtosis:      f64,
    u_4th_cubic:         f64,
    u_total:             f64,
    var_1st:             f64,
    var_hessian:         f64,
    var_skewness:        f64,
    var_kurtosis:        f64,
    var_cubic:           f64,
    var_total:           f64,
    rel_hess_residual:   f64,
    rel_fourth_residual: f64,
    dominant_index:      i32,
    success:             bool,
}

fn m5_variance_zero() -> VarianceBudget4th {
    VarianceBudget4th {
        u_1st: 0.0, u_2nd_hessian: 0.0, u_2nd_skewness: 0.0,
        u_4th_kurtosis: 0.0, u_4th_cubic: 0.0, u_total: 0.0,
        var_1st: 0.0, var_hessian: 0.0, var_skewness: 0.0,
        var_kurtosis: 0.0, var_cubic: 0.0, var_total: 0.0,
        rel_hess_residual: 0.0, rel_fourth_residual: 0.0,
        dominant_index: 0, success: false,
    }
}

pub fn variance_budget_4th(
    derivatives: DerivativeBudget,
    priors:      EpPrior28,
    u_mc:        f64,
) -> VarianceBudget4th with Mut, Div, Panic, Epistemic {
    var out = m5_variance_zero()
    if !derivatives.success { return out }
    let n = priors.n

    var i: i32 = 0
    var max_abs_corr: f64 = 0.0
    while i < n {
        let c = derivatives.d1[i]
        let d = derivatives.d2[i]
        let e = derivatives.d3[i]
        let lc = lognormal_cumulants_from_mean_variance(priors.kn[i].value, priors.kn[i].variance)
        let v = lc.variance
        let k3 = lc.kappa3
        let k4 = lc.kappa4
        let central4 = lc.central4

        let v1 = c * c * v
        let v_skew = c * d * k3
        let v_kurt = 0.25 * d * d * (k4 + 2.0 * v * v)
        let v_cubic = (c * e * central4) / 3.0

        out.var_1st = out.var_1st + v1
        out.var_skewness = out.var_skewness + v_skew
        out.var_kurtosis = out.var_kurtosis + v_kurt
        out.var_cubic = out.var_cubic + v_cubic

        let abs_corr = m5_abs(v_skew) + m5_abs(v_kurt) + m5_abs(v_cubic)
        if abs_corr > max_abs_corr {
            max_abs_corr = abs_corr
            out.dominant_index = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    out.var_hessian = out.var_1st + out.var_kurtosis
    out.var_total = out.var_1st + out.var_skewness + out.var_kurtosis + out.var_cubic
    if out.var_total < 0.0 {
        // A truncated asymptotic expansion can go negative when skew/cubic
        // terms dominate.  Keep the signed variance in var_total, but avoid
        // returning NaN for u_total.
        out.u_total = 0.0
    } else {
        out.u_total = m5_sqrt(out.var_total)
    }
    out.u_1st = m5_sqrt(out.var_1st)
    out.u_2nd_hessian = m5_sqrt(out.var_hessian)
    out.u_2nd_skewness = if out.var_skewness >= 0.0 { m5_sqrt(out.var_skewness) } else { 0.0 - m5_sqrt(0.0 - out.var_skewness) }
    out.u_4th_kurtosis = if out.var_kurtosis >= 0.0 { m5_sqrt(out.var_kurtosis) } else { 0.0 - m5_sqrt(0.0 - out.var_kurtosis) }
    out.u_4th_cubic = if out.var_cubic >= 0.0 { m5_sqrt(out.var_cubic) } else { 0.0 - m5_sqrt(0.0 - out.var_cubic) }

    if u_mc > 1.0e-12 {
        out.rel_hess_residual = m5_abs(out.u_2nd_hessian - u_mc) / u_mc
        out.rel_fourth_residual = m5_abs(out.u_total - u_mc) / u_mc
    }
    out.success = true
    return out
}

pub fn variance_budget_4th_from_hessian(
    derivatives: DerivativeBudget,
    hessian:     Pbpk28HessianBudget,
    priors:      EpPrior28,
    u_mc:        f64,
) -> VarianceBudget4th with Mut, Div, Panic, Epistemic {
    var out = m5_variance_zero()
    if !derivatives.success || !hessian.success { return out }
    let n = priors.n

    out.var_1st = hessian.var_first_order
    out.var_hessian = hessian.var_second_order

    var i: i32 = 0
    var max_abs_corr: f64 = 0.0
    while i < n {
        let c = hessian.sensitivity[i]
        let d = hessian.hessian[i * 8 + i]
        let e = derivatives.d3[i]
        let lc = lognormal_cumulants_from_mean_variance(priors.kn[i].value, priors.kn[i].variance)
        let k3 = lc.kappa3
        let k4 = lc.kappa4
        let central4 = lc.central4

        let v_skew = c * d * k3
        let v_extra_kurt = 0.25 * d * d * k4
        let v_cubic = (c * e * central4) / 3.0

        out.var_skewness = out.var_skewness + v_skew
        out.var_kurtosis = out.var_kurtosis + v_extra_kurt
        out.var_cubic = out.var_cubic + v_cubic

        let abs_corr = m5_abs(v_skew) + m5_abs(v_extra_kurt) + m5_abs(v_cubic)
        if abs_corr > max_abs_corr {
            max_abs_corr = abs_corr
            out.dominant_index = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    out.var_total = out.var_hessian + out.var_skewness + out.var_kurtosis + out.var_cubic
    if out.var_total < 0.0 {
        out.u_total = 0.0
    } else {
        out.u_total = m5_sqrt(out.var_total)
    }
    out.u_1st = m5_sqrt(out.var_1st)
    out.u_2nd_hessian = m5_sqrt(out.var_hessian)
    out.u_2nd_skewness = if out.var_skewness >= 0.0 { m5_sqrt(out.var_skewness) } else { 0.0 - m5_sqrt(0.0 - out.var_skewness) }
    out.u_4th_kurtosis = if out.var_kurtosis >= 0.0 { m5_sqrt(out.var_kurtosis) } else { 0.0 - m5_sqrt(0.0 - out.var_kurtosis) }
    out.u_4th_cubic = if out.var_cubic >= 0.0 { m5_sqrt(out.var_cubic) } else { 0.0 - m5_sqrt(0.0 - out.var_cubic) }

    if u_mc > 1.0e-12 {
        out.rel_hess_residual = m5_abs(out.u_2nd_hessian - u_mc) / u_mc
        out.rel_fourth_residual = m5_abs(out.u_total - u_mc) / u_mc
    }
    out.success = true
    return out
}

// M6 canonical MC truth: u_MC of AUC_blood(0-168 h) from
// validation/pbpk28_mc_cross_validation.sio (LogNormal priors, N=2000,
// seed=1729, dt=0.5 h). Re-derived 2026-09-26 after that module moved off the
// floored CN kernel: 0.357945 -> 0.211790 mg·h/L (lean_single run). The old
// value is the one docs/dissertation/results/m6_prior_update_v1.md records;
// it carried the +140% floor bias of the dt=0.5 h kernel.
pub fn m5_pbpk28_u_mc_canonical() -> f64 { return 0.211790 }

pub fn m5_pbpk28_convergence_budget() -> VarianceBudget4th with Mut, Div, Panic, Epistemic {
    let prm = ep28_rapamycin_params()
    let priors = ep28_rapamycin_priors()
    let der = extract_pbpk28_derivatives(prm, priors, 5.0, 168.0)
    let hess = hessian_pbpk28_auc(prm, priors, 5.0, 168.0)
    variance_budget_4th_from_hessian(der, hess, priors, m5_pbpk28_u_mc_canonical())
}

pub fn m5_pbpk28_second_order_reference() -> Pbpk28HessianBudget with Mut, Div, Panic, Epistemic {
    hessian_pbpk28_auc(ep28_rapamycin_params(), ep28_rapamycin_priors(), 5.0, 168.0)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/ddi/mechanistic_ddi.sio ===
// mechanistic_ddi.sio — Darwin PBPK mechanistic_ddi module
// Rewritten in Sounio syntax

fn dpbpk_mechanistic_ddi_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 { term = term * x / (i as f64); result = result + term; i = i + 1 }
    result
}

fn dpbpk_mechanistic_ddi_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn dpbpk_mechanistic_ddi_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn dpbpk_mechanistic_ddi_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn dpbpk_mechanistic_ddi_clamp(x: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 { if x < lo { lo } else if x > hi { hi } else { x } }

struct Mechanistic_ddi_State {
    concentration: f64,
    flow_in: f64,
    flow_out: f64,
    volume: f64,
    kp: f64,
}

fn mechanistic_ddi_state_new(vol: f64, kp: f64) -> Mechanistic_ddi_State {
    Mechanistic_ddi_State { concentration: 0.0, flow_in: 0.0, flow_out: 0.0, volume: vol, kp: kp }
}

fn mechanistic_ddi_compute_flux(c_arterial: f64, c_tissue: f64, kp: f64, blood_flow: f64) -> f64 {
    blood_flow * (c_arterial - c_tissue / kp)
}

fn mechanistic_ddi_update(state: Mechanistic_ddi_State, c_arterial: f64, blood_flow: f64, dt: f64) -> Mechanistic_ddi_State with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let flux = mechanistic_ddi_compute_flux(c_arterial, state.concentration, state.kp, blood_flow)
    var new_state = state
    new_state.concentration = state.concentration + dt * flux / state.volume
    if new_state.concentration < 0.0 { new_state.concentration = 0.0 }
    new_state.flow_in = dpbpk_mechanistic_ddi_max(flux, 0.0)
    new_state.flow_out = dpbpk_mechanistic_ddi_abs(dpbpk_mechanistic_ddi_min(flux, 0.0))
    new_state
}

fn test_mechanistic_ddi_flux_positive() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let flux = mechanistic_ddi_compute_flux(10.0, 5.0, 2.0, 90.0)
    flux > 0.0
}

fn test_mechanistic_ddi_zero_init() -> bool {
    let s = mechanistic_ddi_state_new(1.5, 5.0)
    s.concentration == 0.0 && s.volume == 1.5
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/ddi/polypharmacy_fano.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/ddi/polypharmacy_fano.sio — 168-Theorem Psychiatric Polypharmacy Gate
//
// The 168-theorem (Agourakis & Gerenutti 2026): of 343 ordered CYP enzyme triples,
// 168 are non-associative — drug administration ORDER changes the net DDI outcome.
// The Fano plane structure over the 7 CYP450 isoforms predicts which triples show
// order-dependent vs order-independent drug-drug interactions.
//
// Psychiatric triple: olanzapine (CYP1A2=1) × haloperidol (CYP2D6=6) × carbamazepine (CYP3A4=7)
// Fano elements (1, 6, 7) — NOT on any Fano line → Fano predicts non-associative.
//
// Mechanistic cascade model:
//   When drug A is prescribed BEFORE drug B, A inhibits B's CYP pathway, elevating [B].
//   Elevated [B] then more strongly inhibits drug C's CYP pathway.
//   → The net DDI burden on C is HIGHER when A precedes B than when B precedes A.
//   This ordering effect is large for non-Fano triples, negligible for Fano-line triples.
//
// Associativity definition (DDI analogue of octonion associativity):
//   Does the DDI boost on drug C change if we swap the prescription order of A and B?
//   For Fano-line triple: |boost[A,B,C] - boost[B,A,C]| < eps  (approximately associative)
//   For non-Fano triple:  |boost[A,B,C] - boost[B,A,C]| ≥ eps  (non-associative)
//
// Boost model reuses ddi_f_boost from tacrolimus_sirolimus_ddi.sio:
//   delta_F = R_max × [inhibitor] / (Ki + [inhibitor])
//
// References:
//   Agourakis & Gerenutti (2026): The 168 Theorem. AACA (submitted)
//   Olanzapine CYP2D6 inhibition Ki: Callaghan 1999 Clin Pharmacokinet (~30-50 ng/mL)
//   Haloperidol CYP3A4 inhibition Ki: Desta 2001 Drug Metab Dispos (~10-15 ng/mL estimate)
//   cyp450_fano.sio lines 70-80: Fano line (6,7,2) and interpretation

use medical::cyp450_fano::{is_on_fano_line}
use darwin_pbpk::ddi::tacrolimus_sirolimus_ddi::{ddi_f_boost}

// ============================================================================
// STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

pub struct CypDDITriple {
    cyp_a:  i32,    // Fano element for drug A's primary CYP (1–7)
    cyp_b:  i32,    // Fano element for drug B's primary CYP
    cyp_c:  i32,    // Fano element for drug C's primary CYP (target/victim drug)
    ki_ab:  f64,    // Ki (ng/mL): drug A inhibits drug B's CYP pathway
    ki_bc:  f64,    // Ki (ng/mL): drug B inhibits drug C's CYP pathway
    ki_ac:  f64,    // Ki (ng/mL): drug A inhibits drug C's CYP pathway (direct)
    rmax:   f64,    // Emax for inhibition fraction (reference: Undre 1999 = 0.30)
}

// ============================================================================
// DDI Ki LOOKUP
// ============================================================================

// Returns Ki (ng/mL) for drug 'inhibitor' (0=A, 1=B, 2=C) inhibiting 'target's CYP.
// Directed model: only A→B, A→C, B→C have specified Ki values.
// All reverse directions (B→A, C→A, C→B) use Ki=1000 (clinically negligible).
fn pair_ki(triple: CypDDITriple, inhibitor: i32, target: i32) -> f64 {
    if inhibitor == 0 && target == 1 { return triple.ki_ab }
    if inhibitor == 0 && target == 2 { return triple.ki_ac }
    if inhibitor == 1 && target == 2 { return triple.ki_bc }
    return 1000.0
}

// ============================================================================
// CORE: SEQUENTIAL DDI CASCADE ON DRUG C
// ============================================================================

// Computes the net DDI boost accumulated by drug C (index 2) given a prescription
// ordering of the three drugs.
//
// order[k] ∈ {0=A, 1=B, 2=C} specifies which drug is prescribed at step k.
//
// Cascade logic:
//   (1) If drug A is prescribed before drug B, A inhibits B's CYP pathway:
//         c_eff_b = c_b × (1 + ddi_f_boost(rmax, ki_ab, c_a))
//       This elevates drug B's effective concentration (and thus its inhibitory potency).
//   (2) The boost on drug C = sum of contributions from each drug prescribed before C:
//         boost_from_A = ddi_f_boost(rmax, ki_ac, c_a)        [if A prescribed before C]
//         boost_from_B = ddi_f_boost(rmax, ki_bc, c_eff_b)    [if B prescribed before C]
//
// Non-commutativity: when A precedes B, c_eff_b > c_b → B's boost on C is larger.
pub fn ddi_sequence_inhib(triple: CypDDITriple, order: [i32; 3],
                           c_a: f64, c_b: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // Find position of each drug in the sequence
    var a_pos = 3
    var b_pos = 3
    var c_pos = 3
    var s = 0
    while s < 3 {
        if order[s] == 0 { a_pos = s }
        if order[s] == 1 { b_pos = s }
        if order[s] == 2 { c_pos = s }
        s = s + 1
    }

    // Effective concentration of B: elevated if A was prescribed first
    var c_eff_b = c_b
    if a_pos < b_pos {
        let boost_ab = ddi_f_boost(triple.rmax, triple.ki_ab, c_a)
        c_eff_b = c_b * (1.0 + boost_ab)
    }

    // Accumulate boost on C from drugs prescribed before it
    var boost_c = 0.0
    if a_pos < c_pos {
        boost_c = boost_c + ddi_f_boost(triple.rmax, triple.ki_ac, c_a)
    }
    if b_pos < c_pos {
        boost_c = boost_c + ddi_f_boost(triple.rmax, triple.ki_bc, c_eff_b)
    }

    boost_c
}

// ============================================================================
// ASSOCIATIVITY CHECK
// ============================================================================

// Returns true if the DDI cascade is approximately order-independent within eps.
// Compares orderings [A first, B second, C third] vs [B first, A second, C third].
// Both have C last; only the ordering of A and B is swapped.
//
// For Fano-line triples (symmetric or weak Ki): |diff| < eps → "associative"
// For non-Fano triples (asymmetric Ki with cascade): |diff| ≥ eps → "non-associative"
pub fn ddi_is_associative(triple: CypDDITriple, c_a: f64, c_b: f64, eps: f64)
    -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut
{
    var ord_abc: [i32; 3] = [0; 3]
    ord_abc[0] = 0
    ord_abc[1] = 1
    ord_abc[2] = 2

    var ord_bac: [i32; 3] = [0; 3]
    ord_bac[0] = 1
    ord_bac[1] = 0
    ord_bac[2] = 2

    let net_abc = ddi_sequence_inhib(triple, ord_abc, c_a, c_b)
    let net_bac = ddi_sequence_inhib(triple, ord_bac, c_a, c_b)
    let diff = if net_abc > net_bac { net_abc - net_bac } else { net_bac - net_abc }
    diff < eps
}

// ============================================================================
// CLINICAL TRIPLES
// ============================================================================

// Olanzapine × Haloperidol × Carbamazepine
// CYP mapping: olanzapine=CYP1A2 (e1), haloperidol=CYP2D6 (e6), carbamazepine=CYP3A4 (e7)
// Fano triple (1, 6, 7): NOT on any Fano line → Fano predicts non-associative.
//
// Ki parameters (directed model):
//   ki_ab: olanzapine inhibits CYP2D6 (haloperidol pathway). Ki≈30 ng/mL (Callaghan 1999).
//   ki_bc: haloperidol inhibits CYP3A4 (carbamazepine pathway). Ki≈10 ng/mL (Desta 2001 est.)
//   ki_ac: olanzapine inhibits CYP1A2 via carbamazepine pathway. Ki≈200 ng/mL (very weak).
pub fn olanz_halo_carbamazepine_triple() -> CypDDITriple {
    CypDDITriple {
        cyp_a:  1,
        cyp_b:  6,
        cyp_c:  7,
        ki_ab:  30.0,
        ki_bc:  10.0,
        ki_ac:  200.0,
        rmax:   0.30,
    }
}

// CYP2C gene cluster: CYP2C9 × CYP2C8 × CYP2C19 = (2, 3, 5)
// ON Fano line (2,3,5) → Fano predicts associative (shared substrate chemistry,
// same chromosome 10 gene cluster, highly overlapping substrate profiles).
// All cross-inhibitions within the CYP2C family are weak and bidirectional.
// Large Ki values (200 ng/mL) reflect low cross-inhibition potency within family.
pub fn cyp2c_cluster_triple() -> CypDDITriple {
    CypDDITriple {
        cyp_a:  2,
        cyp_b:  3,
        cyp_c:  5,
        ki_ab:  200.0,
        ki_bc:  200.0,
        ki_ac:  200.0,
        rmax:   0.30,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FANO STRUCTURAL PREDICTOR
// ============================================================================

// Returns true if the Fano plane structure predicts non-associative DDI for this triple.
// This is the algebraic compile-time check — pure structural; no PK calculation required.
// Rationale: non-Fano triples span different CYP families with asymmetric substrate
// overlap, enabling cascade inhibition amplification that depends on prescription order.
pub fn ddi_fano_predicts_nonassoc(a: i32, b: i32, c: i32) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if is_on_fano_line(a, b, c) { return false }
    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN
// ============================================================================

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    println("polypharmacy_fano: 168-theorem DDI non-associativity gate")

    let triple_na = olanz_halo_carbamazepine_triple()
    let triple_fa = cyp2c_cluster_triple()

    // Structural check
    let pred_na = ddi_fano_predicts_nonassoc(triple_na.cyp_a, triple_na.cyp_b, triple_na.cyp_c)
    let pred_fa = ddi_fano_predicts_nonassoc(triple_fa.cyp_a, triple_fa.cyp_b, triple_fa.cyp_c)
    if pred_na  { println("  (1,6,7): Fano NONASSOC prediction OK") }
    if pred_fa  { println("  (2,3,5): Fano NONASSOC prediction UNEXPECTED") }
    if pred_na == false { println("  (1,6,7): Fano ASSOC prediction UNEXPECTED") }
    if pred_fa == false { println("  (2,3,5): Fano ASSOC prediction OK") }

    // Empirical check
    let c_a: f64 = 20.0
    let c_b: f64 = 5.0
    let assoc_na = ddi_is_associative(triple_na, c_a, c_b, 0.001)
    let assoc_fa = ddi_is_associative(triple_fa, c_a, c_b, 0.001)
    if assoc_na        { println("  (1,6,7) empirical: ASSOCIATIVE — unexpected") }
    if assoc_na == false { println("  (1,6,7) empirical: NON-ASSOCIATIVE — correct") }
    if assoc_fa        { println("  (2,3,5) empirical: ASSOCIATIVE — correct") }
    if assoc_fa == false { println("  (2,3,5) empirical: NON-ASSOCIATIVE — unexpected") }

    if pred_na && assoc_na == false && pred_fa == false && assoc_fa {
        println("PASS")
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/ddi/tacrolimus_sirolimus_ddi.sio ===
// stdlib/darwin_pbpk/ddi/tacrolimus_sirolimus_ddi.sio
//
// Mechanistic drug-drug interaction (DDI) between tacrolimus (oral
// CYP3A4 / P-gp substrate) and sirolimus (also CYP3A4 / P-gp substrate;
// the Cypher drug-eluting stent payload). Sirolimus inhibits intestinal
// P-gp efflux, raising the apparent bioavailability of tacrolimus.
//
// This DDI is the canonical post-transplant interaction studied in
// Undre 1999 (Transplant Proc 31:1305, n=12). It illustrates a
// qualitatively distinct GUM source — one that cannot be reduced by
// improved analytical chemistry, only by a separate drug-drug
// pharmacokinetic study. This is the dissertation's "irreducible
// epistemic floor" argument.
//
// Mechanistic model (single-dose, intestinal P-gp competitive inhibition):
//
//   delta_F([S]) = R_max · [S] / (K_i + [S])
//   F_combo([S]) = F_baseline · (1 + delta_F([S]))
//
// Parameter priors (with literature confidence):
//
//   R_max = 0.30   (max fractional F boost; Undre 1999 n=12)
//   K_i   = 5 ng/mL (P-gp inhibition constant; Lampen 1998 Caco-2 in vitro)
//
//   Confidence(R_max) = 0.45 — single n=12 in vivo PK study
//   Confidence(K_i)   = 0.40 — in vitro extrapolation
//
// Epistemic uncertainty on delta_F:
//   u(delta_F) / delta_F = 0.40 (40% CV from the single-study floor)
//
// All combined-F propagation uses the Fréchet outer enclosure pattern
// already proved sound in formal/lean4/SounioFrechet.lean
// (`pb_apply2_monotone_inc_dec` and `pb_apply2_monotone_inc_inc`).
//
// Monotonicity hand-derivation:
//   ∂delta_F / ∂R_max = [S] / (K_i + [S])           > 0 ∀ [S] > 0
//   ∂delta_F / ∂K_i   = − R_max · [S] / (K_i+[S])²  < 0 ∀ [S] > 0
//   → corner enclosure: delta_F at (R_max_lo, K_i_hi) and (R_max_hi, K_i_lo)
//
//   ∂F_combo / ∂F_baseline = 1 + delta_F                > 0 (delta_F ≥ 0)
//   ∂F_combo / ∂delta_F     = F_baseline                 > 0
//   → corner enclosure inc-inc on (F_baseline, delta_F).
//
// Lean obligation: formal/lean4/SounioTacrolimusDDI.lean.

use darwin_pbpk::ddi::mechanistic_ddi::*
use epistemic::knightian::*

// ============================================================================
// POINT-WISE DDI FUNCTIONS (used inline by the PBox enclosure)
// ============================================================================

pub fn ddi_f_boost(r_max: f64, ki_ng_ml: f64, c_siro_ng_ml: f64)
    -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    if c_siro_ng_ml < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let denom = ki_ng_ml + c_siro_ng_ml
    if denom <= 1.0e-12 { return 0.0 }
    r_max * c_siro_ng_ml / denom
}

pub fn ddi_f_boost_uncertainty(r_max: f64, ki_ng_ml: f64, c_siro_ng_ml: f64)
    -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    // 40% CV of the single-study floor: u(delta_F) = 0.40 · delta_F.
    let d = ddi_f_boost(r_max, ki_ng_ml, c_siro_ng_ml)
    let abs_d = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    0.40 * abs_d
}

// ============================================================================
// DDI PARAMETER PRIORS — population means and variance bands
// ============================================================================
// 30% boost is the Undre 1999 central estimate; ±50% CV bracket captures
// the 15–45% range observed in subsequent literature (Hodge 2004,
// Cattaneo 2008 cohort studies).

fn ddi_r_max_mean() -> f64 { 0.30 }
fn ddi_r_max_band() -> f64 { 0.50 }   // ±50% on R_max

fn ddi_ki_mean() -> f64 { 5.0 }       // ng/mL, Lampen 1998
fn ddi_ki_band() -> f64 { 0.60 }      // ±60% on Ki (in vitro extrapolation)

pub fn ddi_r_max_pbox() -> PBox {
    let m = ddi_r_max_mean()
    let b = ddi_r_max_band()
    let lo = (1.0 - b) * m
    let hi = (1.0 + b) * m
    let v = 0.25 * m * m
    pb_new(lo, hi, v, 450)
}

pub fn ddi_ki_pbox() -> PBox {
    let m = ddi_ki_mean()
    let b = ddi_ki_band()
    let lo = (1.0 - b) * m
    let hi = (1.0 + b) * m
    let v = 0.36 * m * m
    pb_new(lo, hi, v, 400)
}

// ============================================================================
// DELTA_F PBOX — Fréchet enclosure on (R_max, K_i) for fixed [S].
// ============================================================================
// Inline corner enumeration; equivalent to pb_apply2_monotone_inc_dec.

pub fn ddi_delta_f_pbox(c_siro_ng_ml: f64) -> PBox with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if c_siro_ng_ml <= 0.0 { return pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 500) }
    let r_pb = ddi_r_max_pbox()
    let k_pb = ddi_ki_pbox()
    // ∂delta_F/∂R_max > 0, ∂delta_F/∂K_i < 0 ⇒
    //   delta_F_min at (R_max_lo, K_i_hi)
    //   delta_F_max at (R_max_hi, K_i_lo)
    let lo = ddi_f_boost(pb_lo_mean(&r_pb), pb_hi_mean(&k_pb), c_siro_ng_ml)
    let hi = ddi_f_boost(pb_hi_mean(&r_pb), pb_lo_mean(&k_pb), c_siro_ng_ml)
    let v = ddi_f_boost_uncertainty(ddi_r_max_mean(), ddi_ki_mean(), c_siro_ng_ml)
    let conf_r = pb_confidence(&r_pb)
    let conf_k = pb_confidence(&k_pb)
    let conf = if conf_r < conf_k { conf_r } else { conf_k }
    pb_new(lo, hi, v * v, conf)
}

// ============================================================================
// COMBINED F_oral PBOX — Fréchet enclosure on (F_baseline, delta_F).
// ============================================================================
// F_combo = F_baseline · (1 + delta_F), monotone INC in both arguments.
// Inline corner enumeration (inc-inc): F_combo_lo at (F_lo, d_lo),
// F_combo_hi at (F_hi, d_hi).

pub fn ddi_combined_f_knightian(f_baseline_pbox: &PBox, c_siro_ng_ml: f64)
    -> PBox with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let d_pb = ddi_delta_f_pbox(c_siro_ng_ml)
    let f_lo = pb_lo_mean(f_baseline_pbox)
    let f_hi = pb_hi_mean(f_baseline_pbox)
    let d_lo = pb_lo_mean(&d_pb)
    let d_hi = pb_hi_mean(&d_pb)
    let combo_lo = f_lo * (1.0 + d_lo)
    let combo_hi = f_hi * (1.0 + d_hi)
    // Bioavailability cannot exceed 1; clamp the upper bound for the gate.
    var clo = combo_lo
    var chi = combo_hi
    if clo < 0.0 { clo = 0.0 }
    if chi > 1.0 { chi = 1.0 }
    let v = pb_variance(f_baseline_pbox) + pb_variance(&d_pb)
    let conf_f = pb_confidence(f_baseline_pbox)
    let conf_d = pb_confidence(&d_pb)
    let conf = if conf_f < conf_d { conf_f } else { conf_d }
    pb_new(clo, chi, v, conf)
}

// ============================================================================
// SELF-TESTS
// ============================================================================

pub fn test_ddi_zero_siro_no_boost() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let pb = ddi_delta_f_pbox(0.0)
    let m = (pb_lo_mean(&pb) + pb_hi_mean(&pb)) * 0.5
    let abs_m = if m < 0.0 { 0.0 - m } else { m }
    abs_m < 1.0e-6
}

pub fn test_ddi_monotone_in_siro() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = ddi_r_max_mean()
    let k = ddi_ki_mean()
    let d_lo = ddi_f_boost(r, k, 1.0)
    let d_hi = ddi_f_boost(r, k, 20.0)
    d_lo < d_hi
}

pub fn test_ddi_combined_inflates_f() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // At therapeutic sirolimus [S] = 12 ng/mL (Sousa 2003), the central
    // F_oral boost should be approximately 30% · 12/(5+12) ≈ 21%.
    let r = ddi_r_max_mean()
    let k = ddi_ki_mean()
    let d = ddi_f_boost(r, k, 12.0)
    d > 0.15 && d < 0.30
}

pub fn test_ddi_combined_pbox_wider() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Co-administration PBox must be at least as wide as baseline.
    let baseline = pb_new(0.20, 0.30, 0.04, 700)
    let combo = ddi_combined_f_knightian(&baseline, 12.0)
    let gap_base = pb_gap(&baseline)
    let gap_combo = pb_gap(&combo)
    gap_combo >= gap_base
}

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var passed = 0
    var failed = 0
    if test_ddi_zero_siro_no_boost() { passed = passed + 1 } else { failed = failed + 1 }
    if test_ddi_monotone_in_siro() { passed = passed + 1 } else { failed = failed + 1 }
    if test_ddi_combined_inflates_f() { passed = passed + 1 } else { failed = failed + 1 }
    if test_ddi_combined_pbox_wider() { passed = passed + 1 } else { failed = failed + 1 }
    print("ddi self-tests passed: "); println(passed)
    if failed == 0 {
        println("DDI MODULE OK")
    } else {
        println("DDI MODULE FAIL")
    }
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/drugs/haloperidol.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/drugs/haloperidol.sio — Haloperidol Systemic PBPK + BBB Parameters
//
// Physiological and transport parameters for haloperidol at the BBB,
// formatted for the darwin_pbpk bbb_core.sio framework (BBBParams / BBBPriors).
//
// Haloperidol pharmacological identity:
//   - First-generation antipsychotic (Janssen 1958); butyrophenone class
//   - High D2 selectivity: Kd ~1.5 nM (Seeman 1976, radioligand binding)
//   - Basic drug: pKa = 8.7; extensive lysosomal trapping in brain cells
//   - High lipophilicity: LogP ≈ 4.0 → high passive BBB permeability (PS_bbb >> rapamycin)
//   - P-gp substrate (Schinkel 1996) but net ACCUMULATION in brain (Kpuu,brain ~3)
//     because lysosomal trapping > P-gp efflux — the opposite of rapamycin.
//   - Strong protein binding: fu_plasma ≈ 0.08 (Haase 1981)
//   - Therapeutic window: D2 occupancy 60-80% (Farde 1992 PET)
//   - EPS onset: D2 occupancy > 80%
//
// The key contrast with rapamycin:
//   Rapamycin:   Kpuu_brain = 0.15 (efflux-dominated, P-gp wins)
//   Haloperidol: Kpuu_brain = 3.0  (accumulation; lysosomal trap > P-gp efflux)
//
// Literature:
//   - Loryan I et al. (2014) J Pharm Sci 103:3145  [Kpuu_brain rat ~3]
//   - Haase D et al. (1981) Arzneimittelforschung   [fu_plasma 0.08]
//   - Schinkel AH et al. (1996) Science 274:1630    [P-gp substrate]
//   - Gaohua L et al. (2016) Drug Metab Pharmacokinet 31:224  [BBB PS class]
//   - Kamiie J et al. (2008) Pharm Res 25:1544      [QTAP P-gp mouse]
//   - Uchida Y et al. (2011) Mol Pharm 8:2163       [human P-gp 6.06 fmol/µg]
//   - Zhu Z et al. (2026) Science doi:10.1126/science.aea2100 [luminal surface]

use darwin_pbpk::absorption::{AbsorptionParams}
use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_core::{BBBParams}
use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_priors::{BBBPriors}
use darwin_pbpk::tsit5_pbpk14::{PBPKParams14}

// ============================================================================
// MEAN PARAMETERS (BBBParams)
// ============================================================================
// Volumes: Davies & Morris 1993 (brain compartments, 70 kg adult)
// q_brain: cerebral blood flow (anatomical reference, not used in BBB ODE)
// ps_bbb: lipophilic drug class (Gaohua 2016), higher than rapamycin (PS=0.30)
// ps_mem: lipophilic basic drug; lysosomal compartment adds apparent ICF load
// fu values: class estimates (Loryan 2014); no direct haloperidol
//   brain microdialysis protein binding data found in primary literature.
// kpuu_brain = 3.0 (Loryan 2014 Table 2, rat haloperidol Kp,uu in vivo)
// kpuu_cell  = 0.5 (slight ICF depletion of free drug; lysosomal sequestration
//   traps protonated form, so FREE concentration in cytoplasm is below ISF)

pub fn haloperidol_bbb_params() -> BBBParams {
    BBBParams {
        v_vasc:     0.013,
        v_isf:      0.270,
        v_icf:      1.080,
        q_brain:    50.0,
        ps_bbb:     2.0,
        ps_mem:     8.0,
        fu_plasma:  0.08,
        fu_isf:     0.035,
        fu_icf:     0.010,
        kpuu_brain: 3.0,
        kpuu_cell:  0.5,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC PRIORS (BBBPriors, 7-parameter)
// ============================================================================
// Follows the same index ordering as bbb_priors.sio (rapamycin):
//   0: ps_bbb, 1: ps_mem, 2: kpuu_brain, 3: kpuu_cell,
//   4: fu_plasma, 5: fu_isf, 6: fu_icf
//
// Confidence rationale uses the same scale as bbb_rapamycin_priors():
//   0.20-0.35: assumption or single structural analogue
//   0.40-0.55: single in vitro or extrapolated in vivo
//   0.55-0.70: single in vivo study, moderate n
//   0.70-0.85: replicated in vivo or measurement-grade wet-lab
//   0.85-0.95: regulatory-submission or meta-analysis grade

pub fn haloperidol_bbb_priors() -> BBBPriors with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var v: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var c: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]

    // 0: ps_bbb (L/h) — effective BBB permeability-surface area.
    // LogP=4 → fast passive influx. Literature PS for basic lipophilic
    // drugs in CNS PBPK: 1-5 L/h (Gaohua 2016 class estimate).
    // Central 2.0 L/h; inter-individual P-gp expression CV ~50%.
    // variance = (2.0 * 0.50)^2 = 1.0
    // confidence = 0.45 (class-level estimate; no direct haloperidol PS measurement)
    m[0] = 2.0;    v[0] = 1.0;       c[0] = 0.45

    // 1: ps_mem (L/h) — cellular membrane permeability-surface area.
    // Lipophilic basic drug; high ps_mem drives lysosomal accumulation.
    // Class estimate 8 L/h; CV ~60%.
    // variance = (8.0 * 0.60)^2 = 23.04
    // confidence = 0.30 (no direct haloperidol brain microdialysis kinetics)
    m[1] = 8.0;    v[1] = 23.04;     c[1] = 0.30

    // 2: kpuu_brain (ISF_unbound / plasma_unbound at SS).
    // Loryan 2014 (J Pharm Sci Table 2): haloperidol rat Kp,uu,brain ≈ 3.
    // Inter-individual variability ~30% (lysosomal pH variability, P-gp expression).
    // Zhu 2026 (Science) confirms P-gp luminal surface localization, adding
    // confidence to the mechanistic framework even without haloperidol-specific
    // quantification (confidence raised 0.55→0.63 analogous to rapamycin kp_brain).
    // variance = (3.0 * 0.30)^2 = 0.81
    // confidence = 0.63 (Loryan 2014 primary source + Zhu 2026 mechanistic confirmation)
    m[2] = 3.0;    v[2] = 0.81;      c[2] = 0.63

    // 3: kpuu_cell (ICF_unbound / ISF_unbound at SS).
    // Lysosomal trapping sequesters protonated haloperidol: total ICF >> ISF,
    // but FREE ICF concentration is BELOW ISF free (trapping reduces free drug).
    // Mean kpuu_cell = 0.5; CV ~50%.
    // variance = (0.5 * 0.50)^2 = 0.0625
    // confidence = 0.25 (no direct subcellular unbound measurement for haloperidol)
    m[3] = 0.5;    v[3] = 0.0625;    c[3] = 0.25

    // 4: fu_plasma — plasma unbound fraction.
    // Haase 1981 (Arzneimittelforschung): ~8% free (92% protein-bound).
    // Replicated across multiple equilibrium dialysis studies. CV ~15%.
    // variance = (0.08 * 0.15)^2 = 1.44e-4
    // confidence = 0.82 (well-characterized wet-lab, multiple sources converge)
    m[4] = 0.08;   v[4] = 0.000144;  c[4] = 0.82

    // 5: fu_isf — brain ISF unbound fraction.
    // Basic drugs bind to ECF proteins (albumin leakage ~0.1-0.3% across BBB,
    // GFAP, non-specific interactions). Estimated 3.5% free.
    // CV ~40% (class estimate, no direct haloperidol brain ECF binding data).
    // variance = (0.035 * 0.40)^2 = 1.96e-4
    // confidence = 0.35 (class estimate; no primary haloperidol brain ECF measurement)
    m[5] = 0.035;  v[5] = 0.000196;  c[5] = 0.35

    // 6: fu_icf — brain ICF unbound fraction.
    // Lower than fu_isf due to lysosomal accumulation and intracellular binding.
    // Mean 1.0%; CV ~50%.
    // variance = (0.010 * 0.50)^2 = 2.5e-5
    // confidence = 0.20 (assumption; no subcellular measurement)
    m[6] = 0.010;  v[6] = 0.000025;  c[6] = 0.20

    BBBPriors { n: 7, mean: m, variance: v, confidence: c }
}

// ============================================================================
// SYSTEMIC PBPK PARAMETERS (PBPKParams14)
// ============================================================================
// Haloperidol mean PK parameters for a 70 kg adult.
//
// MW: 375.86 g/mol
// fu_plasma: 0.08 (Haase 1981; 92% protein-bound, mainly AAG)
// Vd: ~20 L/kg = 1400 L (Forsman & Ohman 1977; extensive tissue distribution)
//   - This large Vd comes from muscle, adipose, and brain accumulation.
//   - Model uses tissue-realistic kp values rather than one depot.
// CL_hepatic: ~40 L/h (~660 mL/min; Forsman 1977, hepatic extraction ~0.7)
//   - CYP3A4/CYP2D6 primary metabolism; large first-pass effect
// t1/2: ~21h (IV; oral apparent t1/2 longer due to distribution)
// Blood:plasma ratio (rb_ratio): 1.0 (moderate AAG binding; negligible RBC partitioning)
//
// Tissue partition coefficients (Kp):
//   Derived from Rodgers-Rowland (basic lipophilic drug, pKa=8.7, LogP=4.0):
//   kp_liver: 18   (high first-pass site; CYP3A4/2D6 metabolic sink)
//   kp_lung:  12   (lipophilic; lung first-pass trapping of basic drug)
//   kp_brain: 15   (extensive accumulation; lysosomal trap in neurons)
//   kp_muscle: 8   (large volume contributor to deep Vd)
//   kp_adipose: 3  (moderate adipose binding vs more lipophilic drugs)
//   Other tissues: scaled by lipophilicity class
//
// Note: q_brain = 44 L/h (physiological; the BBB sub-model handles the
// actual ISF transport via ps_bbb, so systemic brain compartment uses
// the Kp-based perfusion model. BBB is feed-forward decoupled.)
//
// Literature:
//   - Forsman A & Ohman R (1977) Curr Ther Res 21:606  [PK parameters]
//   - Haase D et al. (1981) Arzneimittelforschung      [fu, protein binding]
//   - Cleton A et al. (1999) Pharm Res 16:1582         [tissue distribution]
//   - Midha KK et al. (1989) Psychopharmacology 97:305 [oral SS plasma]

pub fn haloperidol_pbpk_params() -> PBPKParams14 with Mut {
    var prm: PBPKParams14 = PBPKParams14 {
        // Volumes (L) — Davies & Morris 1993 reference human (70 kg)
        v_blood: 5.2, v_liver: 1.69, v_kidney: 0.31, v_brain: 1.37,
        v_heart: 0.31, v_lung: 1.17, v_muscle: 29.0, v_adipose: 18.2,
        v_gut: 1.65, v_skin: 7.8, v_bone: 10.5, v_spleen: 0.19,
        v_pancreas: 0.14, v_other: 4.5,
        // Blood flows (L/h) — Davies & Morris 1993
        q_liver: 87.0, q_kidney: 72.0, q_brain: 44.0, q_heart: 14.4,
        q_lung: 0.0, q_muscle: 73.8, q_adipose: 18.0, q_gut: 57.6,
        q_skin: 18.0, q_bone: 21.6, q_spleen: 10.8, q_pancreas: 4.5,
        q_other: 18.0,
        // Tissue partition coefficients — Rodgers-Rowland method (basic, pKa=8.7, LogP=4.0).
        // Muscle (kp=35) and adipose (kp=12) are the primary Vd drivers:
        //   sum(V_tissue × kp) = ~1468 L → Vd ~ 1400 L/70kg (Forsman 1977, 20 L/kg).
        // kp_brain=15: extensive CNS accumulation (lysosomal trapping in neurons).
        kp_liver: 18.0, kp_kidney: 8.0, kp_brain: 15.0, kp_heart: 6.0,
        kp_lung: 12.0, kp_muscle: 35.0, kp_adipose: 12.0, kp_gut: 6.0,
        kp_skin: 8.0, kp_bone: 6.0, kp_spleen: 8.0, kp_pancreas: 5.0,
        kp_other: 5.0,
        // Clearance (L/h) — hepatic extraction ~70% at liver flow 87 L/h
        cl_hepatic: 40.0,
        cl_renal: 0.5,
        // Binding
        fu_plasma: 0.08,
        rb_ratio: 1.0,
    }
    return prm
}

// ============================================================================
// ORAL ABSORPTION PARAMETERS
// ============================================================================
// Haloperidol oral absorption:
//   Ka: 0.9/h (first-order; Tmax ~2-3h for oral tablet, implies Ka ~0.9)
//   F_bio: 0.65 (65% oral bioavailability; Forsman 1977, first-pass ~35%)
//   tlag: 0.25h (15 min lag — standard tablet dissolution)
//
// Note: despite high hepatic CL (intrinsic ~320 L/h), F=0.65 because
// haloperidol is a moderate first-pass drug (hepatic extraction ratio ~0.35).
// This differs from rapamycin (F=0.14) because haloperidol is not a
// high-affinity CYP3A4 substrate with enterocyte P-gp efflux opposing absorption.
//
// Source: Forsman & Ohman 1977; Froemming et al. (1989) J Clin Psychopharmacol

pub fn haloperidol_absorption_params() -> AbsorptionParams {
    AbsorptionParams { ka: 0.9, f_bio: 0.65, tlag: 0.25 }
}

// ============================================================================
// PGx-ADJUSTED CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================
// These additive constructors derive from the pure parameter fns above and
// apply pharmacogenomic scaling. The existing fns are NOT modified — callers
// that do not need PGx adjustment continue to use haloperidol_pbpk_params().

use darwin_pbpk::pgx::cyp2d6_haloperidol::{halo_cyp2d6_adjusted_cl}
use darwin_pbpk::pgx::abcb1::{abcb1_psbbb_scale}

// CYP2D6-adjusted systemic PBPK params.
// pheno: 0=PM, 1=IM, 2=NM, 3=UM (see pgx/cyp2d6_haloperidol.sio)
pub fn haloperidol_pbpk_params_pgx(pheno: i32) -> PBPKParams14 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var prm = haloperidol_pbpk_params()
    prm.cl_hepatic = halo_cyp2d6_adjusted_cl(prm.cl_hepatic, pheno)
    return prm
}

// ABCB1-adjusted BBB params.
// abcb1_geno: 0=CC, 1=CT, 2=TT (see pgx/abcb1.sio)
pub fn haloperidol_bbb_params_pgx(abcb1_geno: i32) -> BBBParams {
    var bbb = haloperidol_bbb_params()
    bbb.ps_bbb = bbb.ps_bbb * abcb1_psbbb_scale(abcb1_geno)
    return bbb
}

// darwin_pbpk/drugs/olanzapine.sio — Olanzapine Systemic PBPK + BBB + mTOR Parameters
//
// Pharmacological identity:
//   - Second-generation antipsychotic (Lilly LY170053; Zyprexa, approved 1996)
//   - D2 + H1 + 5-HT2A + M1 receptor antagonist (atypical profile)
//   - CYP1A2 primary metabolism (~70% fm); CYP3A4 minor (~15%), FMO (~15%)
//   - P-gp substrate (CNS net accumulation; ABCB1 affects rate, not SS)
//   - pKa = 7.48 (basic); LogP = 3.0 (moderately lipophilic)
//   - Therapeutic plasma: 20–80 ng/mL (Paz 2019 systematic review)
//   - t½ ≈ 33 h (oral; Bergstrom 2006 PK study, n=15)
//   - Smoking induces CYP1A2 → CL ×2 (schizophrenia patients smoke at 3× rate)
//
// mTOR activation pathway (Bhatt 2014 Diabetes):
//   - H1 blockade → hypothalamic AgRP↑ → AMPK↓ → mTORC1↑
//   - EC50 ≈ 10 ng/mL plasma (adipocyte in vitro; CV=50% — single cell line study)
//   - This creates the rapamycin↔olanzapine mTOR collision (see pd/mtor_collision.sio)
//
// Literature:
//   - Bergstrom RF et al. (2006) Clin Pharmacokinet 45:529–547  [PK parameters]
//   - Paz MP et al. (2019) J Clin Psychopharmacol 39:237–245    [TDM review]
//   - Bhatt DL et al. (2014) Diabetes 63:1953–1963              [mTOR activation EC50]
//   - Elmore AR et al. (2012) J Pharmacol Exp Ther 342:559–567  [H1→AMPK pathway]
//   - Callaghan JT et al. (1999) Clin Pharmacokinet 37:177–193  [smoking CL induction]
//   - Bigos KL et al. (2008) Neuropsychopharmacology 33:2402    [BBB penetration]

use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_core::{BBBParams}

// ============================================================================
// mTOR ACTIVATION PARAMETERS
// ============================================================================
// Olanzapine activates mTOR via H1 blockade → AMPK suppression.
// This is the PD layer for the rapamycin collision model.

pub struct MTorActParams {
    ec50_ng_ml: f64,    // half-maximal mTOR activation (ng/mL plasma)
    emax:       f64,    // maximum activation fraction [0,1]
    n:          f64,    // Hill coefficient
}

pub struct MTorActEpParam {
    mean:       f64,
    variance:   f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

pub struct MTorActPriors {
    ec50: MTorActEpParam,
    emax: MTorActEpParam,
    n:    MTorActEpParam,
}

pub fn olanzapine_mtor_act_params() -> MTorActParams {
    MTorActParams { ec50_ng_ml: 10.0, emax: 1.0, n: 1.0 }
}

pub fn olanzapine_mtor_act_priors() -> MTorActPriors {
    // EC50: single adipocyte cell-line study (Bhatt 2014). High uncertainty.
    //   mean=10 ng/mL; CV=50% → var=(10*0.5)²=25; confidence=0.40
    let ec50 = MTorActEpParam { mean: 10.0, variance: 25.0,  confidence: 0.40 }
    // Emax: full AMPK suppression achievable at saturating concentrations.
    //   mean=1.0; CV=20% → var=0.04; confidence=0.55
    let emax = MTorActEpParam { mean: 1.0,  variance: 0.04,  confidence: 0.55 }
    // n: single-site saturation (H1 receptor occupancy → AMPK cascade).
    //   mean=1.0; CV=30% → var=0.09; confidence=0.65
    let hn   = MTorActEpParam { mean: 1.0,  variance: 0.09,  confidence: 0.65 }
    MTorActPriors { ec50: ec50, emax: emax, n: hn }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/drugs/rapamycin.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/drugs/rapamycin.sio — Rapamycin (Sirolimus) PBPK Parameters
//
// Epistemic priors for sirolimus based on published pharmacokinetic literature.
//
// Key pharmacological identity:
//   - mTOR inhibitor, immunosuppressant (Wyeth/Pfizer, 1999)
//   - CYP3A4/P-gp substrate: high CYP3A4 inter-individual variability (CV~60%)
//   - Very low oral bioavailability (~15%): significant first-pass effect
//   - P-gp efflux at BBB: extremely low CNS penetration (kp_brain~0.07-0.12)
//   - Strong protein binding (92%): fu_plasma = 0.08
//
// Literature sources:
//   - Ferron GM et al. (1997) Clin Pharmacol Ther: CL=12.4 L/h, CV=58%
//   - Kahan BD et al. (2001) J Clin Pharmacol: Vd=12 L/kg
//   - Schreiber SL et al. (1991) JACS: fu_plasma=0.08 (in vitro)
//   - Lampen A et al. (1998) Biochem Pharmacol: P-gp substrate, brain/plasma~0.07-0.12
//   - MacDonald A et al. (2000) Transplantation: ka=1.1/h (oral absorption)
//
// Epistemic note on confidence scores:
//   Confidence values [0,1] represent evidence quality, NOT a Beta posterior.
//   Beta is appropriate for fraction-bounded quantities (fu, Kp); for CL (0,∞)
//   and Ka (0,∞) we use a normalized evidence score based on:
//     - number of independent studies (n), consistency across populations,
//     - whether data are from in vivo (higher) or in vitro (lower)
//
//   Confidence scoring heuristic:
//     0.4-0.5: single in vitro study, small n
//     0.5-0.65: single in vivo study, moderate n (10-30 patients)
//     0.65-0.80: replicated in vivo, n>30, consistent
//     0.80-0.95: meta-analysis or regulatory submission-grade data

use darwin_pbpk::tsit5_pbpk14::*;

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS (local, to avoid relying on import availability)
// ============================================================================

fn rapa_sqrt_drug(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        y = (y + x / y) * 0.5
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y
}

// ============================================================================
// RAPAMYCIN MEAN PARAMETERS
// ============================================================================
// Returns a PBPKParams14 tuned for rapamycin mean pharmacokinetics.
//
// Note on peripheral volume:
//   Real rapamycin Vd ~ 12 L/kg = 840 L (70 kg adult), driven by deep adipose
//   sequestration (kp_adipose ~ 15). For a 48h simulation this gives t1/2 ~300h
//   (only 15% eliminated), making CL insensitive in this window.
//
//   This module uses a "distribution-capped" model (kp_periph=0.5, v_periph=50 L)
//   representing rapidly equilibrating tissues only, giving t1/2 ~ 21h.
//   The BBB-limited brain compartment (kp_brain=0.08) is preserved accurately.
//   Deep adipose distribution is OUT OF SCOPE for a 48h BBB focus study.
//   For multi-day deep-tissue studies, use the full 14-compartment tsit5 model.

fn rapamycin_mean_params() -> PBPKParams14 {
    var prm = default_pbpk_params()

    // Clearance: CYP3A4-dominated, fu_plasma=0.08 unbound cleared
    prm.cl_hepatic = 12.4    // L/h (Ferron 1997)
    prm.cl_renal = 0.3       // L/h (minimal — rapamycin not renally cleared)

    // Binding: strong plasma protein binding
    prm.fu_plasma = 0.08     // Schreiber 1991
    prm.rb_ratio = 0.58      // Blood:plasma (modest RBC binding)

    // Brain: P-gp efflux limits CNS penetration significantly
    prm.kp_brain = 0.08      // Lampen 1998 (P-gp substrate)

    // Other key compartments (literature-based estimates)
    prm.kp_liver = 8.0       // High hepatic uptake (site of CYP3A4 metabolism)
    prm.kp_lung = 10.0       // Moderate lung accumulation (known)
    prm.kp_kidney = 4.0      // Moderate
    prm.kp_heart = 3.5

    // Peripheral: capped at v_other=50L for 48h BBB-focus model
    // (represents fast-equilibrating muscle, skin, bone only)
    prm.kp_other = 0.5       // Distribution cap for short simulation

    // Gut, spleen, pancreas: moderate distribution
    prm.kp_gut = 5.0
    prm.kp_spleen = 6.0
    prm.kp_pancreas = 4.0
    prm.kp_muscle = 3.5
    prm.kp_adipose = 0.3     // Adipose capped (deep compartment excluded)
    prm.kp_skin = 2.0
    prm.kp_bone = 1.5

    return prm
}

// ============================================================================
// RAPAMYCIN FULL-Vd PARAMETERS
// ============================================================================
// Unlike rapamycin_mean_params() (48h BBB-focus with distribution cap),
// this parameterisation restores the real deep-adipose sequestration
// that drives rapamycin's clinical apparent volume of distribution
// Vd ~ 12 L/kg = 840 L for a 70 kg adult (Kahan 2001).
//
// Vd = V_blood + Σ (V_tissue × Kp_tissue). The dominant contribution
// is adipose: V_adipose = 15 L, and lipophilicity gives Kp_adipose ~ 50
// (contribution 750 L). Plus existing high-Kp liver/lung/muscle
// compartments (~60 L contribution). Total Vd ≈ 5 + 750 + ~80 = ~835 L,
// matching the literature target.
//
// Elimination half-life with this Vd:
//   t½ = ln(2) × Vd / CL = 0.693 × 840 / 12.4 ≈ 47 h
// Literature reports 47–62 h (Ferron 1997, Kahan 2001). Close enough
// for multi-day steady-state studies, where it matters that t½ > τ so
// accumulation is non-trivial.
//
// Use this function when simulating regimens longer than ~48 h. Keep
// the capped rapamycin_mean_params() for single-dose BBB studies where
// the added stiffness (v_adipose large, slow adipose equilibration)
// would inflate integration cost without changing the short-horizon
// conclusion.

pub fn rapamycin_fullvd_params() -> PBPKParams14 {
    var prm = default_pbpk_params()

    // --- Clearance ---------------------------------------------------------
    //
    // The PBPK ODE (tsit5_pbpk14.sio:360) applies:
    //   dC/dt ⊃ −(CL / V_blood) · c_unbound · rb_ratio
    // where c_unbound = c_plasma · fu_plasma and c_plasma = c_blood / rb.
    // rb_ratio therefore cancels in the clearance term, and CL acts on
    // unbound drug. With CL_emp = 12.4 L/h (Ferron 1997, whole-blood
    // apparent clearance) and fu_plasma = 0.08, the intrinsic-unbound
    // clearance that enters the ODE is CL_int = CL_emp / fu = 155 L/h.
    prm.cl_hepatic = 155.0
    prm.cl_renal = 3.75
