    }
    D2Priors { kd: kd, bmax: bmax }
}

// ============================================================================
// OCCUPANCY FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Fractional D2 occupancy [0, 1] from unbound ISF concentration (mg/L).
pub fn d2_occupancy(c_isf_free: f64, p: D2Params) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if c_isf_free <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    c_isf_free / (c_isf_free + p.kd_d2)
}

// D2 occupancy as percentage (0-100).
pub fn d2_occupancy_pct(c_isf_free: f64, p: D2Params) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    d2_occupancy(c_isf_free, p) * 100.0
}

// Absolute bound receptor concentration (mg/L).
pub fn d2_bound(c_isf_free: f64, p: D2Params) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    p.bmax_d2 * c_isf_free / (c_isf_free + p.kd_d2)
}

// Is occupancy in the antipsychotic therapeutic window [ant_threshold, eps_threshold)?
pub fn d2_in_window(occ: f64, p: D2Params) -> bool {
    occ >= p.ant_threshold && occ < p.eps_threshold
}

// Is occupancy above EPS threshold?
pub fn d2_above_eps(occ: f64, p: D2Params) -> bool {
    occ >= p.eps_threshold
}

// ============================================================================
// TRAJECTORY ENDPOINTS
// ============================================================================
// Takes sampled C_isf_free(t) series; mirrors pd_from_icf_series() in hill_mtor.sio.

pub struct D2Trajectory {
    n_points:       i32,
    times_h:        [f64; 32],
    occupancy:      [f64; 32],
    occ_auc:        f64,   // time-integral of occupancy (h·fraction)
    time_in_window: f64,   // hours in therapeutic window [ant, eps)
    time_above_eps: f64,   // hours above EPS threshold
    max_occ:        f64,
    mean_occ:       f64,
}

pub fn d2_trajectory_zero() -> D2Trajectory {
    D2Trajectory {
        n_points: 0,
        times_h:  [0.0; 32],
        occupancy: [0.0; 32],
        occ_auc:        0.0,
        time_in_window: 0.0,
        time_above_eps: 0.0,
        max_occ:  0.0,
        mean_occ: 0.0,
    }
}

// PGx-adjusted D2 params: override bmax_d2 from DRD2 TaqI A genotype.
// taq1a_allele: 0=A1A1, 1=A1A2, 2=A2A2 (see pgx/drd2_taq1a.sio)
// MW haloperidol = 375.86 g/mol.
use darwin_pbpk::pgx::drd2_taq1a::{drd2_bmax_mgL}

pub fn haloperidol_d2_params_pgx(taq1a_allele: i32) -> D2Params with Div, Panic {
    var p = haloperidol_d2_params()
    p.bmax_d2 = drd2_bmax_mgL(taq1a_allele, 375.86)
    return p
}

pub fn d2_from_isf_series(
    times_h:    [f64; 32],
    c_isf_free: [f64; 32],
    n_points:   i32,
    p: D2Params
) -> D2Trajectory with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var out = d2_trajectory_zero()
    out.n_points = n_points

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_points {
        let idx = i as usize
        let occ = d2_occupancy(c_isf_free[idx], p)
        out.times_h[idx]   = times_h[idx]
        out.occupancy[idx] = occ
        if occ > out.max_occ { out.max_occ = occ }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var auc:   f64 = 0.0
    var t_win: f64 = 0.0
    var t_eps: f64 = 0.0
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < n_points - 1 {
        let a = k as usize
        let b = (k + 1) as usize
        let dt = out.times_h[b] - out.times_h[a]
        auc = auc + 0.5 * dt * (out.occupancy[a] + out.occupancy[b])
        if d2_in_window(out.occupancy[a], p) && d2_in_window(out.occupancy[b], p) {
            t_win = t_win + dt
        }
        if d2_above_eps(out.occupancy[a], p) && d2_above_eps(out.occupancy[b], p) {
            t_eps = t_eps + dt
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    out.occ_auc = auc
    out.time_in_window = t_win
    out.time_above_eps = t_eps

    let total_t = out.times_h[(n_points - 1) as usize] - out.times_h[0]
    out.mean_occ = if total_t > 0.0 { auc / total_t } else { 0.0 }
    out
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/d2_voi.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/pd/d2_voi.sio — Value-of-Information ranking for D2 occupancy
//
// Answers the question: "If I can run exactly one experiment to reduce
// D2 occupancy prediction uncertainty, which parameter should I target?"
//
// Definition (Claxton 1999; Kennedy 2000; EVSI framework):
//
//     VoI_i = share_i × (1 − confidence_i)
//
// where:
//   share_i      — variance fraction contributed by parameter i
//                  (from d2_gum.sio GUM budget; equivalent to first-order
//                  Sobol index under GUM linearisation assumptions)
//   confidence_i — evidence-quality score [0,1] from haloperidol_bbb_priors
//                  and haloperidol_d2_priors (how well-measured is this now)
//
// The VoI formula penalises both:
//   - Low-share parameters: their uncertainty barely propagates to D2 prediction
//   - High-confidence parameters: they're already well-measured; further data
//     gives diminishing returns
//
// Only high-share × low-confidence parameters are worth measuring.
//
// Expected finding (pharmacologically predictable):
//   kd_d2 has 18.7% variance share BUT confidence 0.82 (radioligand
//   binding is the most rigorously measured receptor parameter).
//   → VoI_kd = 0.187 × 0.18 = 0.034 — ranks FOURTH.
//
//   ps_bbb has 32.6% variance share AND only confidence 0.45 (no direct
//   haloperidol BBB permeability measurement in primary literature).
//   → VoI_ps_bbb = 0.326 × 0.55 = 0.179 — ranks FIRST.
//
//   Message: "Don't run more D2 binding assays. Measure BBB permeability
//   for haloperidol." This finding requires both GUM + VoI; neither GUM
//   alone nor Sobol alone delivers the actionable recommendation.
//
// This is dissertation contribution #6 (antipsychotic D2 VoI), the
// counterpart to bbb_voi.sio (rapamycin Kpuu VoI, contribution #5).
//
// Run:
//   SOUNIO_STDLIB_PATH=/workspace/sounio/stdlib \
//     ./bin/souc run stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/d2_voi.sio

use darwin_pbpk::pd::d2_gum::*

// ============================================================================
// VoI STRUCT + COMPUTATION
// ============================================================================

pub struct D2VoI {
    n_rows:     i32,
    share:      [f64; 16],
    confidence: [f64; 16],
    voi:        [f64; 16],
    rank:       [i32; 16],    // rank[k] = param index with k-th highest VoI
    top_idx:    i32,
    top_voi:    f64,
    voi_total:  f64,
}

fn d2voi_zero() -> D2VoI {
    D2VoI {
        n_rows: 0,
        share:  [0.0; 16], confidence: [0.0; 16], voi: [0.0; 16],
        rank:   [0; 16],
        top_idx: 0, top_voi: 0.0, voi_total: 0.0,
    }
}

pub fn d2_voi_from_budget(b: D2GUMBudget) -> D2VoI with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out = d2voi_zero()
    let n = b.n_rows
    out.n_rows = n

    var total: f64 = 0.0
    var best_idx: i32 = 0
    var best_voi: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let s = b.share[idx]
        let c = b.confidence[idx]
        let v = s * (1.0 - c)
        out.share[idx]      = s
        out.confidence[idx] = c
        out.voi[idx]        = v
        total = total + v
        if v > best_voi { best_voi = v; best_idx = i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    out.voi_total = total
    out.top_idx   = best_idx
    out.top_voi   = best_voi

    // Selection sort: rank[k] = index of k-th highest VoI
    var used: [bool; 16] = [false; 16]
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < n {
        var best_j:  i32 = 0
        var best_v: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < n {
            let jdx = j as usize
            if used[jdx] == false && out.voi[jdx] > best_v {
                best_v = out.voi[jdx]
                best_j = j
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        out.rank[k as usize] = best_j
        used[best_j as usize] = true
        k = k + 1
    }

    out
}

// ============================================================================
// PARAMETER NAME LOOKUP
// ============================================================================

fn d2voi_param_name(idx: i32) -> string {
    if idx == 0 { return "ps_bbb" }
    if idx == 1 { return "ps_mem" }
    if idx == 2 { return "kpuu_brain" }
    if idx == 3 { return "kpuu_cell" }
    if idx == 4 { return "fu_plasma" }
    if idx == 5 { return "fu_isf" }
    if idx == 6 { return "fu_icf" }
    if idx == 7 { return "kd_d2" }
    if idx == 8 { return "bmax_d2" }
    "unknown"
}

fn d2voi_action(idx: i32) -> string {
    if idx == 0 { return "Measure haloperidol BBB PS in-vivo (P-gp/passive permeability assay)" }
    if idx == 1 { return "Measure cellular membrane PS (brain ICF kinetics, microdialysis)" }
    if idx == 2 { return "Measure in-vivo Kpuu,brain (brain microdialysis, chronic dosing)" }
    if idx == 3 { return "Measure lysosomal trapping (kpuu_cell via cell fractionation)" }
    if idx == 4 { return "Measure fu_plasma (equilibrium dialysis, already well-characterized)" }
    if idx == 5 { return "Measure fu_isf (brain ECF microdialysis protein binding)" }
    if idx == 6 { return "Measure fu_icf (cell fractionation, unbound intracellular fraction)" }
    if idx == 7 { return "Measure D2 Kd (radioligand binding — already well-characterized)" }
    if idx == 8 { return "Measure Bmax (PET receptor density — does not affect occupancy fraction)" }
    "Unknown parameter"
}

// ============================================================================
// PRINT REPORT
// ============================================================================

pub fn d2_voi_print(v: D2VoI, budget: D2GUMBudget) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  D2 Occupancy Value-of-Information Ranking")
    println("  VoI_i = share_i × (1 − confidence_i)   (Claxton 1999 EVSI)")
    println("  Endpoint: D2 trough at 72h, chronic 3×QD 5 mg haloperidol")
    println("======================================================================")
    print("  D2 trough (mean):    "); print_f64(budget.y_mean);       println("")
    print("  Combined CV:         "); print_f64(budget.y_rel_stddev); println("")
    print("  VoI_total:           "); print_f64(v.voi_total);         println("")
    println("")
    println("  rank | parameter      | share%  | conf  | VoI")
    println("  -----+----------------+---------+-------+--------")
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < v.n_rows {
        let kdx = k as usize
        let p   = v.rank[kdx]
        let pdx = p as usize
        let rank_k = (k + 1) as i64
        print("  ")
        print_int(rank_k);                             print("    | ")
        print(d2voi_param_name(p));                    print(" | ")
        print_f64(v.share[pdx] * 100.0);              print(" | ")
        print_f64(v.confidence[pdx]);                  print(" | ")
        print_f64(v.voi[pdx])
        println("")
        k = k + 1
    }
    println("")
    println("  PRIMARY RECOMMENDATION:")
    print("  #1 parameter: "); println(d2voi_param_name(v.top_idx))
    print("  Action:       "); println(d2voi_action(v.top_idx))
    print("  VoI:          "); print_f64(v.top_voi); println("")
    println("======================================================================")
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN — 8-TEST VALIDATION SUITE
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  D2 Occupancy VoI — Haloperidol CNS-PBPK/PD")
    println("  Value-of-Information from 9-D GUM budget")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("")

    // Build GUM budget then derive VoI
    let priors = haloperidol_d2_gum_priors()
    let budget = d2_gum_build(priors)
    let voi    = d2_voi_from_budget(budget)

    d2_voi_print(voi, budget)
    println("")

    var passed = 0
    var failed = 0

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // TEST 1: ps_bbb ranks #1 (highest VoI)
    //   High variance share (32.6%) + low confidence (0.45) = highest
    //   expected return from measuring BBB permeability.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    println("TEST 1: ps_bbb ranks #1 in VoI (high share, low confidence)")
    println("  VoI rank #1 parameter index:")
    println(voi.top_idx)
    if voi.top_idx == 0 {
        println("  [PASS] ps_bbb is the #1 measurement target")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("  FAIL: Expected ps_bbb (idx=0) to have highest VoI")
        failed = failed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // TEST 2: kd_d2 does NOT rank #1 despite being in top-3 by variance share
    //   Core VoI insight: high confidence (0.82) suppresses kd_d2's VoI
    //   even though it has 18.7% of variance share.
    //   Message: "Don't run more D2 binding assays — it's already measured."
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    println("TEST 2: kd_d2 does NOT rank #1 (high conf suppresses VoI despite large share)")
    let voi_kd = voi.voi[7]
    let voi_ps = voi.voi[0]
    println("  VoI kd_d2:")
    println(voi_kd)
    println("  VoI ps_bbb:")
    println(voi_ps)
    if voi_ps > voi_kd {
        println("  [PASS] ps_bbb VoI > kd_d2 VoI: measuring BBB permeability beats re-measuring Kd")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("  FAIL: Expected ps_bbb VoI > kd_d2 VoI")
        failed = failed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // TEST 3: bmax_d2 VoI = 0 (zero share → zero VoI regardless of confidence)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    println("TEST 3: bmax_d2 VoI = 0 (Emax invariant propagates to VoI = 0)")
    let voi_bmax = voi.voi[8]
    println("  VoI bmax_d2:")
    println(voi_bmax)
    if voi_bmax < 0.0001 {
        println("  [PASS] Bmax has zero VoI: measuring receptor density is irrelevant for occupancy")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("  FAIL: Expected VoI_bmax = 0")
        failed = failed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // TEST 4: fu_plasma VoI < ps_bbb VoI (well-measured parameter ranks lower)
    //   fu_plasma: share 5.9%, confidence 0.82 → VoI = 0.011
    //   ps_bbb:    share 32.6%, confidence 0.45 → VoI = 0.179
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    println("TEST 4: fu_plasma VoI < ps_bbb VoI (well-measured parameter ranks lower)")
    let voi_fup = voi.voi[4]
    println("  VoI fu_plasma:")
    println(voi_fup)
    if voi_fup < voi_ps {
        println("  [PASS] Well-measured fu_plasma has lower VoI than poorly-measured ps_bbb")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("  FAIL: Expected VoI_fu_plasma < VoI_ps_bbb")
        failed = failed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // TEST 5: VoI total > 0 (budget carries non-trivial uncertainty)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    println("TEST 5: VoI_total > 0 (meaningful measurement opportunities exist)")
    println("  VoI total:")
    println(voi.voi_total)
    if voi.voi_total > 0.01 {
        println("  [PASS] Non-trivial VoI indicates measurement opportunities to reduce D2 uncertainty")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("  FAIL: Expected VoI_total > 0.01")
        failed = failed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // TEST 6: Top-3 VoI parameters account for > 70% of total VoI
    //   Pareto principle: a few parameters dominate the measurement agenda.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    println("TEST 6: Top-3 VoI parameters account for > 70% of total VoI")
    let top3_voi = voi.voi[voi.rank[0] as usize]
                 + voi.voi[voi.rank[1] as usize]
                 + voi.voi[voi.rank[2] as usize]
    let top3_pct = if voi.voi_total > 0.0 { top3_voi / voi.voi_total } else { 0.0 }
    println("  Top-3 share of VoI_total (%):")
    println(top3_pct * 100.0)
    if top3_pct > 0.70 {
        println("  [PASS] Pareto: top-3 parameters explain >70% of measurement value")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("  FAIL: Expected top-3 parameters to account for >70% of VoI")
        failed = failed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // TEST 7: kd_d2 VoI < fu_icf VoI
    //   fu_icf: share 20.0%, confidence 0.20 → VoI = 0.160
    //   kd_d2:  share 18.7%, confidence 0.82 → VoI = 0.034
    //   Smaller share but MUCH lower confidence → fu_icf is higher priority
    //   despite being less discussed in literature.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    println("TEST 7: fu_icf VoI > kd_d2 VoI (low confidence elevates ICF over well-known PD)")
    let voi_fuicf = voi.voi[6]
    println("  VoI fu_icf:")
    println(voi_fuicf)
    println("  VoI kd_d2:")
    println(voi_kd)
    if voi_fuicf > voi_kd {
        println("  [PASS] fu_icf has higher VoI than kd_d2 despite similar variance share")
        println("         Reason: fu_icf confidence = 0.20 (unmeasured); kd_d2 = 0.82 (well-known)")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("  FAIL: Expected VoI_fu_icf > VoI_kd_d2")
        failed = failed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // TEST 8: VoI ranking encodes the experimental design recommendation
    //   The #1 VoI parameter is one of the BBB kinetic parameters
    //   (ps_bbb, ps_mem, kpuu_cell, fu_icf) — not a PD parameter.
    //   At 72h pre-SS, the measurement agenda is dominated by BBB kinetics.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    println("TEST 8: Top VoI target is a BBB kinetic parameter (not a PD parameter)")
    let top_is_bbb = voi.top_idx < 7
    println("  Top VoI parameter index (< 7 = BBB, >= 7 = PD):")
    println(voi.top_idx)
    if top_is_bbb {
        println("  [PASS] Experimental agenda at 72h dominated by BBB kinetics, not PD")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("  FAIL: Expected the top VoI target to be a BBB parameter at 72h pre-SS")
        failed = failed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  D2 VoI — TEST SUMMARY")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  Passed:")
    println(passed)
    println("  Failed:")
    println(failed)
    println("")
    if failed == 0 {
        println("  ALL 8 TESTS PASSED")
        println("")
        println("  D2 Occupancy VoI Findings:")
        println("")
        println("    #1: ps_bbb    — Measure haloperidol BBB permeability in vivo")
        println("    #2: fu_icf    — Measure brain ICF unbound fraction (unmeasured)")
        println("    #3: kpuu_cell — Measure lysosomal trapping degree")
        println("    #4: kd_d2     — Already well-measured (radioligand; low priority)")
        println("    #9: bmax_d2   — Irrelevant for occupancy fraction (Emax invariant)")
        println("")
        println("  Key dissertation message:")
        println("    The GUM budget alone might suggest 'measure kd_d2 more carefully'")
        println("    (18.7% of variance). VoI reveals this is wrong: kd_d2 is already")
        println("    well-characterized (confidence 0.82). The bottleneck is BBB kinetics.")
        println("    Without VoI, experimental resources would be mis-allocated.")
        println("")
        println("  This finding requires the full Sounio epistemic stack:")
        println("    GUM (variance shares) + confidence priors + VoI formula = actionable")
        println("    Existing tools (Simcyp, NONMEM, PK-Sim) emit neither GUM nor VoI.")
    } else {
        println("  SOME TESTS FAILED — see diagnostics above")
    }
    println("======================================================================")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/glp1_gipr_gum.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL PASS

// darwin_pbpk/pd/glp1_gipr_gum.sio — Dual GLP-1R/GIPR GUM Uncertainty Budget
//
// Propagates JCGM 100:2008 uncertainty through the Hill-Langmuir occupancy bridge
// for tirzepatide's dual agonist pharmacodynamics.
//
// Model: occ(C_free) = C_free / (C_free + EC50)  [Hill n=1]
//        C_free = fu × C_c
//
// GUM sensitivities (exact, first-order):
//   ∂occ/∂C_c   = fu × EC50 / (C_free + EC50)²
//   ∂occ/∂fu    = C_c × EC50 / (C_free + EC50)²
//   ∂occ/∂EC50  = -C_free / (C_free + EC50)²
//
// Uncertainty sources (tirzepatide, 5 mg SC at Cmax ≈ 298 ng/mL):
//   C_c  : from PK simulation (CV~25% → σ_Cc ≈ 0.25 × 298 = 74.5 ng/mL)
//   fu   : CV~20%, σ_fu = 0.002 (Min 2021)
//   EC50_GLP1R : CV~30%, σ=0.722 ng/mL (Min 2021 in vitro cAMP assay)
//   EC50_GIPR  : CV~30%, σ=0.289 ng/mL
//
// Literature:
//   Min T & Bain SC (2021) Drugs 81:897-906       [binding Ki, selectivity]
//   Frias JP et al. (2021) NEJM 385:503-515         [SURPASS-2 dose-response]
//   Urva S et al. (2022) Clin Pharmacokinet 61:861  [popPK IIV]

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn gg_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 12 {
        y = (y + x / y) * 0.5
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn gg_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// ============================================================================
// OCCUPANCY + GUM PROPAGATION
// ============================================================================

struct GUMOcc {
    occ:     f64,    // fractional occupancy [0,1]
    u_occ:   f64,    // combined GUM uncertainty in occupancy
    u_cc:    f64,    // contribution from C_c uncertainty
    u_fu:    f64,    // contribution from fu uncertainty
    u_ec50:  f64,    // contribution from EC50 uncertainty
}

// Computes occupancy and full GUM budget for one receptor.
// All sigma values are standard deviations (not variances).
fn occupancy_gum(c_c: f64, fu: f64, ec50: f64,
                 sigma_cc: f64, sigma_fu: f64, sigma_ec50: f64
                ) -> GUMOcc with Mut, Div {
    let c_free = fu * c_c
    let denom  = c_free + ec50
    let occ    = c_free / denom

    // GUM sensitivities (JCGM 100:2008 Eq.13)
    let s2 = denom * denom
    let docc_dcc   = fu * ec50 / s2               // ∂occ/∂C_c
    let docc_dfu   = c_c * ec50 / s2              // ∂occ/∂fu
    let docc_dec50 = 0.0 - c_free / s2            // ∂occ/∂EC50

    let uc  = gg_abs(docc_dcc)   * sigma_cc
    let ufu = gg_abs(docc_dfu)   * sigma_fu
    let ue  = gg_abs(docc_dec50) * sigma_ec50

    let u_comb = gg_sqrt(uc*uc + ufu*ufu + ue*ue)

    GUMOcc { occ: occ, u_occ: u_comb, u_cc: uc, u_fu: ufu, u_ec50: ue }
}

// Convenience: compare GUM budgets for dual receptor at same Cmax.
struct DualGUMOcc {
    glp1r: GUMOcc,
    gipr:  GUMOcc,
}

fn tirzepatide_dual_occ_gum(c_c_ngml: f64) -> DualGUMOcc with Mut, Div {
    // Tirzepatide parameters (Min 2021, Urva 2022)
    let fu       = 0.01       // plasma unbound fraction
    let sigma_cc = 0.25 * c_c_ngml   // 25% CV from Urva 2022 popPK IIV

    // GLP-1R: EC50=2.407 ng/mL ± CV=30%
    let ec50_g1 = 2.407
    let sig_g1  = 0.30 * ec50_g1     // 0.722 ng/mL
    let sig_fu  = 0.002              // 20% CV × fu=0.01

    // GIPR: EC50=0.963 ng/mL ± CV=30%
    let ec50_gi = 0.963
    let sig_gi  = 0.30 * ec50_gi     // 0.289 ng/mL

    let glp1r = occupancy_gum(c_c_ngml, fu, ec50_g1, sigma_cc, sig_fu, sig_g1)
    let gipr  = occupancy_gum(c_c_ngml, fu, ec50_gi, sigma_cc, sig_fu, sig_gi)

    DualGUMOcc { glp1r: glp1r, gipr: gipr }
}

// ============================================================================
// GATE TESTS
// ============================================================================
// T1: GUM u_occ < occ (relative uncertainty < 100%)
// T2: GIPR occ > GLP-1R occ at therapeutic Cmax (lower EC50)
// T3: EC50 uncertainty dominates over fu uncertainty for both receptors
// T4: Combined u_occ consistent with manual calculation at Cmax=298 ng/mL

fn test_uncertainty_bounded() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // T1: Both receptor u_occ should be < the occupancy itself
    let r = tirzepatide_dual_occ_gum(298.0)
    if r.glp1r.u_occ < r.glp1r.occ && r.gipr.u_occ < r.gipr.occ {
        println("T1 PASS: GUM u_occ < occ for both receptors")
        1
    } else {
        print("T1 FAIL: GLP-1R u_occ=")
        print(r.glp1r.u_occ)
        print(" occ=")
        print(r.glp1r.occ)
        println("")
        0
    }
}

fn test_gipr_higher() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // T2: GIPR has lower EC50 → higher occupancy at same free concentration
    let r = tirzepatide_dual_occ_gum(298.0)
    if r.gipr.occ > r.glp1r.occ {
        println("T2 PASS: GIPR occ > GLP-1R occ (lower EC50)")
        1
    } else {
        print("T2 FAIL: GIPR occ=")
        print(r.gipr.occ)
        print(" GLP-1R occ=")
        print(r.glp1r.occ)
        println("")
        0
    }
}

fn test_ec50_dominant_near_ec50() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // T3: Near EC50 (C_free ≈ EC50), EC50 uncertainty dominates because
    // d²occ/dEC50 is maximized at C_free = EC50 (maximum sensitivity point).
    // At Cmax=298 ng/mL: C_free = 0.01 × 298 = 2.98 ≈ EC50_GLP1R (2.407) → near peak sensitivity.
    // This is a correct pharmacological finding, not an error.
    let r = tirzepatide_dual_occ_gum(298.0)
    if r.glp1r.u_ec50 > r.glp1r.u_fu {
        println("T3 PASS: EC50 uncertainty > fu uncertainty (near-EC50 peak sensitivity)")
        1
    } else {
        print("T3 FAIL: u_EC50=")
        print(r.glp1r.u_ec50)
        print(" u_fu=")
        print(r.glp1r.u_fu)
        println("")
        0
    }
}

fn test_manual_check() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // T4: Manual calculation at C_c=298, fu=0.01, EC50_GLP1R=2.407:
    //   C_free = 0.01 × 298 = 2.98 ng/mL
    //   occ = 2.98 / (2.98 + 2.407) = 2.98 / 5.387 = 0.5532
    //   ∂occ/∂C_c = fu × EC50 / denom² = 0.01 × 2.407 / 5.387² = 0.000830
    //   u_Cc = 0.000830 × (0.25 × 298) = 0.000830 × 74.5 = 0.0618
    //   Expected u_occ ∈ [0.04, 0.15] (range covers parameter uncertainty)
    let r = tirzepatide_dual_occ_gum(298.0)
    if r.glp1r.occ >= 0.40 && r.glp1r.occ <= 0.75 {
        if r.glp1r.u_occ >= 0.02 && r.glp1r.u_occ <= 0.20 {
            println("T4 PASS: GLP-1R occ and u_occ in expected ranges")
            1
        } else {
            print("T4 FAIL: u_occ=")
            print(r.glp1r.u_occ)
            println(" (expected 0.02-0.20)")
            0
        }
    } else {
        print("T4 FAIL: occ=")
        print(r.glp1r.occ)
        println(" (expected 0.40-0.75)")
        0
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    println("=== Dual GLP-1R/GIPR GUM Budget (Tirzepatide, Cmax=298 ng/mL) ===")
    let r = tirzepatide_dual_occ_gum(298.0)
    print("  GLP-1R occ = ")
    print(r.glp1r.occ)
    print("  u = ")
    println(r.glp1r.u_occ)
    print("  GIPR  occ = ")
    print(r.gipr.occ)
    print("  u = ")
    println(r.gipr.u_occ)
    println("")

    var passed = 0
    passed = passed + test_uncertainty_bounded()
    passed = passed + test_gipr_higher()
    passed = passed + test_ec50_dominant_near_ec50()
    passed = passed + test_manual_check()

    if passed == 4 {
        println("ALL PASS")
    } else {
        print("PARTIAL: ")
        print(passed)
        println("/4 passed")
    }
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/hill_mtor.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/pd/hill_mtor.sio — Hill-equation PD layer for mTOR inhibition
//
// Pharmacodynamic bridge from BBB intracellular unbound concentration
// (C_icf, nM) to fractional mTOR inhibition:
//
//   E(C) = Emax * C^n / (EC50^n + C^n)        (Hill equation, n>0)
//
// For rapamycin:
//   Emax = 1.0  (full saturation achievable at high intracellular exposure)
//   EC50 = 0.5 nM  (mTORC1 S6K1-phosphorylation IC50)
//   n    = 1.0  (classical single-site binding; FKBP12 stoichiometry)
//
// Literature:
//   - Sehgal SN (2003) Transplantation Proc 35:7S–14S
//   - MacKeigan JP et al. (2015) Cancer Res 75:4127–4139
//   - Foster DA et al. (2010) Trends Pharmacol Sci 31:242–248
//
// This module is agnostic to how C_icf(t) was computed. It takes an
// array of unbound intracellular concentrations (already sampled on a
// grid) plus a time grid, and produces inhibition time-series + AUC +
// time-above-threshold endpoints.
//
// Epistemic note:
//   EC50 and n carry material uncertainty — most rapamycin EC50 values
//   are cell-line-specific in vitro. We export priors with confidence
//   scores that feed bbb_gum.sio + bbb_voi.sio (see Phase 3 of the
//   epistemic-PBPK dissertation plan).

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Parameters + priors
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub struct HillParams {
    emax: f64,      // maximum effect [0,1]
    ec50_nM: f64,   // half-maximal effective concentration (nM)
    n: f64,         // Hill coefficient
}

pub fn rapamycin_hill_params() -> HillParams {
    HillParams { emax: 1.0, ec50_nM: 0.5, n: 1.0 }
}

pub struct HillEpParam {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

pub struct HillPriors {
    emax: HillEpParam,
    ec50: HillEpParam,
    n:    HillEpParam,
}

pub fn rapamycin_hill_priors() -> HillPriors {
    // Emax: mean=1.0 (saturation); low variance, good confidence.
    // Multiple cell-lines confirm near-complete mTORC1 inhibition at high C.
    let emax = HillEpParam { mean: 1.0, variance: 0.01, confidence: 0.75 }

    // EC50: mean=0.5 nM, SD=0.3 nM, confidence=0.40.
    //
    // In vitro phospho-endpoint convergence (all S6K1 Thr389 readouts,
    // dose-response curves):
    //   HEK293 (kinase assay):   ~0.1 nM     (Selleckchem S1039)
    //   Jurkat T-cell:           ~0.45 nM    (pooled reports)
    //   Cell-based consensus:    ~1.0 nM     (PMC4834780, Dowling 2008)
    //   Range:                   0.1 – 2 nM  (log-uniform across assays)
    // Geometric-mean centring of these would put the prior closer to
    // 0.3 nM than 0.5 nM, but this is an IN VITRO aggregate.
    //
    // The in vivo brain ICF reality check (this commit's finding):
    //   Clinical Rapamune trough target     = 5 – 15 ng/mL whole blood
    //                                       = 5.5 – 16 nM whole blood
    //   Plasma fu                           = 0.08
    //   Kp,uu,brain (reported "poor")       ≈ 0.1
    //   Estimated unbound ICF               ≈ 0.04 – 0.13 nM
    // That is below the in vitro EC50 — i.e., clinical trough dosing
    // leaves brain mTOR well below its phospho half-max. This matches
    // observed rapalog-brain efficacy challenges (ALS CSF undetectable;
    // TSC-seizure efficacy driven by chronic accumulation + peripheral
    // routes) and is *why* the model's inhibition-AUC output is small.
    //
    // Epistemic gap (kept as-is, not tightened):
    //   No rodent brain microdialysis EC50 for rapamycin S6K1 phospho
    //   was located in primary literature. Using in vitro variance to
    //   tighten an in vivo brain ICF prior would be a category error
    //   (same conflation the hill_n refinement above just corrected).
    //   The VoI rerank's identification of ec50_nM as the next target
    //   IS the dissertation contribution — it points at the real gap.
    //   Variance 0.09 and confidence 0.40 remain conservative pending
    //   direct in vivo brain measurement.
    let ec50 = HillEpParam { mean: 0.5, variance: 0.09, confidence: 0.40 }

    // n: mean=1.0 (classical single-site allosteric inhibition via the
    // FKBP12·rapamycin·FRB ternary complex — one binding site per mTOR,
    // so Hill theory predicts n=1 exactly for the phospho endpoint).
    //
    // Prior refinement (lit-backed) — variance 0.04 → 0.01, conf 0.70 → 0.85:
    //   The earlier wide SD=0.20 conflated two distinct endpoints:
    //     (a) cell-viability curves, which Kuo et al. (PMC6455999) flag
    //         as "unusually shallow" for rapamycin — a cytostatic /
    //         incomplete-kill artifact, NOT Hill behavior at the molecular
    //         target;
    //     (b) S6K1-Thr389 phospho dose-response, which this PD layer
    //         actually models, and which the single-site FRB mechanism
    //         constrains tightly to n≈1.
    //   Cross-cell-line S6K1-phospho curves cluster at n ≈ 1.0 ± 0.1
    //   (HEK293, Jurkat, MCF7, T98G — Dowling et al. 2008 PNAS;
    //   biochemistry per Banaszynski et al. JACS 2005 ternary complex;
    //   pooled kinase datasheet — Selleckchem S1039).
    //   SD=0.10 covers the 0.8–1.2 observed spread; confidence 0.85
    //   reflects the mechanistic constraint + multi-cell-line convergence.
    let hn   = HillEpParam { mean: 1.0, variance: 0.01, confidence: 0.85 }

    HillPriors { emax: emax, ec50: ec50, n: hn }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Math helpers (local, avoid cross-module imports)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn hill_log(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // Natural log via Halley-style iteration on y = ln(x).
    // Only used for non-integer Hill coefficients. For n=1 the direct
    // formula bypasses this path entirely (see hill_inhibition).
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e300 }
    // Scale x into [1, e] range: x = 2^k * m
    var y = 0.0
    var xs = x
    while xs > 2.0 { xs = xs * 0.5; y = y + 0.6931471805599453 }
    while xs < 0.5 { xs = xs * 2.0; y = y - 0.6931471805599453 }
    // Taylor for ln around 1: xs in roughly [0.5, 2]
    let u = xs - 1.0
    // ln(1+u) ~ u - u^2/2 + u^3/3 - ...
    var term = u
    var sum = u
    var k: i32 = 2
    while k < 40 {
        term = term * (0.0 - u)
        sum = sum + term / (k as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }
    y + sum
}

fn hill_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if x >= 0.5 {
        let half = hill_exp(x * 0.5)
        return half * half
    }
    if x <= 0.0 - 0.5 {
        let half = hill_exp(x * 0.5)
        return half * half
    }
    var term: f64 = 1.0
    var sum: f64 = 1.0
    var k: i32 = 1
    while k < 20 {
        term = term * x / (k as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        k = k + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn hill_pow(base: f64, expn: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if base <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    // Integer fast-path for n=1 (by far the common rapamycin case)
    let n_int_round = expn
    if n_int_round > 0.9999 && n_int_round < 1.0001 { return base }
    if n_int_round > 1.9999 && n_int_round < 2.0001 { return base * base }
    hill_exp(expn * hill_log(base))
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Core Hill inhibition
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Fractional inhibition E(C) in [0, Emax].
pub fn hill_inhibition(c_icf_nM: f64, p: HillParams) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if c_icf_nM <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    // Fast path for classical n=1
    if p.n > 0.9999 && p.n < 1.0001 {
        return p.emax * c_icf_nM / (p.ec50_nM + c_icf_nM)
    }
    let cn  = hill_pow(c_icf_nM, p.n)
    let kn  = hill_pow(p.ec50_nM, p.n)
    p.emax * cn / (kn + cn)
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Trajectory endpoints — takes sampled C_icf(t) series
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub struct PDEndpoint {
    inhibition_auc:        f64, // integral of E(C) over simulation (unitless·h)
    time_above_80pct:      f64, // hours spent with E >= 0.8
    max_inhibition:        f64, // peak E reached
    mean_inhibition:       f64, // time-weighted mean E
    n_points:              i32,
    times_h:   [f64; 32],
    inhib:     [f64; 32],
}

pub fn pd_endpoint_zero() -> PDEndpoint {
    PDEndpoint {
        inhibition_auc: 0.0,
        time_above_80pct: 0.0,
        max_inhibition: 0.0,
        mean_inhibition: 0.0,
        n_points: 0,
        times_h: [0.0; 32],
        inhib:   [0.0; 32],
    }
}

// Driven from a sampled C_icf time-series (unbound intracellular nM) on a
// grid of size n_points (<= 32). Mirrors the checkpoint layout used by
// scenarios/des_sirolimus_bbb.sio (DESBBBTrace).
pub fn pd_from_icf_series(
    times_h:  [f64; 32],
    c_icf_nM: [f64; 32],
    n_points: i32,
    p: HillParams
) -> PDEndpoint with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var out = pd_endpoint_zero()
    out.n_points = n_points

    // Per-point inhibition
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_points {
        let idx = i as usize
        let e = hill_inhibition(c_icf_nM[idx], p)
        out.times_h[idx] = times_h[idx]
        out.inhib[idx] = e
        if e > out.max_inhibition { out.max_inhibition = e }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Trapezoidal integral + time-above-threshold
    var auc: f64 = 0.0
    var t_above: f64 = 0.0
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < n_points - 1 {
        let a = k as usize
        let b = (k + 1) as usize
        let dt = out.times_h[b] - out.times_h[a]
        auc = auc + 0.5 * dt * (out.inhib[a] + out.inhib[b])
        // conservative: count dt only if both endpoints >= 0.8
        if out.inhib[a] >= 0.8 && out.inhib[b] >= 0.8 {
            t_above = t_above + dt
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    out.inhibition_auc = auc
    out.time_above_80pct = t_above

    let total_t = out.times_h[(n_points - 1) as usize] - out.times_h[0]
    out.mean_inhibition = if total_t > 0.0 { auc / total_t } else { 0.0 }
    out
}

pub fn pd_print_csv(pd: PDEndpoint) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("time_h,inhibition_fraction")
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < pd.n_points {
        let idx = i as usize
        print_f64(pd.times_h[idx]); print(",")
        print_f64(pd.inhib[idx])
        println("")
        i = i + 1
    }
    println("")
    print("inhibition_AUC,");      print_f64(pd.inhibition_auc);   println("")
    print("time_above_80pct_h,");  print_f64(pd.time_above_80pct); println("")
    print("max_inhibition,");      print_f64(pd.max_inhibition);   println("")
    print("mean_inhibition,");     print_f64(pd.mean_inhibition);  println("")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/mtor_collision.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/pd/mtor_collision.sio — Rapamycin ↔ Olanzapine mTOR collision gate
//
// Two drugs act on mTOR with opposing effects in the same patient:
//
//   Rapamycin  → mTOR INHIBIT  (FKBP12-FRB ternary complex; Cypher DES local + systemic)
//   Olanzapine → mTOR ACTIVATE (H1 blockade → AgRP↑ → AMPK↓ → mTORC1↑; Bhatt 2014)
//
// Net mTOR effect = inhibition - activation  (positive = net inhibition maintained)
//
// Both effects use the same Hill sigmoidal math (hill_mtor.sio::hill_inhibition).
// Rapamycin: IC50 = 0.5 nM ICF; olanzapine: EC50 = 10 ng/mL plasma.
// The units differ because the rapamycin PD is in intracellular nM (BBB-penetrated)
// while the olanzapine PD is referenced to plasma ng/mL (H1 receptor in hypothalamus,
// modelled as peripheral adipocyte proxy from Bhatt 2014).
//
// Knightian uncertainty gate (interval arithmetic):
//   mtor_net_interval() propagates ±2σ corner enclosures.
//   Monotonicity: ∂net/∂c_rapa > 0,  ∂net/∂c_olz < 0
//   → worst-case lower bound: (c_rapa_lo, c_olz_hi)
//   → worst-case upper bound: (c_rapa_hi, c_olz_lo)
//   Same pattern as tacrolimus_sirolimus_ddi.sio:114
//
// Gate verdicts:
//   2 = PROTECTED  (net_lower > 0) — rapamycin dominates; stent efficacy maintained
//   1 = UNCERTAIN  (interval straddles 0) — olanzapine partially offsets rapamycin
//   0 = UNPROTECTED (net_upper ≤ 0) — olanzapine overwhelms rapamycin
//
// Literature:
//   Bhatt DL et al. (2014) Diabetes 63:1953-1963        [EC50 mTOR activation]
//   Elmore AR et al. (2012) J Pharmacol Exp Ther 342:559 [H1→AMPK pathway]
//   MacKeigan JP et al. (2015) Cancer Res 75:4127-4139   [rapamycin IC50]
//   Sehgal SN (2003) Transplantation Proc 35:7S-14S      [sirolimus mechanism]

use darwin_pbpk::pd::hill_mtor::{HillParams, hill_inhibition}
use darwin_pbpk::drugs::olanzapine::{MTorActParams, olanzapine_mtor_act_params}

// ============================================================================
// CORE FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Olanzapine mTOR activation fraction [0, Emax] from plasma concentration (ng/mL).
// Uses the same Hill function as rapamycin inhibition — same sigmoidal math.
// ec50_ng_ml is stored in MTorActParams; we wrap it into HillParams for hill_inhibition.
pub fn mtor_olanz_activate(c_olanz_ng_ml: f64, p: MTorActParams) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if c_olanz_ng_ml <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let hp = HillParams { emax: p.emax, ec50_nM: p.ec50_ng_ml, n: p.n }
    hill_inhibition(c_olanz_ng_ml, hp)
}

// Net mTOR effect (rapamycin inhibition − olanzapine activation).
//   positive → net inhibition dominates (stent protection maintained)
//   negative → net activation dominates (olanzapine overwhelms rapamycin)
//   zero     → opposing effects cancel
//
// c_rapa_icf_nM : rapamycin intracellular unbound (nM), from BBB sub-model
// c_olanz_ng_ml : olanzapine plasma (ng/mL), from systemic PBPK
pub fn mtor_net_effect(
    c_rapa_icf_nM:  f64,
    c_olanz_ng_ml:  f64,
    rapa_p:         HillParams,
    olz_p:          MTorActParams
) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let inhib    = hill_inhibition(c_rapa_icf_nM, rapa_p)
    let activate = mtor_olanz_activate(c_olanz_ng_ml, olz_p)
    inhib - activate
}

// ============================================================================
// INTERVAL ARITHMETIC (Knightian uncertainty propagation)
// ============================================================================

// ±2σ concentration bounds for a measurement.
// Returns (lo, hi) where lo = max(0, mean - 2*SD), hi = mean + 2*SD
fn mct_bounds(mean: f64, cv: f64) -> (f64, f64) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let sd = mean * cv
    let lo = if mean - 2.0 * sd > 0.0 { mean - 2.0 * sd } else { 0.0 }
    let hi = mean + 2.0 * sd
    (lo, hi)
}

// Net mTOR interval: propagates concentration uncertainty to net effect bounds.
// Monotonicity argument:
//   ∂net/∂c_rapa > 0  (more rapamycin → more inhibition → net goes up)
//   ∂net/∂c_olz  < 0  (more olanzapine → more activation → net goes down)
// Corner enclosure:
//   net_lower = net(c_rapa_lo, c_olz_hi)   [worst case: little rapa + lots olz]
//   net_upper = net(c_rapa_hi, c_olz_lo)   [best case: lots rapa + little olz]
pub fn mtor_net_interval(
    c_rapa_mean: f64, c_rapa_cv: f64,
    c_olanz_mean: f64, c_olanz_cv: f64,
    rapa_p: HillParams,
    olz_p:  MTorActParams
) -> (f64, f64) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let rb = mct_bounds(c_rapa_mean, c_rapa_cv)
    let ob = mct_bounds(c_olanz_mean, c_olanz_cv)
    let c_rapa_lo  = rb.0
    let c_rapa_hi  = rb.1
    let c_olz_lo   = ob.0
    let c_olz_hi   = ob.1
    let net_lower = mtor_net_effect(c_rapa_lo,  c_olz_hi,  rapa_p, olz_p)
    let net_upper = mtor_net_effect(c_rapa_hi,  c_olz_lo,  rapa_p, olz_p)
    (net_lower, net_upper)
}

// ============================================================================
// COLLISION GATE
// ============================================================================

// Knightian gate verdict:
//   2 = PROTECTED  (net_lower > 0.0)
//   1 = UNCERTAIN  (net_lower ≤ 0 and net_upper > 0, interval straddles zero)
//   0 = UNPROTECTED (net_upper ≤ 0.0)
pub fn mtor_collision_gate(net_lower: f64, net_upper: f64) -> i32 {
    if net_lower > 0.0                        { return 2 }
    if net_upper > 0.0 && net_lower <= 0.0   { return 1 }
    return 0
}

pub fn mtor_gate_label(g: i32) -> i32 { g }  // pass-through for print routing

// ============================================================================
// CONVENIENCE: rapamycin Hill params at clinical ICF concentrations
// ============================================================================
// ICF concentration from the Cypher DES scenario (local coronary + systemic):
//   Trough systemic ICF ≈ 0.04–0.13 nM (see hill_mtor.sio priors note)
//   DES local ICF at arterial wall: 0.1–5 nM depending on release phase
pub fn rapa_hill_params_clinical() -> HillParams {
    HillParams { emax: 1.0, ec50_nM: 0.5, n: 1.0 }
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    println("mtor_collision: rapamycin-olanzapine net mTOR gate")
    let rapa_p = rapa_hill_params_clinical()
    let olz_p  = olanzapine_mtor_act_params()

    // Scenario A: DES local rapamycin (5 nM ICF) + no olanzapine
    let net_a = mtor_net_effect(5.0, 0.0, rapa_p, olz_p)
    print("  Scenario A (rapa only, 5 nM): net = "); print_f64(net_a); println("")

    // Scenario B: Low rapamycin (0.05 nM) + olanzapine 40 ng/mL (high dose)
    let net_b = mtor_net_effect(0.05, 40.0, rapa_p, olz_p)
    print("  Scenario B (low rapa + high olanz): net = "); print_f64(net_b); println("")

    // Scenario C: Interval for moderate concentrations
    let ivl = mtor_net_interval(0.1, 0.5, 20.0, 0.3, rapa_p, olz_p)
    let gate = mtor_collision_gate(ivl.0, ivl.1)
    print("  Scenario C interval: ["); print_f64(ivl.0); print(", "); print_f64(ivl.1); println("]")
    print("  Gate verdict: "); print(gate); println(" (2=PROTECTED 1=UNCERTAIN 0=UNPROTECTED)")

    println("PASS")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/pd_gate.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/pd/pd_gate.sio — Runtime confidence gate for PD priors.
//
// This is the runtime half of the dissertation's second novel contribution
// (compile-time confidence gates). It enforces that every parameter in a
// PDPriors10 set meets a minimum confidence threshold before downstream
// consumers (sensitivity analysis, VoI ranking, dose-decision code) may
// use it.
//
// Design choices:
//   - Two canonical policies: "exploratory" (floor=0.25, matches current
//     rapamycin research-stage priors) and "clinical" (floor=0.60, the
//     pre-registration aspirational floor). Clinical does NOT pass the
//     current priors — that is by design; the failure *is* the
//     dissertation's VoI-rerank result in gate form.
//   - Always runs to completion, returning a verdict + violation list.
//     Consumers decide whether to halt (REJECT) or flag (WARN).
//   - Mirrors the semantics of stdlib/epistemic/confidence_gate.sio
//     (GatePolicy/GateResult) but is self-contained and operates on
//     the PDPriors10 [f64; 16] arrays directly. A future commit can
//     unify the two once confidence_gate.sio exports its surface as
//     pub (tracked in docs/compiler/CONFIDENCE_EFFECT_DESIGN.md).
//
// References:
//   - JCGM 100:2008 §4.3  — "target uncertainty"
//   - ISO 17025:2017 §7.6 — decision rules for conformity
//   - confidence_gate.sio  — runtime gate semantics

use darwin_pbpk::pd::pd_gum::{PDPriors10}

pub struct PDGatePolicy {
    min_confidence: f64,   // Minimum acceptable confidence level (0-1)
    action:         i32,   // 0 = REJECT, 1 = WARN
    label:          i32,   // 0 = exploratory, 1 = clinical, 2 = strict
}

// The three policy constructors are the first dissertation entry points
// annotated with the compile-time `Confidence(N)` effect (Gen 21 Phase C).
// N = 950 means their own bodies must type-check at ≥ 0.95 — they do,
// since each returns a pure struct literal over typed constants. Callers
// must also declare `Confidence(950)` or weaker, which is the exact
// propagation the dissertation's second novel contribution relies on.
// See docs/compiler/CONFIDENCE_EFFECT_DESIGN.md.

pub fn pd_gate_policy_exploratory() -> PDGatePolicy with Confidence(950) {
    // Matches the current rapamycin research-stage priors: min conf is
    // fu_icf=0.25 / ps_mem=0.25. Floor at 0.25 → all pass.
    PDGatePolicy { min_confidence: 0.25, action: 1, label: 0 }
}

pub fn pd_gate_policy_clinical() -> PDGatePolicy with Confidence(950) {
    // Pre-registration floor. Under the current priors this FAILS on
    // ec50_nM (0.40), kpuu_cell (0.30), fu_isf (0.35), fu_icf (0.25),
    // ps_mem (0.25). That failure set IS the VoI-rerank's measurement
    // priority list, expressed at the gate interface.
    PDGatePolicy { min_confidence: 0.60, action: 0, label: 1 }
}

pub fn pd_gate_policy_strict() -> PDGatePolicy with Confidence(950) {
    // Post-measurement, regulatory-dossier floor.
    PDGatePolicy { min_confidence: 0.90, action: 0, label: 2 }
}

pub struct PDGateResult {
    passed:            bool,
    n_checked:         i32,
    n_violations:      i32,
    violation_idx:     [i32; 16],   // prior indices that failed
    violation_values:  [f64; 16],   // actual confidence values
    worst_idx:         i32,
    worst_confidence:  f64,
    floor_used:        f64,
    policy_label:      i32,
}

fn pd_gate_zero() -> PDGateResult {
    PDGateResult {
        passed: true,
        n_checked: 0, n_violations: 0,
        violation_idx: [0; 16], violation_values: [0.0; 16],
        worst_idx: 0 - 1, worst_confidence: 1.0,
        floor_used: 0.0, policy_label: 0,
    }
}

pub fn pd_gate_check(priors: PDPriors10, policy: PDGatePolicy) -> PDGateResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = pd_gate_zero()
    r.floor_used   = policy.min_confidence
    r.policy_label = policy.label

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < priors.n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let conf = priors.confidence[idx]

        r.n_checked = r.n_checked + 1
        if conf < r.worst_confidence {
            r.worst_confidence = conf
            r.worst_idx = i
        }

        if conf < policy.min_confidence {
            let vi = r.n_violations as usize
            if (vi as i32) < 16 {
                r.violation_idx[vi]    = i
                r.violation_values[vi] = conf
            }
            r.n_violations = r.n_violations + 1
            r.passed = false
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

fn pd_gate_policy_name(label: i32) -> string {
    if label == 0 { return "exploratory" }
    if label == 1 { return "clinical"    }
    if label == 2 { return "strict"      }
    "unknown"
}

fn pd_gate_param_name(idx: i32) -> string {
    if idx == 0 { return "ps_bbb"     }
    if idx == 1 { return "ps_mem"     }
    if idx == 2 { return "kpuu_brain" }
    if idx == 3 { return "kpuu_cell"  }
    if idx == 4 { return "fu_plasma"  }
    if idx == 5 { return "fu_isf"     }
    if idx == 6 { return "fu_icf"     }
    if idx == 7 { return "emax"       }
    if idx == 8 { return "ec50_nM"    }
    if idx == 9 { return "hill_n"     }
    "unknown"
}

pub fn pd_gate_print(r: PDGateResult) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("PD gate ("); print(pd_gate_policy_name(r.policy_label))
    print(", floor = "); print_f64(r.floor_used); println(")")

    if r.passed {
        print("  VERDICT: PASSED — "); print_i64(r.n_checked as i64)
        println(" parameters meet confidence floor")
    } else {
        print("  VERDICT: FAILED — "); print_i64(r.n_violations as i64)
        print(" of "); print_i64(r.n_checked as i64)
        println(" parameters below floor")
        var k: i32 = 0
        while k < r.n_violations && k < 16 {
            let kdx = k as usize
            print("    - "); print(pd_gate_param_name(r.violation_idx[kdx]))
            print(" (conf = "); print_f64(r.violation_values[kdx]); println(")")
            k = k + 1
        }
    }
    if r.worst_idx >= 0 {
        print("  worst: "); print(pd_gate_param_name(r.worst_idx))
        print(" @ "); print_f64(r.worst_confidence); println("")
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/pd_gum.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/pd/pd_gum.sio — Extended GUM budget including PD (Hill) params
//
// The baseline bbb_gum.sio builds a 7-D uncertainty budget on BBB
// transport/binding parameters with Kpuu_AUC as the endpoint. This
// module extends the analysis to a 10-D budget that adds the three
// Hill-equation PD priors (Emax, EC50, n) and uses mTOR inhibition AUC
// as the endpoint — the dissertation's clinically meaningful output.
//
// Why a separate module:
//   - BBBPriors arrays are fixed at [_; 8]; widening them is a breaking
//     change to bbb_gum.sio + bbb_hdmr.sio + bbb_voi.sio. Keeping those
//     intact protects the committed contribution #3/#5 pipelines.
//   - The 10-D budget has a different endpoint function (Y = E_AUC,
//     not Kpuu_AUC), a different perturbation primitive (Hill params
//     live on HillParams, not BBBParams), and a different coupling
//     (it must run oral_bbb_run, not bbb_coupled_run, because the
//     PD curve needs ICF exposure from an absorbed-dose scenario).
//
// Indexing:
//   0–6: same BBB parameters as bbb_gum / bbb_voi (ps_bbb … fu_icf)
//   7:   Emax
//   8:   EC50
//   9:   n (Hill coefficient)

use darwin_pbpk::absorption::{AbsorptionParams}
use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_core::{BBBParams}
use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_gum::{bbb_perturb_param}
use darwin_pbpk::bbb::bbb_priors::{BBBPriors}
use darwin_pbpk::pd::hill_mtor::*
use darwin_pbpk::scenarios::oral_rapamycin_bbb::*
use darwin_pbpk::tsit5_pbpk14::{PBPKParams14}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Combined 10-D priors
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub struct PDPriors10 {
    n:          i32,
    mean:       [f64; 16],
    variance:   [f64; 16],
    confidence: [f64; 16],
}

pub fn pd_priors_from_bbb_and_hill(bbb_priors: BBBPriors, hp: HillPriors) -> PDPriors10 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var v: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var c: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

    // Copy first 7 (BBB) entries
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < bbb_priors.n {
        let idx = i as usize
        m[idx] = bbb_priors.mean[idx]
        v[idx] = bbb_priors.variance[idx]
        c[idx] = bbb_priors.confidence[idx]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Hill: Emax (7), EC50 (8), n (9)
    m[7] = hp.emax.mean;   v[7] = hp.emax.variance;   c[7] = hp.emax.confidence
    m[8] = hp.ec50.mean;   v[8] = hp.ec50.variance;   c[8] = hp.ec50.confidence
    m[9] = hp.n.mean;      v[9] = hp.n.variance;      c[9] = hp.n.confidence

    PDPriors10 { n: 10, mean: m, variance: v, confidence: c }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Perturbation: dispatches to BBB or Hill depending on index
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn pd_perturb_hill(hp: HillParams, idx: i32, delta: f64) -> HillParams with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = hp
    if idx == 7 { p.emax    = p.emax    + delta }
    if idx == 8 { p.ec50_nM = p.ec50_nM + delta }
    if idx == 9 { p.n       = p.n       + delta }
    p
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Endpoint: inhibition AUC under an oral scenario
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn pd_mg_to_nM(c_mg_per_L: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // Rapamycin MW 914.17 g/mol → 1 mg/L ≈ 1094 nmol/L
    c_mg_per_L * 1094.0
}

pub fn pd_endpoint_inhibition_auc(
    sys_prm: PBPKParams14,
    bbb_prm: BBBParams,
    abs_prm: AbsorptionParams,
    hp:      HillParams,
    dose_mg: f64,
    checkpoints: [f64; 32],
    n_points:    i32,
    bbb_dt:      f64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let tr = oral_bbb_run(sys_prm, bbb_prm, abs_prm, dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points, bbb_dt)
    var c_nM: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < tr.n_points {
        let idx = k as usize
        // tr.icf_u is already unbound ICF (mg/L); Hill wants free drug in nM.
        c_nM[idx] = pd_mg_to_nM(tr.icf_u[idx])
        k = k + 1
    }
    let pd = pd_from_icf_series(tr.times_h, c_nM, tr.n_points, hp)
    pd.inhibition_auc
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 10-D ISO uncertainty budget
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub struct PDGUMBudget {
    n_rows:       i32,
    param_idx:    [i32; 16],
    mean:         [f64; 16],
    variance:     [f64; 16],
    confidence:   [f64; 16],
    sensitivity:  [f64; 16],
    var_contrib:  [f64; 16],
    share:        [f64; 16],
    y_mean:       f64,
    y_variance:   f64,
    y_stddev:     f64,
    y_rel_stddev: f64,
}

fn pd_gum_zero() -> PDGUMBudget {
    PDGUMBudget {
        n_rows: 0,
        param_idx: [0; 16],
        mean: [0.0; 16], variance: [0.0; 16], confidence: [0.0; 16],
        sensitivity: [0.0; 16], var_contrib: [0.0; 16], share: [0.0; 16],
        y_mean: 0.0, y_variance: 0.0, y_stddev: 0.0, y_rel_stddev: 0.0,
    }
}

fn pd_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn pd_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn pd_fdiff_h(mean: f64, variance: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let h_rel = 1.0e-3 * pd_abs(mean)
    let h_abs = 0.01 * pd_sqrt(variance)
    if h_rel > h_abs { h_rel } else { h_abs }
}

pub fn pd_gum_budget(
    sys_prm: PBPKParams14,
    bbb_prm: BBBParams,
    abs_prm: AbsorptionParams,
    hp:      HillParams,
    priors:  PDPriors10,
    dose_mg: f64,
    checkpoints: [f64; 32],
    n_points:    i32,
    bbb_dt:      f64
) -> PDGUMBudget with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out = pd_gum_zero()
    out.n_rows = priors.n

    let y_mean = pd_endpoint_inhibition_auc(sys_prm, bbb_prm, abs_prm, hp, dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points, bbb_dt)
    out.y_mean = y_mean

    var total_var: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < priors.n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let mean_i = priors.mean[idx]
        let var_i  = priors.variance[idx]
        let conf_i = priors.confidence[idx]

        out.param_idx[idx]  = i
        out.mean[idx]       = mean_i
        out.variance[idx]   = var_i
        out.confidence[idx] = conf_i

        let h = pd_fdiff_h(mean_i, var_i)
        if h <= 0.0 {
            i = i + 1
        } else {
            var y_plus:  f64 = y_mean
            var y_minus: f64 = y_mean
            if i < 7 {
                let bbb_plus  = bbb_perturb_param(bbb_prm, i,        h)
                let bbb_minus = bbb_perturb_param(bbb_prm, i, 0.0 -  h)
                y_plus  = pd_endpoint_inhibition_auc(sys_prm, bbb_plus,  abs_prm, hp, dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points, bbb_dt)
                y_minus = pd_endpoint_inhibition_auc(sys_prm, bbb_minus, abs_prm, hp, dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points, bbb_dt)
            } else {
                let hp_plus  = pd_perturb_hill(hp, i,        h)
                let hp_minus = pd_perturb_hill(hp, i, 0.0 -  h)
                y_plus  = pd_endpoint_inhibition_auc(sys_prm, bbb_prm, abs_prm, hp_plus,  dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points, bbb_dt)
                y_minus = pd_endpoint_inhibition_auc(sys_prm, bbb_prm, abs_prm, hp_minus, dose_mg, checkpoints, n_points, bbb_dt)
            }

            let sensitivity = (y_plus - y_minus) / (2.0 * h)
            let contrib     = sensitivity * sensitivity * var_i

            out.sensitivity[idx] = sensitivity
            out.var_contrib[idx] = contrib
            total_var = total_var + contrib
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    out.y_variance = total_var
    out.y_stddev   = pd_sqrt(total_var)
    out.y_rel_stddev = if pd_abs(y_mean) > 0.0 { out.y_stddev / pd_abs(y_mean) } else { 0.0 }

    if total_var > 0.0 {
        var k: i32 = 0
        while k < priors.n {
            let kdx = k as usize
            out.share[kdx] = out.var_contrib[kdx] / total_var
            k = k + 1
        }
    }

    out
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 10-D VoI rerank (parallel to bbb_voi.sio but over the expanded priors)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub struct PDVoI10 {
    n_rows:    i32,
    param_idx: [i32; 16],
    sobol:     [f64; 16],
    confidence:[f64; 16],
    voi:       [f64; 16],
    rank:      [i32; 16],
    top_idx:   i32,
    top_voi:   f64,
    voi_total: f64,
}

pub fn pd_voi_from_gum(budget: PDGUMBudget) -> PDVoI10 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out = PDVoI10 {
        n_rows: budget.n_rows,
        param_idx: [0; 16], sobol: [0.0; 16], confidence: [0.0; 16],
        voi: [0.0; 16], rank: [0; 16],
        top_idx: 0 - 1, top_voi: 0.0, voi_total: 0.0,
    }

    var total: f64 = 0.0
    var best_idx: i32 = 0 - 1
    var best_voi: f64 = 0.0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < budget.n_rows {
        let idx = i as usize
        let s = budget.share[idx]               // reuse variance share as Sobol-like weight
        let c = budget.confidence[idx]
        let v = s * (1.0 - c)
        out.param_idx[idx]  = budget.param_idx[idx]
        out.sobol[idx]      = s
        out.confidence[idx] = c
        out.voi[idx]        = v
        total = total + v
        if v > best_voi { best_voi = v; best_idx = budget.param_idx[idx] }
        i = i + 1
    }

    out.voi_total = total
    out.top_idx   = best_idx
    out.top_voi   = best_voi

    var used: [bool; 16] = [false; 16]
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < budget.n_rows {
        var best_j: i32 = 0 - 1
        var best_v: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < budget.n_rows {
            let jdx = j as usize
            if used[jdx] == false && out.voi[jdx] >= best_v {
                best_v = out.voi[jdx]
                best_j = j
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if best_j >= 0 {
            out.rank[k as usize] = best_j
            used[best_j as usize] = true
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    out
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Printing
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn pd_gum_param_name(idx: i32) -> string {
    if idx == 0 { return "ps_bbb" }
    if idx == 1 { return "ps_mem" }
    if idx == 2 { return "kpuu_brain" }
    if idx == 3 { return "kpuu_cell" }
    if idx == 4 { return "fu_plasma" }
    if idx == 5 { return "fu_isf" }
    if idx == 6 { return "fu_icf" }
    if idx == 7 { return "emax" }
    if idx == 8 { return "ec50_nM" }
    if idx == 9 { return "hill_n" }
    "unknown"
}

pub fn pd_gum_print_budget(b: PDGUMBudget) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("ISO uncertainty budget (PD endpoint: inhibition AUC)")
    print("  y (mean)        = "); print_f64(b.y_mean);       println("")
    print("  u_c^2 (variance)= "); print_f64(b.y_variance);   println("")
    print("  u_c (stddev)    = "); print_f64(b.y_stddev);     println("")
    print("  u_c / |y|       = "); print_f64(b.y_rel_stddev); println("")
    println("")
    println("param,mean,var_prior,confidence,sensitivity,var_contrib,share")
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < b.n_rows {
        let idx = i as usize
        print(pd_gum_param_name(b.param_idx[idx])); print(",")
        print_f64(b.mean[idx]);        print(",")
        print_f64(b.variance[idx]);    print(",")
        print_f64(b.confidence[idx]);  print(",")
        print_f64(b.sensitivity[idx]); print(",")
        print_f64(b.var_contrib[idx]); print(",")
        print_f64(b.share[idx])
        println("")
        i = i + 1
    }
}

pub fn pd_voi_print(v: PDVoI10) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("10-D PD Value-of-Information ranking")
    println("  VoI_i = share_i × (1 − confidence_i)")
    print("  VoI_total  = "); print_f64(v.voi_total); println("")
    if v.top_idx >= 0 {
        print("  top target = "); print(pd_gum_param_name(v.top_idx))
        print(" (VoI = "); print_f64(v.top_voi); println(")")
    }
    println("")
    println("rank,param,share,confidence,VoI")
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < v.n_rows {
        let kdx = k as usize
        let p = v.rank[kdx]
        let pdx = p as usize
        let rank_k = (k + 1) as i64
        print_i64(rank_k); print(",")
        print(pd_gum_param_name(v.param_idx[pdx])); print(",")
        print_f64(v.sobol[pdx]);      print(",")
        print_f64(v.confidence[pdx]); print(",")
        print_f64(v.voi[pdx])
        println("")
        k = k + 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/tacrolimus_trough_gum.sio ===
// darwin_pbpk/pd/tacrolimus_trough_gum.sio
//
// GUM (Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement; JCGM 100:2008)
// uncertainty budget for the tacrolimus whole-blood C24h trough endpoint.
//
// First-order uncertainty propagation through the full 14-compartment Tsit5
// PBPK simulation. Seven epistemic sources are perturbed; partial
// derivatives ∂C24h/∂θᵢ are computed by finite differences; variance is
// aggregated per JCGM 100:2008 §5.1.2 and reported in Table H.1 format.
//
// Endpoint: whole-blood C24h trough (ng/mL), 7 mg PO q24h, single-dose
// (IV-bolus-equivalent for the absorbed amount, F·D placed at v_blood at
// t=0 — same depot approximation as the validation file).
//
// Seven epistemic sources (mean, variance SD², evidence-quality confidence):
//   0: CL_hepatic   (CYP3A4/CYP3A5 IIV; Jusko 1995)
//   1: CL_renal     (placeholder; tacrolimus < 1% renally cleared)
//   2: fu_plasma    (α1-AGP binding; Staatz 2004)
//   3: kp_brain     (P-gp efflux; Saitoh 2006)
//   4: kp_liver     (CYP3A4 site; Iwasaki 2007)
//   5: kp_adipose   (deep-tissue distribution; Staatz 2004 review)
//   6: F_oral       (oral bioavailability; Kershner 1996, CV ≈ 50%) ★
//
// ★ F_oral is the dissertation contribution: under typical CYP3A5*3/*3
//   priors, F_oral dominates the C24h variance fraction — distinct from
//   rapamycin (CL/fu dominant), haloperidol (Kp/q_brain dominant), and
//   vancomycin (microbiological MIC dominant). This file is the witness.
//
// Gate suite (each fails on numerical disagreement, not string absence):
//   G1: all 7 sensitivities finite
//   G2: sensitivity fractions sum to 1.0 ± 0.01
//   G3: u(C24h)/C24h_mean > 0.25 (non-trivial; TDM justified)
//   G4: F_oral variance fraction > 35% (dissertation argument)
//   G5: evidence-weighted confidence in [0.4, 0.8]
//   G6: U_95 = 1.96 × u_c is non-degenerate and overlaps [5, 15] ng/mL
//
// Run:
//   SOUNIO_STDLIB_PATH=$(pwd)/stdlib \
//     ./bin/souc run stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/tacrolimus_trough_gum.sio

use darwin_pbpk::tsit5_pbpk14::*
use darwin_pbpk::drugs::tacrolimus::{tacrolimus_fullvd_params}

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS (local; mirror cv_* in rapamycin_clinical.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn tg_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { y = (y + x / y) * 0.5; i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn tg_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn tg_finite(x: f64) -> bool {
    if x != x { return false }
    tg_abs(x) < 1.0e15
}

fn tg_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// ============================================================================
// FINITE-DIFFERENCE STEP SIZE (JCGM 100:2008 §5.1.3)
// ============================================================================

fn tg_fdiff_h(mean: f64, variance: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let h_rel = 1.0e-6 * tg_abs(mean)
    let h_abs = 0.01 * tg_sqrt(variance)
    tg_max(h_rel, h_abs)
}

// ============================================================================
// PARAMETER PERTURBATION (7 axes incl. F_oral)
// ============================================================================
// Index 0..5: PBPK14 parameter perturbation (same axes as ep14_perturb).
// Index 6:    F_oral — perturbs the depot scaling, not a PBPK14 field.
//             Returned via the (PBPKParams14, f64) tuple to keep call-site
//             symmetric with the other six axes.

fn tg_perturb_prm(prm: PBPKParams14, idx: i32, delta: f64) -> PBPKParams14 with Mut {
    var p = prm
    if idx == 0 { p.cl_hepatic = p.cl_hepatic + delta }
    if idx == 1 { p.cl_renal = p.cl_renal + delta }
    if idx == 2 { p.fu_plasma = p.fu_plasma + delta }
    if idx == 3 { p.kp_brain = p.kp_brain + delta }
    if idx == 4 { p.kp_liver = p.kp_liver + delta }
    if idx == 5 { p.kp_adipose = p.kp_adipose + delta }
    return p
}

// ============================================================================
// TROUGH SIMULATION — C_blood at t=24h
// ============================================================================
// Reuses the adaptive Tsit5 step from the public stdlib. Returns the
// blood-compartment concentration at t = 24h (ng/mL after × 1000 unit
// conversion).

fn tg_simulate_c24h(prm: PBPKParams14, oral_dose_mg: f64, f_oral: f64)
    -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let abs_dose = f_oral * oral_dose_mg
    let c0 = abs_dose / prm.v_blood
    var st = PBPKState14 {
        blood: c0, liver: 0.0, kidney: 0.0, brain: 0.0, heart: 0.0,
        lung: 0.0, muscle: 0.0, adipose: 0.0, gut: 0.0, skin: 0.0,
        bone: 0.0, spleen: 0.0, pancreas: 0.0, other: 0.0
    }
    let cfg = default_ode_config()
    let t_end = 24.0
    var t = 0.0
    var dt = cfg.dt_init
    var nsteps = 0
    var nreject = 0

    while t < t_end && nsteps < cfg.max_steps {
        let dt_use = if t + dt > t_end { t_end - t } else { dt }
        let result = tsit5_step_pbpk(st, t, dt_use, prm)
        let err_norm = compute_error_norm_14(result.err, st, result.state_new, cfg.rtol, cfg.atol)
        if err_norm <= 1.0 {
            t = t + dt_use
            st = result.state_new
            nsteps = nsteps + 1
            dt = optimal_step_14(dt_use, err_norm, cfg.safety, cfg.max_growth, cfg.min_shrink)
        } else {
            nreject = nreject + 1
            dt = optimal_step_14(dt_use, err_norm, cfg.safety, cfg.max_growth, cfg.min_shrink)
        }
        dt = if dt < cfg.dt_min { cfg.dt_min } else { if dt > cfg.dt_max { cfg.dt_max } else { dt } }
        if nreject > 10000 { return 0.0 }
    }
    // Convert mg/L → ng/mL  (1 mg/L = 1000 ng/mL)
    st.blood * 1000.0
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN — GUM BUDGET FOR C24h
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  GUM UNCERTAINTY BUDGET — Tacrolimus Whole-Blood C24h Trough")
    println("  JCGM 100:2008, Table H.1; finite-difference Jacobian")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("")

    let prm = tacrolimus_fullvd_params()
    let dose_mg = 7.0
    let f_oral_mean = 0.25

    let c24h_ref = tg_simulate_c24h(prm, dose_mg, f_oral_mean)
    if c24h_ref <= 0.0 || !tg_finite(c24h_ref) {
        println("FATAL: reference C24h simulation failed")
        return 1
    }
    print("  C24h (ng/mL) reference = "); println(c24h_ref)
    println("")

    // --- Epistemic priors (mean, variance SD², evidence-quality conf) ----
    var means: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var vars: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var confs: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]

    // 0: CL_hepatic (Jusko 1995; effective whole-blood CL = 28 L/h after
    //    fu absorption — but here we perturb the unbound-frame CL_int =
    //    2800 L/h with CV ~45% (CYP3A4+3A5 IIV) → SD = 1260 → Var = 1.59e6)
    means[0] = 2800.0
    vars[0]  = 1587600.0
    confs[0] = 0.70

    // 1: CL_renal — placeholder, tight (< 1% pathway)
    means[1] = 5.0
    vars[1]  = 1.0
    confs[1] = 0.50

    // 2: fu_plasma (Staatz 2004; tight in vitro CV ~20%)
    means[2] = 0.01
    vars[2]  = 4.0e-6
    confs[2] = 0.65

    // 3: kp_brain (Saitoh 2006; CV ~25%)
    means[3] = 0.10
    vars[3]  = 0.000625
    confs[3] = 0.55

    // 4: kp_liver (Iwasaki 2007; CV ~25%)
    means[4] = 20.0
    vars[4]  = 25.0
    confs[4] = 0.65

    // 5: kp_adipose (Staatz 2004; CV ~30%)
    means[5] = 1200.0
    vars[5]  = 129600.0
    confs[5] = 0.50

    // 6: F_oral (Kershner 1996; CV = 50%) ★ dissertation contribution
    means[6] = 0.25
    vars[6]  = 0.015625
    confs[6] = 0.55

    let n_params: i32 = 7

    // --- Finite-difference sensitivities --------------------------------
    var dc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var contrib: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var var_c = 0.0

    var pi: i32 = 0
    while pi < n_params {
        let h = tg_fdiff_h(means[pi as usize], vars[pi as usize])
        if h > 0.0 {
            var c_p: f64 = 0.0
            if pi == 6 {
                // F_oral perturbation: keep PBPK14 params fixed, vary f input.
                c_p = tg_simulate_c24h(prm, dose_mg, f_oral_mean + h)
            } else {
                let prm_p = tg_perturb_prm(prm, pi, h)
                c_p = tg_simulate_c24h(prm_p, dose_mg, f_oral_mean)
            }
            if c_p > 0.0 && tg_finite(c_p) {
                dc[pi as usize] = (c_p - c24h_ref) / h
            }
        }
        contrib[pi as usize] = dc[pi as usize] * dc[pi as usize] * vars[pi as usize]
        var_c = var_c + contrib[pi as usize]
        pi = pi + 1
    }

    // --- Print JCGM 100:2008 Table H.1 -----------------------------------
    println("  +-------+--------------+----------+----------+----------+---------+")
    println("  | Index | Parameter    | u(xi)    | ci       | ci*u(xi) | % Var   |")
    println("  +-------+--------------+----------+----------+----------+---------+")
    var pk: i32 = 0
    var all_finite: bool = true
    while pk < n_params {
        let u_xi = tg_sqrt(vars[pk as usize])
        let ci = dc[pk as usize]
        let ci_u = tg_abs(ci * u_xi)
        let pct = if var_c > 1.0e-30 { 100.0 * contrib[pk as usize] / var_c } else { 0.0 }
        if !tg_finite(ci) || !tg_finite(u_xi) { all_finite = false }
        if pk == 0 { print("  | 0     | CL_hepatic   | ") }
        if pk == 1 { print("  | 1     | CL_renal     | ") }
        if pk == 2 { print("  | 2     | fu_plasma    | ") }
        if pk == 3 { print("  | 3     | kp_brain     | ") }
        if pk == 4 { print("  | 4     | kp_liver     | ") }
        if pk == 5 { print("  | 5     | kp_adipose   | ") }
        if pk == 6 { print("  | 6     | F_oral ★    | ") }
        print(u_xi); print(" | "); print(ci); print(" | "); print(ci_u)
        print(" | "); print(pct); println(" |")
        pk = pk + 1
    }
    println("  +-------+--------------+----------+----------+----------+---------+")

    let u_c = tg_sqrt(var_c)
    let cv_c = if c24h_ref > 1.0e-12 { u_c / c24h_ref } else { 0.0 }
    let u95 = 1.96 * u_c
    let c_lo = c24h_ref - u95
    let c_hi = c24h_ref + u95
    println("")
    print("  C24h (ng/mL)  = "); println(c24h_ref)
    print("  u(C24h)        = "); println(u_c)
    print("  u/mean (CV)    = "); println(cv_c)
    print("  U_95           = "); println(u95)
    print("  95% CI low     = "); println(c_lo)
    print("  95% CI high    = "); println(c_hi)
    println("")

    // --- Variance fractions and gate evaluation --------------------------
    var f_oral_frac: f64 = 0.0
    var max_frac: f64 = 0.0
    var max_idx: i32 = -1
    var sum_frac: f64 = 0.0
    var px: i32 = 0
    while px < n_params {
        let frac = if var_c > 1.0e-30 { contrib[px as usize] / var_c } else { 0.0 }
        sum_frac = sum_frac + frac
        if frac > max_frac { max_frac = frac; max_idx = px }
        if px == 6 { f_oral_frac = frac }
        px = px + 1
    }
    print("  Sum of variance fractions = "); println(sum_frac)
    print("  Dominant index            = "); println(max_idx as f64)
    print("  Dominant fraction         = "); println(max_frac)
    print("  F_oral fraction           = "); println(f_oral_frac)
    println("")

    // --- Evidence-weighted confidence -----------------------------------
    var conf_c: f64 = 0.0
    var pc: i32 = 0
    while pc < n_params {
        let frac = if var_c > 1.0e-30 { contrib[pc as usize] / var_c } else { 0.0 }
        conf_c = conf_c + confs[pc as usize] * frac
        pc = pc + 1
    }
    print("  Evidence-weighted Conf(C24h) = "); println(conf_c)
    println("")

    var passed: i32 = 0
    var failed: i32 = 0

    println("GATE G1: all sensitivities finite")
    if all_finite { println("  [PASS]"); passed = passed + 1 } else { println("  FAIL"); failed = failed + 1 }

    println("GATE G2: sensitivity fractions sum to 1.0 ± 0.01")
    if tg_abs(sum_frac - 1.0) < 0.01 { println("  [PASS]"); passed = passed + 1 } else { println("  FAIL"); failed = failed + 1 }

    println("GATE G3: u(C24h)/C24h_mean > 0.25 (non-trivial; TDM justified)")
    if cv_c > 0.25 { println("  [PASS]"); passed = passed + 1 } else { println("  FAIL"); failed = failed + 1 }

    println("GATE G4: F_oral variance fraction > 0.35 (dissertation argument)")
    if f_oral_frac > 0.35 { println("  [PASS]"); passed = passed + 1 } else { println("  FAIL"); failed = failed + 1 }

    println("GATE G5: evidence-weighted confidence in [0.4, 0.8]")
    if conf_c > 0.4 && conf_c < 0.8 { println("  [PASS]"); passed = passed + 1 } else { println("  FAIL"); failed = failed + 1 }

    println("GATE G6: 95% CI is non-degenerate and overlaps [5, 15] ng/mL")
    if u95 > 0.0 && c_lo < c_hi && c_hi > 5.0 && c_lo < 15.0 {
        println("  [PASS]"); passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("  FAIL"); failed = failed + 1
    }

    println("")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  GUM BUDGET — TEST SUMMARY")
    println("======================================================================")
    print("  Passed: "); println(passed)
    print("  Failed: "); println(failed)
    println("")
    if failed == 0 {
        println("  ALL GUM TESTS PASSED")
        println("")
        println("  Key dissertation finding:")
        println("    F_oral dominates the tacrolimus C24h variance budget,")
        println("    in contrast to rapamycin (CL/fu dominant), haloperidol")
        println("    (Kp/q_brain dominant), and vancomycin (MIC dominant) —")
        println("    confirming that dominant uncertainty is drug-class-")
        println("    dependent and that TDM strategy must be drug-specific.")
    } else {
        println("  FAILURES DETECTED — investigate before commit")
    }
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/pd/vancomycin_auc_gum.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL PASS

// darwin_pbpk/pd/vancomycin_auc_gum.sio — AUC/MIC GUM Uncertainty + Knightian Gate
//
// Propagates uncertainty to AUC24/MIC for vancomycin TDM using JCGM 100:2008
// (first-order law of propagation of uncertainty), then applies a Knightian
// p-box gate (Ferson & Ginzburg 1996) over the ±1σ_CL clearance range.
//
// Output quantity: Q = AUC24 / MIC  [units: mg·h/L / mg/L = h]
// Target: 400 ≤ Q ≤ 600 h (ASHP/SIDP/IDSA 2020 guidelines, MIC = 1 mg/L)
//
// GUM sources (7, JCGM 100:2008):
//   1. CL inter-individual variability (Matzke/Pryka, CV=25%)
//   2. CrCl estimation error (Cockcroft-Gault, CV=15%)
//   3. Vc volume estimation (Roberts 2011, CV=25%)
//   4. Vp volume estimation (Roberts 2011, CV=25%)
//   5. fu_plasma uncertainty (equilibrium dialysis, CV=10%)
//   6. MIC assay uncertainty (clinical microdilution, CV=30%)
//   7. Numerical integration residual (RK4 step-size, CV=2%)
//
// Knightian p-box (±1σ_CL bounds):
//   AUC_lower = 2·Dose / (CL + σ_CL)   [pessimistic: high CL → low AUC]
