// === FILE: stdlib/encoding/base64.sio ===
// stdlib/encoding/base64.sio — Base64 Encoding / Decoding (RFC 4648)
//
// Standard and URL-safe Base64.
// Operates on fixed-size arrays (no heap allocation).
//
// # Capacity
//   - Encode: up to 192 input bytes → 256 output bytes (includes padding)
//   - Decode: up to 256 encoded bytes → 192 output bytes
//
// # Example
//   var out: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
//   let len = base64_encode(&input, n, &!out)
//   // out[0..len] contains the Base64 string

// =============================================================================
// Alphabet helpers
// =============================================================================

// Standard Base64 alphabet: index → ASCII character (RFC 4648 §4)
fn b64_char_std(idx: u8) -> u8 {
    if idx < (26 as u8) { return (65 as u8) + idx }        // A-Z (ASCII 65-90)
    if idx < (52 as u8) { return (97 as u8) + (idx - (26 as u8)) }  // a-z (ASCII 97-122)
    if idx < (62 as u8) { return (48 as u8) + (idx - (52 as u8)) }  // 0-9 (ASCII 48-57)
    if idx == (62 as u8) { return (43 as u8) }              // + (ASCII 43)
    (47 as u8)                                         // / (ASCII 47)
}

// URL-safe Base64 alphabet (RFC 4648 §5): + → -, / → _, no padding
fn b64_char_url(idx: u8) -> u8 {
    if idx < (26 as u8) { return (65 as u8) + idx }
    if idx < (52 as u8) { return (97 as u8) + (idx - (26 as u8)) }
    if idx < (62 as u8) { return (48 as u8) + (idx - (52 as u8)) }
    if idx == (62 as u8) { return (45 as u8) }  // - (ASCII 45)
    (95 as u8)                            // _ (ASCII 95)
}

// Decode a base64 character to 6-bit value. Returns 255 for invalid/padding.
fn b64_decode_char(c: u8) -> u8 {
    if c >= (65 as u8) && c <= (90 as u8)  { return c - (65 as u8) }          // A-Z → 0-25
    if c >= (97 as u8) && c <= (122 as u8) { return c - (97 as u8) + (26 as u8) }   // a-z → 26-51
    if c >= (48 as u8) && c <= (57 as u8)  { return c - (48 as u8) + (52 as u8) }   // 0-9 → 52-61
    if c == (43 as u8) || c == (45 as u8)  { return (62 as u8) }               // + or - → 62
    if c == (47 as u8) || c == (95 as u8)  { return (63 as u8) }               // / or _ → 63
    (255 as u8)   // invalid or padding (=)
}

// =============================================================================
// Encode — Standard Base64
// =============================================================================

/// Encode bytes to standard Base64 (RFC 4648 §4, with = padding).
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `data`: Input byte array (max 192 bytes)
/// - `data_len`: Number of valid bytes in `data`
/// - `out`: Output array for the Base64 ASCII bytes
///
/// # Return
/// Number of bytes written to `out` (multiple of 4), or -1 on error.
pub fn base64_encode(data: &[u8; 256], data_len: i32, out: &![u8; 256]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if data_len < 0 || data_len > 192 { return 0 - 1 }

    var out_pos: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0

    while i + 2 < data_len {
        let b0 = data[i as usize]
        let b1 = data[(i + 1) as usize]
        let b2 = data[(i + 2) as usize]

        out[out_pos as usize]       = b64_char_std((b0 >> (2 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 1) as usize] = b64_char_std(((b0 << (4 as u8)) | (b1 >> (4 as u8))) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 2) as usize] = b64_char_std(((b1 << (2 as u8)) | (b2 >> (6 as u8))) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 3) as usize] = b64_char_std(b2 & (63 as u8))

        i = i + 3
        out_pos = out_pos + 4
    }

    // Handle remaining 1 or 2 bytes
    let rem = data_len - i
    if rem == 1 {
        let b0 = data[i as usize]
        out[out_pos as usize]       = b64_char_std((b0 >> (2 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 1) as usize] = b64_char_std((b0 << (4 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 2) as usize] = (61 as u8)   // =
        out[(out_pos + 3) as usize] = (61 as u8)   // =
        out_pos = out_pos + 4
    } else if rem == 2 {
        let b0 = data[i as usize]
        let b1 = data[(i + 1) as usize]
        out[out_pos as usize]       = b64_char_std((b0 >> (2 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 1) as usize] = b64_char_std(((b0 << (4 as u8)) | (b1 >> (4 as u8))) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 2) as usize] = b64_char_std((b1 << (2 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 3) as usize] = (61 as u8)   // =
        out_pos = out_pos + 4
    }

    out_pos
}

// =============================================================================
// Encode — URL-safe Base64
// =============================================================================

/// Encode bytes to URL-safe Base64 (RFC 4648 §5).
/// Uses - and _ instead of + and /. No = padding.
///
/// # Return
/// Number of bytes written, or -1 on error.
pub fn base64_encode_url_safe(data: &[u8; 256], data_len: i32, out: &![u8; 256]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if data_len < 0 || data_len > 192 { return 0 - 1 }

    var out_pos: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0

    while i + 2 < data_len {
        let b0 = data[i as usize]
        let b1 = data[(i + 1) as usize]
        let b2 = data[(i + 2) as usize]

        out[out_pos as usize]       = b64_char_url((b0 >> (2 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 1) as usize] = b64_char_url(((b0 << (4 as u8)) | (b1 >> (4 as u8))) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 2) as usize] = b64_char_url(((b1 << (2 as u8)) | (b2 >> (6 as u8))) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 3) as usize] = b64_char_url(b2 & (63 as u8))

        i = i + 3
        out_pos = out_pos + 4
    }

    let rem = data_len - i
    if rem == 1 {
        let b0 = data[i as usize]
        out[out_pos as usize]       = b64_char_url((b0 >> (2 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 1) as usize] = b64_char_url((b0 << (4 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out_pos = out_pos + 2
    } else if rem == 2 {
        let b0 = data[i as usize]
        let b1 = data[(i + 1) as usize]
        out[out_pos as usize]       = b64_char_url((b0 >> (2 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 1) as usize] = b64_char_url(((b0 << (4 as u8)) | (b1 >> (4 as u8))) & (63 as u8))
        out[(out_pos + 2) as usize] = b64_char_url((b1 << (2 as u8)) & (63 as u8))
        out_pos = out_pos + 3
    }

    out_pos
}

// =============================================================================
// Decode
// =============================================================================

/// Decode standard or URL-safe Base64 to raw bytes.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `data`: Base64 ASCII bytes (may include = padding; max 256 bytes)
/// - `data_len`: Number of valid bytes
/// - `out`: Output for decoded bytes (max 192 bytes)
///
/// # Return
/// Number of decoded bytes, or -1 on invalid input.
pub fn base64_decode(data: &[u8; 256], data_len: i32, out: &![u8; 256]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if data_len < 0 || data_len > 256 { return 0 - 1 }

    var out_pos: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0

    while i + 3 < data_len {
        let c0 = b64_decode_char(data[i as usize])
        let c1 = b64_decode_char(data[(i + 1) as usize])
        let c2 = b64_decode_char(data[(i + 2) as usize])
        let c3 = b64_decode_char(data[(i + 3) as usize])

        if c0 == (255 as u8) || c1 == (255 as u8) { return 0 - 1 }

        out[out_pos as usize] = ((c0 << (2 as u8)) | (c1 >> (4 as u8))) & (255 as u8)
        out_pos = out_pos + 1

        if data[(i + 2) as usize] != (61 as u8) {
            if c2 == (255 as u8) { return 0 - 1 }
            out[out_pos as usize] = ((c1 << (4 as u8)) | (c2 >> (2 as u8))) & (255 as u8)
            out_pos = out_pos + 1
        }

        if data[(i + 3) as usize] != (61 as u8) {
            if c3 == (255 as u8) { return 0 - 1 }
            out[out_pos as usize] = ((c2 << (6 as u8)) | c3) & (255 as u8)
            out_pos = out_pos + 1
        }

        i = i + 4
    }

    out_pos
}


// === FILE: stdlib/encoding/hex.sio ===
// stdlib/encoding/hex.sio — Hexadecimal Encoding / Decoding
//
// Encode bytes to lowercase or uppercase hex strings, and decode back.
// Operates on fixed-size arrays (no heap allocation).
//
// # Capacity
//   - Encode: up to 256 input bytes → 512 output hex chars
//   - Decode: up to 512 hex chars → 256 output bytes
//
// # Example
//   var out: [u8; 512] = [0; 512]
//   let len = hex_encode(&input, n, &!out)
//   // out[0..len] is the hex string (lowercase, no prefix)

// =============================================================================
// Nibble helpers
// =============================================================================

// Low nibble of byte → lowercase hex digit
fn nibble_to_hex_lo(b: u8) -> u8 {
    let n = b & (15 as u8)
    if n < (10 as u8) { (48 as u8) + n } else { (87 as u8) + n }  // '0'+n or 'a'-10+n
}

// Low nibble of byte → uppercase hex digit
fn nibble_to_hex_up(b: u8) -> u8 {
    let n = b & (15 as u8)
    if n < (10 as u8) { (48 as u8) + n } else { (55 as u8) + n }  // '0'+n or 'A'-10+n
}

// Hex digit (ASCII) → nibble value. Returns 255 on invalid.
fn hex_digit_val(c: u8) -> u8 {
    if c >= (48 as u8) && c <= (57 as u8)  { return c - (48 as u8) }         // 0-9
    if c >= (97 as u8) && c <= (102 as u8) { return c - (97 as u8) + (10 as u8) }  // a-f
    if c >= (65 as u8) && c <= (70 as u8)  { return c - (65 as u8) + (10 as u8) }  // A-F
    (255 as u8)   // invalid
}

// =============================================================================
// Encode — Lowercase hex
// =============================================================================

/// Encode bytes to lowercase hex (e.g. 0xDE → "de").
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `data`: Input bytes (max 256)
/// - `data_len`: Number of valid bytes
/// - `out`: Output array for hex ASCII (needs 2*data_len bytes)
///
/// # Return
/// Number of hex characters written (= 2*data_len), or -1 on error.
pub fn hex_encode(data: &[u8; 256], data_len: i32, out: &![u8; 512]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if data_len < 0 || data_len > 256 { return 0 - 1 }

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < data_len {
        let b = data[i as usize]
        out[(i * 2) as usize]       = nibble_to_hex_lo(b >> (4 as u8))
        out[(i * 2 + 1) as usize]   = nibble_to_hex_lo(b)
        i = i + 1
    }

    data_len * 2
}

// =============================================================================
// Encode — Uppercase hex
// =============================================================================

/// Encode bytes to uppercase hex (e.g. 0xDE → "DE").
///
/// # Return
/// Number of hex characters written, or -1 on error.
pub fn hex_encode_upper(data: &[u8; 256], data_len: i32, out: &![u8; 512]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if data_len < 0 || data_len > 256 { return 0 - 1 }

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < data_len {
        let b = data[i as usize]
        out[(i * 2) as usize]       = nibble_to_hex_up(b >> (4 as u8))
        out[(i * 2 + 1) as usize]   = nibble_to_hex_up(b)
        i = i + 1
    }

    data_len * 2
}

// =============================================================================
// Encode with 0x prefix
// =============================================================================

/// Encode bytes to lowercase hex with "0x" prefix.
///
/// # Return
/// Number of characters written (2 + 2*data_len), or -1 on error.
pub fn hex_encode_with_prefix(data: &[u8; 256], data_len: i32, out: &![u8; 512]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if data_len < 0 || data_len > 255 { return 0 - 1 }

    out[0] = (48 as u8)   // '0'
    out[1] = (120 as u8)  // 'x'

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < data_len {
        let b = data[i as usize]
        out[(2 + i * 2) as usize]       = nibble_to_hex_lo(b >> (4 as u8))
        out[(2 + i * 2 + 1) as usize]   = nibble_to_hex_lo(b)
        i = i + 1
    }

    2 + data_len * 2
}

// =============================================================================
// Decode
// =============================================================================

/// Decode lowercase or uppercase hex string to bytes.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `hex`: ASCII hex characters (max 512; must be even length)
/// - `hex_len`: Number of valid hex characters (must be even)
/// - `out`: Output bytes (max 256)
///
/// # Return
/// Number of bytes decoded, or -1 on invalid input / odd length.
pub fn hex_decode(hex: &[u8; 512], hex_len: i32, out: &![u8; 256]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if hex_len < 0 || hex_len > 512 { return 0 - 1 }
    // Skip optional "0x" prefix
    var start: i32 = 0
    if hex_len >= 2 && hex[0] == (48 as u8) && (hex[1] == (120 as u8) || hex[1] == (88 as u8)) {
        start = 2
    }
    let effective_len = hex_len - start
    if effective_len < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    // Must be even number of hex digits
    if effective_len % 2 != 0 { return 0 - 1 }

    let n_bytes = effective_len / 2

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_bytes {
        let hi = hex_digit_val(hex[(start + i * 2) as usize])
        let lo = hex_digit_val(hex[(start + i * 2 + 1) as usize])
        if hi == (255 as u8) || lo == (255 as u8) { return 0 - 1 }
        out[i as usize] = (hi << (4 as u8)) | lo
        i = i + 1
    }

    n_bytes
}

// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/active.sio ===
//! stdlib/epistemic/active.d
//!
//! Active Inference: Uncertainty-Driven Exploration
//!
//! In Active Inference, agents minimize expected free energy by:
//! 1. Reducing uncertainty about hidden states (exploration)
//! 2. Achieving preferred outcomes (exploitation)
//!
//! High variance in Knowledge values signals where to explore next.
//!
//! # Core Concepts
//!
//! - **Expected Free Energy (EFE)**: Combines epistemic value (info gain) and
//!   pragmatic value (goal achievement)
//! - **Precision**: Inverse variance - high precision = confident knowledge
//! - **Information Gain**: How much we expect to learn from an action
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```sounio
//! use epistemic::{Knowledge, active}
//!
//! // Current beliefs about drug efficacy
//! let drug_a = Knowledge::measured(0.65, 0.10, "trial_small")
//! let drug_b = Knowledge::measured(0.60, 0.02, "trial_large")
//!
//! // Which should we investigate further?
//! let priority = active::exploration_priority([drug_a, drug_b])
//! // Returns drug_a - higher variance means more to learn
//! ```

use epistemic::knowledge::{Epistemic, BetaConfidence};

// ============================================================================
// PRECISION AND INFORMATION METRICS
// ============================================================================

// Precision: inverse of variance (how confident are we?)
// Higher precision = more confident = less need to explore
pub fn precision(k: &Epistemic) -> f64 {
    1.0 / max_f64(k.variance, 0.0000001)
}

// Entropy of a Knowledge value (assuming Gaussian)
// H = 0.5 * ln(2πe * variance)
pub fn entropy(k: &Epistemic) -> f64 {
    let two_pi_e = 17.0794684453  // 2 * π * e
    0.5 * ln_f64(two_pi_e * max_f64(k.variance, 0.0000001))
}

// Expected information gain from observing a variable
// For Gaussian: IG ≈ 0.5 * ln(prior_var / posterior_var)
//
// If we expect posterior variance to be reduced by factor r:
// IG = 0.5 * ln(1 / r) = -0.5 * ln(r)
pub fn expected_info_gain(k: &Epistemic, expected_reduction: f64) -> f64 {
    0.0 - 0.5 * ln_f64(max_f64(min_f64(expected_reduction, 1.0), 0.01))
}

// Relative uncertainty: variance / value²
// Useful for comparing uncertainties across different scales
pub fn relative_uncertainty(k: &Epistemic) -> f64 {
    k.variance / max_f64(k.value * k.value, 0.0000001)
}

// Coefficient of variation: std / |mean|
pub fn coefficient_of_variation(k: &Epistemic) -> f64 {
    sqrt_f64(k.variance) / max_f64(abs_f64(k.value), 0.0000001)
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPLORATION PRIORITY
// ============================================================================

// Exploration score for a single Knowledge value
// Higher score = should explore this more
//
// Components:
// - Variance contribution: high variance → high score
// - Confidence penalty: low confidence → high score
// - Value bonus: important values get priority
pub fn exploration_score(k: &Epistemic, importance: f64) -> f64 {
    let variance_term = ln_f64(1.0 + k.variance)
    let confidence_term = 1.0 - k.confidence.mean()
    let importance_term = importance

    variance_term + confidence_term + importance_term
}

// Find the index with highest exploration priority (highest score = explore first)
pub fn exploration_priority(values: &[Epistemic]) -> usize {
    let n = values.len()
    if n == 0 { return 0 }

    var best_idx = 0
    var best_score = exploration_score(&values[0], 1.0)

    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        let s = exploration_score(&values[i], 1.0)
        if s > best_score {
            best_score = s
            best_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    best_idx
}

// Get the Knowledge value most worth exploring
pub fn most_uncertain<'a>(values: &'a [Epistemic]) -> Option<&'a Epistemic> {
    if values.is_empty() {
        return None
    }

    let priority = exploration_priority(values)
    Some(&values[priority])
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPECTED FREE ENERGY
// ============================================================================

// Expected Free Energy components
pub struct EFEComponents {
    /// Epistemic value: expected information gain
    epistemic: f64,

    /// Pragmatic value: expected reward/goal achievement
    pragmatic: f64,

    /// Total EFE (lower is better)
    total: f64,
}

// Compute Expected Free Energy for an action
//
// EFE = -epistemic_value - pragmatic_value
//     = -E[info_gain] - E[reward]
//
// We want to MINIMIZE EFE (maximize epistemic + pragmatic value)
pub fn expected_free_energy(
    current: &Epistemic,
    expected_posterior_var: f64,
    expected_reward: f64,
    reward_weight: f64,
) -> EFEComponents {
    // Epistemic value: how much will we learn?
    let info_gain = 0.5 * ln_f64(current.variance / max_f64(expected_posterior_var, 0.0000001))
    let epistemic = max_f64(info_gain, 0.0)

    // Pragmatic value: how much reward do we expect?
    let pragmatic = expected_reward * reward_weight

    // EFE: we want to minimize this (so negate the values we want to maximize)
    let total = 0.0 - epistemic - pragmatic

    EFEComponents {
        epistemic: epistemic,
        pragmatic: pragmatic,
        total: total,
    }
}

// Select action index that minimizes EFE
// Returns the index of the best action in the actions slice.
pub fn select_action_idx(
    actions: &[(f64, f64)],  // (expected_var_reduction, expected_reward) pairs
    current: &Epistemic,
    reward_weight: f64,
) -> Option<usize> {
    if actions.is_empty() {
        return None
    }

    var best_idx = 0
    var best_efe = 1.0e308  // f64::MAX equivalent

    var i = 0
    while i < actions.len() {
        let var_reduction = actions[i].0
        let reward = actions[i].1
        let posterior_var = current.variance * var_reduction
        let efe = expected_free_energy(current, posterior_var, reward, reward_weight)

        if efe.total < best_efe {
            best_efe = efe.total
            best_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    Some(best_idx)
}

// ============================================================================
// BELIEF UPDATING (PREDICTIVE PROCESSING)
// ============================================================================

// Prediction error: difference between observation and belief
pub fn prediction_error(belief: &Epistemic, observation: f64) -> f64 {
    observation - belief.value
}

// Precision-weighted prediction error
// This is the key quantity in predictive processing
pub fn precision_weighted_error(belief: &Epistemic, observation: f64) -> f64 {
    let error = observation - belief.value
    let prec = precision(belief)
    prec * error
}

// Update belief with observation using precision weighting
//
// posterior_mean = (prior_precision * prior_mean + obs_precision * obs)
//                / (prior_precision + obs_precision)
pub fn update_belief(
    prior: &Epistemic,
    observation: f64,
    observation_variance: f64,
) -> Epistemic {
    let prior_prec = precision(prior)
    let obs_prec = 1.0 / max_f64(observation_variance, 0.0000001)
    let total_prec = prior_prec + obs_prec

    let posterior_mean = (prior_prec * prior.value + obs_prec * observation) / total_prec
    let posterior_var = 1.0 / total_prec

    // Update confidence based on evidence accumulation
    let evidence_ratio = obs_prec / prior_prec
    let new_conf = prior.confidence.update(
        (evidence_ratio * 10.0) as i64,  // Pseudo-successes
        1,                                // Pseudo-failures
    )

    Epistemic {
        value: posterior_mean,
        variance: posterior_var,
        confidence: new_conf,
        provenance: prior.provenance.with_step("belief_update"),
    }
}

// Sequential belief updating with multiple observations
pub fn update_sequential(
    prior: Epistemic,
    observations: &[(f64, f64)],  // (value, variance) pairs
) -> Epistemic {
    var current = prior

    var i = 0
    while i < observations.len() {
        current = update_belief(&current, observations[i].0, observations[i].1)
        i = i + 1
    }

    current
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPLORATION STRATEGIES
// ============================================================================

// Epsilon-greedy exploration
// With probability epsilon, explore (pick most uncertain)
// Otherwise exploit (pick highest value)
pub fn epsilon_greedy(
    values: &[Epistemic],
    epsilon: f64,
    random_value: f64,  // Should be in [0, 1]
) -> Option<usize> {
    if values.is_empty() {
        return None
    }

    if random_value < epsilon {
        // Explore: pick most uncertain
        let priority = exploration_priority(values)
        Some(priority)
    } else {
        // Exploit: pick highest value
        var best_idx = 0
        var best_val = values[0].value

        var i = 1
        while i < values.len() {
            if values[i].value > best_val {
                best_val = values[i].value
                best_idx = i
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        Some(best_idx)
    }
}

// Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) selection
// Balances exploitation (high value) with exploration (high uncertainty)
//
// UCB = value + c * sqrt(variance)
pub fn ucb_select(values: &[Epistemic], exploration_constant: f64) -> Option<usize> {
    if values.is_empty() {
        return None
    }

    var best_idx = 0
    var best_ucb = values[0].value + exploration_constant * sqrt_f64(values[0].variance)

    var i = 1
    while i < values.len() {
        let ucb = values[i].value + exploration_constant * sqrt_f64(values[i].variance)
        if ucb > best_ucb {
            best_ucb = ucb
            best_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    Some(best_idx)
}

// Thompson Sampling: sample from posterior and pick highest
// Approximation: sample from N(value, variance)
pub fn thompson_select(values: &[Epistemic], random_normals: &[f64]) -> Option<usize> {
    if values.is_empty() || random_normals.len() < values.len() {
        return None
    }

    var best_idx = 0
    var best_sample = values[0].value + random_normals[0] * sqrt_f64(values[0].variance)

    var i = 1
    while i < values.len() {
        let sample = values[i].value + random_normals[i] * sqrt_f64(values[i].variance)
        if sample > best_sample {
            best_sample = sample
            best_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    Some(best_idx)
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 999999.0 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    let y = (x - 1.0) / (x + 1.0)
    var result = 0.0
    var term = y
    var i = 1
    while i < 30 {
        result = result + term / (i as f64)
        term = term * y * y
        i = i + 2
    }
    2.0 * result
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/aleatoric.sio ===
// Aleatoric uncertainty type — irreducible inherent randomness
//
// Aleatoric<T> wraps a value with irreducible uncertainty.
// Unlike Epistemic<T>, aleatoric uncertainty cannot be reduced
// by collecting more data or improving the model.
//
// Examples:
//   - Thermal sensor noise (physical limit)
//   - Quantum measurement outcomes
//   - Molecular Brownian motion

module epistemic::aleatoric

// Aleatoric uncertainty value wrapper.
// epsilon: relative uncertainty bound in [0, 1]
struct AleatoricValue {
    value: f64,
    epsilon: f64,
    source_description: i64,  // string table index for description
}

// Construct an aleatoric value with given uncertainty
fn aleatoric_new(value: f64, epsilon: f64) -> AleatoricValue {
    AleatoricValue {
        value: value,
        epsilon: epsilon,
        source_description: -1,
    }
}

// Integer square root approximation (Newton's method, 10 iterations)
fn sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 {
        0.0
    } else {
        var est: f64 = x
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < 10 {
            est = (est + x / est) / 2.0
            i = i + 1
        }
        est
    }
}

// Propagate through addition: a + b
// Rule: independent aleatoric uncertainties add in quadrature (they are uncorrelated)
fn aleatoric_add(a: AleatoricValue, b: AleatoricValue) -> AleatoricValue with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let combined_eps = sqrt_approx(a.epsilon * a.epsilon + b.epsilon * b.epsilon)
    AleatoricValue {
        value: a.value + b.value,
        epsilon: combined_eps,
        source_description: -1,
    }
}

// Propagate through multiplication
fn aleatoric_mul(a: AleatoricValue, b: AleatoricValue) -> AleatoricValue with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let combined_eps = sqrt_approx(a.epsilon * a.epsilon + b.epsilon * b.epsilon)
    AleatoricValue {
        value: a.value * b.value,
        epsilon: combined_eps,
        source_description: -1,
    }
}

// Extract the raw value (discarding uncertainty metadata)
fn aleatoric_value(a: AleatoricValue) -> f64 {
    a.value
}

// Extract the epsilon bound
fn aleatoric_epsilon(a: AleatoricValue) -> f64 {
    a.epsilon
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/audit_runtime.sio ===
//! Runtime audit log for W3C PROV-DM style provenance tracking.
//!
//! The log is a fixed-size circular buffer to keep runtime overhead bounded.
//! Entry ordering is exposed oldest-to-newest via `audit_get_entry`.

struct AuditEntry {
    // Store small enums in i64 slots so array-of-struct reads stay stable in the
    // current runtime/compiler layout.
    entry_type: i64,       // 0=data_read, 1=transform, 2=observe, 3=stat_test, 4=regulatory
    timestamp: i64,        // monotonic logical counter
    entity_id: i64,        // generated PROV entity identifier
    activity_id: i64,      // generating PROV activity identifier
    input1_id: i64,        // first input entity or encoded source metadata
    input2_id: i64,        // second input entity or encoded source metadata
    output_id: i64,        // output entity identifier
    operation: i64,        // 0=read, 1=add, 2=mul, 3=div, ...
    regulatory_layer: i64, // 0=none, 1=iso_17025, 2=ich_e6, 3=cfr_part11
    value: f64,            // recorded value (for stat tests: p-value)
    extra: f64,            // extra value (for stat tests: effect size)
}

var AUDIT_ENTRY_TYPES: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]
var AUDIT_TIMESTAMPS: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]
var AUDIT_ENTITY_IDS: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]
var AUDIT_ACTIVITY_IDS: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]
var AUDIT_INPUT1_IDS: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]
var AUDIT_INPUT2_IDS: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]
var AUDIT_OUTPUT_IDS: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]
var AUDIT_OPERATIONS: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]
var AUDIT_REGULATORY_LAYERS: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]
var AUDIT_VALUES: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
var AUDIT_EXTRAS: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]

struct AuditLog {
    entries: [AuditEntry; 4096]
    count: i64
    next_entity_id: i64
    next_activity_id: i64
    timestamp_counter: i64
}

fn audit_entry_zero() -> AuditEntry {
    AuditEntry {
        entry_type: 0,
        timestamp: 0,
        entity_id: 0,
        activity_id: 0,
        input1_id: 0,
        input2_id: 0,
        output_id: 0,
        operation: 0,
        regulatory_layer: 0,
        value: 0.0,
        extra: 0.0,
    }
}

fn audit_log_slot(seq: i64) -> i64 {
    if seq < 4096 { return seq }
    audit_log_slot(seq - 4096)
}

fn audit_log_oldest_timestamp(log: &AuditLog) -> i64 {
    if log.timestamp_counter <= log.count { return 0 }
    log.timestamp_counter - log.count
}

fn audit_log_new() -> AuditLog {
    AuditLog {
        entries: [audit_entry_zero(); 4096],
        count: 0,
        next_entity_id: 1,
        next_activity_id: 1,
        timestamp_counter: 0,
    }
}

fn audit_log_append(
    log: &!AuditLog,
    entry_type: i32,
    input1_id: i64,
    input2_id: i64,
    operation: i32,
    regulatory_layer: i32,
    value: f64,
    extra: f64
) -> i64 with Mut {
    let entity_id = log.next_entity_id
    let activity_id = log.next_activity_id
    let timestamp = log.timestamp_counter
    let slot = audit_log_slot(timestamp)

    AUDIT_ENTRY_TYPES[slot as usize] = entry_type
    AUDIT_TIMESTAMPS[slot as usize] = timestamp
    AUDIT_ENTITY_IDS[slot as usize] = entity_id
    AUDIT_ACTIVITY_IDS[slot as usize] = activity_id
    AUDIT_INPUT1_IDS[slot as usize] = input1_id
    AUDIT_INPUT2_IDS[slot as usize] = input2_id
    AUDIT_OUTPUT_IDS[slot as usize] = entity_id
    AUDIT_OPERATIONS[slot as usize] = operation
    AUDIT_REGULATORY_LAYERS[slot as usize] = regulatory_layer
    AUDIT_VALUES[slot as usize] = value
    AUDIT_EXTRAS[slot as usize] = extra

    log.entries[slot as usize] = AuditEntry {
        entry_type: entry_type,
        timestamp: timestamp,
        entity_id: entity_id,
        activity_id: activity_id,
        input1_id: input1_id,
        input2_id: input2_id,
        output_id: entity_id,
        operation: operation,
        regulatory_layer: regulatory_layer,
        value: value,
        extra: extra,
    }

    if log.count < 4096 {
        log.count = log.count + 1
    }
    log.next_entity_id = entity_id + 1
    log.next_activity_id = activity_id + 1
    log.timestamp_counter = timestamp + 1
    entity_id
}

fn audit_log_read(log: &!AuditLog, path_hash: i64, byte_start: i64, byte_end: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    // Preserve the source hash and byte window without expanding the entry schema.
    audit_log_append(log, 0, path_hash, byte_start, 0, 0, byte_end as f64, 0.0)
}

fn audit_log_transform(log: &!AuditLog, op: i32, in1: i64, in2: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    audit_log_append(log, 1, in1, in2, op, 0, 0.0, 0.0)
}

fn audit_log_observe(log: &!AuditLog, entity: i64, pre_hash: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    audit_log_append(log, 2, entity, pre_hash, 0, 0, 0.0, 0.0)
}

fn audit_log_test(log: &!AuditLog, test_name: i32, statistic: f64, p_value: f64, effect_size: f64) -> i64 with Mut {
    // Encode the test statistic in input1_id so the fixed record format retains it.
    let statistic_encoded = (statistic * 1000000.0) as i64
    audit_log_append(log, 3, statistic_encoded, 0, test_name, 0, p_value, effect_size)
}

fn audit_log_count(log: &AuditLog) -> i64 {
    log.count
}

fn audit_get_entry(log: &AuditLog, idx: i64) -> AuditEntry {
    if idx < 0 || idx >= log.count {
        return audit_entry_zero()
    }

    let oldest = audit_log_oldest_timestamp(log)
    let slot = audit_log_slot(oldest + idx)
    AuditEntry {
        entry_type: AUDIT_ENTRY_TYPES[slot as usize],
        timestamp: AUDIT_TIMESTAMPS[slot as usize],
        entity_id: AUDIT_ENTITY_IDS[slot as usize],
        activity_id: AUDIT_ACTIVITY_IDS[slot as usize],
        input1_id: AUDIT_INPUT1_IDS[slot as usize],
        input2_id: AUDIT_INPUT2_IDS[slot as usize],
        output_id: AUDIT_OUTPUT_IDS[slot as usize],
        operation: AUDIT_OPERATIONS[slot as usize],
        regulatory_layer: AUDIT_REGULATORY_LAYERS[slot as usize],
        value: AUDIT_VALUES[slot as usize],
        extra: AUDIT_EXTRAS[slot as usize],
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/audited.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/audited.sio
//
// Audited<T> — witness-bearing surgery (G9).
//
// Every surgical operation (unlearn, edit, gate, compose, revive) on a
// value of type `Audited<T>` produces not only the new value but also a
// *machine-checkable derivation* that the operation was performed
// correctly with respect to the sedenion ZD kernel.  The derivation is
// emitted as a Lean 4 term that compiles without `sorry` and without
// Mathlib, reducible to `native_decide` over the 168 ZD classes of 𝕊.
//
// Unlike post-hoc logging, the witness is intrinsic to the value:
// downstream code cannot separate the surgical effect from its proof.
// A value of type Audited<T> is, operationally, a pair
//     (post_surgery_state, lean_witness_bytes).
//
// Required effects: `with ZD, Witness`.  Compiler enforces via error 205.
// Formal backing: `audit_witness_is_derivation` (constructive Lean term)
// in formal/lean4/SounioSurgicalInterventions.lean.
// Operational benchmark: examples/zd_audit_witness.sio.

// WITNESS_BUF: simple ring-buffer backing store for Lean witnesses emitted
// during a run.  Each witness is a short ASCII-encoded sequence of the
// form  `unlearning_kernel_exact primA <hash>\n`  suitable for
// `lean --run` verification.
var WITNESS_BUF: [i8; 4096] = [0 as i8; 4096]
var WITNESS_LEN: i64 = 0

// witness_reset: clear the buffer before an audited session.
fn witness_reset() with Mut, ZD {
    var i = 0
    while i < 4096 { WITNESS_BUF[i] = 0 as i8; i = i + 1 }
    WITNESS_LEN = 0
}

// witness_push_byte: append a single byte to the witness buffer.  Drops
// silently if the buffer is full (in a full run we would panic; here we
// prefer graceful degradation so the surgical op completes).
fn witness_push_byte(b: i8) with Mut, ZD {
    if WITNESS_LEN < 4096 {
        WITNESS_BUF[WITNESS_LEN as usize] = b
        WITNESS_LEN = WITNESS_LEN + 1
    }
}

fn witness_push_str_bytes(buf: &[i8; 64], n: i64) with Mut, ZD {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        witness_push_byte((*buf)[i as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// witness_emit_unlearn_header: write the canonical header for an
// unlearning witness into the buffer.  Header format:
//   `[audit] surgical_op=unlearn witness=unlearning_kernel_exact\n`
// This is the prefix verified by audit.sio against the Lean theorem
// name.  The full witness must be emitted by the caller; this helper
// only writes the machine-checkable prefix.
fn witness_emit_unlearn_header() with Mut, ZD {
    // "[audit] surgical_op=unlearn witness=unlearning_kernel_exact\n"
    let header: [i8; 64] = [
        91 as i8, 97 as i8, 117 as i8, 100 as i8, 105 as i8, 116 as i8, 93 as i8, 32 as i8,  // "[audit] "
        115 as i8, 117 as i8, 114 as i8, 103 as i8, 105 as i8, 99 as i8, 97 as i8, 108 as i8, // "surgical"
        95 as i8, 111 as i8, 112 as i8, 61 as i8, 117 as i8, 110 as i8, 108 as i8, 101 as i8, // "_op=unle"
        97 as i8, 114 as i8, 110 as i8, 32 as i8, 119 as i8, 105 as i8, 116 as i8, 110 as i8, // "arn witn"
        101 as i8, 115 as i8, 115 as i8, 61 as i8, 107 as i8, 101 as i8, 114 as i8, 110 as i8, // "ess=kern"
        101 as i8, 108 as i8, 95 as i8, 101 as i8, 120 as i8, 97 as i8, 99 as i8, 116 as i8,  // "el_exact"
        10 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8,
        0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8, 0 as i8,
    ]
    witness_push_str_bytes(&header, 49)
}

// witness_verify_residual: given the post-surgery vector `w` and the
// target-surgery reference `target`, compute the L2 residual and record
// it in the witness.  A residual of 0.0 fp-exact corresponds to the
// theorem `unlearning_kernel_exact` being applicable; any non-zero value
// means the operation was not an exact ZD action.
fn witness_verify_residual(w: &[f64; 16], target: &[f64; 16]) -> f64 with Mut, ZD {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        let d = (*w)[i] - (*target)[i]
        s = s + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    s
}

// witness_is_exact_zd: predicate used by audit harnesses to decide if
// the recorded surgery satisfies the algebraic exactness predicate
// backed by the Lean theorem.  Tolerates a 1e-10 fp epsilon to account
// for the 0.707107 vs exact 1/sqrt(2) representation used in examples.
fn witness_is_exact_zd(residual: f64) -> bool with Mut, ZD {
    if residual < 0.0 { residual > 0.0 - 0.0000000001 }
    else { residual < 0.0000000001 }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/autodiff.sio ===
//! Automatic Differentiation for Sensitivity Coefficients
//!
//! GUM's law of propagation requires partial derivatives ("sensitivity coefficients"):
//!   u_c²(y) = Σᵢ (∂f/∂xᵢ)² u²(xᵢ) + 2 Σᵢ Σⱼ>ᵢ (∂f/∂xᵢ)(∂f/∂xⱼ) u(xᵢ,xⱼ)
//!
//! This module implements forward-mode AD using dual numbers:
//!   (value, derivative) pairs that propagate derivatives automatically.
//!
//! Benefits over numerical differentiation:
//!   - Exact derivatives (no truncation error)
//!   - Efficient (single forward pass)
//!   - Handles arbitrary compositions
//!
//! References:
//!   - GUM (JCGM 100:2008) Section 5.1: Law of propagation of uncertainty

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sin(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn cos(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL NUMBER: THE CORE OF FORWARD-MODE AD
// ============================================================================

// A dual number carries both value and derivative
// For computing ∂f/∂xᵢ: set xᵢ = Dual(value, 1.0), all others = Dual(value, 0.0)
struct Dual {
    val: f64,   // The value f(x)
    der: f64,   // The derivative ∂f/∂x
}

fn dual_const(x: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: x, der: 0.0 }
}

fn dual_var(x: f64) -> Dual {
    // Mark this as the variable we're differentiating with respect to
    return Dual { val: x, der: 1.0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL ARITHMETIC
// ============================================================================

// Addition: (a, a') + (b, b') = (a+b, a'+b')
fn dual_add(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual {
        val: a.val + b.val,
        der: a.der + b.der,
    }
}

// Subtraction: (a, a') - (b, b') = (a-b, a'-b')
fn dual_sub(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual {
        val: a.val - b.val,
        der: a.der - b.der,
    }
}

// Multiplication: (a, a') * (b, b') = (a*b, a*b' + a'*b)
fn dual_mul(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual {
        val: a.val * b.val,
        der: a.val * b.der + a.der * b.val,
    }
}

// Division: (a, a') / (b, b') = (a/b, (a'*b - a*b') / b²)
fn dual_div(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    if abs_f64(b.val) < 1.0e-15 {
        return Dual { val: 0.0, der: 0.0 }
    }
    return Dual {
        val: a.val / b.val,
        der: (a.der * b.val - a.val * b.der) / (b.val * b.val),
    }
}

// Negation: -(a, a') = (-a, -a')
fn dual_neg(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: 0.0 - a.val, der: 0.0 - a.der }
}

// Scale by constant: k * (a, a') = (k*a, k*a')
fn dual_scale(k: f64, a: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: k * a.val, der: k * a.der }
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL TRANSCENDENTAL FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Exponential: exp(a, a') = (exp(a), exp(a) * a')
fn dual_exp(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    let e = exp(a.val)
    return Dual { val: e, der: e * a.der }
}

// Natural log: log(a, a') = (log(a), a'/a)
fn dual_log(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    if a.val <= 0.0 {
        return Dual { val: 0.0 - 1.0e308, der: 0.0 }
    }
    return Dual { val: log(a.val), der: a.der / a.val }
}

// Square root: sqrt(a, a') = (sqrt(a), a' / (2*sqrt(a)))
fn dual_sqrt(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    if a.val < 0.0 {
        return Dual { val: 0.0, der: 0.0 }
    }
    let s = sqrt(a.val)
    if s < 1.0e-15 {
        return Dual { val: 0.0, der: 0.0 }
    }
    return Dual { val: s, der: a.der / (2.0 * s) }
}

// Power: a^n where n is constant
// (a, a')^n = (a^n, n * a^(n-1) * a')
fn dual_pow(a: Dual, n: f64) -> Dual {
    if abs_f64(a.val) < 1.0e-15 && n < 1.0 {
        return Dual { val: 0.0, der: 0.0 }
    }
    var pow_val: f64 = 1.0
    var pow_deriv: f64 = 0.0

    // Compute a^n using exp/log for general n
    if abs_f64(a.val) > 1.0e-15 {
        pow_val = exp(n * log(abs_f64(a.val)))
        if a.val < 0.0 {
            // Handle negative base for odd integer powers
            pow_val = 0.0 - pow_val
        }
        pow_deriv = n * exp((n - 1.0) * log(abs_f64(a.val))) * a.der
        if a.val < 0.0 && n != 2.0 {
            pow_deriv = 0.0 - pow_deriv
        }
    }

    return Dual { val: pow_val, der: pow_deriv }
}

// Sine: sin(a, a') = (sin(a), cos(a) * a')
fn dual_sin(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: sin(a.val), der: cos(a.val) * a.der }
}

// Cosine: cos(a, a') = (cos(a), -sin(a) * a')
fn dual_cos(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: cos(a.val), der: 0.0 - sin(a.val) * a.der }
}

// ============================================================================
// SENSITIVITY COEFFICIENT COMPUTATION
// ============================================================================

// Result of sensitivity analysis for a single input
struct SensitivityResult {
    value: f64,         // f(x)
    sensitivity: f64,   // ∂f/∂x
}

// Result of multi-input sensitivity analysis (up to 4 inputs)
struct MultiSensitivity {
    value: f64,
    sens1: f64,  // ∂f/∂x₁
    sens2: f64,  // ∂f/∂x₂
    sens3: f64,  // ∂f/∂x₃
    sens4: f64,  // ∂f/∂x₄
    n_inputs: i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// COMMON FUNCTION PATTERNS WITH AD
// ============================================================================

// f(x) = x² → ∂f/∂x = 2x
fn sensitivity_square(x: f64) -> SensitivityResult {
    let d = dual_var(x)
    let result = dual_mul(d, d)
    return SensitivityResult { value: result.val, sensitivity: result.der }
}

// f(x,y) = x + y → ∂f/∂x = 1, ∂f/∂y = 1
fn sensitivity_add(x: f64, y: f64) -> MultiSensitivity {
    // Copy parameters to locals (workaround for codegen bug with reused params)
    let x_val = x
    let y_val = y

    // Compute ∂f/∂x
    let dx = dual_var(x_val)
    let dy_const = dual_const(y_val)
    let r1 = dual_add(dx, dy_const)

    // Compute ∂f/∂y
    let dx_const = dual_const(x_val)
    let dy = dual_var(y_val)
    let r2 = dual_add(dx_const, dy)

    // Store in intermediates before struct return
    let val = r1.val
    let s1 = r1.der
    let s2 = r2.der

    return MultiSensitivity {
        value: val,
        sens1: s1,
        sens2: s2,
        sens3: 0.0,
        sens4: 0.0,
        n_inputs: 2,
    }
}

// f(x,y) = x * y → ∂f/∂x = y, ∂f/∂y = x
fn sensitivity_mul(x: f64, y: f64) -> MultiSensitivity {
    // Copy parameters to locals (workaround for codegen bug with reused params)
    let x_val = x
    let y_val = y

    let dx = dual_var(x_val)
    let dy_const = dual_const(y_val)
    let r1 = dual_mul(dx, dy_const)

    let dx_const = dual_const(x_val)
    let dy = dual_var(y_val)
    let r2 = dual_mul(dx_const, dy)

    let val = r1.val
    let s1 = r1.der
    let s2 = r2.der

    return MultiSensitivity {
        value: val,
        sens1: s1,
        sens2: s2,
        sens3: 0.0,
        sens4: 0.0,
        n_inputs: 2,
    }
}

// f(x,y) = x / y → ∂f/∂x = 1/y, ∂f/∂y = -x/y²
fn sensitivity_div(x: f64, y: f64) -> MultiSensitivity {
    // Copy parameters to locals (workaround for codegen bug with reused params)
    let x_val = x
    let y_val = y

    let dx = dual_var(x_val)
    let dy_const = dual_const(y_val)
    let r1 = dual_div(dx, dy_const)

    let dx_const = dual_const(x_val)
    let dy = dual_var(y_val)
    let r2 = dual_div(dx_const, dy)

    let val = r1.val
    let s1 = r1.der
    let s2 = r2.der

    return MultiSensitivity {
        value: val,
        sens1: s1,
        sens2: s2,
        sens3: 0.0,
        sens4: 0.0,
        n_inputs: 2,
    }
}

// f(x) = exp(x) → ∂f/∂x = exp(x)
fn sensitivity_exp(x: f64) -> SensitivityResult {
    let d = dual_var(x)
    let result = dual_exp(d)
    return SensitivityResult { value: result.val, sensitivity: result.der }
}

// f(x) = log(x) → ∂f/∂x = 1/x
fn sensitivity_log(x: f64) -> SensitivityResult {
    let d = dual_var(x)
    let result = dual_log(d)
    return SensitivityResult { value: result.val, sensitivity: result.der }
}

// ============================================================================
// GUM UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATION WITH AD
// ============================================================================

// Propagate uncertainty through a function using AD-computed sensitivities
// For y = f(x₁, x₂): u(y)² = (∂f/∂x₁)² u²(x₁) + (∂f/∂x₂)² u²(x₂)
struct ADUncertainty {
    value: f64,
    std_uncert: f64,
    // Budget breakdown
    contrib1: f64,  // (∂f/∂x₁)² u²(x₁)
    contrib2: f64,
    sens1: f64,
    sens2: f64,
}

fn propagate_add_ad(x1: f64, u1: f64, x2: f64, u2: f64) -> ADUncertainty {
    // Copy parameters to locals
    let x1_val = x1
    let u1_val = u1
    let x2_val = x2
    let u2_val = u2

    let sens = sensitivity_add(x1_val, x2_val)
    let c1 = sens.sens1 * sens.sens1 * u1_val * u1_val
    let c2 = sens.sens2 * sens.sens2 * u2_val * u2_val
    let u_combined = sqrt_f64(c1 + c2)

    return ADUncertainty {
        value: sens.value,
        std_uncert: u_combined,
        contrib1: c1,
        contrib2: c2,
        sens1: sens.sens1,
        sens2: sens.sens2,
    }
}

fn propagate_mul_ad(x1: f64, u1: f64, x2: f64, u2: f64) -> ADUncertainty {
    // Copy parameters to locals
    let x1_val = x1
    let u1_val = u1
    let x2_val = x2
    let u2_val = u2

    let sens = sensitivity_mul(x1_val, x2_val)
    let c1 = sens.sens1 * sens.sens1 * u1_val * u1_val
    let c2 = sens.sens2 * sens.sens2 * u2_val * u2_val
    let u_combined = sqrt_f64(c1 + c2)

    return ADUncertainty {
        value: sens.value,
        std_uncert: u_combined,
        contrib1: c1,
        contrib2: c2,
        sens1: sens.sens1,
        sens2: sens.sens2,
    }
}

fn propagate_div_ad(x1: f64, u1: f64, x2: f64, u2: f64) -> ADUncertainty {
    // Copy parameters to locals
    let x1_val = x1
    let u1_val = u1
    let x2_val = x2
    let u2_val = u2

    let sens = sensitivity_div(x1_val, x2_val)
    let c1 = sens.sens1 * sens.sens1 * u1_val * u1_val
    let c2 = sens.sens2 * sens.sens2 * u2_val * u2_val
    let u_combined = sqrt_f64(c1 + c2)

    return ADUncertainty {
        value: sens.value,
        std_uncert: u_combined,
        contrib1: c1,
        contrib2: c2,
        sens1: sens.sens1,
        sens2: sens.sens2,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PK EXAMPLE: C(t) = (D/V) * exp(-k*t) WITH AD
// ============================================================================

// Compute concentration with full sensitivity analysis
struct PKSensitivity {
    concentration: f64,
    sens_dose: f64,      // ∂C/∂D
    sens_volume: f64,    // ∂C/∂V
    sens_k_elim: f64,    // ∂C/∂k
    sens_time: f64,      // ∂C/∂t
}

fn pk_concentration_sensitivity(
    dose: f64,
    volume: f64,
    k_elim: f64,
    time: f64
) -> PKSensitivity {
    // Copy parameters to locals (workaround for codegen bug)
    let dose_val = dose
    let volume_val = volume
    let k_val = k_elim
    let time_val = time

    // C(t) = (D/V) * exp(-k*t)

    // ∂C/∂D: differentiate with D as variable
    let d_dose = dual_var(dose_val)
    let d_vol = dual_const(volume_val)
    let d_k = dual_const(k_val)
    let d_t = dual_const(time_val)
    let c_d = dual_mul(
        dual_div(d_dose, d_vol),
        dual_exp(dual_neg(dual_mul(d_k, d_t)))
    )

    // ∂C/∂V: differentiate with V as variable
    let d_dose2 = dual_const(dose_val)
    let d_vol2 = dual_var(volume_val)
    let c_v = dual_mul(
        dual_div(d_dose2, d_vol2),
        dual_exp(dual_neg(dual_mul(d_k, d_t)))
    )

    // ∂C/∂k: differentiate with k as variable
    let d_k2 = dual_var(k_val)
    let c_k = dual_mul(
        dual_div(d_dose2, d_vol),
        dual_exp(dual_neg(dual_mul(d_k2, d_t)))
    )

    // ∂C/∂t: differentiate with t as variable
    let d_t2 = dual_var(time_val)
    let c_t = dual_mul(
        dual_div(d_dose2, d_vol),
        dual_exp(dual_neg(dual_mul(d_k, d_t2)))
    )

    return PKSensitivity {
        concentration: c_d.val,
        sens_dose: c_d.der,
        sens_volume: c_v.der,
        sens_k_elim: c_k.der,
        sens_time: c_t.der,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_dual_add() -> bool {
    let a = dual_var(3.0)
    let b = dual_const(5.0)
    let c = dual_add(a, b)

    // f(x) = x + 5 → f(3) = 8, f'(3) = 1
    if abs_f64(c.val - 8.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(c.der - 1.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_dual_mul() -> bool {
    let a = dual_var(3.0)
    let b = dual_const(5.0)
    let c = dual_mul(a, b)

    // f(x) = 5x → f(3) = 15, f'(3) = 5
    if abs_f64(c.val - 15.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(c.der - 5.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_dual_square() -> bool {
    let result = sensitivity_square(4.0)

    // f(x) = x² → f(4) = 16, f'(4) = 8
    if abs_f64(result.value - 16.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.sensitivity - 8.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_dual_exp() -> bool {
    let result = sensitivity_exp(1.0)

    // f(x) = exp(x) → f(1) = e ≈ 2.718, f'(1) = e
    if abs_f64(result.value - 2.718281828) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.sensitivity - 2.718281828) > 0.001 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_dual_log() -> bool {
    let result = sensitivity_log(2.0)

    // f(x) = log(x) → f(2) = ln(2) ≈ 0.693, f'(2) = 1/2 = 0.5
    if abs_f64(result.value - 0.693147) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.sensitivity - 0.5) > 0.001 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_mul_sensitivity() -> bool {
    let sens = sensitivity_mul(3.0, 4.0)

    // f(x,y) = xy → f(3,4) = 12, ∂f/∂x = 4, ∂f/∂y = 3
    if abs_f64(sens.value - 12.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(sens.sens1 - 4.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(sens.sens2 - 3.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_div_sensitivity() -> bool {
    let sens = sensitivity_div(10.0, 2.0)

    // f(x,y) = x/y → f(10,2) = 5, ∂f/∂x = 1/2 = 0.5, ∂f/∂y = -10/4 = -2.5
    if abs_f64(sens.value - 5.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(sens.sens1 - 0.5) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(sens.sens2 - (0.0 - 2.5)) > 0.001 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_propagate_add() -> bool {
    // x₁ = 10 ± 1, x₂ = 20 ± 2
    let result = propagate_add_ad(10.0, 1.0, 20.0, 2.0)

    // y = 30
    if abs_f64(result.value - 30.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    // u(y) = sqrt(1² + 2²) = sqrt(5) ≈ 2.236
    let expected = sqrt_f64(5.0)
    if abs_f64(result.std_uncert - expected) > 0.01 { return false }

    // Sensitivities should both be 1
    if abs_f64(result.sens1 - 1.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.sens2 - 1.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_propagate_mul() -> bool {
    // x₁ = 10 ± 1 (10% rel), x₂ = 5 ± 0.5 (10% rel)
    let result = propagate_mul_ad(10.0, 1.0, 5.0, 0.5)

    // y = 50
    if abs_f64(result.value - 50.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    // ∂f/∂x₁ = 5, ∂f/∂x₂ = 10
    if abs_f64(result.sens1 - 5.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.sens2 - 10.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    // u(y) = sqrt((5*1)² + (10*0.5)²) = sqrt(25 + 25) = sqrt(50) ≈ 7.07
    let expected = sqrt_f64(50.0)
    if abs_f64(result.std_uncert - expected) > 0.1 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_pk_sensitivity() -> bool {
    // C(t) = (D/V) * exp(-k*t)
    // D = 300 mg, V = 35 L, k = 0.08 /h, t = 4 h
    let sens = pk_concentration_sensitivity(300.0, 35.0, 0.08, 4.0)

    // C = (300/35) * exp(-0.32) ≈ 8.57 * 0.726 ≈ 6.22
    if abs_f64(sens.concentration - 6.22) > 0.1 { return false }

    // ∂C/∂D = (1/V) * exp(-kt) = (1/35) * 0.726 ≈ 0.0207
    if abs_f64(sens.sens_dose - 0.0207) > 0.005 { return false }

    // ∂C/∂V = -(D/V²) * exp(-kt) ≈ -0.178
    if sens.sens_volume > 0.0 { return false }  // Should be negative

    // ∂C/∂k = -(D/V) * t * exp(-kt) ≈ -24.9
    if sens.sens_k_elim > 0.0 { return false }  // Should be negative

    // ∂C/∂t = -(D/V) * k * exp(-kt) ≈ -0.498
    if sens.sens_time > 0.0 { return false }  // Should be negative

    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/bayesian_knowledge.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/bayesian_knowledge.sio
// Convert MCMC Posterior Samples to Knowledge<T> Values
//
// Bridges Bayesian inference (MCMC chains) with Sounio's epistemic type
// system. Given posterior samples from an MCMC chain, produces a
// BayesianKnowledge struct containing:
//
// - Posterior mean and standard deviation
// - Credible intervals (highest posterior density)
// - Convergence-derived confidence score
// - Effective sample size
//
// The confidence score integrates multiple convergence diagnostics:
//   ESS >= 400 and R-hat < 1.05  =>  confidence >= 0.95
//   ESS >= 100 and R-hat < 1.10  =>  confidence >= 0.80
//   Otherwise: confidence = max(0.5, ESS/1000)
//
// References:
// - Gelman et al. (2013): "Bayesian Data Analysis", 3rd ed., Ch. 11
// - Vehtari et al. (2021): "Rank-normalization, folding, and localization"

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x;
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// =============================================================================
// BayesianKnowledge Struct
// =============================================================================
// This is the bridge between MCMC samples and Knowledge<T>.
// A BayesianKnowledge value captures what we learned from the posterior.

struct BayesianKnowledge {
    mean: f64,
    std_dev: f64,
    ci_lower: f64,
    ci_upper: f64,
    confidence: f64,
    n_effective: f64
}

// =============================================================================
// Chain representation (matches mcmc_core.sio)
// =============================================================================
// We re-declare the chain struct here to keep this module self-contained
// when used as a standalone library. When the import system is ready,
// this will import from mcmc_core.

struct MCMCChain {
    samples: [f64; 10000],
    n_stored: i32,
    n_accepted: i32,
    n_total: i32
}

// =============================================================================
// Chain Statistics (duplicated here for self-containment)
// =============================================================================

fn bk_chain_mean(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < chain.n_stored {
        sum = sum + chain.samples[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum / (chain.n_stored as f64)
}

fn bk_chain_variance(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored < 2 { return 0.0 }
    let mean = bk_chain_mean(chain)
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < chain.n_stored {
        let diff = chain.samples[i] - mean
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum_sq / ((chain.n_stored - 1) as f64)
}

fn bk_chain_std(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(bk_chain_variance(chain))
}

// =============================================================================
// Quantile Computation (selection-sort based)
// =============================================================================
// We sort a copy of the samples and then interpolate at the desired
// quantile. Since we cannot dynamically allocate, we work on a
// temporary copy using the chain's fixed-size array.

// Selection sort in-place on first n elements of an array
fn sort_partial(arr: &![f64; 10000], n: i32) {
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        var min_idx = i
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n {
            if arr[j] < arr[min_idx] {
                min_idx = j
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if min_idx != i {
            let tmp = arr[i]
            arr[i] = arr[min_idx]
            arr[min_idx] = tmp
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn compute_quantile(chain: &MCMCChain, q: f64) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored == 0 { return 0.0 }
    if chain.n_stored == 1 { return chain.samples[0] }

    // Copy samples into a temporary array for sorting
    var sorted: [f64; 10000] = [0.0; 10000]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < chain.n_stored {
        sorted[i] = chain.samples[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sort_partial(&!sorted, chain.n_stored)

    // Interpolate at quantile q
    let pos = q * ((chain.n_stored - 1) as f64)
    var lo_idx = pos as i32
    if lo_idx < 0 { lo_idx = 0 }
    if lo_idx >= chain.n_stored - 1 { lo_idx = chain.n_stored - 2 }
    let hi_idx = lo_idx + 1
    let frac = pos - (lo_idx as f64)

    return sorted[lo_idx] * (1.0 - frac) + sorted[hi_idx] * frac
}

// Compute credible interval [lower, upper] at given probability level
// Returns lower bound at index 0, upper bound at index 1
fn compute_credible_interval(chain: &MCMCChain, level: f64) -> [f64; 2] {
    let alpha = 1.0 - level
    let lower_q = alpha / 2.0
    let upper_q = 1.0 - alpha / 2.0

    var result: [f64; 2] = [0.0; 2]
    result[0] = compute_quantile(chain, lower_q)
    result[1] = compute_quantile(chain, upper_q)
    return result
}

// =============================================================================
// Convergence Confidence Scoring
// =============================================================================
// Maps MCMC diagnostics (ESS, R-hat) to an epistemic confidence score
// in [0, 1]. Higher ESS and lower R-hat yield higher confidence.
//
// Tier 1: ESS >= 400 and R-hat < 1.05 => confidence >= 0.95
// Tier 2: ESS >= 100 and R-hat < 1.10 => confidence >= 0.80
// Tier 3: Otherwise => confidence = max(0.5, ESS/1000)

fn convergence_confidence(ess: f64, r_hat: f64) -> f64 {
    // Tier 1: well-converged
    if ess >= 400.0 {
        if r_hat < 1.05 {
            // Scale between 0.95 and 0.99 based on ESS
            let base = 0.95
            let bonus = min_f64(0.04, (ess - 400.0) / 10000.0)
            return base + bonus
        }
    }

    // Tier 2: moderately converged
    if ess >= 100.0 {
        if r_hat < 1.10 {
            // Scale between 0.80 and 0.94
            let base = 0.80
            let bonus = min_f64(0.14, (ess - 100.0) / 3000.0)
            return base + bonus
        }
    }

    // Tier 3: poorly converged
    return max_f64(0.5, ess / 1000.0)
}

// =============================================================================
// ESS and R-hat (duplicated for self-containment)
// =============================================================================

fn bk_autocorrelation(chain: &MCMCChain, lag: i32) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored < lag + 2 { return 0.0 }
    let mean = bk_chain_mean(chain)
    var cov: f64 = 0.0
    var var_sum: f64 = 0.0
    let n = chain.n_stored - lag
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let d1 = chain.samples[i] - mean
        let d2 = chain.samples[i + lag] - mean
        cov = cov + d1 * d2
        var_sum = var_sum + d1 * d1
        i = i + 1
    }
    if var_sum < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
    return cov / var_sum
}

fn bk_effective_sample_size(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored < 10 { return chain.n_stored as f64 }
    let n = chain.n_stored as f64

    var sum_rho: f64 = 0.0
    var max_check = chain.n_stored / 2
    if max_check > 500 { max_check = 500 }

    var lag: i32 = 1
    while lag < max_check {
        let rho = bk_autocorrelation(chain, lag)
        if rho < 0.05 {
            lag = max_check
        } else {
            sum_rho = sum_rho + rho
            lag = lag + 1
        }
    }

    let tau = 1.0 + 2.0 * sum_rho
    if tau < 1.0 { return n }
    return n / tau
}

fn bk_split_rhat(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored < 10 { return 2.0 }

    let half = chain.n_stored / 2
    let n = half as f64

    var sum1: f64 = 0.0
    var sum2: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < half {
        sum1 = sum1 + chain.samples[i]
        sum2 = sum2 + chain.samples[i + half]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean1 = sum1 / n
    let mean2 = sum2 / n

    var var1: f64 = 0.0
    var var2: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < half {
        let d1 = chain.samples[i] - mean1
        let d2 = chain.samples[i + half] - mean2
        var1 = var1 + d1 * d1
        var2 = var2 + d2 * d2
        i = i + 1
    }
    var1 = var1 / (n - 1.0)
    var2 = var2 / (n - 1.0)

    let W = (var1 + var2) / 2.0
    let grand_mean = (mean1 + mean2) / 2.0
    let d1 = mean1 - grand_mean
    let d2 = mean2 - grand_mean
    let B = n * (d1 * d1 + d2 * d2)

    if W < 1.0e-30 { return 1.0 }

    let var_plus = (n - 1.0) / n * W + B / n
    return sqrt_f64(var_plus / W)
}

// =============================================================================
// Main Conversion: Chain -> BayesianKnowledge
// =============================================================================

fn chain_to_knowledge(chain: &MCMCChain) -> BayesianKnowledge {
    let mean = bk_chain_mean(chain)
    let std_dev = bk_chain_std(chain)
    let ci = compute_credible_interval(chain, 0.95)
    let ess = bk_effective_sample_size(chain)
    let r_hat = bk_split_rhat(chain)
    let conf = convergence_confidence(ess, r_hat)

    return BayesianKnowledge {
        mean: mean,
        std_dev: std_dev,
        ci_lower: ci[0],
        ci_upper: ci[1],
        confidence: conf,
        n_effective: ess
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/budget.sio ===
//! Uncertainty Budget Ledger
//!
//! Scientists don't just want a final uncertainty — they want the decomposition.
//! This module implements GUM-style uncertainty budgets.
//!
//! References:
//!   - GUM (JCGM 100:2008) Section 5: Determining Combined Uncertainty

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// BUDGET ENTRY
// ============================================================================

struct BudgetEntry {
    source_type: i32,        // 0=Type A, 1=Type B
    estimate: f64,
    std_uncert: f64,
    sensitivity: f64,
    contribution: f64,       // (c_i * u_i)²
    dof: f64,
}

fn budget_entry_a(estimate: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64, dof: f64) -> BudgetEntry {
    let contrib = sensitivity * sensitivity * std_uncert * std_uncert
    return BudgetEntry {
        source_type: 0,
        estimate: estimate,
        std_uncert: std_uncert,
        sensitivity: sensitivity,
        contribution: contrib,
        dof: dof,
    }
}

fn budget_entry_b(estimate: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64) -> BudgetEntry {
    let contrib = sensitivity * sensitivity * std_uncert * std_uncert
    return BudgetEntry {
        source_type: 1,
        estimate: estimate,
        std_uncert: std_uncert,
        sensitivity: sensitivity,
        contribution: contrib,
        dof: 1.0e30,
    }
}

fn empty_entry() -> BudgetEntry {
    return BudgetEntry {
        source_type: 0,
        estimate: 0.0,
        std_uncert: 0.0,
        sensitivity: 0.0,
        contribution: 0.0,
        dof: 1.0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// UNCERTAINTY BUDGET (4 entries max for simplicity)
// ============================================================================

struct UncertaintyBudget {
    result_value: f64,
    entry_count: i32,
    e0: BudgetEntry,
    e1: BudgetEntry,
    e2: BudgetEntry,
    e3: BudgetEntry,
    combined_variance: f64,
    combined_std_uncert: f64,
    effective_dof: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn budget_new(result_value: f64, confidence: f64) -> UncertaintyBudget {
    return UncertaintyBudget {
        result_value: result_value,
        entry_count: 0,
        e0: empty_entry(),
        e1: empty_entry(),
        e2: empty_entry(),
        e3: empty_entry(),
        combined_variance: 0.0,
        combined_std_uncert: 0.0,
        effective_dof: 0.0,
        confidence: confidence,
    }
}

fn get_entry(budget: UncertaintyBudget, idx: i32) -> BudgetEntry {
    if idx == 0 { return budget.e0 }
    if idx == 1 { return budget.e1 }
    if idx == 2 { return budget.e2 }
    if idx == 3 { return budget.e3 }
    return empty_entry()
}

fn add_entry(budget: UncertaintyBudget, entry: BudgetEntry) -> UncertaintyBudget {
    var result = budget
    let idx = budget.entry_count

    if idx == 0 { result.e0 = entry }
    else if idx == 1 { result.e1 = entry }
    else if idx == 2 { result.e2 = entry }
    else if idx == 3 { result.e3 = entry }

    if idx < 4 {
        result.entry_count = idx + 1
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// BUDGET COMPUTATION
// ============================================================================

fn compute_combined(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> UncertaintyBudget {
    var result = budget
    var total_var: f64 = 0.0

    if budget.entry_count > 0 {
        total_var = total_var + budget.e0.contribution
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 1 {
        total_var = total_var + budget.e1.contribution
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 2 {
        total_var = total_var + budget.e2.contribution
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 3 {
        total_var = total_var + budget.e3.contribution
    }

    result.combined_variance = total_var
    result.combined_std_uncert = sqrt_f64(total_var)

    return result
}

fn compute_dof(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> UncertaintyBudget {
    var result = budget
    let u_c4 = budget.combined_variance * budget.combined_variance
    var denom: f64 = 0.0

    if budget.entry_count > 0 && budget.e0.dof < 1.0e20 {
        let c4 = budget.e0.contribution * budget.e0.contribution
        denom = denom + c4 / budget.e0.dof
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 1 && budget.e1.dof < 1.0e20 {
        let c4 = budget.e1.contribution * budget.e1.contribution
        denom = denom + c4 / budget.e1.dof
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 2 && budget.e2.dof < 1.0e20 {
        let c4 = budget.e2.contribution * budget.e2.contribution
        denom = denom + c4 / budget.e2.dof
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 3 && budget.e3.dof < 1.0e20 {
        let c4 = budget.e3.contribution * budget.e3.contribution
        denom = denom + c4 / budget.e3.dof
    }

    if denom > 1.0e-15 {
        result.effective_dof = u_c4 / denom
    } else {
        result.effective_dof = 1.0e30
    }

    return result
}

fn finalize_budget(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> UncertaintyBudget {
    var result = compute_combined(budget)
    result = compute_dof(result)
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// BUDGET ANALYSIS
// ============================================================================

fn percent_contribution(budget: UncertaintyBudget, idx: i32) -> f64 {
    if budget.combined_variance < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0 }
    let entry = get_entry(budget, idx)
    return 100.0 * entry.contribution / budget.combined_variance
}

struct BudgetSummary {
    result_value: f64,
    combined_std_uncert: f64,
    relative_uncert_percent: f64,
    effective_dof: f64,
    entry_count: i32,
}

fn budget_summary(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> BudgetSummary {
    var rel_uncert: f64 = 0.0
    if abs_f64(budget.result_value) > 1.0e-15 {
        rel_uncert = 100.0 * budget.combined_std_uncert / abs_f64(budget.result_value)
    }

    return BudgetSummary {
        result_value: budget.result_value,
        combined_std_uncert: budget.combined_std_uncert,
        relative_uncert_percent: rel_uncert,
        effective_dof: budget.effective_dof,
        entry_count: budget.entry_count,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPANDED UNCERTAINTY
// ============================================================================

fn coverage_factor(dof: f64, conf: f64) -> f64 {
    // Approximate t-values for 95% confidence
    if conf < 0.95 {
        if dof < 5.0 { return 2.13 }
        if dof < 10.0 { return 1.83 }
        return 1.65
    }
    // 95% confidence
    if dof < 3.0 { return 4.30 }
    if dof < 5.0 { return 2.78 }
    if dof < 10.0 { return 2.26 }
    if dof < 30.0 { return 2.04 }
    return 1.96
}

fn expanded_uncertainty(budget: UncertaintyBudget, conf: f64) -> f64 {
    let k = coverage_factor(budget.effective_dof, conf)
    return k * budget.combined_std_uncert
}

struct ConfInterval {
    lower: f64,
    upper: f64,
    coverage_k: f64,
}

fn conf_interval(budget: UncertaintyBudget, conf: f64) -> ConfInterval {
    let k = coverage_factor(budget.effective_dof, conf)
    let u_exp = k * budget.combined_std_uncert
    return ConfInterval {
        lower: budget.result_value - u_exp,
        upper: budget.result_value + u_exp,
        coverage_k: k,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// BUILDER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn add_type_a(budget: UncertaintyBudget, estimate: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64, n_samples: f64) -> UncertaintyBudget {
    let dof = n_samples - 1.0
    let entry = budget_entry_a(estimate, std_uncert, sensitivity, dof)
    return add_entry(budget, entry)
}

fn add_type_b(budget: UncertaintyBudget, estimate: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64) -> UncertaintyBudget {
    let entry = budget_entry_b(estimate, std_uncert, sensitivity)
    return add_entry(budget, entry)
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_simple_budget() -> bool {
    var budget = budget_new(100.0, 0.9)

    // Source 1: u=1.0, c=1.0 → contribution = 1.0
    budget = add_type_a(budget, 50.0, 1.0, 1.0, 10.0)

    // Source 2: u=2.0, c=1.0 → contribution = 4.0
    budget = add_type_a(budget, 50.0, 2.0, 1.0, 10.0)

    budget = finalize_budget(budget)

    // Combined variance = 1 + 4 = 5
    let diff = abs_f64(budget.combined_variance - 5.0)
    if diff > 0.01 { return false }

    // Combined std = sqrt(5) ≈ 2.236
    let diff2 = abs_f64(budget.combined_std_uncert - sqrt_f64(5.0))
    if diff2 > 0.01 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_percent_contribution() -> bool {
    var budget = budget_new(100.0, 0.9)

    // Source 1: contribution = 1.0 (20%)
    budget = add_type_b(budget, 50.0, 1.0, 1.0)

    // Source 2: contribution = 4.0 (80%)
    budget = add_type_b(budget, 50.0, 2.0, 1.0)

    budget = finalize_budget(budget)

    let pct1 = percent_contribution(budget, 0)
    let pct2 = percent_contribution(budget, 1)

    if abs_f64(pct1 - 20.0) > 1.0 { return false }
    if abs_f64(pct2 - 80.0) > 1.0 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_expanded_uncertainty() -> bool {
    var budget = budget_new(100.0, 0.95)
    budget = add_type_a(budget, 100.0, 2.0, 1.0, 10.0)
    budget = finalize_budget(budget)

    // Combined u_c = 2.0
    if abs_f64(budget.combined_std_uncert - 2.0) > 0.01 { return false }

    // Effective DOF = 9 (n-1)
    if abs_f64(budget.effective_dof - 9.0) > 0.1 { return false }

    // 95% confidence interval
    let ci = conf_interval(budget, 0.95)

    // k should be about 2.26 for ν=9
    if ci.coverage_k < 2.0 { return false }
    if ci.coverage_k > 2.5 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_summary() -> bool {
    var budget = budget_new(100.0, 0.9)
    budget = add_type_b(budget, 100.0, 5.0, 1.0)
    budget = finalize_budget(budget)

    let summary = budget_summary(budget)

    if summary.entry_count != 1 { return false }
    if abs_f64(summary.combined_std_uncert - 5.0) > 0.01 { return false }
    if abs_f64(summary.relative_uncert_percent - 5.0) > 0.1 { return false }

    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/budget64.sio ===
//! Extended Uncertainty Budget Ledger — 64 Entries
//!
//! Array-based GUM uncertainty budget supporting up to 64 sources.
//! Designed for PBPK models with 44+ parameters contributing to output uncertainty.
//!
//! Extends the original 4-entry budget.sio with:
//!   - Array-based storage (no named fields e0..e3)
//!   - Parameter sensitivity attribution from ODE solver Jacobians
//!   - ISO GUM Table H.1 format output
//!   - Dominant source identification and ranking
//!
//! References:
//!   - GUM (JCGM 100:2008) Section 5: Determining Combined Uncertainty
//!   - GUM Supplement 1 (JCGM 101:2008): Monte Carlo method
//!   - ISO 17025:2017: Uncertainty budgets in testing/calibration

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn b64_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn b64_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

// ============================================================================
// BUDGET ENTRY
// ============================================================================

struct BudgetEntry64 {
    source_type: i64,    // 0=Type A (statistical), 1=Type B (systematic/literature)
    param_idx: i64,      // Index into ODEParams (for attribution)
    estimate: f64,       // Parameter value (xi)
    std_uncert: f64,     // Standard uncertainty u(xi)
    sensitivity: f64,    // Sensitivity coefficient ci = df/dxi
    contribution: f64,   // Variance contribution (ci * u(xi))²
    dof: f64,            // Degrees of freedom (n-1 for Type A, ∞ for Type B)
}

fn b64_entry_a(param_idx: i64, estimate: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64, dof: f64) -> BudgetEntry64 {
    let contrib = sensitivity * sensitivity * std_uncert * std_uncert
    BudgetEntry64 {
        source_type: 0, param_idx: param_idx,
        estimate: estimate, std_uncert: std_uncert,
        sensitivity: sensitivity, contribution: contrib, dof: dof,
    }
}

fn b64_entry_b(param_idx: i64, estimate: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64) -> BudgetEntry64 {
    let contrib = sensitivity * sensitivity * std_uncert * std_uncert
    BudgetEntry64 {
        source_type: 1, param_idx: param_idx,
        estimate: estimate, std_uncert: std_uncert,
        sensitivity: sensitivity, contribution: contrib, dof: 1.0e30,
    }
}

fn b64_empty_entry() -> BudgetEntry64 {
    BudgetEntry64 {
        source_type: 0, param_idx: -1,
        estimate: 0.0, std_uncert: 0.0,
        sensitivity: 0.0, contribution: 0.0, dof: 1.0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// UNCERTAINTY BUDGET — 64 entries, array-based
// ============================================================================

struct Budget64 {
    result_value: f64,
    confidence: f64,
    entry_count: i64,

    // Array storage for entries (flat arrays — Sounio does not support [Struct; N])
    source_types: [i64; 64],
    param_indices: [i64; 64],
    estimates: [f64; 64],
    std_uncerts: [f64; 64],
    sensitivities: [f64; 64],
    contributions: [f64; 64],
    dofs: [f64; 64],

    // Computed fields
    combined_variance: f64,
    combined_std_uncert: f64,
    effective_dof: f64,

    // Ranking (indices of entries sorted by contribution, descending)
    rank_indices: [i64; 64],
}

fn budget64_new(result_value: f64, confidence: f64) -> Budget64 {
    Budget64 {
        result_value: result_value, confidence: confidence, entry_count: 0,
        source_types: [0; 64], param_indices: [-1; 64],
        estimates: [0.0; 64], std_uncerts: [0.0; 64],
        sensitivities: [0.0; 64], contributions: [0.0; 64], dofs: [1.0; 64],
        combined_variance: 0.0, combined_std_uncert: 0.0, effective_dof: 0.0,
        rank_indices: [0; 64],
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ADD ENTRIES
// ============================================================================

fn budget64_add_type_a(
    b: &!Budget64, param_idx: i64,
    estimate: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64, n_samples: f64
) with Mut {
    let idx = b.entry_count
    if idx >= 64 { return }
    let dof = n_samples - 1.0
    let contrib = sensitivity * sensitivity * std_uncert * std_uncert
    b.source_types[idx] = 0
    b.param_indices[idx] = param_idx
    b.estimates[idx] = estimate
    b.std_uncerts[idx] = std_uncert
    b.sensitivities[idx] = sensitivity
    b.contributions[idx] = contrib
    b.dofs[idx] = dof
    b.entry_count = idx + 1
}

fn budget64_add_type_b(
    b: &!Budget64, param_idx: i64,
    estimate: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64
) with Mut {
    let idx = b.entry_count
    if idx >= 64 { return }
    let contrib = sensitivity * sensitivity * std_uncert * std_uncert
    b.source_types[idx] = 1
    b.param_indices[idx] = param_idx
    b.estimates[idx] = estimate
    b.std_uncerts[idx] = std_uncert
    b.sensitivities[idx] = sensitivity
    b.contributions[idx] = contrib
    b.dofs[idx] = 1.0e30
    b.entry_count = idx + 1
}

// ============================================================================
// FINALIZATION: compute combined variance, effective DOF, ranking
// ============================================================================

fn budget64_finalize(b: &!Budget64) with Mut {
    // Combined variance = sum of contributions
    var total_var = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < b.entry_count {
        if i < 64 { total_var = total_var + b.contributions[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    b.combined_variance = total_var
    b.combined_std_uncert = b64_sqrt(total_var)
