    // Welch-Satterthwaite effective degrees of freedom
    let u_c4 = total_var * total_var
    var denom = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < b.entry_count {
        if i < 64 && b.dofs[i] < 1.0e20 {
            let c4 = b.contributions[i] * b.contributions[i]
            denom = denom + c4 / b.dofs[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if denom > 1.0e-15 { b.effective_dof = u_c4 / denom }
    else { b.effective_dof = 1.0e30 }

    // Ranking: insertion sort by contribution (descending)
    i = 0
    while i < b.entry_count {
        if i < 64 { b.rank_indices[i] = i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 1
    while i < b.entry_count {
        if i < 64 {
            let key_idx = b.rank_indices[i]
            let key_val = b.contributions[key_idx]
            var j = i - 1
            var done = false
            while j >= 0 && !done {
                if j < 64 {
                    let rj = b.rank_indices[j]
                    if b.contributions[rj] < key_val {
                        b.rank_indices[j + 1] = b.rank_indices[j]
                        j = j - 1
                    } else { done = true }
                } else { done = true }
            }
            b.rank_indices[j + 1] = key_idx
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// QUERY
// ============================================================================

fn budget64_percent(b: &Budget64, idx: i64) -> f64 {
    if b.combined_variance < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0 }
    if idx < 0 || idx >= b.entry_count { return 0.0 }
    100.0 * b.contributions[idx] / b.combined_variance
}

fn budget64_dominant_idx(b: &Budget64) -> i64 {
    if b.entry_count == 0 { return -1 }
    b.rank_indices[0]
}

fn budget64_dominant_percent(b: &Budget64) -> f64 {
    if b.entry_count == 0 { return 0.0 }
    budget64_percent(b, b.rank_indices[0])
}

// ============================================================================
// COVERAGE FACTOR AND EXPANDED UNCERTAINTY
// ============================================================================

fn b64_coverage_factor(dof: f64, conf: f64) -> f64 {
    if conf < 0.95 {
        if dof < 5.0 { return 2.13 }
        if dof < 10.0 { return 1.83 }
        return 1.65
    }
    if conf < 0.99 {
        if dof < 3.0 { return 4.30 }
        if dof < 5.0 { return 2.78 }
        if dof < 10.0 { return 2.26 }
        if dof < 30.0 { return 2.04 }
        return 1.96
    }
    // 99% confidence
    if dof < 3.0 { return 9.92 }
    if dof < 5.0 { return 4.60 }
    if dof < 10.0 { return 3.25 }
    if dof < 30.0 { return 2.75 }
    return 2.576
}

fn budget64_expanded(b: &Budget64, conf: f64) -> f64 {
    let k = b64_coverage_factor(b.effective_dof, conf)
    k * b.combined_std_uncert
}

struct ConfInterval64 {
    lower: f64,
    upper: f64,
    coverage_k: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn budget64_interval(b: &Budget64, conf: f64) -> ConfInterval64 {
    let k = b64_coverage_factor(b.effective_dof, conf)
    let u_exp = k * b.combined_std_uncert
    ConfInterval64 {
        lower: b.result_value - u_exp,
        upper: b.result_value + u_exp,
        coverage_k: k, confidence: conf,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PARAMETER SENSITIVITY BUDGET FROM ODE SOLVER
//
// Build a budget from ODEParams variances and a Jacobian row (df/dp)
// at the output of interest (e.g., C_max, AUC).
//
// For each parameter p[k] with variance Var(p[k]):
//   sensitivity[k] = df/dp[k] (from Jacobian)
//   contribution[k] = (sensitivity[k])² * Var(p[k])
//
// This gives the JCGM 100:2008 eq. 10 decomposition by parameter.
// ============================================================================

struct ODEParams64 {
    params: [f64; 64],
    param_variances: [f64; 64],
    n_params: i64,
}

fn budget64_from_ode_params(
    result_value: f64,
    confidence: f64,
    params: &ODEParams64,
    sensitivities: &[f64; 64],
    n_params: i64
) -> Budget64 with Mut {
    var b = budget64_new(result_value, confidence)
    var k = 0
    while k < n_params {
        if k < 64 {
            let u_k = b64_sqrt(params.param_variances[k])
            if u_k > 1.0e-30 {
                // All PBPK params are Type B (literature/population estimates)
                budget64_add_type_b(&!b, k, params.params[k], u_k, sensitivities[k])
            }
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    budget64_finalize(&!b)
    b
}

// ============================================================================
// TEXT REPORT (ISO GUM Table H.1 style)
// ============================================================================

fn budget64_print_report(b: &Budget64) with IO, Mut {
    println("================================================================")
    println("  GUM UNCERTAINTY BUDGET (JCGM 100:2008)")
    println("================================================================")
    println("  Result value: "); println(b.result_value)
    println("  Combined std uncertainty: "); println(b.combined_std_uncert)

    let rel_pct = if b64_abs(b.result_value) > 1.0e-15 {
        100.0 * b.combined_std_uncert / b64_abs(b.result_value)
    } else { 0.0 }
    println("  Relative uncertainty: "); println(rel_pct); println(" %")
    println("  Effective DOF: "); println(b.effective_dof)

    let ci = budget64_interval(b, b.confidence)
    println("  Expanded uncertainty (k="); println(ci.coverage_k); println("): ")
    println(ci.coverage_k * b.combined_std_uncert)
    println("  Interval: ["); println(ci.lower); println(", "); println(ci.upper); println("]")

    println("")
    println("  --- Sources ranked by contribution ---")
    var i = 0
    while i < b.entry_count {
        if i < 64 && i < 10 {
            let idx = b.rank_indices[i]
            let pct = budget64_percent(b, idx)
            let typ = if b.source_types[idx] == 0 { "A" } else { "B" }
            println("  ["); println(i + 1); println("] p["); println(b.param_indices[idx])
            println("] Type "); println(typ)
            println("    Estimate: "); println(b.estimates[idx])
            println("    u(xi): "); println(b.std_uncerts[idx])
            println("    ci: "); println(b.sensitivities[idx])
            println("    Contribution: "); println(pct); println(" %")
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    println("================================================================")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/causal.sio ===
// epistemic/causal.sio — Causal Inference with Epistemic Uncertainty
// Pearl's do-calculus with Bayesian uncertainty tracking using fixed-size arrays

fn ec_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn ec_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}
fn ec_clamp01(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 } else if x > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { x } }

// Node types in causal DAG
enum NodeType {
    Treatment,
    Outcome,
    Confounder,
    Mediator,
    Collider,
    Instrument,
}

// Beta distribution for edge existence probability
struct EcBeta {
    alpha: f64,
    beta_p: f64,
}

fn ec_beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> EcBeta { EcBeta { alpha: a, beta_p: b } }
fn ec_beta_mean(b: EcBeta) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta_p) }
fn ec_beta_variance(b: EcBeta) -> f64 {
    let n = b.alpha + b.beta_p
    (b.alpha * b.beta_p) / (n * n * (n + 1.0))
}
fn ec_beta_update(prior: EcBeta, successes: f64, failures: f64) -> EcBeta {
    EcBeta { alpha: prior.alpha + successes, beta_p: prior.beta_p + failures }
}

struct EcEpistemicSummary {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    ci_lo: f64,
    ci_hi: f64,
}

fn ec_beta_summary(b: EcBeta) -> EcEpistemicSummary {
    let m = ec_beta_mean(b)
    let v = ec_beta_variance(b)
    let s = ec_sqrt(v)
    EcEpistemicSummary { mean: m, variance: v, ci_lo: ec_clamp01(m - 1.96 * s), ci_hi: ec_clamp01(m + 1.96 * s) }
}

fn ec_beta_from_mean_variance(mean: f64, variance: f64) -> EcBeta {
    let m = ec_clamp01(mean)
    let max_var = m * (1.0 - m)
    var v = variance
    if v > max_var * 0.99 { v = max_var * 0.99 }
    if v < 0.0001 { v = 0.0001 }
    let c = m * (1.0 - m) / v - 1.0
    let cc = if c < 2.0 { 2.0 } else { c }
    EcBeta { alpha: m * cc, beta_p: (1.0 - m) * cc }
}

// Causal edge with epistemic uncertainty
struct CausalEdge {
    from_id: i32,
    to_id: i32,
    exists: EcBeta,
    strength: f64,
    strength_var: f64,
}

// Causal DAG (fixed-size, up to 16 nodes, 64 edges)
struct CausalDAG {
    adj: [i32; 256],      // 16x16 adjacency matrix
    edge_exists: [EcBeta; 64],
    edge_strength: [f64; 64],
    edge_strength_var: [f64; 64],
    node_types: [i32; 16],
    n_nodes: i32,
    n_edges: i32,
}

fn causal_dag_new() -> CausalDAG {
    CausalDAG {
        adj: [0; 256],
        edge_exists: [ec_beta_new(1.0, 1.0); 64],
        edge_strength: [0.0; 64],
        edge_strength_var: [0.0; 64],
        node_types: [0; 16],
        n_nodes: 0,
        n_edges: 0,
    }
}

fn dag_add_node(dag: CausalDAG, node_type: i32) -> CausalDAG with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = dag
    if result.n_nodes < 16 {
        result.node_types[result.n_nodes] = node_type
        result.n_nodes = result.n_nodes + 1
    }
    result
}

fn dag_add_edge(dag: CausalDAG, from: i32, to: i32, exists: EcBeta, strength: f64, strength_var: f64) -> CausalDAG with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = dag
    result.adj[from * 16 + to] = 1
    if result.n_edges < 64 {
        result.edge_exists[result.n_edges] = exists
        result.edge_strength[result.n_edges] = strength
        result.edge_strength_var[result.n_edges] = strength_var
        result.n_edges = result.n_edges + 1
    }
    result
}

// Pearl's do-operator: remove incoming edges to a node
fn do_intervention(dag: CausalDAG, target: i32) -> CausalDAG with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = dag
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < dag.n_nodes {
        result.adj[i * 16 + target] = 0
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Backdoor adjustment: ATE via blocking confounders
fn average_treatment_effect(
    dag: &CausalDAG,
    treatment: i32,
    outcome: i32,
    outcomes_treated: &[f64; 64],
    outcomes_control: &[f64; 64],
    n_treated: i32,
    n_control: i32
) -> EcEpistemicSummary with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n_treated <= 0 || n_control <= 0 {
        return EcEpistemicSummary { mean: 0.0, variance: 1.0, ci_lo: 0.0 - 1.0, ci_hi: 1.0 }
    }
    var sum_t = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_treated { sum_t = sum_t + outcomes_treated[i]; i = i + 1 }
    let mean_t = sum_t / (n_treated as f64)

    var sum_c = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_control { sum_c = sum_c + outcomes_control[i]; i = i + 1 }
    let mean_c = sum_c / (n_control as f64)

    let ate = mean_t - mean_c
    let se = ec_sqrt(1.0 / (n_treated as f64) + 1.0 / (n_control as f64))
    EcEpistemicSummary { mean: ate, variance: se * se, ci_lo: ate - 1.96 * se, ci_hi: ate + 1.96 * se }
}

fn test_dag_construction() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var dag = causal_dag_new()
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, 0) // treatment
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, 1) // outcome
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, 0, 1, ec_beta_new(8.0, 2.0), 0.5, 0.1)
    dag.n_nodes == 2 && dag.n_edges == 1
}

fn test_do_intervention() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var dag = causal_dag_new()
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, 2) // confounder
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, 0) // treatment
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, 1) // outcome
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, 0, 1, ec_beta_new(8.0, 2.0), 0.5, 0.1)
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, 0, 2, ec_beta_new(6.0, 4.0), 0.3, 0.2)
    let intervened = do_intervention(dag, 1)
    intervened.adj[0 * 16 + 1] == 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/combine.sio ===
// combine.d - Epistemic Combination Calculus
//
// Every combination of beliefs follows principled rules.
// Every fusion of sources respects conflict.
// Every propagation knows its assumptions.
//
// Philosophy:
// When two sources say different things, averaging is a lie.
// Dempster-Shafer respects conflict. Bayesian fusion respects priors.
// Interval arithmetic respects ignorance. This module implements all three.
//
// The choice of combination rule is itself epistemic metadata.
//
// References:
// - Shafer (1976): "A Mathematical Theory of Evidence"
// - Dezert & Smarandache: "Advances in DSmT for Information Fusion"
// - Ferson et al.: "Constructing Probability Boxes"
// - Walley: "Statistical Reasoning with Imprecise Probabilities"

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    return y
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000000.0 }
    var y = x - 1.0
    if abs_f64(y) < 1.0 {
        var result = y
        var term = y
        var i: i64 = 2
        while i < 20 {
            term = 0.0 - term * y
            result = result + term / (i as f64)
            i = i + 1
        }
        return result
    }
    var guess = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 30 {
        let exp_guess = exp_f64(guess)
        guess = guess + (x - exp_guess) / exp_guess
        i = i + 1
    }
    return guess
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < 30 {
        term = term * x / (i as f64)
        result = result + term
        if abs_f64(term) < 0.000000000000001 { i = 30 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// BETA CONFIDENCE (Epistemic Uncertainty)
// ============================================================================

// Beta distribution for representing confidence
// Alpha = successes + 1, Beta = failures + 1
struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_confidence_new(alpha: f64, beta: f64) -> BetaConfidence {
    return BetaConfidence { alpha: alpha, beta: beta }
}

fn beta_confidence_from_evidence(successes: i64, failures: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
    return BetaConfidence {
        alpha: (successes + 1) as f64,
        beta: (failures + 1) as f64
    }
}

fn beta_confidence_strong(mean: f64) -> BetaConfidence {
    // High confidence at the given mean
    let alpha = mean * 20.0 + 1.0
    let beta = (1.0 - mean) * 20.0 + 1.0
    return BetaConfidence { alpha: alpha, beta: beta }
}

fn beta_confidence_weak(mean: f64) -> BetaConfidence {
    // Low confidence at the given mean
    let alpha = mean * 2.0 + 1.0
    let beta = (1.0 - mean) * 2.0 + 1.0
    return BetaConfidence { alpha: alpha, beta: beta }
}

fn beta_confidence_uniform() -> BetaConfidence {
    // Complete uncertainty
    return BetaConfidence { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
}

fn beta_mean(c: BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
    return c.alpha / (c.alpha + c.beta)
}

fn beta_variance(c: BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
    let ab = c.alpha + c.beta
    return (c.alpha * c.beta) / (ab * ab * (ab + 1.0))
}

fn beta_entropy(c: BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
    // Simplified entropy approximation
    let p = beta_mean(c)
    if p <= 0.0 || p >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    return 0.0 - p * ln_f64(p) - (1.0 - p) * ln_f64(1.0 - p)
}

// ============================================================================
// PROBABILITY INTERVALS (Imprecise Probabilities)
// ============================================================================

// Probability interval [lower, upper] for imprecise probabilities
struct ProbabilityInterval {
    lower: f64,
    upper: f64
}

fn prob_interval_new(lower: f64, upper: f64) -> ProbabilityInterval {
    var l = lower
    var u = upper
    if l < 0.0 { l = 0.0 }
    if u > 1.0 { u = 1.0 }
    if l > u { l = u }
    return ProbabilityInterval { lower: l, upper: u }
}

fn prob_interval_precise(p: f64) -> ProbabilityInterval {
    return prob_interval_new(p, p)
}

fn prob_interval_vacuous() -> ProbabilityInterval {
    return ProbabilityInterval { lower: 0.0, upper: 1.0 }
}

fn prob_interval_width(p: ProbabilityInterval) -> f64 {
    return p.upper - p.lower
}

fn prob_interval_midpoint(p: ProbabilityInterval) -> f64 {
    return (p.lower + p.upper) / 2.0
}

fn prob_interval_is_precise(p: ProbabilityInterval) -> i64 {
    if prob_interval_width(p) < 0.0000000001 { return 1 }
    return 0
}

// Conjunction: P(A AND B) under independence
fn prob_interval_and_independent(p1: ProbabilityInterval, p2: ProbabilityInterval) -> ProbabilityInterval {
    return ProbabilityInterval {
        lower: p1.lower * p2.lower,
        upper: p1.upper * p2.upper
    }
}

// Disjunction: P(A OR B) under independence
fn prob_interval_or_independent(p1: ProbabilityInterval, p2: ProbabilityInterval) -> ProbabilityInterval {
    var lower = p1.lower + p2.lower - p1.upper * p2.upper
    var upper = p1.upper + p2.upper - p1.lower * p2.lower
    if lower < 0.0 { lower = 0.0 }
    if upper > 1.0 { upper = 1.0 }
    return ProbabilityInterval { lower: lower, upper: upper }
}

// Negation: P(NOT A)
fn prob_interval_not(p: ProbabilityInterval) -> ProbabilityInterval {
    return ProbabilityInterval {
        lower: 1.0 - p.upper,
        upper: 1.0 - p.lower
    }
}

// Freshet bounds for conjunction (no independence assumption)
fn prob_interval_and_frechet(p1: ProbabilityInterval, p2: ProbabilityInterval) -> ProbabilityInterval {
    var lower = p1.lower + p2.lower - 1.0
    if lower < 0.0 { lower = 0.0 }
    let upper = min_f64(p1.upper, p2.upper)
    return ProbabilityInterval { lower: lower, upper: upper }
}

// Freshet bounds for disjunction
fn prob_interval_or_frechet(p1: ProbabilityInterval, p2: ProbabilityInterval) -> ProbabilityInterval {
    let lower = max_f64(p1.lower, p2.lower)
    var upper = p1.upper + p2.upper
    if upper > 1.0 { upper = 1.0 }
    return ProbabilityInterval { lower: lower, upper: upper }
}

// ============================================================================
// DEMPSTER-SHAFER BELIEF FUNCTIONS (Simplified)
// ============================================================================

// For a frame of discernment with up to 4 hypotheses
// We use a fixed array for masses on each subset

// Belief mass for a simple 2-hypothesis frame (e.g., True/False)
struct BinaryMass {
    m_empty: f64,      // Should be 0
    m_true: f64,       // Mass on {True}
    m_false: f64,      // Mass on {False}
    m_both: f64        // Mass on {True, False} = ignorance
}

fn binary_mass_new() -> BinaryMass {
    return BinaryMass {
        m_empty: 0.0,
        m_true: 0.0,
        m_false: 0.0,
        m_both: 1.0  // Start with total ignorance
    }
}

fn binary_mass_from_evidence(true_mass: f64, false_mass: f64, ignorance: f64) -> BinaryMass {
    let total = true_mass + false_mass + ignorance
    var t = true_mass
    var f = false_mass
    var i = ignorance
    if total > 0.0 {
        t = true_mass / total
        f = false_mass / total
        i = ignorance / total
    }
    return BinaryMass {
        m_empty: 0.0,
        m_true: t,
        m_false: f,
        m_both: i
    }
}

// Belief: lower bound on probability
fn binary_mass_belief_true(m: BinaryMass) -> f64 {
    return m.m_true
}

fn binary_mass_belief_false(m: BinaryMass) -> f64 {
    return m.m_false
}

// Plausibility: upper bound on probability
fn binary_mass_plausibility_true(m: BinaryMass) -> f64 {
    return m.m_true + m.m_both
}

fn binary_mass_plausibility_false(m: BinaryMass) -> f64 {
    return m.m_false + m.m_both
}

// Dempster's rule of combination
fn dempster_combine_binary(m1: BinaryMass, m2: BinaryMass) -> BinaryMass {
    // Compute unnormalized masses
    var new_true = 0.0
    var new_false = 0.0
    var new_both = 0.0
    var conflict = 0.0

    // m1_true AND m2_true -> true
    new_true = new_true + m1.m_true * m2.m_true
    // m1_true AND m2_both -> true
    new_true = new_true + m1.m_true * m2.m_both
    // m1_both AND m2_true -> true
    new_true = new_true + m1.m_both * m2.m_true

    // m1_false AND m2_false -> false
    new_false = new_false + m1.m_false * m2.m_false
    // m1_false AND m2_both -> false
    new_false = new_false + m1.m_false * m2.m_both
    // m1_both AND m2_false -> false
    new_false = new_false + m1.m_both * m2.m_false

    // m1_both AND m2_both -> both
    new_both = m1.m_both * m2.m_both

    // Conflict: m1_true AND m2_false OR m1_false AND m2_true
    conflict = m1.m_true * m2.m_false + m1.m_false * m2.m_true

    // Normalize
    let norm = 1.0 - conflict
    if norm > 0.0001 {
        new_true = new_true / norm
        new_false = new_false / norm
        new_both = new_both / norm
    }

    return BinaryMass {
        m_empty: 0.0,
        m_true: new_true,
        m_false: new_false,
        m_both: new_both
    }
}

// Conflict measure
fn dempster_conflict_binary(m1: BinaryMass, m2: BinaryMass) -> f64 {
    return m1.m_true * m2.m_false + m1.m_false * m2.m_true
}

// ============================================================================
// BAYESIAN FUSION (Simplified)
// ============================================================================

// Bayesian belief state for a binary hypothesis
struct BayesianBelief {
    prior_true: f64,
    likelihood_true: f64,
    likelihood_false: f64
}

fn bayesian_belief_new(prior: f64) -> BayesianBelief {
    return BayesianBelief {
        prior_true: prior,
        likelihood_true: 1.0,
        likelihood_false: 1.0
    }
}

fn bayesian_update(belief: BayesianBelief, likelihood_if_true: f64, likelihood_if_false: f64) -> BayesianBelief {
    let new_lt = belief.likelihood_true * likelihood_if_true
    let new_lf = belief.likelihood_false * likelihood_if_false
    return BayesianBelief {
        prior_true: belief.prior_true,
        likelihood_true: new_lt,
        likelihood_false: new_lf
    }
}

fn bayesian_posterior(belief: BayesianBelief) -> f64 {
    let p_true = belief.prior_true
    let p_false = 1.0 - belief.prior_true
    let numerator = belief.likelihood_true * p_true
    let denominator = belief.likelihood_true * p_true + belief.likelihood_false * p_false
    if denominator > 0.0 {
        return numerator / denominator
    }
    return belief.prior_true
}

fn bayesian_odds_ratio(belief: BayesianBelief) -> f64 {
    let post = bayesian_posterior(belief)
    if post >= 1.0 { return 1000000.0 }
    if post <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return post / (1.0 - post)
}

// ============================================================================
// CONFIDENCE COMBINATION RULES
// ============================================================================

// Combination rule types
fn rule_multiplicative() -> i64 { return 0 }
fn rule_quadrature() -> i64 { return 1 }
fn rule_minimum() -> i64 { return 2 }
fn rule_dempster() -> i64 { return 3 }

// Combine two confidences using specified rule
fn combine_confidence(c1: BetaConfidence, c2: BetaConfidence, rule: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
    let m1 = beta_mean(c1)
    let m2 = beta_mean(c2)

    if rule == rule_multiplicative() {
        // Independent errors: multiply means
        let combined = m1 * m2
        return beta_confidence_strong(combined)
    }

    if rule == rule_quadrature() {
        // Correlated errors: use quadrature
        let v1 = 1.0 - m1
        let v2 = 1.0 - m2
        let combined_uncertainty = sqrt_f64(v1 * v1 + v2 * v2)
        var combined = 1.0 - combined_uncertainty
        if combined < 0.0 { combined = 0.0 }
        return beta_confidence_strong(combined)
    }

    if rule == rule_minimum() {
        // Conservative: take minimum
        let combined = min_f64(m1, m2)
        return beta_confidence_strong(combined)
    }

    if rule == rule_dempster() {
        // Dempster-Shafer style
        let conflict = (1.0 - m1) * m2 + m1 * (1.0 - m2)
        let combined = m1 * m2
        var norm = 1.0 - conflict
        if norm < 0.01 { norm = 0.01 }
        return beta_confidence_strong(combined / norm)
    }

    // Default: multiplicative
    return beta_confidence_strong(m1 * m2)
}

// Combine multiple confidences
fn combine_confidence_many(confidences: [BetaConfidence], n: i64, rule: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
    if n <= 0 { return beta_confidence_uniform() }
    if n == 1 { return confidences[0] }

    var result = confidences[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        result = combine_confidence(result, confidences[i], rule)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// CONFIDENCE PROPAGATION
// ============================================================================

// Propagate confidence through arithmetic
fn propagate_arithmetic(c1: BetaConfidence, c2: BetaConfidence, independent: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
    if independent > 0 {
        return combine_confidence(c1, c2, rule_multiplicative())
    }
    return combine_confidence(c1, c2, rule_minimum())
}

// Propagate confidence through comparison
fn propagate_comparison(c1: BetaConfidence, c2: BetaConfidence, value_distance: f64, combined_std: f64) -> BetaConfidence {
    if combined_std <= 0.0 {
        return combine_confidence(c1, c2, rule_minimum())
    }

    // How many standard deviations apart?
    let z = abs_f64(value_distance) / combined_std

    // Higher z = more confident in comparison
    var comparison_confidence = 1.0 - exp_f64(0.0 - z * z / 2.0)

    // Combined with input confidences
    let total = comparison_confidence * beta_mean(c1) * beta_mean(c2)
    return beta_confidence_strong(total)
}

// Propagate confidence through aggregation
fn propagate_aggregation(confidences: [BetaConfidence], n: i64, independent: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
    if n <= 0 { return beta_confidence_uniform() }

    if independent > 0 {
        // For independent sources, confidence grows with sqrt(n)
        var product = 1.0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            product = product * beta_mean(confidences[i])
            i = i + 1
        }
        let boost = sqrt_f64(n as f64) / (n as f64)
        var result = exp_f64(boost * ln_f64(product))
        if result > 0.999 { result = 0.999 }
        return beta_confidence_strong(result)
    }

    // For correlated, take minimum
    var min_conf = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let m = beta_mean(confidences[i])
        if m < min_conf { min_conf = m }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return beta_confidence_strong(min_conf)
}

// ============================================================================
// PRINTING UTILITIES
// ============================================================================

fn print_beta_confidence(name: [u8], c: BetaConfidence) -> i64 {
    print("  ")
    print(name)
    print(": mean=")
    print(beta_mean(c))
    print(", var=")
    println(beta_variance(c))
    return 0
}

fn print_prob_interval(name: [u8], p: ProbabilityInterval) -> i64 {
    print("  ")
    print(name)
    print(": [")
    print(p.lower)
    print(", ")
    print(p.upper)
    println("]")
    return 0
}

    print("  ")
    print(name)
    print(": m(T)=")
    print(m.m_true)
    print(", m(F)=")

    print(", m(TF)=")

    return 0
}

// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/composable.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/composable.sio
//
// Composable<T> — ZD-orthogonal model merge (G8).
//
// Given two trained sedenion-encoded weight vectors W_A and W_B whose
// capabilities live in *ZD-orthogonal* subspaces of the 16-dim sedenion
// algebra, the composition W = W_A + W_B preserves each component's
// capabilities without mutual perturbation.  Concretely:
//
//   - W_A lives in the 4D right-annihilator of operator `A` (say, A = e3+e10)
//   - W_B lives in the orthogonal complement (the 12D non-kernel subspace)
//   - Then for any capability readout r_A encoded as an inner product with
//     a vector in W_A's subspace, <r_A, W> = <r_A, W_A> (the W_B term
//     vanishes by orthogonality), and similarly for r_B.
//
// This is the algebraic foundation for `Composable<T>`, which substitutes
// parameter-averaging (that leaks across capabilities) with a provably
// non-interfering merge.
//
// All functions declare `with ZD`.  Compiler enforces via error 204.
// Formal backing: `composition_preserves_orthogonal_complement` in
// formal/lean4/SounioSurgicalInterventions.lean.
// Operational benchmark: examples/zd_model_composition.sio.

// zd_kernel_u1, zd_kernel_u2: the 2D orthonormal basis of the right-
// annihilator of A = e3 + e10 used by ExactlyPrivate/Editable/Revocable.
// We re-declare them here so the privacy path does not have to import
// the epistemic layer for composition.
fn zd_kernel_u1() -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD {
    var v: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    v[6]  = 0.707107
    v[15] = 0.0 - 0.707107
    v
}

fn zd_kernel_u2() -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD {
    var v: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    v[7]  = 0.707107
    v[14] = 0.707107
    v
}

// inner16: dense 16-dim inner product.
fn inner16(a: &[f64; 16], b: &[f64; 16]) -> f64 with Mut {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { s = s + (*a)[i] * (*b)[i]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

// project_kernel: projection onto the 2D ZD kernel of A = e3+e10.
// Exact to fp precision; the basis is orthonormal.
fn project_kernel(v: &[f64; 16]) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD {
    let u1 = zd_kernel_u1()
    let u2 = zd_kernel_u2()
    let c1 = inner16(v, &u1)
    let c2 = inner16(v, &u2)
    var out: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { out[i] = c1 * u1[i] + c2 * u2[i]; i = i + 1 }
    out
}

// project_complement: v minus its kernel projection.
fn project_complement(v: &[f64; 16]) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD {
    let k = project_kernel(v)
    var out: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { out[i] = (*v)[i] - k[i]; i = i + 1 }
    out
}

// compose_orthogonal: given W_A (capabilities in kernel) and W_B
// (capabilities in complement), return the merged weight.  Crucially,
// the caller is responsible for the invariant that W_A is in kernel and
// W_B in complement.  The `with ZD` effect on this function signals that
// the compiler treats the result as ZD-structured.
fn compose_orthogonal(w_a: &[f64; 16], w_b: &[f64; 16]) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD {
    var out: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { out[i] = (*w_a)[i] + (*w_b)[i]; i = i + 1 }
    out
}

// decompose_into_orthogonal: given any 16-dim weight vector w, return the
// pair (w_kernel, w_complement) such that w = w_kernel + w_complement and
// the two components live in ZD-orthogonal subspaces.  This is the inverse
// of compose_orthogonal.
fn decompose_kernel_part(w: &[f64; 16]) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD {
    project_kernel(w)
}

fn decompose_complement_part(w: &[f64; 16]) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD {
    project_complement(w)
}

// interference_residual: quantify the cross-contamination between two
// weight vectors once composed.  For a truly ZD-orthogonal pair this
// returns 0 (fp exact); for weights sharing capability directions it
// returns the squared overlap.  Used for compliance auditing.
fn interference_residual(w_a: &[f64; 16], w_b: &[f64; 16]) -> f64 with Mut, ZD {
    let ka = project_kernel(w_a)
    let cb = project_complement(w_b)
    let d1 = inner16(&ka, w_b)
    let d2 = inner16(&cb, w_a)
    d1 * d1 + d2 * d2
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/composed_effects.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/composed_effects.sio
//
// Composition of three algebraic effects: Approx, Causal, Knowledge.
//
// This module defines a single composed value type `ComposedKnowledge` that
// carries simultaneously:
//   - the Knowledge<T> GUM data (value, variance, confidence)
//   - the Causal edge probability (Beta(alpha, beta) for "X causes Y" exists)
//   - the Approx numerical bound (worst-case error introduced by approximation)
//
// The motivating use case is verified clinical decision support: a predicted
// drug concentration depends on (a) measurement-uncertainty-with-bias (Knowledge),
// (b) causal-graph-uncertainty about which covariates affect clearance (Causal),
// (c) ODE-integrator approximation error (Approx). These three uncertainties
// must compose without information loss.
//
// References:
//   - JCGM 100:2008 — GUM (variance propagation)
//   - Pearl 2009, Hernán & Robins 2020 — causal inference
//   - Higham 2002 *Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms* — Approx bounds
//
// Soundness theorem (Lean: formal/lean4/SounioApproxCausalKnowledge.lean):
//   For monotone f and well-formed inputs c1, c2, the composed operation
//   `compose_apply(f, c1, c2)` produces a `ComposedKnowledge` whose
//   bounds dominate the true joint uncertainty.

// ============================================================================
// SCALAR HELPERS (pure)
// ============================================================================

fn ce_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn ce_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn ce_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

fn ce_min_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn ce_clamp_conf(c: i64) -> i64 {
    if c < 0 { return 0 }
    if c > 1000 { return 1000 }
    c
}

fn ce_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 12 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// ============================================================================
// COMPOSED VALUE
// ============================================================================
//
// Layout chosen to minimise BSS pressure (per known PR #53 BSS-shift class):
// 6 scalar f64 + 2 i64 + 2 i64 = 64 bytes flat.
//
// Fields:
//   value          — point estimate of the underlying scalar (e.g., Cmin in mg/L)
//   variance       — GUM σ² (from Knowledge effect)
//   approx_bound   — worst-case absolute error from numerical approximation
//   causal_alpha   — Beta α (causal edge "input → output" exists)
//   causal_beta    — Beta β (the same)
//   confidence     — 0..1000 evidence quality (lower bound of all three sources)
//   provenance_tag — i64 hashed provenance source (e.g., RCT=1, Cohort=2)
//   epoch          — i64 monotonic version counter (immutable arithmetic)

pub struct ComposedKnowledge {
    value: f64,
    variance: f64,
    approx_bound: f64,
    causal_alpha: f64,
    causal_beta: f64,
    confidence: i64,
    provenance_tag: i64,
    epoch: i64,
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

pub fn ck_new(value: f64, variance: f64, approx_bound: f64,
              alpha: f64, beta: f64, confidence: i64,
              provenance_tag: i64) -> ComposedKnowledge {
    ComposedKnowledge {
        value: value,
        variance: variance,
        approx_bound: approx_bound,
        causal_alpha: alpha,
        causal_beta: beta,
        confidence: ce_clamp_conf(confidence),
        provenance_tag: provenance_tag,
        epoch: 0,
    }
}

// Lift a Knowledge<f64>-style triple into ComposedKnowledge with
// vacuous Causal and zero Approx bound. This is the canonical lift
// from existing Sounio Epistemic values.
pub fn ck_from_knowledge(value: f64, variance: f64, confidence: i64) -> ComposedKnowledge {
    ck_new(value, variance, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, confidence, 0)
}

// Vacuous knowledge: maximum uncertainty, undeclared provenance.
pub fn ck_vacuous(value: f64) -> ComposedKnowledge {
    ck_new(value, 1.0e9, 1.0e9, 1.0, 1.0, 0, 0)
}

// ============================================================================
// ACCESSORS
// ============================================================================

pub fn ck_value(c: &ComposedKnowledge) -> f64 { c.value }
pub fn ck_variance(c: &ComposedKnowledge) -> f64 { c.variance }
pub fn ck_approx_bound(c: &ComposedKnowledge) -> f64 { c.approx_bound }
pub fn ck_confidence(c: &ComposedKnowledge) -> i64 { c.confidence }

pub fn ck_std_dev(c: &ComposedKnowledge) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    ce_sqrt(c.variance)
}

// Causal edge mean (Beta(α, β) mean): probability that the causal
// dependence asserted by this value's derivation is real.
pub fn ck_causal_mean(c: &ComposedKnowledge) -> f64 with Div {
    let denom = c.causal_alpha + c.causal_beta
    if denom == 0.0 { return 0.5 }
    c.causal_alpha / denom
}

// Total uncertainty as a single scalar: GUM σ + approx + causal-doubt
// (worst-case linear combination, conservative).
pub fn ck_total_uncertainty(c: &ComposedKnowledge) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let gum = ce_sqrt(c.variance)
    let causal_doubt = 1.0 - ck_causal_mean(c)
    let causal_term = ce_abs(c.value) * causal_doubt
    gum + c.approx_bound + causal_term
}

// ============================================================================
// PREDICATES (refinement-style)
// ============================================================================

pub fn ck_is_credible(c: &ComposedKnowledge, min_conf: i64) -> bool {
    c.confidence >= min_conf
}

pub fn ck_is_causally_confirmed(c: &ComposedKnowledge, min_alpha_share: f64) -> bool with Div {
    ck_causal_mean(c) >= min_alpha_share
}

pub fn ck_is_approx_safe(c: &ComposedKnowledge, max_approx: f64) -> bool {
    c.approx_bound <= max_approx
}

// Composite gate: all three must pass. Returns true iff the value is
// safe for downstream clinical use given the supplied bounds.
pub fn ck_passes_gate(c: &ComposedKnowledge,
                      min_conf: i64, min_alpha_share: f64,
                      max_approx: f64) -> bool with Div {
    if !ck_is_credible(c, min_conf) { return false }
    if !ck_is_causally_confirmed(c, min_alpha_share) { return false }
    if !ck_is_approx_safe(c, max_approx) { return false }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// ARITHMETIC — variance propagates by GUM, approx by triangle inequality,
// causal Beta combines independence (alpha+alpha, beta+beta), confidence
// by min with multiplicative decay.
// ============================================================================

fn ce_decay(c: i64) -> i64 {
    ce_clamp_conf(c * 99 / 100)
}

pub fn ck_add(a: &ComposedKnowledge, b: &ComposedKnowledge) -> ComposedKnowledge {
    ComposedKnowledge {
        value: a.value + b.value,
        variance: a.variance + b.variance,
        approx_bound: a.approx_bound + b.approx_bound,
        causal_alpha: a.causal_alpha + b.causal_alpha,
        causal_beta: a.causal_beta + b.causal_beta,
        confidence: ce_decay(ce_min_i64(a.confidence, b.confidence)),
        provenance_tag: ce_min_i64(a.provenance_tag, b.provenance_tag),
        epoch: ce_min_i64(a.epoch, b.epoch) + 1,
    }
}

pub fn ck_sub(a: &ComposedKnowledge, b: &ComposedKnowledge) -> ComposedKnowledge {
    ComposedKnowledge {
        value: a.value - b.value,
        variance: a.variance + b.variance,
        approx_bound: a.approx_bound + b.approx_bound,
        causal_alpha: a.causal_alpha + b.causal_alpha,
        causal_beta: a.causal_beta + b.causal_beta,
        confidence: ce_decay(ce_min_i64(a.confidence, b.confidence)),
        provenance_tag: ce_min_i64(a.provenance_tag, b.provenance_tag),
        epoch: ce_min_i64(a.epoch, b.epoch) + 1,
    }
}

// GUM mul (delta method): Var(XY) ≈ y² Var(X) + x² Var(Y) + Var(X)·Var(Y)
//   (the σx²σy² term is added for full Gaussian-product variance; Sounio
//    keeps it for honesty even though it is small when CV ≪ 1.)
// Approx (triangle inequality, all three terms kept):
//   |xy_approx - xy_true| ≤ |y|·δx + |x|·δy + δx·δy
//   The δx·δy cross-term is required: at x=y=0 with δx=δy=1, the
//   first two terms vanish but the true error can be up to 1.
// Causal: independent-evidence pooling — alphas SUM, betas SUM
//   (Beta(α₁,β₁) ∗ Beta(α₂,β₂) under conjugate Bernoulli pooling →
//    Beta(α₁+α₂, β₁+β₂); not multiplication).
pub fn ck_mul(a: &ComposedKnowledge, b: &ComposedKnowledge) -> ComposedKnowledge {
    let av = a.value
    let bv = b.value
    let var_term = bv * bv * a.variance + av * av * b.variance + a.variance * b.variance
    let approx_term = ce_abs(bv) * a.approx_bound + ce_abs(av) * b.approx_bound + a.approx_bound * b.approx_bound
    ComposedKnowledge {
        value: av * bv,
        variance: var_term,
        approx_bound: approx_term,
        causal_alpha: a.causal_alpha + b.causal_alpha,
        causal_beta: a.causal_beta + b.causal_beta,
        confidence: ce_decay(ce_min_i64(a.confidence, b.confidence)),
        provenance_tag: ce_min_i64(a.provenance_tag, b.provenance_tag),
        epoch: ce_min_i64(a.epoch, b.epoch) + 1,
    }
}

// GUM div: Var(X/Y) ≈ Var(X)/y² + x²·Var(Y)/y⁴ + Var(X)·Var(Y)/y⁴ (cross)
// Approx: |x/y_approx - x/y_true| ≤ δx/|y| + |x|·δy/y² + δx·δy/y²
//         (cross-term required by triangle inequality on the quotient).
pub fn ck_div(a: &ComposedKnowledge, b: &ComposedKnowledge) -> ComposedKnowledge with Div, Mut, Panic {
    let av = a.value
    let bv = b.value
    if bv == 0.0 { return ck_vacuous(0.0) }
    let bv2 = bv * bv
    let bv4 = bv2 * bv2
    let var_term = a.variance / bv2 + (av * av) * b.variance / bv4 + a.variance * b.variance / bv4
    let approx_term = a.approx_bound / ce_abs(bv) + ce_abs(av) * b.approx_bound / bv2 + a.approx_bound * b.approx_bound / bv2
    ComposedKnowledge {
        value: av / bv,
        variance: var_term,
        approx_bound: approx_term,
        causal_alpha: a.causal_alpha + b.causal_alpha,
        causal_beta: a.causal_beta + b.causal_beta,
        confidence: ce_decay(ce_min_i64(a.confidence, b.confidence)),
        provenance_tag: ce_min_i64(a.provenance_tag, b.provenance_tag),
        epoch: ce_min_i64(a.epoch, b.epoch) + 1,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// COMPOSITION HANDLERS — discharge effects in commuting order.
//
// The PL-paper claim (M1): the three handlers Approx, Causal, Knowledge
// commute under the ck_* arithmetic, i.e. discharging in any order produces
// the same ComposedKnowledge up to confidence-decay equivalence.
//
// Operationally these are no-ops on the data (the data already carries
// all three channels), but they exist as semantic anchors for the
// effect-row inference.
// ============================================================================

pub fn handle_approx(c: ComposedKnowledge) -> ComposedKnowledge with Approx {
    c
}

pub fn handle_causal(c: ComposedKnowledge) -> ComposedKnowledge with Causal {
    c
}

pub fn handle_knowledge(c: ComposedKnowledge) -> ComposedKnowledge {
    c
}

// All three discharged in canonical order: Approx -> Causal -> Knowledge.
// Lean theorem (target): canonical_discharge ≡ any_other_order.
pub fn canonical_discharge(c: ComposedKnowledge) -> ComposedKnowledge with Approx, Causal {
    let after_approx = handle_approx(c)
    let after_causal = handle_causal(after_approx)
    handle_knowledge(after_causal)
}

// ============================================================================
// CLINICAL PROVENANCE TAG CONSTANTS
// (used by stdlib/clinical/* in M3)
// ============================================================================

pub fn provenance_unknown() -> i64 { 0 }
pub fn provenance_rct() -> i64 { 1 }
pub fn provenance_cohort() -> i64 { 2 }
pub fn provenance_case_series() -> i64 { 3 }
pub fn provenance_expert() -> i64 { 4 }
pub fn provenance_simulation() -> i64 { 5 }

// ============================================================================
// SELF-TEST main() — invoked by `souc check`/`souc run` of this file.
// Validates round-trip of constructors, arithmetic identities, and gate.
// ============================================================================

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic, Approx, Causal {
    let a = ck_new(10.0, 0.04, 0.001, 9.0, 1.0, 950, 1)
    let b = ck_new(2.0, 0.01, 0.0005, 8.0, 2.0, 920, 1)

    let sum = ck_add(&a, &b)
    let prod = ck_mul(&a, &b)
    let quot = ck_div(&a, &b)

    println(ck_value(&sum))
    println(ck_value(&prod))
    println(ck_value(&quot))

    let gate_pass = ck_passes_gate(&prod, 800, 0.5, 1.0)
    if gate_pass {
        println("composed_effects gate: PASS")
    } else {
        println("composed_effects gate: FAIL")
    }

    let discharged = canonical_discharge(prod)
    println(ck_value(&discharged))
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/confidence_gate.sio ===
//! Confidence Gates for Epistemic Computing
//!
//! A confidence gate enforces that all epistemic values entering a computation
//! meet a minimum confidence threshold. This is the second novel contribution
//! of the dissertation: preventing low-confidence data from contaminating
//! high-confidence computations.
//!
//! Architecture:
//!   - GatePolicy: specifies threshold, action on violation
//!   - gate_check: validates a single value against the policy
//!   - gate_check_array: validates an array of values
//!   - GateResult: pass/fail + violation details
//!
//! Future work: compile-time enforcement via the effect system
//!   (e.g., `fn dosing(c: Epistemic) with Confidence(0.95)` rejects at type-check)
//!
//! References:
//!   - JCGM 100:2008 §4.3: "target uncertainty"
//!   - ISO 17025:2017 §7.6: "decision rules" for conformity assessment

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn cg_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn cg_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// ============================================================================
// GATE POLICY
// ============================================================================

// Action to take when confidence is below threshold
//   0 = REJECT (fail hard)
//   1 = WARN   (continue with degraded confidence flag)
//   2 = DEMOTE (reduce to lower-confidence tier automatically)

struct GatePolicy {
    min_confidence: f64,     // Minimum acceptable confidence level (0-1)
    max_cv_percent: f64,     // Maximum acceptable CV% (0 = unchecked)
    min_dof: f64,            // Minimum degrees of freedom (0 = unchecked)
    action: i64,             // 0=REJECT, 1=WARN, 2=DEMOTE
}

fn gate_policy_strict(min_confidence: f64) -> GatePolicy {
    GatePolicy {
        min_confidence: min_confidence,
        max_cv_percent: 0.0,
        min_dof: 0.0,
        action: 0,  // REJECT
    }
}

fn gate_policy_clinical(min_confidence: f64, max_cv: f64) -> GatePolicy {
    GatePolicy {
        min_confidence: min_confidence,
        max_cv_percent: max_cv,
        min_dof: 5.0,
        action: 0,  // REJECT
    }
}

fn gate_policy_exploratory() -> GatePolicy {
    GatePolicy {
        min_confidence: 0.5,
        max_cv_percent: 100.0,
        min_dof: 0.0,
        action: 1,  // WARN
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// GATE RESULT
// ============================================================================

struct GateViolation {
    param_idx: i64,
    actual_confidence: f64,
    actual_cv: f64,
    actual_dof: f64,
    reason: i64,   // 1=low confidence, 2=high CV, 3=low DOF
}

struct GateResult {
    passed: bool,
    n_checked: i64,
    n_violations: i64,
    violations: [i64; 64],          // param indices that failed
    violation_reasons: [i64; 64],   // reason codes
    violation_values: [f64; 64],    // actual values that failed
    worst_confidence: f64,
    worst_idx: i64,
}

fn gate_result_new() -> GateResult {
    GateResult {
        passed: true, n_checked: 0, n_violations: 0,
        violations: [0; 64], violation_reasons: [0; 64], violation_values: [0.0; 64],
        worst_confidence: 1.0, worst_idx: -1,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SINGLE VALUE CHECK
// ============================================================================

fn gate_check_value(
    policy: &GatePolicy,
    param_idx: i64,
    confidence: f64,
    value: f64,
    std_uncert: f64,
    dof: f64,
    result: &!GateResult
) with Mut {
    result.n_checked = result.n_checked + 1

    // Track worst confidence
    if confidence < result.worst_confidence {
        result.worst_confidence = confidence
        result.worst_idx = param_idx
    }

    // Check confidence threshold
    if confidence < policy.min_confidence {
        let vi = result.n_violations
        if vi < 64 {
            result.violations[vi] = param_idx
            result.violation_reasons[vi] = 1
            result.violation_values[vi] = confidence
            result.n_violations = vi + 1
        }
        result.passed = false
    }

    // Check CV% if requested
    if policy.max_cv_percent > 0.0 && cg_abs(value) > 1.0e-15 {
        let cv = 100.0 * std_uncert / cg_abs(value)
        if cv > policy.max_cv_percent {
            let vi = result.n_violations
            if vi < 64 {
                result.violations[vi] = param_idx
                result.violation_reasons[vi] = 2
                result.violation_values[vi] = cv
                result.n_violations = vi + 1
            }
            result.passed = false
        }
    }

    // Check DOF if requested
    if policy.min_dof > 0.0 && dof < policy.min_dof {
        let vi = result.n_violations
        if vi < 64 {
            result.violations[vi] = param_idx
            result.violation_reasons[vi] = 3
            result.violation_values[vi] = dof
            result.n_violations = vi + 1
        }
        result.passed = false
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ARRAY CHECK (for ODEParams-like structures)
// ============================================================================

fn gate_check_params(
    policy: &GatePolicy,
    params: &[f64; 64],
    param_variances: &[f64; 64],
    param_confidences: &[f64; 64],
    n_params: i64
) -> GateResult with Mut {
    var result = gate_result_new()
    var k = 0
    while k < n_params {
        if k < 64 {
            let std_u = cg_sqrt(param_variances[k])
            gate_check_value(
                policy, k, param_confidences[k],
                params[k], std_u, 1.0e30, &!result
            )
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// CONVENIENCE: Quick gate check with default policies
// ============================================================================

// Returns true if all confidence values meet the threshold
fn confidence_gate(
    confidences: &[f64; 64],
    n: i64,
    min_confidence: f64
) -> bool {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            if confidences[i] < min_confidence { return false }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}

// Returns true if all CVs are below max_cv%
fn cv_gate(
    values: &[f64; 64],
    variances: &[f64; 64],
    n: i64,
    max_cv_percent: f64
) -> bool with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            if cg_abs(values[i]) > 1.0e-15 {
                let cv = 100.0 * cg_sqrt(variances[i]) / cg_abs(values[i])
                if cv > max_cv_percent { return false }
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// REPORT
// ============================================================================

fn gate_print_result(result: &GateResult) with IO {
    if result.passed {
        println("  GATE: PASSED — all inputs meet confidence requirements")
    } else {
        println("  GATE: FAILED — confidence requirements not met")
        println("  Violations: "); println(result.n_violations)
        var i = 0
        while i < result.n_violations {
            if i < 64 && i < 10 {
                let reason = if result.violation_reasons[i] == 1 { "low confidence" }
                    else if result.violation_reasons[i] == 2 { "high CV%" }
                    else { "low DOF" }
                println("    p["); println(result.violations[i])
                println("]: "); println(reason)
                println(" (actual="); println(result.violation_values[i]); println(")")
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    println("  Worst confidence: "); println(result.worst_confidence)
    println("  at index: "); println(result.worst_idx)
}
