// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/discovery.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/discovery.sio
//
// Causal Discovery with Epistemic Uncertainty
//
// Core: adjacency matrix representation of causal graph,
// Fisher-Z conditional independence test, PC algorithm skeleton.
// Max 32 variables.

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn disc_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn disc_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn disc_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Series approximation of ln(x) for x > 0
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000000.0 }
    var v = x
    var adj = 0.0
    while v > 2.0 { v = v / 2.0; adj = adj + 0.6931471805599453 }
    while v < 0.5 { v = v * 2.0; adj = adj - 0.6931471805599453 }
    let t = (v - 1.0) / (v + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var result = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 20 {
        term = term * t2
        let denom = (2 * k + 1) as f64
        result = result + term / denom
        k = k + 1
    }
    adj + 2.0 * result
}

// ============================================================================
// Data Matrix: n_obs observations, n_vars variables
// Fixed max: 32 variables, observations stored as flat array
// ============================================================================

struct DataMatrix {
    // Flat storage: data[obs * n_vars + var]
    data: [f64; 4096],
    n_obs: i64,
    n_vars: i64,
}

fn data_matrix_new(n_obs: i64, n_vars: i64) -> DataMatrix {
    DataMatrix {
        data: [0.0; 4096],
        n_obs: n_obs,
        n_vars: n_vars,
    }
}

fn data_matrix_set(dm: &!DataMatrix, obs: i64, v: i64, val: f64) {
    let idx = obs * dm.n_vars + v
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 4096 {
        dm.data[idx] = val
    }
}

fn data_matrix_get(dm: &DataMatrix, obs: i64, v: i64) -> f64 {
    let idx = obs * dm.n_vars + v
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 4096 { dm.data[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

// Compute mean of variable v
fn data_mean(dm: &DataMatrix, v: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < dm.n_obs {
        sum = sum + data_matrix_get(dm, i, v)
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / (dm.n_obs as f64)
}

// Compute covariance between variables a and b
fn data_cov(dm: &DataMatrix, a: i64, b: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ma = data_mean(dm, a)
    let mb = data_mean(dm, b)
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < dm.n_obs {
        let da = data_matrix_get(dm, i, a) - ma
        let db = data_matrix_get(dm, i, b) - mb
        sum = sum + da * db
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / ((dm.n_obs - 1) as f64)
}

// Compute correlation between variables a and b
fn data_cor(dm: &DataMatrix, a: i64, b: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let cov_ab = data_cov(dm, a, b)
    let var_a = data_cov(dm, a, a)
    let var_b = data_cov(dm, b, b)
    let denom = disc_sqrt(var_a * var_b)
    if denom < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0 }
    cov_ab / denom
}

// ============================================================================
// Correlation Matrix (max 32x32)
// ============================================================================

struct CorMatrix {
    vals: [f64; 1024],
    n: i64,
}

fn cor_matrix_from_data(dm: &DataMatrix) -> CorMatrix with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cm = CorMatrix { vals: [0.0; 1024], n: dm.n_vars }
    var i = 0
    while i < dm.n_vars {
        var j = 0
        while j < dm.n_vars {
            cm.vals[i * dm.n_vars + j] = data_cor(dm, i, j)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    cm
}

fn cor_get(cm: &CorMatrix, i: i64, j: i64) -> f64 {
    cm.vals[i * cm.n + j]
}

// ============================================================================
// Causal Graph: adjacency matrix (max 32 variables)
// ============================================================================

// Edge types as i64
fn EDGE_NONE() -> i64 { 0 }
fn EDGE_UNDIRECTED() -> i64 { 1 }
fn EDGE_DIRECTED() -> i64 { 2 }

struct CausalGraph {
    // adj[i * 32 + j] = edge type from i to j
    adj: [i64; 1024],
    // confidence[i * 32 + j] = confidence of edge existence [0,1]
    confidence: [f64; 1024],
    // p_values[i * 32 + j] = p-value of independence test
    p_values: [f64; 1024],
    n_vars: i64,
}

fn causal_graph_new(n_vars: i64) -> CausalGraph with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Start fully connected (undirected)
    var g = CausalGraph {
        adj: [0; 1024],
        confidence: [0.0; 1024],
        p_values: [1.0; 1024],
        n_vars: n_vars,
    }
    var i = 0
    while i < n_vars {
        var j = 0
        while j < n_vars {
            if i != j {
                g.adj[i * 32 + j] = EDGE_UNDIRECTED()
                g.confidence[i * 32 + j] = 0.5
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    g
}

fn graph_has_edge(g: &CausalGraph, i: i64, j: i64) -> bool {
    g.adj[i * 32 + j] != EDGE_NONE()
}

fn graph_remove_edge(g: &!CausalGraph, i: i64, j: i64) {
    g.adj[i * 32 + j] = EDGE_NONE()
    g.adj[j * 32 + i] = EDGE_NONE()
    g.confidence[i * 32 + j] = 0.0
    g.confidence[j * 32 + i] = 0.0
}

fn graph_orient_edge(g: &!CausalGraph, from: i64, to: i64) {
    g.adj[from * 32 + to] = EDGE_DIRECTED()
    g.adj[to * 32 + from] = EDGE_NONE()
}

// ============================================================================
// Fisher-Z Conditional Independence Test
// ============================================================================

// Fisher-Z test: test independence of X and Y given conditioning set is empty
// Returns p-value approximation
fn fisher_z_test_unconditional(
    r: f64,
    n: i64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if disc_abs(r) > 0.9999 { return 0.0 }
    let z = 0.5 * disc_ln((1.0 + r) / (1.0 - r))
    let se = 1.0 / disc_sqrt((n - 3) as f64)
    let stat = disc_abs(z) / se
    // Approximate p-value from normal CDF tail
    // Using simple approximation: p ~ exp(-0.5 * stat^2) / stat for large stat
    if stat < 0.1 { return 1.0 }
    if stat > 6.0 { return 0.0 }
    // Rough normal tail approximation
    let t = stat
    let p = 2.0 * (0.5 - 0.5 * (1.0 - disc_sqrt(1.0 - (0.0 - (t * t / 2.0)) + 0.5)))
    // Very rough: just use exp approximation
    var exp_approx = 1.0
    let x = 0.0 - 0.5 * t * t
    // Taylor: e^x ~ 1 + x + x^2/2 + x^3/6 + x^4/24
    exp_approx = 1.0 + x + x * x * 0.5 + x * x * x / 6.0 + x * x * x * x / 24.0
    if exp_approx < 0.0 { exp_approx = 0.0 }
    exp_approx
}

// ============================================================================
// PC Algorithm (simplified skeleton)
// ============================================================================

// PC algorithm step 0: remove edges where unconditional independence holds
fn pc_step0(
    g: &!CausalGraph,
    cm: &CorMatrix,
    n_obs: i64,
    alpha: f64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < g.n_vars {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < g.n_vars {
            let r = cor_get(cm, i, j)
            let p = fisher_z_test_unconditional(r, n_obs)
            g.p_values[i * 32 + j] = p
            g.p_values[j * 32 + i] = p
            if p > alpha {
                graph_remove_edge(g, i, j)
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Count edges in the graph
fn graph_edge_count(g: &CausalGraph) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < g.n_vars {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < g.n_vars {
            if graph_has_edge(g, i, j) { count = count + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    count
}

// Compute structural confidence: fraction of tested edges that survived
fn graph_structural_confidence(g: &CausalGraph) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = g.n_vars
    let max_edges = (n * (n - 1)) / 2
    if max_edges == 0 { return 1.0 }
    let surviving = graph_edge_count(g)
    (surviving as f64) / (max_edges as f64)
}

// Run simplified PC algorithm on data
fn pc_discover(dm: &DataMatrix, alpha: f64) -> CausalGraph with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let cm = cor_matrix_from_data(dm)
    var g = causal_graph_new(dm.n_vars)
    pc_step0(&!g, &cm, dm.n_obs, alpha)
    g
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/dp.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/dp.sio
//
// Dynamic Programming for finite MDPs — exact Bellman solvers.
//
// First principles:
//   Bellman optimality, exact fixed-point:
//     V*(s) = max_a  E_{s' ~ P(.|s,a)}[ r(s,a,s') + gamma * V*(s') ]
//   Policy: pi*(s) = argmax_a Q*(s,a).
//
// We solve it exactly over a finite, dense, fixed-size MDP via:
//   - value_iteration  (synchronous Bellman backup, ||V_new - V||_inf)
//   - policy_iteration (Bellman eval under fixed pi, then improve)
//
// Layer 1 (this file, top half) — PRECISE Epistemic MDPs.
//   GUM var/conf propagate through the reward term. Transitions are
//   precise f64 (sum to 1).
//
// Layer 2 (this file, bottom half) — KNIGHTIAN-ROBUST MDPs.
//   Two entry points:
//     - robust_value_iteration       (one-step, caller pre-bakes p-box
//                                     continuation per (s,a))
//     - robust_value_iteration_full  (full Bellman backup, per-s'
//                                     Knightian credal set)
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SOUNIO QUIRKS in effect on this file
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// (A) const-dimensioned array types in function PARAMETER / RETURN positions
//     are rejected by the self-hosted type checker ("arity mismatch"). We use
//     literal `8` and `4` in function signatures. The file-scope consts are
//     used only in struct field types and local declarations.
// (B) const-dimensioned struct FIELD types (e.g. `reward: [Epistemic; MAX_FLAT]`
//     where MAX_FLAT is a const) are silently accepted by the type checker
//     but produce a struct that segfaults on field read. Use literal `256`.
//     Verified 2026-06-04 (re-verified 2026-06-05 against the new
//     canonical compiler): this defect is in the postfix-array-index
//     codegen for the `ExprIndex` AST node. The defect lives in the
//     canonical self-hosted compiler — currently
//     self-hosted/bootstrap/bootstrap_v0.sio:12529-12534 (the old
//     self-hosted/compiler/lean_single.sio:13415-13437 location, which
//     earlier investigations pointed to, is now stale — lean_single
//     is no longer the canonical compiler; the bootstrap_v0 single-file
//     compiler is what the JIT binary is built from). For local arrays
//     of struct-typed elements, the bootstrap_v0 codegen falls into the
//     else branch (`mov rax, [rcx + rax*8]`, an i64-sized load) which
//     reads only 8 bytes of a 24-byte Epistemic struct. The 5-field MDP
//     shape (trans_p f64 + reward Epistemic + 3 scalars) happens to
//     dodge the bad path on the current build; the minimal single-
//     field [Epistemic; N] struct trips it. When the codegen defect is
//     fixed upstream, this workaround can be retired: replace
//     `trans_p: [f64; 256]` with `trans_p: [f64; MAX_FLAT]` and
//     `reward: [Epistemic; 256]` with `reward: [Epistemic; MAX_FLAT]`.
// (C) Reading an UNINITIALISED struct field of `[T; N]` where T is a
//     non-primitive type segfaults (same defect as quirk (B), in the
//     canonical compiler at self-hosted/bootstrap/bootstrap_v0.sio:12529-
//     12534; the older reference self-hosted/compiler/lean_single.sio
//     is now stale). Workaround: in `mdp_new` we PRE-POPULATE every
//     slot of `trans_p` and `reward` so the value-iteration read path
//     never sees an uninitialised slot. Empirically re-verified
//     2026-06-05 against the current bin/souc (built from
//     bootstrap_v0.sio, the canonical compiler on feat/exact-orc-
//     machinery): the minimal `struct M { reward: [Epistemic; 1] }`
//     uninit-read pattern segfaults; pre-population makes it pass.
//     Retire this loop only when the postfix-index codegen defect is
//     patched upstream.
// (D) Struct-typed (PBox, Epistemic) arrays inside structs read through
//     `&` / `&!` corrupt or crash. The robust MDP struct holds only
//     scalar fields; the PBox tables are passed as separate array
//     parameters.
// (E) The 2D-nested-array-in-struct case crashes on `&!` (separate defect
//     from C). We use FLAT 1D arrays with manual indexing.
//     index(s, a, sp) = s * A * Sp + a * Sp + sp.
//
// Library file (Layer 1 has no `pub fn main`); the LAYER 2 chunk below
// carries a self-test `pub fn main` that exercises both layers.

use epistemic::knowledge::{Epistemic}

// ============================================================================
// FILE-SCOPE SIZE PARAMETERS
// ============================================================================
//
// Used as documentation for the matching struct field literal dims and
// as a knob for the LAYER 1 `dp_index` helper. Do NOT use these in
// function parameter or return types (quirk A) or in struct field array
// dimensions (quirk B). Use literal `8` / `4` / `256` there.

const MAX_STATES:  i64 = 8
const MAX_ACTIONS: i64 = 4
const MAX_SP:      i64 = 8

// Compute the flat index from (s, a, sp). Helper used by all MDP code.
fn dp_index(s: i64, a: i64, sp: i64) -> i64 {
    s * MAX_ACTIONS * MAX_SP + a * MAX_SP + sp
}

// ============================================================================
// NUMERIC HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn dp_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn dp_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn dp_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn dp_min_i(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

// ============================================================================
// LAYER 1 — PRECISE EPITEMIC MDP
// ============================================================================

pub struct EpistemicMDP {
    n_states: i64,
    n_actions: i64,
    trans_p:  [f64;      256],   // literal dim (quirk B)
    reward:   [Epistemic; 256],   // literal dim (quirk B)
    gamma: f64,
}

pub fn mdp_new(n_states: i64, n_actions: i64, gamma: f64) -> EpistemicMDP with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m: EpistemicMDP
    m.n_states = n_states
    m.n_actions = n_actions
    m.gamma = gamma
    // PRE-POPULATE every slot of trans_p and reward (quirk C).
    // The codegen for an uninitialised struct field of [T; N] with struct T
    // emits a byte-load that segfaults on first read. Filling every slot
    // here eliminates the read-of-uninitialised case in value_iteration.
    let zero_e: Epistemic = Epistemic { val: 0.0, variance: 0.0, confidence: 1000 }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 256 {
        m.trans_p[i] = 0.0
        m.reward[i]  = zero_e
        i = i + 1
    }
    m
}

pub fn mdp_set_trans(m: &!EpistemicMDP, s: i64, a: i64, sp: i64, p: f64, r: Epistemic) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s >= 0 && s < m.n_states && a >= 0 && a < m.n_actions && sp >= 0 && sp < m.n_states {
        let idx = dp_index(s, a, sp)
        m.trans_p[idx] = p
        m.reward[idx] = r
    }
}

// Standard synchronous value iteration. V[s] is Epistemic — carries
// GUM var/conf through the backup. Stops when the sup-norm on .val
// is below `epsilon`.
pub fn value_iteration(m: &EpistemicMDP, epsilon: f64, max_iter: i64) -> [Epistemic; 8] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var V: [Epistemic; 8] = [Epistemic { val: 0.0, variance: 0.0, confidence: 1000 }; 8]
    var iter: i64 = 0
    var converged: bool = false
    while iter < max_iter && !converged {
        var Vnew: [Epistemic; 8] = [Epistemic { val: 0.0, variance: 0.0, confidence: 1000 }; 8]
        var max_diff: f64 = 0.0
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < m.n_states {
            var best_val:  f64 = 0.0 - 1.0e18
            var best_var:  f64 = 0.0
            var best_conf: i64 = 1000
            var a: i64 = 0
            while a < m.n_actions {
                var qv: f64 = 0.0
                var qvar: f64 = 0.0
                var qconf: i64 = 1000
                var sp: i64 = 0
                while sp < m.n_states {
                    let idx = dp_index(s, a, sp)
                    let p = m.trans_p[idx]
                    if p > 0.0 {
                        let r = m.reward[idx]
                        let vsp = V[sp]
                        let one_v   = r.val + m.gamma * vsp.val
                        let one_var = r.variance + m.gamma * m.gamma * vsp.variance
                        let one_cf  = dp_min_i(r.confidence, vsp.confidence)
                        qv    = qv    + p * one_v
                        // GUM: Var(p * X) = p^2 * Var(X).
                        qvar  = qvar  + p * p * one_var
                        qconf = dp_min_i(qconf, one_cf)
                    }
                    sp = sp + 1
                }
                if qv > best_val {
                    best_val = qv
                    best_var = qvar
                    best_conf = qconf
                }
                a = a + 1
            }
            Vnew[s] = Epistemic { val: best_val, variance: best_var, confidence: best_conf }
            let diff = dp_abs(Vnew[s].val - V[s].val)
            if diff > max_diff { max_diff = diff }
            s = s + 1
        }
        V = Vnew
        if max_diff < epsilon { converged = true }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    V
}

pub fn extract_policy(m: &EpistemicMDP, V: &[Epistemic; 8]) -> [i64; 8] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pi: [i64; 8] = [0; 8]
    var s: i64 = 0
    while s < m.n_states {
        var best_a: i64 = 0
        var best_q: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0e18
        var a: i64 = 0
        while a < m.n_actions {
            var q: f64 = 0.0
            var sp: i64 = 0
            while sp < m.n_states {
                let idx = dp_index(s, a, sp)
                let p = m.trans_p[idx]
                if p > 0.0 {
                    let rmean = m.reward[idx].val
                    let vsp   = V[sp].val
                    q = q + p * (rmean + m.gamma * vsp)
                }
                sp = sp + 1
            }
            if q > best_q {
                best_q = q
                best_a = a
            }
            a = a + 1
        }
        pi[s] = best_a
        s = s + 1
    }
    pi
}

// Policy evaluation: Bellman backup with a fixed policy pi until the
// value function converges. We solve (I - gamma * P^pi) V = R^pi by
// repeated sweeping (small |S|; cheaper than building the matrix).
pub fn policy_evaluation(m: &EpistemicMDP, pi: &[i64; 8], epsilon: f64, max_iter: i64) -> [Epistemic; 8] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var V: [Epistemic; 8] = [Epistemic { val: 0.0, variance: 0.0, confidence: 1000 }; 8]
    var iter: i64 = 0
    var converged: bool = false
    while iter < max_iter && !converged {
        var Vnew: [Epistemic; 8] = [Epistemic { val: 0.0, variance: 0.0, confidence: 1000 }; 8]
        var max_diff: f64 = 0.0
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < m.n_states {
            let a = pi[s]
            var qv: f64 = 0.0
            var qvar: f64 = 0.0
            var qconf: i64 = 1000
            var sp: i64 = 0
            while sp < m.n_states {
                let idx = dp_index(s, a, sp)
                let p = m.trans_p[idx]
                if p > 0.0 {
                    let r = m.reward[idx]
                    let vsp = V[sp]
                    let one_v   = r.val + m.gamma * vsp.val
                    let one_var = r.variance + m.gamma * m.gamma * vsp.variance
                    let one_cf  = dp_min_i(r.confidence, vsp.confidence)
                    qv    = qv    + p * one_v
                    qvar  = qvar  + p * p * one_var
                    qconf = dp_min_i(qconf, one_cf)
                }
                sp = sp + 1
            }
            Vnew[s] = Epistemic { val: qv, variance: qvar, confidence: qconf }
            let diff = dp_abs(Vnew[s].val - V[s].val)
            if diff > max_diff { max_diff = diff }
            s = s + 1
        }
        V = Vnew
        if max_diff < epsilon { converged = true }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    V
}

pub fn policy_improvement(m: &EpistemicMDP, V: &[Epistemic; 8]) -> [i64; 8] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    extract_policy(m, V)
}

// Policy iteration: alternate evaluation and improvement until pi is stable.
// (V*, pi*) returned.
pub fn policy_iteration(m: &EpistemicMDP, max_outer: i64, eval_eps: f64, eval_iter: i64) -> ([Epistemic; 8], [i64; 8]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pi: [i64; 8] = [0; 8]
    var V:  [Epistemic; 8] = [Epistemic { val: 0.0, variance: 0.0, confidence: 1000 }; 8]
    var k: i64 = 0
    var stable: bool = false
    while k < max_outer && !stable {
        V = policy_evaluation(m, &pi, eval_eps, eval_iter)
        let new_pi = policy_improvement(m, &V)
        var sames: i64 = 0
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < m.n_states {
            if new_pi[s] == pi[s] { sames = sames + 1 }
            s = s + 1
        }
        if sames == m.n_states { stable = true }
        pi = new_pi
        k = k + 1
    }
    (V, pi)
}

// ============================================================================
// LAYER 2 — KNIGHTIAN-ROBUST DP
// ============================================================================
//
// First principles (math this implements):
//
//   Robust Bellman under Knightian (p-box) uncertainty on the continuation
//   value:
//     V_lower(s) = max_a  lower-prevision  E[ r(s,a,s') + gamma * V_lower(s') ]
//     V_upper(s) = max_a  upper-prevision  E[ r(s,a,s') + gamma * V_upper(s') ]
//
//   We compute the prevision envelope via the Frechet (point-mass) outer
//   enclosure. For each (s, a, s') we build a p-box for the contribution
//     X(s, a, s') = p(s, a, s') * ( r(s, a, s') + gamma * V(s') )
//   with p(s, a, s') in [p_lo, p_hi] and V(s') in [V_lower, V_upper]. The
//   enclosure is a 4-corner Frechet bound: for positive quantities, the
//   min corner is (p_lo, r + gamma*V_lower) and the max corner is
//   (p_hi, r + gamma*V_upper). This is monotone in both args, so we use
//   `pb_apply2_monotone_inc_inc`. The enclosure is sound for the
//   counter-monotonic (worst-case) copula and conservative under positive
//   correlation.
//
// Two entry points:
//   - robust_value_iteration       (one-step, caller pre-bakes the
//                                   continuation p-box for each (s, a))
//   - robust_value_iteration_full  (full Bellman backup; per-s' Knightian)
//
// Storage: 1D arrays with manual (s, a) -> s*A + a and
// (s, a, sp) -> s*A*Sp + a*Sp + sp indexing.

use epistemic::knightian::*

// ============================================================================
// KNIGHTIAN MDP — minimal scalar-only struct (PBox tables passed separately
// to keep the struct readable through `&` without segfault).
// ============================================================================

pub struct KnightianMDP {
    n_states: i64,
    n_actions: i64,
    gamma: f64,
}

pub fn kmdp_new(n_states: i64, n_actions: i64, gamma: f64) -> KnightianMDP with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m: KnightianMDP
    m.n_states = n_states
    m.n_actions = n_actions
    m.gamma = gamma
    m
}

// Multiplication closure for pb_apply2_monotone_inc_inc. Sounio requires
// a free fn, not a closure.
fn kmdp_mul(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64 { x * y }

// ============================================================================
// ENTRY POINT 1 — one-step, caller pre-bakes the continuation p-box.
//
// cont_pbox is 1D, indexed by s * A + a. Each element is a p-box whose
// lo_mean is the lower-prevision Q(s, a) and whose hi_mean is the upper.
// Solver returns V_lower[s] = max_a pb_lo_mean(cont_pbox[s*A+a]) and
// V_upper[s] = max_a pb_hi_mean(cont_pbox[s*A+a]).
// ============================================================================

pub fn robust_value_iteration(
    m: &KnightianMDP,
    cont_pbox: &[PBox; 8],
    eps: f64,
    max_iter: i64
) -> ([f64; 8], [f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var V_lower: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var V_upper: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var iter: i64 = 0
    var converged: bool = false
    while iter < max_iter && !converged {
        var VL: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
        var VU: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
        var max_diff: f64 = 0.0
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < m.n_states {
            var best_lo: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0e18
            var best_hi: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0e18
            var a: i64 = 0
            while a < m.n_actions {
                let idx = s * m.n_actions + a
                let pb = (*cont_pbox)[idx]
                let lo = pb_lo_mean(&pb)
                let hi = pb_hi_mean(&pb)
                if lo > best_lo { best_lo = lo }
                if hi > best_hi { best_hi = hi }
                a = a + 1
            }
            VL[s] = best_lo
            VU[s] = best_hi
            let dl = dp_abs(VL[s] - V_lower[s])
            let du = dp_abs(VU[s] - V_upper[s])
            let dd = dp_max(dl, du)
            if dd > max_diff { max_diff = dd }
            s = s + 1
        }
        V_lower = VL
        V_upper = VU
        if max_diff < eps { converged = true }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    (V_lower, V_upper)
}

// ============================================================================
// ENTRY POINT 2 — full Bellman backup, per-s' Knightian credal set.
//
// r_kn / p_kn_lo / p_kn_hi / r_kn_var are 1D arrays indexed by
// s * A * Sp + a * Sp + sp. For each (s, a, sp) we build a p-box for
// (r + gamma * V[sp]) and a p-box for the credal-set probability p(sp),
// then combine via pb_apply2_monotone_inc_inc with kmdp_mul (4-corner
// Frechet). The sum across sp gives the lower / upper prevision Q-values
// for (s, a).
// ============================================================================

pub fn robust_value_iteration_full(
    m: &KnightianMDP,
    r_kn: &[f64; 32],
    p_kn_lo: &[f64; 32],
    p_kn_hi: &[f64; 32],
    r_kn_var: &[f64; 32],
    eps: f64,
    max_iter: i64
) -> ([f64; 8], [f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var V_lower: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var V_upper: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var iter: i64 = 0
    var converged: bool = false
    while iter < max_iter && !converged {
        var VL: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
        var VU: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
        var max_diff: f64 = 0.0
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < m.n_states {
            var best_lo: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0e18
            var best_hi: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0e18
            var a: i64 = 0
            while a < m.n_actions {
                var q_lo: f64 = 0.0
                var q_hi: f64 = 0.0
                var sp: i64 = 0
                while sp < m.n_states {
                    let idx = s * m.n_actions * m.n_states + a * m.n_states + sp
                    let r_mean = (*r_kn)[idx]
                    let p_lo = (*p_kn_lo)[idx]
                    let p_hi = (*p_kn_hi)[idx]
                    let r_v = (*r_kn_var)[idx]
                    let rv_lo = r_mean + m.gamma * V_lower[sp]
                    let rv_hi = r_mean + m.gamma * V_upper[sp]
                    let rv_box = PBox { lo_mean: rv_lo, hi_mean: rv_hi, variance: r_v, confidence: 1000 }
                    let p_box = PBox { lo_mean: p_lo, hi_mean: p_hi, variance: 0.0, confidence: 1000 }
                    let contrib = pb_apply2_monotone_inc_inc(kmdp_mul, &p_box, &rv_box)
                    q_lo = q_lo + pb_lo_mean(&contrib)
                    q_hi = q_hi + pb_hi_mean(&contrib)
                    sp = sp + 1
                }
                if q_lo > best_lo { best_lo = q_lo }
                if q_hi > best_hi { best_hi = q_hi }
                a = a + 1
            }
            VL[s] = best_lo
            VU[s] = best_hi
            let dl = dp_abs(VL[s] - V_lower[s])
            let du = dp_abs(VU[s] - V_upper[s])
            let dd = dp_max(dl, du)
            if dd > max_diff { max_diff = dd }
            s = s + 1
        }
        V_lower = VL
        V_upper = VU
        if max_diff < eps { converged = true }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    (V_lower, V_upper)
}

// ============================================================================
// ROBUST POLICY EXTRACTION (pessimistic / lower-prevision argmax).
// ============================================================================

pub fn robust_extract_policy(
    m: &KnightianMDP,
    V_lower: &[f64; 8],
    cont_pbox: &[PBox; 8]
) -> [i64; 8] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pi: [i64; 8] = [0; 8]
    var s: i64 = 0
    while s < m.n_states {
        var best_a: i64 = 0
        var best_lo: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0e18
        var a: i64 = 0
        while a < m.n_actions {
            let idx = s * m.n_actions + a
            let pb = (*cont_pbox)[idx]
            let lo = pb_lo_mean(&pb)
            if lo > best_lo {
                best_lo = lo
                best_a = a
            }
            a = a + 1
        }
        pi[s] = best_a
        s = s + 1
    }
    pi
}

// ============================================================================
// LAYER 2 SELF-TEST (run as `pub fn main` so the library is exercisable
// in isolation via `bin/souc check` and direct invocation).
// ============================================================================

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = kmdp_new(2, 2, 0.9)

    // ---------- Tight (no Knightian gap) ----------
    var cp_tight: [PBox; 8] = [pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000)]
    let p_risky_tight = pb_new(0.909090909, 0.909090909, 0.0, 1000)
    cp_tight[0] = p_risky_tight
    let p_safe_tight = pb_new(1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1000)
    cp_tight[1] = p_safe_tight
    let p_term = pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000)
    cp_tight[2] = p_term
    cp_tight[3] = p_term

    let (VL_tight, VU_tight) = robust_value_iteration(&m, &cp_tight, 1e-9, 100)
    let pi_tight = robust_extract_policy(&m, &VL_tight, &cp_tight)

    println("TIGHT_VL0")
    println(VL_tight[0])
    println("TIGHT_VU0")
    println(VU_tight[0])
    println("TIGHT_PI0")
    println(pi_tight[0])

    // ---------- Knightian gap on safe's transition ----------
    var cp_gap: [PBox; 8] = [pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000), pb_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1000)]
    cp_gap[0] = p_risky_tight
    let p_safe_gap = pb_new(0.4, 1.0, 0.0, 1000)
    cp_gap[1] = p_safe_gap
    cp_gap[2] = p_term
    cp_gap[3] = p_term

    let (VL_gap, VU_gap) = robust_value_iteration(&m, &cp_gap, 1e-9, 100)
    let pi_gap = robust_extract_policy(&m, &VL_gap, &cp_gap)

    println("GAP_VL0")
    println(VL_gap[0])
    println("GAP_VU0")
    println(VU_gap[0])
    println("GAP_PI0")
    println(pi_gap[0])

    // ---------- Full iterative solver with per-s' Knightian ----------
    var r_arr: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var plo_arr: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var phi_arr: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var rvar_arr: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]

    // s=0, a=0 (risky): p(0->0)=0.5, p(0->1)=0.5, r(0->0)=0, r(0->1)=1
    plo_arr[0] = 0.5
    phi_arr[0] = 0.5
    r_arr[0] = 0.0
    plo_arr[1] = 0.5
    phi_arr[1] = 0.5
    r_arr[1] = 1.0
    // s=0, a=1 (safe, Knightian): p(0->0) in [0, 0.6], p(0->1) in [0.4, 1.0]
    plo_arr[2] = 0.0
    phi_arr[2] = 0.6
    r_arr[2] = 1.0
    plo_arr[3] = 0.4
    phi_arr[3] = 1.0
    r_arr[3] = 1.0
    // s=1 (terminal): p(1->0)=0, p(1->1)=1, r=0
    plo_arr[4] = 0.0
    phi_arr[4] = 0.0
    r_arr[4] = 0.0
    plo_arr[5] = 1.0
    phi_arr[5] = 1.0
    r_arr[5] = 0.0
    plo_arr[6] = 0.0
    phi_arr[6] = 0.0
    r_arr[6] = 0.0
    plo_arr[7] = 1.0
    phi_arr[7] = 1.0
    r_arr[7] = 0.0

    let (VL_full, VU_full) = robust_value_iteration_full(&m, &r_arr, &plo_arr, &phi_arr, &rvar_arr, 1e-9, 200)

    println("FULL_VL0")
    println(VL_full[0])
    println("FULL_VU0")
    println(VU_full[0])
    println("FULL_VL1")
    println(VL_full[1])

    println("LAYER2_OK")
    return 0
}

// ============================================================================
// SUGGESTED EXTENSION (user "suggest" 2026-06): Epistemic MCTS / PUCT with DP backups
// under Knightian (p-box / credal) model.
// ============================================================================
//
// First principles (why this is the natural next after exact DP + MC sampling):
//   - Pure DP is exact but explodes with |S| or horizon (your stiff ODEs are "continuous"
//     infinite state; discretization + Knightian p-box on params gives a finite but
//     ambiguous MDP).
//   - Pure MCTS/PUCT (as in prior discussion) is asymmetric sampling + UCT/ PUCT selection
//     + MC rollouts; it approximates the Bellman optimality but only explores a tiny
//     fraction of the tree.
//   - Hybrid: use the exact robust DP (this module) for "full backup" whenever a leaf
//     or fringe node has a small local MDP (or when we have precomputed a p-box model
//     for a sub-dynamics, e.g. discretized vdp from test_stiff_ode_knightian_mc).
//     For unknown / large parts, fall back to MC rollout (using propagate::monte_carlo
//     on the epistemic params) wrapped in p-box outer bounds (knightian) for the value
//     estimate at the leaf.
//   - Selection still PUCT, but the "value" of a node can be the robust lower from DP
//     when available, or Klibanoff CE of the ambiguous leaf value (via the bridge) for
//     ambiguity-averse search.
//   - This gives "DP-style backups inside MCTS" exactly as noted in the DP definition query.
//
// High-level pseudocode (implement as a separate mcts_dp.sio or inside a planner example):
//
// struct EpistemicNode {
//     s: State (or discretized ODE state),
//     n: i64, w: f64,  // visit count, total return (Epistemic or p-box summary)
//     children: map<Action, Node>,
//     is_leaf: bool,
// }
//
// fn select(node, C_puct) -> Action:
//     for a in actions:
//         if unvisited: return a
//         uct = Q(a) + C_puct * p(a) * sqrt(N) / (1 + n(a))   // PUCT
//     return argmax uct
//
// fn expand(node):
//     if small_local_mdp(node.s):   // e.g. |reachable S'| < 16
//         (V_l, V_u) = robust_value_iteration( build_local_knightian_mdp(node.s, pbox_model) )
//         node.value = (V_l, V_u)   // exact robust backup
//         return
//     // else MC rollout under Knightian model
//     samples = monte_carlo( epistemic_params_of(node.s), rollout_f, 1024 )
//     leaf_box = pbox_from_samples_or_credal( samples )   // or klib CE
//     node.value = leaf_box
//
// fn backup(path, leaf_value):
//     for node in reversed(path):
//         node.n += 1
//         node.w = combine(node.w, leaf_value)   // Epistemic add or pbox join
//         if node has exact DP value: use it preferentially for Q
//
// fn search(root, budget, model_pbox):
//     for _ in budget:
//         leaf = select + expand (using DP when possible)
//         leaf_v = simulate or DP
//         backup(path, leaf_v)
//     return argmax Q(root)   // or Klib CE of the root action values for final choice
//
// Integration points (already exist):
// - knightian::PBox / walley::CredalSet for the "model" (transition/reward ambiguity)
// - propagate::monte_carlo for the rollout distribution
// - klibanoff::klibanoff_compose_with_active + active::expected_free_energy for the
//   leaf "value" when we want ambiguity aversion in the search (exactly as in the
//   stiff_ode_knightian_mc test)
// - dp::robust_* for the exact sub-MDP backups
//
// This would let a "planner" for the stiff ODE (discretized) use exact robust DP on
// the reachable discrete states under the p-box on mu/CL/etc., while using MC + p-box
// outer for the unknown parts — the best of both worlds the user described.
//
// Suggested first file: examples/planning/epistemic_mcts_dp.sio (small grid or discretized vdp)
// or stdlib/epistemic/mcts.sio (library version using the same fixed-array style as dp.sio).
//
// When ready, the exact command could be:
//   write examples/planning/epistemic_mcts_dp.sio with the hybrid skeleton + one test case
//   that re-uses the vdp from test_stiff_ode_knightian_mc and asserts that the hybrid
//   policy has lower robust regret than pure MC or pure one-step robust VI.



// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/dual_check.sio ===
//! Dual Propagation Cross-Check: GUM vs Monte Carlo
//!
//! JCGM 101 explicitly positions Monte Carlo as guidance when:
//!   "the conditions for the GUM uncertainty framework are not fulfilled,
//!    or it is unclear whether they are fulfilled"
//!
//! This module runs BOTH methods and catches the most common scientific lie:
//! linear uncertainty propagation through a nonlinear model that breaks it.
//!
//! The invariant is:
//!   |u_mc - u_linear| / u_mc < policy.max_linearization_error
//!
//! If violated: warn or REFUSE and switch to Monte Carlo.
//!
//! References:
//!   - JCGM 101:2008 Section 5.8: Comparison with GUM uncertainty framework
//!   - JCGM 100:2008 Section 5.1.2: Conditions for valid linearization

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sin(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn cos(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

// ============================================================================
// LINEARIZATION ERROR POLICY
// ============================================================================

struct LinearizationPolicy {
    max_relative_error: f64,    // Maximum |u_mc - u_gum| / u_mc
    auto_switch_to_mc: bool,    // Automatically use MC if linearization fails
    min_samples_for_check: i32, // Minimum MC samples for reliable comparison
    warn_only: bool,            // Warn instead of refuse
}

fn default_linearization_policy() -> LinearizationPolicy {
    return LinearizationPolicy {
        max_relative_error: 0.10,   // 10% max discrepancy
        auto_switch_to_mc: true,
        min_samples_for_check: 100,
        warn_only: false,
    }
}

fn strict_linearization_policy() -> LinearizationPolicy {
    return LinearizationPolicy {
        max_relative_error: 0.05,   // 5% max discrepancy
        auto_switch_to_mc: true,
        min_samples_for_check: 500,
        warn_only: false,
    }
}

fn lenient_linearization_policy() -> LinearizationPolicy {
    return LinearizationPolicy {
        max_relative_error: 0.20,   // 20% max discrepancy
        auto_switch_to_mc: false,
        min_samples_for_check: 50,
        warn_only: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SIMPLE LCG FOR MC
// ============================================================================

struct Rng {
    state: i64,
}

// Result of random generation: value and updated RNG
struct RngResult {
    value: f64,
    rng: Rng,
}

fn rng_new(seed: i64) -> Rng {
    return Rng { state: seed }
}

fn rng_next(s: Rng) -> RngResult {
    let a: i64 = 1103515245
    let c: i64 = 12345
    let m: i64 = 2147483648

    var next_state = a * s.state + c
    next_state = next_state % m
    if next_state < 0 { next_state = next_state + m }

    let u = (next_state as f64) / (m as f64)
    return RngResult { value: u, rng: Rng { state: next_state } }
}

fn rng_normal(s: Rng) -> RngResult {
    let r1 = rng_next(s)
    let u1 = r1.value
    let rng2 = r1.rng

    let r2 = rng_next(rng2)
    let u2 = r2.value
    let rng3 = r2.rng

    var u1_safe = u1
    if u1_safe < 1.0e-10 { u1_safe = 1.0e-10 }

    let pi = 3.14159265358979323846
    let r = sqrt_f64(0.0 - 2.0 * log(u1_safe))
    let theta = 2.0 * pi * u2
    let z = r * cos(theta)

    return RngResult { value: z, rng: rng3 }
}

fn rng_normal_params(s: Rng, mean: f64, std: f64) -> RngResult {
    let r = rng_normal(s)
    return RngResult { value: mean + std * r.value, rng: r.rng }
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL PROPAGATION RESULT
// ============================================================================

struct GumMcResult {
    // GUM (linearized) estimate
    gum_mean: f64,
    gum_std: f64,

    // Monte Carlo estimate
    mc_mean: f64,
    mc_std: f64,
    mc_samples: i32,

    // Discrepancy analysis
    mean_discrepancy: f64,      // |mc_mean - gum_mean| / |gum_mean|
    std_discrepancy: f64,       // |mc_std - gum_std| / gum_std
    is_linear: bool,            // True if linearization is reliable
    linearization_error: f64,   // Actual relative error

    // Decision
    use_mc: bool,               // True if MC should be used
    warning_code: i32,          // 0=ok, 1=warn, 2=switched_to_mc, 3=refused
}

fn dual_result_gum_only(mean: f64, std: f64) -> GumMcResult {
    return GumMcResult {
        gum_mean: mean,
        gum_std: std,
        mc_mean: mean,
        mc_std: std,
        mc_samples: 0,
        mean_discrepancy: 0.0,
        std_discrepancy: 0.0,
        is_linear: true,
        linearization_error: 0.0,
        use_mc: false,
        warning_code: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL CHECK: UNIVARIATE FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Input specification for dual check
struct UncertainInput {
    mean: f64,
    std: f64,
}

fn dual_input(mean: f64, std: f64) -> UncertainInput {
    return UncertainInput { mean: mean, std: std }
}

// Check y = exp(x) - highly nonlinear for large σ_x
fn dual_check_exp(x: UncertainInput, n_samples: i32, policy: LinearizationPolicy) -> GumMcResult {
    // GUM estimate: ∂y/∂x = exp(x), so u_y = |exp(μ_x)| * u_x
    let gum_mean = exp(x.mean)
    let gum_std = abs_f64(gum_mean) * x.std

    // Monte Carlo
    var rng = rng_new(12345)
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_samples {
        let r = rng_normal_params(rng, x.mean, x.std)
        let samp = r.value
        rng = r.rng

        let y = exp(samp)
        sum = sum + y
        sum_sq = sum_sq + y * y
        i = i + 1
    }

    let mc_mean = sum / (n_samples as f64)
    let mc_var = sum_sq / (n_samples as f64) - mc_mean * mc_mean
    let mc_std = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(mc_var))

    // Compute discrepancy
    var mean_disc: f64 = 0.0
    if abs_f64(gum_mean) > 1.0e-15 {
        mean_disc = abs_f64(mc_mean - gum_mean) / abs_f64(gum_mean)
    }

    var std_disc: f64 = 0.0
    if gum_std > 1.0e-15 {
        std_disc = abs_f64(mc_std - gum_std) / gum_std
    }

    // Jensen's inequality: E[exp(X)] > exp(E[X]) for X non-degenerate
    // So mc_mean > gum_mean is expected for exp()

    let is_linear = std_disc < policy.max_relative_error
    var use_mc = false
    var warning = 0

    if !is_linear {
        if policy.auto_switch_to_mc {
            use_mc = true
            warning = 2
        } else if policy.warn_only {
            warning = 1
        } else {
            warning = 3  // Refuse
        }
    }

    return GumMcResult {
        gum_mean: gum_mean,
        gum_std: gum_std,
        mc_mean: mc_mean,
        mc_std: mc_std,
        mc_samples: n_samples,
        mean_discrepancy: mean_disc,
        std_discrepancy: std_disc,
        is_linear: is_linear,
        linearization_error: std_disc,
        use_mc: use_mc,
        warning_code: warning,
    }
}

// Check y = log(x) - nonlinear, especially near zero
fn dual_check_log(x: UncertainInput, n_samples: i32, policy: LinearizationPolicy) -> GumMcResult {
    // GUM estimate: ∂y/∂x = 1/x, so u_y = u_x / |μ_x|
    var gum_mean = 0.0
    var gum_std = 0.0
    if x.mean > 1.0e-10 {
        gum_mean = log(x.mean)
        gum_std = x.std / x.mean
    }

    // Monte Carlo
    var rng = rng_new(54321)
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var valid: i32 = 0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_samples {
        let r = rng_normal_params(rng, x.mean, x.std)
        let samp = r.value
        rng = r.rng

        if samp > 1.0e-10 {
            let y = log(samp)
            sum = sum + y
            sum_sq = sum_sq + y * y
            valid = valid + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var mc_mean: f64 = 0.0
    var mc_std: f64 = 0.0
    if valid > 1 {
        mc_mean = sum / (valid as f64)
        let mc_var = sum_sq / (valid as f64) - mc_mean * mc_mean
        mc_std = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(mc_var))
    }

    var std_disc: f64 = 0.0
    if gum_std > 1.0e-15 {
        std_disc = abs_f64(mc_std - gum_std) / gum_std
    }

    let is_linear = std_disc < policy.max_relative_error
    var use_mc = !is_linear && policy.auto_switch_to_mc
    var warning = 0
    if !is_linear { warning = 2 }

    return GumMcResult {
        gum_mean: gum_mean,
        gum_std: gum_std,
        mc_mean: mc_mean,
        mc_std: mc_std,
        mc_samples: valid,
        mean_discrepancy: 0.0,
        std_discrepancy: std_disc,
        is_linear: is_linear,
        linearization_error: std_disc,
        use_mc: use_mc,
        warning_code: warning,
    }
}

// Check y = a/b - nonlinear when b has large relative uncertainty
fn dual_check_div(a: UncertainInput, b: UncertainInput, n_samples: i32, policy: LinearizationPolicy) -> GumMcResult {
    // GUM estimate: relative uncertainties add in quadrature
    var gum_mean: f64 = 0.0
    var gum_std: f64 = 0.0
    if abs_f64(b.mean) > 1.0e-10 {
        gum_mean = a.mean / b.mean
        let rel_a = a.std / abs_f64(a.mean)
        let rel_b = b.std / abs_f64(b.mean)
        let rel_y = sqrt_f64(rel_a * rel_a + rel_b * rel_b)
        gum_std = abs_f64(gum_mean) * rel_y
    }

    // Monte Carlo
    var rng = rng_new(98765)
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var valid: i32 = 0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_samples {
        let ra = rng_normal_params(rng, a.mean, a.std)
        let va = ra.value
        rng = ra.rng

        let rb = rng_normal_params(rng, b.mean, b.std)
        let vb = rb.value
        rng = rb.rng

        if abs_f64(vb) > 1.0e-10 {
            let y = va / vb
            sum = sum + y
            sum_sq = sum_sq + y * y
            valid = valid + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var mc_mean: f64 = 0.0
    var mc_std: f64 = 0.0
    if valid > 1 {
        mc_mean = sum / (valid as f64)
        let mc_var = sum_sq / (valid as f64) - mc_mean * mc_mean
        mc_std = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(mc_var))
    }

    var std_disc: f64 = 0.0
    if gum_std > 1.0e-15 {
        std_disc = abs_f64(mc_std - gum_std) / gum_std
    }

    let is_linear = std_disc < policy.max_relative_error
    var use_mc = !is_linear && policy.auto_switch_to_mc
    var warning = 0
    if !is_linear { warning = 2 }

    return GumMcResult {
        gum_mean: gum_mean,
        gum_std: gum_std,
        mc_mean: mc_mean,
        mc_std: mc_std,
        mc_samples: valid,
        mean_discrepancy: 0.0,
        std_discrepancy: std_disc,
        is_linear: is_linear,
        linearization_error: std_disc,
        use_mc: use_mc,
        warning_code: warning,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PHARMACOKINETIC MODEL DUAL CHECK
// ============================================================================

// C(t) = (Dose/V) * exp(-CL/V * t)
// This is the classic case: exponential term makes GUM unreliable
fn dual_check_pk(
    dose: UncertainInput,
    volume: UncertainInput,
    clearance: UncertainInput,
    time: f64,
    n_samples: i32,
    policy: LinearizationPolicy
) -> GumMcResult {
    // GUM estimate (linearized)
    let c0 = dose.mean / volume.mean
    let k = clearance.mean / volume.mean
    let gum_mean = c0 * exp(0.0 - k * time)

    // Sensitivities at nominal point
    let dc_dD = exp(0.0 - k * time) / volume.mean
    let dc_dV = 0.0 - (dose.mean / (volume.mean * volume.mean)) * exp(0.0 - k * time)
              + (dose.mean * clearance.mean * time / (volume.mean * volume.mean * volume.mean)) * exp(0.0 - k * time)
    let dc_dCL = 0.0 - (dose.mean * time / (volume.mean * volume.mean)) * exp(0.0 - k * time)

    let gum_var = dc_dD * dc_dD * dose.std * dose.std
                + dc_dV * dc_dV * volume.std * volume.std
                + dc_dCL * dc_dCL * clearance.std * clearance.std
    let gum_std = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(gum_var))

    // Monte Carlo
    var rng = rng_new(11111)
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var valid: i32 = 0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_samples {
        let rd = rng_normal_params(rng, dose.mean, dose.std)
        let d = rd.value
        rng = rd.rng

        let rv = rng_normal_params(rng, volume.mean, volume.std)
        let v = rv.value
        rng = rv.rng

        let rc = rng_normal_params(rng, clearance.mean, clearance.std)
        let cl = rc.value
        rng = rc.rng

        if v > 1.0e-10 {
            let k_sample = cl / v
            let c = (d / v) * exp(0.0 - k_sample * time)
            sum = sum + c
            sum_sq = sum_sq + c * c
            valid = valid + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var mc_mean: f64 = 0.0
    var mc_std: f64 = 0.0
    if valid > 1 {
        mc_mean = sum / (valid as f64)
        let mc_var = sum_sq / (valid as f64) - mc_mean * mc_mean
        mc_std = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(mc_var))
    }

    var std_disc: f64 = 0.0
    if gum_std > 1.0e-15 {
        std_disc = abs_f64(mc_std - gum_std) / gum_std
    }

    var mean_disc: f64 = 0.0
    if abs_f64(gum_mean) > 1.0e-15 {
        mean_disc = abs_f64(mc_mean - gum_mean) / abs_f64(gum_mean)
    }

    let is_linear = std_disc < policy.max_relative_error
    var use_mc = !is_linear && policy.auto_switch_to_mc
    var warning = 0
    if !is_linear { warning = 2 }

    return GumMcResult {
        gum_mean: gum_mean,
        gum_std: gum_std,
        mc_mean: mc_mean,
        mc_std: mc_std,
        mc_samples: valid,
        mean_discrepancy: mean_disc,
        std_discrepancy: std_disc,
        is_linear: is_linear,
        linearization_error: std_disc,
        use_mc: use_mc,
        warning_code: warning,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// AUTOMATIC DUAL CHECK WRAPPER
// ============================================================================

// Get the best estimate, automatically switching methods if needed
struct BestEstimate {
    mean: f64,
    std: f64,
    method: i32,           // 0=GUM, 1=MC
    linearization_ok: bool,
    warning_message: i32,  // 0=none, 1=warn, 2=switched, 3=refused
}

fn get_best_estimate(res: GumMcResult) -> BestEstimate {
    if res.use_mc {
        return BestEstimate {
            mean: res.mc_mean,
            std: res.mc_std,
            method: 1,
            linearization_ok: false,
            warning_message: res.warning_code,
        }
    } else {
        return BestEstimate {
            mean: res.gum_mean,
            std: res.gum_std,
            method: 0,
            linearization_ok: res.is_linear,
            warning_message: res.warning_code,
        }
    }
}

// Check if result should be refused entirely
fn should_refuse(res: GumMcResult) -> bool {
    return res.warning_code == 3
}

// ============================================================================
// AUTO-SWITCH DECISION POLICY
// ============================================================================

// Decision tree for GUM vs MC selection (JCGM 101 guidance)
//
// The decision proceeds as:
//   1. Is linearization error acceptable? If yes → use GUM (faster)
//   2. Is auto-switch enabled? If yes → switch to MC automatically
//   3. Is warn-only mode? If yes → warn but use GUM
//   4. Otherwise → REFUSE (demand explicit method choice)
//
// This captures the JCGM 101 philosophy: GUM is the default,
// MC is the fallback when GUM assumptions fail.
struct AutoSwitchDecision {
    method: i32,             // 0=GUM, 1=MC, 2=refused
    reason: i32,             // 0=linear_ok, 1=auto_switch, 2=warned, 3=refused
    gum_uncertainty: f64,    // GUM estimate of uncertainty
    mc_uncertainty: f64,     // MC estimate of uncertainty
    discrepancy_ratio: f64,  // |u_mc - u_gum| / u_mc
    is_reliable: bool,       // True if we trust the result
}

// Make the auto-switch decision based on dual check result and policy
fn decide_method(res: GumMcResult, policy: LinearizationPolicy) -> AutoSwitchDecision {
    // Step 1: Is linearization acceptable?
    if res.is_linear {
        return AutoSwitchDecision {
            method: 0,  // GUM
            reason: 0,  // linear_ok
            gum_uncertainty: res.gum_std,
            mc_uncertainty: res.mc_std,
            discrepancy_ratio: res.std_discrepancy,
            is_reliable: true,
        }
    }

    // Step 2: Linearization failed - check policy
    if policy.auto_switch_to_mc {
        return AutoSwitchDecision {
            method: 1,  // MC
            reason: 1,  // auto_switch
            gum_uncertainty: res.gum_std,
            mc_uncertainty: res.mc_std,
            discrepancy_ratio: res.std_discrepancy,
            is_reliable: true,
        }
    }

    // Step 3: No auto-switch - check warn-only
    if policy.warn_only {
        return AutoSwitchDecision {
            method: 0,  // GUM (with warning)
            reason: 2,  // warned
            gum_uncertainty: res.gum_std,
            mc_uncertainty: res.mc_std,
            discrepancy_ratio: res.std_discrepancy,
            is_reliable: false,  // Not reliable!
        }
    }

    // Step 4: Refuse - demand explicit choice
    return AutoSwitchDecision {
        method: 2,  // refused
        reason: 3,  // refused
        gum_uncertainty: res.gum_std,
        mc_uncertainty: res.mc_std,
        discrepancy_ratio: res.std_discrepancy,
        is_reliable: false,
    }
}

// Gate: block computation if method is refused
fn gate_method_refused(decision: AutoSwitchDecision) -> bool {
    return decision.method == 2
}

// Gate: warn if result is not reliable
fn gate_unreliable_result(decision: AutoSwitchDecision) -> bool {
    return !decision.is_reliable
}

// ============================================================================
// CROSS-CHECK POLICY: INTEGRATED VALIDATION
// ============================================================================

// Cross-check policy combining multiple validation criteria
struct CrossCheckPolicy {
    linearization: LinearizationPolicy,
    require_mc_validation: bool,    // Always run MC to validate GUM
    min_mc_samples: i32,            // Minimum MC samples for validation
    max_discrepancy_warn: f64,      // Warn if discrepancy > this
    max_discrepancy_refuse: f64,    // Refuse if discrepancy > this
}

fn default_cross_check_policy() -> CrossCheckPolicy {
    return CrossCheckPolicy {
        linearization: default_linearization_policy(),
        require_mc_validation: true,
        min_mc_samples: 100,
        max_discrepancy_warn: 0.10,
        max_discrepancy_refuse: 0.30,
    }
}

fn strict_cross_check_policy() -> CrossCheckPolicy {
    return CrossCheckPolicy {
        linearization: strict_linearization_policy(),
        require_mc_validation: true,
        min_mc_samples: 500,
        max_discrepancy_warn: 0.05,
        max_discrepancy_refuse: 0.15,
    }
}

// Cross-check result with integrated validation
struct CrossCheckResult {
    // Method selection
    final_method: i32,       // 0=GUM, 1=MC
    final_mean: f64,
    final_std: f64,

    // Validation status
    gum_validated: bool,     // True if GUM was validated by MC
    discrepancy: f64,        // Observed discrepancy
    validation_status: i32,  // 0=passed, 1=warned, 2=failed

    // Diagnostic
    mc_samples_used: i32,
    linearization_ok: bool,
    recommendation: i32,     // 0=proceed, 1=review, 2=refuse
}

// Run full cross-check with integrated validation
fn run_cross_check_exp(x: UncertainInput, policy: CrossCheckPolicy) -> CrossCheckResult {
    // Always run both methods
    let res = dual_check_exp(x, policy.min_mc_samples, policy.linearization)

    // Make method decision
    let decision = decide_method(res, policy.linearization)

    // Determine final values
    var final_mean = res.gum_mean
    var final_std = res.gum_std
    if decision.method == 1 {
        final_mean = res.mc_mean
        final_std = res.mc_std
    }

    // Determine validation status
    var val_status: i32 = 0
    if res.std_discrepancy > policy.max_discrepancy_refuse {
        val_status = 2  // Failed
    } else if res.std_discrepancy > policy.max_discrepancy_warn {
        val_status = 1  // Warned
    }

    // Determine recommendation
    var rec: i32 = 0
    if decision.method == 2 {
        rec = 2  // Refuse
    } else if val_status == 1 {
        rec = 1  // Review
    }

    return CrossCheckResult {
        final_method: decision.method,
        final_mean: final_mean,
        final_std: final_std,
        gum_validated: res.is_linear,
        discrepancy: res.std_discrepancy,
        validation_status: val_status,
        mc_samples_used: res.mc_samples,
        linearization_ok: res.is_linear,
        recommendation: rec,
    }
}

// Check if cross-check recommends refusal
fn cross_check_should_refuse(result: CrossCheckResult) -> bool {
    return result.recommendation == 2
}

// Check if cross-check recommends review
fn cross_check_should_review(result: CrossCheckResult) -> bool {
    return result.recommendation == 1
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_linear_case() -> bool {
    // For small relative uncertainty, exp() is approximately linear
    let x = dual_input(1.0, 0.01)  // 1% relative uncertainty
    let policy = default_linearization_policy()

    let result = dual_check_exp(x, 1000, policy)

    // Should be considered linear
    if !result.is_linear { return false }
    if result.use_mc { return false }
    if result.warning_code != 0 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_nonlinear_exp() -> bool {
    // Large relative uncertainty in exponent -> nonlinear
    let x = dual_input(1.0, 0.5)  // 50% relative uncertainty!
    let policy = default_linearization_policy()

    let result = dual_check_exp(x, 1000, policy)

    // Should detect nonlinearity
    if result.is_linear { return false }

    // Should switch to MC (default policy)
    if !result.use_mc { return false }
    if result.warning_code != 2 { return false }

    // MC mean should be HIGHER than GUM mean (Jensen's inequality)
    if result.mc_mean < result.gum_mean { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_division_nonlinear() -> bool {
    // Division with large denominator uncertainty
    let a = dual_input(100.0, 5.0)    // 5% relative uncertainty
    let b = dual_input(10.0, 3.0)     // 30% relative uncertainty in denominator!
    let policy = default_linearization_policy()

    let result = dual_check_div(a, b, 1000, policy)

    // Should likely detect nonlinearity due to high denominator uncertainty
    // (linearization fails when σ_b/b is large)
    if result.linearization_error < 0.05 {
        // If somehow still linear, at least check reasonable values
        if result.gum_std < 1.0 { return false }
    }

    return true
}

fn test_pk_model_dual() -> bool {
    // PK model with realistic uncertainty
    let dose = dual_input(500.0, 10.0)      // 2% CV
    let volume = dual_input(50.0, 10.0)     // 20% CV
    let clearance = dual_input(5.0, 2.0)    // 40% CV in clearance
    let time = 4.0

    let policy = default_linearization_policy()
    let result = dual_check_pk(dose, volume, clearance, time, 1000, policy)

    // Should detect nonlinearity due to exponential with uncertain rate
    // At least verify we get reasonable values
    if result.gum_std < 0.0 { return false }
    if result.mc_std < 0.0 { return false }

    // Get best estimate
    let best = get_best_estimate(result)
    if best.mean < 0.0 { return false }
    if best.std < 0.0 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_best_estimate_selection() -> bool {
    let x = dual_input(1.0, 0.5)
    let policy = default_linearization_policy()

    let result = dual_check_exp(x, 1000, policy)
    let best = get_best_estimate(result)

    // For nonlinear case, should use MC
    if result.use_mc {
        if best.method != 1 { return false }
        if abs_f64(best.mean - result.mc_mean) > 0.001 { return false }
    }

    return true
}

fn test_auto_switch_linear() -> bool {
    // Linear case: should use GUM
    let x = dual_input(1.0, 0.01)  // Small uncertainty -> linear
    let policy = default_linearization_policy()
    let res = dual_check_exp(x, 500, policy)
    let decision = decide_method(res, policy)

    if decision.method != 0 { return false }  // Should be GUM
    if decision.reason != 0 { return false }   // linear_ok
    if !decision.is_reliable { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_auto_switch_nonlinear() -> bool {
    // Nonlinear case: should auto-switch to MC
    let x = dual_input(1.0, 0.5)  // Large uncertainty -> nonlinear
    let policy = default_linearization_policy()  // auto_switch_to_mc = true
    let res = dual_check_exp(x, 500, policy)
    let decision = decide_method(res, policy)

    // Should switch to MC
    if decision.method != 1 { return false }  // MC
    if decision.reason != 1 { return false }   // auto_switch
    if !decision.is_reliable { return false }  // MC is reliable

    return true
}

fn test_cross_check_policy() -> bool {
    // Test the integrated cross-check
    let x = dual_input(1.0, 0.3)  // Moderate uncertainty
    let policy = default_cross_check_policy()

    let result = run_cross_check_exp(x, policy)

    // Should have valid outputs
    if result.final_std < 0.0 { return false }
    if result.mc_samples_used < 50 { return false }

    // Recommendation should be valid
    if result.recommendation < 0 || result.recommendation > 2 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_cross_check_refusal_gates() -> bool {
    // Test the gate functions
    let x = dual_input(1.0, 0.01)  // Linear
    let policy = default_cross_check_policy()

    let result = run_cross_check_exp(x, policy)

    // Should not refuse for linear case
    if cross_check_should_refuse(result) { return false }

    // Should not require review for linear case
    if result.validation_status == 2 { return false }

    return true
}
