// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/editable.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/editable.sio
//
// Editable<T> helpers — locality-bounded model editing backed by the
// sedenion ZD kernel.
//
// Given a stored fact encoded as a sedenion value v_i with a key k_i
// living in the 4-dimensional right-annihilator of A = e3 + e10, a
// ZD-class edit delta ∈ span(e3 + e10) produces zero ripple on facts
// whose keys stay inside the kernel.
//
// Formal backing: `editing_locality_kernel_bound` in
// formal/lean4/SounioSurgicalInterventions.lean.
// Operational benchmark: examples/zd_model_editing_locality.sio
// (safe-fact ripple = 0.000000, ROME ripple ≈ 0.509902).

// zd_edit_delta: a canonical edit delta in span(e3 + e10), scaled by
// magnitude `alpha`.  The result is guaranteed to annihilate any stored
// value whose key lies in the kernel.
fn zd_edit_delta(alpha: f64) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD {
    var d: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    d[3]  = alpha
    d[10] = alpha
    d
}

// is_kernel_key: a sanity check that a key has no support outside the
// kernel basis {e6-e15, e7+e14}/√2.  Returns true when the key is a
// linear combination of the two basis vectors.  In production this
// would be a compile-time refinement; here it is a runtime assertion.
fn is_kernel_key(k: &[f64; 16]) -> bool with Mut, ZD {
    let s = 0.707107
    // The only non-zero supports allowed are indices 6, 7, 14, 15
    // and they must satisfy k[6] = -k[15]  (for u1 direction) and
    //                      k[7] =  k[14]  (for u2 direction).
    var i = 0
    var ok = true
    while i < 16 {
        if i == 6 || i == 7 || i == 14 || i == 15 {
            // allowed
        } else {
            if (*k)[i] > 0.000001 || (*k)[i] < 0.0 - 0.000001 { ok = false }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let d1 = (*k)[6] + (*k)[15]    // must be ~0
    let d2 = (*k)[7] - (*k)[14]    // must be ~0
    if d1 > 0.000001 || d1 < 0.0 - 0.000001 { ok = false }
    if d2 > 0.000001 || d2 < 0.0 - 0.000001 { ok = false }
    ok
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/epistemic_kind.sio ===
// Epistemic uncertainty type — reducible model uncertainty
//
// Epistemic<T> wraps a value with reducible uncertainty.
// Epistemic uncertainty can in principle be reduced by:
//   - Collecting more data
//   - Improving the model
//   - Bayesian updating
//
// Contrast with Aleatoric<T> which is irreducible.

module epistemic::epistemic_kind

// Epistemic uncertainty value wrapper.
struct EpistemicValue {
    value: f64,
    epsilon: f64,
    reducible_by_n_samples: i64,   // samples needed to halve uncertainty (-1 = unknown)
}

// Construct an epistemic value
fn epistemic_new(value: f64, epsilon: f64) -> EpistemicValue {
    EpistemicValue {
        value: value,
        epsilon: epsilon,
        reducible_by_n_samples: -1,
    }
}

// Integer square root approximation (Newton's method, 10 iterations)
fn sqrt_ep_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 {
        0.0
    } else {
        var est: f64 = x
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < 10 {
            est = (est + x / est) / 2.0
            i = i + 1
        }
        est
    }
}

// Bayesian update: combine prior epistemic estimate with new data
// New epsilon ~= prior_eps / sqrt(1 + n_new_samples)
fn epistemic_update(prior: EpistemicValue, n_new_samples: i64) -> EpistemicValue with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n_new_samples <= 0 {
        prior
    } else {
        let n_f = n_new_samples as f64
        let new_eps = prior.epsilon / sqrt_ep_approx(1.0 + n_f)
        EpistemicValue {
            value: prior.value,
            epsilon: new_eps,
            reducible_by_n_samples: prior.reducible_by_n_samples,
        }
    }
}

fn epistemic_value(e: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    e.value
}

fn epistemic_epsilon(e: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    e.epsilon
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/fusion.sio ===
//! Evidence Fusion Module
//!
//! This module provides rigorous evidence combination for epistemic computing.
//!
//! TWO DISTINCT FUSION PARADIGMS:
//!
//! 1. DEMPSTER-SHAFER (for propositions/hypotheses)
//!    - Combines belief masses over discrete hypotheses
//!    - Explicit conflict handling (K factor)
//!    - Appropriate for: binary outcomes, categorical decisions
//!
//! 2. BAYESIAN (for continuous beliefs)
//!    - Likelihood-ratio updates
//!    - Proper posterior computation
//!    - Appropriate for: parameter estimation, probability updates
//!
//! CRITICAL: DS is NOT for combining numeric measurements.
//! Use inverse-variance weighting (see core.d fuse_measurements) for that.

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

fn log_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return -1.0e308 }
    return log(x)
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return exp(x)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn clamp_f64(x: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < lo { return lo }
    if x > hi { return hi }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// DEMPSTER-SHAFER FOR BINARY PROPOSITIONS
// ============================================================================

// Binary mass function: masses on {H}, {¬H}, {H,¬H} (uncertainty)
// INVARIANT: m_h + m_not_h + m_uncertain = 1.0
// INVARIANT: all masses >= 0
struct BinaryMass {
    m_h: f64,           // mass on hypothesis H
    m_not_h: f64,       // mass on ¬H
    m_uncertain: f64,   // mass on {H, ¬H} (ignorance)
}

// Create a binary mass function from belief and plausibility
fn binary_mass_new(belief_h: f64, plausibility_h: f64) -> BinaryMass {
    // Bel(H) <= Pl(H), both in [0,1]
    let bel = clamp_f64(belief_h, 0.0, 1.0)
    let pl = clamp_f64(plausibility_h, bel, 1.0)

    // m(H) = Bel(H)
    // m(¬H) = 1 - Pl(H)
    // m({H,¬H}) = Pl(H) - Bel(H)
    return BinaryMass {
        m_h: bel,
        m_not_h: 1.0 - pl,
        m_uncertain: pl - bel,
    }
}

// Create from direct mass assignment
fn binary_mass_direct(m_h: f64, m_not_h: f64, m_uncertain: f64) -> BinaryMass {
    // Normalize to ensure sum = 1
    let total = m_h + m_not_h + m_uncertain
    if total < 1.0e-15 {
        // Complete ignorance
        return BinaryMass { m_h: 0.0, m_not_h: 0.0, m_uncertain: 1.0 }
    }

    return BinaryMass {
        m_h: max_f64(0.0, m_h / total),
        m_not_h: max_f64(0.0, m_not_h / total),
        m_uncertain: max_f64(0.0, m_uncertain / total),
    }
}

// Complete ignorance (vacuous belief)
fn binary_mass_vacuous() -> BinaryMass {
    return BinaryMass { m_h: 0.0, m_not_h: 0.0, m_uncertain: 1.0 }
}

// Complete belief in H
fn binary_mass_certain_h() -> BinaryMass {
    return BinaryMass { m_h: 1.0, m_not_h: 0.0, m_uncertain: 0.0 }
}

// Complete belief in ¬H
fn binary_mass_certain_not_h() -> BinaryMass {
    return BinaryMass { m_h: 0.0, m_not_h: 1.0, m_uncertain: 0.0 }
}

// Get belief in H: Bel(H) = m(H)
fn binary_belief_h(m: BinaryMass) -> f64 {
    return m.m_h
}

// Get plausibility of H: Pl(H) = m(H) + m({H,¬H}) = 1 - m(¬H)
fn binary_plausibility_h(m: BinaryMass) -> f64 {
    return m.m_h + m.m_uncertain
}

// Get uncertainty interval width: Pl(H) - Bel(H)
fn binary_uncertainty_width(m: BinaryMass) -> f64 {
    return m.m_uncertain
}

// ============================================================================
// DEMPSTER'S RULE OF COMBINATION
// ============================================================================

// Result of DS combination includes conflict measure
struct DSCombineResult {
    combined: BinaryMass,
    conflict_k: f64,    // K ∈ [0,1), higher = more conflict
    is_valid: bool,     // false if K = 1 (total conflict)
}

// Combine two binary mass functions using Dempster's rule
// WARNING: High conflict (K near 1) indicates inconsistent evidence
fn ds_combine_binary(m1: BinaryMass, m2: BinaryMass) -> DSCombineResult {
    // Compute unnormalized combined masses
    // m12(H) comes from: m1(H)·m2(H) + m1(H)·m2(Θ) + m1(Θ)·m2(H)
    // m12(¬H) comes from: m1(¬H)·m2(¬H) + m1(¬H)·m2(Θ) + m1(Θ)·m2(¬H)
    // m12(Θ) comes from: m1(Θ)·m2(Θ)

    let raw_h = m1.m_h * m2.m_h +
                m1.m_h * m2.m_uncertain +
                m1.m_uncertain * m2.m_h

    let raw_not_h = m1.m_not_h * m2.m_not_h +
                    m1.m_not_h * m2.m_uncertain +
                    m1.m_uncertain * m2.m_not_h

    let raw_uncertain = m1.m_uncertain * m2.m_uncertain

    // Conflict: mass assigned to empty set
    // K = m1(H)·m2(¬H) + m1(¬H)·m2(H)
    let conflict_k = m1.m_h * m2.m_not_h + m1.m_not_h * m2.m_h

    // Check for total conflict
    if conflict_k >= 1.0 - 1.0e-10 {
        return DSCombineResult {
            combined: binary_mass_vacuous(),
            conflict_k: 1.0,
            is_valid: false,
        }
    }

    // Normalize by (1 - K)
    let norm = 1.0 / (1.0 - conflict_k)

    return DSCombineResult {
        combined: BinaryMass {
            m_h: raw_h * norm,
            m_not_h: raw_not_h * norm,
            m_uncertain: raw_uncertain * norm,
        },
        conflict_k: conflict_k,
        is_valid: true,
    }
}

// Combine multiple evidence sources
fn ds_combine_multiple(masses: &[BinaryMass], n: i64) -> DSCombineResult {
    if n <= 0 {
        return DSCombineResult {
            combined: binary_mass_vacuous(),
            conflict_k: 0.0,
            is_valid: true,
        }
    }
    if n == 1 {
        return DSCombineResult {
            combined: masses[0],
            conflict_k: 0.0,
            is_valid: true,
        }
    }

    var result = masses[0]
    var total_conflict = 0.0

    for i in 1..n {
        let combined = ds_combine_binary(result, masses[i as i64])
        if !combined.is_valid {
            return combined
        }
        result = combined.combined
        // Accumulate conflict (approximately)
        total_conflict = total_conflict + combined.conflict_k * (1.0 - total_conflict)
    }

    return DSCombineResult {
        combined: result,
        conflict_k: total_conflict,
        is_valid: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// BAYESIAN BELIEF (for probability updates)
// ============================================================================

// Beta distribution parameters (conjugate prior for binomial)
struct BetaBelief {
    alpha: f64,     // successes + 1
    beta: f64,      // failures + 1
}

// Create uniform prior (complete ignorance)
fn beta_uniform() -> BetaBelief {
    return BetaBelief { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
}

// Create from observed data
fn beta_from_data(successes: f64, failures: f64) -> BetaBelief {
    return BetaBelief {
        alpha: max_f64(0.0, successes) + 1.0,
        beta: max_f64(0.0, failures) + 1.0,
    }
}

// Create informative prior
fn beta_prior(alpha: f64, beta: f64) -> BetaBelief {
    return BetaBelief {
        alpha: max_f64(0.001, alpha),
        beta: max_f64(0.001, beta),
    }
}

// Get mean of Beta distribution
fn beta_mean(b: BetaBelief) -> f64 {
    return b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta)
}

// Get variance of Beta distribution
fn beta_variance(b: BetaBelief) -> f64 {
    let total = b.alpha + b.beta
    return (b.alpha * b.beta) / (total * total * (total + 1.0))
}

// Get standard deviation
fn beta_std(b: BetaBelief) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(beta_variance(b))
}

// Get effective sample size (measure of certainty)
fn beta_sample_size(b: BetaBelief) -> f64 {
    return b.alpha + b.beta - 2.0  // subtract prior counts
}

// ============================================================================
// BAYESIAN UPDATES
// ============================================================================

// Update Beta belief with new observations
fn beta_update(prior: BetaBelief, successes: f64, failures: f64) -> BetaBelief {
    return BetaBelief {
        alpha: prior.alpha + max_f64(0.0, successes),
        beta: prior.beta + max_f64(0.0, failures),
    }
}

// Combine two independent Beta beliefs (product of experts)
fn beta_combine_independent(b1: BetaBelief, b2: BetaBelief) -> BetaBelief {
    // Approximate: add pseudo-counts
    return BetaBelief {
        alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0,  // subtract one prior
        beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0,
    }
}

// Convert Beta belief to confidence score
// Uses the probability that the true rate is above 0.5 (for H)
fn beta_to_confidence(b: BetaBelief) -> f64 {
    // Approximate using normal approximation for large samples
    let mean = beta_mean(b)
    let std = beta_std(b)

    if std < 1.0e-10 {
        return if mean > 0.5 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 }
    }

    // z-score for mean being above 0.5
    let z = (mean - 0.5) / std

    // Approximate CDF using logistic approximation
    let conf = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp_f64(-1.7 * z))
    return clamp_f64(conf, 0.0, 1.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// LIKELIHOOD RATIO UPDATES
// ============================================================================

// Odds form of probability
struct OddsBelief {
    log_odds: f64,    // log(p / (1-p))
}

// Convert probability to odds
fn odds_from_prob(p: f64) -> OddsBelief {
    let prob = clamp_f64(p, 1.0e-10, 1.0 - 1.0e-10)
    return OddsBelief {
        log_odds: log_f64(prob / (1.0 - prob)),
    }
}

// Convert odds to probability
fn odds_to_prob(o: OddsBelief) -> f64 {
    let odds = exp_f64(o.log_odds)
    return odds / (1.0 + odds)
}

// Update odds with likelihood ratio
// LR = P(evidence | H) / P(evidence | ¬H)
fn odds_update(prior: OddsBelief, log_likelihood_ratio: f64) -> OddsBelief {
    return OddsBelief {
        log_odds: prior.log_odds + log_likelihood_ratio,
    }
}

// Combine independent odds (in log space, just add)
fn odds_combine(o1: OddsBelief, o2: OddsBelief) -> OddsBelief {
    // This assumes the evidence is independent
    // Posterior odds = prior odds × LR1 × LR2 × ...
    // In log space: log(posterior) = log(prior) + log(LR1) + log(LR2)
    return OddsBelief {
        log_odds: o1.log_odds + o2.log_odds,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// BRIDGE: DS ↔ BAYESIAN
// ============================================================================

// Convert DS belief to probability (pignistic transformation)
fn ds_to_probability(m: BinaryMass) -> f64 {
    // Pignistic probability: P(H) = m(H) + m(Θ)/2
    return m.m_h + m.m_uncertain / 2.0
}

// Convert probability + confidence to DS mass
fn probability_to_ds(prob: f64, confidence: f64) -> BinaryMass {
    let p = clamp_f64(prob, 0.0, 1.0)
    let c = clamp_f64(confidence, 0.0, 1.0)

    // Higher confidence = more mass on singletons
    // Lower confidence = more mass on Θ
    return BinaryMass {
        m_h: p * c,
        m_not_h: (1.0 - p) * c,
        m_uncertain: 1.0 - c,
    }
}

// Convert Beta to DS mass
fn beta_to_ds(b: BetaBelief) -> BinaryMass {
    let mean = beta_mean(b)
    let confidence = beta_to_confidence(b)
    return probability_to_ds(mean, confidence)
}

// ============================================================================
// INVARIANT CHECKS
// ============================================================================

fn is_valid_binary_mass(m: BinaryMass) -> bool {
    // All masses non-negative
    if m.m_h < -1.0e-10 || m.m_not_h < -1.0e-10 || m.m_uncertain < -1.0e-10 {
        return false
    }
    // Sum to 1
    let sum = m.m_h + m.m_not_h + m.m_uncertain
    if abs_f64(sum - 1.0) > 1.0e-6 {
        return false
    }
    return true
}

fn is_valid_beta(b: BetaBelief) -> bool {
    return b.alpha > 0.0 && b.beta > 0.0
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_ds_vacuous_combination() -> bool {
    // Combining with vacuous belief should not change the other
    let m1 = binary_mass_new(0.6, 0.8)
    let m2 = binary_mass_vacuous()
    let result = ds_combine_binary(m1, m2)

    if !result.is_valid { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.combined.m_h - m1.m_h) > 0.01 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_ds_conflict_detection() -> bool {
    // Completely contradictory evidence should have high conflict
    let m1 = binary_mass_certain_h()
    let m2 = binary_mass_certain_not_h()
    let result = ds_combine_binary(m1, m2)

    // Should be invalid (K = 1)
    return !result.is_valid && result.conflict_k > 0.99
}

fn test_beta_update_increases_certainty() -> bool {
    let prior = beta_uniform()
    let posterior = beta_update(prior, 10.0, 2.0)

    // More data = less variance
    return beta_variance(posterior) < beta_variance(prior)
}

fn test_ds_mass_validity() -> bool {
    let m = binary_mass_new(0.3, 0.7)
    return is_valid_binary_mass(m)
}

// MAIN


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/graded_effects.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/graded_effects.sio — Graded Epistemic Effects
//
// Fuses row-polymorphic algebraic effects (Track A) with the
// epistemic/aleatoric uncertainty split (Track B) into a unified
// graded modality system.
//
// Theory (PLDI 2027, Track C):
//   - Grade an effect row with an uncertainty bound: Prob<ε>
//   - Epistemic grade composition: Prob<ε1> ∘ Prob<ε2> = Prob<√(ε1² + ε2²)]
//   - Aleatoric grade composition: Prob<ε1> ∘ Prob<ε2> = Prob<ε1 + ε2>
//   - Subsumption: Prob<ε_tight> satisfies Prob<ε_loose> iff ε_tight ≤ ε_loose
//
// GUM compliance: grade composition is GUM-sound (ISO/IEC Guide 98-3).
//
// References:
//   - Granule: graded modal types (Orchard/McBride)
//   - GMDT: graded modal dependent types (Abel/Orchard POPL 2023)
//   - DEUP: decomposed epistemic/aleatoric uncertainty (Bengio 2021)

module epistemic::graded_effects

// GradedProb: runtime representation of a Prob<ε>-graded computation result.
// Carries the value, the achieved grade ε, and whether the grade is epistemic or aleatoric.
struct GradedProb {
    value: f64,
    epsilon: f64,       // achieved uncertainty grade ε ∈ [0,1]
    is_aleatoric: bool, // false = epistemic (reducible), true = aleatoric (irreducible)
}

// Construct an epistemic-graded value: reducible by more data
fn graded_epistemic(value: f64, epsilon: f64) -> GradedProb {
    GradedProb {
        value: value,
        epsilon: epsilon,
        is_aleatoric: false,
    }
}

// Construct an aleatoric-graded value: irreducible physical uncertainty
fn graded_aleatoric(value: f64, epsilon: f64) -> GradedProb {
    GradedProb {
        value: value,
        epsilon: epsilon,
        is_aleatoric: true,
    }
}

// Integer square root approximation (10 Newton iterations)
fn graded_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 {
        0.0
    } else {
        var est: f64 = x
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < 10 {
            est = (est + x / est) / 2.0
            i = i + 1
        }
        est
    }
}

// Grade composition: a ∘ b
// Composes two graded computations following the GUM propagation rule.
// Mixed (epistemic + aleatoric) → aleatoric (worst case, irreducibility dominates).
fn graded_compose(a: GradedProb, b: GradedProb) -> GradedProb with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a.is_aleatoric || b.is_aleatoric {
        // Aleatoric dominates: additive composition
        GradedProb {
            value: a.value,
            epsilon: a.epsilon + b.epsilon,
            is_aleatoric: true,
        }
    } else {
        // Epistemic: quadrature — sqrt(ε1² + ε2²)
        let sum_sq = a.epsilon * a.epsilon + b.epsilon * b.epsilon
        GradedProb {
            value: a.value,
            epsilon: graded_sqrt(sum_sq),
            is_aleatoric: false,
        }
    }
}

// Subsumption check: does `provided` satisfy `required` grade?
// Returns true iff provided.ε ≤ required.ε
fn graded_subsumes(provided: GradedProb, required_epsilon: f64) -> bool {
    provided.epsilon <= required_epsilon
}

// Bayesian update: reduce epistemic grade by n new samples
// New ε ~= ε_prior / sqrt(1 + n)  (Bernstein-von Mises convergence rate)
fn graded_epistemic_update(prior: GradedProb, n_samples: i64) -> GradedProb with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if prior.is_aleatoric || n_samples <= 0 {
        prior
    } else {
        let n_f = n_samples as f64
        let new_eps = prior.epsilon / graded_sqrt(1.0 + n_f)
        GradedProb {
            value: prior.value,
            epsilon: new_eps,
            is_aleatoric: false,
        }
    }
}

// Extract the grade (uncertainty bound)
fn graded_epsilon(g: GradedProb) -> f64 {
    g.epsilon
}

// Extract the value
fn graded_value(g: GradedProb) -> f64 {
    g.value
}

// Check if this grade is at the threshold for a safety-critical decision
// Returns true if epsilon <= threshold (safe to act on)
fn graded_is_safe(g: GradedProb, threshold: f64) -> bool {
    g.epsilon <= threshold
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/gradient_bridge.sio ===
// Sprint 24 Moonshot: SGD -> Langevin -> Gibbs bridge
// References: Welling & Teh (2011) SGLD, Roberts & Tweedie (1996)

fn sgd_as_langevin(learning_rate: f64, temperature: f64) -> f64 {
    // Diffusion coefficient sigma^2 = 2 * lr * T for Langevin dynamics
    2.0 * learning_rate * temperature
}

fn gibbs_log_weight(energy: f64, beta: f64) -> f64 {
    // Unnormalized log Gibbs weight: -beta * U(x)
    0.0 - beta * energy
}

fn langevin_chain_demo(x0: f64, grad_f: f64, lr: f64, temp: f64, n_steps: i64) -> f64 {
    // n steps of Langevin MCMC: x_{t+1} = x_t - lr*grad_f + sqrt(2*lr*T)*noise
    // For demo: use deterministic noise=0.1 per step
    let noise: f64 = 0.1
    let diffusion: f64 = 2.0 * lr * temp
    var x: f64 = x0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        x = x - lr * grad_f + noise * diffusion
        i = i + 1
    }
    x
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/gum.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL PASS

// stdlib/epistemic/gum.sio — GUM-compliant uncertainty propagation
//
// Implements JCGM 100:2008 uncertainty framework:
//   - Type A (statistical) and Type B (a priori) uncertainty components
//   - Combined standard uncertainty via sensitivity coefficients
//   - Welch-Satterthwaite effective degrees of freedom
//   - Coverage factors from t-distribution table
//   - Expanded uncertainty at 95% and 99% confidence
//
// Reference: JCGM 100:2008 (GUM)

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn gum_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

fn gum_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn gum_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn gum_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// t-distribution 95% quantile by degrees of freedom (1-based lookup)
fn t95(dof: i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if dof <= 0 { return 12.71 }
    if dof == 1 { return 12.71 }
    if dof == 2 { return 4.303 }
    if dof == 3 { return 3.182 }
    if dof == 4 { return 2.776 }
    if dof == 5 { return 2.571 }
    if dof == 6 { return 2.447 }
    if dof == 7 { return 2.365 }
    if dof == 8 { return 2.306 }
    if dof == 9 { return 2.262 }
    if dof == 10 { return 2.228 }
    if dof == 11 { return 2.201 }
    if dof == 12 { return 2.179 }
    if dof == 13 { return 2.160 }
    if dof == 14 { return 2.145 }
    if dof == 15 { return 2.131 }
    if dof == 16 { return 2.120 }
    if dof == 17 { return 2.110 }
    if dof == 18 { return 2.101 }
    if dof == 19 { return 2.093 }
    if dof < 30 { return 2.086 }
    if dof < 60 { return 2.042 }
    if dof < 120 { return 2.000 }
    1.96  // normal approximation
}

fn t99(dof: i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if dof <= 0 { return 63.66 }
    if dof == 1 { return 63.66 }
    if dof == 2 { return 9.925 }
    if dof == 3 { return 5.841 }
    if dof == 4 { return 4.604 }
    if dof == 5 { return 4.032 }
    if dof == 6 { return 3.707 }
    if dof == 7 { return 3.499 }
    if dof == 8 { return 3.355 }
    if dof == 9 { return 3.250 }
    if dof == 10 { return 3.169 }
    if dof < 20 { return 2.845 }
    if dof < 30 { return 2.763 }
    2.576  // normal approximation
}

// Convert f64 dof to i64 for table lookup (infinity → large value)
fn dof_to_i64(dof: f64) -> i64 with Div, Panic {
    if dof > 1.0e8 { return 10000 }
    return dof as i64
}

// ============================================================================
// UNCERTAINTY COMPONENT
// ============================================================================

// A single uncertainty source with sensitivity coefficient and degrees of freedom.
pub struct GUMComponent {
    std_u: f64,        // standard uncertainty u(x_i)
    sensitivity: f64,  // sensitivity coefficient c_i = ∂f/∂x_i
    dof: f64,          // degrees of freedom ν_i (1e9 = infinity for Type B)
}

// Type A: statistical, u = std_dev / sqrt(n), ν = n-1
pub fn gum_type_a(std_dev: f64, n: i64) -> GUMComponent with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let denom = if n > 0 { gum_sqrt(n as f64) } else { 1.0 }
    let std_u = if n > 0 { std_dev / denom } else { std_dev }
    let dof = if n > 1 { (n - 1) as f64 } else { 1.0 }
    GUMComponent { std_u: std_u, sensitivity: 1.0, dof: dof }
}

// Type B: a priori, ν = ∞ (1e9)
pub fn gum_type_b(std_u: f64) -> GUMComponent {
    GUMComponent { std_u: gum_abs(std_u), sensitivity: 1.0, dof: 1.0e9 }
}

// Type B from uniform distribution ±a: u = a/sqrt(3)
pub fn gum_type_b_uniform(half_width: f64) -> GUMComponent {
    let std_u = gum_abs(half_width) / 1.732050808
    GUMComponent { std_u: std_u, sensitivity: 1.0, dof: 1.0e9 }
}

// Type B from triangular distribution ±a: u = a/sqrt(6)
pub fn gum_type_b_triangular(half_width: f64) -> GUMComponent {
    let std_u = gum_abs(half_width) / 2.449489743
    GUMComponent { std_u: std_u, sensitivity: 1.0, dof: 1.0e9 }
}

// Type B from expanded uncertainty U with coverage factor k
pub fn gum_type_b_expanded(expanded_u: f64, k: f64) -> GUMComponent with Div, Panic {
    let std_u = if k > 0.0 { expanded_u / k } else { expanded_u }
    GUMComponent { std_u: gum_abs(std_u), sensitivity: 1.0, dof: 1.0e9 }
}

pub fn gum_with_sensitivity(c: GUMComponent, s: f64) -> GUMComponent {
    GUMComponent { std_u: c.std_u, sensitivity: s, dof: c.dof }
}

// ============================================================================
// GUM RESULT
// ============================================================================

pub struct GUMResult {
    value: f64,
    std_u: f64,        // combined standard uncertainty u_c
    dof: f64,          // effective degrees of freedom ν_eff
    k95: f64,          // coverage factor at 95%
    u95: f64,          // expanded uncertainty at 95%
    k99: f64,          // coverage factor at 99%
    u99: f64,          // expanded uncertainty at 99%
}

fn gum_result_from_parts(value: f64, std_u: f64, dof: f64) -> GUMResult with Div, Panic {
    let di = dof_to_i64(dof)
    let k95v = t95(di)
    let k99v = t99(di)
    GUMResult {
        value: value,
        std_u: std_u,
        dof: dof,
        k95: k95v,
        u95: k95v * std_u,
        k99: k99v,
        u99: k99v * std_u,
    }
}

// Welch-Satterthwaite: ν_eff = u_c^4 / Σ (c_i u_i)^4 / ν_i
// Two-component version
fn ws2(u1: GUMComponent, u2: GUMComponent) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let cu1 = u1.sensitivity * u1.std_u
    let cu2 = u2.sensitivity * u2.std_u
    let u_c_sq = cu1 * cu1 + cu2 * cu2
    let u_c_4 = u_c_sq * u_c_sq
    let t1 = if u1.dof > 1.0e8 { 0.0 } else { cu1 * cu1 * cu1 * cu1 / u1.dof }
    let t2 = if u2.dof > 1.0e8 { 0.0 } else { cu2 * cu2 * cu2 * cu2 / u2.dof }
    let denom = t1 + t2
    if denom < 1.0e-30 { return 1.0e9 }
    gum_min(u_c_4 / denom, 1.0e9)
}

// Combine two GUM components with sensitivity coefficients
pub fn gum_combine2(value: f64, u1: GUMComponent, u2: GUMComponent) -> GUMResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let cu1 = u1.sensitivity * u1.std_u
    let cu2 = u2.sensitivity * u2.std_u
    let std_u = gum_sqrt(cu1 * cu1 + cu2 * cu2)
    let dof = ws2(u1, u2)
    gum_result_from_parts(value, std_u, dof)
}

// Combine three GUM components
pub fn gum_combine3(value: f64, u1: GUMComponent, u2: GUMComponent, u3: GUMComponent) -> GUMResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let cu1 = u1.sensitivity * u1.std_u
    let cu2 = u2.sensitivity * u2.std_u
    let cu3 = u3.sensitivity * u3.std_u
    let std_u = gum_sqrt(cu1*cu1 + cu2*cu2 + cu3*cu3)
    let t1 = if u1.dof > 1.0e8 { 0.0 } else { cu1*cu1*cu1*cu1 / u1.dof }
    let t2 = if u2.dof > 1.0e8 { 0.0 } else { cu2*cu2*cu2*cu2 / u2.dof }
    let t3 = if u3.dof > 1.0e8 { 0.0 } else { cu3*cu3*cu3*cu3 / u3.dof }
    let u_c_sq = cu1*cu1 + cu2*cu2 + cu3*cu3
    let u_c_4 = u_c_sq * u_c_sq
    let denom = t1 + t2 + t3
    let dof = if denom < 1.0e-30 { 1.0e9 } else { gum_min(u_c_4 / denom, 1.0e9) }
    gum_result_from_parts(value, std_u, dof)
}

// ============================================================================
// ARITHMETIC PROPAGATION (standalone GUM-compliant operations)
// ============================================================================

// y = x1 + x2: sensitivities both 1, Var(y) = Var(x1) + Var(x2)
pub fn gum_add(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult) -> GUMResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let u1 = GUMComponent { std_u: x1.std_u, sensitivity: 1.0, dof: x1.dof }
    let u2 = GUMComponent { std_u: x2.std_u, sensitivity: 1.0, dof: x2.dof }
    gum_combine2(x1.value + x2.value, u1, u2)
}

// y = x1 - x2: same variance as addition
pub fn gum_sub(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult) -> GUMResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let u1 = GUMComponent { std_u: x1.std_u, sensitivity: 1.0, dof: x1.dof }
    let u2 = GUMComponent { std_u: x2.std_u, sensitivity: 1.0, dof: x2.dof }
    gum_combine2(x1.value - x2.value, u1, u2)
}

// y = x1 * x2: c1 = |x2|, c2 = |x1| (delta method)
pub fn gum_mul(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult) -> GUMResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let u1 = GUMComponent { std_u: x1.std_u, sensitivity: gum_abs(x2.value), dof: x1.dof }
    let u2 = GUMComponent { std_u: x2.std_u, sensitivity: gum_abs(x1.value), dof: x2.dof }
    gum_combine2(x1.value * x2.value, u1, u2)
}

// y = x1 / x2: c1 = 1/|x2|, c2 = |x1|/x2² (delta method)
pub fn gum_div(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult) -> GUMResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if gum_abs(x2.value) < 1.0e-15 {
        return gum_result_from_parts(0.0, 1.0e308, 1.0)
    }
    let c1 = 1.0 / gum_abs(x2.value)
    let c2 = gum_abs(x1.value) / (x2.value * x2.value)
    let u1 = GUMComponent { std_u: x1.std_u, sensitivity: c1, dof: x1.dof }
    let u2 = GUMComponent { std_u: x2.std_u, sensitivity: c2, dof: x2.dof }
    gum_combine2(x1.value / x2.value, u1, u2)
}

// Scale by constant c: c1 = |c|, Var(c·x) = c²·Var(x)
pub fn gum_scale(x: GUMResult, c: f64) -> GUMResult with Div, Panic {
    gum_result_from_parts(x.value * c, gum_abs(c) * x.std_u, x.dof)
}

// Accessors
pub fn gum_value(r: GUMResult) -> f64 { r.value }
pub fn gum_std_u(r: GUMResult) -> f64 { r.std_u }
pub fn gum_u95(r: GUMResult) -> f64 { r.u95 }
pub fn gum_u99(r: GUMResult) -> f64 { r.u99 }
pub fn gum_dof(r: GUMResult) -> f64 { r.dof }
pub fn gum_k95(r: GUMResult) -> f64 { r.k95 }

pub fn gum_rel_uncertainty(r: GUMResult) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if gum_abs(r.value) < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0 }
    r.std_u / gum_abs(r.value)
}

// Simple constructors
pub fn gum_simple(value: f64, std_u: f64) -> GUMResult with Div, Panic {
    gum_result_from_parts(value, std_u, 1.0e9)
}

// ============================================================================
// BACKWARD-COMPATIBILITY: GUMUncertainty (legacy struct used by some tests)
// ============================================================================

pub struct GUMUncertainty {
    std_uncertainty: f64,
    degrees_of_freedom: f64,
    sensitivity: f64,
}

/// Welch-Satterthwaite for three components (legacy API).
pub fn welch_satterthwaite_3(u1: GUMUncertainty, u2: GUMUncertainty, u3: GUMUncertainty) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let c1 = u1.sensitivity * u1.std_uncertainty
    let c2 = u2.sensitivity * u2.std_uncertainty
    let c3 = u3.sensitivity * u3.std_uncertainty
    let u_c_sq = c1*c1 + c2*c2 + c3*c3
    let u_c_4 = u_c_sq * u_c_sq
    let t1 = if u1.degrees_of_freedom > 1.0e8 { 0.0 } else { c1*c1*c1*c1 / u1.degrees_of_freedom }
    let t2 = if u2.degrees_of_freedom > 1.0e8 { 0.0 } else { c2*c2*c2*c2 / u2.degrees_of_freedom }
    let t3 = if u3.degrees_of_freedom > 1.0e8 { 0.0 } else { c3*c3*c3*c3 / u3.degrees_of_freedom }
    let denom = t1 + t2 + t3
    if denom < 1.0e-30 { return 1.0e9 }
    gum_min(u_c_4 / denom, 1.0e9)
}

/// Coverage factor at 95 %% from effective DOF (legacy API).
pub fn coverage_factor_95(dof: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    t95(dof_to_i64(dof))
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

var CNT: [i64; 2] = [0; 2]

fn chk(label: i64, ok: i64) with IO, Mut {
    if ok == 1 {
        print("  PASS ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[0] = CNT[0] + 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[1] = CNT[1] + 1
    }
}

fn near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> i64 {
    let d = a - b
    let d2 = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    if d2 <= tol { 1 } else { 0 }
}

fn test_components() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Type A: 5 measurements, std_dev = 0.1 → u = 0.1/sqrt(5) ≈ 0.04472, ν = 4
    let a = gum_type_a(0.1, 5)
    chk(1, near(a.std_u, 0.04472135955, 1e-8))
    chk(2, near(a.dof, 4.0, 1e-12))
    chk(3, near(a.sensitivity, 1.0, 1e-12))

    // Type B: std_u = 0.05, ν = ∞
    let b = gum_type_b(0.05)
    chk(4, near(b.std_u, 0.05, 1e-12))
    chk(5, if b.dof > 1.0e8 { 1 } else { 0 })

    // Type B uniform: half_width = 0.1 → u = 0.1/sqrt(3) ≈ 0.05774
    let u = gum_type_b_uniform(0.1)
    chk(6, near(u.std_u, 0.05773502692, 1e-8))
}

fn test_combine() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Two Type B components: u1=0.1, c1=1; u2=0.2, c2=1
    // Combined: u_c = sqrt(0.01 + 0.04) = sqrt(0.05) ≈ 0.22361
    let u1 = gum_type_b(0.1)
    let u2 = gum_type_b(0.2)
    let r = gum_combine2(5.0, u1, u2)
    chk(7, near(r.value, 5.0, 1e-12))
    chk(8, near(r.std_u, 0.2236067977, 1e-8))
    // Both Type B → ν_eff = ∞ → k95 = 1.96
    chk(9, near(r.k95, 1.96, 1e-12))
    chk(10, near(r.u95, 1.96 * 0.2236067977, 1e-6))
}

fn test_welch_satterthwaite() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Type A: n=5 (ν=4), u=0.1; Type B: u=0.05 (ν=∞)
    // Combined variance: 0.01 + 0.0025 = 0.0125 → u_c = sqrt(0.0125) ≈ 0.11180
    // W-S: only Type A contributes to finite dof sum
    // ν_eff ≈ u_c^4 / (0.1^4/4) = 0.01125² / (0.0001/4) = 0.0000125 / 0.000025... let me compute
    let u1 = gum_type_a(0.1, 5)    // std_u=0.04472, ν=4
    let u2 = gum_type_b(0.05)      // std_u=0.05, ν=∞
    let r = gum_combine2(10.0, u1, u2)
    chk(11, near(r.value, 10.0, 1e-12))
    // u_c = sqrt(0.04472² + 0.05²) = sqrt(0.002 + 0.0025) = sqrt(0.0045) ≈ 0.06708
    chk(12, near(r.std_u, 0.067082039, 1e-6))
    // ν_eff ≈ 0.06708^4 / (0.04472^4/4) ≈ large (Type B dominates)
    // With Type B having ∞ dof, ν_eff gets inflated — just check it's > 10
    chk(13, if r.dof > 5.0 { 1 } else { 0 })
}

fn test_arithmetic() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // r1 = 10 ± 0.1, r2 = 5 ± 0.2 (both Type B, ν=∞)
    let r1 = gum_simple(10.0, 0.1)
    let r2 = gum_simple(5.0, 0.2)

    // Add: value=15, u_c=sqrt(0.01+0.04)=sqrt(0.05)≈0.22361
    let s = gum_add(r1, r2)
    chk(14, near(s.value, 15.0, 1e-12))
    chk(15, near(s.std_u, 0.2236067977, 1e-8))

    // Sub: value=5, same u_c
    let d = gum_sub(r1, r2)
    chk(16, near(d.value, 5.0, 1e-12))
    chk(17, near(d.std_u, 0.2236067977, 1e-8))

    // Mul: value=50, c1=|r2|=5, c2=|r1|=10
    // u_c = sqrt(25·0.01 + 100·0.04) = sqrt(0.25 + 4.0) = sqrt(4.25) ≈ 2.0616
    let p = gum_mul(r1, r2)
    chk(18, near(p.value, 50.0, 1e-12))
    chk(19, near(p.std_u, 2.0615528, 1e-5))

    // Div: value=2, c1=1/5=0.2, c2=10/25=0.4
    // u_c = sqrt(0.04·0.01 + 0.16·0.04) = sqrt(0.0004 + 0.0064) = sqrt(0.0068) ≈ 0.08246
    let q = gum_div(r1, r2)
    chk(20, near(q.value, 2.0, 1e-12))
    chk(21, near(q.std_u, 0.08246211, 1e-6))

    // Scale: value=20, u_c=0.2
    let sc = gum_scale(r1, 2.0)
    chk(22, near(sc.value, 20.0, 1e-12))
    chk(23, near(sc.std_u, 0.2, 1e-12))
}

fn test_coverage_factors() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Normal approximation (ν=∞): k95=1.96
    let r = gum_simple(5.0, 1.0)
    chk(24, near(r.k95, 1.96, 1e-12))
    chk(25, near(r.u95, 1.96, 1e-12))

    // Small DoF: Type A n=3 (ν=2), k95=4.303
    let u = gum_type_a(0.1, 3)   // ν=2
    let r2 = gum_combine2(0.0, u, gum_type_b(0.0))
    chk(26, near(r2.k95, 4.303, 1e-3))
}

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    CNT[0] = 0; CNT[1] = 0
    print("─── stdlib/epistemic/gum tests ───\n")
    test_components()
    test_combine()
    test_welch_satterthwaite()
    test_arithmetic()
    test_coverage_factors()
    print("─── "); print(CNT[0]); print("/"); print(CNT[0]+CNT[1]); print(" PASS ───\n")
    if CNT[1] == 0 { print("ALL PASS\n"); 0 } else { 1 }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/gum_supplement1.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/gum_supplement1.sio
// GUM Supplement 1: Propagation of distributions using a Monte Carlo method
//
// Implements multivariate uncertainty propagation with full covariance:
//   Sigma_y = J * Sigma_x * J^T
//
// where J is the Jacobian matrix of partial derivatives.
//
// This extends GUM (JCGM 100:2008) to handle:
//   - Correlated input quantities
//   - Multivariate output quantities
//   - Non-zero off-diagonal covariance terms
//
// The key equation (GUM Supplement 1, Section 7.3):
//   u^2(y) = sum_i sum_j (df/dx_i)(df/dx_j) u(x_i,x_j)
//
// When inputs are uncorrelated, u(x_i,x_j) = 0 for i != j, and this
// reduces to the standard GUM formula.
//
// Reference: JCGM 101:2008

// =============================================================================
// Helper Functions
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    y
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

// =============================================================================
// Upper-Triangular Index (must match covariance.sio)
// =============================================================================

fn tri_index(n: i32, i: i32, j: i32) -> i32 {
    var row = i
    var col = j
    if i > j {
        row = j
        col = i
    }
    return row * n - (row * (row - 1)) / 2 + (col - row)
}

// =============================================================================
// Covariance Matrix Type (mirrors covariance.sio)
// =============================================================================

pub struct CovarianceMatrix {
    pub n: i32,
    pub data: [f64; 300],
}

fn cov_new(n: i32) -> CovarianceMatrix {
    var dim = n
    if dim < 1 { dim = 1 }
    if dim > 24 { dim = 24 }
    return CovarianceMatrix {
        n: dim,
        data: [0.0; 300],
    }
}

fn cov_get(cov: &CovarianceMatrix, i: i32, j: i32) -> f64 {
    if i < 0 { return 0.0 }
    if j < 0 { return 0.0 }
    if i >= cov.n { return 0.0 }
    if j >= cov.n { return 0.0 }
    return cov.data[tri_index(cov.n, i, j)]
}

fn cov_set(cov: &!CovarianceMatrix, i: i32, j: i32, val: f64) {
    if i < 0 { return }
    if j < 0 { return }
    if i >= cov.n { return }
    if j >= cov.n { return }
    cov.data[tri_index(cov.n, i, j)] = val
}

// =============================================================================
// GUM Result Type (mirrors gum.sio)
// =============================================================================

pub struct GUMResult {
    pub value: f64,
    pub std_uncertainty: f64,
    pub degrees_of_freedom: f64,
    pub coverage_factor_95: f64,
    pub expanded_uncertainty_95: f64,
}

// Coverage factor for 95% at infinite DoF (normal distribution)
fn k_normal_95() -> f64 { 1.96 }

fn gum_result_from(value: f64, std_u: f64) -> GUMResult {
    let k = k_normal_95()
    return GUMResult {
        value: value,
        std_uncertainty: abs_f64(std_u),
        degrees_of_freedom: 1.0e9,
        coverage_factor_95: k,
        expanded_uncertainty_95: k * abs_f64(std_u),
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// GUM Multivariate Result
// =============================================================================

// Result of multivariate propagation: scalar output with full covariance info
pub struct GUMMultiResult {
    // Best estimate of the output
    pub value: f64,

    // Combined standard uncertainty u_c(y)
    pub std_uncertainty: f64,

    // Degrees of freedom (infinite for analytic propagation)
    pub degrees_of_freedom: f64,

    // Coverage factor k (95%)
    pub coverage_factor_95: f64,

    // Expanded uncertainty U = k * u_c
    pub expanded_uncertainty_95: f64,

    // Number of input variables
    pub n_inputs: i32,

    // Input covariance matrix (for reference)
    pub input_covariance: CovarianceMatrix,
}

fn gum_multi_result(value: f64, std_u: f64, n_in: i32, cov_x: CovarianceMatrix) -> GUMMultiResult {
    let k = k_normal_95()
    let su = abs_f64(std_u)
    return GUMMultiResult {
        value: value,
        std_uncertainty: su,
        degrees_of_freedom: 1.0e9,
        coverage_factor_95: k,
        expanded_uncertainty_95: k * su,
        n_inputs: n_in,
        input_covariance: cov_x,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Numerical Jacobian Computation
// =============================================================================

// Central difference approximation for df/dx at point x
// df/dx ~ (f(x+h) - f(x-h)) / (2h)
//
// Step size h should be ~ sqrt(epsilon_machine) * |x|
// For f64: epsilon ~ 2.2e-16, so h ~ 1.5e-8 * |x|
pub fn numerical_jacobian_1d(f: fn(f64) -> f64, x: f64, h: f64) -> f64 {
    let step = if abs_f64(h) > 0.0 { abs_f64(h) } else { 1.0e-8 * max_f64(abs_f64(x), 1.0) }
    let f_plus = f(x + step)
    let f_minus = f(x - step)
    return (f_plus - f_minus) / (2.0 * step)
}

// Numerical gradient of f(x1, x2) -> [df/dx1, df/dx2]
pub fn numerical_jacobian_2d(f: fn(f64, f64) -> f64, x1: f64, x2: f64, h: f64) -> [f64; 2] {
    let step = if abs_f64(h) > 0.0 { abs_f64(h) } else { 1.0e-8 }

    // df/dx1 via central difference (hold x2 fixed)
    let h1 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x1), 1.0)
    let df_dx1 = (f(x1 + h1, x2) - f(x1 - h1, x2)) / (2.0 * h1)

    // df/dx2 via central difference (hold x1 fixed)
    let h2 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x2), 1.0)
    let df_dx2 = (f(x1, x2 + h2) - f(x1, x2 - h2)) / (2.0 * h2)

    return [df_dx1, df_dx2]
}

// Numerical gradient of f(x1, x2, x3) -> [df/dx1, df/dx2, df/dx3]
pub fn numerical_jacobian_3d(f: fn(f64, f64, f64) -> f64, x1: f64, x2: f64, x3: f64, h: f64) -> [f64; 3] {
    let step = if abs_f64(h) > 0.0 { abs_f64(h) } else { 1.0e-8 }

    let h1 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x1), 1.0)
    let df_dx1 = (f(x1 + h1, x2, x3) - f(x1 - h1, x2, x3)) / (2.0 * h1)

    let h2 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x2), 1.0)
    let df_dx2 = (f(x1, x2 + h2, x3) - f(x1, x2 - h2, x3)) / (2.0 * h2)

    let h3 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x3), 1.0)
    let df_dx3 = (f(x1, x2, x3 + h3) - f(x1, x2, x3 - h3)) / (2.0 * h3)

    return [df_dx1, df_dx2, df_dx3]
}

// =============================================================================
// 2D Covariance Propagation
// =============================================================================

// Propagate covariance for y = f(x1, x2) with correlated inputs
//
// Var(y) = J * Sigma_x * J^T
//        = (df/dx1)^2 * Var(x1) + (df/dx2)^2 * Var(x2)
//          + 2 * (df/dx1) * (df/dx2) * Cov(x1, x2)
//
// The cross-term 2*(df/dx1)*(df/dx2)*Cov(x1,x2) is what distinguishes
// GUM Supplement 1 from basic GUM propagation.
pub fn propagate_covariance_2d(
    f: fn(f64, f64) -> f64,
    x: [f64; 2],
    cov_x: CovarianceMatrix
) -> GUMMultiResult {
    // Compute function value
    let y_val = f(x[0], x[1])

    // Compute numerical Jacobian
    let jac = numerical_jacobian_2d(f, x[0], x[1], 1.0e-8)

    // Propagate: Var(y) = J * Sigma_x * J^T
    let j0 = jac[0]
    let j1 = jac[1]

    let s00 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 0)
    let s01 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 1)
    let s11 = cov_get(&cov_x, 1, 1)

    let var_y = j0 * j0 * s00 + 2.0 * j0 * j1 * s01 + j1 * j1 * s11

    let std_y = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_multi_result(y_val, std_y, 2, cov_x)
}

// =============================================================================
// 3D Covariance Propagation
// =============================================================================

// Propagate covariance for y = f(x1, x2, x3) with correlated inputs
pub fn propagate_covariance_3d(
    f: fn(f64, f64, f64) -> f64,
    x: [f64; 3],
    cov_x: CovarianceMatrix
) -> GUMMultiResult {
    let y_val = f(x[0], x[1], x[2])

    let jac = numerical_jacobian_3d(f, x[0], x[1], x[2], 1.0e-8)

    let j0 = jac[0]
    let j1 = jac[1]
    let j2 = jac[2]

    let s00 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 0)
    let s01 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 1)
    let s02 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 2)
    let s11 = cov_get(&cov_x, 1, 1)
    let s12 = cov_get(&cov_x, 1, 2)
    let s22 = cov_get(&cov_x, 2, 2)

    let var_y = j0*j0*s00 + j1*j1*s11 + j2*j2*s22
              + 2.0*j0*j1*s01 + 2.0*j0*j2*s02 + 2.0*j1*j2*s12

    let std_y = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_multi_result(y_val, std_y, 3, cov_x)
}

// =============================================================================
// Correlated Operations on GUMResult
// =============================================================================

// Add two correlated measurements: y = x1 + x2
//
// Var(y) = Var(x1) + Var(x2) + 2*rho*sigma_1*sigma_2
//
// When rho = 0: reduces to standard GUM RSS
// When rho = 1: uncertainties add linearly (worst case)
// When rho = -1: uncertainties cancel (best case)
pub fn gum_s1_add_correlated(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> GUMResult {
    let value = x1.value + x2.value

    let u1 = x1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = x2.std_uncertainty

    // Clamp correlation to [-1, 1]
    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 + 2*rho*u1*u2
    let var_y = u1*u1 + u2*u2 + 2.0 * rho * u1 * u2

    // Protect against numerical noise giving negative variance
    let std_u = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))

    return gum_result_from(value, std_u)
}

// Subtract two correlated measurements: y = x1 - x2
//
// Var(y) = Var(x1) + Var(x2) - 2*rho*sigma_1*sigma_2
//
// Note the sign flip vs. addition: positive correlation REDUCES
// uncertainty in subtraction (common-mode rejection).
pub fn gum_s1_sub_correlated(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> GUMResult {
    let value = x1.value - x2.value

    let u1 = x1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = x2.std_uncertainty

    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 - 2*rho*u1*u2
    let var_y = u1*u1 + u2*u2 - 2.0 * rho * u1 * u2

    let std_u = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_result_from(value, std_u)
}

// Multiply two correlated measurements: y = x1 * x2
//
// Using first-order Taylor expansion:
//   dy/dx1 = x2,  dy/dx2 = x1
//   Var(y) = x2^2*Var(x1) + x1^2*Var(x2) + 2*x1*x2*rho*u1*u2
pub fn gum_s1_product_correlated(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> GUMResult {
    let value = x1.value * x2.value

    let u1 = x1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = x2.std_uncertainty
    let v1 = x1.value
    let v2 = x2.value

    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Var(y) = x2^2*u1^2 + x1^2*u2^2 + 2*x1*x2*rho*u1*u2
    let var_y = v2*v2*u1*u1 + v1*v1*u2*u2 + 2.0*v1*v2*rho*u1*u2

    let std_u = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_result_from(value, std_u)
}

// Divide two correlated measurements: y = x1 / x2
//
// Using first-order Taylor expansion:
//   dy/dx1 = 1/x2,  dy/dx2 = -x1/x2^2
//   Var(y) = (1/x2)^2*Var(x1) + (x1/x2^2)^2*Var(x2)
//            + 2*(1/x2)*(-x1/x2^2)*rho*u1*u2
pub fn gum_s1_div_correlated(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> GUMResult {
    if abs_f64(x2.value) < 1.0e-15 {
        return gum_result_from(0.0, 1.0e308)
    }

    let value = x1.value / x2.value

    let u1 = x1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = x2.std_uncertainty
    let v1 = x1.value
    let v2 = x2.value

    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Sensitivity coefficients
    let c1 = 1.0 / v2                   // dy/dx1
    let c2 = 0.0 - v1 / (v2 * v2)       // dy/dx2

    // Var(y) = c1^2*u1^2 + c2^2*u2^2 + 2*c1*c2*rho*u1*u2
    let var_y = c1*c1*u1*u1 + c2*c2*u2*u2 + 2.0*c1*c2*rho*u1*u2

    let std_u = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_result_from(value, std_u)
}

// =============================================================================
// Convenience: Build covariance from two GUMResults + correlation
// =============================================================================

// Create a 2x2 covariance matrix from two GUMResults and their correlation
pub fn cov_from_gum_results_2(r1: GUMResult, r2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> CovarianceMatrix {
    var cov = cov_new(2)

    let u1 = r1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = r2.std_uncertainty

    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Diagonal: variances
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 0, u1 * u1)
    cov_set(&!cov, 1, 1, u2 * u2)

    // Off-diagonal: covariance = rho * u1 * u2
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 1, rho * u1 * u2)

    return cov
}

// Create a 3x3 covariance matrix from three GUMResults and pairwise correlations
pub fn cov_from_gum_results_3(
    r1: GUMResult, r2: GUMResult, r3: GUMResult,
    rho_12: f64, rho_13: f64, rho_23: f64
) -> CovarianceMatrix {
    var cov = cov_new(3)

    let u1 = r1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = r2.std_uncertainty
    let u3 = r3.std_uncertainty

    // Diagonal: variances
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 0, u1 * u1)
    cov_set(&!cov, 1, 1, u2 * u2)
    cov_set(&!cov, 2, 2, u3 * u3)

    // Off-diagonal: covariances
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 1, rho_12 * u1 * u2)
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 2, rho_13 * u1 * u3)
    cov_set(&!cov, 1, 2, rho_23 * u2 * u3)

    return cov
}

// =============================================================================
// Validation: Compare Supplement 1 with basic GUM for uncorrelated case
// =============================================================================

// For uncorrelated inputs, GUM Supplement 1 should reduce to basic GUM.
// This function computes the relative difference between the two approaches.
// A small value (< 1e-6) confirms consistency.
pub fn validate_s1_vs_gum(s1_uncertainty: f64, gum_uncertainty: f64) -> f64 {
    let avg = 0.5 * (abs_f64(s1_uncertainty) + abs_f64(gum_uncertainty))
    if avg < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
    return abs_f64(s1_uncertainty - gum_uncertainty) / avg
}

// =============================================================================
// Effective degrees of freedom for correlated case
// =============================================================================

// Welch-Satterthwaite with correlation (extended form)
// For two correlated inputs:
//   v_eff = u_c^4 / (c1^4*u1^4/v1 + c2^4*u2^4/v2)
//
// Note: The correlation affects u_c but not the W-S denominator
// (which depends on individual contributions, not their correlation).
pub fn welch_satterthwaite_correlated_2(
    u1: f64, dof1: f64, c1: f64,
    u2: f64, dof2: f64, c2: f64,
    correlation: f64
) -> f64 {
    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Combined variance including correlation
    let var_y = c1*c1*u1*u1 + c2*c2*u2*u2 + 2.0*c1*c2*rho*u1*u2
    let u_c_sq = abs_f64(var_y)
    let u_c_4 = u_c_sq * u_c_sq

    // Denominator: sum of (c_i * u_i)^4 / v_i
    let term1 = c1*c1*u1*u1 * c1*c1*u1*u1 / max_f64(dof1, 1.0)
    let term2 = c2*c2*u2*u2 * c2*c2*u2*u2 / max_f64(dof2, 1.0)
    let denom = term1 + term2

    if denom < 1.0e-30 {
        return 1.0e9
    }

    return min_f64(u_c_4 / denom, 1.0e9)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/interval_ieee.sio ===
//! IEEE 1788-2015 Interval Arithmetic Semantics
//!
//! This module aligns Sounio interval arithmetic with IEEE 1788 standard,
//! ensuring reproducibility and well-defined behavior for edge cases.
//!
//! Key IEEE 1788 concepts:
//!   - Empty interval: {} (result of impossible constraints)
//!   - Entire interval: [-∞, +∞] (maximum ignorance)
//!   - Exception handling for division by interval spanning zero
//!   - Decorations for tracking validity
//!
//! References:
//!   - IEEE 1788-2015: "Standard for Interval Arithmetic"
//!   - IEEE 1788.1-2017: "Simplified subset (Level 1)"

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 INTERVAL REPRESENTATION
// ============================================================================

// IEEE 1788 bare interval [a, b]
// Special cases:
//   - Empty: is_empty = true
//   - Entire: lo = -inf, hi = +inf
//   - Point: lo == hi
struct Interval {
    lo: f64,
    hi: f64,
    is_empty: bool,
}

fn interval_empty() -> Interval {
    return Interval {
        lo: 0.0,
        hi: 0.0,
        is_empty: true,
    }
}

fn interval_entire() -> Interval {
    return Interval {
        lo: 0.0 - 1.0e308,
        hi: 1.0e308,
        is_empty: false,
    }
}

fn interval_new(lo: f64, hi: f64) -> Interval {
    if lo > hi {
        // Invalid bounds -> empty
        return interval_empty()
    }
    return Interval {
        lo: lo,
        hi: hi,
        is_empty: false,
    }
}

fn interval_point(x: f64) -> Interval {
    return Interval {
        lo: x,
        hi: x,
        is_empty: false,
    }
}

fn interval_symmetric(center: f64, half_width: f64) -> Interval {
    return interval_new(center - half_width, center + half_width)
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 DECORATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Decorations track interval validity through computations
// Per IEEE 1788 Section 9
// 0 = ill (undefined/invalid)
// 1 = trv (trivial - could be any value)
// 2 = def (defined but possibly unbounded)
// 3 = dac (defined and continuous)
// 4 = com (common - bounded and continuous)
struct Decoration {
    value: i32,
}

fn dec_ill() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 0 } }  // Invalid
fn dec_trv() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 1 } }  // Trivial
fn dec_def() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 2 } }  // Defined
fn dec_dac() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 3 } }  // DAC
fn dec_com() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 4 } }  // Common

// Decorated interval: interval + decoration
struct DecoratedInterval {
    interval: Interval,
    decoration: Decoration,
}

fn decorated_new(interval: Interval, dec: Decoration) -> DecoratedInterval {
    return DecoratedInterval {
        interval: interval,
        decoration: dec,
    }
}

fn decorated_common(lo: f64, hi: f64) -> DecoratedInterval {
    let interval = interval_new(lo, hi)
    if interval.is_empty {
        return DecoratedInterval { interval: interval, decoration: dec_ill() }
    }
    return DecoratedInterval { interval: interval, decoration: dec_com() }
}

// Combine decorations (take minimum)
fn dec_combine(a: Decoration, b: Decoration) -> Decoration {
    if a.value < b.value {
        return a
    }
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 BASIC OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Addition: [a, b] + [c, d] = [a+c, b+d]
fn interval_add(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return interval_empty()
    }
    return interval_new(x.lo + y.lo, x.hi + y.hi)
}

// Subtraction: [a, b] - [c, d] = [a-d, b-c]
fn interval_sub(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return interval_empty()
    }
    return interval_new(x.lo - y.hi, x.hi - y.lo)
}

// Multiplication: [a, b] × [c, d]
fn interval_mul(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return interval_empty()
    }

    // All four products
    let p1 = x.lo * y.lo
    let p2 = x.lo * y.hi
    let p3 = x.hi * y.lo
    let p4 = x.hi * y.hi

    let lo = min_f64(min_f64(p1, p2), min_f64(p3, p4))
    let hi = max_f64(max_f64(p1, p2), max_f64(p3, p4))

    return interval_new(lo, hi)
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 DIVISION: THE CRITICAL OPERATION
// ============================================================================

// Division result with exception handling
struct DivisionResult {
    result: Interval,
    exception: i32,    // 0=none, 1=div_by_zero, 2=entire_result
    decoration: Decoration,
}

// Division: [a, b] / [c, d]
// Per IEEE 1788, division by interval containing zero is well-defined
// but requires careful handling:
//   - If 0 ∈ [c, d]: result may be unbounded or split
//   - If [c, d] = [0, 0]: result is empty (not infinity!)
fn interval_div(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> DivisionResult {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return DivisionResult {
            result: interval_empty(),
            exception: 0,
            decoration: dec_ill(),
        }
    }

    // Check if y contains zero
    let y_contains_zero = y.lo <= 0.0 && y.hi >= 0.0

    if y_contains_zero {
        // Special cases per IEEE 1788
        if y.lo == 0.0 && y.hi == 0.0 {
            // [c, d] = [0, 0]: division by zero interval -> empty
            return DivisionResult {
                result: interval_empty(),
                exception: 1,  // Division by zero
                decoration: dec_ill(),
            }
        }

        if y.lo == 0.0 {
            // [0, d] with d > 0: result is [a/d, +∞] or similar
            if x.lo >= 0.0 {
                return DivisionResult {
                    result: interval_new(x.lo / y.hi, 1.0e308),
                    exception: 2,  // Entire result
                    decoration: dec_def(),
                }
            } else if x.hi <= 0.0 {
                return DivisionResult {
                    result: interval_new(0.0 - 1.0e308, x.hi / y.hi),
                    exception: 2,
                    decoration: dec_def(),
                }
            }
        }

        if y.hi == 0.0 {
            // [c, 0] with c < 0: result is [-∞, a/c] or similar
            if x.lo >= 0.0 {
                return DivisionResult {
                    result: interval_new(0.0 - 1.0e308, x.lo / y.lo),
                    exception: 2,
                    decoration: dec_def(),
                }
            } else if x.hi <= 0.0 {
                return DivisionResult {
                    result: interval_new(x.hi / y.lo, 1.0e308),
                    exception: 2,
                    decoration: dec_def(),
                }
            }
        }

        // General case: 0 strictly inside [c, d]
        // Result is entire (two disconnected pieces reunited)
        return DivisionResult {
            result: interval_entire(),
            exception: 2,
            decoration: dec_trv(),
        }
    }

    // Normal division: 0 ∉ [c, d]
    // [a, b] / [c, d] = [a, b] × [1/d, 1/c]
    let inv_lo = 1.0 / y.hi
    let inv_hi = 1.0 / y.lo

    let p1 = x.lo * inv_lo
    let p2 = x.lo * inv_hi
    let p3 = x.hi * inv_lo
    let p4 = x.hi * inv_hi

    let lo = min_f64(min_f64(p1, p2), min_f64(p3, p4))
    let hi = max_f64(max_f64(p1, p2), max_f64(p3, p4))

    return DivisionResult {
        result: interval_new(lo, hi),
        exception: 0,
        decoration: dec_com(),
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 ELEMENTARY FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Square root: sqrt([a, b])
fn interval_sqrt(x: Interval) -> DecoratedInterval {
    if x.is_empty {
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    if x.hi < 0.0 {
        // Entirely negative -> empty (no real square root)
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    let lo = max_f64(0.0, x.lo)
    return decorated_new(
        interval_new(sqrt_f64(lo), sqrt_f64(x.hi)),
        if x.lo >= 0.0 { dec_com() } else { dec_def() }
    )
}

// Exponential: exp([a, b])
fn interval_exp(x: Interval) -> DecoratedInterval {
    if x.is_empty {
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    // exp is monotonically increasing
    return decorated_new(
        interval_new(exp(x.lo), exp(x.hi)),
        dec_com()
    )
}

// Natural logarithm: log([a, b])
fn interval_log(x: Interval) -> DecoratedInterval {
    if x.is_empty {
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    if x.hi <= 0.0 {
        // Entirely non-positive -> undefined
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    var dec = dec_com()
    var lo_val: f64 = 0.0

    if x.lo <= 0.0 {
        // Interval includes non-positive -> clamp, degrade decoration
        lo_val = 0.0 - 1.0e308  // -infinity for log(0+)
        dec = dec_def()
    } else {
        lo_val = log(x.lo)
    }

    return decorated_new(
        interval_new(lo_val, log(x.hi)),
        dec
    )
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 SET OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Intersection: [a, b] ∩ [c, d]
fn interval_intersect(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return interval_empty()
    }

    let lo = max_f64(x.lo, y.lo)
    let hi = min_f64(x.hi, y.hi)

    if lo > hi {
        return interval_empty()
    }
    return interval_new(lo, hi)
}

// Hull (convex union): hull([a, b], [c, d])
fn interval_hull(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty { return y }
    if y.is_empty { return x }

    return interval_new(
        min_f64(x.lo, y.lo),
        max_f64(x.hi, y.hi)
    )
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 COMPARISONS
// ============================================================================

// Check if interval is subset of another
fn interval_subset(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> bool {
    if x.is_empty { return true }  // Empty is subset of everything
    if y.is_empty { return false } // Non-empty not subset of empty

    return x.lo >= y.lo && x.hi <= y.hi
}

// Check if intervals overlap
fn interval_overlaps(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> bool {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty { return false }

    return x.lo <= y.hi && y.lo <= x.hi
}

// Width of interval
fn interval_width(x: Interval) -> f64 {
    if x.is_empty { return 0.0 }
    return x.hi - x.lo
}

// Midpoint of interval
fn interval_mid(x: Interval) -> f64 {
    if x.is_empty { return 0.0 }
    return (x.lo + x.hi) / 2.0
}

// Radius of interval
fn interval_rad(x: Interval) -> f64 {
    if x.is_empty { return 0.0 }
    return (x.hi - x.lo) / 2.0
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 EXCEPTION HANDLING
// ============================================================================

// Exception flags per IEEE 1788
struct IntervalException {
    undefined_operation: bool,   // e.g., sqrt of negative
    possibly_undefined: bool,    // e.g., sqrt of interval spanning 0
    division_by_zero: bool,
    overflow: bool,
}

fn exception_none() -> IntervalException {
    return IntervalException {
        undefined_operation: false,
        possibly_undefined: false,
        division_by_zero: false,
        overflow: false,
    }
}

fn exception_from_div(result: DivisionResult) -> IntervalException {
    return IntervalException {
        undefined_operation: result.exception == 1,
        possibly_undefined: result.exception == 2,
        division_by_zero: result.exception == 1,
        overflow: false,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_interval_add() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let b = interval_new(3.0, 4.0)
    let c = interval_add(a, b)

    if abs_f64(c.lo - 4.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(c.hi - 6.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_mul() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(-2.0, 3.0)
    let b = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let c = interval_mul(a, b)

    // Products: -2*1=-2, -2*2=-4, 3*1=3, 3*2=6
    // Min = -4, Max = 6
    if abs_f64(c.lo - (0.0 - 4.0)) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(c.hi - 6.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_div_normal() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(2.0, 4.0)
    let b = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let result = interval_div(a, b)

    // [2,4] / [1,2] = [2/2, 4/1] = [1, 4]
    if result.exception != 0 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.result.lo - 1.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.result.hi - 4.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_div_by_zero() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let b = interval_new(0.0, 0.0)
    let result = interval_div(a, b)

    // Division by [0,0] -> empty with exception
    if !result.result.is_empty { return false }
    if result.exception != 1 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_div_spanning_zero() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let b = interval_new(-1.0, 1.0)  // Spans zero
    let result = interval_div(a, b)

    // Should be entire or have exception
    if result.exception != 2 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_sqrt() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(4.0, 9.0)
    let result = interval_sqrt(a)

    if result.interval.is_empty { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.interval.lo - 2.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.interval.hi - 3.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    // Negative interval -> empty
    let b = interval_new(-4.0, -1.0)
    let result2 = interval_sqrt(b)
    if !result2.interval.is_empty { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_decorated_operations() -> bool {
    let a = decorated_common(1.0, 2.0)
    let b = decorated_common(3.0, 4.0)

    if a.decoration.value != 4 { return false }  // com
    if b.decoration.value != 4 { return false }

    return true
}

// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/invariants.sio ===
//! Property-Based Tests for Epistemic Laws
//!
//! These invariants must ALWAYS hold. Violation indicates a bug.
//!
//! Categories:
//!   1. Beta Posterior Laws (Bayesian consistency)
//!   2. GUM Propagation Laws (uncertainty conservation)
//!   3. Entropy Conservation (information theory)
//!   4. Combination Calculus Laws (algebraic identities)
//!   5. Ledger Invariants (entropic accounting)

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// Tolerance for floating point comparisons
fn EPS() -> f64 { return 1.0e-10 }

// ============================================================================
// BETA DISTRIBUTION PROPERTIES
// ============================================================================

struct Beta {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64,
}

fn beta_mean(b: Beta) -> f64 {
    let ba = b.alpha
    let bb = b.beta
    return ba / (ba + bb)
}

fn beta_variance(b: Beta) -> f64 {
    let ba = b.alpha
    let bb = b.beta
    let n = ba + bb
    return (ba * bb) / (n * n * (n + 1.0))
}

// Law 1: Mean must be in [0, 1] for valid Beta
fn law_beta_mean_bounded(b: Beta) -> bool {
    let m = beta_mean(b)
    return m >= 0.0 && m <= 1.0
}

// Law 2: Variance must be positive and bounded
fn law_beta_variance_positive(b: Beta) -> bool {
    let v = beta_variance(b)
    return v > 0.0 && v <= 0.25  // Max variance at Beta(1,1)
}

// Law 3: More observations -> lower variance
fn law_beta_observations_reduce_variance(alpha1: f64, beta1: f64, k: f64) -> bool {
    let a1 = alpha1
    let b1 = beta1
    let k_val = k

    let prior = Beta { alpha: a1, beta: b1 }
    let posterior = Beta { alpha: a1 + k_val, beta: b1 + k_val }

    let v_prior = beta_variance(prior)
    let v_post = beta_variance(posterior)

    return v_post < v_prior  // Variance must decrease
}

// Law 4: Uniform prior is symmetric (Beta(1,1))
fn law_uniform_prior_symmetric() -> bool {
    let uniform = Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
    let m = beta_mean(uniform)
    return abs_f64(m - 0.5) < EPS()
}

// Law 5: After k successes, n-k failures, mean = (1+k)/(2+n)
fn law_beta_posterior_formula(k: i32, n: i32) -> bool {
    let k_f = 0.0 + k
    let n_f = 0.0 + n
    if n < k { return true }  // Invalid input
    if k < 0 { return true }

    let posterior = Beta { alpha: 1.0 + k_f, beta: 1.0 + (n_f - k_f) }
    let expected = (1.0 + k_f) / (2.0 + n_f)
    let actual = beta_mean(posterior)

    return abs_f64(actual - expected) < EPS()
}

// ============================================================================
// GUM PROPAGATION LAWS
// ============================================================================

// GUM uncertainty for y = f(x1, x2) with sensitivities c1, c2
fn gum_combined_uncertainty(u1: f64, u2: f64, c1: f64, c2: f64) -> f64 {
    return sqrt(c1*c1*u1*u1 + c2*c2*u2*u2)
}

// Law 6: Combined uncertainty >= max individual contribution
fn law_gum_uncertainty_additive(u1: f64, u2: f64, c1: f64, c2: f64) -> bool {
    let u1_val = u1
    let u2_val = u2
    let c1_val = c1
    let c2_val = c2

    let u_combined = gum_combined_uncertainty(u1_val, u2_val, c1_val, c2_val)
    let contrib1 = abs_f64(c1_val) * u1_val
    let contrib2 = abs_f64(c2_val) * u2_val
    let max_contrib = max_f64(contrib1, contrib2)

    return u_combined >= max_contrib - EPS()
}

// Law 7: Zero input uncertainty -> zero contribution
fn law_gum_zero_uncertainty_zero_contribution(u1: f64, c1: f64, c2: f64) -> bool {
    let u1_val = u1
    let c1_val = c1
    let c2_val = c2

    // u2 = 0, so contribution from x2 should be 0
    let u_combined = gum_combined_uncertainty(u1_val, 0.0, c1_val, c2_val)
    let u_from_x1_only = abs_f64(c1_val) * u1_val

    return abs_f64(u_combined - u_from_x1_only) < EPS()
}

// Law 8: Zero sensitivity -> zero contribution
fn law_gum_zero_sensitivity_zero_contribution(u1: f64, u2: f64, c1: f64) -> bool {
    let u1_val = u1
    let u2_val = u2
    let c1_val = c1

    // c2 = 0, so x2 doesn't contribute
    let u_combined = gum_combined_uncertainty(u1_val, u2_val, c1_val, 0.0)
    let u_from_x1_only = abs_f64(c1_val) * u1_val

    return abs_f64(u_combined - u_from_x1_only) < EPS()
}

// Law 9: Scaling uncertainty scales output
fn law_gum_scaling(u1: f64, c1: f64, k: f64) -> bool {
    let u1_val = u1
    let c1_val = c1
    let k_val = k

    let u_orig = gum_combined_uncertainty(u1_val, 0.0, c1_val, 0.0)
    let u_scaled = gum_combined_uncertainty(k_val * u1_val, 0.0, c1_val, 0.0)

    return abs_f64(u_scaled - abs_f64(k_val) * u_orig) < EPS()
}

// ============================================================================
// ENTROPY CONSERVATION LAWS
// ============================================================================

// Shannon entropy H(p) = -p log(p) - (1-p) log(1-p)
fn shannon_entropy(p: f64) -> f64 {
    let p_val = p
    if p_val <= 0.0 || p_val >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    let ln2 = 0.693147180559945
    let h = 0.0 - (p_val * log(p_val) + (1.0 - p_val) * log(1.0 - p_val)) / ln2
    return h
}

// Law 10: Entropy is maximized at p = 0.5
fn law_entropy_max_at_half() -> bool {
    let h_half = shannon_entropy(0.5)
    let h_quarter = shannon_entropy(0.25)
    let h_threequarter = shannon_entropy(0.75)

    return h_half > h_quarter && h_half > h_threequarter
}

// Law 11: Entropy is symmetric around 0.5
fn law_entropy_symmetric(p: f64) -> bool {
    let p_val = p
    if p_val < 0.0 || p_val > 1.0 { return true }

    let h_p = shannon_entropy(p_val)
    let h_1mp = shannon_entropy(1.0 - p_val)

    return abs_f64(h_p - h_1mp) < EPS()
}

// Law 12: Entropy is non-negative
fn law_entropy_non_negative(p: f64) -> bool {
    let h = shannon_entropy(p)
    return h >= 0.0 - EPS()
}

// Law 13: Entropy at certainty (p=0 or p=1) is zero
fn law_entropy_zero_at_certainty() -> bool {
    let h0 = shannon_entropy(0.0)
    let h1 = shannon_entropy(1.0)
    return abs_f64(h0) < EPS() && abs_f64(h1) < EPS()
}

// ============================================================================
// COMBINATION CALCULUS LAWS
// ============================================================================

// Law 14: Dempster-Shafer plausibility >= belief
fn law_ds_plausibility_ge_belief(bel_true: f64, pl_true: f64) -> bool {
    return pl_true >= bel_true - EPS()
}

// Law 15: Frechet bounds are valid (P(A AND B) >= max(0, P(A)+P(B)-1))
fn law_frechet_lower_bound(p_a: f64, p_b: f64, p_and: f64) -> bool {
    let pa = p_a
    let pb = p_b
    let pab = p_and

    let lower = max_f64(0.0, pa + pb - 1.0)
    return pab >= lower - EPS()
}

// Law 16: Frechet bounds upper (P(A AND B) <= min(P(A), P(B)))
fn law_frechet_upper_bound(p_a: f64, p_b: f64, p_and: f64) -> bool {
    let pa = p_a
    let pb = p_b
    let pab = p_and

    let upper = min_f64(pa, pb)
    return pab <= upper + EPS()
}

// Law 17: Bayesian update preserves total probability
fn law_bayes_preserves_probability(prior: f64, likelihood_t: f64, likelihood_f: f64) -> bool {
    let pr = prior
    let lt = likelihood_t
    let lf = likelihood_f

    if pr <= 0.0 || pr >= 1.0 { return true }
    if lt < 0.0 || lf < 0.0 { return true }

    // Posterior = P(H|E) = P(E|H)P(H) / P(E)
    // P(E) = P(E|H)P(H) + P(E|not H)P(not H)
    let p_evidence = lt * pr + lf * (1.0 - pr)
    if p_evidence < EPS() { return true }

    let posterior = (lt * pr) / p_evidence

    return posterior >= 0.0 && posterior <= 1.0
}

// ============================================================================
// LEDGER INVARIANTS
// ============================================================================

struct MockLedger {
    total_debt: f64,
    total_credit: f64,
    net_balance: f64,
}

// Law 18: Net balance = debt - credit
fn law_ledger_balance_correct(ledger: MockLedger) -> bool {
    let l = ledger
    let expected = l.total_debt - l.total_credit
    return abs_f64(l.net_balance - expected) < EPS()
}

// Law 19: Debt is non-negative
fn law_ledger_debt_non_negative(ledger: MockLedger) -> bool {
    return ledger.total_debt >= 0.0 - EPS()
}

// Law 20: Credit is non-negative
fn law_ledger_credit_non_negative(ledger: MockLedger) -> bool {
    return ledger.total_credit >= 0.0 - EPS()
}

// Law 21: Debt monotonically increases (or stays same)
fn law_ledger_debt_monotonic(old_debt: f64, new_debt: f64) -> bool {
    return new_debt >= old_debt - EPS()
}

// Law 22: Credit monotonically increases (or stays same)
fn law_ledger_credit_monotonic(old_credit: f64, new_credit: f64) -> bool {
    return new_credit >= old_credit - EPS()
}

// TEST HARNESS
