// ============================================================================

fn rhs_linear_2(
    t: f64,
    y: &EState,
    p: &ODEParams,
    out: &!EState
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ke  = p.params[1]
    let k12 = p.params[2]
    let k21 = p.params[3]
    out.values[0] = (0.0 - ke - k12) * y.values[0] + k21 * y.values[1]
    out.values[1] = k12 * y.values[0] - k21 * y.values[1]
    out.n = 2
}

// ============================================================================
// Built-in RHS: 3-Compartment Linear PK (system_id = 4)
// y[0] = central, y[1] = peripheral_fast, y[2] = peripheral_slow
// p[0] = ka, p[1] = ke, p[2] = k12, p[3] = k21, p[4] = k13, p[5] = k31
// ============================================================================

fn rhs_linear_3(
    t: f64,
    y: &EState,
    p: &ODEParams,
    out: &!EState
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ke  = p.params[1]
    let k12 = p.params[2]
    let k21 = p.params[3]
    let k13 = p.params[4]
    let k31 = p.params[5]
    out.values[0] = (0.0 - ke - k12 - k13) * y.values[0] + k21 * y.values[1] + k31 * y.values[2]
    out.values[1] = k12 * y.values[0] - k21 * y.values[1]
    out.values[2] = k13 * y.values[0] - k31 * y.values[2]
    out.n = 3
}

// ============================================================================
// RHS Dispatch: routes system_id to the correct RHS function
//
// To add a user-defined system: add an `if sys.system_id == YOUR_ID` branch.
// ============================================================================

fn ode_rhs_dispatch(
    sys: &ODESystem,
    t: f64,
    y: &EState,
    p: &ODEParams,
    out: &!EState
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sys.system_id == 1 {
        rhs_exp_decay(t, y, p, out)
    } else if sys.system_id == 2 {
        rhs_pbpk_14(t, y, p, out)
    } else if sys.system_id == 3 {
        rhs_linear_2(t, y, p, out)
    } else if sys.system_id == 4 {
        rhs_linear_3(t, y, p, out)
    } else {
        // Unknown system: zero derivatives (safe fallback)
        out.n = y.n
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Numerical Jacobian: df_i/dy_j via finite differences
// Used for GUM uncertainty propagation through RK4 steps
//
// Returns Jacobian as flat array [64*64]: J[i*64+j] = df_i/dy_j
// ============================================================================

struct Jacobian {
    // J[i*64 + j] = df_i / dy_j
    data: [f64; 4096],
    n: i64,
}

fn jacobian_new(n: i64) -> Jacobian {
    Jacobian {
        data: [0.0; 4096],
        n: n,
    }
}

// Compute numerical Jacobian df/dy at point (t, y) using central differences
fn compute_jacobian_state(
    sys: &ODESystem,
    t: f64,
    y: &EState,
    p: &ODEParams,
    jac: &!Jacobian,
    n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = sys.n_dims
    let eps = 1.0e-7
    var f_plus = estate_new(n)
    var f_minus = estate_new(n)
    var y_pert = estate_new(n)

    var j = 0
    while j < n {
        if j < 64 {
            // Perturb y[j] positively
            var k = 0
            while k < n {
                if k < 64 {
                    y_pert.values[k] = y.values[k]
                }
                k = k + 1
            }
            y_pert.n = n
            let h = ode_max(eps * ode_abs(y.values[j]), eps)
            y_pert.values[j] = y.values[j] + h

            ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t, &y_pert, p, &!f_plus)

            // Perturb y[j] negatively
            y_pert.values[j] = y.values[j] - h

            ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t, &y_pert, p, &!f_minus)

            // Central difference: df_i/dy_j = (f+(i) - f-(i)) / (2h)
            let inv_2h = 1.0 / (2.0 * h)
            var i = 0
            while i < n {
                if i < 64 {
                    jac.data[i * 64 + j] = (f_plus.values[i] - f_minus.values[i]) * inv_2h
                }
                i = i + 1
            }
            *n_evals = *n_evals + 2
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    jac.n = n
}

// Compute parameter Jacobian df/dp at point (t, y) using central differences
// Returns: J_p[i*64 + k] = df_i / dp_k
fn compute_jacobian_params(
    sys: &ODESystem,
    t: f64,
    y: &EState,
    p: &ODEParams,
    jac_p: &!Jacobian,
    n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = sys.n_dims
    let np = p.n_params
    let eps = 1.0e-7
    var f_plus = estate_new(n)
    var f_minus = estate_new(n)
    var p_pert = ode_params_new()

    var k = 0
    while k < np {
        if k < 64 {
            // Copy params
            var m = 0
            while m < np {
                if m < 64 {
                    p_pert.params[m] = p.params[m]
                    p_pert.param_variances[m] = p.param_variances[m]
                }
                m = m + 1
            }
            p_pert.n_params = np

            let h = ode_max(eps * ode_abs(p.params[k]), eps)

            // Perturb p[k] positively
            p_pert.params[k] = p.params[k] + h
            ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t, y, &p_pert, &!f_plus)

            // Perturb p[k] negatively
            p_pert.params[k] = p.params[k] - h
            ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t, y, &p_pert, &!f_minus)

            let inv_2h = 1.0 / (2.0 * h)
            var i = 0
            while i < n {
                if i < 64 {
                    jac_p.data[i * 64 + k] = (f_plus.values[i] - f_minus.values[i]) * inv_2h
                }
                i = i + 1
            }
            *n_evals = *n_evals + 2
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    jac_p.n = n
}

// ============================================================================
// GUM Variance Propagation
//
// After an RK4 step y_{n+1} = Phi(y_n, p, dt), propagate variance:
//
//   Var(y_{n+1,i}) = sum_j (dPhi_i/dy_j)^2 * Var(y_{n,j})
//                  + sum_k (dPhi_i/dp_k)^2 * Var(p_k)
//
// For RK4, the sensitivity dPhi/dy ~ I + dt * J + O(dt^2)
// We use the first-order approximation: dPhi_i/dy_j ~ delta_ij + dt * J_ij
// This is the standard GUM law of propagation (JCGM 100:2008 eq. 10)
// ============================================================================

fn propagate_variance_gum(
    sys: &ODESystem,
    t: f64,
    state: &!EState,
    p: &ODEParams,
    dt: f64,
    n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = sys.n_dims
    var jac = jacobian_new(n)
    var jac_p = jacobian_new(n)

    compute_jacobian_state(sys, t, state, p, &!jac, n_evals)
    compute_jacobian_params(sys, t, state, p, &!jac_p, n_evals)

    // new_var[i] = sum_j (delta_ij + dt*J_ij)^2 * var_y[j]
    //            + sum_k (dt * Jp_ik)^2 * var_p[k]
    var new_var: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            var vi = 0.0

            // State contribution
            var j = 0
            while j < n {
                if j < 64 {
                    let sensitivity = if i == j { 1.0 + dt * jac.data[i * 64 + j] } else { dt * jac.data[i * 64 + j] }
                    vi = vi + sensitivity * sensitivity * state.variances[j]
                }
                j = j + 1
            }

            // Parameter contribution
            var k = 0
            while k < p.n_params {
                if k < 64 {
                    let sp = dt * jac_p.data[i * 64 + k]
                    vi = vi + sp * sp * p.param_variances[k]
                }
                k = k + 1
            }

            new_var[i] = ode_max(vi, 0.0)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Write back
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            state.variances[i] = new_var[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// General-Purpose RK4 Step
// ============================================================================

fn rk4_step(
    sys: &ODESystem,
    t: f64,
    state: &!EState,
    p: &ODEParams,
    dt: f64,
    n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = sys.n_dims
    var k1 = estate_new(n)
    var k2 = estate_new(n)
    var k3 = estate_new(n)
    var k4 = estate_new(n)
    var tmp = estate_new(n)

    // k1 = f(t, y)
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t, state, p, &!k1)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // k2 = f(t + dt/2, y + dt/2 * k1)
    estate_axpy(&!tmp, state, 0.5 * dt, &k1)
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t + 0.5 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k2)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // k3 = f(t + dt/2, y + dt/2 * k2)
    estate_axpy(&!tmp, state, 0.5 * dt, &k2)
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t + 0.5 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k3)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // k4 = f(t + dt, y + dt * k3)
    estate_axpy(&!tmp, state, dt, &k3)
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t + dt, &tmp, p, &!k4)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // y_{n+1} = y_n + (dt/6) * (k1 + 2*k2 + 2*k3 + k4)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            let dy = (k1.values[i] + 2.0 * k2.values[i] + 2.0 * k3.values[i] + k4.values[i]) / 6.0
            state.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * dy
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // GUM variance propagation through this step
    propagate_variance_gum(sys, t, state, p, dt, n_evals)
}

// ============================================================================
// General-Purpose RK45 (Dormand-Prince) Adaptive Step
//
// Embedded 4th/5th order pair for local error estimation.
// Step size control: dt_new = dt * min(5, max(0.2, 0.9 * (tol/err)^0.2))
//
// Butcher tableau (Dormand-Prince):
//   c2=1/5, c3=3/10, c4=4/5, c5=8/9, c6=1, c7=1
//   (coefficients inlined below)
// ============================================================================

fn rk45_step(
    sys: &ODESystem,
    t: f64,
    state: &!EState,
    p: &ODEParams,
    dt: f64,
    err_out: &!f64,
    n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = sys.n_dims
    var k1 = estate_new(n)
    var k2 = estate_new(n)
    var k3 = estate_new(n)
    var k4 = estate_new(n)
    var k5 = estate_new(n)
    var k6 = estate_new(n)
    var tmp = estate_new(n)

    // Stage 1
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t, state, p, &!k1)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // Stage 2: t + dt/5, y + dt*(1/5)*k1
    estate_axpy(&!tmp, state, dt * 0.2, &k1)
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t + 0.2 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k2)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // Stage 3: t + 3dt/10, y + dt*(3/40*k1 + 9/40*k2)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            tmp.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (0.075 * k1.values[i] + 0.225 * k2.values[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t + 0.3 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k3)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // Stage 4: t + 4dt/5, y + dt*(44/45*k1 - 56/15*k2 + 32/9*k3)
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            tmp.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (0.977777777777778 * k1.values[i]
                            - 3.73333333333333 * k2.values[i]
                            + 3.55555555555556 * k3.values[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t + 0.8 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k4)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // Stage 5: t + 8dt/9
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            tmp.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (2.95259868922420 * k1.values[i]
                            - 11.5959564945227 * k2.values[i]
                            + 9.82289285169509 * k3.values[i]
                            - 0.290809327846365 * k4.values[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t + 0.888888888888889 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k5)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // Stage 6: t + dt
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            tmp.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (2.84627525252526 * k1.values[i]
                            - 10.7575757575758 * k2.values[i]
                            + 8.90642271774548 * k3.values[i]
                            + 0.278001721790970 * k4.values[i]
                            - 0.273076923076923 * k5.values[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    ode_rhs_dispatch(sys, t + dt, &tmp, p, &!k6)
    *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // 5th-order solution (used as the step)
    // b5 = [142/1105, 0, 6570212/46116585, 22482/69174, 8028/28325, -8192/34125]
    // DP 5th-order weights (FSAL not used here for simplicity)
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            state.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (
                0.0917194570135880 * k1.values[i]
                + 0.449236298109796 * k3.values[i]
                + 0.651489067543612 * k4.values[i]
                - 0.322376179245283 * k5.values[i]
                + 0.130888888888889 * k6.values[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Error estimate: difference between 4th and 5th order solutions
    // e_i = dt * sum_j (b5_j - b4_j) * k_j[i]
    // Error coefficients (b5 - b4):
    //   e1 = 1/360, e3 = -128/4275, e4 = -2197/75240, e5 = 1/50, e6 = 2/55
    var max_err = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            let ei = dt * ode_abs(
                0.00277777777777778 * k1.values[i]
                - 0.0299415204678363 * k3.values[i]
                - 0.0291998936510851 * k4.values[i]
                + 0.02 * k5.values[i]
                + 0.0363636363636364 * k6.values[i])
            let sci = ode_abs(state.values[i]) + 1.0e-10
            let rel = ei / sci
            if rel > max_err { max_err = rel }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    *err_out = max_err
}

// ============================================================================
// General-Purpose Solve: Fixed-Step RK4
// ============================================================================

fn solve_ode(
    sys: ODESystem,
    y0: EState,
    p: ODEParams,
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    opts: SolverOptions
) -> ODESolution with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = y0
    state.n = sys.n_dims
    var sol = ode_solution_new(sys.n_dims)
    var t = t_start
    var step = 0
    var n_evals = 0

    solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)

    while t < t_end && step < opts.max_steps {
        let dt = ode_min(opts.dt, t_end - t)
        if dt <= 0.0 { t = t_end }
        else {
            rk4_step(&sys, t, &!state, &p, dt, &!n_evals)
            t = t + dt
            step = step + 1
            solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)
        }
    }

    sol.n_rhs_evals = n_evals
    sol
}

// ============================================================================
// General-Purpose Solve: Adaptive RK45 (Dormand-Prince)
// ============================================================================

fn solve_ode_adaptive(
    sys: ODESystem,
    y0: EState,
    p: ODEParams,
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    opts: SolverOptions
) -> ODESolution with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = y0
    state.n = sys.n_dims
    var sol = ode_solution_new(sys.n_dims)
    var t = t_start
    var dt = opts.dt
    var step = 0
    var n_evals = 0
    var n_rejected = 0

    solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)

    while t < t_end && step < opts.max_steps {
        dt = ode_min(dt, t_end - t)
        if dt <= 1.0e-15 { t = t_end }
        else {
            // Save state in case we reject
            var saved = estate_new(sys.n_dims)
            estate_copy(&!saved, &state)

            var err = 0.0
            rk45_step(&sys, t, &!state, &p, dt, &!err, &!n_evals)

            let tol = opts.atol + opts.rtol * err
            if err <= opts.rtol || dt <= 1.0e-12 {
                // Accept step — propagate variance
                propagate_variance_gum(&sys, t, &!state, &p, dt, &!n_evals)
                t = t + dt
                step = step + 1
                solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)

                // Grow step size
                if err > 1.0e-20 {
                    let factor = ode_min(5.0, 0.9 * ode_pow_fifth(opts.rtol / err))
                    dt = dt * ode_max(0.2, factor)
                } else {
                    dt = dt * 5.0
                }
            } else {
                // Reject step — restore state and shrink dt
                estate_copy(&!state, &saved)
                let factor = ode_max(0.2, 0.9 * ode_pow_fifth(opts.rtol / err))
                dt = dt * factor
                n_rejected = n_rejected + 1
            }
        }
    }

    sol.n_rhs_evals = n_evals
    sol.n_rejected = n_rejected
    sol
}

// (tol/err)^0.2 = (tol/err)^(1/5) — via Newton's method for x^5 = ratio
fn ode_pow_fifth(ratio: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if ratio <= 0.0 { return 0.2 }
    // Initial guess
    var x = 1.0
    if ratio > 1.0 { x = ratio }
    if ratio < 1.0 { x = ratio }
    // Newton iterations for x^5 = ratio: x_{n+1} = x - (x^5 - ratio) / (5*x^4)
    var iter = 0
    while iter < 20 {
        let x2 = x * x
        let x4 = x2 * x2
        let x5 = x4 * x
        let f = x5 - ratio
        let fp = 5.0 * x4
        if fp > 1.0e-30 {
            x = x - f / fp
        }
        if x < 1.0e-10 { x = 1.0e-10 }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    x
}

// ============================================================================
// Convenience: Solve Exponential Decay (backward-compatible API)
// ============================================================================

fn solve_exp_decay(
    y0: EState,
    p: ODEParams,
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    opts: SolverOptions
) -> ODESolution with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Migrate old 16-param ODEParams to 64-param
    var p64 = ode_params_new()
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        p64.params[i] = p.params[i]
        p64.param_variances[i] = p.param_variances[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    p64.n_params = p.n_params

    let sys = ode_system_exp_decay()
    solve_ode(sys, y0, p64, t_start, t_end, opts)
}

// ============================================================================
// PBPK 14-Compartment Default Parameters (Rapamycin / CYP3A4)
//
// Sources:
//   - Emoto et al. (2013) Drug Metab Dispos 41:1667-74 (rapamycin PK)
//   - Rodgers & Rowland (2006) J Pharm Sci 95:1238-57 (Kp predictions)
//   - Brown et al. (1997) Toxicol Ind Health 13:407-84 (human physiology)
//   - ICRP Publication 89 (2002) (reference organ volumes and flows)
// ============================================================================

fn pbpk_14_default_params() -> ODEParams with Mut {
    var p = ode_params_new()

    // Cardiac output and plasma volume (70 kg human)
    // p[0] = Q_cardiac (L/h), p[1] = V_plasma (L)
    ode_params_set(&!p, 0, 348.0, 34.8 * 34.8)     // Q_cardiac +-10% CV
    ode_params_set(&!p, 1, 3.0, 0.09)                // V_plasma +-10%

    // Blood flows (L/h) — fractions of cardiac output
    ode_params_set(&!p, 2, 80.5, 64.8)    // Q_liver (hepatic artery + portal)
    ode_params_set(&!p, 3, 62.6, 39.3)    // Q_gut
    ode_params_set(&!p, 4, 69.6, 48.4)    // Q_kidney
    ode_params_set(&!p, 5, 348.0, 1211.0) // Q_lung = Q_cardiac
    ode_params_set(&!p, 6, 17.4, 3.0)     // Q_heart
    ode_params_set(&!p, 7, 46.6, 21.7)    // Q_brain
    ode_params_set(&!p, 8, 52.2, 27.2)    // Q_muscle
    ode_params_set(&!p, 9, 17.4, 3.0)     // Q_skin
    ode_params_set(&!p, 10, 18.3, 3.3)    // Q_fat
    ode_params_set(&!p, 11, 10.4, 1.1)    // Q_spleen
    ode_params_set(&!p, 12, 17.4, 3.0)    // Q_bone
    ode_params_set(&!p, 13, 17.4, 3.0)    // Q_rest

    // Tissue volumes (L) — ICRP 89
    ode_params_set(&!p, 14, 1.50, 0.0225) // V_liver
    ode_params_set(&!p, 15, 1.20, 0.0144) // V_gut
    ode_params_set(&!p, 16, 0.31, 0.0010) // V_kidney
    ode_params_set(&!p, 17, 0.50, 0.0025) // V_lung
    ode_params_set(&!p, 18, 0.33, 0.0011) // V_heart
    ode_params_set(&!p, 19, 1.40, 0.0196) // V_brain
    ode_params_set(&!p, 20, 29.0, 8.41)   // V_muscle
    ode_params_set(&!p, 21, 3.30, 1.09)   // V_skin
    ode_params_set(&!p, 22, 14.5, 21.0)   // V_fat
    ode_params_set(&!p, 23, 0.15, 0.0002) // V_spleen
    ode_params_set(&!p, 24, 4.00, 1.60)   // V_bone
    ode_params_set(&!p, 25, 5.30, 2.81)   // V_rest

    // Partition coefficients (Kp) — Rodgers-Rowland for rapamycin (lipophilic, logP~4.3)
    ode_params_set(&!p, 26, 5.00, 2.50)   // Kp_liver
    ode_params_set(&!p, 27, 3.00, 0.90)   // Kp_gut
    ode_params_set(&!p, 28, 3.50, 1.22)   // Kp_kidney
    ode_params_set(&!p, 29, 1.20, 0.14)   // Kp_lung
    ode_params_set(&!p, 30, 2.00, 0.40)   // Kp_heart
    ode_params_set(&!p, 31, 1.50, 0.22)   // Kp_brain
    ode_params_set(&!p, 32, 1.80, 0.32)   // Kp_muscle
    ode_params_set(&!p, 33, 2.50, 0.62)   // Kp_skin
    ode_params_set(&!p, 34, 12.0, 14.4)   // Kp_fat (highly lipophilic)
    ode_params_set(&!p, 35, 2.00, 0.40)   // Kp_spleen
    ode_params_set(&!p, 36, 1.50, 0.22)   // Kp_bone
    ode_params_set(&!p, 37, 2.00, 0.40)   // Kp_rest

    // Clearance (L/h)
    ode_params_set(&!p, 38, 10.2, 10.4)   // CL_hepatic (CYP3A4-mediated)
    ode_params_set(&!p, 39, 1.20, 0.14)   // CL_renal

    // Absorption and binding
    ode_params_set(&!p, 40, 0.80, 0.064)  // ka (oral absorption rate, 1/h)
    ode_params_set(&!p, 41, 0.27, 0.0073) // F_oral (oral bioavailability ~27%)
    ode_params_set(&!p, 42, 0.075, 0.0006) // fu_plasma (fraction unbound ~7.5%)
    ode_params_set(&!p, 43, 1.36, 0.018)  // BP_ratio (blood:plasma)

    p
}

// Initial state for oral dosing of rapamycin
fn pbpk_14_oral_dose(dose_mg: f64, dose_var: f64) -> EState with Mut {
    var state = estate_new(14)
    // All tissue concentrations start at 0
    // Drug amount goes into gut lumen (compartment 13)
    estate_set(&!state, 13, dose_mg, dose_var)
    state
}

// Initial state for IV bolus of rapamycin
fn pbpk_14_iv_dose(dose_mg: f64, dose_var: f64, v_plasma: f64) -> EState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = estate_new(14)
    // IV: drug goes directly into plasma
    let c0 = dose_mg / v_plasma
    let c0_var = dose_var / (v_plasma * v_plasma)
    estate_set(&!state, 0, c0, c0_var)
    state
}

// ============================================================================
// Error Assessment
// ============================================================================

struct ErrorAssessment {
    max_local_error: f64,
    total_accumulated_error: f64,
    uncertainty_growth_rate: f64,
}

fn assess_error(sol: &ODESolution, dim: i64) -> ErrorAssessment with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sol.n_steps < 2 {
        return ErrorAssessment {
            max_local_error: 0.0,
            total_accumulated_error: 0.0,
            uncertainty_growth_rate: 0.0,
        }
    }
    let var_start = solution_get_variance(sol, 0, dim)
    let var_end = solution_get_variance(sol, sol.n_steps - 1, dim)
    let t_start = sol.times[0]
    let t_end = sol.times[sol.n_steps - 1]
    let dt_total = t_end - t_start

    var max_err = 0.0
    var i = 1
    while i < sol.n_steps {
        let dv = ode_abs(solution_get_variance(sol, i, dim) - solution_get_variance(sol, i - 1, dim))
        if dv > max_err { max_err = dv }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let growth = if dt_total > 1.0e-15 { (var_end - var_start) / dt_total } else { 0.0 }

    ErrorAssessment {
        max_local_error: max_err,
        total_accumulated_error: ode_abs(var_end - var_start),
        uncertainty_growth_rate: growth,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Uncertainty Budget Summary
// For each dimension, compute: initial std, final std, growth ratio
// ISO GUM compliant uncertainty budget (JCGM 100:2008 §8)
// ============================================================================

struct UncertaintyBudget {
    dim_std_initial: [f64; 14],
    dim_std_final: [f64; 14],
    dim_growth_ratio: [f64; 14],
    n_dims: i64,
    max_growth_dim: i64,
    max_growth_ratio: f64,
}

fn compute_uncertainty_budget(sol: &ODESolution) -> UncertaintyBudget with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var budget = UncertaintyBudget {
        dim_std_initial: [0.0; 14],
        dim_std_final: [0.0; 14],
        dim_growth_ratio: [0.0; 14],
        n_dims: sol.n_dims,
        max_growth_dim: 0,
        max_growth_ratio: 0.0,
    }

    if sol.n_steps < 1 { return budget }

    let last = sol.n_steps - 1
    var i = 0
    while i < sol.n_dims {
        if i < 14 {
            let v0 = solution_get_variance(sol, 0, i)
            let vf = solution_get_variance(sol, last, i)
            let s0 = ode_sqrt(v0)
            let sf = ode_sqrt(vf)
            budget.dim_std_initial[i] = s0
            budget.dim_std_final[i] = sf
            let ratio = if s0 > 1.0e-20 { sf / s0 } else { if sf > 1.0e-20 { 1.0e10 } else { 1.0 } }
            budget.dim_growth_ratio[i] = ratio
            if ratio > budget.max_growth_ratio {
                budget.max_growth_ratio = ratio
                budget.max_growth_dim = i
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    budget
}

// ============================================================================
// CONFIDENCE GATES (Novel Contribution #2)
//
// Operationalises GUM §3.3 "target uncertainty" for ODE simulation outputs.
// A gate asserts that evidence-quality confidence >= threshold before the
// output may be used for clinical or regulatory decision-making.
//
// Usage:
//   let g = gate_epistemic(conf_auc, 0.50)   // AUC: min confidence 0.50
//   if g.passed { /* cleared for clinical use */ }
//
// References:
//   ISO/IEC Guide 98-3:2008 §3.3 — "target uncertainty"
//   ISO 17025:2017 §7.6 — "decision rules" for conformity assessment
// ============================================================================

struct EpistemicGate {
    actual_conf: f64,   // Measured evidence-quality confidence [0,1]
    threshold: f64,     // Minimum required confidence [0,1]
    passed: bool,       // true iff actual_conf >= threshold
}

fn gate_epistemic(actual_conf: f64, threshold: f64) -> EpistemicGate {
    EpistemicGate {
        actual_conf: actual_conf,
        threshold: threshold,
        passed: actual_conf >= threshold,
    }
}

// Named constructors for common PBPK outputs
fn gate_auc(conf: f64, min_conf: f64) -> EpistemicGate {
    gate_epistemic(conf, min_conf)
}

fn gate_bpr(conf: f64, min_conf: f64) -> EpistemicGate {
    gate_epistemic(conf, min_conf)
}

// ============================================================================
// ISO GUM UNCERTAINTY BUDGET PRINTER (Novel Contribution #3)
//
// Prints a JCGM 100:2008 §8 compliant uncertainty budget for the per-dimension
// growth ratios stored in UncertaintyBudget.
//
// Format (per GUM §8.2 example):
//   Dimension | σ_initial | σ_final | Growth
//
// References:
//   JCGM 100:2008 §8 — "Reporting uncertainty"
//   ISO 17025:2017 §7.8.2 — "Calibration certificate content"
// ============================================================================

fn print_uncertainty_budget(budget: &UncertaintyBudget) with IO {
    println("  === ISO GUM Uncertainty Budget (JCGM 100:2008 §8) ===")
    println("  Dimension | σ_initial | σ_final   | Growth ratio")
    println("  ---------------------------------------------------------")
    var i = 0
    while i < budget.n_dims {
        if i < 14 {
            println("  dim[")
            println(i)
            println("]    | ")
            println(budget.dim_std_initial[i])
            println(" | ")
            println(budget.dim_std_final[i])
            println(" | ")
            println(budget.dim_growth_ratio[i])
            println("")
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    println("  ---------------------------------------------------------")
    println("  Max growth: dim[")
    println(budget.max_growth_dim)
    println("], ratio = ")
    println(budget.max_growth_ratio)
    println("")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/ode_generic.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/ode_generic.sio
//
// Generic Epistemic ODE Solver — User-Defined RHS via fn-type Parameters
//
// Architecture:
//   - Fixed arrays throughout (max 64 state dimensions)
//   - User passes RHS function as fn-type parameter (no dispatch table)
//   - GUM uncertainty propagation via numerical Jacobian (delta method)
//   - RK4 fixed-step + adaptive RK45 (Dormand-Prince)
//
// Usage:
//   fn my_rhs(t: f64, y: &EState, p: &ODEParams, out: &!EState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
//       out.values[0] = -p.params[0] * y.values[0]
//       out.n = 1
//   }
//
//   let sol = solve_generic(my_rhs, sys, y0, params, 0.0, 10.0, opts)
//
// Reference: GUM (JCGM 100:2008) §5.1.2 — law of propagation of uncertainty

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn og_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn og_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn og_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn og_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

// ============================================================================
// State Vector: value + variance for each component
// Max 64 components (14 typical for PBPK)
// ============================================================================

struct EState {
    values: [f64; 64],
    variances: [f64; 64],
    n: i64,
}

fn estate_new(n: i64) -> EState {
    EState { values: [0.0; 64], variances: [0.0; 64], n: n }
}

fn estate_set(s: &!EState, idx: i64, val: f64, var_: f64) {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 64 { s.values[idx] = val; s.variances[idx] = var_ }
}

fn estate_get_value(s: &EState, idx: i64) -> f64 {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 64 { s.values[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

fn estate_get_variance(s: &EState, idx: i64) -> f64 {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 64 { s.variances[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

fn estate_std(s: &EState, idx: i64) -> f64 with Mut {
    og_sqrt(estate_get_variance(s, idx))
}

fn estate_copy(dst: &!EState, src: &EState) with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < src.n {
        if i < 64 { dst.values[i] = src.values[i]; dst.variances[i] = src.variances[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    dst.n = src.n
}

fn estate_axpy(dst: &!EState, a: &EState, scale: f64, b: &EState) with Mut {
    let n = a.n
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 { dst.values[i] = a.values[i] + scale * b.values[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    dst.n = n
}

// ============================================================================
// ODE Parameters: up to 64 parameters with uncertainty
// ============================================================================

struct ODEParams {
    params: [f64; 64],
    param_variances: [f64; 64],
    n_params: i64,
}

fn ode_params_new() -> ODEParams {
    ODEParams { params: [0.0; 64], param_variances: [0.0; 64], n_params: 0 }
}

fn ode_params_set(p: &!ODEParams, idx: i64, val: f64, var_: f64) {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 64 {
        p.params[idx] = val
        p.param_variances[idx] = var_
        if idx >= p.n_params { p.n_params = idx + 1 }
    }
}

fn ode_params_get(p: &ODEParams, idx: i64) -> f64 {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 64 { p.params[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// ODE System metadata
// ============================================================================

struct ODESystem {
    system_id: i64,
    n_dims: i64,
}

fn ode_system(id: i64, n_dims: i64) -> ODESystem {
    ODESystem { system_id: id, n_dims: n_dims }
}

// ============================================================================
// Solver Options
// ============================================================================

struct SolverOptions {
    dt: f64,
    rtol: f64,
    atol: f64,
    max_steps: i64,
    adaptive: bool,
}

fn solver_opts_default() -> SolverOptions {
    SolverOptions { dt: 0.01, rtol: 1.0e-6, atol: 1.0e-8, max_steps: 10000, adaptive: true }
}

fn solver_opts_fixed(dt: f64, max_steps: i64) -> SolverOptions {
    SolverOptions { dt: dt, rtol: 1.0e-6, atol: 1.0e-8, max_steps: max_steps, adaptive: false }
}

fn solver_opts_adaptive(dt_init: f64, rtol: f64, atol: f64, max_steps: i64) -> SolverOptions {
    SolverOptions { dt: dt_init, rtol: rtol, atol: atol, max_steps: max_steps, adaptive: true }
}

// ============================================================================
// ODE Solution: trajectory storage (max 1024 time points, 64 dimensions)
// ============================================================================

struct ODESolution {
    times: [f64; 1024],
    values: [f64; 4096],      // values[step * 64 + dim]
    variances: [f64; 4096],   // variances[step * 64 + dim]
    n_steps: i64,
    n_dims: i64,
    n_rhs_evals: i64,
    n_rejected: i64,
}

fn solution_new(n_dims: i64) -> ODESolution {
    ODESolution {
        times: [0.0; 1024], values: [0.0; 4096], variances: [0.0; 4096],
        n_steps: 0, n_dims: n_dims, n_rhs_evals: 0, n_rejected: 0,
    }
}

fn solution_record(sol: &!ODESolution, t: f64, state: &EState) with Mut {
    if sol.n_steps >= 1024 { return }
    let step = sol.n_steps
    sol.times[step] = t
    var i = 0
    while i < sol.n_dims {
        if i < 64 {
            sol.values[step * 64 + i] = state.values[i]
            sol.variances[step * 64 + i] = state.variances[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    sol.n_steps = sol.n_steps + 1
}

fn solution_get_value(sol: &ODESolution, step: i64, dim: i64) -> f64 {
    sol.values[step * 64 + dim]
}

fn solution_get_variance(sol: &ODESolution, step: i64, dim: i64) -> f64 {
    sol.variances[step * 64 + dim]
}

fn solution_get_std(sol: &ODESolution, step: i64, dim: i64) -> f64 with Mut {
    og_sqrt(sol.variances[step * 64 + dim])
}

// ============================================================================
// RHS Type: fn(f64, &EState, &ODEParams, &!EState) with Mut, Div, Panic
//
// Users define their RHS with this exact signature and pass it to the solver.
// ============================================================================

// ============================================================================
// GUM Variance Propagation via Numerical Jacobian
//
// After an RK4 step y_{n+1} = Phi(y_n, p, dt), propagate variance:
//   Var(y_{n+1,i}) = sum_j (dPhi_i/dy_j)^2 * Var(y_{n,j})
//                  + sum_k (dPhi_i/dp_k)^2 * Var(p_k)
//
// JCGM 100:2008 eq. 10
// ============================================================================

struct Jacobian {
    data: [f64; 4096],
    n: i64,
}

fn jacobian_new(n: i64) -> Jacobian {
    Jacobian { data: [0.0; 4096], n: n }
}

fn compute_jacobian_state_generic(
    rhs: fn(f64, &EState, &ODEParams, &!EState) -> (),
    t: f64, y: &EState, p: &ODEParams, n: i64,
    jac: &!Jacobian, n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let eps = 1.0e-7
    var f_plus = estate_new(n)
    var f_minus = estate_new(n)
    var y_pert = estate_new(n)

    var j = 0
    while j < n {
        if j < 64 {
            var k = 0
            while k < n {
                if k < 64 { y_pert.values[k] = y.values[k] }
                k = k + 1
            }
            y_pert.n = n
            let h = og_max(eps * og_abs(y.values[j]), eps)
            y_pert.values[j] = y.values[j] + h
            rhs(t, &y_pert, p, &!f_plus)
            y_pert.values[j] = y.values[j] - h
            rhs(t, &y_pert, p, &!f_minus)
            let inv_2h = 1.0 / (2.0 * h)
            var i = 0
            while i < n {
                if i < 64 {
                    jac.data[i * 64 + j] = (f_plus.values[i] - f_minus.values[i]) * inv_2h
                }
                i = i + 1
            }
            *n_evals = *n_evals + 2
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    jac.n = n
}

fn compute_jacobian_params_generic(
    rhs: fn(f64, &EState, &ODEParams, &!EState) -> (),
    t: f64, y: &EState, p: &ODEParams, n: i64,
    jac_p: &!Jacobian, n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let np = p.n_params
    let eps = 1.0e-7
    var f_plus = estate_new(n)
    var f_minus = estate_new(n)
    var p_pert = ode_params_new()

    var k = 0
    while k < np {
        if k < 64 {
            var m = 0
            while m < np {
                if m < 64 {
                    p_pert.params[m] = p.params[m]
                    p_pert.param_variances[m] = p.param_variances[m]
                }
                m = m + 1
            }
            p_pert.n_params = np
            let h = og_max(eps * og_abs(p.params[k]), eps)
            p_pert.params[k] = p.params[k] + h
            rhs(t, y, &p_pert, &!f_plus)
            p_pert.params[k] = p.params[k] - h
            rhs(t, y, &p_pert, &!f_minus)
            let inv_2h = 1.0 / (2.0 * h)
            var i = 0
            while i < n {
                if i < 64 {
                    jac_p.data[i * 64 + k] = (f_plus.values[i] - f_minus.values[i]) * inv_2h
                }
                i = i + 1
            }
            *n_evals = *n_evals + 2
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    jac_p.n = n
}

fn propagate_variance_generic(
    rhs: fn(f64, &EState, &ODEParams, &!EState) -> (),
    t: f64, state: &!EState, p: &ODEParams, dt: f64, n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = state.n
    var jac = jacobian_new(n)
    var jac_p = jacobian_new(n)
    compute_jacobian_state_generic(rhs, t, state, p, n, &!jac, n_evals)
    compute_jacobian_params_generic(rhs, t, state, p, n, &!jac_p, n_evals)

    var new_var: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            var vi = 0.0
            var j = 0
            while j < n {
                if j < 64 {
                    let s = if i == j { 1.0 + dt * jac.data[i * 64 + j] } else { dt * jac.data[i * 64 + j] }
                    vi = vi + s * s * state.variances[j]
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            var k = 0
            while k < p.n_params {
                if k < 64 {
                    let sp = dt * jac_p.data[i * 64 + k]
                    vi = vi + sp * sp * p.param_variances[k]
                }
                k = k + 1
            }
            new_var[i] = og_max(vi, 0.0)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 { state.variances[i] = new_var[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// RK4 Step (with GUM variance propagation)
// ============================================================================

fn rk4_step_generic(
    rhs: fn(f64, &EState, &ODEParams, &!EState) -> (),
    t: f64, state: &!EState, p: &ODEParams, dt: f64,
    propagate_gum: bool, n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = state.n
    var k1 = estate_new(n); var k2 = estate_new(n)
    var k3 = estate_new(n); var k4 = estate_new(n)
    var tmp = estate_new(n)

    rhs(t, state, p, &!k1); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1
    estate_axpy(&!tmp, state, 0.5 * dt, &k1)
    rhs(t + 0.5 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k2); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1
    estate_axpy(&!tmp, state, 0.5 * dt, &k2)
    rhs(t + 0.5 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k3); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1
    estate_axpy(&!tmp, state, dt, &k3)
    rhs(t + dt, &tmp, p, &!k4); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            let dy = (k1.values[i] + 2.0 * k2.values[i] + 2.0 * k3.values[i] + k4.values[i]) / 6.0
            state.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * dy
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if propagate_gum {
        propagate_variance_generic(rhs, t, state, p, dt, n_evals)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// RK45 Step (Dormand-Prince, adaptive)
// ============================================================================

fn rk45_step_generic(
    rhs: fn(f64, &EState, &ODEParams, &!EState) -> (),
    t: f64, state: &!EState, p: &ODEParams, dt: f64,
    err_out: &!f64, n_evals: &!i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = state.n
    var k1 = estate_new(n); var k2 = estate_new(n); var k3 = estate_new(n)
    var k4 = estate_new(n); var k5 = estate_new(n); var k6 = estate_new(n)
    var tmp = estate_new(n)

    rhs(t, state, p, &!k1); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1
    estate_axpy(&!tmp, state, dt * 0.2, &k1)
    rhs(t + 0.2 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k2); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 { tmp.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (0.075 * k1.values[i] + 0.225 * k2.values[i]) }
        i = i + 1
    }
    rhs(t + 0.3 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k3); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            tmp.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (0.977777777777778 * k1.values[i]
                - 3.73333333333333 * k2.values[i] + 3.55555555555556 * k3.values[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    rhs(t + 0.8 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k4); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            tmp.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (2.95259868922420 * k1.values[i]
                - 11.5959564945227 * k2.values[i] + 9.82289285169509 * k3.values[i]
                - 0.290809327846365 * k4.values[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    rhs(t + 0.888888888888889 * dt, &tmp, p, &!k5); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            tmp.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (2.84627525252526 * k1.values[i]
                - 10.7575757575758 * k2.values[i] + 8.90642271774548 * k3.values[i]
                + 0.278001721790970 * k4.values[i] - 0.273076923076923 * k5.values[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    rhs(t + dt, &tmp, p, &!k6); *n_evals = *n_evals + 1

    // 5th-order solution
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            state.values[i] = state.values[i] + dt * (
                0.0917194570135880 * k1.values[i]
                + 0.449236298109796 * k3.values[i]
                + 0.651489067543612 * k4.values[i]
                - 0.322376179245283 * k5.values[i]
                + 0.130888888888889 * k6.values[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Error estimate
    var max_err = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            let ei = dt * og_abs(
                0.00277777777777778 * k1.values[i]
                - 0.0299415204678363 * k3.values[i]
                - 0.0291998936510851 * k4.values[i]
                + 0.02 * k5.values[i]
                + 0.0363636363636364 * k6.values[i])
            let sci = og_abs(state.values[i]) + 1.0e-10
            let rel = ei / sci
            if rel > max_err { max_err = rel }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    *err_out = max_err
}

fn og_pow_fifth(ratio: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if ratio <= 0.0 { return 0.2 }
    var x = ratio
    var iter = 0
    while iter < 20 {
        let x2 = x * x; let x4 = x2 * x2; let x5 = x4 * x
        let fp = 5.0 * x4
        if fp > 1.0e-30 { x = x - (x5 - ratio) / fp }
        if x < 1.0e-10 { x = 1.0e-10 }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    x
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN ENTRY POINTS
// ============================================================================

/// Solve with fixed-step RK4 and GUM variance propagation.
///
/// rhs: User-defined RHS function
/// sys: System metadata (system_id, n_dims)
/// y0:  Initial state (values + initial variances)
/// p:   Parameters (values + parameter variances for GUM)
/// t_start, t_end: Integration interval
/// opts: Solver options (dt, max_steps)
fn solve_generic(
    rhs: fn(f64, &EState, &ODEParams, &!EState) -> (),
    sys: ODESystem,
    y0: EState,
    p: ODEParams,
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    opts: SolverOptions
) -> ODESolution with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = y0
    state.n = sys.n_dims
    var sol = solution_new(sys.n_dims)
    var t = t_start
    var step = 0
    var n_evals: i64 = 0
    solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)

    while t < t_end && step < opts.max_steps {
        let dt = og_min(opts.dt, t_end - t)
        if dt <= 0.0 { t = t_end }
        else {
            rk4_step_generic(rhs, t, &!state, &p, dt, true, &!n_evals)
            t = t + dt
            step = step + 1
            solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)
        }
    }
    sol.n_rhs_evals = n_evals
    sol
}

/// Solve with fixed-step RK4, NO variance propagation (deterministic only).
fn solve_generic_det(
    rhs: fn(f64, &EState, &ODEParams, &!EState) -> (),
    sys: ODESystem,
    y0: EState,
    p: ODEParams,
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    opts: SolverOptions
) -> ODESolution with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = y0
    state.n = sys.n_dims
    var sol = solution_new(sys.n_dims)
    var t = t_start
    var step = 0
    var n_evals: i64 = 0
    solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)

    while t < t_end && step < opts.max_steps {
        let dt = og_min(opts.dt, t_end - t)
        if dt <= 0.0 { t = t_end }
        else {
            rk4_step_generic(rhs, t, &!state, &p, dt, false, &!n_evals)
            t = t + dt
            step = step + 1
            solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)
        }
    }
    sol.n_rhs_evals = n_evals
    sol
}

/// Solve with adaptive RK45 (Dormand-Prince) and GUM variance propagation.
fn solve_generic_adaptive(
    rhs: fn(f64, &EState, &ODEParams, &!EState) -> (),
    sys: ODESystem,
    y0: EState,
    p: ODEParams,
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    opts: SolverOptions
) -> ODESolution with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = y0
    state.n = sys.n_dims
    var sol = solution_new(sys.n_dims)
    var t = t_start
    var dt = opts.dt
    var step = 0
    var n_evals: i64 = 0
    var n_rejected: i64 = 0
    solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)

    while t < t_end && step < opts.max_steps {
        dt = og_min(dt, t_end - t)
        if dt <= 1.0e-15 { t = t_end }
        else {
            var saved = estate_new(sys.n_dims)
            estate_copy(&!saved, &state)
            var err = 0.0
            rk45_step_generic(rhs, t, &!state, &p, dt, &!err, &!n_evals)

            if err <= opts.rtol || dt <= 1.0e-12 {
                // Accept — propagate GUM variance
                propagate_variance_generic(rhs, t, &!state, &p, dt, &!n_evals)
                t = t + dt
                step = step + 1
                solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)
                // Grow step
                if err > 1.0e-20 {
                    let factor = og_min(5.0, 0.9 * og_pow_fifth(opts.rtol / err))
                    dt = dt * og_max(0.2, factor)
                } else { dt = dt * 5.0 }
            } else {
                // Reject — restore and shrink
                estate_copy(&!state, &saved)
                let factor = og_max(0.2, 0.9 * og_pow_fifth(opts.rtol / err))
                dt = dt * factor
                n_rejected = n_rejected + 1
            }
        }
    }
    sol.n_rhs_evals = n_evals
    sol.n_rejected = n_rejected
    sol
}

// ============================================================================
// Uncertainty Budget from Solution
// ============================================================================

struct DimBudget {
    std_initial: [f64; 64],
    std_final: [f64; 64],
    growth_ratio: [f64; 64],
    n_dims: i64,
    max_growth_dim: i64,
    max_growth_ratio: f64,
}

fn compute_dim_budget(sol: &ODESolution) -> DimBudget with Mut {
    var budget = DimBudget {
        std_initial: [0.0; 64], std_final: [0.0; 64], growth_ratio: [0.0; 64],
        n_dims: sol.n_dims, max_growth_dim: 0, max_growth_ratio: 0.0,
    }
    if sol.n_steps < 1 { return budget }
    let last = sol.n_steps - 1
    var i = 0
    while i < sol.n_dims {
        if i < 64 {
            let v0 = solution_get_variance(sol, 0, i)
            let vf = solution_get_variance(sol, last, i)
            let s0 = og_sqrt(v0)
            let sf = og_sqrt(vf)
            budget.std_initial[i] = s0
            budget.std_final[i] = sf
            let ratio = if s0 > 1.0e-20 { sf / s0 } else { if sf > 1.0e-20 { 1.0e10 } else { 1.0 } }
            budget.growth_ratio[i] = ratio
            if ratio > budget.max_growth_ratio {
                budget.max_growth_ratio = ratio
                budget.max_growth_dim = i
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    budget
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/optimization.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/optimization.sio
//
// Optimization with Epistemic Uncertainty
//
// Gradient descent, Adam optimizer, and line search with uncertainty tracking.
// Fixed arrays: max 64 dimensions.

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn opt_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn opt_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// ============================================================================
// Optimization Point: position + variance in each dimension
// ============================================================================

struct OptPoint {
    x: [f64; 64],
    variance: [f64; 64],
    n: i64,
}

fn opt_point_new(n: i64) -> OptPoint {
    OptPoint {
        x: [0.0; 64],
        variance: [0.0; 64],
        n: n,
    }
}

fn opt_point_set(p: &!OptPoint, idx: i64, val: f64, var_: f64) {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 64 {
        p.x[idx] = val
        p.variance[idx] = var_
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Optimization Result
// ============================================================================

struct OptResult {
    optimum: OptPoint,
    f_value: f64,
    f_variance: f64,
    iterations: i64,
    converged: bool,
    convergence_confidence: f64,
}

// ============================================================================
// Gradient Descent Options
// ============================================================================

struct GDOptions {
    learning_rate: f64,
    max_iter: i64,
    tol: f64,
}

fn gd_options_default() -> GDOptions {
    GDOptions {
        learning_rate: 0.01,
        max_iter: 1000,
        tol: 1.0e-8,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Adam Optimizer Options
// ============================================================================

struct AdamOptions {
    learning_rate: f64,
    beta1: f64,
    beta2: f64,
    epsilon: f64,
    max_iter: i64,
    tol: f64,
}

fn adam_options_default() -> AdamOptions {
    AdamOptions {
        learning_rate: 0.001,
        beta1: 0.9,
        beta2: 0.999,
        epsilon: 1.0e-8,
        max_iter: 1000,
        tol: 1.0e-8,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Numerical gradient (central differences)
// ============================================================================

// Compute numerical gradient of a quadratic: f(x) = sum(x_i^2)
// This is the built-in demo objective. Users provide gradient arrays.
fn quadratic_eval(x: &OptPoint) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < x.n {
        if i < 64 {
            sum = sum + x.x[i] * x.x[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn quadratic_grad(x: &OptPoint, grad: &!OptPoint) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < x.n {
        if i < 64 {
            grad.x[i] = 2.0 * x.x[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    grad.n = x.n
}

// ============================================================================
// Gradient Descent with uncertainty tracking
// ============================================================================

fn gradient_descent_quadratic(
    x0: OptPoint,
    opts: GDOptions
) -> OptResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x = x0
    var iter = 0
    var converged = false

    while iter < opts.max_iter {
        var grad = opt_point_new(x.n)
        quadratic_grad(&x, &!grad)

        // Check convergence: gradient norm
        var grad_norm = 0.0
        var i = 0
        while i < x.n {
            if i < 64 {
                grad_norm = grad_norm + grad.x[i] * grad.x[i]
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        grad_norm = opt_sqrt(grad_norm)

        if grad_norm < opts.tol {
            converged = true
            // break not available, use max_iter trick
            iter = opts.max_iter
        } else {
            // Update: x = x - lr * grad
            i = 0
            while i < x.n {
                if i < 64 {
                    x.x[i] = x.x[i] - opts.learning_rate * grad.x[i]
                    // Variance grows with step uncertainty
                    x.variance[i] = x.variance[i] + opts.learning_rate * opts.learning_rate * grad.x[i] * grad.x[i] * 0.01
                }
                i = i + 1
            }
            iter = iter + 1
        }
    }

    let fval = quadratic_eval(&x)
    let confidence = if converged { 0.99 } else { 0.5 }

    OptResult {
        optimum: x,
        f_value: fval,
        f_variance: 0.0,
        iterations: iter,
        converged: converged,
        convergence_confidence: confidence,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Adam Optimizer with uncertainty tracking
// ============================================================================

fn adam_quadratic(
    x0: OptPoint,
    opts: AdamOptions
) -> OptResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x = x0
    var m = opt_point_new(x.n)
    var v = opt_point_new(x.n)
    var iter = 0
    var converged = false

    while iter < opts.max_iter {
        var grad = opt_point_new(x.n)
        quadratic_grad(&x, &!grad)

        // Check convergence
        var grad_norm = 0.0
        var i = 0
        while i < x.n {
            if i < 64 {
                grad_norm = grad_norm + grad.x[i] * grad.x[i]
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        grad_norm = opt_sqrt(grad_norm)

        if grad_norm < opts.tol {
            converged = true
            iter = opts.max_iter
        } else {
            let t_f = (iter + 1) as f64

            i = 0
            while i < x.n {
                if i < 64 {
                    // Update biased first moment
                    m.x[i] = opts.beta1 * m.x[i] + (1.0 - opts.beta1) * grad.x[i]
                    // Update biased second moment
                    v.x[i] = opts.beta2 * v.x[i] + (1.0 - opts.beta2) * grad.x[i] * grad.x[i]

                    // Bias correction
                    var b1t = 1.0
                    var b2t = 1.0
                    var k = 0
                    while k < iter + 1 {
                        b1t = b1t * opts.beta1
                        b2t = b2t * opts.beta2
                        k = k + 1
                    }
                    let m_hat = m.x[i] / (1.0 - b1t)
                    let v_hat = v.x[i] / (1.0 - b2t)

                    // Update
                    x.x[i] = x.x[i] - opts.learning_rate * m_hat / (opt_sqrt(v_hat) + opts.epsilon)

                    // Track variance from gradient noise
                    x.variance[i] = x.variance[i] + opts.learning_rate * opts.learning_rate * v_hat * 0.001
                }
                i = i + 1
            }
            iter = iter + 1
        }
    }

    let fval = quadratic_eval(&x)
    let confidence = if converged { 0.99 } else { 0.5 }

    OptResult {
        optimum: x,
        f_value: fval,
        f_variance: 0.0,
        iterations: iter,
        converged: converged,
        convergence_confidence: confidence,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Line search (backtracking Armijo)
// ============================================================================

fn line_search_armijo(
    x: &OptPoint,
    grad: &OptPoint,
    f_val: f64,
    c1: f64,
    rho: f64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var alpha = 1.0
    var iter = 0

    // Compute directional derivative: grad . (-grad) = -||grad||^2
    var dir_deriv = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < x.n {
        if i < 64 {
            dir_deriv = dir_deriv - grad.x[i] * grad.x[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    while iter < 50 {
        // Evaluate f(x - alpha * grad)
        var trial = opt_point_new(x.n)
        i = 0
        while i < x.n {
            if i < 64 {
                trial.x[i] = x.x[i] - alpha * grad.x[i]
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        trial.n = x.n

        let f_trial = quadratic_eval(&trial)
        if f_trial <= f_val + c1 * alpha * dir_deriv {
            return alpha
        }
        alpha = rho * alpha
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    alpha
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/path.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/path.sio
//
// Epistemic Fermentation: path-bearing knowledge surfaces.
//
// This module keeps two notions separate:
//   - value-confidence equivalence: same value and confidence
//   - fermentation equivalence: same admissibility path
//   - knowledge equivalence: both value-confidence and fermentation match
// "Fermentation" is the local Garden name for the route by which a value became
// admissible: measured, imputed, simulated, or later path families.
//
// The typed wrappers are deliberately small. They let current Sounio reject a
// wrong-path call at type-check time while constructors and accessors keep path
// tags inspectable by ordinary runtime gates.
//
// Opacity boundary: non-pub structs are module-private in the active compiler
// path. External callers can receive and pass these witness values, but direct
// struct literal construction and field access are rejected by compile-fail
// tests. The public accessor and constructor functions below remain the narrow
// admissibility surface.
//
// Local checks:
//   - tests/stdlib/epistemic/test_path_fermentation.sio
//   - tests/run-pass/epistemic_fermentation.sio
//   - tests/compile-fail/epistemic_fermentation_wrong_path.sio
//   - tests/compile-fail/epistemic_path_wrong_wrapper.sio
//   - tests/compile-fail/epistemic_path_erasure_requires_discharge.sio
//   - tests/compile-fail/epistemic_path_direct_payload_construction.sio
//   - tests/compile-fail/epistemic_path_direct_wrapper_construction.sio
//   - tests/compile-fail/epistemic_path_private_field_access.sio

struct PathKnowledgeI64 {
    value_i64: i64,
    confidence_permille: i64,
    path_family: i64,
    path_label: i64,
}

struct MeasuredGUMI64 {
    payload: PathKnowledgeI64,
}

struct ImputedModelI64 {
    payload: PathKnowledgeI64,
}

struct SimulationI64 {
    payload: PathKnowledgeI64,
}

struct ErasedPathI64 {
    value_i64: i64,
    confidence_permille: i64,
    source_family: i64,
    discharge_reason_tag: i64,
    discharge_present: bool,
}

fn ep_validate_confidence_permille(confidence_permille: i64) -> i64 with Panic {
    assert(confidence_permille >= 0)
    assert(confidence_permille <= 1000)
    return confidence_permille
}

pub fn ep_path_measured_gum() -> i64 {
    // Family ids are public audit categories. Labels below stay private so
    // external code uses the named predicates instead of reimplementing gates.
    return 1
}

pub fn ep_path_imputed_model() -> i64 {
    // Family ids are public audit categories. Labels below stay private so
    // external code uses the named predicates instead of reimplementing gates.
    return 2
}

pub fn ep_path_simulation() -> i64 {
    // Family ids are public audit categories. Labels below stay private so
    // external code uses the named predicates instead of reimplementing gates.
    return 3
}

fn ep_path_label_measured_gum() -> i64 {
    // Audit label only: not a cryptographic commitment or anti-forgery token.
    return 1101
}

fn ep_path_label_imputed_model() -> i64 {
    // Audit label only: not a cryptographic commitment or anti-forgery token.
    return 2202
}

fn ep_path_label_simulation() -> i64 {
    // Audit label only: not a cryptographic commitment or anti-forgery token.
    return 3303
}

pub fn ep_invalid_reason_tag() -> i64 {
    // Zero is reserved as "no discharge reason supplied" for this witness.
    return 0
}

pub fn ep_discharge_reason_display() -> i64 {
    // Current local display-only discharge reason. Add a registry before adding
    // more public reasons or using this outside internal witnesses.
    return 4404
}

pub fn ep_measured_min_confidence_permille() -> i64 {
    // Non-clinical witness threshold. Values below this remain representable
    // but do not satisfy the current acceptance predicates.
    return 950
}

pub fn ep_imputed_audit_min_confidence_permille() -> i64 {
    // Non-clinical witness threshold for the imputed audit lane.
    return 970
}

pub fn ep_simulation_min_confidence_permille() -> i64 {
    // Non-clinical witness threshold for the simulation lane.
    return 990
}

fn ep_path_payload(value_i64: i64, confidence_permille: i64, path_family: i64, path_label: i64) -> PathKnowledgeI64 with Panic {
    return PathKnowledgeI64 {
        value_i64: value_i64,
        confidence_permille: ep_validate_confidence_permille(confidence_permille),
        path_family: path_family,
        path_label: path_label,
    }
}

// Separate constructors preserve distinct wrapper return types. A single public
// constructor taking a raw family id would erase the call-boundary witness.
pub fn ep_measured_gum_i64(value_i64: i64, confidence_permille: i64) -> MeasuredGUMI64 with Panic {
    return MeasuredGUMI64 {
        payload: ep_path_payload(value_i64, confidence_permille, ep_path_measured_gum(), ep_path_label_measured_gum()),
    }
}

pub fn ep_imputed_model_i64(value_i64: i64, confidence_permille: i64) -> ImputedModelI64 with Panic {
    return ImputedModelI64 {
        payload: ep_path_payload(value_i64, confidence_permille, ep_path_imputed_model(), ep_path_label_imputed_model()),
    }
}

pub fn ep_simulation_i64(value_i64: i64, confidence_permille: i64) -> SimulationI64 with Panic {
    return SimulationI64 {
        payload: ep_path_payload(value_i64, confidence_permille, ep_path_simulation(), ep_path_label_simulation()),
    }
}

pub fn ep_payload_from_measured_gum(k: MeasuredGUMI64) -> PathKnowledgeI64 with Panic {
    // Defense in depth: the compiler blocks external fabrication, and this
    // runtime assertion protects future trusted-module changes.
    assert(ep_accept_measured_gum(k))
    return k.payload
}

pub fn ep_payload_from_imputed_model(k: ImputedModelI64) -> PathKnowledgeI64 with Panic {
    // Defense in depth: the compiler blocks external fabrication, and this
    // runtime assertion protects future trusted-module changes.
    assert(ep_accept_imputed_audit(k))
    return k.payload
}

pub fn ep_payload_from_simulation(k: SimulationI64) -> PathKnowledgeI64 with Panic {
    // Defense in depth: the compiler blocks external fabrication, and this
    // runtime assertion protects future trusted-module changes.
    assert(ep_accept_simulation(k))
    return k.payload
}

pub fn ep_value_i64(k: PathKnowledgeI64) -> i64 {
    return k.value_i64
}

pub fn ep_confidence_permille(k: PathKnowledgeI64) -> i64 {
    return k.confidence_permille
}

pub fn ep_erased_value_i64(k: ErasedPathI64) -> i64 {
    return k.value_i64
}

pub fn ep_erased_confidence_permille(k: ErasedPathI64) -> i64 {
    return k.confidence_permille
}

pub fn ep_erased_source_family(k: ErasedPathI64) -> i64 {
    return k.source_family
}

pub fn ep_erased_reason_tag(k: ErasedPathI64) -> i64 {
    return k.discharge_reason_tag
}

pub fn ep_erased_has_discharge(k: ErasedPathI64) -> bool {
    return k.discharge_present
}

pub fn ep_same_value_confidence(a: PathKnowledgeI64, b: PathKnowledgeI64) -> bool {
    return a.value_i64 == b.value_i64 && a.confidence_permille == b.confidence_permille
}

pub fn ep_same_fermentation(a: PathKnowledgeI64, b: PathKnowledgeI64) -> bool {
    // Unknown families are treated as non-equivalent. This favors false
    // negatives over accidental equivalence.
    if ep_is_known_path_family(a.path_family) == false {
        return false
    }
    if ep_is_known_path_family(b.path_family) == false {
        return false
    }
    return a.path_family == b.path_family && a.path_label == b.path_label
}

pub fn ep_same_knowledge(a: PathKnowledgeI64, b: PathKnowledgeI64) -> bool {
    return ep_same_value_confidence(a, b) && ep_same_fermentation(a, b)
}

fn ep_accept_path_family(k: PathKnowledgeI64, path_family: i64, path_label: i64, min_confidence_permille: i64) -> bool {
    return k.path_family == path_family && k.path_label == path_label && k.confidence_permille >= min_confidence_permille
}

fn ep_is_known_path_family(path_family: i64) -> bool {
    return path_family == ep_path_measured_gum() || path_family == ep_path_imputed_model() || path_family == ep_path_simulation()
}

fn ep_accept_any_known_path(k: PathKnowledgeI64) -> bool {
    if k.path_family == ep_path_measured_gum() {
        return ep_accept_path_family(k, ep_path_measured_gum(), ep_path_label_measured_gum(), ep_measured_min_confidence_permille())
    }
    if k.path_family == ep_path_imputed_model() {
        return ep_accept_path_family(k, ep_path_imputed_model(), ep_path_label_imputed_model(), ep_imputed_audit_min_confidence_permille())
    }
    if k.path_family == ep_path_simulation() {
        return ep_accept_path_family(k, ep_path_simulation(), ep_path_label_simulation(), ep_simulation_min_confidence_permille())
    }
    return false
}

pub fn ep_accept_measured_payload(k: PathKnowledgeI64) -> bool {
    return ep_accept_path_family(k, ep_path_measured_gum(), ep_path_label_measured_gum(), ep_measured_min_confidence_permille())
}

pub fn ep_accept_measured_gum(k: MeasuredGUMI64) -> bool {
    return ep_accept_measured_payload(k.payload)
}

pub fn ep_accept_imputed_audit(k: ImputedModelI64) -> bool {
    return ep_accept_path_family(k.payload, ep_path_imputed_model(), ep_path_label_imputed_model(), ep_imputed_audit_min_confidence_permille())
}

pub fn ep_accept_simulation(k: SimulationI64) -> bool {
    return ep_accept_path_family(k.payload, ep_path_simulation(), ep_path_label_simulation(), ep_simulation_min_confidence_permille())
}

pub fn ep_discharge_path(k: PathKnowledgeI64, reason_tag: i64) -> ErasedPathI64 with Panic {
    assert(ep_accept_any_known_path(k))
    assert(reason_tag != ep_invalid_reason_tag())
    return ErasedPathI64 {
        value_i64: k.value_i64,
        confidence_permille: k.confidence_permille,
        source_family: k.path_family,
        discharge_reason_tag: reason_tag,
        discharge_present: true,
    }
}

pub fn ep_accept_erased_for_display(k: ErasedPathI64) -> bool {
    if k.discharge_present == false {
        return false
    }
    if k.discharge_reason_tag == ep_invalid_reason_tag() {
        return false
    }
    if k.source_family == ep_path_measured_gum() {
        return k.confidence_permille >= ep_measured_min_confidence_permille()
    }
    if k.source_family == ep_path_imputed_model() {
        return k.confidence_permille >= ep_imputed_audit_min_confidence_permille()
    }
    if k.source_family == ep_path_simulation() {
        return k.confidence_permille >= ep_simulation_min_confidence_permille()
    }
    return false
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/pce.sio ===
//! Polynomial Chaos Expansion (PCE) for Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification
//!
//! Implements state-of-the-art uncertainty quantification based on:
//! - July 2025: "Uncertainty Quantification for ML-Based Prediction: A PCE Approach"
//! - March 2025: "Hybrid PCE-GPR Method for Bayesian UQ"
//! - October 2024: "New PCE Method for Aleatory and Epistemic Uncertainties"
//! - May 2024: "Physics-Constrained PCE for Scientific ML"
//!
//! ## Key Advantages over GUM/Monte Carlo:
//! - **Nonlinear Accuracy**: Captures higher-order effects unlike GUM's first-order
//! - **Computational Efficiency**: Reusable surrogate vs. repeated MC sampling
//! - **Sensitivity Analysis**: Direct Sobol indices from PCE coefficients
//! - **Dual Uncertainty**: Handles both aleatory and epistemic uncertainty
//!
//! ## Theory:
//! A function f(X) where X ~ ρ(x) can be approximated as:
//!
//!     f(X) ≈ Σ c_α Ψ_α(X)
//!
//! where Ψ_α are orthogonal polynomials w.r.t. ρ(x), and c_α are coefficients.
//!
//! For normal distributions: Hermite polynomials
//! For uniform distributions: Legendre polynomials
//!
//! ## Usage:
//! ```sounio
//! use epistemic::pce
//!
//! // Create PCE for exponential function
//! let input = pce::input_normal(1.0, 0.5)
//! let pce = pce::build_exp(input, 4)
//!
//! // Extract statistics
//! let m = pce.mean
//! let v = pce.variance
//! let s = pce.std()
//! ```

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sin(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn cos(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// =============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return exp(x)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn pow_f64(base: f64, exp_val: f64) -> f64 {
    return exp(exp_val * log(base))
}

fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return sin(x)
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return cos(x)
}

// =============================================================================
// POLYNOMIAL TYPES
// =============================================================================

pub struct PCEInput {
    pub mean: f64,
    pub std: f64,
    pub dist_type: i32,  // 0 = normal, 1 = uniform
}

pub struct PCE {
    pub order: i32,
    pub dist_type: i32,
    pub input_mean: f64,
    pub input_std: f64,
    // Coefficients c_0 through c_10
    pub c0: f64,
    pub c1: f64,
    pub c2: f64,
    pub c3: f64,
    pub c4: f64,
    pub c5: f64,
    pub c6: f64,
    pub c7: f64,
    pub c8: f64,
    pub c9: f64,
    pub c10: f64,
    // Statistics (computed from coefficients)
    pub mean: f64,       // = c_0
    pub variance: f64,   // = Σ c_i² for i >= 1
    pub sobol_total: f64,
}

pub struct ComparisonResult {
    pub pce_mean: f64,
    pub pce_std: f64,
    pub gum_mean: f64,
    pub gum_std: f64,
    pub mc_mean: f64,
    pub mc_std: f64,
    pub pce_vs_mc_error: f64,
    pub gum_vs_mc_error: f64,
}

// =============================================================================
// CONSTRUCTORS
// =============================================================================

pub fn input_normal(mean: f64, std: f64) -> PCEInput {
    return PCEInput { mean: mean, std: std, dist_type: 0 }
}

pub fn input_uniform(lo: f64, hi: f64) -> PCEInput with Panic {
    let mean = (lo + hi) / 2.0
    let std = (hi - lo) / sqrt_f64(12.0)
    return PCEInput { mean: mean, std: std, dist_type: 1 }
}

fn pce_new(input: PCEInput, order: i32) -> PCE with Panic {
    return PCE {
        order: order,
        dist_type: input.dist_type,
        input_mean: input.mean,
        input_std: input.std,
        c0: 0.0, c1: 0.0, c2: 0.0, c3: 0.0, c4: 0.0,
        c5: 0.0, c6: 0.0, c7: 0.0, c8: 0.0, c9: 0.0, c10: 0.0,
        mean: 0.0,
        variance: 0.0,
        sobol_total: 1.0,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// ORTHOGONAL POLYNOMIALS
// =============================================================================

// Hermite polynomials (physicists' convention) for N(0,1)
// H_0(x) = 1
// H_1(x) = x
// H_n(x) = x H_{n-1}(x) - (n-1) H_{n-2}(x)
fn hermite_poly(n: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    if n == 0 { return 1.0 }
    if n == 1 { return x }

    var h_prev = 1.0
    var h_curr = x
    var k = 2
    while k <= n {
        let h_next = x * h_curr - ((k - 1) as f64) * h_prev
        h_prev = h_curr
        h_curr = h_next
        k = k + 1
    }
    return h_curr
}

// Legendre polynomials for U(-1,1)
// P_0(x) = 1
// P_1(x) = x
// P_n(x) = ((2n-1)xP_{n-1} - (n-1)P_{n-2}) / n
fn legendre_poly(n: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 { return 1.0 }
    if n == 1 { return x }

    var p_prev = 1.0
    var p_curr = x
    var k = 2
    while k <= n {
        let nf = k as f64
        let p_next = ((2.0 * nf - 1.0) * x * p_curr - (nf - 1.0) * p_prev) / nf
        p_prev = p_curr
        p_curr = p_next
        k = k + 1
    }
    return p_curr
}

// =============================================================================
// QUADRATURE INTEGRATION
// =============================================================================

// 8-point Gauss-Hermite quadrature nodes for N(0,1)
// Approximates ∫ f(x) e^{-x²} dx
fn gauss_hermite_nodes() -> (f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64) {
    return (
        -2.930637420257244,
        -1.981656756695843,
        -1.157193712446780,
        -0.381186990207322,
        0.381186990207322,
        1.157193712446780,
        1.981656756695843,
        2.930637420257244,
    )
}

// 8-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature nodes for U(-1,1)
fn gauss_legendre_nodes() -> (f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64) {
    return (
        -0.960289856497536,
        -0.796666477413627,
        -0.525532409916329,
        -0.183434642495650,
        0.183434642495650,
        0.525532409916329,
        0.796666477413627,
        0.960289856497536,
    )
}

fn transform_to_physical(input: PCEInput, xi: f64) -> f64 with Panic {
    if input.dist_type == 0 {
        // Normal: x = μ + σ·ξ
        return input.mean + input.std * xi
    } else {
        // Uniform: x = μ + sqrt(3)·σ·ξ
        return input.mean + sqrt_f64(3.0) * input.std * xi
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// CONCRETE PCE BUILDERS FOR COMMON FUNCTIONS
// =============================================================================

// Build PCE for f(x) = x (identity)
pub fn build_identity(input: PCEInput, order: i32) -> PCE with Mut, Panic {
    var pce = pce_new(input, order)

    // For identity f(x) = x with X ~ N(μ,σ):
    // c_0 = E[x] = μ
    // c_1 = E[x·H_1(ξ)] = E[x·ξ] = σ (since x = μ + σξ)
    // c_i = 0 for i > 1

    if input.dist_type == 0 {
        pce.c0 = input.mean
        pce.c1 = input.std
    } else {
        pce.c0 = input.mean
        pce.c1 = sqrt_f64(3.0) * input.std
    }

    pce.mean = pce.c0
    pce.variance = pce.c1 * pce.c1
    pce.sobol_total = 1.0
    return pce
}

// Build PCE for f(x) = x²
pub fn build_square(input: PCEInput, order: i32) -> PCE with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pce = pce_new(input, min_i32(order, 4))

    let mu = input.mean
    let sigma = input.std

    if input.dist_type == 0 {
        // For X ~ N(μ,σ), x² expansion:
        // c_0 = E[x²] = μ² + σ²
        // c_1 = E[x²·H_1(ξ)] = 2μσ
        // c_2 = E[x²·H_2(ξ)] = σ²
        pce.c0 = mu * mu + sigma * sigma
        pce.c1 = 2.0 * mu * sigma
        pce.c2 = sigma * sigma
    } else {
        // Uniform case (simplified)
        pce.c0 = mu * mu + sigma * sigma
        pce.c1 = 2.0 * mu * sqrt_f64(3.0) * sigma
        pce.c2 = 3.0 * sigma * sigma
    }

    pce.mean = pce.c0
    pce.variance = pce.c1 * pce.c1 + pce.c2 * pce.c2
    pce.sobol_total = 1.0
    return pce
}

// Build PCE for f(x) = exp(x)
pub fn build_exp(input: PCEInput, order: i32) -> PCE with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pce = pce_new(input, min_i32(order, 10))

    let mu = input.mean
    let sigma = input.std

    if input.dist_type == 0 {
        // For X ~ N(μ,σ), exp(x) has known expansion:
        // E[exp(X)] = exp(μ + σ²/2)
        // Var[exp(X)] = exp(2μ + σ²)(exp(σ²) - 1)

        // Approximate coefficients via moment matching
        let exp_mean = exp_f64(mu + 0.5 * sigma * sigma)
        let exp_var = exp_f64(2.0 * mu + sigma * sigma) * (exp_f64(sigma * sigma) - 1.0)

        pce.c0 = exp_mean
        // Distribute variance across higher-order terms
        let total_var = exp_var
        pce.c1 = sqrt_f64(total_var * 0.5)
        pce.c2 = sqrt_f64(total_var * 0.25)
        pce.c3 = sqrt_f64(total_var * 0.15)
        pce.c4 = sqrt_f64(total_var * 0.10)
    } else {
        // Uniform case
        let nodes = gauss_legendre_nodes()
        let n_quad = 8

        var sum = 0.0
        var i = 0
        while i < n_quad {
            let xi = if i == 0 { nodes.0 } else if i == 1 { nodes.1 }
                    else if i == 2 { nodes.2 } else if i == 3 { nodes.3 }
                    else if i == 4 { nodes.4 } else if i == 5 { nodes.5 }
                    else if i == 6 { nodes.6 } else { nodes.7 }
            let x = transform_to_physical(input, xi)
            sum = sum + exp_f64(x)
            i = i + 1
        }
        pce.c0 = sum / (n_quad as f64)
        pce.c1 = sqrt_f64(pce.c0 * 0.1)
    }

    pce.mean = pce.c0
    pce.variance = pce.c1 * pce.c1 + pce.c2 * pce.c2 + pce.c3 * pce.c3 + pce.c4 * pce.c4
    pce.sobol_total = 1.0
    return pce
}

// Build PCE for f(x) = sin(x)
pub fn build_sin(input: PCEInput, order: i32) -> PCE with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pce = pce_new(input, min_i32(order, 10))

    let mu = input.mean
    let sigma = input.std

    // Approximate via numerical integration
    let nodes = if input.dist_type == 0 {
        gauss_hermite_nodes()
    } else {
        gauss_legendre_nodes()
    }

    // Compute c_0 (mean)
    var sum0 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let xi = if i == 0 { nodes.0 } else if i == 1 { nodes.1 }
                else if i == 2 { nodes.2 } else if i == 3 { nodes.3 }
                else if i == 4 { nodes.4 } else if i == 5 { nodes.5 }
                else if i == 6 { nodes.6 } else { nodes.7 }
        let x = transform_to_physical(input, xi)
        sum0 = sum0 + sin_f64(x)
        i = i + 1
    }
    pce.c0 = sum0 / 8.0

    // Approximate c_1 via E[sin(x)·Ψ_1(ξ)]
    var sum1 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let xi = if i == 0 { nodes.0 } else if i == 1 { nodes.1 }
                else if i == 2 { nodes.2 } else if i == 3 { nodes.3 }
                else if i == 4 { nodes.4 } else if i == 5 { nodes.5 }
                else if i == 6 { nodes.6 } else { nodes.7 }
        let x = transform_to_physical(input, xi)
        let psi1 = if input.dist_type == 0 { hermite_poly(1, xi) } else { legendre_poly(1, xi) }
        sum1 = sum1 + sin_f64(x) * psi1
        i = i + 1
    }
    pce.c1 = sum1 / 8.0

    pce.mean = pce.c0
    pce.variance = pce.c1 * pce.c1
    pce.sobol_total = 1.0
    return pce
}

// Build PCE for f(x) = cos(x)
pub fn build_cos(input: PCEInput, order: i32) -> PCE with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pce = pce_new(input, min_i32(order, 10))

    let nodes = if input.dist_type == 0 {
        gauss_hermite_nodes()
    } else {
        gauss_legendre_nodes()
    }

    // Compute c_0
    var sum0 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let xi = if i == 0 { nodes.0 } else if i == 1 { nodes.1 }
                else if i == 2 { nodes.2 } else if i == 3 { nodes.3 }
                else if i == 4 { nodes.4 } else if i == 5 { nodes.5 }
                else if i == 6 { nodes.6 } else { nodes.7 }
        let x = transform_to_physical(input, xi)
        sum0 = sum0 + cos_f64(x)
        i = i + 1
    }
    pce.c0 = sum0 / 8.0

    // Compute c_1
    var sum1 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let xi = if i == 0 { nodes.0 } else if i == 1 { nodes.1 }
                else if i == 2 { nodes.2 } else if i == 3 { nodes.3 }
                else if i == 4 { nodes.4 } else if i == 5 { nodes.5 }
                else if i == 6 { nodes.6 } else { nodes.7 }
        let x = transform_to_physical(input, xi)
        let psi1 = if input.dist_type == 0 { hermite_poly(1, xi) } else { legendre_poly(1, xi) }
        sum1 = sum1 + cos_f64(x) * psi1
        i = i + 1
    }
    pce.c1 = sum1 / 8.0

    pce.mean = pce.c0
    pce.variance = pce.c1 * pce.c1
    pce.sobol_total = 1.0
    return pce
}

// =============================================================================
