// === FILE: stdlib/genomics/alignment.sio ===
//! stdlib/genomics/alignment (disabled — pending parser support)


// === FILE: stdlib/genomics/core.sio ===
// stdlib/genomics/core.sio — DNA sequence operations
//
// Base encoding: A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3 (GF(4) field elements)
// Sequences stored as [i32; 256] arrays.
//
// NOTE: Uses return-by-value structs to work around the JIT &! reference
// visibility limitation (mutations through exclusive refs not reflected
// in caller in Cranelift JIT mode).
//
// API:
//   dna_complement        — complement a single base
//   dna_complement_seq    — complement a full sequence (returns Seq256)
//   dna_reverse_complement — reverse complement (returns Seq256)
//   dna_gc_content        — fraction of G+C bases
//   dna_hamming           — Hamming distance between two sequences
//   dna_align_score       — simple alignment score (match/mismatch)
//   codon_to_aa           — translate a codon (3 bases) to amino acid index
//   dna_translate         — translate a sequence to amino acids (returns AA64)
//   dna_kmer_count        — count k-mers (k<=4, returns Kmer256)
//   ascii_to_base         — convert ASCII character to base index
//
// References:
//   - Lesk (2014): Introduction to Genomics, 3rd ed.
//   - Needleman & Wunsch (1970): A general method applicable to the search
//     for similarities in the amino acid sequence of two proteins.

// ============================================================================
// Return-value wrappers (avoids JIT &! bug)
// ============================================================================

struct Seq256 {
    data: [i32; 256],
    len: i32,
}

struct AA64 {
    data: [i32; 64],
    n: i32,
}

struct Kmer256 {
    counts: [i32; 256],
    k: i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// Base constants
// ============================================================================

fn base_A() -> i32 { 0 }
fn base_C() -> i32 { 1 }
fn base_G() -> i32 { 2 }
fn base_T() -> i32 { 3 }

// ============================================================================
// Math helpers
// ============================================================================

fn core_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn core_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// ============================================================================
// Single-base complement
// A<->T (0<->3), C<->G (1<->2)
// ============================================================================

fn dna_complement(base: i32) -> i32 {
    if base == 0 { return 3 }  // A -> T
    if base == 1 { return 2 }  // C -> G
    if base == 2 { return 1 }  // G -> C
    if base == 3 { return 0 }  // T -> A
    base                        // unknown: identity
}

// ============================================================================
// Complement of a full sequence — returns Seq256
// ============================================================================

fn dna_complement_seq(seq: &[i32; 256], seq_len: i32) -> Seq256 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out = Seq256 { data: [0; 256], len: seq_len }
    var i = 0
    while i < seq_len {
        out.data[i] = dna_complement(seq[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    out
}

// ============================================================================
// Reverse complement — returns Seq256
// ============================================================================

fn dna_reverse_complement(seq: &[i32; 256], seq_len: i32) -> Seq256 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out = Seq256 { data: [0; 256], len: seq_len }
    var i = 0
    while i < seq_len {
        out.data[i] = dna_complement(seq[seq_len - 1 - i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    out
}

// ============================================================================
// GC content: fraction of bases that are G or C
// Returns value in [0.0, 1.0]
// ============================================================================

fn dna_gc_content(seq: &[i32; 256], seq_len: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if seq_len <= 0 { return 0.0 }
    var gc = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < seq_len {
        let b = seq[i]
        if b == base_C() { gc = gc + 1 }
        if b == base_G() { gc = gc + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    (gc as f64) / (seq_len as f64)
}

// ============================================================================
// Hamming distance (equal-length sequences)
// Returns number of positions where bases differ.
// ============================================================================

fn dna_hamming(a: &[i32; 256], b: &[i32; 256], len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var dist = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < len {
        if a[i] != b[i] { dist = dist + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    dist
}

// ============================================================================
// Alignment score — simple scoring without gaps
// match_score: reward for identical bases
// mismatch_penalty: penalty (positive number, subtracted) for differences
// ============================================================================

fn dna_align_score(
    a: &[i32; 256],
    b: &[i32; 256],
    len: i32,
    match_score: i32,
    mismatch_penalty: i32,
) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var score = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < len {
        if a[i] == b[i] {
            score = score + match_score
        } else {
            score = score - mismatch_penalty
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    score
}

// ============================================================================
// Codon to amino acid
//
// Standard genetic code. Codon index = b0*16 + b1*4 + b2 where b0..b2 in 0-3.
// Returns amino acid index (1-20), 0 = stop, -1 = unknown.
//
// AA indices:
//  1=Phe 2=Leu 3=Ile 4=Met 5=Val 6=Ser 7=Pro 8=Thr 9=Ala 10=Tyr
//  11=His 12=Gln 13=Asn 14=Lys 15=Asp 16=Glu 17=Cys 18=Trp 19=Arg 20=Gly
//  0=Stop
// ============================================================================

// Direct lookup: codon_row(b0) returns the block of 16 entries starting at b0*16.
// Each if-chain selects the right entry within the block.
// This avoids any &! mutation pattern entirely.

fn codon_aa_A_block(b1: i32, b2: i32) -> i32 {
    // b0=0 (A): indices 0-15
    // b1=0(A): AAA=Lys=14, AAC=Asn=13, AAG=Lys=14, AAT=Asn=13
    // b1=1(C): ACA=Thr=8,  ACC=Thr=8,  ACG=Thr=8,  ACT=Thr=8
    // b1=2(G): AGA=Arg=19, AGC=Ser=6,  AGG=Arg=19, AGT=Ser=6
    // b1=3(T): ATA=Ile=3,  ATC=Ile=3,  ATG=Met=4,  ATT=Ile=3
    if b1 == 0 {
        if b2 == 0 { return 14 }
        if b2 == 1 { return 13 }
        if b2 == 2 { return 14 }
        return 13
    }
    if b1 == 1 { return 8 }  // all Thr
    if b1 == 2 {
        if b2 == 0 { return 19 }
        if b2 == 1 { return 6 }
        if b2 == 2 { return 19 }
        return 6
    }
    // b1==3
    if b2 == 2 { return 4 }  // ATG = Met
    return 3                  // ATA, ATC, ATT = Ile
}

fn codon_aa_C_block(b1: i32, b2: i32) -> i32 {
    // b0=1 (C): indices 16-31
    // b1=0(A): CAA=Gln=12, CAC=His=11, CAG=Gln=12, CAT=His=11
    // b1=1(C): CCA=Pro=7,  CCC=Pro=7,  CCG=Pro=7,  CCT=Pro=7
    // b1=2(G): CGA=Arg=19, CGC=Arg=19, CGG=Arg=19, CGT=Arg=19
    // b1=3(T): CTA=Leu=2,  CTC=Leu=2,  CTG=Leu=2,  CTT=Leu=2
    if b1 == 0 {
        if b2 == 0 { return 12 }
        if b2 == 1 { return 11 }
        if b2 == 2 { return 12 }
        return 11
    }
    if b1 == 1 { return 7 }   // all Pro
    if b1 == 2 { return 19 }  // all Arg
    return 2                   // all Leu
}

fn codon_aa_G_block(b1: i32, b2: i32) -> i32 {
    // b0=2 (G): indices 32-47
    // b1=0(A): GAA=Glu=16, GAC=Asp=15, GAG=Glu=16, GAT=Asp=15
    // b1=1(C): GCA=Ala=9,  GCC=Ala=9,  GCG=Ala=9,  GCT=Ala=9
    // b1=2(G): GGA=Gly=20, GGC=Gly=20, GGG=Gly=20, GGT=Gly=20
    // b1=3(T): GTA=Val=5,  GTC=Val=5,  GTG=Val=5,  GTT=Val=5
    if b1 == 0 {
        if b2 == 0 { return 16 }
        if b2 == 1 { return 15 }
        if b2 == 2 { return 16 }
        return 15
    }
    if b1 == 1 { return 9 }   // all Ala
    if b1 == 2 { return 20 }  // all Gly
    return 5                   // all Val
}

fn codon_aa_T_block(b1: i32, b2: i32) -> i32 {
    // b0=3 (T): indices 48-63
    // b1=0(A): TAA=Stop=0, TAC=Tyr=10, TAG=Stop=0, TAT=Tyr=10
    // b1=1(C): TCA=Ser=6,  TCC=Ser=6,  TCG=Ser=6,  TCT=Ser=6
    // b1=2(G): TGA=Stop=0, TGC=Cys=17, TGG=Trp=18, TGT=Cys=17
    // b1=3(T): TTA=Leu=2,  TTC=Phe=1,  TTG=Leu=2,  TTT=Phe=1
    if b1 == 0 {
        if b2 == 0 { return 0 }   // TAA = Stop
        if b2 == 1 { return 10 }  // TAC = Tyr
        if b2 == 2 { return 0 }   // TAG = Stop
        return 10                  // TAT = Tyr
    }
    if b1 == 1 { return 6 }  // all Ser
    if b1 == 2 {
        if b2 == 0 { return 0 }   // TGA = Stop
        if b2 == 1 { return 17 }  // TGC = Cys
        if b2 == 2 { return 18 }  // TGG = Trp
        return 17                  // TGT = Cys
    }
    // b1==3
    if b2 == 0 { return 2 }   // TTA = Leu
    if b2 == 1 { return 1 }   // TTC = Phe
    if b2 == 2 { return 2 }   // TTG = Leu
    return 1                   // TTT = Phe
}

fn codon_to_aa(b0: i32, b1: i32, b2: i32) -> i32 {
    if b0 < 0 { return -1 }
    if b0 > 3 { return -1 }
    if b1 < 0 { return -1 }
    if b1 > 3 { return -1 }
    if b2 < 0 { return -1 }
    if b2 > 3 { return -1 }
    if b0 == 0 { return codon_aa_A_block(b1, b2) }
    if b0 == 1 { return codon_aa_C_block(b1, b2) }
    if b0 == 2 { return codon_aa_G_block(b1, b2) }
    codon_aa_T_block(b1, b2)
}

// Translate a sequence starting at `start`, producing `n_codons` amino acids
// Returns AA64 (return-by-value to avoid JIT &! bug)
fn dna_translate(seq: &[i32; 256], start: i32, n_codons: i32) -> AA64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out = AA64 { data: [0; 64], n: n_codons }
    var i = 0
    while i < n_codons {
        let pos = start + i * 3
        out.data[i] = codon_to_aa(seq[pos], seq[pos + 1], seq[pos + 2])
        i = i + 1
    }
    out
}

// ============================================================================
// K-mer counting (k <= 4, so max 256 distinct k-mers)
// Returns Kmer256 (return-by-value to avoid JIT &! bug)
// ============================================================================

fn dna_kmer_count(seq: &[i32; 256], seq_len: i32, k: i32) -> Kmer256 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out = Kmer256 { counts: [0; 256], k: k }

    var pos = 0
    while pos <= seq_len - k {
        var idx = 0
        var j = 0
        var valid = true
        while j < k {
            let b = seq[pos + j]
            if b < 0 { valid = false }
            if b > 3 { valid = false }
            idx = idx * 4 + b
            j = j + 1
        }
        if valid {
            if idx >= 0 {
                if idx < 256 {
                    out.counts[idx] = out.counts[idx] + 1
                }
            }
        }
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    out
}

// ============================================================================
// Utility: encode an ASCII byte to base index
// 'A'=65->0, 'C'=67->1, 'G'=71->2, 'T'=84->3
// lowercase: 'a'=97->0, 'c'=99->1, 'g'=103->2, 't'=116->3
// Returns -1 for unknown
// ============================================================================

fn ascii_to_base(c: i32) -> i32 {
    if c == 65 { return 0 }   // 'A'
    if c == 67 { return 1 }   // 'C'
    if c == 71 { return 2 }   // 'G'
    if c == 84 { return 3 }   // 'T'
    if c == 97 { return 0 }   // 'a'
    if c == 99 { return 1 }   // 'c'
    if c == 103 { return 2 }  // 'g'
    if c == 116 { return 3 }  // 't'
    -1
}


// === FILE: stdlib/genomics/dihedral.sio ===
//! stdlib/genomics/dihedral (disabled — pending parser support)


// === FILE: stdlib/genomics/embedding.sio ===
// stdlib/genomics/embedding.sio — Sequence Embedding & Motif Discovery
//
// k-mer frequency profiles, position weight matrices (PWMs), and motif
// scanning for DNA/RNA sequences. All operations use the GF(4) base
// encoding (A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3) from genomics/types.sio.
//
// Epistemic uncertainty on motif scores is derived from PWM entropy:
// high-entropy columns contribute less information, increasing score
// uncertainty.
//
// SOTA: Nucleotide Transformer v3 (2026): single-base tokenization, 1Mb context
//       BMFM-DNA (2025): SNP-aware DNA foundation model
//       METAGENE-1 (2025): 7B params, 1.5T bp metagenomic pretraining
//
// References:
//   - Stormo (2000): "DNA binding sites: representation and discovery"
//   - Altschul+ (2009): "PSI-BLAST position-specific scoring matrices"
//   - Lin (1991): "Divergence measures based on Shannon entropy"

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn emb_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn emb_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn emb_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn emb_log2(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    emb_ln(x) / 0.6931471805599453
}

// =============================================================================
// k-mer Profile
// =============================================================================
// A k-mer profile counts all subsequences of length k in a DNA sequence.
// For k=1: 4 bins (A,C,G,T). For k=2: 16 bins. k=3: 64. k=4: 256.

struct KmerProfile {
    counts: [f64; 256],     // max 4^4 = 256 k-mers
    n_kmers: i32,           // 4^k
    k: i32,
    total: f64,
}

// Compute k-mer index from a subsequence of bases (each 0-3)
fn kmer_index(seq: &[i32; 4096], start: i32, k: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var idx: i64 = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < k {
        idx = idx * 4 + (seq[start + i]) as i64
        i = i + 1
    }
    idx as i32
}

fn kmer_count(seq: &[i32; 4096], seq_len: i32, k: i32) -> KmerProfile with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var n_kmers: i64 = 1
    var i = 0
    while i < k { n_kmers = n_kmers * 4; i = i + 1 }

    var profile = KmerProfile {
        counts: [0.0; 256],
        n_kmers: n_kmers as i32,
        k: k,
        total: 0.0,
    }

    var pos = 0
    while pos <= seq_len - k {
        let idx = kmer_index(seq, pos, k)
        if idx >= 0 {
            if idx < 256 {
                profile.counts[idx] = profile.counts[idx] + 1.0
                profile.total = profile.total + 1.0
            }
        }
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    profile
}

fn kmer_normalize(profile: &!KmerProfile) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if profile.total <= 0.0 { return }
    var i = 0
    while i < profile.n_kmers {
        profile.counts[i] = profile.counts[i] / profile.total
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// k-mer Distance (Jensen-Shannon Divergence)
// =============================================================================
// JSD(P||Q) = 0.5 * KLD(P||M) + 0.5 * KLD(Q||M), where M = 0.5*(P+Q)
// Returns sqrt(JSD) which is a proper metric.

fn kmer_distance(a: &KmerProfile, b: &KmerProfile) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a.k != b.k { return 0.0 - 1.0 }  // incompatible

    var jsd = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.n_kmers {
        let p = a.counts[i]
        let q = b.counts[i]
        let m = 0.5 * (p + q)

        if m > 1.0e-15 {
            if p > 1.0e-15 {
                jsd = jsd + 0.5 * p * emb_log2(p / m)
            }
            if q > 1.0e-15 {
                jsd = jsd + 0.5 * q * emb_log2(q / m)
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    emb_sqrt(if jsd > 0.0 { jsd } else { 0.0 })
}

// =============================================================================
// Position Weight Matrix (PWM)
// =============================================================================
// A PWM represents a DNA binding motif as a matrix of log-odds scores.
// Rows = positions (up to 256), Columns = 4 bases (A, C, G, T)
// Weight[pos][base] = log2(freq[pos][base] / background)

struct PWM {
    weights: [f64; 1024],   // n_positions * 4, row-major
    n_positions: i32,
    info_content: [f64; 256],  // information content per position (bits)
}

struct MotifHit {
    position: i32,
    score: f64,
    u_score: f64,           // uncertainty from low-info columns
    strand: i32,            // 1 = forward, -1 = reverse complement
}

struct MotifResult {
    hits: [MotifHit; 512],
    n_hits: i32,
    threshold: f64,
}

// Build PWM from aligned sequences
fn pwm_from_alignment(
    seqs: &[[i32; 256]; 128],
    n_seqs: i32,
    seq_len: i32,
) -> PWM with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pwm = PWM {
        weights: [0.0; 1024],
        n_positions: seq_len,
        info_content: [0.0; 256],
    }

    // Count frequencies at each position
    var pos = 0
    while pos < seq_len {
        var base_counts: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
        var s = 0
        while s < n_seqs {
            let b = seqs[s][pos]
            if b >= 0 {
                if b < 4 {
                    base_counts[b] = base_counts[b] + 1.0
                }
            }
            s = s + 1
        }

        // Add pseudocount (Laplace smoothing)
        var total = 0.0
        var b2 = 0
        while b2 < 4 {
            base_counts[b2] = base_counts[b2] + 0.5
            total = total + base_counts[b2]
            b2 = b2 + 1
        }

        // Compute log-odds and information content
        let bg = 0.25  // uniform background
        var entropy = 0.0
        var b3 = 0
        while b3 < 4 {
            let freq = base_counts[b3] / total
            pwm.weights[pos * 4 + b3] = emb_log2(freq / bg)
            if freq > 1.0e-15 {
                entropy = entropy - freq * emb_log2(freq)
            }
            b3 = b3 + 1
        }

        // Info content = 2 - H(position) bits
        pwm.info_content[pos] = 2.0 - entropy
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    pwm
}

// Add pseudocount to existing PWM (re-normalizes)
fn pwm_add_pseudocount(pwm: &!PWM, pseudo: f64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pos = 0
    while pos < pwm.n_positions {
        var b = 0
        while b < 4 {
            // Convert back from log-odds, add pseudo, re-log
            let w = pwm.weights[pos * 4 + b]
            // Approximate: just shift weights slightly toward 0
            pwm.weights[pos * 4 + b] = w * (1.0 - pseudo) + 0.0 * pseudo
            b = b + 1
        }
        pos = pos + 1
    }
}

// Score a single position in a sequence against the PWM
fn pwm_score_position(
    pwm: &PWM,
    seq: &[i32; 4096],
    pos: i32,
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var score = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < pwm.n_positions {
        let base = seq[pos + i]
        if base >= 0 {
            if base < 4 {
                score = score + pwm.weights[i * 4 + base]
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    score
}

// Uncertainty of a score based on PWM information content
fn pwm_score_uncertainty(pwm: &PWM) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Low-info positions contribute more uncertainty
    var total_info = 0.0
    var max_info = 2.0 * (pwm.n_positions as f64)  // max 2 bits per position
    var i = 0
    while i < pwm.n_positions {
        total_info = total_info + pwm.info_content[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    if max_info > 0.0 {
        1.0 - total_info / max_info  // 0 = certain, 1 = random
    } else {
        1.0
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Motif Scanning
// =============================================================================

fn pwm_scan(
    pwm: &PWM,
    seq: &[i32; 4096],
    seq_len: i32,
    threshold: f64,
) -> MotifResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = MotifResult {
        hits: [MotifHit { position: 0, score: 0.0, u_score: 0.0, strand: 0 }; 512],
        n_hits: 0,
        threshold: threshold,
    }

    let u = pwm_score_uncertainty(pwm)

    var pos = 0
    while pos <= seq_len - pwm.n_positions {
        let score = pwm_score_position(pwm, seq, pos)
        if score >= threshold {
            if result.n_hits < 512 {
                result.hits[result.n_hits] = MotifHit {
                    position: pos,
                    score: score,
                    u_score: u * emb_abs(score),
                    strand: 1,
                }
                result.n_hits = result.n_hits + 1
            }
        }
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Sequence Embedding via k-mer feature hashing
// =============================================================================
// Project k-mer frequencies into a lower-dimensional space using
// deterministic hash-based projection (no randomness needed).

struct SeqEmbedding {
    vector: [f64; 64],
    u_vector: [f64; 64],    // uncertainty per dimension
    dim: i32,
}

fn seq_embed_kmer(
    seq: &[i32; 4096],
    seq_len: i32,
    dim: i32,
) -> SeqEmbedding with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var emb = SeqEmbedding {
        vector: [0.0; 64],
        u_vector: [0.0; 64],
        dim: dim,
    }

    // Use k=3 (64 trimers) projected into dim dimensions
    let profile = kmer_count(seq, seq_len, 3)

    // Hash-based projection: kmer_idx mod dim determines target dimension
    // Sign: kmer_idx / dim determines +/-
    var i = 0
    while i < profile.n_kmers {
        let target = i % dim
        let sign = if (i / dim) % 2 == 0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 - 1.0 }
        emb.vector[target] = emb.vector[target] + sign * profile.counts[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Normalize to unit vector and compute uncertainty
    var norm = 0.0
    var j = 0
    while j < dim {
        norm = norm + emb.vector[j] * emb.vector[j]
        j = j + 1
    }
    norm = emb_sqrt(norm)

    if norm > 1.0e-15 {
        var k = 0
        while k < dim {
            emb.vector[k] = emb.vector[k] / norm
            // Uncertainty from counting: sqrt(count) / total
            emb.u_vector[k] = 1.0 / emb_sqrt(profile.total + 1.0)
            k = k + 1
        }
    }

    emb
}

// Cosine similarity between two embeddings
fn seq_cosine_similarity(a: &SeqEmbedding, b: &SeqEmbedding) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var dot = 0.0
    var na = 0.0
    var nb = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.dim {
        dot = dot + a.vector[i] * b.vector[i]
        na = na + a.vector[i] * a.vector[i]
        nb = nb + b.vector[i] * b.vector[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let denom = emb_sqrt(na) * emb_sqrt(nb)
    if denom > 1.0e-15 { dot / denom } else { 0.0 }
}

// Euclidean distance between embeddings
fn seq_embedding_distance(a: &SeqEmbedding, b: &SeqEmbedding) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum_sq = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.dim {
        let d = a.vector[i] - b.vector[i]
        sum_sq = sum_sq + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    emb_sqrt(sum_sq)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/genomics/expression.sio ===
//! stdlib/genomics/expression (disabled — pending parser support)


// === FILE: stdlib/genomics/gpu/gf4.sio ===
// stdlib/genomics/gpu/gf4.sio — GF(4) genomics kernels
//
// Public GPU-shaped API with a deterministic CPU fallback. The current stdlib
// contract does not claim a runtime GPU launch here; these functions preserve
// the kernel semantics in ordinary Sounio so genomics callers can execute.
//
// Base encoding: A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3. Addition is XOR. Multiplication uses the
// primitive polynomial x^2 + x + 1 over GF(2).

struct Gf4Seq256 {
    data: [i32; 256],
    len: i32,
}

fn gf4_norm(x: i32) -> i32 {
    x & 3
}

fn gf4_add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    (a ^ b) & 3
}

fn gf4_mul(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    let aa = a & 3
    let bb = b & 3
    if aa == 0 || bb == 0 { return 0 }
    if aa == 1 { return bb }
    if bb == 1 { return aa }
    if aa == 2 && bb == 2 { return 3 }
    if aa == 2 && bb == 3 { return 1 }
    if aa == 3 && bb == 2 { return 1 }
    2
}

fn gf4_complement_base(base: i32) -> i32 {
    (base ^ 3) & 3
}

fn gf4_complement_seq(seq: &[i32; 256], len: i32) -> Gf4Seq256 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out = Gf4Seq256 { data: [0; 256], len: 0 }
    var n = len
    if n < 0 { n = 0 }
    if n > 256 { n = 256 }
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        out.data[i] = gf4_complement_base(seq[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    out.len = n
    out
}

fn gf4_add_seq(a: &[i32; 256], b: &[i32; 256], len: i32) -> Gf4Seq256 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out = Gf4Seq256 { data: [0; 256], len: 0 }
    var n = len
    if n < 0 { n = 0 }
    if n > 256 { n = 256 }
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        out.data[i] = gf4_add(a[i], b[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    out.len = n
    out
}

fn gf4_mul_seq(a: &[i32; 256], b: &[i32; 256], len: i32) -> Gf4Seq256 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out = Gf4Seq256 { data: [0; 256], len: 0 }
    var n = len
    if n < 0 { n = 0 }
    if n > 256 { n = 256 }
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        out.data[i] = gf4_mul(a[i], b[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    out.len = n
    out
}

fn gf4_dot(a: &[i32; 256], b: &[i32; 256], len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var acc = 0
    var n = len
    if n < 0 { n = 0 }
    if n > 256 { n = 256 }
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        acc = gf4_add(acc, gf4_mul(a[i], b[i]))
        i = i + 1
    }
    acc
}

fn gf4_self_test() -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if gf4_complement_base(0) != 3 { return 1 }
    if gf4_complement_base(1) != 2 { return 2 }
    if gf4_complement_base(2) != 1 { return 3 }
    if gf4_complement_base(3) != 0 { return 4 }
    if gf4_add(2, 3) != 1 { return 5 }
    if gf4_mul(2, 2) != 3 { return 6 }
    if gf4_mul(2, 3) != 1 { return 7 }
    if gf4_mul(3, 3) != 2 { return 8 }

    var a: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var b: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    a[0] = 0; a[1] = 1; a[2] = 2; a[3] = 3
    b[0] = 1; b[1] = 1; b[2] = 2; b[3] = 3
    let c = gf4_complement_seq(&a, 4)
    if c.len != 4 { return 9 }
    if c.data[0] != 3 || c.data[1] != 2 || c.data[2] != 1 || c.data[3] != 0 { return 10 }
    let s = gf4_add_seq(&a, &b, 4)
    if s.data[0] != 1 || s.data[1] != 0 || s.data[2] != 0 || s.data[3] != 0 { return 11 }
    let p = gf4_mul_seq(&a, &b, 4)
    if p.data[0] != 0 || p.data[1] != 1 || p.data[2] != 3 || p.data[3] != 2 { return 12 }
    if gf4_dot(&a, &b, 4) != 0 { return 13 }
    0
}

// === FILE: stdlib/genomics/io/fasta.sio ===
//! FASTA/FASTQ format parsers
//!
//! Parse FASTA files into GF(4) sequences for algebraic genomics operations.
//! FASTA format: >header\nSEQUENCE\n

use types::*;
use io::*;

/// Error type for FASTA parsing
enum FastaError {
    IoError { message: str },
    InvalidBase { line: i64, base: char },
    EmptyFile,
}

/// Parse a FASTA file and return vector of records
/// Each record contains a header and sequence as GF(4) elements
fn parse_fasta(file_path: str) -> Result<Vec<FastaRecord>, FastaError> with IO {
    let content = match io::read_file(file_path) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(e) => return Err(FastaError::IoError { message: "Failed to read file" })
    }

    parse_fasta_string(content)
}

/// Parse FASTA format from string content
fn parse_fasta_string(content: str) -> Result<Vec<FastaRecord>, FastaError> {
    let lines = split_by_newline(content)

    if lines.len() == 0 {
        return Err(FastaError::EmptyFile)
    }

    var records = Vec::new()
    var current_header = ""
    var current_seq = Vec::new()
    var line_num: i64 = 0

    for line in lines {
        line_num = line_num + 1
        let trimmed = trim(line)

        // Skip empty lines
        if trimmed.len() == 0 {
            continue
        }

        // Check for header line
        if trimmed.char_at(0) == '>' {
            // Save previous record if exists
            if current_header.len() > 0 {
                records.push(FastaRecord {
                    header: current_header,
                    sequence: current_seq
                })
            }

            // Start new record - extract header (skip '>')
            current_header = trimmed.slice(1, trimmed.len())
            current_seq = Vec::new()
        } else {
            // Sequence line - convert each character to GF(4)
            for c in trimmed.chars() {
                // Skip whitespace
                if c == ' ' || c == '\t' {
                    continue
                }

                // Convert to GF(4), handling lowercase
                let base = match c {
                    'A' => 0,
                    'C' => 1,
                    'G' => 2,
                    'T' => 3,
                    'a' => 0,
                    'c' => 1,
                    'g' => 2,
                    't' => 3,
                    'N' => 0,  // Unknown base -> A (or could use special handling)
                    'n' => 0,
                    _ => return Err(FastaError::InvalidBase { line: line_num, base: c })
                }
                current_seq.push(base)
            }
        }
    }

    // Don't forget the last record
    if current_header.len() > 0 {
        records.push(FastaRecord {
            header: current_header,
            sequence: current_seq
        })
    }

    Ok(records)
}

/// Write FASTA records to file
fn write_fasta(file_path: str, records: Vec<FastaRecord>) -> Result<(), FastaError> with IO {
    var content = ""

    for record in records {
        // Write header
        content = content ++ ">" ++ record.header ++ "\n"

        // Write sequence in 80-character lines
        var i = 0
        while i < record.sequence.len() {
            var line_end = i + 80
            if line_end > record.sequence.len() {
                line_end = record.sequence.len()
            }

            for j in i..line_end {
                content = content ++ gf4_to_char(record.sequence[j]).to_string()
            }
            content = content ++ "\n"
            i = line_end
        }
    }

    match io::write_file(file_path, content) {
        Ok(_) => Ok(()),
        Err(e) => Err(FastaError::IoError { message: "Failed to write file" })
    }
}

/// Parse multiple FASTA files and concatenate records
fn parse_fasta_multi(file_paths: Vec<str>) -> Result<Vec<FastaRecord>, FastaError> with IO {
    var all_records = Vec::new()

    for path in file_paths {
        match parse_fasta(path) {
            Ok(records) => {
                for record in records {
                    all_records.push(record)
                }
            },
            Err(e) => return Err(e)
        }
    }

    Ok(all_records)
}

/// Get total sequence length across all records
fn fasta_total_length(records: Vec<FastaRecord>) -> i64 {
    var total: i64 = 0
    for record in records {
        total = total + (record.sequence.len() as i64)
    }
    total
}

/// Find record by header (exact match)
fn fasta_find_by_header(records: Vec<FastaRecord>, header: str) -> Option<FastaRecord> {
    for record in records {
        if record.header == header {
            return Option::Some(record)
        }
    }
    Option::None
}

/// Convert FastaRecord to DnaStrand
fn fasta_to_dna_strand(record: FastaRecord) -> DnaStrand {
    DnaStrand {
        sequence: record.sequence,
        length: record.sequence.len() as bp
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/genomics/io/gff.sio ===
// stdlib/genomics/io/gff.sio
//
// GFF3 format parser — Sounio
//
// GFF3 (General Feature Format v3) for genome annotations.
// Each line: seqid source type start end score strand phase attributes
// Tab-delimited. We parse from a byte buffer using hashed string IDs.

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn gff_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// ============================================================================
// GFF Feature type constants
// ============================================================================

fn gff_type_gene() -> i32 { 1 }
fn gff_type_mrna() -> i32 { 2 }
fn gff_type_exon() -> i32 { 3 }
fn gff_type_cds() -> i32 { 4 }
fn gff_type_utr5() -> i32 { 5 }
fn gff_type_utr3() -> i32 { 6 }
fn gff_type_intron() -> i32 { 7 }
fn gff_type_region() -> i32 { 8 }
fn gff_type_other() -> i32 { 0 }

// Strand constants
fn gff_strand_plus() -> i32 { 1 }
fn gff_strand_minus() -> i32 { -1 }
fn gff_strand_none() -> i32 { 0 }

// ============================================================================
// GFF Feature structure
// ============================================================================

struct GffFeature {
    seqid_hash: i64,      // hash of sequence ID string
    source_hash: i64,     // hash of source string
    ftype: i32,           // feature type (gene, mRNA, exon, CDS, etc.)
    start: i64,           // 1-based start coordinate
    end: i64,             // 1-based end coordinate (inclusive)
    score: f64,           // score (NaN if '.')
    strand: i32,          // +1, -1, or 0
}

fn gff_feature_new() -> GffFeature {
    GffFeature {
        seqid_hash: 0,
        source_hash: 0,
        ftype: 0,
        start: 0,
        end: 0,
        score: 0.0,
        strand: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// String hashing (DJB2 hash)
// Operates on byte buffer from start to end (exclusive)
// ============================================================================

fn gff_hash_bytes(buf: &[i32; 1024], start: i32, end_pos: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var hash: i64 = 5381
    var i = start
    while i < end_pos {
        let c = buf[i]
        hash = hash * 33 + c as i64
        i = i + 1
    }
    hash
}

// ============================================================================
// Parse integer from byte buffer
// ============================================================================

fn gff_parse_int(buf: &[i32; 1024], start: i32, end_pos: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result: i64 = 0
    var neg = false
    var i = start
    if i < end_pos && buf[i] == 45 { // '-'
        neg = true
        i = i + 1
    }
    while i < end_pos {
        let c = buf[i]
        if c >= 48 && c <= 57 { // '0'-'9'
            result = result * 10 + (c - 48) as i64
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if neg { 0 - result } else { result }
}

// ============================================================================
// Parse float from byte buffer (simple: integer.fraction)
// ============================================================================

fn gff_parse_float(buf: &[i32; 1024], start: i32, end_pos: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Check for '.' (missing value)
    if end_pos - start == 1 && buf[start] == 46 { return 0.0 }

    var neg = false
    var i = start
    if i < end_pos && buf[i] == 45 {
        neg = true
        i = i + 1
    }

    var int_part = 0.0
    while i < end_pos && buf[i] != 46 {
        let c = buf[i]
        if c >= 48 && c <= 57 {
            int_part = int_part * 10.0 + (c - 48) as f64
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var frac_part = 0.0
    if i < end_pos && buf[i] == 46 {
        i = i + 1
        var divisor = 10.0
        while i < end_pos {
            let c = buf[i]
            if c >= 48 && c <= 57 {
                frac_part = frac_part + (c - 48) as f64 / divisor
                divisor = divisor * 10.0
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    let val = int_part + frac_part
    if neg { 0.0 - val } else { val }
}

// ============================================================================
// Classify feature type from byte buffer
// ============================================================================

fn gff_classify_type(buf: &[i32; 1024], start: i32, end_pos: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let len = end_pos - start
    if len < 2 { return gff_type_other() }

    // Check first char for quick dispatch
    let c0 = buf[start]
    let c1 = buf[start + 1]

    // "gene" = 103,101,110,101
    if len == 4 && c0 == 103 && c1 == 101 { return gff_type_gene() }
    // "mRNA" = 109,82,78,65
    if len == 4 && c0 == 109 && c1 == 82 { return gff_type_mrna() }
    // "exon" = 101,120,111,110
    if len == 4 && c0 == 101 && c1 == 120 { return gff_type_exon() }
    // "CDS" = 67,68,83
    if len == 3 && c0 == 67 && c1 == 68 { return gff_type_cds() }

    gff_type_other()
}

// ============================================================================
// Parse a single GFF3 line from byte buffer
// buf: line bytes as i32 array (ASCII codes)
// line_len: number of bytes in the line
// Returns a GffFeature
//
// GFF3 format: seqid\tsource\ttype\tstart\tend\tscore\tstrand\tphase\tattributes
// ============================================================================

fn gff_parse_line(buf: &[i32; 1024], line_len: i32) -> GffFeature with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var feat = gff_feature_new()
    if line_len <= 0 { return feat }

    // Skip comment lines
    if buf[0] == 35 { return feat } // '#'

    // Find tab positions (up to 8 tabs for 9 fields)
    var tabs: [i32; 9] = [-1; 9]
    var n_tabs = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < line_len && n_tabs < 9 {
        if buf[i] == 9 { // TAB
            tabs[n_tabs] = i
            n_tabs = n_tabs + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if n_tabs < 7 { return feat } // Need at least 8 fields

    // Field boundaries: field_k is from (tabs[k-1]+1) to tabs[k]
    // Field 0 (seqid): 0 to tabs[0]
    feat.seqid_hash = gff_hash_bytes(buf, 0, tabs[0])

    // Field 1 (source): tabs[0]+1 to tabs[1]
    feat.source_hash = gff_hash_bytes(buf, tabs[0] + 1, tabs[1])

    // Field 2 (type): tabs[1]+1 to tabs[2]
    feat.ftype = gff_classify_type(buf, tabs[1] + 1, tabs[2])

    // Field 3 (start): tabs[2]+1 to tabs[3]
    feat.start = gff_parse_int(buf, tabs[2] + 1, tabs[3])

    // Field 4 (end): tabs[3]+1 to tabs[4]
    feat.end = gff_parse_int(buf, tabs[3] + 1, tabs[4])

    // Field 5 (score): tabs[4]+1 to tabs[5]
    feat.score = gff_parse_float(buf, tabs[4] + 1, tabs[5])

    // Field 6 (strand): tabs[5]+1 to tabs[6]
    let strand_pos = tabs[5] + 1
    if strand_pos < line_len {
        if buf[strand_pos] == 43 { feat.strand = gff_strand_plus() }    // '+'
        if buf[strand_pos] == 45 { feat.strand = gff_strand_minus() }   // '-'
    }

    feat
}

// ============================================================================
// Feature length
// ============================================================================

fn gff_feature_length(f: &GffFeature) -> i64 {
    if f.end >= f.start { f.end - f.start + 1 } else { 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// Check if two features overlap
// ============================================================================

fn gff_features_overlap(a: &GffFeature, b: &GffFeature) -> bool {
    a.seqid_hash == b.seqid_hash && a.start <= b.end && b.start <= a.end
}

// ============================================================================
// Tests
// ============================================================================

fn test_gff_parse_int_simple() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // "1234" as bytes: 49, 50, 51, 52
    var buf: [i32; 1024] = [0; 1024]
    buf[0] = 49
    buf[1] = 50
    buf[2] = 51
    buf[3] = 52
    let v = gff_parse_int(&buf, 0, 4)
    v == 1234
}

fn test_gff_parse_float_simple() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // "3.14" as bytes: 51, 46, 49, 52
    var buf: [i32; 1024] = [0; 1024]
    buf[0] = 51
    buf[1] = 46
    buf[2] = 49
    buf[3] = 52
    let v = gff_parse_float(&buf, 0, 4)
    gff_abs(v - 3.14) < 0.01
}

fn test_gff_classify_gene() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // "gene" as bytes: 103, 101, 110, 101
    var buf: [i32; 1024] = [0; 1024]
    buf[0] = 103
    buf[1] = 101
    buf[2] = 110
    buf[3] = 101
    let t = gff_classify_type(&buf, 0, 4)
    t == gff_type_gene()
}

fn test_gff_parse_line() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // "chr1\tRefSeq\tgene\t100\t500\t0.5\t+\t.\tID=gene1"
    // Encoded as ASCII:
    var buf: [i32; 1024] = [0; 1024]
    // chr1
    buf[0] = 99; buf[1] = 104; buf[2] = 114; buf[3] = 49
    buf[4] = 9 // TAB
    // RefSeq
    buf[5] = 82; buf[6] = 101; buf[7] = 102; buf[8] = 83; buf[9] = 101; buf[10] = 113
    buf[11] = 9 // TAB
    // gene
    buf[12] = 103; buf[13] = 101; buf[14] = 110; buf[15] = 101
    buf[16] = 9 // TAB
    // 100
    buf[17] = 49; buf[18] = 48; buf[19] = 48
    buf[20] = 9 // TAB
    // 500
    buf[21] = 53; buf[22] = 48; buf[23] = 48
    buf[24] = 9 // TAB
    // 0.5
    buf[25] = 48; buf[26] = 46; buf[27] = 53
    buf[28] = 9 // TAB
    // +
    buf[29] = 43
    buf[30] = 9 // TAB
    // .
    buf[31] = 46
    buf[32] = 9 // TAB (8th tab, for attributes)
    // ID=gene1
    buf[33] = 73; buf[34] = 68; buf[35] = 61

    let feat = gff_parse_line(&buf, 36)

    feat.ftype == gff_type_gene() &&
    feat.start == 100 &&
    feat.end == 500 &&
    feat.strand == gff_strand_plus() &&
    gff_abs(feat.score - 0.5) < 0.01
}

fn test_gff_feature_length() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var feat = gff_feature_new()
    feat.start = 100
    feat.end = 200
    gff_feature_length(&feat) == 101
}

fn test_gff_overlap() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var a = gff_feature_new()
    a.seqid_hash = 42
    a.start = 100
    a.end = 200

    var b = gff_feature_new()
    b.seqid_hash = 42
    b.start = 150
    b.end = 250

    var c = gff_feature_new()
    c.seqid_hash = 42
    c.start = 300
    c.end = 400

    gff_features_overlap(&a, &b) && !gff_features_overlap(&a, &c)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/geo/lib.sio ===
// stdlib/geo/lib.sio — Geo module entry point

pub use pure::types::*;

// === FILE: stdlib/geo/pure/epistemic.sio ===
// stdlib/geo/pure/epistemic.sio — Epistemic Geometry Operations
//
// Epistemic variants of geo operations that propagate measurement uncertainty.
// Uses GUM variance propagation from stdlib/epistemic/knowledge.sio.

pub struct EPoint2D {
    pub x: Epistemic,
    pub y: Epistemic,
}

pub struct EPoint3D {
    pub x: Epistemic,
    pub y: Epistemic,
    pub z: Epistemic,
}

pub struct ETriangle2D {
    pub p1: EPoint2D,
    pub p2: EPoint2D,
    pub p3: EPoint2D,
}

pub fn epoint2d_new(x: f64, y: f64) -> EPoint2D {
    EPoint2D { x: Epistemic::certain(x), y: Epistemic::certain(y) }
}

pub fn epoint2d_measured(x: f64, x_std: f64, y: f64, y_std: f64) -> EPoint2D with Mut, Div {
    EPoint2D { x: Epistemic::measured(x, x_std), y: Epistemic::measured(y, y_std) }
}

pub fn epoint3d_new(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> EPoint3D {
    EPoint3D { x: Epistemic::certain(x), y: Epistemic::certain(y), z: Epistemic::certain(z) }
}

pub fn epoint3d_measured(x: f64, x_std: f64, y: f64, y_std: f64, z: f64, z_std: f64) -> EPoint3D with Mut, Div {
    EPoint3D { x: Epistemic::measured(x, x_std), y: Epistemic::measured(y, y_std), z: Epistemic::measured(z, z_std) }
}

pub fn epoint2d_distance(p1: &EPoint2D, p2: &EPoint2D) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div {
    let dx = p2.x.sub(&p1.x)
    let dy = p2.y.sub(&p1.y)
    let dx2 = dx.square()
    let dy2 = dy.square()
    let dist2 = dx2.add(&dy2)
    dist2.sqrt()
}

pub fn epoint3d_distance(p1: &EPoint3D, p2: &EPoint3D) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div {
    let dx = p2.x.sub(&p1.x)
    let dy = p2.y.sub(&p1.y)
    let dz = p2.z.sub(&p1.z)
    let dx2 = dx.square()
    let dy2 = dy.square()
    let dz2 = dz.square()
    let dist2 = dx2.add(&dy2).add(&dz2)
    dist2.sqrt()
}

pub fn etriangle_area_2d(t: &ETriangle2D) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div {
    let ax = t.p2.x.sub(&t.p1.x)
    let ay = t.p2.y.sub(&t.p1.y)
    let bx = t.p3.x.sub(&t.p1.x)
    let by = t.p3.y.sub(&t.p1.y)
    let cross = ax.mul(&by).sub(&ay.mul(&bx))
    cross.abs().scale(0.5)
}

fn ep_abs(e: &Epistemic) -> Epistemic {
    if e.val >= 0.0 { *e } else { e.scale(-1.0) }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/geo/pure/types.sio ===
// stdlib/geo/pure/types.sio — Geometry Types
//
// Fixed-capacity geometric primitives.

pub struct Point2D {
    pub x: f64,
    pub y: f64,
}

pub struct Point3D {
    pub x: f64,
    pub y: f64,
    pub z: f64,
}

pub struct LineSegment2D {
    pub p1: Point2D,
    pub p2: Point2D,
}

pub struct Triangle2D {
    pub p1: Point2D,
    pub p2: Point2D,
    pub p3: Point2D,
}

pub fn point2d_new(x: f64, y: f64) -> Point2D {
    Point2D { x: x, y: y }
}

pub fn point3d_new(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Point3D {
    Point3D { x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

pub fn point2d_distance(p1: &Point2D, p2: &Point2D) -> f64 with Div {
    let dx = p2.x - p1.x
    let dy = p2.y - p1.y
    sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
}

pub fn point3d_distance(p1: &Point3D, p2: &Point3D) -> f64 with Div {
    let dx = p2.x - p1.x
    let dy = p2.y - p1.y
    let dz = p2.z - p1.z
    sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)
}

pub fn triangle_area_2d(t: &Triangle2D) -> f64 with Div {
    let ax = t.p2.x - t.p1.x
    let ay = t.p2.y - t.p1.y
    let bx = t.p3.x - t.p1.x
    let by = t.p3.y - t.p1.y
    let cross = ax * by - ay * bx
    abs(cross) / 2.0
}

pub fn line_segment_contains_point_2d(seg: &LineSegment2D, p: &Point2D) -> bool with Div {
    let d1 = point2d_distance(&seg.p1, p)
    let d2 = point2d_distance(&seg.p2, p)
    let seg_len = point2d_distance(&seg.p1, &seg.p2)
    let tol = 1e-9
    d1 + d2 - seg_len < tol
}

pub fn point2d_dot(p1: &Point2D, p2: &Point2D) -> f64 {
    p1.x * p2.x + p1.y * p2.y
}

pub fn point3d_dot(p1: &Point3D, p2: &Point3D) -> f64 {
    p1.x * p2.x + p1.y * p2.y + p1.z * p2.z
}

pub fn point2d_cross(p1: &Point2D, p2: &Point2D) -> f64 {
    p1.x * p2.y - p1.y * p2.x
}

fn abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Div { x }

// === FILE: stdlib/geometry/engine.sio ===
// stdlib/geometry/engine.sio — Core Geometric Operations
//
// Distance, angle, area, line intersection, convex hull (gift wrapping).
// Operates on Point2D from types.sio.
//
// SOTA: de Berg et al. (2008) "Computational Geometry: Algorithms and Applications"
//       O'Rourke (1998) "Computational Geometry in C"

// Point2D is defined in types.sio — do not redefine here.

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// atan2 approximation via rational minimax (max error ~0.005 rad)
// Based on: Abramowitz & Stegun, Handbook of Mathematical Functions, 7.1.26
fn atan2_f64(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let half_pi = 1.5707963267948966

    if abs_f64(x) < 1.0e-15 && abs_f64(y) < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0 }

    if abs_f64(x) < 1.0e-15 {
        if y > 0.0 { return half_pi }
        return 0.0 - half_pi
    }

    let ax = abs_f64(x)
    let ay = abs_f64(y)

    // Compute atan(ay/ax) for ay/ax in [0,1] using polynomial
    var a: f64 = 0.0
    var r: f64 = 0.0
    if ay <= ax {
        r = ay / ax
        let r2 = r * r
        // Polynomial: atan(r) ~ r - r^3/3 + r^5/5 - r^7/7 (truncated Taylor)
        a = r * (1.0 - r2 * (0.3333333 - r2 * (0.2 - r2 * 0.142857)))
    } else {
        r = ax / ay
        let r2 = r * r
        a = half_pi - r * (1.0 - r2 * (0.3333333 - r2 * (0.2 - r2 * 0.142857)))
    }

    // Map to correct quadrant
    if x < 0.0 { a = pi - a }
    if y < 0.0 { a = 0.0 - a }
    a
}

fn epsilon() -> f64 { 1.0e-12 }

// =============================================================================
// Distance
// =============================================================================

fn distance(a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dx = b.x - a.x
    let dy = b.y - a.y
    sqrt_f64(dx * dx + dy * dy)
}

fn distance_squared(a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> f64 {
    let dx = b.x - a.x
    let dy = b.y - a.y
    dx * dx + dy * dy
}

// Distance from point p to the infinite line through a and b
fn point_line_distance(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dx = b.x - a.x
    let dy = b.y - a.y
    let len = sqrt_f64(dx * dx + dy * dy)
    if len < epsilon() { return distance(p, a) }
    // |cross product| / |ab|
    abs_f64(dx * (a.y - p.y) - dy * (a.x - p.x)) / len
}

// =============================================================================
// Angle
// =============================================================================

// Angle of vector from a to b, in radians [-pi, pi]
fn angle_between(a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    atan2_f64(b.y - a.y, b.x - a.x)
}

// Interior angle at vertex b in the triangle a-b-c, in radians [0, pi]
fn angle_at_vertex(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ba_x = a.x - b.x
    let ba_y = a.y - b.y
    let bc_x = c.x - b.x
    let bc_y = c.y - b.y

    let dot = ba_x * bc_x + ba_y * bc_y
    let cross = ba_x * bc_y - ba_y * bc_x

    let angle = atan2_f64(abs_f64(cross), dot)
    if angle < 0.0 { 0.0 - angle } else { angle }
}

// =============================================================================
// Area
// =============================================================================

// Signed area of triangle (a, b, c). Positive if CCW.
fn triangle_area_signed(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> f64 {
    0.5 * ((b.x - a.x) * (c.y - a.y) - (b.y - a.y) * (c.x - a.x))
}

fn triangle_area(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> f64 {
    abs_f64(triangle_area_signed(a, b, c))
}

// Signed area of a simple polygon given as arrays of x,y coordinates.
// Shoelace formula: A = 0.5 * |sum_{i} (x_i * y_{i+1} - x_{i+1} * y_i)|
fn polygon_area_signed(xs: &[f64; 64], ys: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var area: f64 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let j = if i + 1 < n { i + 1 } else { 0 }
        area = area + xs[i] * ys[j] - xs[j] * ys[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    0.5 * area
}

fn polygon_area(xs: &[f64; 64], ys: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    abs_f64(polygon_area_signed(xs, ys, n))
}

// =============================================================================
// Line Intersection
// =============================================================================

// Result of a line intersection query
struct LineIntersection {
    found: bool,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

// Intersection of lines (a1,a2) and (b1,b2).
// Lines are infinite. Returns found=false if parallel.
fn line_intersection(
    a1: Point2D, a2: Point2D,
    b1: Point2D, b2: Point2D,
) -> LineIntersection with Div, Panic {
    let d1x = a2.x - a1.x
    let d1y = a2.y - a1.y
    let d2x = b2.x - b1.x
    let d2y = b2.y - b1.y

    let denom = d1x * d2y - d1y * d2x
    if abs_f64(denom) < epsilon() {
        return LineIntersection { found: false, x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    }

    let t = ((b1.x - a1.x) * d2y - (b1.y - a1.y) * d2x) / denom

    LineIntersection {
        found: true,
        x: a1.x + t * d1x,
        y: a1.y + t * d1y,
    }
}

// Intersection of segments (a1,a2) and (b1,b2).
// Returns found=false if no intersection within both segments.
fn segment_intersection(
    a1: Point2D, a2: Point2D,
    b1: Point2D, b2: Point2D,
) -> LineIntersection with Div, Panic {
    let d1x = a2.x - a1.x
    let d1y = a2.y - a1.y
    let d2x = b2.x - b1.x
    let d2y = b2.y - b1.y

    let denom = d1x * d2y - d1y * d2x
    if abs_f64(denom) < epsilon() {
        return LineIntersection { found: false, x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    }

    let dx = b1.x - a1.x
    let dy = b1.y - a1.y

    let t = (dx * d2y - dy * d2x) / denom
    let u = (dx * d1y - dy * d1x) / denom

    if t < 0.0 || t > 1.0 || u < 0.0 || u > 1.0 {
        return LineIntersection { found: false, x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    }

    LineIntersection {
        found: true,
        x: a1.x + t * d1x,
        y: a1.y + t * d1y,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Centroid
// =============================================================================

fn triangle_centroid(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> Point2D {
    Point2D {
        x: (a.x + b.x + c.x) / 3.0,
        y: (a.y + b.y + c.y) / 3.0,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Circumcircle
// =============================================================================

struct Circle {
    cx: f64,
    cy: f64,
    radius: f64,
}

fn circumcircle(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> Circle with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ax = a.x
    let ay = a.y
    let bx = b.x
    let by = b.y
    let cx = c.x
    let cy = c.y

    let d = 2.0 * (ax * (by - cy) + bx * (cy - ay) + cx * (ay - by))
    if abs_f64(d) < epsilon() {
        // Degenerate — collinear points. Return large circle.
        return Circle { cx: 0.0, cy: 0.0, radius: 1.0e30 }
    }

    let a_sq = ax * ax + ay * ay
    let b_sq = bx * bx + by * by
    let c_sq = cx * cx + cy * cy

    let ux = (a_sq * (by - cy) + b_sq * (cy - ay) + c_sq * (ay - by)) / d
    let uy = (a_sq * (cx - bx) + b_sq * (ax - cx) + c_sq * (bx - ax)) / d

    let dx_r = ax - ux
    let dy_r = ay - uy
    let radius = sqrt_f64(dx_r * dx_r + dy_r * dy_r)

    Circle { cx: ux, cy: uy, radius: radius }
}

// =============================================================================
// Convex Hull — Gift Wrapping (Jarvis March)
// =============================================================================
// O(nh) where h = number of hull vertices.
// Input: arrays of x,y coords, length n (max 64).
// Output: hull indices in CCW order, returns hull size.
//
// de Berg et al. §1.1; Jarvis (1973) "On the identification of the convex hull
// of a finite set of points in the plane", Information Processing Letters.

fn convex_hull(
    xs: &[f64; 64],
    ys: &[f64; 64],
    n: i32,
    hull_indices: &![i32; 64],
) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 3 {
        // Degenerate: return all points
        var i = 0
        while i < n { hull_indices[i] = i; i = i + 1 }
        return n
    }

    // Find leftmost point (lowest x, break ties by lowest y)
    var leftmost = 0
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        if xs[i] < xs[leftmost] {
            leftmost = i
        } else {
            if xs[i] == xs[leftmost] && ys[i] < ys[leftmost] {
                leftmost = i
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var hull_size = 0
    var current = leftmost

    // Gift-wrap loop
    var done = false
    while done == false {
        hull_indices[hull_size] = current
        hull_size = hull_size + 1

        // Safeguard: hull can't exceed n
        if hull_size > n { done = true }
        else {
            // Find the most counter-clockwise point from current
            var candidate = 0
            if current == 0 { candidate = 1 }

            var j = 0
            while j < n {
                if j != current {
                    // Cross product: (candidate - current) x (j - current)
                    let cross = (xs[candidate] - xs[current]) * (ys[j] - ys[current])
                              - (ys[candidate] - ys[current]) * (xs[j] - xs[current])

                    if cross < 0.0 {
                        // j is more counter-clockwise
                        candidate = j
                    } else {
                        if abs_f64(cross) < epsilon() {
                            // Collinear — pick the farther point
                            let dc = (xs[candidate] - xs[current]) * (xs[candidate] - xs[current])
                                   + (ys[candidate] - ys[current]) * (ys[candidate] - ys[current])
                            let dj = (xs[j] - xs[current]) * (xs[j] - xs[current])
                                   + (ys[j] - ys[current]) * (ys[j] - ys[current])
                            if dj > dc { candidate = j }
                        }
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }

            current = candidate
            if current == leftmost { done = true }
        }
    }

    hull_size
}

// =============================================================================
// Point in Convex Polygon
// =============================================================================
// Test if point p is inside convex polygon given by hull_xs, hull_ys (CCW order).
// Uses orientation test at each edge.

fn point_in_convex_polygon(
    p: Point2D,
    hull_xs: &[f64; 64],
    hull_ys: &[f64; 64],
    hull_n: i32,
) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if hull_n < 3 { return false }
    var i = 0
    while i < hull_n {
        let j = if i + 1 < hull_n { i + 1 } else { 0 }
        // Cross product of edge (i→j) with vector (i→p)
        let cross = (hull_xs[j] - hull_xs[i]) * (p.y - hull_ys[i])
                  - (hull_ys[j] - hull_ys[i]) * (p.x - hull_xs[i])
        if cross < (0.0 - epsilon()) { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// =============================================================================
// Validation entry point
// =============================================================================

fn main() with Mut, Panic, IO, Div {
    // Distance
    let a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let b = Point2D { x: 3.0, y: 4.0 }
    let d = distance(a, b)
    // Should be 5.0
    assert(d > 4.99)
    assert(d < 5.01)

    // Distance squared
    let d2 = distance_squared(a, b)
    assert(d2 > 24.99)
    assert(d2 < 25.01)

    // Triangle area: (0,0), (4,0), (0,3) → area = 6.0
    let t1 = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let t2 = Point2D { x: 4.0, y: 0.0 }
    let t3 = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 3.0 }
    let area = triangle_area(t1, t2, t3)
    assert(area > 5.99)
    assert(area < 6.01)

    // Centroid
    let ctr = triangle_centroid(t1, t2, t3)
    assert(ctr.x > 1.32)
    assert(ctr.x < 1.34)
    assert(ctr.y > 0.99)
    assert(ctr.y < 1.01)

    // Line intersection: y=x and y=-x+2 → (1,1)
    let l1a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let l1b = Point2D { x: 2.0, y: 2.0 }
    let l2a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 2.0 }
    let l2b = Point2D { x: 2.0, y: 0.0 }
    let isect = line_intersection(l1a, l1b, l2a, l2b)
    assert(isect.found)
    assert(isect.x > 0.99)
    assert(isect.x < 1.01)
    assert(isect.y > 0.99)
    assert(isect.y < 1.01)

    // Parallel lines — no intersection
    let p1a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let p1b = Point2D { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 }
    let p2a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 }
    let p2b = Point2D { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 }
    let no_isect = line_intersection(p1a, p1b, p2a, p2b)
    assert(no_isect.found == false)

    // Segment intersection (should find)
    let seg_isect = segment_intersection(l1a, l1b, l2a, l2b)
    assert(seg_isect.found)

    // Segment intersection (should NOT find — segments don't reach)
    let s1a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let s1b = Point2D { x: 0.4, y: 0.4 }
    let s2a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 2.0 }
    let s2b = Point2D { x: 2.0, y: 0.0 }
    let no_seg = segment_intersection(s1a, s1b, s2a, s2b)
    assert(no_seg.found == false)

    // Circumcircle of right triangle (0,0),(4,0),(0,3) → center at (2,1.5), r=2.5
    let cc = circumcircle(t1, t2, t3)
    assert(cc.cx > 1.99)
    assert(cc.cx < 2.01)
    assert(cc.cy > 1.49)
    assert(cc.cy < 1.51)
    assert(cc.radius > 2.49)
    assert(cc.radius < 2.51)

    // Convex hull of a square: (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1) + interior point (0.5,0.5)
    var hx: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var hy: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    hx[0] = 0.0; hy[0] = 0.0
    hx[1] = 1.0; hy[1] = 0.0
    hx[2] = 1.0; hy[2] = 1.0
    hx[3] = 0.0; hy[3] = 1.0
    hx[4] = 0.5; hy[4] = 0.5
    var hull_idx: [i32; 64] = [0; 64]
    let hn = convex_hull(&hx, &hy, 5, &!hull_idx)
    // Hull should have 4 vertices (the square corners)
    assert(hn == 4)

    // Point in convex polygon
    var hull_xs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var hull_ys: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    // Build CCW square hull
    hull_xs[0] = 0.0; hull_ys[0] = 0.0
    hull_xs[1] = 1.0; hull_ys[1] = 0.0
    hull_xs[2] = 1.0; hull_ys[2] = 1.0
    hull_xs[3] = 0.0; hull_ys[3] = 1.0
    let inside = Point2D { x: 0.5, y: 0.5 }
    let outside = Point2D { x: 2.0, y: 2.0 }
    assert(point_in_convex_polygon(inside, &hull_xs, &hull_ys, 4))
    assert(point_in_convex_polygon(outside, &hull_xs, &hull_ys, 4) == false)

    // Point-line distance: point (1,1) to x-axis → distance 1.0
    let pl = Point2D { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 }
    let la = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let lb = Point2D { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 }
    let pld = point_line_distance(pl, la, lb)
    assert(pld > 0.99)
    assert(pld < 1.01)

    return
}


// === FILE: stdlib/geometry/information.sio ===
// stdlib/geometry/information.sio — Information Geometry on Statistical Manifolds
//
// Fisher-Rao metric, natural gradient, geodesics on manifolds of probability
// distributions. The correct geometry for optimization on parameter spaces.
//
// SOTA: GSI 2025 (Saint-Malo): "From Classical to Quantum Information Geometry"
//       Geomstats (2023-2025): Computations on manifolds
//       Amari (2016): "Information Geometry and Its Applications"
//
// Theory:
//   A statistical model {p(x|theta)} is a manifold M with coordinates theta.
//   The Fisher information matrix g_ij(theta) = E[d_i log p * d_j log p]
//   defines a Riemannian metric. The natural gradient is:
//     grad_nat = g^{-1} * grad_euclidean
//   which gives the steepest descent direction ON THE MANIFOLD.
//
// Why it matters:
//   Euclidean gradient descent on probability distributions is WRONG.
//   It treats the parameter space as flat, but probability distributions
//   live on curved manifolds. Natural gradient respects the geometry.

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers
// =============================================================================

fn abs_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn sqrt_val(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn ln_val(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e_val = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e_val = e_val + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e_val = e_val - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e_val as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn exp_val(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2_c = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = x / ln2_c
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2_c
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 { var i = 0; while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    else { var i = 0; while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Statistical Manifold
// =============================================================================

// A point on a statistical manifold with its Fisher information matrix
struct StatisticalManifold {
    params: [f64; 16],              // manifold coordinates (max 16 parameters)
    n_params: i32,
    fisher: [f64; 256],             // Fisher information matrix (16x16 max)
}

fn manifold_new(n: i32) -> StatisticalManifold {
    StatisticalManifold {
        params: [0.0; 16],
        n_params: n,
        fisher: [0.0; 256],
    }
}

// Access Fisher matrix element
fn fisher_get(m: &StatisticalManifold, i: i32, j: i32) -> f64 with Panic {
    m.fisher[i * m.n_params + j]
}

fn fisher_set(m: &!StatisticalManifold, i: i32, j: i32, val: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    m.fisher[i * m.n_params + j] = val
}

// =============================================================================
// Fisher Information for Common Distributions
// =============================================================================

// Normal distribution: theta = (mu, sigma)
// Fisher matrix: [[1/sigma^2, 0], [0, 2/sigma^2]]
fn fisher_normal(mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> StatisticalManifold with Mut, Panic {
    var m = manifold_new(2)
    m.params[0] = mu
    m.params[1] = sigma
    let s2 = sigma * sigma
    // F[0,0] = 1/sigma^2, F[0,1] = 0, F[1,0] = 0, F[1,1] = 2/sigma^2
    m.fisher[0] = 1.0 / s2
    m.fisher[1] = 0.0
    m.fisher[2] = 0.0
    m.fisher[3] = 2.0 / s2
    return m
}

// Exponential distribution: theta = lambda
// Fisher matrix: [[1/lambda^2]]
fn fisher_exponential(lambda: f64) -> StatisticalManifold with Mut, Panic {
    var m = manifold_new(1)
    m.params[0] = lambda
    m.fisher[0] = 1.0 / (lambda * lambda)
    return m
}

// Bernoulli distribution: theta = p
// Fisher matrix: [[1/(p*(1-p))]]
fn fisher_bernoulli(p: f64) -> StatisticalManifold with Mut, Panic {
    var m = manifold_new(1)
    m.params[0] = p
    m.fisher[0] = 1.0 / (p * (1.0 - p))
    return m
}

// Gamma distribution: theta = (alpha, beta)
// Fisher[0,0] = trigamma(alpha), Fisher[1,1] = alpha/beta^2
// Fisher[0,1] = Fisher[1,0] = -1/beta
fn fisher_gamma(alpha: f64, beta_param: f64) -> StatisticalManifold with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m = manifold_new(2)
    m.params[0] = alpha
    m.params[1] = beta_param

    // Trigamma approximation: psi_1(x) ~ 1/x + 1/(2x^2) + 1/(6x^3) - ...
    var tx = alpha
    var shift: f64 = 0.0
    while tx < 8.0 { shift = shift + 1.0 / (tx * tx); tx = tx + 1.0 }
    let inv_t = 1.0 / tx
    let trigamma = inv_t + 0.5 * inv_t * inv_t + inv_t * inv_t * inv_t / 6.0 + shift

    m.fisher[0] = trigamma
    m.fisher[1] = 0.0 - 1.0 / beta_param
    m.fisher[2] = 0.0 - 1.0 / beta_param
    m.fisher[3] = alpha / (beta_param * beta_param)
    return m
}

// =============================================================================
// Natural Gradient
// =============================================================================
// g_nat = F^{-1} * g_euclidean
// For optimization on manifolds, this is the correct gradient direction.

// 2x2 matrix inverse (covers Normal, Gamma, etc.)
fn fisher_inverse_2x2(m: &StatisticalManifold) -> [f64; 4] with Mut, Panic {
    let a = m.fisher[0]
    let b = m.fisher[1]
    let c = m.fisher[2]
    let d = m.fisher[3]
    let det = a * d - b * c
    var inv: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
    inv[0] = d / det
    inv[1] = (0.0 - b) / det
    inv[2] = (0.0 - c) / det
    inv[3] = a / det
    return inv
}

// Natural gradient for 2-parameter manifold
fn natural_gradient_2d(
    m: &StatisticalManifold,
    euclidean_grad: &[f64; 2],
) -> [f64; 2] with Panic, Mut {
    let inv = fisher_inverse_2x2(m)
    var nat_grad: [f64; 2] = [0.0; 2]
    nat_grad[0] = inv[0] * euclidean_grad[0] + inv[1] * euclidean_grad[1]
    nat_grad[1] = inv[2] * euclidean_grad[0] + inv[3] * euclidean_grad[1]
    return nat_grad
}

// General natural gradient via Cholesky solve (for n_params <= 16)
fn natural_gradient(
    m: &StatisticalManifold,
    euclidean_grad: &[f64; 16],
    result: &![f64; 16],
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = m.n_params

    // Cholesky decomposition: F = L * L^T
    var lower: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j <= i {
            var sum: f64 = 0.0
            if i == j {
                var k = 0
                while k < j {
                    let l_jk = lower[j * n + k]
                    sum = sum + l_jk * l_jk
                    k = k + 1
                }
                lower[j * n + j] = sqrt_val(m.fisher[j * n + j] - sum)
            } else {
                var k = 0
                while k < j {
                    sum = sum + lower[i * n + k] * lower[j * n + k]
                    k = k + 1
                }
                lower[i * n + j] = (m.fisher[i * n + j] - sum) / lower[j * n + j]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Forward substitution: L * y = g
    var y: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var s: f64 = 0.0
        var k = 0
        while k < i { s = s + lower[i * n + k] * y[k]; k = k + 1 }
        y[i] = (euclidean_grad[i] - s) / lower[i * n + i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Back substitution: L^T * x = y
    i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var s: f64 = 0.0
        var k = i + 1
        while k < n { s = s + lower[k * n + i] * result[k]; k = k + 1 }
        result[i] = (y[i] - s) / lower[i * n + i]
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// KL Divergence via Fisher Metric (local approximation)
// =============================================================================
// KL(p_theta || p_{theta+d}) ~ 0.5 * d^T * F * d
// Valid for small perturbations d

fn fisher_kl_local(
    m: &StatisticalManifold,
    delta: &[f64; 16],
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = m.n_params
    var kl: f64 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            kl = kl + delta[i] * m.fisher[i * n + j] * delta[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0.5 * kl
}

// =============================================================================
// Geodesic Distance (approximate via shooting)
// =============================================================================
// Geodesic equation: d^2 theta^k / dt^2 + Gamma^k_{ij} dtheta^i/dt dtheta^j/dt = 0
// We approximate via the local Fisher metric: d ~ sqrt(delta^T F delta)

fn fisher_distance(
    m1: &StatisticalManifold,
    m2: &StatisticalManifold,
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var delta: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < m1.n_params {
        delta[i] = m2.params[i] - m1.params[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Use m1's Fisher metric as the local metric
    let kl_sq = fisher_kl_local(m1, &delta)
    sqrt_val(2.0 * kl_sq)
}

// =============================================================================
// Natural Gradient Descent Step
// =============================================================================

fn natural_gradient_step(
    m: &!StatisticalManifold,
    euclidean_grad: &[f64; 16],
    learning_rate: f64,
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var nat_grad: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    natural_gradient(m, euclidean_grad, &!nat_grad)
    var i = 0
    while i < m.n_params {
        m.params[i] = m.params[i] - learning_rate * nat_grad[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

//! stdlib/geometry - Neuro-symbolic Geometry Reasoning
