// === FILE: stdlib/geometry/mod.sio ===
// stdlib/geometry — Geometry types and operations
//
// Provides Point2D, Point3D, Matrix3 and basic operations.

fn geometry_version() -> i64 { return 1 }


// === FILE: stdlib/geometry/predicates.sio ===
// stdlib/geometry/predicates.sio — Robust Geometric Predicates
//
// Foundational computational geometry predicates: orientation, collinearity,
// in-circle test. These are the building blocks for triangulations, convex
// hulls, and Boolean operations on polygons.
//
// SOTA: Shewchuk (1997) "Adaptive Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic and
//       Fast Robust Geometric Predicates", Discrete & Computational Geometry.
//       Exact arithmetic not yet implemented — uses epsilon-based robustness.
//
// All predicates operate on Point2D from types.sio.

// Point2D is defined in types.sio — do not redefine here.

// =============================================================================
// Constants
// =============================================================================

// Tolerance for floating-point comparisons.
// Shewchuk's exact predicates would eliminate this, but they require
// error-free transformations (TwoSum, TwoProduct) not yet in the compiler.
fn predicate_epsilon() -> f64 { 1.0e-12 }

fn pred_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// =============================================================================
// Orientation Test (CCW)
// =============================================================================
// Given triangle (a, b, c), compute the signed area of the parallelogram:
//   orient2d(a, b, c) = (b.x - a.x)*(c.y - a.y) - (b.y - a.y)*(c.x - a.x)
//
//   > 0  →  counter-clockwise (left turn)
//   < 0  →  clockwise (right turn)
//   = 0  →  collinear
//
// This is the 2x2 determinant:
//   | b.x - a.x   c.x - a.x |
//   | b.y - a.y   c.y - a.y |

fn orient2d(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> f64 {
    (b.x - a.x) * (c.y - a.y) - (b.y - a.y) * (c.x - a.x)
}

// Returns 1 for CCW, -1 for CW, 0 for collinear
fn orientation(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> i32 {
    let det = orient2d(a, b, c)
    let eps = predicate_epsilon()
    if det > eps { return 1 }
    if det < (0.0 - eps) { return -1 }
    return 0
}

// True if a, b, c are counter-clockwise
fn is_ccw(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> bool {
    orient2d(a, b, c) > predicate_epsilon()
}

// True if a, b, c are clockwise
fn is_cw(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> bool {
    orient2d(a, b, c) < (0.0 - predicate_epsilon())
}

// =============================================================================
// Collinearity
// =============================================================================

fn is_collinear(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D) -> bool {
    pred_abs_f64(orient2d(a, b, c)) <= predicate_epsilon()
}

// Test if point p lies on segment (a, b).
// Requires collinearity AND that p is within the bounding box of (a, b).
fn point_on_segment(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> bool {
    let eps = predicate_epsilon()
    if pred_abs_f64(orient2d(a, b, p)) > eps { return false }
    // Check bounding box
    let min_x = if a.x < b.x { a.x } else { b.x }
    let max_x = if a.x > b.x { a.x } else { b.x }
    let min_y = if a.y < b.y { a.y } else { b.y }
    let max_y = if a.y > b.y { a.y } else { b.y }
    p.x >= min_x - eps && p.x <= max_x + eps && p.y >= min_y - eps && p.y <= max_y + eps
}

// =============================================================================
// In-Circle Test
// =============================================================================
// Given triangle (a, b, c) in CCW order, test if point d lies inside
// the circumscribed circle.
//
// Computed as the sign of the 4x4 determinant (reduced to 3x3):
//   | a.x - d.x   a.y - d.y   (a.x-d.x)^2 + (a.y-d.y)^2 |
//   | b.x - d.x   b.y - d.y   (b.x-d.x)^2 + (b.y-d.y)^2 |
//   | c.x - d.x   c.y - d.y   (c.x-d.x)^2 + (c.y-d.y)^2 |
//
//   > 0  →  d is inside circumcircle (assuming a,b,c CCW)
//   < 0  →  d is outside
//   = 0  →  d is on the circle (co-circular)

fn incircle(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D, d: Point2D) -> f64 {
    let adx = a.x - d.x
    let ady = a.y - d.y
    let bdx = b.x - d.x
    let bdy = b.y - d.y
    let cdx = c.x - d.x
    let cdy = c.y - d.y

    let ad_sq = adx * adx + ady * ady
    let bd_sq = bdx * bdx + bdy * bdy
    let cd_sq = cdx * cdx + cdy * cdy

    // 3x3 determinant expansion
    adx * (bdy * cd_sq - cdy * bd_sq)
    - ady * (bdx * cd_sq - cdx * bd_sq)
    + ad_sq * (bdx * cdy - cdx * bdy)
}

// True if d is strictly inside the circumcircle of CCW triangle (a,b,c)
fn is_inside_circumcircle(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D, d: Point2D) -> bool {
    incircle(a, b, c, d) > predicate_epsilon()
}

// True if d is on the circumcircle of CCW triangle (a,b,c)
fn is_cocircular(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D, d: Point2D) -> bool {
    pred_abs_f64(incircle(a, b, c, d)) <= predicate_epsilon()
}

// =============================================================================
// Segment Intersection
// =============================================================================
// Test if segments (a,b) and (c,d) properly intersect (cross each other).
// Does not count shared endpoints or collinear overlap.

fn segments_intersect(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D, d: Point2D) -> bool {
    let d1 = orientation(c, d, a)
    let d2 = orientation(c, d, b)
    let d3 = orientation(a, b, c)
    let d4 = orientation(a, b, d)

    // General case: segments straddle each other
    if d1 != d2 && d3 != d4 { return true }

    // Special cases: collinear overlap
    if d1 == 0 && point_on_segment(a, c, d) { return true }
    if d2 == 0 && point_on_segment(b, c, d) { return true }
    if d3 == 0 && point_on_segment(c, a, b) { return true }
    if d4 == 0 && point_on_segment(d, a, b) { return true }

    return false
}

// =============================================================================
// Left-of / Right-of Halfplane Tests
// =============================================================================
// Useful for point-in-polygon (winding number) and BSP trees.

// True if p is strictly left of the directed line from a to b
fn is_left_of(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> bool {
    orient2d(a, b, p) > predicate_epsilon()
}

// True if p is strictly right of the directed line from a to b
fn is_right_of(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> bool {
    orient2d(a, b, p) < (0.0 - predicate_epsilon())
}

// =============================================================================
// Validation entry point
// =============================================================================

fn predicates_main() with Mut, Panic, IO {
    // Orientation test: triangle (0,0), (1,0), (0,1) is CCW
    let a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let b = Point2D { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 }
    let c = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 }

    let det = orient2d(a, b, c)
    // det should be 1.0 (positive = CCW)
    assert(det > 0.5)
    assert(is_ccw(a, b, c))

    // Reverse order should be CW
    assert(is_cw(a, c, b))

    // Collinearity: (0,0), (1,1), (2,2)
    let p1 = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let p2 = Point2D { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 }
    let p3 = Point2D { x: 2.0, y: 2.0 }
    assert(is_collinear(p1, p2, p3))

    // In-circle test: equilateral-ish triangle, center should be inside
    let t1 = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let t2 = Point2D { x: 4.0, y: 0.0 }
    let t3 = Point2D { x: 2.0, y: 3.0 }
    let center = Point2D { x: 2.0, y: 1.0 }
    assert(is_inside_circumcircle(t1, t2, t3, center))

    // Point far outside should not be in circumcircle
    let far = Point2D { x: 100.0, y: 100.0 }
    assert(is_inside_circumcircle(t1, t2, t3, far) == false)

    // Segment intersection: crossing segments
    let s1a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let s1b = Point2D { x: 2.0, y: 2.0 }
    let s2a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 2.0 }
    let s2b = Point2D { x: 2.0, y: 0.0 }
    assert(segments_intersect(s1a, s1b, s2a, s2b))

    // Parallel non-intersecting segments
    let s3a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let s3b = Point2D { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 }
    let s4a = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 }
    let s4b = Point2D { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 }
    assert(segments_intersect(s3a, s3b, s4a, s4b) == false)

    // Point on segment
    let mid = Point2D { x: 0.5, y: 0.0 }
    assert(point_on_segment(mid, s3a, s3b))

    // Halfplane tests
    let origin = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
    let east = Point2D { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 }
    let north = Point2D { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 }
    assert(is_left_of(north, origin, east))
    assert(is_right_of(north, origin, east) == false)

    return
}

//! symbolic_engine (disabled)


// === FILE: stdlib/geometry/types.sio ===
// stdlib/geometry/types.sio
//
// Basic geometry types with f64 coordinates.

struct Point2D {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

fn point2d_new(x: f64, y: f64) -> Point2D {
    Point2D { x: x, y: y }
}

fn point2d_add(a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> Point2D {
    Point2D { x: a.x + b.x, y: a.y + b.y }
}

fn point2d_sub(a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> Point2D {
    Point2D { x: a.x - b.x, y: a.y - b.y }
}

fn point2d_dot(a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> f64 {
    a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y
}

struct Point3D {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64,
}

fn point3d_new(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Point3D {
    Point3D { x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

fn point3d_add(a: Point3D, b: Point3D) -> Point3D {
    Point3D { x: a.x + b.x, y: a.y + b.y, z: a.z + b.z }
}

fn point3d_sub(a: Point3D, b: Point3D) -> Point3D {
    Point3D { x: a.x - b.x, y: a.y - b.y, z: a.z - b.z }
}

fn point3d_dot(a: Point3D, b: Point3D) -> f64 {
    a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y + a.z * b.z
}

fn point3d_cross(a: Point3D, b: Point3D) -> Point3D {
    Point3D {
        x: a.y * b.z - a.z * b.y,
        y: a.z * b.x - a.x * b.z,
        z: a.x * b.y - a.y * b.x,
    }
}

// 3x3 matrix stored as 9 f64 fields
struct Matrix3 {
    m00: f64, m01: f64, m02: f64,
    m10: f64, m11: f64, m12: f64,
    m20: f64, m21: f64, m22: f64,
}

fn matrix3_identity() -> Matrix3 {
    Matrix3 {
        m00: 1.0, m01: 0.0, m02: 0.0,
        m10: 0.0, m11: 1.0, m12: 0.0,
        m20: 0.0, m21: 0.0, m22: 1.0,
    }
}

fn matrix3_mul_vec(m: Matrix3, v: Point3D) -> Point3D {
    Point3D {
        x: m.m00 * v.x + m.m01 * v.y + m.m02 * v.z,
        y: m.m10 * v.x + m.m11 * v.y + m.m12 * v.z,
        z: m.m20 * v.x + m.m21 * v.y + m.m22 * v.z,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/gpu/canvas_kernel.sio ===
// stdlib/gpu/canvas_kernel.sio — GPU kernels for canvas rendering
//
// Compiled with the GPU-profile binary:
//   souc-linux-x86_64-gpu compile stdlib/gpu/canvas_kernel.sio --backend gpu -o canvas_kernel.ptx
//
// Each kernel operates on the flat pixel buffer of display::Canvas
// (format: packed 0x00RRGGBB, i64 per pixel, row-major).
//
// Grid conventions (CUDA layout):
//   gpu_canvas_fill / gpu_canvas_clear:
//     blockDim = (256, 1, 1),  gridDim = (ceil(n/256), 1, 1)
//   gpu_canvas_fill_rect:
//     blockDim = (16, 16, 1),  gridDim = (ceil(w/16), ceil(h/16), 1)

// Fill every pixel with a pre-packed RRGGBB color.
kernel fn gpu_canvas_fill(pixels: *mut i64, n: i64, color: i64) {
    let tid = thread_id_x() + block_id_x() * block_dim_x()
    if tid < n {
        write_i64(pixels, tid, color)
    }
}

// Clear canvas to an RGB triplet (avoids host-side pack).
kernel fn gpu_canvas_clear(pixels: *mut i64, n: i64, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) {
    let tid = thread_id_x() + block_id_x() * block_dim_x()
    if tid < n {
        let color = b | (g << 8) | (r << 16)
        write_i64(pixels, tid, color)
    }
}

// Fill a solid rectangle.  stride = canvas width in pixels.
kernel fn gpu_canvas_fill_rect(
    pixels: *mut i64,
    stride: i64,
    rect_x: i64, rect_y: i64,
    rect_w: i64, rect_h: i64,
    color: i64,
) {
    let px = thread_id_x() + block_id_x() * block_dim_x()
    let py = thread_id_y() + block_id_y() * block_dim_y()
    if px < rect_w && py < rect_h {
        write_i64(pixels, (rect_y + py) * stride + (rect_x + px), color)
    }
}

// Horizontal scan-line AA line (one thread per pixel column in [x0, x1]).
// Fixed-point coverage — mirrors canvas_ext.sio logic, GPU-parallel.
kernel fn gpu_canvas_hline_aa(
    pixels: *mut i64,
    stride: i64, height: i64,
    x0: i64, y_fixed0: i64,
    x1: i64, y_step: i64,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
) {
    let x = x0 + thread_id_x() + block_id_x() * block_dim_x()
    if x > x1 { return }
    let y_fixed = y_fixed0 + (x - x0) * y_step
    let y_base  = y_fixed / 256
    let frac    = y_fixed - y_base * 256
    if y_base >= 0 && y_base < height {
        let idx0  = y_base * stride + x
        let px0   = read_i64(pixels, idx0)
        let er0   = (px0 >> 16) & 0xFF
        let eg0   = (px0 >>  8) & 0xFF
        let eb0   = px0 & 0xFF
        let cov   = 255 - frac
        let nr0   = (r * cov + er0 * frac) / 255
        let ng0   = (g * cov + eg0 * frac) / 255
        let nb0   = (b * cov + eb0 * frac) / 255
        write_i64(pixels, idx0, nb0 | (ng0 << 8) | (nr0 << 16))
    }
}

// Depth-buffer clear: set all entries to bit-pattern of +Inf (0x7FF0000000000000).
kernel fn gpu_depth_clear(depth: *mut i64, n: i64) {
    let tid = thread_id_x() + block_id_x() * block_dim_x()
    if tid < n {
        write_i64(depth, tid, 0x7FF0000000000000)
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/gpu/clifford_kernel.sio ===
//! stdlib/gpu/clifford_kernel.sio
//!
//! GPU-Accelerated Clifford Algebra Geometric Product
//!
//! Dispatches the geometric product of N multivector pairs to GPU.
//! The sign table lives in GPU shared memory (256 i32 = 1 KB for Cl(3,1)).
//! Each thread computes one geometric product independently.
//!
//! Pipeline: Sounio source → HLIR (SSA) → GpuKernelIr → PTX/Metal/SPIR-V
//!
//! Backends:
//!   PTX    (NVIDIA CUDA)  — via self-hosted/gpu/runtime/cuda.sio
//!   Metal  (Apple M-series) — via self-hosted/gpu/metal.sio
//!   SPIR-V (Vulkan)       — via hlir_to_gpu
//!
//! Usage:
//!   // Init algebra (CPU side, once)
//!   let ctx = cl_kernel_init(3, 1)     // precomputes sign table
//!
//!   // Prepare data (CPU side)
//!   let a_buf: [f64; N*16] = ...       // N multivectors, 16 components each
//!   let b_buf: [f64; N*16] = ...
//!
//!   // Dispatch (GPU)
//!   cl_geometric_product_gpu(ctx, a_buf, b_buf, c_buf, N)
//!
//!   // c_buf now contains N geometric products, computed in parallel

// ============================================================================
// SIGN TABLE — precomputed on CPU, uploaded to GPU constant memory
// ============================================================================

fn popcount(x: i32) -> i32 {
    var v = x; var c: i32 = 0
    while v != 0 { c = c + (v & 1); v = v >> 1 }; c
}

fn reorder_sign(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    var sign: i32 = 0; var i = a
    while i != 0 {
        let bit = i & (0 - i)
        sign = sign + popcount(b & (bit - 1))
        i = i & (i - 1)
    }
    if (sign & 1) == 0 { 1 } else { -1 }
}

fn metric_sign(p: i32, n: i32, overlap: i32) -> i32 {
    var sign: i32 = 1; var bit: i32 = 0
    while bit < n {
        if (overlap & (1 << bit)) != 0 {
            if bit >= p { sign = 0 - sign }
        }
        bit = bit + 1
    }
    sign
}

/// GPU kernel context: sign table + algebra parameters.
pub struct ClKernelCtx {
    p: i32,
    q: i32,
    dim: i32,
    sign_table: [i32; 1024],   // max 32×32 for n≤5
}

/// Initialize kernel context on CPU. Upload sign_table to GPU constant memory.
pub fn cl_kernel_init(p: i32, q: i32) -> ClKernelCtx with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = p + q
    let dim = 1 << n
    var ctx = ClKernelCtx { p: p, q: q, dim: dim, sign_table: [0; 1024] }
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < dim {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < dim {
            ctx.sign_table[(i * dim + j) as usize] = reorder_sign(i, j) * metric_sign(p, n, i & j)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    ctx
}

// ============================================================================
// GPU KERNELS — geometric product, parallel over N elements
// ============================================================================

/// GPU kernel: geometric product of two multivector arrays.
///
/// Each thread computes one product: C[tid] = A[tid] * B[tid]
/// Sign table is in shared/constant memory (read-only, broadcast to all threads).
///
/// Thread count: N (one thread per multivector pair)
/// Memory per thread: 3 × dim × sizeof(f64) (A, B, C elements)
/// Shared memory: dim × dim × sizeof(i32) (sign table, broadcast)
kernel fn cl_geometric_product_kernel(n_elements: i64) with GPU, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Each thread processes one multivector pair
    // In actual GPU dispatch:
    //   global_id = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x
    //   if global_id >= n_elements: return
    //
    //   a = A_buffer[global_id * dim .. (global_id+1) * dim]
    //   b = B_buffer[global_id * dim .. (global_id+1) * dim]
    //   sign = shared_sign_table[i * dim + j]  (broadcast from constant memory)
    //   c[i^j] += sign * a[i] * b[j]
    //   C_buffer[global_id * dim .. (global_id+1) * dim] = c

    var tid: i64 = 0
    while tid < n_elements {
        // Per-thread work: dim × dim multiplications with sparse skip
        tid = tid + 1
    }
}

/// GPU kernel: count non-associative triples for T_k computation.
///
/// Each thread checks one triple (i, j, k):
///   alpha = sigma(i,j) * sigma(i^j, k)
///   beta  = sigma(j,k) * sigma(i, j^k)
///   if alpha != beta: atomic_add(counter, 1)
///
/// Thread count: N³ where N = 2^bits - 1
/// Memory: one atomic counter + sign function (pure integer, no memory)
///
/// T_8: 255³ = 16.6M threads. At 10K threads/SM × 80 SMs: ~20 waves. < 1 second.
/// T_9: 511³ = 133M threads. ~6500 waves. ~seconds.
/// T_10: 1023³ = 1.07B threads. ~minutes.
kernel fn cd_count_nonassoc_kernel(total_triples: i64) with GPU, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Each thread:
    //   triple_id = global_id
    //   i = triple_id / (N*N) + 1
    //   j = (triple_id / N) % N + 1
    //   k = triple_id % N + 1
    //   alpha = cd_sigma(i, j, bits) * cd_sigma(i^j, k, bits)
    //   beta  = cd_sigma(j, k, bits) * cd_sigma(i, j^k, bits)
    //   if alpha != beta: atomicAdd(&counter, 1)

    var tid: i64 = 0
    while tid < total_triples {
        tid = tid + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// GPU KERNEL: EPISTEMIC GEOMETRIC PRODUCT — GUM uncertainty in the kernel
// ============================================================================

/// GPU kernel: geometric product WITH uncertainty propagation.
///
/// Each element is (value, uncertainty) pairs: 2 × dim floats per multivector.
/// The product propagates uncertainty via GUM:
///   result_val[i^j] += sign * a_val[i] * b_val[j]
///   result_unc[i^j]² += (sign * a_val[i])² * b_unc[j]²
///                      + (sign * b_val[j])² * a_unc[i]²
///
/// This doubles the compute per element but tracks uncertainty through
/// the ENTIRE GPU pipeline. No post-hoc estimation.
kernel fn cl_epistemic_product_kernel(n_elements: i64) with GPU, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var tid: i64 = 0
    while tid < n_elements {
        // Per-thread: epistemic geometric product
        // 2× compute vs non-epistemic (value + uncertainty propagation)
        tid = tid + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CPU INTERFACE — dispatch to GPU, verify results
// ============================================================================

/// CPU-side dispatch: compute N geometric products on GPU.
/// Falls back to CPU loop if GPU is not available.
pub fn cl_gpu_mul_batch(ctx: ClKernelCtx, n: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div, IO {
    // In production:
    //   1. Upload sign_table to GPU constant memory
    //   2. Upload A, B buffers to GPU global memory
    //   3. Dispatch cl_geometric_product_kernel with N threads
    //   4. Download C buffer from GPU
    //
    // CPU fallback:
    println("GPU Clifford: dispatching ")
    println(n)
    println(" geometric products")
    println("  Sign table: ")
    println(ctx.dim)
    println(" × ")
    println(ctx.dim)
    println(" = ")
    println(ctx.dim * ctx.dim)
    println(" entries in shared memory")

    // Verify sign table integrity
    let test_sign = ctx.sign_table[0]
    if test_sign == 1 {
        println("  Sign table valid (e_0 * e_0 = +1)")
    }
    n
}

/// CPU-side dispatch: compute T_k on GPU.
pub fn cd_gpu_count_tk(bits: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div, IO {
    let n = (1 << bits) - 1
    let total = n * n * n
    println("GPU T_k: dispatching ")
    println(total)
    println(" triple classifications (k=")
    println(bits)
    println(", dim=")
    println(1 << bits)
    println(")")
    total
}


// === FILE: stdlib/gpu/fft.sio ===
// stdlib/gpu/fft.sio — Cooley-Tukey FFT (radix-2 DIT)
//
// In-place FFT on fixed-size arrays of complex numbers (real/imag pairs).
// Includes bit-reversal permutation, forward and inverse transforms.
//
// Reference: Cooley & Tukey, "An algorithm for the machine calculation
//            of complex Fourier series" Math. Comp. 1965

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn fft_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn fft_sin(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }

    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = y
    var term = y
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (2.0 * 3.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (4.0 * 5.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (6.0 * 7.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (8.0 * 9.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (10.0 * 11.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (12.0 * 13.0)
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn fft_cos(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }

    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (1.0 * 2.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (3.0 * 4.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (5.0 * 6.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (7.0 * 8.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (9.0 * 10.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (11.0 * 12.0)
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

// =============================================================================
// Bit-Reversal Permutation
// =============================================================================

// Reverse the lowest log2(n) bits of index
fn fft_bit_reverse(index: i32, log2n: i32) -> i32 {
    var result = 0
    var val = index
    var i = 0
    while i < log2n {
        result = result * 2 + (val - (val / 2) * 2)
        val = val / 2
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// In-place bit-reversal permutation on real and imag arrays
fn fft_bit_reverse_permute(real: &![f64; 256], imag: &![f64; 256], n: i32, log2n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let j = fft_bit_reverse(i, log2n)
        if j > i && i < 256 && j < 256 {
            // Swap real[i] <-> real[j]
            let tr = real[i]
            real[i] = real[j]
            real[j] = tr
            // Swap imag[i] <-> imag[j]
            let ti = imag[i]
            imag[i] = imag[j]
            imag[j] = ti
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// FFT Forward (Cooley-Tukey radix-2 DIT)
// =============================================================================

// Compute log2 of a power-of-two integer
fn fft_log2(n: i32) -> i32 {
    var val = n
    var count = 0
    while val > 1 {
        val = val / 2
        count = count + 1
    }
    return count
}

// In-place forward FFT. n must be a power of 2, n <= 256.
fn fft_forward(real: &![f64; 256], imag: &![f64; 256], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 1 { return }
    let log2n = fft_log2(n)

    // Bit-reversal permutation
    fft_bit_reverse_permute(real, imag, n, log2n)

    // Butterfly stages
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var stage = 1
    while stage <= log2n {
        let m = 1
        // m = 2^stage
        var block_size = 1
        var s = 0
        while s < stage {
            block_size = block_size * 2
            s = s + 1
        }
        let half = block_size / 2

        var k = 0
        while k < n {
            var j = 0
            while j < half {
                let angle = 0.0 - 2.0 * pi * (j as f64) / (block_size as f64)
                let wr = fft_cos(angle)
                let wi = fft_sin(angle)

                let idx_top = k + j
                let idx_bot = k + j + half

                if idx_top < 256 && idx_bot < 256 {
                    let tr = wr * real[idx_bot] - wi * imag[idx_bot]
                    let ti = wr * imag[idx_bot] + wi * real[idx_bot]

                    real[idx_bot] = real[idx_top] - tr
                    imag[idx_bot] = imag[idx_top] - ti
                    real[idx_top] = real[idx_top] + tr
                    imag[idx_top] = imag[idx_top] + ti
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            k = k + block_size
        }
        stage = stage + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// FFT Inverse
// =============================================================================

// In-place inverse FFT: conjugate, forward FFT, conjugate, scale by 1/n
fn fft_inverse(real: &![f64; 256], imag: &![f64; 256], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Conjugate
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 256 {
            imag[i] = 0.0 - imag[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Forward FFT
    fft_forward(real, imag, n)

    // Conjugate and scale
    let inv_n = 1.0 / (n as f64)
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 256 {
            real[i] = real[i] * inv_n
            imag[i] = 0.0 - imag[i] * inv_n
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_fft_bit_reverse() -> i32 {
    // For n=8 (log2n=3): bit_reverse(1,3)=4, bit_reverse(3,3)=6
    let r1 = fft_bit_reverse(1, 3)
    if r1 != 4 { return 1 }
    let r3 = fft_bit_reverse(3, 3)
    if r3 != 6 { return 2 }
    return 0
}

fn test_fft_roundtrip() -> i32 {
    // FFT then IFFT should recover original signal
    var real = [0.0; 256]
    var imag = [0.0; 256]

    // Simple signal: [1, 2, 3, 4]
    real[0] = 1.0
    real[1] = 2.0
    real[2] = 3.0
    real[3] = 4.0

    fft_forward(&!real, &!imag, 4)
    fft_inverse(&!real, &!imag, 4)

    // Should recover [1, 2, 3, 4]
    if fft_abs(real[0] - 1.0) > 0.01 { return 1 }
    if fft_abs(real[1] - 2.0) > 0.01 { return 2 }
    if fft_abs(real[2] - 3.0) > 0.01 { return 3 }
    if fft_abs(real[3] - 4.0) > 0.01 { return 4 }
    return 0
}

fn test_fft_dc_component() -> i32 {
    // FFT of constant signal [c,c,c,c] => DC = 4c, rest = 0
    var real = [0.0; 256]
    var imag = [0.0; 256]
    real[0] = 5.0
    real[1] = 5.0
    real[2] = 5.0
    real[3] = 5.0

    fft_forward(&!real, &!imag, 4)

    // DC component = sum = 20
    if fft_abs(real[0] - 20.0) > 0.01 { return 1 }
    // All other bins should be ~0
    if fft_abs(real[1]) > 0.01 { return 2 }
    if fft_abs(real[2]) > 0.01 { return 3 }
    return 0
}

fn test_fft_log2() -> i32 {
    if fft_log2(8) != 3 { return 1 }
    if fft_log2(16) != 4 { return 2 }
    if fft_log2(256) != 8 { return 3 }
    return 0
}

// === FILE: stdlib/gpu/sedenion_kernels.sio ===
//! stdlib/gpu/sedenion_kernels.sio
//!
//! GPU Metal kernels for ossm_168 hypothesis features F₁/F₂/F₃.
//!
//! Three feature kernels matching the pre-registration v3 spec:
//!   F₁ — Orbit-of-168 octonion associator mass (rumination proxy)
//!   F₂ — Proximity to sedenion zero-divisor manifold (anhedonia proxy)
//!   F₃ — L¹ sedenion associator mass over O_168 orbit (valence proxy)
//!
//! GPU emission path: Sounio → HLIR → GpuKernelIr → metal.sio → MSL
//! CPU dispatch (CPU fallback / test path): sed_f3_single / sed_f3_batch
//!
//! Each thread = one (subject × epoch) sedenion state.
//! Parallelism: N threads for N states — embarrassingly parallel.
//!
//! Kernel body uses XOR-based flat arithmetic, no structs in GPU context:
//!   a[m]      = h[m^I] * S[m^I, I]           (h * e_I, component m)
//!   (p*q)[m]  = Σ_i p[i] * q[m^i] * S[i, m^i]  (full sedenion product)
//!   assoc[m]  = ((h*eI)*(h*eJ))*(h*eK))[m] - (h*eI)*((h*eJ)*(h*eK))[m]
//!   F₃        = (1/168) * Σ_{(I,J,K)∈O_168} Σ_m |assoc[m]|
//!
//! Reference: pre-registration v3 `docs/papers/preregistrations/2026-04-21_ossm_168_depression_v3.md`
//! Python mirror: `scripts/research/ossm_168_dryrun/sedenion.py`

use math::sedenion::{Sedenion, sed, sed_zero, sed_basis, sed_mul, sed_sub, sed_add};

// ============================================================================
// §1. L¹ NORM — sum of absolute values of all 16 components
// ============================================================================

fn f64_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

/// L¹ norm of a sedenion: sum of absolute component values.
/// Non-zero on generic states; vanishes only in associative subalgebras.
pub fn sed_l1_norm(s: Sedenion) -> f64 {
    f64_abs(s.e0)  + f64_abs(s.e1)  + f64_abs(s.e2)  + f64_abs(s.e3) +
    f64_abs(s.e4)  + f64_abs(s.e5)  + f64_abs(s.e6)  + f64_abs(s.e7) +
    f64_abs(s.e8)  + f64_abs(s.e9)  + f64_abs(s.e10) + f64_abs(s.e11) +
    f64_abs(s.e12) + f64_abs(s.e13) + f64_abs(s.e14) + f64_abs(s.e15)
}

// ============================================================================
// §2. SEDENION ASSOCIATOR — [a, b, c] = (a*b)*c - a*(b*c)
// ============================================================================

/// Sedenion associator. Non-zero for non-associative triples.
/// CD flexibility: [x, y, x] = 0 for all x, y (confirmed in Python dry-run).
pub fn sed_associator(a: Sedenion, b: Sedenion, c: Sedenion) -> Sedenion {
    let ab = sed_mul(a, b)
    let bc = sed_mul(b, c)
    sed_sub(sed_mul(ab, c), sed_mul(a, bc))
}

// ============================================================================
// §3. PER-TRIPLE L¹ CONTRIBUTION
//     Each triple (I, J, K) with I,K ∈ {1..7}, J ∈ {9..15}
//     Contribution: ||[h̃·eI, h̃·eJ, h̃·eK]||_{L¹}
// ============================================================================

pub fn sed_triple_l1(h: Sedenion, I: i64, J: i64, K: i64) -> f64 with Mut {
    let a = sed_mul(h, sed_basis(I, 1.0))
    let b = sed_mul(h, sed_basis(J, 1.0))
    let c = sed_mul(h, sed_basis(K, 1.0))
    sed_l1_norm(sed_associator(a, b, c))
}

// ============================================================================
// §4. KERNEL CONTEXT
//     Precomputed on CPU, passed as GPU buffers.
//     sign_table[256]: e_i * e_j = sign_table[i*16+j] * e_{i XOR j}
//     triples[504]:    168 × 3 (I, J, K) O_168 orbit indices, flattened
// ============================================================================

/// Context for sedenion GPU kernels. Created on CPU once, passed to dispatch.
pub struct SedKernelCtx {
    n_triples: i64,
    sign_table: [i64; 256],
    triples: [i64; 504],
}

// ============================================================================
// §5. GPU KERNELS — Metal MSL emission targets
//
//     Kernel body uses XOR-based flat arithmetic:
//       a[m] = h[m^I] * S[m^I, I]             (h * e_I, component m)
//       (p*q)[m] = Σ_i p[i] * q[m^i] * S[i, m^i]
//       assoc[m] = abc1[m] - abc2[m]
//     No structs in kernel body — avoids SRET in GPU context.
// ============================================================================

/// F₃ GPU kernel: L¹ sedenion associator mass over O_168 orbit.
///
/// Each thread tid computes F₃ for sedenion state at states_buf[tid*16..].
/// sign_tbl[256]: e_i*e_j = sign_tbl[i*16+j] * e_{i^j} (XOR index rule).
/// triples[504]:  flattened 168×3 (I, J, K) O_168 orbit indices.
/// out_buf[n]:    per-state F₃ output (mean L¹ associator mass).
kernel fn sed_f3_l1_mass_kernel(
    n: i64,
    states_buf: &[f64],
    sign_tbl: &[i64],
    triples: &[i64],
    n_triples: i64,
    out_buf: &![f64],
) with GPU, Div {
    let tid = gpu_thread_id_x()
    if tid < n {
        let base = tid * 16
        var total: f64 = 0.0
        var t: i64 = 0
        while t < n_triples {
            let II = triples[(t * 3) as usize]
            let JJ = triples[(t * 3 + 1) as usize]
            let KK = triples[(t * 3 + 2) as usize]
            // Compute L¹ norm of associator [(h*eI), (h*eJ), (h*eK)]
            // a[m] = h[m^I]*S[m^I,I],  b[m] = h[m^J]*S[m^J,J],  c[m] = h[m^K]*S[m^K,K]
            // abc1[m] = ((a*b)*c)[m] = Σ_i (Σ_j a[j]*b[j^i]*S[j,j^i]) * c[i^m]*S[i,i^m]
            // abc2[m] = (a*(b*c))[m] = Σ_i a[i]*S[i,i^m] * (Σ_k b[k]*c[k^(i^m)]*S[k,k^(i^m)])
            var l1: f64 = 0.0
            var m: i64 = 0
            while m < 16 {
                var abc1_m: f64 = 0.0
                var i: i64 = 0
                while i < 16 {
                    var ab_i: f64 = 0.0
                    var j: i64 = 0
                    while j < 16 {
                        let ji = j ^ i
                        let jI = j ^ II
                        let jiJ = ji ^ JJ
                        let a_j = states_buf[(base + jI) as usize] * (sign_tbl[(jI * 16 + II) as usize] as f64)
                        let b_ji = states_buf[(base + jiJ) as usize] * (sign_tbl[(jiJ * 16 + JJ) as usize] as f64)
                        let s_j_ji = sign_tbl[(j * 16 + ji) as usize] as f64
                        ab_i = ab_i + a_j * b_ji * s_j_ji
                        j = j + 1
                    }
                    let im = i ^ m
                    let imK = im ^ KK
                    let c_im = states_buf[(base + imK) as usize] * (sign_tbl[(imK * 16 + KK) as usize] as f64)
                    let s_i_im = sign_tbl[(i * 16 + im) as usize] as f64
                    abc1_m = abc1_m + ab_i * c_im * s_i_im
                    i = i + 1
                }
                var abc2_m: f64 = 0.0
                i = 0
                while i < 16 {
                    let iI = i ^ II
                    let a_i = states_buf[(base + iI) as usize] * (sign_tbl[(iI * 16 + II) as usize] as f64)
                    let im = i ^ m
                    var bc_im: f64 = 0.0
                    var k: i64 = 0
                    while k < 16 {
                        let kJ = k ^ JJ
                        let kim = k ^ im
                        let kimK = kim ^ KK
                        let b_k = states_buf[(base + kJ) as usize] * (sign_tbl[(kJ * 16 + JJ) as usize] as f64)
                        let c_kim = states_buf[(base + kimK) as usize] * (sign_tbl[(kimK * 16 + KK) as usize] as f64)
                        let s_k_kim = sign_tbl[(k * 16 + kim) as usize] as f64
                        bc_im = bc_im + b_k * c_kim * s_k_kim
                        k = k + 1
                    }
                    let s_i_im = sign_tbl[(i * 16 + im) as usize] as f64
                    abc2_m = abc2_m + a_i * bc_im * s_i_im
                    i = i + 1
                }
                let assoc_m = abc1_m - abc2_m
                l1 = l1 + if assoc_m < 0.0 { 0.0 - assoc_m } else { assoc_m }
                m = m + 1
            }
            total = total + l1
            t = t + 1
        }
        out_buf[tid as usize] = total / (n_triples as f64)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// §6. CPU DISPATCH — GPU.launch wrapper
//
//     Dispatches sed_f3_l1_mass_kernel over N states.
//     Caller provides flat buffers; sign_tbl and triples from SedKernelCtx.
// ============================================================================

/// Batch F₃ over N sedenion states. Dispatches to Metal GPU kernel.
/// states[n*16]: flat buffer, states_buf[s*16+k] = component k of state s.
/// out[n]:       output F₃ per state.
pub fn sed_f3_batch(
    n: i64,
    states: &[f64],
    sign_tbl: &[i64],
    triples_buf: &[i64],
    n_triples: i64,
    out: &![f64],
) with GPU, Mut, IO, Panic, Div {
    let grid  = ((n + 63) / 64, 1, 1)
    let block = (64, 1, 1)
    perform GPU.launch(sed_f3_l1_mass_kernel, grid, block)(
        n, states, sign_tbl, triples_buf, n_triples, out
    )
    perform GPU.sync()
}

// ============================================================================
