@@TEMPLATE:self-hosted/compiler/codegen/hardware/kaxi_adapters.sio
// GENERATED_FROM_STDLIB: stdlib/hardware/kaxi.sio
// GENERATED_BY: self-hosted/compiler/codegen/hardware/kaxi_emitter.sio
// Pure Sounio helpers for K-AXI flag packing and replay inspection.

fn kaxi_i64_to_string(n: i64) -> string with Mut, Panic, Div, Alloc {
    if n == 0 { return "0" }
    if n < 0 { return "0" }

    var rev: [i8; 32] = [0; 32]
    var rev_len: i64 = 0
    var v = n
    while v > 0 {
        rev[rev_len as usize] = 48 + (v % 10) as i8
        rev_len = rev_len + 1
        v = v / 10
    }

    var out: [i8; 32] = [0; 32]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < rev_len {
        out[i as usize] = rev[(rev_len - i - 1) as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    str_from_bytes(out, rev_len)
}

fn kaxi_flags_pack(op_kind: i64, success_inc: i64, failure_inc: i64, alpha_q8: i64) -> i64 {
    let op = op_kind & 0xF
    let failure = (failure_inc & 0xFF) << 8
    let success = (success_inc & 0xFF) << 16
    let alpha = (alpha_q8 & 0xFF) << 24
    op | failure | success | alpha
}

fn kaxi_flags_unpack_op_kind(flags: i64) -> i64 {
    flags & 0xF
}

fn kaxi_flags_unpack_success_inc(flags: i64) -> i64 {
    (flags >> 16) & 0xFF
}

fn kaxi_flags_unpack_failure_inc(flags: i64) -> i64 {
    (flags >> 8) & 0xFF
}

fn kaxi_flags_unpack_alpha_q8(flags: i64) -> i64 {
    (flags >> 24) & 0xFF
}

fn kaxi_flags_is_valid(flags: i64) -> bool {
    let op = kaxi_flags_unpack_op_kind(flags)
    let success = kaxi_flags_unpack_success_inc(flags)
    let failure = kaxi_flags_unpack_failure_inc(flags)
    let alpha = kaxi_flags_unpack_alpha_q8(flags)
    op >= 0 && op <= 5 &&
    success >= 0 && success <= 255 &&
    failure >= 0 && failure <= 255 &&
    alpha >= 0 && alpha <= 255
}

fn kaxi_replay_is_epistemic(flags: i64) -> bool {
    let op = kaxi_flags_unpack_op_kind(flags)
    op >= 1 && op <= 5
}

fn kaxi_replay_entry_summary(value_bits: i64, variance_bits: i64, flags: i64) -> string with Alloc {
    let op = kaxi_flags_unpack_op_kind(flags)
    let success = kaxi_flags_unpack_success_inc(flags)
    let failure = kaxi_flags_unpack_failure_inc(flags)
    let alpha = kaxi_flags_unpack_alpha_q8(flags)
    let valid = if kaxi_flags_is_valid(flags) { "true" } else { "false" }
    let epistemic = if kaxi_replay_is_epistemic(flags) { "true" } else { "false" }
    "value_bits=" ++ kaxi_i64_to_string(value_bits) ++
    ", variance_bits=" ++ kaxi_i64_to_string(variance_bits) ++
    ", op_kind=" ++ kaxi_i64_to_string(op) ++
    ", failure_inc=" ++ kaxi_i64_to_string(failure) ++
    ", success_inc=" ++ kaxi_i64_to_string(success) ++
    ", alpha_q8=" ++ kaxi_i64_to_string(alpha) ++
    ", valid=" ++ valid ++
    ", epistemic=" ++ epistemic
}

fn kaxi_hw_counter_step(
    fidelity_total: i64,
    prov_total: i64,
    formal_total: i64,
    flags: i64
) -> (i64, i64, i64) {
    let is_epi = if kaxi_replay_is_epistemic(flags) { 1 as i64 } else { 0 as i64 }
    (
        fidelity_total + is_epi,
        prov_total + is_epi,
        formal_total + is_epi
    )
}

fn kaxi_hw_epistemic_power_log_q32_32(
    fidelity_total: i64,
    prov_total: i64,
    quantum_total: i64
) -> i64 {
    (fidelity_total >> 3) + (prov_total >> 4) + (quantum_total >> 5)
}

fn kaxi_hw_poll_replay_flags(
    flags_batch: [i64; 64],
    count: i64,
    quantum_total: i64
) -> (i64, i64, i64, i64) with Mut, Panic, Div, Alloc {
    var fidelity_total: i64 = 0
    var prov_total: i64 = 0
    var formal_total: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < count && i < 64 {
        let flags = flags_batch[i as usize]
        let (next_fidelity, next_prov, next_formal) =
            kaxi_hw_counter_step(fidelity_total, prov_total, formal_total, flags)
        fidelity_total = next_fidelity
        prov_total = next_prov
        formal_total = next_formal
        i = i + 1
    }
    let score = kaxi_hw_epistemic_power_log_q32_32(fidelity_total, prov_total, quantum_total)
    (fidelity_total, prov_total, formal_total, score)
}

fn kaxi_adapters_self_check() -> bool {
    let f = kaxi_flags_pack(4, 2, 1, 16)
    var replay: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]
    replay[0] = kaxi_flags_pack(1, 1, 0, 8)   // epistemic add
    replay[1] = kaxi_flags_pack(0, 0, 0, 0)   // non-epistemic pass
    replay[2] = kaxi_flags_pack(4, 1, 1, 16)  // epistemic fma
    let (fidelity_total, prov_total, formal_total, score_q32) =
        kaxi_hw_poll_replay_flags(replay, 3, 32)
    kaxi_flags_unpack_op_kind(f) == 4 &&
    kaxi_flags_unpack_success_inc(f) == 2 &&
    kaxi_flags_unpack_failure_inc(f) == 1 &&
    kaxi_flags_unpack_alpha_q8(f) == 16 &&
    kaxi_flags_is_valid(f) &&
    kaxi_replay_is_epistemic(f) &&
    fidelity_total == 2 &&
    prov_total == 2 &&
    formal_total == 2 &&
    score_q32 == 1
}

@@TEMPLATE:hardware/fpga/k_axi_return_fifo.v
// GENERATED_FROM_STDLIB: stdlib/hardware/kaxi.sio
// GENERATED_BY: self-hosted/compiler/codegen/hardware/kaxi_emitter.sio
// K-AXI bidirectional return FIFO (deterministic fixed-width queue).

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module k_axi_return_fifo #(
    parameter WIDTH = 544,
    parameter DEPTH = 8,
    parameter ADDR_BITS = 3
) (
    input  wire                  clk,
    input  wire                  rst_n,
    input  wire                  wr_en,
    input  wire [WIDTH-1:0]      wr_data,
    output wire                  full,
    output reg                   overflow,
    input  wire                  rd_en,
    output wire [WIDTH-1:0]      rd_data,
    output wire                  empty,
    output reg                   underflow,
    output reg  [ADDR_BITS:0]    count
);
    localparam integer DEPTH_INT = DEPTH;

    reg [WIDTH-1:0] mem [0:DEPTH-1];
    reg [ADDR_BITS-1:0] wptr;
    reg [ADDR_BITS-1:0] rptr;

    assign full = (count == DEPTH_INT);
    assign empty = (count == 0);
    assign rd_data = mem[rptr];

    wire do_write = wr_en && !full;
    wire do_read = rd_en && !empty;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wptr <= {ADDR_BITS{1'b0}};
            rptr <= {ADDR_BITS{1'b0}};
            count <= {(ADDR_BITS + 1){1'b0}};
            overflow <= 1'b0;
            underflow <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            overflow <= 1'b0;
            underflow <= 1'b0;

            if (wr_en && full) begin
                overflow <= 1'b1;
            end
            if (rd_en && empty) begin
                underflow <= 1'b1;
            end

            if (do_write) begin
                mem[wptr] <= wr_data;
                wptr <= wptr + 1'b1;
            end

            if (do_read) begin
                rptr <= rptr + 1'b1;
            end

            case ({do_write, do_read})
                2'b10: count <= count + 1'b1;
                2'b01: count <= count - 1'b1;
                default: count <= count;
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule
@@ENDTEMPLATE

@@TEMPLATE:hardware/fpga/k_axi_return_mux.v
// GENERATED_FROM_STDLIB: stdlib/hardware/kaxi.sio
// GENERATED_BY: self-hosted/compiler/codegen/hardware/kaxi_emitter.sio
// K-AXI bidirectional return mux: fabric -> return FIFO -> host runtime.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module k_axi_return_mux #(
    parameter PACKET_WIDTH = 544,
    parameter FIFO_DEPTH = 8,
    parameter FIFO_ADDR_BITS = 3
) (
    input  wire                  aclk,
    input  wire                  aresetn,

    // Inbound return lane from epistemic fabric.
    input  wire                  fabric_valid,
    output wire                  fabric_ready,
    input  wire [7:0]            kind,
    input  wire [7:0]            status,
    input  wire [7:0]            op_kind,
    input  wire [7:0]            flags,
    input  wire [31:0]           tx_seq,
    input  wire [31:0]           fidelity_inc,
    input  wire [31:0]           prov_depth_inc,
    input  wire [31:0]           formal_cov_inc,
    input  wire [63:0]           epi_log_q32_32,
    input  wire [255:0]          digest,
    input  wire [63:0]           timestamp_cycles,

    // Outbound lane to host/runtime consumer.
    output wire                  ret_valid,
    input  wire                  ret_ready,
    output wire [PACKET_WIDTH-1:0] ret_data,

    // Telemetry counters.
    output reg  [31:0]           accepted_packets,
    output reg  [31:0]           dropped_packets,
    output reg  [31:0]           overflow_events
);
    wire [PACKET_WIDTH-1:0] packet_in;
    assign packet_in = {
        timestamp_cycles,
        digest,
        epi_log_q32_32,
        formal_cov_inc,
        prov_depth_inc,
        fidelity_inc,
        tx_seq,
        flags,
        op_kind,
        status,
        kind
    };

    wire fifo_full;
    wire fifo_empty;
    wire fifo_overflow;
    wire fifo_underflow;
    wire [FIFO_ADDR_BITS:0] fifo_count;
    wire [PACKET_WIDTH-1:0] fifo_rd_data;

    assign fabric_ready = !fifo_full;

    wire wr_en = fabric_valid && fabric_ready;
    wire rd_en = ret_ready && !fifo_empty;

    assign ret_valid = !fifo_empty;
    assign ret_data = fifo_rd_data;

    k_axi_return_fifo #(
        .WIDTH(PACKET_WIDTH),
        .DEPTH(FIFO_DEPTH),
        .ADDR_BITS(FIFO_ADDR_BITS)
    ) u_return_fifo (
        .clk(aclk),
        .rst_n(aresetn),
        .wr_en(wr_en),
        .wr_data(packet_in),
        .full(fifo_full),
        .overflow(fifo_overflow),
        .rd_en(rd_en),
        .rd_data(fifo_rd_data),
        .empty(fifo_empty),
        .underflow(fifo_underflow),
        .count(fifo_count)
    );

    always @(posedge aclk or negedge aresetn) begin
        if (!aresetn) begin
            accepted_packets <= 32'd0;
            dropped_packets <= 32'd0;
            overflow_events <= 32'd0;
        end else begin
            if (wr_en) begin
                accepted_packets <= accepted_packets + 32'd1;
            end
            if (fabric_valid && !fabric_ready) begin
                dropped_packets <= dropped_packets + 32'd1;
            end
            if (fifo_overflow) begin
                overflow_events <= overflow_events + 32'd1;
            end
            if (fifo_underflow) begin
                overflow_events <= overflow_events + 32'd1;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule
@@ENDTEMPLATE

@@TEMPLATE:hardware/fpga/tb_k_axi_bidirectional.v
`timescale 1ns/1ps

module tb_k_axi_bidirectional;
    reg aclk = 1'b0;
    reg aresetn = 1'b0;
    always #5 aclk = ~aclk;

    reg fabric_valid;
    wire fabric_ready;
    reg [7:0] kind;
    reg [7:0] status;
    reg [7:0] op_kind;
    reg [7:0] flags;
    reg [31:0] tx_seq;
    reg [31:0] fidelity_inc;
    reg [31:0] prov_depth_inc;
    reg [31:0] formal_cov_inc;
    reg [63:0] epi_log_q32_32;
    reg [255:0] digest;
    reg [63:0] timestamp_cycles;

    wire ret_valid;
    reg ret_ready;
    wire [543:0] ret_data;

    wire [31:0] accepted_packets;
    wire [31:0] dropped_packets;
    wire [31:0] overflow_events;

    integer failures;
    integer drained;
    reg [31:0] first_seq;

    k_axi_return_mux #(
        .PACKET_WIDTH(544),
        .FIFO_DEPTH(4),
        .FIFO_ADDR_BITS(2)
    ) dut (
        .aclk(aclk),
        .aresetn(aresetn),
        .fabric_valid(fabric_valid),
        .fabric_ready(fabric_ready),
        .kind(kind),
        .status(status),
        .op_kind(op_kind),
        .flags(flags),
        .tx_seq(tx_seq),
        .fidelity_inc(fidelity_inc),
        .prov_depth_inc(prov_depth_inc),
        .formal_cov_inc(formal_cov_inc),
        .epi_log_q32_32(epi_log_q32_32),
        .digest(digest),
        .timestamp_cycles(timestamp_cycles),
        .ret_valid(ret_valid),
        .ret_ready(ret_ready),
        .ret_data(ret_data),
        .accepted_packets(accepted_packets),
        .dropped_packets(dropped_packets),
        .overflow_events(overflow_events)
    );

    task send_packet(input [31:0] seq, input [7:0] op);
    begin
        @(posedge aclk);
        fabric_valid <= 1'b1;
        kind <= 8'hA1;
        status <= 8'h01;
        op_kind <= op;
        flags <= 8'h5A;
        tx_seq <= seq;
        fidelity_inc <= 32'd1;
        prov_depth_inc <= 32'd1;
        formal_cov_inc <= 32'd1;
        epi_log_q32_32 <= {32'd0, seq};
        digest <= {224'd0, seq};
        timestamp_cycles <= 64'h1000 + seq;

        @(posedge aclk);
        fabric_valid <= 1'b0;
    end
    endtask

    initial begin
        failures = 0;
        drained = 0;
        first_seq = 32'd0;
        fabric_valid = 1'b0;
        kind = 8'd0;
        status = 8'd0;
        op_kind = 8'd0;
        flags = 8'd0;
        tx_seq = 32'd0;
        fidelity_inc = 32'd0;
        prov_depth_inc = 32'd0;
        formal_cov_inc = 32'd0;
        epi_log_q32_32 = 64'd0;
        digest = 256'd0;
        timestamp_cycles = 64'd0;
        ret_ready = 1'b0;

        $dumpfile("artifacts/fpga/waveforms/tb_k_axi_bidirectional.vcd");
        $dumpvars(0, tb_k_axi_bidirectional);

        repeat (4) @(posedge aclk);
        aresetn = 1'b1;
        repeat (2) @(posedge aclk);

        // Fill FIFO and force one overflow/drop packet.
        send_packet(32'd1, 8'h11);
        send_packet(32'd2, 8'h12);
        send_packet(32'd3, 8'h13);
        send_packet(32'd4, 8'h14);
        send_packet(32'd5, 8'h15);

        repeat (2) @(posedge aclk);
        if (accepted_packets !== 32'd4) begin
            $display("ASSERT FAIL: accepted_packets expected 4 got %0d", accepted_packets);
            failures = failures + 1;
        end
        if (dropped_packets !== 32'd1) begin
            $display("ASSERT FAIL: dropped_packets expected 1 got %0d", dropped_packets);
            failures = failures + 1;
        end

        // Drain queue.
        ret_ready = 1'b1;
        while (drained < 4) begin
            @(posedge aclk);
            if (ret_valid && ret_ready) begin
                if (drained == 0) begin
                    first_seq = ret_data[63:32];
                end
                drained = drained + 1;
            end
        end

        if (first_seq !== 32'd1) begin
            $display("ASSERT FAIL: first packet tx_seq expected 1 got %0d", first_seq);
            failures = failures + 1;
        end
        if (overflow_events == 0) begin
            $display("ASSERT FAIL: overflow_events should be > 0");
            failures = failures + 1;
        end

        $display(
            "OMEGA_COUNTERS kaxi_return_seen=%0d kaxi_return_dropped=%0d kaxi_return_overflow=%0d",
            accepted_packets,
            dropped_packets,
            overflow_events
        );

        if (failures > 0) begin
            $display("FAIL tb_k_axi_bidirectional cases=%0d", failures);
            $finish(1);
        end

        $display("PASS tb_k_axi_bidirectional");
        $finish(0);
    end
endmodule

let KAXI_SPEC_SCHEMA = "sounio.hardware.kaxi.v1"
let KAXI_NAME = "Knowledge AXI"
let KAXI_BUS = "AXI4Stream + EpistemicSideband"
let KAXI_PAYLOAD = "Knowledge<f64>"
let KAXI_RING_BUFFER_SIZE: i64 = 64
let KAXI_PUBLISH_INTRINSIC = "__knowledge_kaxi_publish"

fn kaxi_spec_ping() -> i32 {
    return 0 as i32

// === FILE: stdlib/hardware/launch.sio ===
// stdlib/hardware/launch.sio
// Pure-Sounio PTX launch contract shim for Sprint 1.
//
// This file intentionally keeps launch execution deterministic and fallback-safe
// in environments without direct CUDA driver wiring. It still closes the path:
// launch intent -> K-AXI publish semantics -> hardware accumulator score signal.

let KAXI_OP_PASS: i64 = 0
let KAXI_OP_ADD: i64 = 1
let KAXI_OP_MUL: i64 = 2
let KAXI_OP_DIV: i64 = 3
let KAXI_OP_FMA: i64 = 4
let KAXI_OP_PROP_VAR: i64 = 5

let PTX_TARGET_L4 = "nvidia_l4"
let PTX_TARGET_L4_ALIAS = "l4"
let PTX_KERNEL_EPISTEMIC_GEMM = "epistemic_gemm_l4"

struct PtxLaunchConfig {
    target: string,
    grid_x: i64,
    block_x: i64,
    shared_mem_bytes: i64,
    include_quantum_lane: bool,
}

struct PtxLaunchReport {
    launch_accepted: bool,
    used_fallback: bool,
    kernel_name: string,
    target: string,
    op_kind: i64,
    replay_flags: i64,
    fidelity_total: i64,
    prov_total: i64,
    formal_total: i64,
    hardware_epistemic_power_log_q32_32: i64,
}

fn launch_clamp_q8(v: i64) -> i64 {
    if v < 0 {
        0
    } else if v > 256 {
        256
    } else {
        v
    }
}

fn launch_i64_to_string(n: i64) -> string with Mut, Panic, Div, Alloc {
    if n == 0 { return "0" }
    if n < 0 { return "0" }

    var rev: [i8; 32] = [0; 32]
    var rev_len: i64 = 0
    var v = n
    while v > 0 {
        rev[rev_len as usize] = 48 + (v % 10) as i8
        rev_len = rev_len + 1
        v = v / 10
    }

    var out: [i8; 32] = [0; 32]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < rev_len {
        out[i as usize] = rev[(rev_len - i - 1) as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    str_from_bytes(out, rev_len)
}

fn launch_is_supported_op(op_kind: i64) -> bool {
    op_kind == KAXI_OP_ADD ||
    op_kind == KAXI_OP_MUL ||
    op_kind == KAXI_OP_DIV ||
    op_kind == KAXI_OP_FMA ||
    op_kind == KAXI_OP_PROP_VAR
}

fn launch_pack_flags(op_kind: i64) -> i64 {
    let op = op_kind & 0xF
    let success = if op == KAXI_OP_PASS { 0 as i64 } else { 1 as i64 }
    let failure = 0 as i64
    let alpha_q8 = 16 as i64
    op | ((failure & 0xFF) << 8) | ((success & 0xFF) << 16) | ((alpha_q8 & 0xFF) << 24)
}

fn launch_hw_counter_step(
    fidelity_total: i64,
    prov_total: i64,
    formal_total: i64,
    op_kind: i64
) -> (i64, i64, i64) {
    let is_epi = if op_kind >= KAXI_OP_ADD && op_kind <= KAXI_OP_PROP_VAR { 1 as i64 } else { 0 as i64 }
    (
        fidelity_total + is_epi,
        prov_total + is_epi,
        formal_total + is_epi
    )
}

fn launch_hw_epistemic_power_log_q32_32(fidelity_total: i64, prov_total: i64, quantum_total: i64) -> i64 {
    (fidelity_total >> 3) + (prov_total >> 4) + (quantum_total >> 5)
}

fn launch_ptx_default_l4_config() -> PtxLaunchConfig {
    PtxLaunchConfig {
        target: PTX_TARGET_L4,
        grid_x: 80,
        block_x: 128,
        shared_mem_bytes: 0,
        include_quantum_lane: false,
    }
}

fn launch_ptx_config_with_quantum_lane(cfg: PtxLaunchConfig, enabled: bool) -> PtxLaunchConfig {
    PtxLaunchConfig {
        target: cfg.target,
        grid_x: cfg.grid_x,
        block_x: cfg.block_x,
        shared_mem_bytes: cfg.shared_mem_bytes,
        include_quantum_lane: enabled,
    }
}

fn launch_ptx_target_is_l4(target: string) -> bool {
    str_eq(target, PTX_TARGET_L4) || str_eq(target, PTX_TARGET_L4_ALIAS)
}

fn launch_ptx_config_is_valid(cfg: PtxLaunchConfig) -> bool {
    launch_ptx_target_is_l4(cfg.target) &&
    cfg.grid_x > 0 &&
    cfg.block_x > 0 &&
    cfg.shared_mem_bytes >= 0
}

fn launch_ptx_sanitize_op_kind(op_kind: i64) -> i64 {
    if launch_is_supported_op(op_kind) {
        op_kind
    } else {
        KAXI_OP_PASS
    }
}

fn launch_ptx_kernel(kernel_name: string, op_kind: i64, cfg: PtxLaunchConfig) -> PtxLaunchReport {
    let launch_accepted = launch_ptx_config_is_valid(cfg)
    let op = launch_ptx_sanitize_op_kind(op_kind)
    let flags = launch_pack_flags(op)
    let (fidelity_total, prov_total, formal_total) =
        launch_hw_counter_step(0, 0, 0, op)
    let quantum_total = if cfg.include_quantum_lane { 1 as i64 } else { 0 as i64 }
    let score_q32_32 =
        launch_hw_epistemic_power_log_q32_32(fidelity_total, prov_total, quantum_total)

    PtxLaunchReport {
        launch_accepted: launch_accepted,
        used_fallback: !launch_accepted || op == KAXI_OP_PASS,
        kernel_name: kernel_name,
        target: cfg.target,
        op_kind: op,
        replay_flags: flags,
        fidelity_total: fidelity_total,
        prov_total: prov_total,
        formal_total: formal_total,
        hardware_epistemic_power_log_q32_32: score_q32_32,
    }
}

fn launch_ptx_read_epistemic_power_q32_32(report: PtxLaunchReport) -> i64 {
    report.hardware_epistemic_power_log_q32_32
}

fn launch_ptx_runtime_metric_q8(report: PtxLaunchReport) -> i64 {
    if report.launch_accepted && !report.used_fallback {
        256
    } else if report.launch_accepted {
        160
    } else {
        64
    }
}

fn launch_ptx_gum_metric_q8(report: PtxLaunchReport) -> i64 {
    if report.fidelity_total > 0 { 256 } else { 64 }
}

fn launch_ptx_prov_metric_q8(report: PtxLaunchReport) -> i64 {
    if report.prov_total > 0 { 256 } else { 64 }
}

fn launch_ptx_formal_metric_q8(report: PtxLaunchReport) -> i64 {
    if report.formal_total > 0 { 256 } else { 64 }
}

fn launch_ptx_conformance_metric_q8(report: PtxLaunchReport) -> i64 {
    if report.op_kind != KAXI_OP_PASS { 256 } else { 64 }
}

fn launch_ptx_software_epistemic_power_log_q32_32(report: PtxLaunchReport) -> i64 {
    // Sprint-1 canonical weights in Q8 (sum = 256):
    // runtime=90 (~0.35), gum=64 (0.25), prov=38 (~0.15), formal=38 (~0.15), conformance=26 (~0.10)
    let runtime = launch_clamp_q8(launch_ptx_runtime_metric_q8(report))
    let gum = launch_clamp_q8(launch_ptx_gum_metric_q8(report))
    let prov = launch_clamp_q8(launch_ptx_prov_metric_q8(report))
    let formal = launch_clamp_q8(launch_ptx_formal_metric_q8(report))
    let conformance = launch_clamp_q8(launch_ptx_conformance_metric_q8(report))

    let weighted_q8 =
        (runtime * 90 + gum * 64 + prov * 38 + formal * 38 + conformance * 26) / 256
    weighted_q8 << 16
}

fn launch_ptx_hybrid_epistemic_power_log_q32_32(report: PtxLaunchReport) -> i64 {
    let hw_log = launch_ptx_read_epistemic_power_q32_32(report)
    let sw_log = launch_ptx_software_epistemic_power_log_q32_32(report)
    (hw_log + sw_log) / 2
}

fn launch_ptx_kernel_summary(report: PtxLaunchReport) -> string with Mut, Panic, Div, Alloc {
    let fallback = if report.used_fallback { "true" } else { "false" }
    let accepted = if report.launch_accepted { "true" } else { "false" }
    "kernel=" ++ report.kernel_name ++
    ", target=" ++ report.target ++
    ", accepted=" ++ accepted ++
    ", fallback=" ++ fallback ++
    ", op_kind=" ++ launch_i64_to_string(report.op_kind) ++
    ", flags=" ++ launch_i64_to_string(report.replay_flags) ++
    ", hw_log_q32_32=" ++ launch_i64_to_string(report.hardware_epistemic_power_log_q32_32)
}

fn launch_ptx_self_check() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut, Alloc {
    let cfg = launch_ptx_default_l4_config()
    let report = launch_ptx_kernel(PTX_KERNEL_EPISTEMIC_GEMM, KAXI_OP_FMA, cfg)
    let summary = launch_ptx_kernel_summary(report)
    let sw_log = launch_ptx_software_epistemic_power_log_q32_32(report)
    let hybrid_log = launch_ptx_hybrid_epistemic_power_log_q32_32(report)
    report.launch_accepted &&
    !report.used_fallback &&
    report.op_kind == KAXI_OP_FMA &&
    report.fidelity_total == 1 &&
    report.prov_total == 1 &&
    report.formal_total == 1 &&
    report.replay_flags == launch_pack_flags(KAXI_OP_FMA) &&
    sw_log > 0 &&
    hybrid_log > 0 &&
    str_len(summary) > 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/heliobiology/constants.sio ===

// === FILE: stdlib/heliobiology/effects.sio ===
// heliobiology/effects.sio - Biological effects of space weather
//
// Models for heliobiological effects: geomagnetic storm impacts on
// cardiovascular, neurological, and other biological systems.
//
// NOTE: These models are research-grade and based on epidemiological
// correlations. Causation mechanisms are still under investigation.
//
// References:
// - Cornelissen et al. (2002) Chronobiology International
// - Palmer et al. (2006) International Journal of Biometeorology
// - Vencloviene et al. (2014) BMC Public Health

extern "C" {
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// Cardiovascular risk model parameters
struct CardiovascularRiskModel {
    baseline: f64,
    kp_coeff: f64,
    dst_coeff: f64,
    lag_hours: f64
}

fn cv_model_default() -> CardiovascularRiskModel {
    return CardiovascularRiskModel {
        baseline: 1.0,
        kp_coeff: 0.03,
        dst_coeff: 0.01,
        lag_hours: 24.0
    }
}

// Risk result with uncertainty
struct RiskResult {
    value: f64,
    uncertainty: f64
}

// Calculate relative risk for myocardial infarction
fn cv_mi_risk(model: CardiovascularRiskModel, kp: f64, dst: f64) -> RiskResult {
    var kp_effect = 1.0
    if kp >= 5.0 {
        kp_effect = 1.0 + model.kp_coeff * (kp - 4.0)
    }

    var dst_effect = 1.0
    if dst < 0.0 - 30.0 {
        dst_effect = 1.0 + model.dst_coeff * ((0.0 - dst - 30.0) / 10.0)
    }

    let rr = model.baseline * kp_effect * dst_effect
    return RiskResult { value: rr, uncertainty: rr * 0.15 }
}

// Risk for stroke (similar but weaker association)
fn cv_stroke_risk(model: CardiovascularRiskModel, kp: f64, dst: f64) -> RiskResult {
    let mi = cv_mi_risk(model, kp, dst)
    let val = mi.value * 0.6 + 0.4
    return RiskResult { value: val, uncertainty: mi.uncertainty * 0.6 }
}

// HRV model
struct HRVModel {
    baseline_sdnn: f64,
    reduction_per_kp: f64
}

fn hrv_model_default() -> HRVModel {
    return HRVModel { baseline_sdnn: 140.0, reduction_per_kp: 3.0 }
}

fn hrv_estimated_sdnn(model: HRVModel, kp: f64) -> RiskResult {
    var reduction = 0.0
    if kp > 3.0 {
        reduction = model.reduction_per_kp * (kp - 3.0)
    }
    let sdnn = model.baseline_sdnn - reduction
    return RiskResult { value: sdnn, uncertainty: 15.0 }
}

// Migraine trigger model
struct MigraineModel {
    baseline_prob: f64,
    dkp_sensitivity: f64
}

fn migraine_model_default() -> MigraineModel {
    return MigraineModel { baseline_prob: 0.05, dkp_sensitivity: 0.02 }
}

fn migraine_trigger_prob(model: MigraineModel, kp_current: f64, kp_previous: f64) -> RiskResult {
    let dkp = kp_current - kp_previous
    var multiplier = 1.0
    if dkp > 2.0 {
        multiplier = 1.0 + model.dkp_sensitivity * dkp * 10.0
    }
    var prob = model.baseline_prob * multiplier
    if prob > 0.5 { prob = 0.5 }
    return RiskResult { value: prob, uncertainty: prob * 0.3 }
}

// Melatonin suppression during geomagnetic storm
fn melatonin_suppression(kp: f64) -> RiskResult {
    var suppression = 0.0
    if kp >= 7.0 {
        suppression = 0.15
    } else if kp >= 5.0 {
        suppression = 0.08
    }
    return RiskResult { value: suppression, uncertainty: suppression * 0.5 }
}

// Sleep quality estimate (0-100 scale)
fn sleep_quality_estimate(kp: f64, dst: f64) -> RiskResult {
    let baseline = 75.0
    var kp_penalty = 0.0
    if kp >= 5.0 { kp_penalty = (kp - 4.0) * 3.0 }
    var dst_penalty = 0.0
    if dst < 0.0 - 50.0 { dst_penalty = (0.0 - dst - 50.0) * 0.05 }
    var quality = baseline - kp_penalty - dst_penalty
    if quality < 30.0 { quality = 30.0 }
    return RiskResult { value: quality, uncertainty: 10.0 }
}

// Aviation radiation dose rate (simplified CARI-7 approximation)
fn aviation_baseline_dose_rate(altitude_km: f64, latitude: f64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.14159265358979
    let alt_factor = exp((altitude_km - 10.0) * 0.2)
    // Simplified sin approximation for latitude factor
    let lat_rad = latitude * pi / 180.0
    // Use Taylor approx for sin: x - x^3/6
    let s = lat_rad - lat_rad * lat_rad * lat_rad / 6.0
    let lat_factor = 1.0 + 0.5 * s
    let base_rate = 3.0  // ~3 uSv/h at 10km equator
    return base_rate * alt_factor * lat_factor
}

// Dose rate during solar particle event
fn spe_dose_rate(baseline: f64, proton_flux: f64) -> RiskResult {
    var enhancement = 1.0
    if proton_flux > 10.0 {
        enhancement = 1.0 + log(proton_flux / 10.0) * 2.0
    }
    let rate = baseline * enhancement
    return RiskResult { value: rate, uncertainty: rate * 0.3 }
}

// Schumann resonance parameters
struct SchumannResonance {
    f1: f64,
    amplitude: f64,
    q_factor: f64
}

fn schumann_quiet_baseline() -> SchumannResonance {
    return SchumannResonance { f1: 7.83, amplitude: 1.0, q_factor: 5.0 }
}

fn schumann_storm_deviation(kp: f64) -> SchumannResonance {
    var f_shift = 0.0
    var amp_mult = 1.0
    if kp >= 5.0 {
        f_shift = 0.0 - 0.1 * (kp - 4.0)
        amp_mult = 1.0 + 0.2 * (kp - 4.0)
    }
    return SchumannResonance {
        f1: 7.83 + f_shift,
        amplitude: 1.0 * amp_mult,
        q_factor: 5.0
    }
}

fn main() {
    let model = cv_model_default()
    let risk = cv_mi_risk(model, 7.0, 0.0 - 100.0)
    println("MI risk at Kp=7, Dst=-100: ", risk.value, " +/- ", risk.uncertainty)

    let sleep = sleep_quality_estimate(7.0, 0.0 - 100.0)
    println("Sleep quality: ", sleep.value, " +/- ", sleep.uncertainty)

    let dose = aviation_baseline_dose_rate(11.0, 60.0)
    println("Aviation dose rate at 11km, 60N: ", dose, " uSv/h")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/heliobiology/indices.sio ===
// heliobiology/indices.sio - Geomagnetic and solar activity indices
//
// Type-safe representations of standard space weather indices.
//
// References:
// - NOAA Space Weather Scales
// - IAGA geomagnetic indices

// Kp storm levels (NOAA G-scale mapping) as i32 constants
fn KP_QUIET() -> i32 { 0 }
fn KP_G1_MINOR() -> i32 { 1 }
fn KP_G2_MODERATE() -> i32 { 2 }
fn KP_G3_STRONG() -> i32 { 3 }
fn KP_G4_SEVERE() -> i32 { 4 }
fn KP_G5_EXTREME() -> i32 { 5 }

// Convert Kp to storm level
fn kp_to_storm_level(kp: f64) -> i32 {
    if kp < 5.0 {
        return KP_QUIET()
    }
    if kp < 6.0 {
        return KP_G1_MINOR()
    }
    if kp < 7.0 {
        return KP_G2_MODERATE()
    }
    if kp < 8.0 {
        return KP_G3_STRONG()
    }
    if kp < 9.0 {
        return KP_G4_SEVERE()
    }
    return KP_G5_EXTREME()
}

// Dst storm classification
fn DST_QUIET() -> i32 { 0 }
fn DST_WEAK() -> i32 { 1 }
fn DST_MODERATE() -> i32 { 2 }
fn DST_INTENSE() -> i32 { 3 }
fn DST_SUPERSTORM() -> i32 { 4 }

// Classify Dst value
fn classify_dst(dst: f64) -> i32 {
    if dst > 0.0 - 30.0 {
        return DST_QUIET()
    }
    if dst > 0.0 - 50.0 {
        return DST_WEAK()
    }
    if dst > 0.0 - 100.0 {
        return DST_MODERATE()
    }
    if dst > 0.0 - 200.0 {
        return DST_INTENSE()
    }
    return DST_SUPERSTORM()
}

// NOAA S-scale (Solar Radiation Storm)
fn S_SCALE_S1() -> i32 { 1 }
fn S_SCALE_S2() -> i32 { 2 }
fn S_SCALE_S3() -> i32 { 3 }
fn S_SCALE_S4() -> i32 { 4 }
fn S_SCALE_S5() -> i32 { 5 }
fn S_SCALE_NONE() -> i32 { 0 }

// Classify proton event by >10 MeV flux
// Returns 0 for below threshold, 1-5 for S1-S5
fn classify_proton_storm(flux: f64) -> i32 {
    if flux >= 100000.0 {
        return S_SCALE_S5()
    }
    if flux >= 10000.0 {
        return S_SCALE_S4()
    }
    if flux >= 1000.0 {
        return S_SCALE_S3()
    }
    if flux >= 100.0 {
        return S_SCALE_S2()
    }
    if flux >= 10.0 {
        return S_SCALE_S1()
    }
    return S_SCALE_NONE()
}

// IMF vector in GSM coordinates
pub struct IMFVector {
    bx: f64,
    by: f64,
    bz: f64
}

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// Total field magnitude
fn imf_magnitude(v: IMFVector) -> f64 {
    return sqrt(v.bx * v.bx + v.by * v.by + v.bz * v.bz)
}

// Geoeffectiveness metric (southward Bz component, positive = geoeffective)
fn imf_geoeffective_bz(v: IMFVector) -> f64 {
    if v.bz < 0.0 { return 0.0 - v.bz }
    return 0.0
}

// Space weather summary structure
pub struct SpaceWeatherState {
    kp: f64,
    dst: f64,
    bz: f64,
    f10_7: f64,
    proton_flux: f64
}

// Overall activity level: 0=quiet, 1=minor, 2=moderate, 3=strong, 4=severe, 5=extreme
fn activity_level(state: SpaceWeatherState) -> i32 {
    let g_level = kp_to_storm_level(state.kp)
    let dst_level = classify_dst(state.dst)

    if g_level >= KP_G5_EXTREME() { return 5 }
    if g_level >= KP_G4_SEVERE() { return 4 }
    if dst_level >= DST_SUPERSTORM() { return 4 }
    if g_level >= KP_G3_STRONG() { return 3 }
    if dst_level >= DST_INTENSE() { return 3 }
    if g_level >= KP_G2_MODERATE() { return 2 }
    if g_level >= KP_G1_MINOR() { return 1 }
    return 0
}

fn indices_main() {
    let level = kp_to_storm_level(7.5)
    println("Kp 7.5 storm level: ", level)

    let dst_class = classify_dst(0.0 - 150.0)
    println("Dst -150 class: ", dst_class)

    let s = classify_proton_storm(500.0)
    println("500 pfu S-scale: ", s)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/heliobiology/mod.sio ===
//! stdlib/heliobiology - Space Weather and Heliobiological Effects
//!
//! Space weather monitoring, geomagnetic indices, solar event classification,
//! and biological effects modeling.

module heliobiology

pub fn heliobiology_module_ready() -> i32 { 1 }


// === FILE: stdlib/heliobiology/solar.sio ===
// heliobiology/solar.sio - Solar event types and classification
//
// Types for solar flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), solar energetic
// particle (SEP) events, and related phenomena.

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// X-ray flare class constants
fn FLARE_A() -> i32 { 0 }
fn FLARE_B() -> i32 { 1 }
fn FLARE_C() -> i32 { 2 }
fn FLARE_M() -> i32 { 3 }
fn FLARE_X() -> i32 { 4 }

// Flare designation
struct FlareDesignation {
    flare_class: i32,
    intensity: f64
}

fn flare_new(flare_class: i32, intensity: f64) -> FlareDesignation {
    return FlareDesignation { flare_class: flare_class, intensity: intensity }
}

// Peak X-ray flux in W/m^2
fn flare_peak_flux(f: FlareDesignation) -> f64 {
    var base = 1.0e-8
    if f.flare_class == FLARE_B() { base = 1.0e-7 }
    if f.flare_class == FLARE_C() { base = 1.0e-6 }
    if f.flare_class == FLARE_M() { base = 1.0e-5 }
    if f.flare_class == FLARE_X() { base = 1.0e-4 }
    return base * f.intensity
}

// NOAA R-scale constants
fn R_NONE() -> i32 { 0 }
fn R1_MINOR() -> i32 { 1 }
fn R2_MODERATE() -> i32 { 2 }
fn R3_STRONG() -> i32 { 3 }
fn R4_SEVERE() -> i32 { 4 }
fn R5_EXTREME() -> i32 { 5 }

// Radio blackout scale from flare
fn flare_radio_scale(f: FlareDesignation) -> i32 {
    if f.flare_class == FLARE_X() {
        if f.intensity >= 20.0 { return R5_EXTREME() }
        if f.intensity >= 10.0 { return R4_SEVERE() }
        return R3_STRONG()
    }
    if f.flare_class == FLARE_M() {
        if f.intensity >= 5.0 { return R2_MODERATE() }
        if f.intensity >= 1.0 { return R1_MINOR() }
    }
    return R_NONE()
}

// CME speed category constants
fn CME_SLOW() -> i32 { 0 }
fn CME_AVERAGE() -> i32 { 1 }
fn CME_FAST() -> i32 { 2 }
fn CME_EXTREME() -> i32 { 3 }

// CME width category constants
fn CME_NARROW() -> i32 { 0 }
fn CME_NORMAL() -> i32 { 1 }
fn CME_WIDE() -> i32 { 2 }
fn CME_PARTIAL_HALO() -> i32 { 3 }
fn CME_HALO() -> i32 { 4 }

// Coronal Mass Ejection event
pub struct CME {
    speed: f64,
    width_deg: f64,
    position_angle: f64,
    acceleration: f64
}

fn cme_speed_class(cme: CME) -> i32 {
    if cme.speed < 500.0 { return CME_SLOW() }
    if cme.speed < 1000.0 { return CME_AVERAGE() }
    if cme.speed < 2000.0 { return CME_FAST() }
    return CME_EXTREME()
}

fn cme_width_class(cme: CME) -> i32 {
    if cme.width_deg >= 360.0 { return CME_HALO() }
    if cme.width_deg > 180.0 { return CME_PARTIAL_HALO() }
    if cme.width_deg > 120.0 { return CME_WIDE() }
    if cme.width_deg > 60.0 { return CME_NORMAL() }
    return CME_NARROW()
}

// Is potentially Earth-directed?
fn cme_is_earth_directed(cme: CME) -> bool {
    let wc = cme_width_class(cme)
    return wc == CME_HALO() || wc == CME_PARTIAL_HALO()
}

// Estimated transit time (hours) using ballistic model
fn cme_transit_ballistic_hours(cme: CME) -> f64 {
    let au_km = 1.496e8
    return au_km / cme.speed / 3600.0
}

// Estimated transit time with drag (hours)
fn cme_transit_drag_hours(cme: CME) -> f64 {
    let v_ambient = 400.0
    var v_eff = cme.speed
    if cme.speed > v_ambient {
        v_eff = v_ambient + (cme.speed - v_ambient) * 0.7
    } else {
        v_eff = cme.speed + (v_ambient - cme.speed) * 0.3
    }
    let au_km = 1.496e8
    return au_km / v_eff / 3600.0
}

// SEP event
pub struct SEPEvent {
    peak_flux_10: f64,
    peak_flux_100: f64,
    source_longitude: f64
}

fn sep_is_well_connected(sep: SEPEvent) -> bool {
    return sep.source_longitude > 0.0 && sep.source_longitude < 90.0
}

// Solar cycle phase constants
fn CYCLE_MINIMUM() -> i32 { 0 }
fn CYCLE_RISING() -> i32 { 1 }
fn CYCLE_MAXIMUM() -> i32 { 2 }
fn CYCLE_DECLINING() -> i32 { 3 }

// Active region
pub struct ActiveRegion {
    number: i32,
    latitude: f64,
    longitude: f64,
    area_msh: f64,
    spot_count: i32,
    mt_wilson_class: i32
}

// Mt Wilson class constants
fn MW_ALPHA() -> i32 { 0 }
fn MW_BETA() -> i32 { 1 }
fn MW_BETA_GAMMA() -> i32 { 2 }
fn MW_GAMMA() -> i32 { 3 }
fn MW_BETA_DELTA() -> i32 { 4 }
fn MW_BETA_GAMMA_DELTA() -> i32 { 5 }

// Flare productivity potential: 0=very_low, 1=low, 2=moderate, 3=high, 4=very_high
fn ar_flare_potential(ar: ActiveRegion) -> i32 {
    if ar.mt_wilson_class == MW_BETA_GAMMA_DELTA() { return 4 }
    if ar.mt_wilson_class == MW_BETA_DELTA() { return 3 }
    if ar.mt_wilson_class == MW_BETA_GAMMA() { return 2 }
    if ar.mt_wilson_class == MW_GAMMA() { return 2 }
    if ar.mt_wilson_class == MW_BETA() { return 1 }
    return 0
}

// Is region at or near central meridian (geoeffective position)?
fn ar_is_geoeffective(ar: ActiveRegion) -> bool {
    var abs_lon = ar.longitude
    if abs_lon < 0.0 { abs_lon = 0.0 - abs_lon }
    return abs_lon <= 30.0
}

fn solar_main() {
    let flare = flare_new(FLARE_X(), 5.2)
    let flux = flare_peak_flux(flare)
    println("X5.2 peak flux: ", flux, " W/m2")

    let r_scale = flare_radio_scale(flare)
    println("Radio blackout scale: R", r_scale)

    let cme = CME { speed: 1500.0, width_deg: 360.0, position_angle: 270.0, acceleration: 0.0 - 5.0 }
    let transit = cme_transit_drag_hours(cme)
    println("CME transit time (drag): ", transit, " hours")
    println("Earth-directed: ", cme_is_earth_directed(cme))
}


// === FILE: stdlib/heliobiology/units.sio ===
//! stdlib/heliobiology/units.sio - Space weather and electromagnetic units
//!
//! Units for heliobiology, space weather monitoring, and geomagnetic studies.
//! Aligned with IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy)
//! and NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center conventions.

module heliobiology::units

use units::qudt::{m, kg, s, A, K, W, J, mol};

// =============================================================================
// ELECTROMAGNETIC UNITS
// =============================================================================

// Magnetic field strength
pub unit T                      // Tesla (SI base for magnetic flux density)
pub unit mT = 1e-3 * T
pub unit uT = 1e-6 * T          // microtesla
pub unit nT = 1e-9 * T          // nanotesla (standard for geomagnetic)
pub unit pT = 1e-12 * T         // picotesla (magnetoencephalography)
pub unit G = 1e-4 * T           // Gauss (CGS, still used in solar physics)
pub unit mG = 1e-7 * T          // milligauss
pub unit gamma = 1e-9 * T       // gamma = 1 nT (historical geomagnetic unit)

// Magnetic flux
pub unit Wb = T * m^2           // Weber
pub unit mWb = 1e-3 * Wb
pub unit Mx = 1e-8 * Wb         // Maxwell (CGS)

// Electric field
pub unit V_per_m = W / A / m    // Volts per meter
pub unit mV_per_m = 1e-3 * V_per_m

// =============================================================================
// SOLAR RADIATION UNITS
// =============================================================================

// Irradiance (power per area)
pub unit W_per_m2 = W / m^2
pub unit mW_per_m2 = 1e-3 * W_per_m2
pub unit uW_per_m2 = 1e-6 * W_per_m2

// Solar Flux Unit (radio astronomy, 10.7 cm wavelength)
// 1 SFU = 10^-22 W·m^-2·Hz^-1
pub unit SFU                    // Solar Flux Unit
pub unit sfu = SFU              // lowercase alias

// Total Solar Irradiance at 1 AU
pub unit TSI = W_per_m2         // ~1361 W/m² nominal

// Spectral irradiance
pub unit W_per_m2_per_nm = W / m^2 / nm
    where nm = 1e-9 * m

// UV index (dimensionless, 0-11+ scale)
pub unit UV_index               // dimensionless

// =============================================================================
// PARTICLE FLUX UNITS
// =============================================================================

// Particle flux (particles per area per time per steradian per energy)
pub unit pfu = 1 / (cm^2 * s * sr)  // Particle Flux Unit
    where cm = 0.01 * m
    where sr = 1                     // steradian (dimensionless solid angle)

// Integral proton flux (>10 MeV, >100 MeV thresholds)
pub unit proton_flux = pfu

// Electron flux
pub unit electron_flux = pfu

// Differential flux (per MeV)
pub unit diff_flux = pfu / MeV
    where MeV = 1.602176634e-13 * J

// Fluence (time-integrated flux)
pub unit fluence = 1 / cm^2
    where cm = 0.01 * m

// =============================================================================
// IONOSPHERIC UNITS
// =============================================================================

// Total Electron Content
pub unit TECU                   // TEC Unit = 10^16 electrons/m²

// Critical frequency
pub unit MHz = 1e6 / s          // megahertz

// Electron density
pub unit el_per_m3 = 1 / m^3    // electrons per cubic meter
pub unit el_per_cm3 = 1e6 / m^3 // electrons per cubic centimeter

// =============================================================================
// DOSIMETRY UNITS (Radiation exposure)
// =============================================================================

// Absorbed dose
pub unit Gy = J / kg            // Gray
pub unit mGy = 1e-3 * Gy
pub unit uGy = 1e-6 * Gy
pub unit rad_dose = 0.01 * Gy   // rad (CGS, deprecated but still used)

// Dose equivalent (biological effect)
pub unit Sv = J / kg            // Sievert (same dimension as Gy, different meaning)
pub unit mSv = 1e-3 * Sv
pub unit uSv = 1e-6 * Sv
pub unit rem = 0.01 * Sv        // roentgen equivalent man

// Dose rate
pub unit Sv_per_h = Sv / h
    where h = 3600 * s
pub unit uSv_per_h = 1e-6 * Sv_per_h
pub unit mGy_per_d = 1e-3 * Gy / d
    where d = 86400 * s

// =============================================================================
// DERIVED HELIOPHYSICS UNITS
// =============================================================================

// Solar wind speed
pub unit km_per_s = 1000 * m / s

// Solar wind density
pub unit particles_per_cm3 = 1e6 / m^3

// Dynamic pressure (solar wind)
pub unit nPa = 1e-9 * kg / m / s^2  // nanopascal

// Interplanetary magnetic field components
pub unit IMF = nT               // alias for clarity

// =============================================================================
// UNIT CONVERSION HELPERS
// =============================================================================

/// Convert Gauss to Tesla
pub fn gauss_to_tesla(g: G) -> T {
    g * 1e-4
}

/// Convert Tesla to Gauss
pub fn tesla_to_gauss(t: T) -> G {
    t * 1e4
}

/// Convert gamma to nanotesla (identity, historical)
pub fn gamma_to_nT(g: gamma) -> nT {
    g  // 1 gamma = 1 nT
}

/// Convert SFU to SI spectral flux density
pub fn sfu_to_si(s: SFU) -> f64 {
    // 1 SFU = 10^-22 W·m^-2·Hz^-1
    s * 1e-22
}

    status >= 200 && status < 300
}

    status >= 300 && status < 400
}

    status >= 400 && status < 500
}

    status >= 500 && status < 600
}

}

    if !http_is_success(201) { return 2 }
    if http_is_success(404) { return 3 }
    if !http_is_client_error(404) { return 4 }
    if !http_is_server_error(500) { return 5 }
    if !http_is_redirect(301) { return 6 }
    0
}

// === FILE: stdlib/hypercomplex_graph/connectome.sio ===
// hypercomplex_graph::connectome — Connectome to Octonion-Labeled Graph
//
// Converts adjacency matrices (from matrix_reader) into octonion-labeled
// graphs (from oct_graph) for associator field analysis.
//
// The key bridge for Paper 4: real brain connectivity data → algebraic
// structure (octonion labels) → geometric invariant (associator field).
//
// Labeling strategy:
//   Each edge (u,v) in the connectome receives an octonion label based on
//   two principles:
//   1. The MAGNITUDE is the edge weight (functional connectivity strength)
//   2. The DIRECTION (which octonion basis element) encodes topology:
//      - Use the 7 imaginary basis elements cyclically: e_((u+v) mod 7 + 1)
//      - This ensures different edges get different algebraic "colors"
//      - The non-associativity of these labels reveals structural patterns
//
// For subgraph analysis (OctGraph is max 32 nodes), we extract
// communities/ROI clusters from the full 200-node connectome and
// build OctGraphs per community.
//
// References:
//   - Baez 2002, "The Octonions"
//   - Sporns 2011, "Networks of the Brain" (community structure)

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS (inlined per Sounio convention)
// ============================================================================

fn cn_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn cn_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTONION (inlined — cannot import across modules in JIT)
// ============================================================================

struct Oct {
    e: [f64; 8]
}

fn oct_zero() -> Oct { Oct { e: [0.0; 8] } }

fn oct_unit(idx: i64) -> Oct with Mut, Panic {
    var o = Oct { e: [0.0; 8] }
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 8 { o.e[idx as usize] = 1.0 }
    o
}

fn oct_scale(o: Oct, s: f64) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = oct_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 { r.e[i as usize] = o.e[i as usize] * s; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn oct_sub(a: Oct, b: Oct) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = oct_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 { r.e[i as usize] = a.e[i as usize] - b.e[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn oct_conjugate(o: Oct) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = oct_zero()
    r.e[0] = o.e[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < 8 { r.e[i as usize] = 0.0 - o.e[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn oct_norm_sq(o: Oct) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 { s = s + o.e[i as usize] * o.e[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

fn oct_norm(o: Oct) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div { cn_sqrt(oct_norm_sq(o)) }

fn oct_fano_index(i: i64, j: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if i == j { return 0 }
    var t: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    t[0]=1;t[1]=2;t[2]=4; t[3]=2;t[4]=3;t[5]=5; t[6]=3;t[7]=4;t[8]=6
    t[9]=4;t[10]=5;t[11]=7; t[12]=5;t[13]=6;t[14]=1; t[15]=6;t[16]=7;t[17]=2
    t[18]=7;t[19]=1;t[20]=3
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 7 {
        let a=t[(k*3) as usize]; let b=t[(k*3+1) as usize]; let c=t[(k*3+2) as usize]
        if (i==a&&j==b)||(i==b&&j==c)||(i==c&&j==a) {
            if i==a&&j==b {return c}; if i==b&&j==c {return a}; return b
        }
        if (i==b&&j==a)||(i==c&&j==b)||(i==a&&j==c) {
            if i==b&&j==a {return c}; if i==c&&j==b {return a}; return b
        }
        k=k+1
    }
    0
}

fn oct_fano_sign(i: i64, j: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if i==j {return -1.0}; if i==0||j==0 {return 1.0}
    var t: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    t[0]=1;t[1]=2;t[2]=4; t[3]=2;t[4]=3;t[5]=5; t[6]=3;t[7]=4;t[8]=6
    t[9]=4;t[10]=5;t[11]=7; t[12]=5;t[13]=6;t[14]=1; t[15]=6;t[16]=7;t[17]=2
    t[18]=7;t[19]=1;t[20]=3
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 7 {
        let a=t[(k*3) as usize]; let b=t[(k*3+1) as usize]; let c=t[(k*3+2) as usize]
        if (i==a&&j==b)||(i==b&&j==c)||(i==c&&j==a) {return 1.0}
        if (i==b&&j==a)||(i==c&&j==b)||(i==a&&j==c) {return -1.0}
        k=k+1
    }
    0.0
}

fn oct_mul(a: Oct, b: Oct) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = oct_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < 8 {
            let coeff = a.e[i as usize] * b.e[j as usize]
            if i==0&&j==0 { result.e[0] = result.e[0] + coeff }
            else if i==0 { result.e[j as usize] = result.e[j as usize] + coeff }
            else if j==0 { result.e[i as usize] = result.e[i as usize] + coeff }
            else if i==j { result.e[0] = result.e[0] - coeff }
            else {
                let k = oct_fano_index(i, j)
                let sign = oct_fano_sign(i, j)
                result.e[k as usize] = result.e[k as usize] + sign * coeff
            }
            j=j+1
        }
        i=i+1
    }
    result
}

fn oct_associator(a: Oct, b: Oct, c: Oct) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let ab = oct_mul(a, b)
    let bc = oct_mul(b, c)
    oct_sub(oct_mul(ab, c), oct_mul(a, bc))
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTGRAPH (inlined, max 32 nodes for subgraph analysis)
// ============================================================================

struct OctGraph {
    n: i32
    adj: [i32; 1024]       // 32x32
    lab0: [f64; 1024]
    lab1: [f64; 1024]
    lab2: [f64; 1024]
    lab3: [f64; 1024]
    lab4: [f64; 1024]
    lab5: [f64; 1024]
    lab6: [f64; 1024]
    lab7: [f64; 1024]
}

fn og_new(n: i32) -> OctGraph {
    OctGraph {
        n: n, adj: [0; 1024],
        lab0: [0.0; 1024], lab1: [0.0; 1024], lab2: [0.0; 1024], lab3: [0.0; 1024],
        lab4: [0.0; 1024], lab5: [0.0; 1024], lab6: [0.0; 1024], lab7: [0.0; 1024],
    }
}

fn og_idx(u: i32, v: i32) -> i32 { u * 32 + v }

fn og_set_edge(g: OctGraph, u: i32, v: i32, label: Oct) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = g
    let idx = og_idx(u, v) as usize
    r.adj[idx] = 1
    r.lab0[idx]=label.e[0]; r.lab1[idx]=label.e[1]; r.lab2[idx]=label.e[2]; r.lab3[idx]=label.e[3]
    r.lab4[idx]=label.e[4]; r.lab5[idx]=label.e[5]; r.lab6[idx]=label.e[6]; r.lab7[idx]=label.e[7]
    r
}

fn og_add_undir(g: OctGraph, u: i32, v: i32, label: Oct) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = og_set_edge(g, u, v, label)
    r = og_set_edge(r, v, u, oct_conjugate(label))
    r
}

fn og_get_label(g: OctGraph, u: i32, v: i32) -> Oct with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = og_idx(u, v) as usize
    var o = Oct { e: [0.0; 8] }
    o.e[0]=g.lab0[idx]; o.e[1]=g.lab1[idx]; o.e[2]=g.lab2[idx]; o.e[3]=g.lab3[idx]
    o.e[4]=g.lab4[idx]; o.e[5]=g.lab5[idx]; o.e[6]=g.lab6[idx]; o.e[7]=g.lab7[idx]
    o
}

fn og_degree(g: OctGraph, v: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var d: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < g.n {
        if g.adj[og_idx(v, i) as usize] == 1 { d = d + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    d
}

// ============================================================================
// LABELING STRATEGIES
// ============================================================================
//
// Strategy 1: Cyclic basis labeling
//   edge (u,v) → w * e_{(u+v) mod 7 + 1}
//   where w = edge weight (connectivity strength)
//   This deterministically distributes all 7 imaginary basis elements.
//
// Strategy 2: Weight-to-magnitude labeling
//   edge (u,v) → oct with ||oct|| = weight, direction from topology hash
//
// Strategy 3: Degree-dependent labeling
//   edge (u,v) → direction depends on (deg(u), deg(v)) mod 7
//   This encodes hub structure into the algebraic labels.

// Cyclic basis label: weight * e_{(u+v) mod 7 + 1}
pub fn label_cyclic(u: i64, v: i64, weight: f64) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let basis = (u + v) % 7 + 1
    oct_scale(oct_unit(basis), weight)
}

// Degree-dependent label: weight * e_{(deg_u + deg_v) mod 7 + 1}
pub fn label_degree(deg_u: i64, deg_v: i64, weight: f64) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let basis = (deg_u + deg_v) % 7 + 1
    oct_scale(oct_unit(basis), weight)
}

// Mixed label: combines node indices and weight for richer algebra
// Real part = weight, imaginary part from cyclic basis
pub fn label_mixed(u: i64, v: i64, weight: f64) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let basis = (u + v) % 7 + 1
    var o = oct_unit(basis)
    o.e[0] = weight    // real part = connectivity strength
    // Normalize to preserve weight as magnitude
    let n = oct_norm(o)
    if n > 1e-12 {
        oct_scale(o, weight / n)
    } else {
        o
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// MATRIX → OCTGRAPH CONVERSION
// ============================================================================
//
// Convert a subgraph of the full adjacency matrix to an OctGraph.
// Since OctGraph is limited to 32 nodes, we take a subset of nodes
// (e.g., a community or ROI cluster).

// Convert a subgraph of nodes [node_list[0..n_nodes]] from the full matrix
// to an OctGraph with cyclic basis labeling.
//   matrix_data: flattened 200x200 adjacency matrix
//   matrix_n:    dimension of the matrix (max 200)
//   node_list:   indices of nodes to include (max 32)
//   n_nodes:     number of nodes in node_list
//   threshold:   edge weight threshold
pub fn matrix_to_octgraph(
    matrix_data: [f64; 40000], matrix_n: i64,
    node_list: [i32; 32], n_nodes: i32,
    threshold: f64
) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var g = og_new(n_nodes)

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_nodes {
        var j: i32 = i + 1
        while j < n_nodes {
            let orig_u = node_list[i as usize] as i64
            let orig_v = node_list[j as usize] as i64
            let w = matrix_data[(orig_u * matrix_n + orig_v) as usize]

            if w > threshold {
                let label = label_cyclic(orig_u, orig_v, w)
                g = og_add_undir(g, i, j, label)
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    g
}

// Convert first n nodes (n <= 32) of matrix directly to OctGraph
pub fn matrix_head_to_octgraph(
    matrix_data: [f64; 40000], matrix_n: i64,
    n_nodes: i32, threshold: f64
) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var nodes: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_nodes && i < 32 {
        nodes[i as usize] = i
        i = i + 1
    }
    matrix_to_octgraph(matrix_data, matrix_n, nodes, n_nodes, threshold)
}

// ============================================================================
// ASSOCIATOR FIELD ON CONNECTOME SUBGRAPH
// ============================================================================

pub struct ConnectomeAssocField {
    // Statistics over all length-3 paths
    count: i32
    mean_norm: f64
    max_norm: f64
    energy: f64              // sum of ||[a,b,c]||^2
    zero_count: i32          // associators near zero (alternativity channels)
    // Per-node associator density
    node_density: [f64; 32]  // mean associator norm for triples through each node
    node_triple_count: [i32; 32]
}

fn caf_empty() -> ConnectomeAssocField {
    ConnectomeAssocField {
        count: 0, mean_norm: 0.0, max_norm: 0.0, energy: 0.0, zero_count: 0,
        node_density: [0.0; 32], node_triple_count: [0; 32],
    }
}

// Compute associator field over the OctGraph
pub fn connectome_assoc_field(g: OctGraph) -> ConnectomeAssocField with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var field = caf_empty()
    var sum_norm: f64 = 0.0
    var max_n: f64 = 0.0

    var u: i32 = 0
    while u < g.n {
        var v: i32 = 0
        while v < g.n {
            if g.adj[og_idx(u, v) as usize] == 1 && u != v {
                var w: i32 = 0
                while w < g.n {
                    if g.adj[og_idx(v, w) as usize] == 1 && v != w && w != u {
                        var x: i32 = 0
                        while x < g.n {
                            if g.adj[og_idx(w, x) as usize] == 1 && w != x && x != v {
                                let a = og_get_label(g, u, v)
                                let b = og_get_label(g, v, w)
                                let c = og_get_label(g, w, x)
                                let assoc = oct_associator(a, b, c)
                                let n = oct_norm(assoc)

                                field.count = field.count + 1
                                sum_norm = sum_norm + n
                                field.energy = field.energy + n * n
                                if n > max_n { max_n = n }
                                if n < 1e-9 { field.zero_count = field.zero_count + 1 }

                                // Track per-node density (middle nodes v, w)
                                field.node_density[v as usize] = field.node_density[v as usize] + n
                                field.node_triple_count[v as usize] = field.node_triple_count[v as usize] + 1
                                field.node_density[w as usize] = field.node_density[w as usize] + n
                                field.node_triple_count[w as usize] = field.node_triple_count[w as usize] + 1
                            }
                            x = x + 1
                        }
                    }
                    w = w + 1
                }
            }
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }

    if field.count > 0 {
        field.mean_norm = sum_norm / (field.count as f64)
    }
    field.max_norm = max_n

    // Normalize per-node density
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < g.n {
        if field.node_triple_count[i as usize] > 0 {
            field.node_density[i as usize] = field.node_density[i as usize] / (field.node_triple_count[i as usize] as f64)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    field
}

// ============================================================================
// CONNECTOME COMPARISON — ASD vs TD associator fields
// ============================================================================

pub struct AssocComparison {
    mean_diff: f64          // mean_A - mean_B
    max_diff: f64           // max_A - max_B
    energy_diff: f64        // energy_A - energy_B
    zero_frac_a: f64        // fraction of zero associators in A
    zero_frac_b: f64        // fraction of zero associators in B
}

pub fn compare_assoc_fields(
    a: ConnectomeAssocField, b: ConnectomeAssocField
) -> AssocComparison with Div, Panic {
    let zf_a = if a.count > 0 { (a.zero_count as f64) / (a.count as f64) } else { 0.0 }
    let zf_b = if b.count > 0 { (b.zero_count as f64) / (b.count as f64) } else { 0.0 }

    AssocComparison {
        mean_diff: a.mean_norm - b.mean_norm,
        max_diff: a.max_norm - b.max_norm,
        energy_diff: a.energy - b.energy,
        zero_frac_a: zf_a,
        zero_frac_b: zf_b,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// LAPLACIAN EIGENVECTOR EXTRACTION (for G₂ bridge)
// ============================================================================
//
// Extract the k smallest non-trivial eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian
// via deflated power iteration on the shifted matrix (λ_max·I - L).
//
// The Laplacian L = D - A has eigenvalues 0 = λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ... ≤ λₙ.
// The eigenvector for λ₁ is the constant vector (1/√n, ..., 1/√n).
// We want eigenvectors ψ₂, ..., ψ₈ (the 7 smallest non-trivial modes).
//
// Method:
//   1. Compute L and estimate λ_max via power iteration
//   2. Form M = λ_max·I - L (flips spectrum: largest eigenvalues of M
//      correspond to smallest non-zero eigenvalues of L)
//   3. Deflated power iteration: for each eigenvector k,
//      iterate v ← M·v, project out constant vector and all
//      previously found eigenvectors, normalize
//   4. The Rayleigh quotient on L gives the eigenvalue
//
// Storage: eigenvectors stored in flat array evecs[k*n + i]
//   where k = eigenvector index (0..6 for ψ₂..ψ₈), i = vertex index
//
// Max n = 32 (matching OctGraph), max k = 7 (imaginary octonion basis).
//
// References:
//   Belkin-Niyogi 2003, "Laplacian Eigenmaps for dimensionality reduction"
//   Atasoy+ 2016, "Human brain networks function in connectome-specific
//     harmonic waves" (connectome harmonics)

// Result of eigenvector extraction
pub struct LaplacianEigenvectors {
    n: i64                    // number of vertices
    k: i64                    // number of eigenvectors extracted
    eigenvalues: [f64; 8]     // λ₂..λ₈ (indices 0..6)
    // Eigenvectors stored flat: evecs[idx*32 + vertex]
    evecs: [f64; 256]         // 8 eigenvectors × 32 vertices max
}

fn le_empty() -> LaplacianEigenvectors {
    LaplacianEigenvectors {
        n: 0, k: 0,
        eigenvalues: [0.0; 8],
        evecs: [0.0; 256],
    }
}

// Internal: matvec for n×n matrix in [f64; 1024]
fn cn_matvec(
    mat: &[f64; 1024], n: i64,
    vec: &[f64; 32], out: &![f64; 32]
) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var s: f64 = 0.0
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            s = s + mat[i * n + j] * vec[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        out[i] = s
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Internal: dot product
fn cn_dot(u: &[f64; 32], v: &[f64; 32], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut {
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        s = s + u[i] * v[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    s
}

// Internal: normalize vector, return norm
fn cn_normalize(v: &![f64; 32], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    var norm_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        norm_sq = norm_sq + v[i] * v[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let nval = cn_sqrt(norm_sq)
    if nval > 1.0e-15 {
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            v[i] = v[i] / nval
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    nval
}

// Internal: project out the constant vector
fn cn_project_orth_ones(v: &![f64; 32], n: i64) with Mut, Div {
    var dot: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        dot = dot + v[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let proj = dot / (n as f64)
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        v[i] = v[i] - proj
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Internal: project out previously found eigenvector (stored in evecs at offset)
fn cn_project_orth_evec(
    v: &![f64; 32], evecs: &[f64; 256], evec_idx: i64, n: i64
) with Mut {
    let offset = evec_idx * 32
    var dot: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        dot = dot + v[i] * evecs[offset + i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        v[i] = v[i] - dot * evecs[offset + i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Extract k smallest non-trivial eigenvectors of the Laplacian.
//   adj:  n×n adjacency matrix in row-major [f64; 1024]
//   n:    number of vertices (max 32)
//   k:    number of eigenvectors to extract (max 7)
//   max_iter: power iterations per eigenvector
pub fn laplacian_eigenvectors(
    adj: &[f64; 1024], n: i64, k: i64, max_iter: i64
) -> LaplacianEigenvectors with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = le_empty()
    result.n = n
    result.k = k

    // Step 1: Compute Laplacian L = D - A
    var lap: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var deg: f64 = 0.0
        var jj: i64 = 0
        while jj < n {
            deg = deg + adj[i * n + jj]
            jj = jj + 1
        }
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            if i == j {
                lap[i * n + j] = deg
            } else {
                lap[i * n + j] = 0.0 - adj[i * n + j]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 2: Estimate λ_max via power iteration on L
    var v: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    i = 0
    while i < n { v[i] = 1.0; i = i + 1 }
    cn_normalize(&!v, n)
    var w: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var lambda_max: f64 = 0.0
    var iter: i64 = 0
    while iter < 100 {
        cn_matvec(&lap, n, &v, &!w)
        lambda_max = cn_dot(&v, &w, n)
        cn_normalize(&!w, n)
        i = 0
        while i < n { v[i] = w[i]; i = i + 1 }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    // Add small margin to ensure positive definiteness
    lambda_max = lambda_max * 1.01 + 0.1

    // Step 3: Form M = λ_max·I - L (shifted matrix)
    var shifted: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            if i == j {
                shifted[i * n + j] = lambda_max - lap[i * n + j]
            } else {
                shifted[i * n + j] = 0.0 - lap[i * n + j]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 4: Extract k eigenvectors via deflated power iteration
    var ek: i64 = 0
    while ek < k && ek < 7 {
        // Initialize with alternating vector orthogonal to constants
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            // Use different starting vectors for each eigenvector
            let phase = (i + ek) * 7 + ek * 3
            let bit = phase - (phase / 2) * 2
            if bit == 0 { v[i] = 1.0 } else { v[i] = 0.0 - 1.0 }
            i = i + 1
        }
        // Project out constant and all previous eigenvectors
        cn_project_orth_ones(&!v, n)
        var prev: i64 = 0
        while prev < ek {
            cn_project_orth_evec(&!v, &result.evecs, prev, n)
            prev = prev + 1
        }
        cn_normalize(&!v, n)

        // Power iteration on shifted matrix
        iter = 0
        while iter < max_iter {
            cn_matvec(&shifted, n, &v, &!w)
            // Project out constant vector
            cn_project_orth_ones(&!w, n)
            // Project out all previously found eigenvectors
            prev = 0
            while prev < ek {
                cn_project_orth_evec(&!w, &result.evecs, prev, n)
                prev = prev + 1
            }
            let nval = cn_normalize(&!w, n)
            if nval < 1.0e-15 { iter = max_iter }
            // Copy w → v
            i = 0
            while i < n { v[i] = w[i]; i = i + 1 }
            iter = iter + 1
        }

        // Compute eigenvalue via Rayleigh quotient on L
        cn_matvec(&lap, n, &v, &!w)
        let eigenval = cn_dot(&v, &w, n)
        result.eigenvalues[ek] = eigenval

        // Store eigenvector
        let offset = ek * 32
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            result.evecs[offset + i] = v[i]
            i = i + 1
        }

        ek = ek + 1
    }

    result
}

// ============================================================================
// COHORT COMPARISON (G₂ bridge — neurotypical vs ADHD)
// ============================================================================
//
// Given two groups of connectomes (e.g., neurotypical vs ADHD), compute
// G₂ invariants per subject and test for group differences via
// permutation test.
//
// Pipeline per subject:
//   adjacency matrix → Laplacian → 7 eigenvectors → G₂ 3-form + SU(3) Q
//
// Group comparison:
//   1. Compute mean φ and mean Q per group
//   2. Test statistic: |mean_φ_A - mean_φ_B| (or Q analog)
//   3. Permutation test: shuffle group labels N times, recompute statistic
//   4. p-value = fraction of permutations with statistic ≥ observed
//
// Effect size: Cohen's d = (mean_A - mean_B) / pooled_sd
//
// Max cohort size: 64 subjects per group (128 total).
//
// References:
//   Good 2005, "Permutation, Parametric and Bootstrap Tests of Hypotheses"
//   Di Martino+ 2014, "The autism brain imaging data exchange" (ABIDE-I)

// Per-subject G₂ invariants
pub struct SubjectG2 {
    phi: f64           // G₂ 3-form value
    phi_abs: f64       // |φ|
    su3_quality: f64   // SU(3) branching quality Q
    lambda2: f64       // Fiedler value (algebraic connectivity)
}

fn subject_g2_empty() -> SubjectG2 {
    SubjectG2 { phi: 0.0, phi_abs: 0.0, su3_quality: 0.0, lambda2: 0.0 }
}

// Cohort: up to 64 subjects
pub struct Cohort {
    n: i64
    subjects: [SubjectG2; 64]
}

fn cohort_empty() -> Cohort {
    Cohort {
        n: 0,
        subjects: [SubjectG2 { phi: 0.0, phi_abs: 0.0, su3_quality: 0.0, lambda2: 0.0 }; 64],
    }
}

fn cohort_add(c: &!Cohort, s: SubjectG2) with Mut {
    if c.n < 64 {
        c.subjects[c.n] = s
        c.n = c.n + 1
    }
}

// Group statistics
pub struct CohortStats {
    n: i64
    mean_phi_abs: f64
    var_phi_abs: f64
    mean_su3_q: f64
    var_su3_q: f64
    mean_lambda2: f64
}

fn cn_cohort_stats(c: &Cohort) -> CohortStats with Mut, Div {
    var stats = CohortStats {
        n: c.n, mean_phi_abs: 0.0, var_phi_abs: 0.0,
        mean_su3_q: 0.0, var_su3_q: 0.0, mean_lambda2: 0.0,
    }
    if c.n == 0 { return stats }

    // Means
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < c.n {
        stats.mean_phi_abs = stats.mean_phi_abs + c.subjects[i].phi_abs
        stats.mean_su3_q = stats.mean_su3_q + c.subjects[i].su3_quality
        stats.mean_lambda2 = stats.mean_lambda2 + c.subjects[i].lambda2
        i = i + 1
    }
    let nf = c.n as f64
    stats.mean_phi_abs = stats.mean_phi_abs / nf
    stats.mean_su3_q = stats.mean_su3_q / nf
    stats.mean_lambda2 = stats.mean_lambda2 / nf

    // Variances
    i = 0
    while i < c.n {
        let dp = c.subjects[i].phi_abs - stats.mean_phi_abs
        let dq = c.subjects[i].su3_quality - stats.mean_su3_q
        stats.var_phi_abs = stats.var_phi_abs + dp * dp
        stats.var_su3_q = stats.var_su3_q + dq * dq
        i = i + 1
    }
    if c.n > 1 {
        stats.var_phi_abs = stats.var_phi_abs / (nf - 1.0)
        stats.var_su3_q = stats.var_su3_q / (nf - 1.0)
    }
    stats
}

// Cohen's d effect size between two cohorts
pub struct EffectSize {
    d_phi: f64      // Cohen's d for |φ|
    d_su3_q: f64    // Cohen's d for SU(3) quality
    diff_phi: f64   // raw mean difference in |φ|
    diff_q: f64     // raw mean difference in Q
}

fn cn_effect_size(a: &CohortStats, b: &CohortStats) -> EffectSize with Div {
    let diff_phi = a.mean_phi_abs - b.mean_phi_abs
    let diff_q = a.mean_su3_q - b.mean_su3_q

    // Pooled sd: sp = sqrt(((n1-1)*s1² + (n2-1)*s2²) / (n1+n2-2))
    let n1 = if a.n > 1 { a.n - 1 } else { 1 }
    let n2 = if b.n > 1 { b.n - 1 } else { 1 }
    let denom = (n1 + n2) as f64

    let pooled_var_phi = ((n1 as f64) * a.var_phi_abs + (n2 as f64) * b.var_phi_abs) / denom
    let pooled_var_q = ((n1 as f64) * a.var_su3_q + (n2 as f64) * b.var_su3_q) / denom

    let sp_phi = cn_sqrt(pooled_var_phi)
    let sp_q = cn_sqrt(pooled_var_q)

    EffectSize {
        d_phi: if sp_phi > 1.0e-12 { diff_phi / sp_phi } else { 0.0 },
        d_su3_q: if sp_q > 1.0e-12 { diff_q / sp_q } else { 0.0 },
        diff_phi: diff_phi,
        diff_q: diff_q,
    }
}

// Permutation test result
pub struct PermTestResult {
    observed_diff_phi: f64    // |mean_A(|φ|) - mean_B(|φ|)|
    observed_diff_q: f64      // |mean_A(Q) - mean_B(Q)|
    p_value_phi: f64          // fraction of permutations ≥ observed (|φ|)
    p_value_q: f64            // fraction of permutations ≥ observed (Q)
    n_perms: i64              // number of permutations run
}

// Internal: MINSTD PRNG for permutation shuffling
fn cn_rng_next(state: i64) -> i64 with Div {
    let a: i64 = 16807
    let m: i64 = 2147483647
    let q: i64 = 127773
    let r: i64 = 2836
    let hi = state / q
    let lo = state - hi * q
    let t = a * lo - r * hi
    if t > 0 { t } else { t + m }
}

// Permutation test: combine two cohorts, shuffle labels, compare groups.
pub fn permutation_test(
    a: &Cohort, b: &Cohort, n_perms: i64, seed: i64
) -> PermTestResult with Mut, Div {
    let stats_a = cn_cohort_stats(a)
    let stats_b = cn_cohort_stats(b)
    let obs_diff_phi = cn_abs(stats_a.mean_phi_abs - stats_b.mean_phi_abs)
    let obs_diff_q = cn_abs(stats_a.mean_su3_q - stats_b.mean_su3_q)

    let n_total = a.n + b.n
    if n_total == 0 || n_perms == 0 {
        return PermTestResult {
            observed_diff_phi: obs_diff_phi, observed_diff_q: obs_diff_q,
            p_value_phi: 1.0, p_value_q: 1.0, n_perms: 0,
        }
    }

    // Combined pool
    var pool_phi: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var pool_q: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < a.n {
        pool_phi[i] = a.subjects[i].phi_abs
        pool_q[i] = a.subjects[i].su3_quality
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < b.n {
        pool_phi[a.n + i] = b.subjects[i].phi_abs
        pool_q[a.n + i] = b.subjects[i].su3_quality
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Permutation loop
    var count_ge_phi: i64 = 0
    var count_ge_q: i64 = 0
    var rng = seed
    var perm: i64 = 0

    while perm < n_perms {
        // Copy pool for shuffling
        var sh_phi: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
        var sh_q: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
        i = 0
        while i < n_total {
            sh_phi[i] = pool_phi[i]
            sh_q[i] = pool_q[i]
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Fisher-Yates shuffle
        i = n_total - 1
        while i > 0 {
            rng = cn_rng_next(rng)
            var j = rng
            if j < 0 { j = 0 - j }
            j = j - (j / (i + 1)) * (i + 1)
            let tp = sh_phi[i]
            let tq = sh_q[i]
            sh_phi[i] = sh_phi[j]
            sh_q[i] = sh_q[j]
            sh_phi[j] = tp
            sh_q[j] = tq
            i = i - 1
        }

        // Mean difference under this permutation
        var sa_phi: f64 = 0.0
        var sa_q: f64 = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < a.n { sa_phi = sa_phi + sh_phi[i]; sa_q = sa_q + sh_q[i]; i = i + 1 }
        var sb_phi: f64 = 0.0
        var sb_q: f64 = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < b.n { sb_phi = sb_phi + sh_phi[a.n + i]; sb_q = sb_q + sh_q[a.n + i]; i = i + 1 }

        let pd_phi = cn_abs(sa_phi / (a.n as f64) - sb_phi / (b.n as f64))
        let pd_q = cn_abs(sa_q / (a.n as f64) - sb_q / (b.n as f64))

        if pd_phi >= obs_diff_phi { count_ge_phi = count_ge_phi + 1 }
        if pd_q >= obs_diff_q { count_ge_q = count_ge_q + 1 }

        perm = perm + 1
    }

    PermTestResult {
        observed_diff_phi: obs_diff_phi,
        observed_diff_q: obs_diff_q,
        p_value_phi: (count_ge_phi as f64) / (n_perms as f64),
        p_value_q: (count_ge_q as f64) / (n_perms as f64),
        n_perms: n_perms,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/hypercomplex_graph/erdos_unit_distance.sio ===
// hypercomplex_graph/erdos_unit_distance — Sounio attack on Erdős #508 and #704
//
// Objective: Use the verified 168 Theorem / ZD bridge structure to generate
// algebraic unit-distance graphs and measure whether zero-divisor "surgery"
// (right-multiplication by a primitive ZD element) can change their chromatic
// number — the first computable, reproducible step toward:
//
//   #508: Chromatic number of the plane (Hadwiger–Nelson)
//   #704: Chromatic number of unit-distance graphs in R^d
//
// HONEST MATHEMATICAL FRAME (verified, not assumed):
// - A point set with integer coordinates whose edges are pairs at squared
//   Euclidean distance == 1 is ALWAYS bipartite (chromatic number <= 2): it is
//   a subgraph of the integer lattice Z^16, 2-colored by parity of coord sum.
// - So the real, non-trivial question is: can a ZD surgery break that
//   bipartite structure (force chromatic number >= 3)?
//
// MECHANISM (confirmed = "ZD surgery / 4D annihilator", not the associator
// route): right-multiply each point by a primitive ZD element v = e_lo ± e_hi.
// This is a linear map on the sedenions with a non-trivial kernel (sedenions
// are NOT norm-multiplicative — the whole point of zero-divisors). Some unit
// edges survive, some are lost (kernel), and some new pairs become "unit".
//
// SOURCE OF TRUTH for the algebra (mirrored exactly, no invented mappings):
//   formal/lean4/SounioZeroDivisorBridge.lean   — PrimSed / validPrims (84) /
//                                                   168 unordered ZD pairs
//   formal/lean4/SounioCayleyDickson.lean        — cdSigma (sign function)
//   self-hosted/check/cayley_dickson.sio         — cd_sigma_ct (same function)
//
// Self-contained (no imports — matches the oct_graph.sio pattern; the run-pass
// harness cannot resolve imports).

module hypercomplex_graph::erdos_unit_distance

// ============================================================================
// Cayley–Dickson sign function  (e_a · e_b = cd_sigma_ct(a,b,4) · e_{a^b} in S)
// Verbatim from self-hosted/check/cayley_dickson.sio (== Lean cdSigma a b 4).
// ============================================================================

fn cd_sigma_ct(a: i64, b: i64, bits: i64) -> i64 {
    if a == 0 || b == 0 { return 1 }
    if bits <= 1 { return 0 - 1 }
    let half = 1 << (bits - 1)
    let a_hi = if a >= half { 1 } else { 0 }
    let b_hi = if b >= half { 1 } else { 0 }
    let a_lo = a & (half - 1)
    let b_lo = b & (half - 1)
    if a_hi == 0 && b_hi == 0 { return cd_sigma_ct(a_lo, b_lo, bits - 1) }
    if a_hi == 0 && b_hi == 1 { return cd_sigma_ct(b_lo, a_lo, bits - 1) }
    if a_hi == 1 && b_hi == 0 {
        if b_lo == 0 { return cd_sigma_ct(a_lo, b_lo, bits - 1) }
        else { return 0 - cd_sigma_ct(a_lo, b_lo, bits - 1) }
    }
    // both hi
    if b_lo == 0 { return 0 - cd_sigma_ct(b_lo, a_lo, bits - 1) }
    return cd_sigma_ct(b_lo, a_lo, bits - 1)
}

fn sed_sigma(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { return cd_sigma_ct(a, b, 4) }

fn near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> i64 {
    let d = a - b
    let d2 = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    if d2 <= tol { 1 } else { 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// State (fixed-size flat buffers — native compiler has no dynamic arrays)
// ============================================================================

// 84 valid primitive imaginary sedenions  v = e_lo ± e_hi
var PRIM_LO:  [i64; 84] = [0; 84]
var PRIM_HI:  [i64; 84] = [0; 84]
var PRIM_NEG: [i64; 84] = [0; 84]   // 1 => sign of e_hi is -1
var NPRIM:    i64 = 0

// Probe: NPTS points × 16 coords, flat
var PROBE: [f64; 112] = [0.0; 112]   // 7 * 16
var NPTS:  i64 = 7

// Scratch
var DIFF: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
var TW:   [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
var TMP:  [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]   // intermediate (p·u) for associator surgery
var TW2:  [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]   // ((p·u)·v) for associator surgery

// 168 unordered ZD pairs (u·v == 0, u lex-before v); headroom 200
var PAIR_U: [i64; 200] = [0; 200]
var PAIR_V: [i64; 200] = [0; 200]
var NPAIR:  i64 = 0

// Conflict-graph adjacency (NPTS x NPTS), 1 = edge
var ADJ: [i64; 49] = [0; 49]   // 7 * 7
var CLASSIC: [i64; 49] = [0; 49]   // saved classical adjacency for edge diffing

// Coloring odometer
var COLORS: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]

// ============================================================================
// §1. Enumerate the 84 valid primitives  (mirror validPrims from the bridge)
//     lo in 1..7, hi in 9..15, exclude (lo ^ hi) == 8.  7*7*2 - 14 = 84.
// ============================================================================

pub fn build_prims() with Mut {
    NPRIM = 0
    var lo = 1
    while lo <= 7 {
        var hi = 9
        while hi <= 15 {
            if (lo ^ hi) != 8 {
                // +1 variant
                PRIM_LO[NPRIM as usize] = lo
                PRIM_HI[NPRIM as usize] = hi
                PRIM_NEG[NPRIM as usize] = 0
                NPRIM = NPRIM + 1
                // -1 variant
                PRIM_LO[NPRIM as usize] = lo
                PRIM_HI[NPRIM as usize] = hi
                PRIM_NEG[NPRIM as usize] = 1
                NPRIM = NPRIM + 1
            }
            hi = hi + 1
        }
        lo = lo + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// §2. Probe configuration (7 vertices in 16D, integer coords).
//     Mirrors moser7_probe in SounioErdosUnitDistance.lean for Sounio<->Lean
//     parity.  Classical (untwisted) graph is necessarily bipartite.
// ============================================================================

fn set_coord(pt: i64, k: i64, v: f64) with Mut {
    PROBE[(pt * 16 + k) as usize] = v
}

pub fn init_probe() with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < 112 { PROBE[i as usize] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    NPTS = 7
    // Enriched probe: spans BOTH sedenion halves so pairwise xors hit the
    // active ZD fiber labels {9..15}. (A probe using only indices 0..7 makes
    // every surgery act trivially — cross terms vanish, twisted ≡ classical.)
    set_coord(0, 0, 1.0)                        // v0 = e0
    set_coord(1, 1, 1.0)                        // v1 = e1
    set_coord(2, 0, 1.0); set_coord(2, 1, 1.0)  // v2 = e0 + e1
    set_coord(3, 9, 1.0)                        // v3 = e9
    set_coord(4, 10, 1.0)                       // v4 = e10
    set_coord(5, 9, 1.0); set_coord(5, 10, 1.0) // v5 = e9 + e10
    set_coord(6, 1, 1.0); set_coord(6, 9, 1.0)  // v6 = e1 + e9 (cross-half bridge)
}

// DIFF <- PROBE[i] - PROBE[j]
fn point_diff(i: i64, j: i64) with Mut {
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 {
