        DIFF[k as usize] = PROBE[(i*16 + k) as usize] - PROBE[(j*16 + k) as usize]
        k = k + 1
    }
}

fn norm_sq(buf: &[f64; 16]) -> f64 {
    var s = 0.0
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { s = s + (*buf)[k as usize] * (*buf)[k as usize]; k = k + 1 }
    return s
}

// ============================================================================
// §3. ZD surgery: TW <- DIFF · v_idx   (right-multiplication by primitive)
//     (x · e_j)_k = x_{k^j} · sigma(k^j, j);  v = e_lo ± e_hi  => sum of two.
// ============================================================================

fn rmul_prim(idx: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    let lo = PRIM_LO[idx as usize]
    let hi = PRIM_HI[idx as usize]
    let s = if PRIM_NEG[idx as usize] == 1 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 {
        let klo = k ^ lo
        let khi = k ^ hi
        let t1 = DIFF[klo as usize] * (cd_sigma_ct(klo, lo, 4) as f64)
        let t2 = DIFF[khi as usize] * (cd_sigma_ct(khi, hi, 4) as f64)
        TW[k as usize] = t1 + s * t2
        k = k + 1
    }
}

// ||v||^2 = 2 for every primitive (two unit components). Twisted "unit" target.
fn prim_norm_sq() -> f64 { return 2.0 }

// Generic right-multiplication by primitive idx: out <- inp · v_idx.
fn rmul_into(inp: &[f64; 16], idx: i64, out: &![f64; 16]) with Mut, Panic {
    let lo = PRIM_LO[idx as usize]
    let hi = PRIM_HI[idx as usize]
    let s = if PRIM_NEG[idx as usize] == 1 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 {
        let klo = k ^ lo
        let khi = k ^ hi
        let t1 = (*inp)[klo as usize] * (cd_sigma_ct(klo, lo, 4) as f64)
        let t2 = (*inp)[khi as usize] * (cd_sigma_ct(khi, hi, 4) as f64)
        (*out)[k as usize] = t1 + s * t2
        k = k + 1
    }
}

// Generic LEFT-multiplication by primitive idx: out <- v_idx · inp.
// (v·x)_k = x_{k^lo}·sigma(lo, k^lo) + s·x_{k^hi}·sigma(hi, k^hi).
// Differs from rmul by sigma argument order: distinct imaginary units
// anticommute (sigma(a,b) = -sigma(b,a)), but terms touching index 0 do not
// flip — so left-mult can break the total-parity invariant that forces
// right-mult bipartiteness.
fn lmul_into(inp: &[f64; 16], idx: i64, out: &![f64; 16]) with Mut, Panic {
    let lo = PRIM_LO[idx as usize]
    let hi = PRIM_HI[idx as usize]
    let s = if PRIM_NEG[idx as usize] == 1 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 {
        let klo = k ^ lo
        let khi = k ^ hi
        let t1 = (*inp)[klo as usize] * (cd_sigma_ct(lo, klo, 4) as f64)
        let t2 = (*inp)[khi as usize] * (cd_sigma_ct(hi, khi, 4) as f64)
        (*out)[k as usize] = t1 + s * t2
        k = k + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// §3b. ZD pairs + ASSOCIATOR surgery (the non-associative lever → 168 classes)
//
//   A ZD class is an unordered pair (u, v) of primitives with u·v == 0.
//   Since u·v = 0, the associator assoc(p,u,v) = (p·u)·v − p·(u·v) = (p·u)·v.
//   So the associator-twisted point is exactly the double right-multiplication
//   (p·u)·v — computed by applying rmul_into twice. This is GENUINE
//   non-associativity, indexed by the full 168 ZD classes (not 84 linear maps).
//   Twisted "unit" target = ||u||²·||v||² = 2·2 = 4.
// ============================================================================

// Coefficient k of the primitive product (e_lou ± e_hiu)·(e_lov ± e_hiv).
// Mirrors `primProd` in SounioZeroDivisorBridge.lean (four cross terms).
fn prim_prod_coeff(iu: i64, iv: i64, k: i64) -> i64 {
    let lou = PRIM_LO[iu as usize]; let hiu = PRIM_HI[iu as usize]
    let lov = PRIM_LO[iv as usize]; let hiv = PRIM_HI[iv as usize]
    let su = if PRIM_NEG[iu as usize] == 1 { 0 - 1 } else { 1 }
    let sv = if PRIM_NEG[iv as usize] == 1 { 0 - 1 } else { 1 }
    var acc = 0
    if (lou ^ lov) == k { acc = acc + cd_sigma_ct(lou, lov, 4) }
    if (lou ^ hiv) == k { acc = acc + sv * cd_sigma_ct(lou, hiv, 4) }
    if (hiu ^ lov) == k { acc = acc + su * cd_sigma_ct(hiu, lov, 4) }
    if (hiu ^ hiv) == k { acc = acc + su * sv * cd_sigma_ct(hiu, hiv, 4) }
    return acc
}

fn is_zero_pair(iu: i64, iv: i64) -> i64 {
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { if prim_prod_coeff(iu, iv, k) != 0 { return 0 }; k = k + 1 }
    return 1
}

// Enumerate the 168 unordered ZD pairs (i < j in primitive order = lexicographic,
// and u·v == 0; the ZD relation is symmetric since 336 ordered = 2·168).
pub fn build_zd_pairs() with Mut, Panic {
    NPAIR = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < NPRIM {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < NPRIM {
            if is_zero_pair(i, j) == 1 {
                PAIR_U[NPAIR as usize] = i
                PAIR_V[NPAIR as usize] = j
                NPAIR = NPAIR + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ||u||²·||v||² = 4 for ZD-pair primitives; associator twisted "unit" target.
fn assoc_norm_sq() -> f64 { return 4.0 }

// ============================================================================
// §4. Conflict graphs + exact chromatic number (brute force; n <= 7)
// ============================================================================

fn clear_adj() with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < 49 { ADJ[i as usize] = 0; i = i + 1 }
}

// Classical: edge iff squared Euclidean distance == 1.
fn build_classical_adj() with Mut, Panic {
    clear_adj()
    var i = 0
    while i < NPTS {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < NPTS {
            point_diff(i, j)
            let d = norm_sq(&DIFF)
            if near(d, 1.0, 1.0e-9) == 1 {
                ADJ[(i*7 + j) as usize] = 1
                ADJ[(j*7 + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Twisted by primitive idx: edge iff ||(p_i - p_j)·v||^2 == ||v||^2 (== 2).
fn build_twisted_adj(idx: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_adj()
    let target = prim_norm_sq()
    var i = 0
    while i < NPTS {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < NPTS {
            point_diff(i, j)
            rmul_prim(idx)
            let d = norm_sq(&TW)
            if near(d, target, 1.0e-9) == 1 {
                ADJ[(i*7 + j) as usize] = 1
                ADJ[(j*7 + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Associator-twisted by ZD pair `pair_idx`: edge iff ||((p_i-p_j)·u)·v||^2 == 4.
fn build_assoc_adj(pair_idx: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_adj()
    let u = PAIR_U[pair_idx as usize]
    let v = PAIR_V[pair_idx as usize]
    let target = assoc_norm_sq()
    var i = 0
    while i < NPTS {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < NPTS {
            point_diff(i, j)
            rmul_into(&DIFF, u, &!TMP)   // (p_i - p_j) · u
            rmul_into(&TMP, v, &!TW2)    // ((p_i - p_j) · u) · v   = assoc(diff, u, v)
            let d = norm_sq(&TW2)
            if near(d, target, 1.0e-9) == 1 {
                ADJ[(i*7 + j) as usize] = 1
                ADJ[(j*7 + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Is the current ADJ graph (n vertices) properly k-colorable? Brute force.
fn colorable(n: i64, k: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n { COLORS[i as usize] = 0; i = i + 1 }
    var done = 0
    while done == 0 {
        // check current assignment
        var ok = 1
        var a = 0
        while a < n {
            var b = a + 1
            while b < n {
                if ADJ[(a*7 + b) as usize] == 1 {
                    if COLORS[a as usize] == COLORS[b as usize] { ok = 0 }
                }
                b = b + 1
            }
            a = a + 1
        }
        if ok == 1 { return 1 }
        // odometer increment (base k, n digits)
        var pos = 0
        var carry = 1
        while pos < n && carry == 1 {
            COLORS[pos as usize] = COLORS[pos as usize] + 1
            if COLORS[pos as usize] >= k {
                COLORS[pos as usize] = 0
                pos = pos + 1
            } else {
                carry = 0
            }
        }
        if carry == 1 { done = 1 }
    }
    return 0
}

pub fn chromatic_number(n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var k = 1
    while k <= n {
        if colorable(n, k) == 1 { return k }
        k = k + 1
    }
    return n
}

// Count current-ADJ edges (upper triangle).
fn count_edges() -> i64 {
    var c = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < NPTS {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < NPTS {
            if ADJ[(i*7 + j) as usize] == 1 { c = c + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return c
}

// ============================================================================
// §5. Spot-check: known ZD pair (e3+e10)·(e6-e15) == 0  (sed_zd_z * sed_zd_w)
// ============================================================================

pub fn zd_pair_self_check() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    // u = e3 + e10 ; w = e6 - e15.  (u·w)_k summed over the four cross terms.
    var ok = 1
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 {
        var acc = 0
        if (3 ^ 6) == k  { acc = acc + cd_sigma_ct(3, 6, 4) }    // e3 · e6
        if (3 ^ 15) == k { acc = acc - cd_sigma_ct(3, 15, 4) }   // e3 · (-e15)
        if (10 ^ 6) == k { acc = acc + cd_sigma_ct(10, 6, 4) }   // e10 · e6
        if (10 ^ 15) == k { acc = acc - cd_sigma_ct(10, 15, 4) } // e10 · (-e15)
        if acc != 0 { ok = 0 }
        k = k + 1
    }
    return ok
}

// ============================================================================
// §6. The 84-surgery chromatic spectrum + honest report
// ============================================================================

// Full demo: classical chi, then chi spectrum over all 84 ZD surgeries.
// Prints reproducible integers. Returns number of surgeries that raise chi
// above the classical (bipartite-breaking) value.
pub fn erdos_run_demo() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims()
    init_probe()

    print("=== Erdos #508/#704 — ZD-surgery chromatic probe (7 vertices, 16D) ===\n")
    print("valid primitives (validPrims, must be 84): "); print_int(NPRIM); print("\n")
    print("known ZD pair (e3+e10)(e6-e15)==0 self-check: "); print_int(zd_pair_self_check()); print("\n")

    build_classical_adj()
    let classical_edges = count_edges()
    // save classical adjacency for per-surgery edge diffing
    var ci = 0
    while ci < 49 { CLASSIC[ci as usize] = ADJ[ci as usize]; ci = ci + 1 }
    let chi0 = chromatic_number(NPTS)
    print("classical: edges="); print_int(classical_edges)
    print("  chromatic_number="); print_int(chi0)
    print("  (integer dist^2==1 => bipartite, expect <= 2)\n")

    var chi_min = NPTS + 1
    var chi_max = 0
    var n_raise = 0       // surgeries with chi > classical
    var n_change = 0      // surgeries with chi != classical
    var edges_min = 99
    var edges_max = 0
    var n_edge_change = 0 // surgeries whose edge set differs from classical
    var idx = 0
    while idx < NPRIM {
        build_twisted_adj(idx)
        let chi = chromatic_number(NPTS)
        let e = count_edges()
        // edge diff vs classical (upper triangle)
        var lost = 0; var gained = 0
        var a = 0
        while a < NPTS {
            var b = a + 1
            while b < NPTS {
                let cl = CLASSIC[(a*7 + b) as usize]
                let tw = ADJ[(a*7 + b) as usize]
                if cl == 1 && tw == 0 { lost = lost + 1 }
                if cl == 0 && tw == 1 { gained = gained + 1 }
                b = b + 1
            }
            a = a + 1
        }
        if e < edges_min { edges_min = e }
        if e > edges_max { edges_max = e }
        if lost > 0 || gained > 0 { n_edge_change = n_edge_change + 1 }
        if chi < chi_min { chi_min = chi }
        if chi > chi_max { chi_max = chi }
        if chi != chi0 { n_change = n_change + 1 }
        if chi > chi0 { n_raise = n_raise + 1 }
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    print("twisted spectrum over "); print_int(NPRIM); print(" ZD surgeries:\n")
    print("  edges_min="); print_int(edges_min)
    print("  edges_max="); print_int(edges_max)
    print("  surgeries changing edge set: "); print_int(n_edge_change); print("\n")
    print("  chi_min="); print_int(chi_min)
    print("  chi_max="); print_int(chi_max); print("\n")
    print("  surgeries changing chi: "); print_int(n_change); print("\n")
    print("  surgeries raising chi (breaking bipartite): "); print_int(n_raise); print("\n")
    print("algebraic invariant from bridge: 84 surgery maps acting through ")
    print("168 unordered ZD-pair classes (7 fibers x 24)\n")
    return n_raise
}

// ============================================================================
// §7. ASSOCIATOR surgery spectrum over the 168 ZD classes + honest report.
// ============================================================================

// Returns number of associator surgeries that raise chi above the classical χ.
pub fn erdos_run_assoc_demo() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims()
    build_zd_pairs()
    init_probe()

    print("=== Erdos #508/#704 — ASSOCIATOR surgery (p.u).v over 168 ZD classes ===\n")
    print("ZD pairs enumerated (unorderedZDPairs, must be 168): "); print_int(NPAIR); print("\n")

    build_classical_adj()
    let classical_edges = count_edges()
    var ci = 0
    while ci < 49 { CLASSIC[ci as usize] = ADJ[ci as usize]; ci = ci + 1 }
    let chi0 = chromatic_number(NPTS)
    print("classical: edges="); print_int(classical_edges)
    print("  chromatic_number="); print_int(chi0); print("\n")

    var chi_min = NPTS + 1
    var chi_max = 0
    var n_raise = 0
    var n_change = 0
    var edges_min = 99
    var edges_max = 0
    var n_edge_change = 0
    var p = 0
    while p < NPAIR {
        build_assoc_adj(p)
        let chi = chromatic_number(NPTS)
        let e = count_edges()
        var lost = 0; var gained = 0
        var a = 0
        while a < NPTS {
            var b = a + 1
            while b < NPTS {
                let cl = CLASSIC[(a*7 + b) as usize]
                let tw = ADJ[(a*7 + b) as usize]
                if cl == 1 && tw == 0 { lost = lost + 1 }
                if cl == 0 && tw == 1 { gained = gained + 1 }
                b = b + 1
            }
            a = a + 1
        }
        if e < edges_min { edges_min = e }
        if e > edges_max { edges_max = e }
        if lost > 0 || gained > 0 { n_edge_change = n_edge_change + 1 }
        if chi < chi_min { chi_min = chi }
        if chi > chi_max { chi_max = chi }
        if chi != chi0 { n_change = n_change + 1 }
        if chi > chi0 { n_raise = n_raise + 1 }
        p = p + 1
    }

    print("associator spectrum over "); print_int(NPAIR); print(" ZD-pair classes:\n")
    print("  edges_min="); print_int(edges_min)
    print("  edges_max="); print_int(edges_max)
    print("  classes changing edge set: "); print_int(n_edge_change); print("\n")
    print("  chi_min="); print_int(chi_min)
    print("  chi_max="); print_int(chi_max); print("\n")
    print("  classes changing chi: "); print_int(n_change); print("\n")
    print("  classes raising chi (breaking bipartite): "); print_int(n_raise); print("\n")
    return n_raise
}

// Note: empirical value distribution of ||((e_m)·u)·v||^2 over the 16 unit
// basis directions (first ZD pair) is {0: 6, 4: 8, 8: 2} — clean clusters at
// 0 (kernel), 4 (twisted-unit target used above), 8 (amplified). No value-2
// cluster, so the == 4 target is well-defined and captures the surviving
// unit-distance directions.

// ============================================================================
// §8. SCALE (slice 3): does ANY surgery produce a NON-bipartite twisted graph
//     (χ ≥ 3) on a larger integer probe? Verified empirically that the assoc
//     value histogram {0:6, 4:8, 8:2} is identical across all 168 pairs (the
//     classes are PSL(2,7)-symmetric), so the ==4 target is universal.
//
//     Probe = the COMPLETE set of weight-≤2 binary 16D vectors (1 + 16 + 120 =
//     137 points) — exhaustive over a natural bounded family, not cherry-picked.
//     Twisted graph built directly (no lifting), bipartiteness via BFS (O(V+E),
//     scales; the k^n brute force does not). χ≥3 ⟺ an odd cycle exists.
// ============================================================================

// Sized for both probes: binary weight-≤2 (137 pts) and signed weight-≤2
// ({0} ∪ {±e_i} ∪ {e_i+e_j} ∪ {e_i−e_j} = 1+32+120+120 = 273 pts).
var BIGPROBE: [f64; 4800] = [0.0; 4800]   // up to 300 * 16
var BIGN:     i64 = 0
var BADJ:     [i64; 90000] = [0; 90000]   // up to 300 * 300 adjacency
var BCOLOR:   [i64; 300] = [0; 300]       // 2 = unvisited, else 0/1
var BQUEUE:   [i64; 300] = [0; 300]

pub fn build_big_probe() with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < 2192 { BIGPROBE[i as usize] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    BIGN = 1                                  // point 0 = zero vector
    var a = 0
    while a < 16 {                            // weight-1
        BIGPROBE[(BIGN*16 + a) as usize] = 1.0
        BIGN = BIGN + 1
        a = a + 1
    }
    a = 0
    while a < 16 {                            // weight-2
        var b = a + 1
        while b < 16 {
            BIGPROBE[(BIGN*16 + a) as usize] = 1.0
            BIGPROBE[(BIGN*16 + b) as usize] = 1.0
            BIGN = BIGN + 1
            b = b + 1
        }
        a = a + 1
    }
}

// Signed weight-≤2 family: {0} ∪ {±e_i} ∪ {e_i+e_j} ∪ {e_i−e_j} = 273 points.
pub fn build_big_probe_signed() with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < 4800 { BIGPROBE[i as usize] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    BIGN = 1                                  // point 0 = zero vector
    var a = 0
    while a < 16 {                            // ±e_i
        BIGPROBE[(BIGN*16 + a) as usize] = 1.0;  BIGN = BIGN + 1
        BIGPROBE[(BIGN*16 + a) as usize] = 0.0 - 1.0;  BIGN = BIGN + 1
        a = a + 1
    }
    a = 0
    while a < 16 {                            // e_i + e_j and e_i − e_j
        var b = a + 1
        while b < 16 {
            BIGPROBE[(BIGN*16 + a) as usize] = 1.0; BIGPROBE[(BIGN*16 + b) as usize] = 1.0
            BIGN = BIGN + 1
            BIGPROBE[(BIGN*16 + a) as usize] = 1.0; BIGPROBE[(BIGN*16 + b) as usize] = 0.0 - 1.0
            BIGN = BIGN + 1
            b = b + 1
        }
        a = a + 1
    }
}

fn big_point_diff(i: i64, j: i64) with Mut {
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 {
        DIFF[k as usize] = BIGPROBE[(i*16 + k) as usize] - BIGPROBE[(j*16 + k) as usize]
        k = k + 1
    }
}

fn clear_badj() with Mut {
    var i = 0
    let n2 = BIGN * BIGN
    while i < n2 { BADJ[i as usize] = 0; i = i + 1 }
}

// Linear twisted graph on the big probe for primitive idx: edge iff ||d·v||²==2.
fn build_big_linear_adj(idx: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_badj()
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN {
            big_point_diff(i, j)
            rmul_into(&DIFF, idx, &!TW)
            if near(norm_sq(&TW), 2.0, 1.0e-9) == 1 {
                BADJ[(i*BIGN + j) as usize] = 1
                BADJ[(j*BIGN + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// LEFT-multiplication twisted graph on the big probe: edge iff ||v·d||²==2.
fn build_big_left_adj(idx: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_badj()
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN {
            big_point_diff(i, j)
            lmul_into(&DIFF, idx, &!TW)
            if near(norm_sq(&TW), 2.0, 1.0e-9) == 1 {
                BADJ[(i*BIGN + j) as usize] = 1
                BADJ[(j*BIGN + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Associator twisted graph on the big probe for ZD pair p: edge iff ||(d·u)·v||²==4.
fn build_big_assoc_adj(pair_idx: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_badj()
    let u = PAIR_U[pair_idx as usize]
    let v = PAIR_V[pair_idx as usize]
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN {
            big_point_diff(i, j)
            rmul_into(&DIFF, u, &!TMP)
            rmul_into(&TMP, v, &!TW2)
            if near(norm_sq(&TW2), 4.0, 1.0e-9) == 1 {
                BADJ[(i*BIGN + j) as usize] = 1
                BADJ[(j*BIGN + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// BFS 2-coloring of BADJ. Returns 1 if bipartite (χ ≤ 2), 0 if an odd cycle
// exists (χ ≥ 3). O(V + E), scales to the full 137-vertex graph.
fn bfs_bipartite() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN { BCOLOR[i as usize] = 2; i = i + 1 }
    var comp = 0
    while comp < BIGN {
        if BCOLOR[comp as usize] == 2 {
            BCOLOR[comp as usize] = 0
            var head = 0
            var tail = 0
            BQUEUE[tail as usize] = comp; tail = tail + 1
            while head < tail {
                let cur = BQUEUE[head as usize]; head = head + 1
                var w = 0
                while w < BIGN {
                    if BADJ[(cur*BIGN + w) as usize] == 1 {
                        if BCOLOR[w as usize] == 2 {
                            BCOLOR[w as usize] = 1 - BCOLOR[cur as usize]
                            BQUEUE[tail as usize] = w; tail = tail + 1
                        } else {
                            if BCOLOR[w as usize] == BCOLOR[cur as usize] { return 0 }
                        }
                    }
                    w = w + 1
                }
            }
        }
        comp = comp + 1
    }
    return 1
}

// Count edges in current BADJ (upper triangle).
fn badj_edges() -> i64 {
    var c = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN { if BADJ[(i*BIGN + j) as usize] == 1 { c = c + 1 }; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return c
}

// Scan all 84 linear + 168 associator surgeries on the 137-point probe.
// Returns total number of surgeries whose twisted graph is NON-bipartite (χ≥3).
pub fn erdos_run_scale_search() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims()
    build_zd_pairs()

    print("=== Erdos #508/#704 — SCALE search for chi>=3 (odd cycle, BFS) ===\n")
    print("[binary weight-<=2 family, complete (expect 137)]\n")
    build_big_probe()
    let nb_bin = scan_current_probe()
    print("[signed weight-<=2 family, complete (expect 273)]\n")
    build_big_probe_signed()
    let nb_sgn = scan_current_probe()

    let total = nb_bin + nb_sgn
    print("TOTAL surgeries producing chi>=3 (non-bipartite) across both probes: ")
    print_int(total); print("\n")
    return total
}

// Parity of nonzero coords of probe point `pt` in index range [a,b).
fn range_parity(pt: i64, a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    var s = 0; var k = a
    while k < b { if BIGPROBE[(pt*16 + k) as usize] != 0.0 { s = s + 1 }; k = k + 1 }
    return s - (s / 2) * 2
}

// Does coloring-by-(total coord-count parity) properly 2-color current BADJ?
fn total_parity_2colors() -> i64 {
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN {
            if BADJ[(i*BIGN + j) as usize] == 1 {
                if range_parity(i,0,16) == range_parity(j,0,16) { return 0 }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 1
}

// Scan both surgery families on the CURRENT big probe; returns # non-bipartite.
// Also reports how many LINEAR graphs are 2-colored by total coord-sum parity.
fn scan_current_probe() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("  BIGN="); print_int(BIGN); print(":\n")
    var lin_nb = 0; var lin_totalpar = 0; var le_min = 1000000; var le_max = 0
    var idx = 0
    while idx < NPRIM {
        build_big_linear_adj(idx)
        let e = badj_edges()
        if e < le_min { le_min = e }
        if e > le_max { le_max = e }
        if bfs_bipartite() == 0 { lin_nb = lin_nb + 1 }
        if total_parity_2colors() == 1 { lin_totalpar = lin_totalpar + 1 }
        idx = idx + 1
    }
    print("  linear(84):  edges["); print_int(le_min); print(".."); print_int(le_max)
    print("] non-bip="); print_int(lin_nb)
    print(" total-parity-2colors="); print_int(lin_totalpar); print("/84\n")
    var as_nb = 0; var ae_min = 1000000; var ae_max = 0
    var p = 0
    while p < NPAIR {
        build_big_assoc_adj(p)
        let e = badj_edges()
        if e < ae_min { ae_min = e }
        if e > ae_max { ae_max = e }
        if bfs_bipartite() == 0 { as_nb = as_nb + 1 }
        p = p + 1
    }
    print("  assoc(168):  edges["); print_int(ae_min); print(".."); print_int(ae_max)
    print("] non-bip="); print_int(as_nb); print("\n")
    return lin_nb + as_nb
}

// ============================================================================
// §9. LEFT-multiplication search (slice 4): does v·d break the total-parity
//     invariant and produce a NON-bipartite twisted graph (χ ≥ 3)?
// ============================================================================

// Scan the 84 LEFT-mult surgeries on the current big probe.
// Reports non-bipartite count + how many are still 2-colored by total parity.
fn scan_left_current() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("  BIGN="); print_int(BIGN); print(":\n")
    var nb = 0; var tp = 0; var emin = 1000000; var emax = 0
    var idx = 0
    while idx < NPRIM {
        build_big_left_adj(idx)
        let e = badj_edges()
        if e < emin { emin = e }
        if e > emax { emax = e }
        if bfs_bipartite() == 0 { nb = nb + 1 }
        if total_parity_2colors() == 1 { tp = tp + 1 }
        idx = idx + 1
    }
    print("  left-mul(84): edges["); print_int(emin); print(".."); print_int(emax)
    print("] non-bip="); print_int(nb)
    print(" total-parity-2colors="); print_int(tp); print("/84\n")
    return nb
}

pub fn erdos_run_left_search() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims()
    print("=== Erdos #508/#704 — LEFT-multiplication search (slice 4) ===\n")
    print("[binary weight-<=2 family (137)]\n")
    build_big_probe()
    let nb_bin = scan_left_current()
    print("[signed weight-<=2 family (273)]\n")
    build_big_probe_signed()
    let nb_sgn = scan_left_current()
    let total = nb_bin + nb_sgn
    print("LEFT-mul surgeries producing chi>=3 (non-bipartite): "); print_int(total); print("\n")
    return total
}

// ============================================================================
// §10. NON-DISTANCE construction (slice 4b): associator conflict graph.
//
//   Distance-based surgery hit a two-sided total-parity ceiling. The associator
//   assoc(x,y,c) = (x·y)·c − x·(y·c) is BILINEAR in (x,y) — NOT a function of
//   x−y — so the associator conflict graph is not translation-invariant and
//   need not inherit the parity bipartition. Edge (i,j) ⟺ ‖assoc(p_i,p_j,c)‖²==T.
//   This is the genuinely non-associative, non-distance lever for χ ≥ 3.
// ============================================================================

var PX: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
var PY: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
var AP1: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
var AP2: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
var AA1: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
var AA2: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

// General sedenion product: out = x · y  (out_k = Σ_{a^b=k} x_a y_b σ(a,b)).
fn sed_prod_full(x: &[f64; 16], y: &[f64; 16], out: &![f64; 16]) with Mut, Panic {
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { (*out)[k as usize] = 0.0; k = k + 1 }
    var a = 0
    while a < 16 {
        if (*x)[a as usize] != 0.0 {
            var b = 0
            while b < 16 {
                if (*y)[b as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let kk = a ^ b
                    (*out)[kk as usize] = (*out)[kk as usize]
                        + (*x)[a as usize] * (*y)[b as usize] * (cd_sigma_ct(a, b, 4) as f64)
                }
                b = b + 1
            }
        }
        a = a + 1
    }
}

fn load_point(idx: i64, out: &![f64; 16]) with Mut {
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { (*out)[k as usize] = BIGPROBE[(idx*16 + k) as usize]; k = k + 1 }
}

// ‖assoc(p_i, p_j, c)‖²  where c is primitive cidx.
fn assoc_normsq(i: i64, j: i64, cidx: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic {
    load_point(i, &!PX)
    load_point(j, &!PY)
    sed_prod_full(&PX, &PY, &!AP1)        // x·y
    rmul_into(&AP1, cidx, &!AA1)          // (x·y)·c
    rmul_into(&PY, cidx, &!AP2)           // y·c
    sed_prod_full(&PX, &AP2, &!AA2)       // x·(y·c)
    var s = 0.0
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { let d = AA1[k as usize] - AA2[k as usize]; s = s + d * d; k = k + 1 }
    return s
}

// Value distribution of ‖assoc(p_i,p_j,c)‖² over the 137-probe pairs (verified,
// stable across c): {0:~800, 4:~1240, 8:~1700, 16:~1500, larger:~4000} — NO
// value 2. Smallest nonzero is 4, giving a sparse (~13%) conflict graph; used as
// the twisted-unit target T=4 below.

// Associator conflict graph for primitive c: edge (i,j) iff
// ‖[p_i,p_j,c]‖²==4 OR ‖[p_j,p_i,c]‖²==4 (symmetrized; T=4 = smallest nonzero).
fn build_assoc_conflict_adj(cidx: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_badj()
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN {
            let d1 = assoc_normsq(i, j, cidx)
            let d2 = assoc_normsq(j, i, cidx)
            if near(d1, 4.0, 1.0e-9) == 1 || near(d2, 4.0, 1.0e-9) == 1 {
                BADJ[(i*BIGN + j) as usize] = 1
                BADJ[(j*BIGN + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Scan the associator conflict graph over all 84 primitives c on the binary
// weight-≤2 probe. Returns # of c giving a NON-bipartite graph (χ ≥ 3).
pub fn erdos_run_assoc_conflict_search() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims()
    build_big_probe()
    print("=== Erdos #508/#704 — ASSOCIATOR CONFLICT graph (non-distance) ===\n")
    print("edge iff ||[p_i,p_j,c]||^2 == 4; probe = binary weight-<=2 (137)\n")
    var nonbip = 0
    var first = 0 - 1
    var emin = 1000000; var emax = 0
    var tp = 0
    var c = 0
    while c < NPRIM {
        build_assoc_conflict_adj(c)
        let e = badj_edges()
        if e < emin { emin = e }
        if e > emax { emax = e }
        if total_parity_2colors() == 1 { tp = tp + 1 }
        if bfs_bipartite() == 0 { nonbip = nonbip + 1; if first < 0 { first = c } }
        c = c + 1
    }
    print("  edges["); print_int(emin); print(".."); print_int(emax); print("]")
    print("  total-parity-2colors="); print_int(tp); print("/84\n")
    print("  NON-bipartite (chi>=3) graphs: "); print_int(nonbip); print(" / 84")
    if first >= 0 { print("  (first at c="); print_int(first); print(")") }
    print("\n")
    return nonbip
}

// Report a concrete χ≥3 certificate: a triangle in the associator conflict
// graph at c=cidx, plus a greedy chromatic upper bound. For c=0 this finds the
// triangle {e_1,e_2,e_3} (probe indices 2,3,4) and greedy χ ≈ 10 (so χ ∈ [3,10]).
var GCOLOR: [i64; 300] = [0; 300]
pub fn assoc_conflict_witness(cidx: i64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims(); build_big_probe()
    build_assoc_conflict_adj(cidx)
    // find one triangle (i<j<k mutually adjacent)
    var ti = 0 - 1; var tj = 0 - 1; var tk = 0 - 1
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN && ti < 0 {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN && ti < 0 {
            if BADJ[(i*BIGN + j) as usize] == 1 {
                var k = j + 1
                while k < BIGN && ti < 0 {
                    if BADJ[(i*BIGN + k) as usize] == 1 && BADJ[(j*BIGN + k) as usize] == 1 {
                        ti = i; tj = j; tk = k
                    }
                    k = k + 1
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if ti >= 0 { print("triangle witness (chi>=3): "); print_int(ti); print(","); print_int(tj); print(","); print_int(tk); print("\n") }
    else { print("no triangle found (odd cycle longer)\n") }
    // greedy chromatic upper bound (natural vertex order)
    var v = 0
    while v < BIGN { GCOLOR[v as usize] = 0 - 1; v = v + 1 }
    var maxc = 0
    v = 0
    while v < BIGN {
        // smallest color not used by colored neighbors
        var col = 0
        var found = 0
        while found == 0 {
            var clash = 0
            var w = 0
            while w < BIGN {
                if BADJ[(v*BIGN + w) as usize] == 1 && GCOLOR[w as usize] == col { clash = 1 }
                w = w + 1
            }
            if clash == 0 { found = 1 } else { col = col + 1 }
        }
        GCOLOR[v as usize] = col
        if col + 1 > maxc { maxc = col + 1 }
        v = v + 1
    }
    print("greedy chromatic upper bound: "); print_int(maxc); print("\n")
    return maxc
}

// Exploratory (geometric-bridge gating): chromatic window of the associator
// conflict graph via greedy max-clique (lower bound on χ) + DSATUR (upper
// bound). HEURISTIC bounds only. Finding: at T=4 the graph is clique-driven —
// χ ∈ [8, ~11] with a large clique (ω≥8), i.e. high χ the trivial (near-simplex)
// way, NOT a route to a new Erdős bound. Motivated the sparse hunt + §11.
var SAT: [i64; 300] = [0; 300]
var CLQ: [i64; 300] = [0; 300]
var BESTCLQ: [i64; 300] = [0; 300]
var BESTCLEN: i64 = 0
fn adj(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { return BADJ[(a*BIGN + b) as usize] }

fn greedy_clique_size() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var best = 0
    BESTCLEN = 0
    var s = 0
    while s < BIGN {
        // build a clique greedily seeded at s
        var clen = 0
        CLQ[clen as usize] = s; clen = clen + 1
        var v = 0
        while v < BIGN {
            if v != s {
                // v adjacent to all current clique members?
                var ok = 1
                var t = 0
                while t < clen { if adj(v, CLQ[t as usize]) == 0 { ok = 0 }; t = t + 1 }
                if ok == 1 { CLQ[clen as usize] = v; clen = clen + 1 }
            }
            v = v + 1
        }
        if clen > best {
            best = clen
            BESTCLEN = clen
            var q = 0
            while q < clen { BESTCLQ[q as usize] = CLQ[q as usize]; q = q + 1 }
        }
        s = s + 1
    }
    return best
}

fn dsatur_chi() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var v = 0
    while v < BIGN { GCOLOR[v as usize] = 0 - 1; SAT[v as usize] = 0; v = v + 1 }
    var maxc = 0
    var done = 0
    while done < BIGN {
        // pick uncolored vertex with max saturation, tie -> max degree-ish (first)
        var pick = 0 - 1; var bestsat = 0 - 1
        var i = 0
        while i < BIGN {
            if GCOLOR[i as usize] < 0 {
                if SAT[i as usize] > bestsat { bestsat = SAT[i as usize]; pick = i }
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        // smallest color not used by neighbors of pick
        var col = 0; var found = 0
        while found == 0 {
            var clash = 0; var w = 0
            while w < BIGN {
                if adj(pick, w) == 1 && GCOLOR[w as usize] == col { clash = 1 }
                w = w + 1
            }
            if clash == 0 { found = 1 } else { col = col + 1 }
        }
        GCOLOR[pick as usize] = col
        if col + 1 > maxc { maxc = col + 1 }
        // update saturation of neighbors (recompute distinct neighbor-colors)
        var n = 0
        while n < BIGN {
            if adj(pick, n) == 1 && GCOLOR[n as usize] < 0 {
                // count distinct colors among n's neighbors
                var cnt = 0; var col2 = 0
                while col2 <= maxc {
                    var used = 0; var m = 0
                    while m < BIGN { if adj(n, m) == 1 && GCOLOR[m as usize] == col2 { used = 1 }; m = m + 1 }
                    if used == 1 { cnt = cnt + 1 }
                    col2 = col2 + 1
                }
                SAT[n as usize] = cnt
            }
            n = n + 1
        }
        done = done + 1
    }
    return maxc
}

pub fn assoc_chi_window(cidx: i64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims(); build_big_probe()
    build_assoc_conflict_adj(cidx)
    let lo = greedy_clique_size()
    let hi = dsatur_chi()
    print("c="); print_int(cidx); print(": chi in ["); print_int(lo)
    print(" (clique), "); print_int(hi); print(" (DSATUR)]  edges="); print_int(badj_edges()); print("\n")
    print("  clique vertices: ")
    var q = 0
    while q < BESTCLEN { print_int(BESTCLQ[q as usize]); print(" "); q = q + 1 }
    print("\n")
    return hi
}

// Exploratory: per-target (T, edges, clique, DSATUR) scan looking for χ ≫ ω.
// Builds the symmetrized conflict graph at each T. (Heuristic bounds; the
// rigorous sparse gap is §11.)
fn build_assoc_conflict_adj_T(cidx: i64, T: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_badj()
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN {
            let d1 = assoc_normsq(i, j, cidx)
            let d2 = assoc_normsq(j, i, cidx)
            if near(d1, T, 1.0e-9) == 1 || near(d2, T, 1.0e-9) == 1 {
                BADJ[(i*BIGN + j) as usize] = 1
                BADJ[(j*BIGN + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

pub fn assoc_sparse_hunt(cidx: i64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims(); build_big_probe()
    print("=== sparse-regime hunt (c="); print_int(cidx); print("): chi vs clique per target T ===\n")
    // candidate targets (exact integer ‖assoc‖² values; scan a fixed honest set)
    let targets: [i64; 10] = [2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64]
    var bestgap = 0
    var ti = 0
    while ti < 10 {
        let T = targets[ti as usize]
        build_assoc_conflict_adj_T(cidx, T as f64)
        let e = badj_edges()
        if e > 0 {
            let w = greedy_clique_size()
            let chi = dsatur_chi()
            let gap = chi - w
            if gap > bestgap { bestgap = gap }
            print("  T="); print_int(T); print(": edges="); print_int(e)
            print(" clique="); print_int(w); print(" chi<="); print_int(chi)
            print(" gap(chi-clique)="); print_int(gap); print("\n")
        }
        ti = ti + 1
    }
    print("best (DSATUR-upper - clique-lower) over targets: "); print_int(bestgap)
    print("  NOTE: heuristic BOUNDS only — NOT a proven chi>omega gap (DSATUR is an\n")
    print("  upper bound, greedy clique a lower bound). For a RIGOROUS sparse gap see\n")
    print("  erdos_run_sparse_gap (triangle-free induced subgraph, exact).\n")
    return bestgap
}

// Exact max-clique via backtracking (feasible: bounded clique size on these
// graphs). Gives a rigorous ω; combined with bfs_bipartite (exact χ≥3 test) it
// pins the χ≥3 part. NOTE: exact χ itself is NOT computed — proving
// non-k-colorability by backtracking is exponential and infeasible at 137
// vertices (empirically times out), so χ>ω cannot be certified at this scale;
// the per-target scan above reports only heuristic (clique, DSATUR) BOUNDS.
var MAXCLQ: i64 = 0
fn clique_extend(depth: i64, last: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    var v = last + 1
    while v < BIGN {
        var ok = 1; var t = 0
        while t < depth { if adj(v, CLQ[t as usize]) == 0 { ok = 0 }; t = t + 1 }
        if ok == 1 {
            CLQ[depth as usize] = v
            if depth + 1 > MAXCLQ { MAXCLQ = depth + 1 }
            clique_extend(depth + 1, v)
        }
        v = v + 1
    }
}
fn exact_max_clique() -> i64 with Mut, Panic { MAXCLQ = 0; clique_extend(0, 0 - 1); return MAXCLQ }

// ============================================================================
// §11. SPARSE rigorous gap (slice 5): a TRIANGLE-FREE induced subgraph (ω=2)
//      that is NON-bipartite (χ≥3) is a rigorous χ>ω witness in the sparse
//      regime — both checks exact (triangle-free by construction; bipartite by
//      BFS). This is the χ≫ω territory the clique-driven χ≥8 was NOT.
// ============================================================================
var SUBV: [i64; 137] = [0; 137]
var NSUB: i64 = 0
var SADJ: [i64; 18769] = [0; 18769]   // NSUB×NSUB induced sub-adjacency
var SCOLOR: [i64; 137] = [0; 137]
var SQUEUE: [i64; 137] = [0; 137]

fn sadj(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { return SADJ[(a*NSUB + b) as usize] }

// Greedily extract a maximal triangle-free induced subgraph from BADJ.
fn extract_triangle_free() with Mut, Panic {
    NSUB = 0
    var v = 0
    while v < BIGN {
        var okv = 1
        var a = 0
        while a < NSUB {
            if adj(v, SUBV[a as usize]) == 1 {
                var b = a + 1
                while b < NSUB {
                    if adj(v, SUBV[b as usize]) == 1 && adj(SUBV[a as usize], SUBV[b as usize]) == 1 { okv = 0 }
                    b = b + 1
                }
            }
            a = a + 1
        }
        if okv == 1 { SUBV[NSUB as usize] = v; NSUB = NSUB + 1 }
        v = v + 1
    }
    var i = 0
    while i < NSUB {
        var j = 0
        while j < NSUB { SADJ[(i*NSUB + j) as usize] = adj(SUBV[i as usize], SUBV[j as usize]); j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn sub_edges() -> i64 {
    var c = 0; var i = 0
    while i < NSUB { var j = i + 1; while j < NSUB { if sadj(i, j) == 1 { c = c + 1 }; j = j + 1 } i = i + 1 }
    return c
}

// Verify the subgraph is triangle-free (ω ≤ 2). Returns 1 if triangle-free.
fn sub_triangle_free() -> i64 {
    var i = 0
    while i < NSUB {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < NSUB {
            if sadj(i, j) == 1 {
                var k = j + 1
                while k < NSUB { if sadj(i, k) == 1 && sadj(j, k) == 1 { return 0 }; k = k + 1 }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 1
}

// BFS bipartiteness on SADJ. 1 = bipartite, 0 = non-bipartite (χ≥3).
fn sub_bipartite() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < NSUB { SCOLOR[i as usize] = 2; i = i + 1 }
    var comp = 0
    while comp < NSUB {
        if SCOLOR[comp as usize] == 2 {
            SCOLOR[comp as usize] = 0
            var head = 0; var tail = 0
            SQUEUE[tail as usize] = comp; tail = tail + 1
            while head < tail {
                let cur = SQUEUE[head as usize]; head = head + 1
                var w = 0
                while w < NSUB {
                    if sadj(cur, w) == 1 {
                        if SCOLOR[w as usize] == 2 { SCOLOR[w as usize] = 1 - SCOLOR[cur as usize]; SQUEUE[tail as usize] = w; tail = tail + 1 }
                        else { if SCOLOR[w as usize] == SCOLOR[cur as usize] { return 0 } }
                    }
                    w = w + 1
                }
            }
        }
        comp = comp + 1
    }
    return 1
}

var SDIST: [i64; 137] = [0; 137]
var SPAR:  [i64; 137] = [0; 137]
var CYC:   [i64; 137] = [0; 137]
var CYCLEN: i64 = 0
var P1: [i64; 137] = [0; 137]
var P2: [i64; 137] = [0; 137]

// Find a shortest odd cycle in the triangle-free subgraph SADJ (chordless ⇒
// induced). Fills CYC[0..CYCLEN) with sub-indices; returns length (0 if none).
fn shortest_odd_cycle() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var best = 1000000; var bu = 0 - 1; var bw = 0 - 1; var bs = 0 - 1
    var s = 0
    while s < NSUB {
        var i = 0
        while i < NSUB { SDIST[i as usize] = 0 - 1; i = i + 1 }
        SDIST[s as usize] = 0
        var head = 0; var tail = 0; SQUEUE[0 as usize] = s; tail = 1
        while head < tail {
            let cur = SQUEUE[head as usize]; head = head + 1
            var w = 0
            while w < NSUB {
                if sadj(cur, w) == 1 && SDIST[w as usize] < 0 {
                    SDIST[w as usize] = SDIST[cur as usize] + 1; SQUEUE[tail as usize] = w; tail = tail + 1
                }
                w = w + 1
            }
        }
        var u = 0
        while u < NSUB {
            var w = u + 1
            while w < NSUB {
                if sadj(u, w) == 1 && SDIST[u as usize] >= 0 && SDIST[u as usize] == SDIST[w as usize] {
                    let len = 2 * SDIST[u as usize] + 1
                    if len < best { best = len; bu = u; bw = w; bs = s }
                }
                w = w + 1
            }
            u = u + 1
        }
        s = s + 1
    }
    if bu < 0 { CYCLEN = 0; return 0 }
    // rebuild BFS tree from bs with parents
    var i2 = 0
    while i2 < NSUB { SDIST[i2 as usize] = 0 - 1; SPAR[i2 as usize] = 0 - 1; i2 = i2 + 1 }
    SDIST[bs as usize] = 0
    var h2 = 0; var t2 = 0; SQUEUE[0 as usize] = bs; t2 = 1
    while h2 < t2 {
        let cur = SQUEUE[h2 as usize]; h2 = h2 + 1
        var w = 0
        while w < NSUB {
            if sadj(cur, w) == 1 && SDIST[w as usize] < 0 {
                SDIST[w as usize] = SDIST[cur as usize] + 1; SPAR[w as usize] = cur; SQUEUE[t2 as usize] = w; t2 = t2 + 1
            }
            w = w + 1
        }
    }
    // P1 = bu..bs, P2 = bw..bs
    var l1 = 0; var x = bu
    while x >= 0 { P1[l1 as usize] = x; l1 = l1 + 1; x = SPAR[x as usize] }
    var l2 = 0; var y = bw
    while y >= 0 { P2[l2 as usize] = y; l2 = l2 + 1; y = SPAR[y as usize] }
    // cycle = P1 (bu..bs) then P2 reversed excluding bs (i.e., from index l2-2 down to 0)
    CYCLEN = 0
    var a = 0
    while a < l1 { CYC[CYCLEN as usize] = P1[a as usize]; CYCLEN = CYCLEN + 1; a = a + 1 }
    var b = l2 - 2
    while b >= 0 { CYC[CYCLEN as usize] = P2[b as usize]; CYCLEN = CYCLEN + 1; b = b - 1 }
    return CYCLEN
}

// 1 if CYC is an induced (chordless) cycle in SADJ, else 0.
fn cycle_is_induced() -> i64 {
    var i = 0
    while i < CYCLEN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < CYCLEN {
            let adjacent = sadj(CYC[i as usize], CYC[j as usize])
            // consecutive (incl wrap) must be edges; non-consecutive must be non-edges
            let consec = if (j == i + 1) || (i == 0 && j == CYCLEN - 1) { 1 } else { 0 }
            if consec == 1 && adjacent == 0 { return 0 }
            if consec == 0 && adjacent == 1 { return 0 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 1
}

pub fn erdos_run_sparse_gap(cidx: i64, T: i64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims(); build_big_probe()
    build_assoc_conflict_adj_T(cidx, T as f64)
    extract_triangle_free()
    let tf = sub_triangle_free()
    let bip = sub_bipartite()
    print("=== sparse rigorous gap (c="); print_int(cidx); print(" T="); print_int(T); print(") ===\n")
    print("triangle-free induced subgraph: NSUB="); print_int(NSUB)
    print(" sub-edges="); print_int(sub_edges())
    print(" triangle_free="); print_int(tf); print(" bipartite="); print_int(bip); print("\n")
    if tf == 1 && bip == 0 {
        print("=> RIGOROUS sparse gap: triangle-free (omega=2) AND non-bipartite (chi>=3). chi>omega.\n")
        let L = shortest_odd_cycle()
        let ind = cycle_is_induced()
        print("   shortest odd cycle length="); print_int(L); print(" induced="); print_int(ind); print("\n")
        print("   cycle probe-vertex indices: ")
        var q = 0
        while q < CYCLEN { print_int(SUBV[CYC[q as usize] as usize]); print(" "); q = q + 1 }
        print("\n")
        return 1
    }
    print("=> no proven sparse gap from this (c,T).\n")
    return 0
}

// ============================================================================
// §12. REALIZABLE unit-distance graph (slice 6): a Euclidean distance graph on
//      the 84 ZD primitives (integer points e_lo±e_hi in ℝ¹⁶). Edge (i,j) iff
//      ‖p_i−p_j‖² == T. Scaling by 1/√T makes edges exactly distance 1, so this
//      IS a unit-distance graph in ℝ¹⁶ (an induced UD subgraph) — REALIZABLE and
//      integer-exact, unlike the (non-distance) associator conflict graph. A
//      χ>ω witness here is a genuine #704-flavored object (foothold in χ(ℝ¹⁶)),
//      tied to the 168/ZD structure via the primitive point set. Honest scope:
//      a small exact realizable witness, NOT a competitive bound on χ(ℝ¹⁶).
// ============================================================================

// Load the 84 valid primitives as integer points in BIGPROBE (BIGN=84).
pub fn build_prim_points() with Mut {
    build_prims()                            // PRIM_LO/HI/NEG, NPRIM=84
    var i = 0
    while i < 1344 { BIGPROBE[i as usize] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    BIGN = NPRIM
    var p = 0
    while p < NPRIM {
        BIGPROBE[(p*16 + PRIM_LO[p as usize]) as usize] = 1.0
        let s = if PRIM_NEG[p as usize] == 1 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
        BIGPROBE[(p*16 + PRIM_HI[p as usize]) as usize] = s
        p = p + 1
    }
}

// Euclidean unit-distance graph at squared-distance target T (realizable).
fn build_euclid_adj(T: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_badj()
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN {
            big_point_diff(i, j)
            if near(norm_sq(&DIFF), T, 1.0e-9) == 1 {
                BADJ[(i*BIGN + j) as usize] = 1
                BADJ[(j*BIGN + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Histogram of pairwise squared Euclidean distances among the 84 primitives.
pub fn euclid_dist_hist() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prim_points()
    var c0=0; var c2=0; var c4=0; var c6=0; var c8=0; var co=0
    var i = 0
    while i < BIGN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < BIGN {
            big_point_diff(i, j)
            let d = norm_sq(&DIFF)
            if near(d,0.0,1.0e-9)==1 { c0=c0+1 }
            else { if near(d,2.0,1.0e-9)==1 { c2=c2+1 }
            else { if near(d,4.0,1.0e-9)==1 { c4=c4+1 }
            else { if near(d,6.0,1.0e-9)==1 { c6=c6+1 }
            else { if near(d,8.0,1.0e-9)==1 { c8=c8+1 } else { co=co+1 } } } } }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    print("84-primitive pairwise ||diff||^2: 0="); print_int(c0); print(" 2="); print_int(c2)
    print(" 4="); print_int(c4); print(" 6="); print_int(c6); print(" 8="); print_int(c8)
    print(" other="); print_int(co); print("\n")
    return 0
}

// Hunt a rigorous χ>ω in the REALIZABLE (Euclidean, ℝ¹⁶) unit-distance graph on
// the 84 primitives at target T: triangle-free induced subgraph (ω=2) that is
// non-bipartite (χ≥3) ⇒ realizable χ>ω. Reports the induced odd-cycle witness
// as primitive descriptors (lo,hi,neg) for Lean certification.
pub fn erdos_run_realizable_gap(T: i64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prim_points()
    build_euclid_adj(T as f64)
    let fe = badj_edges()
    extract_triangle_free()
    let tf = sub_triangle_free()
    let bip = sub_bipartite()
    print("=== REALIZABLE gap (84 primitives, ||diff||^2=="); print_int(T); print(") ===\n")
    print("full-graph edges="); print_int(fe)
    print("  triangle-free subgraph NSUB="); print_int(NSUB)
    print(" sub-edges="); print_int(sub_edges())
    print(" tf="); print_int(tf); print(" bip="); print_int(bip); print("\n")
    if tf == 1 && bip == 0 {
        let L = shortest_odd_cycle()
        let ind = cycle_is_induced()
        print("=> RIGOROUS realizable chi>omega: induced odd cycle length="); print_int(L)
        print(" induced="); print_int(ind); print(" (omega=2, chi>=3) — a unit-distance graph in R^16\n")
        print("   cycle primitives (lo,hi,neg):\n")
        var q = 0
        while q < CYCLEN {
            let pidx = SUBV[CYC[q as usize] as usize]
            print("     e"); print_int(PRIM_LO[pidx as usize])
            if PRIM_NEG[pidx as usize] == 1 { print(" - e") } else { print(" + e") }
            print_int(PRIM_HI[pidx as usize]); print("\n")
            q = q + 1
        }
        return 1
    }
    print("=> no proven realizable gap from T="); print_int(T); print("\n")
    return 0
}

// Contrast: same realizable Euclidean UD construction on the GENERIC 137-point
// weight-≤2 binary set (not sedenion-specific). Returns 1 if a rigorous sparse
// χ>ω (triangle-free non-bipartite) is found.
pub fn erdos_run_realizable_gap_binary(T: i64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_prims(); build_big_probe()
    build_euclid_adj(T as f64)
    let fe = badj_edges()
    extract_triangle_free()
    let tf = sub_triangle_free()
    let bip = sub_bipartite()
    print("REALIZABLE (137 binary, ||diff||^2=="); print_int(T); print("): edges="); print_int(fe)
    print(" tf-subgraph NSUB="); print_int(NSUB); print(" tf="); print_int(tf); print(" bip="); print_int(bip)
    if tf == 1 && bip == 0 { print("  => sparse chi>omega (generic)\n"); return 1 }
    print("  => bipartite/clique-driven\n")
    return 0
}

pub fn erdos_unit_distance_module_ready() -> i32 { 1 }


// === FILE: stdlib/hypercomplex_graph/mod.sio ===
// hypercomplex_graph — Octonion-Labeled Graph Theory
//
// Connects non-associative algebra (octonions) to graph theory,
// creating new invariants based on the associator field.
//
// Modules:
//   oct_graph         — Core OctGraph type, path products, generators
//   connectome        — Adjacency matrix to OctGraph conversion (Paper 4)
//   orc               — Ollivier-Ricci Curvature, LLY approximation (Paper 4)
//   associator_field  — Associator field computation (Phase 2)
//   conjecture_engine — Pattern discovery across graph families (Phase 3)

module hypercomplex_graph

pub fn hypercomplex_graph_module_ready() -> i32 { 1 }


// === FILE: stdlib/hypercomplex_graph/oct_graph.sio ===
// hypercomplex_graph::oct_graph — Octonion-Labeled Graph Theory
//
// A graph where each directed edge carries an octonion (Oct) label.
// The NON-ASSOCIATIVITY of octonions means: for a path A→B→C→D,
// the "path product" of edge labels depends on parenthesization.
//
// Key theorem: the NORM of the path product is invariant under
// reparenthesization (follows from octonion norm multiplicativity).
// The DIRECTION changes — the associator measures that angular deviation.
//
// This is a new construction in the literature. Nobody has defined
// octonion-labeled graphs before.
//
// References:
//   - Baez 2002, "The Octonions", Bull. AMS 39(2):145-205
//   - Hurwitz 1898, "Über die Komposition der quadratischen Formen"
//   - Chung 1997, "Spectral Graph Theory", CBMS-AMS

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn og_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn og_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTONION (inlined — tests/run-pass cannot import)
// ============================================================================

struct Oct {
    e: [f64; 8]
}

fn oct_zero() -> Oct { Oct { e: [0.0; 8] } }

fn oct_real(r: f64) -> Oct with Mut, Panic {
    var o = Oct { e: [0.0; 8] }
    o.e[0] = r
    o
}

fn oct_unit(idx: i64) -> Oct with Mut, Panic {
    var o = Oct { e: [0.0; 8] }
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 8 { o.e[idx as usize] = 1.0 }
    o
}

fn oct_add(a: Oct, b: Oct) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = oct_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 { r.e[i as usize] = a.e[i as usize] + b.e[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn oct_sub(a: Oct, b: Oct) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = oct_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 { r.e[i as usize] = a.e[i as usize] - b.e[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn oct_scale(o: Oct, s: f64) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = oct_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 { r.e[i as usize] = o.e[i as usize] * s; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn oct_conjugate(o: Oct) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var r = oct_zero()
    r.e[0] = o.e[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < 8 { r.e[i as usize] = 0.0 - o.e[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn oct_norm_sq(o: Oct) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 { s = s + o.e[i as usize] * o.e[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

fn oct_norm(o: Oct) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    og_sqrt(oct_norm_sq(o))
}

// Fano plane: 7 triples encoding octonion multiplication
// (1,2,4) (2,3,5) (3,4,6) (4,5,7) (5,6,1) (6,7,2) (7,1,3)
fn oct_fano_index(i: i64, j: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if i == j { return 0 }
    var triples: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    triples[0] = 1; triples[1] = 2; triples[2] = 4
    triples[3] = 2; triples[4] = 3; triples[5] = 5
    triples[6] = 3; triples[7] = 4; triples[8] = 6
    triples[9] = 4; triples[10] = 5; triples[11] = 7
    triples[12] = 5; triples[13] = 6; triples[14] = 1
    triples[15] = 6; triples[16] = 7; triples[17] = 2
    triples[18] = 7; triples[19] = 1; triples[20] = 3
    var t: i64 = 0
    while t < 7 {
        let a = triples[(t * 3) as usize]
        let b = triples[(t * 3 + 1) as usize]
        let c = triples[(t * 3 + 2) as usize]
        if (i == a && j == b) || (i == b && j == c) || (i == c && j == a) {
            if i == a && j == b { return c }
            if i == b && j == c { return a }
            return b
        }
        if (i == b && j == a) || (i == c && j == b) || (i == a && j == c) {
            if i == b && j == a { return c }
            if i == c && j == b { return a }
            return b
        }
        t = t + 1
    }
    0
}

fn oct_fano_sign(i: i64, j: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if i == j { return -1.0 }
    if i == 0 || j == 0 { return 1.0 }
    var triples: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    triples[0] = 1; triples[1] = 2; triples[2] = 4
    triples[3] = 2; triples[4] = 3; triples[5] = 5
    triples[6] = 3; triples[7] = 4; triples[8] = 6
    triples[9] = 4; triples[10] = 5; triples[11] = 7
    triples[12] = 5; triples[13] = 6; triples[14] = 1
    triples[15] = 6; triples[16] = 7; triples[17] = 2
    triples[18] = 7; triples[19] = 1; triples[20] = 3
    var t: i64 = 0
    while t < 7 {
        let a = triples[(t * 3) as usize]
        let b = triples[(t * 3 + 1) as usize]
        let c = triples[(t * 3 + 2) as usize]
        if (i == a && j == b) || (i == b && j == c) || (i == c && j == a) { return 1.0 }
        if (i == b && j == a) || (i == c && j == b) || (i == a && j == c) { return -1.0 }
        t = t + 1
    }
    0.0
}

fn oct_mul(a: Oct, b: Oct) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = oct_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < 8 {
            let coeff = a.e[i as usize] * b.e[j as usize]
            if i == 0 && j == 0 {
                result.e[0] = result.e[0] + coeff
            } else if i == 0 {
                result.e[j as usize] = result.e[j as usize] + coeff
            } else if j == 0 {
                result.e[i as usize] = result.e[i as usize] + coeff
            } else if i == j {
                result.e[0] = result.e[0] - coeff
            } else {
                let k = oct_fano_index(i, j)
                let sign = oct_fano_sign(i, j)
                result.e[k as usize] = result.e[k as usize] + sign * coeff
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn oct_associator(a: Oct, b: Oct, c: Oct) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // [a,b,c] = (ab)c - a(bc)
    let ab = oct_mul(a, b)
    let bc = oct_mul(b, c)
    let ab_c = oct_mul(ab, c)
    let a_bc = oct_mul(a, bc)
    oct_sub(ab_c, a_bc)
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTONION-LABELED GRAPH (max 32 nodes)
// ============================================================================
//
// Each directed edge (u,v) carries an Oct label.
// adj[u*32+v] = 1 if edge exists, 0 otherwise.
// labels stored at labels_e[k][u*32+v] for component k of the octonion.
// (Flat arrays — matching CurvGraph pattern from stdlib/graph/curvature.sio)
//
// Convention for undirected graphs:
//   label(v,u) = oct_conjugate(label(u,v))
// This is algebraically natural: conjugation reverses multiplication order.

struct OctGraph {
    n: i32                      // number of nodes (max 32)
    adj: [i32; 1024]            // 32x32 adjacency matrix
    // Octonion edge labels stored per-component (avoid nested arrays)
    lab0: [f64; 1024]           // e[0] component of each edge label
    lab1: [f64; 1024]           // e[1]
    lab2: [f64; 1024]           // e[2]
    lab3: [f64; 1024]           // e[3]
    lab4: [f64; 1024]           // e[4]
    lab5: [f64; 1024]           // e[5]
    lab6: [f64; 1024]           // e[6]
    lab7: [f64; 1024]           // e[7]
}

fn og_new(n: i32) -> OctGraph {
    OctGraph {
        n: n,
        adj: [0; 1024],
        lab0: [0.0; 1024], lab1: [0.0; 1024], lab2: [0.0; 1024], lab3: [0.0; 1024],
        lab4: [0.0; 1024], lab5: [0.0; 1024], lab6: [0.0; 1024], lab7: [0.0; 1024],
    }
}

fn og_idx(u: i32, v: i32) -> i32 { u * 32 + v }

fn og_has_edge(g: OctGraph, u: i32, v: i32) -> bool with Panic {
    g.adj[og_idx(u, v) as usize] == 1
}

fn og_get_label(g: OctGraph, u: i32, v: i32) -> Oct with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = og_idx(u, v) as usize
    var o = Oct { e: [0.0; 8] }
    o.e[0] = g.lab0[idx]
    o.e[1] = g.lab1[idx]
    o.e[2] = g.lab2[idx]
    o.e[3] = g.lab3[idx]
    o.e[4] = g.lab4[idx]
    o.e[5] = g.lab5[idx]
    o.e[6] = g.lab6[idx]
    o.e[7] = g.lab7[idx]
    o
}

// Add directed edge with octonion label (by-value return pattern)
fn og_add_edge(g: OctGraph, u: i32, v: i32, label: Oct) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = g
    let idx = og_idx(u, v) as usize
    result.adj[idx] = 1
    result.lab0[idx] = label.e[0]
    result.lab1[idx] = label.e[1]
    result.lab2[idx] = label.e[2]
    result.lab3[idx] = label.e[3]
    result.lab4[idx] = label.e[4]
    result.lab5[idx] = label.e[5]
    result.lab6[idx] = label.e[6]
    result.lab7[idx] = label.e[7]
    result
}

// Add undirected edge: (u,v) gets label, (v,u) gets conjugate(label)
fn og_add_undirected_edge(g: OctGraph, u: i32, v: i32, label: Oct) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = og_add_edge(g, u, v, label)
    let conj = oct_conjugate(label)
    result = og_add_edge(result, v, u, conj)
    result
}

fn og_degree(g: OctGraph, v: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var d: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < g.n {
        if g.adj[og_idx(v, i) as usize] == 1 { d = d + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    d
}

fn og_edge_count(g: OctGraph) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var count: i32 = 0
    var u: i32 = 0
    while u < g.n {
        var v: i32 = 0
        while v < g.n {
            if g.adj[og_idx(u, v) as usize] == 1 { count = count + 1 }
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    count
}

// ============================================================================
// PATH PRODUCTS — the core construction
// ============================================================================
//
// A path is a sequence of node indices [v0, v1, v2, ..., vk].
// The edge labels along the path are: L1=label(v0,v1), L2=label(v1,v2), ...
//
// Because octonion multiplication is NON-ASSOCIATIVE, the product of
// these labels depends on how we parenthesize:
//   Left:     ((L1 * L2) * L3) * L4
//   Right:    L1 * (L2 * (L3 * L4))
//   Balanced: (L1 * L2) * (L3 * L4)
//
// KEY THEOREM: ||product|| is the SAME for all parenthesizations.
//              (Follows from norm multiplicativity of octonions)
//
// What changes is the DIRECTION. The associator measures that deviation.

// Left-associative path product: ((L1 * L2) * L3) * ...
fn og_path_product_left(g: OctGraph, path: [i32; 32], path_len: i32) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if path_len < 2 { return oct_real(1.0) }

    var acc = og_get_label(g, path[0], path[1])
    var i: i32 = 2
    while i < path_len {
        let edge = og_get_label(g, path[(i - 1) as usize], path[i as usize])
        acc = oct_mul(acc, edge)
        i = i + 1
    }
    acc
}

// Right-associative path product: L1 * (L2 * (L3 * ...))
fn og_path_product_right(g: OctGraph, path: [i32; 32], path_len: i32) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if path_len < 2 { return oct_real(1.0) }

    let last_edge_idx = path_len - 2
    var acc = og_get_label(g, path[last_edge_idx as usize], path[(path_len - 1) as usize])
    var i: i32 = last_edge_idx - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        let edge = og_get_label(g, path[i as usize], path[(i + 1) as usize])
        acc = oct_mul(edge, acc)
        i = i - 1
    }
    acc
}

// Balanced path product (binary tree): split in half, recurse
// For 4 edges: (L1*L2) * (L3*L4)
fn og_path_product_balanced_range(
    g: OctGraph, path: [i32; 32], lo: i32, hi: i32
) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // lo..hi are node indices; edges are between consecutive nodes
    let n_edges = hi - lo
    if n_edges <= 0 { return oct_real(1.0) }
    if n_edges == 1 {
        return og_get_label(g, path[lo as usize], path[(lo + 1) as usize])
    }
    // Split in the middle
    let mid = lo + n_edges / 2
    let left = og_path_product_balanced_range(g, path, lo, mid)
    let right = og_path_product_balanced_range(g, path, mid, hi)
    oct_mul(left, right)
}

fn og_path_product_balanced(g: OctGraph, path: [i32; 32], path_len: i32) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if path_len < 2 { return oct_real(1.0) }
    og_path_product_balanced_range(g, path, 0, path_len - 1)
}

// ============================================================================
// ASSOCIATOR FIELD — measures non-associativity over the graph
// ============================================================================
//
// For every triple of consecutive edges (u→v, v→w, w→x):
//   a = label(u,v), b = label(v,w), c = label(w,x)
//   associator = [a,b,c] = (ab)c - a(bc)
//
// The collection of all such associators is the "associator field" —
// a new graph invariant measuring how non-associative the labeled graph is.

struct AssocSample {
    u: i32
    v: i32
    w: i32
    x: i32
    norm: f64       // ||[a,b,c]||
}

struct AssocField {
    samples: [AssocSample; 512]
    count: i32
    mean_norm: f64
    max_norm: f64
    total_norm_sq: f64     // spectral energy: sum of ||[a,b,c]||^2
}

fn af_empty() -> AssocField {
    let empty_sample = AssocSample { u: 0, v: 0, w: 0, x: 0, norm: 0.0 }
    AssocField {
        samples: [empty_sample; 512],
        count: 0,
        mean_norm: 0.0,
        max_norm: 0.0,
        total_norm_sq: 0.0,
    }
}

// Compute the associator field over all length-3 paths in the graph
fn og_associator_field(g: OctGraph) -> AssocField with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var field = af_empty()
    var sum_norm: f64 = 0.0
    var max_n: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0

    var u: i32 = 0
    while u < g.n {
        var v: i32 = 0
        while v < g.n {
            if g.adj[og_idx(u, v) as usize] == 1 && u != v {
                var w: i32 = 0
                while w < g.n {
                    if g.adj[og_idx(v, w) as usize] == 1 && v != w {
                        var x: i32 = 0
                        while x < g.n {
                            if g.adj[og_idx(w, x) as usize] == 1 && w != x {
                                if field.count < 512 {
                                    let a = og_get_label(g, u, v)
                                    let b = og_get_label(g, v, w)
                                    let c = og_get_label(g, w, x)
                                    let assoc = oct_associator(a, b, c)
                                    let n = oct_norm(assoc)

                                    field.samples[field.count as usize] = AssocSample {
                                        u: u, v: v, w: w, x: x, norm: n,
                                    }
                                    field.count = field.count + 1
                                    sum_norm = sum_norm + n
                                    sum_sq = sum_sq + n * n
                                    if n > max_n { max_n = n }
                                }
                            }
                            x = x + 1
                        }
                    }
                    w = w + 1
                }
            }
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }

    if field.count > 0 {
        field.mean_norm = sum_norm / (field.count as f64)
    }
    field.max_norm = max_n
    field.total_norm_sq = sum_sq
    field
}

// ============================================================================
// NORM INVARIANCE — computational verification of the theorem
// ============================================================================
//
// Verify that left, right, and balanced products all have the same norm.
// This is the computational shadow of our Lean theorem.

fn og_verify_norm_invariance(g: OctGraph, path: [i32; 32], path_len: i32) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if path_len < 3 { return true }  // trivial for 1-2 edges

    let left = og_path_product_left(g, path, path_len)
    let right = og_path_product_right(g, path, path_len)
    let balanced = og_path_product_balanced(g, path, path_len)

    let norm_left = oct_norm(left)
    let norm_right = oct_norm(right)
    let norm_balanced = oct_norm(balanced)

    let tol = 1e-6
    let ok_lr = og_abs(norm_left - norm_right) < tol
    let ok_lb = og_abs(norm_left - norm_balanced) < tol
    ok_lr && ok_lb
}

// Verify that left and right products DIFFER (non-associativity is real)
fn og_verify_non_associativity(g: OctGraph, path: [i32; 32], path_len: i32) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if path_len < 4 { return false }  // need >= 3 edges

    let left = og_path_product_left(g, path, path_len)
    let right = og_path_product_right(g, path, path_len)
    let diff = oct_sub(left, right)
    oct_norm(diff) > 1e-6
}

// ============================================================================
// ANGULAR DEVIATION — what DOES change across parenthesizations
// ============================================================================
//
// Since ||product|| is invariant, we can normalize both products to S^7
// and measure the angular distance between them. This is the "associator
// angle" — how much reparenthesization rotates the result on the 7-sphere.

fn og_angular_deviation(g: OctGraph, path: [i32; 32], path_len: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if path_len < 4 { return 0.0 }

    let left = og_path_product_left(g, path, path_len)
    let right = og_path_product_right(g, path, path_len)

    let norm_l = oct_norm(left)
    let norm_r = oct_norm(right)
    if norm_l < 1e-12 || norm_r < 1e-12 { return 0.0 }

    // Normalize to unit octonions
    let ul = oct_scale(left, 1.0 / norm_l)
    let ur = oct_scale(right, 1.0 / norm_r)

    // Inner product on S^7
    var dot: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        dot = dot + ul.e[i as usize] * ur.e[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Clamp to [-1, 1] for numerical safety
    if dot > 1.0 { dot = 1.0 }
    if dot < -1.0 { dot = -1.0 }

    // Angular distance (in radians)
    // acos not available in JIT, use: angle ≈ sqrt(2*(1-dot)) for small angles
    // For large angles, use the full formula: angle = acos(dot)
    // Approximation: angle = sqrt(2 - 2*dot) (chord length ≈ angle for unit sphere)
    og_sqrt(2.0 - 2.0 * dot)
}

// ============================================================================
// SIMPLE GRAPH GENERATORS
// ============================================================================

// Linear congruential generator (matches stdlib/graph/random.sio pattern)
fn og_lcg_next(state: i64) -> i64 {
    // Numerical Recipes LCG (modulo 2^63 via overflow)
    let a: i64 = 6364136223846793005
    let c: i64 = 1442695040888963407
    state * a + c
}

fn og_lcg_to_f64(state: i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    // Map i64 to [0, 1) — take absolute value first
    let s = if state < 0 { 0 - state } else { state }
    (s as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0
}

// Generate a random unit octonion (uniform on S^7)
fn og_random_unit_oct(seed: i64) -> Oct with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var o = Oct { e: [0.0; 8] }
    var s = seed
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        s = og_lcg_next(s)
        // Map to [-1, 1]
        o.e[i as usize] = 2.0 * og_lcg_to_f64(s) - 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Normalize to unit
    let n = oct_norm(o)
    if n < 1e-12 { return oct_real(1.0) }
    oct_scale(o, 1.0 / n)
}

// Complete graph K_n with random unit octonion edge labels
fn og_complete_random(n: i32, seed: i64) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var g = og_new(n)
    var s = seed
    var u: i32 = 0
    while u < n {
        var v: i32 = u + 1
        while v < n {
            s = og_lcg_next(s)
            let label = og_random_unit_oct(s)
            g = og_add_undirected_edge(g, u, v, label)
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    g
}

// Path graph P_n with random unit octonion edge labels
fn og_path_random(n: i32, seed: i64) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var g = og_new(n)
    var s = seed
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        s = og_lcg_next(s)
        let label = og_random_unit_oct(s)
        g = og_add_undirected_edge(g, i, i + 1, label)
        i = i + 1
    }
    g
}

// Cycle graph C_n with random unit octonion edge labels
fn og_cycle_random(n: i32, seed: i64) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var g = og_path_random(n, seed)
    // Close the cycle
    var s = seed
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n + 1 { s = og_lcg_next(s); i = i + 1 }
    let label = og_random_unit_oct(s)
    g = og_add_undirected_edge(g, n - 1, 0, label)
    g
}

// Star graph S_n (node 0 is hub, connected to all others)
fn og_star_random(n: i32, seed: i64) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var g = og_new(n)
    var s = seed
    var i: i32 = 1
    while i < n {
        s = og_lcg_next(s)
        let label = og_random_unit_oct(s)
        g = og_add_undirected_edge(g, 0, i, label)
        i = i + 1
    }
    g
}

// Basis-labeled complete graph: edge (i,j) labeled with basis element e_{(i+j) mod 7 + 1}
fn og_complete_basis(n: i32) -> OctGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var g = og_new(n)
    var u: i32 = 0
    while u < n {
        var v: i32 = u + 1
        while v < n {
            let basis_idx = ((u + v) % 7 + 1) as i64
            let label = oct_unit(basis_idx)
            g = og_add_undirected_edge(g, u, v, label)
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    g
}


// === FILE: stdlib/hypercomplex_graph/orc.sio ===
// hypercomplex_graph::orc — Ollivier-Ricci Curvature for Brain Networks
//
// Computes discrete Ricci curvature on graphs, following the Lin-Lu-Yau
// (LLY) approximation of Ollivier-Ricci curvature. This is the main
// geometric tool for Paper 4: Brain ORC + Associator Field.
//
// For a graph G and edge (u,v):
//   ORC(u,v) = 1 - W_1(mu_u, mu_v) / d(u,v)
//
// where mu_u is the uniform distribution on neighbors of u and W_1 is
// the Wasserstein-1 (earth mover's) distance.
//
// The LLY simplification avoids solving the full optimal transport:
//   LLY(u,v) = 2/d_max - 2/(d_u * d_v) * |N(u) intersect N(v)|
//            + 2/(d_max) * (1/d_u + 1/d_v - 2/(d_u*d_v))
//
// For this implementation we use the exact discrete LLY formula:
//   kappa(u,v) = (2/d_u + 2/d_v - 2) + |triangle(u,v)|*(1/d_u + 1/d_v)
//             where d_u = deg(u), d_v = deg(v), triangle = common neighbors
//
// Simplified LLY (Lin-Lu-Yau 2011):
//   kappa(u,v) = |triangle(u,v)| * (1/d_u + 1/d_v) - (1 - 1/d_u - 1/d_v)
//
// Phase classification:
//   kappa > 0  → sphere-like (positive curvature)
//   kappa = 0  → flat (Euclidean-like)
//   kappa < 0  → hyperbolic (negative curvature)
//
// References:
//   - Ollivier, "Ricci curvature of Markov chains on metric spaces",
//     J. Funct. Anal. 256(3), 2009
//   - Lin, Lu, Yau, "Ricci curvature of graphs",
//     Tohoku Math. J. 63(4), 2011
//   - Sia, Jonckheere, Lux, "Ollivier-Ricci Curvature-Based Method to
//     Community Detection in Complex Networks", Sci Rep 9, 2019

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn orc_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn orc_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn orc_max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn orc_min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

// ============================================================================
// GRAPH REPRESENTATION — binary adjacency, max 200 nodes
// ============================================================================
// Uses the same flat-array pattern as AdjMatrix but stores binary adjacency
// (i32) for efficient neighbor lookups. Separate from AdjMatrix to avoid
// carrying weight data through curvature computations.

pub struct BinGraph {
    adj: [i32; 40000]       // 200*200 binary adjacency
    n: i64                  // node count (max 200)
}

fn bg_new(n: i64) -> BinGraph {
    BinGraph { adj: [0; 40000], n: n }
}

fn bg_idx(n: i64, i: i64, j: i64) -> i64 { i * n + j }

pub fn bg_has_edge(g: BinGraph, u: i64, v: i64) -> bool with Panic {
    g.adj[bg_idx(g.n, u, v) as usize] == 1
}

pub fn bg_set_edge(g: BinGraph, u: i64, v: i64) -> BinGraph with Mut, Panic {
    var out = g
    out.adj[bg_idx(g.n, u, v) as usize] = 1
    out.adj[bg_idx(g.n, v, u) as usize] = 1
    out
}

// Build binary graph from weighted matrix with threshold
pub fn bg_from_matrix(data: [f64; 40000], n: i64, threshold: f64) -> BinGraph with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var g = bg_new(n)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n {
            let w = data[(i * n + j) as usize]
            if w > threshold {
                g = bg_set_edge(g, i, j)
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    g
}

// ============================================================================
// DEGREE AND NEIGHBORS
// ============================================================================

pub fn bg_degree(g: BinGraph, v: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var d: i64 = 0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < g.n {
        if g.adj[bg_idx(g.n, v, j) as usize] == 1 { d = d + 1 }
        j = j + 1
    }
    d
}

// Count common neighbors: |N(u) intersect N(v)|
pub fn bg_common_neighbors(g: BinGraph, u: i64, v: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var count: i64 = 0
    var w: i64 = 0
    while w < g.n {
        if w != u && w != v {
            let u_w = g.adj[bg_idx(g.n, u, w) as usize]
            let v_w = g.adj[bg_idx(g.n, v, w) as usize]
            if u_w == 1 && v_w == 1 {
                count = count + 1
            }
        }
        w = w + 1
    }
    count
}

// Count triangles through edge (u,v) — same as common neighbors when edge exists
pub fn bg_triangles(g: BinGraph, u: i64, v: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    bg_common_neighbors(g, u, v)
}

// ============================================================================
// LIN-LU-YAU RICCI CURVATURE
// ============================================================================
//
// For edge (u,v) with degrees d_u, d_v, and t = |triangles(u,v)|:
//
//   kappa_LLY(u,v) = t * (1/d_u + 1/d_v) + (1/d_u + 1/d_v - 1)
//                   = (1/d_u + 1/d_v) * (t + 1) - 1
//
// This is the "lazy random walk" LLY formula. For the alpha=0 version:
//   kappa(u,v) = (t/d_u + t/d_v) - 1 + 1/d_u + 1/d_v
//
// We implement the standard formulation from Lin-Lu-Yau 2011 Theorem 1.1.

pub fn orc_lly_edge(g: BinGraph, u: i64, v: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let d_u = bg_degree(g, u)
    let d_v = bg_degree(g, v)
    if d_u == 0 || d_v == 0 { return 0.0 }

    let t = bg_common_neighbors(g, u, v)

    // LLY curvature: kappa(u,v) = t*(1/d_u + 1/d_v) + 1/d_u + 1/d_v - 1
    let inv_du = 1.0 / (d_u as f64)
    let inv_dv = 1.0 / (d_v as f64)
    let tri_term = (t as f64) * (inv_du + inv_dv)
    tri_term + inv_du + inv_dv - 1.0
}

// ============================================================================
// CURVATURE DISTRIBUTION OVER ALL EDGES
// ============================================================================

// Store per-edge curvature values (max 4000 edges for a 200-node graph)
pub struct OrcResult {
    // Per-edge data (flattened: edge_u[k], edge_v[k], kappa[k])
    edge_u: [i64; 4000]
    edge_v: [i64; 4000]
