    kappa:  [f64; 4000]
    n_edges: i64

    // Distribution statistics
    mean_kappa: f64
    min_kappa: f64
    max_kappa: f64
    std_kappa: f64

    // Phase counts
    n_positive: i64     // kappa > epsilon
    n_zero: i64         // |kappa| <= epsilon
    n_negative: i64     // kappa < -epsilon
}

fn orc_result_empty() -> OrcResult {
    OrcResult {
        edge_u: [0; 4000], edge_v: [0; 4000], kappa: [0.0; 4000],
        n_edges: 0,
        mean_kappa: 0.0, min_kappa: 0.0, max_kappa: 0.0, std_kappa: 0.0,
        n_positive: 0, n_zero: 0, n_negative: 0,
    }
}

// Compute LLY curvature for all edges in the graph
pub fn orc_compute(g: BinGraph) -> OrcResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = orc_result_empty()
    var sum_k: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_k2: f64 = 0.0
    var min_k: f64 = 1000.0
    var max_k: f64 = 0.0 - 1000.0
    let epsilon = 0.01

    var u: i64 = 0
    while u < g.n {
        var v: i64 = u + 1
        while v < g.n {
            if bg_has_edge(g, u, v) && result.n_edges < 4000 {
                let k = orc_lly_edge(g, u, v)
                let idx = result.n_edges as usize
                result.edge_u[idx] = u
                result.edge_v[idx] = v
                result.kappa[idx] = k
                result.n_edges = result.n_edges + 1

                sum_k = sum_k + k
                sum_k2 = sum_k2 + k * k
                if k < min_k { min_k = k }
                if k > max_k { max_k = k }

                if k > epsilon { result.n_positive = result.n_positive + 1 }
                else if k < (0.0 - epsilon) { result.n_negative = result.n_negative + 1 }
                else { result.n_zero = result.n_zero + 1 }
            }
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }

    if result.n_edges > 0 {
        let ne = result.n_edges as f64
        result.mean_kappa = sum_k / ne
        result.min_kappa = min_k
        result.max_kappa = max_k
        // std = sqrt(E[X^2] - E[X]^2)
        let var_k = sum_k2 / ne - (sum_k / ne) * (sum_k / ne)
        result.std_kappa = orc_sqrt(orc_abs(var_k))
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// PHASE CLASSIFICATION
// ============================================================================
//
// Classify the curvature distribution into geometric phases:
//   SPHERICAL (0):  majority positive curvature → densely connected core
//   FLAT (1):       curvature near zero → lattice-like regularity
//   HYPERBOLIC (2): majority negative curvature → tree-like, sparse
//   MIXED (3):      no dominant phase → heterogeneous geometry
//
// The hypothesis for Paper 4:
//   TD (typically developing) brains → more SPHERICAL (stronger communities)
//   ASD brains → more MIXED or HYPERBOLIC (disrupted module boundaries)

pub fn orc_phase_classify(result: OrcResult) -> i64 with Div, Panic {
    if result.n_edges == 0 { return 3 }  // MIXED by default

    let ne = result.n_edges as f64
    let frac_pos = (result.n_positive as f64) / ne
    let frac_neg = (result.n_negative as f64) / ne

    // Dominant phase: >50% of edges
    if frac_pos > 0.5 { return 0 }      // SPHERICAL
    if frac_neg > 0.5 { return 2 }      // HYPERBOLIC

    // Near-flat: mean curvature near zero AND low variance
    if orc_abs(result.mean_kappa) < 0.05 && result.std_kappa < 0.1 {
        return 1                          // FLAT
    }

    3  // MIXED
}

// ============================================================================
// CURVATURE ENTROPY — measures phase heterogeneity
// ============================================================================
// Shannon entropy of the curvature distribution (binned into K bins).
// High entropy = heterogeneous curvature = complex geometry.
// Low entropy = uniform curvature = regular geometry.
//
// For brain networks, ASD may show HIGHER entropy (more geometric disorder).

pub fn orc_curvature_entropy(result: OrcResult, n_bins: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if result.n_edges == 0 || n_bins <= 0 { return 0.0 }

    // Bin curvature values into n_bins bins over [min_kappa, max_kappa]
    var bins: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]
    let actual_bins = if n_bins > 64 { 64 } else { n_bins }
    let range = result.max_kappa - result.min_kappa
    if range < 1e-12 { return 0.0 }  // all same curvature

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < result.n_edges {
        let k = result.kappa[i as usize]
        var bin = ((k - result.min_kappa) / range * (actual_bins as f64)) as i64
        if bin >= actual_bins { bin = actual_bins - 1 }
        if bin < 0 { bin = 0 }
        bins[bin as usize] = bins[bin as usize] + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Shannon entropy: H = -sum p_i * log(p_i)
    // Use log2 approximation: log2(x) ~ (x - 1) * (1 + (x-1)/2 * ...)
    // For practical purposes, count non-empty bins and use uniform proxy
    var n_nonempty: i64 = 0
    var entropy: f64 = 0.0
    let ne = result.n_edges as f64

    var b: i64 = 0
    while b < actual_bins {
        if bins[b as usize] > 0 {
            n_nonempty = n_nonempty + 1
            let p = (bins[b as usize] as f64) / ne
            // log2(p) approximation using repeated squaring trick:
            // -p*log2(p) = p * log2(1/p)
            // For entropy calculation, we use: -p*ln(p) / ln(2)
            // Approximate ln(p) via ln(1 + (p-1)) Taylor expansion
            // Better approach: use the identity entropy = log2(n) - D_KL
            // Simplest correct approach: just count bits
            // We approximate -p*log2(p) using the relation for p = k/N:
            //   -p*log2(p) = (k/N) * log2(N/k) = (k/N)*(log2(N) - log2(k))
            // We approximate log2 via successive halving
            entropy = entropy + p * orc_approx_log2_inv(p)
        }
        b = b + 1
    }
    entropy
}

// Approximate log2(1/p) for 0 < p <= 1 using Newton's method on 2^x = 1/p
fn orc_approx_log2_inv(p: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if p <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    if p >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    // log2(1/p) = -log2(p)
    // Use the identity: log2(x) = (ln x) / ln 2
    // Approximate ln(x) for x in (0,1]: ln(x) = -sum_{k=1}^{inf} (1-x)^k / k
    let inv = 1.0 / p
    // For inv > 1: count powers of 2
    var x = inv
    var result: f64 = 0.0
    // Integer part
    while x >= 2.0 {
        x = x / 2.0
        result = result + 1.0
    }
    // Fractional part: x in [1, 2), log2(x) ~ (x - 1) - (x-1)^2/2 + ...
    // Using 3-term Taylor: log2(x) ~ (x-1)/ln(2) - (x-1)^2/(2*ln2) + (x-1)^3/(3*ln2)
    let d = x - 1.0
    let ln2 = 0.693147
    result = result + (d - d * d / 2.0 + d * d * d / 3.0) / ln2
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// NODE-LEVEL CURVATURE — average curvature at each node
// ============================================================================

pub struct NodeOrc {
    kappa: [f64; 200]     // average edge curvature per node
    n: i64
}

pub fn orc_node_curvature(g: BinGraph, edge_result: OrcResult) -> NodeOrc with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var node = NodeOrc { kappa: [0.0; 200], n: g.n }
    var count: [i64; 200] = [0; 200]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < edge_result.n_edges {
        let u = edge_result.edge_u[i as usize]
        let v = edge_result.edge_v[i as usize]
        let k = edge_result.kappa[i as usize]

        node.kappa[u as usize] = node.kappa[u as usize] + k
        count[u as usize] = count[u as usize] + 1
        node.kappa[v as usize] = node.kappa[v as usize] + k
        count[v as usize] = count[v as usize] + 1

        i = i + 1
    }

    // Average
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < g.n {
        if count[j as usize] > 0 {
            node.kappa[j as usize] = node.kappa[j as usize] / (count[j as usize] as f64)
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    node
}

// ============================================================================
// CURVATURE COMPARISON — for ASD vs TD analysis
// ============================================================================

pub struct OrcComparison {
    mean_diff: f64          // mean(kappa_A) - mean(kappa_B)
    entropy_diff: f64       // entropy(A) - entropy(B)
    phase_a: i64            // phase classification of A
    phase_b: i64            // phase classification of B
    frac_pos_diff: f64      // fraction positive curvature difference
    frac_neg_diff: f64      // fraction negative curvature difference
}

pub fn orc_compare(a: OrcResult, b: OrcResult) -> OrcComparison with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let ent_a = orc_curvature_entropy(a, 20)
    let ent_b = orc_curvature_entropy(b, 20)

    let frac_pos_a = if a.n_edges > 0 { (a.n_positive as f64) / (a.n_edges as f64) } else { 0.0 }
    let frac_pos_b = if b.n_edges > 0 { (b.n_positive as f64) / (b.n_edges as f64) } else { 0.0 }
    let frac_neg_a = if a.n_edges > 0 { (a.n_negative as f64) / (a.n_edges as f64) } else { 0.0 }
    let frac_neg_b = if b.n_edges > 0 { (b.n_negative as f64) / (b.n_edges as f64) } else { 0.0 }

    OrcComparison {
        mean_diff: a.mean_kappa - b.mean_kappa,
        entropy_diff: ent_a - ent_b,
        phase_a: orc_phase_classify(a),
        phase_b: orc_phase_classify(b),
        frac_pos_diff: frac_pos_a - frac_pos_b,
        frac_neg_diff: frac_neg_a - frac_neg_b,
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/image/pure/types.sio ===

pub struct Image {
    pub width: i32,
    pub height: i32,
    pub pixels: [u32; 65536],  // max 256x256 pixels
}

pub fn image_new(w: i32, h: i32) -> Image {
    Image { width: w, height: h, pixels: [0; 65536] }
}

pub fn image_get_pixel(img: &Image, x: i32, y: i32) -> u32 {
    if x < 0 || x >= img.width || y < 0 || y >= img.height { return 0 }
    let idx = (y * img.width + x) as usize
    img.pixels[idx]
}

pub fn image_set_pixel(img: &! Image, x: i32, y: i32, c: u32) with Mut {
    if x < 0 || x >= img.width || y < 0 || y >= img.height { return }
    let idx = (y * img.width + x) as usize
    img.pixels[idx] = c
}

pub fn image_width(img: &Image) -> i32 { img.width }

pub fn image_height(img: &Image) -> i32 { img.height }

// === FILE: stdlib/integrate/epistemic_ode.sio ===
// stdlib/integrate/epistemic_ode.sio
// Epistemic ODE Solver with GUM Uncertainty Propagation
//
// Integrates ordinary differential equations while tracking measurement
// uncertainty through each integration step via the Guide to the Expression
// of Uncertainty in Measurement (GUM, JCGM 100:2008).
//
// Uncertainty propagation model (linear, first-order GUM):
//   u(y_{n+1}) = sqrt(u(y_n)^2 + (dt * u(f))^2)
//
// This conservative linear bound is valid when the sensitivity of the
// numerical flux to initial uncertainty is close to unity — an assumption
// that holds for smooth, non-chaotic systems over short integration intervals.
//
// References:
//   JCGM 100:2008 (GUM) — https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf
//   Hairer, Norsett, Wanner — "Solving ODEs I" (2nd ed., 1993)
//   Kutta, M. (1901) — Beitrag zur näherungsweisen Integration totaler DGL

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn ode_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

fn ode_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// GUM combined uncertainty for independent additive contributions:
//   u_combined = sqrt(u1^2 + (scale * u2)^2)
fn gum_combine(u1: f64, scale: f64, u2: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let a = u1 * u1
    let b = scale * u2
    return ode_sqrt(a + b * b)
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC STATE — state vector with per-component GUM uncertainty
// ============================================================================

pub struct EpistemicState {
    pub values: [f64; 16],         // state values y_i
    pub uncertainties: [f64; 16],  // standard uncertainties u(y_i)
    pub n: i32,                    // number of active components
}

// Zero-initialise an EpistemicState for n active components.
pub fn epistemic_state_new(n: i32) -> EpistemicState with Mut, Panic {
    var s = EpistemicState {
        values:        [0.0; 16],
        uncertainties: [0.0; 16],
        n:             n,
    }
    return s
}

// ============================================================================
// SINGLE RK4-LIKE STEP WITH GUM UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATION
//
// The derivative is supplied by the caller as two arrays:
//   deriv_values[i]  — best-estimate of dy_i/dt at current state
//   deriv_unc[i]     — standard uncertainty of the derivative
//
// Value update  : y_{n+1} = y_n + dt * f
// Uncertainty   : u(y_{n+1}) = sqrt(u(y_n)^2 + (dt * u(f))^2)
//
// Note: This is a single Euler-style propagation in uncertainty space.
// The value step uses a provided derivative directly (no internal RK stages),
// which is consistent with the caller computing k-stages externally or using
// Euler forward integration as the deterministic method.
// ============================================================================

pub fn epistemic_rk4_step(
    state:       EpistemicState,
    t:           f64,
    dt:          f64,
    deriv_values: &[f64; 16],
    deriv_unc:   &[f64; 16]
) -> EpistemicState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var next = epistemic_state_new(state.n)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < state.n {
        let y_i   = state.values[i]
        let u_y   = state.uncertainties[i]
        let f_i   = deriv_values[i]
        let u_f   = deriv_unc[i]
        // Value step: standard forward Euler using provided derivative
        next.values[i] = y_i + dt * f_i
        // GUM propagation: u(y_{n+1}) = sqrt(u(y_n)^2 + (dt * u(f))^2)
        next.uncertainties[i] = gum_combine(u_y, dt, u_f)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return next
}

// ============================================================================
// DERIVATIVE FUNCTIONS
//
// Each function returns values and uncertainties into two caller-supplied
// mutable arrays.  Derivative uncertainty is estimated from state uncertainty
// using first-order GUM sensitivity analysis.
//
// idx=0  exponential decay  : dy/dt = -k*y,  k=0.1
//        u(f) = k * u(y)   (sensitivity ∂f/∂y = -k)
//
// idx=1  logistic growth    : dy/dt = r*y*(1 - y/K), r=0.5, K=100
//        u(f) ≈ |r*(1 - 2*y/K)| * u(y)  (linearised sensitivity)
//
// idx=2  harmonic oscillator: y = [y1, y2], dy1/dt=y2, dy2/dt=-y1
//        u(dy1/dt) = u(y2),  u(dy2/dt) = u(y1)
// ============================================================================

fn deriv_decay(
    state:  EpistemicState,
    out_v:  &![f64; 16],
    out_u:  &![f64; 16]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let k = 0.1
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < state.n {
        let y_i = state.values[i]
        let u_i = state.uncertainties[i]
        out_v[i] = 0.0 - k * y_i
        out_u[i] = k * u_i
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn deriv_logistic(
    state:  EpistemicState,
    out_v:  &![f64; 16],
    out_u:  &![f64; 16]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r   = 0.5
    let cap = 100.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < state.n {
        let y_i  = state.values[i]
        let u_i  = state.uncertainties[i]
        // Clamp y to [0, K] to keep derivative bounded
        var y_safe = y_i
        if y_safe < 0.0  { y_safe = 0.0 }
        if y_safe > cap  { y_safe = cap }
        let growth = r * y_safe * (1.0 - y_safe / cap)
        out_v[i] = growth
        // Linearised sensitivity |∂f/∂y| = |r*(1 - 2*y/K)|
        var sens = r * (1.0 - 2.0 * y_safe / cap)
        if sens < 0.0 { sens = 0.0 - sens }
        out_u[i] = sens * u_i
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn deriv_harmonic(
    state:  EpistemicState,
    out_v:  &![f64; 16],
    out_u:  &![f64; 16]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Requires at least 2 components: y[0]=position, y[1]=velocity
    // dy[0]/dt = y[1]   u = u(y[1])
    // dy[1]/dt = -y[0]  u = u(y[0])
    if state.n >= 2 {
        out_v[0] = state.values[1]
        out_u[0] = state.uncertainties[1]
        out_v[1] = 0.0 - state.values[0]
        out_u[1] = state.uncertainties[0]
    }
    // Any remaining components set to zero derivatives
    var i: i32 = 2
    while i < state.n {
        out_v[i] = 0.0
        out_u[i] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// EULER INTEGRATION WITH UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATION
//
// deriv_fn_idx selects the ODE:
//   0 — exponential decay   dy/dt = -0.1*y
//   1 — logistic growth     dy/dt = 0.5*y*(1 - y/100)
//   2 — harmonic oscillator dy/dt = [y2, -y1]
// ============================================================================

pub fn epistemic_euler_solve(
    y0:          EpistemicState,
    t0:          f64,
    t1:          f64,
    n_steps:     i32,
    deriv_fn_idx: i32
) -> EpistemicState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var n_safe = n_steps
    if n_safe < 1 { n_safe = 1 }
    let dt = (t1 - t0) / (n_safe as f64)
    var state = y0
    var dv: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var du: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var step: i32 = 0
    while step < n_safe {
        // Evaluate derivative
        if deriv_fn_idx == 0 {
            deriv_decay(state, &!dv, &!du)
        } else if deriv_fn_idx == 1 {
            deriv_logistic(state, &!dv, &!du)
        } else {
            deriv_harmonic(state, &!dv, &!du)
        }
        // Advance state with uncertainty propagation
        state = epistemic_rk4_step(state, t0 + (step as f64) * dt, dt, &dv, &du)
        step = step + 1
    }
    return state
}

// ============================================================================
// CONVENIENCE WRAPPER — Exponential Decay with Uncertain Rate
//
// Solves  dy/dt = -k*y,  y(0) = y0
// where both y0 and k carry standard uncertainties u_y0 and u_k.
//
// GUM sensitivity for the rate constant:
//   u(f) = sqrt((k * u_y)^2 + (y * u_k)^2)
//
// This is a first-order Taylor expansion of f(y, k) = -k*y.
// ============================================================================

pub fn epistemic_solve_decay(
    y0:      f64,
    u_y0:    f64,
    k:       f64,
    u_k:     f64,
    t_end:   f64,
    n_steps: i32
) -> EpistemicState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var n_safe = n_steps
    if n_safe < 1 { n_safe = 1 }
    let dt = t_end / (n_safe as f64)

    // Set up initial state: single-component decay
    var state = epistemic_state_new(1)
    state.values[0]        = y0
    state.uncertainties[0] = u_y0

    var dv: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var du: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

    var step: i32 = 0
    while step < n_safe {
        let y_i = state.values[0]
        let u_y = state.uncertainties[0]
        // Best-estimate derivative
        dv[0] = 0.0 - k * y_i
        // GUM uncertainty: u(f)^2 = (k * u_y)^2 + (y * u_k)^2
        let a = k * u_y
        let b = y_i * u_k
        du[0] = ode_sqrt(a * a + b * b)
        state = epistemic_rk4_step(state, (step as f64) * dt, dt, &dv, &du)
        step = step + 1
    }
    return state
}


// === FILE: stdlib/integrate/mod.sio ===
// integrate — Numerical Quadrature Module
//
// Provides composite Newton-Cotes rules (trapezoid, Simpson, Simpson 3/8,
// Boole, midpoint), Gauss-Legendre quadrature (2-5 points + composite),
// Romberg integration with Richardson extrapolation, and adaptive Simpson
// refinement.
//
// References:
//   Stoer & Bulirsch, "Introduction to Numerical Analysis" (2002)
//   Burden & Faires, "Numerical Analysis" (10th ed.)
//   Abramowitz & Stegun, Table 25.4 (Gauss-Legendre nodes/weights)

// ============================================================================
// RESULT TYPE
// ============================================================================

struct QuadResult {
    value: f64,
    error_estimate: f64,
    intervals: i32,
    converged: bool,
}

fn quad_result(value: f64, err: f64, intervals: i32, converged: bool) -> QuadResult with Mut, Panic {
    QuadResult { value: value, error_estimate: err, intervals: intervals, converged: converged }
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// NEWTON-COTES RULES
// ============================================================================

// Composite trapezoidal rule
fn trapezoid(a: f64, b: f64, n: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let h = (b - a) / (n as f64)
    var sum = 0.5 * (f(a) + f(b))
    var i: i32 = 1
    while i < n {
        let x = a + (i as f64) * h
        sum = sum + f(x)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum * h
}

// Composite Simpson's 1/3 rule (n must be even; if odd, bump to n+1)
fn simpson(a: f64, b: f64, n: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var nn = n
    if nn < 2 { nn = 2 }
    // Ensure even
    let rem = nn - 2 * (nn / 2)
    if rem != 0 { nn = nn + 1 }

    let h = (b - a) / (nn as f64)
    var sum = f(a) + f(b)

    var i: i32 = 1
    while i < nn {
        let x = a + (i as f64) * h
        let rem_i = i - 2 * (i / 2)
        if rem_i != 0 {
            sum = sum + 4.0 * f(x)
        } else {
            sum = sum + 2.0 * f(x)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum * h / 3.0
}

// Composite Simpson's 3/8 rule (n must be divisible by 3; adjusted if not)
fn simpson38(a: f64, b: f64, n: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var nn = n
    if nn < 3 { nn = 3 }
    // Make divisible by 3
    let r = nn - 3 * (nn / 3)
    if r != 0 { nn = nn + (3 - r) }

    let h = (b - a) / (nn as f64)
    var sum = f(a) + f(b)

    var i: i32 = 1
    while i < nn {
        let x = a + (i as f64) * h
        let r3 = i - 3 * (i / 3)
        if r3 == 0 {
            sum = sum + 2.0 * f(x)
        } else {
            sum = sum + 3.0 * f(x)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum * 3.0 * h / 8.0
}

// Composite midpoint rule
fn midpoint(a: f64, b: f64, n: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let h = (b - a) / (n as f64)
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let x = a + ((i as f64) + 0.5) * h
        sum = sum + f(x)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum * h
}

// Boole's rule (Newton-Cotes degree 4, n must be divisible by 4)
fn boole(a: f64, b: f64, n: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var nn = n
    if nn < 4 { nn = 4 }
    let r = nn - 4 * (nn / 4)
    if r != 0 { nn = nn + (4 - r) }

    let h = (b - a) / (nn as f64)
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < nn / 4 {
        let x0 = a + (4 * i) as f64 * h
        let x1 = x0 + h
        let x2 = x0 + 2.0 * h
        let x3 = x0 + 3.0 * h
        let x4 = x0 + 4.0 * h
        sum = sum + (7.0 * f(x0) + 32.0 * f(x1) + 12.0 * f(x2) + 32.0 * f(x3) + 7.0 * f(x4)) * 2.0 * h / 45.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// ============================================================================
// GAUSS-LEGENDRE QUADRATURE
// ============================================================================

// Transform from [-1,1] to [a,b]: x = 0.5*(b-a)*t + 0.5*(a+b)
// dx = 0.5*(b-a)*dt

// 2-point Gauss-Legendre
// Nodes: +/- 1/sqrt(3) = +/- 0.5773502691896258
// Weights: 1.0, 1.0
fn gauss_legendre_2(a: f64, b: f64, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let half_len = 0.5 * (b - a)
    let mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
    let n1 = 0.5773502691896258
    let x0 = mid - half_len * n1
    let x1 = mid + half_len * n1
    return half_len * (f(x0) + f(x1))
}

// 3-point Gauss-Legendre
// Nodes: 0, +/- 0.7745966692414834
// Weights: 8/9, 5/9, 5/9
fn gauss_legendre_3(a: f64, b: f64, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let half_len = 0.5 * (b - a)
    let mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
    let n1 = 0.7745966692414834
    let w0 = 8.0 / 9.0
    let w1 = 5.0 / 9.0
    let x0 = mid
    let x1 = mid - half_len * n1
    let x2 = mid + half_len * n1
    return half_len * (w0 * f(x0) + w1 * f(x1) + w1 * f(x2))
}

// 4-point Gauss-Legendre
// Nodes: +/- 0.8611363115940526, +/- 0.3399810435848563
// Weights: 0.3478548451374538, 0.6521451548625461
fn gauss_legendre_4(a: f64, b: f64, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let half_len = 0.5 * (b - a)
    let mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
    let n1 = 0.8611363115940526
    let n2 = 0.3399810435848563
    let w1 = 0.3478548451374538
    let w2 = 0.6521451548625461
    let x0 = mid - half_len * n1
    let x1 = mid + half_len * n1
    let x2 = mid - half_len * n2
    let x3 = mid + half_len * n2
    return half_len * (w1 * f(x0) + w1 * f(x1) + w2 * f(x2) + w2 * f(x3))
}

// 5-point Gauss-Legendre
// Nodes: +/- 0.9061798459386640, +/- 0.5384693101056831, 0
// Weights: 0.2369268850561891, 0.4786286704993665, 0.5688888888888889
fn gauss_legendre_5(a: f64, b: f64, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let half_len = 0.5 * (b - a)
    let mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
    let n1 = 0.9061798459386640
    let n2 = 0.5384693101056831
    let w1 = 0.2369268850561891
    let w2 = 0.4786286704993665
    let w0 = 0.5688888888888889
    let x0 = mid
    let x1 = mid - half_len * n1
    let x2 = mid + half_len * n1
    let x3 = mid - half_len * n2
    let x4 = mid + half_len * n2
    return half_len * (w0 * f(x0) + w1 * f(x1) + w1 * f(x2) + w2 * f(x3) + w2 * f(x4))
}

// Composite Gauss-Legendre: split [a,b] into m sub-intervals, apply n_points GL on each
fn composite_gauss_legendre(a: f64, b: f64, m: i32, n_points: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let h = (b - a) / (m as f64)
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < m {
        let sub_a = a + (i as f64) * h
        let sub_b = sub_a + h
        if n_points == 2 {
            sum = sum + gauss_legendre_2(sub_a, sub_b, f)
        } else if n_points == 3 {
            sum = sum + gauss_legendre_3(sub_a, sub_b, f)
        } else if n_points == 4 {
            sum = sum + gauss_legendre_4(sub_a, sub_b, f)
        } else {
            sum = sum + gauss_legendre_5(sub_a, sub_b, f)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// ============================================================================
// ROMBERG INTEGRATION
// ============================================================================

// Romberg integration with Richardson extrapolation
// Uses a triangular table R[level][k], stored flat in [f64; 256]
// Index: R[level * 16 + k]
// max_level capped at 15 (so up to 16 rows, 16 cols = 256 entries)
fn romberg(a: f64, b: f64, max_level: i32, tol: f64, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> QuadResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var mlev = max_level
    if mlev > 15 { mlev = 15 }
    if mlev < 1 { mlev = 1 }

    var R: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]

    // R[0,0] = basic trapezoid
    R[0] = 0.5 * (b - a) * (f(a) + f(b))

    var level: i32 = 1
    while level <= mlev {
        // Compute R[level, 0] = trapezoid with 2^level panels
        let n_panels = 1 << level
        let h = (b - a) / (n_panels as f64)

        // Sum the new midpoints (odd-indexed points)
        var mid_sum = 0.0
        var j: i32 = 1
        while j < n_panels {
            let j_rem = j - 2 * (j / 2)
            if j_rem != 0 {
                let x = a + (j as f64) * h
                mid_sum = mid_sum + f(x)
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        R[level * 16] = 0.5 * R[(level - 1) * 16] + h * mid_sum

        // Richardson extrapolation
        var k: i32 = 1
        while k <= level {
            let prev = R[level * 16 + (k - 1)]
            let prev_level = R[(level - 1) * 16 + (k - 1)]
            let four_k = 1 << (2 * k)
            R[level * 16 + k] = prev + (prev - prev_level) / ((four_k as f64) - 1.0)
            k = k + 1
        }

        // Check convergence
        let current = R[level * 16 + level]
        let previous = R[(level - 1) * 16 + (level - 1)]
        let err = abs_f64(current - previous)
        if err < tol {
            return quad_result(current, err, 1 << level, true)
        }

        level = level + 1
    }

    let final_val = R[mlev * 16 + mlev]
    let prev_val = R[(mlev - 1) * 16 + (mlev - 1)]
    let final_err = abs_f64(final_val - prev_val)
    return quad_result(final_val, final_err, 1 << mlev, false)
}

// ============================================================================
// ADAPTIVE SIMPSON
// ============================================================================

// Recursive adaptive Simpson step
fn adaptive_simpson_step(
    a: f64, b: f64,
    fa: f64, fb: f64, fm: f64,
    whole: f64,
    tol: f64,
    depth: i32,
    f: fn(f64) -> f64
) -> QuadResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
    let ml = 0.5 * (a + mid)
    let mr = 0.5 * (mid + b)
    let fml = f(ml)
    let fmr = f(mr)

    let h = b - a
    let left = (h / 12.0) * (fa + 4.0 * fml + fm)
    let right = (h / 12.0) * (fm + 4.0 * fmr + fb)
    let refined = left + right
    let err = (refined - whole) / 15.0

    if depth <= 0 || abs_f64(err) < tol {
        let val = refined + err
        return quad_result(val, abs_f64(err), 2, true)
    }

    let left_result = adaptive_simpson_step(a, mid, fa, fm, fml, left, tol / 2.0, depth - 1, f)
    let right_result = adaptive_simpson_step(mid, b, fm, fb, fmr, right, tol / 2.0, depth - 1, f)

    let total_val = left_result.value + right_result.value
    let total_err = left_result.error_estimate + right_result.error_estimate
    let total_intervals = left_result.intervals + right_result.intervals
    let conv = left_result.converged && right_result.converged

    return quad_result(total_val, total_err, total_intervals, conv)
}

// Adaptive Simpson integration
fn adaptive_simpson(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> QuadResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let fa = f(a)
    let fb = f(b)
    let fm = f(0.5 * (a + b))
    let h = b - a
    let whole = (h / 6.0) * (fa + 4.0 * fm + fb)

    return adaptive_simpson_step(a, b, fa, fb, fm, whole, tol, 20, f)
}

// ============================================================================
// CONVENIENCE WRAPPER
// ============================================================================

// Default integration routine: uses Romberg with tolerance
fn integrate(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> QuadResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    return romberg(a, b, 15, tol, f)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/interop/medlang.sio ===
// interop/medlang.sio — MedLang interoperability layer
// Bridges Sounio PK/PD types to MedLang specification
//
// Uses struct-of-arrays layout to avoid BSS aliasing bugs with
// large array-of-struct fields in the native codegen.

pub struct MedLangDose {
    amount: f64,
    route: i64,       // 0=IV, 1=oral, 2=IM
    time: f64,
    duration: f64,
}

pub fn medlang_dose_iv(amount: f64, time: f64) -> MedLangDose {
    MedLangDose { amount: amount, route: 0, time: time, duration: 0.0 }
}

pub fn medlang_dose_oral(amount: f64, time: f64) -> MedLangDose {
    MedLangDose { amount: amount, route: 1, time: time, duration: 0.0 }
}

pub fn medlang_dose_infusion(amount: f64, time: f64, duration: f64) -> MedLangDose {
    MedLangDose { amount: amount, route: 0, time: time, duration: duration }
}

pub struct MedLangObservation {
    time: f64,
    dv: f64,
    cmt: i64,
    mdv: i64,
}

pub fn medlang_obs_new(time: f64, dv: f64, cmt: i64) -> MedLangObservation {
    MedLangObservation { time: time, dv: dv, cmt: cmt, mdv: 0 }
}

// MedLangSubject uses struct-of-arrays to avoid BSS aliasing with large arrays
pub struct MedLangSubject {
    id: i64,
    weight: f64,
    age: f64,
    sex: i64,
    // Doses (SoA layout, max 16)
    dose_amounts:    [f64; 16],
    dose_routes:     [i64; 16],
    dose_times:      [f64; 16],
    dose_durations:  [f64; 16],
    n_doses: i64,
    // Observations (SoA layout, max 64)
    obs_times: [f64; 64],
    obs_dvs:   [f64; 64],
    obs_cmts:  [i64; 64],
    obs_mdvs:  [i64; 64],
    n_obs: i64,
}

pub fn medlang_subject_new(id: i64, weight: f64, age: f64, sex: i64) -> MedLangSubject {
    MedLangSubject {
        id: id, weight: weight, age: age, sex: sex,
        dose_amounts: [0.0; 16], dose_routes: [0; 16],
        dose_times: [0.0; 16], dose_durations: [0.0; 16],
        n_doses: 0,
        obs_times: [0.0; 64], obs_dvs: [0.0; 64],
        obs_cmts: [0; 64], obs_mdvs: [0; 64],
        n_obs: 0,
    }
}

pub fn medlang_add_dose(subj: &! MedLangSubject, dose: MedLangDose) with Mut, Panic {
    if subj.n_doses < 16 {
        let n = subj.n_doses
        subj.dose_amounts[n] = dose.amount
        subj.dose_routes[n] = dose.route
        subj.dose_times[n] = dose.time
        subj.dose_durations[n] = dose.duration
        subj.n_doses = n + 1
    }
}

pub fn medlang_add_obs(subj: &! MedLangSubject, obs: MedLangObservation) with Mut, Panic {
    if subj.n_obs < 64 {
        let n = subj.n_obs
        subj.obs_times[n] = obs.time
        subj.obs_dvs[n] = obs.dv
        subj.obs_cmts[n] = obs.cmt
        subj.obs_mdvs[n] = obs.mdv
        subj.n_obs = n + 1
    }
}

// One-compartment model evaluation
pub fn medlang_onecomp_conc(cl: f64, v: f64, ka: f64, dose: f64, t: f64, is_iv: bool) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if t <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ke = cl / v
    // exp approximation
    var exp_ke = 1.0
    var term_ke = 1.0
    let x_ke = 0.0 - ke * t
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 { term_ke = term_ke * x_ke / (i as f64); exp_ke = exp_ke + term_ke; i = i + 1 }

    if is_iv {
        (dose / v) * exp_ke
    } else {
        var exp_ka = 1.0
        var term_ka = 1.0
        let x_ka = 0.0 - ka * t
        i = 1
        while i < 20 { term_ka = term_ka * x_ka / (i as f64); exp_ka = exp_ka + term_ka; i = i + 1 }
        (dose * ka / (v * (ka - ke))) * (exp_ke - exp_ka)
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/interp/basis168.sio ===
// stdlib/interp/basis168.sio
//
// The canonical 168-class basis of Sounio's Algebraic Mechanistic
// Interpretability (AMI).
//
// Paper B (SounioZeroDivisorBridge.lean) proves that the sedenion
// algebra 𝕊 has exactly 168 projective (unordered) zero-divisor classes
// and 336 ordered ZD pairs, arranged into a 4-regular graph over
// 84 two-support primitive elements.  The 168 classes partition the
// ZD structure exactly, and — crucially for AMI — they form a FIXED
// BASIS that is independent of any trained model.
//
// This means: unlike SAEs (Sparse Autoencoders) or transcoders, which
// discover interpretability bases empirically on each new checkpoint,
// the AMI basis is determined a priori by the algebraic structure.
// Interpretability becomes a projection, not a discovery.
//
// Each of the 168 classes corresponds to an unordered pair {u, v} of
// sedenion primitives with u·v = 0.  For each class we emit:
//   - class_index : i64 (0..167)
//   - fiber       : i64 (0..6, the Fano-fibre tag = u.lo XOR u.hi)
//   - position    : i64 (0..23, the ordinal of the class within its fibre)
//
// The 168 = 7 × 24 decomposition: 7 Fano fibres × 24 classes per fibre.
//
// This file provides helpers to enumerate the basis classes and map
// activations to their 168-coefficient decomposition.  The full Lean
// completeness theorem is in formal/lean4/SounioInterpBasis.lean.

// N_CLASSES: total number of projective ZD classes.
let N_CLASSES: i64 = 168

// N_FIBERS: number of Fano fibres in the 168-graph decomposition.
let N_FIBERS: i64 = 7

// N_PER_FIBER: classes per fibre (168 / 7).
let N_PER_FIBER: i64 = 24

// class_fiber: maps a class index (0..167) to its Fano fibre (0..6).
// The Sedenion algebra's Fano-like 7-colouring is the XOR label of the
// two components' supports (verified in SounioZeroDivisorBridge.lean).
fn class_fiber(class_idx: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    class_idx / N_PER_FIBER
}

// class_position: ordinal position within the fibre (0..23).
fn class_position(class_idx: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    class_idx % N_PER_FIBER
}

// fiber_of: the non-trivial fibre tags (1..7) used by the ZD graph.
// Fibre 0 is reserved for the identity element; the seven non-trivial
// fibres correspond to the 7 lines of the Fano plane in the standard
// octonion/sedenion multiplication table.
fn fiber_tag(fiber_idx: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    fiber_idx + 1
}

// class_exists: sanity check that an index refers to a valid class.
fn class_exists(class_idx: i64) -> bool with Mut, Panic, ZD {
    class_idx >= 0 && class_idx < N_CLASSES
}

// total_classes: expose N_CLASSES through a function (for callers that
// want the effect-typed guarantee).
fn total_classes() -> i64 with Mut, ZD { N_CLASSES }


// === FILE: stdlib/interp/capability_probe.sio ===
// stdlib/interp/capability_probe.sio
//
// Per-class capability probes — the substitute for SAE/transcoder
// interpretability in the AMI framework.
//
// A "capability probe" is a small function that, given a sedenion
// activation h and a ZD class index (0..83 for two-support primitives,
// 0..167 for full ZD-pair classes), returns a single f64 coefficient
// describing the activation's magnitude along that capability direction.
//
// Unlike SAEs (which train a dictionary of 2^N latent features for a
// specific model), probes are STATIC: the same probe can be applied to
// any sedenion-structured activation in any model, because the basis
// is defined by the ZD graph, not by the data.
//
// Operational claim, Paper D:
//   Every activation of a Sounio-compiled SSM admits a unique, sparse
//   decomposition onto the 84-class two-support basis, with most mass
//   concentrated in 2-5 fibres for typical linguistic inputs.

// probe_class: simplified scalar probe for a two-support class (i_idx, j_idx).
// Returns the squared activation magnitude along the basis direction.
fn probe_class(h: &[f64; 16], i_idx: i64, j_idx: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    let s = 0.707107
    let c = (*h)[i_idx as usize] * s + (*h)[j_idx as usize] * s
    c * c
}

// probe_fiber_mass: total squared mass of activations in a Fano fibre.
// A fibre is characterized by its XOR label (0..6 for the 7 non-trivial
// lines of the Fano plane structure in the sedenion multiplication).
// For simplicity we use the XOR of the two support indices (as used in
// SounioZeroDivisorBridge.lean's fiberPrims definition).
fn probe_fiber_mass(h: &[f64; 16], target_label: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    let s = 0.707107
    var total = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < 16 {
            let label = i ^ j
            if label == target_label {
                let c = (*h)[i as usize] * s + (*h)[j as usize] * s
                total = total + c * c
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    total
}

// top_fiber: which of the 7 Fano fibres has the greatest activation mass
// in this hidden state.  Returns an index 1..7 (0 reserved for identity).
fn top_fiber(h: &[f64; 16]) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    var best_label: i64 = 1
    var best_mass = probe_fiber_mass(h, 1)
    var lab: i64 = 2
    while lab <= 7 {
        let m = probe_fiber_mass(h, lab)
        if m > best_mass { best_mass = m; best_label = lab }
        lab = lab + 1
    }
    best_label
}

// sparsity: count of classes with capability_activation above `threshold`.
// Low sparsity (few active classes) is the AMI analogue of SAE's
// "sparse feature activation" — but here the sparsity pattern is
// determined by the ZD algebra, not by optimization.
fn sparsity(h: &[f64; 16], threshold: f64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    let s = 0.707107
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < 16 {
            let c = (*h)[i as usize] * s + (*h)[j as usize] * s
            let mag = if c < 0.0 { 0.0 - c } else { c }
            if mag > threshold { count = count + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    count
}


// === FILE: stdlib/interp/projection.sio ===
// stdlib/interp/projection.sio
//
// Projection / reconstruction utilities for the AMI 168-basis.
//
// The key claim of Paper D (paper_d_ami.tex): interpretability is a
// projection problem, not a discovery problem.  Given a 16-dim sedenion
// activation h(t), we decompose it onto the 168-class basis in a fixed,
// model-independent way, and every non-zero coefficient corresponds to
// a known algebraic capability of the ZD graph.
//
// Full reconstruction is not pointwise for a 16-dim vector onto a 168-dim
// basis: 168 > 16, so the basis is over-complete.  We provide:
//
//   - decompose_onto_two_support_classes: the 84-primitive projection
//     onto the canonical two-support basis.  This is the invertible part:
//     every 16-dim vector has a unique decomposition here.
//
//   - capability_activation: for a given ZD class (indexed 0..167), the
//     inner-product magnitude of the activation with the class's
//     characteristic vector.  This is the "heatmap" quantity used in
//     examples/interp_168_basis.sio.
//
// Runtime cost: O(dim²) per activation, embarrassingly parallel.

// sqrt2_inv: a single-precision approximation of 1/sqrt(2), used
// throughout the examples to match the reference implementation.
fn sqrt2_inv() -> f64 with Mut, ZD { 0.707107 }

// two_support_basis_pair: maps a class index (0..83) to its pair of
// sedenion indices (i, j) with 0 <= i < j < 16.  We return (i, j)
// concatenated as a single i64 (i * 16 + j).  This is a compact
// representation; callers split with div/mod.
//
// The enumeration is lex order: classes 0..15 are (0, 1..15); classes
// 16..29 are (1, 2..15); etc.  Total 16*15/2 = 120 pairs, but only 84
// of them correspond to primitives valid under the ZD-graph structure
// used by SounioZeroDivisorBridge.lean.  For the 84-valid subset the
// lower-level `validPrims` table (in Lean) is authoritative.
fn lex_pair_ij(class_idx: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    // Compute (i, j) such that class_idx = sum_{k<i}(15-k) + (j - i - 1)
    // and return encoded as i * 16 + j.
    var i: i64 = 0
    var remaining = class_idx
    while i < 15 {
        let row_len = 15 - i
        if remaining < row_len {
            let j = i + 1 + remaining
            return i * 16 + j
        }
        remaining = remaining - row_len
        i = i + 1
    }
    0   // unreachable for class_idx < 120
}

// inner16: 16-dim inner product (replicated here to keep this file
// self-contained so the interp path does not pull in epistemic/).
fn inner16(a: &[f64; 16], b: &[f64; 16]) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, ZD {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { s = s + (*a)[i] * (*b)[i]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

// two_support_basis_vector: writes into `out` the (orthonormal) basis
// vector for a two-support class.  Specifically (e_i + e_j)/sqrt(2)
// for classes with positive phase, (e_i - e_j)/sqrt(2) for negative
// phase.  For this stdlib shim we default to positive phase; the full
// signed basis is handled by the enumeration macro in Paper D's
// reference implementation.
fn two_support_basis_vector(i_idx: i64, j_idx: i64, out: &![f64; 16]) with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    let s = sqrt2_inv()
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { (*out)[k] = 0.0; k = k + 1 }
    (*out)[i_idx as usize] = s
    (*out)[j_idx as usize] = s
}

// capability_activation: projection coefficient of activation `h`
// onto the basis vector for class with indices (i, j).  This is what
// Paper D's heatmap plots.
fn capability_activation(h: &[f64; 16], i_idx: i64, j_idx: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic, ZD {
    let s = sqrt2_inv()
    (*h)[i_idx as usize] * s + (*h)[j_idx as usize] * s
}


// === FILE: stdlib/interpolation/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/interpolation/lib.sio - Interpolation functions
//!
//! Provides interpolation utilities for scientific computing:
//! - Linear interpolation (lerp)
//! - Piecewise linear interpolation
//! - Cubic spline interpolation
//!
//! These functions are essential for resampling data, function approximation,
//! and visualization of irregular datasets.

// Linearly interpolates between two values a and b using parameter t.
// When t=0 returns a, when t=1 returns b.
// Extrapolates if t is outside [0, 1].
pub fn lerp(a: f64, b: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    a + t * (b - a)
}

// Inverse lerp: given a, b, and a value v, returns the t such that lerp(a, b, t) = v.
// Returns 0.0 if a == b to avoid division by zero.
pub fn inverse_lerp(a: f64, b: f64, v: f64) -> f64 {
    if a == b {
        return 0.0
    }
    (v - a) / (b - a)
}

// Remaps a value from one range to another.
// Equivalent to lerp(out_min, out_max, inverse_lerp(in_min, in_max, value)).
pub fn remap(value: f64, in_min: f64, in_max: f64, out_min: f64, out_max: f64) -> f64 {
    let t = inverse_lerp(in_min, in_max, value)
    lerp(out_min, out_max, t)
}

// Clamps t to [0, 1] then performs lerp.
pub fn lerp_clamped(a: f64, b: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    let t_clamped = if t < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { if t > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { t } }
    lerp(a, b, t_clamped)
}

// Smooth step interpolation using 3t² - 2t³ (Hermite interpolation).
// Provides smooth acceleration and deceleration.
pub fn smoothstep(a: f64, b: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    let t_clamped = if t < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { if t > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { t } }
    let s = t_clamped * t_clamped * (3.0 - 2.0 * t_clamped)
    lerp(a, b, s)
}

// Smoother step interpolation using 6t⁵ - 15t⁴ + 10t³ (Perlin's improved interpolation).
// Has zero first and second derivatives at endpoints.
pub fn smootherstep(a: f64, b: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    let t_clamped = if t < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { if t > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { t } }
    let s = t_clamped * t_clamped * t_clamped * (t_clamped * (t_clamped * 6.0 - 15.0) + 10.0)
    lerp(a, b, s)
}

// Bilinear interpolation on a 2D grid.
// c00, c01, c10, c11 are the four corner values.
// tx is the x interpolation parameter [0,1], ty is the y parameter [0,1].
pub fn bilerp(c00: f64, c10: f64, c01: f64, c11: f64, tx: f64, ty: f64) -> f64 {
    let a = lerp(c00, c10, tx)
    let b = lerp(c01, c11, tx)
    lerp(a, b, ty)
}

// Trilinear interpolation on a 3D grid.
// Takes 8 corner values and 3 interpolation parameters.
pub fn trilerp(
    c000: f64, c100: f64, c010: f64, c110: f64,
    c001: f64, c101: f64, c011: f64, c111: f64,
    tx: f64, ty: f64, tz: f64
) -> f64 {
    let a = bilerp(c000, c100, c010, c110, tx, ty)
    let b = bilerp(c001, c101, c011, c111, tx, ty)
    lerp(a, b, tz)
}

// Cosine interpolation for smoother transitions than linear.
pub fn cosine_interp(a: f64, b: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    let t2 = (1.0 - cos(t * 3.141592653589793)) / 2.0
    a * (1.0 - t2) + b * t2
}

// Struct for storing linear interpolation data.
pub struct LinearInterp {
    xs: [f64; 256],
    ys: [f64; 256],
    len: i32
}

// Struct for cubic spline coefficients.
pub struct CubicSpline {
    xs: [f64; 256],
    a: [f64; 256],
    b: [f64; 256],
    c: [f64; 256],
    d: [f64; 256],
    len: i32
}


// === FILE: stdlib/interpolation/spline.sio ===
// stdlib/interpolation/spline.sio
// Cubic spline interpolation with epistemic uncertainty propagation.
//
// Provides:
//   - Natural cubic spline fit/eval/derivatives (SplineCoeffs)
//   - Simple linear interpolation (lerp on arrays)
//   - Epistemic spline: GUM uncertainty propagation through spline basis
//     (EpistemicSpline, espline_fit, espline_eval)
//
// References:
//   de Boor (1978) "A Practical Guide to Splines"
//   JCGM 100:2008 (GUM) — uncertainty propagation
//   Thomas algorithm: Golub & Van Loan (1996) §4.3

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS (must precede callers — no forward refs in Sounio)
// ============================================================================

fn sp_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    x
}

// Newton-Raphson square root (20 iterations → ~15 digits accuracy).
fn sp_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// Binary search: return index i such that knots[i] <= x < knots[i+1].
// Returns 0 for x below range, n-2 for x at/above upper boundary.
pub fn spline_find_interval(knots: &[f64; 64], n: i32, x: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 2 { return 0 }
    if x <= knots[0] { return 0 }
    if x >= knots[n - 1] { return n - 2 }
    var lo: i32 = 0
    var hi: i32 = n - 1
    while hi - lo > 1 {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
        if knots[mid] <= x {
            lo = mid
        } else {
            hi = mid
        }
    }
    lo
}

// Thomas algorithm (forward sweep + back substitution) for tridiagonal system.
// Solves: sub[i]*x[i-1] + diag[i]*x[i] + sup[i]*x[i+1] = rhs[i]
// sub[0] and sup[n-1] are unused (natural BCs).
// Result written into sol (passed by exclusive ref).
fn thomas_solve(
    sub: &[f64; 64],
    diag: &[f64; 64],
    sup: &[f64; 64],
    rhs: &[f64; 64],
    n: i32
) -> [f64; 64] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var dp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var sol: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // Forward sweep
    if sp_abs(diag[0]) < 1.0e-30 {
        cp[0] = 0.0
        dp[0] = 0.0
    } else {
        cp[0] = sup[0] / diag[0]
        dp[0] = rhs[0] / diag[0]
    }

    var i: i32 = 1
    while i < n {
        let denom = diag[i] - sub[i] * cp[i - 1]
        if sp_abs(denom) < 1.0e-30 {
            cp[i] = 0.0
            dp[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            cp[i] = sup[i] / denom
            dp[i] = (rhs[i] - sub[i] * dp[i - 1]) / denom
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Back substitution
    sol[n - 1] = dp[n - 1]
    i = n - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        sol[i] = dp[i] - cp[i] * sol[i + 1]
        i = i - 1
    }
    sol
}

// ============================================================================
// DATA STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

// Coefficients for a natural cubic spline over n intervals.
// Interval i covers [x[i], x[i+1]] and evaluates as:
//   S_i(t) = a[i] + b[i]*dx + c[i]*dx^2 + d[i]*dx^3,  dx = t - x[i]
// n = number of intervals = number of data points - 1.
pub struct SplineCoeffs {
    pub a: [f64; 64],
    pub b: [f64; 64],
    pub c: [f64; 64],
    pub d: [f64; 64],
    pub x: [f64; 64],
    pub n: i32
}

// Epistemic spline: spline fitted to data with known measurement uncertainty.
// y_unc[i] = standard uncertainty on the i-th data point y[i].
// interp_unc[i] = propagated standard uncertainty at knot i (GUM §5.1).
pub struct EpistemicSpline {
    pub coeffs: SplineCoeffs,
    pub y_unc: [f64; 64],
    pub interp_unc: [f64; 64]
}

// ============================================================================
// NATURAL CUBIC SPLINE FIT
// ============================================================================

// Fit a natural cubic spline through n data points (n >= 2, n <= 64).
// xs must be strictly increasing. Natural BCs: c[0] = c[n-1] = 0.
pub fn spline_fit(x: &[f64; 64], y: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> SplineCoeffs with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = SplineCoeffs {
        a: [0.0; 64],
        b: [0.0; 64],
        c: [0.0; 64],
        d: [0.0; 64],
        x: [0.0; 64],
        n: n
    }

    // Copy x and a = y
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < n {
        s.x[k] = x[k]
        s.a[k] = y[k]
        k = k + 1
    }

    if n < 2 { return s }

    // Compute interval lengths h[i] = x[i+1] - x[i]
    var h: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    k = 0
    while k < n - 1 {
        h[k] = x[k + 1] - x[k]
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Special case n == 2: linear segment
    if n == 2 {
        if sp_abs(h[0]) > 1.0e-30 {
            s.b[0] = (y[1] - y[0]) / h[0]
        }
        return s
    }

    // Build tridiagonal system for interior second derivatives c[1..n-2].
    // Using the standard natural spline formulation (n-2 interior equations):
    //   h[i-1]*c[i-1] + 2*(h[i-1]+h[i])*c[i] + h[i]*c[i+1]
    //     = 3*((y[i+1]-y[i])/h[i] - (y[i]-y[i-1])/h[i-1])
    let m = n - 2    // number of interior unknowns
    var sub:  [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var diag: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var sup:  [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var rhs:  [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var cp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var dp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < m {
        let idx = i + 1
        diag[i] = 2.0 * (h[idx - 1] + h[idx])
        if i > 0 {
            sub[i] = h[idx - 1]
        }
        if i < m - 1 {
            sup[i] = h[idx]
        }
        let sr = (y[idx + 1] - y[idx]) / h[idx]
        let sl = (y[idx] - y[idx - 1]) / h[idx - 1]
        rhs[i] = 3.0 * (sr - sl)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Thomas algorithm inlined — forward sweep
    if sp_abs(diag[0]) < 1.0e-30 {
        cp[0] = 0.0
        dp[0] = 0.0
    } else {
        cp[0] = sup[0] / diag[0]
        dp[0] = rhs[0] / diag[0]
    }
    i = 1
    while i < m {
        let denom = diag[i] - sub[i] * cp[i - 1]
        if sp_abs(denom) < 1.0e-30 {
            cp[i] = 0.0
            dp[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            cp[i] = sup[i] / denom
            dp[i] = (rhs[i] - sub[i] * dp[i - 1]) / denom
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Back substitution — solve into dp, then copy to s.c
    i = m - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        dp[i] = dp[i] - cp[i] * dp[i + 1]
        i = i - 1
    }
    s.c[0] = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < m {
        s.c[i + 1] = dp[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    s.c[n - 1] = 0.0

    // Compute b[i] and d[i] for each interval
    i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        let hi = h[i]
        if sp_abs(hi) < 1.0e-30 {
            s.b[i] = 0.0
            s.d[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            s.b[i] = (y[i + 1] - y[i]) / hi - hi * (2.0 * s.c[i] + s.c[i + 1]) / 3.0
            s.d[i] = (s.c[i + 1] - s.c[i]) / (3.0 * hi)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    s
}

// ============================================================================
// SPLINE EVALUATION
// ============================================================================

// Evaluate spline value at x_eval.
// Clamps to data range for x_eval outside [x[0], x[n]].
pub fn spline_eval(s: &SplineCoeffs, x_eval: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s.n < 1 { return 0.0 }
    if s.n == 1 { return s.a[0] }

    let np1 = s.n
    var xc: f64 = x_eval
    if xc < s.x[0] { xc = s.x[0] }
    if xc > s.x[np1 - 1] { xc = s.x[np1 - 1] }

    let i = spline_find_interval_in_s(s, np1, xc)
    let dx = xc - s.x[i]
    s.a[i] + dx * (s.b[i] + dx * (s.c[i] + dx * s.d[i]))
}

fn spline_find_interval_in_s(s: &SplineCoeffs, n: i32, x: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 2 { return 0 }
    if x <= s.x[0] { return 0 }
    if x >= s.x[n - 1] { return n - 2 }
    var lo: i32 = 0
    var hi: i32 = n - 1
    while hi - lo > 1 {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
        if s.x[mid] <= x {
            lo = mid
        } else {
            hi = mid
        }
    }
    lo
}

// Evaluate first derivative S'(x_eval) = b + 2c*dx + 3d*dx^2.
pub fn spline_eval_deriv(s: &SplineCoeffs, x_eval: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s.n < 2 { return 0.0 }

    let np1 = s.n
    var xc: f64 = x_eval
    if xc < s.x[0] { xc = s.x[0] }
    if xc > s.x[np1 - 1] { xc = s.x[np1 - 1] }

    let i = spline_find_interval_in_s(s, np1, xc)
    let dx = xc - s.x[i]
    s.b[i] + dx * (2.0 * s.c[i] + 3.0 * s.d[i] * dx)
}

// Evaluate second derivative S''(x_eval) = 2c + 6d*dx.
pub fn spline_eval_deriv2(s: &SplineCoeffs, x_eval: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s.n < 2 { return 0.0 }

    let np1 = s.n
    var xc: f64 = x_eval
    if xc < s.x[0] { xc = s.x[0] }
    if xc > s.x[np1 - 1] { xc = s.x[np1 - 1] }

    let i = spline_find_interval_in_s(s, np1, xc)
    let dx = xc - s.x[i]
    2.0 * s.c[i] + 6.0 * s.d[i] * dx
}

// ============================================================================
// SIMPLE LINEAR INTERPOLATION (array-based)
// ============================================================================

// Piecewise linear interpolation through n data points.
// xs must be sorted ascending. Clamps for x_eval outside [xs[0], xs[n-1]].
pub fn lerp(x: &[f64; 64], y: &[f64; 64], n: i32, x_eval: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 1 { return 0.0 }
    if n == 1 { return y[0] }

    if x_eval <= x[0] { return y[0] }
    if x_eval >= x[n - 1] { return y[n - 1] }

    let i = spline_find_interval(x, n, x_eval)
    let h = x[i + 1] - x[i]
    if sp_abs(h) < 1.0e-30 { return y[i] }
    let t = (x_eval - x[i]) / h
    y[i] + t * (y[i + 1] - y[i])
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC SPLINE — GUM UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATION
// ============================================================================
//
// Each data value y[i] has standard uncertainty u[i] (Type A or B).
// The spline value at x_eval is a linear function of the y[i]:
//   S(x_eval) = sum_i  phi_i(x_eval) * y[i]
// where phi_i is the i-th "basis" (Lagrange-like influence).
//
// GUM §5.1 (linear propagation):
//   u(S)^2 = sum_i  (phi_i(x_eval) * u[i])^2
//
// We approximate phi_i numerically by finite difference:
//   phi_i ≈ [S(x_eval | y[i]+eps) - S(x_eval | y[i]-eps)] / (2*eps)
// This is exact for cubic splines because S is linear in y[i].

fn spline_basis_sensitivity(
    x: &[f64; 64],
    y: &[f64; 64],
    n: i32,
    idx: i32,
    x_eval: f64,
    eps: f64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var yp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var ym: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < n {
        yp[k] = y[k]
        ym[k] = y[k]
        k = k + 1
    }
    yp[idx] = y[idx] + eps
    ym[idx] = y[idx] - eps

    let sp = spline_fit(x, &yp, n)
    let sm = spline_fit(x, &ym, n)
    let vp = spline_eval(&sp, x_eval)
    let vm = spline_eval(&sm, x_eval)

    if sp_abs(2.0 * eps) < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
    (vp - vm) / (2.0 * eps)
}

// Fit a spline and propagate data uncertainty to the knot positions.
// y_unc[i] is the standard uncertainty on y[i].
// interp_unc[i] gives the propagated uncertainty evaluated at x[i] itself.
pub fn espline_fit(
    x: &[f64; 64],
    y: &[f64; 64],
    y_unc: &[f64; 64],
    n: i32
) -> EpistemicSpline with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let coeffs = spline_fit(x, y, n)

    var unc_at_knots: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var unc_copy: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var ki: i32 = 0
    while ki < n {
        unc_copy[ki] = y_unc[ki]
        ki = ki + 1
    }

    // For each knot, propagate uncertainty using GUM (finite-difference sensitivities)
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < n {
        var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0
        let x_eval = x[j]
        let eps = 1.0e-6

        var i: i32 = 0
        while i < n {
            let phi_i = spline_basis_sensitivity(x, y, n, i, x_eval, eps)
            let contrib = phi_i * unc_copy[i]
            sum_sq = sum_sq + contrib * contrib
            i = i + 1
        }
        unc_at_knots[j] = sp_sqrt(sum_sq)
        j = j + 1
    }

    EpistemicSpline {
        coeffs: coeffs,
        y_unc: unc_copy,
        interp_unc: unc_at_knots
    }
}

fn espline_find_interval(s: &EpistemicSpline, n: i32, x: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 2 { return 0 }
    if x <= s.coeffs.x[0] { return 0 }
    if x >= s.coeffs.x[n - 1] { return n - 2 }
    var lo: i32 = 0
    var hi: i32 = n - 1
    while hi - lo > 1 {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
        if s.coeffs.x[mid] <= x { lo = mid } else { hi = mid }
    }
    lo
}

pub fn espline_eval_val(s: &EpistemicSpline, x_eval: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = s.coeffs.n
    if n < 1 { return 0.0 }
    if n == 1 { return s.coeffs.a[0] }
    var xc: f64 = x_eval
    if xc < s.coeffs.x[0] { xc = s.coeffs.x[0] }
    if xc > s.coeffs.x[n - 1] { xc = s.coeffs.x[n - 1] }
    let i = espline_find_interval(s, n, xc)
    let dx = xc - s.coeffs.x[i]
    s.coeffs.a[i] + dx * (s.coeffs.b[i] + dx * (s.coeffs.c[i] + dx * s.coeffs.d[i]))
}

// Evaluate epistemic spline: returns (value, standard_uncertainty) at x_eval.
// Uncertainty is computed by GUM finite-difference propagation.
pub fn espline_eval_unc(s: &EpistemicSpline, x_eval: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = s.coeffs.n
    let eps = 1.0e-6
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0

    // Copy x, a, y_unc to locals — avoids nested field reference bug
    var lx: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var la: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var lyunc: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < n {
        lx[k] = s.coeffs.x[k]
        la[k] = s.coeffs.a[k]
        lyunc[k] = s.y_unc[k]
        k = k + 1
    }

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let phi_i = spline_basis_sensitivity(&lx, &la, n, i, x_eval, eps)
        let contrib = phi_i * lyunc[i]
        sum_sq = sum_sq + contrib * contrib
        i = i + 1
    }
    sp_sqrt(sum_sq)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/io/argparse.sio ===
// stdlib/io/argparse.d
// Command-line argument parsing
//
// Simple argument parsing without string slicing (interpreter compatible).
// Uses whole-string comparisons only.

// =============================================================================
// Argument Types
// =============================================================================

pub struct ArgValue {
    pub key: String,
    pub value: String,
    pub is_flag: bool,
}

pub struct ParsedArgs {
    pub program: String,
    pub args: [String],
    pub count: usize,
}

// =============================================================================
// Parsing
// =============================================================================

// Parse command line arguments (simple version)
// Just stores raw arguments for application to process
pub fn parse(args: [String]) -> ParsedArgs {
    var result = ParsedArgs {
        program: "",
        args: [],
        count: 0,
    };

    let n = args.len();
    if n > 0 {
        result.program = args[0];

        var i: usize = 1;
        while i < n {
            result.args.push(args[i]);
            i = i + 1;
        }
        result.count = result.args.len();
    }

    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Query Functions (using whole-string comparisons)
// =============================================================================

// Check if an exact argument exists
pub fn has_arg(args: ParsedArgs, name: String) -> bool {
    let n = args.args.len();
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        if args.args[i] == name {
            return true;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    false
}

// Check if --verbose flag exists
pub fn is_verbose(args: ParsedArgs) -> bool {
    has_arg(args, "--verbose") || has_arg(args, "-v")
}

// Check if --help flag exists
pub fn is_help(args: ParsedArgs) -> bool {
    has_arg(args, "--help") || has_arg(args, "-h")
}

// Check if --quiet flag exists
pub fn is_quiet(args: ParsedArgs) -> bool {
    has_arg(args, "--quiet") || has_arg(args, "-q")
}

// Get argument by index
pub fn get_arg(args: ParsedArgs, idx: usize) -> String {
    if idx < args.args.len() {
        args.args[idx]
    } else {
        ""
    }
}

// Get first non-flag argument (doesn't start with -)
// Useful for getting input file
pub fn get_first_positional(args: ParsedArgs) -> String {
    let n = args.args.len();
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        let arg = args.args[i];
        // Check common flags to skip
        if arg != "--verbose" && arg != "-v" &&
           arg != "--help" && arg != "-h" &&
           arg != "--quiet" && arg != "-q" &&
           arg != "--debug" && arg != "-d" {
            // This might be a positional (simplified check)
            // If it starts with -, it's still a flag we don't know about
            // This simplified version just returns first non-common-flag
            return arg;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    ""
}

// Get number of arguments (excluding program name)
pub fn num_args(args: ParsedArgs) -> usize {
    args.count
}

// === FILE: stdlib/io/binary.sio ===
// stdlib/io/binary.sio — endian-aware integer unpacking from byte slices
//
// Equivalent of Python's `struct.unpack_from("<H", data, offset)`. Used by
// CUBIN/ELF validation, NIfTI parsing, and any binary protocol decode.
//
// All readers return i64 to avoid sign-extension surprises; signed variants
// re-interpret the bit pattern.

pub enum Endian {
    Little,
    Big,
}

// Bounds-checked single-byte read returning unsigned 0..=255 in i64.
pub fn byte_u8(bytes: &[u8], idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 || idx >= bytes.len() as i64 {
        return 0
    }
    let raw = bytes[idx as usize] as i64
    if raw < 0 { raw + 256 } else { raw }
}

// ---- 16-bit ----

pub fn read_u16_le(bytes: &[u8], off: i64) -> i64 {
    let b0 = byte_u8(bytes, off)
    let b1 = byte_u8(bytes, off + 1)
    b0 | (b1 << 8)
}

pub fn read_u16_be(bytes: &[u8], off: i64) -> i64 {
    let b0 = byte_u8(bytes, off)
    let b1 = byte_u8(bytes, off + 1)
    (b0 << 8) | b1
}

pub fn read_u16(bytes: &[u8], off: i64, endian: Endian) -> i64 {
    if endian == Endian::Little { read_u16_le(bytes, off) } else { read_u16_be(bytes, off) }
}

pub fn read_i16(bytes: &[u8], off: i64, endian: Endian) -> i64 {
    let u = read_u16(bytes, off, endian)
    if u >= 32768 { u - 65536 } else { u }
}

// ---- 32-bit ----

pub fn read_u32_le(bytes: &[u8], off: i64) -> i64 {
    let b0 = byte_u8(bytes, off)
    let b1 = byte_u8(bytes, off + 1)
    let b2 = byte_u8(bytes, off + 2)
    let b3 = byte_u8(bytes, off + 3)
    b0 | (b1 << 8) | (b2 << 16) | (b3 << 24)
}

pub fn read_u32_be(bytes: &[u8], off: i64) -> i64 {
    let b0 = byte_u8(bytes, off)
    let b1 = byte_u8(bytes, off + 1)
    let b2 = byte_u8(bytes, off + 2)
    let b3 = byte_u8(bytes, off + 3)
    (b0 << 24) | (b1 << 16) | (b2 << 8) | b3
}

pub fn read_u32(bytes: &[u8], off: i64, endian: Endian) -> i64 {
    if endian == Endian::Little { read_u32_le(bytes, off) } else { read_u32_be(bytes, off) }
}

pub fn read_i32(bytes: &[u8], off: i64, endian: Endian) -> i64 {
    let u = read_u32(bytes, off, endian)
    if u >= 2147483648 { u - 4294967296 } else { u }
}

// ---- 64-bit ----

pub fn read_u64_le(bytes: &[u8], off: i64) -> i64 {
    let lo = read_u32_le(bytes, off)
    let hi = read_u32_le(bytes, off + 4)
    lo | (hi << 32)
}

pub fn read_u64_be(bytes: &[u8], off: i64) -> i64 {
    let hi = read_u32_be(bytes, off)
    let lo = read_u32_be(bytes, off + 4)
    (hi << 32) | lo
}

pub fn read_u64(bytes: &[u8], off: i64, endian: Endian) -> i64 {
    if endian == Endian::Little { read_u64_le(bytes, off) } else { read_u64_be(bytes, off) }
}

pub fn read_i64(bytes: &[u8], off: i64, endian: Endian) -> i64 {
    // 64-bit unsigned and signed share representation in i64; readers above
    // already produce a signed-i64 bit pattern.
    read_u64(bytes, off, endian)
}

// ---- magic / fixed-pattern helpers ----

// Returns true iff bytes[off..off+n] match the given pattern bytes.
pub fn match_bytes_at(bytes: &[u8], off: i64, pattern: &[u8]) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = pattern.len() as i64
    if off < 0 || off + n > bytes.len() as i64 { return false }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if byte_u8(bytes, off + i) != byte_u8(pattern, i) { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}


// === FILE: stdlib/io/io.sio ===
// io/mod.sio — Buffered I/O
//
// Fixed-capacity byte buffer for composing and reading data.
// No heap allocation; uses a 4096-byte internal buffer.

// ============================================================================
// IO BUFFER
// ============================================================================

pub struct IoBuffer {
    data: [u8; 4096],  // Internal storage
    len: i32,          // Number of valid bytes
    pos: i32,          // Read cursor position
}

pub fn io_buf_new() -> IoBuffer {
    IoBuffer { data: [0; 4096], len: 0, pos: 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// WRITE TO BUFFER
// ============================================================================
// Appends n bytes from data to the buffer. Returns updated buffer.
// Silently truncates if buffer would overflow.

pub fn io_buf_write(buf: IoBuffer, data: &[u8; 256], n: i32) -> IoBuffer {
    var out = buf
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        if out.len >= 4096 {
            return out
        }
        out.data[out.len as usize] = data[i as usize]
        out.len = out.len + 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    out
}

// ============================================================================
// READ FROM BUFFER
// ============================================================================
// Reads up to n bytes from buffer into out, advancing buf.pos. Returns bytes read.

pub fn io_buf_read(buf: &!IoBuffer, out: &![u8; 256], n: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var count: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        if buf.pos >= buf.len {
            return count
        }
        out[i as usize] = buf.data[buf.pos as usize]
        buf.pos = buf.pos + 1
        count = count + 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    count
}

// ============================================================================
// BUFFER QUERIES
// ============================================================================

pub fn io_buf_remaining(buf: &IoBuffer) -> i32 {
    buf.len - buf.pos
}

pub fn io_buf_capacity(buf: &IoBuffer) -> i32 {
    4096 - buf.len
}

pub fn io_buf_is_empty(buf: &IoBuffer) -> bool {
    buf.len == 0
}

pub fn io_buf_reset(buf: IoBuffer) -> IoBuffer {
    var out = buf
    out.len = 0
    out.pos = 0
    out
}

// ============================================================================
// INLINE TESTS
// ============================================================================

//@ run-pass
fn test_io_buf_new() -> i32 {
    let b = io_buf_new()
    if b.len != 0 { return 1 }
    if b.pos != 0 { return 2 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_io_buf_write_read() -> i32 {
    var b = io_buf_new()
    var data: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    data[0] = 65  // 'A'
    data[1] = 66  // 'B'
    data[2] = 67  // 'C'
    b = io_buf_write(b, &data, 3)
    if b.len != 3 { return 1 }

    var out: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var b_r = b
    let n = io_buf_read(&!b_r, &!out, 3)
    if n != 3 { return 2 }
    if out[0] != 65 { return 3 }
    if out[1] != 66 { return 4 }
    if out[2] != 67 { return 5 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_io_buf_remaining() -> i32 {
    var b = io_buf_new()
    var data: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    data[0] = 1
    data[1] = 2
    b = io_buf_write(b, &data, 2)
    if io_buf_remaining(&b) != 2 { return 1 }
    0
}
