// === FILE: stdlib/json/parser.sio ===
// stdlib/json/parser.sio — Minimal JSON parser and serializer
//
// Represents JSON as a flat key-value document (up to 32 entries).
// No heap allocation — all storage is fixed-size arrays.
// Supports: null, bool, number, string at the top-level object.
//
// JIT note: only &!Struct field mutations propagate to callers.
// Standalone &!array and &!scalar do NOT propagate in JIT mode.
// All helpers use struct-wrapping or by-value returns for correctness.
//
// # Limits
//   - Up to 32 key-value pairs per document
//   - Keys up to 63 bytes (UTF-8, null-terminated in 64-byte slot)
//   - String values up to 127 bytes (UTF-8, null-terminated in 128-byte slot)
//   - Serialize output up to 4095 bytes
//   - Parse input up to 4095 bytes

// ============================================================================
// JSON VALUE TYPES
// ============================================================================

pub fn JSON_NULL() -> i32 { 0 }
pub fn JSON_BOOL() -> i32 { 1 }
pub fn JSON_NUMBER() -> i32 { 2 }
pub fn JSON_STRING() -> i32 { 3 }
pub fn JSON_ARRAY() -> i32 { 4 }
pub fn JSON_OBJECT() -> i32 { 5 }

// ============================================================================
// JsonValue — holds one JSON value of any scalar type
// ============================================================================

pub struct JsonValue {
    pub kind: i32,
    pub num_val: f64,
    pub bool_val: i32,
    pub str_val: [u8; 128],
    pub str_len: i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// JsonDoc — flat key→value store, up to 32 entries
// ============================================================================

pub struct JsonDoc {
    pub keys: [u8; 2048],
    pub key_lens: [i32; 32],
    pub values: [JsonValue; 32],
    pub count: i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// JsonBuf — serialization output buffer (used by serialize, avoids &!array bug)
// ============================================================================

pub struct JsonBuf {
    pub data: [u8; 4096],
    pub len: i32,
}

// Internal parse state for string body parsing.
struct StrResult {
    data: [u8; 128],
    str_len: i32,
    new_pos: i32,  // -1 on error
}

// Internal parse state for number parsing.
struct NumResult {
    value: f64,
    new_pos: i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// JsonValue constructors
// ============================================================================

pub fn json_value_null() -> JsonValue {
    JsonValue {
        kind: 0,
        num_val: 0.0,
        bool_val: 0,
        str_val: [0; 128],
        str_len: 0,
    }
}

pub fn json_value_bool(b: i32) -> JsonValue {
    JsonValue {
        kind: 1,
        num_val: 0.0,
        bool_val: b,
        str_val: [0; 128],
        str_len: 0,
    }
}

pub fn json_value_number(n: f64) -> JsonValue {
    JsonValue {
        kind: 2,
        num_val: n,
        bool_val: 0,
        str_val: [0; 128],
        str_len: 0,
    }
}

pub fn json_value_string(s: &[u8; 128], len: i32) -> JsonValue {
    var v = JsonValue {
        kind: 3,
        num_val: 0.0,
        bool_val: 0,
        str_val: [0; 128],
        str_len: 0,
    }
    var cap = len
    if cap > 127 { cap = 127 }
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < cap {
        v.str_val[i as usize] = s[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    v.str_len = cap
    v
}

// ============================================================================
// JsonDoc constructor
// ============================================================================

pub fn json_doc_new() -> JsonDoc {
    JsonDoc {
        keys: [0; 2048],
        key_lens: [0; 32],
        values: [JsonValue {
            kind: 0,
            num_val: 0.0,
            bool_val: 0,
            str_val: [0; 128],
            str_len: 0,
        }; 32],
        count: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Internal helpers
// ============================================================================

// Compare two key slots up to their lengths. Returns 1 if equal.
fn jkeys_equal(doc: &JsonDoc, slot: i32, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if doc.key_lens[slot as usize] != key_len { return 0 }
    let base = slot * 64
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < key_len {
        if doc.keys[(base + i) as usize] != key[i as usize] { return 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    1
}

// Find index of key in doc. Returns index or -1.
fn jdoc_find(doc: &JsonDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < doc.count {
        if jkeys_equal(doc, i, key, key_len) == 1 {
            return i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0 - 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Document mutation — set (using &!JsonDoc struct field mutation — works in JIT)
// ============================================================================

pub fn json_doc_set_number(doc: &!JsonDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32, value: f64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = jdoc_find(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx >= 0 {
        doc.values[idx as usize].kind = 2
        doc.values[idx as usize].num_val = value
    } else {
        if doc.count < 32 {
            let slot = doc.count
            // Copy key bytes directly.
            let base = slot * 64
            var ki: i32 = 0
            while ki < key_len {
                doc.keys[(base + ki) as usize] = key[ki as usize]
                ki = ki + 1
            }
            doc.key_lens[slot as usize] = key_len
            doc.values[slot as usize].kind = 2
            doc.values[slot as usize].num_val = value
            doc.values[slot as usize].bool_val = 0
            doc.values[slot as usize].str_len = 0
            doc.count = doc.count + 1
        }
    }
}

pub fn json_doc_set_bool(doc: &!JsonDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32, value: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = jdoc_find(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx >= 0 {
        doc.values[idx as usize].kind = 1
        doc.values[idx as usize].bool_val = value
    } else {
        if doc.count < 32 {
            let slot = doc.count
            let base = slot * 64
            var ki: i32 = 0
            while ki < key_len {
                doc.keys[(base + ki) as usize] = key[ki as usize]
                ki = ki + 1
            }
            doc.key_lens[slot as usize] = key_len
            doc.values[slot as usize].kind = 1
            doc.values[slot as usize].num_val = 0.0
            doc.values[slot as usize].bool_val = value
            doc.values[slot as usize].str_len = 0
            doc.count = doc.count + 1
        }
    }
}

pub fn json_doc_set_string(doc: &!JsonDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32, s: &[u8; 128], s_len: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cap = s_len
    if cap > 127 { cap = 127 }
    let idx = jdoc_find(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx >= 0 {
        doc.values[idx as usize].kind = 3
        doc.values[idx as usize].str_len = cap
        var si: i32 = 0
        while si < cap {
            doc.values[idx as usize].str_val[si as usize] = s[si as usize]
            si = si + 1
        }
    } else {
        if doc.count < 32 {
            let slot = doc.count
            let base = slot * 64
            var ki: i32 = 0
            while ki < key_len {
                doc.keys[(base + ki) as usize] = key[ki as usize]
                ki = ki + 1
            }
            doc.key_lens[slot as usize] = key_len
            doc.values[slot as usize].kind = 3
            doc.values[slot as usize].num_val = 0.0
            doc.values[slot as usize].bool_val = 0
            doc.values[slot as usize].str_len = cap
            var si: i32 = 0
            while si < cap {
                doc.values[slot as usize].str_val[si as usize] = s[si as usize]
                si = si + 1
            }
            doc.count = doc.count + 1
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Document access — get
// ============================================================================

pub fn json_doc_get_number(doc: &JsonDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = jdoc_find(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx >= 0 {
        if doc.values[idx as usize].kind == 2 {
            return doc.values[idx as usize].num_val
        }
    }
    0.0
}

pub fn json_doc_get_bool(doc: &JsonDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = jdoc_find(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx >= 0 {
        if doc.values[idx as usize].kind == 1 {
            return doc.values[idx as usize].bool_val
        }
    }
    0
}

pub fn json_doc_get_string(doc: &JsonDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32, out: &!JsonDoc) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // NOTE: `out` parameter is unused — this signature exists only for API compatibility.
    // Use doc.values[idx].str_val and doc.values[idx].str_len directly.
    let idx = jdoc_find(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx >= 0 {
        if doc.values[idx as usize].kind == 3 {
            return doc.values[idx as usize].str_len
        }
    }
    0
}

pub fn json_doc_contains(doc: &JsonDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = jdoc_find(doc, key, key_len)
    idx >= 0
}

pub fn json_doc_count(doc: &JsonDoc) -> i32 {
    doc.count
}

// ============================================================================
// Serialization — JsonBuf helpers (by-value: structs work in JIT)
// ============================================================================

fn jbuf_new() -> JsonBuf {
    JsonBuf { data: [0; 4096], len: 0 }
}

// Write a single byte. Returns updated buf.
fn jbuf_byte(buf: JsonBuf, b: u8) -> JsonBuf {
    var nb = buf
    if nb.len < 4095 {
        nb.data[nb.len as usize] = b
        nb.len = nb.len + 1
    }
    nb
}

// Write decimal digits of non-negative i64. Returns updated buf.
fn jbuf_u64(buf: JsonBuf, n: i64) -> JsonBuf with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 {
        return jbuf_byte(buf, (48 as u8))
    }
    var digits: [u8; 20] = [0; 20]
    var count: i32 = 0
    var rem = n
    while rem > 0 {
        let d = rem - (rem / 10) * 10
        digits[count as usize] = (48 + d) as u8
        rem = rem / 10
        count = count + 1
    }
    var nb = buf
    var i: i32 = count - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        nb = jbuf_byte(nb, digits[i as usize])
        i = i - 1
    }
    nb
}

// Write f64 as JSON number (integer if whole, 6dp otherwise). Returns updated buf.
fn jbuf_number(buf: JsonBuf, n: f64) -> JsonBuf with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var nb = buf
    var absn = n
    if n < 0.0 {
        nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (45 as u8))  // '-'
        absn = 0.0 - n
    }
    let int_part = absn as i64
    let frac = absn - int_part as f64
    nb = jbuf_u64(nb, int_part)
    if frac >= 0.000001 {
        nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (46 as u8))  // '.'
        var remaining = frac
        var d: i32 = 0
        while d < 6 {
            remaining = remaining * 10.0
            let digit = remaining as i64
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (48 + digit) as u8)
            remaining = remaining - digit as f64
            d = d + 1
        }
    }
    nb
}

// Write a key string (quoted, basic escaping). Returns updated buf.
fn jbuf_key(buf: JsonBuf, doc: &JsonDoc, slot: i32) -> JsonBuf with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var nb = jbuf_byte(buf, (34 as u8))  // '"'
    let klen = doc.key_lens[slot as usize]
    let base = slot * 64
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < klen {
        let b = doc.keys[(base + i) as usize]
        if b == (34 as u8) {
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (92 as u8))
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (34 as u8))
        } else if b == (92 as u8) {
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (92 as u8))
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (92 as u8))
        } else {
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, b)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (34 as u8))  // '"'
    nb
}

// Write a string value (quoted, basic escaping). Returns updated buf.
fn jbuf_str_val(buf: JsonBuf, doc: &JsonDoc, slot: i32) -> JsonBuf with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var nb = jbuf_byte(buf, (34 as u8))  // '"'
    let slen = doc.values[slot as usize].str_len
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < slen {
        let b = doc.values[slot as usize].str_val[i as usize]
        if b == (34 as u8) {
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (92 as u8))
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (34 as u8))
        } else if b == (92 as u8) {
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (92 as u8))
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (92 as u8))
        } else if b == (10 as u8) {
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (92 as u8))
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (110 as u8))
        } else {
            nb = jbuf_byte(nb, b)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    nb = jbuf_byte(nb, (34 as u8))  // '"'
    nb
}

// ============================================================================
// Serialization — json_serialize_to_buf (returns JsonBuf)
// ============================================================================

pub fn json_serialize_to_buf(doc: &JsonDoc) -> JsonBuf with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var buf = jbuf_new()
    buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (123 as u8))  // '{'
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < doc.count {
        if i > 0 {
            buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (44 as u8))  // ','
        }
        buf = jbuf_key(buf, doc, i)
        buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (58 as u8))  // ':'
        let kind = doc.values[i as usize].kind
        if kind == 0 {
            buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (110 as u8))  // 'n'
            buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (117 as u8))  // 'u'
            buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (108 as u8))  // 'l'
            buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (108 as u8))  // 'l'
        } else if kind == 1 {
            if doc.values[i as usize].bool_val != 0 {
                buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (116 as u8))  // 't'
                buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (114 as u8))  // 'r'
                buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (117 as u8))  // 'u'
                buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (101 as u8))  // 'e'
            } else {
                buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (102 as u8))  // 'f'
                buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (97 as u8))   // 'a'
                buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (108 as u8))  // 'l'
                buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (115 as u8))  // 's'
                buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (101 as u8))  // 'e'
            }
        } else if kind == 2 {
            buf = jbuf_number(buf, doc.values[i as usize].num_val)
        } else if kind == 3 {
            buf = jbuf_str_val(buf, doc, i)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    buf = jbuf_byte(buf, (125 as u8))  // '}'
    buf
}

// ============================================================================
// Serialization — json_serialize (writes to &!JsonBuf for API compatibility)
// ============================================================================

// Serialize doc to a JsonBuf struct (mutations through &!JsonBuf work in JIT).
// Returns bytes written (also stored in out.len).
pub fn json_serialize(doc: &JsonDoc, out: &!JsonBuf) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let result = json_serialize_to_buf(doc)
    // Copy result fields into out (struct field mutation works in JIT).
    out.len = result.len
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < result.len {
        out.data[i as usize] = result.data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    out.len
}

// ============================================================================
// Parsing helpers
// ============================================================================

// Skip whitespace in input array. Returns new position.
fn jskip_ws(input: &[u8; 4096], pos: i32, input_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = pos
    while p < input_len {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        if c == (32 as u8) || c == (9 as u8) || c == (10 as u8) || c == (13 as u8) {
            p = p + 1
        } else {
            return p
        }
    }
    p
}

// Parse string body (after opening '"'). Returns StrResult with new_pos=-1 on error.
fn jparse_str(input: &[u8; 4096], start: i32, input_len: i32) -> StrResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = StrResult {
        data: [0; 128],
        str_len: 0,
        new_pos: 0 - 1,
    }
    var p = start
    var wpos: i32 = 0
    var done: i32 = 0
    while p < input_len && done == 0 {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        if c == (34 as u8) {
            p = p + 1
            done = 1
        } else if c == (92 as u8) {
            p = p + 1
            if p >= input_len { return r }
            let esc = input[p as usize]
            if esc == (34 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 34; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == (92 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 92; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == (110 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 10; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == (114 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 13; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == (116 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 9; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = esc; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            }
            p = p + 1
        } else {
            if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = c; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            p = p + 1
        }
    }
    if done == 0 { return r }
    r.str_len = wpos
    r.new_pos = p
    r
}

// Parse a JSON number starting at pos. Returns NumResult.
fn jparse_num(input: &[u8; 4096], start: i32, input_len: i32) -> NumResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = start
    var negative: i32 = 0
    if p < input_len && input[p as usize] == (45 as u8) {
        negative = 1
        p = p + 1
    }
    var int_part: f64 = 0.0
    // Parse integer digits (stop at non-digit).
    var int_done: i32 = 0
    while p < input_len && int_done == 0 {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        if c >= (48 as u8) && c <= (57 as u8) {
            int_part = int_part * 10.0 + (c - (48 as u8)) as f64
            p = p + 1
        } else {
            int_done = 1
        }
    }
    var frac: f64 = 0.0
    var frac_div: f64 = 1.0
    if p < input_len && input[p as usize] == (46 as u8) {
        p = p + 1
        var frac_done: i32 = 0
        while p < input_len && frac_done == 0 {
            let c = input[p as usize]
            if c >= (48 as u8) && c <= (57 as u8) {
                frac = frac * 10.0 + (c - (48 as u8)) as f64
                frac_div = frac_div * 10.0
                p = p + 1
            } else {
                frac_done = 1
            }
        }
    }
    var result = int_part + frac / frac_div
    if negative == 1 {
        result = 0.0 - result
    }
    NumResult { value: result, new_pos: p }
}

// ============================================================================
// Parsing — json_parse
// ============================================================================

// Parse a JSON object from input byte array (shared ref — read-only works in JIT).
// Populates doc via &!JsonDoc (struct field mutations work in JIT).
// Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
pub fn json_parse(input: &[u8; 4096], input_len: i32, doc: &!JsonDoc) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = jskip_ws(input, 0, input_len)
    if p >= input_len { return 0 - 1 }
    if input[p as usize] != (123 as u8) { return 0 - 1 }  // '{'
    p = p + 1

    p = jskip_ws(input, p, input_len)
    if p >= input_len { return 0 - 1 }
    if input[p as usize] == (125 as u8) { return 0 }  // empty object

    var done: i32 = 0
    while done == 0 {
        p = jskip_ws(input, p, input_len)
        if p >= input_len { return 0 - 1 }

        // Parse key string.
        if input[p as usize] != (34 as u8) { return 0 - 1 }
        p = p + 1
        let kres = jparse_str(input, p, input_len)
        if kres.new_pos < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
        p = kres.new_pos

        // Truncate key to 63 bytes.
        var key64: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
        var klen = kres.str_len
        if klen > 63 { klen = 63 }
        var ki: i32 = 0
        while ki < klen {
            key64[ki as usize] = kres.data[ki as usize]
            ki = ki + 1
        }

        p = jskip_ws(input, p, input_len)
        if p >= input_len { return 0 - 1 }
        if input[p as usize] != (58 as u8) { return 0 - 1 }  // ':'
        p = p + 1

        p = jskip_ws(input, p, input_len)
        if p >= input_len { return 0 - 1 }

        let c0 = input[p as usize]

        if doc.count < 32 {
            let slot = doc.count

            // Copy key.
            let base = slot * 64
            var kki: i32 = 0
            while kki < klen {
                doc.keys[(base + kki) as usize] = key64[kki as usize]
                kki = kki + 1
            }
            doc.key_lens[slot as usize] = klen

            if c0 == (34 as u8) {
                // String value.
                p = p + 1
                let sres = jparse_str(input, p, input_len)
                if sres.new_pos < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
                p = sres.new_pos
                doc.values[slot as usize].kind = 3
                doc.values[slot as usize].num_val = 0.0
                doc.values[slot as usize].bool_val = 0
                doc.values[slot as usize].str_len = sres.str_len
                var svi: i32 = 0
                while svi < sres.str_len {
                    doc.values[slot as usize].str_val[svi as usize] = sres.data[svi as usize]
                    svi = svi + 1
                }

            } else if c0 == (116 as u8) {
                // "true"
                if p + 3 >= input_len { return 0 - 1 }
                if input[(p + 1) as usize] == (114 as u8) &&
                   input[(p + 2) as usize] == (117 as u8) &&
                   input[(p + 3) as usize] == (101 as u8) {
                    doc.values[slot as usize].kind = 1
                    doc.values[slot as usize].num_val = 0.0
                    doc.values[slot as usize].bool_val = 1
                    doc.values[slot as usize].str_len = 0
                    p = p + 4
                } else {
                    return 0 - 1
                }

            } else if c0 == (102 as u8) {
                // "false"
                if p + 4 >= input_len { return 0 - 1 }
                if input[(p + 1) as usize] == (97 as u8) &&
                   input[(p + 2) as usize] == (108 as u8) &&
                   input[(p + 3) as usize] == (115 as u8) &&
                   input[(p + 4) as usize] == (101 as u8) {
                    doc.values[slot as usize].kind = 1
                    doc.values[slot as usize].num_val = 0.0
                    doc.values[slot as usize].bool_val = 0
                    doc.values[slot as usize].str_len = 0
                    p = p + 5
                } else {
                    return 0 - 1
                }

            } else if c0 == (110 as u8) {
                // "null"
                if p + 3 >= input_len { return 0 - 1 }
                if input[(p + 1) as usize] == (117 as u8) &&
                   input[(p + 2) as usize] == (108 as u8) &&
                   input[(p + 3) as usize] == (108 as u8) {
                    doc.values[slot as usize].kind = 0
                    doc.values[slot as usize].num_val = 0.0
                    doc.values[slot as usize].bool_val = 0
                    doc.values[slot as usize].str_len = 0
                    p = p + 4
                } else {
                    return 0 - 1
                }

            } else if (c0 >= (48 as u8) && c0 <= (57 as u8)) || c0 == (45 as u8) {
                // Number.
                let nres = jparse_num(input, p, input_len)
                if nres.new_pos <= p { return 0 - 1 }
                p = nres.new_pos
                doc.values[slot as usize].kind = 2
                doc.values[slot as usize].num_val = nres.value
                doc.values[slot as usize].bool_val = 0
                doc.values[slot as usize].str_len = 0

            } else {
                return 0 - 1
            }

            doc.count = doc.count + 1
        }

        p = jskip_ws(input, p, input_len)
        if p >= input_len { return 0 - 1 }

        let sep = input[p as usize]
        if sep == (44 as u8) {
            p = p + 1
        } else if sep == (125 as u8) {
            done = 1
        } else {
            return 0 - 1
        }
    }

    0
}

// ============================================================================
// Self-tests
// ============================================================================

pub fn json_self_test() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail: i32 = 0

    // T1: null value
    let vn = json_value_null()
    if vn.kind != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T2: bool value
    let vb = json_value_bool(1)
    if vb.kind != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if vb.bool_val != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T3: number value
    let vnum = json_value_number(3.14)
    if vnum.kind != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T4: doc set number (use direct field access)
    var k_age: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    k_age[0] = (97 as u8)   // 'a'
    k_age[1] = (103 as u8)  // 'g'
    k_age[2] = (101 as u8)  // 'e'
    var doc = json_doc_new()
    json_doc_set_number(&!doc, &k_age, 3, 42.0)
    if doc.count != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    let diff = doc.values[0].num_val - 42.0
    let adiff = if diff < 0.0 { 0.0 - diff } else { diff }
    if adiff > 0.0001 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T5: doc set bool
    var k_ok: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    k_ok[0] = (111 as u8)  // 'o'
    k_ok[1] = (107 as u8)  // 'k'
    json_doc_set_bool(&!doc, &k_ok, 2, 1)
    if doc.count != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.values[1].bool_val != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T6: serialize_to_buf
    let jb = json_serialize_to_buf(&doc)
    if jb.len < 3 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if jb.data[0] != (123 as u8) { fail = fail + 1 }  // '{'
    if jb.data[(jb.len - 1) as usize] != (125 as u8) { fail = fail + 1 }  // '}'

    // T7: parse
    var raw: [u8; 4096] = [0; 4096]
    raw[0]  = (123 as u8)  // '{'
    raw[1]  = (34 as u8)   // '"'
    raw[2]  = (120 as u8)  // 'x'
    raw[3]  = (34 as u8)   // '"'
    raw[4]  = (58 as u8)   // ':'
    raw[5]  = (55 as u8)   // '7'
    raw[6]  = (44 as u8)   // ','
    raw[7]  = (34 as u8)   // '"'
    raw[8]  = (121 as u8)  // 'y'
    raw[9]  = (34 as u8)   // '"'
    raw[10] = (58 as u8)   // ':'
    raw[11] = (102 as u8)  // 'f'
    raw[12] = (97 as u8)   // 'a'
    raw[13] = (108 as u8)  // 'l'
    raw[14] = (115 as u8)  // 's'
    raw[15] = (101 as u8)  // 'e'
    raw[16] = (125 as u8)  // '}'
    let raw_len: i32 = 17
    var parsed = json_doc_new()
    let pres = json_parse(&raw, raw_len, &!parsed)
    if pres != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if parsed.count != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }
    let xdiff = parsed.values[0].num_val - 7.0
    let axdiff = if xdiff < 0.0 { 0.0 - xdiff } else { xdiff }
    if axdiff > 0.0001 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if parsed.values[1].bool_val != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }

    fail
}


// === FILE: stdlib/json/value.sio ===
// stdlib/json/value — Lightweight JSON leaf value
//
// Tagged-union style. Each JsonValue holds one of:
//   null, bool, int, float, or short string.
// For full JSON documents, see json/parser.sio.

fn JV_NULL() -> i32 { 0 }
fn JV_INT() -> i32 { 1 }
fn JV_FLOAT() -> i32 { 2 }
fn JV_STRING() -> i32 { 3 }
fn JV_BOOL() -> i32 { 4 }

struct JsonValue {
    kind: i32,
    int_val: i64,
    float_val: f64,
    str_val: [u8; 64],
    str_len: i32
}

fn jv_null() -> JsonValue {
    JsonValue { kind: 0, int_val: 0, float_val: 0.0, str_val: [0; 64], str_len: 0 }
}

fn jv_int(v: i64) -> JsonValue {
    JsonValue { kind: 1, int_val: v, float_val: 0.0, str_val: [0; 64], str_len: 0 }
}

fn jv_float(v: f64) -> JsonValue {
    JsonValue { kind: 2, int_val: 0, float_val: v, str_val: [0; 64], str_len: 0 }
}

fn jv_string(s: &[u8; 64], len: i32) -> JsonValue with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var jv = JsonValue { kind: 3, int_val: 0, float_val: 0.0, str_val: [0; 64], str_len: len }
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < len && i < 64 {
        jv.str_val[i] = s[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    jv
}

fn jv_bool(v: bool) -> JsonValue {
    JsonValue { kind: 4, int_val: if v { 1 } else { 0 }, float_val: 0.0, str_val: [0; 64], str_len: 0 }
}

fn jv_is_null(v: JsonValue) -> bool { v.kind == 0 }
fn jv_is_int(v: JsonValue) -> bool { v.kind == 1 }
fn jv_is_float(v: JsonValue) -> bool { v.kind == 2 }
fn jv_is_string(v: JsonValue) -> bool { v.kind == 3 }
fn jv_is_bool(v: JsonValue) -> bool { v.kind == 4 }

fn jv_get_int(v: JsonValue) -> i64 { v.int_val }
fn jv_get_float(v: JsonValue) -> f64 { v.float_val }
fn jv_get_bool(v: JsonValue) -> bool { v.int_val != 0 }

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_jv_null() -> bool {
    let v = jv_null()
    jv_is_null(v) && !jv_is_int(v)
}

fn test_jv_int() -> bool {
    let v = jv_int(42)
    jv_is_int(v) && jv_get_int(v) == 42
}

fn test_jv_float() -> bool {
    let v = jv_float(3.14)
    jv_is_float(v) && jv_get_float(v) == 3.14
}

fn test_jv_bool() -> bool {
    let v = jv_bool(true)
    jv_is_bool(v) && jv_get_bool(v)
}

fn main() with IO {
    if test_jv_null() { print("json null: PASS\n") } else { print("json null: FAIL\n") }
    if test_jv_int() { print("json int: PASS\n") } else { print("json int: FAIL\n") }
    if test_jv_float() { print("json float: PASS\n") } else { print("json float: FAIL\n") }
    if test_jv_bool() { print("json bool: PASS\n") } else { print("json bool: FAIL\n") }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/learn/surgical_adam.sio ===
// stdlib/learn/surgical_adam.sio
//
// SurgicalAdam — Adam (Kingma & Ba 2014) adapted to preserve the
// ZD annihilator subspace at every step.
//
// The standard Adam update is:
//   m_t  = β1 m_{t-1} + (1-β1) g_t
//   v_t  = β2 v_{t-1} + (1-β2) g_t²
//   m̂_t  = m_t / (1 - β1^t)
//   v̂_t  = v_t / (1 - β2^t)
//   w_t  = w_{t-1} - lr * m̂_t / (√v̂_t + ε)
//
// A naive surgical adaptation would project the final update
// direction u_t onto the orthogonal complement of the kernel.  That
// works for exact preservation but loses Adam's signal in the
// kernel momentum.
//
// This implementation takes the stronger route: project the raw
// gradient onto the productive subspace BEFORE feeding it to the
// Adam moments.  This guarantees both m_t and v_t live entirely in
// the productive subspace, so the final update is kernel-safe by
// construction (not by post-hoc projection).
//
// Invariant: at every step, kernel_mass(w_t) == kernel_mass(w_0).
// Lean companion: SounioLearningDynamics.lean::surgical_adam_preserves_kernel.

// Kernel projectors (same as surgical_sgd.sio).  Duplicated for
// self-containment; a future refactor could share a common module.

fn sa_u1() -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD, Learn {
    var v: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    v[6]  =  0.707107
    v[15] = 0.0 - 0.707107
    v
}
fn sa_u2() -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD, Learn {
    var v: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    v[7]  =  0.707107
    v[14] =  0.707107
    v
}

fn sa_inner(a: &[f64; 16], b: &[f64; 16]) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, ZD, Learn {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { s = s + (*a)[i] * (*b)[i]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

fn sa_project_productive(grad: &[f64; 16]) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, Panic, ZD, Learn {
    let u1 = sa_u1()
    let u2 = sa_u2()
    let c1 = sa_inner(grad, &u1)
    let c2 = sa_inner(grad, &u2)
    var out: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        let ann_i = c1 * u1[i] + c2 * u2[i]
        out[i] = (*grad)[i] - ann_i
        i = i + 1
    }
    out
}

// State: Adam moments and a step counter.
struct AdamState {
    m: [f64; 16],
    v: [f64; 16],
    t: i64,
}

fn adam_state_new() -> AdamState with Mut {
    AdamState { m: [0.0; 16], v: [0.0; 16], t: 0 }
}

fn sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Single Newton step from the hardware-free seed 0.5*(1+x).
    // Accurate enough for adam denominator; ε below dominates tiny-x.
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = 0.5 * (1.0 + x)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

fn pow_int(base: f64, n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var acc = 1.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n { acc = acc * base; i = i + 1 }
    acc
}

// surgical_adam_step: one Adam step where the gradient has been
// projected onto the productive subspace before being absorbed into
// the moments.  Kernel component of w is preserved bit-exact.
fn surgical_adam_step(
    w: &![f64; 16],
    grad: &[f64; 16],
    st: &!AdamState,
    lr: f64,
    b1: f64,
    b2: f64,
    eps: f64,
) with Mut, Panic, Div, ZD, Learn {
    let g = sa_project_productive(grad)
    (*st).t = (*st).t + 1
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        (*st).m[i] = b1 * (*st).m[i] + (1.0 - b1) * g[i]
        (*st).v[i] = b2 * (*st).v[i] + (1.0 - b2) * g[i] * g[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let bc1 = 1.0 - pow_int(b1, (*st).t)
    let bc2 = 1.0 - pow_int(b2, (*st).t)
    var j = 0
    while j < 16 {
        let mhat = (*st).m[j] / bc1
        let vhat = (*st).v[j] / bc2
        let upd = mhat / (sqrt_approx(vhat) + eps)
        (*w)[j] = (*w)[j] - lr * upd
        j = j + 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/learn/surgical_sgd.sio ===
// stdlib/learn/surgical_sgd.sio
//
// SurgicalSGD — a gradient-descent optimizer that preserves ZD
// surgical invariants at every step.
//
// Problem: a standard SGD step  w <- w - lr * grad  will drift the
// weight vector off the ZD kernel subspace that a previous
// unlearn/gate/edit operation carved out.  The surgical invariant
// (e.g. "w has zero projection onto alice_kernel") is therefore NOT
// preserved by standard training.  This is the central technical
// issue Paper H addresses.
//
// SurgicalSGD decomposes the gradient at each step into:
//   grad = grad_productive ⊕ grad_annihilator
// where grad_annihilator is the component in the preserved-kernel
// subspace.  The surgical step is:
//   w <- w - lr * grad_productive
// which never perturbs the kernel component of w.
//
// Required effects: with ZD, Learn
// Proof of invariance: SounioLearningDynamics.lean::surgical_sgd_preserves_kernel.

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Kernel basis (replicated for self-containment).
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fn sk_u1() -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD, Learn {
    var v: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    v[6]  =  0.707107
    v[15] = 0.0 - 0.707107
    v
}
fn sk_u2() -> [f64; 16] with Mut, ZD, Learn {
    var v: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    v[7]  =  0.707107
    v[14] =  0.707107
    v
}

fn sk_inner(a: &[f64;16], b: &[f64;16]) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, ZD, Learn {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { s = s + (*a)[i] * (*b)[i]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

// project_annihilator: component of gradient that would move w off
// the preserved kernel subspace.  We RETURN this so the caller can
// discard it OR record it for analysis.
fn project_annihilator(grad: &[f64; 16]) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, Panic, ZD, Learn {
    let u1 = sk_u1()
    let u2 = sk_u2()
    let c1 = sk_inner(grad, &u1)
    let c2 = sk_inner(grad, &u2)
    var out: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { out[i] = c1 * u1[i] + c2 * u2[i]; i = i + 1 }
    out
}

// project_productive: the orthogonal complement — the safe direction
// to follow for gradient descent.
fn project_productive(grad: &[f64; 16]) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, Panic, ZD, Learn {
    let ann = project_annihilator(grad)
    var out: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { out[i] = (*grad)[i] - ann[i]; i = i + 1 }
    out
}

// surgical_sgd_step: standard SGD update restricted to productive
// gradient.  w is mutated in place; the kernel component of w is
// preserved bit-exact.
fn surgical_sgd_step(w: &![f64; 16], grad: &[f64; 16], lr: f64) with Mut, Panic, ZD, Learn {
    let prod = project_productive(grad)
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { (*w)[i] = (*w)[i] - lr * prod[i]; i = i + 1 }
}

// kernel_mass: compliance metric — squared mass in the kernel basis.
// Should remain constant across SurgicalSGD steps (the theorem).
fn kernel_mass(w: &[f64; 16]) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, ZD, Learn {
    let u1 = sk_u1()
    let u2 = sk_u2()
    let c1 = sk_inner(w, &u1)
    let c2 = sk_inner(w, &u2)
    c1 * c1 + c2 * c2
}


// === FILE: stdlib/linalg/blas_fallback.sio ===
// stdlib/linalg/blas_fallback.sio
// Pure Sounio fallback implementations for BLAS Level 1-3
//
// Uses fixed arrays. Suitable for small matrices (n < 16).

fn bls_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn bls_sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var iter: i64 = 0
    while iter < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    return y
}

// DAXPY: y = alpha * x + y
fn daxpy_fallback(n: i64, alpha: f64, x: [f64; 64], y: &![f64; 64]) {
    if alpha == 0.0 { return }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        y[i] = y[i] + alpha * x[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// DDOT: dot product
fn ddot_fallback(n: i64, x: [f64; 64], y: [f64; 64]) -> f64 {
    var result = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        result = result + x[i] * y[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// DNRM2: Euclidean norm
fn dnrm2_fallback(n: i64, x: [f64; 64]) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var scale = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let val = bls_abs_f64(x[i])
        if val > 0.0 {
            if scale < val {
                let ratio = scale / val
                sum = 1.0 + sum * ratio * ratio
                scale = val
            } else {
                let ratio = val / scale
                sum = sum + ratio * ratio
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return scale * bls_sqrt_f64(sum)
}

// DSCAL: x = alpha * x
fn dscal_fallback(n: i64, alpha: f64, x: &![f64; 64]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        x[i] = alpha * x[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// DASUM: sum of absolute values
fn dasum_fallback(n: i64, x: [f64; 64]) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + bls_abs_f64(x[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// IDAMAX: index of max absolute value
fn idamax_fallback(n: i64, x: [f64; 64]) -> i64 {
    if n <= 0 { return 0 }
    var max_idx: i64 = 0
    var max_val = bls_abs_f64(x[0])
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        let val = bls_abs_f64(x[i])
        if val > max_val {
            max_val = val
            max_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return max_idx
}

// DCOPY: y = x
fn dcopy_fallback(n: i64, x: [f64; 64], y: &![f64; 64]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        y[i] = x[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// DSWAP: swap x and y
fn dswap_fallback(n: i64, x: &![f64; 64], y: &![f64; 64]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let temp = x[i]
        x[i] = y[i]
        y[i] = temp
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// DGEMV: y = alpha * A * x + beta * y (row-major, no transpose)
// A is [m x n], x is [n], y is [m]
fn dgemv_fallback(m: i64, n: i64, alpha: f64, a: [f64; 256], x: [f64; 64], beta: f64, y: &![f64; 64]) {
    // Scale y by beta
    if beta != 1.0 {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < m {
            y[i] = beta * y[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    if alpha == 0.0 { return }

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < m {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            sum = sum + a[i * n + j] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        y[i] = y[i] + alpha * sum
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// DGEMM: C = alpha * A * B + beta * C (row-major, no transpose)
// A is [m x k], B is [k x n], C is [m x n]
fn dgemm_fallback(m: i64, n: i64, k: i64, alpha: f64, a: [f64; 256], b: [f64; 256], beta: f64, c: &![f64; 256]) {
    // Scale C by beta
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < m {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            c[i * n + j] = beta * c[i * n + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if alpha == 0.0 { return }

    i = 0
    while i < m {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            var sum = 0.0
            var l: i64 = 0
            while l < k {
                sum = sum + a[i * k + l] * b[l * n + j]
                l = l + 1
            }
            c[i * n + j] = c[i * n + j] + alpha * sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn blas_fallback_approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, eps: f64) -> i64 {
    let diff = a - b
    let ad = if diff < 0.0 { 0.0 - diff } else { diff }
    if ad < eps { return 1 }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/linalg/blas_ffi.sio ===
// stdlib/linalg/blas_ffi.sio — BLAS-compatible Matrix Operations (Pure Sounio)
//
// Provides BLAS-compatible matrix multiplication interface in pure Sounio.
// The ffi:: modules are not available in this build, so all operations are
// implemented as optimised pure-Sounio loops.
//
// Matrices are stored in ROW-MAJOR order, max 16x16 = 256 elements.
//
// Interface matches what epistemic_matrix.sio expects.
// blas_available() returns false — callers should use GUM propagation path.
//
// References:
//   BLAS Technical Forum Standard (2001)
//   Golub & Van Loan (2013) "Matrix Computations" 4th ed.

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers
// =============================================================================

fn abs_blas(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// =============================================================================
// Availability (always false — no FFI in this build)
// =============================================================================

/// Returns false: BLAS FFI is not compiled into this build.
/// Callers should use the pure-Sounio GUM propagation path.
pub fn blas_available() -> bool { false }

/// Returns false: DGEMM via FFI is not available.
pub fn dgemm_available() -> bool { false }

/// Returns false: SVD via LAPACK FFI is not available.
pub fn dgesvd_available() -> bool { false }

// =============================================================================
// DGEMM — C = alpha * A * B + beta * C  (row-major, general matrices)
// =============================================================================

/// Compute C = alpha * A * B + beta * C (row-major storage).
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `m`: Rows of A and C
/// - `n`: Columns of B and C
/// - `k`: Columns of A = rows of B
/// - `alpha`: Scalar multiplier for A*B
/// - `a`: Input matrix A (m x k, row-major, 256 elements)
/// - `b`: Input matrix B (k x n, row-major, 256 elements)
/// - `beta`: Scalar multiplier for C
/// - `c`: In/out matrix C (m x n, row-major, 256 elements)
///
/// # Return
/// 0 on success, -1 on dimension error
pub fn blas_dgemm_rowmajor(
    m: i32, n: i32, k: i32,
    alpha: f64,
    a: &[f64; 256],
    b: &[f64; 256],
    beta: f64,
    c: &![f64; 256],
) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Bounds check
    if m <= 0 || n <= 0 || k <= 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    if m * k > 256 || k * n > 256 || m * n > 256 { return 0 - 1 }

    var i = 0
    while i < m {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            // Scale existing C element
            var acc: f64 = beta * c[i * n + j]

            // Accumulate alpha * row_i(A) · col_j(B)
            var l = 0
            while l < k {
                acc = acc + alpha * a[i * k + l] * b[l * n + j]
                l = l + 1
            }

            c[i * n + j] = acc
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    0
}

/// Convenience wrapper: C = A * B (alpha=1, beta=0).
pub fn blas_dgemm(
    a: &[f64; 256], b: &[f64; 256], c: &![f64; 256],
    m: i32, n: i32, k: i32,
) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    blas_dgemm_rowmajor(m, n, k, 1.0, a, b, 0.0, c)
}

// =============================================================================
// DGESVD — Approximate SVD via power iteration (rank-1 approximation)
// =============================================================================

/// Compute approximate singular values via power iteration.
///
/// For a matrix A (m x n, row-major), computes s[0] = largest singular value.
/// Full SVD is not implemented — only the dominant singular value.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `a`: Input matrix A (m x n, 256 elements), overwritten
/// - `m`: Rows
/// - `n`: Columns
/// - `s`: Output singular values (min(m,n) values)
/// - `iters`: Power iteration steps (higher = more accurate)
///
/// # Return
/// 0 on success, -1 on error
pub fn blas_dgesvd_approx(
    a: &[f64; 256],
    m: i32, n: i32,
    s: &![f64; 16],
    iters: i32,
) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if m <= 0 || n <= 0 || m * n > 256 { return 0 - 1 }

    let p = if m < n { m } else { n }

    // Power iteration for dominant singular value
    // v = initial vector (all ones, normalised)
    var v: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var v_norm: f64 = 0.0
    var vi = 0
    while vi < n {
        v[vi] = 1.0
        v_norm = v_norm + 1.0
        vi = vi + 1
    }
    // Normalise
    let inv_norm = if v_norm > 1.0e-30 { 1.0 / v_norm } else { 0.0 }
    var vi2 = 0
    while vi2 < n {
        v[vi2] = v[vi2] * inv_norm
        vi2 = vi2 + 1
    }

    // Power iteration: v ← A'*A*v / ||A'*A*v||
    var it = 0
    while it < iters {
        // u = A * v  (m-vector)
        var u: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
        var ri = 0
        while ri < m {
            var ci = 0
            while ci < n {
                u[ri] = u[ri] + a[ri * n + ci] * v[ci]
                ci = ci + 1
            }
            ri = ri + 1
        }

        // v = A' * u  (n-vector)
        var v2: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
        var ci2 = 0
        while ci2 < n {
            var ri2 = 0
            while ri2 < m {
                v2[ci2] = v2[ci2] + a[ri2 * n + ci2] * u[ri2]
                ri2 = ri2 + 1
            }
            ci2 = ci2 + 1
        }

        // Compute norm of v2
        var norm: f64 = 0.0
        var ni = 0
        while ni < n {
            norm = norm + v2[ni] * v2[ni]
            ni = ni + 1
        }
        // sigma = sqrt(norm)
        var sigma = norm
        var sq_i = 0
        while sq_i < 15 {
            sigma = 0.5 * (sigma + norm / sigma)
            sq_i = sq_i + 1
        }

        // Normalise v2 → v
        let inv = if sigma > 1.0e-30 { 1.0 / sigma } else { 0.0 }
        var ni2 = 0
        while ni2 < n {
            v[ni2] = v2[ni2] * inv
            ni2 = ni2 + 1
        }

        it = it + 1
    }

    // Compute s[0] = ||A*v||
    var u_final: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var rf = 0
    while rf < m {
        var cf = 0
        while cf < n {
            u_final[rf] = u_final[rf] + a[rf * n + cf] * v[cf]
            cf = cf + 1
        }
        rf = rf + 1
    }
    var s0: f64 = 0.0
    var si = 0
    while si < m {
        s0 = s0 + u_final[si] * u_final[si]
        si = si + 1
    }
    // sqrt(s0)
    var sq = s0
    var sq_j = 0
    while sq_j < 15 {
        sq = 0.5 * (sq + s0 / sq)
        sq_j = sq_j + 1
    }
    s[0] = sq

    // Remaining singular values set to 0 (not computed)
    var pi = 1
    while pi < p {
        s[pi] = 0.0
        pi = pi + 1
    }

    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/linalg/decomp.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL PASS

// decomp.sio - Matrix Decompositions for Sounio Linear Algebra
//
// Fixed-size QR, Eigendecomposition, and SVD for matrices up to 8x8.
// Uses flat array representation [f64; 64] for 8x8 row-major storage.
//
// Algorithms:
//   QR:    Householder reflections
//   Eigen: QR algorithm with Wilkinson shift (symmetric via tridiagonalization)
//   SVD:   Via eigendecomposition of A^T A

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 {
        return 0.0 - x
    }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    // Range reduction: scale x into [1, 4) by multiplying by powers of 4
    // then scale the result back by dividing by the power of 2
    var scaled = x
    var scale_back = 1.0
    // Scale up small numbers
    while scaled < 1.0 {
        scaled = scaled * 4.0
        scale_back = scale_back * 2.0
    }
    // Scale down large numbers
    while scaled > 4.0 {
        scaled = scaled * 0.25
        scale_back = scale_back * 0.5
    }
    // Newton-Raphson on scaled value (now in [1, 4))
    var y = 1.5
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    return y / scale_back
}

fn sign_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x >= 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    return 0.0 - 1.0
}

fn max_i32(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_i32(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// DATA STRUCTURES
