// === FILE: stdlib/logic/proof_certificates.sio ===
// Sprint 24 Track D: Proof Certificate stdlib
// References: Wadler (2015), Martin-Lof (1984), Chlipala CPDT

fn constructive_add_comm(a: i64, b: i64) -> bool {
    // Constructive proof of commutativity (trivially true for integers)
    a + b == b + a
}

fn lemma_transitivity(ab: bool, bc: bool) -> bool {
    // Transitivity: (A->B) ^ (B->C) -> (A->C)
    ab && bc
}

fn axiom_minimum(arr: [i64; 8], n: i64) -> i64 {
    // Axiom of choice: select minimum from first n elements
    var m: i64 = arr[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        let v: i64 = arr[i as usize]
        if v < m { m = v }
        i = i + 1
    }
    m
}

fn proof_confidence_combine(c1: f64, c2: f64) -> f64 {
    // Conservative combination: minimum of two independent confidences
    if c1 < c2 { c1 } else { c2 }
}

fn is_constructive_proof(proof_kind: i64) -> bool {
    proof_kind == 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/logic/pure/types.sio ===
// stdlib/logic/pure/types.sio — Logic/Propositional Types

pub enum Proposition {
    True,
    False,
    Var(string),
    Not(Box<Proposition>),
    And(Box<Proposition>, Box<Proposition>),
    Or(Box<Proposition>, Box<Proposition>),
    Imp(Box<Proposition>, Box<Proposition>),
}

pub struct TruthAssignment {
    pub vars: [string; 64],
    pub values: [bool; 64],
    pub n_vars: i32,
}

pub fn assignment_new() -> TruthAssignment {
    TruthAssignment { vars: [""; 64], values: [false; 64], n_vars: 0 }
}

pub fn assignment_set(a: &! TruthAssignment, v: string, val: bool) with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < a.n_vars {
        if a.vars[i as usize] == v {
            a.values[i as usize] = val
            return
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if a.n_vars < 64 {
        let idx = a.n_vars as usize
        a.vars[idx] = v
        a.values[idx] = val
        a.n_vars = a.n_vars + 1
    }
}

pub fn assignment_get(a: &TruthAssignment, v: string) -> bool {
    var i = 0
    while i < a.n_vars {
        if a.vars[i as usize] == v {
            return a.values[i as usize]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    false
}

pub fn proposition_evaluate(p: &Proposition, a: &TruthAssignment) -> bool {
    match p {
        Proposition::True => true,
        Proposition::False => false,
        Proposition::Var(name) => assignment_get(a, name),
        Proposition::Not(q) => !proposition_evaluate(q, a),
        Proposition::And(q1, q2) => proposition_evaluate(q1, a) && proposition_evaluate(q2, a),
        Proposition::Or(q1, q2) => proposition_evaluate(q1, a) || proposition_evaluate(q2, a),
        Proposition::Imp(q1, q2) => !proposition_evaluate(q1, a) || proposition_evaluate(q2, a),
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Boolean logic primitives (i64-encoded 0/1 truth values)
// =============================================================================

pub fn prop_and(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a != 0 && b != 0 { 1 } else { 0 } }
pub fn prop_or(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a != 0 || b != 0 { 1 } else { 0 } }
pub fn prop_not(a: i64) -> i64 { if a == 0 { 1 } else { 0 } }
pub fn prop_implies(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a != 0 && b == 0 { 0 } else { 1 } }
pub fn prop_iff(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if (a != 0) == (b != 0) { 1 } else { 0 } }
pub fn prop_xor(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if (a != 0) != (b != 0) { 1 } else { 0 } }
pub fn prop_nand(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { prop_not(prop_and(a, b)) }
pub fn prop_nor(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { prop_not(prop_or(a, b)) }

pub fn truth_table_2(op: i64) -> [i64; 4] {
    // op: 0=AND, 1=OR, 2=XOR, 3=IMPLIES, 4=IFF
    if op == 0 {
        [0, 0, 0, 1]
    } else if op == 1 {
        [0, 1, 1, 1]
    } else if op == 2 {
        [0, 1, 1, 0]
    } else if op == 3 {
        [1, 1, 0, 1]
    } else if op == 4 {
        [1, 0, 0, 1]
    } else {
        [0, 0, 0, 0]
    }
}

pub fn is_tautology_2(op: i64) -> bool {
    let tbl = truth_table_2(op)
    tbl[0] == 1 && tbl[1] == 1 && tbl[2] == 1 && tbl[3] == 1
}

pub fn is_contradiction_2(op: i64) -> bool {
    let tbl = truth_table_2(op)
    tbl[0] == 0 && tbl[1] == 0 && tbl[2] == 0 && tbl[3] == 0
}

pub fn de_morgan_and(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    // not(a and b) == (not a) or (not b)
    let lhs = prop_not(prop_and(a, b))
    let rhs = prop_or(prop_not(a), prop_not(b))
    prop_iff(lhs, rhs)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/math/approx.sio ===
// stdlib/math/approx.sio — Approximation theory
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Chebyshev approximation: coefficients, Clenshaw evaluation, derivative, integral
//   Pade approximation: compute [p/q] approximant from Taylor coefficients
//   Minimax polynomial: Remez exchange algorithm
//
// References:
//   Mason & Handscomb (2003): "Chebyshev Polynomials"
//   Trefethen (2019): "Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice"
//   Press et al. (2007): "Numerical Recipes" Ch. 5.8, 5.12
//   Powell (1981): "Approximation Theory and Methods"

// =============================================================================
// Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn ap_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn ap_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

fn ap_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var a = x
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 { term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64; sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    sum
}

fn ap_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

// =============================================================================
// Chebyshev approximation
// =============================================================================

// Compute Chebyshev coefficients c[0..n-1] for f on [a, b].
// Uses the DCT at Chebyshev nodes: x_k = cos(pi*(k+0.5)/n), k=0..n-1.
// c_j = (2/n) * sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(x_k) * cos(pi*j*(k+0.5)/n)
fn cheb_coeffs(f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
               a: f64, b: f64, n: i32,
               out: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let bma = 0.5 * (b - a)
    let bpa = 0.5 * (b + a)

    // Evaluate f at Chebyshev nodes
    var fvals: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var k = 0
    while k < n {
        let theta = ap_pi() * ((k as f64) + 0.5) / (n as f64)
        let x = ap_cos(theta) * bma + bpa
        fvals[k] = f(x)
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Compute coefficients via DCT
    var j = 0
    while j < n {
        var sum = 0.0
        k = 0
        while k < n {
            let theta = ap_pi() * (j as f64) * ((k as f64) + 0.5) / (n as f64)
            sum = sum + fvals[k] * ap_cos(theta)
            k = k + 1
        }
        out[j] = 2.0 * sum / (n as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// Evaluate Chebyshev approximation at x in [a, b] using Clenshaw recurrence.
// coeffs[0..n-1] are the Chebyshev coefficients.
fn cheb_eval(coeffs: &[f64; 128], n: i32, a: f64, b: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Map x from [a, b] to [-1, 1]
    let y = (2.0 * x - a - b) / (b - a)

    // Clenshaw recurrence: evaluate sum c_k * T_k(y)
    var d1 = 0.0
    var d2 = 0.0
    var j = n - 1
    while j >= 1 {
        let temp = d1
        d1 = 2.0 * y * d1 - d2 + coeffs[j]
        d2 = temp
        j = j - 1
    }
    y * d1 - d2 + 0.5 * coeffs[0]
}

// Derivative of Chebyshev series.
// If c[0..n-1] are coefficients of f, compute c'[0..n-2] of f'.
// Scaled to [a, b]: multiply by 2/(b-a).
fn cheb_derivative(coeffs: &[f64; 128], n: i32, a: f64, b: f64,
                   out: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let scale = 2.0 / (b - a)
    out[n - 1] = 0.0
    if n >= 2 { out[n - 2] = 2.0 * ((n - 1) as f64) * coeffs[n - 1] }

    var j = n - 3
    while j >= 0 {
        out[j] = out[j + 2] + 2.0 * ((j + 1) as f64) * coeffs[j + 1]
        j = j - 1
    }
    // Scale all coefficients
    var i = 0
    while i < n { out[i] = out[i] * scale; i = i + 1 }
    // First coefficient halved (standard convention)
    out[0] = out[0] * 0.5
}

// Integral of Chebyshev series.
// Computes antiderivative coefficients c_int[0..n] from c[0..n-1].
// c_int[0] is set to 0 (arbitrary constant).
fn cheb_integral(coeffs: &[f64; 128], n: i32, a: f64, b: f64,
                 out: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let scale = 0.5 * (b - a)
    out[0] = 0.0

    var j = 1
    while j < n {
        if j == 1 {
            out[1] = scale * (coeffs[0] - 0.5 * coeffs[2])
        } else if j < n - 1 {
            out[j] = scale * (coeffs[j - 1] - coeffs[j + 1]) / (2.0 * (j as f64))
        } else {
            out[j] = scale * coeffs[j - 1] / (2.0 * (j as f64))
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// Truncation: number of significant Chebyshev coefficients.
// Returns the smallest m such that |c[m]|, |c[m+1]|, ... are all < tol.
fn cheb_truncate(coeffs: &[f64; 128], n: i32, tol: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m = n
    while m > 1 {
        if ap_abs(coeffs[m - 1]) > tol { return m }
        m = m - 1
    }
    1
}

// =============================================================================
// Pade approximation
// =============================================================================

// Compute [p/q] Pade approximant from Taylor coefficients.
// Given f(x) = sum_{k=0}^{p+q} taylor[k] * x^k, find
// num[0..p] and den[0..q] such that num(x)/den(x) agrees with f(x)
// to order p+q.
//
// Method: solve the linear system for denominator coefficients,
// then compute numerator coefficients.
// Returns true if successful, false if singular.
fn pade_coeffs(taylor: &[f64; 64], n_taylor: i32,
               p: i32, q: i32,
               num: &![f64; 32], den: &![f64; 32]) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if p + q >= n_taylor { return false }

    // den[0] = 1 (normalization)
    den[0] = 1.0

    if q == 0 {
        // Polynomial approximation (no denominator)
        var i = 0
        while i <= p { num[i] = taylor[i]; i = i + 1 }
        return true
    }

    // Solve for den[1..q] from the equations:
    // sum_{j=0}^{q} den[j] * taylor[p+1-j+i] = 0, i = 0..q-1
    // (where taylor[k] = 0 for k < 0)
    // This is a q x q system: A * d = -b

    // Build the system (row-major in a flat array)
    var mat: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]  // q x q matrix
    var rhs: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]

    var i = 0
    while i < q {
        var j = 0
        while j < q {
            let idx = p + 1 + i - j - 1
            if idx >= 0 && idx < n_taylor {
                mat[i * q + j] = taylor[idx]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        let rhs_idx = p + 1 + i
        if rhs_idx >= 0 && rhs_idx < n_taylor {
            rhs[i] = 0.0 - taylor[rhs_idx]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting
    var col = 0
    while col < q {
        // Find pivot
        var max_val = ap_abs(mat[col * q + col])
        var max_row = col
        var row = col + 1
        while row < q {
            if ap_abs(mat[row * q + col]) > max_val {
                max_val = ap_abs(mat[row * q + col])
                max_row = row
            }
            row = row + 1
        }
        if max_val < 1.0e-14 { return false }

        // Swap rows
        if max_row != col {
            var j = 0
            while j < q {
                let temp = mat[col * q + j]
                mat[col * q + j] = mat[max_row * q + j]
                mat[max_row * q + j] = temp
                j = j + 1
            }
            let temp_r = rhs[col]
            rhs[col] = rhs[max_row]
            rhs[max_row] = temp_r
        }

        // Eliminate
        row = col + 1
        while row < q {
            let factor = mat[row * q + col] / mat[col * q + col]
            var j = col
            while j < q { mat[row * q + j] = mat[row * q + j] - factor * mat[col * q + j]; j = j + 1 }
            rhs[row] = rhs[row] - factor * rhs[col]
            row = row + 1
        }
        col = col + 1
    }

    // Back substitution
    var k = q - 1
    while k >= 0 {
        var s = rhs[k]
        var j = k + 1
        while j < q { s = s - mat[k * q + j] * den[j + 1]; j = j + 1 }
        den[k + 1] = s / mat[k * q + k]
        k = k - 1
    }

    // Compute numerator: num[k] = sum_{j=0}^{min(k,q)} den[j] * taylor[k-j]
    i = 0
    while i <= p {
        var s = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j <= q && j <= i {
            s = s + den[j] * taylor[i - j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        num[i] = s
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// Evaluate Pade rational function num(x)/den(x).
fn pade_eval(num: &[f64; 32], p: i32,
             den: &[f64; 32], q: i32,
             x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Horner evaluation for numerator
    var numer = num[p]
    var i = p - 1
    while i >= 0 { numer = numer * x + num[i]; i = i - 1 }

    // Horner evaluation for denominator
    var denom = den[q]
    i = q - 1
    while i >= 0 { denom = denom * x + den[i]; i = i - 1 }

    numer / denom
}

// =============================================================================
// Minimax polynomial (Remez exchange algorithm)
// =============================================================================

// Remez exchange algorithm to find the minimax polynomial of degree d
// approximating f on [a, b].
// Stores polynomial coefficients (monomial basis) in coeffs[0..d].
// Returns the maximum approximation error (equioscillation error).
fn remez(f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
         a: f64, b: f64, degree: i32,
         coeffs: &![f64; 32]) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = degree + 2  // n = d+2 reference points

    // Initialize reference points as Chebyshev nodes on [a, b]
    var refs: [f64; 34] = [0.0; 34]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let theta = ap_pi() * (i as f64) / ((n - 1) as f64)
        refs[i] = 0.5 * (a + b) - 0.5 * (b - a) * ap_cos(theta)
        i = i + 1
    }

    var max_err = 0.0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < 50 {
        // Solve the interpolation system:
        // p(x_i) + (-1)^i * E = f(x_i), i = 0..n-1
        // This is a (d+2) x (d+2) system for coeffs[0..d] and E.

        // Build matrix (row-major)
        var mat: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
        var rhs: [f64; 34] = [0.0; 34]

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            // Monomial basis: x^0, x^1, ..., x^d
            var x_pow = 1.0
            var j = 0
            while j <= degree {
                mat[i * n + j] = x_pow
                x_pow = x_pow * refs[i]
                j = j + 1
            }
            // Error column
            let sign = if i - (i / 2) * 2 == 0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 - 1.0 }
            mat[i * n + (degree + 1)] = sign
            rhs[i] = f(refs[i])
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Gaussian elimination
        var col = 0
        while col < n {
            var max_val = ap_abs(mat[col * n + col])
            var max_row = col
            var row = col + 1
            while row < n {
                if ap_abs(mat[row * n + col]) > max_val { max_val = ap_abs(mat[row * n + col]); max_row = row }
                row = row + 1
            }
            if max_row != col {
                var j = 0
                while j < n {
                    let temp = mat[col * n + j]; mat[col * n + j] = mat[max_row * n + j]; mat[max_row * n + j] = temp
                    j = j + 1
                }
                let tr = rhs[col]; rhs[col] = rhs[max_row]; rhs[max_row] = tr
            }
            row = col + 1
            while row < n {
                if ap_abs(mat[col * n + col]) > 1.0e-30 {
                    let factor = mat[row * n + col] / mat[col * n + col]
                    var j = col
                    while j < n { mat[row * n + j] = mat[row * n + j] - factor * mat[col * n + j]; j = j + 1 }
                    rhs[row] = rhs[row] - factor * rhs[col]
                }
                row = row + 1
            }
            col = col + 1
        }

        // Back substitution
        var sol: [f64; 34] = [0.0; 34]
        var k = n - 1
        while k >= 0 {
            var s = rhs[k]
            var j = k + 1
            while j < n { s = s - mat[k * n + j] * sol[j]; j = j + 1 }
            if ap_abs(mat[k * n + k]) > 1.0e-30 { sol[k] = s / mat[k * n + k] }
            k = k - 1
        }

        // Extract coefficients and error
        i = 0
        while i <= degree { coeffs[i] = sol[i]; i = i + 1 }
        let levelled_err = ap_abs(sol[degree + 1])

        // Check convergence
        if ap_abs(levelled_err - max_err) < 1.0e-14 * ap_max(levelled_err, 1.0) {
            return levelled_err
        }
        max_err = levelled_err

        // Exchange step: find new reference points where error is maximal
        // Sample error at many points
        let n_sample = 200
        var new_refs: [f64; 34] = [0.0; 34]
        var ref_count = 0

        // Find extrema of error function by sampling
        var prev_err = 0.0
        var prev_x = a
        var si = 0
        while si <= n_sample && ref_count < n {
            let x = a + (b - a) * (si as f64) / (n_sample as f64)
            // Evaluate polynomial
            var px = 0.0
            var x_pow = 1.0
            var j = 0
            while j <= degree { px = px + coeffs[j] * x_pow; x_pow = x_pow * x; j = j + 1 }
            let err = f(x) - px

            if si > 0 {
                // Check for sign change (local extremum between prev and current)
                if (err > 0.0 && prev_err < 0.0) || (err < 0.0 && prev_err > 0.0) {
                    // Extremum near midpoint
                    if ref_count < n {
                        new_refs[ref_count] = 0.5 * (prev_x + x)
                        ref_count = ref_count + 1
                    }
                }
            }
            prev_err = err
            prev_x = x
            si = si + 1
        }

        // If we found enough reference points, update
        if ref_count >= n {
            i = 0
            while i < n { refs[i] = new_refs[i]; i = i + 1 }
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }
    max_err
}

// ============================================================================
// Approx-effect primitives (Gen 22)
//
// Functions that introduce numerical approximation are marked with `with Approx`.
// This makes approximation a first-class tracked effect in the Sounio type system.
// ============================================================================

pub fn approx_taylor_sin(x: f64, terms: i64) -> f64 with Approx, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var sign: f64 = 1.0
    var power: f64 = x
    var fact: f64 = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < terms {
        let term = sign * power / fact
        sum = sum + term
        sign = 0.0 - sign
        power = power * x * x
        fact = fact * ((2.0 * (i as f64) + 2.0) * (2.0 * (i as f64) + 3.0))
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

pub fn approx_newton_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Approx, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    if x == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y: f64 = x
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

pub fn approx_finite_diff(f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Approx, x: f64, h: f64) -> f64 with Approx, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let f_plus = f(x + h)
    let f_minus = f(x - h)
    (f_plus - f_minus) / (2.0 * h)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/cayley_dickson.sio ===
//! stdlib/math/cayley_dickson.sio - Cayley-Dickson Construction Helpers (f64)
//!
//! Concrete helper functions for the Cayley-Dickson doubling construction:
//!   R -> C -> H -> O -> S
//! Provides f64-precision octonionic multiplication and conjugation components
//! used by sedenion64.sio for the FSNN pipeline.
//!
//! The Cayley-Dickson product rule for (a,b)*(c,d):
//!   real part = a*c - conj(d)*b
//!   imag part = d*a + b*conj(c)
//! where a,b,c,d are elements of the algebra at the previous level.
//!
//! References:
//! - Baez, "The Octonions", Bull. AMS 2002
//! - Cayley-Dickson construction: each level doubles dimension, loses one property
//!   C: loses ordering | H: loses commutativity | O: loses associativity | S: loses alternativity

// ============================================================================
// RESULT TYPES (structs to avoid tuple index limitations)
// ============================================================================

// 8-component result for octonionic operations
pub struct Oct8 {
    c0: f64,
    c1: f64,
    c2: f64,
    c3: f64,
    c4: f64,
    c5: f64,
    c6: f64,
    c7: f64,
}

// 16-component result for sedenion multiplication
pub struct Sed16Comp {
    r0: f64,
    r1: f64,
    r2: f64,
    r3: f64,
    r4: f64,
    r5: f64,
    r6: f64,
    r7: f64,
    r8: f64,
    r9: f64,
    r10: f64,
    r11: f64,
    r12: f64,
    r13: f64,
    r14: f64,
    r15: f64,
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTONIONIC MULTIPLICATION (f64)
// ============================================================================
// Standard Cayley-Dickson multiplication table for octonions.
// Same formula as oct_mul in octonion.sio but with f64 precision.
// Verified for norm multiplicativity |ab| = |a||b| and Moufang identities.
// Complexity: 64 multiplications + 56 additions = 120 FLOPs

fn oct64_mul_components(
    a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64, a4: f64, a5: f64, a6: f64, a7: f64,
    b0: f64, b1: f64, b2: f64, b3: f64, b4: f64, b5: f64, b6: f64, b7: f64
) -> Oct8 {
    let c0 = a0*b0 - a1*b1 - a2*b2 - a3*b3 - a4*b4 - a5*b5 - a6*b6 - a7*b7
    let c1 = a0*b1 + a1*b0 + a2*b3 - a3*b2 + a4*b5 - a5*b4 - a6*b7 + a7*b6
    let c2 = a0*b2 - a1*b3 + a2*b0 + a3*b1 + a4*b6 + a5*b7 - a6*b4 - a7*b5
    let c3 = a0*b3 + a1*b2 - a2*b1 + a3*b0 + a4*b7 - a5*b6 + a6*b5 - a7*b4
    let c4 = a0*b4 - a1*b5 - a2*b6 - a3*b7 + a4*b0 + a5*b1 + a6*b2 + a7*b3
    let c5 = a0*b5 + a1*b4 - a2*b7 + a3*b6 - a4*b1 + a5*b0 - a6*b3 + a7*b2
    let c6 = a0*b6 + a1*b7 + a2*b4 - a3*b5 - a4*b2 + a5*b3 + a6*b0 - a7*b1
    let c7 = a0*b7 - a1*b6 + a2*b5 + a3*b4 - a4*b3 - a5*b2 + a6*b1 + a7*b0
    Oct8 { c0: c0, c1: c1, c2: c2, c3: c3, c4: c4, c5: c5, c6: c6, c7: c7 }
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTONIONIC CONJUGATION (f64)
// ============================================================================
// conj(a0 + a1*e1 + ... + a7*e7) = a0 - a1*e1 - ... - a7*e7
// Property: conj(ab) = conj(b)*conj(a) (anti-automorphism)

fn oct64_conj_components(
    a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64, a4: f64, a5: f64, a6: f64, a7: f64
) -> Oct8 {
    Oct8 {
        c0: a0,
        c1: 0.0 - a1,
        c2: 0.0 - a2,
        c3: 0.0 - a3,
        c4: 0.0 - a4,
        c5: 0.0 - a5,
        c6: 0.0 - a6,
        c7: 0.0 - a7,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CAYLEY-DICKSON SEDENION PRODUCT (f64)
// ============================================================================
// Given sedenion s1 = (a, b) and s2 = (c, d) where a,b,c,d are octonions:
//   (a,b) * (c,d) = (a*c - conj(d)*b, d*a + b*conj(c))
//
// This requires 4 octonionic multiplications + 2 conjugations:
//   p1 = a * c
//   p2 = conj(d) * b
//   p3 = d * a
//   p4 = b * conj(c)
//   result_lo = p1 - p2
//   result_hi = p3 + p4
//
// Complexity: 4 * 120 + 16 + 16 = 512 FLOPs

fn cd_product_16(
    a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64, a4: f64, a5: f64, a6: f64, a7: f64,
    b0: f64, b1: f64, b2: f64, b3: f64, b4: f64, b5: f64, b6: f64, b7: f64,
    c0: f64, c1: f64, c2: f64, c3: f64, c4: f64, c5: f64, c6: f64, c7: f64,
    d0: f64, d1: f64, d2: f64, d3: f64, d4: f64, d5: f64, d6: f64, d7: f64
) -> Sed16Comp {

    // p1 = a * c
    let p1 = oct64_mul_components(a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7,
                                   c0, c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c7)

    // p2 = conj(d) * b
    let cd = oct64_conj_components(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d6, d7)
    let p2 = oct64_mul_components(cd.c0, cd.c1, cd.c2, cd.c3, cd.c4, cd.c5, cd.c6, cd.c7,
                                   b0, b1, b2, b3, b4, b5, b6, b7)

    // p3 = d * a
    let p3 = oct64_mul_components(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d6, d7,
                                   a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7)

    // p4 = b * conj(c)
    let cc = oct64_conj_components(c0, c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c7)
    let p4 = oct64_mul_components(b0, b1, b2, b3, b4, b5, b6, b7,
                                   cc.c0, cc.c1, cc.c2, cc.c3, cc.c4, cc.c5, cc.c6, cc.c7)

    // result_lo = p1 - p2 (real octonion half)
    // result_hi = p3 + p4 (imaginary octonion half)
    Sed16Comp {
        r0:  p1.c0 - p2.c0,
        r1:  p1.c1 - p2.c1,
        r2:  p1.c2 - p2.c2,
        r3:  p1.c3 - p2.c3,
        r4:  p1.c4 - p2.c4,
        r5:  p1.c5 - p2.c5,
        r6:  p1.c6 - p2.c6,
        r7:  p1.c7 - p2.c7,
        r8:  p3.c0 + p4.c0,
        r9:  p3.c1 + p4.c1,
        r10: p3.c2 + p4.c2,
        r11: p3.c3 + p4.c3,
        r12: p3.c4 + p4.c4,
        r13: p3.c5 + p4.c5,
        r14: p3.c6 + p4.c6,
        r15: p3.c7 + p4.c7,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTONIONIC NORM SQUARED (f64)
// ============================================================================

fn oct64_norm_sq_components(
    a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64, a4: f64, a5: f64, a6: f64, a7: f64
) -> f64 {
    a0*a0 + a1*a1 + a2*a2 + a3*a3 + a4*a4 + a5*a5 + a6*a6 + a7*a7
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/combinatorics.sio ===
// stdlib/math/combinatorics.sio — Combinatorial functions
//
// Pure Sounio implementations of classical combinatorial quantities:
//   Binomial coefficients, Stirling numbers (1st & 2nd kind), Catalan numbers,
//   Bell numbers, integer partitions, derangements, multinomial coefficients,
//   falling/rising factorials, harmonic numbers, Bernoulli numbers, Euler numbers.
//
// All functions are pure Sounio — zero FFI.
//
// References:
//   Graham, Knuth, Patashnik (1994): "Concrete Mathematics" (2nd ed.)
//   Stanley (2011): "Enumerative Combinatorics" Vol. 1 (2nd ed.)
//   Comtet (1974): "Advanced Combinatorics"
//   DLMF Ch. 24, 26

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (must precede callers)
// =============================================================================

fn comb_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn comb_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn comb_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    var k_f = x / 0.6931471805599453
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    } else {
        var i = 0
        while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    }
    result
}

fn comb_lgamma(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 1.0e30 }
    var val = x
    var shift = 0.0
    while val < 8.0 {
        shift = shift + comb_ln(val)
        val = val + 1.0
    }
    var result = (val - 0.5) * comb_ln(val) - val + 0.5 * 1.8378770664093453
    let inv_v = 1.0 / val
    let iv2 = inv_v * inv_v
    result = result + inv_v / 12.0
    result = result - inv_v * iv2 / 360.0
    result = result + inv_v * iv2 * iv2 / 1260.0
    result - shift
}

// =============================================================================
// Binomial coefficients
// =============================================================================

// Exact integer binomial coefficient C(n, k) = n! / (k! * (n-k)!).
// Uses the multiplicative formula to avoid overflow as long as possible.
// For n, k >= 0.
fn binomial(n: i64, k: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if k < 0 || k > n { return 0 }
    if k == 0 || k == n { return 1 }
    // Use symmetry: C(n, k) = C(n, n-k)
    var kk = k
    if kk > n - kk { kk = n - kk }

    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < kk {
        result = result * (n - i)
        result = result / (i + 1)
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Generalized binomial coefficient for real arguments via lgamma.
// C(n, k) = Gamma(n+1) / (Gamma(k+1) * Gamma(n-k+1))
fn binomial_f64(n: f64, k: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if k < 0.0 || k > n { return 0.0 }
    comb_exp(comb_lgamma(n + 1.0) - comb_lgamma(k + 1.0) - comb_lgamma(n - k + 1.0))
}

// =============================================================================
// Falling / Rising factorials
// =============================================================================

// Falling factorial: (n)_k = n * (n-1) * ... * (n-k+1)
// Also known as Pochhammer symbol (in some conventions).
fn falling_factorial(n: i64, k: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if k <= 0 { return 1 }
    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < k {
        result = result * (n - (i as i64))
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Rising factorial (Pochhammer symbol): n^{(k)} = n * (n+1) * ... * (n+k-1)
fn rising_factorial(n: i64, k: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if k <= 0 { return 1 }
    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < k {
        result = result * (n + (i as i64))
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Stirling numbers
// =============================================================================

// Unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind |s(n, k)|.
// Number of permutations of n elements with exactly k disjoint cycles.
// Recurrence: |s(n, k)| = (n-1)*|s(n-1, k)| + |s(n-1, k-1)|
// Uses a DP table. Max n, k = 20.
fn stirling_first(n: i32, k: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 || k < 0 || k > n { return 0 }
    if n == 0 && k == 0 { return 1 }
    if n == 0 || k == 0 { return 0 }
    if k == n { return 1 }

    // DP: use two rows
    var prev: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    var curr: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    prev[0] = 1   // s(0, 0) = 1

    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        var j = 0
        while j <= 20 { curr[j] = 0; j = j + 1 }

        j = 1
        while j <= i {
            curr[j] = ((i - 1) as i64) * prev[j] + prev[j - 1]
            j = j + 1
        }
        // Copy curr to prev
        j = 0
        while j <= 20 { prev[j] = curr[j]; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    prev[k]
}

// Stirling numbers of the second kind S(n, k).
// Number of ways to partition n elements into k non-empty subsets.
// Recurrence: S(n, k) = k*S(n-1, k) + S(n-1, k-1)
// Max n, k = 20.
fn stirling_second(n: i32, k: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 || k < 0 || k > n { return 0 }
    if n == 0 && k == 0 { return 1 }
    if n == 0 || k == 0 { return 0 }
    if k == 1 || k == n { return 1 }

    var prev: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    var curr: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    prev[0] = 1

    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        var j = 0
        while j <= 20 { curr[j] = 0; j = j + 1 }

        j = 1
        while j <= i {
            curr[j] = (j as i64) * prev[j] + prev[j - 1]
            j = j + 1
        }
        j = 0
        while j <= 20 { prev[j] = curr[j]; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    prev[k]
}

// =============================================================================
// Named sequences
// =============================================================================

// Catalan number C_n = C(2n, n) / (n+1).
// Counts Dyck paths, valid parenthesizations, binary trees with n+1 leaves, etc.
fn catalan_number(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    if n <= 1 { return 1 }
    let b = binomial((2 * n) as i64, n as i64)
    b / ((n + 1) as i64)
}

// Bell number B_n = total partitions of an n-element set.
// Uses the Bell triangle. Max n = 25.
fn bell(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    if n <= 1 { return 1 }

    var row: [i64; 26] = [0; 26]
    row[0] = 1  // B_0

    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        // Bell triangle: row starts with last element of previous row
        var new_row: [i64; 26] = [0; 26]
        new_row[0] = row[i - 1]
        var j = 1
        while j <= i {
            new_row[j] = new_row[j - 1] + row[j - 1]
            j = j + 1
        }
        // Copy
        j = 0
        while j <= i { row[j] = new_row[j]; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    row[0]
}

// Partition function p(n) = number of integer partitions of n.
// Uses Euler's pentagonal number theorem recurrence:
//   p(n) = sum_{k!=0} (-1)^{k+1} * p(n - k*(3k-1)/2)
// Max n = 500.
fn partition_count(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    if n <= 1 { return 1 }

    var table: [i64; 501] = [0; 501]
    table[0] = 1

    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        var sum: i64 = 0
        var k = 1
        var done = false
        while !done {
            // Generalized pentagonal numbers: k*(3k-1)/2 and k*(3k+1)/2
            let pent1 = k * (3 * k - 1) / 2
            let pent2 = k * (3 * k + 1) / 2

            if pent1 > i { done = true }
            else {
                let sign: i64 = if k - (k / 2) * 2 == 1 { 1 } else { 0 - 1 }
                sum = sum + sign * table[i - pent1]
                if pent2 <= i {
                    sum = sum + sign * table[i - pent2]
                }
                k = k + 1
            }
        }
        table[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
    table[n]
}

// Derangement (subfactorial) !n = number of permutations with no fixed points.
// D(n) = (n-1) * (D(n-1) + D(n-2)), D(0) = 1, D(1) = 0.
fn derangements(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 { return 1 }
    if n == 1 { return 0 }
    if n == 2 { return 1 }

    var prev2: i64 = 1   // D(0)
    var prev1: i64 = 0   // D(1)
    var i = 2
    while i <= n {
        let current = ((i - 1) as i64) * (prev1 + prev2)
        prev2 = prev1
        prev1 = current
        i = i + 1
    }
    prev1
}

// Multinomial coefficient: (n1 + n2 + ... + nc)! / (n1! * n2! * ... * nc!)
// Input: array ks of length count.
fn multinomial(ks: &[i32; 16], count: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if count <= 0 { return 1 }

    var total: i64 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < count { total = total + (ks[i] as i64); i = i + 1 }

    var result: i64 = 1
    var running: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < count {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < ks[i] {
            running = running + 1
            result = result * running
            result = result / ((j + 1) as i64)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Harmonic numbers
// =============================================================================

// Harmonic number H_n = 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/n.
fn harmonic(n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 0 { return 0.0 }
    if n == 1 { return 1.0 }

    // For large n, use asymptotic: H_n ~ ln(n) + gamma + 1/(2n) - 1/(12n^2) + ...
    if n > 1000 {
        let nf = n as f64
        let gamma = 0.57721566490153286061
        return comb_ln(nf) + gamma + 1.0 / (2.0 * nf) - 1.0 / (12.0 * nf * nf) + 1.0 / (120.0 * nf * nf * nf * nf)
    }

    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        sum = sum + 1.0 / (i as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

// Generalized harmonic number H_{n, s} = sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k^s.
fn generalized_harmonic(n: i32, s: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 0 { return 0.0 }
    var sum = 0.0
    var k = 1
    while k <= n {
        let kf = k as f64
        // k^s = exp(s * ln(k))
        let term = if s == 1.0 { 1.0 / kf }
                   else if s == 2.0 { 1.0 / (kf * kf) }
                   else { 1.0 / comb_exp(s * comb_ln(kf)) }
        sum = sum + term
        k = k + 1
    }
    sum
}

// =============================================================================
// Bernoulli numbers
// =============================================================================

// Bernoulli number B_n via the Akiyama-Tanigawa algorithm.
// B_0=1, B_1=-1/2, B_2=1/6, B_3=0, B_4=-1/30, B_5=0, ...
// Odd B_n = 0 for n >= 3.
// Max n = 30.
fn bernoulli(n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0.0 }
    if n == 0 { return 1.0 }
    if n == 1 { return 0.0 - 0.5 }
    // Odd Bernoulli numbers (n >= 3) are 0
    if n >= 3 && n - (n / 2) * 2 == 1 { return 0.0 }

    // Akiyama-Tanigawa algorithm
    var a: [f64; 31] = [0.0; 31]
    var i = 0
    while i <= n {
        a[i] = 1.0 / ((i + 1) as f64)
        var j = i
        while j >= 1 {
            a[j - 1] = (j as f64) * (a[j - 1] - a[j])
            j = j - 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    a[0]
}

// =============================================================================
// Euler (zigzag) numbers
// =============================================================================

// Euler number E_n (also called secant/tangent numbers).
// E_0=1, E_1=0, E_2=-1, E_3=0, E_4=5, ...
// Related to sec(x) = sum E_{2n} * x^{2n} / (2n)!
// Uses the triangle method. Max n = 20.
fn euler_number(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    if n == 0 { return 1 }
    if n - (n / 2) * 2 == 1 { return 0 }

    // Compute via tangent/secant number triangle
    let m = n / 2

    var t: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    t[0] = 1  // E_0 = 1

    var i = 1
    while i <= m {
        // Build up using recurrence for secant numbers
        t[i] = 0
        var j = i
        while j >= 1 {
            t[j] = t[j - 1] * ((2 * (i - j) + 1) as i64) + t[j]
            j = j - 1
        }
        t[0] = 0
        j = 0
        while j < i {
            t[j] = t[j + 1]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Sign: (-1)^m
    let val = t[0]
    if m - (m / 2) * 2 == 0 { val } else { 0 - val }
}

// =============================================================================
// Double factorial
// =============================================================================

// Double factorial n!! = n * (n-2) * (n-4) * ... * (1 or 2).
fn double_factorial(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 0 { return 1 }
    if n <= 2 { return n as i64 }
    var result: i64 = 1
    var k = n
    while k > 1 {
        result = result * (k as i64)
        k = k - 2
    }
    result
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/combinatorics_perm.sio ===
// stdlib/math/combinatorics_perm.sio — In-place permutation generation
//
// Pure Sounio implementations of lexicographic permutation generation,
// permutation counting, and Fisher-Yates shuffle with MINSTD PRNG.
//
// Uses struct wrapper pattern for i64 array mutation (native compiler safe).
//
// References:
//   Knuth (2011): "The Art of Computer Programming" Vol. 4A, Section 7.2.1.2
//   Sedgewick (1977): "Permutation Generation Methods" Computing Surveys
//   Park & Miller (1988): "Random Number Generators: Good Ones Are Hard to Find"

// ============================================================================
// DATA STRUCTURE
// ============================================================================

struct Perm128 {
    data: [i64; 128]
}

// ============================================================================
// CORE PERMUTATION ALGORITHM
// ============================================================================

// Generates the next lexicographic permutation in-place.
// Returns true if a next permutation exists, false if already at last.
// Algorithm: find rightmost i where arr[i] < arr[i+1], find rightmost j
// where arr[j] > arr[i], swap, reverse suffix.
pub fn next_permutation(p: &!Perm128, n: i32) -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    // 1. Find largest i such that p.data[i] < p.data[i+1]
    var i = n - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        if p.data[i] < p.data[i + 1] {
            // Found the pivot
            // 2. Find largest j such that p.data[j] > p.data[i]
            var j = n - 1
            while p.data[j] <= p.data[i] {
                j = j - 1
            }

            // 3. Swap p.data[i] and p.data[j]
            let tmp = p.data[i]
            p.data[i] = p.data[j]
            p.data[j] = tmp

            // 4. Reverse suffix starting at p.data[i+1]
            var lo = i + 1
            var hi = n - 1
            while lo < hi {
                let t = p.data[lo]
                p.data[lo] = p.data[hi]
                p.data[hi] = t
                lo = lo + 1
                hi = hi - 1
            }
            return true
        }
        i = i - 1
    }
    // No pivot found => last permutation
    return false
}

// Count total permutations by iterating (for small n).
// Useful for testing: factorial(n) permutations expected.
pub fn count_permutations(n: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic {
    var p = Perm128 { data: [0; 128] }
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        p.data[i] = i as i64
        i = i + 1
    }
    var count: i32 = 1
    while next_permutation(&!p, n) {
        count = count + 1
    }
    count
}

// Fisher-Yates shuffle using MINSTD PRNG (Park-Miller).
// Shuffles first n elements of p.data in-place.
// Returns updated PRNG state.
pub fn shuffle_perm(p: &!Perm128, n: i32, seed: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var rng = seed
    var i = n - 1
    while i > 0 {
        // MINSTD: rng = (16807 * rng) mod 2^31-1
        let a: i64 = 16807
        let m: i64 = 2147483647
        let q: i64 = 127773
        let r_val: i64 = 2836
        let hi = rng / q
        let lo = rng - hi * q
        let t = a * lo - r_val * hi
        if t > 0 {
            rng = t
        } else {
            rng = t + m
        }

        // Map to range [0, i]
        var j_val = rng
        if j_val < 0 {
            j_val = 0 - j_val
        }
        j_val = j_val - (j_val / ((i as i64) + 1)) * ((i as i64) + 1)

        // Swap p.data[i] and p.data[j_val]
        let j_i32 = j_val as i32
        let tmp = p.data[i]
        p.data[i] = p.data[j_i32]
        p.data[j_i32] = tmp
        i = i - 1
    }
    rng
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/constants.sio ===
// stdlib/math/constants.sio — Extended mathematical constants
//
// Provides fundamental mathematical constants beyond PI and E.
// All values are given to full f64 precision (15-17 significant digits).
//
// References:
//   OEIS (https://oeis.org)
//   DLMF (https://dlmf.nist.gov)
//   Borwein & Bailey (2004): "Mathematics by Experiment"

// =============================================================================
// Circle constants
// =============================================================================

fn pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

// === FILE: stdlib/math/constrained.sio ===
// stdlib/math/constrained.sio — Constrained nonlinear optimization
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   L-BFGS (limited-memory quasi-Newton)
//   Projected gradient descent (box constraints)
//   Augmented Lagrangian method
//   Quadratic penalty method
//   Log-barrier interior point method
//   KKT violation checking
//
// References:
//   Nocedal & Wright (2006): "Numerical Optimization" Ch. 17-18
//   Bertsekas (1999): "Nonlinear Programming"
//   Boyd & Vandenberghe (2004): "Convex Optimization" Ch. 11

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (co_ prefix, self-contained)
// =============================================================================

fn co_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn co_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn co_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn co_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// exp(x) via Taylor series with Div, Mut, Panic, range reduction
fn co_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 700.0 { return 1.0e308 }
    if x < -700.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = x / ln2
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f - 1.0) as i32 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 30 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    var j = 0
    if k >= 0 {
        while j < k { result = result * 2.0; j = j + 1 }
    } else {
        var neg_k = 0 - k
        while j < neg_k { result = result * 0.5; j = j + 1 }
    }
    result
}

// ln(x) via series with Div, Mut, Panic, range reduction
fn co_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e308 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var m = x
    var k: i32 = 0
    while m > 2.0 { m = m * 0.5; k = k + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; k = k - 1 }
    let u = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let u2 = u * u
    var sum = u
    var term = u
    var n = 1
    while n < 40 {
        term = term * u2
        sum = sum + term / (2.0 * (n as f64) + 1.0)
        n = n + 1
    }
    2.0 * sum + (k as f64) * ln2
}

// =============================================================================
// Vector helpers (fixed-size [f64; 64])
// =============================================================================

fn co_dot(a: &[f64; 64], b: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n { s = s + a[i] * b[i]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

fn co_norm2(a: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n { s = s + a[i] * a[i]; i = i + 1 }
    co_sqrt(s)
}

fn co_norminf(a: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var mx = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let v = co_abs(a[i])
        if v > mx { mx = v }
        i = i + 1
    }
    mx
}

fn co_copy(src: &[f64; 64], dst: &![f64; 64], n: i32) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < n { dst[i] = src[i]; i = i + 1 }
}

fn co_axpy(alpha: f64, x: &[f64; 64], dst: &![f64; 64], n: i32) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < n { dst[i] = dst[i] + alpha * x[i]; i = i + 1 }
}

fn co_scale(dst: &![f64; 64], alpha: f64, n: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < n { dst[i] = dst[i] * alpha; i = i + 1 }
}

fn co_zero(dst: &![f64; 64], n: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < n { dst[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
}

// =============================================================================
// Structs
// =============================================================================

struct ConstrainedConfig {
    max_iter: i32,
    tol_opt: f64,
    tol_feas: f64,
    mu_init: f64,
    mu_max: f64,
    rho: f64
}

struct ConstrainedResult {
    x: [f64; 64],
    obj_val: f64,
    constraint_viol: f64,
    iterations: i32,
    converged: bool,
    n_dim: i32
}

struct LBFGSState {
    s_store: [f64; 4096],
    y_store: [f64; 4096],
    rho_store: [f64; 64],
    m: i32,
    n: i32,
    count: i32
}

// =============================================================================
// Numerical gradient (central differences)
// =============================================================================

fn co_numerical_grad(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                     x: &[f64; 64], n: i32,
                     grad: &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var xp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var xm: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    let cbrt_eps = 6.0554544523933429e-6
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n { xp[j] = x[j]; xm[j] = x[j]; j = j + 1 }
        let h = cbrt_eps * co_max(co_abs(x[i]), 1.0)
        xp[i] = x[i] + h
        xm[i] = x[i] - h
        grad[i] = (f(&xp, n) - f(&xm, n)) / (2.0 * h)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Armijo backtracking line search
// =============================================================================

// f(x + alpha*dir) <= f(x) + c1*alpha*grad'*dir, c1=1e-4, shrink by 0.5
fn co_armijo_search(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    x: &[f64; 64], dir: &[f64; 64], grad: &[f64; 64],
                    n: i32, alpha_init: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let c1 = 1.0e-4
    let min_alpha = 1.0e-16
    let f0 = f(x, n)
    let dg = co_dot(grad, dir, n)
    if dg >= 0.0 { return min_alpha }
    var alpha = alpha_init
    var trial: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var iter = 0
    while iter < 40 {
        var i = 0
        while i < n { trial[i] = x[i] + alpha * dir[i]; i = i + 1 }
        let f_trial = f(&trial, n)
        if f_trial <= f0 + c1 * alpha * dg { return alpha }
        alpha = alpha * 0.5
        if alpha < min_alpha { return min_alpha }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    alpha
}

// =============================================================================
// L-BFGS: Limited-memory BFGS (inner solver)
// =============================================================================

fn lbfgs_init(state: &!LBFGSState, n: i32, m: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    state.n = n
    state.m = m
    state.count = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < 4096 { state.s_store[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    i = 0
    while i < 4096 { state.y_store[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    i = 0
    while i < 64 { state.rho_store[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
}

// Store curvature pair s = x_{k+1} - x_k, y = g_{k+1} - g_k (circular buffer)
fn lbfgs_update(state: &!LBFGSState, s: &[f64; 64], y: &[f64; 64]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let n = state.n
    let m = state.m
    let slot = state.count - (state.count / m) * m
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        state.s_store[slot * n + i] = s[i]
        state.y_store[slot * n + i] = y[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    var ys = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n { ys = ys + y[i] * s[i]; i = i + 1 }
    if co_abs(ys) < 1.0e-30 { ys = 1.0e-30 }
    state.rho_store[slot] = 1.0 / ys
    state.count = state.count + 1
}

// Two-loop recursion (Nocedal Algorithm 7.4): dir = -H_k * grad
fn lbfgs_direction(state: &LBFGSState, grad: &[f64; 64], dir: &![f64; 64]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let n = state.n
    let m = state.m
    let k = state.count
    var bound = k
    if bound > m { bound = m }

    var q: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < n { q[i] = grad[i]; i = i + 1 }

    var alpha: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // First loop: most recent to oldest
    var idx = 0
    while idx < bound {
        let raw = k - 1 - idx
        var slot = raw - (raw / m) * m
        if slot < 0 { slot = slot + m }
        var stq = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n { stq = stq + state.s_store[slot * n + i] * q[i]; i = i + 1 }
        alpha[idx] = state.rho_store[slot] * stq
        i = 0
        while i < n { q[i] = q[i] - alpha[idx] * state.y_store[slot * n + i]; i = i + 1 }
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    // Initial Hessian scaling: gamma = s_{k-1}^T y_{k-1} / y_{k-1}^T y_{k-1}
    var gamma = 1.0
    if bound > 0 {
        let nraw = k - 1
        var nslot = nraw - (nraw / m) * m
        if nslot < 0 { nslot = nslot + m }
        var sy = 0.0
        var yy = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            sy = sy + state.s_store[nslot * n + i] * state.y_store[nslot * n + i]
            yy = yy + state.y_store[nslot * n + i] * state.y_store[nslot * n + i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        if co_abs(yy) > 1.0e-30 { gamma = sy / yy }
    }

    var r: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    i = 0
    while i < n { r[i] = gamma * q[i]; i = i + 1 }

    // Second loop: oldest to most recent
    idx = bound - 1
    while idx >= 0 {
        let raw2 = k - 1 - idx
        var slot2 = raw2 - (raw2 / m) * m
        if slot2 < 0 { slot2 = slot2 + m }
        var ytr = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n { ytr = ytr + state.y_store[slot2 * n + i] * r[i]; i = i + 1 }
        let beta = state.rho_store[slot2] * ytr
        i = 0
        while i < n { r[i] = r[i] + (alpha[idx] - beta) * state.s_store[slot2 * n + i]; i = i + 1 }
        idx = idx - 1
    }

    i = 0
    while i < n { dir[i] = 0.0 - r[i]; i = i + 1 }
}

// Full L-BFGS minimization. Memory depth m=7, convergence on ||grad||_inf < tol.
fn lbfgs_minimize(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                  grad_f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                  x0: &[f64; 64], n: i32, max_iter: i32, tol: f64,
                  result: &!ConstrainedResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state: LBFGSState = LBFGSState {
        s_store: [0.0; 4096], y_store: [0.0; 4096],
        rho_store: [0.0; 64], m: 0, n: 0, count: 0
    }
    lbfgs_init(&!state, n, 7)

    var x: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    co_copy(x0, &!x, n)
    var grad: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var grad_prev: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var dir: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var x_prev: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var s_vec: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var y_vec: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    grad_f(&x, n, &!grad)
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        // Copy grad to avoid shared+mutable borrow conflict in loop body
        var grad_tmp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var gi = 0
        while gi < n { grad_tmp[gi] = grad[gi]; gi = gi + 1 }
        let gnorm = co_norminf(&grad_tmp, n)
        if gnorm < tol {
            co_copy(&x, &!result.x, n)
            result.obj_val = f(&x, n)
            result.constraint_viol = 0.0
            result.iterations = iter
            result.converged = true
            result.n_dim = n
            return
        }
        co_copy(&x, &!x_prev, n)
        co_copy(&grad, &!grad_prev, n)

        if iter == 0 {
            var i = 0
            while i < n { dir[i] = 0.0 - grad[i]; i = i + 1 }
        } else {
            lbfgs_direction(&state, &grad_tmp, &!dir)
        }

        let alpha = co_armijo_search(f, &x, &dir, &grad_tmp, n, 1.0)
        var i = 0
        while i < n { x[i] = x[i] + alpha * dir[i]; i = i + 1 }
        grad_f(&x, n, &!grad)

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            s_vec[i] = x[i] - x_prev[i]
            y_vec[i] = grad[i] - grad_prev[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        let sy = co_dot(&s_vec, &y_vec, n)
        if sy > 1.0e-16 { lbfgs_update(&!state, &s_vec, &y_vec) }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    co_copy(&x, &!result.x, n)
    result.obj_val = f(&x, n)
    result.constraint_viol = 0.0
    result.iterations = iter
    result.converged = false
    result.n_dim = n
}

// =============================================================================
// Box-constrained optimization
// =============================================================================

// Project x[i] = clamp(x[i], lower[i], upper[i])
fn box_project(x: &![f64; 64], lower: &[f64; 64], upper: &[f64; 64], n: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if x[i] < lower[i] { x[i] = lower[i] }
        if x[i] > upper[i] { x[i] = upper[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Projected gradient descent with Div, Mut, Panic, Armijo line search on projected iterates.
// Converges when ||project(x - grad) - x||_inf < tol.
fn projected_gradient(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                      grad_f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                      x0: &[f64; 64], lower: &[f64; 64], upper: &[f64; 64],
                      n: i32, max_iter: i32, tol: f64,
                      result: &!ConstrainedResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    co_copy(x0, &!x, n)
    box_project(&!x, lower, upper, n)

    var grad: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var x_trial: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var proj_test: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        grad_f(&x, n, &!grad)

        // Optimality: ||project(x - grad) - x||_inf
        var i = 0
        while i < n { proj_test[i] = x[i] - grad[i]; i = i + 1 }
        box_project(&!proj_test, lower, upper, n)
        var opt_viol = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            let diff = co_abs(proj_test[i] - x[i])
            if diff > opt_viol { opt_viol = diff }
            i = i + 1
        }
        if opt_viol < tol {
            co_copy(&x, &!result.x, n)
            result.obj_val = f(&x, n)
            result.constraint_viol = 0.0
            result.iterations = iter
            result.converged = true
            result.n_dim = n
            return
        }

        // Projected Armijo backtracking
        // Copy x for f evaluation to avoid shared+mutable borrow conflict
        var x_for_f: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        i = 0
        while i < n { x_for_f[i] = x[i]; i = i + 1 }
        let f0 = f(&x_for_f, n)
        var alpha = 1.0
        let c1 = 1.0e-4
        var ls_iter = 0
        while ls_iter < 30 {
            i = 0
            while i < n { x_trial[i] = x[i] - alpha * grad[i]; i = i + 1 }
            box_project(&!x_trial, lower, upper, n)
            let f_trial = f(&x_trial, n)
            var descent = 0.0
            i = 0
            while i < n { descent = descent + grad[i] * (x_trial[i] - x[i]); i = i + 1 }
            if f_trial <= f0 + c1 * descent {
                // Manual copy x_trial -> x to avoid co_copy borrow conflict
                var ci = 0
                while ci < n { x[ci] = x_trial[ci]; ci = ci + 1 }
                ls_iter = 30
            } else {
                alpha = alpha * 0.5
                if alpha < 1.0e-16 {
                    var ci = 0
                    while ci < n { x[ci] = x_trial[ci]; ci = ci + 1 }
                    ls_iter = 30
                } else {
                    ls_iter = ls_iter + 1
                }
            }
        }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    co_copy(&x, &!result.x, n)
    result.obj_val = f(&x, n)
    result.constraint_viol = 0.0
    result.iterations = iter
    result.converged = false
    result.n_dim = n
}

// =============================================================================
// Augmented Lagrangian: helper functions (MUST precede auglag_minimize)
// =============================================================================

// Evaluate augmented Lagrangian objective:
//   L_A = f(x) + sum_i (lambda_eq_i * ceq_i + (mu/2) * ceq_i^2)
//       + sum_j (1/(2*mu)) * (max(0, lambda_ineq_j + mu*cineq_j)^2 - lambda_ineq_j^2)
fn auglag_eval_obj(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   c_eq: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   n_eq: i32,
                   c_ineq: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   n_ineq: i32,
                   x: &[f64; 64], n: i32,
                   lambda_eq: &[f64; 64], lambda_ineq: &[f64; 64],
                   mu: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var val = f(x, n)
    if n_eq > 0 {
        var ceq: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        c_eq(x, n, &!ceq, n_eq)
        var i = 0
        while i < n_eq {
            val = val + lambda_eq[i] * ceq[i] + 0.5 * mu * ceq[i] * ceq[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    // Inequality: Powell-Hestenes-Rockafellar formulation
    if n_ineq > 0 {
        var cineq: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        c_ineq(x, n, &!cineq, n_ineq)
        var j = 0
        while j < n_ineq {
            let shifted = lambda_ineq[j] + mu * cineq[j]
            if shifted > 0.0 {
                val = val + (shifted * shifted - lambda_ineq[j] * lambda_ineq[j]) / (2.0 * mu)
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }
    val
}

// Backtracking line search on augmented Lagrangian objective.
fn auglag_line_search(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                      c_eq: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                      n_eq: i32,
                      c_ineq: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                      n_ineq: i32,
                      x: &[f64; 64], dir: &[f64; 64], grad: &[f64; 64],
                      n: i32,
                      lambda_eq: &[f64; 64], lambda_ineq: &[f64; 64],
                      mu: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let c1 = 1.0e-4
    let min_alpha = 1.0e-16
    let f0 = auglag_eval_obj(f, c_eq, n_eq, c_ineq, n_ineq, x, n,
                             lambda_eq, lambda_ineq, mu)
    let dg = co_dot(grad, dir, n)
    if dg >= 0.0 { return min_alpha }
    var alpha = 1.0
    var trial: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var iter = 0
    while iter < 30 {
        var i = 0
        while i < n { trial[i] = x[i] + alpha * dir[i]; i = i + 1 }
        let f_trial = auglag_eval_obj(f, c_eq, n_eq, c_ineq, n_ineq, &trial, n,
                                      lambda_eq, lambda_ineq, mu)
        if f_trial <= f0 + c1 * alpha * dg { return alpha }
        alpha = alpha * 0.5
        if alpha < min_alpha { return min_alpha }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    alpha
}

// =============================================================================
// Augmented Lagrangian method
// =============================================================================

// Solves: min f(x) s.t. c_eq(x)=0, c_ineq(x)<=0
// Outer loop: update multipliers lambda, increase penalty mu.
// Inner loop: L-BFGS on augmented Lagrangian with Div, Mut, Panic, numerical gradients.
fn auglag_minimize(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   grad_f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   c_eq: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   n_eq: i32,
                   c_ineq: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   n_ineq: i32,
                   x0: &[f64; 64], n: i32,
                   config: &ConstrainedConfig,
                   result: &!ConstrainedResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    co_copy(x0, &!x, n)
    var lambda_eq: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var lambda_ineq: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var mu = config.mu_init
    var ceq_val: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var cineq_val: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var outer = 0
    while outer < config.max_iter {
        // Evaluate constraints and check feasibility
        if n_eq > 0 { c_eq(&x, n, &!ceq_val, n_eq) }
        if n_ineq > 0 { c_ineq(&x, n, &!cineq_val, n_ineq) }
        var feas_viol = 0.0
        var i = 0
        while i < n_eq {
            let v = co_abs(ceq_val[i])
            if v > feas_viol { feas_viol = v }
            i = i + 1
        }
        i = 0
        while i < n_ineq {
            if cineq_val[i] > 0.0 {
                if cineq_val[i] > feas_viol { feas_viol = cineq_val[i] }
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        if feas_viol < config.tol_feas {
            var grad_L: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
            grad_f(&x, n, &!grad_L)
            let gnorm = co_norminf(&grad_L, n)
            if gnorm < config.tol_opt {
                co_copy(&x, &!result.x, n)
                result.obj_val = f(&x, n)
                result.constraint_viol = feas_viol
                result.iterations = outer
                result.converged = true
                result.n_dim = n
                return
            }
        }

        // Inner L-BFGS solve on augmented Lagrangian
        var istate: LBFGSState = LBFGSState {
            s_store: [0.0; 4096], y_store: [0.0; 4096],
            rho_store: [0.0; 64], m: 0, n: 0, count: 0
        }
        lbfgs_init(&!istate, n, 7)
        var grad_aug: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var grad_aug_prev: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var dir_aug: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var x_prev: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var s_in: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var y_in: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var xp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var xm: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        let cbrt_eps = 6.0554544523933429e-6

        var inner = 0
        while inner < 50 {
            // Numerical gradient of augmented Lagrangian
            var gi = 0
            while gi < n {
                var j = 0
                while j < n { xp[j] = x[j]; xm[j] = x[j]; j = j + 1 }
                let h = cbrt_eps * co_max(co_abs(x[gi]), 1.0)
                xp[gi] = x[gi] + h
                xm[gi] = x[gi] - h
                let fp = auglag_eval_obj(f, c_eq, n_eq, c_ineq, n_ineq,
                                         &xp, n, &lambda_eq, &lambda_ineq, mu)
                let fm = auglag_eval_obj(f, c_eq, n_eq, c_ineq, n_ineq,
                                         &xm, n, &lambda_eq, &lambda_ineq, mu)
                grad_aug[gi] = (fp - fm) / (2.0 * h)
                gi = gi + 1
            }
            let gnorm_in = co_norminf(&grad_aug, n)
            if gnorm_in < config.tol_opt * 10.0 {
                inner = 50
            } else {
                co_copy(&x, &!x_prev, n)
                co_copy(&grad_aug, &!grad_aug_prev, n)
                if inner == 0 {
                    var di = 0
                    while di < n { dir_aug[di] = 0.0 - grad_aug[di]; di = di + 1 }
                } else {
                    lbfgs_direction(&istate, &grad_aug, &!dir_aug)
                }
                let a_aug = auglag_line_search(f, c_eq, n_eq, c_ineq, n_ineq,
                                               &x, &dir_aug, &grad_aug,
                                               n, &lambda_eq, &lambda_ineq, mu)
                var ui = 0
                while ui < n { x[ui] = x[ui] + a_aug * dir_aug[ui]; ui = ui + 1 }

                // Recompute gradient for L-BFGS update
                gi = 0
                while gi < n {
                    var j = 0
                    while j < n { xp[j] = x[j]; xm[j] = x[j]; j = j + 1 }
                    let h = cbrt_eps * co_max(co_abs(x[gi]), 1.0)
                    xp[gi] = x[gi] + h
                    xm[gi] = x[gi] - h
                    let fp2 = auglag_eval_obj(f, c_eq, n_eq, c_ineq, n_ineq,
                                              &xp, n, &lambda_eq, &lambda_ineq, mu)
                    let fm2 = auglag_eval_obj(f, c_eq, n_eq, c_ineq, n_ineq,
                                              &xm, n, &lambda_eq, &lambda_ineq, mu)
                    grad_aug[gi] = (fp2 - fm2) / (2.0 * h)
                    gi = gi + 1
                }
                var si = 0
                while si < n {
                    s_in[si] = x[si] - x_prev[si]
                    y_in[si] = grad_aug[si] - grad_aug_prev[si]
                    si = si + 1
                }
                let sy_in = co_dot(&s_in, &y_in, n)
                if sy_in > 1.0e-16 { lbfgs_update(&!istate, &s_in, &y_in) }
                inner = inner + 1
            }
        }

        // Update multipliers
        if n_eq > 0 { c_eq(&x, n, &!ceq_val, n_eq) }
        if n_ineq > 0 { c_ineq(&x, n, &!cineq_val, n_ineq) }
        i = 0
        while i < n_eq { lambda_eq[i] = lambda_eq[i] + mu * ceq_val[i]; i = i + 1 }
        i = 0
        while i < n_ineq {
            let cand = lambda_ineq[i] + mu * cineq_val[i]
            if cand > 0.0 { lambda_ineq[i] = cand } else { lambda_ineq[i] = 0.0 }
            i = i + 1
        }
        mu = mu * config.rho
        if mu > config.mu_max { mu = config.mu_max }
        outer = outer + 1
    }

    // Did not converge
    if n_eq > 0 { c_eq(&x, n, &!ceq_val, n_eq) }
    if n_ineq > 0 { c_ineq(&x, n, &!cineq_val, n_ineq) }
    var fv = 0.0
    var vi = 0
    while vi < n_eq {
        let v = co_abs(ceq_val[vi])
        if v > fv { fv = v }
        vi = vi + 1
    }
    vi = 0
    while vi < n_ineq {
        if cineq_val[vi] > 0.0 { if cineq_val[vi] > fv { fv = cineq_val[vi] } }
        vi = vi + 1
    }
    co_copy(&x, &!result.x, n)
    result.obj_val = f(&x, n)
    result.constraint_viol = fv
    result.iterations = outer
    result.converged = false
    result.n_dim = n
}

// =============================================================================
// Penalty method: helper functions (MUST precede penalty_minimize)
// =============================================================================

// Evaluate penalized objective: f(x) + (mu/2) * ||c(x)||^2
fn penalty_eval_obj(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    c: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    n_c: i32,
                    x: &[f64; 64], n: i32,
                    mu: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var val = f(x, n)
    var c_val: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    c(x, n, &!c_val, n_c)
    var penalty = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n_c { penalty = penalty + c_val[i] * c_val[i]; i = i + 1 }
    val + 0.5 * mu * penalty
}

// Backtracking line search on penalized objective
fn penalty_line_search(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                       c: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                       n_c: i32,
                       x: &[f64; 64], dir: &[f64; 64], grad: &[f64; 64],
                       n: i32, mu: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let c1 = 1.0e-4
    let min_alpha = 1.0e-16
    let f0 = penalty_eval_obj(f, c, n_c, x, n, mu)
    let dg = co_dot(grad, dir, n)
    if dg >= 0.0 { return min_alpha }
    var alpha = 1.0
    var trial: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var iter = 0
    while iter < 30 {
        var i = 0
        while i < n { trial[i] = x[i] + alpha * dir[i]; i = i + 1 }
        let f_trial = penalty_eval_obj(f, c, n_c, &trial, n, mu)
        if f_trial <= f0 + c1 * alpha * dg { return alpha }
        alpha = alpha * 0.5
        if alpha < min_alpha { return min_alpha }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    alpha
}

// =============================================================================
// Quadratic penalty method
// =============================================================================

// Quadratic penalty: min f(x) + (mu/2)*||c(x)||^2, increase mu by rho each outer iter.
fn penalty_minimize(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    grad_f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    c: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    n_c: i32,
                    x0: &[f64; 64], n: i32,
                    config: &ConstrainedConfig,
                    result: &!ConstrainedResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    co_copy(x0, &!x, n)
    var mu = config.mu_init
    var c_val: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var outer = 0
    while outer < config.max_iter {
        // Inner L-BFGS on penalized objective
        var istate: LBFGSState = LBFGSState {
            s_store: [0.0; 4096], y_store: [0.0; 4096],
            rho_store: [0.0; 64], m: 0, n: 0, count: 0
        }
        lbfgs_init(&!istate, n, 7)
        var gp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var gp_prev: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var dp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var xprev: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var sp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var yp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var xpp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var xmm: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        let cbrt_eps = 6.0554544523933429e-6

        var inner = 0
        while inner < 50 {
            var gi = 0
            while gi < n {
                var j = 0
                while j < n { xpp[j] = x[j]; xmm[j] = x[j]; j = j + 1 }
                let h = cbrt_eps * co_max(co_abs(x[gi]), 1.0)
                xpp[gi] = x[gi] + h
                xmm[gi] = x[gi] - h
                let fp = penalty_eval_obj(f, c, n_c, &xpp, n, mu)
                let fm = penalty_eval_obj(f, c, n_c, &xmm, n, mu)
                gp[gi] = (fp - fm) / (2.0 * h)
                gi = gi + 1
            }
            let gnorm = co_norminf(&gp, n)
            if gnorm < config.tol_opt * 10.0 {
                inner = 50
            } else {
                co_copy(&x, &!xprev, n)
                co_copy(&gp, &!gp_prev, n)
                if inner == 0 {
                    var di = 0
                    while di < n { dp[di] = 0.0 - gp[di]; di = di + 1 }
                } else {
                    lbfgs_direction(&istate, &gp, &!dp)
                }
                let ap = penalty_line_search(f, c, n_c, &x, &dp, &gp, n, mu)
                var ui = 0
                while ui < n { x[ui] = x[ui] + ap * dp[ui]; ui = ui + 1 }

                // Recompute gradient for L-BFGS
                gi = 0
                while gi < n {
                    var j = 0
                    while j < n { xpp[j] = x[j]; xmm[j] = x[j]; j = j + 1 }
                    let h = cbrt_eps * co_max(co_abs(x[gi]), 1.0)
                    xpp[gi] = x[gi] + h
                    xmm[gi] = x[gi] - h
                    let fp2 = penalty_eval_obj(f, c, n_c, &xpp, n, mu)
                    let fm2 = penalty_eval_obj(f, c, n_c, &xmm, n, mu)
                    gp[gi] = (fp2 - fm2) / (2.0 * h)
                    gi = gi + 1
                }
                var si = 0
                while si < n {
                    sp[si] = x[si] - xprev[si]
                    yp[si] = gp[si] - gp_prev[si]
                    si = si + 1
                }
                let syp = co_dot(&sp, &yp, n)
                if syp > 1.0e-16 { lbfgs_update(&!istate, &sp, &yp) }
                inner = inner + 1
            }
        }

        // Check feasibility
        c(&x, n, &!c_val, n_c)
        var fv = 0.0
        var vi = 0
        while vi < n_c {
            let v = co_abs(c_val[vi])
            if v > fv { fv = v }
            vi = vi + 1
        }
        if fv < config.tol_feas {
            co_copy(&x, &!result.x, n)
            result.obj_val = f(&x, n)
            result.constraint_viol = fv
            result.iterations = outer
            result.converged = true
            result.n_dim = n
            return
        }
        mu = mu * config.rho
        if mu > config.mu_max { mu = config.mu_max }
        outer = outer + 1
    }

    c(&x, n, &!c_val, n_c)
    var fv = 0.0
    var vi = 0
    while vi < n_c {
        let v = co_abs(c_val[vi])
        if v > fv { fv = v }
        vi = vi + 1
    }
    co_copy(&x, &!result.x, n)
    result.obj_val = f(&x, n)
    result.constraint_viol = fv
    result.iterations = outer
    result.converged = false
    result.n_dim = n
}

// =============================================================================
// Barrier method: helper functions (MUST precede barrier_minimize)
// =============================================================================

// Evaluate barrier objective: f(x) - (1/t) * sum_j ln(-c_ineq_j(x))
// Returns 1e308 if any constraint is non-negative (infeasible).
fn barrier_eval_obj(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    c_ineq: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    n_ineq: i32,
                    x: &[f64; 64], n: i32,
                    t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var val = f(x, n)
    var cineq: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    c_ineq(x, n, &!cineq, n_ineq)
    var j = 0
    while j < n_ineq {
        if cineq[j] >= 0.0 { return 1.0e308 }
        val = val - co_ln(0.0 - cineq[j]) / t
        j = j + 1
    }
    val
}

// Backtracking line search for barrier method with Div, Mut, Panic, feasibility enforcement.
fn barrier_line_search(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                       c_ineq: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                       n_ineq: i32,
                       x: &[f64; 64], dir: &[f64; 64], grad: &[f64; 64],
                       n: i32, t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let c1 = 1.0e-4
    let min_alpha = 1.0e-16
    let f0 = barrier_eval_obj(f, c_ineq, n_ineq, x, n, t)
    let dg = co_dot(grad, dir, n)
    if dg >= 0.0 { return min_alpha }
    var alpha = 1.0
    var trial: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var ct: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var iter = 0
    while iter < 40 {
        var i = 0
        while i < n { trial[i] = x[i] + alpha * dir[i]; i = i + 1 }
        // Check feasibility
        c_ineq(&trial, n, &!ct, n_ineq)
        var feasible = true
        i = 0
        while i < n_ineq {
            if ct[i] >= 0.0 { feasible = false }
            i = i + 1
        }
        if feasible {
            let f_trial = barrier_eval_obj(f, c_ineq, n_ineq, &trial, n, t)
            if f_trial <= f0 + c1 * alpha * dg { return alpha }
        }
        alpha = alpha * 0.5
        if alpha < min_alpha { return min_alpha }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    alpha
}

// =============================================================================
// Log-barrier interior point method
// =============================================================================

// Interior point: min f(x) - (1/t)*sum_j ln(-c_ineq_j(x))
// Requires strictly feasible x0 (all c_ineq_j(x0) < 0).
// Increases t by rho each outer iteration.
fn barrier_minimize(f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    grad_f: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    c_ineq: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    n_ineq: i32,
                    x0: &[f64; 64], n: i32,
                    config: &ConstrainedConfig,
                    result: &!ConstrainedResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    co_copy(x0, &!x, n)
    var t = 1.0
    var cv: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // Verify initial strict feasibility
    c_ineq(&x, n, &!cv, n_ineq)
    var i = 0
    while i < n_ineq {
        if cv[i] >= 0.0 {
            co_copy(x0, &!result.x, n)
            result.obj_val = f(x0, n)
            result.constraint_viol = 1.0e30
            result.iterations = 0
            result.converged = false
            result.n_dim = n
            return
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var outer = 0
    while outer < config.max_iter {
        // Inner L-BFGS on barrier objective
        var istate: LBFGSState = LBFGSState {
            s_store: [0.0; 4096], y_store: [0.0; 4096],
            rho_store: [0.0; 64], m: 0, n: 0, count: 0
        }
        lbfgs_init(&!istate, n, 7)
        var gb: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var gb_prev: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var db: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var xprev: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var sb: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var yb: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var xpp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        var xmm: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        let cbrt_eps = 6.0554544523933429e-6

        var inner = 0
        while inner < 80 {
            // Gradient via central differences
            var gi = 0
            while gi < n {
                var j = 0
                while j < n { xpp[j] = x[j]; xmm[j] = x[j]; j = j + 1 }
                let h = cbrt_eps * co_max(co_abs(x[gi]), 1.0)
                xpp[gi] = x[gi] + h
                xmm[gi] = x[gi] - h
                let fp = barrier_eval_obj(f, c_ineq, n_ineq, &xpp, n, t)
                let fm = barrier_eval_obj(f, c_ineq, n_ineq, &xmm, n, t)
                let diff = fp - fm
                if co_abs(diff) < 1.0e300 {
                    gb[gi] = diff / (2.0 * h)
