    // Extract grade 0
    let g0 = ga_grade_select(mv, 0)
    let g0_ok = ga_approx_eq(g0.coeffs[0 as usize], 3.0)
    // Extract grade 1
    let g1 = ga_grade_select(mv, 1)
    let g1_ok = ga_approx_eq(g1.coeffs[1 as usize], 1.0) && ga_approx_eq(g1.coeffs[2 as usize], 1.0)
    g0_ok && g1_ok
}

// Test 14: Geometric product of vectors gives scalar + bivector
// (ae1 + be2) * (ce1 + de2) = ac*e1e1 + ad*e1e2 + bc*e2e1 + bd*e2e2
//                            = (ac + bd)*1 + (ad - bc)*e12
fn test_vector_product_components() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    // v1 = 2*e1 + 3*e2
    var v1 = ga_zero()
    v1.coeffs[1 as usize] = 2.0
    v1.coeffs[2 as usize] = 3.0
    // v2 = 4*e1 + 5*e2
    var v2 = ga_zero()
    v2.coeffs[1 as usize] = 4.0
    v2.coeffs[2 as usize] = 5.0
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, v1, v2)
    // scalar part = 2*4 + 3*5 = 8 + 15 = 23
    let scalar_ok = ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 23.0)
    // bivector e12 part = 2*5 - 3*4 = 10 - 12 = -2
    let bv_ok = ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[3 as usize], 0.0 - 2.0)
    scalar_ok && bv_ok
}

// Test 15: Degenerate metric — e0^2 = 0 in PGA
fn test_degenerate_pga() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_pga3d()  // Cl(3,0,1): e1^2=1, e2^2=1, e3^2=1, e4^2=0
    // e4 is the degenerate basis vector (index 3, bitmap 8 = 2^3)
    let e4 = ga_basis(8)   // bitmap 0b1000
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, e4, e4)
    // e4^2 = 0
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0)
}

// Test 16: Popcount correctness
fn test_popcount() -> bool {
    ga_popcount(0) == 0 &&
    ga_popcount(1) == 1 &&
    ga_popcount(3) == 2 &&
    ga_popcount(7) == 3 &&
    ga_popcount(15) == 4 &&
    ga_popcount(31) == 5
}

// Test 17: Algebra dimensions
fn test_algebra_dim() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig3 = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let sig4 = ga_sig_pga3d()
    let sig5 = ga_sig_cga()
    ga_dim(sig3) == 3 && ga_algebra_dim(sig3) == 8 &&
    ga_dim(sig4) == 4 && ga_algebra_dim(sig4) == 16 &&
    ga_dim(sig5) == 5 && ga_algebra_dim(sig5) == 32
}

// Test 18: Add and subtract
fn test_add_sub() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let a = ga_scalar(5.0)
    let b = ga_scalar(3.0)
    let sum = ga_add(a, b)
    let diff = ga_sub(a, b)
    ga_approx_eq(sum.coeffs[0 as usize], 8.0) && ga_approx_eq(diff.coeffs[0 as usize], 2.0)
}

// Test 19: Scale
fn test_scale() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let scaled = ga_scale(e1, 7.0)
    ga_approx_eq(scaled.coeffs[1 as usize], 7.0)
}

// Test 20: Quaternion i^2 = j^2 = k^2 = -1
fn test_quaternion_squares() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_quaternion()
    let i_q = ga_basis(1)
    let j_q = ga_basis(2)
    let k_q = ga_basis(3)

    let i2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, i_q, i_q)
    let j2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, j_q, j_q)
    let k2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, k_q, k_q)

    // i^2 = e1^2 = -1
    let i2_ok = ga_approx_eq(i2.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)
    // j^2 = e2^2 = -1
    let j2_ok = ga_approx_eq(j2.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)
    // k^2 = e12^2 = e1*e2*e1*e2 = -e1*e1*e2*e2 = -(-1)(-1) = -1
    let k2_ok = ga_approx_eq(k2.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)

    i2_ok && j2_ok && k2_ok
}


// == Quaternion module: Cl(0,2) specialization ==

fn quat_sig() -> AlgebraSignature {
    ga_sig_quaternion()
}

fn quat_new(w: f64, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var mv = ga_zero()
    mv.coeffs[0 as usize] = w
    mv.coeffs[1 as usize] = x
    mv.coeffs[2 as usize] = y
    mv.coeffs[3 as usize] = z
    mv
}

fn quat_w(q: Multivector) -> f64 { ga_get(q, 0) }
fn quat_x(q: Multivector) -> f64 { ga_get(q, 1) }
fn quat_y(q: Multivector) -> f64 { ga_get(q, 2) }
fn quat_z(q: Multivector) -> f64 { ga_get(q, 3) }

fn quat_mul(a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = quat_sig()
    ga_geometric_product(sig, a, b)
}

fn quat_conjugate(q: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    result.coeffs[0 as usize] = quat_w(q)
    result.coeffs[1 as usize] = 0.0 - quat_x(q)
    result.coeffs[2 as usize] = 0.0 - quat_y(q)
    result.coeffs[3 as usize] = 0.0 - quat_z(q)
    result
}

fn quat_norm_sq(q: Multivector) -> f64 {
    let w = quat_w(q)
    let x = quat_x(q)
    let y = quat_y(q)
    let z = quat_z(q)
    w * w + x * x + y * y + z * z
}

fn quat_identity() -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    quat_new(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
}

fn quat_rotate_vec3(q: Multivector, vx: f64, vy: f64, vz: f64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let v = quat_new(0.0, vx, vy, vz)
    let q_conj = quat_conjugate(q)
    let tmp = quat_mul(q, v)
    quat_mul(tmp, q_conj)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/ga/simd.sio ===
// == ga/base preamble inlined ==
// stdlib::math::ga::base — Self-contained Geometric Algebra foundation
//
// Implements Clifford algebras Cl(p,q,r) up to 5 dimensions (2^5 = 32 blades).
// Reference: Dorst, Fontijne, Mann — "Geometric Algebra for Computer Science"
//
// Basis blades are indexed by bitmap:
//   0 = scalar, 1 = e1, 2 = e2, 3 = e12, 4 = e3, 5 = e13, 6 = e23, 7 = e123, ...
// The coefficient of blade i is stored at coeffs[i].

// ============================================================================
// Algebra signature
// ============================================================================

struct AlgebraSignature {
    p: i64,       // positive basis vectors (e_i^2 = +1)
    q: i64,       // negative basis vectors (e_j^2 = -1)
    r: i64        // degenerate basis vectors (e_k^2 = 0)
}

// ============================================================================
// Multivector
// ============================================================================

struct Multivector {
    coeffs: [f64; 32],
    n_coeffs: i64
}

// ============================================================================
// Bit manipulation helpers (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn ga_popcount(x: i64) -> i64 {
    var count: i64 = 0
    var v: i64 = x
    while v > 0 {
        count = count + (v % 2)
        v = v / 2
    }
    count
}

fn ga_grade(blade: i64) -> i64 {
    ga_popcount(blade)
}

fn ga_bit(n: i64) -> i64 {
    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        result = result * 2
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn ga_has_bit(mask: i64, bit: i64) -> bool {
    (mask / ga_bit(bit)) % 2 == 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Metric helpers
// ============================================================================

fn ga_dim(sig: AlgebraSignature) -> i64 {
    sig.p + sig.q + sig.r
}

fn ga_algebra_dim(sig: AlgebraSignature) -> i64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 0
    let d = ga_dim(sig)
    while i < d {
        result = result * 2
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Metric factor for basis vector e_i squaring with itself.
// In Cl(p,q,r): first p vectors square to +1, next q to -1, next r to 0.
fn ga_metric_factor(sig: AlgebraSignature, vector_index: i64) -> i64 {
    if vector_index < sig.p {
        1
    } else if vector_index < sig.p + sig.q {
        0 - 1
    } else {
        0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Common signatures
// ============================================================================

fn ga_sig_euclidean3d() -> AlgebraSignature {
    AlgebraSignature { p: 3, q: 0, r: 0 }
}

fn ga_sig_pga3d() -> AlgebraSignature {
    AlgebraSignature { p: 3, q: 0, r: 1 }
}

fn ga_sig_cga() -> AlgebraSignature {
    AlgebraSignature { p: 4, q: 1, r: 0 }
}

fn ga_sig_quaternion() -> AlgebraSignature {
    AlgebraSignature { p: 0, q: 2, r: 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// Constructors
// ============================================================================

fn ga_zero() -> Multivector {
    Multivector { coeffs: [0.0; 32], n_coeffs: 32 }
}

fn ga_scalar(v: f64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var mv = ga_zero()
    mv.coeffs[0 as usize] = v
    mv
}

fn ga_basis(i: i64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var mv = ga_zero()
    if i >= 0 && i < 32 {
        mv.coeffs[i as usize] = 1.0
    }
    mv
}

// ============================================================================
// Component access
// ============================================================================

fn ga_get(mv: Multivector, index: i64) -> f64 {
    if index >= 0 && index < 32 {
        mv.coeffs[index as usize]
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

fn ga_set(mv: &! Multivector, index: i64, value: f64) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if index >= 0 && index < 32 {
        mv.coeffs[index as usize] = value
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// THE CORE: Blade product sign computation
// ============================================================================

// Count transpositions needed to sort the combined blade a*b into canonical order.
// Uses the standard algorithm: for each set bit j in b, count how many set bits
// in a are at positions above j. This gives the number of anticommutation swaps.
fn ga_canonical_reorder_sign(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var sum: i64 = 0
    // For each bit position j in b, count bits in a above position j.
    // Equivalent: shift a right, AND with b, popcount — summed over shifts.
    var i: i64 = a / 2   // a >> 1
    while i > 0 {
        sum = sum + ga_popcount(i & b)
        i = i / 2
    }
    if sum % 2 == 0 { 1 } else { 0 - 1 }
}

// Full blade product sign including metric.
// Algorithm:
//   1. Compute anticommutation sign from reordering
//   2. For each shared basis vector (in a AND b):
//      - If that vector has degenerate metric (r-type), return 0
//      - If that vector has negative metric (q-type), flip sign
//   3. Return final sign: +1, -1, or 0
fn ga_blade_product_sign(a: i64, b: i64, sig: AlgebraSignature) -> i64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var sign = ga_canonical_reorder_sign(a, b)

    let shared = a & b
    let dim = ga_dim(sig)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < dim {
        if ga_has_bit(shared, i) {
            let mf = ga_metric_factor(sig, i)
            if mf == 0 {
                return 0
            }
            sign = sign * mf
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    sign
}

// ============================================================================
// Geometric product — the fundamental operation
// ============================================================================
// For each pair of basis blades (i, j):
//   result[i XOR j] += coeffs[i] * coeffs[j] * blade_product_sign(i, j, sig)

fn ga_geometric_product(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    let n = ga_algebra_dim(sig)

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if a.coeffs[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < n {
                if b.coeffs[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let sign = ga_blade_product_sign(i, j, sig)
                    if sign != 0 {
                        let result_blade = i ^ j
                        let coeff = a.coeffs[i as usize] * b.coeffs[j as usize] * (sign as f64)
                        result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] = result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] + coeff
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Outer (wedge) product
// ============================================================================
// Keep only terms where grade(result_blade) == grade(a_blade) + grade(b_blade)

fn ga_outer_product(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    let n = ga_algebra_dim(sig)

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if a.coeffs[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            let ga = ga_grade(i)
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < n {
                if b.coeffs[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let gb = ga_grade(j)
                    let result_blade = i ^ j
                    let gr = ga_grade(result_blade)
                    if gr == ga + gb {
                        let sign = ga_canonical_reorder_sign(i, j)
                        let coeff = a.coeffs[i as usize] * b.coeffs[j as usize] * (sign as f64)
                        result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] = result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] + coeff
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Inner product (left contraction)
// ============================================================================
// Keep only terms where grade(result_blade) == |grade(a_blade) - grade(b_blade)|

fn ga_inner_product(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    let n = ga_algebra_dim(sig)

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if a.coeffs[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            let ga = ga_grade(i)
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < n {
                if b.coeffs[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let gb = ga_grade(j)
                    let result_blade = i ^ j
                    let gr = ga_grade(result_blade)
                    let target = if ga > gb { ga - gb } else { gb - ga }
                    if gr == target && (ga > 0 || gb > 0) {
                        let sign = ga_blade_product_sign(i, j, sig)
                        if sign != 0 {
                            let coeff = a.coeffs[i as usize] * b.coeffs[j as usize] * (sign as f64)
                            result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] = result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] + coeff
                        }
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Reverse: reverses order of basis vectors in each blade
// ============================================================================
// For a grade-k blade: sign = (-1)^(k*(k-1)/2)
// grade 0: +1, grade 1: +1, grade 2: -1, grade 3: -1, grade 4: +1, ...

fn ga_reverse(a: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        let k = ga_grade(i)
        let exp = (k * (k - 1)) / 2
        let sign = if exp % 2 == 0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 - 1.0 }
        result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize] * sign
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Grade selection
// ============================================================================

fn ga_grade_select(a: Multivector, grade: i64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        if ga_grade(i) == grade {
            result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Arithmetic
// ============================================================================

fn ga_add(a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize] + b.coeffs[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn ga_sub(a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize] - b.coeffs[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn ga_scale(a: Multivector, s: f64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize] * s
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Norm squared: scalar part of a * reverse(a)
// ============================================================================

fn ga_norm_squared(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector) -> f64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let rev_a = ga_reverse(a)
    let product = ga_geometric_product(sig, a, rev_a)
    product.coeffs[0 as usize]
}

// ============================================================================
// Dual: multiply by pseudoscalar
// ============================================================================

fn ga_dual(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let n = ga_algebra_dim(sig)
    // Pseudoscalar index = 2^dim - 1 (all bits set)
    let ps_idx = n - 1
    let ps = ga_basis(ps_idx)
    let ps_rev = ga_reverse(ps)
    ga_geometric_product(sig, a, ps_rev)
}

// ============================================================================
// Helper: approximate equality for tests
// ============================================================================

fn ga_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn ga_approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
    ga_abs(a - b) < 0.000001
}

// ============================================================================
// Inline tests
// ============================================================================

// Test 1: Geometric product of two vectors in R^3 gives scalar + bivector
// e1 * e2 = e12 (bivector), so product should have coeffs[3] = 1.0
fn test_vector_product_r3() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)   // e1 = bitmap 0b01
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)   // e2 = bitmap 0b10
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, e1, e2)
    // e1 * e2 = e12 (blade index 3 = 0b11), coefficient should be +1
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[3 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 2: e1*e1 = +1 in Euclidean 3D
fn test_e1_squared_euclidean() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, e1, e1)
    // e1^2 = +1 (scalar), so coeffs[0] = 1.0
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 3: Quaternion algebra Cl(0,2): e1*e2 product
// In Cl(0,2): e1^2 = -1, e2^2 = -1
// e1*e2 = e12 (blade 3)
fn test_quaternion_e1e2() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_quaternion()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, e1, e2)
    // e1*e2 = e12
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[3 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 4: Quaternion i*j=k, j*k=i, k*i=j
// In Cl(0,2): i=e1, j=e2, k=e12
// i*j = e1*e2 = e12 = k  => coeffs[3] = 1.0
fn test_quaternion_ijk() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_quaternion()
    let i_q = ga_basis(1)   // e1
    let j_q = ga_basis(2)   // e2
    let k_q = ga_basis(3)   // e12

    // i*j = k
    let ij = ga_geometric_product(sig, i_q, j_q)
    let ij_ok = ga_approx_eq(ij.coeffs[3 as usize], 1.0)

    // j*k = e2*e12
    // canonical_reorder_sign(2, 3): a=2=0b10, b=3=0b11
    //   i = a/2 = 1 = 0b01, popcount(1 & 3) = popcount(1) = 1, sum=1
    //   i = 1/2 = 0, stop. sign = -1
    // shared = 2 & 3 = 2 = 0b10, bit 1 set => metric_factor(sig, 1) = -1
    // total sign = (-1)*(-1) = +1
    // result blade = 2 ^ 3 = 1 (e1)
    // So j*k = +e1 = i
    let jk = ga_geometric_product(sig, j_q, k_q)
    let jk_ok = ga_approx_eq(jk.coeffs[1 as usize], 1.0)

    // k*i = e12*e1
    // canonical_reorder_sign(3, 1): a=3=0b11, b=1=0b01
    //   i = 3/2 = 1 = 0b01, popcount(1 & 1) = 1, sum=1
    //   i = 1/2 = 0, stop. sign = -1
    // shared = 3 & 1 = 1 = 0b01, bit 0 set => metric_factor(sig, 0) = -1
    // total sign = (-1)*(-1) = +1
    // result blade = 3 ^ 1 = 2 (e2)
    // So k*i = +e2 = j
    let ki = ga_geometric_product(sig, k_q, i_q)
    let ki_ok = ga_approx_eq(ki.coeffs[2 as usize], 1.0)

    ij_ok && jk_ok && ki_ok
}

// Test 5: Reverse of a bivector negates it
// reverse(e12) = e21 = -e12
fn test_reverse_bivector() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let bv = ga_basis(3)   // e12
    let rev = ga_reverse(bv)
    // grade 2: sign = (-1)^(2*1/2) = (-1)^1 = -1
    ga_approx_eq(rev.coeffs[3 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)
}

// Test 6: Reverse of a vector leaves it unchanged
fn test_reverse_vector() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let v = ga_basis(1)   // e1
    let rev = ga_reverse(v)
    // grade 1: sign = (-1)^(1*0/2) = (-1)^0 = +1
    ga_approx_eq(rev.coeffs[1 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 7: Norm squared of unit vector e1 in Euclidean 3D = +1
fn test_norm_squared_euclidean() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let ns = ga_norm_squared(sig, e1)
    ga_approx_eq(ns, 1.0)
}

// Test 8: Norm squared of e1 in Cl(0,2) (quaternion) = -1
// e1^2 = -1, reverse(e1) = e1, so e1 * reverse(e1) = e1*e1 = -1
fn test_norm_squared_negative() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_quaternion()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let ns = ga_norm_squared(sig, e1)
    ga_approx_eq(ns, 0.0 - 1.0)
}

// Test 9: Outer product of e1 and e2 gives e12
fn test_outer_product() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)
    let result = ga_outer_product(sig, e1, e2)
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[3 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 10: Outer product of e1 with itself is zero (e1 ^ e1 = 0)
fn test_outer_product_self_zero() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let result = ga_outer_product(sig, e1, e1)
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0) && ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[1 as usize], 0.0)
}

// Test 11: Inner product of two orthogonal vectors is zero
fn test_inner_product_orthogonal() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)
    let result = ga_inner_product(sig, e1, e2)
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0)
}

// Test 12: Inner product e1 . e1 = 1 in Euclidean space
fn test_inner_product_same() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let result = ga_inner_product(sig, e1, e1)
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 13: Grade selection extracts correct grade
fn test_grade_select() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)
    // v = e1 + e2 (pure grade-1)
    let v = ga_add(e1, e2)
    // Add a scalar part: mv = 3.0 + e1 + e2
    let s = ga_scalar(3.0)
    let mv = ga_add(s, v)
    // Extract grade 0
    let g0 = ga_grade_select(mv, 0)
    let g0_ok = ga_approx_eq(g0.coeffs[0 as usize], 3.0)
    // Extract grade 1
    let g1 = ga_grade_select(mv, 1)
    let g1_ok = ga_approx_eq(g1.coeffs[1 as usize], 1.0) && ga_approx_eq(g1.coeffs[2 as usize], 1.0)
    g0_ok && g1_ok
}

// Test 14: Geometric product of vectors gives scalar + bivector
// (ae1 + be2) * (ce1 + de2) = ac*e1e1 + ad*e1e2 + bc*e2e1 + bd*e2e2
//                            = (ac + bd)*1 + (ad - bc)*e12
fn test_vector_product_components() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    // v1 = 2*e1 + 3*e2
    var v1 = ga_zero()
    v1.coeffs[1 as usize] = 2.0
    v1.coeffs[2 as usize] = 3.0
    // v2 = 4*e1 + 5*e2
    var v2 = ga_zero()
    v2.coeffs[1 as usize] = 4.0
    v2.coeffs[2 as usize] = 5.0
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, v1, v2)
    // scalar part = 2*4 + 3*5 = 8 + 15 = 23
    let scalar_ok = ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 23.0)
    // bivector e12 part = 2*5 - 3*4 = 10 - 12 = -2
    let bv_ok = ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[3 as usize], 0.0 - 2.0)
    scalar_ok && bv_ok
}

// Test 15: Degenerate metric — e0^2 = 0 in PGA
fn test_degenerate_pga() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_pga3d()  // Cl(3,0,1): e1^2=1, e2^2=1, e3^2=1, e4^2=0
    // e4 is the degenerate basis vector (index 3, bitmap 8 = 2^3)
    let e4 = ga_basis(8)   // bitmap 0b1000
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, e4, e4)
    // e4^2 = 0
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0)
}

// Test 16: Popcount correctness
fn test_popcount() -> bool {
    ga_popcount(0) == 0 &&
    ga_popcount(1) == 1 &&
    ga_popcount(3) == 2 &&
    ga_popcount(7) == 3 &&
    ga_popcount(15) == 4 &&
    ga_popcount(31) == 5
}

// Test 17: Algebra dimensions
fn test_algebra_dim() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig3 = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let sig4 = ga_sig_pga3d()
    let sig5 = ga_sig_cga()
    ga_dim(sig3) == 3 && ga_algebra_dim(sig3) == 8 &&
    ga_dim(sig4) == 4 && ga_algebra_dim(sig4) == 16 &&
    ga_dim(sig5) == 5 && ga_algebra_dim(sig5) == 32
}

// Test 18: Add and subtract
fn test_add_sub() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let a = ga_scalar(5.0)
    let b = ga_scalar(3.0)
    let sum = ga_add(a, b)
    let diff = ga_sub(a, b)
    ga_approx_eq(sum.coeffs[0 as usize], 8.0) && ga_approx_eq(diff.coeffs[0 as usize], 2.0)
}

// Test 19: Scale
fn test_scale() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let scaled = ga_scale(e1, 7.0)
    ga_approx_eq(scaled.coeffs[1 as usize], 7.0)
}

// Test 20: Quaternion i^2 = j^2 = k^2 = -1
fn test_quaternion_squares() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_quaternion()
    let i_q = ga_basis(1)
    let j_q = ga_basis(2)
    let k_q = ga_basis(3)

    let i2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, i_q, i_q)
    let j2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, j_q, j_q)
    let k2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, k_q, k_q)

    // i^2 = e1^2 = -1
    let i2_ok = ga_approx_eq(i2.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)
    // j^2 = e2^2 = -1
    let j2_ok = ga_approx_eq(j2.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)
    // k^2 = e12^2 = e1*e2*e1*e2 = -e1*e1*e2*e2 = -(-1)(-1) = -1
    let k2_ok = ga_approx_eq(k2.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)

    i2_ok && j2_ok && k2_ok
}


// == SIMD batch multivector operations ==
// Adapted to use base.sio Multivector (coeffs[32])

struct MvBatch4 {
    comp: [f64; 128],
    sig: AlgebraSignature,
    count: i64,
}

fn mv_batch4_zero(sig: AlgebraSignature) -> MvBatch4 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    MvBatch4 { comp: [0.0; 128], sig: sig, count: 4 }
}

fn mv_batch4_load(sig: AlgebraSignature, m0: Multivector, m1: Multivector, m2: Multivector, m3: Multivector) -> MvBatch4 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var batch = mv_batch4_zero(sig)
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < 32 {
        let base = c * 4
        batch.comp[(base + 0) as usize] = m0.coeffs[c as usize]
        batch.comp[(base + 1) as usize] = m1.coeffs[c as usize]
        batch.comp[(base + 2) as usize] = m2.coeffs[c as usize]
        batch.comp[(base + 3) as usize] = m3.coeffs[c as usize]
        c = c + 1
    }
    batch.count = 4
    batch
}

fn mv_batch4_extract(batch: MvBatch4, lane: i64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var mv = ga_zero()
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < 32 {
        mv.coeffs[c as usize] = batch.comp[(c * 4 + lane) as usize]
        c = c + 1
    }
    mv
}

fn mv_batch4_add(a: MvBatch4, b: MvBatch4) -> MvBatch4 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = mv_batch4_zero(a.sig)
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < 32 {
        let base = c * 4
        var lane: i64 = 0
        while lane < 4 {
            result.comp[(base + lane) as usize] = a.comp[(base + lane) as usize] + b.comp[(base + lane) as usize]
            lane = lane + 1
        }
        c = c + 1
    }
    result.count = a.count
    result
}

fn mv_batch4_scale(a: MvBatch4, s: f64) -> MvBatch4 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = mv_batch4_zero(a.sig)
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < 32 {
        let base = c * 4
        var lane: i64 = 0
        while lane < 4 {
            result.comp[(base + lane) as usize] = a.comp[(base + lane) as usize] * s
            lane = lane + 1
        }
        c = c + 1
    }
    result.count = a.count
    result
}

fn mv_batch4_sub(a: MvBatch4, b: MvBatch4) -> MvBatch4 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = mv_batch4_zero(a.sig)
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < 32 {
        let base = c * 4
        var lane: i64 = 0
        while lane < 4 {
            result.comp[(base + lane) as usize] = a.comp[(base + lane) as usize] - b.comp[(base + lane) as usize]
            lane = lane + 1
        }
        c = c + 1
    }
    result.count = a.count
    result
}

fn mv_batch4_product(a: MvBatch4, b: MvBatch4) -> MvBatch4 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = a.sig
    let m0a = mv_batch4_extract(a, 0)
    let m1a = mv_batch4_extract(a, 1)
    let m2a = mv_batch4_extract(a, 2)
    let m3a = mv_batch4_extract(a, 3)
    let m0b = mv_batch4_extract(b, 0)
    let m1b = mv_batch4_extract(b, 1)
    let m2b = mv_batch4_extract(b, 2)
    let m3b = mv_batch4_extract(b, 3)
    let r0 = ga_geometric_product(sig, m0a, m0b)
    let r1 = ga_geometric_product(sig, m1a, m1b)
    let r2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, m2a, m2b)
    let r3 = ga_geometric_product(sig, m3a, m3b)
    mv_batch4_load(sig, r0, r1, r2, r3)
}

fn mv_batch4_reverse(a: MvBatch4) -> MvBatch4 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let m0 = ga_reverse(mv_batch4_extract(a, 0))
    let m1 = ga_reverse(mv_batch4_extract(a, 1))
    let m2 = ga_reverse(mv_batch4_extract(a, 2))
    let m3 = ga_reverse(mv_batch4_extract(a, 3))
    mv_batch4_load(a.sig, m0, m1, m2, m3)
}

fn pga_motor_batch4_sandwich(motors: MvBatch4, points: MvBatch4) -> MvBatch4 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let rev = mv_batch4_reverse(motors)
    let mp = mv_batch4_product(motors, points)
    mv_batch4_product(mp, rev)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/ga/uncertainty.sio ===
// == ga/base preamble inlined ==
// stdlib::math::ga::base — Self-contained Geometric Algebra foundation
//
// Implements Clifford algebras Cl(p,q,r) up to 5 dimensions (2^5 = 32 blades).
// Reference: Dorst, Fontijne, Mann — "Geometric Algebra for Computer Science"
//
// Basis blades are indexed by bitmap:
//   0 = scalar, 1 = e1, 2 = e2, 3 = e12, 4 = e3, 5 = e13, 6 = e23, 7 = e123, ...
// The coefficient of blade i is stored at coeffs[i].

// ============================================================================
// Algebra signature
// ============================================================================

struct AlgebraSignature {
    p: i64,       // positive basis vectors (e_i^2 = +1)
    q: i64,       // negative basis vectors (e_j^2 = -1)
    r: i64        // degenerate basis vectors (e_k^2 = 0)
}

// ============================================================================
// Multivector
// ============================================================================

struct Multivector {
    coeffs: [f64; 32],
    n_coeffs: i64
}

// ============================================================================
// Bit manipulation helpers (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn ga_popcount(x: i64) -> i64 {
    var count: i64 = 0
    var v: i64 = x
    while v > 0 {
        count = count + (v % 2)
        v = v / 2
    }
    count
}

fn ga_grade(blade: i64) -> i64 {
    ga_popcount(blade)
}

fn ga_bit(n: i64) -> i64 {
    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        result = result * 2
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn ga_has_bit(mask: i64, bit: i64) -> bool {
    (mask / ga_bit(bit)) % 2 == 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Metric helpers
// ============================================================================

fn ga_dim(sig: AlgebraSignature) -> i64 {
    sig.p + sig.q + sig.r
}

fn ga_algebra_dim(sig: AlgebraSignature) -> i64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 0
    let d = ga_dim(sig)
    while i < d {
        result = result * 2
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Metric factor for basis vector e_i squaring with itself.
// In Cl(p,q,r): first p vectors square to +1, next q to -1, next r to 0.
fn ga_metric_factor(sig: AlgebraSignature, vector_index: i64) -> i64 {
    if vector_index < sig.p {
        1
    } else if vector_index < sig.p + sig.q {
        0 - 1
    } else {
        0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Common signatures
// ============================================================================

fn ga_sig_euclidean3d() -> AlgebraSignature {
    AlgebraSignature { p: 3, q: 0, r: 0 }
}

fn ga_sig_pga3d() -> AlgebraSignature {
    AlgebraSignature { p: 3, q: 0, r: 1 }
}

fn ga_sig_cga() -> AlgebraSignature {
    AlgebraSignature { p: 4, q: 1, r: 0 }
}

fn ga_sig_quaternion() -> AlgebraSignature {
    AlgebraSignature { p: 0, q: 2, r: 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// Constructors
// ============================================================================

fn ga_zero() -> Multivector {
    Multivector { coeffs: [0.0; 32], n_coeffs: 32 }
}

fn ga_scalar(v: f64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var mv = ga_zero()
    mv.coeffs[0 as usize] = v
    mv
}

fn ga_basis(i: i64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var mv = ga_zero()
    if i >= 0 && i < 32 {
        mv.coeffs[i as usize] = 1.0
    }
    mv
}

// ============================================================================
// Component access
// ============================================================================

fn ga_get(mv: Multivector, index: i64) -> f64 {
    if index >= 0 && index < 32 {
        mv.coeffs[index as usize]
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

fn ga_set(mv: &! Multivector, index: i64, value: f64) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if index >= 0 && index < 32 {
        mv.coeffs[index as usize] = value
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// THE CORE: Blade product sign computation
// ============================================================================

// Count transpositions needed to sort the combined blade a*b into canonical order.
// Uses the standard algorithm: for each set bit j in b, count how many set bits
// in a are at positions above j. This gives the number of anticommutation swaps.
fn ga_canonical_reorder_sign(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var sum: i64 = 0
    // For each bit position j in b, count bits in a above position j.
    // Equivalent: shift a right, AND with b, popcount — summed over shifts.
    var i: i64 = a / 2   // a >> 1
    while i > 0 {
        sum = sum + ga_popcount(i & b)
        i = i / 2
    }
    if sum % 2 == 0 { 1 } else { 0 - 1 }
}

// Full blade product sign including metric.
// Algorithm:
//   1. Compute anticommutation sign from reordering
//   2. For each shared basis vector (in a AND b):
//      - If that vector has degenerate metric (r-type), return 0
//      - If that vector has negative metric (q-type), flip sign
//   3. Return final sign: +1, -1, or 0
fn ga_blade_product_sign(a: i64, b: i64, sig: AlgebraSignature) -> i64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var sign = ga_canonical_reorder_sign(a, b)

    let shared = a & b
    let dim = ga_dim(sig)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < dim {
        if ga_has_bit(shared, i) {
            let mf = ga_metric_factor(sig, i)
            if mf == 0 {
                return 0
            }
            sign = sign * mf
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    sign
}

// ============================================================================
// Geometric product — the fundamental operation
// ============================================================================
// For each pair of basis blades (i, j):
//   result[i XOR j] += coeffs[i] * coeffs[j] * blade_product_sign(i, j, sig)

fn ga_geometric_product(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    let n = ga_algebra_dim(sig)

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if a.coeffs[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < n {
                if b.coeffs[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let sign = ga_blade_product_sign(i, j, sig)
                    if sign != 0 {
                        let result_blade = i ^ j
                        let coeff = a.coeffs[i as usize] * b.coeffs[j as usize] * (sign as f64)
                        result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] = result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] + coeff
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Outer (wedge) product
// ============================================================================
// Keep only terms where grade(result_blade) == grade(a_blade) + grade(b_blade)

fn ga_outer_product(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    let n = ga_algebra_dim(sig)

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if a.coeffs[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            let ga = ga_grade(i)
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < n {
                if b.coeffs[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let gb = ga_grade(j)
                    let result_blade = i ^ j
                    let gr = ga_grade(result_blade)
                    if gr == ga + gb {
                        let sign = ga_canonical_reorder_sign(i, j)
                        let coeff = a.coeffs[i as usize] * b.coeffs[j as usize] * (sign as f64)
                        result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] = result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] + coeff
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Inner product (left contraction)
// ============================================================================
// Keep only terms where grade(result_blade) == |grade(a_blade) - grade(b_blade)|

fn ga_inner_product(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    let n = ga_algebra_dim(sig)

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if a.coeffs[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            let ga = ga_grade(i)
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < n {
                if b.coeffs[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let gb = ga_grade(j)
                    let result_blade = i ^ j
                    let gr = ga_grade(result_blade)
                    let target = if ga > gb { ga - gb } else { gb - ga }
                    if gr == target && (ga > 0 || gb > 0) {
                        let sign = ga_blade_product_sign(i, j, sig)
                        if sign != 0 {
                            let coeff = a.coeffs[i as usize] * b.coeffs[j as usize] * (sign as f64)
                            result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] = result.coeffs[result_blade as usize] + coeff
                        }
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Reverse: reverses order of basis vectors in each blade
// ============================================================================
// For a grade-k blade: sign = (-1)^(k*(k-1)/2)
// grade 0: +1, grade 1: +1, grade 2: -1, grade 3: -1, grade 4: +1, ...

fn ga_reverse(a: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        let k = ga_grade(i)
        let exp = (k * (k - 1)) / 2
        let sign = if exp % 2 == 0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 - 1.0 }
        result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize] * sign
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Grade selection
// ============================================================================

fn ga_grade_select(a: Multivector, grade: i64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        if ga_grade(i) == grade {
            result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Arithmetic
// ============================================================================

fn ga_add(a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize] + b.coeffs[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn ga_sub(a: Multivector, b: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize] - b.coeffs[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn ga_scale(a: Multivector, s: f64) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = ga_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        result.coeffs[i as usize] = a.coeffs[i as usize] * s
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Norm squared: scalar part of a * reverse(a)
// ============================================================================

fn ga_norm_squared(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector) -> f64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let rev_a = ga_reverse(a)
    let product = ga_geometric_product(sig, a, rev_a)
    product.coeffs[0 as usize]
}

// ============================================================================
// Dual: multiply by pseudoscalar
// ============================================================================

fn ga_dual(sig: AlgebraSignature, a: Multivector) -> Multivector with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let n = ga_algebra_dim(sig)
    // Pseudoscalar index = 2^dim - 1 (all bits set)
    let ps_idx = n - 1
    let ps = ga_basis(ps_idx)
    let ps_rev = ga_reverse(ps)
    ga_geometric_product(sig, a, ps_rev)
}

// ============================================================================
// Helper: approximate equality for tests
// ============================================================================

fn ga_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn ga_approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
    ga_abs(a - b) < 0.000001
}

// ============================================================================
// Inline tests
// ============================================================================

// Test 1: Geometric product of two vectors in R^3 gives scalar + bivector
// e1 * e2 = e12 (bivector), so product should have coeffs[3] = 1.0
fn test_vector_product_r3() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)   // e1 = bitmap 0b01
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)   // e2 = bitmap 0b10
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, e1, e2)
    // e1 * e2 = e12 (blade index 3 = 0b11), coefficient should be +1
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[3 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 2: e1*e1 = +1 in Euclidean 3D
fn test_e1_squared_euclidean() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, e1, e1)
    // e1^2 = +1 (scalar), so coeffs[0] = 1.0
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 3: Quaternion algebra Cl(0,2): e1*e2 product
// In Cl(0,2): e1^2 = -1, e2^2 = -1
// e1*e2 = e12 (blade 3)
fn test_quaternion_e1e2() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_quaternion()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, e1, e2)
    // e1*e2 = e12
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[3 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 4: Quaternion i*j=k, j*k=i, k*i=j
// In Cl(0,2): i=e1, j=e2, k=e12
// i*j = e1*e2 = e12 = k  => coeffs[3] = 1.0
fn test_quaternion_ijk() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_quaternion()
    let i_q = ga_basis(1)   // e1
    let j_q = ga_basis(2)   // e2
    let k_q = ga_basis(3)   // e12

    // i*j = k
    let ij = ga_geometric_product(sig, i_q, j_q)
    let ij_ok = ga_approx_eq(ij.coeffs[3 as usize], 1.0)

    // j*k = e2*e12
    // canonical_reorder_sign(2, 3): a=2=0b10, b=3=0b11
    //   i = a/2 = 1 = 0b01, popcount(1 & 3) = popcount(1) = 1, sum=1
    //   i = 1/2 = 0, stop. sign = -1
    // shared = 2 & 3 = 2 = 0b10, bit 1 set => metric_factor(sig, 1) = -1
    // total sign = (-1)*(-1) = +1
    // result blade = 2 ^ 3 = 1 (e1)
    // So j*k = +e1 = i
    let jk = ga_geometric_product(sig, j_q, k_q)
    let jk_ok = ga_approx_eq(jk.coeffs[1 as usize], 1.0)

    // k*i = e12*e1
    // canonical_reorder_sign(3, 1): a=3=0b11, b=1=0b01
    //   i = 3/2 = 1 = 0b01, popcount(1 & 1) = 1, sum=1
    //   i = 1/2 = 0, stop. sign = -1
    // shared = 3 & 1 = 1 = 0b01, bit 0 set => metric_factor(sig, 0) = -1
    // total sign = (-1)*(-1) = +1
    // result blade = 3 ^ 1 = 2 (e2)
    // So k*i = +e2 = j
    let ki = ga_geometric_product(sig, k_q, i_q)
    let ki_ok = ga_approx_eq(ki.coeffs[2 as usize], 1.0)

    ij_ok && jk_ok && ki_ok
}

// Test 5: Reverse of a bivector negates it
// reverse(e12) = e21 = -e12
fn test_reverse_bivector() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let bv = ga_basis(3)   // e12
    let rev = ga_reverse(bv)
    // grade 2: sign = (-1)^(2*1/2) = (-1)^1 = -1
    ga_approx_eq(rev.coeffs[3 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)
}

// Test 6: Reverse of a vector leaves it unchanged
fn test_reverse_vector() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let v = ga_basis(1)   // e1
    let rev = ga_reverse(v)
    // grade 1: sign = (-1)^(1*0/2) = (-1)^0 = +1
    ga_approx_eq(rev.coeffs[1 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 7: Norm squared of unit vector e1 in Euclidean 3D = +1
fn test_norm_squared_euclidean() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let ns = ga_norm_squared(sig, e1)
    ga_approx_eq(ns, 1.0)
}

// Test 8: Norm squared of e1 in Cl(0,2) (quaternion) = -1
// e1^2 = -1, reverse(e1) = e1, so e1 * reverse(e1) = e1*e1 = -1
fn test_norm_squared_negative() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_quaternion()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let ns = ga_norm_squared(sig, e1)
    ga_approx_eq(ns, 0.0 - 1.0)
}

// Test 9: Outer product of e1 and e2 gives e12
fn test_outer_product() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)
    let result = ga_outer_product(sig, e1, e2)
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[3 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 10: Outer product of e1 with itself is zero (e1 ^ e1 = 0)
fn test_outer_product_self_zero() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let result = ga_outer_product(sig, e1, e1)
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0) && ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[1 as usize], 0.0)
}

// Test 11: Inner product of two orthogonal vectors is zero
fn test_inner_product_orthogonal() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)
    let result = ga_inner_product(sig, e1, e2)
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0)
}

// Test 12: Inner product e1 . e1 = 1 in Euclidean space
fn test_inner_product_same() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let result = ga_inner_product(sig, e1, e1)
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 1.0)
}

// Test 13: Grade selection extracts correct grade
fn test_grade_select() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let e2 = ga_basis(2)
    // v = e1 + e2 (pure grade-1)
    let v = ga_add(e1, e2)
    // Add a scalar part: mv = 3.0 + e1 + e2
    let s = ga_scalar(3.0)
    let mv = ga_add(s, v)
    // Extract grade 0
    let g0 = ga_grade_select(mv, 0)
    let g0_ok = ga_approx_eq(g0.coeffs[0 as usize], 3.0)
    // Extract grade 1
    let g1 = ga_grade_select(mv, 1)
    let g1_ok = ga_approx_eq(g1.coeffs[1 as usize], 1.0) && ga_approx_eq(g1.coeffs[2 as usize], 1.0)
    g0_ok && g1_ok
}

// Test 14: Geometric product of vectors gives scalar + bivector
// (ae1 + be2) * (ce1 + de2) = ac*e1e1 + ad*e1e2 + bc*e2e1 + bd*e2e2
//                            = (ac + bd)*1 + (ad - bc)*e12
fn test_vector_product_components() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    // v1 = 2*e1 + 3*e2
    var v1 = ga_zero()
    v1.coeffs[1 as usize] = 2.0
    v1.coeffs[2 as usize] = 3.0
    // v2 = 4*e1 + 5*e2
    var v2 = ga_zero()
    v2.coeffs[1 as usize] = 4.0
    v2.coeffs[2 as usize] = 5.0
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, v1, v2)
    // scalar part = 2*4 + 3*5 = 8 + 15 = 23
    let scalar_ok = ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 23.0)
    // bivector e12 part = 2*5 - 3*4 = 10 - 12 = -2
    let bv_ok = ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[3 as usize], 0.0 - 2.0)
    scalar_ok && bv_ok
}

// Test 15: Degenerate metric — e0^2 = 0 in PGA
fn test_degenerate_pga() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_pga3d()  // Cl(3,0,1): e1^2=1, e2^2=1, e3^2=1, e4^2=0
    // e4 is the degenerate basis vector (index 3, bitmap 8 = 2^3)
    let e4 = ga_basis(8)   // bitmap 0b1000
    let result = ga_geometric_product(sig, e4, e4)
    // e4^2 = 0
    ga_approx_eq(result.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0)
}

// Test 16: Popcount correctness
fn test_popcount() -> bool {
    ga_popcount(0) == 0 &&
    ga_popcount(1) == 1 &&
    ga_popcount(3) == 2 &&
    ga_popcount(7) == 3 &&
    ga_popcount(15) == 4 &&
    ga_popcount(31) == 5
}

// Test 17: Algebra dimensions
fn test_algebra_dim() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig3 = ga_sig_euclidean3d()
    let sig4 = ga_sig_pga3d()
    let sig5 = ga_sig_cga()
    ga_dim(sig3) == 3 && ga_algebra_dim(sig3) == 8 &&
    ga_dim(sig4) == 4 && ga_algebra_dim(sig4) == 16 &&
    ga_dim(sig5) == 5 && ga_algebra_dim(sig5) == 32
}

// Test 18: Add and subtract
fn test_add_sub() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let a = ga_scalar(5.0)
    let b = ga_scalar(3.0)
    let sum = ga_add(a, b)
    let diff = ga_sub(a, b)
    ga_approx_eq(sum.coeffs[0 as usize], 8.0) && ga_approx_eq(diff.coeffs[0 as usize], 2.0)
}

// Test 19: Scale
fn test_scale() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let e1 = ga_basis(1)
    let scaled = ga_scale(e1, 7.0)
    ga_approx_eq(scaled.coeffs[1 as usize], 7.0)
}

// Test 20: Quaternion i^2 = j^2 = k^2 = -1
fn test_quaternion_squares() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let sig = ga_sig_quaternion()
    let i_q = ga_basis(1)
    let j_q = ga_basis(2)
    let k_q = ga_basis(3)

    let i2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, i_q, i_q)
    let j2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, j_q, j_q)
    let k2 = ga_geometric_product(sig, k_q, k_q)

    // i^2 = e1^2 = -1
    let i2_ok = ga_approx_eq(i2.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)
    // j^2 = e2^2 = -1
    let j2_ok = ga_approx_eq(j2.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)
    // k^2 = e12^2 = e1*e2*e1*e2 = -e1*e1*e2*e2 = -(-1)(-1) = -1
    let k2_ok = ga_approx_eq(k2.coeffs[0 as usize], 0.0 - 1.0)

    i2_ok && j2_ok && k2_ok
}


// == Uncertainty propagation module ==
// Adapted to use base.sio Multivector (coeffs[32])

fn ga_sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x
    if x > 1.0 { guess = x / 2.0 } else { guess = 1.0 }
    guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
    guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
    guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
    guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
    guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
    guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
    guess
}

fn ga_product_jacobian_a(b: Multivector, sig: AlgebraSignature) -> [f64; 1024] with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let n: i64 = 32
    var jac: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            let j = k ^ i
            if j < n {
                let sign = ga_blade_product_sign(i, j, sig)
                if sign != 0 {
                    jac[(k * 32 + i) as usize] = (sign as f64) * b.coeffs[j as usize]
                }
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    jac
}

fn ga_product_jacobian_b(a: Multivector, sig: AlgebraSignature) -> [f64; 1024] with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let n: i64 = 32
    var jac: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            let i = k ^ j
            if i < n {
                let sign = ga_blade_product_sign(i, j, sig)
                if sign != 0 {
                    jac[(k * 32 + j) as usize] = (sign as f64) * a.coeffs[i as usize]
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    jac
}

fn propagate_bilinear_uncertainty(
    eps_a: [f64; 32],
    eps_b: [f64; 32],
    jac_a: [f64; 1024],
    jac_b: [f64; 1024],
    n: i64
) -> [f64; 32] with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var eps_c: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n {
        var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            let ja = jac_a[(k * 32 + i) as usize]
            if ja != 0.0 {
                let contrib = ja * eps_a[i as usize]
                sum_sq = sum_sq + contrib * contrib
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            let jb = jac_b[(k * 32 + j) as usize]
            if jb != 0.0 {
                let contrib = jb * eps_b[j as usize]
                sum_sq = sum_sq + contrib * contrib
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        eps_c[k as usize] = ga_sqrt_approx(sum_sq)
        k = k + 1
    }
    eps_c
}

fn bingham_concentration_to_sigma(kappa1: f64, kappa2: f64, kappa3: f64) -> [f64; 4] with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var sigma: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
    sigma[0] = 0.001
    let abs_k1 = if kappa1 < 0.0 { 0.0 - kappa1 } else { kappa1 }
    let abs_k2 = if kappa2 < 0.0 { 0.0 - kappa2 } else { kappa2 }
    let abs_k3 = if kappa3 < 0.0 { 0.0 - kappa3 } else { kappa3 }
    if abs_k1 > 0.01 { sigma[1] = ga_sqrt_approx(1.0 / (2.0 * abs_k1)) } else { sigma[1] = 1.0 }
    if abs_k2 > 0.01 { sigma[2] = ga_sqrt_approx(1.0 / (2.0 * abs_k2)) } else { sigma[2] = 1.0 }
    if abs_k3 > 0.01 { sigma[3] = ga_sqrt_approx(1.0 / (2.0 * abs_k3)) } else { sigma[3] = 1.0 }
    sigma
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/gp.sio ===
// stdlib/math/gp.sio — Gaussian process regression
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Kernel functions (RBF, Matern-3/2, Matern-5/2, periodic, rational quadratic)
//   Kernel matrix assembly with Div, Mut, Panic, noise
//   Cholesky factorization and triangular solves
//   GP training (compute L, alpha = K^{-1}y)
//   GP prediction with Div, Mut, Panic, posterior mean and variance
//   Log marginal likelihood
//   Hyperparameter optimization via Nelder-Mead
//   GP sampling from prior and posterior
//
// References:
//   Rasmussen & Williams (2006): "Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning"
//   Quinonero-Candela & Rasmussen (2005): "A Unifying View of Sparse GP Approximations"
//   Bishop (2006): "Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning" Ch. 6

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (all prefixed gp_h_ to avoid name collisions)
// =============================================================================

fn gp_h_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn gp_h_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn gp_h_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn gp_h_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn gp_h_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Range reduction: exp(x) = 2^k * exp(r) where x = k*ln2 + r
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    let inv_ln2 = 1.4426950408889634

    if x > 709.0 { return 1.0e308 }
    if x < -709.0 { return 0.0 }

    var k_f = x * inv_ln2
    var k: i64 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = (k_f + 0.5) as i64 } else { k = (k_f - 0.5) as i64 }

    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2

    // Taylor series for exp(r), |r| <= ln2/2
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }

    // Multiply by 2^k via repeated squaring
    var result = sum
    var kabs = k
    if kabs < 0 { kabs = 0 - kabs }
    var pow2 = 2.0
    var ka = kabs
    var acc = 1.0
    while ka > 0 {
        if ka - (ka / 2) * 2 != 0 { acc = acc * pow2 }
        pow2 = pow2 * pow2
        ka = ka / 2
    }
    if k >= 0 { result = result * acc } else { result = result / acc }
    result
}

fn gp_h_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Natural logarithm via Halley iteration: converges cubically
    if x <= 0.0 { return -1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    // Initial guess via range reduction
    var y = 0.0
    var a = x
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    while a > 2.0 { a = a * 0.5; y = y + ln2 }
    while a < 0.5 { a = a * 2.0; y = y - ln2 }

    // Now a is in [0.5, 2.0], compute ln(a) via series around 1
    let t = (a - 1.0) / (a + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var power = t
    var n = 1
    while n <= 30 {
        power = power * t2
        sum = sum + power / (2.0 * (n as f64) + 1.0)
        n = n + 1
    }
    y + 2.0 * sum
}

fn gp_h_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var a = x
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 18 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn gp_h_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    gp_h_sin(x + 1.57079632679489661923)
}

fn gp_h_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

// =============================================================================
// Inlined PRNG (for sampling)
// =============================================================================

// Linear congruential generator: x_{n+1} = (a*x_n + c) mod m
// Using Knuth's MMIX constants
fn gp_lcg_next(state: &!i64) -> i64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let a: i64 = 6364136223846793005
    let c: i64 = 1442695040888963407
    state[0] = state[0] * a + c
    state[0]
}

// Uniform on [0, 1)
fn gp_lcg_uniform(state: &!i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let raw = gp_lcg_next(state)
    var bits = raw
    if bits < 0 { bits = 0 - bits }
    // Map to [0, 1)
    let denom = 9223372036854775807.0  // 2^63 - 1
    (bits as f64) / denom
}

// Box-Muller transform: generate one standard normal variate
fn gp_box_muller(state: &!i64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var u1 = gp_lcg_uniform(state)
    if u1 < 1.0e-30 { u1 = 1.0e-30 }
    let u2 = gp_lcg_uniform(state)
    let r = gp_h_sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * gp_h_ln(u1))
    r * gp_h_cos(2.0 * gp_h_pi() * u2)
}

// =============================================================================
// Structs
// =============================================================================

struct GPData {
    x_train: [f64; 128],
    y_train: [f64; 128],
    n_train: i32,
    noise_var: f64
}

struct GPHyper {
    signal_var: f64,
    length_scale: f64,
    noise_var: f64,
    kernel_type: i32,
    extra_param: f64
}

struct GPModel {
    L: [f64; 4096],
    alpha: [f64; 128],
    x_train: [f64; 128],
    y_train: [f64; 128],
    n_train: i32,
    hyper: GPHyper,
    log_ml: f64
}

struct GPPrediction {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    std_dev: f64
}

struct GPBatchPred {
    means: [f64; 256],
    variances: [f64; 256],
    n_pred: i32
}

// =============================================================================
// Kernel functions
// =============================================================================

// RBF (squared exponential) kernel:
//   k(x,y) = signal_var * exp(-0.5 * (x-y)^2 / length_scale^2)
fn kernel_rbf(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let d = x - y
    let l = hyper.length_scale
    hyper.signal_var * gp_h_exp(0.0 - 0.5 * d * d / (l * l))
}

// Matern 3/2 kernel:
//   k(x,y) = signal_var * (1 + sqrt(3)*r/l) * exp(-sqrt(3)*r/l)
//   where r = |x - y|
fn kernel_matern32(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let r = gp_h_abs(x - y)
    let l = hyper.length_scale
    let sqrt3 = 1.7320508075688772
    let z = sqrt3 * r / l
    hyper.signal_var * (1.0 + z) * gp_h_exp(0.0 - z)
}

// Matern 5/2 kernel:
//   k(x,y) = signal_var * (1 + sqrt(5)*r/l + 5*r^2/(3*l^2)) * exp(-sqrt(5)*r/l)
fn kernel_matern52(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let r = gp_h_abs(x - y)
    let l = hyper.length_scale
    let sqrt5 = 2.2360679774997896
    let z = sqrt5 * r / l
    let z2 = 5.0 * r * r / (3.0 * l * l)
    hyper.signal_var * (1.0 + z + z2) * gp_h_exp(0.0 - z)
}

// Periodic kernel:
//   k(x,y) = signal_var * exp(-2 * sin^2(pi*|x-y|/p) / l^2)
//   where p = extra_param (period)
fn kernel_periodic(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let r = gp_h_abs(x - y)
    let l = hyper.length_scale
    let p = hyper.extra_param
    let s = gp_h_sin(gp_h_pi() * r / p)
    hyper.signal_var * gp_h_exp(0.0 - 2.0 * s * s / (l * l))
}

// Rational quadratic kernel:
//   k(x,y) = signal_var * (1 + r^2 / (2*alpha*l^2))^{-alpha}
//   where alpha = extra_param, r = |x - y|
fn kernel_rq(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let d = x - y
    let l = hyper.length_scale
    let alpha = hyper.extra_param
    let base = 1.0 + d * d / (2.0 * alpha * l * l)
    // base^{-alpha} = exp(-alpha * ln(base))
    hyper.signal_var * gp_h_exp(0.0 - alpha * gp_h_ln(base))
}

// Kernel dispatch: evaluate kernel based on kernel_type field
//   0 = RBF, 1 = Matern 3/2, 2 = Matern 5/2, 3 = periodic, 4 = rational quadratic
fn kernel_eval(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if hyper.kernel_type == 0 { return kernel_rbf(x, y, hyper) }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 1 { return kernel_matern32(x, y, hyper) }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 2 { return kernel_matern52(x, y, hyper) }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 3 { return kernel_periodic(x, y, hyper) }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 4 { return kernel_rq(x, y, hyper) }
    // Default to RBF
    kernel_rbf(x, y, hyper)
}

// =============================================================================
// Kernel matrix assembly
// =============================================================================

// Build the n x n kernel matrix K where K_ij = k(x_i, x_j) + delta_ij * noise_var.
// K is stored row-major in a flat [f64; 4096] (supports up to n=64).
fn gp_kernel_matrix(data: &GPData, hyper: &GPHyper, K: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let n = data.n_train
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            let kval = kernel_eval(data.x_train[i], data.x_train[j], hyper)
            if i == j {
                K[i * n + j] = kval + hyper.noise_var
            } else {
                K[i * n + j] = kval
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Cholesky factorization
// =============================================================================

// Cholesky factorization: L * L^T = K.
// K is n x n symmetric positive definite, stored row-major in flat array.
// L is output lower triangular, also stored row-major.
// Returns true if successful, false if K is not positive definite.
// Standard column-by-column algorithm (Golub & Van Loan).
fn gp_cholesky(K: &[f64; 4096], n: i32, L: &![f64; 4096]) -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Zero out L
    var idx = 0
    while idx < n * n { L[idx] = 0.0; idx = idx + 1 }

    var j = 0
    while j < n {
        // Compute L[j][j] = sqrt(K[j][j] - sum_{k=0}^{j-1} L[j][k]^2)
        var sum_diag = 0.0
        var k = 0
        while k < j {
            let ljk = L[j * n + k]
            sum_diag = sum_diag + ljk * ljk
            k = k + 1
        }
        let diag_val = K[j * n + j] - sum_diag
        if diag_val <= 0.0 { return false }  // Not positive definite
        L[j * n + j] = gp_h_sqrt(diag_val)

        // Compute L[i][j] for i > j:
        //   L[i][j] = (K[i][j] - sum_{k=0}^{j-1} L[i][k]*L[j][k]) / L[j][j]
        var i = j + 1
        while i < n {
            var sum_off = 0.0
            k = 0
            while k < j {
                sum_off = sum_off + L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k]
                k = k + 1
            }
            L[i * n + j] = (K[i * n + j] - sum_off) / L[j * n + j]
            i = i + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    true
}

// Solve L * L^T * x = b given the Cholesky factor L.
// Two-step: forward substitution (L * z = b), then back substitution (L^T * x = z).
fn gp_cholesky_solve(L: &[f64; 4096], b: &[f64; 128], n: i32, x: &![f64; 128]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Forward substitution: L * z = b
    var z: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < i {
            sum = sum + L[i * n + j] * z[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        z[i] = (b[i] - sum) / L[i * n + i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Back substitution: L^T * x = z
    i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n {
            sum = sum + L[j * n + i] * x[j]  // L^T[i][j] = L[j][i]
            j = j + 1
        }
        x[i] = (z[i] - sum) / L[i * n + i]
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// Forward substitution only: solve L * v = b.
// Used for computing predictive variance.
fn gp_forward_solve(L: &[f64; 4096], b: &[f64; 128], n: i32, v: &![f64; 128]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < i {
            sum = sum + L[i * n + j] * v[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        v[i] = (b[i] - sum) / L[i * n + i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// GP training
// =============================================================================

// Train a Gaussian process model: build kernel matrix, factorize, compute alpha.
//
// Given training data (x, y) and hyperparameters, computes:
//   - L: Cholesky factor of K + sigma_n^2 * I
//   - alpha = K^{-1} * y (via Cholesky solve)
//   - log marginal likelihood: -0.5*y^T*alpha - sum(log(L_ii)) - n/2*log(2*pi)
//
// Returns true on success (K was positive definite), false on failure.
fn gp_train(data: &GPData, hyper: &GPHyper, model: &!GPModel) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = data.n_train

    // Copy training data into model
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        model.x_train[i] = data.x_train[i]
        model.y_train[i] = data.y_train[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    model.n_train = n
    model.hyper.signal_var = hyper.signal_var
    model.hyper.length_scale = hyper.length_scale
    model.hyper.noise_var = hyper.noise_var
    model.hyper.kernel_type = hyper.kernel_type
    model.hyper.extra_param = hyper.extra_param

    // Build kernel matrix
    var K: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            let kval = kernel_eval(data.x_train[i], data.x_train[j], hyper)
            if i == j {
                K[i * n + j] = kval + hyper.noise_var
            } else {
                K[i * n + j] = kval
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Cholesky factorization: L * L^T = K
    let ok = gp_cholesky(&K, n, &!model.L)
    if !ok { return false }

    // Compute alpha = K^{-1} * y via Cholesky solve
    // Copy model.L to avoid simultaneous shared+mutable borrow of model
    var L_copy: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var ci = 0
    while ci < n * n { L_copy[ci] = model.L[ci]; ci = ci + 1 }
    gp_cholesky_solve(&L_copy, &data.y_train, n, &!model.alpha)

    // Compute log marginal likelihood
    //   log p(y|X,theta) = -0.5 * y^T * alpha - sum(log(L_ii)) - n/2 * log(2*pi)
    var data_fit = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        data_fit = data_fit + data.y_train[i] * model.alpha[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    data_fit = 0.0 - 0.5 * data_fit

    var complexity = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        complexity = complexity + gp_h_ln(model.L[i * n + i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    complexity = 0.0 - complexity

    let norm_const = 0.0 - 0.5 * (n as f64) * gp_h_ln(2.0 * gp_h_pi())

    model.log_ml = data_fit + complexity + norm_const
    true
}

// =============================================================================
// GP prediction
// =============================================================================

// Predict at a single test point x_star.
//
// Computes posterior mean and variance:
//   k_star = [k(x_star, x_1), ..., k(x_star, x_n)]
//   mean = k_star^T * alpha
//   v = L \ k_star  (forward substitution)
//   variance = k(x_star, x_star) - v^T * v
//   std_dev = sqrt(variance)
fn gp_predict(model: &GPModel, x_star: f64, pred: &!GPPrediction) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = model.n_train

    // Compute k_star vector
    var k_star: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        k_star[i] = kernel_eval(x_star, model.x_train[i], &model.hyper)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Posterior mean: mean = k_star^T * alpha
    var mean = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        mean = mean + k_star[i] * model.alpha[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    pred.mean = mean

    // Solve L * v = k_star (forward substitution)
    var v: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    gp_forward_solve(&model.L, &k_star, n, &!v)

    // Posterior variance: k(x_star, x_star) - v^T * v
    let k_ss = kernel_eval(x_star, x_star, &model.hyper)
    var v_dot_v = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        v_dot_v = v_dot_v + v[i] * v[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    var variance = k_ss - v_dot_v
    // Clamp to non-negative (numerical safety)
    if variance < 0.0 { variance = 0.0 }
    pred.variance = variance
    pred.std_dev = gp_h_sqrt(variance)
}

// Predict at multiple test points.
fn gp_predict_batch(model: &GPModel, x_stars: &[f64; 256], n_pred: i32,
                    batch: &!GPBatchPred) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    batch.n_pred = n_pred
    var pred: GPPrediction = GPPrediction { mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, std_dev: 0.0 }
    var i = 0
    while i < n_pred {
        gp_predict(model, x_stars[i], &!pred)
        batch.means[i] = pred.mean
        batch.variances[i] = pred.variance
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Log marginal likelihood
// =============================================================================

// Return the stored log marginal likelihood from a trained model.
fn gp_log_marginal(model: &GPModel) -> f64 {
    model.log_ml
}

// Compute log marginal likelihood for given hyperparameters without storing model.
// Useful as objective function for hyperparameter optimization.
fn gp_log_ml_at_hyper(data: &GPData, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = data.n_train

    // Build kernel matrix
    var K: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            let kval = kernel_eval(data.x_train[i], data.x_train[j], hyper)
            if i == j {
                K[i * n + j] = kval + hyper.noise_var
            } else {
                K[i * n + j] = kval
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Cholesky factorization
    var L: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    let ok = gp_cholesky(&K, n, &!L)
    if !ok {
        // Not positive definite: return very negative log ML
        return -1.0e30
    }

    // Solve for alpha = K^{-1} * y
    // Copy L to avoid simultaneous shared+mutable borrow
    var L_copy: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var ci = 0
    while ci < n * n { L_copy[ci] = L[ci]; ci = ci + 1 }
    var alpha: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    gp_cholesky_solve(&L_copy, &data.y_train, n, &!alpha)

    // Data fit term: -0.5 * y^T * alpha
    var data_fit = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        data_fit = data_fit + data.y_train[i] * alpha[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    data_fit = 0.0 - 0.5 * data_fit

    // Complexity term: -sum(log(L_ii))
    var complexity = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        complexity = complexity + gp_h_ln(L[i * n + i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    complexity = 0.0 - complexity

    // Normalization: -n/2 * log(2*pi)
    let norm_const = 0.0 - 0.5 * (n as f64) * gp_h_ln(2.0 * gp_h_pi())

    data_fit + complexity + norm_const
}

// =============================================================================
// Hyperparameter optimization via Nelder-Mead
// =============================================================================

// Negative log marginal likelihood as a function of log-space hyperparameters.
// theta = [log(signal_var), log(length_scale), log(noise_var)]
// Working in log-space ensures all hyperparameters remain positive.
fn gp_neg_lml_objective(data: &GPData, theta: &[f64; 3], kernel_type: i32,
                        extra_param: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var hyper: GPHyper = GPHyper {
        signal_var: gp_h_exp(theta[0]),
        length_scale: gp_h_exp(theta[1]),
        noise_var: gp_h_exp(theta[2]),
        kernel_type: kernel_type,
        extra_param: extra_param
    }
    0.0 - gp_log_ml_at_hyper(data, &hyper)
}

// Nelder-Mead simplex optimization for GP hyperparameters.
//
// Optimizes signal_var, length_scale, and noise_var in log-space.
// The simplex has 4 vertices (dim+1) in 3D space.
//
// Algorithm: reflection, expansion, contraction, shrink
// (Nelder & Mead, 1965; as described in Nocedal & Wright, Ch. 9)
fn gp_optimize_hyper(data: &GPData, hyper_init: &GPHyper, max_iter: i32,
                     hyper_opt: &!GPHyper) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dim = 3
    let n_verts = 4  // dim + 1

    // Nelder-Mead parameters
    let alpha_nm = 1.0   // reflection
    let gamma_nm = 2.0   // expansion
    let rho_nm = 0.5     // contraction
    let sigma_nm = 0.5   // shrink

    // Initialize simplex vertices in log-space
    // Vertices stored row-major: simplex[v * dim + d]
    var simplex: [f64; 12] = [0.0; 12]  // 4 vertices x 3 dimensions
    var f_vals: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]

    // First vertex: initial hyperparameters
    simplex[0] = gp_h_ln(hyper_init.signal_var)
    simplex[1] = gp_h_ln(hyper_init.length_scale)
    simplex[2] = gp_h_ln(hyper_init.noise_var)

    // Other vertices: perturb each dimension by a step
    let step = 0.5
    var v = 1
    while v < n_verts {
        var d = 0
        while d < dim {
            simplex[v * dim + d] = simplex[d]  // copy from vertex 0
            d = d + 1
        }
        // Perturb dimension (v-1)
        simplex[v * dim + (v - 1)] = simplex[v - 1] + step
        v = v + 1
    }

    // Evaluate objective at all vertices
    v = 0
    while v < n_verts {
        var theta: [f64; 3] = [0.0; 3]
        theta[0] = simplex[v * dim + 0]
        theta[1] = simplex[v * dim + 1]
        theta[2] = simplex[v * dim + 2]
        f_vals[v] = gp_neg_lml_objective(data, &theta, hyper_init.kernel_type,
                                         hyper_init.extra_param)
        v = v + 1
    }

    // Main optimization loop
    var iter = 0
    while iter < max_iter {
        // Find best, worst, second worst
        var i_best = 0
        var i_worst = 0
        var i_second = 0
        var v2 = 1
        while v2 < n_verts {
            if f_vals[v2] < f_vals[i_best] { i_best = v2 }
            if f_vals[v2] > f_vals[i_worst] { i_worst = v2 }
            v2 = v2 + 1
        }
        // Find second worst
        i_second = i_best
        v2 = 0
        while v2 < n_verts {
            if v2 != i_worst {
                if f_vals[v2] > f_vals[i_second] { i_second = v2 }
            }
            v2 = v2 + 1
        }

        // Convergence check: range of function values
        let f_range = gp_h_abs(f_vals[i_worst] - f_vals[i_best])
        if f_range < 1.0e-8 { iter = max_iter }  // break

        // Compute centroid of all vertices except worst
        var centroid: [f64; 3] = [0.0; 3]
        v2 = 0
        while v2 < n_verts {
            if v2 != i_worst {
                var d = 0
                while d < dim {
                    centroid[d] = centroid[d] + simplex[v2 * dim + d]
                    d = d + 1
                }
            }
            v2 = v2 + 1
        }
        var d = 0
        while d < dim {
            centroid[d] = centroid[d] / ((n_verts - 1) as f64)
            d = d + 1
        }

        // Reflection: x_r = centroid + alpha*(centroid - x_worst)
        var x_r: [f64; 3] = [0.0; 3]
        d = 0
        while d < dim {
            x_r[d] = centroid[d] + alpha_nm * (centroid[d] - simplex[i_worst * dim + d])
            d = d + 1
        }
        let f_r = gp_neg_lml_objective(data, &x_r, hyper_init.kernel_type,
                                       hyper_init.extra_param)

        if f_r < f_vals[i_best] {
            // Expansion: x_e = centroid + gamma*(x_r - centroid)
            var x_e: [f64; 3] = [0.0; 3]
            d = 0
            while d < dim {
                x_e[d] = centroid[d] + gamma_nm * (x_r[d] - centroid[d])
                d = d + 1
            }
            let f_e = gp_neg_lml_objective(data, &x_e, hyper_init.kernel_type,
                                           hyper_init.extra_param)

            if f_e < f_r {
                // Accept expansion
                d = 0
                while d < dim { simplex[i_worst * dim + d] = x_e[d]; d = d + 1 }
                f_vals[i_worst] = f_e
            } else {
                // Accept reflection
                d = 0
                while d < dim { simplex[i_worst * dim + d] = x_r[d]; d = d + 1 }
                f_vals[i_worst] = f_r
            }
        } else if f_r < f_vals[i_second] {
            // Accept reflection
            d = 0
            while d < dim { simplex[i_worst * dim + d] = x_r[d]; d = d + 1 }
            f_vals[i_worst] = f_r
        } else {
            // Contraction
            if f_r < f_vals[i_worst] {
                // Outside contraction: x_c = centroid + rho*(x_r - centroid)
                var x_c: [f64; 3] = [0.0; 3]
                d = 0
                while d < dim {
                    x_c[d] = centroid[d] + rho_nm * (x_r[d] - centroid[d])
                    d = d + 1
                }
                let f_c = gp_neg_lml_objective(data, &x_c, hyper_init.kernel_type,
                                               hyper_init.extra_param)
                if f_c <= f_r {
                    d = 0
                    while d < dim { simplex[i_worst * dim + d] = x_c[d]; d = d + 1 }
                    f_vals[i_worst] = f_c
                } else {
                    // Shrink: move all vertices except best toward best
                    v2 = 0
                    while v2 < n_verts {
                        if v2 != i_best {
                            d = 0
                            while d < dim {
