pub fn sed64_add(a: Sedenion64, b: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 {
    Sedenion64 {
        e0: a.e0 + b.e0, e1: a.e1 + b.e1, e2: a.e2 + b.e2, e3: a.e3 + b.e3,
        e4: a.e4 + b.e4, e5: a.e5 + b.e5, e6: a.e6 + b.e6, e7: a.e7 + b.e7,
        e8: a.e8 + b.e8, e9: a.e9 + b.e9, e10: a.e10 + b.e10, e11: a.e11 + b.e11,
        e12: a.e12 + b.e12, e13: a.e13 + b.e13, e14: a.e14 + b.e14, e15: a.e15 + b.e15
    }
}

pub fn sed64_sub(a: Sedenion64, b: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 {
    Sedenion64 {
        e0: a.e0 - b.e0, e1: a.e1 - b.e1, e2: a.e2 - b.e2, e3: a.e3 - b.e3,
        e4: a.e4 - b.e4, e5: a.e5 - b.e5, e6: a.e6 - b.e6, e7: a.e7 - b.e7,
        e8: a.e8 - b.e8, e9: a.e9 - b.e9, e10: a.e10 - b.e10, e11: a.e11 - b.e11,
        e12: a.e12 - b.e12, e13: a.e13 - b.e13, e14: a.e14 - b.e14, e15: a.e15 - b.e15
    }
}

pub fn sed64_scale(s: Sedenion64, k: f64) -> Sedenion64 {
    Sedenion64 {
        e0: s.e0 * k, e1: s.e1 * k, e2: s.e2 * k, e3: s.e3 * k,
        e4: s.e4 * k, e5: s.e5 * k, e6: s.e6 * k, e7: s.e7 * k,
        e8: s.e8 * k, e9: s.e9 * k, e10: s.e10 * k, e11: s.e11 * k,
        e12: s.e12 * k, e13: s.e13 * k, e14: s.e14 * k, e15: s.e15 * k
    }
}

pub fn sed64_neg(s: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 {
    Sedenion64 {
        e0: 0.0 - s.e0, e1: 0.0 - s.e1, e2: 0.0 - s.e2, e3: 0.0 - s.e3,
        e4: 0.0 - s.e4, e5: 0.0 - s.e5, e6: 0.0 - s.e6, e7: 0.0 - s.e7,
        e8: 0.0 - s.e8, e9: 0.0 - s.e9, e10: 0.0 - s.e10, e11: 0.0 - s.e11,
        e12: 0.0 - s.e12, e13: 0.0 - s.e13, e14: 0.0 - s.e14, e15: 0.0 - s.e15
    }
}

// Conjugation: conj(alpha, beta) = (conj(alpha), -beta)
// Equivalently: negate all imaginary components e1..e15, keep e0
pub fn sed64_conj(s: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 {
    Sedenion64 {
        e0: s.e0,
        e1: 0.0 - s.e1, e2: 0.0 - s.e2, e3: 0.0 - s.e3,
        e4: 0.0 - s.e4, e5: 0.0 - s.e5, e6: 0.0 - s.e6, e7: 0.0 - s.e7,
        e8: 0.0 - s.e8, e9: 0.0 - s.e9, e10: 0.0 - s.e10, e11: 0.0 - s.e11,
        e12: 0.0 - s.e12, e13: 0.0 - s.e13, e14: 0.0 - s.e14, e15: 0.0 - s.e15
    }
}

// Norm squared: |z|^2 = sum of squares of all components
pub fn sed64_norm_sq(s: Sedenion64) -> f64 {
    s.e0*s.e0 + s.e1*s.e1 + s.e2*s.e2 + s.e3*s.e3 +
    s.e4*s.e4 + s.e5*s.e5 + s.e6*s.e6 + s.e7*s.e7 +
    s.e8*s.e8 + s.e9*s.e9 + s.e10*s.e10 + s.e11*s.e11 +
    s.e12*s.e12 + s.e13*s.e13 + s.e14*s.e14 + s.e15*s.e15
}

// Euclidean norm
fn sed64_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

fn sed64_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn sed64_ln(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Natural log via Halley's method: ln(x) where x > 0
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    // Initial guess using exponent decomposition
    var y = 0.0
    var t = x
    if t > 1.0 {
        while t > 2.718281828 {
            t = t / 2.718281828
            y = y + 1.0
        }
        y = y + (t - 1.0) / t
    } else {
        while t < 0.367879441 {
            t = t * 2.718281828
            y = y - 1.0
        }
        y = y + (t - 1.0) / t
    }
    // Newton refinement for exp(y) = x  =>  y = y + (x - exp(y))/exp(y)
    // Use exp approximation
    var i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        // exp(y) via Taylor
        let ey = sed64_exp_approx(y)
        y = y + (x - ey) / ey
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y
}

fn sed64_exp_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // exp(x) via range reduction + polynomial
    var k = 0
    var r = x
    while r > 1.0 {
        r = r * 0.5
        k = k + 1
    }
    while r < -1.0 {
        r = r * 0.5
        k = k + 1
    }
    // Taylor: 1 + r + r^2/2 + r^3/6 + r^4/24 + r^5/120 + r^6/720
    let r2 = r * r
    let r3 = r2 * r
    let r4 = r3 * r
    let r5 = r4 * r
    let r6 = r5 * r
    var result = 1.0 + r + r2 * 0.5 + r3 / 6.0 + r4 / 24.0 + r5 / 120.0 + r6 / 720.0
    var j = 0
    while j < k {
        result = result * result
        j = j + 1
    }
    return result
}

pub fn sed64_norm(s: Sedenion64) -> f64 {
    sed64_sqrt(sed64_norm_sq(s))
}

// Dot product
pub fn sed64_dot(a: Sedenion64, b: Sedenion64) -> f64 {
    a.e0*b.e0 + a.e1*b.e1 + a.e2*b.e2 + a.e3*b.e3 +
    a.e4*b.e4 + a.e5*b.e5 + a.e6*b.e6 + a.e7*b.e7 +
    a.e8*b.e8 + a.e9*b.e9 + a.e10*b.e10 + a.e11*b.e11 +
    a.e12*b.e12 + a.e13*b.e13 + a.e14*b.e14 + a.e15*b.e15
}

// ============================================================================
// MULTIPLICATION (Cayley-Dickson)
// ============================================================================
// (a,b) * (c,d) = (a*c - conj(d)*b, d*a + b*conj(c))
// Delegates to cd_product_16 in cayley_dickson.sio

pub fn sed64_mul(a: Sedenion64, b: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 {
    let r = cd_product_16(
        a.e0, a.e1, a.e2, a.e3, a.e4, a.e5, a.e6, a.e7,
        a.e8, a.e9, a.e10, a.e11, a.e12, a.e13, a.e14, a.e15,
        b.e0, b.e1, b.e2, b.e3, b.e4, b.e5, b.e6, b.e7,
        b.e8, b.e9, b.e10, b.e11, b.e12, b.e13, b.e14, b.e15
    )
    Sedenion64 {
        e0: r.r0, e1: r.r1, e2: r.r2, e3: r.r3,
        e4: r.r4, e5: r.r5, e6: r.r6, e7: r.r7,
        e8: r.r8, e9: r.r9, e10: r.r10, e11: r.r11,
        e12: r.r12, e13: r.r13, e14: r.r14, e15: r.r15
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ALGEBRAIC PRODUCTS
// ============================================================================

// Jordan product: {a,b} = ab + ba (always commutative)
pub fn sed64_jordan(a: Sedenion64, b: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 {
    sed64_add(sed64_mul(a, b), sed64_mul(b, a))
}

// Commutator: [a,b] = ab - ba (zero iff a,b commute)
pub fn sed64_commutator(a: Sedenion64, b: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 {
    sed64_sub(sed64_mul(a, b), sed64_mul(b, a))
}

// Associator: [a,b,c] = (ab)c - a(bc)
pub fn sed64_associator(a: Sedenion64, b: Sedenion64, c: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 {
    sed64_sub(sed64_mul(sed64_mul(a, b), c), sed64_mul(a, sed64_mul(b, c)))
}

// ============================================================================
// MULTIPLICATION MATRICES (16x16)
// ============================================================================
// These are the hot path for the Jacobian recursion in the FSNN orbit.

// Left multiplication matrix L_a: column j = a * e_j
// L_a[i][j] = component i of (a * basis(j))
// Stored row-major in [f64; 256]: index = i * 16 + j
pub fn sed64_left_mul_matrix(a: Sedenion64) -> [f64; 256] {
    var L = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j < 16 {
        let ej = sed64_basis(j)
        let col = sed64_mul(a, ej)
        L[0 * 16 + j] = col.e0
        L[1 * 16 + j] = col.e1
        L[2 * 16 + j] = col.e2
        L[3 * 16 + j] = col.e3
        L[4 * 16 + j] = col.e4
        L[5 * 16 + j] = col.e5
        L[6 * 16 + j] = col.e6
        L[7 * 16 + j] = col.e7
        L[8 * 16 + j] = col.e8
        L[9 * 16 + j] = col.e9
        L[10 * 16 + j] = col.e10
        L[11 * 16 + j] = col.e11
        L[12 * 16 + j] = col.e12
        L[13 * 16 + j] = col.e13
        L[14 * 16 + j] = col.e14
        L[15 * 16 + j] = col.e15
        j = j + 1
    }
    return L
}

// Right multiplication matrix R_a: column j = e_j * a
pub fn sed64_right_mul_matrix(a: Sedenion64) -> [f64; 256] {
    var R = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j < 16 {
        let ej = sed64_basis(j)
        let col = sed64_mul(ej, a)
        R[0 * 16 + j] = col.e0
        R[1 * 16 + j] = col.e1
        R[2 * 16 + j] = col.e2
        R[3 * 16 + j] = col.e3
        R[4 * 16 + j] = col.e4
        R[5 * 16 + j] = col.e5
        R[6 * 16 + j] = col.e6
        R[7 * 16 + j] = col.e7
        R[8 * 16 + j] = col.e8
        R[9 * 16 + j] = col.e9
        R[10 * 16 + j] = col.e10
        R[11 * 16 + j] = col.e11
        R[12 * 16 + j] = col.e12
        R[13 * 16 + j] = col.e13
        R[14 * 16 + j] = col.e14
        R[15 * 16 + j] = col.e15
        j = j + 1
    }
    return R
}

// Jordan operator matrix J_a = L_a + R_a
// J_a * x = a*x + x*a (Jordan product as matrix-vector multiply)
pub fn sed64_jordan_matrix(a: Sedenion64) -> [f64; 256] {
    let L = sed64_left_mul_matrix(a)
    let R = sed64_right_mul_matrix(a)
    var J = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < 256 {
        J[i] = L[i] + R[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return J
}

// ============================================================================
// ZERO-DIVISOR CHECK
// ============================================================================
// A sedenion z = alpha + beta*l is a zero divisor iff (Moreno 1998):
//   (1) |alpha| = |beta|           (norm equality)
//   (2) <alpha, beta> = 0          (orthogonality of the two 8D halves)
// Both conditions are necessary and sufficient.

pub fn sed64_is_zero_divisor(s: Sedenion64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let alpha_nsq = oct64_norm_sq_components(s.e0, s.e1, s.e2, s.e3, s.e4, s.e5, s.e6, s.e7)
    let beta_nsq = oct64_norm_sq_components(s.e8, s.e9, s.e10, s.e11, s.e12, s.e13, s.e14, s.e15)
    let a_norm = sed64_sqrt(alpha_nsq)
    let b_norm = sed64_sqrt(beta_nsq)
    // Condition 1: |alpha| ~ |beta|
    let norm_diff = sed64_abs(a_norm - b_norm)
    if norm_diff >= tol * (a_norm + b_norm + 1e-15) { return false }
    // Condition 2: <alpha, beta> ~ 0  (Euclidean dot product of the two halves)
    let inner = s.e0*s.e8 + s.e1*s.e9 + s.e2*s.e10 + s.e3*s.e11 +
                s.e4*s.e12 + s.e5*s.e13 + s.e6*s.e14 + s.e7*s.e15
    sed64_abs(inner) < tol * (a_norm * b_norm + 1e-15)
}

// ============================================================================
// ARRAY CONVERSIONS
// ============================================================================

pub fn sed64_to_array(s: Sedenion64) -> [f64; 16] {
    var arr = [0.0; 16]
    arr[0] = s.e0
    arr[1] = s.e1
    arr[2] = s.e2
    arr[3] = s.e3
    arr[4] = s.e4
    arr[5] = s.e5
    arr[6] = s.e6
    arr[7] = s.e7
    arr[8] = s.e8
    arr[9] = s.e9
    arr[10] = s.e10
    arr[11] = s.e11
    arr[12] = s.e12
    arr[13] = s.e13
    arr[14] = s.e14
    arr[15] = s.e15
    return arr
}

pub fn sed64_from_array(c: [f64; 16]) -> Sedenion64 {
    Sedenion64 {
        e0: c[0], e1: c[1], e2: c[2], e3: c[3],
        e4: c[4], e5: c[5], e6: c[6], e7: c[7],
        e8: c[8], e9: c[9], e10: c[10], e11: c[11],
        e12: c[12], e13: c[13], e14: c[14], e15: c[15]
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// NORMALIZATION AND INVERSE
// ============================================================================

pub fn sed64_normalize(s: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 with Panic {
    let n = sed64_norm(s)
    if n < 1e-30 {
        sed64_one()
    } else {
        sed64_scale(s, 1.0 / n)
    }
}

// Putative inverse: conj(z) / |z|^2
// WARNING: undefined at zero divisors
pub fn sed64_putative_inv(s: Sedenion64) -> Sedenion64 with Panic {
    let nsq = sed64_norm_sq(s)
    if nsq < 1e-30 {
        sed64_one()
    } else {
        sed64_scale(sed64_conj(s), 1.0 / nsq)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ZERO-DIVISOR GEOMETRY
// ============================================================================

// Analytic distance to the zero-divisor variety Z ⊂ S (Moreno 1998).
// z = (α, β) is a zero divisor iff |α| = |β| AND ⟨α, β⟩ = 0.
// This function returns a non-negative distance that is 0 exactly on Z.
// O(1), deterministic — use this in FSNN feature pipelines instead of
// Monte Carlo estimators.
//
// Formula: combined relative deviation from the two Moreno conditions.
//   norm_imb  = |‖α‖ − ‖β‖| / (‖α‖ + ‖β‖ + ε)     — 0 when ‖α‖ = ‖β‖
//   orth_viol = |⟨α, β⟩| / (‖α‖ · ‖β‖ + ε)          — 0 when α ⊥ β
//   distance  = sqrt(norm_imb² + orth_viol²)
pub fn sed64_zero_divisor_distance(s: Sedenion64) -> f64 {
    let alpha_nsq = s.e0*s.e0 + s.e1*s.e1 + s.e2*s.e2 + s.e3*s.e3 +
                    s.e4*s.e4 + s.e5*s.e5 + s.e6*s.e6 + s.e7*s.e7
    let beta_nsq  = s.e8*s.e8 + s.e9*s.e9 + s.e10*s.e10 + s.e11*s.e11 +
                    s.e12*s.e12 + s.e13*s.e13 + s.e14*s.e14 + s.e15*s.e15
    let a_norm = sed64_sqrt(alpha_nsq)
    let b_norm = sed64_sqrt(beta_nsq)
    let norm_sum = a_norm + b_norm + 1e-30
    let norm_imb = sed64_abs(a_norm - b_norm) / norm_sum
    let inner = s.e0*s.e8 + s.e1*s.e9 + s.e2*s.e10 + s.e3*s.e11 +
                s.e4*s.e12 + s.e5*s.e13 + s.e6*s.e14 + s.e7*s.e15
    let orth_viol = sed64_abs(inner) / (a_norm * b_norm + 1e-30)
    sed64_sqrt(norm_imb * norm_imb + orth_viol * orth_viol)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/spectral.sio ===
// stdlib/math/spectral.sio — Spectral methods for differential equations
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto collocation points
//   Chebyshev differentiation matrices (1st and 2nd order)
//   Mapped Chebyshev methods on [a,b]
//   Spectral BVP solver for 2nd-order ODEs
//   Spectral eigenvalue solver (Sturm-Liouville)
//   Fourier differentiation matrices (periodic domains)
//   Clenshaw-Curtis quadrature
//   Spectral interpolation
//
// References:
//   Trefethen (2000): "Spectral Methods in MATLAB"
//   Boyd (2001): "Chebyshev and Fourier Spectral Methods"
//   Canuto et al. (2006): "Spectral Methods: Fundamentals"

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (all prefixed sp_ to avoid collisions)
// =============================================================================

fn sp_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn sp_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn sp_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn sp_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn sp_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn sp_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var a = x
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 18 { term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64; sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    sum
}

fn sp_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    sp_sin(x + 1.57079632679489661923)
}

fn sp_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Range reduction: e^x = 2^k * e^r, where r = x - k*ln(2)
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = x / ln2
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2
    // Taylor series for e^r, |r| < ln(2)
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    // Multiply by 2^k
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    } else {
        var i = 0
        while i < (0 - k) { result = result * 0.5; i = i + 1 }
    }
    result
}

fn sp_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    // Reduce to [1, 2): x = m * 2^e, ln(x) = ln(m) + e*ln(2)
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var m = x
    var e: i32 = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m * 0.5; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 1.0 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    // Now m in [1, 2). Use series: ln(m) = 2 * sum_{k=0}^{inf} ((m-1)/(m+1))^{2k+1} / (2k+1)
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var power = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { power = power * t2; sum = sum + power / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * ln2
}

// =============================================================================
// Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting
// =============================================================================

// Solve A*x = b for x, where A is n x n stored row-major in flat array.
// Overwrites A and b in place; result stored in x.
fn sp_gauss_solve(A: &![f64; 4096], b: &![f64; 256], x: &![f64; 256], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Forward elimination with partial pivoting
    var col = 0
    while col < n {
        // Find pivot
        var max_val = sp_abs(A[col * n + col])
        var max_row = col
        var row = col + 1
        while row < n {
            let val = sp_abs(A[row * n + col])
            if val > max_val { max_val = val; max_row = row }
            row = row + 1
        }

        // Swap rows col and max_row in A and b
        if max_row != col {
            var j = 0
            while j < n {
                let tmp = A[col * n + j]
                A[col * n + j] = A[max_row * n + j]
                A[max_row * n + j] = tmp
                j = j + 1
            }
            let tmp_b = b[col]
            b[col] = b[max_row]
            b[max_row] = tmp_b
        }

        // Eliminate below
        let pivot = A[col * n + col]
        if sp_abs(pivot) < 1.0e-30 {
            col = col + 1
            // Skip singular column
        } else {
            row = col + 1
            while row < n {
                let factor = A[row * n + col] / pivot
                var j = col + 1
                while j < n {
                    A[row * n + j] = A[row * n + j] - factor * A[col * n + j]
                    j = j + 1
                }
                A[row * n + col] = 0.0
                b[row] = b[row] - factor * b[col]
                row = row + 1
            }
            col = col + 1
        }
    }

    // Back substitution
    var i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum = b[i]
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n { sum = sum - A[i * n + j] * x[j]; j = j + 1 }
        if sp_abs(A[i * n + i]) < 1.0e-30 {
            x[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            x[i] = sum / A[i * n + i]
        }
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto nodes
// =============================================================================

// Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto collocation points on [-1, 1].
// x_j = cos(j * pi / n), j = 0, ..., n. Stores n+1 points in x[0..n].
fn cheb_nodes(n: i32, x: &![f64; 256]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        x[j] = sp_cos((j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64))
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto nodes mapped to [a, b].
// x_j = (a+b)/2 + (b-a)/2 * cos(j * pi / n), j = 0, ..., n.
fn cheb_nodes_ab(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64, x: &![f64; 256]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
    let half = 0.5 * (b - a)
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        x[j] = mid + half * sp_cos((j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64))
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Chebyshev differentiation matrix (1st order)
// =============================================================================

// Build (n+1) x (n+1) Chebyshev differentiation matrix on [-1, 1].
// Stored row-major in D[i * (n+1) + j]. Uses Trefethen's formula.
//
// D_{ij} = c_i * (-1)^{i+j} / (c_j * (x_i - x_j))   for i != j
// D_{ii} = -x_i / (2 * (1 - x_i^2))                   for 0 < i < n
// D_{00} = (2*n^2 + 1) / 6
// D_{nn} = -(2*n^2 + 1) / 6
//
// where c_0 = c_n = 2, c_j = 1 otherwise.
fn cheb_diffmat(n: i32, D: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let np = n + 1

    // Compute CGL nodes
    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n { x[j] = sp_cos((j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64)); j = j + 1 }

    // c_i coefficients: c_0 = c_n = 2, rest = 1
    var c: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i <= n { c[i] = 1.0; i = i + 1 }
    c[0] = 2.0
    c[n] = 2.0

    // Fill matrix
    i = 0
    while i <= n {
        j = 0
        while j <= n {
            if i != j {
                // (-1)^{i+j}
                var sign = 1.0
                if (i + j) - ((i + j) / 2) * 2 != 0 { sign = 0.0 - 1.0 }
                D[i * np + j] = c[i] * sign / (c[j] * (x[i] - x[j]))
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Diagonal entries for interior points: D_{ii} = -x_i / (2*(1 - x_i^2))
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        D[i * np + i] = 0.0 - x[i] / (2.0 * (1.0 - x[i] * x[i]))
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Corner entries
    let n2 = (n as f64) * (n as f64)
    D[0] = (2.0 * n2 + 1.0) / 6.0
    D[n * np + n] = 0.0 - (2.0 * n2 + 1.0) / 6.0
}

// =============================================================================
// Chebyshev differentiation matrix (2nd order)
// =============================================================================

// Second derivative matrix: D2 = D * D (matrix product).
// Both are (n+1) x (n+1) stored row-major.
fn cheb_diffmat2(n: i32, D2: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let np = n + 1

    // Build D1 first
    var D1: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    cheb_diffmat(n, &!D1)

    // Matrix multiply: D2 = D1 * D1
    var i = 0
    while i < np {
        var j = 0
        while j < np {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < np {
                sum = sum + D1[i * np + k] * D1[k * np + j]
                k = k + 1
            }
            D2[i * np + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Mapped Chebyshev differentiation matrices on [a, b]
// =============================================================================

// First derivative matrix mapped to [a, b]: D_ab = (2/(b-a)) * D.
fn cheb_diffmat_ab(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64, D: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let np = n + 1
    cheb_diffmat(n, D)
    let scale = 2.0 / (b - a)
    var i = 0
    while i < np {
        var j = 0
        while j < np {
            D[i * np + j] = D[i * np + j] * scale
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Second derivative matrix mapped to [a, b]: D2_ab = (2/(b-a))^2 * D2.
fn cheb_diffmat2_ab(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64, D2: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let np = n + 1
    cheb_diffmat2(n, D2)
    let scale = 2.0 / (b - a)
    let scale2 = scale * scale
    var i = 0
    while i < np {
        var j = 0
        while j < np {
            D2[i * np + j] = D2[i * np + j] * scale2
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Spectral BVP solver for 2nd-order ODEs
// =============================================================================

// Solve:  -u''(x) + p(x)*u'(x) + q(x)*u(x) = f(x)  on [a, b]
// with boundary conditions u(a) = alpha, u(b) = beta.
//
// Method: Chebyshev collocation. Build the operator matrix
//   L = -D2 + diag(p(x_j)) * D1 + diag(q(x_j))
// at n+1 Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto nodes mapped to [a, b].
// Replace rows 0 and n with boundary conditions, then solve the linear system.
//
// Result: u[0..n] contains the solution at the n+1 CGL nodes.
fn spectral_bvp_2nd(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64,
                    p_fn: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    q_fn: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    f_fn: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    alpha: f64, beta: f64,
                    u: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let np = n + 1

    // Compute CGL nodes on [a, b]
    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes_ab(n, a, b, &!x)

    // Build D1 and D2 on [a, b]
    var D1: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var D2: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    cheb_diffmat_ab(n, a, b, &!D1)
    cheb_diffmat2_ab(n, a, b, &!D2)

    // Build operator matrix L = -D2 + diag(p) * D1 + diag(q)
    var L: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < np {
        let p_val = p_fn(x[i])
        let q_val = q_fn(x[i])
        var j = 0
        while j < np {
            L[i * np + j] = 0.0 - D2[i * np + j] + p_val * D1[i * np + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        // Add q(x_i) on diagonal
        L[i * np + i] = L[i * np + i] + q_val
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Build RHS
    var rhs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    i = 0
    while i < np { rhs[i] = f_fn(x[i]); i = i + 1 }

    // Apply boundary conditions: replace row 0 and row n
    // Row 0: u(x_0) = alpha. CGL node 0 is cos(0) = 1 -> maps to rightmost
    // Note: CGL nodes are ordered x_0 > x_1 > ... > x_n (decreasing).
    // On [a, b], x_0 = b, x_n = a (since cos(0)=1 -> right end, cos(pi)=-1 -> left end).
    // So u(x_0) = beta (right BC), u(x_n) = alpha (left BC).
    var j = 0
    while j < np { L[0 * np + j] = 0.0; j = j + 1 }
    L[0 * np + 0] = 1.0
    rhs[0] = beta

    j = 0
    while j < np { L[n * np + j] = 0.0; j = j + 1 }
    L[n * np + n] = 1.0
    rhs[n] = alpha

    // Solve the linear system L * u = rhs
    sp_gauss_solve(&!L, &!rhs, u, np)
}

// =============================================================================
// Arctangent helpers (needed by eigenvalue solver — must precede caller)
// =============================================================================

// Core atan Taylor series for |t| <= 1: atan(t) = t - t^3/3 + t^5/5 - ...
fn sp_atan_core(t: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var power = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        power = 0.0 - power * t2
        sum = sum + power / (2 * k + 1) as f64
        k = k + 1
    }
    sum
}

// Arctangent via series: atan(t) for any t.
// Uses identity: for |t| > 1, atan(t) = pi/2 - atan(1/t).
fn sp_atan_series(t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sp_abs(t) > 1.0 {
        let inv = 1.0 / t
        let a = sp_atan_core(inv)
        if t > 0.0 { return sp_pi() / 2.0 - a }
        return 0.0 - sp_pi() / 2.0 - a
    }
    sp_atan_core(t)
}

// Helper: atan2 via series.
fn sp_atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sp_abs(x) < 1.0e-30 {
        if y > 0.0 { return sp_pi() / 2.0 }
        if y < 0.0 { return 0.0 - sp_pi() / 2.0 }
        return 0.0
    }
    let ratio = y / x
    var a = sp_atan_series(ratio)
    if x < 0.0 {
        if y >= 0.0 { a = a + sp_pi() } else { a = a - sp_pi() }
    }
    a
}

// =============================================================================
// Spectral eigenvalue solver (Sturm-Liouville)
// =============================================================================

// Find eigenvalues of the Sturm-Liouville problem:
//   -u''(x) + V(x)*u(x) = lambda * u(x)  on [a, b]
//   u(a) = 0, u(b) = 0
//
// Method: Build the operator L = -D2 + diag(V(x_j)) at interior CGL nodes
// (rows/columns 1..n-1, removing boundary points 0 and n).
// Solve the (n-1) x (n-1) symmetric eigenvalue problem using the Jacobi method.
//
// Returns sorted eigenvalues in eigenvalues[0..n_found-1].
fn spectral_eigval(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64,
                   V_fn: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   eigenvalues: &![f64; 256],
                   n_found: &!i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let np = n + 1

    // Compute CGL nodes on [a, b]
    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes_ab(n, a, b, &!x)

    // Build D2 on [a, b]
    var D2: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    cheb_diffmat2_ab(n, a, b, &!D2)

    // Build reduced operator matrix: L_int = -D2_int + diag(V)
    // Interior points are indices 1..n-1, so dimension is m = n-1
    let m = n - 1
    if m <= 0 { n_found[0] = 0; return }

    // Extract interior block into a flat m x m matrix
    var L: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < m {
        var j = 0
        while j < m {
            // Map interior index (i, j) to full index (i+1, j+1)
            L[i * m + j] = 0.0 - D2[(i + 1) * np + (j + 1)]
            j = j + 1
        }
        // Add potential on diagonal
        L[i * m + i] = L[i * m + i] + V_fn(x[i + 1])
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Jacobi eigenvalue algorithm for symmetric matrices
    // Iteratively apply Givens rotations to diagonalize L
    var max_iter = 100 * m * m
    if max_iter > 100000 { max_iter = 100000 }
    var iter = 0
    while iter < max_iter {
        // Find largest off-diagonal element
        var max_off = 0.0
        var p = 0
        var q = 1
        i = 0
        while i < m {
            var j = i + 1
            while j < m {
                let val = sp_abs(L[i * m + j])
                if val > max_off { max_off = val; p = i; q = j }
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Convergence check
        if max_off < 1.0e-12 { iter = max_iter }
        else {
            // Compute rotation angle
            let app = L[p * m + p]
            let aqq = L[q * m + q]
            let apq = L[p * m + q]

            var theta = 0.0
            let diff = aqq - app
            if sp_abs(diff) < 1.0e-30 {
                theta = sp_pi() / 4.0
            } else {
                theta = 0.5 * sp_atan2(2.0 * apq, diff)
            }

            let cos_t = sp_cos(theta)
            let sin_t = sp_sin(theta)

            // Apply rotation: update rows and columns p, q
            // For each row k: update L[k,p] and L[k,q]
            var k = 0
            while k < m {
                if k != p && k != q {
                    let lkp = L[k * m + p]
                    let lkq = L[k * m + q]
                    L[k * m + p] = cos_t * lkp + sin_t * lkq
                    L[k * m + q] = 0.0 - sin_t * lkp + cos_t * lkq
                    L[p * m + k] = L[k * m + p]
                    L[q * m + k] = L[k * m + q]
                }
                k = k + 1
            }

            // Update diagonal and off-diagonal at (p, q)
            let new_pp = cos_t * cos_t * app + 2.0 * cos_t * sin_t * apq + sin_t * sin_t * aqq
            let new_qq = sin_t * sin_t * app - 2.0 * cos_t * sin_t * apq + cos_t * cos_t * aqq
            L[p * m + p] = new_pp
            L[q * m + q] = new_qq
            L[p * m + q] = 0.0
            L[q * m + p] = 0.0

            iter = iter + 1
        }
    }

    // Extract eigenvalues from diagonal
    i = 0
    while i < m { eigenvalues[i] = L[i * m + i]; i = i + 1 }

    // Sort eigenvalues (insertion sort, ascending)
    i = 1
    while i < m {
        let key = eigenvalues[i]
        var j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 && eigenvalues[j] > key {
            eigenvalues[j + 1] = eigenvalues[j]
            j = j - 1
        }
        eigenvalues[j + 1] = key
        i = i + 1
    }

    n_found[0] = m
}

// =============================================================================
// Fourier differentiation matrix (1st order)
// =============================================================================

// n x n differentiation matrix for periodic domain [0, 2*pi) with h = 2*pi/n.
// D_{ij} = 0.5 * (-1)^{i+j} * cot((i-j)*h/2)   for i != j
// D_{ii} = 0
//
// Reference: Trefethen (2000), Chapter 3.
fn fourier_diffmat(n: i32, D: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let h = 2.0 * sp_pi() / (n as f64)

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            if i == j {
                D[i * n + j] = 0.0
            } else {
                let diff = i - j
                // (-1)^{i+j}: same parity as diff
                var sign = 1.0
                let abs_diff = if diff > 0 { diff } else { 0 - diff }
                if abs_diff - (abs_diff / 2) * 2 != 0 { sign = 0.0 - 1.0 }

                let arg = (diff as f64) * h / 2.0
                let sin_val = sp_sin(arg)
                let cos_val = sp_cos(arg)

                if sp_abs(sin_val) < 1.0e-30 {
                    D[i * n + j] = 0.0
                } else {
                    D[i * n + j] = 0.5 * sign * cos_val / sin_val
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Fourier differentiation matrix (2nd order)
// =============================================================================

// Second derivative matrix for periodic domain [0, 2*pi).
// D2_{ij} = -0.5 * (-1)^{i+j} / sin^2((i-j)*h/2)   for i != j
// D2_{ii} = -(n^2 - 1)/12 for odd n, or -(n^2)/12 for even n.
//
// Reference: Trefethen (2000), Eq. (3.7).
fn fourier_diffmat2(n: i32, D2: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let h = 2.0 * sp_pi() / (n as f64)

    // Determine if n is even or odd
    let n_even = (n - (n / 2) * 2) == 0

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            if i == j {
                if n_even {
                    D2[i * n + j] = 0.0 - (n as f64) * (n as f64) / 12.0
                } else {
                    D2[i * n + j] = 0.0 - ((n as f64) * (n as f64) - 1.0) / 12.0
                }
            } else {
                let diff = i - j
                let abs_diff = if diff > 0 { diff } else { 0 - diff }
                var sign = 1.0
                if abs_diff - (abs_diff / 2) * 2 != 0 { sign = 0.0 - 1.0 }

                let arg = (diff as f64) * h / 2.0
                let sin_val = sp_sin(arg)
                let sin2 = sin_val * sin_val

                if sp_abs(sin2) < 1.0e-30 {
                    D2[i * n + j] = 0.0
                } else {
                    D2[i * n + j] = 0.0 - 0.5 * sign / sin2
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Clenshaw-Curtis quadrature weights
// =============================================================================

// Compute Clenshaw-Curtis quadrature weights for n+1 Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto
// points on [-1, 1].
//
// w_j = (c_j / n) * sum_{k=0}^{floor(n/2)} b_k * cos(2*k*j*pi/n)
// where b_0 = 1, b_{n/2} = 1, b_k = 2 for 0 < k < n/2,
// and the sum terms include the factor 1/(1 - 4*k^2).
//
// Reference: Trefethen (2000), Chapter 12; Waldvogel (2006).
fn cc_weights(n: i32, w: &![f64; 256]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Special cases
    if n == 0 { w[0] = 2.0; return }
    if n == 1 { w[0] = 1.0; w[1] = 1.0; return }

    let np = n + 1

    // Compute theta_j values
    // theta_j = j * pi / n

    // Compute weights using the formula:
    // w_j = (2/n) * sum_{k=0}^{n/2} '' cos(2*k*j*pi / n) / (1 - 4*k^2)
    // where '' means first and last terms halved.
    let half_n = n / 2

    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var k = 0
        while k <= half_n {
            let denom = 1.0 - 4.0 * (k as f64) * (k as f64)
            let theta = 2.0 * (k as f64) * (j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64)
            var term = sp_cos(theta) / denom

            // Double-prime sum: halve first and last terms
            if k == 0 { term = term * 0.5 }
            if k == half_n { term = term * 0.5 }

            sum = sum + term
            k = k + 1
        }

        w[j] = 2.0 * sum / (n as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Clenshaw-Curtis integration on [-1, 1]
// =============================================================================

// Integrate f(x) on [-1, 1] given function values at n+1 CGL points.
// f_vals[j] = f(x_j) where x_j = cos(j*pi/n), j = 0, ..., n.
// Returns the integral approximation.
fn cc_integrate(f_vals: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var w: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cc_weights(n, &!w)

    var sum = 0.0
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        sum = sum + w[j] * f_vals[j]
        j = j + 1
    }
    sum
}

// =============================================================================
// Clenshaw-Curtis integration on [a, b]
// =============================================================================

// Integrate f(x) on [a, b] via Clenshaw-Curtis.
// f_vals[j] = f(x_j) where x_j are CGL nodes mapped to [a, b].
// Scaling: integral on [a,b] = (b-a)/2 * integral on [-1,1].
fn cc_integrate_ab(f_vals: &[f64; 256], n: i32, a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let scale = 0.5 * (b - a)
    let I_ref = cc_integrate(f_vals, n)
    scale * I_ref
}

// =============================================================================
// Spectral (barycentric Chebyshev) interpolation on [-1, 1]
// =============================================================================

// Barycentric Chebyshev interpolation at an arbitrary point x in [-1, 1].
// f_vals[j] = f(x_j) at the n+1 CGL nodes x_j = cos(j*pi/n), j = 0, ..., n.
//
// Uses the second barycentric form with weights:
//   w_j = (-1)^j * delta_j, where delta_0 = delta_n = 0.5, delta_j = 1 otherwise.
//
// p(x) = sum_j w_j * f_j / (x - x_j)  /  sum_j w_j / (x - x_j)
//
// Reference: Berrut & Trefethen (2004), SIAM Review.
fn cheb_interpolate(f_vals: &[f64; 256], n: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Compute CGL nodes
    var nodes: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n { nodes[j] = sp_cos((j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64)); j = j + 1 }

    // Check if x coincides with a node
    j = 0
    while j <= n {
        if sp_abs(x - nodes[j]) < 1.0e-15 { return f_vals[j] }
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Barycentric interpolation
    var numer = 0.0
    var denom = 0.0
    j = 0
    while j <= n {
        // w_j = (-1)^j * delta_j
        var w = 1.0
        if j - (j / 2) * 2 != 0 { w = 0.0 - 1.0 }
        if j == 0 || j == n { w = w * 0.5 }

        let term = w / (x - nodes[j])
        numer = numer + term * f_vals[j]
        denom = denom + term
        j = j + 1
    }
    numer / denom
}

// =============================================================================
// Spectral interpolation on [a, b]
// =============================================================================

// Barycentric Chebyshev interpolation mapped to [a, b].
// Maps x from [a, b] to xi in [-1, 1] via xi = (2*x - a - b) / (b - a).
fn cheb_interpolate_ab(f_vals: &[f64; 256], n: i32, a: f64, b: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let xi = (2.0 * x - a - b) / (b - a)
    cheb_interpolate(f_vals, n, xi)
}

// =============================================================================
// Chebyshev coefficients from function values (DCT-I)
// =============================================================================

// Compute Chebyshev expansion coefficients from function values at CGL points.
// Given f_vals[j] = f(x_j) at n+1 CGL nodes, compute coefficients a_k such that
//   f(x) approx sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k * T_k(x)
//
// Using the DCT-I relation:
//   a_k = (2/n) * sum_{j=0}^{n} '' f(x_j) * cos(k*j*pi/n)
// where '' means first and last terms halved.
fn cheb_coeffs_from_values(f_vals: &[f64; 256], n: i32, coeffs: &![f64; 256]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var k = 0
    while k <= n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j <= n {
            let theta = (k as f64) * (j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64)
            var term = f_vals[j] * sp_cos(theta)

            // Double-prime: halve j=0 and j=n terms
            if j == 0 { term = term * 0.5 }
            if j == n { term = term * 0.5 }

            sum = sum + term
            j = j + 1
        }

        coeffs[k] = 2.0 * sum / (n as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }

    // The k=0 and k=n coefficients have an extra factor of 0.5
    coeffs[0] = coeffs[0] * 0.5
    if n > 0 { coeffs[n] = coeffs[n] * 0.5 }
}

// =============================================================================
// Clenshaw recurrence evaluation from Chebyshev coefficients
// =============================================================================

// Evaluate the Chebyshev expansion sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k * T_k(x) at point x
// using Clenshaw's recurrence algorithm.
//
// Clenshaw recurrence:
//   b_{n+2} = 0, b_{n+1} = 0
//   b_k = 2*x*b_{k+1} - b_{k+2} + a_k,  k = n, n-1, ..., 1
//   result = a_0 + x*b_1 - b_2
//
// This is numerically stable and O(n).
fn cheb_eval_from_coeffs(coeffs: &[f64; 256], n: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if n == 0 { return coeffs[0] }
    if n == 1 { return coeffs[0] + coeffs[1] * x }

    var b_next = 0.0    // b_{k+2}
    var b_curr = 0.0    // b_{k+1}

    var k = n
    while k >= 1 {
        let b_new = 2.0 * x * b_curr - b_next + coeffs[k]
        b_next = b_curr
        b_curr = b_new
        k = k - 1
    }

    // result = a_0 + x*b_1 - b_2
    coeffs[0] + x * b_curr - b_next
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/stochastic_calc.sio ===
// stdlib/math/stochastic_calc.sio — Stochastic calculus and SDEs
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Linear congruential PRNG with Box-Muller normal generation
//   Euler-Maruyama scheme (weak order 1.0)
//   Milstein scheme (strong order 1.0)
//   Stratonovich-Heun predictor-corrector
//   Geometric Brownian Motion (exact + Euler)
//   Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process (exact + Euler)
//   Monte Carlo simulation with terminal statistics
//   Strong error estimation between fine/coarse paths
//   Path analysis: time-average, running max, quadratic variation
//   Ito <-> Stratonovich drift corrections
//   Multi-dimensional Euler-Maruyama (flat storage, dim components per step)
//
// References:
//   Kloeden & Platen (1999): "Numerical Solution of Stochastic DEs"
//   Higham (2001): "An Algorithmic Introduction to Numerical Simulation of SDEs"
//   Oksendal (2003): "Stochastic Differential Equations"
//   Glasserman (2003): "Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering"

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (all prefixed sc_ to avoid name collisions)
// =============================================================================

fn sc_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn sc_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn sc_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn sc_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn sc_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Range reduction: exp(x) = 2^k * exp(r) where x = k*ln2 + r, |r| <= ln2/2
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    let inv_ln2 = 1.4426950408889634

    // Clamp to avoid overflow/underflow
    if x > 709.0 { return 1.0e308 }
    if x < -709.0 { return 0.0 }

    // Compute k = round(x / ln2)
    var k_f = x * inv_ln2
    var k: i64 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = (k_f + 0.5) as i64 } else { k = (k_f - 0.5) as i64 }

    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2

    // Taylor series for exp(r), |r| <= ln2/2 ~ 0.347
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }

    // Multiply by 2^k using repeated squaring
    var result = sum
    if k > 0 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < k { result = result * 2.0; j = j + 1 }
    } else if k < 0 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < (0 - k) { result = result * 0.5; j = j + 1 }
    }
    result
}

fn sc_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // ln(x) via Newton iteration on exp(y) = x
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e308 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    // Initial guess using range reduction: x = m * 2^e, ln(x) = ln(m) + e*ln(2)
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var m = x
    var e: i64 = 0
    while m > 2.0 { m = m * 0.5; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }

    // ln(m) for m in [0.5, 2] using series around 1: ln(1+u) = u - u^2/2 + u^3/3 - ...
    let u = m - 1.0
    var sum = 0.0
    var term = u
    var n = 1
    while n <= 30 {
        sum = sum + term / (n as f64)
        term = 0.0 - term * u
        n = n + 1
    }

    sum + (e as f64) * ln2
}

fn sc_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Reduce to [-pi, pi]
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    var a = x
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 18 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn sc_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    sc_sin(x + 1.57079632679489661923)
}

fn sc_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn sc_floor_i64(x: f64) -> i64 {
    let n = x as i64
    if (n as f64) > x { n - 1 } else { n }
}

// =============================================================================
// Structs
// =============================================================================

// Single-dimensional SDE path with up to 4096 time steps.
// x[i] stores the solution at time t_start + i * (t_end - t_start) / n_steps.
struct SDEPath {
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    x: [f64; 4096],
    n_steps: i32
}

// Multi-dimensional SDE path with flat storage.
// x[i * dim + d] stores the d-th component at time step i.
// Requires dim * n_steps <= 4096.
struct SDEPathND {
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    x: [f64; 4096],
    dim: i32,
    n_steps: i32
}

// Terminal statistics from Monte Carlo simulation.
struct SDEStats {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    std_dev: f64,
    n_paths: i32
}

// =============================================================================
// Inlined LCG PRNG + Box-Muller
// =============================================================================

// Linear congruential generator: state = (a * state + c) mod m.
// Uses the Numerical Recipes LCG parameters:
//   a = 1664525, c = 1013904223, m = 2^32 (implicit via i64 masking).
fn sc_lcg_next(state: &!i64) -> i64 with Panic, Mut {
    // Constants from Knuth / Numerical Recipes
    let a: i64 = 1664525
    let c: i64 = 1013904223
    let mask: i64 = 4294967295   // 2^32 - 1
    state[0] = (a * state[0] + c) & mask
    state[0]
}

// Uniform random in [0, 1) from LCG.
fn sc_lcg_uniform(state: &!i64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut {
    let val = sc_lcg_next(state)
    // Divide by 2^32 to get [0, 1)
    (val as f64) / 4294967296.0
}

// Standard normal N(0,1) via Box-Muller transform.
// Generates two normals per call but discards one for simplicity.
// Z = sqrt(-2 * ln(U1)) * cos(2 * pi * U2)
fn sc_box_muller(state: &!i64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Ensure U1 is bounded away from 0 to avoid ln(0)
    var u1 = sc_lcg_uniform(state)
    while u1 < 1.0e-10 { u1 = sc_lcg_uniform(state) }
    let u2 = sc_lcg_uniform(state)

    let r = sc_sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * sc_ln(u1))
    let theta = 2.0 * sc_pi() * u2
    r * sc_cos(theta)
}

// =============================================================================
// Core SDE Solvers
// =============================================================================

// Euler-Maruyama scheme for scalar SDE:
//   dX = a(t, X) dt + b(t, X) dW
// Weak order 1.0, strong order 0.5.
//   X_{n+1} = X_n + a(t_n, X_n) * dt + b(t_n, X_n) * dW_n
// where dW_n ~ N(0, dt).
fn sde_euler_maruyama(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)

        // Euler-Maruyama update
        path.x[i + 1] = x + drift(t, x) * dt + diffusion(t, x) * dW
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Milstein scheme for scalar SDE:
//   dX = a(t, X) dt + b(t, X) dW
// Strong order 1.0. Requires the derivative b'(t, x) = db/dx.
//   X_{n+1} = X_n + a*dt + b*dW + 0.5*b*b'*(dW^2 - dt)
fn sde_milstein(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diff_prime: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)

        let a_val = drift(t, x)
        let b_val = diffusion(t, x)
        let bp_val = diff_prime(t, x)

        // Milstein correction: 0.5 * b * b' * (dW^2 - dt)
        let milstein_term = 0.5 * b_val * bp_val * (dW * dW - dt)

        path.x[i + 1] = x + a_val * dt + b_val * dW + milstein_term
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Stratonovich-Heun predictor-corrector scheme:
//   Predictor: X_bar = X_n + a(t, X_n)*dt + b(t, X_n)*dW
//   Corrector: X_{n+1} = X_n + a(t, X_n)*dt
//              + 0.5*(b(t, X_n) + b(t+dt, X_bar))*dW
// This scheme is consistent with the Stratonovich interpretation.
fn sde_heun(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)

        let a_val = drift(t, x)
        let b_val = diffusion(t, x)

        // Predictor (Euler step)
        let x_bar = x + a_val * dt + b_val * dW

        // Corrector: average diffusion at both endpoints
        let b_bar = diffusion(t + dt, x_bar)
        path.x[i + 1] = x + a_val * dt + 0.5 * (b_val + b_bar) * dW

        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Specific Processes: Geometric Brownian Motion
// =============================================================================

// Geometric Brownian Motion — exact (analytic) solution.
//   dS = mu * S * dt + sigma * S * dW
//   S(t) = S0 * exp((mu - sigma^2/2)*t + sigma*W(t))
// Accumulates Wiener increments to build W(t_k).
fn gbm_exact(
    S0: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64,
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)
    let drift_coeff = mu - 0.5 * sigma * sigma

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = S0

    // Accumulate Wiener path W(t_k) = sum of dW_j for j < k
    var W = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        W = W + dW
        let t = (i + 1) as f64 * dt
        path.x[i + 1] = S0 * sc_exp(drift_coeff * t + sigma * W)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Geometric Brownian Motion via Euler-Maruyama (for comparison/convergence tests).
//   X_{n+1} = X_n + mu*X_n*dt + sigma*X_n*dW
fn gbm_euler(
    S0: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64,
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = S0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        path.x[i + 1] = x + mu * x * dt + sigma * x * dW
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Specific Processes: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck
// =============================================================================

// Ornstein-Uhlenbeck exact solution using the conditional Gaussian distribution.
//   dX = theta * (mu - X) * dt + sigma * dW
//   X(t_{k+1}) | X(t_k) ~ N(mean_k, var_k) where:
//     mean_k = mu + (X(t_k) - mu) * exp(-theta * dt)
//     var_k  = sigma^2 * (1 - exp(-2*theta*dt)) / (2*theta)
fn ou_exact(
    x0: f64, theta: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64,
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)

    // Precompute transition parameters
    let decay = sc_exp(0.0 - theta * dt)
    let var_factor = sigma * sigma * (1.0 - sc_exp(0.0 - 2.0 * theta * dt)) / (2.0 * theta)
    let std_factor = sc_sqrt(var_factor)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let x = path.x[i]
        let z = sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)

        // Conditional Gaussian: X_{k+1} = mean + std * Z
        let mean_k = mu + (x - mu) * decay
        path.x[i + 1] = mean_k + std_factor * z
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Ornstein-Uhlenbeck via Euler-Maruyama (for convergence comparison).
//   X_{n+1} = X_n + theta*(mu - X_n)*dt + sigma*dW
fn ou_euler(
    x0: f64, theta: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64,
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        path.x[i + 1] = x + theta * (mu - x) * dt + sigma * dW
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Monte Carlo Simulation
// =============================================================================

// Run n_paths independent Euler-Maruyama simulations and compute terminal
// value statistics (mean, variance, std_dev).
// Each path uses seed + path_index as its RNG seed for reproducibility.
fn sde_monte_carlo(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, n_paths: i32, seed: i64,
    stats: &!SDEStats
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var sum_x = 0.0
    var sum_x2 = 0.0

    var p = 0
    while p < n_paths {
        // Each path gets a distinct seed
        var rng_state: i64 = seed + (p as i64) * 1000003

        var x = x0
        var i = 0
        while i < n_steps {
            let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
            let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
            x = x + drift(t, x) * dt + diffusion(t, x) * dW
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Accumulate terminal value
        sum_x = sum_x + x
        sum_x2 = sum_x2 + x * x
        p = p + 1
    }

    let n_f = n_paths as f64
    let mean = sum_x / n_f
    let variance = sum_x2 / n_f - mean * mean

    stats.mean = mean
    stats.variance = variance
    stats.std_dev = sc_sqrt(sc_max(variance, 0.0))
    stats.n_paths = n_paths
}

// =============================================================================
// Path Analysis
// =============================================================================

// Strong error between a fine and coarse path.
// Compares paths at the coarse grid points.
// Returns max |X_fine(t_k) - X_coarse(t_k)| where t_k are coarse time points.
// Assumes fine.n_steps is a multiple of coarse.n_steps.
fn sde_strong_error(path_fine: &SDEPath, path_coarse: &SDEPath) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let ratio = path_fine.n_steps / path_coarse.n_steps
    var max_err = 0.0

    var k = 0
    while k <= path_coarse.n_steps {
        let fine_idx = k * ratio
        let err = sc_abs(path_fine.x[fine_idx] - path_coarse.x[k])
        if err > max_err { max_err = err }
        k = k + 1
    }
    max_err
}

// Time-average of a path: (1/T) * integral X(t) dt
// approximated by trapezoidal rule.
fn sde_path_mean(path: &SDEPath) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let n = path.n_steps
    if n <= 0 { return path.x[0] }

    let dt = (path.t_end - path.t_start) / (n as f64)
    var sum = 0.5 * path.x[0] + 0.5 * path.x[n]

    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + path.x[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    sum * dt / (path.t_end - path.t_start)
}

// Running maximum of the path: max_{k=0..n} X(t_k).
fn sde_path_max(path: &SDEPath) -> f64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var mx = path.x[0]
    var i = 1
    while i <= path.n_steps {
        if path.x[i] > mx { mx = path.x[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    mx
}

// Running minimum of the path: min_{k=0..n} X(t_k).
fn sde_path_min(path: &SDEPath) -> f64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var mn = path.x[0]
    var i = 1
    while i <= path.n_steps {
        if path.x[i] < mn { mn = path.x[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    mn
}

// Quadratic variation of the path: sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (X_{i+1} - X_i)^2.
// For Brownian motion, this should converge to diffusion^2 * T as n -> inf.
fn sde_path_quadratic_var(path: &SDEPath) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var qv = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < path.n_steps {
        let dx = path.x[i + 1] - path.x[i]
        qv = qv + dx * dx
        i = i + 1
    }
    qv
}

// Terminal value of the path: X(t_end).
fn sde_path_terminal(path: &SDEPath) -> f64 {
    path.x[path.n_steps]
}

// =============================================================================
// Ito <-> Stratonovich Corrections
// =============================================================================

// Ito-to-Stratonovich drift correction.
// If the Ito SDE is dX = a_ito * dt + b * dW,
// the equivalent Stratonovich SDE is dX = a_strat * dt + b o dW where:
//   a_strat = a_ito + 0.5 * b(t,x) * b'(t,x)
// This function returns the correction term: 0.5 * b * b'.
fn ito_to_strat_correction(
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diff_prime: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    t: f64, x: f64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let b_val = diffusion(t, x)
    let bp_val = diff_prime(t, x)
    0.5 * b_val * bp_val
}

// Stratonovich-to-Ito drift correction.
// If the Stratonovich SDE is dX = a_strat * dt + b o dW,
// the equivalent Ito SDE is dX = a_ito * dt + b * dW where:
//   a_ito = a_strat - 0.5 * b(t,x) * b'(t,x)
// This function returns the correction term: -0.5 * b * b'.
fn strat_to_ito_correction(
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diff_prime: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    t: f64, x: f64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let b_val = diffusion(t, x)
    let bp_val = diff_prime(t, x)
    0.0 - 0.5 * b_val * bp_val
}

// =============================================================================
// Multi-dimensional Euler-Maruyama
// =============================================================================

// Euler-Maruyama for a dim-dimensional SDE system:
//   dX_d = drift_d(X, t) * dt + diffusion_d(X, t) * dW_d
// Each component has its own independent Wiener increment.
//
// drift(dim, x_state, t, out): writes drift vector into out[0..dim-1]
// diffusion(dim, x_state, t, out): writes diffusion vector into out[0..dim-1]
// x0[0..dim-1]: initial condition
//
// Path stored as flat array: path.x[step * dim + d] = X_d(t_step).
fn sde_euler_nd(
    drift: fn(i32, &[f64; 64], f64, &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(i32, &[f64; 64], f64, &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: &[f64; 64], dim: i32, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPathND
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.dim = dim
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed

    // Store initial condition at step 0
    var d = 0
    while d < dim {
        path.x[d] = x0[d]
        d = d + 1
    }

    // Temporary arrays for current state, drift, and diffusion vectors
    var x_cur: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var a_vec: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var b_vec: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt

        // Copy current state from path storage
        d = 0
        while d < dim {
            x_cur[d] = path.x[i * dim + d]
            d = d + 1
        }

        // Evaluate drift and diffusion vectors
        drift(dim, &x_cur, t, &!a_vec)
        diffusion(dim, &x_cur, t, &!b_vec)

        // Update each component with independent Wiener increments
        d = 0
        while d < dim {
            let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
            path.x[(i + 1) * dim + d] = x_cur[d] + a_vec[d] * dt + b_vec[d] * dW
            d = d + 1
        }

        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Multi-dimensional Path Analysis
// =============================================================================

// Extract the d-th component from a multi-dimensional path into a 1D path.
fn sde_nd_extract(nd_path: &SDEPathND, d: i32, out: &!SDEPath) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    out.t_start = nd_path.t_start
    out.t_end = nd_path.t_end
    out.n_steps = nd_path.n_steps

    var i = 0
    while i <= nd_path.n_steps {
        out.x[i] = nd_path.x[i * nd_path.dim + d]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Compute the Euclidean norm of the state vector at time step k.
fn sde_nd_norm_at(nd_path: &SDEPathND, k: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var sum_sq = 0.0
    var d = 0
    while d < nd_path.dim {
        let val = nd_path.x[k * nd_path.dim + d]
        sum_sq = sum_sq + val * val
        d = d + 1
    }
    sc_sqrt(sum_sq)
}

// =============================================================================
// Advanced Solvers
// =============================================================================

// Stochastic Runge-Kutta (SRK) method of order 1.0 (strong).
// A two-stage explicit method by Rossler (2010) for additive noise
// (constant diffusion). Falls back to improved behavior for multiplicative noise.
//   Stage 1: K1 = a(t, X_n)
//   Predictor: X_hat = X_n + K1 * dt + b(t, X_n) * sqrt(dt)
//   Stage 2: K2 = a(t + dt, X_hat)
//   X_{n+1} = X_n + 0.5*(K1+K2)*dt + b(t, X_n)*dW
fn sde_srk(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)

        let b_val = diffusion(t, x)
        let k1 = drift(t, x)

        // Predictor using sqrt(dt) supporting term
        let x_hat = x + k1 * dt + b_val * sqrt_dt
        let k2 = drift(t + dt, x_hat)

        // Two-stage update
        path.x[i + 1] = x + 0.5 * (k1 + k2) * dt + b_val * dW
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Implicit Euler-Maruyama (drift-implicit) for stiff SDEs.
// Solves X_{n+1} = X_n + a(t_{n+1}, X_{n+1})*dt + b(t_n, X_n)*dW
// via fixed-point iteration on the implicit drift term.
// max_iter controls the number of fixed-point iterations per step.
fn sde_implicit_euler(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    max_iter: i32,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
        let t_next = t + dt
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)

        // Explicit diffusion term (evaluated at current point)
        let stoch_part = diffusion(t, x) * dW

        // Initial guess for X_{n+1} via explicit Euler
        var x_next = x + drift(t, x) * dt + stoch_part

        // Fixed-point iteration: x_next = x + a(t_next, x_next)*dt + stoch_part
        var iter = 0
        while iter < max_iter {
            x_next = x + drift(t_next, x_next) * dt + stoch_part
            iter = iter + 1
        }

        path.x[i + 1] = x_next
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Wiener Process Utilities
// =============================================================================

// Generate a standard Wiener process (Brownian motion) path.
// W(0) = 0, W(t_{k+1}) = W(t_k) + sqrt(dt) * Z_k where Z_k ~ N(0,1).
fn wiener_path(
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = 0.0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        path.x[i + 1] = path.x[i] + dW
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Brownian bridge: W(0) = a, W(T) = b, with correct conditional distribution.
// At intermediate points, W(t_k) is drawn from the bridge distribution:
//   W(t_k) | W(t_{k-1}), W(T) ~ N(mean, var) where
//   mean = W(t_{k-1}) + (b - W(t_{k-1})) * dt / (T - t_{k-1})
//   var  = dt * (T - t_k) / (T - t_{k-1})
fn brownian_bridge(
    a: f64, b: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = a
    path.x[n_steps] = b

    // Fill intermediate points using conditional Gaussian
    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps - 1 {
        let t_cur = (i as f64) * dt
        let t_next = ((i + 1) as f64) * dt
        let remaining = t_end - t_cur

        // Conditional mean and variance
        let cond_mean = path.x[i] + (b - path.x[i]) * dt / remaining
        let cond_var = dt * (t_end - t_next) / remaining
        let cond_std = sc_sqrt(sc_max(cond_var, 0.0))

        let z = sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        path.x[i + 1] = cond_mean + cond_std * z
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Convergence Analysis Utilities
// =============================================================================

// Compute the weak error estimate: |E[g(X_T)] - reference|
// by running multiple paths and comparing the sample mean of g(X_T).
// Here g is the identity function g(x) = x, so it computes |E[X_T] - ref|.
fn sde_weak_error(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32,
    n_paths: i32, seed: i64, reference: f64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var sum_terminal = 0.0
    var p = 0
    while p < n_paths {
        var rng_state: i64 = seed + (p as i64) * 999983

        var x = x0
        var i = 0
        while i < n_steps {
            let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
            let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
            x = x + drift(t, x) * dt + diffusion(t, x) * dW
            i = i + 1
        }
        sum_terminal = sum_terminal + x
        p = p + 1
    }

    let mean_terminal = sum_terminal / (n_paths as f64)
    sc_abs(mean_terminal - reference)
}

// Compute the path increment covariance estimate between two consecutive
// time steps. For Brownian motion increments, this should be near zero
// (independent increments property).
fn sde_increment_covariance(path: &SDEPath) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let n = path.n_steps
    if n < 2 { return 0.0 }

    // Compute mean of increments
    var sum_inc = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum_inc = sum_inc + (path.x[i + 1] - path.x[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean_inc = sum_inc / (n as f64)

    // Compute covariance of consecutive increments
    var sum_cov = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        let inc1 = path.x[i + 1] - path.x[i] - mean_inc
        let inc2 = path.x[i + 2] - path.x[i + 1] - mean_inc
        sum_cov = sum_cov + inc1 * inc2
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum_cov / ((n - 1) as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// Moment Estimation
// =============================================================================

// Compute the k-th moment of the terminal value from Monte Carlo paths.
// E[X_T^k] estimated by (1/n) * sum X_T(i)^k.
fn sde_terminal_moment(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32,
    n_paths: i32, seed: i64, k: i32
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var sum_moment = 0.0
    var p = 0
    while p < n_paths {
        var rng_state: i64 = seed + (p as i64) * 1000033

        var x = x0
        var i = 0
        while i < n_steps {
            let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
            let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
            x = x + drift(t, x) * dt + diffusion(t, x) * dW
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Compute x^k via repeated multiplication
        var x_pow = 1.0
        var j = 0
        while j < k { x_pow = x_pow * x; j = j + 1 }
        sum_moment = sum_moment + x_pow
        p = p + 1
    }

    sum_moment / (n_paths as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// Absorbed / Reflected Boundary Conditions
// =============================================================================

// Euler-Maruyama with absorbing boundary at x = barrier.
// Once X hits the barrier (from above if barrier < x0, or below if barrier > x0),
// X stays there for all subsequent steps.
fn sde_euler_absorbed(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    barrier: f64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)
    let above = x0 > barrier

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0
    var absorbed = false

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        if absorbed {
            path.x[i + 1] = barrier
        } else {
            let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
            let x = path.x[i]
            let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
            let x_new = x + drift(t, x) * dt + diffusion(t, x) * dW

            // Check if path crossed barrier
            if above {
                if x_new <= barrier { absorbed = true; path.x[i + 1] = barrier }
                else { path.x[i + 1] = x_new }
            } else {
                if x_new >= barrier { absorbed = true; path.x[i + 1] = barrier }
                else { path.x[i + 1] = x_new }
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Euler-Maruyama with reflecting boundary at x = barrier.
// If X crosses barrier, it is reflected back: X = 2*barrier - X.
fn sde_euler_reflected(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    barrier: f64, reflect_above: bool,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        var x_new = x + drift(t, x) * dt + diffusion(t, x) * dW

        // Reflect if crossing barrier
        if reflect_above {
            // Reflect from above: if x_new > barrier, fold back
            if x_new > barrier { x_new = 2.0 * barrier - x_new }
        } else {
            // Reflect from below: if x_new < barrier, fold back
            if x_new < barrier { x_new = 2.0 * barrier - x_new }
        }

        path.x[i + 1] = x_new
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// First Passage Time Estimation
// =============================================================================

// Estimate the first passage time (FPT) to a level 'barrier' via Monte Carlo.
// Returns the mean first passage time across n_paths simulations.
// If a path never hits the barrier within [t0, t_end], it contributes t_end.
fn sde_first_passage_time(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32,
    barrier: f64, n_paths: i32, seed: i64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)
    let above = x0 > barrier

    var sum_fpt = 0.0
    var p = 0
    while p < n_paths {
        var rng_state: i64 = seed + (p as i64) * 1000037
        var x = x0
        var fpt = t_end    // Default: never hit

        var i = 0
        var hit = false
        while i < n_steps {
            if hit == false {
                let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
                let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
                x = x + drift(t, x) * dt + diffusion(t, x) * dW

                // Check crossing
                if above {
                    if x <= barrier { fpt = t + dt; hit = true }
                } else {
                    if x >= barrier { fpt = t + dt; hit = true }
                }
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        sum_fpt = sum_fpt + fpt
        p = p + 1
    }

    sum_fpt / (n_paths as f64)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/symbolic.sio ===
// stdlib/math/symbolic.sio -- Symbolic differentiation for automatic Jacobian generation
//
// Arena-based flat expression representation with symbolic differentiation,
// evaluation, basic simplification, and printing.
//
// Expression nodes are stored in parallel arrays (arena pattern) to avoid
// recursive types. Each node has a tag, two child indices, a constant value,
// and a variable ID.
//
// Tags: 0=Const, 1=Var, 2=Add, 3=Sub, 4=Mul, 5=Div, 6=Neg,
//       7=Sin, 8=Cos, 9=Exp, 10=Log, 11=Pow
//
// Differentiation rules implemented:
//   d/dx[c]       = 0
//   d/dx[x]       = 1, d/dx[y] = 0 (for y != x)
//   d/dx[f + g]   = f' + g'
//   d/dx[f - g]   = f' - g'
//   d/dx[f * g]   = f'*g + f*g'           (product rule)
//   d/dx[f / g]   = (f'*g - f*g') / g^2   (quotient rule)
//   d/dx[-f]      = -f'
//   d/dx[sin(f)]  = cos(f) * f'           (chain rule)
//   d/dx[cos(f)]  = -sin(f) * f'          (chain rule)
//   d/dx[exp(f)]  = exp(f) * f'           (chain rule)
//   d/dx[log(f)]  = f' / f                (chain rule)
//   d/dx[f^g]     = f^g * (g'*log(f) + g*f'/f)  (general power rule)
//
// References:
//   Griewank & Walther (2008): "Evaluating Derivatives", SIAM
//   Rall (1981): "Automatic Differentiation: Techniques and Applications"

// =============================================================================
// Constants for node tags
// =============================================================================

fn TAG_CONST() -> i64 { 0 }
fn TAG_VAR() -> i64 { 1 }
fn TAG_ADD() -> i64 { 2 }
fn TAG_SUB() -> i64 { 3 }
fn TAG_MUL() -> i64 { 4 }
fn TAG_DIV() -> i64 { 5 }
fn TAG_NEG() -> i64 { 6 }
fn TAG_SIN() -> i64 { 7 }
fn TAG_COS() -> i64 { 8 }
fn TAG_EXP() -> i64 { 9 }
fn TAG_LOG() -> i64 { 10 }
fn TAG_POW() -> i64 { 11 }

// =============================================================================
// Expression Arena
// =============================================================================

struct ExprArena {
    tags: [i64; 256],
    left: [i64; 256],
    right: [i64; 256],
    values: [f64; 256],
    var_ids: [i64; 256],
    count: i64,
}

fn arena_new() -> ExprArena {
    ExprArena {
        tags: [0; 256],
        left: [0; 256],
        right: [0; 256],
        values: [0.0; 256],
        var_ids: [0; 256],
        count: 0,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Node constructors — each returns the index of the new node
// =============================================================================

fn expr_const(arena: &!ExprArena, value: f64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = arena.count
    arena.tags[idx] = TAG_CONST()
    arena.left[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.right[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.values[idx] = value
    arena.var_ids[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.count = arena.count + 1
    idx
}

fn expr_var(arena: &!ExprArena, var_id: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = arena.count
    arena.tags[idx] = TAG_VAR()
    arena.left[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.right[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.values[idx] = 0.0
    arena.var_ids[idx] = var_id
    arena.count = arena.count + 1
    idx
}

fn expr_add(arena: &!ExprArena, l: i64, r: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = arena.count
    arena.tags[idx] = TAG_ADD()
    arena.left[idx] = l
    arena.right[idx] = r
    arena.values[idx] = 0.0
    arena.var_ids[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.count = arena.count + 1
    idx
}

fn expr_sub(arena: &!ExprArena, l: i64, r: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = arena.count
    arena.tags[idx] = TAG_SUB()
    arena.left[idx] = l
    arena.right[idx] = r
    arena.values[idx] = 0.0
    arena.var_ids[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.count = arena.count + 1
    idx
}

    let idx = arena.count
    arena.tags[idx] = TAG_MUL()
    arena.left[idx] = l
    arena.right[idx] = r
    arena.values[idx] = 0.0
    arena.var_ids[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.count = arena.count + 1
    idx
}

    let idx = arena.count
    arena.tags[idx] = TAG_DIV()
    arena.left[idx] = l
    arena.right[idx] = r

    arena.var_ids[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.count = arena.count + 1
    idx
}

    let idx = arena.count
    arena.tags[idx] = TAG_NEG()
    arena.left[idx] = child
    arena.right[idx] = 0 - 1
    arena.values[idx] = 0.0

}

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers (Taylor series — self-contained, no FFI)
// =============================================================================

fn sym_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sym_floor(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let i = x as i32
    let f = i as f64
    if x < 0.0 && f != x { return f - 1.0 }
    return f
}

fn sym_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 6.283185307179586
    var t = x - sym_floor(x / two_pi) * two_pi
    if t > pi { t = t - two_pi }
    if t < 0.0 - pi { t = t + two_pi }
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var n = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        term = 0.0 - term * t * t / (((2 * n) as f64) * ((2 * n + 1) as f64))
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    return sum
}

fn sym_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
