// === FILE: stdlib/msgpack/msgpack.sio ===
// msgpack/mod.sio — MessagePack Encoding
//
// Compact binary serialization following the MessagePack specification.
// Encodes integers, floats, and nil values.
//
// Reference: https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack/blob/master/spec.md

// ============================================================================
// INTEGER ENCODING
// ============================================================================
// MessagePack format for integers:
//   positive fixint: 0x00 - 0x7f (single byte, value 0-127)
//   negative fixint: 0xe0 - 0xff (single byte, value -32 to -1)
//   uint 8:  0xcc + 1 byte
//   uint 16: 0xcd + 2 bytes
//   uint 32: 0xce + 4 bytes
//   int 8:   0xd0 + 1 byte
//   int 16:  0xd1 + 2 bytes
//   int 32:  0xd2 + 4 bytes

pub fn msgpack_encode_int(val: i64, out: &![u8; 16]) -> i32 with Mut, Panic {
    // Positive fixint: 0-127
    if val >= 0 && val <= 127 {
        out[0] = (val as i32) as u8
        return 1
    }

    // Negative fixint: -32 to -1
    if val >= 0 - 32 && val < 0 {
        // 0xe0 | (val & 0x1f)
        let byte = 224 + (val + 32)
        out[0] = (byte as i32) as u8
        return 1
    }

    // Positive: uint 8 (128-255)
    if val >= 0 && val <= 255 {
        out[0] = 204  // 0xcc
        out[1] = (val as i32) as u8
        return 2
    }

    // Positive: uint 16 (256-65535)
    if val >= 0 && val <= 65535 {
        out[0] = 205  // 0xcd
        let v = val as i32
        out[1] = ((v / 256) % 256) as u8
        out[2] = (v % 256) as u8
        return 3
    }

    // Negative: int 8 (-128 to -33)
    if val >= 0 - 128 && val < 0 - 32 {
        out[0] = 208  // 0xd0
        let byte = (val + 256) % 256
        out[1] = (byte as i32) as u8
        return 2
    }

    // Negative: int 16 (-32768 to -129)
    if val >= 0 - 32768 && val < 0 - 128 {
        out[0] = 209  // 0xd1
        let v = (val + 65536) % 65536
        let vi = v as i32
        out[1] = ((vi / 256) % 256) as u8
        out[2] = (vi % 256) as u8
        return 3
    }

    // Positive: uint 32
    if val >= 0 && val <= 4294967295 {
        out[0] = 206  // 0xce
        var v = val
        out[4] = ((v % 256) as i32) as u8
        v = v / 256
        out[3] = ((v % 256) as i32) as u8
        v = v / 256
        out[2] = ((v % 256) as i32) as u8
        v = v / 256
        out[1] = ((v % 256) as i32) as u8
        return 5
    }

    // Negative: int 32
    out[0] = 210  // 0xd2
    let v = (val + 4294967296) % 4294967296
    var rem = v
    out[4] = ((rem % 256) as i32) as u8
    rem = rem / 256
    out[3] = ((rem % 256) as i32) as u8
    rem = rem / 256
    out[2] = ((rem % 256) as i32) as u8
    rem = rem / 256
    out[1] = ((rem % 256) as i32) as u8
    5
}

// ============================================================================
// FLOAT ENCODING
// ============================================================================
// MessagePack float 64: 0xcb + 8 bytes (IEEE 754 big-endian)
// We use a simplified encoding that stores the f64 as raw bytes.

pub fn msgpack_encode_float(val: f64, out: &![u8; 16]) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // float 64 format: 0xcb + 8 bytes big-endian IEEE 754
    out[0] = 203  // 0xcb

    // For a pure-Sounio implementation without bit-cast intrinsics,
    // we encode a simplified representation:
    // Store as integer * scale approach (limited precision).
    // NOTE: A full implementation would need a reinterpret_cast intrinsic.

    // Detect special cases
    if val == 0.0 {
        var i: i32 = 1
        while i <= 8 {
            out[i as usize] = 0
            i = i + 1
        }
        return 9
    }

    // For non-zero values, store a marker + approximate encoding
    // This is a placeholder for the bit-level encoding.
    // In practice, the JIT can provide f64_to_bits intrinsic.
    out[1] = 0
    out[2] = 0
    out[3] = 0
    out[4] = 0
    out[5] = 0
    out[6] = 0
    out[7] = 0
    out[8] = 1  // non-zero marker
    9
}

// ============================================================================
// NIL ENCODING
// ============================================================================
// MessagePack nil: single byte 0xc0

pub fn msgpack_encode_nil(out: &![u8; 16]) -> i32 with Mut, Panic {
    out[0] = 192  // 0xc0
    1
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_encode_positive_fixint() -> i32 {
    var buf: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
    let n = msgpack_encode_int(42, &!buf)
    if n != 1 { return 1 }
    if buf[0] != 42 { return 2 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_encode_zero() -> i32 {
    var buf: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
    let n = msgpack_encode_int(0, &!buf)
    if n != 1 { return 1 }
    if buf[0] != 0 { return 2 }
    0
}

fn test_encode_negative_fixint() -> i32 {
    var buf: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
    let n = msgpack_encode_int(0 - 1, &!buf)
    if n != 1 { return 1 }
    // -1 should be 0xff = 255
    if buf[0] != 255 { return 2 }
    0
}

    var buf: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
    let n = msgpack_encode_nil(&!buf)
    if n != 1 { return 1 }
    if buf[0] != 192 { return 2 }
    0
}

    if n != 2 { return 1 }
    if buf[0] != 204 { return 2 }  // 0xcc
    if buf[1] != 200 { return 3 }
    0
}

}


// === FILE: stdlib/net/addr.sio ===
// stdlib/net/addr — Network address types

struct IPv4Addr {
    a: i64,
    b: i64,
    c: i64,
    d: i64,
}

fn ipv4_new(a: i64, b: i64, c: i64, d: i64) -> IPv4Addr {
    IPv4Addr { a: a, b: b, c: c, d: d }
}

fn ipv4_loopback() -> IPv4Addr {
    IPv4Addr { a: 127, b: 0, c: 0, d: 1 }
}

fn ipv4_any() -> IPv4Addr {
    IPv4Addr { a: 0, b: 0, c: 0, d: 0 }
}

impl IPv4Addr {
    fn is_loopback(self: &IPv4Addr) -> bool { self.a == 127 }

    fn is_private(self: &IPv4Addr) -> bool {
        if self.a == 10 { return true }
        if self.a == 172 && self.b >= 16 && self.b <= 31 { return true }
        if self.a == 192 && self.b == 168 { return true }
        return false
    }

    fn is_any(self: &IPv4Addr) -> bool {
        self.a == 0 && self.b == 0 && self.c == 0 && self.d == 0
    }

    fn to_u32(self: &IPv4Addr) -> i64 {
        self.a * 16777216 + self.b * 65536 + self.c * 256 + self.d
    }

    fn equals(self: &IPv4Addr, other: &IPv4Addr) -> bool {
        self.a == other.a && self.b == other.b && self.c == other.c && self.d == other.d
    }
}

struct SocketAddr {
    ip: IPv4Addr,
    port: i64,
}

fn socket_addr_new(ip: IPv4Addr, port: i64) -> SocketAddr {
    SocketAddr { ip: ip, port: port }
}

impl SocketAddr {
    fn port(self: &SocketAddr) -> i64 { self.port }
    fn is_loopback(self: &SocketAddr) -> bool { self.ip.is_loopback() }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/neuro/connectome.sio ===
//! stdlib/neuro/connectome.sio - Connectome-to-Sedenion Embedding Pipeline
//!
//! Takes a brain connectome (per-ROI feature vectors) and produces a graph-level
//! sedenion c in S for FSNN processing.
//!
//! Per-ROI feature mapping (16 components -> 1 sedenion per ROI):
//!   [0]  node strength       (fMRI)
//!   [1]  clustering coeff    (fMRI)
//!   [2]  betweenness cent    (DTI)
//!   [3]  eigenvector cent    (fMRI)
//!   [4]  participation coeff (fMRI)
//!   [5]  local efficiency    (DTI)
//!   [6]  PageRank            (fMRI)
//!   [7]  degree              (structural)
//!   [8]  ORC mean            (Ollivier-Ricci curvature)
//!   [9]  ORC std dev         (curvature heterogeneity)
//!   [10] Shannon entropy     (signal complexity)
//!   [11] within-module z     (modular hub score)
//!   [12] k-core number       (resilience)
//!   [13] closeness cent      (DTI)
//!   [14] triangle count      (motif density)
//!   [15] noise / spare       (measurement noise)
//!
//! Embedding strategies:
//! - Mean: c = (1/N) sum_i s_i
//! - Interaction: c = (1/M) sum_m s_{i_m} * s_{j_m} over top-M edges

use math::sedenion64::*
use fractal::mandelbrot::{OrbitConfig, compute_orbit}
use fractal::fsnn::{FSNNFeatures, fsnn_extract_features}

// ============================================================================
// ROI FEATURES
// ============================================================================

pub struct ROIFeatures {
    data: [f64; 16],
}

pub fn roi_features_zero() -> ROIFeatures {
    ROIFeatures { data: [0.0; 16] }
}

pub fn roi_to_sedenion(r: ROIFeatures) -> Sedenion64 {
    sed64(r.data[0], r.data[1], r.data[2], r.data[3],
          r.data[4], r.data[5], r.data[6], r.data[7],
          r.data[8], r.data[9], r.data[10], r.data[11],
          r.data[12], r.data[13], r.data[14], r.data[15])
}

// ============================================================================
// MEAN EMBEDDING
// ============================================================================
// c = (1/N) sum_{i=0}^{N-1} s_i
// Simplest strategy. Preserves mean feature magnitudes.

pub fn connectome_embed_mean(features: [ROIFeatures; 256], n_rois: i32) -> Sedenion64 {
    var sum = sed64_zero()
    var i = 0
    while i < n_rois {
        let si = roi_to_sedenion(features[i])
        sum = sed64_add(sum, si)
        i = i + 1
    }
    if n_rois > 0 {
        sed64_scale(sum, 1.0 / (n_rois as f64))
    } else {
        sed64_zero()
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// INTERACTION EMBEDDING
// ============================================================================
// c = (1/M) sum_{m=0}^{M-1} s_{i_m} * s_{j_m}
// Non-commutative product encodes edge directionality.
// Top-M edges are pre-selected by weight (caller provides edge lists).

pub fn connectome_embed_interaction(
    features: [ROIFeatures; 256],
    edge_i: [i32; 256],
    edge_j: [i32; 256],
    n_edges: i32
) -> Sedenion64 {
    var sum = sed64_zero()
    var m = 0
    while m < n_edges {
        let si = roi_to_sedenion(features[edge_i[m]])
        let sj = roi_to_sedenion(features[edge_j[m]])
        let product = sed64_mul(si, sj)
        sum = sed64_add(sum, product)
        m = m + 1
    }
    if n_edges > 0 {
        sed64_scale(sum, 1.0 / (n_edges as f64))
    } else {
        sed64_zero()
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FULL PIPELINE
// ============================================================================
// Connectome -> sedenion embedding -> Mandelbrot orbit -> FSNN features

pub fn connectome_to_features(
    features: [ROIFeatures; 256],
    n_rois: i32,
    config: OrbitConfig
) -> FSNNFeatures {
    let c = connectome_embed_mean(features, n_rois)
    let orbit = compute_orbit(c, config)
    fsnn_extract_features(orbit, config)
}

pub fn connectome_to_features_interaction(
    features: [ROIFeatures; 256],
    edge_i: [i32; 256],
    edge_j: [i32; 256],
    n_edges: i32,
    config: OrbitConfig
) -> FSNNFeatures {
    let c = connectome_embed_interaction(features, edge_i, edge_j, n_edges)
    let orbit = compute_orbit(c, config)
    fsnn_extract_features(orbit, config)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/neuro/ct.sio ===
//! stdlib/neuro/ct.sio — Structural CT/MRI Morphometry Pipeline
//!
//! CT and structural MRI provide ANATOMICAL information:
//! cortical thickness, volume, surface area, curvature.
//!
//! Input: per-ROI morphometric features from FreeSurfer/FSL
//!        (e.g., aparc.stats → thickness, area, volume per region)
//!
//! Unlike fMRI/EEG/MEG (which measure functional connectivity),
//! structural imaging measures the SUBSTRATE on which functional
//! networks operate. The ORC phase classification applies to
//! structural covariance networks: edges connect regions whose
//! morphometric features covary across subjects.
//!
//! For the Sounio pipeline, structural data provides:
//!   - The graph SUBSTRATE (which regions are physically connected)
//!   - Morphometric FEATURES per ROI (for sedenion encoding)
//!   - Structural covariance NETWORK (for ORC phase classification)
//!
//! The sedenion encoding for structural data:
//!   e0-e7:  8 morphometric features per ROI
//!           (thickness, area, volume, curvature, sulcal_depth,
//!            folding_index, gray_matter_vol, white_matter_vol)
//!   e8-e15: 8 inter-regional structural covariance features
//!           (correlation of morphometry between ROI pairs)
//!
//! Clinical relevance:
//!   ENIGMA-MDD (Schmaal 2017): cortical thinning in depression
//!   ENIGMA-SCZ: volume reductions in schizophrenia
//!   ENIGMA-ASD: atypical surface area patterns
//!
//! References:
//!   Schmaal et al. (2017): Cortical abnormalities in MDD (ENIGMA)
//!   Desikan et al. (2006): FreeSurfer parcellation atlas

/// Per-ROI morphometric features from structural imaging.
pub struct MorphometricROI {
    thickness: f64,       // cortical thickness (mm)
    surface_area: f64,    // surface area (mm²)
    volume: f64,          // gray matter volume (mm³)
    mean_curvature: f64,  // mean surface curvature (1/mm)
    sulcal_depth: f64,    // sulcal depth (mm)
    folding_index: f64,   // gyrification index
    gm_volume: f64,       // gray matter volume (voxel-based)
    wm_volume: f64,       // white matter volume (voxel-based)
}

/// Structural covariance network.
///
/// Edges represent statistical covariance of morphometric features
/// ACROSS SUBJECTS (population-level), not within a single brain.
/// This is conceptually different from fMRI/EEG connectivity
/// (which is within-subject, within-session).
pub struct StructuralCovariance {
    // Covariance matrix of thickness across subjects (max 64×64)
    thickness_cov: [f64; 4096],
    // Binary adjacency
    adj: [i32; 4096],
    n_rois: i32,
    threshold: f64,
    // Per-ROI morphometric data (population means)
    roi_data: [MorphometricROI; 64],
}

/// Create empty structural covariance network.
pub fn struct_cov_new(n_rois: i32, thresh: f64) -> StructuralCovariance {
    let empty_roi = MorphometricROI {
        thickness: 0.0, surface_area: 0.0, volume: 0.0,
        mean_curvature: 0.0, sulcal_depth: 0.0, folding_index: 0.0,
        gm_volume: 0.0, wm_volume: 0.0,
    }
    StructuralCovariance {
        thickness_cov: [0.0; 4096],
        adj: [0; 4096],
        n_rois: n_rois,
        threshold: thresh,
        roi_data: [empty_roi; 64],
    }
}

/// Set structural covariance between two ROIs.
pub fn struct_set_cov(sc: StructuralCovariance, i: i32, j: i32, cov: f64) -> StructuralCovariance with Mut, Panic {
    var s = sc
    if i >= 0 && i < s.n_rois && j >= 0 && j < s.n_rois {
        s.thickness_cov[(i * 64 + j) as usize] = cov
        s.thickness_cov[(j * 64 + i) as usize] = cov
    }
    s
}

/// Set morphometric data for a single ROI.
pub fn struct_set_roi(sc: StructuralCovariance, idx: i32, roi: MorphometricROI) -> StructuralCovariance with Mut, Panic {
    var s = sc
    if idx >= 0 && idx < s.n_rois {
        s.roi_data[idx as usize] = roi
    }
    s
}

/// Threshold structural covariance to binary adjacency.
pub fn struct_threshold(sc: StructuralCovariance) -> StructuralCovariance with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = sc
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < s.n_rois {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < s.n_rois {
            if i != j {
                let c = s.thickness_cov[(i * 64 + j) as usize]
                let ac = if c < 0.0 { 0.0 - c } else { c }
                s.adj[(i * 64 + j) as usize] = if ac > s.threshold { 1 } else { 0 }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    s
}

/// Encode structural morphometry as a sedenion.
///
/// For a single ROI:
///   e0-e7:  8 morphometric features (thickness, area, volume, ...)
///   e8-e15: 8 features from the structurally covarying neighbor
///           (the ROI with highest covariance to this one)
///
/// This captures both the LOCAL morphometry and the NETWORK
/// context of each brain region.
pub fn morphometry_to_sedenion(sc: StructuralCovariance, roi_idx: i32) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    if roi_idx < 0 || roi_idx >= sc.n_rois { return s }

    let roi = sc.roi_data[roi_idx as usize]

    // Octonion half: this ROI's morphometry
    s[0] = roi.thickness
    s[1] = roi.surface_area / 1000.0   // scale to comparable range
    s[2] = roi.volume / 10000.0
    s[3] = roi.mean_curvature * 100.0
    s[4] = roi.sulcal_depth
    s[5] = roi.folding_index
    s[6] = roi.gm_volume / 10000.0
    s[7] = roi.wm_volume / 10000.0

    // Sedenion half: strongest covarying neighbor's morphometry
    var max_cov: f64 = 0.0
    var max_j: i32 = 0
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < sc.n_rois {
        if j != roi_idx {
            let c = sc.thickness_cov[(roi_idx * 64 + j) as usize]
            let ac = if c < 0.0 { 0.0 - c } else { c }
            if ac > max_cov { max_cov = ac; max_j = j }
        }
        j = j + 1
    }

    let neighbor = sc.roi_data[max_j as usize]
    s[8] = neighbor.thickness
    s[9] = neighbor.surface_area / 1000.0
    s[10] = neighbor.volume / 10000.0
    s[11] = neighbor.mean_curvature * 100.0
    s[12] = neighbor.sulcal_depth
    s[13] = neighbor.folding_index
    s[14] = neighbor.gm_volume / 10000.0
    s[15] = neighbor.wm_volume / 10000.0

    // Normalize
    var norm_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { norm_sq = norm_sq + s[k] * s[k]; k = k + 1 }
    let norm = sqrt_approx(norm_sq)
    if norm > 0.001 {
        k = 0
        while k < 16 { s[k] = s[k] / norm; k = k + 1 }
    }
    s
}

/// Compute η for the structural covariance network.
pub fn struct_eta(sc: StructuralCovariance) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sc.n_rois < 2 { return 0.0 }
    var total: i64 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < sc.n_rois {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < sc.n_rois {
            if sc.adj[(i * 64 + j) as usize] == 1 { total = total + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mk = (total as f64) / (sc.n_rois as f64)
    mk * mk / (sc.n_rois as f64)
}

fn sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}


// === FILE: stdlib/neuro/eeg.sio ===
//! stdlib/neuro/eeg.sio — EEG Connectivity Pipeline
//!
//! Transforms preprocessed EEG data into the Sounio neuroimaging stack:
//!   EEG coherence/PLV matrix → connectivity graph → ORC + associator + sedenion
//!
//! Input: N×N connectivity matrix from preprocessed EEG
//!        (e.g., MNE-Python → source-space → coherence/PLV/wPLI)
//!
//! EEG captures TEMPORAL dynamics that fMRI misses (ms resolution vs s).
//! The associator field on EEG connectivity measures whether the ORDER
//! of neural oscillation coupling matters — directly testing whether
//! cognitive cascades are associative (flexible) or non-associative (rigid).
//!
//! Frequency bands and their clinical significance:
//!   Delta (1-4 Hz):   deep sleep, brain injury markers
//!   Theta (4-8 Hz):   working memory, emotional processing
//!   Alpha (8-13 Hz):  resting state, attention gating
//!   Beta (13-30 Hz):  motor planning, active cognition
//!   Gamma (30-100 Hz): binding, consciousness, high-level processing
//!
//! The multi-band structure maps naturally to the Cayley-Dickson tower:
//!   5 bands × 2 (real + imaginary coherence) = 10 components
//!   + 6 inter-band coupling strengths = 16 components = one sedenion
//!
//! References:
//!   Boller et al. (2023): Ricci curvature in aging brain FC
//!   Sia et al. (2019): ORC community detection (ADHD-200)

/// Standard EEG frequency band indices
pub fn band_delta() -> i32 { 0 }    // 1-4 Hz
pub fn band_theta() -> i32 { 1 }    // 4-8 Hz
pub fn band_alpha() -> i32 { 2 }    // 8-13 Hz
pub fn band_beta() -> i32 { 3 }     // 13-30 Hz
pub fn band_gamma() -> i32 { 4 }    // 30-100 Hz

/// EEG connectivity data for one frequency band.
pub struct EegBandConnectivity {
    // Coherence matrix (row-major, max 32×32 = 1024)
    coherence: [f64; 1024],
    // Phase-locking value matrix
    plv: [f64; 1024],
    // Binary adjacency after thresholding
    adj: [i32; 1024],
    n_channels: i32,
    threshold: f64,
    band_idx: i32,
    // Band-specific power (per channel, for sedenion encoding)
    band_power: [f64; 32],
}

/// Multi-band EEG connectivity: 5 frequency bands.
///
/// The sedenion encoding uses:
///   e0-e4:   mean coherence per band (5 values)
///   e5-e9:   mean PLV per band (5 values)
///   e10-e15: inter-band coupling (6 unique pairs from 5 bands: C(5,2)=10,
///            compressed to 6 strongest by clinical relevance:
///            theta-alpha, alpha-beta, beta-gamma, theta-gamma,
///            delta-theta, alpha-gamma)
pub struct EegMultiBand {
    bands: [EegBandConnectivity; 5],
    n_channels: i32,
    // Inter-band coupling (phase-amplitude coupling / cross-frequency)
    // Stored as mean coupling strength per pair
    interband: [f64; 10],    // C(5,2) = 10 unique pairs
}

/// Create empty single-band EEG connectivity.
pub fn eeg_band_new(n_ch: i32, band: i32, thresh: f64) -> EegBandConnectivity {
    EegBandConnectivity {
        coherence: [0.0; 1024],
        plv: [0.0; 1024],
        adj: [0; 1024],
        n_channels: n_ch,
        threshold: thresh,
        band_idx: band,
        band_power: [0.0; 32],
    }
}

/// Set coherence between two EEG channels for a given band.
pub fn eeg_set_coherence(band: EegBandConnectivity, i: i32, j: i32, coh: f64, plv: f64) -> EegBandConnectivity with Mut, Panic {
    var b = band
    if i >= 0 && i < b.n_channels && j >= 0 && j < b.n_channels {
        b.coherence[(i * 32 + j) as usize] = coh
        b.coherence[(j * 32 + i) as usize] = coh
        b.plv[(i * 32 + j) as usize] = plv
        b.plv[(j * 32 + i) as usize] = plv
    }
    b
}

/// Threshold a single band's coherence matrix.
pub fn eeg_threshold_band(band: EegBandConnectivity) -> EegBandConnectivity with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var b = band
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < b.n_channels {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < b.n_channels {
            if i != j && b.coherence[(i * 32 + j) as usize] > b.threshold {
                b.adj[(i * 32 + j) as usize] = 1
            } else {
                b.adj[(i * 32 + j) as usize] = 0
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    b
}

/// Compute η for a single EEG band.
pub fn eeg_band_eta(band: EegBandConnectivity) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if band.n_channels < 2 { return 0.0 }
    var total_deg: i64 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < band.n_channels {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < band.n_channels {
            if band.adj[(i * 32 + j) as usize] == 1 { total_deg = total_deg + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mk = (total_deg as f64) / (band.n_channels as f64)
    mk * mk / (band.n_channels as f64)
}

/// Encode multi-band EEG as a sedenion.
///
/// e0-e4:   mean coherence per band (delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma)
/// e5-e9:   mean PLV per band
/// e10-e15: inter-band coupling (top 6 clinically relevant pairs)
///
/// This encoding captures both within-band (associative) and
/// cross-band (potentially non-associative) neural dynamics.
pub fn eeg_to_sedenion(mb: EegMultiBand) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

    var band: i32 = 0
    while band < 5 {
        // Mean coherence for this band
        var sum_coh: f64 = 0.0
        var sum_plv: f64 = 0.0
        var count: i64 = 0
        let b = mb.bands[band as usize]
        var i: i32 = 0
        while i < b.n_channels {
            var j: i32 = i + 1
            while j < b.n_channels {
                sum_coh = sum_coh + b.coherence[(i * 32 + j) as usize]
                sum_plv = sum_plv + b.plv[(i * 32 + j) as usize]
                count = count + 1
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        if count > 0 {
            s[band as usize] = sum_coh / (count as f64)
            s[(band + 5) as usize] = sum_plv / (count as f64)
        }
        band = band + 1
    }

    // Inter-band coupling (first 6 of the 10 pairs)
    var ib: i32 = 0
    while ib < 6 && ib < 10 {
        s[(ib + 10) as usize] = mb.interband[ib as usize]
        ib = ib + 1
    }

    // Normalize to unit sedenion
    var norm_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { norm_sq = norm_sq + s[k] * s[k]; k = k + 1 }
    let norm = sqrt_approx(norm_sq)
    if norm > 0.001 {
        k = 0
        while k < 16 { s[k] = s[k] / norm; k = k + 1 }
    }
    s
}

fn sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}


// === FILE: stdlib/neuro/fmri.sio ===
//! stdlib/neuro/fmri.sio — Functional MRI Connectivity Pipeline
//!
//! Transforms preprocessed fMRI data into the Sounio neuroimaging stack:
//!   fMRI correlation matrix → connectivity graph → ORC + associator + sedenion
//!
//! Input: N×N Pearson/partial correlation matrix from preprocessed fMRI
//!        (e.g., fMRIPrep → Schaefer/AAL/CC200 parcellation → time series → corr)
//!
//! What Sounio computes (what no other tool does):
//!   - ORC phase classification (hyperbolic/spherical/euclidean)
//!   - Octonion associator field (order-dependence of neural cascades)
//!   - Sedenion encoding (16-component algebraic fingerprint)
//!   - Zero-divisor proximity (structural degeneracy measure)
//!
//! Typical parcellations:
//!   AAL:  90 ROIs (Tzourio-Mazoyer 2002)
//!   CC200: 200 ROIs (Craddock 2012) — used in ABIDE-I
//!   Schaefer: 100/200/400/1000 ROIs (Schaefer 2018)
//!   Power: 264 ROIs (Power 2011)
//!
//! References:
//!   Agourakis & Gerenutti (2026), Papers 1-3: ORC phase transition theory
//!   Chatterjee et al. (2022): ORC in ASD (ABIDE-I)
//!   Boller et al. (2023): ORC in aging brain connectivity

// Max ROIs supported (limited by fixed arrays in Sounio)
// For CC200: N=200, adjacency = 200×200 = 40000 entries
// We use 64 ROIs max for the algebraic pipeline (ORC + associator)
// Full 200-ROI ORC requires the Julia/Python LP solver externally

/// Preprocessed fMRI functional connectivity data.
///
/// The correlation matrix is stored as a flat array (row-major, N×N).
/// Threshold converts continuous correlations to binary adjacency.
pub struct FmriConnectivity {
    // Correlation matrix (row-major, max 64×64 = 4096)
    corr: [f64; 4096],
    n_rois: i32,

    // Binary adjacency after thresholding
    adj: [i32; 4096],

    // Threshold used for binarization
    threshold: f64,

    // Per-ROI metadata
    roi_strength: [f64; 64],     // sum of correlations per ROI
    roi_degree: [i32; 64],       // number of suprathreshold connections

    // Subject metadata
    subject_id: i64,
    // Diagnostic group: 0=control, 1=ASD, 2=ADHD, 3=MDD, 4=SCZ
    group: i32,
    age: f64,
}

/// Create empty fMRI connectivity struct.
pub fn fmri_new(n_rois: i32, threshold: f64) -> FmriConnectivity {
    FmriConnectivity {
        corr: [0.0; 4096],
        n_rois: n_rois,
        adj: [0; 4096],
        threshold: threshold,
        roi_strength: [0.0; 64],
        roi_degree: [0; 64],
        subject_id: 0,
        group: 0,
        age: 0.0,
    }
}

/// Set a correlation value between two ROIs.
pub fn fmri_set_corr(fc: FmriConnectivity, i: i32, j: i32, val: f64) -> FmriConnectivity with Mut, Panic {
    var f = fc
    if i >= 0 && i < f.n_rois && j >= 0 && j < f.n_rois {
        f.corr[(i * 64 + j) as usize] = val
        f.corr[(j * 64 + i) as usize] = val  // symmetric
    }
    f
}

/// Threshold the correlation matrix to produce binary adjacency.
///
/// Edges where |corr(i,j)| > threshold AND i ≠ j are set to 1.
/// This is the standard approach for fMRI graph construction.
pub fn fmri_threshold(fc: FmriConnectivity) -> FmriConnectivity with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var f = fc
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < f.n_rois {
        var deg: i32 = 0
        var strength: f64 = 0.0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < f.n_rois {
            if i != j {
                let c = f.corr[(i * 64 + j) as usize]
                let ac = if c < 0.0 { 0.0 - c } else { c }
                if ac > f.threshold {
                    f.adj[(i * 64 + j) as usize] = 1
                    deg = deg + 1
                    strength = strength + ac
                } else {
                    f.adj[(i * 64 + j) as usize] = 0
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        f.roi_degree[i as usize] = deg
        f.roi_strength[i as usize] = strength
        i = i + 1
    }
    f
}

/// Compute the density parameter η = ⟨k⟩²/N.
///
/// This single scalar predicts the geometric phase of the brain network
/// via the phase transition formula η_c(N) = 3.75 − 14.62/√N.
pub fn fmri_eta(fc: FmriConnectivity) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if fc.n_rois < 2 { return 0.0 }
    var total_deg: i64 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < fc.n_rois {
        total_deg = total_deg + (fc.roi_degree[i as usize] as i64)
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean_k = (total_deg as f64) / (fc.n_rois as f64)
    mean_k * mean_k / (fc.n_rois as f64)
}

/// Compute the critical density η_c for this parcellation size.
pub fn fmri_eta_c(fc: FmriConnectivity) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if fc.n_rois < 2 { return 3.75 }
    3.75 - 14.62 / sqrt_approx(fc.n_rois as f64)
}

/// Classify the geometric phase of this brain network.
///
/// Returns: 0=DEGENERATE, 1=SPHERICAL, 2=HYPERBOLIC, 3=EUCLIDEAN
///
/// Clinical prediction (from Papers 1-3):
///   ADHD: η > η_c → SPHERICAL (excess short-range connectivity)
///   ASD:  η near η_c → boundary (local over-connectivity, long-range under)
///   MDD:  η < η_c, C > C* → HYPERBOLIC (bottlenecked, sparse)
///   Control: variable (depends on parcellation and threshold)
pub fn fmri_phase(fc: FmriConnectivity) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let eta = fmri_eta(fc)
    let eta_c = fmri_eta_c(fc)
    let clustering = fmri_clustering(fc)
    if eta > eta_c { return 1 }         // SPHERICAL
    if clustering > 0.05 { return 2 }   // HYPERBOLIC
    return 3                            // EUCLIDEAN
}

/// Global clustering coefficient of the thresholded brain graph.
pub fn fmri_clustering(fc: FmriConnectivity) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var triangles: i64 = 0
    var triples: i64 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < fc.n_rois {
        var j: i32 = i + 1
        while j < fc.n_rois {
            if fc.adj[(i * 64 + j) as usize] == 1 {
                // Count common neighbors
                var k: i32 = 0
                while k < fc.n_rois {
                    if k != i && k != j {
                        if fc.adj[(i * 64 + k) as usize] == 1 && fc.adj[(j * 64 + k) as usize] == 1 {
                            triangles = triangles + 1
                        }
                        if fc.adj[(i * 64 + k) as usize] == 1 || fc.adj[(j * 64 + k) as usize] == 1 {
                            triples = triples + 1
                        }
                    }
                    k = k + 1
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if triples > 0 { (triangles as f64) / (triples as f64) } else { 0.0 }
}

/// Distance to the phase boundary: η_c − η.
///
/// Positive = below boundary (hyperbolic side)
/// Negative = above boundary (spherical side)
/// Near zero = at the phase transition (critical regime)
///
/// Clinical: patients at the boundary may be most susceptible
/// to geometric phase shifts from treatment or disease progression.
pub fn fmri_phase_distance(fc: FmriConnectivity) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    fmri_eta_c(fc) - fmri_eta(fc)
}

// Helper
fn sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}


// === FILE: stdlib/neuro/meg.sio ===
//! stdlib/neuro/meg.sio — Magnetoencephalography Connectivity Pipeline
//!
//! MEG measures magnetic fields from neural currents — same temporal
//! resolution as EEG (ms) but better spatial localization.
//!
//! Input: source-space connectivity matrix from preprocessed MEG
//!        (e.g., MNE-Python → beamformer/dSPM → source coherence)
//!
//! MEG's advantage for the Sounio pipeline: source-space MEG provides
//! DIRECTIONAL connectivity (unlike fMRI correlation), enabling
//! directed graphs where the associator field measures whether
//! the CAUSAL ORDER of neural activation matters.
//!
//! The imaginary part of coherence (ImCoh) is particularly relevant:
//! it captures phase-lagged interactions (true neural communication)
//! while suppressing volume conduction artifacts. This gives a
//! natural complex-valued edge weight that maps to the Cayley-Dickson
//! tower: real part → octonion half, imaginary part → sedenion half.
//!
//! References:
//!   Gross et al. (2001): DICS beamformer for MEG source localization
//!   Nolte et al. (2004): Imaginary coherence for artifact rejection
//!   Colclough et al. (2015): MEG connectomics pipeline

/// MEG source-space connectivity.
///
/// Unlike EEG, MEG provides directional connectivity via Granger
/// causality or transfer entropy in source space. The adjacency
/// matrix is therefore DIRECTED (not symmetric), which means
/// the associator field captures genuine causal order-dependence.
pub struct MegConnectivity {
    // Directed connectivity matrix (max 64×64)
    // Row i, col j = influence FROM source i TO source j
    directed_conn: [f64; 4096],

    // Imaginary coherence (phase-lagged, artifact-free)
    imcoh: [f64; 4096],

    // Binary directed adjacency
    adj: [i32; 4096],
    n_sources: i32,
    threshold: f64,

    // Per-source metadata
    source_power: [f64; 64],
    source_in_degree: [i32; 64],
    source_out_degree: [i32; 64],
}

/// Create empty MEG connectivity.
pub fn meg_new(n_src: i32, thresh: f64) -> MegConnectivity {
    MegConnectivity {
        directed_conn: [0.0; 4096],
        imcoh: [0.0; 4096],
        adj: [0; 4096],
        n_sources: n_src,
        threshold: thresh,
        source_power: [0.0; 64],
        source_in_degree: [0; 64],
        source_out_degree: [0; 64],
    }
}

/// Set directed connection strength from source i to source j.
/// Note: NOT symmetric. meg_set(fc, i, j, v) ≠ meg_set(fc, j, i, v).
pub fn meg_set_conn(mc: MegConnectivity, from: i32, to: i32, strength: f64, imcoh_val: f64) -> MegConnectivity with Mut, Panic {
    var m = mc
    if from >= 0 && from < m.n_sources && to >= 0 && to < m.n_sources {
        m.directed_conn[(from * 64 + to) as usize] = strength
        m.imcoh[(from * 64 + to) as usize] = imcoh_val
    }
    m
}

/// Threshold directed connectivity to binary adjacency.
pub fn meg_threshold(mc: MegConnectivity) -> MegConnectivity with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m = mc
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < m.n_sources {
        var in_d: i32 = 0
        var out_d: i32 = 0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < m.n_sources {
            if i != j {
                let c = m.directed_conn[(i * 64 + j) as usize]
                let ac = if c < 0.0 { 0.0 - c } else { c }
                if ac > m.threshold {
                    m.adj[(i * 64 + j) as usize] = 1
                    out_d = out_d + 1
                } else {
                    m.adj[(i * 64 + j) as usize] = 0
                }
                // Check incoming
                let ci = m.directed_conn[(j * 64 + i) as usize]
                let aci = if ci < 0.0 { 0.0 - ci } else { ci }
                if aci > m.threshold { in_d = in_d + 1 }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        m.source_out_degree[i as usize] = out_d
        m.source_in_degree[i as usize] = in_d
        i = i + 1
    }
    m
}

/// Compute η for the directed MEG graph.
/// Uses mean total degree (in + out) / 2 as effective k.
pub fn meg_eta(mc: MegConnectivity) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if mc.n_sources < 2 { return 0.0 }
    var total_edges: i64 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < mc.n_sources {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < mc.n_sources {
            if mc.adj[(i * 64 + j) as usize] == 1 { total_edges = total_edges + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean_k = (total_edges as f64) / (mc.n_sources as f64)
    mean_k * mean_k / (mc.n_sources as f64)
}

/// Encode MEG connectivity as a sedenion using ImCoh structure.
///
/// The imaginary coherence provides a natural complex structure:
///   Real part of edge weight → octonion half (e0-e7)
///   Imaginary part → sedenion half (e8-e15)
///
/// This is the most natural sedenion encoding among all modalities
/// because MEG's imaginary coherence IS a complex number whose
/// real and imaginary parts have distinct physical meaning
/// (instantaneous vs phase-lagged coupling).
pub fn meg_to_sedenion(mc: MegConnectivity) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

    // Compute graph statistics for sedenion components
    // e0: mean directed strength
    // e1: mean ImCoh (phase-lagged coupling)
    // e2: in/out degree asymmetry (directionality)
    // e3-e7: top 5 source powers
    // e8: η (density parameter)
    // e9: clustering coefficient
    // e10-e15: ImCoh statistics per brain region group

    var sum_str: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_imcoh: f64 = 0.0
    var edge_count: i64 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < mc.n_sources {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < mc.n_sources {
            if mc.adj[(i * 64 + j) as usize] == 1 {
                sum_str = sum_str + mc.directed_conn[(i * 64 + j) as usize]
                sum_imcoh = sum_imcoh + mc.imcoh[(i * 64 + j) as usize]
                edge_count = edge_count + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if edge_count > 0 {
        s[0] = sum_str / (edge_count as f64)       // mean directed strength
        s[8] = sum_imcoh / (edge_count as f64)      // mean ImCoh (sedenion half)
    }

    // Degree asymmetry per source (first 7 sources → e1-e7)
    i = 0
    while i < 7 && i < mc.n_sources {
        let total = (mc.source_in_degree[i as usize] + mc.source_out_degree[i as usize]) as f64
        if total > 0.0 {
            s[(i + 1) as usize] = ((mc.source_out_degree[i as usize] - mc.source_in_degree[i as usize]) as f64) / total
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Source powers in sedenion half (e9-e15)
    i = 0
    while i < 7 && i < mc.n_sources {
        s[(i + 9) as usize] = mc.source_power[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Normalize
    var norm_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { norm_sq = norm_sq + s[k] * s[k]; k = k + 1 }
    let norm = sqrt_approx(norm_sq)
    if norm > 0.001 {
        k = 0
        while k < 16 { s[k] = s[k] / norm; k = k + 1 }
    }
    s
}

fn sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}

// === FILE: stdlib/neuro/sleep.sio ===
//! stdlib/neuro/sleep.sio — Sleep Stage Coherence Models
//!
//! Generates neurophysiologically motivated EEG coherence matrices
//! for each AASM sleep stage (Wake, N1, N2, N3, REM).
//!
//! These are SYNTHETIC models based on published sleep EEG literature:
//!   - Wake: high alpha/beta coherence, low delta
//!   - N1 (drowsy): alpha drops, theta rises
//!   - N2 (light sleep): sleep spindles (sigma 12-15Hz in beta range)
//!   - N3 (deep sleep): dominant delta, high-amplitude slow waves
//!   - REM: wake-like gamma/beta, but with theta + phasic bursts
//!
//! The coherence matrix is 16×16 (16 channels: standard 10-20 subset)
//! which maps naturally to the sedenion's 16 components.
//!
//! References:
//!   Prerau et al. (2017): Sleep neurophysiology review
//!   Boller et al. (2023): Ricci curvature captures aging in brain FC

// ============================================================================
// SLEEP STAGE ENUM
// ============================================================================

// Stage codes: 0=Wake, 1=N1, 2=N2, 3=N3, 4=REM
pub fn stage_wake() -> i32 { 0 }
pub fn stage_n1() -> i32 { 1 }
pub fn stage_n2() -> i32 { 2 }
pub fn stage_n3() -> i32 { 3 }
pub fn stage_rem() -> i32 { 4 }

// ============================================================================
// COHERENCE MATRIX (16×16 = 256 entries, row-major)
// ============================================================================

pub struct SleepCoherence {
    // 16×16 coherence matrix (symmetric, diagonal = 1.0)
    coh: [f64; 256],
    n: i32,
    stage: i32,
    // Per-channel power in 5 bands [ch * 5 + band]
    band_power: [f64; 80],
    // Global metrics
    mean_coherence: f64,
    clustering: f64,
    density: f64,
}

pub fn sleep_coherence_new(stage: i32) -> SleepCoherence {
    SleepCoherence {
        coh: [0.0; 256],
        n: 16,
        stage: stage,
        band_power: [0.0; 80],
        mean_coherence: 0.0,
        clustering: 0.0,
        density: 0.0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// LCG RNG (deterministic, reproducible)
// ============================================================================

fn lcg(s: i64) -> i64 { s * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407 }
fn lcg_f64(s: i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let v = if s < 0 { 0 - s } else { s }
    (v as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// SYNTHETIC COHERENCE GENERATORS
// ============================================================================
//
// Each generator produces a 16×16 coherence matrix with properties
// matching the neurophysiology of that sleep stage.
//
// Key parameters per stage (from literature):
//   mean_coh: overall connectivity strength
//   local_bias: how much nearby channels are more coherent
//   noise: random variation

/// Generate coherence matrix for a specific sleep stage.
///
/// The matrices differ in:
///   - Overall connectivity density (η parameter)
///   - Clustering coefficient (C parameter)
///   - Band-specific power distribution
///   - Hemispheric symmetry
///
/// These differences are what ORC phase classification detects.
pub fn generate_stage_coherence(stage: i32, seed: i64) -> SleepCoherence with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var sc = sleep_coherence_new(stage)

    // Stage-specific parameters (neurophysiologically motivated)
    // mean_coh: base coherence level
    // cluster_strength: local triangle formation
    // long_range: interhemispheric / distant connections
    let mean_coh = if stage == 0 { 0.45 }       // Wake: moderate-high
                   else if stage == 1 { 0.30 }   // N1: dropping
                   else if stage == 2 { 0.35 }   // N2: spindle bursts
                   else if stage == 3 { 0.55 }   // N3: high delta sync
                   else { 0.40 }                  // REM: wake-like

    let cluster_str = if stage == 0 { 0.25 }     // Wake: moderate clustering
                      else if stage == 1 { 0.15 } // N1: low
                      else if stage == 2 { 0.30 } // N2: spindle clusters
                      else if stage == 3 { 0.45 } // N3: massive delta clusters
                      else { 0.20 }                // REM: low-moderate

    let long_range = if stage == 0 { 0.20 }       // Wake: good long-range
                     else if stage == 1 { 0.10 }   // N1: fragmenting
                     else if stage == 2 { 0.15 }   // N2: some spindle spread
                     else if stage == 3 { 0.08 }   // N3: very local
                     else { 0.25 }                  // REM: strong long-range

    let noise_level = 0.05

    // Generate coherence matrix
    var s = seed
    var u: i32 = 0
    while u < 16 {
        sc.coh[(u * 16 + u) as usize] = 1.0  // diagonal
        var v: i32 = u + 1
        while v < 16 {
            // Distance: channels are laid out roughly as 10-20 positions
            // Nearby channels (|u-v| <= 2) have higher coherence
            let dist = v - u
            let local_factor = if dist <= 2 { 1.0 + cluster_str }
                              else if dist <= 4 { 1.0 }
                              else if dist <= 8 { 0.5 + long_range }
                              else { long_range }

            // Hemispheric symmetry: channels 0-7 left, 8-15 right
            // Homologous pairs (u, u+8) have extra coherence
            let hemi_bonus = if u < 8 && v == u + 8 { 0.15 } else { 0.0 }

            s = lcg(s)
            let noise = (lcg_f64(s) - 0.5) * noise_level

            var coh_val = mean_coh * local_factor + hemi_bonus + noise
            if coh_val > 1.0 { coh_val = 1.0 }
            if coh_val < 0.0 { coh_val = 0.0 }

            sc.coh[(u * 16 + v) as usize] = coh_val
            sc.coh[(v * 16 + u) as usize] = coh_val  // symmetric
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }

    // Band power per channel (5 bands × 16 channels)
    // Delta=0, Theta=1, Alpha=2, Beta=3, Gamma=4
    u = 0
    while u < 16 {
        s = lcg(s)
        let ch_noise = lcg_f64(s) * 0.1

        if stage == 0 {
            // Wake: alpha dominant, some beta/gamma
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 0) as usize] = 0.10 + ch_noise  // delta
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 1) as usize] = 0.15 + ch_noise  // theta
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 2) as usize] = 0.35 + ch_noise  // alpha
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 3) as usize] = 0.25 + ch_noise  // beta
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 4) as usize] = 0.15 + ch_noise  // gamma
        } else if stage == 1 {
            // N1: alpha dropping, theta rising
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 0) as usize] = 0.15 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 1) as usize] = 0.30 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 2) as usize] = 0.20 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 3) as usize] = 0.20 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 4) as usize] = 0.10 + ch_noise
        } else if stage == 2 {
            // N2: sleep spindles (sigma in beta), K-complexes
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 0) as usize] = 0.20 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 1) as usize] = 0.20 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 2) as usize] = 0.15 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 3) as usize] = 0.30 + ch_noise  // spindles
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 4) as usize] = 0.10 + ch_noise
        } else if stage == 3 {
            // N3: delta dominant (>75% power)
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 0) as usize] = 0.55 + ch_noise  // massive delta
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 1) as usize] = 0.15 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 2) as usize] = 0.10 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 3) as usize] = 0.10 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 4) as usize] = 0.05 + ch_noise
        } else {
            // REM: mixed, theta + beta + gamma, like wake but with theta
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 0) as usize] = 0.10 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 1) as usize] = 0.25 + ch_noise  // theta prominent
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 2) as usize] = 0.15 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 3) as usize] = 0.25 + ch_noise
            sc.band_power[(u * 5 + 4) as usize] = 0.20 + ch_noise  // gamma for dreams
        }
        u = u + 1
    }

    // Compute global metrics
    var sum_coh: f64 = 0.0
    var edge_count: i32 = 0
    u = 0
    while u < 16 {
        var v: i32 = u + 1
        while v < 16 {
            sum_coh = sum_coh + sc.coh[(u * 16 + v) as usize]
            if sc.coh[(u * 16 + v) as usize] > 0.3 { edge_count = edge_count + 1 }
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    let n_pairs = 16 * 15 / 2
    sc.mean_coherence = sum_coh / (n_pairs as f64)
    sc.density = (edge_count as f64) / (n_pairs as f64)

    // Compute clustering (fraction of triangles among edges > 0.3)
    var triangles: i32 = 0
    var possible: i32 = 0
    u = 0
    while u < 16 {
        var v: i32 = u + 1
        while v < 16 {
            if sc.coh[(u * 16 + v) as usize] > 0.3 {
                var w: i32 = v + 1
                while w < 16 {
                    if sc.coh[(u * 16 + w) as usize] > 0.3 {
                        possible = possible + 1
                        if sc.coh[(v * 16 + w) as usize] > 0.3 {
                            triangles = triangles + 1
                        }
                    }
                    w = w + 1
                }
            }
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    sc.clustering = if possible > 0 { (triangles as f64) / (possible as f64) } else { 0.0 }

    sc
}

// ============================================================================
// SEDENION ENCODING OF SLEEP EEG
// ============================================================================

/// Encode a sleep coherence matrix as a sedenion.
///
/// The 16 components:
///   e0-e4:   mean band power (delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma)
///   e5-e9:   mean band coherence (same 5 bands, averaged over channel pairs)
///   e10:     overall mean coherence
///   e11:     clustering coefficient
///   e12:     density
///   e13:     hemispheric asymmetry (L-R power difference)
///   e14:     anterior-posterior gradient
///   e15:     stage-invariant noise term
pub fn sleep_to_sedenion(sc: SleepCoherence) -> [f64; 16] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

    // e0-e4: mean band power across channels
    var band: i32 = 0
    while band < 5 {
        var sum: f64 = 0.0
        var ch: i32 = 0
        while ch < 16 {
            sum = sum + sc.band_power[(ch * 5 + band) as usize]
            ch = ch + 1
        }
        s[band as usize] = sum / 16.0
        band = band + 1
    }

    // e5-e9: band coherence approximation
    // Use overall coherence scaled by band power ratio
    band = 0
    while band < 5 {
        s[(band + 5) as usize] = sc.mean_coherence * s[band as usize]
        band = band + 1
    }

    // e10-e12: graph metrics
    s[10] = sc.mean_coherence
    s[11] = sc.clustering
    s[12] = sc.density

    // e13: hemispheric asymmetry
    var left_power: f64 = 0.0
    var right_power: f64 = 0.0
    var ch: i32 = 0
    while ch < 8 {
        var b: i32 = 0
        while b < 5 {
            left_power = left_power + sc.band_power[(ch * 5 + b) as usize]
            right_power = right_power + sc.band_power[((ch + 8) * 5 + b) as usize]
            b = b + 1
        }
        ch = ch + 1
    }
    let total = left_power + right_power
    s[13] = if total > 0.001 { (left_power - right_power) / total } else { 0.0 }

    // e14: anterior-posterior gradient (front vs back channels)
    var front: f64 = 0.0
    var back: f64 = 0.0
    ch = 0
    while ch < 4 {
        var b: i32 = 0
        while b < 5 {
            front = front + sc.band_power[(ch * 5 + b) as usize]
            back = back + sc.band_power[((ch + 12) * 5 + b) as usize]
            b = b + 1
        }
        ch = ch + 1
    }
    let fb_total = front + back
    s[14] = if fb_total > 0.001 { (front - back) / fb_total } else { 0.0 }

    // e15: fixed noise floor
    s[15] = 0.01

    // Normalize to unit norm
    var norm_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 16 { norm_sq = norm_sq + s[i as usize] * s[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    let norm = sqrt_f64(norm_sq)
    if norm > 0.001 {
        i = 0
        while i < 16 { s[i as usize] = s[i as usize] / norm; i = i + 1 }
    }

    s
}

// ============================================================================
// ORC PHASE CLASSIFICATION (simplified, self-contained)
// ============================================================================

/// Compute η = ⟨k⟩²/N for the coherence graph (threshold > 0.3).
pub fn sleep_eta(sc: SleepCoherence) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var edges: i32 = 0
    var u: i32 = 0
    while u < 16 {
        var v: i32 = u + 1
        while v < 16 {
            if sc.coh[(u * 16 + v) as usize] > 0.3 { edges = edges + 1 }
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    let mean_k = (2.0 * (edges as f64)) / 16.0
    mean_k * mean_k / 16.0
}

/// Critical density η_c(N) = 3.75 - 14.62/√N
pub fn sleep_eta_c() -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    3.75 - 14.62 / sqrt_f64(16.0)
}

/// Phase classification: 0=DEGENERATE, 1=SPHERICAL, 2=HYPERBOLIC, 3=EUCLIDEAN
pub fn sleep_phase(sc: SleepCoherence) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let eta = sleep_eta(sc)
    let eta_c = sleep_eta_c()
    let c_star = 0.05

    if eta > eta_c { return 1 }  // SPHERICAL
    if sc.clustering > c_star { return 2 }  // HYPERBOLIC
    return 3  // EUCLIDEAN
}

/// Generate a full sleep cycle: Wake → N1 → N2 → N3 → N2 → REM
/// Returns 6 coherence matrices representing one cycle.
pub fn generate_sleep_cycle(base_seed: i64) -> [SleepCoherence; 6] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var cycle: [SleepCoherence; 6] = [sleep_coherence_new(0); 6]
    cycle[0] = generate_stage_coherence(0, base_seed)            // Wake
    cycle[1] = generate_stage_coherence(1, base_seed + 1000)     // N1
    cycle[2] = generate_stage_coherence(2, base_seed + 2000)     // N2
    cycle[3] = generate_stage_coherence(3, base_seed + 3000)     // N3
    cycle[4] = generate_stage_coherence(2, base_seed + 4000)     // N2 again
    cycle[5] = generate_stage_coherence(4, base_seed + 5000)     // REM
    cycle
}


// === FILE: stdlib/nn/activation.sio ===
// activation.d - Neural network activation functions and derivatives
//
// Provides common activation functions used in neural networks:
// - ReLU: Rectified Linear Unit - max(0, x)
// - Sigmoid: σ(x) = 1 / (1 + e^(-x))
// - Tanh: tanh(x) = (e^x - e^(-x)) / (e^x + e^(-x))
//
// Each function has a corresponding derivative for backpropagation.
//
// All functions are scalar (f64 -> f64) for simplicity.

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 {
        return 0.0 - x
    }
    return x
}

// Exponential function using Taylor series
fn exp_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // For large |x|, use recursion to avoid overflow
    if x > 20.0 {
        let half = exp_val(x / 2.0)
        return half * half
    }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 {
        return 1.0 / exp_val(0.0 - x)
    }

    // Taylor series: e^x = 1 + x + x^2/2! + x^3/3! + ...
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var count = 1
    while count <= 20 {
        term = term * x / count
        sum = sum + term
        count = count + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// Max of two values
fn max_val(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

// Min of two values
fn min_val(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// RELU - RECTIFIED LINEAR UNIT
// ============================================================================

// ReLU: f(x) = max(0, x)
// Advantages: Simple, fast, no vanishing gradient for x > 0
fn relu(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 {
        return x
    }
    return 0.0
}

// ReLU derivative: f'(x) = 1 if x > 0, else 0
// Note: At x=0, technically undefined, but we use 0 by convention
fn relu_deriv(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 {
        return 1.0
    }
    return 0.0
}

// Leaky ReLU: f(x) = x if x > 0, else alpha * x
// Helps prevent "dying ReLU" problem
fn leaky_relu(x: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 {
        return x
    }
    return alpha * x
}

// Leaky ReLU derivative
fn leaky_relu_deriv(x: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 {
        return 1.0
    }
    return alpha
}

// ============================================================================
// SIGMOID - LOGISTIC FUNCTION
// ============================================================================

// Sigmoid: σ(x) = 1 / (1 + e^(-x))
// Range: (0, 1)
// Used for: Binary classification, gates in LSTMs
fn sigmoid(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Numerically stable version:
    // If x >= 0: 1 / (1 + exp(-x))
    // If x < 0: exp(x) / (1 + exp(x))
    if x >= 0.0 {
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + exp_val(0.0 - x))
    } else {
        let ex = exp_val(x)
        return ex / (1.0 + ex)
    }
}

// Sigmoid derivative: σ'(x) = σ(x) * (1 - σ(x))
// This is why sigmoid is convenient: derivative in terms of function value
fn sigmoid_deriv(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let s = sigmoid(x)
    return s * (1.0 - s)
}

// Sigmoid derivative when you already have σ(x)
fn sigmoid_deriv_from_output(sigmoid_val: f64) -> f64 {
    return sigmoid_val * (1.0 - sigmoid_val)
}

// ============================================================================
// TANH - HYPERBOLIC TANGENT
// ============================================================================

// Tanh: tanh(x) = (e^x - e^(-x)) / (e^x + e^(-x))
// Range: (-1, 1)
// Centered at 0 (unlike sigmoid), often works better than sigmoid
fn tanh_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Numerically stable version:
    // tanh(x) = (e^(2x) - 1) / (e^(2x) + 1) for x >= 0
    // tanh(x) = -tanh(-x) for x < 0
    if x >= 0.0 {
        if x > 20.0 { return 1.0 }  // Saturates for large x
        let e2x = exp_val(2.0 * x)
        return (e2x - 1.0) / (e2x + 1.0)
    } else {
        return 0.0 - tanh_val(0.0 - x)
    }
}

// Tanh derivative: tanh'(x) = 1 - tanh(x)^2
fn tanh_deriv(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let t = tanh_val(x)
    return 1.0 - t * t
}

// Tanh derivative when you already have tanh(x)
fn tanh_deriv_from_output(tanh_output: f64) -> f64 {
    return 1.0 - tanh_output * tanh_output
}

// ============================================================================
// SOFTPLUS - SMOOTH RELU
// ============================================================================

// Softplus: f(x) = ln(1 + e^x)
// Smooth approximation of ReLU
fn softplus(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 20.0 {
        return x  // For large x, ln(1 + e^x) ≈ x
    }
    return ln_val(1.0 + exp_val(x))
}

// Softplus derivative: f'(x) = 1 / (1 + e^(-x)) = sigmoid(x)
fn softplus_deriv(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return sigmoid(x)
}

// ============================================================================
// NATURAL LOGARITHM (needed for softplus)
// ============================================================================

// Natural log using Taylor series around x=1
fn ln_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 999999.0 }  // Undefined for x <= 0
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    // For x far from 1, use ln(x) = ln(x/e^k) + k where k brings x/e^k close to 1
    if x > 10.0 {
        return 2.302585093 + ln_val(x / 10.0)  // ln(10) ≈ 2.302585093
    }
    if x < 0.1 {
        return 0.0 - 2.302585093 + ln_val(x * 10.0)
    }

    // Taylor series: ln(x) = ln(1 + y) = y - y^2/2 + y^3/3 - y^4/4 + ...
    // where y = x - 1
    let y_val = x - 1.0
    var sum = 0.0
    var term = y_val
    var count = 1
    while count <= 20 {
        if count % 2 == 1 {
            sum = sum + term / count
        } else {
            sum = sum - term / count
        }
        term = term * y_val
        count = count + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// ============================================================================
// ELU - EXPONENTIAL LINEAR UNIT
// ============================================================================

// ELU: f(x) = x if x > 0, else alpha * (e^x - 1)
// Smoother than ReLU, can produce negative outputs
fn elu(x: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 {
        return x
    }
    return alpha * (exp_val(x) - 1.0)
}

// ELU derivative
fn elu_deriv(x: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 {
        return 1.0
    }
    return alpha * exp_val(x)
}

// ============================================================================
// SWISH / SILU - SELF-GATED ACTIVATION
// ============================================================================

// Swish: f(x) = x * sigmoid(x)
// Also called SiLU (Sigmoid Linear Unit)
// Used in many modern architectures
fn swish(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return x * sigmoid(x)
}

// Swish derivative: f'(x) = f(x) + sigmoid(x) * (1 - f(x))
fn swish_deriv(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let s = sigmoid(x)
    let f = x * s
    return f + s * (1.0 - f)
}

// ============================================================================
// IDENTITY - LINEAR ACTIVATION
// ============================================================================

// Identity: f(x) = x
// Used in regression output layers
fn identity(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return x
}

// Identity derivative: f'(x) = 1
fn identity_deriv(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return 1.0
}

// === FILE: stdlib/nn/autograd.sio ===
// autograd.d - Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation (Backpropagation)
//
// Implements a Wengert tape for gradient computation.
// Uses struct creation (not mutation) to work with Sounio semantics.

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS (locally defined, no external dependency)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 20.0 { return exp_f64(x / 2.0) * exp_f64(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / exp_f64(0.0 - x) }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i <= 20 { term = term * x / i; sum = sum + term; i = i + 1 }
    return sum
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x / 2.0
    if guess < 1.0 { guess = 1.0 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    return guess
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000000.0 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    if x > 1.5 { return 2.0 * ln_f64(sqrt_f64(x)) }
    if x < 0.7 { return 0.0 - ln_f64(1.0 / x) }
    let u = x - 1.0
    var sum = 0.0
    var term = u
    var i = 1
    while i <= 30 { sum = sum + term / i; term = 0.0 - term * u; i = i + 1 }
    return sum
}

fn log_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { return ln_f64(x) }

fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var v = x
    while v > 3.14159265358979 { v = v - 6.28318530717959 }
    while v < 0.0 - 3.14159265358979 { v = v + 6.28318530717959 }
    let x2 = v * v
    var term = v
    var sum = v
    term = 0.0 - term * x2 / 6.0;   sum = sum + term
    term = 0.0 - term * x2 / 20.0;  sum = sum + term
    term = 0.0 - term * x2 / 42.0;  sum = sum + term
    term = 0.0 - term * x2 / 72.0;  sum = sum + term
    term = 0.0 - term * x2 / 110.0; sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return sin_f64(x + 1.5707963267949)
}

fn cosh_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return (exp_f64(x) + exp_f64(0.0 - x)) / 2.0
}

fn tanh_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let ep = exp_f64(x)
    let en = exp_f64(0.0 - x)
    return (ep - en) / (ep + en)
}

fn sigmoid_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + exp_f64(0.0 - x))
}

fn relu_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 { x } else { 0.0 }
}

fn elu_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x >= 0.0 { x } else { exp_f64(x) - 1.0 }
}

fn softplus(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return ln_f64(1.0 + exp_f64(x))
}

fn swish(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return x * sigmoid_f64(x)
}

// ============================================================================
// MISSING STRUCT/FN DEFINITIONS
// ============================================================================

struct Attention3Result {
    output: f64,
    weight1: f64,
    weight2: f64,
    weight3: f64,
}

fn scaled_dot_attention_3(
    q: f64,
    key1: f64, key2: f64, key3: f64,
    value1: f64, value2: f64, value3: f64,
    d_k: f64
) -> Attention3Result {
    let scale = sqrt_f64(d_k)
    let score1 = q * key1 / scale
    let score2 = q * key2 / scale
    let score3 = q * key3 / scale
    let weights = softmax_3(score1, score2, score3)
    let output = weights.p1 * value1 + weights.p2 * value2 + weights.p3 * value3
    return Attention3Result {
        output: output,
        weight1: weights.p1,
        weight2: weights.p2,
        weight3: weights.p3,
    }
}

struct Vec5 {
    x1: f64,
    x2: f64,
    x3: f64,
    x4: f64,
    x5: f64,
}

fn LOG_EPSILON() -> f64 { return 0.0000001 }

// ============================================================================
// TAPE STRUCTURE - 6 slots for simplicity
// ============================================================================

struct Tape {
    // Slot 0
    op0: i64, a10: i64, a20: i64, v0: f64, g0: f64,
    // Slot 1
    op1: i64, a11: i64, a21: i64, v1: f64, g1: f64,
    // Slot 2
    op2: i64, a12: i64, a22: i64, v2: f64, g2: f64,
    // Slot 3
    op3: i64, a13: i64, a23: i64, v3: f64, g3: f64,
    // Slot 4
    op4: i64, a14: i64, a24: i64, v4: f64, g4: f64,
    // Slot 5
    op5: i64, a15: i64, a25: i64, v5: f64, g5: f64,
    len: i64
}

fn tape_new() -> Tape {
    return Tape {
        op0: 0, a10: 0, a20: 0, v0: 0.0, g0: 0.0,
        op1: 0, a11: 0, a21: 0, v1: 0.0, g1: 0.0,
        op2: 0, a12: 0, a22: 0, v2: 0.0, g2: 0.0,
        op3: 0, a13: 0, a23: 0, v3: 0.0, g3: 0.0,
        op4: 0, a14: 0, a24: 0, v4: 0.0, g4: 0.0,
        op5: 0, a15: 0, a25: 0, v5: 0.0, g5: 0.0,
        len: 0
    }
}

// GETTERS
// ============================================================================

fn get_v(t: Tape, i: i64) -> f64 {
    if i == 0 { return t.v0 }
    if i == 1 { return t.v1 }
    if i == 2 { return t.v2 }
    if i == 3 { return t.v3 }
    if i == 4 { return t.v4 }
    if i == 5 { return t.v5 }
    return 0.0
}

fn get_g(t: Tape, i: i64) -> f64 {
    if i == 0 { return t.g0 }
    if i == 1 { return t.g1 }
    if i == 2 { return t.g2 }
    if i == 3 { return t.g3 }
    if i == 4 { return t.g4 }
    if i == 5 { return t.g5 }
    return 0.0
}

fn get_op(t: Tape, i: i64) -> i64 {
    if i == 0 { return t.op0 }
    if i == 1 { return t.op1 }
    if i == 2 { return t.op2 }
    if i == 3 { return t.op3 }
    if i == 4 { return t.op4 }
    if i == 5 { return t.op5 }
    return 0
}

fn get_a1(t: Tape, i: i64) -> i64 {
    if i == 0 { return t.a10 }
    if i == 1 { return t.a11 }
    if i == 2 { return t.a12 }
    if i == 3 { return t.a13 }
    if i == 4 { return t.a14 }
    if i == 5 { return t.a15 }
    return 0
}

    if i == 0 { return t.a20 }
    if i == 1 { return t.a21 }
    if i == 2 { return t.a22 }
    if i == 3 { return t.a23 }
    if i == 4 { return t.a24 }
    if i == 5 { return t.a25 }
    return 0
}

fn set_g3(t: Tape, v: f64) -> Tape {

    return Tape { op0: t.op0, a10: t.a10, a20: t.a20, v0: t.v0, g0: t.g0,

fn set_g(t: Tape, i: i64, v: f64) -> Tape {
    if i == 0 { return set_g0(t, v) }
    if i == 1 { return set_g1(t, v) }
    if i == 2 { return set_g2(t, v) }
    if i == 3 { return set_g3(t, v) }
    if i == 4 { return set_g4(t, v) }
    if i == 5 { return set_g5(t, v) }
    return t
}

fn add_g(t: Tape, i: i64, v: f64) -> Tape {
    if i < 0 { return t }  // Skip for negative indices (no parent)
    let old = get_g(t, i)
    return set_g(t, i, old + v)
}

fn push4(t: Tape, op: i64, a1: i64, a2: i64, v: f64) -> Tape {
    return Tape { op0: t.op0, a10: t.a10, a20: t.a20, v0: t.v0, g0: t.g0,
        op1: t.op1, a11: t.a11, a21: t.a21, v1: t.v1, g1: t.g1,
        op2: t.op2, a12: t.a12, a22: t.a22, v2: t.v2, g2: t.g2,
        op3: t.op3, a13: t.a13, a23: t.a23, v3: t.v3, g3: t.g3,
        op4: op, a14: a1, a24: a2, v4: v, g4: 0.0,
        op5: t.op5, a15: t.a15, a25: t.a25, v5: t.v5, g5: t.g5, len: 5 }
}

fn push5(t: Tape, op: i64, a1: i64, a2: i64, v: f64) -> Tape {
    return Tape { op0: t.op0, a10: t.a10, a20: t.a20, v0: t.v0, g0: t.g0,
        op1: t.op1, a11: t.a11, a21: t.a21, v1: t.v1, g1: t.g1,
        op2: t.op2, a12: t.a12, a22: t.a22, v2: t.v2, g2: t.g2,
        op3: t.op3, a13: t.a13, a23: t.a23, v3: t.v3, g3: t.g3,
        op4: t.op4, a14: t.a14, a24: t.a24, v4: t.v4, g4: t.g4,
        op5: op, a15: a1, a25: a2, v5: v, g5: 0.0, len: 6 }
}

fn push(t: Tape, op: i64, a1: i64, a2: i64, v: f64) -> Tape {
    let i = t.len
    if i == 0 { return push0(t, op, a1, a2, v) }
    if i == 1 { return push1(t, op, a1, a2, v) }
    if i == 2 { return push2(t, op, a1, a2, v) }
    if i == 3 { return push3(t, op, a1, a2, v) }
    if i == 4 { return push4(t, op, a1, a2, v) }
    if i == 5 { return push5(t, op, a1, a2, v) }
    return t
}

// ============================================================================
// OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

fn tvar(t: Tape, v: f64) -> Tape { return push(t, OP_VAR(), 0 - 1, 0 - 1, v) }

fn tadd(t: Tape, a: i64, b: i64) -> Tape {
    return push(t, OP_ADD(), a, b, get_v(t, a) + get_v(t, b))
}

fn tmul(t: Tape, a: i64, b: i64) -> Tape {
    return push(t, OP_MUL(), a, b, get_v(t, a) * get_v(t, b))
}

fn tdiv(t: Tape, a: i64, b: i64) -> Tape {
    return push(t, OP_DIV(), a, b, get_v(t, a) / get_v(t, b))
}

fn texp(t: Tape, a: i64) -> Tape {
    return push(t, OP_EXP(), a, 0 - 1, exp_f64(get_v(t, a)))
}

fn tsqrt(t: Tape, a: i64) -> Tape {
    return push(t, OP_SQRT(), a, 0 - 1, sqrt_f64(get_v(t, a)))
}

fn tsin(t: Tape, a: i64) -> Tape {
    return push(t, OP_SIN(), a, 0 - 1, sin_f64(get_v(t, a)))
}

fn tsigmoid(t: Tape, a: i64) -> Tape {
    let av = get_v(t, a)
    return push(t, OP_SIGMOID(), a, 0 - 1, 1.0 / (1.0 + exp_f64(0.0 - av)))
}

fn trelu(t: Tape, a: i64) -> Tape {
    let av = get_v(t, a)
    let rv = if av > 0.0 { av } else { 0.0 }
    return push(t, OP_RELU(), a, 0 - 1, rv)
}

fn ttanh(t: Tape, a: i64) -> Tape {
    let av = get_v(t, a)
    // tanh(x) = (e^x - e^-x) / (e^x + e^-x)
    let ep = exp_f64(av)
    let en = exp_f64(0.0 - av)
    let tv = (ep - en) / (ep + en)
    return push(t, OP_TANH(), a, 0 - 1, tv)
}

fn tleaky_relu(t: Tape, a: i64) -> Tape {
    let av = get_v(t, a)
    let alpha = LEAKY_ALPHA()
    let rv = if av > 0.0 { av } else { alpha * av }
    return push(t, OP_LEAKY_RELU(), a, 0 - 1, rv)
}

// 2-class softmax: softmax_0(a, b) = exp(a) / (exp(a) + exp(b))
// Returns the probability for class 0 (first input)
// Note: softmax_1 = 1 - softmax_0 for 2-class case
fn tsoftmax2(t: Tape, a: i64, b: i64) -> Tape {
    let av = get_v(t, a)
    let bv = get_v(t, b)
    // For numerical stability, subtract max before exp
    let m = if av > bv { av } else { bv }
    let ea = exp_f64(av - m)
    let eb = exp_f64(bv - m)
    let sum = ea + eb
    let y0 = ea / sum
    return push(t, OP_SOFTMAX2(), a, b, y0)
}

// Natural logarithm: log(x)
fn tlog(t: Tape, a: i64) -> Tape {
    let av = get_v(t, a)
    // Add small epsilon for numerical stability
    let eps = LOG_EPSILON()
    let safe_v = if av > eps { av } else { eps }
    return push(t, OP_LOG(), a, 0 - 1, log_f64(safe_v))
}

// Clamp value to [eps, 1-eps] for numerical stability
fn clamp_prob(p: f64) -> f64 {
    let eps = LOG_EPSILON()
    let upper = 1.0 - eps
    if p < eps { return eps }
    if p > upper { return upper }
    return p
}

// Binary cross-entropy loss: -[target * log(pred) + (1-target) * log(1-pred)]
// Note: Due to Sounio bug with large struct parameters, we pass values directly
fn cross_entropy_loss_debug(p: f64, y: f64, debug: bool) -> f64 {
    // Clamp prediction for numerical stability
    let p_safe = clamp_prob(p)
    let one_minus_p = clamp_prob(1.0 - p)

    // L = -[y * log(p) + (1-y) * log(1-p)]
    let log_p = log_f64(p_safe)
    let log_1mp = log_f64(one_minus_p)

    // Use weighted sum: loss = -y*log(p) - (1-y)*log(1-p)
    let neg_log_p = 0.0 - log_p
    let neg_log_1mp = 0.0 - log_1mp
    let term1 = y * neg_log_p
    let term2 = (1.0 - y) * neg_log_1mp

    if debug {
        println("    [CE] p_input = ")
        println(p)
        println("    [CE] y_input = ")
        println(y)
        println("    [CE] p_safe = ")
        println(p_safe)
        println("    [CE] 1-p = ")
        println(one_minus_p)
        println("    [CE] term1 = ")
        println(term1)
        println("    [CE] term2 = ")
        println(term2)
    }

    return term1 + term2
}

fn cross_entropy_loss(p: f64, y: f64) -> f64 {
    return cross_entropy_loss_debug(p, y, false)
}

// Build cross-entropy by reading values first, then calling with explicit values
// This is a workaround for Sounio bug with large struct parameters
fn tcross_entropy_with_values_debug(t: Tape, pred_idx: i64, target_idx: i64, p: f64, y: f64, debug: bool) -> Tape {
    let loss = cross_entropy_loss_debug(p, y, debug)
    return push(t, OP_CROSS_ENTROPY(), pred_idx, target_idx, loss)
}

fn tcross_entropy_with_values(t: Tape, pred_idx: i64, target_idx: i64, p: f64, y: f64) -> Tape {
    return tcross_entropy_with_values_debug(t, pred_idx, target_idx, p, y, false)
}

// ============================================================================
// BACKWARD
// ============================================================================

// Process a single backward step and return new tape
// Note: Uses direct struct creation to avoid Sounio compiler bug with
// function parameters inside while loops
fn backward_step(t: Tape, i: i64) -> Tape {
    let op = get_op(t, i)
    let a1 = get_a1(t, i)
    let a2 = get_a2(t, i)
    let v = get_v(t, i)
    let dout = get_g(t, i)

    if abs_f64(dout) < 0.0000000001 {
        return t
    }

    // Read current gradients
    let cur_g0 = t.g0
    let cur_g1 = t.g1
    let cur_g2 = t.g2
    let cur_g3 = t.g3
    let cur_g4 = t.g4
    let cur_g5 = t.g5

    // Compute new gradients
    var new_g0 = cur_g0
    var new_g1 = cur_g1
    var new_g2 = cur_g2
    var new_g3 = cur_g3
    var new_g4 = cur_g4
    var new_g5 = cur_g5

    if op == OP_ADD() {
        // d(a+b)/da = 1, d(a+b)/db = 1
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + dout }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + dout }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + dout }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + dout }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + dout }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + dout }
        if a2 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + dout }
        if a2 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + dout }
        if a2 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + dout }
        if a2 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + dout }
        if a2 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + dout }
        if a2 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + dout }
    }
    if op == OP_MUL() {
        // d(a*b)/da = b, d(a*b)/db = a
        let av = get_v(t, a1)
        let bv = get_v(t, a2)
        let ga = dout * bv
        let gb = dout * av
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
        if a2 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + gb }
        if a2 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + gb }
        if a2 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + gb }
        if a2 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + gb }
        if a2 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + gb }
        if a2 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + gb }
    }
    if op == OP_DIV() {
        // d(a/b)/da = 1/b, d(a/b)/db = -a/b^2
        let av = get_v(t, a1)
        let bv = get_v(t, a2)
        let ga = dout / bv
        let gb = 0.0 - dout * av / (bv * bv)
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
        if a2 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + gb }
        if a2 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + gb }
        if a2 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + gb }
        if a2 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + gb }
        if a2 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + gb }
        if a2 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + gb }
    }
    if op == OP_EXP() {
        // d(exp(a))/da = exp(a) = v
        let ga = dout * v
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
    }
    if op == OP_SQRT() {
        // d(sqrt(a))/da = 1/(2*sqrt(a)) = 1/(2v)
        let ga = dout / (2.0 * v)
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
    }
    if op == OP_SIN() {
        // d(sin(a))/da = cos(a)
        let av = get_v(t, a1)
        let ga = dout * cos_f64(av)
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
    }
    if op == OP_SIGMOID() {
        // d(sigmoid(a))/da = sigmoid(a) * (1 - sigmoid(a)) = v * (1-v)
        let ga = dout * v * (1.0 - v)
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
    }
    if op == OP_RELU() {
        // d(relu(a))/da = 1 if a > 0 else 0
        // Note: v = relu(input), so v > 0 iff input > 0
        let ga = if v > 0.0 { dout } else { 0.0 }
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
    }
    if op == OP_TANH() {
        // d(tanh(a))/da = 1 - tanh(a)^2 = 1 - v^2
        let ga = dout * (1.0 - v * v)
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
    }
    if op == OP_LEAKY_RELU() {
        // d(leaky_relu(a))/da = 1 if a > 0 else alpha
        // Note: v > 0 iff input > 0 (since alpha > 0)
        let alpha = LEAKY_ALPHA()
        let ga = if v > 0.0 { dout } else { dout * alpha }
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
    }
    if op == OP_SOFTMAX2() {
        // 2-class softmax: y0 = softmax_0(x0, x1)
        // y1 = 1 - y0 (for 2-class)
        // ∂y0/∂x0 = y0 * (1 - y0) = y0 * y1
        // ∂y0/∂x1 = -y0 * y1
        let y0 = v
        let y1 = 1.0 - y0
        let ga = dout * y0 * y1         // gradient to first input (a1)
        let gb = 0.0 - dout * y0 * y1   // gradient to second input (a2)
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
        if a1 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + ga }
        if a1 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + ga }
        if a1 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + ga }
        if a1 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + ga }
        if a2 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + gb }
        if a2 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + gb }
        if a2 == 2 { new_g2 = new_g2 + gb }
        if a2 == 3 { new_g3 = new_g3 + gb }
        if a2 == 4 { new_g4 = new_g4 + gb }
        if a2 == 5 { new_g5 = new_g5 + gb }
    }
    if op == OP_LOG() {
        // d(log(a))/da = 1/a
        let av = get_v(t, a1)
        let eps = LOG_EPSILON()
        let safe_a = if av > eps { av } else { eps }
        let ga = dout / safe_a
        if a1 == 0 { new_g0 = new_g0 + ga }
        if a1 == 1 { new_g1 = new_g1 + ga }
