// === FILE: stdlib/ot/swow_orc.sio ===
//! stdlib/ot/swow_orc.sio — Native exact Ollivier–Ricci curvature over a SWOW edge list.
//!
//! Pipeline (all native, no scipy/Julia in any numeric path):
//!   read_file CSV -> intern words (insertion order) -> dedup undirected adjacency
//!   -> union-find LCC (re-index LCC nodes in first-appearance order, 0-based)
//!   -> BFS hop distances -> lazy-walk measure (alpha=1/2, uniform, exact Rational)
//!   -> exact W1 via stdlib/ot/transport_exact -> kappa = 1 - W1  (edges have d=1).
//!
//! Node id convention matches the reference: insertion order among LCC nodes, 0-based.

use math::rational::*
use ot::transport_exact::*

let ORC_NB: i64 = 262144           // hash buckets

// ---- word table ------------------------------------------------------------
pub var ORC_CH:    [i64; 1048576] = [0; 1048576]   // copied word bytes
pub var ORC_WST:   [i64; 131072]  = [0; 131072]    // word start in ORC_CH
pub var ORC_WLEN:  [i64; 131072]  = [0; 131072]    // word length
pub var ORC_NW:    i64 = 0
pub var ORC_CHLEN: i64 = 0
var ORC_HB:   [i64; 262144] = [0 - 1; 262144]      // hash bucket heads
var ORC_HNXT: [i64; 131072] = [0 - 1; 131072]

// ---- adjacency (full graph) ------------------------------------------------
var ORC_AH:  [i64; 131072]  = [0 - 1; 131072]      // adjacency head per node
var ORC_ATO: [i64; 4194304]                         = [0; 4194304]
var ORC_ANX: [i64; 4194304]                         = [0 - 1; 4194304]
var ORC_AEC: i64 = 0
pub var ORC_DEG: [i64; 131072] = [0; 131072]
pub var ORC_NE:  i64 = 0           // undirected edge count (full graph)

// ---- LCC -------------------------------------------------------------------
var ORC_UF:    [i64; 131072] = [0; 131072]
pub var ORC_LID:   [i64; 131072] = [0 - 1; 131072] // full-id -> lcc-id (or -1)
pub var ORC_L2F:   [i64; 131072] = [0 - 1; 131072] // lcc-id -> full-id
pub var ORC_LCC_N: i64 = 0
pub var ORC_LCC_M: i64 = 0

// ---- BFS -------------------------------------------------------------------
var ORC_DIST: [i64; 131072] = [0 - 1; 131072]
var ORC_Q:    [i64; 131072] = [0; 131072]
var ORC_MARK: [i64; 131072] = [0; 131072]   // timestamp marker for common-neighbor test
var ORC_MT:   i64 = 0

// ============================================================================
// Word interning
// ============================================================================
fn orc_hash(s: str, start: i64, len: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var h: i64 = 1469598103934665603
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len {
        h = (h ^ s[(start + i) as usize]) * 1099511628211
        i = i + 1
    }
    if h < 0 { h = 0 - h }
    return h
}

fn orc_streq(s: str, start: i64, cstart: i64, len: i64) -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len {
        if s[(start + i) as usize] != ORC_CH[(cstart + i) as usize] { return false; }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Intern substring s[start..start+len); returns its insertion-order id.
fn orc_intern(s: str, start: i64, len: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let h = orc_hash(s, start, len)
    let b = h % ORC_NB
    var id = ORC_HB[b as usize]
    while id >= 0 {
        if ORC_WLEN[id as usize] == len {
            if orc_streq(s, start, ORC_WST[id as usize], len) { return id; }
        }
        id = ORC_HNXT[id as usize]
    }
    let nid = ORC_NW
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < len { ORC_CH[(ORC_CHLEN + k) as usize] = s[(start + k) as usize]; k = k + 1; }
    ORC_WST[nid as usize] = ORC_CHLEN
    ORC_WLEN[nid as usize] = len
    ORC_CHLEN = ORC_CHLEN + len
    ORC_HNXT[nid as usize] = ORC_HB[b as usize]
    ORC_HB[b as usize] = nid
    ORC_NW = nid + 1
    return nid
}

// Lookup an existing word; returns id or -1 (does NOT insert).
pub fn orc_lookup(s: str, start: i64, len: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let h = orc_hash(s, start, len)
    let b = h % ORC_NB
    var id = ORC_HB[b as usize]
    while id >= 0 {
        if ORC_WLEN[id as usize] == len {
            if orc_streq(s, start, ORC_WST[id as usize], len) { return id; }
        }
        id = ORC_HNXT[id as usize]
    }
    return 0 - 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Graph build (dedup undirected)
// ============================================================================
pub fn orc_has_edge(u: i64, v: i64) -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var e = ORC_AH[u as usize]
    while e >= 0 {
        if ORC_ATO[e as usize] == v { return true; }
        e = ORC_ANX[e as usize]
    }
    return false
}

fn orc_add_dir(u: i64, v: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    ORC_ATO[ORC_AEC as usize] = v
    ORC_ANX[ORC_AEC as usize] = ORC_AH[u as usize]
    ORC_AH[u as usize] = ORC_AEC
    ORC_AEC = ORC_AEC + 1
}

fn orc_add_edge(u: i64, v: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    if orc_has_edge(u, v) { return; }
    orc_add_dir(u, v)
    orc_add_dir(v, u)
    ORC_DEG[u as usize] = ORC_DEG[u as usize] + 1
    ORC_DEG[v as usize] = ORC_DEG[v as usize] + 1
    ORC_NE = ORC_NE + 1
}

// Parse a SWOW CSV "source,target,weight" (skip header). Build dedup graph.
pub fn orc_load_csv(path: str) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let s = read_file(path)
    let n = s.len() as i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    // skip header line
    while i < n {
        if s[i as usize] == 10 { i = i + 1; i = n + n; }
        else { i = i + 1; }
    }
    if i >= n + n { i = i - n - n; } else { i = 0; }
    // (i now points just past the first newline, or 0 if none)
    var pos: i64 = 0
    // find first newline robustly
    var hn: i64 = 0
    while hn < n { if s[hn as usize] == 10 { pos = hn + 1; hn = n; } else { hn = hn + 1; } }
    i = pos
    while i < n {
        // source field
        let s0 = i
        while i < n && s[i as usize] != 44 && s[i as usize] != 10 { i = i + 1; }
        let l0 = i - s0
        if i < n && s[i as usize] == 44 {
            i = i + 1
            let s1 = i
            while i < n && s[i as usize] != 44 && s[i as usize] != 10 { i = i + 1; }
            let l1 = i - s1
            // skip to end of line
            while i < n && s[i as usize] != 10 { i = i + 1; }
            if i < n { i = i + 1; }
            if l0 > 0 && l1 > 0 {
                let u = orc_intern(s, s0, l0)
                let v = orc_intern(s, s1, l1)
                if u != v { orc_add_edge(u, v); }
            }
        } else {
            while i < n && s[i as usize] != 10 { i = i + 1; }
            if i < n { i = i + 1; }
        }
    }
    return ORC_NW
}

// ============================================================================
// LCC via union-find, then re-index LCC nodes in first-appearance (id) order.
// ============================================================================
fn orc_find(x: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var r = x
    while ORC_UF[r as usize] != r { r = ORC_UF[r as usize]; }
    var c = x
    while ORC_UF[c as usize] != r { let nx = ORC_UF[c as usize]; ORC_UF[c as usize] = r; c = nx; }
    return r
}

pub fn orc_build_lcc() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < ORC_NW { ORC_UF[i as usize] = i; i = i + 1; }
    i = 0
    while i < ORC_NW {
        var e = ORC_AH[i as usize]
        while e >= 0 {
            let j = ORC_ATO[e as usize]
            let ri = orc_find(i)
            let rj = orc_find(j)
            if ri != rj { ORC_UF[ri as usize] = rj; }
            e = ORC_ANX[e as usize]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // component sizes
    var best_root: i64 = 0 - 1
    var best_sz: i64 = 0 - 1
    i = 0
    while i < ORC_NW {
        if orc_find(i) == i {
            // count members
            var cnt: i64 = 0
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < ORC_NW { if orc_find(j) == i { cnt = cnt + 1; } j = j + 1; }
            if cnt > best_sz { best_sz = cnt; best_root = i; }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // assign LCC ids in first-appearance order
    var lid: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < ORC_NW {
        if orc_find(i) == best_root {
            ORC_LID[i as usize] = lid
            ORC_L2F[lid as usize] = i
            lid = lid + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    ORC_LCC_N = lid
    // LCC edge count
    var m: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < ORC_NW {
        if ORC_LID[i as usize] >= 0 {
            var e = ORC_AH[i as usize]
            while e >= 0 {
                let j = ORC_ATO[e as usize]
                if j > i && ORC_LID[j as usize] >= 0 { m = m + 1; }
                e = ORC_ANX[e as usize]
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    ORC_LCC_M = m
}

// full-id of an LCC node id
pub fn orc_lcc_node(lcc_id: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic { return ORC_L2F[lcc_id as usize]; }

// ============================================================================
// BFS hop distances from full-id src; fills ORC_DIST (full-id indexed), -1 if unreachable.
// ============================================================================
fn orc_bfs(src: i64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < ORC_NW { ORC_DIST[i as usize] = 0 - 1; i = i + 1; }
    ORC_DIST[src as usize] = 0
    var qh: i64 = 0
    var qt: i64 = 0
    ORC_Q[0] = src; qt = 1
    while qh < qt {
        let u = ORC_Q[qh as usize]
        qh = qh + 1
        var e = ORC_AH[u as usize]
        while e >= 0 {
            let v = ORC_ATO[e as usize]
            if ORC_DIST[v as usize] < 0 {
                ORC_DIST[v as usize] = ORC_DIST[u as usize] + 1
                ORC_Q[qt as usize] = v; qt = qt + 1
            }
            e = ORC_ANX[e as usize]
        }
    }
}

// Exact hop distance between supports a,b of an EDGE (u~v): guaranteed <= 3,
// since d(a,b) <= d(a,u) + d(u,v) + d(v,b) <= 1 + 1 + 1. Computed in O(deg) via
// adjacency + a common-neighbor test — no BFS (so dense hub graphs stay fast).
fn orc_dist_le3(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    if a == b { return 0; }
    if orc_has_edge(a, b) { return 1; }
    ORC_MT = ORC_MT + 1
    var e = ORC_AH[a as usize]
    while e >= 0 { ORC_MARK[ORC_ATO[e as usize] as usize] = ORC_MT; e = ORC_ANX[e as usize]; }
    var f = ORC_AH[b as usize]
    while f >= 0 {
        if ORC_MARK[ORC_ATO[f as usize] as usize] == ORC_MT { return 2; }
        f = ORC_ANX[f as usize]
    }
    return 3
}

// kth neighbor (full-id) of full-id u, k in [0, deg(u))
fn orc_neighbor(u: i64, k: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var e = ORC_AH[u as usize]
    var c: i64 = 0
    while e >= 0 {
        if c == k { return ORC_ATO[e as usize]; }
        c = c + 1
        e = ORC_ANX[e as usize]
    }
    return 0 - 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Exact kappa for an edge between two full-ids u, v (assumes u~v, d=1).
// Lazy walk alpha=1/2 uniform: mass(self)=1/2, mass(each nbr)=1/(2*deg).
// Returns Rational kappa = 1 - W1. W1 stored in ORC_LAST_W1.
// ============================================================================
pub var ORC_LAST_W1_NUM: i64 = 0
pub var ORC_LAST_W1_DEN: i64 = 1

// Per-edge exact kappa over the whole LCC (filled by orc_compute_all_kappa).
pub var ORC_EK_N: [i64; 2097152] = [0; 2097152]   // kappa numerator per edge
pub var ORC_EK_D: [i64; 2097152] = [1; 2097152]   // kappa denominator per edge
pub var ORC_EU:   [i64; 2097152] = [0; 2097152]   // edge endpoint u (lcc id)
pub var ORC_EV:   [i64; 2097152] = [0; 2097152]   // edge endpoint v (lcc id)
pub var ORC_NEDGE: i64 = 0

// Build support arrays into OT buffers and compute. Support = [self] ++ neighbors.
pub fn orc_kappa_edge(u: i64, v: i64) -> Rational with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let du = ORC_DEG[u as usize]
    let dv = ORC_DEG[v as usize]
    let ns = du + 1
    let nd = dv + 1
    // supply masses (u side)
    OT_SNUM[0] = 1; OT_SDEN[0] = 2
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i <= du { OT_SNUM[i as usize] = 1; OT_SDEN[i as usize] = 2 * du; i = i + 1; }
    // demand masses (v side)
    OT_DNUM[0] = 1; OT_DDEN[0] = 2
    var j: i64 = 1
    while j <= dv { OT_DNUM[j as usize] = 1; OT_DDEN[j as usize] = 2 * dv; j = j + 1; }
    // Precompute support full-ids: index 0 -> self, index 1+k -> kth neighbor.
    var SU: [i64; 1024] = [0; 1024]
    var SV: [i64; 1024] = [0; 1024]
    SU[0] = u; SV[0] = v
    var a: i64 = 1
    var eu = ORC_AH[u as usize]
    while eu >= 0 { SU[a as usize] = ORC_ATO[eu as usize]; a = a + 1; eu = ORC_ANX[eu as usize]; }
    var b: i64 = 1
    var ev = ORC_AH[v as usize]
    while ev >= 0 { SV[b as usize] = ORC_ATO[ev as usize]; b = b + 1; ev = ORC_ANX[ev as usize]; }
    // cost matrix = exact hop distance (<=3) among supports, no BFS.
    a = 0
    while a < ns {
        b = 0
        while b < nd {
            OT_COST[(a * nd + b) as usize] = orc_dist_le3(SU[a as usize], SV[b as usize])
            b = b + 1
        }
        a = a + 1
    }
    let w1 = w1_rational(ns, nd)
    ORC_LAST_W1_NUM = w1.num
    ORC_LAST_W1_DEN = w1.den
    return rat_sub(rat_one(), w1)
}

// Compute exact kappa for EVERY LCC edge; fill ORC_EK_N/ORC_EK_D/ORC_EU/ORC_EV.
pub fn orc_compute_all_kappa() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    ORC_NEDGE = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < ORC_NW {
        if ORC_LID[i as usize] >= 0 {
            var e = ORC_AH[i as usize]
            while e >= 0 {
                let j = ORC_ATO[e as usize]
                if j > i {
                    if ORC_LID[j as usize] >= 0 {
                        let k = orc_kappa_edge(i, j)
                        ORC_EK_N[ORC_NEDGE as usize] = k.num
                        ORC_EK_D[ORC_NEDGE as usize] = k.den
                        ORC_EU[ORC_NEDGE as usize] = ORC_LID[i as usize]
                        ORC_EV[ORC_NEDGE as usize] = ORC_LID[j as usize]
                        ORC_NEDGE = ORC_NEDGE + 1
                    }
                }
                e = ORC_ANX[e as usize]
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ot/transport_exact.sio ===
//! stdlib/ot/transport_exact.sio — Exact discrete optimal transport / W1 over Q.
//!
//! The discrete OT LP (transportation problem) has a totally-unimodular constraint
//! matrix, so with INTEGER supplies/demands the LP optimum is integral. We solve it
//! EXACTLY as an integer min-cost max-flow (successive shortest paths / SPFA), with
//! NO floating point and NO Sinkhorn anywhere. Rational masses are scaled to a common
//! integer denominator D = lcm(denominators); the exact Wasserstein-1 distance is
//! W1 = (optimal integer cost) / D  ∈  Q.
//!
//! Inputs are passed via module-global buffers (filled by the caller) to avoid
//! large array-by-value copies and stack spills:
//!   OT_COST[i*nd + j]                 integer cost matrix (hop distances)
//!   OT_SUPPLY[i], OT_DEMAND[j]        integer masses  (for w1_int)
//!   OT_SNUM/OT_SDEN, OT_DNUM/OT_DDEN  rational masses (for w1_rational)

use math::rational::*

// ---- caller-filled input buffers -------------------------------------------
pub var OT_SUPPLY: [i64; 1024]    = [0; 1024]
pub var OT_DEMAND: [i64; 1024]    = [0; 1024]
pub var OT_COST:   [i64; 1048576] = [0; 1048576]
pub var OT_SNUM:   [i64; 1024]    = [0; 1024]
pub var OT_SDEN:   [i64; 1024]    = [1; 1024]
pub var OT_DNUM:   [i64; 1024]    = [0; 1024]
pub var OT_DDEN:   [i64; 1024]    = [1; 1024]
pub var OT_LAST_D: i64 = 1     // common denominator used by the last w1_rational call

// ---- residual-graph storage (module globals) -------------------------------
var MF_HEAD: [i64; 2050]    = [0 - 1; 2050]
var MF_TO:   [i64; 2097152] = [0; 2097152]
var MF_NXT:  [i64; 2097152] = [0 - 1; 2097152]
var MF_CAP:  [i64; 2097152] = [0; 2097152]
var MF_COST: [i64; 2097152] = [0; 2097152]
var MF_EC:   i64 = 0
var MF_DIST: [i64; 2050]    = [0; 2050]
var MF_INQ:  [i64; 2050]    = [0; 2050]
var MF_PREV: [i64; 2050]    = [0 - 1; 2050]
var MF_QUE:  [i64; 1048576] = [0; 1048576]

let MF_INF: i64 = 1000000000000000000   // 1e18

fn mcmf_reset(nnodes: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    MF_EC = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < nnodes { MF_HEAD[i as usize] = 0 - 1; i = i + 1; }
}

fn mcmf_add_edge(u: i64, v: i64, cap: i64, cost: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    MF_TO[MF_EC as usize] = v
    MF_CAP[MF_EC as usize] = cap
    MF_COST[MF_EC as usize] = cost
    MF_NXT[MF_EC as usize] = MF_HEAD[u as usize]
    MF_HEAD[u as usize] = MF_EC
    MF_EC = MF_EC + 1
    MF_TO[MF_EC as usize] = u
    MF_CAP[MF_EC as usize] = 0
    MF_COST[MF_EC as usize] = 0 - cost
    MF_NXT[MF_EC as usize] = MF_HEAD[v as usize]
    MF_HEAD[v as usize] = MF_EC
    MF_EC = MF_EC + 1
}

fn mcmf_spfa(s: i64, t: i64, nnodes: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < nnodes { MF_DIST[i as usize] = MF_INF; MF_INQ[i as usize] = 0; MF_PREV[i as usize] = 0 - 1; i = i + 1; }
    MF_DIST[s as usize] = 0
    var qh: i64 = 0
    var qt: i64 = 0
    MF_QUE[0] = s; qt = 1
    MF_INQ[s as usize] = 1
    while qh < qt {
        let u = MF_QUE[(qh % 1048576) as usize]
        qh = qh + 1
        MF_INQ[u as usize] = 0
        var e = MF_HEAD[u as usize]
        while e >= 0 {
            if MF_CAP[e as usize] > 0 {
                let v = MF_TO[e as usize]
                let nd = MF_DIST[u as usize] + MF_COST[e as usize]
                if nd < MF_DIST[v as usize] {
                    MF_DIST[v as usize] = nd
                    MF_PREV[v as usize] = e
                    if MF_INQ[v as usize] == 0 {
                        MF_QUE[(qt % 1048576) as usize] = v; qt = qt + 1
                        MF_INQ[v as usize] = 1
                    }
                }
            }
            e = MF_NXT[e as usize]
        }
    }
    if MF_DIST[t as usize] < MF_INF { return 1; }
    return 0
}

// Min-cost MAX-flow from s to t; returns total integer cost.
fn mcmf_min_cost(s: i64, t: i64, nnodes: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var total: i64 = 0
    while mcmf_spfa(s, t, nnodes) == 1 {
        var f = MF_INF
        var v = t
        while v != s {
            let e = MF_PREV[v as usize]
            if MF_CAP[e as usize] < f { f = MF_CAP[e as usize] }
            v = MF_TO[(e ^ 1) as usize]
        }
        v = t
        while v != s {
            let e = MF_PREV[v as usize]
            MF_CAP[e as usize] = MF_CAP[e as usize] - f
            MF_CAP[(e ^ 1) as usize] = MF_CAP[(e ^ 1) as usize] + f
            v = MF_TO[(e ^ 1) as usize]
        }
        total = total + f * MF_DIST[t as usize]
    }
    return total
}

// Transportation problem on integer masses in OT_SUPPLY/OT_DEMAND/OT_COST.
// Node layout: 0=source, 1..ns=supply, 1+ns..ns+nd=demand, ns+nd+1=sink.
// Requires sum(OT_SUPPLY)==sum(OT_DEMAND). Returns optimal integer cost.
pub fn w1_int(ns: i64, nd: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let src: i64 = 0
    let snk = ns + nd + 1
    let nnodes = ns + nd + 2
    mcmf_reset(nnodes)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < ns { mcmf_add_edge(src, 1 + i, OT_SUPPLY[i as usize], 0); i = i + 1; }
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < nd { mcmf_add_edge(1 + ns + j, snk, OT_DEMAND[j as usize], 0); j = j + 1; }
    i = 0
    while i < ns {
        j = 0
        while j < nd {
            mcmf_add_edge(1 + i, 1 + ns + j, MF_INF, OT_COST[(i * nd + j) as usize])
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return mcmf_min_cost(src, snk, nnodes)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Exact LP dual (MODI / u-v potentials) for a Farkas certificate of W1.
// After w1_int(ns,nd), recovers flow on each transport edge, builds the basis
// (flow>0) potentials u_i, v_j with u_i + v_j = c_ij on basic cells, and exposes
// them as rationals. Dual feasibility u_i+v_j <= c_ij for ALL i,j plus objective
// sum(supply_i u_i)+sum(demand_j v_j) > d certifies W1 > d (UNSAT of "exists plan
// with cost <= d"), i.e. kappa < 0, by LP weak duality.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
pub var DU_N: [i64; 1024] = [0; 1024]      // u_i numerator (per supply)
pub var DU_D: [i64; 1024] = [1; 1024]
pub var DV_N: [i64; 1024] = [0; 1024]      // v_j numerator (per demand)
pub var DV_D: [i64; 1024] = [1; 1024]
var DU_SET: [i64; 1024] = [0; 1024]
var DV_SET: [i64; 1024] = [0; 1024]
var DMODI_Q: [i64; 4096] = [0; 4096]

// transport edge (i,j) forward index in the residual arrays built by w1_int:
//   first ns source edges (2 each) + nd sink edges (2 each), then i*nd+j (2 each)
fn d_flow(ns: i64, nd: i64, i: i64, j: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    let fwd = (ns + nd) * 2 + (i * nd + j) * 2
    return MF_CAP[(fwd + 1) as usize]   // reverse-edge cap == flow pushed
}

// Build MODI potentials after a solve. Returns 1 on success (all reachable).
pub fn modi_duals(ns: i64, nd: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < ns { DU_SET[i as usize] = 0; i = i + 1; }
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < nd { DV_SET[j as usize] = 0; j = j + 1; }
    // start: u_0 = 0. Nodes encoded as supply i -> i, demand j -> ns+j.
    DU_N[0] = 0; DU_D[0] = 1; DU_SET[0] = 1
    var qh: i64 = 0
    var qt: i64 = 0
    DMODI_Q[0] = 0; qt = 1
    while qh < qt {
        let node = DMODI_Q[qh as usize]
        qh = qh + 1
        if node < ns {
            let si = node
            var jj: i64 = 0
            while jj < nd {
                if d_flow(ns, nd, si, jj) > 0 {
                    if DV_SET[jj as usize] == 0 {
                        // v_j = c_ij - u_i
                        let c = Rational { num: OT_COST[(si * nd + jj) as usize], den: 1 }
                        let ui = Rational { num: DU_N[si as usize], den: DU_D[si as usize] }
                        let v = rat_sub(c, ui)
                        DV_N[jj as usize] = v.num; DV_D[jj as usize] = v.den; DV_SET[jj as usize] = 1
                        DMODI_Q[qt as usize] = ns + jj; qt = qt + 1
                    }
                }
                jj = jj + 1
            }
        } else {
            let dj = node - ns
            var ii: i64 = 0
            while ii < ns {
                if d_flow(ns, nd, ii, dj) > 0 {
                    if DU_SET[ii as usize] == 0 {
                        let c = Rational { num: OT_COST[(ii * nd + dj) as usize], den: 1 }
                        let vj = Rational { num: DV_N[dj as usize], den: DV_D[dj as usize] }
                        let u = rat_sub(c, vj)
                        DU_N[ii as usize] = u.num; DU_D[ii as usize] = u.den; DU_SET[ii as usize] = 1
                        DMODI_Q[qt as usize] = ii; qt = qt + 1
                    }
                }
                ii = ii + 1
            }
        }
    }
    // any unset -> set 0 (degenerate basis); feasibility is checked separately.
    i = 0
    while i < ns { if DU_SET[i as usize] == 0 { DU_N[i as usize] = 0; DU_D[i as usize] = 1; } i = i + 1; }
    j = 0
    while j < nd { if DV_SET[j as usize] == 0 { DV_N[j as usize] = 0; DV_D[j as usize] = 1; } j = j + 1; }
    return 1
}

fn ot_lcm(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x = a; var y = b;
    while y > 0 { let t = y; y = x - (x / y) * y; x = t; }
    if x == 0 { return 0; }
    return a / x * b
}

// Exact rational W1 from rational masses in OT_SNUM/OT_SDEN, OT_DNUM/OT_DDEN and
// integer OT_COST. Scales to common denominator D, solves integer transport,
// returns rat_make(cost, D). Imbalanced masses -> rat_invalid().
pub fn w1_rational(ns: i64, nd: i64) -> Rational with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var D: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < ns { D = ot_lcm(D, OT_SDEN[i as usize]); i = i + 1; }
    i = 0
    while i < nd { D = ot_lcm(D, OT_DDEN[i as usize]); i = i + 1; }
    OT_LAST_D = D
    var ssum: i64 = 0
    var dsum: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < ns { OT_SUPPLY[i as usize] = OT_SNUM[i as usize] * (D / OT_SDEN[i as usize]); ssum = ssum + OT_SUPPLY[i as usize]; i = i + 1; }
    i = 0
    while i < nd { OT_DEMAND[i as usize] = OT_DNUM[i as usize] * (D / OT_DDEN[i as usize]); dsum = dsum + OT_DEMAND[i as usize]; i = i + 1; }
    if ssum != dsum { return rat_invalid(); }
    let c = w1_int(ns, nd)
    return rat_make(c, D)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/particle_physics/amplitude.sio ===
// stdlib/particle_physics/amplitude.sio — Tree-level amplitudes and cross-sections
//
// Spin-averaged |M|² and cross-section formulas for key Standard Model
// processes.  All results include epistemic uncertainty propagation where
// couplings are involved.
//
// Implemented processes:
//   • e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻        (QED + Z interference)
//   • e⁺e⁻ → q q̄         (QED + QCD color)
//   • Møller scattering    e⁻e⁻ → e⁻e⁻
//   • Bhabha scattering    e⁺e⁻ → e⁺e⁻
//   • Z → f f̄            (partial widths)
//   • H → f f̄ / γγ / gg  (decay widths)
//
// References:
//   - Peskin & Schroeder, Ch. 4-5
//   - PDG 2024, Cross-section formulae

module particle_physics::amplitude

use particle_physics::lorentz::{LorentzVector, lorentz_new, lorentz_dot, lorentz_norm_sq,
                                 lorentz_add, lorentz_sub, lorentz_scale,
                                 mandelstam_s, mandelstam_t, mandelstam_u,
                                 pt, azimuth}
use particle_physics::spinor::{trace_gamma_2, trace_gamma_4}
use particle_physics::gauge::{su3_casimir_cf, su3_dynkin_tf}
use particle_physics::sm_params::{alpha_em, mass_z, mass_w, mass_h,
                                   mass_muon, mass_electron, mass_top, mass_bottom,
                                   mass_charm, mass_strange, mass_tau,
                                   coupling_e, coupling_g, sin2_theta_w}
use particle_physics::propagator::{scalar_propagator_sq, vector_propagator_sq}
use particle_physics::vertex::{neutral_current_couplings, nc_coupling_electron,
                                nc_coupling_muon, nc_coupling_up, nc_coupling_down}
use particle_physics::kinematics::{cm_energy_sq, cm_momentum_final,
                                    diff_cross_section, total_cross_section_isotropic,
                                    decay_width_2_body, cross_section_pb, kallen_lambda}
use epistemic::knowledge::{Epistemic}
use complex::lib::{Complex, complex_new}

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// QED: e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻
// ============================================================================

/// Spin-averaged |M|² for e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻ in QED (massless approximation).
///
/// # Formula
///   |M|² = 2 e⁴ (1 + cos²θ)
/// where θ is the scattering angle in the CM frame.
///
/// GUM propagation via Epistemic::square and ::mul chains.
pub fn eemm_qed_amplitude_sq(s: f64, cos_theta: f64) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // e² with GUM variance, then e⁴ = (e²)²
    let e2 = coupling_e().square()
    let e4 = e2.square()
    // angular factor is exact (geometric)
    let ang = 1.0 + cos_theta * cos_theta
    e4.scale(2.0 * ang)
}

/// Differential cross-section dσ/dΩ for e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻ (QED, massless).
/// Returns Epistemic with α_EM uncertainty propagated.
pub fn eemm_qed_diff_cross_section(s: f64, cos_theta: f64) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s <= 0.0 { return Epistemic::certain(0.0) }
    // α² via GUM: Var(α²) = 4α² Var(α)
    let alpha2 = alpha_em().square()
    let ang = 1.0 + cos_theta * cos_theta
    alpha2.scale(ang / (4.0 * s))
}

/// Total cross-section for e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻ (QED, massless):
///   σ = (4π α²) / (3 s).
/// Returns Epistemic with full GUM variance from PDG α_EM.
pub fn eemm_qed_total_cross_section(s: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let alpha = alpha_em().val()
    4.0 * PI * alpha * alpha / (3.0 * s)
}

/// GUM-exact total cross-section: α² propagated, returns Epistemic in GeV⁻².
pub fn eemm_qed_total_cross_section_ep(s: f64) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s <= 0.0 { return Epistemic::certain(0.0) }
    let alpha2 = alpha_em().square()
    alpha2.scale(4.0 * PI / (3.0 * s))
}

/// Total cross-section for e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻ in picobarn (raw f64).
pub fn eemm_qed_total_cross_section_pb(s: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    cross_section_pb(eemm_qed_total_cross_section(s))
}

/// GUM-exact total cross-section in picobarn with uncertainty.
pub fn eemm_qed_total_cross_section_pb_ep(s: f64) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    eemm_qed_total_cross_section_ep(s).scale(0.389379e9)
}

// ============================================================================
// Z-MEDIATED: e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻
// ============================================================================

/// Spin-averaged |M|² for e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻ via Z exchange (narrow-width approximation).
/// Near the Z pole, the Breit-Wigner dominates:
///   |M|² ≈ (g⁴ / cos⁴θ_W) · (g_V^e² + g_A^e²)(g_V^μ² + g_A^μ²) / [(s − M_Z²)² + (M_Z Γ_Z)²].
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `s`: CM energy squared.
/// - `gamma_z`: Z total width.
///
/// # Returns
/// `Epistemic<f64>`.
pub fn eemm_z_amplitude_sq(s: f64, gamma_z: f64) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mz = mass_z()
    let g = coupling_g()
    let s2w = sin2_theta_w()
    let mz_val = mz.val()
    let gz_val = g.val()
    let cw_sq = 1.0 - s2w.val()
    let cw4 = cw_sq * cw_sq

    let (gv_e, ga_e) = nc_coupling_electron()
    let (gv_m, ga_m) = nc_coupling_muon()

    let c_e = gv_e * gv_e + ga_e * ga_e
    let c_m = gv_m * gv_m + ga_m * ga_m

    let numerator = gz_val * gz_val * gz_val * gz_val * c_e * c_m / cw4
    let denom_re = s - mz_val * mz_val
    let denom_im = mz_val * gamma_z
    let denom = denom_re * denom_re + denom_im * denom_im

    if denom == 0.0 {
        return Epistemic::measured(0.0, 0.0)
    }

    let val = numerator / denom
    // Simplified uncertainty (dominated by M_Z and couplings)
    let std = val * (4.0 * g.std() / g.val() + 2.0 * mz.std() / mz_val)
    Epistemic::measured(val, std)
}

/// Total cross-section for e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻ near the Z pole.
/// Uses the narrow-width approximation with Z propagator.
pub fn eemm_z_total_cross_section(s: f64, gamma_z: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let mz = mass_z().val()
    let mz2 = mz * mz
    let g = coupling_g().val()
    let s2w = sin2_theta_w().val()
    let cw = sqrt(1.0 - s2w)
    let cw2 = cw * cw

    let (gv_e, ga_e) = nc_coupling_electron()
    let (gv_m, ga_m) = nc_coupling_muon()

    let c_e = gv_e * gv_e + ga_e * ga_e
    let c_m = gv_m * gv_m + ga_m * ga_m

    // σ = (g⁴ / (12π cos⁴θ_W)) · c_e · c_m · s / [(s − M_Z²)² + (M_Z Γ_Z)²]
    let numerator = g * g * g * g * c_e * c_m * s / (12.0 * PI * cw2 * cw2)
    let denom = (s - mz2) * (s - mz2) + mz * mz * gamma_z * gamma_z

    if denom == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    numerator / denom
}

/// Peak cross-section at s = M_Z² (narrow-width approximation):
///   σ_peak = (12π / M_Z²) · (Γ_ee Γ_μμ) / Γ_Z².
pub fn eemm_z_peak_cross_section(gamma_ee: f64, gamma_mumu: f64, gamma_z: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mz = mass_z().val()
    let mz2 = mz * mz
    if gamma_z == 0.0 || mz2 == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    12.0 * PI * gamma_ee * gamma_mumu / (mz2 * gamma_z * gamma_z)
}

// ============================================================================
// QCD: e⁺e⁻ → q q̄
// ============================================================================

/// Total cross-section for e⁺e⁻ → q q̄ (QED + QCD color factor).
///
/// # Formula
///   σ = N_c · Q_q² · σ(e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻)
/// where N_c = 3 and Q_q is the quark charge.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `s`: CM energy squared.
/// - `quark_charge`: Quark electric charge (e.g., 2/3 for u, −1/3 for d).
///
/// # Returns
/// Cross-section in GeV⁻².
pub fn eeqq_total_cross_section(s: f64, quark_charge: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let sigma_mu = eemm_qed_total_cross_section(s)
    let nc = 3.0
    let q2 = quark_charge * quark_charge
    nc * q2 * sigma_mu
}

/// R-ratio: σ(e⁺e⁻ → hadrons) / σ(e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻) at energies below QCD resonances.
/// At √s ≈ 10 GeV: R ≈ 3 · Σ_q Q_q² = 3 · (4/9 + 1/9 + 1/9) = 3 · 6/9 = 2.
/// Including b and c at higher energies: R ≈ 3 · (4/9 + 1/9 + 4/9 + 1/9 + 1/9) = 3 · 11/9 ≈ 3.67.
pub fn r_ratio(s: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Active quark flavors depending on energy
    let sqrt_s = sqrt(s)
    var sum_q2: f64 = 0.0
    // u, d, s are always light
    sum_q2 = sum_q2 + 4.0 / 9.0 + 1.0 / 9.0 + 1.0 / 9.0
    if sqrt_s > 2.0 * mass_charm().val() {
        sum_q2 = sum_q2 + 4.0 / 9.0
    }
    if sqrt_s > 2.0 * mass_bottom().val() {
        sum_q2 = sum_q2 + 1.0 / 9.0
    }
    3.0 * sum_q2
}

// ============================================================================
// MØLLER SCATTERING: e⁻e⁻ → e⁻e⁻
// ============================================================================

/// Spin-averaged |M|² for Møller scattering in the massless limit.
///
/// # Formula
///   |M|² = 2 e⁴ [ (s² + u²) / t² + (s² + t²) / u² + 2 s² / (t u) ].
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `s`, `t`, `u`: Mandelstam variables.
///
/// # Returns
/// |M|² value.
pub fn moller_amplitude_sq(s: f64, t: f64, u: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let e = coupling_e().val()
    let e4 = e * e * e * e
    if t == 0.0 || u == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let term1 = (s * s + u * u) / (t * t)
    let term2 = (s * s + t * t) / (u * u)
    let term3 = 2.0 * s * s / (t * u)
    2.0 * e4 * (term1 + term2 + term3)
}

// ============================================================================
// BHABHA SCATTERING: e⁺e⁻ → e⁺e⁻
// ============================================================================

/// Spin-averaged |M|² for Bhabha scattering in the massless limit.
///
/// # Formula
///   |M|² = 2 e⁴ [ (s² + u²) / t² + (t² + u²) / s² + 2 u² / (s t) ].
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `s`, `t`, `u`: Mandelstam variables.
///
/// # Returns
/// |M|² value.
pub fn bhabha_amplitude_sq(s: f64, t: f64, u: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let e = coupling_e().val()
    let e4 = e * e * e * e
    if t == 0.0 || s == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let term1 = (s * s + u * u) / (t * t)
    let term2 = (t * t + u * u) / (s * s)
    let term3 = 2.0 * u * u / (s * t)
    2.0 * e4 * (term1 + term2 + term3)
}

// ============================================================================
// Z DECAY WIDTHS
// ============================================================================

/// Z → f f̄ partial width (tree-level, narrow-width):
///   Γ_f = (G_F M_Z³) / (6√2π) · N_c · (g_V² + g_A²) · (1 + 2 m_f² / M_Z²) · √(1 − 4m_f²/M_Z²).
/// For m_f ≪ M_Z: Γ_f ≈ (G_F M_Z³) / (6√2π) · N_c · (g_V² + g_A²).
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `m_z`: Z mass.
/// - `m_f`: Fermion mass.
/// - `g_v`, `g_a`: Neutral current couplings.
/// - `n_c`: Color factor (3 for quarks, 1 for leptons).
///
/// # Returns
/// Partial width in GeV.
pub fn z_decay_width(m_z: f64, m_f: f64, g_v: f64, g_a: f64, n_c: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if m_z <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let mz2 = m_z * m_z
    let mf2 = m_f * m_f
    let ratio = 4.0 * mf2 / mz2
    if ratio > 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    let beta = sqrt(1.0 - ratio)
    let gf = 1.1663787e-5  // G_F in GeV⁻²
    let prefactor = gf * mz2 * m_z / (6.0 * SQRT2 * PI)
    let coupling_sq = g_v * g_v + g_a * g_a
    let mass_corr = (1.0 + 2.0 * mf2 / mz2) * beta
    n_c * prefactor * coupling_sq * mass_corr
}

/// Z → e⁺e⁻ partial width.
pub fn z_decay_width_ee() -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mz = mass_z().val()
    let me = mass_electron().val()
    let (gv, ga) = nc_coupling_electron()
    z_decay_width(mz, me, gv, ga, 1.0)
}

/// Z → μ⁺μ⁻ partial width.
pub fn z_decay_width_mumu() -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mz = mass_z().val()
    let mm = mass_muon().val()
    let (gv, ga) = nc_coupling_muon()
    z_decay_width(mz, mm, gv, ga, 1.0)
}

/// Z → hadrons partial width (sum of u, d, c, s, b).
pub fn z_decay_width_hadrons() -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mz = mass_z().val()
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    // d, s, b
    let (gv_d, ga_d) = nc_coupling_down()
    sum = sum + z_decay_width(mz, mass_down().val(), gv_d, ga_d, 3.0)
    sum = sum + z_decay_width(mz, mass_strange().val(), gv_d, ga_d, 3.0)
    sum = sum + z_decay_width(mz, mass_bottom().val(), gv_d, ga_d, 3.0)
    // u, c
    let (gv_u, ga_u) = nc_coupling_up()
    sum = sum + z_decay_width(mz, mass_up().val(), gv_u, ga_u, 3.0)
    sum = sum + z_decay_width(mz, mass_charm().val(), gv_u, ga_u, 3.0)
    sum
}

/// Total Z width (sum of partials).
pub fn z_total_width() -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Leptons: e, μ, τ
    var total = z_decay_width_ee() + z_decay_width_mumu()
    let mz = mass_z().val()
    let mt = mass_tau().val()
    let (gv_t, ga_t) = nc_coupling_muon()  // same couplings for tau
    total = total + z_decay_width(mz, mt, gv_t, ga_t, 1.0)
    // Neutrinos (invisible)
    let (gv_nu, ga_nu) = nc_coupling_neutrino()
    total = total + 3.0 * z_decay_width(mz, 0.0, gv_nu, ga_nu, 1.0)
    // Hadrons
    total = total + z_decay_width_hadrons()
    total
}

// ============================================================================
// HIGGS DECAY WIDTHS
// ============================================================================

/// H → f f̄ decay width (tree-level):
///   Γ = (G_F m_f² M_H) / (4√2π) · N_c · β³
/// where β = √(1 − 4m_f²/M_H²).
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `m_h`: Higgs mass.
/// - `m_f`: Fermion mass.
/// - `n_c`: Color factor.
///
/// # Returns
/// Partial width in GeV.
pub fn h_decay_width_ff(m_h: f64, m_f: f64, n_c: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if m_h <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let mh2 = m_h * m_h
    let mf2 = m_f * m_f
    let ratio = 4.0 * mf2 / mh2
    if ratio > 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    let beta = sqrt(1.0 - ratio)
    let gf = 1.1663787e-5
    let prefactor = gf * mf2 * m_h / (4.0 * SQRT2 * PI)
    n_c * prefactor * beta * beta * beta
}

/// H → γγ decay width (loop-level, leading order):
///   Γ = (G_F α² M_H³) / (128√2 π³) · |A_W + A_f|².
///
/// For a light Higgs (M_H ≪ 4 m_t², M_H ≪ 4 M_W²), the loop functions approach:
///   A_W ≈ 7/4,   A_f ≈ −4/3 N_c Q_f².
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `m_h`: Higgs mass.
///
/// # Returns
/// Partial width in GeV.
pub fn h_decay_width_gammagamma(m_h: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if m_h <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let alpha = alpha_em().val()
    let gf = 1.1663787e-5
    let mh3 = m_h * m_h * m_h
    let prefactor = gf * alpha * alpha * mh3 / (128.0 * SQRT2 * PI * PI * PI)

    // W loop contribution (dominant)
    let aw = 1.75  // ≈ 7/4 for light Higgs

    // Top quark loop
    let mt = mass_top().val()
    let tau_t = 4.0 * mt * mt / (m_h * m_h)
    var at: f64 = 0.0
    if tau_t > 1.0 {
        // Heavy top limit: A_t → 4/3
        at = 4.0 / 3.0
    }
    // Charge factor: Q_t = +2/3 → Q_t² = 4/9
    let qt_sq = 4.0 / 9.0
    let a_f = -4.0 / 3.0 * 3.0 * qt_sq * at

    let total_amp = aw + a_f
    prefactor * total_amp * total_amp
}

/// H → gg decay width (loop-level, dominant at LO):
///   Γ = (G_F α_S² M_H³) / (36√2 π³) · |A_t|².
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `m_h`: Higgs mass.
///
/// # Returns
/// Partial width in GeV.
pub fn h_decay_width_gg(m_h: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if m_h <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let alpha_s = 0.1179  // at M_Z, approximate for Higgs scale
    let gf = 1.1663787e-5
    let mh3 = m_h * m_h * m_h
    let prefactor = gf * alpha_s * alpha_s * mh3 / (36.0 * SQRT2 * PI * PI * PI)

    // Top loop dominates
    let mt = mass_top().val()
    let tau_t = 4.0 * mt * mt / (m_h * m_h)
    var at: f64 = 0.0
    if tau_t > 1.0 {
        at = 1.0  // Heavy top limit
    }
    // Color factor for gg: sum over 8 gluons, average over 2 initial Higgs states
    // |A|² ≈ (3/4)² for heavy top
    let amp = 0.75 * at
    prefactor * amp * amp
}

/// Higgs total width (sum of dominant channels).
pub fn h_total_width() -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mh = mass_h().val()
    var total: f64 = 0.0
    // b b̄ (dominant)
    total = total + h_decay_width_ff(mh, mass_bottom().val(), 3.0)
    // τ⁺τ⁻
    total = total + h_decay_width_ff(mh, mass_tau().val(), 1.0)
    // c c̄
    total = total + h_decay_width_ff(mh, mass_charm().val(), 3.0)
    // γγ
    total = total + h_decay_width_gammagamma(mh)
    // gg
    total = total + h_decay_width_gg(mh)
    total
}

// ============================================================================
// LOCAL CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

let PI: f64 = 3.14159265358979323846
let SQRT2: f64 = 1.41421356237309504880


// === FILE: stdlib/particle_physics/approx_effects.sio ===
// stdlib/particle_physics/approx_effects.sio — Physical approximation effects
//
// Two new algebraic effects complete Sounio's approximation calculus:
//
//   Perturbative (bit 23, 8388608)
//     — marks LO-only perturbative calculations where higher-order terms are
//       truncated. Any function calling a Perturbative function must declare
//       `with Perturbative` in its own signature. Effect propagates up call chains.
//
//   NarrowWidthApproximation (bit 24, 16777216)
//     — marks calculations that treat unstable particles as exactly stable
//       (Gamma/M → 0). The approximation improves as Gamma/M decreases:
//       Higgs: Gamma_H/M_H ~ 3e-5 (excellent)
//       Top:   Gamma_top/M_top ~ 8e-3 (good)
//       Z:     Gamma_Z/M_Z ~ 2.7e-2 (adequate, ~2.7% systematic)
//
// Together with NonUnitary (bit 22), Sounio now encodes THREE distinct physical
// approximations at the type level — a uniform calculus with no analogue in
// ROOT, MadGraph, Pythia, or FeynCalc.
//
// References:
//   - Peskin & Schroeder §5, §17.5 (perturbative QCD, RGE)
//   - Stirling et al. (1991) gg→H LO cross-section
//   - PDG 2024: M_Z, Gamma_Z, M_H, M_top, alpha_s(M_Z)

module particle_physics::approx_effects

use epistemic::knowledge::{Epistemic}
use particle_physics::sm_params::{alpha_s_mz, mass_h, mass_top, mass_z}
use particle_physics::rge::{alpha_s_at_mu}

let AE_PI: f64 = 3.14159265358979323846

// ============================================================================
// Perturbative effect — sentinels and LO-only calculations
// ============================================================================
//
// The `with Perturbative` annotation propagates from the sentinel upward:
// every function that calls a Perturbative function must declare the effect
// or the compiler rejects it at typecheck time. This makes perturbative
// truncation visible in the static type of every affected function.

// Sentinel: the root source of the Perturbative effect.
fn perturbative_sentinel() -> bool with Perturbative {
    true
}

// QCD alpha_s at leading order — 1-loop running only, no NNLO matching,
// no resummation. Carries Epistemic uncertainty from PDG alpha_s(M_Z).
// Callers must declare `with Perturbative`.
pub fn alpha_s_lo_ep(mu_gev: f64) -> Epistemic with Perturbative, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let _flag = perturbative_sentinel()
    // alpha_s_at_mu propagates PDG uncertainty via 1-loop beta function.
    alpha_s_at_mu(mu_gev)
}

// gg→H cross-section at LO (K-factor = 1, triangle loop approximation).
// sigma_LO ~ C * alpha_s^2 / s  (dimensional estimate; not full LHC parton-level calc).
// Callers must declare `with Perturbative`.
pub fn ggh_lo_xsec_ep(m_h_gev: f64, sqrt_s_gev: f64) -> Epistemic with Perturbative, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let _flag = perturbative_sentinel()
    let as_lo = alpha_s_lo_ep(m_h_gev)
    // LO proportionality: sigma ~ (pi^2/576) * alpha_s^2 / s
    // C = pi^2 / 576 (from the heavy-top limit of the triangle diagram)
    let c_lo = AE_PI * AE_PI / 576.0
    let s = sqrt_s_gev * sqrt_s_gev
    as_lo.square().scale(c_lo / s)
}

// ============================================================================
// NarrowWidthApproximation effect — sentinels and on-shell calculations
// ============================================================================
//
// The `with NarrowWidthApproximation` annotation ensures that any function
// using the zero-width approximation cannot silently be called from code
// that does not acknowledge the approximation.

// Sentinel: the root source of the NarrowWidthApproximation effect.
fn nwa_sentinel() -> bool with NarrowWidthApproximation {
    true
}

// Z → f fbar partial width in the narrow-width approximation.
// Gamma(Z→ff) = G_F M_Z^3 N_c [(g_V^f)^2 + (g_A^f)^2] / (6 sqrt(2) pi)
//
// The NWA neglects Gamma_Z/M_Z corrections (~2.7%); use with appropriate
// systematic uncertainty in any analysis. GUM uncertainty is propagated
// through M_Z^3 using PDG M_Z = 91.1876 ± 0.0021 GeV.
//
// Arguments:
//   g_v_sq_plus_g_a_sq — (g_V^f)^2 + (g_A^f)^2 (exact neutral-current coupling)
//   n_color            — color factor: 1.0 for leptons, 3.0 for quarks
pub fn z_partial_width_nwa_ep(
    g_v_sq_plus_g_a_sq: f64,
    n_color: f64
) -> Epistemic with NarrowWidthApproximation, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let _flag = nwa_sentinel()
    let mz = mass_z()
    // G_F = 1.16638e-5 GeV^-2 (Fermi constant, PDG 2024)
    let gf = 1.1663787e-5
    let factor = gf * n_color * g_v_sq_plus_g_a_sq / (6.0 * 1.41421356237 * AE_PI)
    // M_Z^3 with GUM propagation: Var(M_Z^3) = (3 M_Z^2)^2 Var(M_Z)
    let mz2 = mz.square()
    let mz3 = mz2.mul(&mz)
    mz3.scale(factor)
}

// H → bb partial width in the narrow-width approximation.
// Gamma(H→bb) ~ 3 G_F m_b^2(M_H) M_H / (4 sqrt(2) pi) * (1 + 5.67 alpha_s/pi)
//
// Uses running bottom mass m_b(M_H) ~ 2.79 GeV (MS-bar at the Higgs scale).
// The QCD correction factor uses alpha_s at LO — this function therefore
// carries BOTH NarrowWidthApproximation and Perturbative effects.
//
// NWA quality: Gamma_H/M_H ~ 3e-5 — this is an excellent approximation.
pub fn h_bb_width_nwa_ep() -> Epistemic with NarrowWidthApproximation, Perturbative, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let _flag = nwa_sentinel()
    let mh = mass_h()
    // Running bottom mass at the Higgs scale (MS-bar scheme)
    let mb_mh = 2.79
    let gf = 1.1663787e-5
    // LO factor: 3 G_F m_b^2 M_H / (4 sqrt(2) pi)
    let factor_lo = 3.0 * gf * mb_mh * mb_mh / (4.0 * 1.41421356237 * AE_PI)
    // QCD correction: 1 + 5.67 alpha_s(M_H) / pi  (Chetyrkin et al. NLO coefficient)
    let as_mh = alpha_s_lo_ep(mh.val())
    let corr_val = 1.0 + 5.67 * as_mh.val() / AE_PI
    let corr = Epistemic::new(corr_val, as_mh.variance() * (5.67 / AE_PI) * (5.67 / AE_PI), as_mh.confidence())
    mh.scale(factor_lo).mul(&corr)
}

// ============================================================================
// Tests
// ============================================================================

var AE_PASS_CNT: [i64; 2] = [0; 2]

fn ae_chk(pass: bool, id: i64) with IO, Mut, Panic {
    if pass {
        AE_PASS_CNT[0] = AE_PASS_CNT[0] + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL approx_effects #")
        print_int(id)
        print("\n")
        AE_PASS_CNT[1] = AE_PASS_CNT[1] + 1
    }
}

pub fn run_approx_effects_tests() with IO, Perturbative, NarrowWidthApproximation, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("=== Approx Effects Tests ===\n")

    // T1: alpha_s_lo at M_Z is in the physical range [0.10, 0.14]
    let as_lo = alpha_s_lo_ep(91.1876)
    ae_chk(as_lo.val() > 0.10 && as_lo.val() < 0.14, 1)

    // T2: alpha_s_lo has nonzero uncertainty
    ae_chk(as_lo.variance() > 0.0, 2)

    // T3: ggh_lo_xsec is positive at 13 TeV
    let sigma_h = ggh_lo_xsec_ep(125.2, 13000.0)
    ae_chk(sigma_h.val() > 0.0, 3)

    // T4: ggh_lo_xsec uncertainty is nonzero (propagated from alpha_s)
    ae_chk(sigma_h.variance() > 0.0, 4)

    // T5: Z→νν partial width in NWA; neutrino couplings gV=gA=0.5
    // Expected ~ 0.167 GeV per species; we check [0.10, 0.25]
    let g_nu = 0.5 * 0.5 + 0.5 * 0.5
    let width_nu = z_partial_width_nwa_ep(g_nu, 1.0)
    ae_chk(width_nu.val() > 0.10 && width_nu.val() < 0.25, 5)

    // T6: Z partial width has GUM uncertainty from M_Z
    ae_chk(width_nu.variance() > 0.0, 6)

    // T7: H→bb width in NWA; expect ~ 0.002–0.005 GeV
    let width_bb = h_bb_width_nwa_ep()
    ae_chk(width_bb.val() > 0.001 && width_bb.val() < 0.01, 7)

    // T8: H→bb width has uncertainty from both M_H and alpha_s
    ae_chk(width_bb.variance() > 0.0, 8)

    // T9: structural check — Perturbative/NWA effects enforced at compile time
    ae_chk(true, 9)

    let n_pass = AE_PASS_CNT[0]
    let n_fail = AE_PASS_CNT[1]
    let total = n_pass + n_fail
    print("Approx Effects: ")
    print_int(n_pass)
    print("/")
    print_int(total)
    print(" PASS\n")
}

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Perturbative, NarrowWidthApproximation, Mut, Div, Panic {
    AE_PASS_CNT[0] = 0
    AE_PASS_CNT[1] = 0
    run_approx_effects_tests()
    if AE_PASS_CNT[1] == 0 { print("ALL PASS\n"); 0 } else { 1 }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/particle_physics/bsm_physics.sio ===
// ============================================================================
// BSM PHYSICS — Beyond the Standard Model simplified models
// ============================================================================
//
// Simplified models for dark matter, supersymmetry, and extra dimensions.
// These are "effective" models: heavy new physics is integrated out, leaving
// a small set of couplings and masses that can be constrained by collider data.
//
// References:
// - Goodman & Wheater, "Constraints on Dark Matter from Colliders" (2010)
// - Buchmueller et al., "Simplified Models for LHC New Physics Searches" (2014)
// - Abercrombie et al., "Dark Matter Benchmark Models" (2015)

module particle_physics::bsm_physics

use particle_physics::lorentz::{LorentzVector, lorentz_new, lorentz_add, lorentz_sub, lorentz_dot, lorentz_mass, lorentz_scale}
use particle_physics::sm_params::{mass_z, mass_w, alpha_em, sin2_theta_w, mass_top}
use particle_physics::cross_section::{mandelstam_s, flux_factor_2body}

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// Dark Matter Simplified Models
// ============================================================================

/// Dark matter candidate particle.
/// `mass` in GeV, `spin` = 0 (scalar), 0.5 (fermion), 1 (vector).
/// `coupling` g_q is the mediator-DM coupling.
pub struct DMCandidate {
    pub mass: f64,
    pub spin: f64,
    pub coupling: f64,
}

/// Mediator between SM and dark sector.
/// `mass` in GeV, `width` in GeV.
/// `mtype` = 0 (vector, e.g. Z'), 1 (scalar, e.g. s), 2 (axial-vector), 3 (pseudo-scalar).
pub struct Mediator {
    pub mass: f64,
    pub width: f64,
    pub mtype: i64,
    pub g_dm: f64,    // coupling to DM
    pub g_sm: f64,    // coupling to SM quarks
}

/// Axial-vector mediator (Z'-like) — common simplified model.
pub fn mediator_zprime(m_med: f64, g_dm: f64, g_q: f64) -> Mediator {
    let gq_sq = g_q * g_q
    let width_sm = 3.0 * 5.0 * gq_sq * m_med / (12.0 * 3.141592653589793)
    return Mediator { mass: m_med, width: width_sm, mtype: 2, g_dm: g_dm, g_sm: g_q }
}

/// Scalar mediator (s-channel).
pub fn mediator_scalar(m_med: f64, g_dm: f64, g_q: f64) -> Mediator {
    let gq_sq = g_q * g_q
    let width_sm = 3.0 * 5.0 * gq_sq * m_med / (8.0 * 3.141592653589793)
    return Mediator { mass: m_med, width: width_sm, mtype: 1, g_dm: g_dm, g_sm: g_q }
}

// ============================================================================
// SUSY Simplified Models
// ============================================================================

/// SUSY particle: squark or gluino.
pub struct SUSYParticle {
    pub pdg_code: i64,
    pub mass: f64,
    pub is_colored: i64,   // 1 = squark/gluino, 0 = neutralino/chargino
}

/// Neutralino (dark-matter candidate in R-parity conserving SUSY).
pub fn neutralino_1(mass: f64) -> SUSYParticle {
    return SUSYParticle { pdg_code: 1000022, mass: mass, is_colored: 0 }
}

/// Light-flavor squark (degenerate u_L, d_L, etc.).
pub fn squark_l(mass: f64) -> SUSYParticle {
    return SUSYParticle { pdg_code: 1000001, mass: mass, is_colored: 1 }
}

/// Gluino.
pub fn gluino(mass: f64) -> SUSYParticle {
    return SUSYParticle { pdg_code: 1000021, mass: mass, is_colored: 1 }
}

// ============================================================================
// Cross Sections for Simplified Models
// ============================================================================

/// Parton-level cross section for p p -> chi chi + jet (mono-jet) via
/// s-channel axial-vector mediator, at LO.
/// Returns sigma in pb.
pub fn xs_monojet_lo(m_dm: f64, m_med: f64, g_q: f64, g_chi: f64, et_min: f64) -> f64 {
    if m_med <= 0.0 || et_min <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let gev2pb = 0.389379e9     // GeV^-2 -> pb
    let suppression = m_med * m_med / (m_med * m_med + et_min * et_min)
    let alpha_s = 0.1
    let prefactor = alpha_s * g_q * g_q * g_chi * g_chi / (m_med * m_med * m_med * m_med)
    let phase_space = et_min * et_min
    let xs = prefactor * phase_space * suppression * suppression * gev2pb
    if xs < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return xs
}

/// Drell-Yan cross section for Z' -> l+ l-.
/// Returns sigma in pb for a narrow-width vector resonance.
pub fn xs_zprime_dilepton(m_zp: f64, width_zp: f64, g_q: f64, g_l: f64) -> f64 {
    if m_zp <= 0.0 || width_zp <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let prod_xs = 0.1 * g_q * g_q * 1.0e6 / (m_zp * m_zp)
    let br_ll = 2.0 * g_l * g_l / (10.0 * g_q * g_q + 2.0 * g_l * g_l)
    return prod_xs * br_ll * 1.0e-3
}

/// Squark-pair production cross section at LO (approximate).
/// Returns sigma in pb.
pub fn xs_squark_pair_lo(m_squark: f64, sqrts: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if m_squark <= 0.0 || sqrts <= 2.0 * m_squark { return 0.0 }
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let alpha_s = 0.1
    let gev2pb = 0.389379e9
    let beta_sq = 1.0 - 4.0 * m_squark * m_squark / (sqrts * sqrts)
    if beta_sq <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let beta = sqrt(beta_sq)
    let xs = (pi * alpha_s * alpha_s) / (12.0 * m_squark * m_squark) * beta * beta * beta
    return xs * gev2pb
}

/// Gluino-pair production cross section at LO (approximate).
/// Returns sigma in pb.
pub fn xs_gluino_pair_lo(m_gluino: f64, sqrts: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if m_gluino <= 0.0 || sqrts <= 2.0 * m_gluino { return 0.0 }
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let alpha_s = 0.1
    let gev2pb = 0.389379e9
    let beta_sq = 1.0 - 4.0 * m_gluino * m_gluino / (sqrts * sqrts)
    if beta_sq <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let beta = sqrt(beta_sq)
    let xs = (9.0 * pi * alpha_s * alpha_s) / (4.0 * m_gluino * m_gluino) * beta
    return xs * gev2pb
}

// ============================================================================
// Signal/Background Discrimination Observables
// ============================================================================

/// MET (missing transverse energy) from a pair of DM candidates.
pub fn met_monojet_approx(m_dm: f64, pT_recoil: f64) -> f64 {
    let denom = pT_recoil * pT_recoil + 4.0 * m_dm * m_dm
    if denom <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return pT_recoil * (1.0 - 2.0 * m_dm * m_dm / denom)
}

/// Effective mass m_eff = sum_jet pT + MET. Common SUSY search variable.
pub fn m_eff(jet_pts: &[f64; 16], n_jets: i64, met: f64) -> f64 {
    var sum: f64 = met
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_jets {
        sum = sum + jet_pts[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

/// MT2 (stransverse mass) for two identical invisible particles of mass m_inv.
pub fn mt2_symmetric(p1: LorentzVector, p2: LorentzVector, met_px: f64, met_py: f64, m_inv: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let et1 = p1.t
    let et2 = p2.t
    let px1 = p1.x
    let py1 = p1.y
    let px2 = p2.x
    let py2 = p2.y
    let m2 = 2.0 * (et1 * et2 - px1 * px2 - py1 * py2)
    var mt2_0: f64 = 0.0
    if m2 > 0.0 { mt2_0 = sqrt(m2) }
    return mt2_0 + m_inv * m_inv
}
