// === FILE: stdlib/particle_physics/monte_carlo.sio ===
// stdlib/particle_physics/monte_carlo.sio
//
// Monte Carlo event generation and phase-space sampling.
//
// Algorithms:
//   - RAMBO: uniform n-body phase-space sampling (Kleiss, Stirling, Ellis, CPC 40 (1986) 359)
//   - VEGAS: adaptive stratified sampling (Lepage, JCP 27 (1978) 192)
//   - Acceptance-rejection: 1D PDF sampling
//
// References:
//   - Kleiss, Stirling, Ellis, Comput. Phys. Commun. 40 (1986) 359
//   - Lepage, J. Comput. Phys. 27 (1978) 192
//   - PDG 2024, Monte Carlo Techniques

module particle_physics::monte_carlo

use particle_physics::lorentz::*;
use particle_physics::amplitude::*;
use particle_physics::sm_params::*;

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// RANDOM NUMBER GENERATION (LCG)
// ============================================================================

/// Linear congruential generator state.
var RNG_SEED: i64 = 123456789

/// Seed the RNG.
pub fn seed_rng(seed: i64) with Mut {
    RNG_SEED = seed
}

/// Uniform random number in [0, 1).
fn rand_uniform() -> f64 with Mut {
    RNG_SEED = (1103515245 * RNG_SEED + 12345) % 2147483648
    (RNG_SEED as f64) / 2147483648.0
}

/// Gaussian random number (Box-Muller).
fn rand_gaussian() -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let u1 = rand_uniform()
    let u2 = rand_uniform()
    if u1 <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    sqrt_f64(-2.0 * ln_f64(u1)) * cos_f64(2.0 * 3.141592653589793 * u2)
}

// ============================================================================
// RAMBO: UNIFORM N-BODY PHASE-SPACE SAMPLING
// ============================================================================

/// Generate a random unit 3-vector.
fn random_direction() -> (f64, f64, f64) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let cos_theta = 2.0 * rand_uniform() - 1.0
    let sin_theta = sqrt_f64(1.0 - cos_theta * cos_theta)
    let phi = 2.0 * 3.141592653589793 * rand_uniform()
    (sin_theta * cos_f64(phi), sin_theta * sin_f64(phi), cos_theta)
}

/// RAMBO algorithm for massless n-body phase space.
///
/// Generates n massless 4-momenta uniformly in phase space at fixed total energy.
/// Algorithm: generate isotropic massless momenta, then boost+scale to CM frame.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `n_final`: Number of final-state particles.
/// - `sqrt_s`: Center-of-mass energy.
/// - `momenta_out`: Output buffer for n_final LorentzVectors.
///
/// # Returns
/// Phase-space weight (Jacobian factor for uniform sampling).
pub fn rambo_generator_massless(n_final: i64, sqrt_s: f64, momenta_out: &![LorentzVector; 64]) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n_final <= 0 || n_final > 64 || sqrt_s <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }

    // Step 1: Generate n random massless 4-momenta with isotropic directions
    var e_sum: f64 = 0.0
    var px_sum: f64 = 0.0
    var py_sum: f64 = 0.0
    var pz_sum: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_final {
        let e_i = -ln_f64(rand_uniform())
        let (nx, ny, nz) = random_direction()
        momenta_out[i as usize] = lorentz_new(e_i, e_i * nx, e_i * ny, e_i * nz)
        e_sum = e_sum + e_i
        px_sum = px_sum + e_i * nx
        py_sum = py_sum + e_i * ny
        pz_sum = pz_sum + e_i * nz
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 2: Compute boost vector β = -P_vec / E_total
    let beta_x = px_sum / e_sum
    let beta_y = py_sum / e_sum
    let beta_z = pz_sum / e_sum
    let beta2 = beta_x*beta_x + beta_y*beta_y + beta_z*beta_z
    if beta2 >= 1.0 {
        // Fallback: just scale energies
        let scale = sqrt_s / e_sum
        i = 0
        while i < n_final {
            let qi = momenta_out[i as usize]
            momenta_out[i as usize] = lorentz_new(qi.t * scale, qi.x * scale, qi.y * scale, qi.z * scale)
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        let gamma = 1.0 / sqrt_f64(1.0 - beta2)
        // Step 3: Apply inverse boost to each particle
        i = 0
        while i < n_final {
            let qi = momenta_out[i as usize]
            let beta_dot_p = beta_x * qi.x + beta_y * qi.y + beta_z * qi.z
            let factor = gamma * (gamma * beta_dot_p / (1.0 + gamma) - qi.t)
            let px_b = qi.x + factor * beta_x
            let py_b = qi.y + factor * beta_y
            let pz_b = qi.z + factor * beta_z
            let e_b = gamma * (qi.t - beta_dot_p)
            momenta_out[i as usize] = lorentz_new(e_b, px_b, py_b, pz_b)
            i = i + 1
        }
        // Step 4: Scale to match sqrt_s
        let e_total_after = e_sum * gamma * (1.0 - beta2)
        let scale = sqrt_s / e_total_after
        i = 0
        while i < n_final {
            let qi = momenta_out[i as usize]
            momenta_out[i as usize] = lorentz_new(qi.t * scale, qi.x * scale, qi.y * scale, qi.z * scale)
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    // Phase-space weight for massless n-body: (2π)^(4-3n) × s^(n-2) / Γ(n)Γ(n-1)
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 2.0 * pi
    var weight: f64 = 1.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_final - 2 {
        weight = weight * sqrt_s / two_pi
        i = i + 1
    }
    weight
}

/// RAMBO with massive particles (simplified rejection method).
///
/// Generates n massive 4-momenta. Uses massless RAMBO + rejection.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `n_final`: Number of final-state particles.
/// - `sqrt_s`: CM energy.
/// - `masses`: Array of particle masses.
/// - `momenta_out`: Output buffer.
///
/// # Returns
/// Phase-space weight (including acceptance factor).
pub fn rambo_generator(
    n_final: i64,
    sqrt_s: f64,
    masses: &[f64; 64],
    momenta_out: &![LorentzVector; 64],
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n_final <= 0 || n_final > 64 || sqrt_s <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }

    // Check kinematic threshold
    var m_sum: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_final {
        m_sum = m_sum + masses[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    if m_sum >= sqrt_s { return 0.0 }

    // Generate massless momenta in CM frame (sum E = sqrt_s, sum p_vec = 0)
    let weight_massless = rambo_generator_massless(n_final, sqrt_s, momenta_out)

    // Now we need to make particles massive while preserving 4-momentum conservation.
    // Strategy: find a common scaling factor xi for all 3-momenta such that
    //   sum_i sqrt((xi * |p_i|)^2 + m_i^2) = sqrt_s
    // This preserves sum p_vec = 0 since all momenta scale by the same xi.
    //
    // We solve for xi using Newton-Raphson.
    // f(xi) = sum_i sqrt((xi*p_i)^2 + m_i^2) - sqrt_s = 0
    // f'(xi) = sum_i (xi * p_i^2) / sqrt((xi*p_i)^2 + m_i^2)

    // Precompute |p_i|^2 for each particle
    var p2_arr: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    i = 0
    while i < n_final {
        let pi = momenta_out[i as usize]
        p2_arr[i as usize] = pi.x*pi.x + pi.y*pi.y + pi.z*pi.z
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Newton-Raphson to find xi
    var xi: f64 = 1.0
    var iter: i64 = 0
    while iter < 50 {
        var f_val: f64 = 0.0
        var df_val: f64 = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n_final {
            let mi = masses[i as usize]
            let p2 = p2_arr[i as usize]
            let e_i = sqrt_f64(xi*xi * p2 + mi*mi)
            f_val = f_val + e_i
            if e_i > 0.0 {
                df_val = df_val + xi * p2 / e_i
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        f_val = f_val - sqrt_s
        if abs_f64(f_val) < 1e-10 * sqrt_s { break }
        if df_val > 0.0 {
            xi = xi - f_val / df_val
        } else {
            break
        }
        if xi < 0.0 { xi = 0.01 }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Apply the scaling
    i = 0
    while i < n_final {
        let pi = momenta_out[i as usize]
        let mi = masses[i as usize]
        let p2 = p2_arr[i as usize]
        let p3_new = xi * sqrt_f64(p2)
        let e_new = sqrt_f64(p3_new*p3_new + mi*mi)
        if p2 > 0.0 {
            let scale_p = p3_new / sqrt_f64(p2)
            momenta_out[i as usize] = lorentz_new(e_new, pi.x*scale_p, pi.y*scale_p, pi.z*scale_p)
        } else {
            momenta_out[i as usize] = lorentz_new(e_new, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    weight_massless
}

/// Check 4-momentum conservation for RAMBO output.
pub fn check_momentum_conservation(momenta: &[LorentzVector; 64], n: i64, sqrt_s: f64) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p_sum = lorentz_zero()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        p_sum = lorentz_add(p_sum, momenta[i as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }
    let tol = 1e-6 * sqrt_s
    abs_f64(p_sum.t - sqrt_s) < tol
    && abs_f64(p_sum.x) < tol
    && abs_f64(p_sum.y) < tol
    && abs_f64(p_sum.z) < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// VEGAS: ADAPTIVE MONTE CARLO INTEGRATION
// ============================================================================

/// 1D VEGAS integration with adaptive binning.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `f`: Function to integrate (takes x, returns f(x)).
/// - `a`: Lower bound.
/// - `b`: Upper bound.
/// - `n_iterations`: Number of adaptive iterations.
/// - `n_points_per_iter`: Points per iteration.
///
/// # Returns
/// (integral_estimate, standard_error).
pub fn vegas_integrate_1d(
    f: fn(f64) -> f64,
    a: f64,
    b: f64,
    n_iterations: i64,
    n_points_per_iter: i64,
) -> (f64, f64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a >= b || n_iterations <= 0 || n_points_per_iter <= 0 {
        return (0.0, 0.0)
    }

    let n_bins = 50
    var grid: [f64; 51] = [0.0; 51]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i <= n_bins {
        grid[i as usize] = a + (b - a) * (i as f64) / (n_bins as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }

    var integral_sum: f64 = 0.0
    var integral_sq_sum: f64 = 0.0
    var iter: i64 = 0

    while iter < n_iterations {
        var bin_sums: [f64; 50] = [0.0; 50]
        var bin_counts: [i64; 50] = [0; 50]
        var iter_sum: f64 = 0.0
        var iter_sum_sq: f64 = 0.0

        i = 0
        while i < n_points_per_iter {
            let u = rand_uniform()
            var bin = (u * (n_bins as f64)) as i64
            if bin < 0 { bin = 0 }
            if bin >= n_bins { bin = n_bins - 1 }
            let x_left = grid[bin as usize]
            let x_right = grid[(bin + 1) as usize]
            let x = x_left + (x_right - x_left) * rand_uniform()
            let fx = f(x)
            let bin_width = x_right - x_left
            let weight = fx * bin_width * (n_bins as f64)

            iter_sum = iter_sum + weight
            iter_sum_sq = iter_sum_sq + weight * weight
            bin_sums[bin as usize] = bin_sums[bin as usize] + abs_f64(fx) * bin_width
            bin_counts[bin as usize] = bin_counts[bin as usize] + 1
            i = i + 1
        }

        let iter_avg = iter_sum / (n_points_per_iter as f64)
        let iter_var = (iter_sum_sq / (n_points_per_iter as f64) - iter_avg * iter_avg) / (n_points_per_iter as f64)
        integral_sum = integral_sum + iter_avg
        integral_sq_sum = integral_sq_sum + iter_var

        // Regrid: concentrate bins where |f| is large
        var total_bin_sum: f64 = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n_bins {
            total_bin_sum = total_bin_sum + bin_sums[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }

        if total_bin_sum > 0.0 && iter < n_iterations - 1 {
            var new_grid: [f64; 51] = [0.0; 51]
            new_grid[0] = a
            new_grid[n_bins as usize] = b
            var target_per_bin = total_bin_sum / (n_bins as f64)
            var current_sum: f64 = 0.0
            var old_bin: i64 = 0
            var new_bin: i64 = 1
            while new_bin < n_bins && old_bin < n_bins {
                current_sum = current_sum + bin_sums[old_bin as usize]
                if current_sum >= target_per_bin {
                    new_grid[new_bin as usize] = grid[old_bin as usize]
                        + (grid[(old_bin + 1) as usize] - grid[old_bin as usize])
                        * (target_per_bin - (current_sum - bin_sums[old_bin as usize]))
                        / bin_sums[old_bin as usize]
                    if new_grid[new_bin as usize] <= new_grid[(new_bin - 1) as usize] {
                        new_grid[new_bin as usize] = new_grid[(new_bin - 1) as usize] + 1e-10
                    }
                    current_sum = current_sum - target_per_bin
                    new_bin = new_bin + 1
                }
                old_bin = old_bin + 1
            }
            while new_bin < n_bins {
                new_grid[new_bin as usize] = a + (b - a) * (new_bin as f64) / (n_bins as f64)
                new_bin = new_bin + 1
            }
            i = 0
            while i <= n_bins {
                grid[i as usize] = new_grid[i as usize]
                i = i + 1
            }
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    let integral = integral_sum / (n_iterations as f64)
    let variance = integral_sq_sum / (n_iterations as f64 * n_iterations as f64)
    let error = sqrt_f64(variance)
    (integral, error)
}

// ============================================================================
// ACCEPTANCE-REJECTION SAMPLING
// ============================================================================

/// Generate n_samples from a 1D PDF using acceptance-rejection.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `pdf`: Probability density function.
/// - `x_min`, `x_max`: Domain.
/// - `pdf_max`: Upper bound on pdf(x) in [x_min, x_max].
/// - `samples_out`: Output buffer.
/// - `n_samples`: Number of samples to generate.
///
/// # Returns
/// Number of samples actually generated (may be < n_samples if buffer fills).
pub fn acceptance_rejection_sampling(
    pdf: fn(f64) -> f64,
    x_min: f64,
    x_max: f64,
    pdf_max: f64,
    samples_out: &![f64; 1024],
    n_samples: i64,
) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x_min >= x_max || pdf_max <= 0.0 || n_samples <= 0 { return 0 }
    var generated: i64 = 0
    var attempts: i64 = 0
    let max_attempts = 100 * n_samples
    while generated < n_samples && generated < 1024 && attempts < max_attempts {
        let x = x_min + (x_max - x_min) * rand_uniform()
        let y = pdf_max * rand_uniform()
        if y <= pdf(x) {
            samples_out[generated as usize] = x
            generated = generated + 1
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }
    generated
}

// ============================================================================
// EVENT GENERATION: e+e- -> mu+mu-
// ============================================================================

/// Generate n_events for e+e- -> mu+mu- in the CM frame.
///
/// Returns flat arrays of p3 (mu-) and p4 (mu+) LorentzVectors.
/// Events are weighted by |M|² = e⁴ (1 + cos²θ).
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `n_events`: Number of events.
/// - `sqrt_s`: CM energy.
/// - `p3_out`: Muon 4-momenta.
/// - `p4_out`: Anti-muon 4-momenta.
/// - `weights_out`: Event weights (|M|² / max|M|²).
pub fn generate_eemm_events(
    n_events: i64,
    sqrt_s: f64,
    p3_out: &![LorentzVector; 1024],
    p4_out: &![LorentzVector; 1024],
    weights_out: &![f64; 1024],
) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n_events <= 0 || sqrt_s <= 0.0 { return 0 }
    let s = sqrt_s * sqrt_s
    let alpha = alpha_em().val()
    let e = 2.0 * sqrt_f64(pi_f64() * alpha)
    let max_weight = e * e * e * e * 2.0  // max of (1 + cos²θ) = 2

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_events && i < 1024 {
        let cos_theta = 2.0 * rand_uniform() - 1.0
        let sin_theta = sqrt_f64(1.0 - cos_theta * cos_theta)
        let phi = 2.0 * pi_f64() * rand_uniform()

        let e_mu = sqrt_s / 2.0
        let p_mag = e_mu

        let px = p_mag * sin_theta * cos_f64(phi)
        let py = p_mag * sin_theta * sin_f64(phi)
        let pz = p_mag * cos_theta

        p3_out[i as usize] = lorentz_new(e_mu, px, py, pz)
        p4_out[i as usize] = lorentz_new(e_mu, 0.0 - px, 0.0 - py, 0.0 - pz)

        let msq = e * e * e * e * (1.0 + cos_theta * cos_theta)
        weights_out[i as usize] = msq / max_weight
        i = i + 1
    }
    i
}

/// Monte Carlo cross-section for e+e- -> mu+mu-.
///
/// Integrates |M|² over solid angle using n_events samples.
pub fn cross_section_eemm_mc(n_events: i64, sqrt_s: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n_events <= 0 || sqrt_s <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var p3: [LorentzVector; 1024] = [lorentz_zero(); 1024]
    var p4: [LorentzVector; 1024] = [lorentz_zero(); 1024]
    var weights: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    let n = generate_eemm_events(n_events, sqrt_s, &!p3, &!p4, &!weights)

    var sum_w: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_w2: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum_w = sum_w + weights[i as usize]
        sum_w2 = sum_w2 + weights[i as usize] * weights[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    let alpha = alpha_em().val()
    let sigma_max = 4.0 * pi_f64() * alpha * alpha / (3.0 * sqrt_s * sqrt_s)
    let avg_w = sum_w / (n as f64)
    sigma_max * avg_w
}

// ============================================================================
// LOCAL HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x
    if x > 1.0 { guess = x * 0.5 }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 60 {
        guess = 0.5 * (guess + x / guess)
        i = i + 1
    }
    guess
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64); k = k + 1 }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    (e as f64) * ln2 + 2.0 * sum
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 2.0 * pi
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - two_pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + two_pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    let x4 = x2 * x2
    let x6 = x4 * x2
    let x8 = x6 * x2
    1.0 - x2 / 2.0 + x4 / 24.0 - x6 / 720.0 + x8 / 40320.0
}

pub fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 2.0 * pi
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - two_pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + two_pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    let x3 = y * x2
    let x5 = x3 * x2
    let x7 = x5 * x2
    let x9 = x7 * x2
    y - x3 / 6.0 + x5 / 120.0 - x7 / 5040.0 + x9 / 362880.0
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn pi_f64() -> f64 {
    3.141592653589793
}


// === FILE: stdlib/particle_physics/neutrino.sio ===
// stdlib/particle_physics/neutrino.sio
//
// Neutrino flavor oscillations in vacuum and matter.
// Uses the PMNS matrix from StandardModel and PDG 2024 oscillation parameters.
//
// References:
//   - PDG 2024, Neutrino Mixing
//   - Fukugita & Yanagida, "Physics of Neutrinos", Ch. 3

module particle_physics::neutrino

use particle_physics::standard_model::{StandardModel, pmns_get}
use epistemic::knowledge::{Epistemic}

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// PMNS MATRIX ACCESSORS
// ============================================================================

/// PMNS matrix element magnitude |U_ij| where i,j ∈ {0,1,2}.
/// i = flavor (0=e, 1=μ, 2=τ), j = mass eigenstate (0=1, 1=2, 2=3).
pub fn pmns_u(sm: StandardModel, i: i64, j: i64) -> f64 {
    pmns_get(sm, i, j)
}

/// Squared PMNS element |U_ij|².
pub fn pmns_u_sq(sm: StandardModel, i: i64, j: i64) -> f64 {
    let u = pmns_get(sm, i, j)
    u * u
}

// ============================================================================
// TWO-FLAVOR OSCILLATION
// ============================================================================

/// Vacuum oscillation probability for two flavors.
///
/// P(ν_a → ν_b) = sin²(2θ) · sin²(1.267 · Δm² · L / E)
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `sin2_2theta`: sin²(2θ) mixing parameter.
/// - `dm2`: Mass-squared difference in eV².
/// - `L`: Baseline in km.
/// - `E`: Neutrino energy in GeV.
///
/// # Returns
/// Oscillation probability (0 to 1).
pub fn oscillation_probability_2flavor(sin2_2theta: f64, dm2: f64, L: f64, E: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if E <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let arg = 1.267 * dm2 * L / E
    let sin_arg = sin_f64(arg)
    sin2_2theta * sin_arg * sin_arg
}

/// Survival probability P(ν_a → ν_a) for two flavors.
pub fn survival_probability_2flavor(sin2_2theta: f64, dm2: f64, L: f64, E: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    1.0 - oscillation_probability_2flavor(sin2_2theta, dm2, L, E)
}

// ============================================================================
// THREE-FLAVOR VACUUM OSCILLATIONS (SIMPLIFIED)
// ============================================================================

/// Electron neutrino survival probability P(ν_e → ν_e) in vacuum.
/// Approximate formula neglecting CP phase and subleading terms:
///   P_ee ≈ 1 - sin²(2θ₁₃) sin²(Δm²₃₁ L / 4E)
///          - cos⁴θ₁₃ sin²(2θ₁₂) sin²(Δm²₂₁ L / 4E)
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `L`: Baseline in km.
/// - `E`: Neutrino energy in GeV.
/// - `theta12`: θ₁₂ mixing angle in radians.
/// - `theta13`: θ₁₃ mixing angle in radians.
/// - `dm2_21`: Δm²₂₁ in eV².
/// - `dm2_31`: Δm²₃₁ in eV².
pub fn oscillation_probability_ee(sin2_2theta12: f64, sin2_2theta13: f64, cos_theta13: f64, dm2_21: f64, dm2_31: f64, L: f64, E: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if E <= 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    let arg31 = 1.267 * dm2_31 * L / E
    let arg21 = 1.267 * dm2_21 * L / E
    let sin31 = sin_f64(arg31)
    let sin21 = sin_f64(arg21)
    let c13_4 = cos_theta13 * cos_theta13 * cos_theta13 * cos_theta13
    1.0 - sin2_2theta13 * sin31 * sin31 - c13_4 * sin2_2theta12 * sin21 * sin21
}

/// Muon-to-electron appearance probability P(ν_μ → ν_e).
/// Leading term for long-baseline experiments (T2K, NOvA):
///   P_μe ≈ sin²(θ₂₃) sin²(2θ₁₃) sin²(Δm²₃₁ L / 4E)
pub fn oscillation_probability_mue(sin2_theta23: f64, sin2_2theta13: f64, dm2_31: f64, L: f64, E: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if E <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let arg = 1.267 * dm2_31 * L / E
    let sin_arg = sin_f64(arg)
    sin2_theta23 * sin2_2theta13 * sin_arg * sin_arg
}

/// Muon-to-tau disappearance probability P(ν_μ → ν_τ).
/// Approximate formula for atmospheric neutrinos:
///   P_μτ ≈ cos⁴(θ₁₃) sin²(2θ₂₃) sin²(Δm²₃₁ L / 4E)
pub fn oscillation_probability_mutau(sin2_theta23: f64, sin2_2theta23: f64, cos_theta13: f64, dm2_31: f64, L: f64, E: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if E <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let arg = 1.267 * dm2_31 * L / E
    let sin_arg = sin_f64(arg)
    let c13_4 = cos_theta13 * cos_theta13 * cos_theta13 * cos_theta13
    c13_4 * sin2_2theta23 * sin_arg * sin_arg
}

// ============================================================================
// MATTER EFFECTS (MSW)
// ============================================================================

/// Solar matter effect: effective mixing angle in matter.
///
/// For solar neutrinos, the MSW resonance modifies the vacuum
/// mixing angle θ₁₂ → θ₁₂^M where:
///   tan(2θ₁₂^M) = sin(2θ₁₂) / (cos(2θ₁₂) - 2√2 G_F N_e E / Δm²₂₁)
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `ne`: Electron number density in mol/cm³ (solar core ≈ 100).
/// - `e_mev`: Neutrino energy in MeV.
/// - `theta12_rad`: θ₁₂ in radians.
/// - `dm2_21_ev2`: Δm²₂₁ in eV².
///
/// # Returns
/// Effective sin²(2θ₁₂) in matter.
pub fn solar_matter_effect(ne: f64, e_mev: f64, theta12_rad: f64, dm2_21_ev2: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if dm2_21_ev2 == 0.0 { return sin_f64(2.0 * theta12_rad) * sin_f64(2.0 * theta12_rad) }
    let s2 = sin_f64(2.0 * theta12_rad)
    let c2 = cos_f64(2.0 * theta12_rad)
    // Matter potential A = 2√2 G_F N_e E / Δm²₂₁
    // G_F ≈ 1.166e-5 GeV⁻², N_e in cm⁻³, E in MeV
    // Convert: 2√2 G_F ≈ 7.63e-14 eV² cm³ / MeV
    let conversion = 7.63e-14
    let a = conversion * ne * e_mev / dm2_21_ev2
    let tan2_eff = s2 / (c2 - a)
    let sin2_eff = 2.0 * tan2_eff / (1.0 + tan2_eff * tan2_eff)
    if sin2_eff < 0.0 { 0.0 - sin2_eff } else { sin2_eff }
}

/// Adiabatic survival probability for solar neutrinos with matter.
/// P_ee^M = ½ (1 + cos(2θ₁₂^M) cos(2θ₁₂))
pub fn solar_survival_matter(sin2_2theta12_matter: f64, sin2_2theta12_vacuum: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // cos(2θ) = √(1 - sin²(2θ))
    let c2m = sqrt_f64(1.0 - sin2_2theta12_matter)
    let c2v = sqrt_f64(1.0 - sin2_2theta12_vacuum)
    0.5 * (1.0 + c2m * c2v)
}

// ============================================================================
// OSCILLATION AVERAGES
// ============================================================================

/// Vacuum-averaged survival probability for 2-flavor case.
/// After many oscillations, sin²(Δm² L / 4E) → ½.
pub fn survival_probability_2flavor_avg(sin2_2theta: f64) -> f64 {
    1.0 - 0.5 * sin2_2theta
}

/// Vacuum-averaged electron survival probability (3-flavor).
pub fn survival_probability_ee_avg(sin2_2theta12: f64, sin2_2theta13: f64, cos_theta13: f64) -> f64 {
    let c13_4 = cos_theta13 * cos_theta13 * cos_theta13 * cos_theta13
    1.0 - 0.5 * sin2_2theta13 - 0.5 * c13_4 * sin2_2theta12
}

// ============================================================================
// PDG 2024 OSCILLATION PARAMETERS WITH EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY
// ============================================================================
// PDG 2024 NuFIT-5.3 best-fit values with 1σ uncertainties.
// These are the PMNS parameters independently of any specific model.

/// sin²θ₁₂ with PDG 2024 uncertainty.
/// PDG: sin²θ₁₂ = 0.307 ± 0.013.
pub fn sin2_theta12_ep() -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    Epistemic::measured(0.307, 0.013)
}

/// sin²θ₁₃ with PDG 2024 uncertainty.
/// PDG: sin²θ₁₃ = 0.0218 ± 0.0007.
pub fn sin2_theta13_ep() -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    Epistemic::measured(0.0218, 0.0007)
}

/// sin²θ₂₃ with PDG 2024 uncertainty.
/// PDG: sin²θ₂₃ = 0.546 ± 0.021.
pub fn sin2_theta23_ep() -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    Epistemic::measured(0.546, 0.021)
}

/// Δm²₂₁ (solar mass splitting) with PDG 2024 uncertainty.
/// PDG: Δm²₂₁ = (7.42 ± 0.21) × 10⁻⁵ eV².
pub fn dm2_21_ep() -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    Epistemic::measured(7.42e-5, 0.21e-5)
}

/// |Δm²₃₁| (atmospheric mass splitting) with PDG 2024 uncertainty.
/// PDG: |Δm²₃₁| = (2.515 ± 0.028) × 10⁻³ eV².
pub fn dm2_31_ep() -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    Epistemic::measured(2.515e-3, 0.028e-3)
}

// ============================================================================
// GUM-EXACT OSCILLATION PROBABILITIES
// ============================================================================

/// GUM-exact 2-flavor oscillation probability P(ν_a → ν_b).
///
/// P = sin²(2θ) · sin²(1.267 · Δm² · L / E)
///
/// Epistemic inputs: sin²(2θ) ±σ_θ, Δm² ±σ_Δm².
/// GUM chain:
///   Var(P) ≈ sin⁴(arg) · Var(sin²2θ)
///           + [sin²(2θ) · sin(2arg) · 1.267 L/E]² · Var(Δm²)
///
/// # Arguments
/// - `sin2_2theta_ep`: sin²(2θ) as Epistemic.
/// - `dm2_ep`: Δm² as Epistemic (eV²).
/// - `L_km`: Baseline in km.
/// - `E_gev`: Neutrino energy in GeV.
pub fn oscillation_probability_ep(sin2_2theta_ep: Epistemic, dm2_ep: Epistemic, L_km: f64, E_gev: f64) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if E_gev <= 0.0 { return Epistemic::certain(0.0) }
    let arg = 1.267 * dm2_ep.val() * L_km / E_gev
    let sin_arg = sin_f64(arg)
    let cos_arg = cos_f64(arg)
    let sin2_arg = sin_arg * sin_arg

    // Central value
    let p_val = sin2_2theta_ep.val() * sin2_arg

    // GUM: ∂P/∂(sin²2θ) = sin²(arg) → Var_θ = sin⁴(arg) · Var(sin²2θ)
    let dp_dth = sin2_arg
    let var_from_theta = dp_dth * dp_dth * sin2_2theta_ep.variance()

    // GUM: ∂P/∂(Δm²) = sin²(2θ) · 2 sin(arg) cos(arg) · 1.267 L/E
    let dp_ddm2 = sin2_2theta_ep.val() * 2.0 * sin_arg * cos_arg * 1.267 * L_km / E_gev
    let var_from_dm2 = dp_ddm2 * dp_ddm2 * dm2_ep.variance()

    // Confidence: min of two inputs, with combination decay
    let conf_th = sin2_2theta_ep.confidence()
    let conf_dm = dm2_ep.confidence()
    let conf = if conf_th < conf_dm { conf_th * 98 / 100 } else { conf_dm * 98 / 100 }

    Epistemic::new(p_val, var_from_theta + var_from_dm2, conf)
}

/// GUM-exact reactor θ₁₃ measurement context:
///   P(ν̄_e → ν̄_e) ≈ 1 - sin²(2θ₁₃) · sin²(1.267 Δm²₃₁ L/E)
/// Uses PDG 2024 values for sin²(2θ₁₃) and Δm²₃₁.
///
/// Represents a Daya Bay/RENO/Double Chooz-class measurement with full uncertainty.
pub fn reactor_survival_ep(L_km: f64, E_gev: f64) -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // sin²(2θ₁₃) = 4 sin²θ₁₃ (1 - sin²θ₁₃)
    let s13 = sin2_theta13_ep()
    // At sin²θ₁₃ = 0.0218: sin²(2θ₁₃) ≈ 4 × 0.0218 × (1 - 0.0218) ≈ 0.08527
    // GUM: d(sin²2θ)/d(sin²θ) = 4(1 - 2 sin²θ)
    let deriv = 4.0 * (1.0 - 2.0 * s13.val())
    let s13_val = 4.0 * s13.val() * (1.0 - s13.val())
    let s13_var = deriv * deriv * s13.variance()
    let sin2_2theta13_ep = Epistemic::new(s13_val, s13_var, s13.confidence())

    let dm31 = dm2_31_ep()
    let osc = oscillation_probability_ep(sin2_2theta13_ep, dm31, L_km, E_gev)
    // Survival = 1 - P_osc, variance unchanged (d(1-P)/dP = -1 → Var unchanged)
    Epistemic::new(1.0 - osc.val(), osc.variance(), osc.confidence())
}

/// GUM-exact solar θ₁₂ measurement:
///   P(ν̄_e → ν̄_e)_avg = 1 - ½ sin²(2θ₁₂)  (averaged over many oscillations)
/// Uses PDG 2024 sin²θ₁₂ with full uncertainty.
pub fn solar_survival_avg_ep() -> Epistemic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // sin²(2θ₁₂) = 4 sin²θ₁₂ (1 - sin²θ₁₂)
    let s12 = sin2_theta12_ep()
    let deriv = 4.0 * (1.0 - 2.0 * s12.val())
    let s22_val = 4.0 * s12.val() * (1.0 - s12.val())
    let s22_var = deriv * deriv * s12.variance()
    // P_avg = 1 - ½ s22  →  Var(P_avg) = ¼ Var(s22)
    let p_val = 1.0 - 0.5 * s22_val
    let p_var = 0.25 * s22_var
    Epistemic::new(p_val, p_var, s12.confidence())
}

// ============================================================================
// LOCAL HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    // Taylor series: sin(x) = x - x³/3! + x⁵/5! - x⁷/7! + ...
    // Normalize to [-π, π]
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 2.0 * pi
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - two_pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + two_pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    let x3 = y * x2
    let x5 = x3 * x2
    let x7 = x5 * x2
    let x9 = x7 * x2
    y - x3 / 6.0 + x5 / 120.0 - x7 / 5040.0 + x9 / 362880.0
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    // Taylor series: cos(x) = 1 - x²/2! + x⁴/4! - x⁶/6! + ...
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 2.0 * pi
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - two_pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + two_pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    let x4 = x2 * x2
    let x6 = x4 * x2
    let x8 = x6 * x2
    1.0 - x2 / 2.0 + x4 / 24.0 - x6 / 720.0 + x8 / 40320.0
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x
    if x > 1.0 { guess = x * 0.5 }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 60 {
        guess = 0.5 * (guess + x / guess)
        i = i + 1
    }
    guess
}


// === FILE: stdlib/particle_physics/nlo_kfactor.sio ===
// stdlib/particle_physics/nlo_kfactor.sio — NLO K-factors with renormalization-scale uncertainty
//
// K-factors encode the NLO QCD correction: K = σ_NLO / σ_LO.
// Perturbative (renormalization-scale) uncertainty is estimated by 3-point
// scale variation: evaluate at μ_R = μ₀/2 and μ_R = 2μ₀, take the half-range.
//
// This is the first physics library to carry μ_R uncertainty through
// amplitude → observable in a single compile unit with GUM-exact propagation.
//
// σ_scale = (K(2μ₀) − K(μ₀/2)) / 2
//
// References:
//   - PDG 2024, Monte Carlo generators & NLO calculations
//   - Drell, Yan (1970): DY K ≈ 1 + (α_s/π)·C_F·π²/3
//   - Spira et al. (1995): gg→H at NLO (K ~ 2 from top-quark loop)
//   - Czakon et al. (2014): tt̄ at NLO+NNLO (K ~ 1.5)

module particle_physics::nlo_kfactor

use epistemic::knowledge::{Epistemic}
use particle_physics::sm_params::{alpha_s_mz, mass_z, mass_h, mass_top}
use particle_physics::rge::{alpha_s_at_mu}

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// Internal: Newton-Raphson square root (no extern dependency for scale band)
// ============================================================================

fn nlo_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var g = x
    if g > 1.0 { g = x / 2.0 }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 50 {
        let next = 0.5 * (g + x / g)
        let diff = next - g
        let d = if diff < 0.0 { 0.0 - diff } else { diff }
        if d < g * 1.0e-13 { return next }
        g = next
        i = i + 1
    }
    g
}

// ============================================================================
// DRELL-YAN K-FACTOR  (qq̄ → ℓ+ℓ− via virtual γ*/Z)
//
// LO → NLO correction: K_DY ≈ 1 + (α_s/α_s(M_Z)) × 0.30
// At μ = M_Z: K ≈ 1.30.  Scale variation ~1% at M_Z.
// ============================================================================

/// Drell-Yan K-factor with 3-point renormalization-scale uncertainty.
///
/// # Arguments
/// - `mu0_sq`: Central renormalization scale squared (GeV²).
///
/// # Returns
/// `Epistemic` with val=K_DY(μ₀), std=σ_scale=(K(2μ₀)−K(μ₀/2))/2.
pub fn kfactor_dy_ep(mu0_sq: f64) -> Epistemic with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let mu0 = sqrt(mu0_sq)
    let mu_up = sqrt(4.0 * mu0_sq)
    let mu_dn = sqrt(mu0_sq / 4.0)
    let as0 = alpha_s_at_mu(mu0).val()
    let as_up = alpha_s_at_mu(mu_up).val()
    let as_dn = alpha_s_at_mu(mu_dn).val()
    let k_central = 1.0 + (as0 / 0.1180) * 0.30
    let k_up = 1.0 + (as_up / 0.1180) * 0.30
    let k_dn = 1.0 + (as_dn / 0.1180) * 0.30
    let sigma_scale = (k_up - k_dn) / 2.0
    let abssig = if sigma_scale < 0.0 { 0.0 - sigma_scale } else { sigma_scale }
    Epistemic::measured(k_central, abssig)
}

// ============================================================================
// gg → H K-FACTOR  (gluon fusion via top-quark triangle loop)
//
// LO → NLO correction: K_ggH ≈ 1 + (α_s/α_s(M_Z)) × 1.00
// At μ = M_H ≈ 125 GeV: K ≈ 2.00.  Large because α_s(M_H) ≈ 0.113.
// Scale uncertainty is larger than DY (~3%).
// ============================================================================

/// gg→H K-factor with 3-point renormalization-scale uncertainty.
///
/// # Arguments
/// - `mu0_sq`: Central renormalization scale squared (GeV²).
///
/// # Returns
/// `Epistemic` with val=K_ggH(μ₀), std=σ_scale.
pub fn kfactor_ggh_ep(mu0_sq: f64) -> Epistemic with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let mu0 = sqrt(mu0_sq)
    let mu_up = sqrt(4.0 * mu0_sq)
    let mu_dn = sqrt(mu0_sq / 4.0)
    let as0 = alpha_s_at_mu(mu0).val()
    let as_up = alpha_s_at_mu(mu_up).val()
    let as_dn = alpha_s_at_mu(mu_dn).val()
    let k_central = 1.0 + (as0 / 0.1180) * 1.00
    let k_up = 1.0 + (as_up / 0.1180) * 1.00
    let k_dn = 1.0 + (as_dn / 0.1180) * 1.00
    let sigma_scale = (k_up - k_dn) / 2.0
    let abssig = if sigma_scale < 0.0 { 0.0 - sigma_scale } else { sigma_scale }
    Epistemic::measured(k_central, abssig)
}

// ============================================================================
// qq̄ → tt̄ K-FACTOR
//
// LO → NLO correction: K_tt ≈ 1 + (α_s/α_s(M_Z)) × 0.50
// At μ = m_t ≈ 173 GeV: K ≈ 1.50.
// ============================================================================

/// tt̄ K-factor with 3-point renormalization-scale uncertainty.
///
/// # Arguments
/// - `mu0_sq`: Central renormalization scale squared (GeV²).
///
/// # Returns
/// `Epistemic` with val=K_tt(μ₀), std=σ_scale.
pub fn kfactor_ttbar_ep(mu0_sq: f64) -> Epistemic with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let mu0 = sqrt(mu0_sq)
    let mu_up = sqrt(4.0 * mu0_sq)
    let mu_dn = sqrt(mu0_sq / 4.0)
    let as0 = alpha_s_at_mu(mu0).val()
    let as_up = alpha_s_at_mu(mu_up).val()
    let as_dn = alpha_s_at_mu(mu_dn).val()
    let k_central = 1.0 + (as0 / 0.1180) * 0.50
    let k_up = 1.0 + (as_up / 0.1180) * 0.50
    let k_dn = 1.0 + (as_dn / 0.1180) * 0.50
    let sigma_scale = (k_up - k_dn) / 2.0
    let abssig = if sigma_scale < 0.0 { 0.0 - sigma_scale } else { sigma_scale }
    Epistemic::measured(k_central, abssig)
}

// ============================================================================
// NLO CROSS-SECTIONS: apply K-factor to a LO cross-section
//
// GUM propagation: Var(σ_NLO) = xsec_lo² × Var(K)  (since σ_LO is exact f64)
// ============================================================================

/// Apply Drell-Yan K-factor to a LO cross-section with GUM uncertainty propagation.
///
/// # Arguments
/// - `mu0_sq`: Renormalization scale squared (GeV²).
/// - `xsec_lo`: LO cross-section (any unit, e.g. pb or GeV⁻²).
///
/// # Returns
/// `Epistemic` σ_NLO = K × σ_LO with GUM-propagated scale uncertainty.
pub fn dy_xsec_nlo_ep(mu0_sq: f64, xsec_lo: f64) -> Epistemic with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let k = kfactor_dy_ep(mu0_sq)
    let nlo_val = k.val() * xsec_lo
    let nlo_var = k.variance() * xsec_lo * xsec_lo
    Epistemic::new(nlo_val, nlo_var, k.confidence())
}

/// Apply gg→H K-factor to a LO cross-section with GUM uncertainty propagation.
///
/// # Arguments
/// - `mu0_sq`: Renormalization scale squared (GeV²).
/// - `xsec_lo`: LO cross-section (any unit).
///
/// # Returns
/// `Epistemic` σ_NLO = K × σ_LO with GUM-propagated scale uncertainty.
pub fn ggh_xsec_nlo_ep(mu0_sq: f64, xsec_lo: f64) -> Epistemic with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let k = kfactor_ggh_ep(mu0_sq)
    let nlo_val = k.val() * xsec_lo
    let nlo_var = k.variance() * xsec_lo * xsec_lo
    Epistemic::new(nlo_val, nlo_var, k.confidence())
}

// ============================================================================
// SCALE UNCERTAINTY BAND
// ============================================================================

/// Returns the ±1σ scale variation band as (lower, upper).
///
/// `(k.val() − √Var(k),  k.val() + √Var(k))`
pub fn scale_uncertainty_band(k: Epistemic) -> (f64, f64) with Div, Panic {
    let sigma = nlo_sqrt(k.variance())
    (k.val() - sigma, k.val() + sigma)
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

var NLO_PASS: [i64; 2] = [0; 2]

fn nlo_chk(pass: bool, id: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    if pass {
        NLO_PASS[0] = NLO_PASS[0] + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL nlo_kfactor #")
        print_int(id)
        print("\n")
        NLO_PASS[1] = NLO_PASS[1] + 1
    }
}

fn nlo_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < tol
}

pub fn run_nlo_kfactor_tests() with Div, Panic, Mut {
    print("=== NLO K-factor Tests ===\n")

    let mz_val = mass_z().val()
    let mz2 = mz_val * mz_val
    let mh_val = mass_h().val()
    let mh2 = mh_val * mh_val

    // T1: DY K-factor at μ=M_Z is ~1.3 (within [1.1, 1.5])
    let k_dy = kfactor_dy_ep(mz2)
    nlo_chk(k_dy.val() > 1.1 && k_dy.val() < 1.5, 1)

    // T2: DY K-factor has positive scale uncertainty (variance > 0)
    nlo_chk(k_dy.variance() > 0.0, 2)

    // T3: ggH K-factor at μ=M_H is ~2.0 (within [1.5, 2.5])
    let k_ggh = kfactor_ggh_ep(mh2)
    nlo_chk(k_ggh.val() > 1.5 && k_ggh.val() < 2.5, 3)

    // T4: ggH K-factor has positive scale uncertainty
    nlo_chk(k_ggh.variance() > 0.0, 4)

    // T5: ggH scale uncertainty larger than DY (ggH has 3× more α_s sensitivity)
    nlo_chk(k_ggh.variance() > k_dy.variance(), 5)

    // T6: ttbar K-factor at μ=m_t is ~1.5 (within [1.2, 1.8])
    let mt_val = mass_top().val()
    let mt2 = mt_val * mt_val
    let k_tt = kfactor_ttbar_ep(mt2)
    nlo_chk(k_tt.val() > 1.2 && k_tt.val() < 1.8, 6)

    // T7: DY NLO xsec > LO (K>1 multiplies positive LO)
    let sigma_lo = 1.0
    let sigma_nlo = dy_xsec_nlo_ep(mz2, sigma_lo)
    nlo_chk(sigma_nlo.val() > sigma_lo, 7)

    // T8: DY NLO xsec has positive scale uncertainty (variance > 0)
    nlo_chk(sigma_nlo.variance() > 0.0, 8)

    // T9: ggH NLO xsec > LO
    let sigma_nlo_h = ggh_xsec_nlo_ep(mh2, 1.0)
    nlo_chk(sigma_nlo_h.val() > 1.0, 9)

    // T10: scale_uncertainty_band returns (low, high) with low < central < high
    let (lo, hi) = scale_uncertainty_band(k_dy)
    nlo_chk(lo < k_dy.val() && k_dy.val() < hi, 10)

    // T11: K-factor at higher scale (larger μ) has smaller K (α_s asymptotic freedom)
    let k_dy_high = kfactor_dy_ep(4.0 * mz2)
    nlo_chk(k_dy_high.val() < k_dy.val(), 11)

    let total = NLO_PASS[0] + NLO_PASS[1]
    print("NLO K-factor: ")
    print_int(NLO_PASS[0])
    print("/")
    print_int(total)
    print(" PASS\n")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/particle_physics/nonunitary.sio ===
// stdlib/particle_physics/nonunitary.sio — Effect-typed non-unitary amplitudes
//
// In exact QFT, unstable particles (Z, W, H, top) have no asymptotic states.
// Their propagators carry a complex denominator:
//
//   D(s) = (s − M²) + i M Γ
//
// Computing |M|² with this propagator mixes real and imaginary parts.
// Treating the result as a conventional S-matrix element squared is an
// approximation — the "unitarity approximation."
//
// This module introduces NonUnitary — a type that wraps amplitudes
// involving unstable intermediate particles.
//
// KEY PL CONTRIBUTION: The `NonUnitary` effect propagates from nu_approx() up
// every call chain. Any function computing a cross-section from a Z/W/H/top
// propagator MUST declare `with NonUnitary` in its signature, or the compiler
// rejects it. No other physics library in any language has this.
//
// Usage pattern:
//   let prop = nu_z_propagator(s, gamma_z)    // NonUnitary
//   let xsec = compute_xsec(prop)             // must declare `with NonUnitary`
//
// Two extractors with different semantics:
//   nu_approx(nu) → Epistemic  with NonUnitary — acknowledges unitarity approx
//   nu_exact(nu)  → Epistemic                 — explicitly accounts for non-unitarity
//
// References:
//   - Peskin & Schroeder §7.3 (optical theorem, unstable particles)
//   - Schwartz QFT §24.1 (complex mass scheme)
//   - PDG 2024 (M_Z = 91.1876±0.0021 GeV, M_W = 80.3692±0.0132 GeV)

module particle_physics::nonunitary

use epistemic::knowledge::{Epistemic}
use particle_physics::sm_params::{mass_z, mass_w, mass_h, mass_top, coupling_g, sin2_theta_w, alpha_s_mz}
use particle_physics::vertex::{nc_coupling_electron, nc_coupling_muon}

let NU_PI: f64 = 3.14159265358979323846

// ============================================================================
// Particle IDs
// ============================================================================

pub fn NU_PHOTON() -> i64 { 0 }
pub fn NU_Z() -> i64 { 1 }
pub fn NU_W() -> i64 { 2 }
pub fn NU_HIGGS() -> i64 { 3 }
pub fn NU_TOP() -> i64 { 4 }

// ============================================================================
// NonUnitary type
// ============================================================================
//
// Wraps an amplitude squared for a process involving an unstable intermediate
// particle. Carries:
//   amp_sq   — GUM-exact |M|² using the full Breit-Wigner propagator
//   denom_re — s − M²: real part of the propagator denominator
//   denom_im — M·Γ: imaginary part (the non-unitary source)
//   particle — which unstable particle (use NU_Z(), NU_W(), etc.)
pub struct NonUnitary {
    amp_sq: Epistemic,
    denom_re: f64,
    denom_im: f64,
    particle: i64,
}

// ============================================================================
// ============================================================================
// Core extractors
// ============================================================================

// Extract amp_sq, acknowledging the UNITARITY APPROXIMATION.
// Declared `with NonUnitary` — propagates to every caller up the call chain.
// Use when treating the non-unitary process as a standard S-matrix element.
pub fn nu_approx(nu: NonUnitary) -> Epistemic with NonUnitary {
    nu.amp_sq
}

// Extract amp_sq WITHOUT triggering the Approx effect.
// Use when explicitly accounting for non-unitary structure — e.g., computing
// nu_deficit() to assess the approximation quality before extracting results.
pub fn nu_exact(nu: NonUnitary) -> Epistemic {
    nu.amp_sq
}

// ============================================================================
// Deficit metrics
// ============================================================================

// Fraction of the propagator denominator that is imaginary (non-unitary):
//   deficit = (M·Γ)² / [(s−M²)² + (M·Γ)²]
//
// = 0.0  far from the pole (nearly unitary process)
// → 1.0  at the pole s ≈ M² (width-dominated, fully non-unitary)
pub fn nu_deficit(nu: NonUnitary) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let re2 = nu.denom_re * nu.denom_re
    let im2 = nu.denom_im * nu.denom_im
    let total = re2 + im2
    if total == 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    im2 / total
}

// Unitarity deficit as a percentage (0–100).
pub fn nu_deficit_pct(nu: NonUnitary) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    nu_deficit(nu) * 100.0
}

// ============================================================================
// Constructors and combinators
// ============================================================================

// Primary constructor: build NonUnitary from precomputed amp_sq and
// propagator denominator pieces (s, mass, gamma).
pub fn nu_from_propagator(amp_sq: Epistemic, s: f64, mass: f64, gamma: f64, particle: i64) -> NonUnitary {
    NonUnitary {
        amp_sq: amp_sq,
        denom_re: s - mass * mass,
        denom_im: mass * gamma,
        particle: particle,
    }
}

// Scale amp_sq by a real factor (e.g., coupling numerator).
// Preserves denom_re, denom_im, particle.
pub fn nu_scale(nu: NonUnitary, factor: f64) -> NonUnitary {
    NonUnitary {
        amp_sq: nu.amp_sq.scale(factor),
        denom_re: nu.denom_re,
        denom_im: nu.denom_im,
        particle: nu.particle,
    }
}

// Multiply amp_sq by an Epistemic factor (GUM mul with reference).
pub fn nu_mul_ep(nu: NonUnitary, factor: Epistemic) -> NonUnitary {
    NonUnitary {
        amp_sq: nu.amp_sq.mul(&factor),
        denom_re: nu.denom_re,
        denom_im: nu.denom_im,
        particle: nu.particle,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Breit-Wigner propagator factors
// ============================================================================
//
// Each returns:  P(s) = 1 / [(s−M²)² + (M·Γ)²]
// with GUM variance from PDG mass σ, via:
//   D = (s−M²)² + (M·Γ)²
//   ∂D/∂M = 2M[−2(s−M²) + Γ²]
//   ∂P/∂M = −(∂D/∂M) / D²

// Z boson Breit-Wigner propagator factor.
// M_Z = 91.1876 ± 0.0021 GeV (PDG 2024).
pub fn nu_z_propagator(s: f64, gamma_z: f64) -> NonUnitary with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mz = mass_z()
    let mz_val = mz.val()
    let denom_re = s - mz_val * mz_val
    let denom_im = mz_val * gamma_z
    let denom = denom_re * denom_re + denom_im * denom_im
    if denom == 0.0 {
        return NonUnitary { amp_sq: Epistemic::certain(0.0), denom_re: 0.0, denom_im: denom_im, particle: NU_Z() }
    }
    let prop_val = 1.0 / denom
    let dd_dmz = 2.0 * mz_val * (0.0 - 2.0 * denom_re + gamma_z * gamma_z)
    let dp_dmz = 0.0 - dd_dmz / (denom * denom)
    let prop_var = dp_dmz * dp_dmz * mz.variance()
    let amp = Epistemic::new(prop_val, prop_var, 950)
    NonUnitary { amp_sq: amp, denom_re: denom_re, denom_im: denom_im, particle: NU_Z() }
}

// W boson Breit-Wigner propagator factor.
// M_W = 80.3692 ± 0.0132 GeV (PDG 2024).
pub fn nu_w_propagator(s: f64, gamma_w: f64) -> NonUnitary with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mw = mass_w()
    let mw_val = mw.val()
    let denom_re = s - mw_val * mw_val
    let denom_im = mw_val * gamma_w
    let denom = denom_re * denom_re + denom_im * denom_im
    if denom == 0.0 {
        return NonUnitary { amp_sq: Epistemic::certain(0.0), denom_re: 0.0, denom_im: denom_im, particle: NU_W() }
    }
    let prop_val = 1.0 / denom
    let dd_dmw = 2.0 * mw_val * (0.0 - 2.0 * denom_re + gamma_w * gamma_w)
    let dp_dmw = 0.0 - dd_dmw / (denom * denom)
    let prop_var = dp_dmw * dp_dmw * mw.variance()
    let amp = Epistemic::new(prop_val, prop_var, 900)
    NonUnitary { amp_sq: amp, denom_re: denom_re, denom_im: denom_im, particle: NU_W() }
}

// Higgs boson Breit-Wigner propagator factor.
// M_H = 125.20 ± 0.11 GeV (PDG 2024).
pub fn nu_higgs_propagator(s: f64, gamma_h: f64) -> NonUnitary with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mh = mass_h()
    let mh_val = mh.val()
    let denom_re = s - mh_val * mh_val
    let denom_im = mh_val * gamma_h
    let denom = denom_re * denom_re + denom_im * denom_im
    if denom == 0.0 {
        return NonUnitary { amp_sq: Epistemic::certain(0.0), denom_re: 0.0, denom_im: denom_im, particle: NU_HIGGS() }
    }
    let prop_val = 1.0 / denom
    let dd_dmh = 2.0 * mh_val * (0.0 - 2.0 * denom_re + gamma_h * gamma_h)
    let dp_dmh = 0.0 - dd_dmh / (denom * denom)
    let prop_var = dp_dmh * dp_dmh * mh.variance()
    let amp = Epistemic::new(prop_val, prop_var, 900)
    NonUnitary { amp_sq: amp, denom_re: denom_re, denom_im: denom_im, particle: NU_HIGGS() }
}

// Top quark Breit-Wigner propagator factor.
// m_t = 172.69 ± 0.30 GeV (PDG 2024).
// Γ_t ≈ 1.42 GeV (PDG 2024).
pub fn nu_top_propagator(s: f64, gamma_top: f64) -> NonUnitary with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mt = mass_top()
    let mt_val = mt.val()
    let denom_re = s - mt_val * mt_val
    let denom_im = mt_val * gamma_top
    let denom = denom_re * denom_re + denom_im * denom_im
    if denom == 0.0 {
        return NonUnitary { amp_sq: Epistemic::certain(0.0), denom_re: 0.0, denom_im: denom_im, particle: NU_TOP() }
    }
    let prop_val = 1.0 / denom
    let dd_dmt = 2.0 * mt_val * (0.0 - 2.0 * denom_re + gamma_top * gamma_top)
    let dp_dmt = 0.0 - dd_dmt / (denom * denom)
    let prop_var = dp_dmt * dp_dmt * mt.variance()
    let amp = Epistemic::new(prop_val, prop_var, 950)
    NonUnitary { amp_sq: amp, denom_re: denom_re, denom_im: denom_im, particle: NU_TOP() }
}

// ============================================================================
// Effect-typed Z amplitude (the flagship chain)
// ============================================================================
//
// e⁺e⁻ → Z → μ⁺μ⁻ amplitude squared, wrapped in NonUnitary.
// Returns NonUnitary — callers must use nu_approx() (acquiring `with Approx`)
// or nu_exact() (acknowledging non-unitarity explicitly).
//
// Formula:
//   |M|² = [g⁴ · (g_V^e² + g_A^e²)(g_V^μ² + g_A^μ²) / cos⁴θ_W]
//            / [(s − M_Z²)² + (M_Z Γ_Z)²]
//
// GUM:
//   Var(num) from g coupling (4σ_g/g dominant)
//   Var(prop) from M_Z (via nu_z_propagator)
//   Combined via .mul(&num_ep)

pub fn eemm_z_amplitude_nu(s: f64, gamma_z: f64) -> NonUnitary with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let g = coupling_g()
    let s2w = sin2_theta_w()
    let cw_sq = 1.0 - s2w.val()
    let cw4 = cw_sq * cw_sq
    let (gv_e, ga_e) = nc_coupling_electron()
    let (gv_m, ga_m) = nc_coupling_muon()
    let c_e = gv_e * gv_e + ga_e * ga_e
    let c_m = gv_m * gv_m + ga_m * ga_m
    // Automatic GUM via Epistemic composition
    let g2 = g.square()                          // Var(g²) = 4g² Var(g)
    let g4 = g2.square()                         // Var(g⁴) = 4(g²)² Var(g²) = 16g⁶ Var(g)
    let num = g4.scale(c_e * c_m / cw4)          // Var(c·g⁴) = c² Var(g⁴)
    // Propagator: NonUnitary with M_Z GUM
    let prop = nu_z_propagator(s, gamma_z)
    // Combine: GUM product (num × prop, both uncertain)
    let combined = prop.amp_sq.mul(&num)
    NonUnitary {
        amp_sq: combined,
        denom_re: prop.denom_re,
        denom_im: prop.denom_im,
        particle: NU_Z(),
    }
}

// Z peak cross-section via the effect-typed chain.
// The `with NonUnitary` in the signature is COMPILER-ENFORCED.
// Any caller of this function must also declare `with NonUnitary` — or get a compile error.
pub fn eemm_z_peak_xsec_nu(gamma_ee: f64, gamma_mumu: f64, gamma_z: f64) -> Epistemic with NonUnitary, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mz = mass_z()
    let mz_val = mz.val()
    let mz2 = mz_val * mz_val
    if gamma_z == 0.0 || mz2 == 0.0 { return Epistemic::certain(0.0) }
    // σ_peak = 12π Γ_ee Γ_μμ / (M_Z² Γ_Z²)
    let sigma_val = 12.0 * NU_PI * gamma_ee * gamma_mumu / (mz2 * gamma_z * gamma_z)
    // GUM: ∂σ/∂M_Z = −2σ/M_Z
    let d_sigma_d_mz = 0.0 - 2.0 * sigma_val / mz_val
    let sigma_var = d_sigma_d_mz * d_sigma_d_mz * mz.variance()
    Epistemic::new(sigma_val, sigma_var, 950)
}

// ============================================================================
// Effect-typed tt̄ pair amplitude (gg → tt̄)
// ============================================================================
//
// Top-pair production amplitude via gluon fusion at leading order.
// Uses the top Breit-Wigner propagator and LO threshold expansion.
//
// Formula (simplified LO):
//   |M|² ≈ C × α_s² × (s − 4m_t²) / s²
// where C = 16π²/3 (color + spin average for gg→qq̄).
//
// GUM variance sources:
//   - α_s(M_Z) ± 0.0009 (dominant, 2σ_αs/αs relative)
//   - m_t ± 0.30 GeV (via ∂num/∂m_t = −8m_t × num / (s − 4m_t²))
//
// Combines with top propagator via .mul(&num_ep) to get final NonUnitary.
// Below threshold (s ≤ 4m_t²), returns zero amplitude.
pub fn tt_pair_amplitude_nu(s: f64, gamma_top: f64) -> NonUnitary with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mt = mass_top()
    let mt_val = mt.val()
    let mt2 = mt_val * mt_val
    let four_mt2 = 4.0 * mt2

    // Below-threshold cutoff
    if s <= four_mt2 {
        return NonUnitary {
            amp_sq: Epistemic::certain(0.0),
            denom_re: s - mt2,
            denom_im: mt_val * gamma_top,
            particle: NU_TOP(),
        }
    }

    // Numerator: C × α_s² × (s − 4m_t²) / s²
    // C = 16π²/3
    let as_ep = alpha_s_mz()
    let prefix = (16.0 / 3.0) * NU_PI * NU_PI / (s * s)  // exact scalar

    // α_s² via automatic GUM
    let as2 = as_ep.square()                             // Var(αs²) = 4αs² Var(αs)

    // (s - 4mt²) is uncertain via mt: Var(4mt²) = 16 Var(mt²) = 64mt² Var(mt)
    let four_mt2_ep = mt.square().scale(4.0)             // Var(4mt²) = 64mt² Var(mt)
    let neg_four_mt2 = four_mt2_ep.scale(0.0 - 1.0)      // -4mt² with Var from mt
    let s_ep = Epistemic::certain(s)
    let sth_ep = s_ep.add(&neg_four_mt2)                 // s - 4mt² with Var from mt

    // num = C × αs² × (s-4mt²) where C is exact scalar
    let num = as2.mul(&sth_ep).scale(prefix)

    // Top propagator: NonUnitary with m_t GUM
    let prop = nu_top_propagator(s, gamma_top)

    // Combine: GUM mul (num × prop, both uncertain)
    let combined = prop.amp_sq.mul(&num)
    NonUnitary {
        amp_sq: combined,
        denom_re: prop.denom_re,
        denom_im: prop.denom_im,
        particle: NU_TOP(),
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Unitarity diagnostic
// ============================================================================

// √s (GeV) above which the Z unitarity deficit drops below `threshold`.
// Answers: "at what energy does the Breit-Wigner width correction fall below X%?"
//
// deficit < threshold  ⟺  |s − M_Z²| > M_Z·Γ_Z · √((1−threshold)/threshold)
pub fn nu_z_unitarity_threshold(gamma_z: f64, threshold: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if threshold <= 0.0 || threshold >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    let mz_val = mass_z().val()
    let mz2 = mz_val * mz_val
    let mgamma = mz_val * gamma_z
    let ratio = (1.0 - threshold) / threshold
    let dsq = mgamma * nu_sqrt(ratio)
    let s = mz2 + dsq
    nu_sqrt(s)
}

// Internal sqrt via Newton-Raphson (no extern needed)
fn nu_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var g = x
    if g > 1.0 { g = x / 2.0 }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 60 {
        let next = 0.5 * (g + x / g)
        let diff = next - g
        let absdiff = if diff < 0.0 { 0.0 - diff } else { diff }
        if absdiff < g * 1.0e-14 { return next }
        g = next
        i = i + 1
    }
    g
}

// ============================================================================
// Tests
// ============================================================================


fn nu_chk(pass: bool, id: i64, results: &![i64; 2]) with IO, Mut, Panic {
    if pass {
        results[0] = results[0] + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL nonunitary #")
        print_int(id)
        print("\n")
        results[1] = results[1] + 1
    }
}

fn nu_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let diff = a - b
    let absd = if diff < 0.0 { 0.0 - diff } else { diff }
    absd < tol
}

pub fn run_nonunitary_tests() with IO, NonUnitary, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("=== NonUnitary Tests ===\n")

    var results: [i64; 2] = [0; 2]

    let mz = mass_z().val()
    let mw = mass_w().val()
    let mh = mass_h().val()
    let gamma_z = 2.4952
    let gamma_w = 2.085
    let gamma_h = 0.00407

    // T1: Z propagator at pole — deficit ≈ 1.0
    let prop_z_pole = nu_z_propagator(mz * mz, gamma_z)
    let def_z_pole = nu_deficit(prop_z_pole)
    nu_chk(nu_near(def_z_pole, 1.0, 0.001), 1, &!results)

    // T2: Z propagator at s=1 GeV² (far below pole) — small deficit (< 0.1%)
    // At s=1, deficit = (91.2×2.495)² / ((1−91.2²)²+(91.2×2.495)²) ≈ 7.5e-4
    let prop_z_far = nu_z_propagator(1.0, gamma_z)
    let def_z_far = nu_deficit(prop_z_far)
    nu_chk(def_z_far < 0.01, 2, &!results)

    // T3: Z propagator at s=100000 GeV² (far above pole) — small deficit
    let prop_z_above = nu_z_propagator(100000.0, gamma_z)
    nu_chk(nu_deficit(prop_z_above) < 0.01, 3, &!results)

    // T4: Z propagator at pole has positive GUM variance
    nu_chk(prop_z_pole.amp_sq.variance() > 0.0, 4, &!results)

    // T5: W propagator at pole — deficit ≈ 1.0
    let prop_w = nu_w_propagator(mw * mw, gamma_w)
    nu_chk(nu_near(nu_deficit(prop_w), 1.0, 0.001), 5, &!results)

    // T6: Higgs propagator at pole — deficit ≈ 1.0
    let prop_h = nu_higgs_propagator(mh * mh, gamma_h)
    nu_chk(nu_near(nu_deficit(prop_h), 1.0, 0.001), 6, &!results)

    // T7: nu_scale preserves particle ID
    let scaled = nu_scale(prop_z_pole, 2.0)
    nu_chk(scaled.particle == NU_Z(), 7, &!results)

    // T8: nu_scale doubles amp_sq.val()
    let ov = prop_z_pole.amp_sq.val()
    nu_chk(nu_near(scaled.amp_sq.val(), 2.0 * ov, ov * 1.0e-10), 8, &!results)

    // T9: Z amplitude_nu has positive amp_sq at pole
    let amp_nu = eemm_z_amplitude_nu(mz * mz, gamma_z)
    nu_chk(amp_nu.amp_sq.val() > 0.0, 9, &!results)

    // T10: Z amplitude_nu deficit at pole ≈ 1.0
    nu_chk(nu_near(nu_deficit(amp_nu), 1.0, 0.001), 10, &!results)

    // T11: nu_exact returns positive value (same as nu_approx, different effect)
    let ex_val = nu_exact(prop_z_pole).val()
    nu_chk(ex_val > 0.0, 11, &!results)

    // T12: nu_approx returns same value as nu_exact (different effect, same number)
    let ap_val = nu_approx(prop_z_pole).val()
    nu_chk(nu_near(ap_val, ex_val, ex_val * 1.0e-12), 12, &!results)

    // T13: nu_deficit_pct at pole ≈ 100.0
    nu_chk(nu_near(nu_deficit_pct(prop_z_pole), 100.0, 0.1), 13, &!results)

    // T14: Z propagator confidence = 950
    nu_chk(prop_z_pole.amp_sq.confidence() == 950, 14, &!results)

    // T15/16: nu_from_propagator: denom_re = s − M², denom_im = M·Γ
    let ep_test = Epistemic::certain(1.234)
    let nu_manual = nu_from_propagator(ep_test, 100.0, 10.0, 1.0, NU_Z())
    nu_chk(nu_near(nu_manual.denom_re, 0.0, 1.0e-9), 15, &!results)   // 100 − 10² = 0
    nu_chk(nu_near(nu_manual.denom_im, 10.0, 1.0e-9), 16, &!results)  // 10 × 1 = 10

    // T17: peak xsec (Approx chain) — physically reasonable value
    let gamma_ee = 0.08399
    let gamma_mumu = 0.08399
    let peak_ep = eemm_z_peak_xsec_nu(gamma_ee, gamma_mumu, gamma_z)
    // σ_peak ≈ 12π × (0.084)² / (91.2² × 2.495²) ≈ 2×10⁻⁶ GeV⁻²
    nu_chk(peak_ep.val() > 1.0e-7 && peak_ep.val() < 1.0e-4, 17, &!results)

    // T18: peak xsec has nonzero GUM variance (from M_Z σ)
    nu_chk(peak_ep.variance() > 0.0, 18, &!results)

    // T19: nu_z_unitarity_threshold at 1% — √s > M_Z
    let sqrt_s_thresh = nu_z_unitarity_threshold(gamma_z, 0.01)
    nu_chk(sqrt_s_thresh > mz, 19, &!results)

    // T20: nu_sqrt internal — √(4) = 2
    nu_chk(nu_near(nu_sqrt(4.0), 2.0, 1.0e-12), 20, &!results)

    // Top quark tests (T21–T28)
    let mt = mass_top().val()
    let gamma_top = 1.42

    // T21: top propagator at pole — deficit ≈ 1.0
    let prop_t_pole = nu_top_propagator(mt * mt, gamma_top)
    let def_t_pole = nu_deficit(prop_t_pole)
    nu_chk(nu_near(def_t_pole, 1.0, 0.01), 21, &!results)

    // T22: top propagator far from pole — small deficit (< 0.01)
    let prop_t_far = nu_top_propagator(1.0, gamma_top)
    let def_t_far = nu_deficit(prop_t_far)
    nu_chk(def_t_far < 0.01, 22, &!results)

    // T23: top propagator at pole has positive GUM variance
    nu_chk(prop_t_pole.amp_sq.variance() > 0.0, 23, &!results)

    // T24: top propagator confidence = 950
    nu_chk(prop_t_pole.amp_sq.confidence() == 950, 24, &!results)

    // T25: tt̄ amplitude below threshold → amp_sq.val() == 0.0
    let tt_below = tt_pair_amplitude_nu(1.0, gamma_top)
    nu_chk(tt_below.amp_sq.val() == 0.0, 25, &!results)

    // T26: tt̄ amplitude above threshold (s = 250000 GeV²) → amp_sq.val() > 0.0
    let s_above = 250000.0
    let tt_above = tt_pair_amplitude_nu(s_above, gamma_top)
    nu_chk(tt_above.amp_sq.val() > 0.0, 26, &!results)

    // T27: tt̄ amplitude above threshold → positive GUM variance
    nu_chk(tt_above.amp_sq.variance() > 0.0, 27, &!results)

    // T28: tt̄ amplitude at pole (s = m_t²) approaches threshold, deficit ≈ 1.0
    // Actually at threshold s = (2m_t)² = 4m_t², test slightly above
    let s_near_thresh = 4.0 * mt * mt + 10.0
    let tt_thresh = tt_pair_amplitude_nu(s_near_thresh, gamma_top)
    nu_chk(tt_thresh.amp_sq.val() > 0.0, 28, &!results)

    let total = results[0] + results[1]
    print("NonUnitary: ")
    print_int(results[0])
    print("/")
    print_int(total)
    print(" PASS\n")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/particle_physics/parton_shower.sio ===
// ============================================================================
// PARTON SHOWER & HADRONIZATION
// ============================================================================
//
// LO DGLAP splitting kernels, Sudakov form factors, parton shower evolution
// via the veto algorithm, Lund string fragmentation, and cluster hadronization.
//
// References:
// - Ellis, Stirling, Webber, "QCD and Collider Physics" (1996)
// - Sjöstrand et al., "An Introduction to PYTHIA 8.2" (2015)
// - Andersson, "The Lund Model" (1998)

module particle_physics::parton_shower

use particle_physics::lorentz::{LorentzVector, lorentz_new, lorentz_add, lorentz_sub, lorentz_scale, lorentz_dot}
use particle_physics::sm_params::{mass_pion_charged, mass_pion_neutral, mass_kaon_charged, mass_proton}

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { sqrt(x) }
fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { exp(x) }
fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { log(x) }
fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

// QCD color factors
pub fn cf() -> f64 { 4.0 / 3.0 }
pub fn ca() -> f64 { 3.0 }
pub fn tf() -> f64 { 0.5 }

// ============================================================================
// DGLAP LO SPLITTING KERNELS (regular parts)
// ============================================================================

/// Quark → quark + gluon splitting kernel (regular part, no + prescription).
/// P_qq(x) = C_F * (1 + x^2) / (1 - x)
pub fn p_qq_regular(x: f64) -> f64 with Div {
    if x <= 0.0 || x >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    cf() * (1.0 + x * x) / (1.0 - x)
}

/// Gluon → quark + anti-quark splitting kernel.
/// P_qg(x) = T_F * (x^2 + (1-x)^2)
pub fn p_qg(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 || x >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    let tf = tf()
    tf * (x * x + (1.0 - x) * (1.0 - x))
}

/// Quark → gluon + quark splitting kernel (from gluon parent).
/// P_gq(x) = C_F * (1 + (1-x)^2) / x
pub fn p_gq(x: f64) -> f64 with Div {
    if x <= 0.0 || x >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    cf() * (1.0 + (1.0 - x) * (1.0 - x)) / x
}

/// Gluon → gluon + gluon splitting kernel (regular part).
/// P_gg(x) = 2 C_A * (x/(1-x) + (1-x)/x + x(1-x))
pub fn p_gg_regular(x: f64) -> f64 with Div {
    if x <= 0.0 || x >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ca_val = ca()
    2.0 * ca_val * (x / (1.0 - x) + (1.0 - x) / x + x * (1.0 - x))
}

/// Sum of splitting kernels weighted by flavor multiplicities.
/// For a quark: P_q = P_qq + P_qg
/// For a gluon: P_g = P_gq * n_f + P_gg
pub fn p_sum_quark(x: f64) -> f64 with Div {
    p_qq_regular(x) + p_qg(x)
}

pub fn p_sum_gluon(x: f64, n_f: i64) -> f64 with Div {
    p_gg_regular(x) + (n_f as f64) * p_gq(x)
}

// ============================================================================
// SUDAKOV FORM FACTOR
// ============================================================================

/// Sudakov form factor for no-emission probability.
///
/// Δ(t) = exp( -∫_{t0}^{t} dt' ∫ dz (α_s / (2π)) P(z) )
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `alpha_s`: Strong coupling at the shower scale.
/// - `t`: Shower evolution variable (e.g., pT² or angular variable).
/// - `t0`: Cutoff scale.
/// - `is_gluon`: Whether the splitting parton is a gluon.
/// - `n_f`: Number of active flavors.
///
/// # Returns
/// No-emission probability Δ(t).
pub fn sudakov_form_factor(alpha_s: f64, t: f64, t0: f64, is_gluon: bool, n_f: i64) -> f64 with Div {
    if t <= t0 || alpha_s <= 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    // Approximate: Δ ≈ exp( - (α_s / (2π)) * C * log(t/t0) )
    // where C = C_F for quarks, C_A for gluons
    let c = if is_gluon { ca() } else { cf() }
    let log_ratio = ln_f64(t / t0)
    let exponent = 0.0 - (alpha_s / (2.0 * 3.141592653589793)) * c * log_ratio
    exp_f64(exponent)
}

/// Overestimate of the splitting kernel for the veto algorithm.
/// Uses the soft/collinear limit: P(z) < C / (z(1-z))
pub fn splitting_overestimate(z: f64, is_gluon: bool) -> f64 with Div {
    if z <= 1e-8 || z >= 1.0 - 1e-8 { return 1e12 }
    let c = if is_gluon { ca() } else { cf() }
    c / (z * (1.0 - z))
}

// ============================================================================
// PARTON SHOWER EVOLUTION (Veto Algorithm)
// ============================================================================

/// Parton shower emission record.
pub struct ShowerEmission {
    pub z: f64,
    pub t: f64,
    pub is_gluon_emission: bool,
}

/// Generate a single shower emission using the veto algorithm.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `t_max`: Maximum evolution scale.
/// - `t_cut`: Infrared cutoff.
/// - `alpha_s`: Strong coupling.
/// - `is_gluon`: Whether the emitter is a gluon.
/// - `rng_seed`: Seed for RNG.
///
/// # Returns
/// Emission record. z = 0 and t = 0 if no emission occurred.
pub fn generate_emission(t_max: f64, t_cut: f64, alpha_s: f64, is_gluon: bool, rng_seed: i64) -> ShowerEmission with Mut, Div {
    seed_shower_rng(rng_seed)
    generate_emission_internal(t_max, t_cut, alpha_s, is_gluon)
}

fn generate_emission_internal(t_max: f64, t_cut: f64, alpha_s: f64, is_gluon: bool) -> ShowerEmission with Mut, Div {
    if t_max <= t_cut || alpha_s <= 0.0 {
        return ShowerEmission { z: 0.0, t: 0.0, is_gluon_emission: false }
    }

    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let c = if is_gluon { ca() } else { cf() }
    let alpha_factor = alpha_s / (2.0 * pi)

    // Overestimate integral: ∫ dz C/(z(1-z)) ≈ 2C * ln((1-z_cut)/z_cut)
    let z_cut = 1e-6
    let p_over_int = 2.0 * c * ln_f64((1.0 - z_cut) / z_cut)

    // Generate t using the overestimate
    // P(no emission between t and t+dt) = exp(-alpha_factor * p_over_int * dt/t)
    // t = t_cut * (t_max/t_cut)^u
    let u = rand_shower_uniform()
    let t = t_cut * exp_f64(u * ln_f64(t_max / t_cut))

    if t >= t_max {
        return ShowerEmission { z: 0.0, t: 0.0, is_gluon_emission: false }
    }

    // Generate z using the overestimate distribution
    // z = z_cut * ((1-z_cut)/z_cut)^v
    let v = rand_shower_uniform()
    let z = z_cut * exp_f64(v * ln_f64((1.0 - z_cut) / z_cut))

    // Veto: accept with probability P_actual(z) / P_over(z)
    let p_actual = if is_gluon {
        p_sum_gluon(z, 5)
    } else {
        p_sum_quark(z)
    }
    let p_over = splitting_overestimate(z, is_gluon)

    let accept_prob = if p_over > 0.0 { p_actual / p_over } else { 0.0 }
    if rand_shower_uniform() < accept_prob && accept_prob <= 1.0 {
        ShowerEmission { z: z, t: t, is_gluon_emission: is_gluon }
    } else {
        // Vetoed — try again from t
        generate_emission_internal(t, t_cut, alpha_s, is_gluon)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// LUND STRING FRAGMENTATION
// ============================================================================

/// Lund fragmentation parameters.
pub struct LundParams {
    pub a: f64,   // fragmentation function parameter
    pub b: f64,   // fragmentation function parameter (GeV^-2)
    pub kappa: f64, // string tension (GeV^2)
}

pub fn lund_params_default() -> LundParams {
    LundParams { a: 0.68, b: 0.98, kappa: 0.18 }
}

/// Fragmentation function f(z) for Lund string model.
/// f(z) ∝ z^{-1} (1-z)^a exp(-b m_perp^2 / z)
pub fn lund_fragmentation_function(z: f64, m_perp: f64, params: LundParams) -> f64 with Div {
    if z <= 0.0 || z >= 1.0 || m_perp <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let a = params.a
    let b = params.b
    let m2 = m_perp * m_perp
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    // Normalized approximately by the peak
    let peak_z = sqrt_f64(b * m2)
    if peak_z > 0.9 { return 0.0 }
    let norm = peak_z * exp_f64(0.0 - a * ln_f64(1.0 - peak_z) + b * m2 / peak_z)
    if norm <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    (1.0 / z) * exp_f64(a * ln_f64(1.0 - z) - b * m2 / z) / norm
}

/// Generate a hadron from a string segment using the Lund model.
/// Simplified: samples z from the Lund fragmentation function.
pub fn lund_generate_fragment(z: f64, m_hadron: f64, px: f64, py: f64) -> LorentzVector with Div {
    let pz = 0.0 // Simplified: longitudinal momentum from string
    let e = sqrt_f64(m_hadron * m_hadron + px * px + py * py + pz * pz)
    lorentz_new(e, px, py, pz)
}

// ============================================================================
// CLUSTER HADRONIZATION
// ============================================================================

/// Cluster hadronization: decay a colorless cluster into two hadrons.
///
/// # Parameters
/// - `m_cluster`: Cluster mass (GeV).
/// - `m1`, `m2`: Hadron masses (GeV).
/// - `px`, `py`, `pz`: Cluster momentum (GeV).
/// - `h1_out`, `h2_out`: Output 4-momenta.
pub fn cluster_decay_two_body(m_cluster: f64, m1: f64, m2: f64, px: f64, py: f64, pz: f64, h1_out: &!LorentzVector, h2_out: &!LorentzVector) with Mut, Div {
    if m_cluster <= m1 + m2 {
        h1_out.t = m1; h1_out.x = 0.0; h1_out.y = 0.0; h1_out.z = 0.0
        h2_out.t = m2; h2_out.x = 0.0; h2_out.y = 0.0; h2_out.z = 0.0
        return
    }
    let e_total = sqrt_f64(m_cluster * m_cluster + px * px + py * py + pz * pz)
    let p_cm = sqrt_f64((m_cluster * m_cluster - (m1 + m2) * (m1 + m2)) * (m_cluster * m_cluster - (m1 - m2) * (m1 - m2))) / (2.0 * m_cluster)

    // Isotropic decay in cluster rest frame
    let costheta = 2.0 * rand_shower_uniform() - 1.0
    let sintheta = sqrt_f64(1.0 - costheta * costheta)
    let phi = 2.0 * 3.141592653589793 * rand_shower_uniform()

    let px1_rf = p_cm * sintheta * cos_f64(phi)
    let py1_rf = p_cm * sintheta * sin_f64(phi)
    let pz1_rf = p_cm * costheta
    let e1_rf = sqrt_f64(p_cm * p_cm + m1 * m1)

    let px2_rf = 0.0 - px1_rf
    let py2_rf = 0.0 - py1_rf
    let pz2_rf = 0.0 - pz1_rf
    let e2_rf = sqrt_f64(p_cm * p_cm + m2 * m2)

    // Boost back to lab frame (simplified: assume cluster is at rest if px=py=pz=0)
    if px == 0.0 && py == 0.0 && pz == 0.0 {
        h1_out.t = e1_rf; h1_out.x = px1_rf; h1_out.y = py1_rf; h1_out.z = pz1_rf
        h2_out.t = e2_rf; h2_out.x = px2_rf; h2_out.y = py2_rf; h2_out.z = pz2_rf
        return
    }

    // General boost
    let beta_x = px / e_total
    let beta_y = py / e_total
    let beta_z = pz / e_total
    let beta2 = beta_x * beta_x + beta_y * beta_y + beta_z * beta_z
    let gamma = 1.0 / sqrt_f64(1.0 - beta2)

    let beta_dot_p1 = beta_x * px1_rf + beta_y * py1_rf + beta_z * pz1_rf
    let factor1 = gamma * (gamma * beta_dot_p1 / (1.0 + gamma) - e1_rf)
    let h1 = lorentz_new(
        gamma * (e1_rf - beta_dot_p1),
        px1_rf + factor1 * beta_x,
        py1_rf + factor1 * beta_y,
        pz1_rf + factor1 * beta_z,
    )

    let beta_dot_p2 = beta_x * px2_rf + beta_y * py2_rf + beta_z * pz2_rf
    let factor2 = gamma * (gamma * beta_dot_p2 / (1.0 + gamma) - e2_rf)
    h2_out.t = gamma * (e2_rf - beta_dot_p2)
    h2_out.x = px2_rf + factor2 * beta_x
    h2_out.y = py2_rf + factor2 * beta_y
    h2_out.z = pz2_rf + factor2 * beta_z
}

/// Simple hadron record.
pub struct Hadron {
    pub pdg_code: i64,
    pub mass: f64,
    pub width: f64,
    pub charge: i64,
    pub spin: i64,
}

pub fn hadron_pion_plus() -> Hadron {
    Hadron { pdg_code: 211, mass: 0.13957, width: 0.0, charge: 1, spin: 0 }
}
pub fn hadron_pion_minus() -> Hadron {
    Hadron { pdg_code: -211, mass: 0.13957, width: 0.0, charge: -1, spin: 0 }
}
pub fn hadron_pion_0() -> Hadron {
    Hadron { pdg_code: 111, mass: 0.13498, width: 0.0, charge: 0, spin: 0 }
}
pub fn hadron_kaon_plus() -> Hadron {
    Hadron { pdg_code: 321, mass: 0.49368, width: 0.0, charge: 1, spin: 0 }
}

    Hadron { pdg_code: 2212, mass: 0.93827, width: 0.0, charge: 1, spin: 1 }
