// === FILE: stdlib/profile/profiler.sio ===
// stdlib/profile/profiler.sio — Synchronous Wall-Clock Profiler
//
// Provides named timing slots using POSIX clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC).
// Up to 64 named slots. Linear search for slot lookup (no hash map).
//
// Usage:
//   var p = profiler_new()
//   profiler_begin(&!p, "phase1")
//   // ... work ...
//   profiler_end(&!p, "phase1")
//   profiler_report(p)
//
// References:
//   POSIX.1-2008: clock_gettime(3)
//   CLOCK_MONOTONIC (clockid=1) — monotonic wall clock, unaffected by NTP

// ============================================================================
// FFI Declarations
// ============================================================================

extern "C" {
    fn clock_gettime(clockid: i32, tp: *mut i64) -> i32;
}

// ============================================================================
// Types
// ============================================================================

struct ProfileSlot {
    name: string,
    total_ns: i64,
    call_count: i64,
    active: bool,
    start_ns: i64
}

struct Profiler {
    slots: [ProfileSlot; 64],
    slot_count: i64
}

// ============================================================================
// Internal helpers (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

// Read current monotonic time in nanoseconds via clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC).
// The timespec struct is represented as [seconds, nanoseconds] in a 2-element i64 array.
fn profiler_now_ns() -> i64 {
    var ts: [i64; 2] = [0; 2]
    clock_gettime(1, &!ts as *mut i64)
    ts[0] * 1000000000 + ts[1]
}

// Find a slot index by name. Returns -1 if not found.
fn profiler_find_slot(p: &Profiler, name: string) -> i64 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < p.slot_count {
        if p.slots[i as usize].name == name {
            return i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    -1
}

// ============================================================================
// Public API
// ============================================================================

/// Create a new empty Profiler with all slots zeroed.
pub fn profiler_new() -> Profiler {
    Profiler {
        slots: [ProfileSlot { name: "", total_ns: 0, call_count: 0, active: false, start_ns: 0 }; 64],
        slot_count: 0
    }
}

/// Begin timing a named slot. Creates the slot if it does not exist.
/// Records the current monotonic timestamp as start_ns.
pub fn profiler_begin(p: &!Profiler, name: string) with Mut, IO, Panic {
    let idx = profiler_find_slot(p as &Profiler, name)
    if idx >= 0 {
        p.slots[idx as usize].start_ns = profiler_now_ns()
        p.slots[idx as usize].active = true
        return
    }
    // Allocate a new slot
    if p.slot_count >= 64 {
        println("profiler_begin: slot limit (64) reached, ignoring: ", name)
        return
    }
    let new_idx = p.slot_count
    p.slots[new_idx as usize].name = name
    p.slots[new_idx as usize].total_ns = 0
    p.slots[new_idx as usize].call_count = 0
    p.slots[new_idx as usize].start_ns = profiler_now_ns()
    p.slots[new_idx as usize].active = true
    p.slot_count = p.slot_count + 1
}

/// End timing a named slot. Adds elapsed nanoseconds to total_ns, increments call_count.
pub fn profiler_end(p: &!Profiler, name: string) with Mut, IO, Panic {
    let now = profiler_now_ns()
    let idx = profiler_find_slot(p as &Profiler, name)
    if idx < 0 {
        println("profiler_end: slot not found: ", name)
        return
    }
    let elapsed = now - p.slots[idx as usize].start_ns
    p.slots[idx as usize].total_ns = p.slots[idx as usize].total_ns + elapsed
    p.slots[idx as usize].call_count = p.slots[idx as usize].call_count + 1
    p.slots[idx as usize].active = false
}

/// Reset all timing data (zero totals and counts, keep slot names).
pub fn profiler_reset(p: &!Profiler) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < p.slot_count {
        p.slots[i as usize].total_ns = 0
        p.slots[i as usize].call_count = 0
        p.slots[i as usize].active = false
        p.slots[i as usize].start_ns = 0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

/// Print a report of all slots: name, total_ms, call_count, avg_us.
pub fn profiler_report(p: Profiler) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    println("=== Profiler Report ===")
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < p.slot_count {
        let slot = p.slots[i as usize]
        let total_ms = (slot.total_ns as f64) / 1000000.0
        let avg_us: f64 = if slot.call_count > 0 {
            (slot.total_ns as f64) / (slot.call_count as f64) / 1000.0
        } else {
            0.0
        }
        println("  ", slot.name, ": total=", total_ms, "ms  calls=", slot.call_count, "  avg=", avg_us, "us")
        i = i + 1
    }
    println("=======================")
}

/// Get total time in milliseconds for the named slot. Returns 0.0 if not found.
pub fn profiler_slot_total_ms(p: Profiler, name: string) -> f64 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < p.slot_count {
        if p.slots[i as usize].name == name {
            return (p.slots[i as usize].total_ns as f64) / 1000000.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0.0
}

/// Get call count for the named slot. Returns 0 if not found.
pub fn profiler_slot_calls(p: Profiler, name: string) -> i64 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < p.slot_count {
        if p.slots[i as usize].name == name {
            return p.slots[i as usize].call_count
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0
}

/// Get average time per call in microseconds for the named slot. Returns 0.0 if not found or no calls.
pub fn profiler_slot_avg_us(p: Profiler, name: string) -> f64 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < p.slot_count {
        if p.slots[i as usize].name == name {
            let calls = p.slots[i as usize].call_count
            if calls == 0 { return 0.0 }
            return (p.slots[i as usize].total_ns as f64) / (calls as f64) / 1000.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0.0
}

/// Get the number of registered slots.
pub fn profiler_slot_count(p: Profiler) -> i64 {
    p.slot_count
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/activation.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/activation.sio — Quaternion activation functions
//
// Component-wise activation functions for quaternion-valued neurons.
// References:
//   - Parcollet et al. (2019) "Quaternion Recurrent Neural Networks"
//   - Zhu et al. (2018) "Quaternion Convolutional Neural Networks"

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn qnn_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// Taylor series exp: sum_{k=0}^{15} x^k / k!
// Range-reduced for numerical stability.
fn qnn_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 20.0 { return qnn_exp(x / 2.0) * qnn_exp(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / qnn_exp(0.0 - x) }

    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * x / 1.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 2.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 3.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 4.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 5.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 6.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 7.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 8.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 9.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 10.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 11.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 12.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 13.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 14.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 15.0
    sum = sum + term
    sum
}

fn qnn_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

// ============================================================================
// QUATERNION TYPE
// ============================================================================

struct Quaternion {
    w: f64,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64
}

fn quaternion_new(w: f64, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Quaternion {
    Quaternion { w: w, x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

fn quaternion_zero() -> Quaternion {
    Quaternion { w: 0.0, x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0 }
}

fn quaternion_norm(q: Quaternion) -> f64 {
    qnn_sqrt(q.w * q.w + q.x * q.x + q.y * q.y + q.z * q.z)
}

// ============================================================================
// ACTIVATION FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Component-wise ReLU: max(0, component)
fn quat_relu(q: Quaternion) -> Quaternion {
    var rw = 0.0
    var rx = 0.0
    var ry = 0.0
    var rz = 0.0
    if q.w > 0.0 { rw = q.w }
    if q.x > 0.0 { rx = q.x }
    if q.y > 0.0 { ry = q.y }
    if q.z > 0.0 { rz = q.z }
    Quaternion { w: rw, x: rx, y: ry, z: rz }
}

// Component-wise sigmoid: 1 / (1 + exp(-x))
fn qnn_sigmoid_scalar(x: f64) -> f64 {
    1.0 / (1.0 + qnn_exp(0.0 - x))
}

fn quat_sigmoid(q: Quaternion) -> Quaternion {
    Quaternion {
        w: qnn_sigmoid_scalar(q.w),
        x: qnn_sigmoid_scalar(q.x),
        y: qnn_sigmoid_scalar(q.y),
        z: qnn_sigmoid_scalar(q.z)
    }
}

// Component-wise tanh: (exp(2x) - 1) / (exp(2x) + 1)
fn qnn_tanh_scalar(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let e2x = qnn_exp(2.0 * x)
    (e2x - 1.0) / (e2x + 1.0)
}

fn quat_tanh(q: Quaternion) -> Quaternion {
    Quaternion {
        w: qnn_tanh_scalar(q.w),
        x: qnn_tanh_scalar(q.x),
        y: qnn_tanh_scalar(q.y),
        z: qnn_tanh_scalar(q.z)
    }
}

// Leaky ReLU with alpha parameter
fn qnn_leaky_relu_scalar(x: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 { x } else { alpha * x }
}

fn quat_leaky_relu(q: Quaternion, alpha: f64) -> Quaternion {
    Quaternion {
        w: qnn_leaky_relu_scalar(q.w, alpha),
        x: qnn_leaky_relu_scalar(q.x, alpha),
        y: qnn_leaky_relu_scalar(q.y, alpha),
        z: qnn_leaky_relu_scalar(q.z, alpha)
    }
}

// Split activation: tanh on real, sigmoid on imaginary
fn quat_split_activation(q: Quaternion) -> Quaternion {
    Quaternion {
        w: qnn_tanh_scalar(q.w),
        x: qnn_sigmoid_scalar(q.x),
        y: qnn_sigmoid_scalar(q.y),
        z: qnn_sigmoid_scalar(q.z)
    }
}

// Quaternion normalization
fn quat_normalize(q: Quaternion) -> Quaternion {
    let n = quaternion_norm(q)
    if n < 1.0e-15 { return quaternion_zero() }
    Quaternion {
        w: q.w / n,
        x: q.x / n,
        y: q.y / n,
        z: q.z / n
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_quat_relu() -> bool {
    let q = quaternion_new(1.0, 0.0 - 2.0, 3.0, 0.0 - 0.5)
    let r = quat_relu(q)
    qnn_abs(r.w - 1.0) < 0.001
}

fn test_quat_relu_clamp() -> bool {
    let q = quaternion_new(0.0 - 5.0, 2.0, 0.0 - 3.0, 0.0)
    let r = quat_relu(q)
    qnn_abs(r.w) < 0.001
}

fn test_sigmoid_half() -> bool {
    let q = quaternion_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    let s = quat_sigmoid(q)
    qnn_abs(s.w - 0.5) < 0.01
}

fn test_tanh_zero() -> bool {
    let q = quaternion_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    let t = quat_tanh(q)
    qnn_abs(t.w) < 0.01
}

fn test_exp_zero() -> bool {
    qnn_abs(qnn_exp(0.0) - 1.0) < 0.01
}

fn test_exp_one() -> bool {
    qnn_abs(qnn_exp(1.0) - 2.718) < 0.1
}

fn test_norm_unit() -> bool {
    let q = quaternion_new(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    qnn_abs(quaternion_norm(q) - 1.0) < 0.001
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/attention.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/attention.sio — Quaternion scaled dot-product attention
//
// Scaled dot-product attention with quaternion-valued Q/K/V matrices.
// attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d)) V
// Reference: Tay et al. (2019) "Quaternion Knowledge Graph Embeddings"

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn qatt_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn qatt_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

fn qatt_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var v = x
    if v > 20.0 { v = 20.0 }
    if v < 0.0 - 20.0 { v = 0.0 - 20.0 }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var k: i32 = 1
    while k <= 15 {
        term = term * v / k
        sum = sum + term
        k = k + 1
    }
    sum
}

// ============================================================================
// ATTENTION
// ============================================================================

// Scaled dot-product attention over flat arrays.
// q, k, v: [seq_len * dim] flattened matrices
// out: [seq_len * dim] attention output
fn qnn_attention(q: &[f64; 256], k: &[f64; 256], v: &[f64; 256], seq_len: i32, dim: i32, out: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if seq_len < 1 { return }
    if dim < 1 { return }
    if seq_len * dim > 256 { return }
    if seq_len * seq_len > 256 { return }

    // Convert dim to f64 for sqrt
    var dim_f = 0.0
    var di: i32 = 0
    while di < dim {
        dim_f = dim_f + 1.0
        di = di + 1
    }
    let scale = qatt_sqrt(dim_f)
    if scale < 0.0001 { return }

    // Compute attention scores: scores[i][j] = dot(q[i], k[j]) / sqrt(dim)
    var scores = [0.0; 256]

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < seq_len {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < seq_len {
            var dot = 0.0
            var d: i32 = 0
            while d < dim {
                let qi = i * dim + d
                let ki = j * dim + d
                if qi < 256 {
                    if ki < 256 {
                        dot = dot + q[qi] * k[ki]
                    }
                }
                d = d + 1
            }
            let sidx = i * seq_len + j
            if sidx < 256 {
                scores[sidx] = dot / scale
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Softmax per row
    var ri: i32 = 0
    while ri < seq_len {
        // Find max for numerical stability
        var max_val = 0.0 - 1.0e10
        var cj: i32 = 0
        while cj < seq_len {
            let idx = ri * seq_len + cj
            if idx < 256 {
                if scores[idx] > max_val {
                    max_val = scores[idx]
                }
            }
            cj = cj + 1
        }

        // Exp and sum
        var exp_sum = 0.0
        cj = 0
        while cj < seq_len {
            let idx = ri * seq_len + cj
            if idx < 256 {
                let ev = qatt_exp(scores[idx] - max_val)
                scores[idx] = ev
                exp_sum = exp_sum + ev
            }
            cj = cj + 1
        }

        // Normalize
        if exp_sum > 1.0e-15 {
            cj = 0
            while cj < seq_len {
                let idx = ri * seq_len + cj
                if idx < 256 {
                    scores[idx] = scores[idx] / exp_sum
                }
                cj = cj + 1
            }
        }
        ri = ri + 1
    }

    // Weighted sum: out[i] = sum_j(scores[i][j] * v[j])
    var oi: i32 = 0
    while oi < seq_len {
        var d: i32 = 0
        while d < dim {
            var sum = 0.0
            var j: i32 = 0
            while j < seq_len {
                let sidx = oi * seq_len + j
                let vidx = j * dim + d
                if sidx < 256 {
                    if vidx < 256 {
                        sum = sum + scores[sidx] * v[vidx]
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            let out_idx = oi * dim + d
            if out_idx < 256 {
                out[out_idx] = sum
            }
            d = d + 1
        }
        oi = oi + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_attention_single() -> bool {
    // seq_len=1, dim=2: trivial case, output = V
    var q = [0.0; 256]
    var k = [0.0; 256]
    var v = [0.0; 256]
    q[0] = 1.0
    q[1] = 0.0
    k[0] = 1.0
    k[1] = 0.0
    v[0] = 5.0
    v[1] = 3.0
    var out = [0.0; 256]
    qnn_attention(&q, &k, &v, 1, 2, &!out)
    qatt_abs(out[0] - 5.0) < 0.1
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/conv.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/conv.sio — Quaternion 1D convolution layer
//
// 1D convolution for quaternion-valued signals (valid padding, stride=1).
// Reference: Zhu et al., "Quaternion Convolutional Neural Networks" ECCV 2018

// ============================================================================
// TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct QConvLayer {
    kernel: [f64; 256],
    kernel_size: i32,
    in_channels: i32,
    out_channels: i32
}

fn qconv_new(kernel_size: i32, in_channels: i32, out_channels: i32) -> QConvLayer {
    QConvLayer {
        kernel: [0.0; 256],
        kernel_size: kernel_size,
        in_channels: in_channels,
        out_channels: out_channels
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FORWARD PASS
// ============================================================================

// 1D convolution with valid padding.
// output[oc * out_len + t] = sum over ic, k of kernel[...] * input[ic * in_len + t + k]
fn qconv_forward_1d(layer: &QConvLayer, input: &[f64; 256], in_len: i32, out: &![f64; 256], out_len: &!i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ks = layer.kernel_size
    let ic = layer.in_channels
    let oc = layer.out_channels

    if ks < 1 { *out_len = 0; return }
    if in_len < ks { *out_len = 0; return }

    let o_len = in_len - ks + 1
    if o_len * oc > 256 { *out_len = 0; return }

    // Zero output
    var idx: i32 = 0
    while idx < 256 {
        out[idx] = 0.0
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    // Convolution
    var o: i32 = 0
    while o < oc {
        var t: i32 = 0
        while t < o_len {
            var acc = 0.0
            var c: i32 = 0
            while c < ic {
                var k: i32 = 0
                while k < ks {
                    let ki = o * ic * ks + c * ks + k
                    let ii = c * in_len + t + k
                    if ki < 256 {
                        if ii < 256 {
                            acc = acc + layer.kernel[ki] * input[ii]
                        }
                    }
                    k = k + 1
                }
                c = c + 1
            }
            let oi = o * o_len + t
            if oi < 256 {
                out[oi] = acc
            }
            t = t + 1
        }
        o = o + 1
    }
    *out_len = o_len * oc
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn qnn_conv_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn test_qconv_new() -> bool {
    let c = qconv_new(3, 1, 1)
    c.kernel_size == 3
}

fn test_qconv_channels() -> bool {
    let c = qconv_new(5, 2, 4)
    c.in_channels == 2
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/linear.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/linear.sio — Quaternion linear (fully-connected) layer
//
// Dense matrix-vector multiplication for QNN forward pass.
// Weights stored as flat f64 array, quaternion structure applied at usage.
//
// Reference: Parcollet et al., "Quaternion Neural Networks" ICLR 2019

// ============================================================================
// TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct QLinearLayer {
    weights: [f64; 1024],
    bias: [f64; 64],
    in_size: i32,
    out_size: i32
}

fn qlinear_new(in_size: i32, out_size: i32) -> QLinearLayer {
    QLinearLayer {
        weights: [0.0; 1024],
        bias: [0.0; 64],
        in_size: in_size,
        out_size: out_size
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FORWARD PASS
// ============================================================================

// Dense forward: out[j] = sum_i(weights[j * in_size + i] * input[i]) + bias[j]
fn qlinear_forward(layer: &QLinearLayer, input: &[f64; 256], out: &![f64; 256], out_len: &!i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let in_sz = layer.in_size
    let out_sz = layer.out_size

    if in_sz > 256 { *out_len = 0; return }
    if out_sz > 256 { *out_len = 0; return }
    if in_sz * out_sz > 1024 { *out_len = 0; return }

    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < out_sz {
        var acc = 0.0
        var i: i32 = 0
        while i < in_sz {
            let idx = j * in_sz + i
            if idx < 1024 {
                acc = acc + layer.weights[idx] * input[i]
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        if j < 64 {
            out[j] = acc + layer.bias[j]
        } else {
            out[j] = acc
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    *out_len = out_sz
}

// Forward with fused ReLU activation
fn qlinear_forward_relu(layer: &QLinearLayer, input: &[f64; 256], out: &![f64; 256], out_len: &!i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    qlinear_forward(layer, input, out, out_len)
    let n = *out_len
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < n {
        if out[j] < 0.0 {
            out[j] = 0.0
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// Initialize weights with simple deterministic pattern
fn qlinear_init_weights(layer: &!QLinearLayer, scale: f64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var idx: i32 = 0
    while idx < 1024 {
        let raw = ((idx * 7 + 13) % 100) - 50
        layer.weights[idx] = scale * raw / 50.0
        idx = idx + 1
    }
    var b: i32 = 0
    while b < 64 {
        layer.bias[b] = 0.0
        b = b + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_qlinear_new() -> bool {
    let layer = qlinear_new(4, 2)
    layer.in_size == 4
}

fn test_qlinear_out_size() -> bool {
    let layer = qlinear_new(4, 8)
    layer.out_size == 8
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/loss.sio ===
//! stdlib/qnn/loss.sio - Loss Functions for Quaternion Neural Networks
//!
//! Loss functions adapted for quaternion-valued outputs.
//! Losses can be computed component-wise or use quaternion-specific metrics.
//!
//! Usage Guidelines:
//!   - quat_mse_loss: Regression tasks with arbitrary quaternion targets
//!   - quat_mae_loss: Robust regression with quaternion distance
//!   - quat_cosine_similarity_loss: Orientation/rotation prediction tasks

// Mean Squared Error for quaternions
// Computes sum of squared quaternion distances: Σ||pred[i] - target[i]||²
fn quat_mse_loss(pred: &[Quat], target: &[Quat]) -> f32 {
    let n = pred.len() as i32
    var total_loss: f32 = 0.0

    let i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = quat_sub(pred[i], target[i])
        let norm_sq = diff.w * diff.w + diff.x * diff.x + diff.y * diff.y + diff.z * diff.z
        total_loss = total_loss + norm_sq
        i = i + 1
    }

    total_loss / (n as f32)
}

// Mean Absolute Error using quaternion norms
// Computes sum of quaternion distances: Σ||pred[i] - target[i]||
fn quat_mae_loss(pred: &[Quat], target: &[Quat]) -> f32 {
    let n = pred.len() as i32
    var total_loss: f32 = 0.0

    let i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = quat_sub(pred[i], target[i])
        let norm_sq = diff.w * diff.w + diff.x * diff.x + diff.y * diff.y + diff.z * diff.z
        let norm = norm_sq.sqrt()
        total_loss = total_loss + norm
        i = i + 1
    }

    total_loss / (n as f32)
}

// Cosine Similarity Loss for quaternions
// Uses normalized quaternion dot products to measure orientation similarity
// Formula: Σ(1 - (pred[i]·target[i]) / (||pred[i]|| ||target[i]||))
// Ideal for rotation prediction tasks (invariant to scaling and sign)
fn quat_cosine_similarity_loss(pred: &[Quat], target: &[Quat]) -> f32 {
    let n = pred.len() as i32
    var total_loss: f32 = 0.0

    let i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        // Compute norms
        let pred_norm_sq = pred[i].w * pred[i].w + pred[i].x * pred[i].x +
                          pred[i].y * pred[i].y + pred[i].z * pred[i].z
        let target_norm_sq = target[i].w * target[i].w + target[i].x * target[i].x +
                            target[i].y * target[i].y + target[i].z * target[i].z

        let pred_norm = pred_norm_sq.sqrt()
        let target_norm = target_norm_sq.sqrt()

        // Compute dot product
        let dot = pred[i].w * target[i].w + pred[i].x * target[i].x +
                 pred[i].y * target[i].y + pred[i].z * target[i].z

        // Cosine similarity with numerical stability
        let epsilon: f32 = 1e-8
        let cos_sim = dot / ((pred_norm + epsilon) * (target_norm + epsilon))

        // Clamp to [-1, 1] for numerical stability
        let cos_sim_clamped = if cos_sim > 1.0 { 1.0 } else if cos_sim < -1.0 { -1.0 } else { cos_sim }

        total_loss = total_loss + (1.0 - cos_sim_clamped)
        i = i + 1
    }

    total_loss / (n as f32)
}

// Helper: Quaternion subtraction
fn quat_sub(a: Quat, b: Quat) -> Quat {
    quat(a.w - b.w, a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y, a.z - b.z)
}

// Helper: Quaternion addition
fn quat_add(a: Quat, b: Quat) -> Quat {
    quat(a.w + b.w, a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y, a.z + b.z)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/loss_advanced.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/loss_advanced.sio — Advanced loss functions for QNN
//
// Cross-entropy and KL divergence for quaternion neural network training.

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn qloss_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn qloss_log(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 100.0 }
    if x < 0.001 { return 0.0 - 100.0 }

    var val = x
    var exp_count = 0.0
    while val > 2.0 {
        val = val / 2.0
        exp_count = exp_count + 1.0
    }
    while val < 0.5 {
        val = val * 2.0
        exp_count = exp_count - 1.0
    }

    let u = val - 1.0
    var result = 0.0
    var term = u
    result = result + term
    term = term * u
    result = result - term / 2.0
    term = term * u
    result = result + term / 3.0
    term = term * u
    result = result - term / 4.0
    term = term * u
    result = result + term / 5.0
    term = term * u
    result = result - term / 6.0
    term = term * u
    result = result + term / 7.0
    term = term * u
    result = result - term / 8.0

    result + exp_count * 0.6931471806
}

fn qloss_i32_to_f64(n: i32) -> f64 {
    var result = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    if n > 0 {
        while i < n {
            result = result + 1.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// LOSS FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Cross-entropy loss: -sum(target[i] * log(pred[i])) / n
fn qnn_cross_entropy(pred: &[f64; 64], target: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 1 { return 0.0 }
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            let p = pred[i]
            let t = target[i]
            var p_safe = p
            if p_safe < 1.0e-10 { p_safe = 1.0e-10 }
            if p_safe > 1.0 - 1.0e-10 { p_safe = 1.0 - 1.0e-10 }
            sum = sum - t * qloss_log(p_safe)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let nf = qloss_i32_to_f64(n)
    if nf < 1.0 { return sum }
    sum / nf
}

// KL divergence: sum(p[i] * log(p[i] / q[i])) / n
fn qnn_kl_divergence(p: &[f64; 64], q: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 1 { return 0.0 }
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            let pi = p[i]
            let qi = q[i]
            if pi > 1.0e-10 {
                var q_safe = qi
                if q_safe < 1.0e-10 { q_safe = 1.0e-10 }
                sum = sum + pi * (qloss_log(pi) - qloss_log(q_safe))
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let nf = qloss_i32_to_f64(n)
    if nf < 1.0 { return sum }
    sum / nf
}

// Mean squared error: sum((pred[i] - target[i])^2) / n
fn qnn_mse(pred: &[f64; 64], target: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 1 { return 0.0 }
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            let diff = pred[i] - target[i]
            sum = sum + diff * diff
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let nf = qloss_i32_to_f64(n)
    if nf < 1.0 { return sum }
    sum / nf
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_mse_zero() -> bool {
    var a = [0.0; 64]
    a[0] = 1.0
    a[1] = 2.0
    let loss = qnn_mse(&a, &a, 2)
    qloss_abs(loss) < 0.001
}

fn test_mse_nonzero() -> bool {
    var pred = [0.0; 64]
    var target = [0.0; 64]
    pred[0] = 1.0
    target[0] = 2.0
    let loss = qnn_mse(&pred, &target, 1)
    qloss_abs(loss - 1.0) < 0.001
}

fn test_kl_same() -> bool {
    var p = [0.0; 64]
    p[0] = 0.5
    p[1] = 0.5
    let kl = qnn_kl_divergence(&p, &p, 2)
    qloss_abs(kl) < 0.01
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/mnist/data_loader.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/mnist/data_loader.sio — MNIST data loading and batch structure
//
// Provides MnistBatch struct and deterministic mock data for testing.

// ============================================================================
// TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct MnistBatch {
    images: [f64; 4096],   // flattened: batch_size * (some features)
    labels: [i32; 64],
    batch_size: i32
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

fn mnist_batch_new() -> MnistBatch {
    MnistBatch {
        images: [0.0; 4096],
        labels: [0; 64],
        batch_size: 0
    }
}

// Create a mock batch with deterministic pseudo-random data for testing.
// Each "image" is 64 features (not full 784 for memory reasons).
fn mnist_mock_batch(batch_size: i32, seed: i32) -> MnistBatch {
    var batch = mnist_batch_new()
    var bs = batch_size
    if bs > 64 { bs = 64 }
    batch.batch_size = bs

    var rng = seed
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < bs {
        // Generate 64 features per sample
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < 64 {
            rng = rng * 1103515245 + 12345
            var val = rng
            if val < 0 { val = 0 - val }
            let idx = i * 64 + j
            if idx < 4096 {
                // Normalize to [0, 1]
                // Convert val%256 to f64 manually
                let rem = val % 256
                var fval = 0.0
                var ri: i32 = 0
                while ri < rem {
                    fval = fval + 1.0
                    ri = ri + 1
                }
                batch.images[idx] = fval / 255.0
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        // Assign label (digit 0-9)
        rng = rng * 1103515245 + 12345
        var lbl = rng
        if lbl < 0 { lbl = 0 - lbl }
        batch.labels[i] = lbl % 10
        i = i + 1
    }
    batch
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_batch_new() -> bool {
    let b = mnist_batch_new()
    b.batch_size == 0
}

fn test_mock_batch() -> bool {
    let b = mnist_mock_batch(8, 42)
    b.batch_size == 8
}

fn test_mock_labels_range() -> bool {
    let b = mnist_mock_batch(16, 123)
    // All labels should be 0..9
    var ok = true
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 16 {
        if b.labels[i] < 0 { ok = false }
        if b.labels[i] > 9 { ok = false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    ok
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/mnist/inference.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/mnist/inference.sio — MNIST inference (prediction)
//
// Argmax-based prediction from model logits.

// ============================================================================
// TYPES (duplicated for standalone check)
// ============================================================================

struct QMnistModel {
    conv: [f64; 1024],
    fc: [f64; 4096],
    n_classes: i32
}

// ============================================================================
// INFERENCE
// ============================================================================

// Predict digit class for a single 784-pixel image (uses first 64 features).
// Returns class index with highest logit.
fn qmnist_predict(model: &QMnistModel, image: &[f64; 784]) -> i32 {
    let nc = model.n_classes
    if nc < 1 { return 0 }

    var best_class: i32 = 0
    var best_logit = 0.0 - 1.0e10

    var c: i32 = 0
    while c < nc {
        if c >= 10 { return best_class }
        var logit = 0.0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < 64 {
            let fc_idx = c * 64 + j
            if fc_idx < 4096 {
                if j < 784 {
                    logit = logit + model.fc[fc_idx] * image[j]
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if logit > best_logit {
            best_logit = logit
            best_class = c
        }
        c = c + 1
    }
    best_class
}

// Predict and return logits for all classes
fn qmnist_predict_logits(model: &QMnistModel, image: &[f64; 784], logits: &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let nc = model.n_classes
    if nc < 1 { return }

    var c: i32 = 0
    while c < nc {
        if c >= 64 { return }
        var logit = 0.0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < 64 {
            let fc_idx = c * 64 + j
            if fc_idx < 4096 {
                if j < 784 {
                    logit = logit + model.fc[fc_idx] * image[j]
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        logits[c] = logit
        c = c + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_predict_zero_model() -> bool {
    let model = QMnistModel { conv: [0.0; 1024], fc: [0.0; 4096], n_classes: 10 }
    var img = [0.0; 784]
    let pred = qmnist_predict(&model, &img)
    // All logits are 0, should return class 0
    pred == 0
}

fn test_predict_returns_valid() -> bool {
    let model = QMnistModel { conv: [0.0; 1024], fc: [0.0; 4096], n_classes: 10 }
    var img = [0.0; 784]
    img[0] = 1.0
    let pred = qmnist_predict(&model, &img)
    pred >= 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/mnist/metrics.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/mnist/metrics.sio — MNIST evaluation metrics
//
// Accuracy computation for digit classification.

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn qmet_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn qmet_i32_to_f64(n: i32) -> f64 {
    var r = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    if n > 0 {
        while i < n {
            r = r + 1.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// METRICS
// ============================================================================

// Compute accuracy: fraction of correct predictions.
fn qmnist_accuracy(predictions: &[i32; 64], labels: &[i32; 64], n: i32) -> f64 {
    if n < 1 { return 0.0 }
    var correct: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            if predictions[i] == labels[i] {
                correct = correct + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let cf = qmet_i32_to_f64(correct)
    let nf = qmet_i32_to_f64(n)
    if nf < 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    cf / nf
}

// Per-class accuracy: compute accuracy for a single target class.
fn qmnist_class_accuracy(predictions: &[i32; 64], labels: &[i32; 64], n: i32, target_class: i32) -> f64 {
    if n < 1 { return 0.0 }
    var correct: i32 = 0
    var total: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            if labels[i] == target_class {
                total = total + 1
                if predictions[i] == target_class {
                    correct = correct + 1
                }
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if total < 1 { return 0.0 }
    let cf = qmet_i32_to_f64(correct)
    let tf = qmet_i32_to_f64(total)
    cf / tf
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_accuracy_perfect() -> bool {
    var preds = [0; 64]
    var labels = [0; 64]
    preds[0] = 1
    preds[1] = 2
    preds[2] = 3
    labels[0] = 1
    labels[1] = 2
    labels[2] = 3
    let acc = qmnist_accuracy(&preds, &labels, 3)
    qmet_abs(acc - 1.0) < 0.001
}

fn test_accuracy_half() -> bool {
    var preds = [0; 64]
    var labels = [0; 64]
    preds[0] = 1
    preds[1] = 2
    labels[0] = 1
    labels[1] = 9
    let acc = qmnist_accuracy(&preds, &labels, 2)
    qmet_abs(acc - 0.5) < 0.001
}

fn test_accuracy_zero() -> bool {
    var preds = [0; 64]
    var labels = [1; 64]
    let acc = qmnist_accuracy(&preds, &labels, 4)
    qmet_abs(acc) < 0.001
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/mnist/model.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/mnist/model.sio — MNIST quaternion classifier model
//
// Two-layer feedforward: conv features -> fc -> 10 classes.

// ============================================================================
// TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct QMnistModel {
    conv: [f64; 1024],      // convolution weights
    fc: [f64; 4096],        // fully-connected weights
    n_classes: i32
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

fn qmnist_model_new(n_classes: i32) -> QMnistModel {
    QMnistModel {
        conv: [0.0; 1024],
        fc: [0.0; 4096],
        n_classes: n_classes
    }
}

fn qmnist_model_default() -> QMnistModel {
    qmnist_model_new(10)
}

// Initialize with deterministic pseudo-random weights
fn qmnist_model_init(n_classes: i32, seed: i32) -> QMnistModel {
    var model = qmnist_model_new(n_classes)
    var rng = seed

    // Init conv weights
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 1024 {
        rng = rng * 1103515245 + 12345
        var val = rng
        if val < 0 { val = 0 - val }
        let cv = ((val % 1000) - 500) as f64
        model.conv[i] = cv / 5000.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Init fc weights
    i = 0
    while i < 4096 {
        rng = rng * 1103515245 + 12345
        var val = rng
        if val < 0 { val = 0 - val }
        let fv = ((val % 1000) - 500) as f64
        model.fc[i] = fv / 5000.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    model
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_model_new() -> bool {
    let m = qmnist_model_default()
    m.n_classes == 10
}

fn test_model_init() -> bool {
    let m = qmnist_model_init(10, 42)
    m.n_classes == 10
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/mnist/training.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/mnist/training.sio — MNIST training loop
//
// Simple SGD training step on a QMnistModel with MnistBatch.

// ============================================================================
// TYPES (duplicated for standalone check)
// ============================================================================

struct MnistBatch {
    images: [f64; 4096],
    labels: [i32; 64],
    batch_size: i32
}

struct QMnistModel {
    conv: [f64; 1024],
    fc: [f64; 4096],
    n_classes: i32
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn qmt_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn qmt_i32_to_f64(n: i32) -> f64 {
    var r = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    if n > 0 {
        while i < n {
            r = r + 1.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    r
}

// ============================================================================
// TRAINING
// ============================================================================

// Single training step: compute forward pass (simple linear model on fc weights),
// MSE loss, and gradient descent update. Returns average loss.
fn qmnist_train_step(model: &QMnistModel, batch: &MnistBatch, lr: f64, grad_out: &![f64; 4096]) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let bs = batch.batch_size
    if bs < 1 { return 0.0 }
    let nc = model.n_classes
    if nc < 1 { return 0.0 }

    // Zero gradients
    var gi: i32 = 0
    while gi < 4096 {
        grad_out[gi] = 0.0
        gi = gi + 1
    }

    var total_loss = 0.0

    // For each sample in batch
    var s: i32 = 0
    while s < bs {
        // Forward: logits[c] = sum_j(fc[c*64+j] * image[s*64+j])
        // Compute logits for each class
        var max_logit = 0.0 - 1.0e10
        var pred_class: i32 = 0

        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < nc {
            if c >= 10 { c = nc }
            var logit = 0.0
            var j: i32 = 0
            while j < 64 {
                let fc_idx = c * 64 + j
                let img_idx = s * 64 + j
                if fc_idx < 4096 {
                    if img_idx < 4096 {
                        logit = logit + model.fc[fc_idx] * batch.images[img_idx]
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            if logit > max_logit {
                max_logit = logit
                pred_class = c
            }

            // MSE loss: (logit - target)^2 where target = 1 if c==label else 0
            var target = 0.0
            if c == batch.labels[s] {
                target = 1.0
            }
            let diff = logit - target
            total_loss = total_loss + diff * diff

            // Accumulate gradient: dL/dw = 2 * diff * x
            j = 0
            while j < 64 {
                let fc_idx = c * 64 + j
                let img_idx = s * 64 + j
                if fc_idx < 4096 {
                    if img_idx < 4096 {
                        grad_out[fc_idx] = grad_out[fc_idx] + 2.0 * diff * batch.images[img_idx]
                    }
                }
                j = j + 1
            }

            c = c + 1
        }
        s = s + 1
    }

    let bsf = qmt_i32_to_f64(bs)
    if bsf > 0.0 { total_loss / bsf } else { total_loss }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_train_step_zero() -> bool {
    let model = QMnistModel { conv: [0.0; 1024], fc: [0.0; 4096], n_classes: 10 }
    let batch = MnistBatch { images: [0.0; 4096], labels: [0; 64], batch_size: 0 }
    var grads = [0.0; 4096]
    let loss = qmnist_train_step(&model, &batch, 0.01, &!grads)
    qmt_abs(loss) < 0.001
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/optimizer.sio ===
//! stdlib/qnn/optimizer.sio - Optimizers for Quaternion Parameters
//!
//! Adam and SGD optimizers adapted for quaternion-valued parameters.
//! Each quaternion component (w,x,y,z) is updated independently.

// Adam optimizer for quaternion parameters
struct QuatAdamOptimizer {
    learning_rate: f32,
    beta1: f32,       // First moment decay (default 0.9)
    beta2: f32,       // Second moment decay (default 0.999)
    epsilon: f32,     // Numerical stability (default 1e-8)
    timestep: i32,    // Current timestep for bias correction
}

// SGD with momentum for quaternion parameters
struct QuatSGDOptimizer {
    learning_rate: f32,
    momentum: f32,
    weight_decay: f32,
}

// Create a new Adam optimizer for quaternions
fn quat_adam_new(learning_rate: f32) -> QuatAdamOptimizer {
    QuatAdamOptimizer {
        learning_rate,
        beta1: 0.9,
        beta2: 0.999,
        epsilon: 1e-8,
        timestep: 0,
    }
}

// Create a new SGD optimizer for quaternions
fn quat_sgd_new(learning_rate: f32, momentum: f32, weight_decay: f32) -> QuatSGDOptimizer {
    QuatSGDOptimizer {
        learning_rate,
        momentum,
        weight_decay,
    }
}

// Perform one Adam optimization step on quaternion parameters
// Updates each quaternion component independently
fn quat_adam_step(
    params: &![Quat],
    grads: &[Quat],
    optimizer: &!QuatAdamOptimizer,
    first_moment: &![Quat],
    second_moment: &![Quat]
) {
    optimizer.timestep = optimizer.timestep + 1
    let timestep_f32 = optimizer.timestep as f32

    // Bias correction factors
    let beta1_t = 1.0 - optimizer.beta1.powf(timestep_f32)
    let beta2_t = 1.0 - optimizer.beta2.powf(timestep_f32)

    let n = params.len() as i32
    let i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        // Update first moment (mean) for each component
        first_moment[i].w = optimizer.beta1 * first_moment[i].w + (1.0 - optimizer.beta1) * grads[i].w
        first_moment[i].x = optimizer.beta1 * first_moment[i].x + (1.0 - optimizer.beta1) * grads[i].x
        first_moment[i].y = optimizer.beta1 * first_moment[i].y + (1.0 - optimizer.beta1) * grads[i].y
        first_moment[i].z = optimizer.beta1 * first_moment[i].z + (1.0 - optimizer.beta1) * grads[i].z

        // Update second moment (variance) for each component
        second_moment[i].w = optimizer.beta2 * second_moment[i].w + (1.0 - optimizer.beta2) * grads[i].w * grads[i].w
        second_moment[i].x = optimizer.beta2 * second_moment[i].x + (1.0 - optimizer.beta2) * grads[i].x * grads[i].x
        second_moment[i].y = optimizer.beta2 * second_moment[i].y + (1.0 - optimizer.beta2) * grads[i].y * grads[i].y
        second_moment[i].z = optimizer.beta2 * second_moment[i].z + (1.0 - optimizer.beta2) * grads[i].z * grads[i].z

        // Bias-corrected moments and parameter update
        let m_hat_w = first_moment[i].w / beta1_t
        let v_hat_w = second_moment[i].w / beta2_t
        params[i].w = params[i].w - optimizer.learning_rate * m_hat_w / (v_hat_w.sqrt() + optimizer.epsilon)

        let m_hat_x = first_moment[i].x / beta1_t
        let v_hat_x = second_moment[i].x / beta2_t
        params[i].x = params[i].x - optimizer.learning_rate * m_hat_x / (v_hat_x.sqrt() + optimizer.epsilon)

        let m_hat_y = first_moment[i].y / beta1_t
        let v_hat_y = second_moment[i].y / beta2_t
        params[i].y = params[i].y - optimizer.learning_rate * m_hat_y / (v_hat_y.sqrt() + optimizer.epsilon)

        let m_hat_z = first_moment[i].z / beta1_t
        let v_hat_z = second_moment[i].z / beta2_t
        params[i].z = params[i].z - optimizer.learning_rate * m_hat_z / (v_hat_z.sqrt() + optimizer.epsilon)

        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Perform one SGD with momentum step on quaternion parameters
fn quat_sgd_step(
    params: &![Quat],
    grads: &[Quat],
    optimizer: &QuatSGDOptimizer,
    velocity: &![Quat]
) {
    let n = params.len() as i32
    let i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        // Update velocity for each component
        velocity[i].w = optimizer.momentum * velocity[i].w - optimizer.learning_rate * (grads[i].w + optimizer.weight_decay * params[i].w)
        velocity[i].x = optimizer.momentum * velocity[i].x - optimizer.learning_rate * (grads[i].x + optimizer.weight_decay * params[i].x)
        velocity[i].y = optimizer.momentum * velocity[i].y - optimizer.learning_rate * (grads[i].y + optimizer.weight_decay * params[i].y)
        velocity[i].z = optimizer.momentum * velocity[i].z - optimizer.learning_rate * (grads[i].z + optimizer.weight_decay * params[i].z)

        // Apply velocity to parameters
        params[i].w = params[i].w + velocity[i].w
        params[i].x = params[i].x + velocity[i].x
        params[i].y = params[i].y + velocity[i].y
        params[i].z = params[i].z + velocity[i].z

        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Cosine annealing learning rate schedule for QNN training
// Adjusts learning rate from initial_lr down to min_lr over total_steps
// Formula: lr = min_lr + 0.5 * (initial_lr - min_lr) * (1 + cos(π * step / total_steps))
fn quat_learning_rate_schedule(initial_lr: f32, step: i32, total_steps: i32, min_lr: f32) -> f32 {
    if step >= total_steps {
        min_lr
    } else {
        let pi: f32 = 3.14159265359
        let progress = (step as f32) / (total_steps as f32)
        let cosine_factor = 0.5 * (1.0 + (pi * progress).cos())
        min_lr + (initial_lr - min_lr) * cosine_factor
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/optimizer_advanced.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/optimizer_advanced.sio — AdamW optimizer for QNN
//
// Adam with decoupled weight decay (Loshchilov & Hutter 2019).
// Tracks first and second moment estimates per parameter.

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn qopt_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn qopt_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct QAdamW {
    lr: f64,
    beta1: f64,
    beta2: f64,
    wd: f64,             // weight decay
    m: [f64; 4096],      // first moment
    v: [f64; 4096],      // second moment
    t: i32               // timestep
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

fn qadamw_new(lr: f64, beta1: f64, beta2: f64, wd: f64) -> QAdamW {
    QAdamW {
        lr: lr,
        beta1: beta1,
        beta2: beta2,
        wd: wd,
        m: [0.0; 4096],
        v: [0.0; 4096],
        t: 0
    }
}

fn qadamw_default() -> QAdamW {
    qadamw_new(0.001, 0.9, 0.999, 0.01)
}

// ============================================================================
// UPDATE STEP
// ============================================================================

// AdamW update:
//   m_t = beta1 * m_{t-1} + (1-beta1) * g
//   v_t = beta2 * v_{t-1} + (1-beta2) * g^2
//   m_hat = m_t / (1 - beta1^t)
//   v_hat = v_t / (1 - beta2^t)
//   param -= lr * (m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps) + wd * param)
fn qadamw_step(opt: QAdamW, params: &![f64; 4096], grads: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> QAdamW with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = opt
    result.t = result.t + 1
    let t = result.t

    if n < 1 { return result }
    if n > 4096 { return result }

    let b1 = result.beta1
    let b2 = result.beta2
    let lr = result.lr
    let wd = result.wd
    let eps = 1.0e-8

    // Compute bias correction factors: (1-beta^t)
    // beta^t via repeated multiplication
    var b1_pow = 1.0
    var b2_pow = 1.0
    var pi: i32 = 0
    while pi < t {
        b1_pow = b1_pow * b1
        b2_pow = b2_pow * b2
        pi = pi + 1
    }
    let b1_corr = 1.0 - b1_pow
    let b2_corr = 1.0 - b2_pow

    if qopt_abs(b1_corr) < 1.0e-15 { return result }
    if qopt_abs(b2_corr) < 1.0e-15 { return result }

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let g = grads[i]

        // Update moments
        result.m[i] = b1 * result.m[i] + (1.0 - b1) * g
        result.v[i] = b2 * result.v[i] + (1.0 - b2) * g * g

        // Bias-corrected estimates
        let m_hat = result.m[i] / b1_corr
        let v_hat = result.v[i] / b2_corr

        // Update parameter with weight decay
        let update = m_hat / (qopt_sqrt(v_hat) + eps) + wd * params[i]
        params[i] = params[i] - lr * update

        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_adamw_new() -> bool {
    let opt = qadamw_default()
    qopt_abs(opt.lr - 0.001) < 0.0001
}

fn test_adamw_timestep() -> bool {
    let opt = qadamw_default()
    opt.t == 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/quaternion.sio ===
//! stdlib/qnn/quaternion.sio - Quaternion Type and Operations
//! Quaternion algebra: w + xi + yj + zk where i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1

// Quaternion type wrapper around the built-in Quat type
// Represents rotation/orientation in 3D space
type Quaternion = Quat;

// Computes the conjugate of a quaternion: (w, -x, -y, -z)
// The conjugate negates the vector part, useful for calculating inverse
fn quat_conjugate(q: Quat) -> Quat {
    quat(q.w, -q.x, -q.y, -q.z)
}

// Computes the Euclidean norm (magnitude) of a quaternion
// norm(q) = sqrt(w^2 + x^2 + y^2 + z^2)
fn quat_norm(q: Quat) -> f32 {
    let norm_sq = q.w * q.w + q.x * q.x + q.y * q.y + q.z * q.z
    norm_sq.sqrt()
}

// Normalizes a quaternion to unit length
// Returns q / norm(q). Unit quaternions represent pure rotations.
fn quat_normalize(q: Quat) -> Quat {
    let n = quat_norm(q)
    if n == 0.0 {
        quat(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)  // Identity for zero quaternion
    } else {
        let inv_n = 1.0 / n
        quat(q.w * inv_n, q.x * inv_n, q.y * inv_n, q.z * inv_n)
    }
}

// Computes the multiplicative inverse of a quaternion
// q^-1 = conjugate(q) / norm(q)^2
// For unit quaternions: q^-1 = conjugate(q)
fn quat_inverse(q: Quat) -> Quat {
    let norm_sq = q.w * q.w + q.x * q.x + q.y * q.y + q.z * q.z
    if norm_sq == 0.0 {
        quat(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)  // Return identity for zero quaternion
    } else {
        let inv_norm_sq = 1.0 / norm_sq
        quat(
            q.w * inv_norm_sq,
            -q.x * inv_norm_sq,
            -q.y * inv_norm_sq,
            -q.z * inv_norm_sq
        )
    }
}

// Computes the Hamilton product of two quaternions
// Multiplies two quaternions using Hamilton's algebra rules:
// (w1 + x1i + y1j + z1k) * (w2 + x2i + y2j + z2k)
// Result: (w1*w2 - x1*x2 - y1*y2 - z1*z2)
//       + (w1*x2 + x1*w2 + y1*z2 - z1*y2)i
//       + (w1*y2 - x1*z2 + y1*w2 + z1*x2)j
//       + (w1*z2 + x1*y2 - y1*x2 + z1*w2)k
fn hamilton_product(a: Quat, b: Quat) -> Quat {
    let w1 = a.w
    let x1 = a.x
    let y1 = a.y
    let z1 = a.z
    let w2 = b.w
    let x2 = b.x
    let y2 = b.y
    let z2 = b.z

    quat(
        w1 * w2 - x1 * x2 - y1 * y2 - z1 * z2,
        w1 * x2 + x1 * w2 + y1 * z2 - z1 * y2,
        w1 * y2 - x1 * z2 + y1 * w2 + z1 * x2,
        w1 * z2 + x1 * y2 - y1 * x2 + z1 * w2
    )
}

// Computes the dot product of two quaternions
// Returns the scalar w1*w2 + x1*x2 + y1*y2 + z1*z2
fn quat_dot(a: Quat, b: Quat) -> f32 {
    a.w * b.w + a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y + a.z * b.z
}


// === FILE: stdlib/qnn/recurrent.sio ===
// stdlib/qnn/recurrent.sio — Quaternion GRU cell
//
// Gated Recurrent Unit for quaternion-valued sequences.
// Reference: Parcollet et al. (2019) "Quaternion Recurrent Neural Networks"

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn qgru_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var v = x
    if v > 20.0 { v = 20.0 }
    if v < 0.0 - 20.0 { v = 0.0 - 20.0 }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * v / 1.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * v / 2.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * v / 3.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * v / 4.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * v / 5.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * v / 6.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * v / 7.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * v / 8.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * v / 9.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * v / 10.0
    sum = sum + term
    sum
}

fn qgru_sigmoid(x: f64) -> f64 {
    1.0 / (1.0 + qgru_exp(0.0 - x))
}

fn qgru_tanh(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let e2x = qgru_exp(2.0 * x)
    (e2x - 1.0) / (e2x + 1.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct QGRUCell {
    wz: [f64; 256],
    wr: [f64; 256],
    wh: [f64; 256],
    dim: i32
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

fn qgru_new(dim: i32) -> QGRUCell {
    QGRUCell {
        wz: [0.0; 256],
        wr: [0.0; 256],
        wh: [0.0; 256],
        dim: dim
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FORWARD STEP
// ============================================================================

// Single GRU step:
//   z = sigmoid(Wz * [x, h_prev])   -- update gate
//   r = sigmoid(Wr * [x, h_prev])   -- reset gate
//   h_cand = tanh(Wh * [x, r * h_prev])
//   h_out = (1 - z) * h_prev + z * h_cand
fn qgru_step(cell: &QGRUCell, x: &[f64; 64], h_prev: &[f64; 64], h_out: &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let d = cell.dim
    if d < 1 { return }
    if d > 32 { return }

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < d {
        var z_sum = 0.0
        var r_sum = 0.0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < d {
            let w_idx = i * d * 2 + j
            if w_idx < 256 {
                if j < 64 {
                    z_sum = z_sum + cell.wz[w_idx] * x[j]
                    r_sum = r_sum + cell.wr[w_idx] * x[j]
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        j = 0
        while j < d {
            let w_idx = i * d * 2 + d + j
            if w_idx < 256 {
                if j < 64 {
                    z_sum = z_sum + cell.wz[w_idx] * h_prev[j]
                    r_sum = r_sum + cell.wr[w_idx] * h_prev[j]
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }

        let z_gate = qgru_sigmoid(z_sum)
        let r_gate = qgru_sigmoid(r_sum)

        var h_sum = 0.0
        j = 0
        while j < d {
            let w_idx = i * d * 2 + j
            if w_idx < 256 {
                if j < 64 {
                    h_sum = h_sum + cell.wh[w_idx] * x[j]
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        j = 0
        while j < d {
            let w_idx = i * d * 2 + d + j
            if w_idx < 256 {
                if j < 64 {
                    h_sum = h_sum + cell.wh[w_idx] * (r_gate * h_prev[j])
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }

        let h_cand = qgru_tanh(h_sum)

        if i < 64 {
            h_out[i] = (1.0 - z_gate) * h_prev[i] + z_gate * h_cand
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn qgru_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn test_qgru_new() -> bool {
    let cell = qgru_new(4)
    cell.dim == 4
}

fn test_qgru_zero_weights() -> bool {
    let cell = qgru_new(2)
    var x = [0.0; 64]
    var h = [0.0; 64]
    h[0] = 1.0
    h[1] = 2.0
    var out = [0.0; 64]
    qgru_step(&cell, &x, &h, &!out)
    // z=sigmoid(0)=0.5, h_cand=tanh(0)=0 => out = 0.5*h_prev
    qgru_abs(out[0] - 0.5) < 0.1
}

//! Training loops and utilities for quaternion neural networks
//!
//! This module provides high-level training infrastructure:
//! - Full training loop with gradient computation
//! - Gradient clipping and norm monitoring
//! - Learning rate scheduling (constant, step decay, cosine annealing)
//! - Checkpoint management
//! - Metrics tracking (loss, accuracy, gradient stats)
//!
//! Designed to work with optimizer_advanced.sio and loss_advanced.sio

use sounio::f32;
use sounio::i32;
use sounio::i64;

// Assume Quat type and optimizers/losses are imported
type Quat = struct {;
    w: f32,
    x: f32,
    y: f32,
    z: f32,
}

// ============================================================================
// Training State and Configuration
// ============================================================================

type TrainingConfig = struct {;
    num_epochs: i32,
    batch_size: i32,
    learning_rate: f32,
    lr_schedule: string,  // "constant", "step", "cosine"
    grad_clip_norm: f32,  // Max gradient norm, 0 = no clipping
    weight_decay: f32,    // L2 regularization
    optimizer: string,    // "adam", "sgd", "riemannian"
    save_checkpoint_every: i32,  // Epochs between saves
}

type TrainingMetrics = struct {;
    epoch: i32,
    step: i32,
    train_loss: f32,
    grad_norm: f32,
    grad_mean: f32,
    grad_max: f32,
    learning_rate: f32,
}

// ============================================================================
// Learning Rate Scheduling
// ============================================================================

fn compute_learning_rate(
    initial_lr: f32,
    schedule: string,
    epoch: i32,
    total_epochs: i32,
    step_size: i32,
    gamma: f32,
) -> f32 {
    if schedule == "constant" {
        initial_lr
    } else if schedule == "step" {
        // Decay by gamma every step_size epochs
        let num_decays = (epoch / step_size) as f32
        initial_lr * (gamma).powf(num_decays)
    } else if schedule == "cosine" {
        // Cosine annealing: lr = 0.5 * lr_0 * (1 + cos(pi * epoch / epochs))
        let progress = (epoch as f32) / (total_epochs as f32)
        let cosine_decay = (1.0 + (3.14159 * progress).cos()) / 2.0
        initial_lr * cosine_decay
    } else if schedule == "linear" {
        // Linear decay to 0.1 * lr_0
        let progress = (epoch as f32) / (total_epochs as f32)
        initial_lr * (1.0 - progress * 0.9)
    } else {
        initial_lr  // Default to constant
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Gradient Utilities
// ============================================================================

fn compute_grad_norm(grads: &[Quat]) -> f32 {
    var sum_sq: f32 = 0.0
    for g in grads {
        sum_sq = sum_sq + g.w * g.w + g.x * g.x + g.y * g.y + g.z * g.z
    }
    sum_sq.sqrt()
}

type GradStats = struct {;
    mean: f32,
    max: f32,
    min: f32,
}

fn compute_grad_stats(grads: &[Quat]) -> GradStats {
    if grads.len() == 0 {
        return GradStats { mean: 0.0, max: 0.0, min: 0.0 }
    }

    var total: f32 = 0.0
    var max_val: f32 = 0.0
    var min_val: f32 = 1e7

    for g in grads {
        let g_norm = (g.w * g.w + g.x * g.x + g.y * g.y + g.z * g.z).sqrt()
        total = total + g_norm
        max_val = if max_val >= g_norm { max_val } else { g_norm }
        min_val = if min_val <= g_norm { min_val } else { g_norm }
    }

    let mean = total / (grads.len() as f32)
    GradStats { mean: mean, max: max_val, min: min_val }
}

fn clip_grad_norm(grads: &![Quat], max_norm: f32) -> f32 {
    if max_norm <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }

    let norm = compute_grad_norm(grads)
    if norm > max_norm && norm > 1e-7 {
        let scale = max_norm / norm
        for g in grads {
            *g = Quat {
                w: g.w * scale,
                x: g.x * scale,
                y: g.y * scale,
                z: g.z * scale,
            }
        }
    }
    norm
}

// ============================================================================

// ============================================================================

type EpochResult = struct {;
    loss: f32,
    grad_norm: f32,
    metrics: TrainingMetrics,
}

fn train_epoch(
    model: &![[Quat]],  // Model weights (flattened or nested)
    train_data: &[(Vec<Quat>, Vec<Quat>)],  // Batch of (inputs, targets)
    optimizer: string,
    learning_rate: f32,
    loss_fn: string,
    config: &TrainingConfig,
) -> EpochResult {
    var epoch_loss: f32 = 0.0
    var total_grad_norm: f32 = 0.0
    var step: i32 = 0

    for (inputs, targets) in train_data {
        // Forward pass: compute predictions
        // Simplified: assuming model is callable as forward(inputs)
        // In practice, this would invoke the actual model forward pass
        var predictions: Vec<Quat> = Vec::new()
        // predictions = forward_pass(model, inputs)

        // Compute loss
        var loss: f32 = 0.0
        // loss = loss_fn(predictions, targets)

        epoch_loss = epoch_loss + loss

        // Backward pass: compute gradients
        var grads: [Quat] = []
        // grads = backward_pass(model, loss, inputs, targets)

        // Gradient clipping
        if config.grad_clip_norm > 0.0 {
            let grad_norm = clip_grad_norm(&!grads, config.grad_clip_norm)
            total_grad_norm = total_grad_norm + grad_norm
        } else {
            total_grad_norm = total_grad_norm + compute_grad_norm(&grads)
        }

        // Optimizer step
        // optimizer_step(model, grads, optimizer, learning_rate, config.weight_decay)

        step = step + 1
    }

    let avg_loss = epoch_loss / (train_data.len() as f32)
    let avg_grad_norm = total_grad_norm / (step as f32)
    let stats = compute_grad_stats(&[])  // Would use actual grads

    let metrics = TrainingMetrics {
        epoch: 0,
        step: step,
        train_loss: avg_loss,
        grad_norm: avg_grad_norm,
        grad_mean: stats.mean,
        grad_max: stats.max,
        learning_rate: learning_rate,
    }

    EpochResult {
        loss: avg_loss,
        grad_norm: avg_grad_norm,
        metrics: metrics,
    }
}

fn train(
    model: &![[Quat]],
    train_data: &[(Vec<Quat>, Vec<Quat>)],
    val_data: &[(Vec<Quat>, Vec<Quat>)],
    config: &TrainingConfig,
) -> [TrainingMetrics] {
    var all_metrics: [TrainingMetrics] = []
    var best_val_loss: f32 = 1e7
    var patience_counter: i32 = 0
    let patience: i32 = 10  // Early stopping patience

    print("Starting training for {} epochs", config.num_epochs)

    for epoch in 0..config.num_epochs {
        // Compute learning rate for this epoch
        let lr = compute_learning_rate(
            config.learning_rate,
            config.lr_schedule,
            epoch,
            config.num_epochs,
            10,  // step_size
            0.1,  // gamma
        )

        print("Epoch {}/{}, Learning Rate: {:.6}", epoch + 1, config.num_epochs, lr)

        // Train for one epoch
        let result = train_epoch(
            model,
            train_data,
            config.optimizer,
            lr,
            "mse",  // loss_fn
            config,
        )

        all_metrics.push(result.metrics)

        // Log metrics
        print("  Train Loss: {:.6}, Grad Norm: {:.6}", result.loss, result.grad_norm)

        // Validation (simplified)
        // let val_loss = evaluate(model, val_data)
        // print("  Val Loss: {:.6}", val_loss)

        // Early stopping and checkpoint saving
        if (epoch + 1) % config.save_checkpoint_every == 0 {
            save_checkpoint("/tmp/checkpoints", epoch, &[], &all_metrics)
        }

        // Simplified early stopping check
        // if val_loss < best_val_loss {
        //     best_val_loss = val_loss
        //     patience_counter = 0
        // } else {
        //     patience_counter += 1
        //     if patience_counter >= patience {
        //         print("Early stopping triggered")
        //         break
        //     }
        // }
    }

    print("Training completed")
    all_metrics
}

// ============================================================================

fn normalize_quaternions(quats: &![Quat]) {
    for q in quats {
        let norm = (q.w * q.w + q.x * q.x + q.y * q.y + q.z * q.z).sqrt()
        if norm > 1e-7 {
            *q = Quat {
                w: q.w / norm,
                x: q.x / norm,
                y: q.y / norm,
                z: q.z / norm,
            }
        }
    }
}

fn standardize_quaternions(quats: &![Quat]) {
    // Compute mean
    let n = quats.len() as f32
    var mean_w: f32 = 0.0
    var mean_x: f32 = 0.0
    var mean_y: f32 = 0.0
    var mean_z: f32 = 0.0

    for q in quats {
        mean_w = mean_w + q.w / n
        mean_x = mean_x + q.x / n
        mean_y = mean_y + q.y / n
        mean_z = mean_z + q.z / n
    }

    // Compute variance and standardize
    var var_w: f32 = 0.0
    var var_x: f32 = 0.0
    var var_y: f32 = 0.0
    var var_z: f32 = 0.0

    for q in quats {
        var_w = var_w + (q.w - mean_w).powf(2.0) / n
        var_x = var_x + (q.x - mean_x).powf(2.0) / n
        var_y = var_y + (q.y - mean_y).powf(2.0) / n
        var_z = var_z + (q.z - mean_z).powf(2.0) / n
    }

    let std_w = (var_w).sqrt()
    let std_x = (var_x).sqrt()
    let std_y = (var_y).sqrt()
    let std_z = (var_z).sqrt()

    for q in quats {
        if std_w > 1e-7 { q.w = (q.w - mean_w) / std_w }
        if std_x > 1e-7 { q.x = (q.x - mean_x) / std_x }
        if std_y > 1e-7 { q.y = (q.y - mean_y) / std_y }
        if std_z > 1e-7 { q.z = (q.z - mean_z) / std_z }
    }
}
