pub use pure::types::*;

// === FILE: stdlib/queue/pure/types.sio ===
// stdlib/queue/pure/types.sio — Queue Types

pub struct Queue {
    pub n_items: i32,
    pub data: [i64; 256],
    pub head: i32,
    pub tail: i32,
}

pub fn queue_new() -> Queue {
    Queue { n_items: 0, data: [0; 256], head: 0, tail: 0 }
}

pub fn queue_push(q: &! Queue, v: i64) with Mut {
    if q.n_items < 256 {
        q.data[q.tail as usize] = v
        q.tail = (q.tail + 1) % 256
        q.n_items = q.n_items + 1
    }
}

pub fn queue_pop(q: &! Queue) -> i64 with Mut {
    if q.n_items == 0 { return -1 }
    let v = q.data[q.head as usize]
    q.head = (q.head + 1) % 256
    q.n_items = q.n_items - 1
    v
}

pub fn queue_size(q: &Queue) -> i32 { q.n_items }

pub fn queue_is_empty(q: &Queue) -> bool { q.n_items == 0 }

// === FILE: stdlib/random/distributions.sio ===
// random::distributions — Probability Distributions
//
// PCG64-XSL-RR-128/64-LCG backend (Sounio-Pure R.2.4 Phase B, 2026-05-17).
// Bit-exact against pcg-cpp HEAD pcg64 (4 seeds × 8 samples = 32/32) and
// against the 256-sample × 4-seed oracle at
// docs/audit/r2_4_pcg64_algorithmic_bug/reference/oracle_seed_*.txt.
//
// History: R.2.1 deprecated the prior dst_pcg64_* impl with two known
// defects — (Cause A) state_hi was dead, output used arithmetic shift on
// signed i64, abs() mishandled i64::MIN; (Cause B / R.2.3) 4-field struct
// SRET aliasing. Cause B was fixed by R.2.3 commit 95b68a04 (slot
// allocator skip). Cause A is fixed by this replacement: full 128-bit
// state advance, unsigned helpers, XSL-RR output from NEW state per
// pcg-cpp setseq_base output_previous=false (itype=pcg128_t).
//
// Park-Miller (random::park_miller) remains the recommended path for
// simple PBPK Monte Carlo; this PCG64 backend is now safe for any new
// use and is reinstated for high-stream multi-substream work.
//
// Sample from common distributions with epistemic awareness.
// Every sample carries its distributional provenance.
//
// Distributions:
// - Uniform: U(low, high)
// - Normal: N(mean, std)
// - LogNormal: ln(X) ~ N(mu, sigma)
// - Exponential: Exp(rate)
// - Gamma: Gamma(shape, rate)
// - Beta: Beta(alpha, beta)
// - Poisson: Pois(rate)
//
// References:
// - Devroye (1986): "Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation"
// - Marsaglia & Tsang (2000): "A Simple Method for Generating Gamma Variables"

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sin(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn cos(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn floor(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// RNG (inline from rng.d for self-contained module)
// ============================================================================

// R.2.8 Phase D — DstPcg64 unified via type alias over canonical PcgState.
// Wrappers forward to pcg64_core::pcg_* one-liners. Bit-exact preserved.

use stdlib::random::pcg64_core::{
    PcgState, pcg_u128_add, pcg_step, pcg_next_f64, pcg_next_f64_nonzero,
}

type DstPcg64 = PcgState

fn dst_pcg64_new(seed: i64) -> DstPcg64 {
    // O'Neill canonical pcg64(seed) with stream=0: inc = PCG_DEFAULT_INCREMENT_128.
    let inc_hi: i64 = 6364136223846793005
    let inc_lo: i64 = 1442695040888963407
    let s0 = PcgState { state_hi: 0, state_lo: 0, inc_hi: inc_hi, inc_lo: inc_lo }
    let r1 = pcg_step(s0)
    let mid = r1.0
    let add = pcg_u128_add(mid.state_hi, mid.state_lo, 0, seed)
    let s2 = PcgState { state_hi: add.hi, state_lo: add.lo, inc_hi: inc_hi, inc_lo: inc_lo }
    let r2 = pcg_step(s2)
    return r2.0
}

fn dst_pcg64_next_i64(rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, i64) { return pcg_step(rng) }

fn dst_pcg64_next_f64(rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) { return pcg_next_f64(rng) }

fn dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) { return pcg_next_f64_nonzero(rng) }

// ============================================================================
// CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn dst_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }
fn e() -> f64 { 2.71828182845904523536 }

// ============================================================================
// UNIFORM DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Uniform {
    low: f64,
    high: f64,
}

fn uniform_new(low: f64, high: f64) -> Uniform {
    Uniform { low: low, high: high }
}

fn uniform_standard() -> Uniform {
    Uniform { low: 0.0, high: 1.0 }
}

fn uniform_sample(dist: Uniform, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let result = dst_pcg64_next_f64(rng)
    let v = dist.low + result.1 * (dist.high - dist.low)
    return (result.0, v)
}

fn uniform_mean(dist: Uniform) -> f64 {
    (dist.low + dist.high) / 2.0
}

fn uniform_variance(dist: Uniform) -> f64 {
    let range = dist.high - dist.low
    range * range / 12.0
}

// ============================================================================
// NORMAL (GAUSSIAN) DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Normal {
    mean: f64,
    std: f64,
}

fn normal_new(mean: f64, std: f64) -> Normal {
    Normal { mean: mean, std: std }
}

fn normal_standard() -> Normal {
    Normal { mean: 0.0, std: 1.0 }
}

// Sample using Box-Muller transform
fn normal_sample(dist: Normal, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let r1 = dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng)
    let rng2 = r1.0
    let u1 = r1.1

    let r2 = dst_pcg64_next_f64(rng2)
    let rng3 = r2.0
    let u2 = r2.1

    // Box-Muller transform
    let mag = sqrt(-2.0 * log(u1))
    let z = mag * cos(2.0 * dst_pi() * u2)

    let v = dist.mean + dist.std * z
    return (rng3, v)
}

// Sample using Box-Muller (returns both values)
fn normal_sample_pair(dist: Normal, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64, f64) {
    let r1 = dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng)
    let r2 = dst_pcg64_next_f64(r1.0)

    let mag = sqrt(-2.0 * log(r1.1))
    let z1 = mag * cos(2.0 * dst_pi() * r2.1)
    let z2 = mag * sin(2.0 * dst_pi() * r2.1)

    let v1 = dist.mean + dist.std * z1
    let v2 = dist.mean + dist.std * z2
    return (r2.0, v1, v2)
}

fn normal_mean(dist: Normal) -> f64 { dist.mean }
fn normal_variance(dist: Normal) -> f64 { dist.std * dist.std }

fn normal_pdf(dist: Normal, x: f64) -> f64 {
    let z = (x - dist.mean) / dist.std
    exp(-0.5 * z * z) / (dist.std * sqrt(2.0 * dst_pi()))
}

// ============================================================================
// LOG-NORMAL DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct LogNormal {
    mu: f64,     // Mean of ln(X)
    sigma: f64,  // Std of ln(X)
}

fn lognormal_new(mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> LogNormal {
    LogNormal { mu: mu, sigma: sigma }
}

// Create from desired mean and std of the distribution (not log-space)
fn lognormal_from_mean_std(mean: f64, std: f64) -> LogNormal {
    let variance = std * std
    let mu = log(mean * mean / sqrt(variance + mean * mean))
    let sigma = sqrt(log(1.0 + variance / (mean * mean)))
    LogNormal { mu: mu, sigma: sigma }
}

fn lognormal_sample(dist: LogNormal, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let n = normal_new(dist.mu, dist.sigma)
    let result = normal_sample(n, rng)
    return (result.0, exp(result.1))
}

fn lognormal_mean(dist: LogNormal) -> f64 {
    exp(dist.mu + dist.sigma * dist.sigma / 2.0)
}

fn lognormal_variance(dist: LogNormal) -> f64 {
    let s2 = dist.sigma * dist.sigma
    return (exp(s2) - 1.0) * exp(2.0 * dist.mu + s2)
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPONENTIAL DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Exponential {
    rate: f64,  // lambda
}

fn exponential_new(rate: f64) -> Exponential {
    Exponential { rate: rate }
}

fn exponential_from_mean(mean: f64) -> Exponential {
    Exponential { rate: 1.0 / mean }
}

fn exponential_sample(dist: Exponential, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let result = dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng)
    let v = -log(result.1) / dist.rate
    return (result.0, v)
}

fn exponential_mean(dist: Exponential) -> f64 { 1.0 / dist.rate }
fn exponential_variance(dist: Exponential) -> f64 { 1.0 / (dist.rate * dist.rate) }

// ============================================================================
// GAMMA DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Gamma {
    shape: f64,  // alpha > 0
    rate: f64,   // beta > 0
}

fn gamma_new(shape: f64, rate: f64) -> Gamma {
    Gamma { shape: shape, rate: rate }
}

fn gamma_with_scale(shape: f64, scale: f64) -> Gamma {
    Gamma { shape: shape, rate: 1.0 / scale }
}

// Marsaglia & Tsang method for shape >= 1
fn gamma_sample_shape_ge1(shape: f64, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let d = shape - 1.0 / 3.0
    let c = 1.0 / sqrt(9.0 * d)
    let n = normal_standard()

    var current_rng = rng

    // Rejection sampling
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 1000 {
        let nr = normal_sample(n, current_rng)
        current_rng = nr.0
        let x = nr.1
        let v = 1.0 + c * x

        if v > 0.0 {
            let v3 = v * v * v
            let ur = dst_pcg64_next_f64(current_rng)
            current_rng = ur.0
            let u = ur.1

            let x2 = x * x
            let x4 = x2 * x2

            if u < 1.0 - 0.0331 * x4 {
                return (current_rng, d * v3)
            }
            if log(u) < 0.5 * x2 + d * (1.0 - v3 + log(v3)) {
                return (current_rng, d * v3)
            }
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }

    // Fallback (shouldn't reach here normally)
    return (current_rng, shape)
}

fn gamma_sample(dist: Gamma, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    if dist.shape >= 1.0 {
        let result = gamma_sample_shape_ge1(dist.shape, rng)
        return (result.0, result.1 / dist.rate)
    } else {
        // For shape < 1: use Gamma(1+shape) * U^(1/shape)
        let g_result = gamma_sample_shape_ge1(1.0 + dist.shape, rng)
        let u_result = dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(g_result.0)
        let scale_factor = pow(u_result.1, 1.0 / dist.shape)
        return (u_result.0, g_result.1 * scale_factor / dist.rate)
    }
}

fn gamma_mean(dist: Gamma) -> f64 { dist.shape / dist.rate }
fn gamma_variance(dist: Gamma) -> f64 { dist.shape / (dist.rate * dist.rate) }

// ============================================================================
// BETA DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Beta {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64,
}

fn beta_new(alpha: f64, beta_val: f64) -> Beta {
    Beta { alpha: alpha, beta: beta_val }
}

fn beta_uniform() -> Beta {
    Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
}

fn beta_jeffreys() -> Beta {
    Beta { alpha: 0.5, beta: 0.5 }
}

// Sample using ratio of gammas: X/(X+Y) where X~Gamma(alpha,1), Y~Gamma(beta,1)
fn beta_sample(dist: Beta, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let g_a = gamma_new(dist.alpha, 1.0)
    let g_b = gamma_new(dist.beta, 1.0)

    let r1 = gamma_sample(g_a, rng)
    let r2 = gamma_sample(g_b, r1.0)

    let x = r1.1
    let y = r2.1
    let v = x / (x + y)

    return (r2.0, v)
}

fn beta_mean(dist: Beta) -> f64 {
    dist.alpha / (dist.alpha + dist.beta)
}

fn beta_variance(dist: Beta) -> f64 {
    let ab = dist.alpha + dist.beta
    return (dist.alpha * dist.beta) / (ab * ab * (ab + 1.0))
}

// ============================================================================
// POISSON DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Poisson {
    rate: f64,  // lambda > 0
}

fn poisson_new(rate: f64) -> Poisson {
    Poisson { rate: rate }
}

// Knuth's algorithm for small lambda
fn poisson_sample(dist: Poisson, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, i64) {
    if dist.rate < 30.0 {
        // Knuth's algorithm
        let l = exp(0.0 - dist.rate)
        var k: i64 = 0
        var p = 1.0
        var current_rng = rng

        var done = false
        while !done {
            k = k + 1
            let ur = dst_pcg64_next_f64(current_rng)
            current_rng = ur.0
            p = p * ur.1
            if p <= l {
                done = true
            }
        }

        return (current_rng, k - 1)
    } else {
        // Normal approximation for large lambda
        let n = normal_new(dist.rate, sqrt(dist.rate))
        let result = normal_sample(n, rng)
        let val = if result.1 < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { result.1 }
        let rounded = floor(val + 0.5) as i64
        return (result.0, rounded)
    }
}

fn poisson_mean(dist: Poisson) -> f64 { dist.rate }
fn poisson_variance(dist: Poisson) -> f64 { dist.rate }

// ============================================================================
// BERNOULLI DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Bernoulli {
    p: f64,
}

fn bernoulli_new(p: f64) -> Bernoulli {
    Bernoulli { p: p }
}

fn bernoulli_sample(dist: Bernoulli, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, bool) {
    let result = dst_pcg64_next_f64(rng)
    return (result.0, result.1 < dist.p)
}

// are now canonical PCG-XSL-RR-128/64-LCG. The `dst_pcg64_*` and
// `smp_pcg64_*` paths are bit-exact against pcg-cpp pcg64 (state=0 seeding);
// `rng.sio` pcg64_* preserves its splitmix64-derived multi-stream seeding
// and ships a committed self-oracle as a regression guard.

// === FILE: stdlib/random/park_miller.sio ===
// stdlib/random/park_miller.sio
//
// Park-Miller minimal-standard multiplicative congruential RNG.
//
//   x_{n+1} = (a · x_n) mod m       with a = 16807, m = 2^31 − 1 = 2147483647
//
// Reference: Park & Miller 1988, "Random Number Generators: Good Ones Are
// Hard to Find" (CACM 31:10). Period ≈ 2.147e9.
//
// QUALITY DISCLAIMER
//   - Passes all 1980-era diehard tests.
//   - FAILS TestU01 SmallCrush::LinearComp (linear-complexity test).
//   - Adequate for biological PBPK Monte Carlo with N ≪ 10^8 samples per
//     cohort: synthesis of 200 patients × 18 time points × 5 replicates =
//     18 000 samples is well within Park-Miller's reliable regime.
//   - NOT suitable for cryptography, high-dimensional stratified sampling,
//     or anything where TestU01-level uniformity matters.
//
// Why this module exists alongside stdlib/random/distributions.sio:
//   The 4-field DstPcg64 struct in distributions.sio currently exhibits a
//   state-aliasing bug under the pinned souc binary (Sounio-Pure dispatch
//   R.2.1 Phase D, 2026-05-16). Park-Miller uses a single f64 state and
//   bypasses that aliasing entirely. Once the codegen issue is resolved,
//   distributions.sio PCG64 becomes the preferred path; this module
//   remains for low-quality-acceptable use cases.
//
// API:
//   pm_new(seed: i64) -> ParkMiller
//   pm_uniform(rng: &!ParkMiller) -> f64           // U[0, 1)
//   pm_normal(rng: &!ParkMiller, mean, std) -> f64 // N(mean, std)
//   pm_lognormal(rng: &!ParkMiller, mean, cv) -> f64
//
// All samplers mutate the rng in place via &!. Deterministic given seed.
//
// Numerical note on storing state in f64:
//   a × m = 16807 × 2147483647 ≈ 3.6 × 10^13 < 2^53 ≈ 9.0 × 10^15.
//   Exact integer arithmetic in f64 holds for all intermediate products,
//   so the recurrence is bit-identical to a pure-integer Park-Miller.

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64
}

pub struct ParkMiller { state: f64 }

pub fn pm_new(seed: i64) -> ParkMiller with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Seed must be in [1, m-1]. Map any i64 to that range deterministically;
    // for any positive seed < m it is the identity, preserving the simple
    // form used in B.1 reference implementations.
    let m: i64 = 2147483647
    var s = seed
    if s < 0 { s = 0 - s }
    if s >= m { s = (s % (m - 1)) + 1 }
    if s == 0 { s = 1 }
    ParkMiller { state: s as f64 }
}

// One Park-Miller step. Returns U[0, 1).
pub fn pm_uniform(rng: &!ParkMiller) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = 2147483647.0
    let a = 16807.0
    let next = rng.state * a
    let q = next / m
    let q_floor = (q as i64) as f64
    let r = next - q_floor * m
    rng.state = r
    r / m
}

// Marsaglia polar method for one standard-normal draw.
// Uses two uniforms; rejects if u1²+u2² ≥ 1 (≤ 21.5% per attempt under
// uniform input on the unit square ↔ disc test). Max 20 attempts; on the
// astronomically unlikely event of 20 consecutive rejections returns 0.
pub fn pm_standard_normal(rng: &!ParkMiller) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var attempts: i64 = 0
    while attempts < 20 {
        let u1 = pm_uniform(rng) * 2.0 - 1.0
        let u2 = pm_uniform(rng) * 2.0 - 1.0
        let s = u1 * u1 + u2 * u2
        if s > 0.0 {
            if s < 1.0 {
                let factor = sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * log(s) / s)
                return u1 * factor
            }
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }
    0.0
}

pub fn pm_normal(rng: &!ParkMiller, mean: f64, std: f64) -> f64
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let z = pm_standard_normal(rng)
    mean + std * z
}

// LogNormal parameterized by mean and CV (coefficient of variation = σ/μ).
// σ_log = sqrt(ln(1 + CV²))
// x = mean · exp(σ_log · z − σ_log²/2)
pub fn pm_lognormal(rng: &!ParkMiller, mean: f64, cv: f64) -> f64
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    if mean <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    if cv <= 0.0 { return mean }
    let sigma_log = sqrt(log(1.0 + cv * cv))
    let z = pm_standard_normal(rng)
    mean * exp(sigma_log * z - 0.5 * sigma_log * sigma_log)
}

// Self-test entry point. Exits 0 if all sanity checks pass.
pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var rng = pm_new(31415)
    let u1 = pm_uniform(&!rng)
    let u2 = pm_uniform(&!rng)
    let u3 = pm_uniform(&!rng)
    println(u1)   // expect 0.245865 (verified in B.1 V3 runner)
    println(u2)   // expect 0.259615
    println(u3)   // expect 0.341197

    // Determinism check: re-seed and confirm first draw matches.
    var rng2 = pm_new(31415)
    let v1 = pm_uniform(&!rng2)
    println(v1 - u1)  // expect 0.0

    // Standard normal sample
    let z = pm_standard_normal(&!rng)
    println(z)        // some value in roughly [-3, 3]

    // LogNormal at (4.5, CV=0.30)
    let cl = pm_lognormal(&!rng, 4.5, 0.30)
    println(cl)       // ~ 4.5 with 30% CV

    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/random/pcg64_core.sio ===
// random::pcg64_core — Shared canonical PCG64-XSL-RR-128/64 helpers.
//
// Authored by Sounio-Pure R.2.6 (2026-05-17) to deduplicate the bit-
// identical helper sets shipped by distributions.sio (R.2.4), rng.sio
// (R.2.5), and sampling.sio (R.2.5). All bodies are byte-equivalent to
// the R.2.4-certified `dst_pcg_*` family; `pcg_umod` is the R.2.5
// rejection-modulo helper.
//
// Stdlib-internal: not part of the user-facing module surface. Callers
// import explicitly via `use stdlib::random::pcg64_core::{...}`.

pub struct PcgU128 {
    hi: i64,
    lo: i64,
}

// Unsigned less-than on u64 bit-patterns stored in i64.
pub fn pcg_u_lt(a: i64, b: i64) -> bool {
    let top: i64 = 1
    let mask = top << 63
    (a ^ mask) < (b ^ mask)
}

// Logical right shift on signed i64. Valid for 0 <= n <= 64.
pub fn pcg_lshr(x: i64, n: i64) -> i64 {
    if n <= 0 { return x }
    if n >= 64 { return 0 }
    let raw = x >> n
    let one: i64 = 1
    let mask = (one << (64 - n)) - 1
    return raw & mask
}

// High 64 of u64 × u64 via 32-bit half decomposition.
pub fn pcg_umul64_high(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    let mask32: i64 = 4294967295
    let al = a & mask32
    let ah = pcg_lshr(a, 32)
    let bl = b & mask32
    let bh = pcg_lshr(b, 32)
    let ll = al * bl
    let lh = al * bh
    let hl = ah * bl
    let hh = ah * bh
    let t = pcg_lshr(ll, 32) + (lh & mask32) + (hl & mask32)
    return pcg_lshr(t, 32) + pcg_lshr(lh, 32) + pcg_lshr(hl, 32) + hh
}

// 128-bit add mod 2^128.
pub fn pcg_u128_add(a_hi: i64, a_lo: i64, b_hi: i64, b_lo: i64) -> PcgU128 {
    let res_lo = a_lo + b_lo
    let carry: i64 = if pcg_u_lt(res_lo, a_lo) { 1 } else { 0 }
    let res_hi = a_hi + b_hi + carry
    return PcgU128 { hi: res_hi, lo: res_lo }
}

// 128-bit multiply mod 2^128.
pub fn pcg_u128_mul(a_hi: i64, a_lo: i64, b_hi: i64, b_lo: i64) -> PcgU128 {
    let res_lo = a_lo * b_lo
    let res_hi = pcg_umul64_high(a_lo, b_lo) + a_hi * b_lo + a_lo * b_hi
    return PcgU128 { hi: res_hi, lo: res_lo }
}

// 64-bit right rotate. Valid for 0 <= rot < 64.
pub fn pcg_rotr64(x: i64, rot: i64) -> i64 {
    let r = rot & 63
    if r == 0 { return x }
    let right = pcg_lshr(x, r)
    let left = x << (64 - r)
    return right | left
}

// Canonical PCG64 state — shared across distributions/rng/sampling callers.
pub struct PcgState {
    state_hi: i64,
    state_lo: i64,
    inc_hi: i64,
    inc_lo: i64,
}

// PCG64-XSL-RR-128/64 step. Bit-exact pcg-cpp output_previous=false.
pub fn pcg_step(rng: PcgState) -> (PcgState, i64) {
    let mult_hi: i64 = 2549297995355413924
    let mult_lo: i64 = 4865540595714422341
    let mul = pcg_u128_mul(rng.state_hi, rng.state_lo, mult_hi, mult_lo)
    let add = pcg_u128_add(mul.hi, mul.lo, rng.inc_hi, rng.inc_lo)
    let new_hi = add.hi
    let new_lo = add.lo
    let xorshifted = new_hi ^ new_lo
    let rot = pcg_lshr(new_hi, 58) & 63
    let output = pcg_rotr64(xorshifted, rot)
    return (PcgState {
        state_hi: new_hi,
        state_lo: new_lo,
        inc_hi: rng.inc_hi,
        inc_lo: rng.inc_lo,
    }, output)
}

// Canonical uniform f64 in [0, 1) — top 53 bits / 2^53.
pub fn pcg_next_f64(rng: PcgState) -> (PcgState, f64) {
    let result = pcg_step(rng)
    let mantissa = pcg_lshr(result.1, 11)
    let fraction = (mantissa as f64) / 9007199254740992.0
    return (result.0, fraction)
}

// Strictly positive uniform f64 — at most 10 retries, then 1e-7 floor.
pub fn pcg_next_f64_nonzero(rng: PcgState) -> (PcgState, f64) {
    var current = rng
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let result = pcg_next_f64(current)
        current = result.0
        if result.1 > 0.0 {
            return (current, result.1)
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }
    (current, 0.0000001)
}

// Rejection-modulo bounded sampler [0, n). n must be > 0.
pub fn pcg_bounded(rng: PcgState, n: i64) -> (PcgState, i64) {
    let result = pcg_step(rng)
    let v = pcg_umod(result.1, n)
    return (result.0, v)
}

// Unsigned 64-bit mod n via binary long-division. n must be > 0.
// Power-of-two fast path. Used by rejection-modulo in *_bounded.
pub fn pcg_umod(x: i64, n: i64) -> i64 {
    let n_minus_1 = n - 1
    if (n & n_minus_1) == 0 { return x & n_minus_1 }
    var rem: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 63
    while i >= 0 {
        let bit = pcg_lshr(x, i) & 1
        rem = rem + rem + bit
        if !pcg_u_lt(rem, n) { rem = rem - n }
        i = i - 1
    }
    return rem
}


// === FILE: stdlib/random/rng.sio ===
// random::rng — Random Number Generators
//
// Fast, high-quality PRNGs for scientific computing.
// PCG64: Default, excellent statistical quality
// RngXoshiro256++: Fast for simulations
// SplitMix64: For seeding other generators
//
// References:
// - O'Neill (2014): "PCG: A Family of Simple Fast Space-Efficient PRNGs"
// - Blackman & Vigna (2018): "Scrambled Linear Pseudorandom Number Generators"

// ============================================================================
// SPLITMIX64 — FOR SEEDING
// ============================================================================

struct SplitMix64 {
    state: i64,
}

fn splitmix64_new(seed: i64) -> SplitMix64 {
    SplitMix64 { state: seed }
}

fn splitmix64_next(rng: SplitMix64) -> (SplitMix64, i64) {
    // state += 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    let new_state = rng.state + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 as i64
    var z = new_state

    // z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = z ^ (z >> 30)
    // Simplified multiplication for interpreter
    z = z * 0xbf58476d as i64

    // z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    z = z ^ (z >> 27)
    z = z * 0x94d049bb as i64

    z = z ^ (z >> 31)

    (SplitMix64 { state: new_state }, z)
}

// ============================================================================
// PCG64 — DEFAULT GENERATOR
// ============================================================================

// R.3.1 Phase D — Pcg64 unified via type alias over canonical PcgState.
// The R.2.8/R.2.9 deferred wiring lands here: TUP_CACHE_KEY collisions
// in Pass 1c.5 are now resolved (R.3.1 compiler patch).
use stdlib::random::pcg64_core::{
    PcgState, pcg_u_lt, pcg_umod, pcg_step, pcg_next_f64, pcg_next_f64_nonzero,
}

type Pcg64 = PcgState

fn pcg64_new(seed: i64) -> Pcg64 {
    // Preserves the multi-stream design rng.sio was built around: each
    // (seed, state_hi, state_lo, inc_hi, inc_lo) tuple is derived from
    // four splitmix64 outputs, giving independent streams across seeds.
    // inc_hi|1 and inc_lo|1 ensure the stream constant is odd (PCG req).
    var sm = splitmix64_new(seed)
    let r1 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r1.0
    let s1 = r1.1
    let r2 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r2.0
    let s2 = r2.1
    let r3 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r3.0
    let s3 = r3.1
    let r4 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    let s4 = r4.1
    PcgState {
        state_hi: s1,
        state_lo: s2,
        inc_hi: s3 | 1,
        inc_lo: s4 | 1,
    }
}

fn pcg64_next_i64(rng: Pcg64) -> (Pcg64, i64) { return pcg_step(rng) }

fn pcg64_next_f64(rng: Pcg64) -> (Pcg64, f64) { return pcg_next_f64(rng) }

fn pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng: Pcg64) -> (Pcg64, f64) { return pcg_next_f64_nonzero(rng) }

fn pcg64_next_bool(rng: Pcg64, p: f64) -> (Pcg64, bool) {
    let result = pcg_next_f64(rng)
    (result.0, result.1 < p)
}

fn pcg64_bounded(rng: Pcg64, n: i64) -> (Pcg64, i64) {
    if n <= 0 { return (rng, 0) }
    let neg_n = 0 - n
    let threshold = pcg_umod(neg_n, n)
    var current = rng
    var attempts: i64 = 0
    while attempts < 100 {
        let r = pcg_step(current)
        current = r.0
        if !pcg_u_lt(r.1, threshold) {
            return (current, pcg_umod(r.1, n))
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }
    (current, 0)
}

// ============================================================================
// XOSHIRO256++ — FAST SIMULATION RNG
// ============================================================================

struct RngXoshiro256 {
    s0: i64,
    s1: i64,
    s2: i64,
    s3: i64,
}

fn xoshiro256_new(seed: i64) -> RngXoshiro256 {
    var sm = splitmix64_new(seed)

    let r1 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r1.0
    let r2 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r2.0
    let r3 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r3.0
    let r4 = splitmix64_next(sm)

    RngXoshiro256 {
        s0: r1.1,
        s1: r2.1,
        s2: r3.1,
        s3: r4.1,
    }
}

fn rng_rotl(x: i64, k: i64) -> i64 {
    (x << k) | (x >> (64 - k))
}

fn xoshiro256_next_i64(rng: RngXoshiro256) -> (RngXoshiro256, i64) {
    // result = rng_rotl(s0 + s3, 23) + s0
    let result = rng_rotl(rng.s0 + rng.s3, 23) + rng.s0

    let t = rng.s1 << 17

    var s2 = rng.s2 ^ rng.s0
    var s3 = rng.s3 ^ rng.s1
    var s1 = rng.s1 ^ s2
    var s0 = rng.s0 ^ s3

    s2 = s2 ^ t
    s3 = rng_rotl(s3, 45)

    (RngXoshiro256 { s0: s0, s1: s1, s2: s2, s3: s3 }, result)
}

fn xoshiro256_next_f64(rng: RngXoshiro256) -> (RngXoshiro256, f64) {
    let result = xoshiro256_next_i64(rng)
    let new_rng = result.0
    let bits = result.1

    let positive = if bits < 0 { 0 - bits } else { bits }
    let fraction = (positive as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0

    (new_rng, fraction)
}

// ============================================================================
// RNG WRAPPER (functional approach)
// ============================================================================

// Since global mutable state isn't supported, we use a functional approach
// where the RNG state is passed through and returned

pub struct RngPcgWrapper {
    rng: Pcg64,
}

pub fn rng_pcg_new(seed: i64) -> RngPcgWrapper {
    RngPcgWrapper { rng: pcg64_new(seed) }
}

fn rng_pcg_next_f64(state: RngPcgWrapper) -> (RngPcgWrapper, f64) {
    let result = pcg64_next_f64(state.rng)
    (RngPcgWrapper { rng: result.0 }, result.1)
}

fn rng_pcg_next_i64(state: RngPcgWrapper) -> (RngPcgWrapper, i64) {
    let result = pcg64_next_i64(state.rng)
    (RngPcgWrapper { rng: result.0 }, result.1)
}

fn rng_pcg_next_bool(state: RngPcgWrapper, p: f64) -> (RngPcgWrapper, bool) {
    let result = pcg64_next_bool(state.rng, p)
    (RngPcgWrapper { rng: result.0 }, result.1)
}

pub fn rng_pcg_bounded(state: RngPcgWrapper, n: i64) -> (RngPcgWrapper, i64) {
    let result = pcg64_bounded(state.rng, n)
    (RngPcgWrapper { rng: result.0 }, result.1)
}

// ============================================================================
// XORSHIFT128+ RNG WITH FUNCTIONAL (VALUE-PASSING) API
// ============================================================================
//
// Design: Explicit state threading — no global mutable state.
// Algorithm: xorshift128+ (Vigna 2014) with splitmix64 seeding.
// Each function returns (value, new_state) so callers chain state.

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Inline math helpers — no imports required
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn rng_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn rng_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e_val = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e_val = e_val + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e_val = e_val - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64
        k = k + 1
    }
    2.0 * sum + (e_val as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn rng_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let twopi = 6.28318530717958647692
    var a = x
    while a >= twopi { a = a - twopi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + twopi }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - twopi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn rng_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let twopi = 6.28318530717958647692
    var a = x
    while a >= twopi { a = a - twopi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + twopi }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - twopi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// RngState — xorshift128+ state (two 64-bit words)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

struct RngState {
    s0: i64,
    s1: i64,
}

// splitmix64 step: expand a single seed word into well-mixed output
fn rng_splitmix_step(s: i64) -> (i64, i64) with Mut {
    let next = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    var z = next
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let out = z ^ (z >> 31)
    (next, out)
}

// Initialize RngState from a seed using splitmix64
fn rng_new(seed: i64) -> RngState with Mut {
    let step1 = rng_splitmix_step(seed)
    let s = step1.0
    let s0 = step1.1
    let step2 = rng_splitmix_step(s)
    let s1 = step2.1
    RngState { s0: s0, s1: s1 }
}

// xorshift128+: returns (random i64, new state)
fn rng_next(state: RngState) -> (i64, RngState) with Mut {
    var x = state.s0
    let y = state.s1
    x = x ^ (x << 23)
    x = x ^ (x >> 17)
    x = x ^ y
    x = x ^ (y >> 26)
    let out = state.s0 + y
    (out, RngState { s0: y, s1: x })
}

// Uniform [0, 1) — clears sign bit via AND, maps to [0, 1) by dividing by 2^63-1
fn rng_uniform(state: RngState) -> (f64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = rng_next(state)
    let bits = r.0
    // Clear sign bit: AND with 0x7fffffffffffffff gives value in [0, 2^63-1]
    let pos = bits & 0x7fffffffffffffff
    let f = (pos as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0
    (f, r.1)
}

// Uniform [lo, hi)
fn rng_uniform_range(state: RngState, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> (f64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = rng_uniform(state)
    (lo + r.0 * (hi - lo), r.1)
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Distributions
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Normal N(mu, sigma) — Box-Muller transform
fn rng_normal(state: RngState, mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> (f64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Need u1 > 0 for log; retry up to 10 times
    var cur = state
    var u1 = 0.0
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        cur = r.1
        if r.0 > 0.0 {
            u1 = r.0
            attempts = 100  // break
        } else {
            attempts = attempts + 1
        }
    }
    if u1 <= 0.0 { u1 = 1.0e-10 }
    let r2 = rng_uniform(cur)
    let u2 = r2.0
    let new_state = r2.1
    let mag = rng_sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * rng_ln(u1))
    let z = mag * rng_cos(2.0 * 3.14159265358979323846 * u2)
    (mu + sigma * z, new_state)
}

// Exponential Exp(lambda) — inverse CDF: -ln(u)/lambda
fn rng_exponential(state: RngState, lambda: f64) -> (f64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var u = 0.0
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        cur = r.1
        if r.0 > 0.0 {
            u = r.0
            attempts = 100
        } else {
            attempts = attempts + 1
        }
    }
    if u <= 0.0 { u = 1.0e-10 }
    ((0.0 - rng_ln(u)) / lambda, cur)
}

// Poisson Pois(lambda) — Knuth's algorithm (good for lambda < 30)
fn rng_poisson(state: RngState, lambda: f64) -> (i64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let l = rng_ln(1.0)  // just 0 — used as a warmup call
    // e^-lambda as a product threshold
    // We compute exp(-lambda) via repeated multiply on ln comparison
    // Using Knuth: generate uniform products until < e^-lambda
    // e^-lambda: approximate via rng_ln(p) < -lambda
    var cur = state
    var k: i64 = 0
    var log_p = 0.0
    var done = false
    while !done {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        cur = r.1
        var u = r.0
        if u <= 0.0 { u = 1.0e-10 }
        log_p = log_p + rng_ln(u)
        if log_p < (0.0 - lambda) {
            done = true
        } else {
            k = k + 1
        }
    }
    (k, cur)
}

// Bernoulli(p) — 1 with probability p, 0 otherwise
fn rng_bernoulli(state: RngState, p: f64) -> (i32, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = rng_uniform(state)
    let v: i32 = if r.0 < p { 1 } else { 0 }
    (v, r.1)
}

// Geometric(p) — number of trials until first success (1-indexed)
fn rng_geometric(state: RngState, p: f64) -> (i64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var u = 0.0
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        cur = r.1
        if r.0 > 0.0 {
            u = r.0
            attempts = 100
        } else {
            attempts = attempts + 1
        }
    }
    if u <= 0.0 { u = 1.0e-10 }
    // ceiling(ln(u) / ln(1-p))
    let log_u = rng_ln(u)
    let log_1mp = rng_ln(1.0 - p)
    var k = log_u / log_1mp
    // ceiling: if k is not already integer
    let ki = k as i64
    let result: i64 = if (ki as f64) < k { ki + 1 } else { ki }
    let final_k: i64 = if result < 1 { 1 } else { result }
    (final_k, cur)
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sampling utilities — fixed-size array operations
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Fisher-Yates shuffle of first n elements in arr (max 256)
// Returns (new_state, shuffled_array) — by-value for JIT compatibility
fn rng_shuffle(state: RngState, arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> (RngState, [f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var out = arr
    var i = n - 1
    while i > 0 {
        // Get random j in [0, i]
        let r = rng_next(cur)
        cur = r.1
        let bits = r.0
        let positive = if bits < 0 { 0 - bits } else { bits }
        let j = (positive % ((i + 1) as i64)) as i32
        let tmp = out[i]
        out[i] = out[j]
        out[j] = tmp
        i = i - 1
    }
    (cur, out)
}

// Fill first n elements with uniform [0, 1) samples
// Returns (new_state, filled_array) — by-value for JIT compatibility
fn rng_fill_uniform(state: RngState, n: i32) -> (RngState, [f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var arr: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        arr[i] = r.0
        cur = r.1
        i = i + 1
    }
    (cur, arr)
}

// Fill first n elements with normal samples N(mu, sigma)
// Returns (new_state, filled_array) — by-value for JIT compatibility
pub fn rng_fill_normal(state: RngState, n: i32, mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> (RngState, [f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var arr: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let r = rng_normal(cur, mu, sigma)
        arr[i] = r.0
        cur = r.1
        i = i + 1
    }
    (cur, arr)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/random/sampling.sio ===
// random::sampling — Random Sampling Utilities
//
// Functions for sampling from collections, shuffling, and PK/PD variability.
//
// Features:
// - sample: Random selection from arrays
// - sample_weighted: Weighted random selection
// - shuffle: Random permutation
// - resample: Bootstrap resampling
// - pk_variability: PK parameter variability (IIV, IOV)
//
// References:
// - Knuth (1997): "The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 2"
// - Lavielle (2014): "Mixed Effects Models for the Population Approach"

// ============================================================================
// RNG (inline from rng.d for self-contained module)
// ============================================================================

// R.2.8 Phase D — SmpPcg64 unified via type alias over canonical PcgState.
use stdlib::random::pcg64_core::{
    PcgState, pcg_u_lt, pcg_u128_add, pcg_umod, pcg_step, pcg_next_f64, pcg_next_f64_nonzero,
}

type SmpPcg64 = PcgState

// ─── PCG64-XSL-RR-128/64 step + canonical seeding (matches pcg-cpp) ───────

fn smp_pcg64_new(seed: i64) -> SmpPcg64 {
    let inc_hi: i64 = 6364136223846793005
    let inc_lo: i64 = 1442695040888963407
    let s0 = PcgState { state_hi: 0, state_lo: 0, inc_hi: inc_hi, inc_lo: inc_lo }
    let r1 = pcg_step(s0)
    let mid = r1.0
    let add = pcg_u128_add(mid.state_hi, mid.state_lo, 0, seed)
    let s2 = PcgState { state_hi: add.hi, state_lo: add.lo, inc_hi: inc_hi, inc_lo: inc_lo }
    let r2 = pcg_step(s2)
    return r2.0
}

fn smp_pcg64_next_i64(rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) { return pcg_step(rng) }

fn smp_pcg64_next_f64(rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) { return pcg_next_f64(rng) }

// Generate integer in [0, n) with unbiased rejection-modulo.
fn smp_pcg64_bounded(rng: SmpPcg64, n: i64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) {
    if n <= 0 { return (rng, 0) }
    let neg_n = 0 - n
    let threshold = pcg_umod(neg_n, n)
    var current = rng
    var attempts: i64 = 0
    while attempts < 100 {
        let r = pcg_step(current)
        current = r.0
        if !pcg_u_lt(r.1, threshold) {
            return (current, pcg_umod(r.1, n))
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }
    return (current, 0)
}

// ============================================================================
// NORMAL DISTRIBUTION (for variability)
// ============================================================================

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn cos(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn smp_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn smp_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    return pcg_next_f64_nonzero(rng)
}

fn sample_normal(mean: f64, std: f64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let r1 = smp_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng)
    let r2 = smp_pcg64_next_f64(r1.0)

    let mag = sqrt(-2.0 * log(r1.1))
    let z = mag * cos(2.0 * smp_pi() * r2.1)

    return (r2.0, mean + std * z)
}

// ============================================================================
// BASIC SAMPLING
// ============================================================================

// Sample a single random index from [0, n)
fn sample_index(n: i64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) {
    return smp_pcg64_bounded(rng, n)
}

// Sample a single element from an f64 array
fn sample_one_f64(arr: [f64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let n = arr.len() as i64
    let idx_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(rng, n)
    return (idx_result.0, arr[idx_result.1 as usize])
}

// Sample a single element from an i64 array
fn sample_one_i64(arr: [i64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) {
    let n = arr.len() as i64
    let idx_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(rng, n)
    return (idx_result.0, arr[idx_result.1 as usize])
}

// ============================================================================
// WEIGHTED SAMPLING
// ============================================================================

// Sample index with weights (weights don't need to sum to 1)
fn sample_weighted_index(weights: [f64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) {
    // Compute total weight
    var total = 0.0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < weights.len() {
        total = total + weights[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Sample uniform [0, total)
    let u_result = smp_pcg64_next_f64(rng)
    let threshold = u_result.1 * total

    // Find which bucket
    var cumsum = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < weights.len() {
        cumsum = cumsum + weights[i]
        if cumsum > threshold {
            return (u_result.0, i as i64)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Fallback to last index
    return (u_result.0, (weights.len() - 1) as i64)
}

// ============================================================================
// SHUFFLING (Fisher-Yates)
// ============================================================================

// Shuffle an array in place using Fisher-Yates
fn smp_shuffle_f64(arr: [f64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, [f64]) {
    var result = arr
    var current_rng = rng
    var i = result.len()

    while i > 1 {
        i = i - 1
        let j_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(current_rng, (i + 1) as i64)
        current_rng = j_result.0
        let j = j_result.1 as usize

        // Swap result[i] and result[j]
        let temp = result[i]
        result[i] = result[j]
        result[j] = temp
    }

    return (current_rng, result)
}

// Shuffle an i64 array
fn shuffle_i64(arr: [i64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, [i64]) {
    var result = arr
    var current_rng = rng
    var i = result.len()

    while i > 1 {
        i = i - 1
        let j_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(current_rng, (i + 1) as i64)
        current_rng = j_result.0
        let j = j_result.1 as usize

        let temp = result[i]
        result[i] = result[j]
        result[j] = temp
    }

    return (current_rng, result)
}

// ============================================================================
// RESAMPLING (BOOTSTRAP)
// ============================================================================

// Bootstrap resample: sample n items with replacement
fn resample_f64(arr: [f64], n: i64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, [f64]) {
    var result: [f64] = []
    var current_rng = rng
    let arr_len = arr.len() as i64

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(current_rng, arr_len)
        current_rng = idx_result.0
        result.push(arr[idx_result.1 as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }

    return (current_rng, result)
}

// ============================================================================
// PK/PD VARIABILITY
// ============================================================================

// Inter-Individual Variability (IIV) parameters
struct IIV {
    omega_cl: f64,   // CV for clearance
    omega_vc: f64,   // CV for central volume
    omega_ka: f64,   // CV for absorption rate
}

fn iiv_new(omega_cl: f64, omega_vc: f64, omega_ka: f64) -> IIV {
    IIV {
        omega_cl: omega_cl,
        omega_vc: omega_vc,
        omega_ka: omega_ka,
    }
}

fn iiv_typical() -> IIV {
    // Typical PK variability (30% CV)
    IIV {
        omega_cl: 0.3,
        omega_vc: 0.3,
        omega_ka: 0.5,
    }
}

// Generate individual PK parameters with IIV
struct IndividualPK {
    cl: f64,   // Individual clearance
    vc: f64,   // Individual central volume
    ka: f64,   // Individual absorption rate constant
}

fn generate_individual_pk(
    pop_cl: f64, pop_vc: f64, pop_ka: f64,
    iiv: IIV, rng: SmpPcg64
) -> (SmpPcg64, IndividualPK) {
    // Sample eta values (random effects)
    let eta_cl_result = sample_normal(0.0, iiv.omega_cl, rng)
    let eta_vc_result = sample_normal(0.0, iiv.omega_vc, eta_cl_result.0)
    let eta_ka_result = sample_normal(0.0, iiv.omega_ka, eta_vc_result.0)

    // Apply exponential transformation
    let ind = IndividualPK {
        cl: pop_cl * exp(eta_cl_result.1),
        vc: pop_vc * exp(eta_vc_result.1),
        ka: pop_ka * exp(eta_ka_result.1),
    }

    return (eta_ka_result.0, ind)
}

// Generate a virtual population
fn generate_population(
    pop_cl: f64, pop_vc: f64, pop_ka: f64,
    iiv: IIV, n_subjects: i64, rng: SmpPcg64
) -> (SmpPcg64, [IndividualPK]) {
    var population: [IndividualPK] = []
    var current_rng = rng

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_subjects {
        let result = generate_individual_pk(pop_cl, pop_vc, pop_ka, iiv, current_rng)
        current_rng = result.0
        population.push(result.1)
        i = i + 1
    }

    return (current_rng, population)
}

// ============================================================================
// RESIDUAL ERROR MODELS
// ============================================================================

// Add proportional residual error
fn add_proportional_error(value: f64, sigma: f64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let eps_result = sample_normal(0.0, sigma, rng)
    return (eps_result.0, value * (1.0 + eps_result.1))
}

// Add additive residual error
fn add_additive_error(value: f64, sigma: f64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let eps_result = sample_normal(0.0, sigma, rng)
    return (eps_result.0, value + eps_result.1)
}

// Add combined (additive + proportional) residual error
fn add_combined_error(value: f64, sigma_add: f64, sigma_prop: f64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let eps1_result = sample_normal(0.0, sigma_add, rng)
    let eps2_result = sample_normal(0.0, sigma_prop, eps1_result.0)
    return (eps2_result.0, value * (1.0 + eps2_result.1) + eps1_result.1)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/random/xoshiro.sio ===
// stdlib/random/xoshiro.sio — Xoshiro256** PRNG with Prob Effect
//
// A proper pseudo-random number generator for Sounio.
// Every probabilistic function declares `with Prob` — effects are the API contract.
//
// Xoshiro256** is the current state-of-the-art PRNG:
//   - Period: 2^256 - 1
//   - Passes BigCrush, PractRand
//   - Very fast: ~1ns per generation
//   - No heap allocation, fixed 256-bit state
//
// SOTA: Blackman & Vigna (2021): "Scrambled Linear Pseudorandom Number Generators"
//
// Note on Prob effect: In Sounio, any function that involves randomness
// MUST declare `with Prob`. This makes non-determinism visible at the type
// level. Pure functions cannot call probabilistic functions.

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_rng(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn ln_rng(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e_val = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e_val = e_val + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e_val = e_val - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e_val as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn cos_rng(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var a = x
    let twopi = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= twopi { a = a - twopi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + twopi }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - twopi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

// =============================================================================
// Xoshiro256** State
// =============================================================================

struct Xoshiro256 {
    s0: i64,
    s1: i64,
    s2: i64,
    s3: i64,
}

// =============================================================================
// Seed from a single i64
// =============================================================================
// Uses SplitMix64 to expand a single seed into the 256-bit state.

fn xoshiro_seed(seed: i64) -> Xoshiro256 with Mut {
    // SplitMix64 expansion
    var s = seed
    s = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    var z = s
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let s0 = z ^ (z >> 31)

    s = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    z = s
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let s1 = z ^ (z >> 31)

    s = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    z = s
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let s2 = z ^ (z >> 31)

    s = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    z = s
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let s3 = z ^ (z >> 31)

    Xoshiro256 { s0: s0, s1: s1, s2: s2, s3: s3 }
}

// =============================================================================
// Core: next_i64
// =============================================================================

fn rotl(x: i64, k: i32) -> i64 {
    (x << k) | (x >> (64 - k))
}

fn xoshiro_next_i64(rng: &!Xoshiro256) -> i64 with Mut {
    let result = rotl(rng.s1 * 5, 7) * 9

    let t = rng.s1 << 17
    rng.s2 = rng.s2 ^ rng.s0
    rng.s3 = rng.s3 ^ rng.s1
    rng.s1 = rng.s1 ^ rng.s2
    rng.s0 = rng.s0 ^ rng.s3
    rng.s2 = rng.s2 ^ t
    rng.s3 = rotl(rng.s3, 45)

    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Uniform [0, 1) — The fundamental distribution
// =============================================================================

fn uniform(rng: &!Xoshiro256) -> f64 with Prob, Mut {
    let bits = xoshiro_next_i64(rng)
    // Use upper 53 bits for double precision
    let shifted = bits >> 11
    // Convert to f64 in [0, 1)
    // Note: i64 to f64 conversion, then divide by 2^53
    let val = (shifted as f64) * 1.1102230246251565e-16
    if val < 0.0 { 0.0 - val } else { val }
}

// Uniform in [lo, hi)
fn uniform_range(rng: &!Xoshiro256, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 with Prob, Mut {
    lo + uniform(rng) * (hi - lo)
}

// =============================================================================
// Normal (Gaussian) — Box-Muller transform
// =============================================================================

fn normal(rng: &!Xoshiro256, mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> f64 with Prob, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var u1 = uniform(rng)
    if u1 < 1.0e-10 { u1 = 1.0e-10 }
    let u2 = uniform(rng)
    let z = sqrt_rng(0.0 - 2.0 * ln_rng(u1)) * cos_rng(2.0 * 3.14159265358979323846 * u2)
    mu + sigma * z
}

// Standard normal N(0, 1)
fn standard_normal(rng: &!Xoshiro256) -> f64 with Prob, Mut, Div, Panic {
    normal(rng, 0.0, 1.0)
}

// =============================================================================
// Exponential distribution
// =============================================================================

fn exponential(rng: &!Xoshiro256, lambda: f64) -> f64 with Prob, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var u = uniform(rng)
    if u < 1.0e-10 { u = 1.0e-10 }
    (0.0 - ln_rng(u)) / lambda
}

// =============================================================================
// Bernoulli distribution
// =============================================================================

fn bernoulli(rng: &!Xoshiro256, p: f64) -> bool with Prob, Mut {
    uniform(rng) < p
}

// =============================================================================
// Discrete uniform [lo, hi] (inclusive)
// =============================================================================

fn discrete_uniform(rng: &!Xoshiro256, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> i32 with Prob, Mut, Panic {
    let range = (hi - lo + 1) as f64
    let u = uniform(rng)
    lo + (u * range) as i32
}

// =============================================================================
// Shuffle (Fisher-Yates)
// =============================================================================

fn shuffle_f64(rng: &!Xoshiro256, arr: &![f64; 1024], n: i32) with Prob, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = n - 1
    while i > 0 {
        let j = discrete_uniform(rng, 0, i)
        // Swap arr[i] and arr[j]
        let tmp = arr[i]
        arr[i] = arr[j]
        arr[j] = tmp
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Summary Statistics (for testing/validation)
// =============================================================================

struct SampleStats {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    min_val: f64,
    max_val: f64,
    n: i32,
}

fn sample_stats(samples: &[f64; 10000], n: i32) -> SampleStats with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 {
        return SampleStats { mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, min_val: 0.0, max_val: 0.0, n: 0 }
    }

    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var min_v = samples[0]
    var max_v = samples[0]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + samples[i]
        if samples[i] < min_v { min_v = samples[i] }
        if samples[i] > max_v { max_v = samples[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean = sum / (n as f64)

    var ss: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let d = samples[i] - mean
        ss = ss + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    let variance = ss / ((n - 1) as f64)

    SampleStats {
        mean: mean,
        variance: variance,
        min_val: min_v,
        max_val: max_v,
        n: n,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/regex/lib.sio ===
// stdlib/regex/lib.sio — Minimal pattern matching
//
// Supported pattern syntax:
//   .    matches any single byte
//   *    matches zero-or-more of the immediately preceding char/dot
//   ?    matches zero-or-one of the immediately preceding char/dot
//   ^    anchor to start of text (must be first character in pattern)
//   $    anchor to end of text   (must be last  character in pattern)
//   otherwise: literal byte match
//
// Fixed-size buffer API (no dynamic allocation):
//   pattern: &[u8; 64]   max pattern length 64 bytes
//   text:    &[u8; 256]  max text length 256 bytes

// =============================================================================
// Result type
// =============================================================================

struct MatchResult {
    matched: i32,   // 1 = match found, 0 = no match
    start:   i32,   // inclusive start position in text
    end:     i32,   // exclusive end position in text
}

// =============================================================================
// Internal helpers — must precede callers
// =============================================================================

// Returns 1 if pattern byte at pi matches text byte at ti
fn byte_matches(pat: &[u8; 64], pi: i32, txt: &[u8; 256], ti: i32) -> i32 {
    let p: u8 = pat[pi as usize]
    if p == 46 { return 1 }    // '.' matches anything
    let t: u8 = txt[ti as usize]
    if p == t { return 1 }
    0
}

// Try to match pattern[pi..pat_len) against text[ti..text_len).
// Returns end position (exclusive) on success, -1 on failure.
// Handles . * ? ^ $ anchoring.
fn match_here(pat: &[u8; 64], pi: i32, pat_len: i32,
              txt: &[u8; 256], ti: i32, text_len: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // Base case: pattern exhausted → match succeeds at current ti
    if pi >= pat_len { return ti }

    // $ anchor: pattern ends here, text must also end here
    let pc: u8 = pat[pi as usize]
    if pc == 36 {       // '$'
        if pi + 1 == pat_len {
            if ti == text_len { return ti }
            return -1
        }
    }

    // Look-ahead for * or ?
    let next_pi = pi + 1
    let has_next: i32 = if next_pi < pat_len { 1 } else { 0 }
    let next_pc: u8 = if has_next == 1 { pat[next_pi as usize] } else { 0 }

    // '*' quantifier: zero or more
    if has_next == 1 && next_pc == 42 {     // '*'
        // Try zero repetitions first (skip both pattern char and '*')
        let zero_result = match_here(pat, pi + 2, pat_len, txt, ti, text_len)
        if zero_result >= 0 { return zero_result }
        // Try one-or-more repetitions
        var cur = ti
        while cur < text_len && byte_matches(pat, pi, txt, cur) == 1 {
            cur = cur + 1
            let r = match_here(pat, pi + 2, pat_len, txt, cur, text_len)
            if r >= 0 { return r }
        }
        return -1
    }

    // '?' quantifier: zero or one
    if has_next == 1 && next_pc == 63 {     // '?'
        // Try one match
        if ti < text_len && byte_matches(pat, pi, txt, ti) == 1 {
            let r = match_here(pat, pi + 2, pat_len, txt, ti + 1, text_len)
            if r >= 0 { return r }
        }
        // Try zero match
        return match_here(pat, pi + 2, pat_len, txt, ti, text_len)
    }

    // Literal or dot (no quantifier)
    if ti < text_len && byte_matches(pat, pi, txt, ti) == 1 {
        return match_here(pat, pi + 1, pat_len, txt, ti + 1, text_len)
    }
    -1
}

// =============================================================================
// Public API
// =============================================================================

// regex_match — find first (leftmost) match of pattern in text.
fn regex_match(pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32,
               text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32) -> MatchResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var pi_start = 0
    var anchored = 0

    // Check for ^ anchor
    if pat_len > 0 {
        let first: u8 = pattern[0]
        if first == 94 {    // '^'
            anchored = 1
            pi_start = 1
        }
    }

    if anchored == 1 {
        let end = match_here(pattern, pi_start, pat_len, text, 0, text_len)
        if end >= 0 {
            return MatchResult { matched: 1, start: 0, end: end }
        }
        return MatchResult { matched: 0, start: 0, end: 0 }
    }

    // Unanchored: try each start position
    var start = 0
    while start <= text_len {
        let end = match_here(pattern, 0, pat_len, text, start, text_len)
        if end >= 0 {
            return MatchResult { matched: 1, start: start, end: end }
        }
        start = start + 1
    }
    MatchResult { matched: 0, start: 0, end: 0 }
}

// regex_match_full — entire text must match pattern (implicitly anchored ^ and $).
fn regex_match_full(pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32,
                    text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32) -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // Build anchored pattern: ^ + original + $
    var anchpat: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    anchpat[0] = 94    // '^'
    var i = 0
    while i < pat_len && i < 62 {
        anchpat[i + 1] = pattern[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let dol_pos = i + 1
    anchpat[dol_pos] = 36    // '$'
    let anchlen = dol_pos + 1

    let r = regex_match(&anchpat, anchlen, text, text_len)
    r.matched == 1
}

// regex_count — count non-overlapping matches.
fn regex_count(pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32,
               text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var count = 0
    var pos = 0
    while pos <= text_len {
        // Try matching at pos by building a sub-view via offset
        // We use a scratch buffer for the remaining text slice
        var sub: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
        var j = 0
        let sublen = text_len - pos
        while j < sublen {
            sub[j] = text[(pos + j) as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let r = regex_match(pattern, pat_len, &sub, sublen)
        if r.matched == 1 {
            count = count + 1
            // Advance past this match (avoid infinite loop on zero-length match)
            let advance = if r.end > r.start { r.end } else { 1 }
            pos = pos + advance
        } else {
            pos = pos + 1
        }
    }
    count
}

// glob_match — shell-style glob: '*' matches any sequence, '?' matches any single char.
// Returns true if the entire text is covered by the pattern.
fn glob_match(pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32,
              text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32) -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // dp table: dp[ti] = 1 if text[0..ti] can be matched by pattern[0..current_pi]
    var dp: [i32; 257] = [0; 257]
    dp[0] = 1

    // Handle leading '*' patterns that can match empty text prefix
    var pi = 0
    while pi < pat_len {
        let pc: u8 = pattern[pi]
        if pc != 42 { break }    // '*'
        dp[0] = 1
        pi = pi + 1
    }

    // Reset pi to 0 and do full DP
    // Standard DP for glob matching
    var dp2: [i32; 257] = [0; 257]
    dp2[0] = 1

    var p = 0
    while p < pat_len {
        var next_dp: [i32; 257] = [0; 257]
        let pc: u8 = pattern[p]

        if pc == 42 {    // '*' matches any sequence (including empty)
            // next_dp[t] = dp2[t] (match empty) OR next_dp[t-1] (extend match)
            var t = 0
            while t <= text_len {
                if dp2[t] == 1 { next_dp[t] = 1 }
                t = t + 1
            }
            // propagate forward: if next_dp[t] then next_dp[t+1]
            t = 0
            while t < text_len {
                if next_dp[t] == 1 { next_dp[t + 1] = 1 }
                t = t + 1
            }
        } else {
            // '?' or literal
            var t = 1
            while t <= text_len {
                if dp2[t - 1] == 1 {
                    let matches: i32 = if pc == 63 {
                        1    // '?' matches anything
                    } else {
                        let tc: u8 = text[(t - 1) as usize]
                        if pc == tc { 1 } else { 0 }
                    }
                    if matches == 1 { next_dp[t] = 1 }
                }
                t = t + 1
            }
        }

        // Copy next_dp → dp2
        var t = 0
        while t <= text_len {
            dp2[t] = next_dp[t]
            t = t + 1
        }

        p = p + 1
    }

    dp2[text_len] == 1
}


// === FILE: stdlib/regex/mod.sio ===
// stdlib/regex — Pattern matching utilities
//
// Main implementation: regex/lib.sio (regex_match, glob_match, regex_count)
// Simple literal-only functions below for basic use cases.

fn regex_match_literal(text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32, pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if text_len != pat_len { return false }
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < text_len {
        if text[i] != pattern[i] { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}

fn regex_find_literal(text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32, pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if pat_len <= 0 { return 0 }
    if pat_len > text_len { return 0 - 1 }

    var i: i32 = 0
    let limit = text_len - pat_len + 1
    while i < limit {
        var j: i32 = 0
        var matched = true
        while j < pat_len && matched {
            if text[i + j] != pattern[j] { matched = false }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if matched { return i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0 - 1
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_literal_match() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var text: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var pat: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    text[0] = 97
    text[1] = 98
    text[2] = 99
    pat[0] = 97
    pat[1] = 98
    pat[2] = 99
    regex_match_literal(&text, 3, &pat, 3)
}

fn test_find_literal() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var text: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var pat: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    // "hello world" find "world"
    text[0] = 104
    text[1] = 101
    text[2] = 108
    text[3] = 108
    text[4] = 111
    text[5] = 32
    text[6] = 119
    text[7] = 111
    text[8] = 114
    text[9] = 108
    text[10] = 100
    pat[0] = 119
    pat[1] = 111
    pat[2] = 114
    pat[3] = 108
    pat[4] = 100
    regex_find_literal(&text, 11, &pat, 5) == 6
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    if test_literal_match() { print("regex literal_match: PASS\n") } else { print("regex literal_match: FAIL\n") }
    if test_find_literal() { print("regex find_literal: PASS\n") } else { print("regex find_literal: FAIL\n") }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/regulatory/eu_aiact.sio ===
// stdlib/regulatory/eu_aiact.sio
//
// EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) compliance surface.
//
// Key provisions operationalized here:
//
//   Art. 5 — Prohibited AI practices.  Requires structural containment
//            of capabilities that fall under the prohibition list.
//            Desugars to: CapabilityGated<T> with ZD + Audited<T>
//            with ZD, Witness to emit the containment proof.
//
//   Art. 10 — Data and data governance for high-risk systems.
//             Requires "appropriate data governance and management
//             practices".  Desugars to ExactlyPrivate<T> with ZD for
//             erasure events and Audited<T> with ZD, Witness for the
//             derivation of their correctness.
//
//   Art. 15 — Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity.  The "robustness"
//             requirement has no obvious ZD-level translation in this
//             module; we restrict attention to Art. 5 and Art. 10.
//
// All functions require  with ZD, Witness.

// eu_aiact_capability_contained: operational predicate for Art. 5
// containment.  Given the post-containment danger-accuracy and the
// chance-level accuracy (1/N for an N-way task), returns true iff
// the danger-accuracy is within `delta` of chance.  Paper C's
// zd_capability_removal benchmark achieves danger-accuracy exactly at
// chance (50.5% for a 2-way task), so `delta = 0.02` is the canonical
// compliance threshold.
fn eu_aiact_capability_contained(post_danger_acc: f64,
                                  chance_level: f64,
                                  delta: f64) -> bool with Mut, ZD, Witness {
    let diff = post_danger_acc - chance_level
    let abs_diff = if diff < 0.0 { 0.0 - diff } else { diff }
    abs_diff <= delta
}

// eu_aiact_benign_preserved: Art. 5 also requires preservation of
// beneficial capabilities; drop by more than `drop_tolerance` is a
// non-compliance signal.
fn eu_aiact_benign_preserved(pre_benign_acc: f64,
                              post_benign_acc: f64,
                              drop_tolerance: f64) -> bool with Mut, ZD, Witness {
    let drop = pre_benign_acc - post_benign_acc
    drop <= drop_tolerance
}

// eu_aiact_art5_witness_header: regulatory citation header for Art. 5
// containment operations.
fn eu_aiact_art5_witness_header() with IO, Mut, ZD, Witness {
    print("[audit] regulation=EU-AI-Act-Art5 surgical_op=gate\n")
    print("[audit] witness=capability_removal_preserves_complement\n")
    print("[audit] danger_tolerance=0.02 benign_tolerance=0.02\n")
}

// eu_aiact_art10_witness_header: regulatory citation header for Art. 10
// data-governance erasure operations.
fn eu_aiact_art10_witness_header() with IO, Mut, ZD, Witness {
    print("[audit] regulation=EU-AI-Act-Art10 surgical_op=unlearn\n")
    print("[audit] witness=unlearning_kernel_exact\n")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/regulatory/gdpr.sio ===
// stdlib/regulatory/gdpr.sio
//
// GDPR Article 17 ("Right to erasure / Right to be forgotten")
// compliance surface, realized as library-level desugars on top of
// Sounio's surgical-intervention types.
//
// Legal text (GDPR Art. 17, paraphrase):
//   "The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the
//    controller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her
//    without undue delay, and the controller shall have the
//    obligation to erase personal data without undue delay."
//
// Operational translation used by this module:
//   A GDPR-compliant erasure is a surgical operation of type
//   ExactlyPrivate<T> with ZD, coupled with an audit trail of type
//   Audited<T> with ZD, Witness.  Both effects together enforce:
//     1. Exact removal   (algebraic zeroing, not epsilon-close)
//     2. Machine-checkable derivation of the removal
//
// Required effects to call any function in this module:
//   with ZD, Witness
//
// Jurisprudence:
//   - Art. 17(1) — the right itself
//   - Art. 17(3) — exceptions (freedom of expression, public interest)
//     NOT handled here; downstream gating is out of scope
//   - Recital 65 — context of the right, especially the "without undue
//     delay" obligation that makes post-hoc retraining impractical.

// gdpr_erase_residual: the operational compliance metric for
// GDPR Art. 17. Given a weight vector w and a reference w_never_trained
// (what the model would look like had the data subject never contributed),
// the compliance holds iff the L2 residual is fp-exact zero.
fn gdpr_erase_residual(w_forgotten: &[f64; 16],
                       w_reference: &[f64; 16]) -> f64 with Mut, ZD, Witness {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        let d = (*w_forgotten)[i] - (*w_reference)[i]
        s = s + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    s
}

// gdpr_art17_compliant: a boolean predicate over the residual.
// Returns true iff residual < 1e-10, the fp-exact threshold matching
// the Lean `native_decide` discharge condition on unlearning_kernel_exact.
fn gdpr_art17_compliant(residual: f64) -> bool with Mut, ZD, Witness {
    residual < 0.0000000001 && residual > 0.0 - 0.0000000001
}

// gdpr_art17_witness_header: emit the regulatory-citation header that
// the Sounio audit harness embeds into the Lean witness for a GDPR
// Art.17 operation.  This is what downstream auditors grep for.
fn gdpr_art17_witness_header() with IO, Mut, ZD, Witness {
    print("[audit] regulation=GDPR-Art17 surgical_op=unlearn\n")
    print("[audit] witness=unlearning_kernel_exact\n")
    print("[audit] compliance_threshold=1e-10\n")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/regulatory/hipaa.sio ===
// stdlib/regulatory/hipaa.sio
//
// HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, 1996)
// Privacy Rule compliance surface for Sounio-compiled ML systems.
//
// Relevant provisions:
//   - 45 CFR §164.502 — General rules for uses and disclosures of PHI
//   - 45 CFR §164.514 — De-identification requirements
//   - §164.514(b)(2) — Safe Harbor: 18 categories of identifier removal
//
// HIPAA's de-identification standard is more restrictive than GDPR in
// two ways:
//   1. Composability.  Datasets combined across hospital systems must
//      remain de-identified post-merge.  This maps directly onto
//      Composable<T>: the ZD-orthogonal merge preserves the kernel
//      projection of every component exactly.
//   2. Auditability.  The Safe Harbor standard requires documentation;
//      Audited<T> provides a Lean witness for every de-identification
//      operation.
//
// Required effects for this module: with ZD, Witness
// (Composable<T> ops additionally require ZD alone, so those are
// a subset.)

// hipaa_deidentification_complete: predicate for whether all 18 Safe
// Harbor categories have their contribution algebraically zeroed from
// the weight vector.  For a toy model we index 0..17 into the first
// 18 dimensions of a 32-dim weight buffer; a real deployment encodes
// each category in a disjoint ZD-kernel subspace.
fn hipaa_deidentification_complete(w: &[f64; 32]) -> bool with Mut, ZD, Witness {
    var all_zero = true
    var i = 0
    while i < 18 {
        let v = (*w)[i as usize]
        let a = if v < 0.0 { 0.0 - v } else { v }
        if a > 0.0000000001 { all_zero = false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    all_zero
}

// hipaa_crossinstitution_merge_safe: check that a merged dataset
// stays de-identified.  Both contributors must have their Safe Harbor
// categories zeroed AND the merge must be ZD-orthogonal; since the
// algorithmic guarantee of Composable<T> is preservation in the ZD
// complement, the predicate here reduces to checking both inputs.
fn hipaa_crossinstitution_merge_safe(w_a: &[f64; 32],
                                      w_b: &[f64; 32]) -> bool with Mut, ZD, Witness {
    hipaa_deidentification_complete(w_a) &&
    hipaa_deidentification_complete(w_b)
}

// hipaa_safeharbor_witness_header: emit the regulatory citation that
// downstream auditors grep for.
fn hipaa_safeharbor_witness_header() with IO, Mut, ZD, Witness {
    print("[audit] regulation=HIPAA-SafeHarbor surgical_op=unlearn+compose\n")
    print("[audit] witness=unlearning_kernel_exact+composition_preserves_orthogonal_complement\n")
    print("[audit] safe_harbor_categories=18\n")
}

// === FILE: stdlib/render/framebuffer.sio ===
// Software framebuffer for PPM rendering
//
// Uses flat [i64; 196608] arrays for R, G, B channels (256x256 max).
// Each pixel stores 0-255 integer color value.
// Output via PPM P3 text format to stdout.

// Max framebuffer size: 256x256 = 65536 pixels
// Each channel is a separate array to avoid struct-of-arrays complexity

struct Framebuffer {
    width: i64,
    height: i64,
    r: [i64; 65536],
    g: [i64; 65536],
    b: [i64; 65536],
    depth: [f64; 65536],
}

fn fb_new(w: i64, h: i64) -> Framebuffer {
    Framebuffer {
        width: w,
        height: h,
        r: [0; 65536],
        g: [0; 65536],
        b: [0; 65536],
        depth: [1000000.0; 65536],
    }
}

fn fb_set_pixel(fb: &!Framebuffer, x: i64, y: i64, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < (*fb).width && y >= 0 && y < (*fb).height {
        let idx = y * (*fb).width + x
        (*fb).r[idx] = r
        (*fb).g[idx] = g
        (*fb).b[idx] = b
    }
}

fn fb_set_pixel_depth(fb: &!Framebuffer, x: i64, y: i64, z: f64, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < (*fb).width && y >= 0 && y < (*fb).height {
        let idx = y * (*fb).width + x
        if z < (*fb).depth[idx] {
            (*fb).r[idx] = r
            (*fb).g[idx] = g
            (*fb).b[idx] = b
            (*fb).depth[idx] = z
        }
    }
}

fn fb_clear(fb: &!Framebuffer, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    let total = (*fb).width * (*fb).height
    while i < total {
        (*fb).r[i] = r
        (*fb).g[i] = g
        (*fb).b[i] = b
        (*fb).depth[i] = 1000000.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn clamp_byte(v: i64) -> i64 {
    if v < 0 { return 0 }
    if v > 255 { return 255 }
    v
}

fn float_to_byte(f: f64) -> i64 {
    let v = (f * 255.0) as i64
    clamp_byte(v)
}

// Emit PPM P3 header + pixels to stdout
fn fb_emit_ppm(fb: &Framebuffer) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("P3\n")
    print_int((*fb).width)
    print(" ")
    print_int((*fb).height)
    print("\n255\n")

    var y: i64 = 0
    while y < (*fb).height {
        var x: i64 = 0
        while x < (*fb).width {
            let idx = y * (*fb).width + x
            print_int(clamp_byte((*fb).r[idx]))
            print(" ")
            print_int(clamp_byte((*fb).g[idx]))
            print(" ")
            print_int(clamp_byte((*fb).b[idx]))
            print("\n")
            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    0
}
