// === FILE: stdlib/render/rasterizer.sio ===
// Software triangle rasterizer using barycentric coordinates
//
// Implements scanline triangle fill with per-pixel color interpolation.
// Supports z-buffer depth testing for correct occlusion.

struct Vec3 { x: f64, y: f64, z: f64 }
struct Color { r: f64, g: f64, b: f64, a: f64 }
struct Vertex2D { x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, r: f64, g: f64, b: f64 }

fn min_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn max_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// Edge function for barycentric coordinates
// Positive = left side, negative = right side
fn edge_fn(ax: f64, ay: f64, bx: f64, by: f64, cx: f64, cy: f64) -> f64 {
    (cx - ax) * (by - ay) - (cy - ay) * (bx - ax)
}

// Rasterize a single triangle into a framebuffer (flat arrays)
// Returns number of pixels written
fn rasterize_triangle(
    v0: Vertex2D, v1: Vertex2D, v2: Vertex2D,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536], fb_g: &![i64; 65536], fb_b: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_depth: &![f64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Bounding box
    let min_x = max_i64(0, (min_f64(min_f64(v0.x, v1.x), v2.x)) as i64)
    let max_x = min_i64(fb_w - 1, (max_f64(max_f64(v0.x, v1.x), v2.x)) as i64 + 1)
    let min_y = max_i64(0, (min_f64(min_f64(v0.y, v1.y), v2.y)) as i64)
    let max_y = min_i64(fb_h - 1, (max_f64(max_f64(v0.y, v1.y), v2.y)) as i64 + 1)

    let area = edge_fn(v0.x, v0.y, v1.x, v1.y, v2.x, v2.y)
    if area == 0.0 { return 0 }  // degenerate triangle

    var pixels_written: i64 = 0
    var py: i64 = min_y
    while py <= max_y {
        var px: i64 = min_x
        while px <= max_x {
            let cx = (px as f64) + 0.5
            let cy = (py as f64) + 0.5

            let w0 = edge_fn(v1.x, v1.y, v2.x, v2.y, cx, cy)
            let w1 = edge_fn(v2.x, v2.y, v0.x, v0.y, cx, cy)
            let w2 = edge_fn(v0.x, v0.y, v1.x, v1.y, cx, cy)

            // Inside triangle if all same sign as area
            let inside = if area > 0.0 {
                w0 >= 0.0 && w1 >= 0.0 && w2 >= 0.0
            } else {
                w0 <= 0.0 && w1 <= 0.0 && w2 <= 0.0
            }

            if inside {
                // Barycentric interpolation
                let b0 = w0 / area
                let b1 = w1 / area
                let b2 = w2 / area

                // Interpolate depth
                let z = b0 * v0.z + b1 * v1.z + b2 * v2.z

                let idx = py * fb_w + px
                if z < (*fb_depth)[idx] {
                    // Interpolate color
                    let r = b0 * v0.r + b1 * v1.r + b2 * v2.r
                    let g = b0 * v0.g + b1 * v1.g + b2 * v2.g
                    let b_col = b0 * v0.b + b1 * v1.b + b2 * v2.b

                    (*fb_r)[idx] = (r * 255.0) as i64
                    (*fb_g)[idx] = (g * 255.0) as i64
                    (*fb_b)[idx] = (b_col * 255.0) as i64
                    (*fb_depth)[idx] = z
                    pixels_written = pixels_written + 1
                }
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }
    pixels_written
}

// Draw a line (Bresenham) into flat framebuffer arrays
fn rasterize_line(
    x0: i64, y0: i64, x1: i64, y1: i64,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536], fb_g: &![i64; 65536], fb_b: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var cx: i64 = x0
    var cy: i64 = y0
    var dx: i64 = x1 - x0
    var dy: i64 = y1 - y0
    if dx < 0 { dx = 0 - dx }
    if dy < 0 { dy = 0 - dy }
    let sx: i64 = if x0 < x1 { 1 } else { 0 - 1 }
    let sy: i64 = if y0 < y1 { 1 } else { 0 - 1 }
    var err: i64 = dx - dy

    var steps: i64 = 0
    let max_steps = dx + dy + 1
    while steps < max_steps {
        if cx >= 0 && cx < fb_w && cy >= 0 && cy < fb_h {
            let idx = cy * fb_w + cx
            (*fb_r)[idx] = r
            (*fb_g)[idx] = g
            (*fb_b)[idx] = b
        }
        if cx == x1 && cy == y1 { steps = max_steps }
        let e2 = err * 2
        if e2 > (0 - dy) {
            err = err - dy
            cx = cx + sx
        }
        if e2 < dx {
            err = err + dx
            cy = cy + sy
        }
        steps = steps + 1
    }
}

fn rasterize_rect(
    x0: i64, y0: i64, rw: i64, rh: i64,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536], fb_g: &![i64; 65536], fb_b: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var dy: i64 = 0
    while dy < rh {
        var dx: i64 = 0
        while dx < rw {
            let px = x0 + dx
            let py = y0 + dy
            if px >= 0 && px < fb_w && py >= 0 && py < fb_h {
                let idx = py * fb_w + px
                (*fb_r)[idx] = r
                (*fb_g)[idx] = g
                (*fb_b)[idx] = b
            }
            dx = dx + 1
        }
        dy = dy + 1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/render/renderer3d.sio ===
// stdlib/render/renderer3d.sio — Software 3D renderer into a Canvas
//
// Self-contained: defines Camera3D / Light3D / Tri3D types (independent of
// the stub-only render/types.sio and render/scene.sio, which have fn main()
// stubs and no pub exports).
//
// Pipeline per triangle:
//   1. Model→View: rotate/translate vertices (caller supplies pre-transformed verts)
//   2. Perspective projection via project_vertex
//   3. Barycentric rasterization with depth test into a per-call depth buffer
//   4. Blinn-Phong shading: ambient + diffuse + specular^32
//   5. Output via canvas_fill_triangle (solid per-triangle colour) + edge lines

use display::canvas::{Canvas}
use display::canvas_ext::{canvas_fill_triangle, canvas_draw_line_aa}

// ============================================================
// Types
// ============================================================

pub struct Vec3f { pub x: f64, pub y: f64, pub z: f64 }

pub struct Camera3D {
    pub pos_x: f64, pub pos_y: f64, pub pos_z: f64,
    pub focal: f64,    // focal length in pixels
}

pub struct Light3D {
    pub dx: f64, pub dy: f64, pub dz: f64,  // normalised direction toward light
    pub r: i64, pub g: i64, pub b: i64,     // light colour (0-255)
    pub ambient: f64,                        // ambient coefficient [0,1]
}

// Linear depth fog: blends shaded colour toward a background colour over [near, far] depth range.
pub struct FogParams {
    pub near: f64, pub far: f64,
    pub r: i64, pub g: i64, pub b: i64,
}

// A triangle in world/view space.
// v0/v1/v2 are (x,y,z) positions; nx/ny/nz is the face normal (unit length).
// base_r/g/b is the material diffuse colour.
pub struct Tri3D {
    pub v0x: f64, pub v0y: f64, pub v0z: f64,
    pub v1x: f64, pub v1y: f64, pub v1z: f64,
    pub v2x: f64, pub v2y: f64, pub v2z: f64,
    pub nx:  f64, pub ny:  f64, pub nz:  f64,
    pub base_r: i64, pub base_g: i64, pub base_b: i64,
}

// ============================================================
// Internal math helpers
// ============================================================

fn r3d_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn r3d_max_f(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn r3d_min_i(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn r3d_max_i(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn r3d_clamp_i(v: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 { if v < lo { lo } else if v > hi { hi } else { v } }

fn r3d_dot(ax: f64, ay: f64, az: f64, bx: f64, by: f64, bz: f64) -> f64 {
    ax * bx + ay * by + az * bz
}

fn r3d_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// Normalise a direction vector; returns components via out-params encoded in a Vec3f.
pub fn r3d_normalise(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Vec3f with Mut, Div {
    let len = r3d_sqrt(x * x + y * y + z * z)
    if len == 0.0 {
        Vec3f { x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 1.0 }
    } else {
        Vec3f { x: x / len, y: y / len, z: z / len }
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Projection
// ============================================================

// Projects a 3D point onto the canvas using a simple perspective model.
// Returns (screen_x, screen_y, depth). depth <= 0 means behind camera.
pub fn r3d_project(wx: f64, wy: f64, wz: f64, cam: &Camera3D, cw: i64, ch: i64) -> Vec3f with Div {
    let rz = wz - cam.pos_z
    if rz >= 0.0 {
        // Behind or at camera plane — signal with depth = 0
        return Vec3f { x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0 }
    }
    let depth = 0.0 - rz      // positive depth
    let scale = cam.focal / depth
    let sx = (wx - cam.pos_x) * scale + (cw as f64) * 0.5
    let sy = (0.0 - (wy - cam.pos_y)) * scale + (ch as f64) * 0.5
    Vec3f { x: sx, y: sy, z: depth }
}

fn r3d_project_viewport(wx: f64, wy: f64, wz: f64, cam: &Camera3D, vx: i64, vy: i64, vw: i64, vh: i64) -> Vec3f with Div {
    let rz = wz - cam.pos_z
    if rz >= 0.0 {
        return Vec3f { x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0 }
    }
    let depth = 0.0 - rz
    let scale = cam.focal / depth
    let sx = (wx - cam.pos_x) * scale + (vx as f64) + (vw as f64) * 0.5
    let sy = (0.0 - (wy - cam.pos_y)) * scale + (vy as f64) + (vh as f64) * 0.5
    Vec3f { x: sx, y: sy, z: depth }
}

// ============================================================
// Shading
// ============================================================

pub fn r3d_shade(
    base_r: i64, base_g: i64, base_b: i64,
    nx: f64, ny: f64, nz: f64,
    light: &Light3D,
) -> Vec3f with Mut, Div {
    let nl = r3d_normalise(nx, ny, nz)
    let diffuse = r3d_max_f(r3d_dot(nl.x, nl.y, nl.z, light.dx, light.dy, light.dz), 0.0)
    let intensity = light.ambient + (1.0 - light.ambient) * diffuse

    // Blinn-Phong specular: H = normalize(L + V), V = (0,0,1) toward camera.
    let hx_u = light.dx
    let hy_u = light.dy
    let hz_u = light.dz + 1.0
    let h_len = r3d_sqrt(hx_u * hx_u + hy_u * hy_u + hz_u * hz_u)
    let ndoth = if h_len > 0.0 {
        r3d_max_f(nl.x * (hx_u / h_len) + nl.y * (hy_u / h_len) + nl.z * (hz_u / h_len), 0.0)
    } else { 0.0 }
    let s2 = ndoth * ndoth
    let s4 = s2 * s2
    let s8 = s4 * s4
    let s32 = s8 * s8 * s8 * s8   // ^32
    let spec = 0.85 * s32

    let fr = base_r as f64 * intensity + 255.0 * spec
    let fg = base_g as f64 * intensity + 255.0 * spec
    let fb = base_b as f64 * intensity + 255.0 * spec
    let sr = r3d_clamp_i(fr as i64, 0, 255)
    let sg = r3d_clamp_i(fg as i64, 0, 255)
    let sb = r3d_clamp_i(fb as i64, 0, 255)
    // Pack into Vec3f channels re-used as i64 via cast (R=x, G=y, B=z)
    Vec3f { x: sr as f64, y: sg as f64, z: sb as f64 }
}

// ============================================================
// Depth buffer (flat heap-allocated f64 array, one entry per pixel)
// ============================================================

pub fn r3d_depth_buf_alloc(w: i64, h: i64) -> *mut i64 with Alloc {
    // We store depth as i64 bit-pattern of f64; caller casts.
    heap_alloc(w * h * 8) as *mut i64
}

pub fn r3d_depth_buf_clear(buf: *mut i64, w: i64, h: i64) with Mut {
    // Write +infinity (0x7FF0000000000000 = +Inf as IEEE 754 double) to all entries.
    let pos_inf_bits: i64 = 0x7FF0000000000000
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < w * h {
        write_i64(buf, i, pos_inf_bits)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Rasterize one triangle into the canvas with depth test
// ============================================================

fn r3d_edge(ax: i64, ay: i64, bx: i64, by: i64, cx: i64, cy: i64) -> i64 {
    (cx - ax) * (by - ay) - (cy - ay) * (bx - ax)
}

fn r3d_rasterize_tri(
    sx0: i64, sy0: i64,
    sx1: i64, sy1: i64,
    sx2: i64, sy2: i64,
    d0: f64, d1: f64, d2: f64,
    cr: i64, cg: i64, cb: i64,
    depth_buf: *mut i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
) with Mut {
    let area = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2)
    if area == 0 { return }

    let min_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, c.width - 1)
    let max_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, c.width - 1)
    let min_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, c.height - 1)
    let max_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, c.height - 1)
    let color = cb | (cg << 8) | (cr << 16)

    var py = min_y
    while py <= max_y {
        var px = min_x
        while px <= max_x {
            let w0 = r3d_edge(sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2, px, py)
            let w1 = r3d_edge(sx2, sy2, sx0, sy0, px, py)
            let w2 = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, px, py)
            let inside = if area > 0 {
                w0 >= 0 && w1 >= 0 && w2 >= 0
            } else {
                w0 <= 0 && w1 <= 0 && w2 <= 0
            }
            if inside {
                let idx = py * c.width + px
                // Depth interpolation (perspective-correct approximation)
                let area_f = area as f64
                let b0 = (w0 as f64) / area_f
                let b1 = (w1 as f64) / area_f
                let b2 = (w2 as f64) / area_f
                let depth = b0 * d0 + b1 * d1 + b2 * d2
                // Compare against stored depth (re-interpret bits)
                let stored_bits = read_i64(depth_buf, idx)
                // Treat stored_bits as f64 bit pattern for comparison.
                // Since depth > 0 and we use IEEE 754, bit comparison holds for positives.
                let depth_bits = depth as i64  // approximate: cast f64→i64 for comparison
                if depth_bits < stored_bits {
                    write_i64(depth_buf, idx, depth_bits)
                    write_i64(c.pixels, idx, color)
                }
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }
}

fn r3d_fog_factor(depth: f64, fog: &FogParams) -> f64 with Div {
    if fog.far == fog.near { return 0.0 }
    let f = (depth - fog.near) / (fog.far - fog.near)
    if f < 0.0 { 0.0 } else if f > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { f }
}

// Gouraud rasterize — per-vertex colours c0/c1/c2, each Vec3f{x=R,y=G,z=B} in [0,255].
// Barycentric interpolation gives smooth shading gradients within the face.
pub fn r3d_rasterize_tri_gouraud(
    sx0: i64, sy0: i64,
    sx1: i64, sy1: i64,
    sx2: i64, sy2: i64,
    d0: f64, d1: f64, d2: f64,
    c0: Vec3f, c1: Vec3f, c2: Vec3f,
    depth_buf: *mut i64,
    cv: &!Canvas,
) with Mut, Div {
    let area = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2)
    if area == 0 { return }
    let min_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, cv.width - 1)
    let max_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, cv.width - 1)
    let min_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, cv.height - 1)
    let max_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, cv.height - 1)
    var py = min_y
    while py <= max_y {
        var px = min_x
        while px <= max_x {
            let w0 = r3d_edge(sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2, px, py)
            let w1 = r3d_edge(sx2, sy2, sx0, sy0, px, py)
            let w2 = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, px, py)
            let inside = if area > 0 {
                w0 >= 0 && w1 >= 0 && w2 >= 0
            } else {
                w0 <= 0 && w1 <= 0 && w2 <= 0
            }
            if inside {
                let idx = py * cv.width + px
                let area_f = area as f64
                let bw0 = (w0 as f64) / area_f
                let bw1 = (w1 as f64) / area_f
                let bw2 = (w2 as f64) / area_f
                let depth = bw0 * d0 + bw1 * d1 + bw2 * d2
                let stored = read_i64(depth_buf, idx)
                let dbits = depth as i64
                if dbits < stored {
                    write_i64(depth_buf, idx, dbits)
                    let fr = bw0 * c0.x + bw1 * c1.x + bw2 * c2.x
                    let fg = bw0 * c0.y + bw1 * c1.y + bw2 * c2.y
                    let fb = bw0 * c0.z + bw1 * c1.z + bw2 * c2.z
                    let pr = r3d_clamp_i(fr as i64, 0, 255)
                    let pg = r3d_clamp_i(fg as i64, 0, 255)
                    let pb = r3d_clamp_i(fb as i64, 0, 255)
                    write_i64(cv.pixels, idx, pb | (pg << 8) | (pr << 16))
                }
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }
}

// Phong rasterize — interpolates vertex normals per-pixel, shades with Blinn-Phong, applies
// linear depth fog. Produces sharper highlights than Gouraud at the cost of ~10 extra ops/px.
pub fn r3d_rasterize_tri_phong(
    sx0: i64, sy0: i64,
    sx1: i64, sy1: i64,
    sx2: i64, sy2: i64,
    d0: f64, d1: f64, d2: f64,
    n0: Vec3f, n1: Vec3f, n2: Vec3f,
    base_r: i64, base_g: i64, base_b: i64,
    fog: &FogParams,
    light: &Light3D,
    depth_buf: *mut i64,
    cv: &!Canvas,
) with Mut, Div {
    let area = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2)
    if area == 0 { return }
    let min_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, cv.width - 1)
    let max_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, cv.width - 1)
    let min_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, cv.height - 1)
    let max_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, cv.height - 1)
    var py = min_y
    while py <= max_y {
        var px = min_x
        while px <= max_x {
            let w0 = r3d_edge(sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2, px, py)
            let w1 = r3d_edge(sx2, sy2, sx0, sy0, px, py)
            let w2 = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, px, py)
            let inside = if area > 0 {
                w0 >= 0 && w1 >= 0 && w2 >= 0
            } else {
                w0 <= 0 && w1 <= 0 && w2 <= 0
            }
            if inside {
                let idx = py * cv.width + px
                let area_f = area as f64
                let bw0 = (w0 as f64) / area_f
                let bw1 = (w1 as f64) / area_f
                let bw2 = (w2 as f64) / area_f
                let depth = bw0 * d0 + bw1 * d1 + bw2 * d2
                let stored = read_i64(depth_buf, idx)
                let dbits = depth as i64
                if dbits < stored {
                    write_i64(depth_buf, idx, dbits)
                    // Per-pixel normal interpolation + Blinn-Phong
                    let ni_x = bw0 * n0.x + bw1 * n1.x + bw2 * n2.x
                    let ni_y = bw0 * n0.y + bw1 * n1.y + bw2 * n2.y
                    let ni_z = bw0 * n0.z + bw1 * n1.z + bw2 * n2.z
                    let col = r3d_shade(base_r, base_g, base_b, ni_x, ni_y, ni_z, light)
                    // Linear depth fog
                    let ff = r3d_fog_factor(depth, fog)
                    let one_ff = 1.0 - ff
                    let out_r = col.x * one_ff + (fog.r as f64) * ff
                    let out_g = col.y * one_ff + (fog.g as f64) * ff
                    let out_b = col.z * one_ff + (fog.b as f64) * ff
                    let pr = r3d_clamp_i(out_r as i64, 0, 255)
                    let pg = r3d_clamp_i(out_g as i64, 0, 255)
                    let pb = r3d_clamp_i(out_b as i64, 0, 255)
                    write_i64(cv.pixels, idx, pb | (pg << 8) | (pr << 16))
                }
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Cel / toon shading
// ============================================================

// r3d_shade_cel — quantizes diffuse into 4 bands + silhouette ring.
// Silhouette: pixels whose interpolated normal faces away from the camera
// (ni_z < edge_thresh, camera along +Z) are rendered dark.
// band thresholds: 0.95 / 0.50 / 0.25 → 1.0 / 0.70 / 0.40 / ambient
pub fn r3d_shade_cel(
    base_r: i64, base_g: i64, base_b: i64,
    nx: f64, ny: f64, nz: f64,
    light: &Light3D,
) -> Vec3f with Mut, Div {
    let nl = r3d_normalise(nx, ny, nz)
    let raw = r3d_dot(nl.x, nl.y, nl.z, light.dx, light.dy, light.dz)
    let diffuse = if raw < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { raw }
    let band = if diffuse > 0.95 { 1.0 }
               else if diffuse > 0.50 { 0.70 }
               else if diffuse > 0.25 { 0.40 }
               else { light.ambient }
    // Silhouette ring: normal nearly perpendicular to eye (camera along +Z)
    let eye_dot = nl.z
    let final_band = if eye_dot < 0.28 { 0.0 } else { band }
    let fr = r3d_clamp_i((base_r as f64 * final_band) as i64, 0, 255)
    let fg = r3d_clamp_i((base_g as f64 * final_band) as i64, 0, 255)
    let fb = r3d_clamp_i((base_b as f64 * final_band) as i64, 0, 255)
    Vec3f { x: fr as f64, y: fg as f64, z: fb as f64 }
}

// r3d_rasterize_tri_cel — same rasterizer as Phong but calls r3d_shade_cel.
// No fog (cel shading looks best without depth fade).
pub fn r3d_rasterize_tri_cel(
    sx0: i64, sy0: i64,
    sx1: i64, sy1: i64,
    sx2: i64, sy2: i64,
    d0: f64, d1: f64, d2: f64,
    n0: Vec3f, n1: Vec3f, n2: Vec3f,
    base_r: i64, base_g: i64, base_b: i64,
    light: &Light3D,
    depth_buf: *mut i64,
    cv: &!Canvas,
) with Mut, Div {
    let area = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2)
    if area == 0 { return }
    let min_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, cv.width - 1)
    let max_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, cv.width - 1)
    let min_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, cv.height - 1)
    let max_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, cv.height - 1)
    var py = min_y
    while py <= max_y {
        var px = min_x
        while px <= max_x {
            let w0 = r3d_edge(sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2, px, py)
            let w1 = r3d_edge(sx2, sy2, sx0, sy0, px, py)
            let w2 = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, px, py)
            let inside = if area > 0 {
                w0 >= 0 && w1 >= 0 && w2 >= 0
            } else {
                w0 <= 0 && w1 <= 0 && w2 <= 0
            }
            if inside {
                let idx = py * cv.width + px
                let area_f = area as f64
                let bw0 = (w0 as f64) / area_f
                let bw1 = (w1 as f64) / area_f
                let bw2 = (w2 as f64) / area_f
                let depth = bw0 * d0 + bw1 * d1 + bw2 * d2
                let stored = read_i64(depth_buf, idx)
                let dbits = depth as i64
                if dbits < stored {
                    write_i64(depth_buf, idx, dbits)
                    let ni_x = bw0 * n0.x + bw1 * n1.x + bw2 * n2.x
                    let ni_y = bw0 * n0.y + bw1 * n1.y + bw2 * n2.y
                    let ni_z = bw0 * n0.z + bw1 * n1.z + bw2 * n2.z
                    let col = r3d_shade_cel(base_r, base_g, base_b, ni_x, ni_y, ni_z, light)
                    let pr = col.x as i64
                    let pg = col.y as i64
                    let pb = col.z as i64
                    write_i64(cv.pixels, idx, pb | (pg << 8) | (pr << 16))
                }
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Cook-Torrance PBR shading (Fresnel-Schlick + GGX, no G term)
// ============================================================
//
// roughness ∈ [0,1]: 0=mirror, 1=diffuse. Typical: 0.25 (metallic) .. 0.5 (plastic).
// F0=0.04 for dielectrics (non-metal atoms, plastic surfaces).
// G term omitted: error <5% for typical roughness, saves ~6 ops/pixel.

pub fn r3d_shade_pbr(
    base_r: i64, base_g: i64, base_b: i64,
    nx: f64, ny: f64, nz: f64,
    light: &Light3D,
    roughness: f64,
) -> Vec3f with Mut, Div {
    let nl = r3d_normalise(nx, ny, nz)
    let ndotl = r3d_max_f(r3d_dot(nl.x, nl.y, nl.z, light.dx, light.dy, light.dz), 0.0)
    // Half-vector H = normalize(L + V), V = (0,0,1) (camera direction)
    let hx = light.dx
    let hy = light.dy
    let hz = light.dz + 1.0
    let h_len = r3d_sqrt(hx * hx + hy * hy + hz * hz)
    let ndoth = if h_len > 0.0 {
        r3d_max_f(nl.x * (hx / h_len) + nl.y * (hy / h_len) + nl.z * (hz / h_len), 0.0)
    } else { 0.0 }
    let ndotv = r3d_max_f(nl.z, 0.0001)  // view = (0,0,1)

    // Fresnel-Schlick: F = F0 + (1-F0)*(1-ndoth)^5
    let f0: f64 = 0.04
    let q = 1.0 - ndoth
    let q2 = q * q
    let q5 = q2 * q2 * q
    let fresnel = f0 + (1.0 - f0) * q5

    // GGX normal distribution: D = α²/[π((n·h)²(α²-1)+1)²]
    let alpha = roughness * roughness
    let alpha2 = alpha * alpha
    let nh2 = ndoth * ndoth
    let d_inner = nh2 * (alpha2 - 1.0) + 1.0
    let d_inner_safe = if d_inner < 0.0001 { 0.0001 } else { d_inner }
    let ggx_d = alpha2 / (3.14159265 * d_inner_safe * d_inner_safe)

    // Specular BRDF (no G): F*D / (4*ndotl*ndotv)
    let spec_denom = 4.0 * r3d_max_f(ndotl * ndotv, 0.0001)
    let spec = (fresnel * ggx_d) / spec_denom

    // Diffuse: energy-conserving Lambertian kd*(ambient + diffuse)
    let kd = (1.0 - fresnel) * (1.0 - roughness * 0.5)
    let diff = kd * (light.ambient + (1.0 - light.ambient) * ndotl)

    let fr = r3d_clamp_i(((base_r as f64) * diff + 255.0 * spec) as i64, 0, 255)
    let fg = r3d_clamp_i(((base_g as f64) * diff + 255.0 * spec) as i64, 0, 255)
    let fb = r3d_clamp_i(((base_b as f64) * diff + 255.0 * spec) as i64, 0, 255)
    Vec3f { x: fr as f64, y: fg as f64, z: fb as f64 }
}

// r3d_rasterize_tri_pbr — same rasterizer loop as Phong but calls r3d_shade_pbr.
// roughness: material roughness ∈ [0,1].
pub fn r3d_rasterize_tri_pbr(
    sx0: i64, sy0: i64,
    sx1: i64, sy1: i64,
    sx2: i64, sy2: i64,
    d0: f64, d1: f64, d2: f64,
    n0: Vec3f, n1: Vec3f, n2: Vec3f,
    base_r: i64, base_g: i64, base_b: i64,
    roughness: f64,
    fog: &FogParams,
    light: &Light3D,
    depth_buf: *mut i64,
    cv: &!Canvas,
) with Mut, Div {
    let area = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2)
    if area == 0 { return }
    let min_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, cv.width - 1)
    let max_x = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sx0, sx1), sx2), 0, cv.width - 1)
    let min_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_min_i(r3d_min_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, cv.height - 1)
    let max_y = r3d_clamp_i(r3d_max_i(r3d_max_i(sy0, sy1), sy2), 0, cv.height - 1)
    var py = min_y
    while py <= max_y {
        var px = min_x
        while px <= max_x {
            let w0 = r3d_edge(sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2, px, py)
            let w1 = r3d_edge(sx2, sy2, sx0, sy0, px, py)
            let w2 = r3d_edge(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, px, py)
            let inside = if area > 0 {
                w0 >= 0 && w1 >= 0 && w2 >= 0
            } else {
                w0 <= 0 && w1 <= 0 && w2 <= 0
            }
            if inside {
                let idx = py * cv.width + px
                let area_f = area as f64
                let bw0 = (w0 as f64) / area_f
                let bw1 = (w1 as f64) / area_f
                let bw2 = (w2 as f64) / area_f
                let depth = bw0 * d0 + bw1 * d1 + bw2 * d2
                let stored = read_i64(depth_buf, idx)
                let dbits = depth as i64
                if dbits < stored {
                    write_i64(depth_buf, idx, dbits)
                    let ni_x = bw0 * n0.x + bw1 * n1.x + bw2 * n2.x
                    let ni_y = bw0 * n0.y + bw1 * n1.y + bw2 * n2.y
                    let ni_z = bw0 * n0.z + bw1 * n1.z + bw2 * n2.z
                    let col = r3d_shade_pbr(base_r, base_g, base_b, ni_x, ni_y, ni_z, light, roughness)
                    let ff = r3d_fog_factor(depth, fog)
                    let one_ff = 1.0 - ff
                    let out_r = col.x * one_ff + (fog.r as f64) * ff
                    let out_g = col.y * one_ff + (fog.g as f64) * ff
                    let out_b = col.z * one_ff + (fog.b as f64) * ff
                    let pr = r3d_clamp_i(out_r as i64, 0, 255)
                    let pg = r3d_clamp_i(out_g as i64, 0, 255)
                    let pb = r3d_clamp_i(out_b as i64, 0, 255)
                    write_i64(cv.pixels, idx, pb | (pg << 8) | (pr << 16))
                }
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Public API: render a list of triangles
// ============================================================

// Render up to n triangles from the tris array into canvas c.
// depth_buf must be allocated with r3d_depth_buf_alloc(c.width, c.height)
// and cleared with r3d_depth_buf_clear before each frame.
pub fn r3d_render(
    tris: &[Tri3D; 4096],
    n: i64,
    cam: &Camera3D,
    light: &Light3D,
    depth_buf: *mut i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
) with Mut, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let tri = tris[i as usize]

        // Project vertices
        let p0 = r3d_project(tri.v0x, tri.v0y, tri.v0z, cam, c.width, c.height)
        let p1 = r3d_project(tri.v1x, tri.v1y, tri.v1z, cam, c.width, c.height)
        let p2 = r3d_project(tri.v2x, tri.v2y, tri.v2z, cam, c.width, c.height)

        // Skip triangles fully behind camera
        if p0.z <= 0.0 || p1.z <= 0.0 || p2.z <= 0.0 {
            i = i + 1
            continue
        }

        // Shade
        let col = r3d_shade(tri.base_r, tri.base_g, tri.base_b, tri.nx, tri.ny, tri.nz, light)

        // Rasterize face
        r3d_rasterize_tri(
            p0.x as i64, p0.y as i64,
            p1.x as i64, p1.y as i64,
            p2.x as i64, p2.y as i64,
            p0.z, p1.z, p2.z,
            col.x as i64, col.y as i64, col.z as i64,
            depth_buf, c,
        )

        // Draw edges — dark silhouette lines for depth separation
        let er = r3d_clamp_i((col.x as i64 * 3) / 10, 0, 255)
        let eg = r3d_clamp_i((col.y as i64 * 3) / 10, 0, 255)
        let eb = r3d_clamp_i((col.z as i64 * 3) / 10, 0, 255)
        canvas_draw_line_aa(c, p0.x as i64, p0.y as i64, p1.x as i64, p1.y as i64, er, eg, eb)
        canvas_draw_line_aa(c, p1.x as i64, p1.y as i64, p2.x as i64, p2.y as i64, er, eg, eb)
        canvas_draw_line_aa(c, p2.x as i64, p2.y as i64, p0.x as i64, p0.y as i64, er, eg, eb)

        i = i + 1
    }
}

pub fn r3d_render_viewport(
    tris: &[Tri3D; 4096],
    n: i64,
    cam: &Camera3D,
    light: &Light3D,
    depth_buf: *mut i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    vx: i64, vy: i64, vw: i64, vh: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let tri = tris[i as usize]
        let p0 = r3d_project_viewport(tri.v0x, tri.v0y, tri.v0z, cam, vx, vy, vw, vh)
        let p1 = r3d_project_viewport(tri.v1x, tri.v1y, tri.v1z, cam, vx, vy, vw, vh)
        let p2 = r3d_project_viewport(tri.v2x, tri.v2y, tri.v2z, cam, vx, vy, vw, vh)

        if p0.z <= 0.0 || p1.z <= 0.0 || p2.z <= 0.0 {
            i = i + 1
            continue
        }

        let col = r3d_shade(tri.base_r, tri.base_g, tri.base_b, tri.nx, tri.ny, tri.nz, light)
        r3d_rasterize_tri(
            p0.x as i64, p0.y as i64,
            p1.x as i64, p1.y as i64,
            p2.x as i64, p2.y as i64,
            p0.z, p1.z, p2.z,
            col.x as i64, col.y as i64, col.z as i64,
            depth_buf, c,
        )
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Scene graph types for Sounio rendering pipeline

struct Camera {
    pos_x: f64,
    pos_y: f64,

    up_y: f64,
    up_z: f64,
    fov: f64,
    near: f64,
    far: f64,
}

fn camera_default() -> Camera {
    Camera {
        pos_x: 0.0, pos_y: 0.0, pos_z: 5.0,
        target_x: 0.0, target_y: 0.0, target_z: 0.0,
        up_x: 0.0, up_y: 1.0, up_z: 0.0,
        fov: 60.0,
        near: 0.1,
        far: 100.0,
    }
}

struct Light {
    pos_x: f64,
    pos_y: f64,
    pos_z: f64,
    color_r: f64,
    color_g: f64,
    color_b: f64,
    intensity: f64,
}

fn light_point(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, intensity: f64) -> Light {
    Light {
        pos_x: x, pos_y: y, pos_z: z,
        color_r: 1.0, color_g: 1.0, color_b: 1.0,
        intensity: intensity,
    }
}

struct Scene {
    triangle_count: i64,
    light_count: i64,
    camera: Camera,
}

fn scene_new() -> Scene {
    Scene {
        triangle_count: 0,
        light_count: 0,
        camera: camera_default(),
    }
}

struct ScreenPt { sx: i64, sy: i64, depth: f64 }

fn project_point3d(
    wx: f64, wy: f64, wz: f64,
    focal: f64, z_offset: f64,
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) -> ScreenPt with Div, Panic {
    let z_cam = wz + z_offset
    let scale = focal / z_cam
    ScreenPt {
        sx: (wx * scale + ((fb_w as f64) * 0.5)) as i64,
        sy: ((0.0 - wy) * scale + ((fb_h as f64) * 0.5)) as i64,
        depth: z_cam,
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    0
}

    Vec3 {
        x: a.y * b.z - a.z * b.y,
        y: a.z * b.x - a.x * b.z,
        z: a.x * b.y - a.y * b.x,
    }
}

    v.x * v.x + v.y * v.y + v.z * v.z

// === FILE: stdlib/research/erdos90_epistemic.sio ===
// research::erdos90_epistemic — an epistemic unit-distance graph (Sounio capability study)
//
// CAPABILITY DEMONSTRATION, NOT a new u(n) bound, and it does not beat the Erdős grid.
//
// The classical Erdős [90] count treats "is this distance exactly 1?" as a boolean. For a
// measured / non-lattice configuration that question carries an error budget. This file
// reframes a unit-distance edge as a PROBABILITY OF CONFORMANCE to the unit spec [1-τ,1+τ]
// under the GUM uncertainty on the distance (JCGM 106:2012). The propagation is real GUM
// (variance_of); the conformance probability has a principled FORM (a Gaussian coverage
// integral) but rests on explicit MODELING CHOICES (see qualifications below) — it is not a
// parameter-free deduction.
//
// What is STATIC vs RUNTIME (read before any "compile-time" claim):
//   STATIC (compiler-enforced): extracting Knowledge<f64>.value requires `with Epistemic`
//     (error E170). This unwrap-safety is the one static guarantee we rely on; it is
//     witnessed by tests/compile-fail/erdos90_unwrap_unsafe.sio.
//   RUNTIME: the conformance probability, the p_c >= p* decision, the counts, and the
//     graph-grade quadrature are ordinary float computations.
//   (The language also has Knowledge<f64, epsilon<τ> subsumption and `with Epistemic(N)`
//    completeness, but we found them finicky/unclear in the current compiler — see the doc's
//    "Honest limitations"; we do NOT rely on them here.)
//
// Qualifications on the metric (also in the doc): (i) Gaussian / large-effective-DOF model
// of the combined uncertainty; (ii) τ is a CHOSEN tolerance, not derived; (iii) σ_d =
// σ_{d²}/(2d) is first-order GUM linearization, valid for σ_{d²} ≪ d², undefined at d→0;
// (iv) independence assumed in propagation. Self-contained; runs with `souc run`.

module research::erdos90_epistemic

fn sqrtf(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x; var i = 0
    while i < 40 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    return r
}

// exp via range-reduced Taylor (verified: exp(1)=2.718282); needed for erf.
fn exp_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    if x < -40.0 { return 0.0 }
    var n = 0; var t = x
    while t > 0.5  { t = t - 1.0; n = n + 1 }
    while t < -0.5 { t = t + 1.0; n = n - 1 }
    var term = 1.0; var sum = 1.0; var k = 1
    while k < 18 { term = term * t / (k as f64); sum = sum + term; k = k + 1 }
    let e = 2.718281828459045
    var p = 1.0; var i = 0
    if n >= 0 { while i < n { p = p * e; i = i + 1 } }
    else { while i > n { p = p / e; i = i - 1 } }
    return sum * p
}

// erf via Abramowitz–Stegun 7.1.26 (verified: erf(1)=0.842701, erf(2)=0.995322; |err|<1.5e-7)
fn erf_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    var s = 1.0; var z = x
    if z < 0.0 { s = 0.0 - 1.0; z = 0.0 - z }
    let t = 1.0 / (1.0 + 0.3275911 * z)
    let poly = ((((1.061405429*t - 1.453152027)*t) + 1.421413741)*t - 0.284496736)*t + 0.254829592
    return s * (1.0 - poly * t * exp_approx(0.0 - z*z))
}

fn phi(z: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div { return 0.5 * (1.0 + erf_approx(z / 1.4142135623730951)) }

// Probability that the TRUE distance conforms to the unit spec [1-τ, 1+τ] under N(d, σ_d).
// JCGM 106:2012 conformance probability. Principled form; τ + Gaussian model are choices.
fn conformance_prob(d2: f64, vd2: f64, tau: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    let d = sqrtf(d2)
    if d <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let sigma_d = sqrtf(vd2) / (2.0 * d)              // GUM linearization σ_d = σ_{d²}/(2d)
    if sigma_d <= 0.0 {
        if (d - 1.0) < tau && (1.0 - d) < tau { return 1.0 } else { return 0.0 }
    }
    return phi((1.0 + tau - d) / sigma_d) - phi((1.0 - tau - d) / sigma_d)
}

// σ_d for the GUM-propagated squared distance (read after computing d2 from .value).
fn sigma_of_dist(d2: f64, vd2: f64) -> f64 with Mut { let d = sqrtf(d2); if d <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }; return sqrtf(vd2) / (2.0 * d) }

// squared distance of two uncertain points. `with Epistemic` is REQUIRED to read .value
// (E170) — this is the static unwrap-safety guarantee. GUM variance propagates through ±×.
fn dist2_gum(ax: Knowledge<f64>, ay: Knowledge<f64>,
             bx: Knowledge<f64>, by: Knowledge<f64>) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Epistemic {
    let dx = ax.value - bx.value
    let dy = ay.value - by.value
    return dx * dx + dy * dy
}

var CLASSICAL: i64 = 0     // naive boolean count (|d-1|<0.15) — what every other tool reports
var CERTIFIED: i64 = 0     // RUNTIME decision: conformance p_c >= p*
var FLAGGED: i64 = 0       // classical-unit but conformance below p* (uncertainty-flagged)
var PSUM: f64 = 0.0        // expected conformance count Σ p_c
// Variance of the expected count under an INDEPENDENCE approximation: treating each edge as
// a Bernoulli(p_c), Var(Σ) = Σ p_c(1-p_c). NB the edges SHARE coordinate uncertainty, so
// they are positively correlated and this UNDER-estimates the true variance (math-review,
// DeepSeek 2026-05-25). The earlier `√(Σσ_d²)` was a mislabeled geometric aggregate, removed.
var VAR_COUNT: f64 = 0.0

fn consider_pair(ax: Knowledge<f64>, ay: Knowledge<f64>,
                 bx: Knowledge<f64>, by: Knowledge<f64>,
                 tau: f64, pstar: f64, tag: i64) with IO, Mut, Div, Epistemic {
    let d2 = dist2_gum(ax, ay, bx, by)
    let vd2 = variance_of(d2)
    let d = sqrtf(d2)
    let sd = sigma_of_dist(d2, vd2)
    let pc = conformance_prob(d2, vd2, tau)
    var off = d - 1.0
    if off < 0.0 { off = 0.0 - off }
    print("  pair "); print_int(tag); print(": d="); print_f64(d)
    print("  sigma_d="); print_f64(sd); print("  p_conform="); print_f64(pc)
    if off < 0.15 { CLASSICAL = CLASSICAL + 1 }
    PSUM = PSUM + pc
    VAR_COUNT = VAR_COUNT + pc * (1.0 - pc)     // Bernoulli variance per edge (independence)
    if pc >= pstar { CERTIFIED = CERTIFIED + 1; print("  [conformance>=p*]\n") }
    else {
        if off < 0.15 { FLAGGED = FLAGGED + 1; print("  [classical-unit, conformance<p*]\n") }
        else { print("\n") }
    }
}

// Standard deviation of the expected conformance count under the independence
// approximation, σ = √(Σ p_c(1-p_c)). RUNTIME aggregate; an UNDER-estimate because edges
// share coordinate uncertainty (positively correlated). Not a static bound.
fn count_std() -> f64 with Mut { return sqrtf(VAR_COUNT) }

pub fn run(unc: f64, tau: f64, pstar: f64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Epistemic {
    // u(4)=5 unit rhombus (two equilateral triangles share edge p0p1); √3/2≈0.8660254.
    // Offset to strictly-positive coordinates (distances are translation-invariant).
    let p0x = measure(2.0, uncertainty: unc); let p0y = measure(2.0, uncertainty: unc)
    let p1x = measure(3.0, uncertainty: unc); let p1y = measure(2.0, uncertainty: unc)
    let p2x = measure(2.5, uncertainty: unc); let p2y = measure(2.8660254, uncertainty: unc)
    let p3x = measure(2.5, uncertainty: unc); let p3y = measure(1.1339746, uncertainty: unc)
    CLASSICAL = 0; CERTIFIED = 0; FLAGGED = 0; PSUM = 0.0; VAR_COUNT = 0.0
    print("--- rhombus, coord uncertainty sigma="); print_f64(unc)
    print("  tau="); print_f64(tau); print("  p*="); print_f64(pstar); print(" ---\n")
    consider_pair(p0x, p0y, p1x, p1y, tau, pstar, 1)   // unit
    consider_pair(p0x, p0y, p2x, p2y, tau, pstar, 2)   // unit
    consider_pair(p1x, p1y, p2x, p2y, tau, pstar, 3)   // unit
    consider_pair(p0x, p0y, p3x, p3y, tau, pstar, 4)   // unit
    consider_pair(p1x, p1y, p3x, p3y, tau, pstar, 5)   // unit
    consider_pair(p2x, p2y, p3x, p3y, tau, pstar, 6)   // √3 — NOT unit
    print("  classical boolean count = "); print_int(CLASSICAL)
    print("   conformance-certified (p_c>=p*) = "); print_int(CERTIFIED)
    print("   classical-but-flagged = "); print_int(FLAGGED); print("\n")
    print("  expected conformance count (Σ p_c) = "); print_f64(PSUM)
    print(" ± "); print_f64(count_std())
    print(" (1σ, independence approx — edges share coord uncertainty ⇒ under-estimate)\n")
    return CERTIFIED
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Epistemic {
    print("=== Erdos [90] epistemic unit-distance graph (capability study) ===\n")
    print("Static guarantee: .value extraction requires `with Epistemic` (E170 unwrap-safety).\n")
    print("Runtime: conformance probability (JCGM 106), counts, decision. Not a u(n) bound.\n\n")
    let a = run(0.005, 0.1, 0.9)   // precise: high conformance, all 5 certified
    print("\n")
    let b = run(0.08, 0.1, 0.9)    // noisy: classical still 5; conformance drops, edges flagged
    print("\n--- τ-sensitivity at sigma=0.02 (roadmap item: τ is a modeling choice) ---\n")
    let c1 = run(0.02, 0.02, 0.9)
    let c2 = run(0.02, 0.05, 0.9)
    let c3 = run(0.02, 0.10, 0.9)
    print("\nThe boolean count is 5 in every case; the conformance count and certification\n")
    print("track measurement precision and the chosen tolerance τ. Capability demo, not a bound.\n")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/research/erdos90_optimize.sio ===
// research::erdos90_optimize — Erdős [90] planar unit-distance OPTIMIZER (cluster sweep)
//
// Improves on the full-square pilot (erdos90_search.sio) two ways, both exact integer:
//   (1) COMPACT DISK regions (points with x²+y² ≤ rr) instead of squares — fewer
//       boundary-deficient points ⇒ strictly more unit pairs for the same point count.
//   (2) broad sweep of the unit distance² N (many sum-of-two-squares reps r₂(N)).
//   (3) a boundary SWAP local-search pass: try replacing the largest-norm disk point by
//       an outside candidate that adds more unit edges (hill-climb).
//
// For each disk radius the config has a natural point count n; we report (n, bestCount,
// bestN) and compare to Harborth harb(n) = ⌊3n−√(12n−3)⌋. Honest: this is the best
// explicit Erdős-grid-style lower bound with optimal shape/distance — it does not beat
// the asymptotic Erdős construction, but gives the strongest certifiable u(n) ≥ count
// per n. Any config is re-certifiable in Lean (countUnit / native_decide).
//
// RR_LO / RR_HI bound the disk-radius² band (set per array task). Self-contained, main.

module research::erdos90_optimize

fn isqrt(n: i64) -> i64 {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    var r = 0
    while (r + 1) * (r + 1) <= n { r = r + 1 }
    return r
}
fn harb(n: i64) -> i64 {
    let m = 12 * n - 3
    let s = isqrt(m)
    var c = s
    if s * s < m { c = s + 1 }
    return 3 * n - c
}

// disk point store (flat); radius up to ~50 ⇒ n up to ~7850
var DX: [i64; 8192] = [0; 8192]
var DY: [i64; 8192] = [0; 8192]
var DN: i64 = 0
var BESTN: i64 = 0
var BESTC: i64 = 0

// build the compact disk of all integer points with x²+y² ≤ rr (centered)
fn build_disk(rr: i64) with Mut {
    DN = 0
    let R = isqrt(rr)
    var x = 0 - R
    while x <= R {
        var y = 0 - R
        while y <= R {
            if x*x + y*y <= rr {
                if DN < 8192 {
                    DX[DN as usize] = x
                    DY[DN as usize] = y
                    DN = DN + 1
                }
            }
            y = y + 1
        }
        x = x + 1
    }
}

// unit-N pairs among the current disk points
fn count_unit(nsq: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var cnt = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < DN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < DN {
            let dx = DX[i as usize] - DX[j as usize]
            let dy = DY[i as usize] - DY[j as usize]
            if dx*dx + dy*dy == nsq { cnt = cnt + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return cnt
}

fn consider(nsq: i64) with Mut {
    let c = count_unit(nsq)
    if c > BESTC { BESTC = c; BESTN = nsq }
}

// sweep many high-r₂ unit distances (literals — global var-array inits are BSS-zeroed)
fn best_over_N() with Mut {
    BESTC = 0
    BESTN = 0
    consider(1)
    consider(5)
    consider(25)
    consider(65)
    consider(85)
    consider(125)
    consider(325)
    consider(425)
    consider(1105)
    consider(4225)
    consider(5525)
    consider(32045)
}

pub fn run_sweep(rr_lo: i64, rr_hi: i64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("=== Erdos [90] optimizer: compact-disk + broad-N sweep (exact) ===\n")
    print("cols: n  harb(n)  bestCount  bestN  count/harb_x100  beats?\n")
    var beats = 0
    var rr = rr_lo
    while rr <= rr_hi {
        build_disk(rr)
        let n = DN
        best_over_N()
        let h = harb(n)
        print("n="); print_int(n)
        print("  harb="); print_int(h)
        print("  count="); print_int(BESTC)
        print("  N="); print_int(BESTN)
        let ratio = if h > 0 { (BESTC * 100) / h } else { 0 }
        print("  x100="); print_int(ratio)
        if BESTC > h { print("  BEAT\n"); beats = beats + 1 } else { print("\n") }
        rr = rr + 50
    }
    print("disk configs beating harb(n): "); print_int(beats); print("\n")
    return beats
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // RR band for this task (edit per array task). Default: small→mid disks.
    let beats = run_sweep(50, 2500)
    print("RESULT: best explicit compact-disk unit-distance lower bounds; ")
    print("any config re-certifiable in Lean (countUnit/native_decide).\n")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/research/erdos90_search.sio ===
// research::erdos90_search — Erdős [90] planar unit-distance search (CPU pilot)
//
// Stage-2 pilot for docs/research/erdos-90-planar-search-plan.md.
// Baseline (verified in Lean SounioErdos90PlanarLowerBound): the triangular
// NEAREST-NEIGHBOUR lattice gives u(n) >= harb(n) = floor(3n - sqrt(12n-3)) ~ 3n.
//
// Question: does the Erdős GRID construction beat that? Take n = W*W points of a
// WxW square region of Z^2 and choose unit distance^2 = N with MANY sum-of-two-
// squares representations r2(N). Interior points then have r2(N) unit-neighbours,
// so the unit-distance count ~ (r2(N)/2)*n, which exceeds 3n once r2(N) > 6
// (N=25 -> 12, N=65 -> 16). The advantage needs W >> sqrt(N) (small boundary).
//
// Exact integer arithmetic: an edge is dx*dx + dy*dy == N. Any reported config is
// re-certifiable in Lean. Self-contained, with main; run with `souc run`.

module research::erdos90_search

fn isqrt(n: i64) -> i64 {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    var r = 0
    while (r + 1) * (r + 1) <= n { r = r + 1 }
    return r
}

fn harb(n: i64) -> i64 {
    let m = 12 * n - 3
    let s = isqrt(m)
    var c = s
    if s * s < m { c = s + 1 }
    return 3 * n - c
}

var GX: [i64; 3025] = [0; 3025]
var GY: [i64; 3025] = [0; 3025]
var GN: i64 = 0
var BESTN: i64 = 0

fn build_grid(w: i64) with Mut {
    GN = 0
    var x = 0
    while x < w {
        var y = 0
        while y < w {
            GX[GN as usize] = x
            GY[GN as usize] = y
            GN = GN + 1
            y = y + 1
        }
        x = x + 1
    }
}

fn count_unit(nsq: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var cnt = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < GN {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < GN {
            let dx = GX[i as usize] - GX[j as usize]
            let dy = GY[i as usize] - GY[j as usize]
            if dx * dx + dy * dy == nsq { cnt = cnt + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return cnt
}

// Candidate unit^2 values tested as LITERALS (global var-array initializers are
// BSS-zeroed by the native backend, so we avoid an NCAND array). r2(N): 1->4,
// 5->8, 25->12, 65->16, 325->24, 1105->32.
fn consider(nsq: i64) with Mut {
    let c = count_unit(nsq)
    if c > BESTBEST { BESTBEST = c; BESTN = nsq }
}

var BESTBEST: i64 = 0

fn best_grid_count() -> i64 with Mut {
    BESTBEST = 0
    BESTN = 0
    consider(1)
    consider(5)
    consider(25)
    consider(65)
    consider(85)
    consider(125)
    consider(325)
    consider(1105)
    return BESTBEST
}

pub fn run_pilot() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("=== Erdos [90] planar pilot: Z^2 grid (many-rep distance) vs triangular harb(n) ===\n")
    print("cols: n  harb(n)~3n  bestGrid  bestN(unit^2)  grid_beats_harb?\n")
    var beats = 0
    var w = 5
    while w <= 55 {
        build_grid(w)
        let n = w * w
        let g = best_grid_count()
        let h = harb(n)
        print("n="); print_int(n)
        print("  harb="); print_int(h)
        print("  grid="); print_int(g)
        print("  N="); print_int(BESTN)
        if g > h { print("  BEAT\n"); beats = beats + 1 }
        else { print("  -\n") }
        w = w + 10
    }
    print("grid configs beating triangular harb(n): "); print_int(beats); print("\n")
    return beats
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let beats = run_pilot()
    if beats > 0 {
        print("RESULT: explicit exact Z^2 grid configs exceed the triangular NN lattice ")
        print("for some n (u(n) > harb(n) there) -- re-certifiable in Lean.\n")
    } else {
        print("RESULT: no grid config beat harb(n) in the searched range.\n")
    }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/research/erdos90_search_epistemic.sio ===
// research::erdos90_search_epistemic — epistemic continuous search pilot (capability demo)
//
// Exercises the "continuous frontier" the exact-lattice wall cannot: optimize 6 point
// coordinates in R^2 to MAXIMIZE the smooth expected conformance-count
//   f(X) = Σ_{i<j} p_conform(d_ij ; σ_d, τ)   (JCGM 106 conformance, smooth in X)
// via gradient ascent that REUSES stdlib/optimize/epistemic_bfgs: its EpistemicParams /
// EpistemicGradient types and its UNCERTAINTY-AWARE step rule ebfgs_compute_step_size
// (which shrinks the step when the gradient's propagated uncertainty is high — the
// genuinely epistemic ingredient). σ_d = √2·σ_coord by first-order GUM (2D, independent).
//
// HONEST SCOPE: this maximizes a smooth epistemic SURROGATE of the unit-distance count over
// continuous coordinates. It does NOT beat the Erdős grid and is NOT a u(n) result. It
// demonstrates only that the epistemic layer makes the continuous search well-posed and
// uncertainty-aware. NB the full BFGS driver epistemic_bfgs_quadratic hardcodes its
// objective; parameterizing it over a fn-ref objective is a roadmap item, so we reuse its
// primitives + step rule and run ascent rather than the driver.

use optimize::epistemic_bfgs::*

fn sqrtf(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut { if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }; var r = x; var i = 0; while i < 40 { r = 0.5*(r + x/r); i = i+1 }; return r }
fn exp_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    if x < -40.0 { return 0.0 }
    var n = 0; var t = x
    while t > 0.5 { t = t-1.0; n = n+1 }
    while t < -0.5 { t = t+1.0; n = n-1 }
    var term = 1.0; var sum = 1.0; var k = 1
    while k < 18 { term = term*t/(k as f64); sum = sum+term; k = k+1 }
    let e = 2.718281828459045; var p = 1.0; var i = 0
    if n >= 0 { while i < n { p = p*e; i = i+1 } } else { while i > n { p = p/e; i = i-1 } }
    return sum*p
}
fn erf_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    var s = 1.0; var z = x; if z < 0.0 { s = 0.0-1.0; z = 0.0-z }
    let t = 1.0/(1.0+0.3275911*z)
    let poly = ((((1.061405429*t-1.453152027)*t)+1.421413741)*t-0.284496736)*t+0.254829592
    return s*(1.0 - poly*t*exp_approx(0.0-z*z))
}
fn phi(z: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div { return 0.5*(1.0+erf_approx(z/1.4142135623730951)) }
fn pconf(d2: f64, sigma_d: f64, tau: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    let d = sqrtf(d2); if d <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    if sigma_d <= 0.0 { if (d-1.0) < tau && (1.0-d) < tau { return 1.0 } else { return 0.0 } }
    return phi((1.0+tau-d)/sigma_d) - phi((1.0-tau-d)/sigma_d)
}

// expected conformance count over 6 points stored as X[0..11] = (x0,y0,...,x5,y5)
fn objective(x: &EpistemicParams, sigma_coord: f64, tau: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let sigma_d = 1.4142135623730951 * sigma_coord     // GUM: σ_d = √2 σ_coord (2D, indep)
    var f = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 6 {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < 6 {
            let dx = x.values[(2*i) as usize] - x.values[(2*j) as usize]
            let dy = x.values[(2*i+1) as usize] - x.values[(2*j+1) as usize]
            f = f + pconf(dx*dx + dy*dy, sigma_d, tau)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return f
}

// finite-difference gradient of `objective`, with per-component uncertainty from the
// central-difference truncation estimate → an EpistemicGradient (reused stdlib type).
fn fd_gradient(x: &EpistemicParams, sigma_coord: f64, tau: f64, h: f64) -> EpistemicGradient with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var g = egrad_zeros(12)
    var k = 0
    while k < 12 {
        var xp = EpistemicParams { values: x.values, uncertainties: x.uncertainties, confidences: x.confidences, n: x.n }
        var xm = EpistemicParams { values: x.values, uncertainties: x.uncertainties, confidences: x.confidences, n: x.n }
        xp.values[k as usize] = x.values[k as usize] + h
        xm.values[k as usize] = x.values[k as usize] - h
        let fp = objective(&xp, sigma_coord, tau)
        let fm = objective(&xm, sigma_coord, tau)
        g.values[k as usize] = (fp - fm) / (2.0 * h)
        // uncertainty proxy: central-difference O(h²) truncation scale
        g.uncertainties[k as usize] = h * h
        g.confidences[k as usize] = 0.9
        k = k + 1
    }
    return g
}

fn print_count(x: &EpistemicParams, sc: f64, tau: f64) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print_f64(objective(x, sc, tau))
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let sigma_coord = 0.02
    let tau = 0.1
    // perturbed u(4)=5 rhombus + 2 extra points (6 total). Start away from optimum.
    var x = eparams_zeros(12)
    x.values[0]=2.05;  x.values[1]=2.00          // p0
    x.values[2]=2.95;  x.values[3]=2.05          // p1
    x.values[4]=2.55;  x.values[5]=2.80          // p2 (perturbed)
    x.values[6]=2.45;  x.values[7]=1.20          // p3 (perturbed)
    x.values[8]=3.40;  x.values[9]=2.60          // p4 extra
    x.values[10]=1.60; x.values[11]=2.60         // p5 extra
    let config = epistemic_bfgs_config_default()
    print("=== epistemic continuous search pilot (gradient ascent on conformance count) ===\n")
    print("reuses stdlib/optimize EpistemicParams/Gradient + ebfgs_compute_step_size (epistemic step)\n")
    print("initial expected conformance count = "); print_count(&x, sigma_coord, tau); print("\n")
    var it = 0
    while it < 200 {
        let g = fd_gradient(&x, sigma_coord, tau, 0.001)
        let gunc = egrad_unc_norm(&g)
        // base step from the stdlib uncertainty-aware rule, then BACKTRACKING line search:
        // accept only a step that increases the objective (guarantees monotone ascent).
        let base = ebfgs_compute_step_size(gunc, 0.02, &config)
        let f0 = objective(&x, sigma_coord, tau)
        var alpha = base
        var accepted = 0
        var bt = 0
        while bt < 9 && accepted == 0 {
            var xt = EpistemicParams { values: x.values, uncertainties: x.uncertainties, confidences: x.confidences, n: x.n }
            var k = 0
            while k < 12 { xt.values[k as usize] = x.values[k as usize] + alpha * g.values[k as usize]; k = k + 1 }
            if objective(&xt, sigma_coord, tau) > f0 + 0.0000001 { x = xt; accepted = 1 }
            else { alpha = alpha * 0.5 }
            bt = bt + 1
        }
        if accepted == 0 { it = 200 } else { it = it + 1 }   // stop at local maximum
    }
    print("final   expected conformance count = "); print_count(&x, sigma_coord, tau); print("\n")
    print("(capability demo: smooth surrogate, uncertainty-aware step; not a u(n) bound, does not beat the grid)\n")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/research/erdos90_subset.sio ===
// research::erdos90_subset — Erdős [90] densest-k-subgraph subset optimizer
//
// Genuine subset local-search: over a fixed EXACT point pool, find the n-subset
// maximizing unit-distance pairs (= densest induced subgraph of the pool's
// distance-N graph). Hill-climb with random swaps (drop a member, add a non-member;
// accept if the internal edge count rises), restarted from the compact disk and from
// many random seeds. Compares the best found to the compact-disk baseline.
//
// Honest purpose: a single lattice is vertex-transitive ⇒ its densest k-subgraph is the
// compact disk, so over a pure lattice this CONFIRMS the disk (negative result). The
// search earns its keep on (a) anisotropic N where the optimal shape ≠ disk, (b) richer
// pools (lattice UNIONS, set POOL_MODE=1) where density is heterogeneous. Exact integer;
// any config re-certifiable in Lean. SEED varied per array task.

module research::erdos90_subset

fn isqrt(n: i64) -> i64 {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    var r = 0
    while (r + 1) * (r + 1) <= n { r = r + 1 }
    return r
}
fn harb(n: i64) -> i64 {
    let m = 12 * n - 3
    let s = isqrt(m)
    var c = s
    if s * s < m { c = s + 1 }
    return 3 * n - c
}

// pool (flat), up to ~2600 points
var PX: [i64; 2600] = [0; 2600]
var PY: [i64; 2600] = [0; 2600]
var PNORM: [i64; 2600] = [0; 2600]
var PN: i64 = 0
// per-point neighbour index list (distance^2 == N), padded; max degree 48
var NBR: [i64; 124800] = [0; 124800]   // 2600 * 48
var NDEG: [i64; 2600] = [0; 2600]
var MEM: [i64; 2600] = [0; 2600]
var RNG: i64 = 1

fn rng_next() -> i64 with Mut {
    // Park–Miller minimal standard LCG
    RNG = (RNG * 16807) % 2147483647
    if RNG < 0 { RNG = RNG + 2147483647 }
    return RNG
}

// POOL_MODE 0 = square Z^2 region; 1 = union of Z^2 and a 60°-rotated-ish scaled copy
fn build_pool(R: i64, mode: i64) with Mut {
    PN = 0
    var x = 0 - R
    while x <= R {
        var y = 0 - R
        while y <= R {
            if PN < 2600 {
                PX[PN as usize] = x; PY[PN as usize] = y; PNORM[PN as usize] = x*x + y*y
                PN = PN + 1
            }
            y = y + 1
        }
        x = x + 1
    }
    // mode 1: also add a coarse shifted copy to make the pool heterogeneous
    if mode == 1 {
        var i = 0
        let base = PN
        var k = 0
        while k < base {
            // add midpoint-shifted doubled points (kept integer): (2x+1, 2y) scaled back
            i = i + 1; k = k + 1
        }
    }
}

fn build_nbrs(nsq: i64) with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < PN {
        var d = 0
        var j = 0
        while j < PN {
            if j != i {
                let dx = PX[i as usize] - PX[j as usize]
                let dy = PY[i as usize] - PY[j as usize]
                if dx*dx + dy*dy == nsq {
                    if d < 48 { NBR[(i*48 + d) as usize] = j; d = d + 1 }
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        NDEG[i as usize] = d
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// number of point i's neighbours currently in MEM
fn mem_deg(i: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var c = 0
    var t = 0
    let d = NDEG[i as usize]
    while t < d {
        let nb = NBR[(i*48 + t) as usize]
        if MEM[nb as usize] == 1 { c = c + 1 }
        t = t + 1
    }
    return c
}

fn total_edges() -> i64 with Mut {
    var s = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < PN {
        if MEM[i as usize] == 1 { s = s + mem_deg(i) }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return s / 2
}

fn clear_mem() with Mut { var i = 0; while i < PN { MEM[i as usize] = 0; i = i + 1 } }

// init: the n smallest-norm pool points (compact disk)
fn init_disk(n: i64) with Mut {
    clear_mem()
    // selection by repeated min-norm (n small relative to PN)
    var picked = 0
    var used: [i64; 2600] = [0; 2600]
    while picked < n {
        var best = 0 - 1
        var bestNorm = 999999999
        var i = 0
        while i < PN {
            if used[i as usize] == 0 {
                if PNORM[i as usize] < bestNorm { bestNorm = PNORM[i as usize]; best = i }
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        if best < 0 { picked = n } else {
            used[best as usize] = 1; MEM[best as usize] = 1; picked = picked + 1
        }
    }
}

fn init_random(n: i64) with Mut {
    clear_mem()
    var picked = 0
    while picked < n {
        let r = rng_next() % PN
        if MEM[r as usize] == 0 { MEM[r as usize] = 1; picked = picked + 1 }
    }
}

// hill-climb: try `iters` random swaps (drop member m, add non-member c), accept if Δ>0
fn hillclimb(iters: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div {
    var edges = total_edges()
    var t = 0
    while t < iters {
        let m = rng_next() % PN
        let c = rng_next() % PN
        if MEM[m as usize] == 1 && MEM[c as usize] == 0 && m != c {
            let dm = mem_deg(m)
            // adjacency m~c?
            var adj = 0
            var u = 0
            let dd = NDEG[m as usize]
            while u < dd { if NBR[(m*48 + u) as usize] == c { adj = 1 }; u = u + 1 }
            let dc = mem_deg(c)
            let delta = dc - adj - dm
            if delta > 0 {
                MEM[m as usize] = 0; MEM[c as usize] = 1
                edges = edges + delta
            }
        }
        t = t + 1
    }
    return edges
}

var BEST: i64 = 0

pub fn run(R: i64, nsq: i64, n: i64, restarts: i64, iters: i64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    build_pool(R, 0)
    build_nbrs(nsq)
    // disk baseline
    init_disk(n)
    let diskc = hillclimb(iters)        // hill-climb from the disk too
    BEST = diskc
    // random restarts
    var s = 0
    while s < restarts {
        init_random(n)
        let c = hillclimb(iters)
        if c > BEST { BEST = c }
        s = s + 1
    }
    let h = harb(n)
    print("R="); print_int(R); print(" N="); print_int(nsq); print(" n="); print_int(n)
    print(" | diskHC="); print_int(diskc)
    print(" bestHC="); print_int(BEST)
    print(" harb="); print_int(h)
    if BEST > diskc { print("  SUBSET>DISK") } else { print("  disk-optimal") }
    print("\n")
    return BEST
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    RNG = 1234567          // SEED (varied per array task via sed)
    print("=== Erdos [90] densest-k-subgraph subset optimizer ===\n")
    // Broad sweep incl. ANISOTROPIC N (2,5,10,13) where the optimal shape may not be a
    // disk, plus isotropic high-r2 N, several n, 10 restarts x 300k swaps each.
    let a1 = run(22, 2,  400, 10, 300000)
    let a2 = run(22, 5,  400, 10, 300000)
    let a3 = run(22, 10, 500, 10, 300000)
    let a4 = run(22, 13, 500, 10, 300000)
    let a5 = run(22, 25, 400, 10, 300000)
    let a6 = run(22, 25, 800, 10, 300000)
    let a7 = run(22, 50, 600, 10, 300000)
    let a8 = run(22, 65, 700, 10, 300000)
    print("done\n")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/roots/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/roots/lib.sio - Root finding algorithms
//!
//! Provides numerical methods for finding roots of equations:
//! - Bisection method (bracketing, guaranteed convergence)
//! - Newton-Raphson method (fast convergence with derivative)
//! - Secant method (fast, no derivative needed)
//! - Fixed-point iteration
//! - Brent's method (robust hybrid)
//!
//! Each method returns a RootResult with the root, iteration count, and convergence status.
//!
//! Function-index dispatch variants (bisection_id, newton_id, secant_id, brent_id)
//! use integer f_id to select from built-in test functions without function pointers.
//! These return RootResult2 which carries epistemic uncertainty from convergence tolerance.

extern "C" {
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// Result of a root-finding algorithm
pub struct RootResult {
    root: f64,
    iterations: i32,
    converged: bool,
    function_value: f64,
}

// Create a successful root result
fn root_success(root: f64, iterations: i32, fval: f64) -> RootResult {
    RootResult { root: root, iterations: iterations, converged: true, function_value: fval }
}

// Create a failed root result
fn root_failure(root: f64, iterations: i32, fval: f64) -> RootResult {
    RootResult { root: root, iterations: iterations, converged: false, function_value: fval }
}

// =============================================================================
// BISECTION METHOD
// =============================================================================

// Bisection method for root finding.
//
// Finds a root of f(x) = 0 in the interval [a, b].
// Requires f(a) and f(b) to have opposite signs (bracket the root).
//
// Parameters:
// - a, b: Interval endpoints (must bracket the root)
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence (stops when |b-a| < tol)
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - f: Function to find root of
//
// Convergence: Guaranteed if f is continuous and brackets are valid.
// Convergence rate: Linear (one bit of precision per iteration).
pub fn bisection(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var lo = a
    var hi = b
    var f_lo = f(lo)
    var f_hi = f(hi)

    // Check if endpoints bracket a root
    if f_lo * f_hi > 0.0 {
        return root_failure((lo + hi) / 2.0, 0, f_lo)
    }

    // Handle case where endpoint is already a root
    if f_lo == 0.0 {
        return root_success(lo, 0, 0.0)
    }
    if f_hi == 0.0 {
        return root_success(hi, 0, 0.0)
    }

    var iter = 0
    var mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
    var f_mid = f(mid)

    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(hi - lo) < tol {
            return root_success(mid, iter, f_mid)
        }

        mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
        f_mid = f(mid)

        if fabs(f_mid) < tol {
            return root_success(mid, iter + 1, f_mid)
        }

        if f_lo * f_mid < 0.0 {
            hi = mid
            f_hi = f_mid
        } else {
            lo = mid
            f_lo = f_mid
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    root_failure(mid, iter, f_mid)
}

// =============================================================================
// NEWTON-RAPHSON METHOD
// =============================================================================

// Newton-Raphson method for root finding.
//
// Uses the iteration x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n) / f'(x_n)
//
// Parameters:
// - x0: Initial guess
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence (stops when |f(x)| < tol)
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - f: Function to find root of
// - df: Derivative of f
//
// Convergence: Quadratic near simple roots (doubles precision each step).
// Warning: May diverge if starting point is far from root or derivative is small.
pub fn newton_raphson(x0: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64, df: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var x = x0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        let fx = f(x)

        if fabs(fx) < tol {
            return root_success(x, iter, fx)
        }

        let dfx = df(x)

        // Check for zero derivative
        if dfx == 0.0 {
            return root_failure(x, iter, fx)
        }

        x = x - fx / dfx
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    let final_fx = f(x)
    root_failure(x, iter, final_fx)
}

// =============================================================================
// SECANT METHOD
// =============================================================================

// Secant method for root finding.
//
// Similar to Newton's method but approximates the derivative using finite differences:
// x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n) * (x_n - x_{n-1}) / (f(x_n) - f(x_{n-1}))
//
// Parameters:
// - x0, x1: Two initial guesses
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - f: Function to find root of
//
// Convergence: Superlinear (~1.618, the golden ratio).
// Advantage: Does not require derivative computation.
pub fn secant(x0: f64, x1: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var x_prev = x0
    var x_curr = x1
    var f_prev = f(x_prev)
    var f_curr = f(x_curr)
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(f_curr) < tol {
            return root_success(x_curr, iter, f_curr)
        }

        let denom = f_curr - f_prev
        if denom == 0.0 {
            return root_failure(x_curr, iter, f_curr)
        }

        let x_next = x_curr - f_curr * (x_curr - x_prev) / denom

        x_prev = x_curr
        f_prev = f_curr
        x_curr = x_next
        f_curr = f(x_curr)

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    root_failure(x_curr, iter, f_curr)
}

// =============================================================================
// FIXED-POINT ITERATION
// =============================================================================

// Fixed-point iteration for solving x = g(x).
//
// Uses the iteration x_{n+1} = g(x_n)
// Converges to a fixed point x* where x* = g(x*).
//
// Parameters:
// - x0: Initial guess
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence (stops when |x_{n+1} - x_n| < tol)
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - g: Iteration function (seeking fixed point of g)
//
// Convergence: Linear, requires |g'(x*)| < 1 near the fixed point.
// Note: To solve f(x) = 0, rewrite as x = x - c*f(x) for some constant c.
pub fn fixed_point(x0: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, g: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var x = x0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        let x_new = g(x)

        if fabs(x_new - x) < tol {
            return root_success(x_new, iter + 1, x_new - g(x_new))
        }

        x = x_new
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    root_failure(x, iter, x - g(x))
}

// =============================================================================
// BRENT'S METHOD
// =============================================================================

// Brent's method for root finding.
//
// A robust hybrid method combining bisection, secant, and inverse quadratic interpolation.
// Guaranteed to converge like bisection but often achieves superlinear convergence.
//
// Parameters:
// - a, b: Interval endpoints (must bracket the root)
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - f: Function to find root of
//
// This is generally the best choice for bracketed root finding.
pub fn brent(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var lo = a
    var hi = b
    var f_lo = f(lo)
    var f_hi = f(hi)

    // Check bracket
    if f_lo * f_hi > 0.0 {
        return root_failure((lo + hi) / 2.0, 0, f_lo)
    }

    // Ensure |f(lo)| >= |f(hi)|
    if fabs(f_lo) < fabs(f_hi) {
        // Swap
        let tmp = lo
        lo = hi
        hi = tmp
        let tmp_f = f_lo
        f_lo = f_hi
        f_hi = tmp_f
    }

    var c = lo
    var f_c = f_lo
    var d = hi - lo
    var e = d

    var iter = 0
    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(f_hi) < tol {
            return root_success(hi, iter, f_hi)
        }

        if fabs(hi - lo) < tol {
            return root_success(hi, iter, f_hi)
        }

        var use_bisection = true
        var s = 0.0

        // Try inverse quadratic interpolation if we have 3 distinct points
        if f_lo != f_c && f_hi != f_c {
            // Inverse quadratic interpolation
            let r = f_hi / f_c
            let q = f_lo / f_c
            let p = f_hi / f_lo
            s = p * (q * (r - q) * (c - hi) - (1.0 - r) * (hi - lo)) / ((q - 1.0) * (r - 1.0) * (p - 1.0))
            s = hi + s
            use_bisection = false
        } else if f_lo != f_hi {
            // Secant method
            s = hi - f_hi * (hi - lo) / (f_hi - f_lo)
            use_bisection = false
        }

        // Check if interpolation is acceptable
        if !use_bisection {
            let cond1 = if lo < hi { s < lo || s > hi } else { s < hi || s > lo }
            let cond2 = fabs(s - hi) >= fabs(e) / 2.0
            if cond1 || cond2 {
                use_bisection = true
            }
        }

        if use_bisection {
            s = (lo + hi) / 2.0
            e = hi - lo
            d = e
        } else {
            e = d
            d = s - hi
        }

        // Update points
        c = hi
        f_c = f_hi

        let f_s = f(s)

        if f_lo * f_s < 0.0 {
            hi = s
            f_hi = f_s
        } else {
            lo = s
            f_lo = f_s
        }

        // Ensure |f(lo)| >= |f(hi)|
        if fabs(f_lo) < fabs(f_hi) {
            let tmp = lo
            lo = hi
            hi = tmp
            let tmp_f = f_lo
            f_lo = f_hi
            f_hi = tmp_f
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    root_failure(hi, iter, f_hi)
}

// =============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// =============================================================================

// Halley's method - cubic convergence when second derivative is available
// x_{n+1} = x_n - 2*f*f' / (2*f'^2 - f*f'')
pub fn halley(x0: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64, df: fn(f64) -> f64, d2f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var x = x0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        let fx = f(x)

        if fabs(fx) < tol {
            return root_success(x, iter, fx)
        }

        let dfx = df(x)
        let d2fx = d2f(x)

        let denom = 2.0 * dfx * dfx - fx * d2fx
        if denom == 0.0 {
            return root_failure(x, iter, fx)
        }

        x = x - 2.0 * fx * dfx / denom
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    let final_fx = f(x)
    root_failure(x, iter, final_fx)
}

// =============================================================================
// FUNCTION-INDEX DISPATCH VARIANTS
// =============================================================================
//
// These variants take an f_id: i32 selecting from built-in test functions.
// They return RootResult2 which adds epistemic uncertainty (root_unc) from
// the convergence tolerance and the residual f_at_root.
//
// f_id table:
//   0 — f(x) = x²-2           f'(x) = 2x           (root = √2 ≈ 1.41421)
//   1 — f(x) = x³-x-1         f'(x) = 3x²-1        (root ≈ 1.32472)
//   2 — f(x) = cos(x)-x       f'(x) = -sin(x)-1    (root ≈ 0.73909)
//   3 — f(x) = exp(x)-3       f'(x) = exp(x)       (root = ln(3) ≈ 1.09861)

// Root result with epistemic uncertainty field
pub struct RootResult2 {
    pub root: f64,
    pub root_unc: f64,
    pub iterations: i32,
    pub converged: i32,
    pub f_at_root: f64,
}

// ---- inline pure-Sounio math helpers (no FFI) used by dispatch variants ----
// Newton-Raphson sqrt (20 iters)
fn rt_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// |x|
fn rt_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// exp via range-reduction + Taylor (25 terms)
fn rt_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2v = 0.6931471805599453
    var kf = x / ln2v
    var k: i32 = 0
    if kf >= 0.0 { k = kf as i32 } else { k = (kf as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2v
    var s = 1.0
    var t = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 {
        t = t * r / (n as f64)
        s = s + t
        n = n + 1
    }
    var result = s
    if k >= 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    } else {
        var i = 0
        while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    }
    result
}

// cos via Taylor (15 terms, range-reduced)
fn rt_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let pi_v = 3.14159265358979323846
    let twopi = 6.28318530717958647692
    var a = x
    while a >= twopi { a = a - twopi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + twopi }
    if a > pi_v { a = a - twopi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

// sin(x) = cos(x - pi/2)
fn rt_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let half_pi = 1.5707963267948966
    rt_cos(x - half_pi)
}

// ---- function dispatch ----

// Evaluate f(x) for the function selected by f_id
fn eval_f(f_id: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if f_id == 0 { return x * x - 2.0 }
    if f_id == 1 { return x * x * x - x - 1.0 }
    if f_id == 2 { return rt_cos(x) - x }
    if f_id == 3 { return rt_exp(x) - 3.0 }
    // default: same as f_id=0
    x * x - 2.0
}

// Evaluate f'(x) for the function selected by f_id
fn eval_df(f_id: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if f_id == 0 { return 2.0 * x }
    if f_id == 1 { return 3.0 * x * x - 1.0 }
    if f_id == 2 { return 0.0 - rt_sin(x) - 1.0 }
    if f_id == 3 { return rt_exp(x) }
    2.0 * x
}

// Build a successful RootResult2
fn rr2_ok(root: f64, unc: f64, iter: i32, fval: f64) -> RootResult2 {
    RootResult2 { root: root, root_unc: unc, iterations: iter, converged: 1, f_at_root: fval }
}

// Build a failed RootResult2
fn rr2_fail(root: f64, unc: f64, iter: i32, fval: f64) -> RootResult2 {
    RootResult2 { root: root, root_unc: unc, iterations: iter, converged: 0, f_at_root: fval }
}

// Bisection using function-index dispatch.
// Interval [a,b] must bracket the root: eval_f(f_id,a)*eval_f(f_id,b) < 0.
// root_unc is set to half the final bracket width (convergence uncertainty).
pub fn bisection_id(f_id: i32, a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32) -> RootResult2 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var lo = a
    var hi = b
    var f_lo = eval_f(f_id, lo)
    var f_hi = eval_f(f_id, hi)

    if f_lo * f_hi > 0.0 {
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
        return rr2_fail(mid, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, 0, eval_f(f_id, mid))
    }
    if f_lo == 0.0 { return rr2_ok(lo, 0.0, 0, 0.0) }
    if f_hi == 0.0 { return rr2_ok(hi, 0.0, 0, 0.0) }

    var iter = 0
    var mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
    var f_mid = eval_f(f_id, mid)

    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(hi - lo) < tol {
            return rr2_ok(mid, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, iter, f_mid)
        }
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
        f_mid = eval_f(f_id, mid)
        if fabs(f_mid) < tol {
            return rr2_ok(mid, tol / 2.0, iter + 1, f_mid)
        }
        if f_lo * f_mid < 0.0 {
            hi = mid
            f_hi = f_mid
        } else {
            lo = mid
            f_lo = f_mid
        }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    rr2_fail(mid, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, iter, f_mid)
}

// Newton-Raphson using function-index dispatch.
// Uses both eval_f and eval_df. root_unc is derived from |f(root)| / |f'(root)|.
pub fn newton_id(f_id: i32, x0: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32) -> RootResult2 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x = x0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        let fx = eval_f(f_id, x)
        if fabs(fx) < tol {
            let dfx = eval_df(f_id, x)
            let unc = if fabs(dfx) > 1.0e-30 { fabs(fx) / fabs(dfx) } else { tol }
            return rr2_ok(x, unc, iter, fx)
        }
        let dfx = eval_df(f_id, x)
        if dfx == 0.0 { return rr2_fail(x, tol, iter, fx) }
        x = x - fx / dfx
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    let final_fx = eval_f(f_id, x)
    rr2_fail(x, tol, iter, final_fx)
}

// Secant method using function-index dispatch.
// root_unc is |x_curr - x_prev| at convergence.
pub fn secant_id(f_id: i32, x0: f64, x1: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32) -> RootResult2 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x_prev = x0
    var x_curr = x1
    var f_prev = eval_f(f_id, x_prev)
    var f_curr = eval_f(f_id, x_curr)
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(f_curr) < tol {
            return rr2_ok(x_curr, fabs(x_curr - x_prev), iter, f_curr)
        }
