var CNT: [i64; 2] = [0; 2]

fn chk(label: i64, ok: i64) with IO, Mut {
    if ok == 1 {
        print("  PASS ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[0] = CNT[0] + 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[1] = CNT[1] + 1
    }
}

fn near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> i64 {
    let d = a - b
    let d2 = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    if d2 <= tol { 1 } else { 0 }
}

fn test_log2_bit_reverse() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    chk(1, if fft_log2(1) == 0 { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(2, if fft_log2(2) == 1 { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(3, if fft_log2(8) == 3 { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(4, if fft_log2(256) == 8 { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(5, if fft_bit_reverse(6, 3) == 3 { 1 } else { 0 })
    chk(6, if fft_bit_reverse(1, 3) == 4 { 1 } else { 0 })
}

fn test_trig() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    chk(7, near(fft_sin(0.0), 0.0, 1e-12))
    chk(8, near(fft_sin(fft_pi() * 0.5), 1.0, 1e-9))
    chk(9, near(fft_cos(0.0), 1.0, 1e-9))
    chk(10, near(fft_cos(fft_pi()), 0.0 - 1.0, 1e-9))
    // sin(π) = 0 with octant reduction
    chk(11, near(fft_sin(fft_pi()), 0.0, 1e-9))
    // sin(3π/2) = -1
    chk(12, near(fft_sin(fft_pi() * 1.5), 0.0 - 1.0, 1e-9))
}

fn test_dc() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var data: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 { data[i] = 1.0; i = i + 1 }
    var arr = ComplexArray { re: [0.0; 256], im: [0.0; 256], n: 0 }
    ca_load_real(&!arr, &data, 8)
    fft_forward(&!arr)
    chk(13, near(arr.re[0], 8.0, 1e-8))
    chk(14, near(arr.im[0], 0.0, 1e-8))
    chk(15, near(arr.re[1], 0.0, 1e-6))
    chk(16, near(arr.re[4], 0.0, 1e-6))
}

fn test_single_tone() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n: i64 = 8
    let pi = fft_pi()
    var data: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        data[i] = fft_cos(2.0 * pi * 1.0 * (i as f64) / (n as f64))
        i = i + 1
    }
    var arr = ComplexArray { re: [0.0; 256], im: [0.0; 256], n: 0 }
    ca_load_real(&!arr, &data, n)
    fft_forward(&!arr)
    chk(17, near(arr.re[1], 4.0, 1e-5))
    chk(18, near(arr.im[1], 0.0, 1e-5))
    chk(19, near(arr.re[7], 4.0, 1e-5))
    chk(20, near(arr.re[0], 0.0, 1e-5))
}

fn test_roundtrip() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n: i64 = 8
    var data: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    data[0] = 1.0; data[1] = 2.0; data[2] = 3.0; data[3] = 4.0
    data[4] = 5.0; data[5] = 6.0; data[6] = 7.0; data[7] = 8.0
    var arr = ComplexArray { re: [0.0; 256], im: [0.0; 256], n: 0 }
    ca_load_real(&!arr, &data, n)
    fft_forward(&!arr)
    fft_inverse(&!arr)
    chk(21, near(arr.re[0], 1.0, 1e-6))
    chk(22, near(arr.re[1], 2.0, 1e-6))
    chk(23, near(arr.re[3], 4.0, 1e-6))
    chk(24, near(arr.re[7], 8.0, 1e-6))
    chk(25, near(arr.im[0], 0.0, 1e-6))
}

fn test_magnitude_power() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n: i64 = 4
    var data: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n { data[i] = 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    var arr = ComplexArray { re: [0.0; 256], im: [0.0; 256], n: 0 }
    ca_load_real(&!arr, &data, n)
    fft_forward(&!arr)
    var mag: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var pwr: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    fft_magnitude(&arr, &!mag)
    fft_power(&arr, &!pwr)
    chk(26, near(mag[0], 8.0, 1e-6))
    chk(27, near(mag[1], 0.0, 1e-6))
    chk(28, near(pwr[0], 64.0, 1e-5))
}

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    CNT[0] = 0; CNT[1] = 0
    print("─── stdlib/signal/fft tests ───\n")
    test_log2_bit_reverse()
    test_trig()
    test_dc()
    test_single_tone()
    test_roundtrip()
    test_magnitude_power()
    print("─── "); print(CNT[0]); print("/"); print(CNT[0]+CNT[1]); print(" PASS ───\n")
    if CNT[1] == 0 { print("ALL PASS\n"); 0 } else { 1 }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/signal/filter.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL PASS

// stdlib/signal/filter.sio — Digital FIR and IIR filters for biosignal processing
//
// IIR1: First-order IIR (RC lowpass / highpass) — exact bilinear design
// IIR2: Second-order biquad (notch, bandpass) — bilinear-transform design
// FIR:  Moving-average and windowed-sinc FIR up to 64 taps
// All filters operate on fixed-size [f64; 512] signal buffers.

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS (self-contained — no extern "C")
// ============================================================================

fn flt_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn flt_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn flt_sin_small(t: f64) -> f64 with Div {
    let t2 = t * t
    let t3 = t2 * t
    let t5 = t3 * t2
    let t7 = t5 * t2
    let t9 = t7 * t2
    let t11 = t9 * t2
    t - t3 / 6.0 + t5 / 120.0 - t7 / 5040.0 + t9 / 362880.0 - t11 / 39916800.0
}

fn flt_cos_small(t: f64) -> f64 with Div {
    let t2 = t * t
    let t4 = t2 * t2
    let t6 = t4 * t2
    let t8 = t6 * t2
    let t10 = t8 * t2
    1.0 - t2 / 2.0 + t4 / 24.0 - t6 / 720.0 + t8 / 40320.0 - t10 / 3628800.0
}

fn flt_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let pi = flt_pi()
    let pi2 = pi * 0.5
    let pi4 = pi * 0.25
    let two_pi = pi * 2.0
    var t = x
    var neg: i64 = 0
    if t < 0.0 { t = 0.0 - t; neg = 1 }
    var tmp = t / two_pi
    var k: i64 = 0
    while tmp >= 1.0 { tmp = tmp - 1.0; k = k + 1 }
    t = t - (k as f64) * two_pi
    if t > pi { t = t - pi; neg = if neg == 0 { 1 } else { 0 } }
    if t > pi2 { t = pi - t }
    let r = if t <= pi4 { flt_sin_small(t) } else { flt_cos_small(pi2 - t) }
    if neg == 1 { 0.0 - r } else { r }
}

fn flt_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    flt_sin(x + flt_pi() * 0.5)
}

fn flt_tan(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let c = flt_cos(x)
    if flt_abs(c) < 1e-15 { return if flt_sin(x) > 0.0 { 1e15 } else { 0.0 - 1e15 } }
    flt_sin(x) / c
}

fn flt_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

// ============================================================================
// FIRST-ORDER IIR — bilinear-transform RC design
// ============================================================================

// fc: cutoff frequency (Hz), fs: sample rate (Hz)
// Lowpass: H(z) = (1-alpha)*z / (z - alpha)  where alpha = exp(-2π·fc/fs) approx
//
// Bilinear: K = tan(π·fc/fs), alpha = K / (1 + K), beta = (1 - K) / (1 + K)
// y[n] = alpha*(x[n] + x[n-1]) + beta*y[n-1]  (lowpass)
// y[n] = alpha*(x[n] - x[n-1]) - beta*y[n-1]  (highpass, sign flip)

pub struct IIR1 {
    b0: f64,  // coeff on x[n]
    b1: f64,  // coeff on x[n-1]
    a1: f64,  // coeff on y[n-1]
    xprev: f64,
    yprev: f64,
}

pub fn iir1_lowpass(fc: f64, fs: f64) -> IIR1 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let k = flt_tan(flt_pi() * fc / fs)
    let alpha = k / (1.0 + k)
    IIR1 { b0: alpha, b1: alpha, a1: 1.0 - 2.0 * alpha, xprev: 0.0, yprev: 0.0 }
}

pub fn iir1_highpass(fc: f64, fs: f64) -> IIR1 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let k = flt_tan(flt_pi() * fc / fs)
    let alpha = k / (1.0 + k)
    IIR1 { b0: 1.0 - alpha, b1: 0.0 - (1.0 - alpha), a1: 1.0 - 2.0 * alpha, xprev: 0.0, yprev: 0.0 }
}

pub fn iir1_step(f: &!IIR1, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    let y = f.b0 * x + f.b1 * f.xprev + f.a1 * f.yprev
    f.xprev = x
    f.yprev = y
    y
}

pub fn iir1_apply(f: &!IIR1, inp: &[f64; 512], out: &![f64; 512], n: i64) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = iir1_step(f, inp[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SECOND-ORDER BIQUAD — bilinear-transform notch/bandpass
// ============================================================================

// y[n] = b0*x[n] + b1*x[n-1] + b2*x[n-2] - a1*y[n-1] - a2*y[n-2]

pub struct IIR2 {
    b0: f64, b1: f64, b2: f64,
    a1: f64, a2: f64,
    x1: f64, x2: f64,
    y1: f64, y2: f64,
}

// Notch (band-reject) at f0, bandwidth bw (all in Hz)
pub fn iir2_notch(f0: f64, bw: f64, fs: f64) -> IIR2 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let pi = flt_pi()
    let omega0 = 2.0 * pi * f0 / fs
    let r = 1.0 - pi * bw / fs
    let c = flt_cos(omega0)
    // H(z) = (1 - 2r·cos(ω₀)·z⁻¹ + r²·z⁻²) / (1 - 2cos(ω₀)·z⁻¹ + z⁻²) approx
    let b0 = 1.0
    let b1 = 0.0 - 2.0 * c
    let b2 = 1.0
    let a1 = 0.0 - 2.0 * r * c
    let a2 = r * r
    // normalize DC gain to 1
    let dc_num = b0 + b1 + b2
    let dc_den = 1.0 + a1 + a2
    let g = if flt_abs(dc_den) > 1e-15 { dc_num / dc_den } else { 1.0 }
    IIR2 { b0: b0 / g, b1: b1 / g, b2: b2 / g, a1: a1, a2: a2, x1: 0.0, x2: 0.0, y1: 0.0, y2: 0.0 }
}

// Bandpass at f0, bandwidth bw
pub fn iir2_bandpass(f0: f64, bw: f64, fs: f64) -> IIR2 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let pi = flt_pi()
    let omega0 = 2.0 * pi * f0 / fs
    let r = 1.0 - pi * bw / fs
    let c = flt_cos(omega0)
    let b0 = 1.0 - r
    let b1 = 0.0
    let b2 = 0.0 - (1.0 - r)
    let a1 = 0.0 - 2.0 * r * c
    let a2 = r * r
    IIR2 { b0: b0, b1: b1, b2: b2, a1: a1, a2: a2, x1: 0.0, x2: 0.0, y1: 0.0, y2: 0.0 }
}

pub fn iir2_step(f: &!IIR2, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    let y = f.b0 * x + f.b1 * f.x1 + f.b2 * f.x2 - f.a1 * f.y1 - f.a2 * f.y2
    f.x2 = f.x1
    f.x1 = x
    f.y2 = f.y1
    f.y1 = y
    y
}

pub fn iir2_apply(f: &!IIR2, inp: &[f64; 512], out: &![f64; 512], n: i64) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = iir2_step(f, inp[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// MOVING-AVERAGE FIR (uniform window, up to 64 taps)
// ============================================================================

pub struct FIR64 {
    buf: [f64; 64],
    head: i64,
    taps: i64,
}

pub fn fir64_ma(taps: i64) -> FIR64 {
    FIR64 { buf: [0.0; 64], head: 0, taps: taps }
}

pub fn fir64_step(f: &!FIR64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    f.buf[f.head] = x
    f.head = (f.head + 1) - (f.head + 1) / f.taps * f.taps
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < f.taps {
        sum = sum + f.buf[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / (f.taps as f64)
}

pub fn fir64_apply(f: &!FIR64, inp: &[f64; 512], out: &![f64; 512], n: i64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = fir64_step(f, inp[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

var CNT: [i64; 2] = [0; 2]

fn chk(label: i64, ok: i64) with IO, Mut {
    if ok == 1 {
        print("  PASS ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[0] = CNT[0] + 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[1] = CNT[1] + 1
    }
}

fn near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> i64 {
    let d = a - b
    let d2 = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    if d2 <= tol { 1 } else { 0 }
}

fn test_iir1() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Lowpass at fc=100Hz, fs=1000Hz — steady-state for DC input should be 1.0
    var lp = iir1_lowpass(100.0, 1000.0)
    // Feed 1.0 for 100 samples to reach steady state
    var y: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 100 { y = iir1_step(&!lp, 1.0); i = i + 1 }
    chk(1, near(y, 1.0, 0.01))

    // Highpass at fc=100Hz, fs=1000Hz — DC should be suppressed (→ 0)
    var hp = iir1_highpass(100.0, 1000.0)
    var yh: f64 = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < 100 { yh = iir1_step(&!hp, 1.0); j = j + 1 }
    chk(2, near(yh, 0.0, 0.01))

    // Lowpass passes low freq, attenuates high freq
    // At f << fc, gain ≈ 1; at f >> fc, gain << 1
    var lp2 = iir1_lowpass(50.0, 1000.0)
    var sum_lo: f64 = 0.0
    let pi = flt_pi()
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 64 {
        // low freq: 5 Hz tone
        let xn = flt_sin(2.0 * pi * 5.0 * (k as f64) / 1000.0)
        sum_lo = sum_lo + flt_abs(iir1_step(&!lp2, xn))
        k = k + 1
    }
    var lp3 = iir1_lowpass(50.0, 1000.0)
    var sum_hi: f64 = 0.0
    var m: i64 = 0
    while m < 64 {
        // high freq: 400 Hz tone
        let xn = flt_sin(2.0 * pi * 400.0 * (m as f64) / 1000.0)
        sum_hi = sum_hi + flt_abs(iir1_step(&!lp3, xn))
        m = m + 1
    }
    // Low-freq energy should be much larger than high-freq energy after LP
    chk(3, if sum_lo > sum_hi * 2.0 { 1 } else { 0 })
}

fn test_iir2_notch() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Notch at 60Hz, bw=5Hz, fs=1000Hz — 60Hz tone should be attenuated
    var notch = iir2_notch(60.0, 5.0, 1000.0)
    let pi = flt_pi()
    // Warm up then measure RMS at 60Hz
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 200 {
        let xn = flt_sin(2.0 * pi * 60.0 * (i as f64) / 1000.0)
        iir2_step(&!notch, xn)
        i = i + 1
    }
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < 100 {
        let xn = flt_sin(2.0 * pi * 60.0 * ((200 + j) as f64) / 1000.0)
        let yn = iir2_step(&!notch, xn)
        sum = sum + yn * yn
        j = j + 1
    }
    let rms_notched = flt_sqrt(sum / 100.0)
    // Input RMS = 1/√2 ≈ 0.707, output should be much smaller after notch
    chk(4, if rms_notched < 0.3 { 1 } else { 0 })

    // DC (0 Hz) should pass through notch unchanged: y[n] → 1.0 at steady state
    var notch2 = iir2_notch(60.0, 5.0, 1000.0)
    var ydc: f64 = 0.0
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 200 { ydc = iir2_step(&!notch2, 1.0); k = k + 1 }
    chk(5, near(ydc, 1.0, 0.05))
}

fn test_fir_ma() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Moving average with 4 taps
    var ma = fir64_ma(4)
    // Feed 0, 0, 0, 4: after 4 samples output = (0+0+0+4)/4 = 1
    fir64_step(&!ma, 0.0)
    fir64_step(&!ma, 0.0)
    fir64_step(&!ma, 0.0)
    let y4 = fir64_step(&!ma, 4.0)
    chk(6, near(y4, 1.0, 1e-10))

    // After more 0s, output decays: next should be (0+0+4+0)/4 = 1 still... no wait
    // buf = [4, 0, 0, 0] head=0, then next x=0: buf[0]=0, head=1
    // sum = 0+0+0+4 = 4... wait, I need to think
    // After feeding 0,0,0,4: buf = [0,0,0,4], output=1
    // Feed 0: buf[(head)]=0, so oldest element replaced.
    // Actually: buf starts at [0,0,0,0], head=0
    // x=0: buf[0]=0, head=1, sum=0, output=0
    // x=0: buf[1]=0, head=2, sum=0, output=0
    // x=0: buf[2]=0, head=3, sum=0, output=0
    // x=4: buf[3]=4, head=0, sum=4, output=1
    // x=0: buf[0]=0, head=1, sum=4 (0+0+4+0=4?? no: buf=[0,0,0,4], head=0)
    // Wait: head after x=4 is (3+1)%4=0. Next x=0: buf[0]=0, head=1, sum=buf[0..4]=[0,0,0,4]=4. output=1
    // Actually the order matters. Let me check manually.
    let y5 = fir64_step(&!ma, 0.0)
    chk(7, near(y5, 1.0, 1e-10))   // (0+0+4+0)=4/4=1 still... actually (0,0,4,0) sum=4 since 4 is still in buf

    // Feed 5 more zeros: eventually the 4 should wash out
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 10 { fir64_step(&!ma, 0.0); i = i + 1 }
    let y_end = fir64_step(&!ma, 0.0)
    chk(8, near(y_end, 0.0, 1e-10))

    // Steady-state response to DC=1: should be 1.0
    var ma2 = fir64_ma(8)
    var ydc: f64 = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < 20 { ydc = fir64_step(&!ma2, 1.0); j = j + 1 }
    chk(9, near(ydc, 1.0, 1e-10))
}

fn test_iir1_apply() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var inp: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    var out: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 50 { inp[i] = 1.0; i = i + 1 }
    var lp = iir1_lowpass(100.0, 1000.0)
    iir1_apply(&!lp, &inp, &!out, 50)
    // After 50 samples of DC, last output should be close to 1
    chk(10, near(out[49], 1.0, 0.01))
    // First sample should be smaller (not settled)
    chk(11, if out[0] < out[49] { 1 } else { 0 })
}

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    CNT[0] = 0; CNT[1] = 0
    print("─── stdlib/signal/filter tests ───\n")
    test_iir1()
    test_iir2_notch()
    test_fir_ma()
    test_iir1_apply()
    print("─── "); print(CNT[0]); print("/"); print(CNT[0]+CNT[1]); print(" PASS ───\n")
    if CNT[1] == 0 { print("ALL PASS\n"); 0 } else { 1 }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/signal/fractal.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL PASS

// stdlib/signal/fractal.sio — Fractal Dimension and Complexity Analysis
//
// Higuchi Fractal Dimension (HFD): time-domain complexity via curve-length scaling
// Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (DFA): long-range correlation exponent
// Permutation Entropy (PE): ordinal pattern diversity (order m ≤ 6)
// All functions operate on fixed-size [f64; 1024] buffers with explicit length n.

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn frc_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn frc_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

// Natural log via identity: ln(x) = 2*arctanh((x-1)/(x+1))
// arctanh(t) = t + t³/3 + t⁵/5 + ... converges for |t| < 1
fn frc_log(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1e15 }
    // Reduce x to [1, 2) by factoring out powers of 2
    var v = x
    var exp2: i64 = 0
    while v >= 2.0 { v = v * 0.5; exp2 = exp2 + 1 }
    while v < 1.0 { v = v * 2.0; exp2 = exp2 - 1 }
    // ln(x) = exp2 * ln(2) + ln(v), v in [1, 2)
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    // t = (v-1)/(v+1) in [0, 1/3)
    let t = (v - 1.0) / (v + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    // arctanh(t) = t(1 + t²/3 + t⁴/5 + t⁶/7 + t⁸/9 + t¹⁰/11 + t¹²/13)
    let series = t * (1.0 + t2 * (1.0 / 3.0 + t2 * (1.0 / 5.0 + t2 * (1.0 / 7.0 + t2 * (1.0 / 9.0 + t2 * (1.0 / 11.0 + t2 / 13.0))))))
    let ln_v = 2.0 * series
    (exp2 as f64) * ln2 + ln_v
}

// ============================================================================
// HIGUCHI FRACTAL DIMENSION
// ============================================================================

// HFD measures slope of log(L(k)) vs log(k); steep slope → complex signal.
// signal[0..n-1]: input, k_max: max scale (typ 8–32), returns (HFD, R²)
pub fn higuchi_fd(signal: &[f64; 1024], n: i64, k_max: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 10 || k_max < 2 { return 0.0 }
    var log_k: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var log_L: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var n_pts: i64 = 0
    var k: i64 = 1
    while k <= k_max && k <= n / 4 {
        var L_sum: f64 = 0.0
        var m: i64 = 1
        while m <= k {
            let n_terms = (n - m) / k
            if n_terms > 0 {
                var curve: f64 = 0.0
                var ii: i64 = 1
                while ii <= n_terms {
                    let idx1 = m + ii * k - 1
                    let idx2 = m + (ii - 1) * k - 1
                    if idx1 < n && idx2 < n {
                        curve = curve + frc_abs(signal[idx1] - signal[idx2])
                    }
                    ii = ii + 1
                }
                let norm = (n - 1) as f64 / ((n_terms as f64) * (k as f64) * (k as f64))
                L_sum = L_sum + curve * norm
            }
            m = m + 1
        }
        let L_k = L_sum / (k as f64)
        if L_k > 0.0 {
            log_k[n_pts] = frc_log(k as f64)
            log_L[n_pts] = frc_log(L_k)
            n_pts = n_pts + 1
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    if n_pts < 2 { return 0.0 }
    // Ordinary least-squares slope of log_L vs log_k
    var sum_x: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_y: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_pts { sum_x = sum_x + log_k[i]; sum_y = sum_y + log_L[i]; i = i + 1 }
    let mx = sum_x / (n_pts as f64)
    let my = sum_y / (n_pts as f64)
    var sxy: f64 = 0.0
    var sxx: f64 = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n_pts {
        let dx = log_k[j] - mx
        sxy = sxy + dx * (log_L[j] - my)
        sxx = sxx + dx * dx
        j = j + 1
    }
    if sxx < 1e-15 { return 0.0 }
    // Slope is negative (L decreases with k); FD = -slope
    0.0 - sxy / sxx
}

// ============================================================================
// PERMUTATION ENTROPY
// ============================================================================

// Order-m PE; m ≤ 6 (6! = 720 patterns fit in [i64; 720])
// Counts ordinal patterns of length m in the signal.
// Returns normalized PE in [0, 1].
pub fn permutation_entropy(signal: &[f64; 1024], n: i64, m: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if m < 2 || m > 6 || n < m + 1 { return 0.0 }
    // Compute ordinal rank pattern index for each embedding
    // Pattern index: encode sort-order of m elements as base-m factorial number
    var counts: [i64; 720] = [0; 720]
    var idx: [i64; 6] = [0; 6]
    var total: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n - m + 1 {
        // Compute rank-order of signal[i..i+m]
        // rank[j] = number of elements in window less than signal[i+j]
        var r: i64 = 0
        var q: i64 = 0
        while q < m {
            let val = signal[i + q]
            var rank: i64 = 0
            var p: i64 = 0
            while p < m {
                if p != q && signal[i + p] < val { rank = rank + 1 }
                p = p + 1
            }
            idx[q] = rank
            q = q + 1
        }
        // Convert rank vector to a single integer index via factoradic encoding
        // Simple approach: encode as mixed-radix number (not full factoradic, but bijective for distinct ranks)
        var pattern: i64 = 0
        var fac: i64 = 1
        var k: i64 = m - 1
        while k >= 0 {
            pattern = pattern + idx[k] * fac
            fac = fac * (m - k)
            k = k - 1
        }
        if pattern >= 0 && pattern < 720 {
            counts[pattern] = counts[pattern] + 1
        }
        total = total + 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    if total == 0 { return 0.0 }
    // Compute Shannon entropy
    var entropy: f64 = 0.0
    var p: i64 = 0
    while p < 720 {
        if counts[p] > 0 {
            let prob = (counts[p] as f64) / (total as f64)
            entropy = entropy - prob * frc_log(prob)
        }
        p = p + 1
    }
    // Normalize by log(m!) = max entropy
    var max_fac: i64 = 1
    var f: i64 = 1
    while f <= m { max_fac = max_fac * f; f = f + 1 }
    let max_ent = frc_log(max_fac as f64)
    if max_ent < 1e-15 { return 0.0 }
    entropy / max_ent
}

// ============================================================================
// DETRENDED FLUCTUATION ANALYSIS (DFA)
// ============================================================================

// Alpha exponent from slope of log(F(s)) vs log(s).
// 0.5 = uncorrelated (white noise), 1.0 = 1/f noise, 1.5 = Brownian motion.
pub fn dfa(signal: &[f64; 1024], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 16 { return 0.5 }
    // Compute cumulative sum profile
    var profile: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var mean: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n { mean = mean + signal[i]; i = i + 1 }
    mean = mean / (n as f64)
    var cum: f64 = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n {
        cum = cum + (signal[j] - mean)
        profile[j] = cum
        j = j + 1
    }
    // Compute F(s) for scales s = 4, 8, 16, 32, 64
    var log_s: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var log_F: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var n_scales: i64 = 0
    var s: i64 = 4
    while s <= n / 4 && n_scales < 8 {
        let n_segs = n / s
        if n_segs < 1 { s = s * 2; }
        if n_segs >= 1 {
            var rms_sum: f64 = 0.0
            var seg: i64 = 0
            while seg < n_segs {
                let seg_start = seg * s
                // Linear detrend: fit y = a*t + b to profile[seg_start..seg_start+s]
                var sx: f64 = 0.0
                var sy: f64 = 0.0
                var sxy2: f64 = 0.0
                var sxx2: f64 = 0.0
                var t: i64 = 0
                while t < s {
                    let tf = t as f64
                    sx = sx + tf
                    sy = sy + profile[seg_start + t]
                    sxy2 = sxy2 + tf * profile[seg_start + t]
                    sxx2 = sxx2 + tf * tf
                    t = t + 1
                }
                let sf = s as f64
                let denom = sf * sxx2 - sx * sx
                var a: f64 = 0.0
                var b: f64 = 0.0
                if frc_abs(denom) > 1e-15 {
                    a = (sf * sxy2 - sx * sy) / denom
                    b = (sy - a * sx) / sf
                }
                var mse: f64 = 0.0
                var u: i64 = 0
                while u < s {
                    let trend = a * (u as f64) + b
                    let res = profile[seg_start + u] - trend
                    mse = mse + res * res
                    u = u + 1
                }
                rms_sum = rms_sum + mse / (s as f64)
                seg = seg + 1
            }
            let F_s = frc_sqrt(rms_sum / (n_segs as f64))
            if F_s > 0.0 {
                log_s[n_scales] = frc_log(s as f64)
                log_F[n_scales] = frc_log(F_s)
                n_scales = n_scales + 1
            }
        }
        s = s * 2
    }
    if n_scales < 2 { return 0.5 }
    var sum_x2: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_y2: f64 = 0.0
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n_scales { sum_x2 = sum_x2 + log_s[k]; sum_y2 = sum_y2 + log_F[k]; k = k + 1 }
    let mx2 = sum_x2 / (n_scales as f64)
    let my2 = sum_y2 / (n_scales as f64)
    var sxy2: f64 = 0.0
    var sxx2: f64 = 0.0
    var q: i64 = 0
    while q < n_scales {
        let dx = log_s[q] - mx2
        sxy2 = sxy2 + dx * (log_F[q] - my2)
        sxx2 = sxx2 + dx * dx
        q = q + 1
    }
    if sxx2 < 1e-15 { return 0.5 }
    sxy2 / sxx2
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

var CNT: [i64; 2] = [0; 2]

fn chk(label: i64, ok: i64) with IO, Mut {
    if ok == 1 {
        print("  PASS ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[0] = CNT[0] + 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL ["); print(label); print("]\n")
        CNT[1] = CNT[1] + 1
    }
}

fn near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> i64 {
    let d = a - b
    let d2 = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    if d2 <= tol { 1 } else { 0 }
}

fn test_log() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // ln(1) = 0
    chk(1, near(frc_log(1.0), 0.0, 1e-10))
    // ln(e) ≈ 1 (e ≈ 2.71828)
    chk(2, near(frc_log(2.71828182845905), 1.0, 1e-6))
    // ln(2) ≈ 0.6931
    chk(3, near(frc_log(2.0), 0.6931471805599453, 1e-8))
    // ln(100) = ln(4) + ln(25) ≈ 4.605
    chk(4, near(frc_log(100.0), 4.605170185988092, 1e-6))
}

fn test_higuchi() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Constant signal → HFD ≈ 0 (flat, minimum complexity)
    var flat: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 128 { flat[i] = 1.0; i = i + 1 }
    let hfd_flat = higuchi_fd(&flat, 128, 8)
    chk(5, if frc_abs(hfd_flat) < 1.0 { 1 } else { 0 })

    // Linear ramp → HFD ≈ 1.0 (smooth, single-scale)
    var ramp: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < 128 { ramp[j] = j as f64; j = j + 1 }
    let hfd_ramp = higuchi_fd(&ramp, 128, 8)
    chk(6, if hfd_ramp > 0.5 && hfd_ramp < 1.5 { 1 } else { 0 })

    // Pseudo-random (LCG) signal → high HFD > ramp HFD
    var noise: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var lcg: i64 = 1234567
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 128 {
        lcg = (lcg * 1664525 + 1013904223) - (lcg * 1664525 + 1013904223) / 1000000000 * 1000000000
        noise[k] = (lcg as f64) / 500000000.0 - 1.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    let hfd_noise = higuchi_fd(&noise, 128, 8)
    // Pseudo-random signal should have higher FD than a smooth ramp
    chk(7, if hfd_noise > hfd_ramp { 1 } else { 0 })
}

fn test_pe() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Constant signal → only one pattern → PE = 0
    var flat: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 64 { flat[i] = 5.0; i = i + 1 }
    let pe_flat = permutation_entropy(&flat, 64, 3)
    chk(8, near(pe_flat, 0.0, 0.01))

    // Monotone increasing → PE = 0 (only one ordinal pattern)
    var ramp: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < 64 { ramp[j] = j as f64; j = j + 1 }
    let pe_ramp = permutation_entropy(&ramp, 64, 3)
    chk(9, near(pe_ramp, 0.0, 0.01))

    // Mixed signal → PE > 0
    var mixed: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 64 {
        // Cycle through 4 values to get mixed ordinal patterns
        let r = k - (k / 4) * 4
        mixed[k] = if r == 0 { 1.0 } else if r == 1 { 3.0 } else if r == 2 { 2.0 } else { 4.0 }
        k = k + 1
    }
    let pe_mixed = permutation_entropy(&mixed, 64, 3)
    chk(10, if pe_mixed > 0.3 { 1 } else { 0 })
}

fn test_dfa() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // White noise (alternating ±1) → DFA exponent ≈ 0.5
    var wn: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 512 {
        wn[i] = if (i - i / 2 * 2) == 0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 - 1.0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let alpha_wn = dfa(&wn, 512)
    // For purely alternating signal, DFA exponent should be < 1
    chk(11, if alpha_wn < 1.2 { 1 } else { 0 })

    // Linear ramp (cumulative DC) → DFA exponent should be > 1 (strong correlations)
    var rw: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < 256 { rw[j] = j as f64; j = j + 1 }
    let alpha_rw = dfa(&rw, 256)
    chk(12, if alpha_rw > 1.0 { 1 } else { 0 })
}

pub fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    CNT[0] = 0; CNT[1] = 0
    print("─── stdlib/signal/fractal tests ───\n")
    test_log()
    test_higuchi()
    test_pe()
    test_dfa()
    print("─── "); print(CNT[0]); print("/"); print(CNT[0]+CNT[1]); print(" PASS ───\n")
    if CNT[1] == 0 { print("ALL PASS\n"); 0 } else { 1 }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/signal/lib.sio ===
// signal — Digital signal processing for biosignal analysis
//
// FFT, digital filters, spectral analysis, wavelet transforms, fractal complexity,
// and event-locked epoching for EEG/ERP and time-series data.
//
// Submodules:
//   fft       — Radix-2 FFT with GUM epistemic uncertainty propagation
//   filter    — IIR/FIR digital filters (Butterworth, Chebyshev, notch, bandpass)
//   spectral  — PSD estimation: periodogram, Welch, EEG band power
//   wavelets  — Discrete wavelet transform (Haar, db4) + thresholding denoising
//   fractal   — Higuchi FD, DFA, permutation entropy for complexity analysis
//   epoch     — Event-locked segmentation with baseline correction and artifact rejection

pub use fft::{
    ComplexArray, EpistemicSpectrum,
    complex_array_new, complex_array_from_real,
    fft_forward, fft_inverse,
    fft_magnitude, fft_phase, fft_power_spectrum,
    fft_epistemic,
}


// === FILE: stdlib/signal/spectral.sio ===
// signal::spectral — Power Spectral Density Estimation
//
// Frequency-domain analysis of signals with uncertainty quantification.
// Essential for EEG band power analysis (delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma).
//
// Methods:
// - Periodogram: Raw FFT-based PSD
// - Welch: Averaged periodograms with overlap (recommended)
// - Band Power: Integrated PSD over frequency bands
//
// References:
// - Welch (1967): "The Use of FFT for Estimation of Power Spectra"
// - Percival & Walden (1993): "Spectral Analysis for Physical Applications"

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sin(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn cos(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64;
}

fn pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

// ============================================================================
// FFT (Radix-2 Cooley-Tukey)
// ============================================================================

// Maximum FFT size
fn MAX_FFT() -> i64 { 2048 }

// Bit reversal for FFT
fn bit_reverse(n: i64, bits: i64) -> i64 {
    var result: i64 = 0
    var n_var = n
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < bits {
        result = (result << 1) | (n_var & 1)
        n_var = n_var >> 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// In-place radix-2 FFT
fn fft_inplace(x_re: [f64; 2048], x_im: [f64; 2048], n: i64, inverse: bool) -> ([f64; 2048], [f64; 2048]) {
    var re = x_re
    var im = x_im

    // Compute number of bits
    var bits: i64 = 0
    var temp = n
    while temp > 1 {
        bits = bits + 1
        temp = temp / 2
    }

    // Bit-reversal permutation
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let j = bit_reverse(i, bits)
        if i < j {
            // Swap
            let tmp_re = re[i as usize]
            let tmp_im = im[i as usize]
            re[i as usize] = re[j as usize]
            im[i as usize] = im[j as usize]
            re[j as usize] = tmp_re
            im[j as usize] = tmp_im
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Cooley-Tukey iterations
    var size: i64 = 2
    while size <= n {
        let half = size / 2
        let angle_mult = if inverse { 2.0 * pi() / (size as f64) } else { -2.0 * pi() / (size as f64) }

        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < n {
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < half {
                let angle = angle_mult * (j as f64)
                let w_re = cos(angle)
                let w_im = sin(angle)

                let idx1 = (k + j) as usize
                let idx2 = (k + j + half) as usize

                let even_re = re[idx1]
                let even_im = im[idx1]
                let odd_re = re[idx2]
                let odd_im = im[idx2]

                // t = w * odd
                let t_re = w_re * odd_re - w_im * odd_im
                let t_im = w_re * odd_im + w_im * odd_re

                re[idx1] = even_re + t_re
                im[idx1] = even_im + t_im
                re[idx2] = even_re - t_re
                im[idx2] = even_im - t_im

                j = j + 1
            }
            k = k + size
        }
        size = size * 2
    }

    // Scale for inverse FFT
    if inverse {
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            re[i as usize] = re[i as usize] / (n as f64)
            im[i as usize] = im[i as usize] / (n as f64)
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    return (re, im)
}

// Compute FFT of real signal
fn rfft(signal: [f64; 2048], n: i64) -> ([f64; 1025], [f64; 1025]) {
    // Copy to work arrays
    var work_re: [f64; 2048] = [0.0; 2048]
    var work_im: [f64; 2048] = [0.0; 2048]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        work_re[i as usize] = signal[i as usize]
        work_im[i as usize] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute FFT
    let result = fft_inplace(work_re, work_im, n, false)
    let fft_re = result.0
    let fft_im = result.1

    // Copy positive frequencies
    var out_re: [f64; 1025] = [0.0; 1025]
    var out_im: [f64; 1025] = [0.0; 1025]
    let n_out = n / 2 + 1
    i = 0
    while i < n_out {
        out_re[i as usize] = fft_re[i as usize]
        out_im[i as usize] = fft_im[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    return (out_re, out_im)
}

// ============================================================================
// WINDOW FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn hann_window(n: i64, i: i64) -> f64 {
    0.5 * (1.0 - cos(2.0 * pi() * (i as f64) / ((n - 1) as f64)))
}

fn hamming_window(n: i64, i: i64) -> f64 {
    0.54 - 0.46 * cos(2.0 * pi() * (i as f64) / ((n - 1) as f64))
}

fn blackman_harris_window(n: i64, i: i64) -> f64 {
    let a0 = 0.35875
    let a1 = 0.48829
    let a2 = 0.14128
    let a3 = 0.01168
    let x = (i as f64) / ((n - 1) as f64)
    return a0 - a1 * cos(2.0 * pi() * x) + a2 * cos(4.0 * pi() * x) - a3 * cos(6.0 * pi() * x)
}

// Window type constants
fn WINDOW_HANN() -> i32 { 0 }
fn WINDOW_HAMMING() -> i32 { 1 }
fn WINDOW_BLACKMAN_HARRIS() -> i32 { 2 }
fn WINDOW_RECT() -> i32 { 3 }

fn apply_window(signal: [f64; 2048], n: i64, window_type: i32) -> [f64; 2048] {
    var output: [f64; 2048] = [0.0; 2048]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let w = if window_type == WINDOW_HANN() {
            hann_window(n, i)
        } else if window_type == WINDOW_HAMMING() {
            hamming_window(n, i)
        } else if window_type == WINDOW_BLACKMAN_HARRIS() {
            blackman_harris_window(n, i)
        } else {
            1.0  // Rectangular
        };
        output[i as usize] = signal[i as usize] * w
        i = i + 1
    }
    return output
}

// Compute window power (for normalization)
fn window_power(n: i64, window_type: i32) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let w = if window_type == WINDOW_HANN() {
            hann_window(n, i)
        } else if window_type == WINDOW_HAMMING() {
            hamming_window(n, i)
        } else if window_type == WINDOW_BLACKMAN_HARRIS() {
            blackman_harris_window(n, i)
        } else {
            1.0
        };
        sum = sum + w * w
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// ============================================================================
// PERIODOGRAM
// ============================================================================

// PSD result
struct PSDResult {
    power: [f64; 1025],     // Power spectral density (n_freqs values)
    freqs: [f64; 1025],     // Frequency bins (Hz)
    n_freqs: i64,           // Number of frequency bins
    df: f64,                // Frequency resolution (Hz)
}

fn psd_result_new() -> PSDResult {
    PSDResult {
        power: [0.0; 1025],
        freqs: [0.0; 1025],
        n_freqs: 0,
        df: 0.0,
    }
}

// Compute periodogram (raw FFT-based PSD)
fn periodogram(signal: [f64; 2048], n: i64, fs: f64, window_type: i32) -> PSDResult {
    var result = psd_result_new()

    // Find next power of 2
    var nfft: i64 = 1
    while nfft < n {
        nfft = nfft * 2
    }

    // Apply window
    let windowed = apply_window(signal, n, window_type)

    // Compute FFT
    let fft_result = rfft(windowed, nfft)
    let fft_re = fft_result.0
    let fft_im = fft_result.1

    // Compute power spectral density
    let n_freqs = nfft / 2 + 1
    let df = fs / (nfft as f64)
    let win_power = window_power(n, window_type)
    let scale = 1.0 / (fs * win_power)

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_freqs {
        let mag_sq = fft_re[i as usize] * fft_re[i as usize] +
                     fft_im[i as usize] * fft_im[i as usize]

        // One-sided PSD (multiply by 2 except DC and Nyquist)
        let factor = if i == 0 || i == n_freqs - 1 { 1.0 } else { 2.0 }
        result.power[i as usize] = factor * scale * mag_sq
        result.freqs[i as usize] = (i as f64) * df

        i = i + 1
    }

    result.n_freqs = n_freqs
    result.df = df
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// WELCH'S METHOD
// ============================================================================

// Welch PSD configuration
struct WelchConfig {
    segment_length: i64,    // Length of each segment (samples)
    overlap: f64,           // Overlap fraction (0.0 to 1.0, typically 0.5)
    window_type: i32,
    detrend: bool,          // Remove linear trend from each segment
}

fn welch_config_default(n: i64) -> WelchConfig {
    // Default: 8 segments with 50% overlap
    let seg_len = n / 4  // Results in ~8 segments with 50% overlap
    WelchConfig {
        segment_length: seg_len,
        overlap: 0.5,
        window_type: WINDOW_HANN(),
        detrend: true,
    }
}

// Remove linear trend from segment
fn detrend_linear(segment: [f64; 2048], n: i64) -> [f64; 2048] {
    var result = segment

    // Compute linear regression: y = a + b*x
    var sum_x = 0.0
    var sum_y = 0.0
    var sum_xx = 0.0
    var sum_xy = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let x = i as f64
        let y = segment[i as usize]
        sum_x = sum_x + x
        sum_y = sum_y + y
        sum_xx = sum_xx + x * x
        sum_xy = sum_xy + x * y
        i = i + 1
    }

    let nf = n as f64
    let denom = nf * sum_xx - sum_x * sum_x
    if denom != 0.0 {
        let b = (nf * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / denom
        let a = (sum_y - b * sum_x) / nf

        // Subtract trend
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            result[i as usize] = result[i as usize] - (a + b * (i as f64))
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    return result
}

// Compute PSD using Welch's method
fn welch(signal: [f64; 2048], n: i64, fs: f64, config: WelchConfig) -> PSDResult {
    var result = psd_result_new()

    let seg_len = config.segment_length
    var step = ((1.0 - config.overlap) * (seg_len as f64)) as i64
    step = if step < 1 { 1 } else { step }

    // Find NFFT (next power of 2 >= seg_len)
    var nfft: i64 = 1
    while nfft < seg_len {
        nfft = nfft * 2
    }

    let n_freqs = nfft / 2 + 1
    let df = fs / (nfft as f64)

    // Initialize accumulator
    var power_sum: [f64; 1025] = [0.0; 1025]
    var n_segments: i64 = 0

    // Process segments
    var start: i64 = 0
    while start + seg_len <= n {
        // Extract segment
        var segment: [f64; 2048] = [0.0; 2048]
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < seg_len {
            segment[i as usize] = signal[(start + i) as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Detrend if requested
        if config.detrend {
            segment = detrend_linear(segment, seg_len)
        }

        // Compute periodogram of segment
        let seg_psd = periodogram(segment, seg_len, fs, config.window_type)

        // Accumulate
        i = 0
        while i < n_freqs {
            power_sum[i as usize] = power_sum[i as usize] + seg_psd.power[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }

        n_segments = n_segments + 1
        start = start + step
    }

    // Average
    if n_segments > 0 {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n_freqs {
            result.power[i as usize] = power_sum[i as usize] / (n_segments as f64)
            result.freqs[i as usize] = (i as f64) * df
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    result.n_freqs = n_freqs
    result.df = df
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// BAND POWER
// ============================================================================

// EEG frequency bands
struct FreqBand {
    name_code: i32,  // 0=delta, 1=theta, 2=alpha, 3=beta, 4=gamma
    f_low: f64,
    f_high: f64,
}

fn band_delta() -> FreqBand { FreqBand { name_code: 0, f_low: 0.5, f_high: 4.0 } }
fn band_theta() -> FreqBand { FreqBand { name_code: 1, f_low: 4.0, f_high: 8.0 } }
fn band_alpha() -> FreqBand { FreqBand { name_code: 2, f_low: 8.0, f_high: 13.0 } }
fn band_beta() -> FreqBand { FreqBand { name_code: 3, f_low: 13.0, f_high: 30.0 } }
fn band_gamma() -> FreqBand { FreqBand { name_code: 4, f_low: 30.0, f_high: 100.0 } }

// Compute band power by integrating PSD over frequency range
fn band_power(psd: PSDResult, f_low: f64, f_high: f64) -> f64 {
    var power = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < psd.n_freqs {
        let f = psd.freqs[i as usize]
        if f >= f_low && f <= f_high {
            power = power + psd.power[i as usize] * psd.df
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return power
}

// Compute relative band power (fraction of total power)
fn relative_band_power(psd: PSDResult, f_low: f64, f_high: f64) -> f64 {
    let bp = band_power(psd, f_low, f_high)
    let total = band_power(psd, 0.5, psd.freqs[(psd.n_freqs - 1) as usize])

    if total > 0.0 {
        return bp / total
    } else {
        return 0.0
    }
}

// Band power result with all standard EEG bands
struct EEGBandPower {
    delta: f64,
    theta: f64,
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64,
    gamma: f64,
    total: f64,
}

fn eeg_band_power(psd: PSDResult) -> EEGBandPower {
    EEGBandPower {
        delta: band_power(psd, 0.5, 4.0),
        theta: band_power(psd, 4.0, 8.0),
        alpha: band_power(psd, 8.0, 13.0),
        beta: band_power(psd, 13.0, 30.0),
        gamma: band_power(psd, 30.0, 100.0),
        total: band_power(psd, 0.5, 100.0),
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PEAK FREQUENCY
// ============================================================================

// Find peak frequency in a band
fn peak_frequency(psd: PSDResult, f_low: f64, f_high: f64) -> f64 {
    var max_power = 0.0
    var peak_freq = (f_low + f_high) / 2.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < psd.n_freqs {
        let f = psd.freqs[i as usize]
        if f >= f_low && f <= f_high {
            if psd.power[i as usize] > max_power {
                max_power = psd.power[i as usize]
                peak_freq = f
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return peak_freq
}

// Individual Alpha Frequency (IAF) — peak in alpha band
fn individual_alpha_frequency(psd: PSDResult) -> f64 {
    return peak_frequency(psd, 8.0, 13.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// SPECTRAL ENTROPY
// ============================================================================

// Compute spectral entropy (measure of signal complexity)
// Returns value between 0 (pure tone) and 1 (white noise)
fn spectral_entropy(psd: PSDResult, f_low: f64, f_high: f64) -> f64 {
    // Normalize PSD to probability distribution
    var total = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < psd.n_freqs {
        let f = psd.freqs[i as usize]
        if f >= f_low && f <= f_high {
            total = total + psd.power[i as usize]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if total == 0.0 {
        return 0.0
    }

    // Compute Shannon entropy
    var entropy = 0.0
    var n_bins: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < psd.n_freqs {
        let f = psd.freqs[i as usize]
        if f >= f_low && f <= f_high {
            let p = psd.power[i as usize] / total
            if p > 0.0 {
                entropy = entropy - p * log(p)
            }
            n_bins = n_bins + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Normalize by maximum entropy (uniform distribution)
    if n_bins > 1 {
        return entropy / log(n_bins as f64)
    } else {
        return 0.0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { -x } else { x }
}

fn test_fft_basic() -> bool {
    // Test FFT of known signal: cos(2*pi*f*t) should have peak at f
    var signal: [f64; 2048] = [0.0; 2048]
    let fs = 256.0
    let f0 = 10.0  // 10 Hz

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 256 {
        let t = (i as f64) / fs
        signal[i as usize] = cos(2.0 * pi() * f0 * t)
        i = i + 1
    }

    let psd = periodogram(signal, 256, fs, WINDOW_HANN())

    // Find peak frequency
    var max_power = 0.0
    var peak_idx: i64 = 0
    i = 1  // Skip DC
    while i < psd.n_freqs - 1 {
        if psd.power[i as usize] > max_power {
            max_power = psd.power[i as usize]
            peak_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let peak_f = psd.freqs[peak_idx as usize]
    return abs_f64(peak_f - f0) < 2.0  // Within 2 Hz
}

fn test_welch() -> bool {
    // Generate noisy sinusoid
    var signal: [f64; 2048] = [0.0; 2048]
    let fs = 256.0
    let f0 = 10.0

    var rng_state: i64 = 42
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 1024 {
        let t = (i as f64) / fs
        // Simple LCG for noise
        rng_state = (rng_state * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let noise = ((rng_state as f64) / 2147483648.0 - 0.5) * 0.5
        signal[i as usize] = cos(2.0 * pi() * f0 * t) + noise
        i = i + 1
    }

    let config = welch_config_default(1024)
    let psd = welch(signal, 1024, fs, config)

    // Check that we have valid PSD
    if psd.n_freqs == 0 {
        return false
    }

    // Peak should be near 10 Hz
    let peak = peak_frequency(psd, 5.0, 15.0)
    return abs_f64(peak - f0) < 3.0
}

fn test_band_power() -> bool {
    // Generate signal with known band content
    var signal: [f64; 2048] = [0.0; 2048]
    let fs = 256.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 512 {
        let t = (i as f64) / fs
        // Alpha: 10 Hz, amplitude 2
        // Beta: 20 Hz, amplitude 1
        signal[i as usize] = 2.0 * cos(2.0 * pi() * 10.0 * t) + 1.0 * cos(2.0 * pi() * 20.0 * t)
        i = i + 1
    }

    let config = welch_config_default(512)
    let psd = welch(signal, 512, fs, config)

    let bands = eeg_band_power(psd)

    // Alpha should have more power than beta (due to higher amplitude)
    return bands.alpha > bands.beta
}

fn test_spectral_entropy() -> bool {
    // Pure tone should have low entropy
    var tone: [f64; 2048] = [0.0; 2048]
    let fs = 256.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 256 {
        let t = (i as f64) / fs
        tone[i as usize] = cos(2.0 * pi() * 10.0 * t)
        i = i + 1
    }

    let psd_tone = periodogram(tone, 256, fs, WINDOW_HANN())
    let entropy_tone = spectral_entropy(psd_tone, 0.5, 100.0)

    // Entropy should be low for pure tone
    entropy_tone < 0.5
}


// === FILE: stdlib/signal/wavelets.sio ===
// signal::wavelets — Discrete Wavelet Transform
//
// Implements single-level and multi-level discrete wavelet transforms (DWT)
// for signal analysis and denoising.
//
// Wavelets supported:
//   - Haar: Oldest and simplest wavelet. Perfect reconstruction.
//   - Daubechies-4 (db4): 4-tap orthogonal wavelet with 2 vanishing moments.
//
// Operations:
//   - Forward DWT: Signal → (approximation, detail) coefficients
//   - Inverse DWT: (approximation, detail) → signal (perfect reconstruction)
//   - Hard thresholding: Zero out |coeff| < threshold (sparse denoising)
//   - Soft thresholding: Shrink by threshold (smooth denoising)
//   - Signal energy: Parseval's theorem: energy preserved under orthogonal DWT
//   - SNR: Signal-to-noise ratio in dB
//
// References:
//   - Daubechies (1992): "Ten Lectures on Wavelets", SIAM
//   - Mallat (1989): "A Theory for Multiresolution Signal Decomposition"
//   - Donoho & Johnstone (1994): "Ideal Spatial Adaptation by Wavelet Shrinkage"

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn wav_f64_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn wav_f64_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn wav_f64_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

fn wav_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

// log base 10 approximation (for SNR in dB)
fn wav_log10(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000.0 }
    // log10(x) = log(x) / log(10), log via Taylor around 1
    // Use: ln(x) = 2 * arctanh((x-1)/(x+1)) — valid for all x > 0
    // First normalize: factor out powers of 2
    var v = x
    var exponent: i64 = 0
    while v > 2.0 { v = v / 2.0 ; exponent = exponent + 1 }
    while v < 0.5 { v = v * 2.0 ; exponent = exponent - 1 }
    // Now v in [0.5, 2]; compute ln(v) via arctanh series
    let u = (v - 1.0) / (v + 1.0)
    let u2 = u * u
    let ln_v = 2.0 * u * (1.0 + u2 / 3.0 + u2 * u2 / 5.0 + u2 * u2 * u2 / 7.0 + u2 * u2 * u2 * u2 / 9.0 + u2 * u2 * u2 * u2 * u2 / 11.0)
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    let log10e = 0.4342944819032518  // 1/ln(10)
    return log10e * (ln_v + (exponent as f64) * ln2)
}

// ============================================================================
// HAAR WAVELET
//
// The Haar wavelet is the simplest orthogonal wavelet:
//   Scaling function φ: indicator of [0, 1)
//   Wavelet function ψ: +1 on [0, 0.5), -1 on [0.5, 1)
//
// Forward transform (analysis):
//   approx[i] = (signal[2i] + signal[2i+1]) / sqrt(2)
//   detail[i]  = (signal[2i] - signal[2i+1]) / sqrt(2)
//
// Inverse transform (synthesis):
//   signal[2i]   = (approx[i] + detail[i]) / sqrt(2)
//   signal[2i+1] = (approx[i] - detail[i]) / sqrt(2)
//
// The sqrt(2) factors ensure orthogonality and energy preservation.
// ============================================================================

// Haar forward DWT: signal[0..n-1] → (approx[0..n/2-1], detail[0..n/2-1])
// n must be even and <= 512
// Returns n/2 (number of coefficients in each output band)
fn wav_haar_forward(signal: [f64; 512], n: i64, out_approx: &! [f64; 256], out_detail: &! [f64; 256]) -> i64 {
    let half_n = n / 2
    let sqrt2 = 1.41421356237309504880  // sqrt(2)
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.70710678118654752440  // 1/sqrt(2)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < half_n {
        let a = signal[(2 * i) as usize]
        let b = signal[(2 * i + 1) as usize]
        out_approx[i as usize] = (a + b) * inv_sqrt2
        out_detail[i as usize] = (a - b) * inv_sqrt2
        i = i + 1
    }
    return half_n
}

// Haar inverse DWT: (approx, detail) → signal
// n: number of coefficients in each band (output has 2*n samples)
// Returns 2*n (length of reconstructed signal)
fn wav_haar_inverse(approx: [f64; 256], detail: [f64; 256], n: i64, out: &! [f64; 512]) -> i64 {
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.70710678118654752440
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let a = approx[i as usize]
        let d = detail[i as usize]
        out[(2 * i) as usize] = (a + d) * inv_sqrt2
        out[(2 * i + 1) as usize] = (a - d) * inv_sqrt2
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 2 * n
}

// ============================================================================
// SIGNAL ENERGY (Parseval's theorem)
//
// E = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} signal[i]^2
// Under an orthonormal DWT: E_signal = E_approx + E_detail
// ============================================================================

fn wav_energy(signal: [f64; 512], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var e = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let x = signal[i as usize]
        e = e + x * x
        i = i + 1
    }
    return e
}

fn wav_energy_256(signal: [f64; 256], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var e = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let x = signal[i as usize]
        e = e + x * x
        i = i + 1
    }
    return e
}

// ============================================================================
// THRESHOLDING
//
// Hard thresholding (Donoho, 1994):
//   T_hard(x, λ) = 0 if |x| < λ, x otherwise
//   Creates sparse representation; discontinuous at ±λ.
//
// Soft thresholding (shrinkage):
//   T_soft(x, λ) = sign(x) * max(0, |x| - λ)
//   Continuous, biased estimator; preferred for denoising.
// ============================================================================

// Hard thresholding: in-place zeroing of small detail coefficients
// Returns number of surviving (non-zero) coefficients
fn wav_threshold_hard(detail: &! [f64; 256], n: i64, thresh: f64) -> i64 {
    var surviving: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let v = detail[i as usize]
        if wav_f64_abs(v) < thresh {
            detail[i as usize] = 0.0
        } else {
            surviving = surviving + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return surviving
}

// Soft thresholding: in-place shrinkage of detail coefficients
// Returns number of surviving (non-zero) coefficients
fn wav_threshold_soft(detail: &! [f64; 256], n: i64, thresh: f64) -> i64 {
    var surviving: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let v = detail[i as usize]
        let av = wav_f64_abs(v)
        if av <= thresh {
            detail[i as usize] = 0.0
        } else {
            if v > 0.0 {
                detail[i as usize] = av - thresh
            } else {
                detail[i as usize] = 0.0 - (av - thresh)
            }
            surviving = surviving + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return surviving
}

// ============================================================================
// SIGNAL-TO-NOISE RATIO
//
// SNR = 10 * log10(E_signal / E_noise)
// where E_noise = sum (original[i] - reconstructed[i])^2
// A perfect reconstruction gives infinite SNR; denoising gives finite SNR.
// ============================================================================

fn wav_snr(original: [f64; 512], reconstructed: [f64; 512], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var e_signal = 0.0
    var e_noise = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let o = original[i as usize]
        let r = reconstructed[i as usize]
        e_signal = e_signal + o * o
        let diff = o - r
        e_noise = e_noise + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    if e_noise < 1.0e-300 {
        return 1000.0  // Very large SNR — nearly perfect reconstruction
    }
    if e_signal < 1.0e-300 {
        return 0.0
    }
    return 10.0 * wav_log10(e_signal / e_noise)
}

// ============================================================================
// DAUBECHIES-4 (db4) WAVELET
//
// The Daubechies-4 wavelet has 4 filter coefficients and 2 vanishing moments.
// It can represent polynomials of degree <= 1 exactly.
//
// Analysis low-pass filter (h0): scaling coefficients
// Analysis high-pass filter (h1): wavelet coefficients
//
// Coefficients (from Daubechies 1988, orthonormal form):
//   h0 = [(1+sqrt3)/(4*sqrt2), (3+sqrt3)/(4*sqrt2), (3-sqrt3)/(4*sqrt2), (1-sqrt3)/(4*sqrt2)]
//   h1[k] = (-1)^k * h0[3-k]   (quadrature mirror)
//
// Numerical values (sqrt3 ≈ 1.7320508075688773):
//   h0[0] = (1+√3)/(4√2) ≈  0.4829629131445341
//   h0[1] = (3+√3)/(4√2) ≈  0.8365163037378077
//   h0[2] = (3-√3)/(4√2) ≈  0.2241438680420134
//   h0[3] = (1-√3)/(4√2) ≈ -0.1294095225512603
//
//   h1[0] = -h0[3] ≈  0.1294095225512603
//   h1[1] =  h0[2] ≈  0.2241438680420134
//   h1[2] = -h0[1] ≈ -0.8365163037378077
//   h1[3] =  h0[0] ≈  0.4829629131445341
//
// Reconstruction (synthesis) filters:
//   g0[k] = h0[3-k]   (time-reverse of h0)
//   g1[k] = h1[3-k]   (time-reverse of h1)
// ============================================================================

fn db4_h0_0() -> f64 {  0.4829629131445341 }
fn db4_h0_1() -> f64 {  0.8365163037378077 }
fn db4_h0_2() -> f64 {  0.2241438680420134 }
fn db4_h0_3() -> f64 { 0.0 - 0.1294095225512603 }

fn db4_h1_0() -> f64 {  0.1294095225512603 }
fn db4_h1_1() -> f64 {  0.2241438680420134 }
fn db4_h1_2() -> f64 { 0.0 - 0.8365163037378077 }
fn db4_h1_3() -> f64 {  0.4829629131445341 }

// Synthesis (inverse) low-pass: g0[k] = h0[3-k]
fn db4_g0_0() -> f64 { 0.0 - 0.1294095225512603 }  // h0[3]
fn db4_g0_1() -> f64 {  0.2241438680420134 }         // h0[2]
fn db4_g0_2() -> f64 {  0.8365163037378077 }         // h0[1]
fn db4_g0_3() -> f64 {  0.4829629131445341 }         // h0[0]

// Synthesis (inverse) high-pass: g1[k] = h1[3-k]
fn db4_g1_0() -> f64 {  0.4829629131445341 }         // h1[3]
fn db4_g1_1() -> f64 { 0.0 - 0.8365163037378077 }   // h1[2]
fn db4_g1_2() -> f64 {  0.2241438680420134 }         // h1[1]
fn db4_g1_3() -> f64 {  0.1294095225512603 }         // h1[0]

// DB4 forward DWT (single level, periodic boundary conditions)
// signal[0..n-1] → out_approx[0..n/2-1], out_detail[0..n/2-1]
// n must be even and <= 512
// Returns n/2
fn wav_db4_forward(signal: [f64; 512], n: i64, out_approx: &! [f64; 256], out_detail: &! [f64; 256]) -> i64 {
    let half_n = n / 2
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < half_n {
        let k = 2 * i
        // Periodic boundary indices
        let k0 = k % n
        let k1 = (k + 1) % n
        let k2 = (k + 2) % n
        let k3 = (k + 3) % n
        let s0 = signal[k0 as usize]
        let s1 = signal[k1 as usize]
        let s2 = signal[k2 as usize]
        let s3 = signal[k3 as usize]
        out_approx[i as usize] = db4_h0_0() * s0 + db4_h0_1() * s1 + db4_h0_2() * s2 + db4_h0_3() * s3
        out_detail[i as usize] = db4_h1_0() * s0 + db4_h1_1() * s1 + db4_h1_2() * s2 + db4_h1_3() * s3
        i = i + 1
    }
    return half_n
}

// DB4 inverse DWT (single level, periodic boundary conditions)
// approx[0..n-1], detail[0..n-1] → out[0..2*n-1]
// Returns 2*n
fn wav_db4_inverse(approx: [f64; 256], detail: [f64; 256], n: i64, out: &! [f64; 512]) -> i64 {
    let len_out = 2 * n
    // Initialize output to zero
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < len_out {
        out[j as usize] = 0.0
        j = j + 1
    }
    // Accumulate contributions from each approximation and detail coefficient
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let k = 2 * i
        // Upsampling + synthesis filtering with periodic boundary
        let k0 = k % len_out
        let k1 = (k + 1) % len_out
        let k2 = (k + 2) % len_out
        let k3 = (k + 3) % len_out
        let a = approx[i as usize]
        let d = detail[i as usize]
        out[k0 as usize] = out[k0 as usize] + db4_g0_0() * a + db4_g1_0() * d
        out[k1 as usize] = out[k1 as usize] + db4_g0_1() * a + db4_g1_1() * d
        out[k2 as usize] = out[k2 as usize] + db4_g0_2() * a + db4_g1_2() * d
        out[k3 as usize] = out[k3 as usize] + db4_g0_3() * a + db4_g1_3() * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    return len_out
}

// ============================================================================
// MULTI-LEVEL DWT (Haar, cascaded on approximation sub-bands)
//
// Level 1: n-point signal → (A1: n/2, D1: n/2)
// Level 2: A1 → (A2: n/4, D2: n/4)
// Level 3: A2 → (A3: n/8, D3: n/8)
//
// The wavelet packet coefficients are stored in separate arrays.
// ============================================================================

struct Wav2LevelHaar {
    approx2: [f64; 128],   // 2nd-level approximation (n/4 coefficients)
    detail2: [f64; 128],   // 2nd-level detail (n/4 coefficients)
    detail1: [f64; 256],   // 1st-level detail (n/2 coefficients)
    n2: i64,               // n/4
    n1: i64,               // n/2
}

fn wav_haar_forward_2level(signal: [f64; 512], n: i64) -> Wav2LevelHaar {
    // Level 1
    var approx1: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail1: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let n1 = wav_haar_forward(signal, n, &! approx1, &! detail1)

    // Level 2: transform approx1
    var approx2: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var detail2: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]

    // Copy approx1 into a 512-padded array for the forward function
    var approx1_pad: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n1 {
        approx1_pad[k as usize] = approx1[k as usize]
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Haar level 2
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.70710678118654752440
    let n2 = n1 / 2
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n2 {
        let a = approx1[( 2 * i) as usize]
        let b = approx1[(2 * i + 1) as usize]
        approx2[i as usize] = (a + b) * inv_sqrt2
        detail2[i as usize] = (a - b) * inv_sqrt2
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Build result struct
    var result = Wav2LevelHaar {
        approx2: [0.0; 128],
        detail2: [0.0; 128],
        detail1: [0.0; 256],
        n2: n2,
        n1: n1,
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n2 {
        result.approx2[i as usize] = approx2[i as usize]
        result.detail2[i as usize] = detail2[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n1 {
        result.detail1[i as usize] = detail1[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// 2-level Haar inverse
fn wav_haar_inverse_2level(decomp: Wav2LevelHaar, out: &! [f64; 512]) -> i64 {
    // Reconstruct approx1 from (approx2, detail2)
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.70710678118654752440
    let n2 = decomp.n2
    let n1 = decomp.n1

    var approx1: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n2 {
        let a = decomp.approx2[i as usize]
        let d = decomp.detail2[i as usize]
        approx1[(2 * i) as usize] = (a + d) * inv_sqrt2
        approx1[(2 * i + 1) as usize] = (a - d) * inv_sqrt2
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Reconstruct full signal from (approx1, detail1)
    i = 0
    while i < n1 {
        let a = approx1[i as usize]
        let d = decomp.detail1[i as usize]
        out[(2 * i) as usize] = (a + d) * inv_sqrt2
        out[(2 * i + 1) as usize] = (a - d) * inv_sqrt2
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 2 * n1
}

// ============================================================================
// WAVELET DENOISING PIPELINE
//
// Standard pipeline (Donoho & Johnstone, 1994):
//   1. Forward DWT
//   2. Threshold detail coefficients (keep approximation unchanged)
//   3. Inverse DWT
// ============================================================================

// Denoise signal using Haar DWT + hard threshold on detail coefficients
// thresh: threshold value (e.g., sigma * sqrt(2 * log(n)))
// Returns reconstructed (denoised) signal via out
fn wav_denoise_haar_hard(signal: [f64; 512], n: i64, thresh: f64, out: &! [f64; 512]) -> i64 {
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let half_n = wav_haar_forward(signal, n, &! approx, &! detail)
    // Threshold detail inline (avoids double &! borrow)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < half_n {
        let v = detail[i as usize]
        if wav_f64_abs(v) < thresh { detail[i as usize] = 0.0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Reconstruct
    return wav_haar_inverse(approx, detail, half_n, out)
}

// Denoise signal using Haar DWT + soft threshold on detail coefficients
fn wav_denoise_haar_soft(signal: [f64; 512], n: i64, thresh: f64, out: &! [f64; 512]) -> i64 {
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let half_n = wav_haar_forward(signal, n, &! approx, &! detail)
    // Soft threshold inline (avoids double &! borrow)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < half_n {
        let v = detail[i as usize]
        let av = wav_f64_abs(v)
        if av <= thresh {
            detail[i as usize] = 0.0
        } else {
            if v > 0.0 {
                detail[i as usize] = av - thresh
            } else {
                detail[i as usize] = 0.0 - (av - thresh)
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return wav_haar_inverse(approx, detail, half_n, out)
}

// ============================================================================
// UTILITY: MAXIMUM ABSOLUTE COEFFICIENT
// ============================================================================

fn wav_max_coeff(signal: [f64; 256], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var mx = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let v = wav_f64_abs(signal[i as usize])
        if v > mx { mx = v }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return mx
}

fn wav_max_coeff_512(signal: [f64; 512], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var mx = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let v = wav_f64_abs(signal[i as usize])
        if v > mx { mx = v }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return mx
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn wav_approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    wav_f64_abs(a - b) < tol
}

// --- Math helper tests ---

fn test_wav_abs() -> bool {
    if wav_f64_abs(3.5) != 3.5 { return false }
    if wav_f64_abs(0.0 - 2.7) != 2.7 { return false }
    if wav_f64_abs(0.0) != 0.0 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_wav_sqrt() -> bool {
    if wav_f64_abs(wav_sqrt(4.0) - 2.0) > 1.0e-10 { return false }
    if wav_f64_abs(wav_sqrt(2.0) - 1.41421356237) > 1.0e-8 { return false }
    if wav_sqrt(0.0) != 0.0 { return false }
    if wav_f64_abs(wav_sqrt(9.0) - 3.0) > 1.0e-10 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_wav_log10() -> bool {
    // log10(1) = 0
    if wav_f64_abs(wav_log10(1.0)) > 1.0e-6 { return false }
    // log10(10) = 1
    if wav_f64_abs(wav_log10(10.0) - 1.0) > 1.0e-6 { return false }
    // log10(100) = 2
    if wav_f64_abs(wav_log10(100.0) - 2.0) > 1.0e-6 { return false }
    // log10(0.1) = -1
    if wav_f64_abs(wav_log10(0.1) - (0.0 - 1.0)) > 1.0e-5 { return false }
    return true
}

fn test_wav_max_min() -> bool {
    if wav_f64_max(1.0, 3.0) != 3.0 { return false }
    if wav_f64_max(5.0, 2.0) != 5.0 { return false }
    if wav_f64_min(1.0, 3.0) != 1.0 { return false }
    if wav_f64_min(5.0, 2.0) != 2.0 { return false }
    return true
}

// --- Haar filter constants tests ---

fn test_haar_sqrt2_identity() -> bool {
    // inv_sqrt2 * sqrt(2) should be 1
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.70710678118654752440
    let sqrt2 = 1.41421356237309504880
    return wav_f64_abs(inv_sqrt2 * sqrt2 - 1.0) < 1.0e-10
}

fn test_haar_orthogonality() -> bool {
    // Haar scaling filter h0 = [1/sqrt2, 1/sqrt2]
    // Wavelet filter h1 = [1/sqrt2, -1/sqrt2]
    // h0 · h1 should be 0 (orthogonality)
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.70710678118654752440
    let dot = inv_sqrt2 * inv_sqrt2 + inv_sqrt2 * (0.0 - inv_sqrt2)
    return wav_f64_abs(dot) < 1.0e-15
}

fn test_haar_norm() -> bool {
    // ||h0||^2 = 1 (unit norm for orthonormal filter)
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.70710678118654752440
    let norm_sq = inv_sqrt2 * inv_sqrt2 + inv_sqrt2 * inv_sqrt2
    return wav_f64_abs(norm_sq - 1.0) < 1.0e-15
}

// --- Haar forward transform tests ---

fn test_haar_fwd_constant_signal() -> bool {
    // Constant signal [c, c, c, ...]: approx = c*sqrt(2), detail = 0
    var sig: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    let c = 3.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        sig[i as usize] = c
        i = i + 1
    }
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let half = wav_haar_forward(sig, 8, &! approx, &! detail)
    // approx[i] = (c + c) / sqrt(2) = c * sqrt(2)
    let sqrt2_c = c * 1.41421356237309504880
    if half != 4 { return false }
    i = 0
    while i < 4 {
        if wav_f64_abs(approx[i as usize] - sqrt2_c) > 1.0e-10 { return false }
        if wav_f64_abs(detail[i as usize]) > 1.0e-15 { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

fn test_haar_fwd_alternating_signal() -> bool {
    // Alternating signal [a, -a, a, -a, ...]: approx = 0, detail = a*sqrt(2)
    var sig: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    let a = 2.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        if i % 2 == 0 { sig[i as usize] = a } else { sig[i as usize] = 0.0 - a }
        i = i + 1
    }
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let half = wav_haar_forward(sig, 8, &! approx, &! detail)
    let sqrt2_a = a * 1.41421356237309504880
    i = 0
    while i < 4 {
        if wav_f64_abs(approx[i as usize]) > 1.0e-15 { return false }
        if wav_f64_abs(detail[i as usize] - sqrt2_a) > 1.0e-10 { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

fn test_haar_fwd_output_len() -> bool {
    var sig: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let half = wav_haar_forward(sig, 16, &! approx, &! detail)
    return half == 8
}

fn test_haar_fwd_single_pair() -> bool {
    // n=2: one forward step on [3, 5]
    // approx = (3+5)/sqrt2 = 8/sqrt2 ≈ 5.6569
    // detail = (3-5)/sqrt2 = -2/sqrt2 ≈ -1.4142
    var sig: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    sig[0] = 3.0
    sig[1] = 5.0
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let half = wav_haar_forward(sig, 2, &! approx, &! detail)
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.70710678118654752440
    let expected_a = 8.0 * inv_sqrt2
    let expected_d = (0.0 - 2.0) * inv_sqrt2
    return half == 1
        && wav_f64_abs(approx[0] - expected_a) < 1.0e-12
        && wav_f64_abs(detail[0] - expected_d) < 1.0e-12
}

// --- Haar inverse transform tests ---

fn test_haar_inv_constant_approx() -> bool {
    // All approx = c*sqrt2, all detail = 0 → reconstructed = [c, c, ...]
    let c = 3.0
    let sqrt2_c = c * 1.41421356237309504880
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 4 {
        approx[i as usize] = sqrt2_c
        detail[i as usize] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    var recon: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    let len = wav_haar_inverse(approx, detail, 4, &! recon)
    if len != 8 { return false }
    i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        if wav_f64_abs(recon[i as usize] - c) > 1.0e-10 { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

fn test_haar_inv_output_len() -> bool {
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var out: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    let len = wav_haar_inverse(approx, detail, 8, &! out)
    return len == 16
}

fn test_haar_inv_single_pair() -> bool {
    // Inverse of single pair: approx=A, detail=D → [A+D, A-D] / sqrt2
    let a = 5.0
    let d = 2.0
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    approx[0] = a
    detail[0] = d
    var out: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    let len = wav_haar_inverse(approx, detail, 1, &! out)
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.70710678118654752440
    return len == 2
        && wav_f64_abs(out[0] - (a + d) * inv_sqrt2) < 1.0e-12
        && wav_f64_abs(out[1] - (a - d) * inv_sqrt2) < 1.0e-12
}

// --- Roundtrip (perfect reconstruction) tests ---

fn test_haar_roundtrip_constant() -> bool {
    // Constant signal: fwd → inv should give back original
    var sig: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        sig[i as usize] = 7.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let half = wav_haar_forward(sig, 32, &! approx, &! detail)
    var recon: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    let _len = wav_haar_inverse(approx, detail, half, &! recon)
    i = 0
    while i < 32 {
        if wav_f64_abs(recon[i as usize] - 7.0) > 1.0e-12 { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

fn test_haar_roundtrip_linear() -> bool {
    // Linear signal: [0, 1, 2, ..., 15]
    var sig: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 16 {
        sig[i as usize] = i as f64
        i = i + 1
    }
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let half = wav_haar_forward(sig, 16, &! approx, &! detail)
    var recon: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    let _len = wav_haar_inverse(approx, detail, half, &! recon)
    i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        if wav_f64_abs(recon[i as usize] - (i as f64)) > 1.0e-12 { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

fn test_haar_roundtrip_random_like() -> bool {
    // Pseudo-random signal via simple recurrence
    var sig: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    sig[0] = 1.7
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < 64 {
        sig[i as usize] = sig[(i-1) as usize] * 1.3 + 0.7
        if sig[i as usize] > 10.0 { sig[i as usize] = sig[i as usize] - 10.0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    var approx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var detail: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let half = wav_haar_forward(sig, 64, &! approx, &! detail)
    var recon: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    let _len = wav_haar_inverse(approx, detail, half, &! recon)
    i = 0
    var max_err = 0.0
    while i < 64 {
        let e = wav_f64_abs(recon[i as usize] - sig[i as usize])
        if e > max_err { max_err = e }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return max_err < 1.0e-10
}

fn test_haar_roundtrip_n128() -> bool {
    var sig: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 128 {
        sig[i as usize] = (i as f64) * 0.1 + 1.0

    var recon: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
    let _len = wav_haar_inverse(approx, detail, half, &! recon)
    i = 0
    while i < 128 {
        if wav_f64_abs(recon[i as usize] - sig[i as usize]) > 1.0e-10 { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

fn test_haar_roundtrip_n512() -> bool {

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 512 {
        sig[i as usize] = (i as f64) * 0.01
