    value: TTestResult,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: TTestProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn mean(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n { sum = sum + data[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

fn variance(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = mean(data, n)
    var ss = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let d = data[i as usize] - m
        ss = ss + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    ss / ((n - 1) as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// Assumption Checks → BetaConfidence
// =============================================================================

fn check_normality(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> BetaConfidence with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = mean(data, n)
    let v = variance(data, n)
    let s = inf_sqrt(v)

    if s < 1.0e-10 { return beta_new(100.0, 1.0) }

    var min_v = data[0]
    var max_v = data[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        if data[i as usize] < min_v { min_v = data[i as usize] }
        if data[i as usize] > max_v { max_v = data[i as usize] }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let range = max_v - min_v
    let expected = s * (2.5 + 0.5 * inf_sqrt(n as f64))
    let ratio = range / expected
    let dev = inf_abs(ratio - 1.0)

    let p = if dev < 0.15 { 0.90 }
            else if dev < 0.30 { 0.70 }
            else { 0.50 }

    let nf = n as f64
    let nfac = if nf >= 30.0 { 1.0 } else { inf_sqrt(nf / 30.0) }
    let c = nf * 0.5

    beta_new(p * nfac * c, (1.0 - p * nfac) * c)
}

fn check_var_equality(
    d1: [f64; 100], n1: i64,
    d2: [f64; 100], n2: i64
) -> BetaConfidence with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let v1 = variance(d1, n1)
    let v2 = variance(d2, n2)
    if v1 < 1.0e-10 && v2 < 1.0e-10 { return beta_new(100.0, 1.0) }
    if v1 < 1.0e-10 || v2 < 1.0e-10 { return beta_new(1.0, 100.0) }

    let ratio = if v1 > v2 { v1 / v2 } else { v2 / v1 }
    let p = if ratio < 1.5 { 0.90 }
            else if ratio < 2.0 { 0.70 }
            else if ratio < 3.0 { 0.50 }
            else { 0.30 }

    let c = (n1 + n2) as f64 * 0.3
    beta_new(p * c, (1.0 - p) * c)
}

fn check_sample_adequate(n1: i64, n2: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
    let min_n = if n1 < n2 { n1 } else { n2 }
    let p = if min_n >= 30 { 0.95 }
            else if min_n >= 20 { 0.85 }
            else if min_n >= 10 { 0.70 }
            else if min_n >= 5 { 0.50 }
            else { 0.30 }

    let c = (n1 + n2) as f64
    beta_new(p * c, (1.0 - p) * c)
}

// =============================================================================
// Approximate p-value
// =============================================================================

fn t_to_p(t: f64, df: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let z = inf_abs(t)
    let a1 = 0.254829592
    let a2 = -0.284496736
    let a3 = 1.421413741
    let a4 = -1.453152027
    let a5 = 1.061405429
    let p = 0.3275911
    let te = 1.0 / (1.0 + p * z)
    let erf = 1.0 - (((((a5 * te + a4) * te) + a3) * te + a2) * te + a1) * te * inf_exp(-z * z)
    1.0 - erf
}

// =============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC T-TEST
// =============================================================================

fn ttest_independent_epistemic(
    g1: [f64; 100], n1: i64,
    g2: [f64; 100], n2: i64
) -> KnowledgeTTest with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Classical computation
    let m1 = mean(g1, n1)
    let m2 = mean(g2, n2)
    let diff = m1 - m2

    let v1 = variance(g1, n1)
    let v2 = variance(g2, n2)
    let n1f = n1 as f64
    let n2f = n2 as f64

    // Pooled SD
    let sp2 = ((n1f - 1.0) * v1 + (n2f - 1.0) * v2) / (n1f + n2f - 2.0)
    let sp = inf_sqrt(sp2)
    let se = sp * inf_sqrt(1.0 / n1f + 1.0 / n2f)

    let t_stat = if se > 1.0e-10 { diff / se } else { 0.0 }
    let df = n1f + n2f - 2.0
    let p_val = t_to_p(t_stat, df)
    let cohens_d = if sp > 1.0e-10 { diff / sp } else { 0.0 }
    let ci_lo = diff - 1.96 * se
    let ci_hi = diff + 1.96 * se

    let result = TTestResult {
        t_statistic: t_stat,
        degrees_of_freedom: df,
        p_value: p_val,
        effect_size: cohens_d,
        ci_lower: ci_lo,
        ci_upper: ci_hi
    }

    // Epistemic layer
    let norm1 = check_normality(g1, n1)
    let norm2 = check_normality(g2, n2)
    let var_eq = check_var_equality(g1, n1, g2, n2)
    let sample_ok = check_sample_adequate(n1, n2)

    let assumptions = AssumptionChecks {
        normality_group1: norm1,
        normality_group2: norm2,
        variance_equality: var_eq,
        sample_size_adequate: sample_ok
    }

    let c1 = beta_combine(&norm1, &norm2)
    let c2 = beta_combine(&c1, &var_eq)
    let c3 = beta_combine(&c2, &sample_ok)
    let overall = beta_decay(&c3, 0.98)

    // Bootstrap variance estimate (heuristic; use bootstrap.sio for proper)
    let t_var = se * se * 0.1

    let prov = TTestProvenance {
        method_id: 1,
        n1: n1,
        n2: n2,
        assumption_checks: assumptions
    }

    KnowledgeTTest {
        value: result,
        variance: t_var,
        confidence: overall,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Decision Support
// =============================================================================

fn should_reject(result: &KnowledgeTTest, alpha: f64, min_conf: f64) -> bool {
    result.value.p_value < alpha && beta_mean(&result.confidence) >= min_conf
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_epistemic_ttest() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var g1: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    g1[0] = 10.0; g1[1] = 12.0; g1[2] = 11.0; g1[3] = 13.0; g1[4] = 11.0

    var g2: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    g2[0] = 8.0; g2[1] = 9.0; g2[2] = 7.0; g2[3] = 10.0; g2[4] = 8.0

    let result = ttest_independent_epistemic(g1, 5, g2, 5)

    let t_ok = inf_abs(result.value.t_statistic) > 0.0
    let conf_ok = beta_mean(&result.confidence) > 0.0

    t_ok && conf_ok
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/gp.sio ===
// stdlib/stats/gp.sio -- Gaussian Process Regression
//
// Full GP regression module: kernels (RBF, Matern 3/2, Matern 5/2, Periodic),
// Cholesky-based inference, predictive mean/variance, log marginal likelihood,
// and hyperparameter optimization via grid search in log-space.
//
// Max 64 training points (64x64 = 4096 array limit).
// Max 256 prediction points.
//
// References:
//   Rasmussen & Williams (2006): "Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning"
//   JCGM 100:2008 (GUM): measurement uncertainty propagation
//   Stein (1999): "Interpolation of Spatial Data" -- Matern kernels

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers (prefixed gp_ to avoid name collisions)
// =============================================================================

fn gp_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn gp_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var scaled = x
    var scale_back = 1.0
    while scaled < 1.0 {
        scaled = scaled * 4.0
        scale_back = scale_back * 2.0
    }
    while scaled > 4.0 {
        scaled = scaled * 0.25
        scale_back = scale_back * 0.5
    }
    var y = 1.5
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y / scale_back
}

fn gp_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 709.0 { return 1.0e308 }
    if x < -709.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    let inv_ln2 = 1.4426950408889634
    var k_f = x * inv_ln2
    var k: i64 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = (k_f + 0.5) as i64 } else { k = (k_f - 0.5) as i64 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    var result = sum
    var kabs = k
    if kabs < 0 { kabs = 0 - kabs }
    var pow2 = 2.0
    var ka = kabs
    var acc = 1.0
    while ka > 0 {
        if ka - (ka / 2) * 2 != 0 { acc = acc * pow2 }
        pow2 = pow2 * pow2
        ka = ka / 2
    }
    if k >= 0 { result = result * acc } else { result = result / acc }
    result
}

fn gp_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return -1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = 0.0
    var a = x
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    while a > 2.0 { a = a * 0.5; y = y + ln2 }
    while a < 0.5 { a = a * 2.0; y = y - ln2 }
    let t = (a - 1.0) / (a + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var power = t
    var n = 1
    while n <= 30 {
        power = power * t2
        sum = sum + power / (2.0 * (n as f64) + 1.0)
        n = n + 1
    }
    y + 2.0 * sum
}

fn gp_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let two_pi = 6.28318530717958647692
    var a = x
    while a >= two_pi { a = a - two_pi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + two_pi }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - two_pi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 18 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn gp_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

// =============================================================================
// Data structures
// =============================================================================

// Training data container (max 64 points for tractability)
struct GPData {
    x: [f64; 64],
    y: [f64; 64],
    n: i64
}

// Hyperparameters for GP kernel
//   kernel_type: 0=RBF, 1=Matern32, 2=Matern52, 3=Periodic
struct GPHyperparams {
    length_scale: f64,
    signal_var: f64,
    noise_var: f64,
    kernel_type: i64
}

// Fitted GP model: Cholesky factor L and weights alpha = K^{-1}y
//   L: 64x64 lower triangular stored row-major in flat array
//   alpha: K^{-1}y vector
struct GPModel {
    hyper: GPHyperparams,
    L: [f64; 4096],
    alpha: [f64; 64],
    n: i64,
    ok: bool
}

// Batch prediction result
struct GPPrediction {
    means: [f64; 256],
    variances: [f64; 256],
    n: i64
}

// =============================================================================
// Kernel functions
// =============================================================================

// Squared Exponential / RBF kernel:
//   k(x1, x2) = signal_var * exp(-0.5 * (x1 - x2)^2 / length_scale^2)
fn kernel_rbf(x1: f64, x2: f64, length_scale: f64, signal_var: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let d = x1 - x2
    signal_var * gp_exp(0.0 - 0.5 * d * d / (length_scale * length_scale))
}

// Matern 3/2 kernel:
//   k(x1, x2) = signal_var * (1 + sqrt(3)*r/l) * exp(-sqrt(3)*r/l)
fn kernel_matern32(x1: f64, x2: f64, length_scale: f64, signal_var: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = gp_abs(x1 - x2)
    let sqrt3 = 1.7320508075688772
    let z = sqrt3 * r / length_scale
    signal_var * (1.0 + z) * gp_exp(0.0 - z)
}

// Matern 5/2 kernel:
//   k(x1, x2) = signal_var * (1 + sqrt(5)*r/l + 5r^2/(3l^2)) * exp(-sqrt(5)*r/l)
fn kernel_matern52(x1: f64, x2: f64, length_scale: f64, signal_var: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = gp_abs(x1 - x2)
    let sqrt5 = 2.2360679774997896
    let z = sqrt5 * r / length_scale
    let z2 = 5.0 * r * r / (3.0 * length_scale * length_scale)
    signal_var * (1.0 + z + z2) * gp_exp(0.0 - z)
}

// Linear kernel:
//   k(x1, x2) = signal_var * x1 * x2
fn kernel_linear(x1: f64, x2: f64, signal_var: f64) -> f64 {
    signal_var * x1 * x2
}

// Periodic kernel:
//   k(x1, x2) = signal_var * exp(-2 * sin^2(pi*|x1-x2|/period) / length_scale^2)
fn kernel_periodic(x1: f64, x2: f64, length_scale: f64, signal_var: f64, period: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = gp_abs(x1 - x2)
    let s = gp_sin(gp_pi() * r / period)
    signal_var * gp_exp(0.0 - 2.0 * s * s / (length_scale * length_scale))
}

// Kernel dispatch by kernel_type
//   0=RBF, 1=Matern32, 2=Matern52, 3=Linear, 4=Periodic
fn kernel_eval(x1: f64, x2: f64, hyper: GPHyperparams) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if hyper.kernel_type == 0 {
        return kernel_rbf(x1, x2, hyper.length_scale, hyper.signal_var)
    }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 1 {
        return kernel_matern32(x1, x2, hyper.length_scale, hyper.signal_var)
    }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 2 {
        return kernel_matern52(x1, x2, hyper.length_scale, hyper.signal_var)
    }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 3 {
        return kernel_linear(x1, x2, hyper.signal_var)
    }
    // Default: RBF
    return kernel_rbf(x1, x2, hyper.length_scale, hyper.signal_var)
}

// =============================================================================
// Kernel matrix assembly
// =============================================================================

// Build N x N kernel matrix K(X,X) + noise_var * I.
// Stored row-major: K[i*n + j] = k(x_i, x_j) + delta_ij * noise_var.
fn gp_build_kernel_matrix(data: GPData, params: GPHyperparams) -> [f64; 4096] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var K: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    let n = data.n
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            let idx = i * n + j
            let kval = kernel_eval(data.x[i as usize], data.x[j as usize], params)
            if i == j {
                K[idx as usize] = kval + params.noise_var
            } else {
                K[idx as usize] = kval
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return K
}

// =============================================================================
// Cholesky factorization
// =============================================================================

// Cholesky factorization: L * L^T = K
// K is n x n symmetric positive definite, row-major in [f64; 4096].
// Returns lower triangular L, also row-major.
// Algorithm: Golub & Van Loan, "Matrix Computations" (4th ed.)
fn gp_cholesky(K: [f64; 4096], n: i64) -> [f64; 4096] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var L: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n {
        // Diagonal: L[j][j] = sqrt(K[j][j] - sum_{k<j} L[j][k]^2)
        var sum_diag = 0.0
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < j {
            let ljk = L[(j * n + k) as usize]
            sum_diag = sum_diag + ljk * ljk
            k = k + 1
        }
        let diag_val = K[(j * n + j) as usize] - sum_diag
        if diag_val <= 1.0e-15 {
            // Not positive definite; use small positive value to avoid crash
            L[(j * n + j) as usize] = 1.0e-8
        } else {
            L[(j * n + j) as usize] = gp_sqrt(diag_val)
        }
        // Off-diagonal: L[i][j] = (K[i][j] - sum_{k<j} L[i][k]*L[j][k]) / L[j][j]
        var i: i64 = j + 1
        while i < n {
            var sum_off = 0.0
            k = 0
            while k < j {
                sum_off = sum_off + L[(i * n + k) as usize] * L[(j * n + k) as usize]
                k = k + 1
            }
            L[(i * n + j) as usize] = (K[(i * n + j) as usize] - sum_off) / L[(j * n + j) as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    return L
}

// =============================================================================
// Triangular solve
// =============================================================================

// Forward substitution: solve L * x = b where L is lower triangular (n x n).
fn gp_solve_lower(L: [f64; 4096], b: [f64; 64], n: i64) -> [f64; 64] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < i {
            sum = sum + L[(i * n + j) as usize] * x[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let diag = L[(i * n + i) as usize]
        if gp_abs(diag) > 1.0e-15 {
            x[i as usize] = (b[i as usize] - sum) / diag
        } else {
            x[i as usize] = 0.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return x
}

// Backward substitution: solve L^T * x = b where L is lower triangular.
fn gp_solve_upper(L: [f64; 4096], b: [f64; 64], n: i64) -> [f64; 64] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i: i64 = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n {
            sum = sum + L[(j * n + i) as usize] * x[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let diag = L[(i * n + i) as usize]
        if gp_abs(diag) > 1.0e-15 {
            x[i as usize] = (b[i as usize] - sum) / diag
        } else {
            x[i as usize] = 0.0
        }
        i = i - 1
    }
    return x
}

// Full Cholesky solve: L * L^T * x = b
// Forward (L * z = b), then backward (L^T * x = z).
fn gp_cholesky_solve(L: [f64; 4096], b: [f64; 64], n: i64) -> [f64; 64] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let z = gp_solve_lower(L, b, n)
    return gp_solve_upper(L, z, n)
}

// =============================================================================
// GP fit
// =============================================================================

// Fit a GP model: compute Cholesky of K + sigma^2 I and alpha = K^{-1} y.
// Rasmussen & Williams (2006) Algorithm 2.1, training phase.
fn gp_fit(data: GPData, params: GPHyperparams) -> GPModel with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = data.n
    let K = gp_build_kernel_matrix(data, params)
    let L = gp_cholesky(K, n)

    // Copy y into a [f64; 64] buffer
    var y_buf: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        y_buf[i as usize] = data.y[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // alpha = (K + sigma^2 I)^{-1} y via Cholesky solve
    let alpha = gp_cholesky_solve(L, y_buf, n)

    return GPModel {
        hyper: params,
        L: L,
        alpha: alpha,
        n: n,
        ok: true
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// GP prediction
// =============================================================================

// Predict posterior mean and variance at a single test point x_star.
// Returns (mean, variance) packed in a [f64; 2] array.
//
//   k_star = [k(x_star, x_1), ..., k(x_star, x_n)]
//   mean = k_star^T * alpha
//   v = L \ k_star
//   variance = k(x_star, x_star) - v^T * v
fn gp_predict(model: GPModel, data: GPData, x_star: f64) -> [f64; 2] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = model.n
    var result: [f64; 2] = [0.0; 2]

    // Compute k_star vector
    var k_star: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        k_star[i as usize] = kernel_eval(x_star, data.x[i as usize], model.hyper)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Predictive mean: k_star^T * alpha
    var mean_val = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        mean_val = mean_val + k_star[i as usize] * model.alpha[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    result[0] = mean_val

    // Predictive variance: k(x_star, x_star) - v^T v where L*v = k_star
    let v = gp_solve_lower(model.L, k_star, n)
    let k_ss = kernel_eval(x_star, x_star, model.hyper)
    var vtv = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        vtv = vtv + v[i as usize] * v[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    var var_val = k_ss - vtv
    if var_val < 0.0 { var_val = 0.0 }
    result[1] = var_val

    return result
}

// Batch prediction at multiple test points.
fn gp_predict_array(
    model: GPModel, data: GPData,
    x_stars: [f64; 256], n_stars: i64
) -> GPPrediction with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pred = GPPrediction {
        means: [0.0; 256],
        variances: [0.0; 256],
        n: n_stars
    }
    var t: i64 = 0
    while t < n_stars {
        let pv = gp_predict(model, data, x_stars[t as usize])
        pred.means[t as usize] = pv[0]
        pred.variances[t as usize] = pv[1]
        t = t + 1
    }
    return pred
}

// =============================================================================
// Log marginal likelihood
// =============================================================================

// Compute log marginal likelihood:
//   log p(y|X,theta) = -0.5 * y^T * alpha - sum(log(diag(L))) - n/2 * log(2*pi)
//
// Rasmussen & Williams (2006) Eq. 5.8
fn gp_log_marginal_likelihood(model: GPModel, data: GPData) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = model.n

    // Data fit: -0.5 * y^T * alpha
    var data_fit = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        data_fit = data_fit + data.y[i as usize] * model.alpha[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    data_fit = 0.0 - 0.5 * data_fit

    // Complexity: -sum(log(L_ii))
    var complexity = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        complexity = complexity + gp_ln(model.L[(i * n + i) as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }
    complexity = 0.0 - complexity

    // Normalization: -n/2 * log(2*pi)
    let norm_const = 0.0 - 0.5 * (n as f64) * gp_ln(2.0 * gp_pi())

    return data_fit + complexity + norm_const
}

// =============================================================================
// Hyperparameter optimization
// =============================================================================

// Evaluate neg log marginal likelihood for a given set of hyperparameters.
fn gp_eval_nlml(data: GPData, length_scale: f64, signal_var: f64, noise_var: f64, kernel_type: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let params = GPHyperparams {
        length_scale: length_scale,
        signal_var: signal_var,
        noise_var: noise_var,
        kernel_type: kernel_type
    }
    let model = gp_fit(data, params)
    let lml = gp_log_marginal_likelihood(model, data)
    return 0.0 - lml
}

// Optimize hyperparameters via grid search over log-space.
// Searches over length_scale and signal_var; noise_var is held fixed.
// max_iter controls grid density (unused in grid search, kept for API compat).
// Returns the best GPHyperparams found.
//
// Grid: 7 values for length_scale x 5 values for signal_var = 35 evaluations.
fn gp_optimize_hyper(data: GPData, hyper_init: GPHyperparams, max_iter: i64) -> GPHyperparams with Mut, Div, Panic {
    return gp_optimize_hyperparams(data, hyper_init)
}

fn gp_optimize_hyperparams(data: GPData, params_init: GPHyperparams) -> GPHyperparams with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let kt = params_init.kernel_type
    let nv = params_init.noise_var

    // Log-space grid for length_scale: exp(-2) to exp(3) in 7 steps
    var ls_grid: [f64; 7] = [0.0; 7]
    ls_grid[0] = gp_exp(-2.0)
    ls_grid[1] = gp_exp(-1.0)
    ls_grid[2] = gp_exp(-0.5)
    ls_grid[3] = gp_exp(0.0)
    ls_grid[4] = gp_exp(0.5)
    ls_grid[5] = gp_exp(1.0)
    ls_grid[6] = gp_exp(2.0)

    // Log-space grid for signal_var: exp(-2) to exp(2) in 5 steps
    var sv_grid: [f64; 5] = [0.0; 5]
    sv_grid[0] = gp_exp(-2.0)
    sv_grid[1] = gp_exp(-1.0)
    sv_grid[2] = gp_exp(0.0)
    sv_grid[3] = gp_exp(1.0)
    sv_grid[4] = gp_exp(2.0)

    var best_nlml = 1.0e30
    var best_ls = params_init.length_scale
    var best_sv = params_init.signal_var

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 7 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < 5 {
            let nlml = gp_eval_nlml(data, ls_grid[i as usize], sv_grid[j as usize], nv, kt)
            if nlml < best_nlml {
                best_nlml = nlml
                best_ls = ls_grid[i as usize]
                best_sv = sv_grid[j as usize]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return GPHyperparams {
        length_scale: best_ls,
        signal_var: best_sv,
        noise_var: nv,
        kernel_type: kt
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/hypothesis.sio ===
// stdlib/stats/hypothesis.sio — Complete hypothesis testing suite
//
// Implements:
//   z_test_one_sample      — one-sample z-test (known σ)
//   z_test_two_sample      — two-sample z-test (known σx, σy)
//   t_test_one_sample      — one-sample t-test (unknown σ)
//   t_test_two_sample      — Welch's two-sample t-test
//   t_test_paired          — paired t-test
//   chi2_goodness_of_fit   — chi-squared goodness-of-fit test
//   f_test                 — F-test for equality of variances
//   mann_whitney_u         — Mann-Whitney U (non-parametric)
//
// All tests return TestResult with epistemic bridge to GUMResult.
//
// References:
//   Student (1908) "The probable error of a mean"
//   Welch (1947) "The generalization of Student's problem"
//   Mann & Whitney (1947) "On a test of whether one of two random variables
//     is stochastically larger than the other"
//   Abramowitz & Stegun (1964) §26 — normal and t distributions
//   Press et al. (2007) "Numerical Recipes" 3rd ed., §14

use special::erf::{normal_cdf}
use special::beta::{ibeta}
use special::igamma::{chi2_cdf}
use epistemic::gum::{GUMResult, gum_simple}

// ============================================================================
// RESULT TYPE
// ============================================================================

pub struct TestResult {
    pub statistic: f64,     // test statistic value
    pub p_value: f64,       // two-tailed p-value
    pub reject: i32,        // 1 if reject H0 at alpha=0.05
    pub df: f64,            // degrees of freedom
    pub effect_size: f64,   // Cohen's d or equivalent
    pub as_gum: GUMResult,  // epistemic bridge: statistic ± standard error
}

// ============================================================================
// INTERNAL HELPERS — must precede all callers
// ============================================================================

fn ht_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// Newton-Raphson square root with range reduction into [1, 4)
fn ht_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var scaled = x
    var scale_back = 1.0
    while scaled < 1.0 { scaled = scaled * 4.0; scale_back = scale_back * 2.0 }
    while scaled > 4.0 { scaled = scaled * 0.25; scale_back = scale_back * 0.5 }
    var y = 1.5
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    return y / scale_back
}

// Sample mean over first n elements
fn ht_mean(data: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum / (n as f64)
}

// Sample variance (unbiased, divide by n-1)
fn ht_variance(data: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = ht_mean(data, n)
    var ss = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let d = data[i as usize] - m
        ss = ss + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    return ss / ((n - 1) as f64)
}

// t-distribution CDF via regularized incomplete beta:
//   P(T <= t | df) = 1 - 0.5 * I_{df/(df+t^2)}(df/2, 1/2)
// Two-tailed: p = I_{df/(df+t^2)}(df/2, 1/2)
fn t_cdf(t: f64, df: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let t2 = t * t
    let x = df / (df + t2)
    return ibeta(df / 2.0, 0.5, x)
}

// F-distribution CDF via regularized incomplete beta:
//   P(F <= f | df1, df2) = I_{df1*f/(df1*f+df2)}(df1/2, df2/2)
fn f_cdf(f: f64, df1: f64, df2: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if f <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let x = df1 * f / (df1 * f + df2)
    return ibeta(df1 / 2.0, df2 / 2.0, x)
}

// Build a TestResult from components
fn ht_make_result(stat: f64, p: f64, df: f64, effect: f64, se: f64) -> TestResult {
    let reject_h0 = if p < 0.05 { 1 } else { 0 }
    let gum = gum_simple(stat, se)
    return TestResult {
        statistic: stat,
        p_value: p,
        reject: reject_h0,
        df: df,
        effect_size: effect,
        as_gum: gum,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 1. ONE-SAMPLE Z-TEST
// ============================================================================
// z = (x̄ - μ₀) / (σ/√n)
// p = 2 * (1 - Φ(|z|))
// Cohen's d = (x̄ - μ₀) / σ

pub fn z_test_one_sample(data: &[f64; 256], n: i32, mu0: f64, sigma: f64) -> TestResult
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let xbar = ht_mean(data, n)
    let se = sigma / ht_sqrt(n as f64)
    let z = (xbar - mu0) / se
    let p = 2.0 * (1.0 - normal_cdf(ht_abs(z)))
    let d = (xbar - mu0) / sigma
    return ht_make_result(z, p, 1.0e9, d, se)
}

// ============================================================================
// 2. TWO-SAMPLE Z-TEST
// ============================================================================
// z = (x̄ - ȳ) / √(σx²/nx + σy²/ny)

pub fn z_test_two_sample(
    x: &[f64; 256], nx: i32,
    y: &[f64; 256], ny: i32,
    sigma_x: f64, sigma_y: f64
) -> TestResult with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let xbar = ht_mean(x, nx)
    let ybar = ht_mean(y, ny)
    let se = ht_sqrt(sigma_x * sigma_x / (nx as f64) + sigma_y * sigma_y / (ny as f64))
    let z = (xbar - ybar) / se
    let p = 2.0 * (1.0 - normal_cdf(ht_abs(z)))
    let pooled_sd = ht_sqrt((sigma_x * sigma_x + sigma_y * sigma_y) * 0.5)
    let d = (xbar - ybar) / pooled_sd
    return ht_make_result(z, p, 1.0e9, d, se)
}

// ============================================================================
// 3. ONE-SAMPLE T-TEST
// ============================================================================
// t = (x̄ - μ₀) / (s/√n),  df = n-1
// p via t_cdf (ibeta)

pub fn t_test_one_sample(data: &[f64; 256], n: i32, mu0: f64) -> TestResult
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let xbar = ht_mean(data, n)
    let s2 = ht_variance(data, n)
    let s = ht_sqrt(s2)
    let se = s / ht_sqrt(n as f64)
    let df = (n - 1) as f64
    let t = (xbar - mu0) / se
    let p = t_cdf(ht_abs(t), df)
    let d = (xbar - mu0) / s
    return ht_make_result(t, p, df, d, se)
}

// ============================================================================
// 4. TWO-SAMPLE T-TEST (WELCH'S)
// ============================================================================
// t = (x̄ - ȳ) / √(sx²/nx + sy²/ny)
// Welch-Satterthwaite: df = (sx²/nx + sy²/ny)² / (sx⁴/(nx²*(nx-1)) + sy⁴/(ny²*(ny-1)))

pub fn t_test_two_sample(
    x: &[f64; 256], nx: i32,
    y: &[f64; 256], ny: i32
) -> TestResult with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let xbar = ht_mean(x, nx)
    let ybar = ht_mean(y, ny)
    let s2x = ht_variance(x, nx)
    let s2y = ht_variance(y, ny)
    let se2x = s2x / (nx as f64)
    let se2y = s2y / (ny as f64)
    let se = ht_sqrt(se2x + se2y)
    let t = (xbar - ybar) / se
    // Welch-Satterthwaite df
    let num = (se2x + se2y) * (se2x + se2y)
    let denom = se2x * se2x / ((nx - 1) as f64) + se2y * se2y / ((ny - 1) as f64)
    let df = num / denom
    let p = t_cdf(ht_abs(t), df)
    // Pooled SD for Cohen's d approximation
    let sp = ht_sqrt((s2x + s2y) * 0.5)
    let d = (xbar - ybar) / sp
    return ht_make_result(t, p, df, d, se)
}

// ============================================================================
// 5. PAIRED T-TEST
// ============================================================================
// Differences: d_i = x_i - y_i; then one-sample t on differences

pub fn t_test_paired(x: &[f64; 256], y: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> TestResult
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    var diffs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        diffs[i as usize] = x[i as usize] - y[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let dbar = ht_mean(&diffs, n)
    let s2d = ht_variance(&diffs, n)
    let sd = ht_sqrt(s2d)
    let se = sd / ht_sqrt(n as f64)
    let df = (n - 1) as f64
    let t = dbar / se
    let p = t_cdf(ht_abs(t), df)
    let d = dbar / sd
    return ht_make_result(t, p, df, d, se)
}

// ============================================================================
// 6. CHI-SQUARED GOODNESS OF FIT
// ============================================================================
// χ² = Σ (O_i - E_i)² / E_i,  df = n_bins - 1
// p = 1 - chi2_cdf(χ², df)

pub fn chi2_goodness_of_fit(
    observed: &[f64; 256],
    expected: &[f64; 256],
    n_bins: i32
) -> TestResult with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    var chi2 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n_bins {
        let o = observed[i as usize]
        let e = expected[i as usize]
        if e > 1.0e-15 {
            let diff = o - e
            chi2 = chi2 + diff * diff / e
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let df = (n_bins - 1) as f64
    // p-value: P(χ² > chi2 | df) = 1 - chi2_cdf(chi2, df)
    let p = 1.0 - chi2_cdf(chi2, df)
    // Effect size: Cramér's V not easily defined for goodness of fit;
    // use standardised residual / sqrt(n_bins) as proxy
    let effect = ht_sqrt(chi2 / df)
    return ht_make_result(chi2, p, df, effect, ht_sqrt(2.0 * df))
}

// ============================================================================
// 7. F-TEST FOR EQUAL VARIANCES
// ============================================================================
// F = s₁²/s₂²,  df1 = nx-1,  df2 = ny-1
// Two-tailed p via F-distribution CDF

pub fn f_test(
    x: &[f64; 256], nx: i32,
    y: &[f64; 256], ny: i32
) -> TestResult with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let s2x = ht_variance(x, nx)
    let s2y = ht_variance(y, ny)
    let df1 = (nx - 1) as f64
    let df2 = (ny - 1) as f64
    let f = s2x / s2y
    // Two-tailed: p = 2 * min(P(F <= f), P(F >= f))
    let cdf_val = f_cdf(f, df1, df2)
    let p_lower = cdf_val
    let p_upper = 1.0 - cdf_val
    let p_one = if p_lower < p_upper { p_lower } else { p_upper }
    let p = 2.0 * p_one
    // Effect size: ratio of SDs
    let effect = ht_sqrt(f)
    let se_f = f * ht_sqrt(2.0 / df1 + 2.0 / df2)
    return ht_make_result(f, p, df1, effect, se_f)
}

// ============================================================================
// 8. MANN-WHITNEY U (NON-PARAMETRIC)
// ============================================================================
// U1 = nx*ny + nx*(nx+1)/2 - R1   where R1 = rank sum of x in combined sample
// Normal approximation: z = (U - mu_U) / sigma_U
// mu_U = nx*ny/2,  sigma_U = sqrt(nx*ny*(nx+ny+1)/12)

pub fn mann_whitney_u(
    x: &[f64; 256], nx: i32,
    y: &[f64; 256], ny: i32
) -> TestResult with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    // Count U1 directly: U1 = #{(i,j): x_i > y_j} + 0.5*#{x_i == y_j}
    var u1 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < nx {
        var j = 0
        while j < ny {
            let xi = x[i as usize]
            let yj = y[j as usize]
            if xi > yj {
                u1 = u1 + 1.0
            } else {
                if ht_abs(xi - yj) < 1.0e-12 {
                    u1 = u1 + 0.5
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let nxf = nx as f64
    let nyf = ny as f64
    let mu_u = nxf * nyf * 0.5
    let sigma_u = ht_sqrt(nxf * nyf * (nxf + nyf + 1.0) / 12.0)
    let z = (u1 - mu_u) / sigma_u
    let p = 2.0 * (1.0 - normal_cdf(ht_abs(z)))
    // Effect size: rank-biserial correlation r = 1 - 2*U / (nx*ny)
    let r = 1.0 - 2.0 * u1 / (nxf * nyf)
    let df_mw = nxf + nyf - 2.0
    return ht_make_result(u1, p, df_mw, ht_abs(r), sigma_u)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/inferential.sio ===
// stats::inferential — Inferential Statistics with Uncertainty
//
// Hypothesis testing with GUM-compliant uncertainty on test statistics
// and effect sizes. Returns p-values and confidence intervals.
//
// References:
// - Student (1908): "The probable error of a mean"
// - Welch (1947): "The generalization of Student's problem"
// - Mann & Whitney (1947): "On a test of whether one of two random variables..."

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64;
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST RESULT TYPES
// ============================================================================

// Result of a t-test
struct TTestResult {
    t_stat: f64,        // t-statistic
    df: f64,            // degrees of freedom
    p_value: f64,       // two-tailed p-value
    mean_diff: f64,     // difference in means
    se_diff: f64,       // standard error of difference
    ci_lower: f64,      // 95% CI lower bound
    ci_upper: f64,      // 95% CI upper bound
    cohens_d: f64,      // effect size (Cohen's d)
}

fn ttest_result_new() -> TTestResult {
    TTestResult {
        t_stat: 0.0,
        df: 0.0,
        p_value: 1.0,
        mean_diff: 0.0,
        se_diff: 0.0,
        ci_lower: 0.0,
        ci_upper: 0.0,
        cohens_d: 0.0,
    }
}

// Result of ANOVA
struct AnovaResult {
    f_stat: f64,        // F-statistic
    df_between: i64,    // between-group df
    df_within: i64,     // within-group df
    p_value: f64,       // p-value
    ss_between: f64,    // sum of squares between
    ss_within: f64,     // sum of squares within
    eta_squared: f64,   // effect size (eta^2)
}

fn anova_result_new() -> AnovaResult {
    AnovaResult {
        f_stat: 0.0,
        df_between: 0,
        df_within: 0,
        p_value: 1.0,
        ss_between: 0.0,
        ss_within: 0.0,
        eta_squared: 0.0,
    }
}

// Result of Mann-Whitney U test
struct MannWhitneyResult {
    u_stat: f64,        // U statistic
    z_stat: f64,        // z-score (normal approx)
    p_value: f64,       // two-tailed p-value
    rank_biserial: f64, // effect size (r)
}

fn mannwhitney_result_new() -> MannWhitneyResult {
    MannWhitneyResult {
        u_stat: 0.0,
        z_stat: 0.0,
        p_value: 1.0,
        rank_biserial: 0.0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn mean(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

fn variance(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    let m = mean(data, n)
    var sum_sq = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = data[i as usize] - m
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum_sq / ((n - 1) as f64)
}

fn std_dev(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    sqrt(variance(data, n))
}

// Approximate p-value from t-distribution using normal approximation
// Valid for df > 30; conservative for smaller df
fn t_to_p_approx(t: f64, df: f64) -> f64 {
    let abs_t = if t < 0.0 { -t } else { t }

    // Normal approximation for large df
    // For df < 30, this underestimates p (conservative)
    // Using logistic approximation to normal CDF
    let z = abs_t

    // Approximate 2-tailed p-value using error function approximation
    // P(|T| > t) ≈ 2 * Φ(-|t|) for large df
    let a1 = 0.254829592
    let a2 = -0.284496736
    let a3 = 1.421413741
    let a4 = -1.453152027
    let a5 = 1.061405429
    let p = 0.3275911

    let sign = if z < 0.0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    let x = if z < 0.0 { -z } else { z }

    let t_erf = 1.0 / (1.0 + p * x)
    let erf = 1.0 - (((((a5 * t_erf + a4) * t_erf) + a3) * t_erf + a2) * t_erf + a1) * t_erf * exp(-x * x)

    // Two-tailed p-value
    1.0 - erf
}

// Approximate p-value from F-distribution
fn f_to_p_approx(f: f64, df1: i64, df2: i64) -> f64 {
    // Very rough approximation using chi-square relationship
    // For production: use proper incomplete beta function
    if f <= 0.0 {
        return 1.0
    }

    // Fisher's approximation for large df
    let x = ((df1 as f64) * f) / ((df1 as f64) * f + (df2 as f64))

    // Approximate p-value (underestimates for small df)
    let p = 1.0 - x

    if p < 0.0 { 0.0 } else if p > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { p }
}

// Approximate p-value from z-score (normal distribution)
fn z_to_p(z: f64) -> f64 {
    let abs_z = if z < 0.0 { -z } else { z }

    // Error function approximation
    let a1 = 0.254829592
    let a2 = -0.284496736
    let a3 = 1.421413741
    let a4 = -1.453152027
    let a5 = 1.061405429
    let p = 0.3275911

    let t = 1.0 / (1.0 + p * abs_z)
    let erf = 1.0 - (((((a5 * t + a4) * t) + a3) * t + a2) * t + a1) * t * exp(-abs_z * abs_z)

    // Two-tailed p-value
    1.0 - erf
}

// ============================================================================
// T-TESTS
// ============================================================================

// One-sample t-test: test if mean differs from mu0
fn t_test_one_sample(data: [f64; 100], n: i64, mu0: f64) -> TTestResult {
    var result = ttest_result_new()

    let m = mean(data, n)
    let s = std_dev(data, n)
    let se = s / sqrt(n as f64)

    result.mean_diff = m - mu0
    result.se_diff = se
    result.df = (n - 1) as f64

    if se > 1e-10 {
        result.t_stat = result.mean_diff / se
    }

    result.p_value = t_to_p_approx(result.t_stat, result.df)

    // 95% CI (using t-critical ≈ 2.0 for large n)
    let t_crit = 2.0
    result.ci_lower = result.mean_diff - t_crit * se
    result.ci_upper = result.mean_diff + t_crit * se

    // Cohen's d = (mean - mu0) / s
    if s > 1e-10 {
        result.cohens_d = result.mean_diff / s
    }

    result
}

// Independent samples t-test (equal variance assumed)
fn t_test_independent(x: [f64; 100], nx: i64, y: [f64; 100], ny: i64) -> TTestResult {
    var result = ttest_result_new()

    let mx = mean(x, nx)
    let my = mean(y, ny)
    let sx = std_dev(x, nx)
    let sy = std_dev(y, ny)

    result.mean_diff = mx - my
    result.df = (nx + ny - 2) as f64

    // Pooled standard deviation
    let var_x = sx * sx
    let var_y = sy * sy
    let sp_sq = (((nx - 1) as f64) * var_x + ((ny - 1) as f64) * var_y) / result.df
    let sp = sqrt(sp_sq)

    // Standard error of difference
    result.se_diff = sp * sqrt(1.0 / (nx as f64) + 1.0 / (ny as f64))

    if result.se_diff > 1e-10 {
        result.t_stat = result.mean_diff / result.se_diff
    }

    result.p_value = t_to_p_approx(result.t_stat, result.df)

    // 95% CI
    let t_crit = 2.0
    result.ci_lower = result.mean_diff - t_crit * result.se_diff
    result.ci_upper = result.mean_diff + t_crit * result.se_diff

    // Cohen's d
    if sp > 1e-10 {
        result.cohens_d = result.mean_diff / sp
    }

    result
}

// Welch's t-test (unequal variance)
fn t_test_welch(x: [f64; 100], nx: i64, y: [f64; 100], ny: i64) -> TTestResult {
    var result = ttest_result_new()

    let mx = mean(x, nx)
    let my = mean(y, ny)
    let var_x = variance(x, nx)
    let var_y = variance(y, ny)

    result.mean_diff = mx - my

    // Welch's SE
    let se_x_sq = var_x / (nx as f64)
    let se_y_sq = var_y / (ny as f64)
    result.se_diff = sqrt(se_x_sq + se_y_sq)

    // Welch-Satterthwaite df
    let num = (se_x_sq + se_y_sq) * (se_x_sq + se_y_sq)
    let denom = se_x_sq * se_x_sq / ((nx - 1) as f64) + se_y_sq * se_y_sq / ((ny - 1) as f64)
    result.df = if denom > 1e-10 { num / denom } else { ((nx + ny - 2) as f64) }

    if result.se_diff > 1e-10 {
        result.t_stat = result.mean_diff / result.se_diff
    }

    result.p_value = t_to_p_approx(result.t_stat, result.df)

    // 95% CI
    let t_crit = 2.0
    result.ci_lower = result.mean_diff - t_crit * result.se_diff
    result.ci_upper = result.mean_diff + t_crit * result.se_diff

    // Cohen's d using pooled SD approximation
    let avg_var = (var_x + var_y) / 2.0
    let sp = sqrt(avg_var)
    if sp > 1e-10 {
        result.cohens_d = result.mean_diff / sp
    }

    result
}

// Paired t-test
fn t_test_paired(x: [f64; 100], y: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> TTestResult {
    // Compute differences
    var diff: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        diff[i as usize] = x[i as usize] - y[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // One-sample t-test on differences
    t_test_one_sample(diff, n, 0.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// ANOVA
// ============================================================================

// One-way ANOVA for 3 groups
fn anova_oneway_3(g1: [f64; 100], n1: i64,
                  g2: [f64; 100], n2: i64,
                  g3: [f64; 100], n3: i64) -> AnovaResult {
    var result = anova_result_new()

    let n_total = n1 + n2 + n3
    let k = 3  // number of groups

    // Group means
    let m1 = mean(g1, n1)
    let m2 = mean(g2, n2)
    let m3 = mean(g3, n3)

    // Grand mean
    var sum_total = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n1 {
        sum_total = sum_total + g1[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n2 {
        sum_total = sum_total + g2[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n3 {
        sum_total = sum_total + g3[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let grand_mean = sum_total / (n_total as f64)

    // SS between
    result.ss_between = (n1 as f64) * (m1 - grand_mean) * (m1 - grand_mean)
                      + (n2 as f64) * (m2 - grand_mean) * (m2 - grand_mean)
                      + (n3 as f64) * (m3 - grand_mean) * (m3 - grand_mean)

    // SS within
    result.ss_within = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n1 {
        let diff = g1[i as usize] - m1
        result.ss_within = result.ss_within + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n2 {
        let diff = g2[i as usize] - m2
        result.ss_within = result.ss_within + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n3 {
        let diff = g3[i as usize] - m3
        result.ss_within = result.ss_within + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }

    result.df_between = k - 1
    result.df_within = n_total - k

    // Mean squares
    let ms_between = result.ss_between / (result.df_between as f64)
    let ms_within = result.ss_within / (result.df_within as f64)

    if ms_within > 1e-10 {
        result.f_stat = ms_between / ms_within
    }

    result.p_value = f_to_p_approx(result.f_stat, result.df_between, result.df_within)

    // Eta squared
    let ss_total = result.ss_between + result.ss_within
    if ss_total > 1e-10 {
        result.eta_squared = result.ss_between / ss_total
    }

    result
}

// ============================================================================
// NON-PARAMETRIC TESTS
// ============================================================================

// Mann-Whitney U test (Wilcoxon rank-sum)
fn mann_whitney_u(x: [f64; 100], nx: i64, y: [f64; 100], ny: i64) -> MannWhitneyResult {
    var result = mannwhitney_result_new()

    // Combine and rank
    // For simplicity, count pairwise comparisons
    var u_x = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < nx {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < ny {
            if x[i as usize] > y[j as usize] {
                u_x = u_x + 1.0
            } else if x[i as usize] == y[j as usize] {
                u_x = u_x + 0.5
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let u_y = (nx as f64) * (ny as f64) - u_x
    result.u_stat = if u_x < u_y { u_x } else { u_y }

    // Normal approximation for z-score
    let n_xy = (nx as f64) * (ny as f64)
    let mu_u = n_xy / 2.0
    let sigma_u = sqrt(n_xy * ((nx + ny + 1) as f64) / 12.0)

    if sigma_u > 1e-10 {
        result.z_stat = (u_x - mu_u) / sigma_u
    }

    result.p_value = z_to_p(result.z_stat)

    // Rank-biserial correlation (effect size)
    if n_xy > 0.0 {
        result.rank_biserial = (2.0 * u_x - n_xy) / n_xy
    }

    result
}

// ============================================================================
// SPEARMAN RANK CORRELATION
// ============================================================================

// Result of Spearman rho test
struct SpearmanResult {
    rho: f64,     // rank correlation in [-1, 1]
    t_stat: f64,  // t = rho * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - rho^2))
    p_value: f64, // two-sided, via t-distribution with n-2 df
    df: f64,
}

fn spearman_result_new() -> SpearmanResult {
    SpearmanResult {
        rho: 0.0,
        t_stat: 0.0,
        p_value: 1.0,
        df: 0.0,
    }
}

// Tie-averaged ranks (1-based). Selection-sort on indices to keep
// memory predictable; n <= 100 is the stdlib convention.
fn rank_f64(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> [f64; 100] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var ranks: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var order: [i64; 100] = [0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        order[i as usize] = i
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        var min_idx = i
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n {
            if data[order[j as usize] as usize] < data[order[min_idx as usize] as usize] {
                min_idx = j
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if min_idx != i {
            let tmp = order[i as usize]
            order[i as usize] = order[min_idx as usize]
            order[min_idx as usize] = tmp
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Walk sorted order, assigning tie-averaged ranks.
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n && data[order[j as usize] as usize] == data[order[i as usize] as usize] {
            j = j + 1
        }
        let tie_len = j - i
        // Average of (i+1)..(j) in 1-based ranks.
        let avg = ((i + 1) as f64 + (j as f64)) / 2.0
        var k: i64 = i
        while k < j {
            ranks[order[k as usize] as usize] = avg
            k = k + 1
        }
        i = j
    }
    ranks
}

// Spearman's rho via Pearson correlation on tie-averaged ranks.
pub fn spearman_rho(x: [f64; 100], y: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 2 { return 0.0 }
    let rx = rank_f64(x, n)
    let ry = rank_f64(y, n)

    var mean_x = 0.0
    var mean_y = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        mean_x = mean_x + rx[i as usize]
        mean_y = mean_y + ry[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    mean_x = mean_x / (n as f64)
    mean_y = mean_y / (n as f64)

    var sxy = 0.0
    var sxx = 0.0
    var syy = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let dx = rx[i as usize] - mean_x
        let dy = ry[i as usize] - mean_y
        sxy = sxy + dx * dy
        sxx = sxx + dx * dx
        syy = syy + dy * dy
        i = i + 1
    }
    let denom = sqrt(sxx * syy)
    if denom < 1.0e-12 { return 0.0 }
    sxy / denom
}

// Full Spearman test: rho plus t-based two-sided p-value.
pub fn spearman_test(x: [f64; 100], y: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> SpearmanResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = spearman_result_new()
    if n < 3 { return result }
    let rho = spearman_rho(x, y, n)
    result.rho = rho
    result.df = (n - 2) as f64
    let one_minus_r2 = 1.0 - rho * rho
    if one_minus_r2 <= 1.0e-12 {
        result.t_stat = if rho >= 0.0 { 1.0e12 } else { 0.0 - 1.0e12 }
        result.p_value = 0.0
        return result
    }
    result.t_stat = rho * sqrt(result.df / one_minus_r2)
    result.p_value = t_to_p_approx(result.t_stat, result.df)
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// EFFECT SIZE INTERPRETATION
// ============================================================================

// Cohen's d interpretation
fn cohens_d_interpret(d: f64) -> i64 {
    let abs_d = if d < 0.0 { -d } else { d }
    if abs_d < 0.2 {
        return 0  // negligible
    }
    if abs_d < 0.5 {
        return 1  // small
    }
    if abs_d < 0.8 {
        return 2  // medium
    }
    3  // large
}

// Eta-squared interpretation
fn eta_squared_interpret(eta2: f64) -> i64 {
    if eta2 < 0.01 {
        return 0  // negligible
    }
    if eta2 < 0.06 {
        return 1  // small
    }
    if eta2 < 0.14 {
        return 2  // medium
    }
    3  // large
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn inf_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { -x } else { x }
}

fn test_one_sample_t() -> bool {
    var data: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    data[0] = 5.0
    data[1] = 6.0
    data[2] = 7.0
    data[3] = 8.0
    data[4] = 9.0

    // Mean = 7, test against mu0 = 7 -> t should be ~0
    let result = t_test_one_sample(data, 5, 7.0)

    inf_abs_f64(result.t_stat) < 0.01
}

fn test_independent_t() -> bool {
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // Group 1: mean = 10
    x[0] = 9.0
    x[1] = 10.0
    x[2] = 11.0
    x[3] = 10.0
    x[4] = 10.0

    // Group 2: mean = 15
    y[0] = 14.0
    y[1] = 15.0
    y[2] = 16.0
    y[3] = 15.0
    y[4] = 15.0

    let result = t_test_independent(x, 5, y, 5)

    // mean_diff should be -5
    inf_abs_f64(result.mean_diff - (-5.0)) < 0.1
}

fn test_paired_t() -> bool {
    var pre: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var post: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // Pre-treatment: 100, 102, 104, 101, 103
    pre[0] = 100.0
    pre[1] = 102.0
    pre[2] = 104.0
    pre[3] = 101.0
    pre[4] = 103.0

    // Post-treatment: 95, 97, 99, 96, 98 (decrease of 5)
    post[0] = 95.0
    post[1] = 97.0
    post[2] = 99.0
    post[3] = 96.0
    post[4] = 98.0

    let result = t_test_paired(pre, post, 5)

    // mean difference should be 5
    inf_abs_f64(result.mean_diff - 5.0) < 0.1
}

fn test_mann_whitney() -> bool {
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // Group with lower values
    x[0] = 1.0
    x[1] = 2.0
    x[2] = 3.0

    // Group with higher values
    y[0] = 4.0
    y[1] = 5.0
    y[2] = 6.0

    let result = mann_whitney_u(x, 3, y, 3)

    // U should reflect clear separation
    result > 0.0
}

fn test_spearman_rho_perfect() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 10 {
        x[i as usize] = i as f64
        y[i as usize] = 2.0 * (i as f64) + 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Monotone-increasing pair → rho == +1 exactly.
    let rho = spearman_rho(x, y, 10)
    inf_abs_f64(rho - 1.0) < 1.0e-9
}

fn test_spearman_rho_reversed() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 10 {
        x[i as usize] = i as f64
        y[i as usize] = 0.0 - (i as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Monotone-decreasing pair → rho == -1 exactly.
    let rho = spearman_rho(x, y, 10)
    inf_abs_f64(rho + 1.0) < 1.0e-9
}

fn test_spearman_ties() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    // Two tied blocks in x, matching ties in y.
    x[0] = 1.0
    x[1] = 1.0
    x[2] = 2.0
    x[3] = 2.0
    x[4] = 3.0
    y[0] = 5.0
    y[1] = 5.0
    y[2] = 6.0
    y[3] = 6.0
    y[4] = 7.0
    let rho = spearman_rho(x, y, 5)
    // Ranks are identical after tie averaging → rho == +1.
    inf_abs_f64(rho - 1.0) < 1.0e-9
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/stats - Statistical Analysis

module stats


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/multiple_testing.sio ===
// stats::multiple_testing — P-value correction for multiple comparisons
//
// Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) corrections.
// Fixed-array implementations, max 100 tests.
//
// References:
// - Bonferroni (1936): correction for familywise error rate
// - Benjamini & Hochberg (1995): "Controlling the false discovery rate"

// =============================================================================
// Bonferroni correction
// =============================================================================

// Multiply each p-value by the number of tests, cap at 1.0
fn bonferroni(
    p_values: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    adjusted: &![f64; 100]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let adj = p_values[i as usize] * (n as f64)
        adjusted[i as usize] = if adj > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { adj }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) correction
// =============================================================================

// Sort indices by p-value (selection sort, small n)
fn sort_indices_by_pval(
    p_values: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    indices: &![i64; 100]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Initialize indices
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        indices[i as usize] = i
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Selection sort
    i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        var min_idx = i
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n {
            if p_values[indices[j as usize] as usize] < p_values[indices[min_idx as usize] as usize] {
                min_idx = j
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if min_idx != i {
            let tmp = indices[i as usize]
            indices[i as usize] = indices[min_idx as usize]
            indices[min_idx as usize] = tmp
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn benjamini_hochberg(
    p_values: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    adjusted: &![f64; 100]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Step 1: Sort p-values
    var indices: [i64; 100] = [0; 100]
    sort_indices_by_pval(p_values, n, &indices)

    // Step 2: Compute adjusted p-values
    // adjusted[rank] = p * n / rank, then enforce monotonicity from bottom up
    var temp: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let rank = i + 1
        let adj = p_values[indices[i as usize] as usize] * (n as f64) / (rank as f64)
        temp[i as usize] = if adj > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { adj }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 3: Enforce monotonicity (cumulative min from end)
    i = n - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        if temp[(i + 1) as usize] < temp[i as usize] {
            temp[i as usize] = temp[(i + 1) as usize]
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    // Step 4: Map back to original order
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        adjusted[indices[i as usize] as usize] = temp[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Holm–Bonferroni (FWER step-down)
// =============================================================================

// Step-down Holm correction (Holm 1979). Controls family-wise error rate
// strictly. For sorted p_(1) <= ... <= p_(n), adjusted p_(i) =
// max_{k<=i} (n - k + 1) * p_(k), capped at 1.0. For n = 3 this matches
// the primary-hypothesis test family in docs/papers/preregistrations/
// 2026-04-21_ossm_168_depression_v3.md §8.
pub fn holm_bonferroni(
    p_values: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    adjusted: &![f64; 100]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var indices: [i64; 100] = [0; 100]
    sort_indices_by_pval(p_values, n, &!indices)

    var temp: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let raw = p_values[indices[i as usize] as usize] * ((n - i) as f64)
        let capped = if raw > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { raw }
        temp[i as usize] = capped
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Enforce monotonicity top-down (running max).
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        if temp[(i - 1) as usize] > temp[i as usize] {
            temp[i as usize] = temp[(i - 1) as usize]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Map back to original order.
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        adjusted[indices[i as usize] as usize] = temp[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Significance counting
// =============================================================================

fn count_significant(adjusted: [f64; 100], n: i64, alpha: f64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if adjusted[i as usize] < alpha {
            count = count + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    count
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn mt_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn test_bonferroni() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pvals: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    pvals[0] = 0.01
    pvals[1] = 0.04
    pvals[2] = 0.03
    pvals[3] = 0.20

    var adj: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    bonferroni(pvals, 4, &adj)

    // 0.01 * 4 = 0.04, 0.04 * 4 = 0.16, 0.03 * 4 = 0.12, 0.20 * 4 = 0.80
    let ok1 = mt_abs(adj[0] - 0.04) < 0.001
    let ok2 = mt_abs(adj[1] - 0.16) < 0.001
    ok1 && ok2
}

fn test_bh() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pvals: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    pvals[0] = 0.01
    pvals[1] = 0.04
    pvals[2] = 0.03
    pvals[3] = 0.20

    var adj: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    benjamini_hochberg(pvals, 4, &adj)

    // Smallest p (0.01) adjusted = 0.01*4/1 = 0.04
    let ok1 = mt_abs(adj[0] - 0.04) < 0.001
    // All adjusted p-values should be <= 1.0
    let ok2 = adj[3] <= 1.0
    ok1 && ok2
}

fn test_holm() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Textbook example: p = {0.01, 0.04, 0.03, 0.20}.
    // Sorted: 0.01, 0.03, 0.04, 0.20 with multipliers 4, 3, 2, 1
    // → raw 0.04, 0.09, 0.08, 0.20. Running max → 0.04, 0.09, 0.09, 0.20.
    var pvals: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    pvals[0] = 0.01
    pvals[1] = 0.04
    pvals[2] = 0.03
    pvals[3] = 0.20

    var adj: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    holm_bonferroni(pvals, 4, &!adj)

    let ok1 = mt_abs(adj[0] - 0.04) < 1.0e-9   // smallest p
    let ok2 = mt_abs(adj[2] - 0.09) < 1.0e-9   // p=0.03
    let ok3 = mt_abs(adj[1] - 0.09) < 1.0e-9   // p=0.04 capped up by monotonicity
    let ok4 = mt_abs(adj[3] - 0.20) < 1.0e-9   // largest
    ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4
}

fn test_holm_family_of_three() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Prereg v3 §8: FWER alpha = 0.05/3 over H1, H2, H3.
    // With p = {0.005, 0.04, 0.30}, sorted multipliers 3, 2, 1:
    // → 0.015, 0.08, 0.30 → running max → 0.015, 0.08, 0.30.
    var pvals: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    pvals[0] = 0.005  // H1
    pvals[1] = 0.040  // H2
    pvals[2] = 0.300  // H3

    var adj: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    holm_bonferroni(pvals, 3, &!adj)

    let ok1 = adj[0] < 0.05           // H1 survives Holm at alpha=0.05
    let ok2 = adj[1] > 0.05            // H2 fails
    let ok3 = mt_abs(adj[2] - 0.30) < 1.0e-9
    ok1 && ok2 && ok3
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/multivariate/cluster.sio ===
// stats::multivariate::cluster — Epistemic Clustering
//
// Unsupervised clustering with epistemic quality metrics:
// - K-means (Lloyd's algorithm)
// - Hierarchical agglomerative (single/complete/average linkage)
// - Silhouette scores for cluster quality
// - Elbow method for optimal K
// - Knowledge<ClusterResult> with confidence
//
// References:
// - Lloyd (1982): "Least squares quantization in PCM"
// - Ward (1963): "Hierarchical grouping to optimize an objective function"
// - Rousseeuw (1987): "Silhouettes: a graphical aid" (silhouette scores)
// - Tibshirani et al. (2001): "Estimating the number of clusters" (gap statistic)

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

fn cl_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn cl_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn cl_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn cl_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// =============================================================================
// Types
// =============================================================================

let MAX_K: i64 = 10
let MAX_N: i64 = 100
let MAX_P: i64 = 10

struct KMeansResult {
    centroids: [[f64; 10]; 10],   // k × p centroid positions
    assignments: [i64; 100],       // Cluster label for each observation
    k: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    n_vars: i64,
    within_ss: f64,                // Total within-cluster sum of squares
    between_ss: f64,               // Between-cluster sum of squares
    total_ss: f64,
    n_iterations: i64,
    converged: bool
}

struct SilhouetteResult {
    scores: [f64; 100],            // Per-observation silhouette score [-1, 1]
    avg_score: f64,                 // Average silhouette width
    cluster_avg: [f64; 10]         // Per-cluster average
}



struct ClusterDiagnostics {
    silhouette: SilhouetteResult,
    calinski_harabasz: f64,   // CH index (higher = better)
    cluster_quality: BetaConfidence
}

struct ClusterProvenance {
    method: String,
    k: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    n_vars: i64,
    diagnostics: ClusterDiagnostics
}

struct KnowledgeCluster {
    value: KMeansResult,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: ClusterProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// Distance Functions
// =============================================================================

fn euclidean_dist(
    a: [f64; 10],
    b: [f64; 10],
    p: i64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        let d = a[j as usize] - b[j as usize]
        sum = sum + d * d
        j = j + 1
    }
    cl_sqrt(sum)
}

fn euclidean_dist_sq(a: [f64; 10], b: [f64; 10], p: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        let d = a[j as usize] - b[j as usize]
        sum = sum + d * d
        j = j + 1
    }
    sum
}

// =============================================================================
// K-MEANS (Lloyd's Algorithm)
// =============================================================================

fn kmeans(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    k: i64,
    max_iter: i64
) -> KMeansResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Initialize centroids (first k observations)
    var centroids: [[f64; 10]; 10] = [[0.0; 10]; 10]
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < k {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < p {
            centroids[c as usize][j as usize] = data[c as usize][j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        c = c + 1
    }

    var assignments: [i64; 100] = [0; 100]
    var converged = false
    var iter: i64 = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        var changed = false

        // Assignment step: assign each point to nearest centroid
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            var best_c: i64 = 0
            var best_dist = euclidean_dist_sq(data[i as usize], centroids[0], p)

            c = 1
            while c < k {
                let d = euclidean_dist_sq(data[i as usize], centroids[c as usize], p)
                if d < best_dist {
                    best_dist = d
                    best_c = c
                }
                c = c + 1
            }

            if assignments[i as usize] != best_c {
                assignments[i as usize] = best_c
                changed = true
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        if !changed {
            converged = true
            break
        }

        // Update step: recompute centroids
        var counts: [i64; 10] = [0; 10]
        var sums: [[f64; 10]; 10] = [[0.0; 10]; 10]

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            let cl = assignments[i as usize]
            counts[cl as usize] = counts[cl as usize] + 1
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < p {
                sums[cl as usize][j as usize] = sums[cl as usize][j as usize] + data[i as usize][j as usize]
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        c = 0
        while c < k {
            if counts[c as usize] > 0 {
                var j: i64 = 0
                while j < p {
                    centroids[c as usize][j as usize] = sums[c as usize][j as usize] / (counts[c as usize] as f64)
                    j = j + 1
                }
            }
            c = c + 1
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Compute within-cluster SS and between-cluster SS
    // Grand mean
    var grand: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        var sum = 0.0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n { sum = sum + data[i as usize][j as usize]; i = i + 1 }
        grand[j as usize] = sum / (n as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }

    var wss = 0.0
    var bss = 0.0
    var tss = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let cl = assignments[i as usize]
        wss = wss + euclidean_dist_sq(data[i as usize], centroids[cl as usize], p)
        tss = tss + euclidean_dist_sq(data[i as usize], grand, p)
        i = i + 1
    }
    bss = tss - wss

    KMeansResult {
        centroids: centroids,
        assignments: assignments,
        k: k,
        n_obs: n,
        n_vars: p,
        within_ss: wss,
        between_ss: bss,
        total_ss: tss,
        n_iterations: iter,
        converged: converged
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// SILHOUETTE SCORES
// =============================================================================

fn silhouette_scores(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    assignments: [i64; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    k: i64
) -> SilhouetteResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var scores: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var cluster_sums: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var cluster_counts: [i64; 10] = [0; 10]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let ci = assignments[i as usize]

        // a(i) = average distance to points in same cluster
        var a_sum = 0.0
        var a_count: i64 = 0

        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            if j != i && assignments[j as usize] == ci {
                a_sum = a_sum + euclidean_dist(data[i as usize], data[j as usize], p)
                a_count = a_count + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        let a_i = if a_count > 0 { a_sum / (a_count as f64) } else { 0.0 }

        // b(i) = min over other clusters of avg distance
        var b_i = 1.0e30
        var c: i64 = 0
        while c < k {
            if c == ci { c = c + 1; continue }

            var b_sum = 0.0
            var b_count: i64 = 0
            j = 0
            while j < n {
                if assignments[j as usize] == c {
                    b_sum = b_sum + euclidean_dist(data[i as usize], data[j as usize], p)
                    b_count = b_count + 1
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            let b_c = if b_count > 0 { b_sum / (b_count as f64) } else { 1.0e30 }
            b_i = cl_min(b_i, b_c)

            c = c + 1
        }

        // s(i) = (b(i) - a(i)) / max(a(i), b(i))
        let max_ab = cl_max(a_i, b_i)
        let s = if max_ab > 1.0e-10 { (b_i - a_i) / max_ab } else { 0.0 }
        scores[i as usize] = s

        cluster_sums[ci as usize] = cluster_sums[ci as usize] + s
        cluster_counts[ci as usize] = cluster_counts[ci as usize] + 1

        i = i + 1
    }

    // Average silhouette
    var total = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n { total = total + scores[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    let avg = total / (n as f64)

    // Per-cluster averages
    var cluster_avg: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < k {
        cluster_avg[c as usize] = if cluster_counts[c as usize] > 0 {
            cluster_sums[c as usize] / (cluster_counts[c as usize] as f64)
        } else { 0.0 }
        c = c + 1
    }

    SilhouetteResult {
        scores: scores,
        avg_score: avg,
        cluster_avg: cluster_avg
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC CLUSTERING
// =============================================================================

fn kmeans_epistemic(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    k: i64
) -> KnowledgeCluster with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let result = kmeans(data, n, p, k, 100)
    let sil = silhouette_scores(data, result.assignments, n, p, k)

    // Calinski-Harabasz index: (BSS/(k-1)) / (WSS/(n-k))
    let ch = if k > 1 && result.within_ss > 1.0e-10 {
        (result.between_ss / ((k - 1) as f64)) / (result.within_ss / ((n - k) as f64))
    } else { 0.0 }

    // Cluster quality confidence
    let sil_conf = if sil.avg_score > 0.70 { 0.95 }      // Strong
                   else if sil.avg_score > 0.50 { 0.80 }   // Reasonable
                   else if sil.avg_score > 0.25 { 0.60 }   // Weak
                   else { 0.40 }                             // No structure
    let quality_beta = beta_new(sil_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - sil_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    let diag = ClusterDiagnostics {
        silhouette: sil,
        calinski_harabasz: ch,
        cluster_quality: quality_beta
    }

    let prov = ClusterProvenance {
        method: "KMeans_Lloyd",
        k: k,
        n_obs: n,
        n_vars: p,
        diagnostics: diag
    }

    KnowledgeCluster {
        value: result,
        variance: 0.0,
        confidence: quality_beta,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_kmeans_two_clusters() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var data: [[f64; 10]; 100] = [[0.0; 10]; 100]

    // Cluster 1: near (0, 0)
    data[0][0] = 0.1; data[0][1] = 0.2
    data[1][0] = 0.3; data[1][1] = 0.1
    data[2][0] = 0.0; data[2][1] = 0.3
    data[3][0] = 0.2; data[3][1] = 0.0
    data[4][0] = 0.1; data[4][1] = 0.1

    // Cluster 2: near (5, 5)
    data[5][0] = 4.9; data[5][1] = 5.1
    data[6][0] = 5.1; data[6][1] = 4.9
    data[7][0] = 5.0; data[7][1] = 5.0
    data[8][0] = 4.8; data[8][1] = 5.2
    data[9][0] = 5.2; data[9][1] = 4.8

    let result = kmeans_epistemic(data, 10, 2, 2)

    // Should separate into two clusters
    let converged = result.value.converged

    // High silhouette (well-separated)
    let sil_ok = result.provenance.diagnostics.silhouette.avg_score > 0.5

    converged && sil_ok
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/multivariate/pca.sio ===
// stats::multivariate::pca — Epistemic Principal Component Analysis
//
// Dimensionality reduction with full uncertainty tracking:
// - SVD-based PCA (power iteration method)
// - Scree analysis with broken-stick model
// - Component loadings and scores
// - Variance explained with bootstrap CIs
// - Knowledge<PCAResult> with epistemic metadata
//
// References:
// - Pearson (1901): "On lines and planes of closest fit"
// - Hotelling (1933): "Analysis of complex statistical variables"
// - Jackson (1993): "Stopping rules in PCA" (broken-stick)
// - Cattell (1966): "The scree test for the number of factors"

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

fn pca_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn pca_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn pca_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

struct EigenResult {
    eigenvalue: f64,
    eigenvector: [f64; 10]
}

// =============================================================================
// Types
// =============================================================================

// Max dimensions: 10 variables, 100 observations
let MAX_VARS: i64 = 10

struct PCAResult {
    eigenvalues: [f64; 10],            // Sorted descending
    variance_explained: [f64; 10],     // Proportion of variance
    cumulative_variance: [f64; 10],    // Cumulative proportion
    loadings: [[f64; 10]; 10],         // Component loadings (p × k)
    scores: [[f64; 10]; 100],          // Observation scores (n × k)
    n_components_optimal: i64,         // Recommended components
    n_vars: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    total_variance: f64
}

struct PCADiagnostics {
    kaiser_criterion: i64,        // Components with eigenvalue > 1
    broken_stick_criterion: i64,  // Broken-stick model
    variance_80_pct: i64,         // Components for 80% variance
    sample_adequate: BetaConfidence  // KMO-like adequacy
}

struct PCAProvenance {
    method_id: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    n_vars: i64,
    standardized: i64,
    diagnostics: PCADiagnostics
}

struct KnowledgePCA {
    value: PCAResult,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: PCAProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// Matrix Operations
// =============================================================================

// Compute column means
fn col_means(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64
) -> [f64; 10] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var means: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        var sum = 0.0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            sum = sum + data[i as usize][j as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
        means[j as usize] = sum / (n as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }
    means
}

// Center data (subtract column means)
fn center_data(
    data: &![[f64; 10]; 100],
    means: [f64; 10],
    n: i64,
    p: i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < p {
            data[i as usize][j as usize] = data[i as usize][j as usize] - means[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Standardize data (center + divide by SD)
fn standardize_data(
    data: &![[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let means = col_means(*data, n, p)

    // Compute SDs
    var sds: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        var ss = 0.0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            let d = data[i as usize][j as usize] - means[j as usize]
            ss = ss + d * d
            i = i + 1
        }
        sds[j as usize] = pca_sqrt(ss / ((n - 1) as f64))
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Center and scale
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            let sd = pca_max(sds[j as usize], 1.0e-10)
            data[i as usize][j as usize] = (data[i as usize][j as usize] - means[j as usize]) / sd
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Compute covariance matrix (p × p) from centered data
fn covariance_matrix(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64
) -> [[f64; 10]; 10] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cov: [[f64; 10]; 10] = [[0.0; 10]; 10]

    var j1: i64 = 0
    while j1 < p {
        var j2: i64 = j1
        while j2 < p {
            var sum = 0.0
            var i: i64 = 0
            while i < n {
                sum = sum + data[i as usize][j1 as usize] * data[i as usize][j2 as usize]
                i = i + 1
            }
            let c = sum / ((n - 1) as f64)
            cov[j1 as usize][j2 as usize] = c
            cov[j2 as usize][j1 as usize] = c  // Symmetric
            j2 = j2 + 1
        }
        j1 = j1 + 1
    }

    cov
}
