// =============================================================================
// Power Iteration for Eigenvalues/Eigenvectors
// =============================================================================

// Extract dominant eigenvalue/eigenvector via power iteration
fn power_iteration(
    mat: [[f64; 10]; 10],
    p: i64,
    max_iter: i64
) -> EigenResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Initial vector
    var v: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        v[j as usize] = 1.0 / pca_sqrt(p as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }

    var eigenvalue = 0.0
    var iter: i64 = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        // w = A * v
        var w: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k: i64 = 0
            while k < p {
                sum = sum + mat[j as usize][k as usize] * v[k as usize]
                k = k + 1
            }
            w[j as usize] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }

        // Eigenvalue = ||w||
        var norm = 0.0
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            norm = norm + w[j as usize] * w[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        eigenvalue = pca_sqrt(norm)

        if eigenvalue < 1.0e-10 { break }

        // Normalize: v = w / ||w||
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            v[j as usize] = w[j as usize] / eigenvalue
            j = j + 1
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    EigenResult { eigenvalue: eigenvalue, eigenvector: v }
}

// Deflate matrix: A' = A - λ·v·v'
fn deflate_matrix(
    mat: &![[f64; 10]; 10],
    eigenvalue: f64,
    eigenvector: [f64; 10],
    p: i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < p {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < p {
            mat[i as usize][j as usize] = mat[i as usize][j as usize] -
                eigenvalue * eigenvector[i as usize] * eigenvector[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Broken-Stick Model (for optimal component selection)
// =============================================================================

fn broken_stick_expected(k: i64, p: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Expected proportion for k-th component under broken-stick:
    // b_k = (1/p) * Σ_{j=k}^{p} 1/j
    var sum = 0.0
    var j: i64 = k
    while j <= p {
        sum = sum + 1.0 / (j as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }
    sum / (p as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// PCA IMPLEMENTATION
// =============================================================================

fn fit_pca(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    standardize: i64
) -> PCAResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Step 1: Center (and optionally standardize)
    var work_data: [[f64; 10]; 100] = data

    if standardize != 0 {
        standardize_data(&work_data, n, p)
    } else {
        let means = col_means(work_data, n, p)
        center_data(&work_data, means, n, p)
    }

    // Step 2: Covariance matrix
    var cov = covariance_matrix(work_data, n, p)

    // Step 3: Total variance
    var total_var = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        total_var = total_var + cov[j as usize][j as usize]
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Step 4: Extract eigenvalues/vectors via repeated power iteration + deflation
    var eigenvalues: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var loadings: [[f64; 10]; 10] = [[0.0; 10]; 10]
    var var_explained: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var cum_var: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]

    var cum = 0.0
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < p {
        let eig = power_iteration(cov, p, 100)
        let ev = eig.eigenvalue
        let evec = eig.eigenvector
        eigenvalues[k as usize] = ev

        // Store loadings
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            loadings[j as usize][k as usize] = evec[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }

        // Variance explained
        let prop = if total_var > 1.0e-10 { ev / total_var } else { 0.0 }
        var_explained[k as usize] = prop
        cum = cum + prop
        cum_var[k as usize] = cum

        // Deflate
        deflate_matrix(&cov, ev, evec, p)

        k = k + 1
    }

    // Step 5: Compute scores (n × k): S = X_centered · V
    var scores: [[f64; 10]; 100] = [[0.0; 10]; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        k = 0
        while k < p {
            var sum = 0.0
            j = 0
            while j < p {
                sum = sum + work_data[i as usize][j as usize] * loadings[j as usize][k as usize]
                j = j + 1
            }
            scores[i as usize][k as usize] = sum
            k = k + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 6: Optimal components
    // Kaiser criterion: eigenvalue > 1 (for correlation PCA)
    var kaiser = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        if eigenvalues[k as usize] > 1.0 { kaiser = kaiser + 1 }
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Broken-stick criterion
    var broken_stick = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        let expected = broken_stick_expected(k + 1, p)
        if var_explained[k as usize] > expected { broken_stick = broken_stick + 1 }
        k = k + 1
    }

    // 80% variance
    var var80 = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        var80 = var80 + 1
        if cum_var[k as usize] >= 0.80 { break }
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Use most conservative criterion
    let optimal = if kaiser < broken_stick { kaiser } else { broken_stick }
    let optimal_final = if optimal < var80 { var80 } else { optimal }

    PCAResult {
        eigenvalues: eigenvalues,
        variance_explained: var_explained,
        cumulative_variance: cum_var,
        loadings: loadings,
        scores: scores,
        n_components_optimal: optimal_final,
        n_vars: p,
        n_obs: n,
        total_variance: total_var
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC PCA
// =============================================================================

fn fit_pca_epistemic(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    standardize: i64
) -> KnowledgePCA with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let result = fit_pca(data, n, p, standardize)

    // Diagnostics
    var kaiser = 0
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < p {
        if result.eigenvalues[k as usize] > 1.0 { kaiser = kaiser + 1 }
        k = k + 1
    }

    var broken = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        let exp = broken_stick_expected(k + 1, p)
        if result.variance_explained[k as usize] > exp { broken = broken + 1 }
        k = k + 1
    }

    var var80 = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        var80 = var80 + 1
        if result.cumulative_variance[k as usize] >= 0.80 { break }
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Sample adequacy: n/p ratio (rule of thumb: 5-10 per variable)
    let np_ratio = (n as f64) / (p as f64)
    let sample_conf = if np_ratio >= 10.0 { 0.95 }
                      else if np_ratio >= 5.0 { 0.80 }
                      else if np_ratio >= 3.0 { 0.60 }
                      else { 0.40 }
    let sample_beta = beta_new(sample_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - sample_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    let diag = PCADiagnostics {
        kaiser_criterion: kaiser as i64,
        broken_stick_criterion: broken as i64,
        variance_80_pct: var80 as i64,
        sample_adequate: sample_beta
    }

    let prov = PCAProvenance {
        method_id: 1,
        n_obs: n,
        n_vars: p,
        standardized: standardize,
        diagnostics: diag
    }

    // Asymptotic variance of first eigenvalue (Girshick 1939):
    // Var(λ̂₁) ≈ 2λ₁² / n  — exact under multivariate normality
    // Reference: Anderson (2003) "An Introduction to Multivariate Statistical Analysis", p.477
    let lambda1 = result.eigenvalues[0]
    let eigenvalue_variance = if n > 0 { 2.0 * lambda1 * lambda1 / (n as f64) } else { 0.0 }

    KnowledgePCA {
        value: result,
        variance: eigenvalue_variance,
        confidence: sample_beta,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_pca_basic() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // 2 variables, 5 observations (correlated)
    var data: [[f64; 10]; 100] = [[0.0; 10]; 100]
    data[0][0] = 1.0; data[0][1] = 2.0
    data[1][0] = 2.0; data[1][1] = 4.0
    data[2][0] = 3.0; data[2][1] = 5.0
    data[3][0] = 4.0; data[3][1] = 7.0
    data[4][0] = 5.0; data[4][1] = 8.0

    let result = fit_pca_epistemic(data, 5, 2, 1)

    // First component should explain most variance (highly correlated)
    let pc1_ok = result.value.variance_explained[0] > 0.80

    // Two eigenvalues (2 variables)
    let ev_ok = result.value.eigenvalues[0] > result.value.eigenvalues[1]

    pc1_ok && ev_ok
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/nlme.sio ===
// stats::nlme — Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Population Pharmacokinetics
//
// NONMEM/Monolix-class population PK estimation via FOCE (First-Order
// Conditional Estimation).  Estimates fixed effects (theta), random effect
// variance-covariance (omega), and residual error variance (sigma)
// simultaneously from pooled multi-individual concentration-time data.
//
// Algorithm:
//   Outer loop — coordinate descent on theta + closed-form omega/sigma updates
//   Inner loop — Newton optimization of individual eta_i (MAP estimate)
//   Objective   — -2 * log-likelihood (Laplacian approximation)
//
// References:
//   Beal & Sheiner 1982: NONMEM technical report
//   Lindstrom & Bates 1990: FOCE for NLME
//   Lavielle 2014: Mixed Effects Models for the Population Approach (SAEM)
//   Plan et al. 2012: Visual Predictive Check (VPC) methodology
//
// SOTA context: Pumas.jl (Julia), nlmixr2 (R), Monolix (Lixoft), NONMEM 7.5

extern "C" {
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64
}

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS (self-contained, no stdlib dependency)
// ============================================================================

fn nlme_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn nlme_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn nlme_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

fn nlme_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

fn nlme_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    return exp(x)
}

fn nlme_log(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    return log(x)
}

// ============================================================================
// CORE DATA STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

// Per-individual observations: max 32 individuals, 64 observations each
// Layout: times[ind * 64 + obs], observations[ind * 64 + obs]
struct NLMEData {
    times: [f64; 2048],
    observations: [f64; 2048],
    n_obs: [i64; 32],
    doses: [f64; 32],
    n_individuals: i64
}

// Population PK parameters
//   theta: fixed effects (population means), e.g. theta[0]=CL, theta[1]=V, ...
//   omega: variance-covariance matrix of random effects (n_eta x n_eta, row-major 16x16)
//   sigma: proportional + additive residual error variance
struct NLMEParams {
    theta: [f64; 16],
    omega: [f64; 256],
    sigma: f64,
    n_theta: i64,
    n_eta: i64
}

// Estimation result
struct NLMEResult {
    theta: [f64; 16],
    omega: [f64; 256],
    sigma: f64,
    obj_function: f64,
    n_iterations: i64,
    converged: i64,
    eta: [f64; 512],
    ipred: [f64; 2048]
}

// Workspace arrays wrapped in structs for &! mutation (JIT workaround)
struct EtaVec { data: [f64; 16] }
struct ParamVec { data: [f64; 16] }
struct GradVec { data: [f64; 16] }
struct HessMat { data: [f64; 256] }
struct PredVec { data: [f64; 64] }
struct ResidVec { data: [f64; 64] }
struct EtaAllBuf { data: [f64; 512] }
struct SimConcBuf { data: [f64; 4096] }
struct SortBuf { data: [f64; 128] }
struct SeedBox { val: i64 }

// VPC output: percentile bands at time grid points (max 128 time points)
struct VPCResult {
    times: [f64; 128],
    p5: [f64; 128],
    p50: [f64; 128],
    p95: [f64; 128],
    n_time_points: i64
}

// ============================================================================
// INDIVIDUAL PARAMETER COMPUTATION
// ============================================================================

// Exponential random-effects model:
//   param_i = theta_i * exp(eta_i)  for i in 0..n_eta
//   param_i = theta_i               for i >= n_eta (no random effect)
//
// This is the standard NONMEM parameterization for log-normally distributed
// PK parameters (CL, V, ka are always positive).
fn compute_individual_params(
    theta: &ParamVec,
    eta: &EtaVec,
    n_theta: i64,
    n_eta: i64,
    out: &!ParamVec
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_theta {
        if i < n_eta {
            out.data[i] = theta.data[i] * nlme_exp(eta.data[i])
        } else {
            out.data[i] = theta.data[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// INDIVIDUAL PREDICTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Compute predicted concentrations for one individual given their parameters.
//
// pk_model: fn(time, params_array_ref, n_params) -> predicted_concentration
//           The user's structural PK model function.
fn compute_individual_predictions(
    pk_model: fn(f64, &ParamVec, i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic,
    ind_params: &ParamVec,
    n_params: i64,
    data: &NLMEData,
    ind_idx: i64,
    pred: &!PredVec
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let base = ind_idx * 64
    let n = data.n_obs[ind_idx]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n {
        let t = data.times[base + j]
        pred.data[j] = pk_model(t, ind_params, n_params)
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// OBJECTIVE FUNCTION COMPONENTS
// ============================================================================

// Individual contribution to -2LL under FOCE (Laplacian approximation):
//
//   -2LL_i = n_i * ln(2*pi*sigma)
//          + (1/sigma) * sum_j (y_ij - f_ij)^2
//          + eta_i' * Omega^{-1} * eta_i
//          + ln(det(Omega))
//
// For diagonal Omega (independent random effects):
//   eta_i' * Omega^{-1} * eta_i = sum_k (eta_k^2 / omega_kk)
//   ln(det(Omega)) = sum_k ln(omega_kk)

fn individual_obj_function(
    pk_model: fn(f64, &ParamVec, i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic,
    data: &NLMEData,
    ind_idx: i64,
    theta: &ParamVec,
    eta: &EtaVec,
    params: &NLMEParams
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n_theta = params.n_theta
    let n_eta = params.n_eta
    let sigma = params.sigma

    // Compute individual parameters: theta * exp(eta)
    var ind_params: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
    compute_individual_params(theta, eta, n_theta, n_eta, &!ind_params)

    // Compute predictions
    var pred: PredVec = PredVec { data: [0.0; 64] }
    compute_individual_predictions(pk_model, &ind_params, n_theta, data, ind_idx, &!pred)

    // Residual sum of squares
    let base = ind_idx * 64
    let n_obs = data.n_obs[ind_idx]
    var rss: f64 = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n_obs {
        let resid = data.observations[base + j] - pred.data[j]
        rss = rss + resid * resid
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Normal log-likelihood for observations: n*ln(2*pi*sigma) + RSS/sigma
    let pi_val: f64 = 3.141592653589793
    var obj: f64 = (n_obs as f64) * nlme_log(2.0 * pi_val * sigma) + rss / sigma

    // Prior on eta: eta' * Omega^{-1} * eta + ln(det(Omega))
    // Diagonal case: sum_k [eta_k^2/omega_kk + ln(omega_kk)]
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n_eta {
        let omega_kk = params.omega[k * 16 + k]
        if omega_kk > 1.0e-30 {
            obj = obj + eta.data[k] * eta.data[k] / omega_kk + nlme_log(omega_kk)
        }
        k = k + 1
    }

    return obj
}

// ============================================================================
// FOCE INNER OPTIMIZATION — Individual Eta Estimation
// ============================================================================

// Newton-Raphson optimization of eta_i for individual i, holding theta/omega
// fixed. Minimizes the individual contribution to -2LL w.r.t. eta.
//
// Gradient (diagonal Omega):
//   d(-2LL_i)/d(eta_k) = -(2/sigma) * sum_j (y_ij - f_ij) * df_ij/d(eta_k)
//                       + 2 * eta_k / omega_kk
//
// where df_ij/d(eta_k) is computed by finite differences on the PK model.
//
// Hessian approximation (Gauss-Newton):
//   H_kl ~= (2/sigma) * sum_j (df/d(eta_k)) * (df/d(eta_l)) + diag(2/omega_kk)
//
// Newton step: eta_new = eta_old - H^{-1} * grad

fn optimize_eta_newton(
    pk_model: fn(f64, &ParamVec, i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic,
    data: &NLMEData,
    ind_idx: i64,
    theta: &ParamVec,
    params: &NLMEParams,
    eta_out: &!EtaVec,
    max_inner_iter: i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n_eta = params.n_eta
    let n_theta = params.n_theta
    let sigma = params.sigma
    let base = ind_idx * 64
    let n_obs = data.n_obs[ind_idx]

    // Initialize eta to zero (population mean)
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 16 { eta_out.data[k] = 0.0; k = k + 1 }

    var iter: i64 = 0
    while iter < max_inner_iter {
        // Current individual parameters
        var ind_params: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
        compute_individual_params(theta, eta_out, n_theta, n_eta, &!ind_params)

        // Predictions at current eta
        var pred: PredVec = PredVec { data: [0.0; 64] }
        compute_individual_predictions(pk_model, &ind_params, n_theta, data, ind_idx, &!pred)

        // Residuals
        var resid: ResidVec = ResidVec { data: [0.0; 64] }
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n_obs {
            resid.data[j] = data.observations[base + j] - pred.data[j]
            j = j + 1
        }

        // Compute gradient and Gauss-Newton Hessian by finite differences
        var grad: GradVec = GradVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
        var hess: HessMat = HessMat { data: [0.0; 256] }
        let fd_eps: f64 = 1.0e-5

        // Sensitivity: df/d(eta_k) for each eta dimension
        // Store sensitivities: sens[k * 64 + j] = df_j / d(eta_k)
        var sens: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]

        k = 0
        while k < n_eta {
            // Perturbed eta
            var eta_pert: EtaVec = EtaVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
            var m: i64 = 0
            while m < n_eta { eta_pert.data[m] = eta_out.data[m]; m = m + 1 }
            eta_pert.data[k] = eta_pert.data[k] + fd_eps

            var ip_pert: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
            compute_individual_params(theta, &eta_pert, n_theta, n_eta, &!ip_pert)

            var pred_pert: PredVec = PredVec { data: [0.0; 64] }
            compute_individual_predictions(pk_model, &ip_pert, n_theta, data, ind_idx, &!pred_pert)

            j = 0
            while j < n_obs {
                sens[k * 64 + j] = (pred_pert.data[j] - pred.data[j]) / fd_eps
                j = j + 1
            }
            k = k + 1
        }

        // Gradient: -(2/sigma)*sum_j resid_j * sens_kj + 2*eta_k/omega_kk
        k = 0
        while k < n_eta {
            var g: f64 = 0.0
            j = 0
            while j < n_obs {
                g = g - 2.0 / sigma * resid.data[j] * sens[k * 64 + j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            let omega_kk = params.omega[k * 16 + k]
            if omega_kk > 1.0e-30 {
                g = g + 2.0 * eta_out.data[k] / omega_kk
            }
            grad.data[k] = g
            k = k + 1
        }

        // Hessian (Gauss-Newton approximation):
        //   H_kl = (2/sigma)*sum_j sens_kj*sens_lj + delta_kl * 2/omega_kk
        k = 0
        while k < n_eta {
            var l: i64 = 0
            while l < n_eta {
                var h: f64 = 0.0
                j = 0
                while j < n_obs {
                    h = h + 2.0 / sigma * sens[k * 64 + j] * sens[l * 64 + j]
                    j = j + 1
                }
                if k == l {
                    let omega_kk = params.omega[k * 16 + k]
                    if omega_kk > 1.0e-30 {
                        h = h + 2.0 / omega_kk
                    }
                }
                hess.data[k * 16 + l] = h
                l = l + 1
            }
            k = k + 1
        }

        // Solve H * delta_eta = -grad  (small system, direct for n_eta <= 4)
        // Diagonal-dominant simplification for robustness:
        //   delta_eta_k = -grad_k / H_kk
        var max_step: f64 = 0.0
        k = 0
        while k < n_eta {
            let h_kk = hess.data[k * 16 + k]
            var delta: f64 = 0.0
            if nlme_abs(h_kk) > 1.0e-30 {
                delta = 0.0 - grad.data[k] / h_kk
            }
            // Damping: limit step size to avoid divergence
            if delta > 2.0 { delta = 2.0 }
            if delta < -2.0 { delta = -2.0 }
            eta_out.data[k] = eta_out.data[k] + delta
            let abs_delta = nlme_abs(delta)
            if abs_delta > max_step { max_step = abs_delta }
            k = k + 1
        }

        // Convergence check
        if max_step < 1.0e-6 {
            iter = max_inner_iter
        } else {
            iter = iter + 1
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TOTAL OBJECTIVE FUNCTION (-2LL)
// ============================================================================

// Sum individual contributions for all individuals in the dataset
fn total_objective_function(
    pk_model: fn(f64, &ParamVec, i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic,
    data: &NLMEData,
    params: &NLMEParams,
    eta_buf: &EtaAllBuf
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var total: f64 = 0.0
    var theta: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < params.n_theta { theta.data[k] = params.theta[k]; k = k + 1 }

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < data.n_individuals {
        // Extract eta for this individual
        var eta_i: EtaVec = EtaVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
        k = 0
        while k < params.n_eta {
            eta_i.data[k] = eta_buf.data[i * 16 + k]
            k = k + 1
        }

        let obj_i = individual_obj_function(pk_model, data, i, &theta, &eta_i, params)
        total = total + obj_i
        i = i + 1
    }
    return total
}

// ============================================================================
// FOCE ESTIMATION — Full Algorithm
// ============================================================================

// Main FOCE fit:
//   1. Initialize theta, omega, sigma from user-provided starting values
//   2. E-step: for each individual, find MAP eta_i via Newton (inner loop)
//   3. M-step: compute total -2LL; perturb theta/omega/sigma and take
//      steepest-descent step (outer loop)
//   4. Repeat until convergence or max_iter
//
// This is a simplified but functional FOCE. Production systems (NONMEM,
// Monolix) use SAEM or full FOCE-I with exact gradient; this implementation
// uses a coordinate-descent outer loop which is robust for 2-6 parameter
// models typical in clinical pharmacometrics.

fn nlme_fit_foce(
    data: &NLMEData,
    params_init: &NLMEParams,
    pk_model: fn(f64, &ParamVec, i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic,
    max_iter: i64
) -> NLMEResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Initialize result
    var result: NLMEResult = NLMEResult {
        theta: [0.0; 16],
        omega: [0.0; 256],
        sigma: 0.0,
        obj_function: 1.0e30,
        n_iterations: 0,
        converged: 0,
        eta: [0.0; 512],
        ipred: [0.0; 2048]
    }

    // Working copy of parameters
    var params: NLMEParams = NLMEParams {
        theta: [0.0; 16],
        omega: [0.0; 256],
        sigma: params_init.sigma,
        n_theta: params_init.n_theta,
        n_eta: params_init.n_eta
    }
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 16 { params.theta[k] = params_init.theta[k]; k = k + 1 }
    k = 0
    while k < 256 { params.omega[k] = params_init.omega[k]; k = k + 1 }

    // Working eta buffer
    var eta_buf: EtaAllBuf = EtaAllBuf { data: [0.0; 512] }

    var outer_iter: i64 = 0
    var prev_obj: f64 = 1.0e30
    let outer_step: f64 = 0.05
    let convergence_tol: f64 = 1.0e-4

    while outer_iter < max_iter {
        // ---- E-step: Optimize individual etas ----
        var theta_vec: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
        k = 0
        while k < params.n_theta { theta_vec.data[k] = params.theta[k]; k = k + 1 }

        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < data.n_individuals {
            var eta_i: EtaVec = EtaVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
            // Warm-start from previous iteration
            k = 0
            while k < params.n_eta { eta_i.data[k] = eta_buf.data[i * 16 + k]; k = k + 1 }

            optimize_eta_newton(pk_model, data, i, &theta_vec, &params, &!eta_i, 20)

            // Store optimized eta
            k = 0
            while k < params.n_eta { eta_buf.data[i * 16 + k] = eta_i.data[k]; k = k + 1 }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // ---- Compute current objective ----
        let current_obj = total_objective_function(pk_model, data, &params, &eta_buf)

        // ---- M-step: Coordinate descent on theta ----
        k = 0
        while k < params.n_theta {
            let orig = params.theta[k]
            let step = nlme_max(nlme_abs(orig) * outer_step, 1.0e-6)

            // Try +step
            params.theta[k] = orig + step
            let obj_plus = total_objective_function(pk_model, data, &params, &eta_buf)

            // Try -step
            params.theta[k] = orig - step
            let obj_minus = total_objective_function(pk_model, data, &params, &eta_buf)

            // Pick best direction
            if obj_plus < current_obj && obj_plus <= obj_minus {
                params.theta[k] = orig + step
            } else {
                if obj_minus < current_obj {
                    params.theta[k] = orig - step
                } else {
                    params.theta[k] = orig
                }
            }
            k = k + 1
        }

        // ---- M-step: Update omega from empirical variance of etas ----
        k = 0
        while k < params.n_eta {
            var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0
            i = 0
            while i < data.n_individuals {
                let eta_ik = eta_buf.data[i * 16 + k]
                sum_sq = sum_sq + eta_ik * eta_ik
                i = i + 1
            }
            let new_omega = sum_sq / (data.n_individuals as f64)
            // Floor to prevent collapse
            if new_omega > 1.0e-6 {
                params.omega[k * 16 + k] = new_omega
            } else {
                params.omega[k * 16 + k] = 1.0e-6
            }
            k = k + 1
        }

        // ---- M-step: Update sigma from residuals ----
        var total_rss: f64 = 0.0
        var total_obs: i64 = 0
        i = 0
        while i < data.n_individuals {
            var ind_params: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
            var eta_i: EtaVec = EtaVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
            k = 0
            while k < params.n_eta { eta_i.data[k] = eta_buf.data[i * 16 + k]; k = k + 1 }
            compute_individual_params(&theta_vec, &eta_i, params.n_theta, params.n_eta, &!ind_params)

            var pred: PredVec = PredVec { data: [0.0; 64] }
            compute_individual_predictions(pk_model, &ind_params, params.n_theta, data, i, &!pred)

            let base = i * 64
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < data.n_obs[i] {
                let r = data.observations[base + j] - pred.data[j]
                total_rss = total_rss + r * r
                j = j + 1
            }
            total_obs = total_obs + data.n_obs[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        if total_obs > 0 {
            let new_sigma = total_rss / (total_obs as f64)
            if new_sigma > 1.0e-10 {
                params.sigma = new_sigma
            }
        }

        // ---- Convergence check ----
        let rel_change = nlme_abs(current_obj - prev_obj) / nlme_max(nlme_abs(prev_obj), 1.0)
        if rel_change < convergence_tol && outer_iter > 2 {
            result.converged = 1
            result.obj_function = current_obj
            result.n_iterations = outer_iter + 1
            outer_iter = max_iter
        } else {
            prev_obj = current_obj
            outer_iter = outer_iter + 1
        }
    }

    // ---- Store final results ----
    k = 0
    while k < 16 { result.theta[k] = params.theta[k]; k = k + 1 }
    k = 0
    while k < 256 { result.omega[k] = params.omega[k]; k = k + 1 }
    result.sigma = params.sigma
    if result.converged == 0 {
        result.obj_function = prev_obj
        result.n_iterations = max_iter
    }

    // Store final etas
    k = 0
    while k < 512 { result.eta[k] = eta_buf.data[k]; k = k + 1 }

    // Compute final individual predictions (ipred)
    var theta_final: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
    k = 0
    while k < params.n_theta { theta_final.data[k] = params.theta[k]; k = k + 1 }

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < data.n_individuals {
        var eta_i: EtaVec = EtaVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
        k = 0
        while k < params.n_eta { eta_i.data[k] = eta_buf.data[i * 16 + k]; k = k + 1 }

        var ind_params: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
        compute_individual_params(&theta_final, &eta_i, params.n_theta, params.n_eta, &!ind_params)

        var pred: PredVec = PredVec { data: [0.0; 64] }
        compute_individual_predictions(pk_model, &ind_params, params.n_theta, data, i, &!pred)

        let base = i * 64
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < data.n_obs[i] {
            result.ipred[base + j] = pred.data[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// BUILT-IN PK MODELS
// ============================================================================

// One-compartment model with first-order absorption (oral dosing)
//
// params[0] = ka  (absorption rate constant, 1/h)
// params[1] = CL  (clearance, L/h)
// params[2] = V   (volume of distribution, L)
// params[3] = F   (bioavailability fraction)
// params[4] = dose (mg)
//
// C(t) = (F * dose * ka) / (V * (ka - ke)) * (exp(-ke*t) - exp(-ka*t))
// where ke = CL / V
fn pk_1comp_oral(t: f64, params: &ParamVec, n: i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let ka = params.data[0]
    let cl = params.data[1]
    let v  = params.data[2]
    let f  = params.data[3]
    let dose = params.data[4]

    if v < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
    let ke = cl / v

    // Avoid division by zero when ka == ke
    let diff = nlme_abs(ka - ke)
    if diff < 1.0e-10 {
        // L'Hopital limit: C(t) = (F*dose*ka/V) * t * exp(-ke*t)
        return f * dose * ka / v * t * nlme_exp(0.0 - ke * t)
    }

    let coeff = f * dose * ka / (v * (ka - ke))
    return coeff * (nlme_exp(0.0 - ke * t) - nlme_exp(0.0 - ka * t))
}

// Two-compartment model with IV bolus
//
// params[0] = CL   (clearance, L/h)
// params[1] = V1   (central volume, L)
// params[2] = Q    (inter-compartmental clearance, L/h)
// params[3] = V2   (peripheral volume, L)
// params[4] = dose (mg)
//
// C(t) = A*exp(-alpha*t) + B*exp(-beta*t)
// where alpha, beta are eigenvalues of the disposition matrix
fn pk_2comp_iv(t: f64, params: &ParamVec, n: i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let cl = params.data[0]
    let v1 = params.data[1]
    let q  = params.data[2]
    let v2 = params.data[3]
    let dose = params.data[4]

    if v1 < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
    if v2 < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }

    let k10 = cl / v1
    let k12 = q / v1
    let k21 = q / v2

    // Eigenvalues: alpha, beta from quadratic
    // alpha + beta = k10 + k12 + k21
    // alpha * beta = k10 * k21
    let sum_k = k10 + k12 + k21
    let prod_k = k10 * k21
    let disc = sum_k * sum_k - 4.0 * prod_k
    if disc < 0.0 { return 0.0 }

    let sqrt_disc = nlme_sqrt(disc)
    let alpha = (sum_k + sqrt_disc) / 2.0
    let beta  = (sum_k - sqrt_disc) / 2.0

    // Macro-constants
    let diff_ab = alpha - beta
    if nlme_abs(diff_ab) < 1.0e-30 { return dose / v1 * nlme_exp(0.0 - alpha * t) }

    let a_coeff = dose / v1 * (alpha - k21) / diff_ab
    let b_coeff = dose / v1 * (k21 - beta) / diff_ab

    return a_coeff * nlme_exp(0.0 - alpha * t) + b_coeff * nlme_exp(0.0 - beta * t)
}

// ============================================================================
// VISUAL PREDICTIVE CHECK (VPC)
// ============================================================================

// Simple LCG pseudo-random number generator (period 2^32)
// Returns value in [0, 1)
fn lcg_next(seed: &!SeedBox) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Numerical Recipes LCG: seed = (1664525 * seed + 1013904223) mod 2^32
    let a: i64 = 1664525
    let c: i64 = 1013904223
    let m: i64 = 4294967296
    var s = seed.val
    s = ((a * s + c) % m + m) % m
    seed.val = s
    return (s as f64) / (m as f64)
}

// Box-Muller transform: uniform (0,1) pair -> standard normal
fn box_muller(u1: f64, u2: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let pi_val: f64 = 3.141592653589793
    let r = nlme_sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * nlme_log(nlme_max(u1, 1.0e-30)))
    let angle = 2.0 * pi_val * u2
    // cos(angle) via Taylor series
    var cos_a: f64 = 1.0
    var term: f64 = 1.0
    var n: i64 = 1
    while n < 12 {
        term = 0.0 - term * angle * angle / ((2 * n - 1) * (2 * n)) as f64
        cos_a = cos_a + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    return r * cos_a
}

// Simulate one virtual population and compute concentrations at grid times.
// For each simulated individual:
//   1. Draw eta from N(0, omega)
//   2. Compute individual params
//   3. Evaluate PK model at each time point
//   4. Add residual noise ~ N(0, sigma)
fn vpc_simulate_population(
    pk_model: fn(f64, &ParamVec, i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic,
    theta: &ParamVec,
    params: &NLMEParams,
    dose: f64,
    times: &[f64; 128],
    n_times: i64,
    n_sim_individuals: i64,
    seed: &!SeedBox,
    out_conc: &!SimConcBuf
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // out_conc layout: [ind * 128 + t_idx]
    var ind: i64 = 0
    while ind < n_sim_individuals {
        // Draw random etas
        var eta: EtaVec = EtaVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < params.n_eta {
            let u1 = lcg_next(seed)
            let u2 = lcg_next(seed)
            let z = box_muller(u1, u2)
            let omega_kk = params.omega[k * 16 + k]
            eta.data[k] = z * nlme_sqrt(omega_kk)
            k = k + 1
        }

        // Compute individual params
        var ind_params: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
        compute_individual_params(theta, &eta, params.n_theta, params.n_eta, &!ind_params)

        // Set dose in params if needed (param index 4 by convention)
        if params.n_theta > 4 {
            ind_params.data[4] = dose
        }

        // Evaluate model at each time point
        var t_idx: i64 = 0
        while t_idx < n_times {
            let pred = pk_model(times[t_idx], &ind_params, params.n_theta)
            // Add residual noise
            let u1 = lcg_next(seed)
            let u2 = lcg_next(seed)
            let noise = box_muller(u1, u2) * nlme_sqrt(params.sigma)
            var conc = pred + noise
            if conc < 0.0 { conc = 0.0 }
            out_conc.data[ind * 128 + t_idx] = conc
            t_idx = t_idx + 1
        }
        ind = ind + 1
    }
}

// Sort n values in-place (selection sort for small n)
fn sort_f64(arr: &!SortBuf, n: i64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        var min_idx: i64 = i
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n {
            if arr.data[j] < arr.data[min_idx] { min_idx = j }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if min_idx != i {
            let tmp = arr.data[i]
            arr.data[i] = arr.data[min_idx]
            arr.data[min_idx] = tmp
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Compute VPC: simulate n_sim populations, extract 5th/50th/95th percentiles
//
// n_sim_individuals: individuals per simulated dataset (typically 200-1000)
// time_grid / n_time_points: evaluation time points
fn compute_vpc(
    pk_model: fn(f64, &ParamVec, i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic,
    result: &NLMEResult,
    params: &NLMEParams,
    dose: f64,
    time_grid: &[f64; 128],
    n_time_points: i64,
    n_sim_individuals: i64,
    seed_init: i64
) -> VPCResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var vpc: VPCResult = VPCResult {
        times: [0.0; 128],
        p5: [0.0; 128],
        p50: [0.0; 128],
        p95: [0.0; 128],
        n_time_points: n_time_points
    }

    // Copy time grid
    var t: i64 = 0
    while t < n_time_points { vpc.times[t] = time_grid[t]; t = t + 1 }

    // Theta from result
    var theta: ParamVec = ParamVec { data: [0.0; 16] }
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < params.n_theta { theta.data[k] = result.theta[k]; k = k + 1 }

    // Simulate population
    var seed: SeedBox = SeedBox { val: seed_init }
    var sim_conc: SimConcBuf = SimConcBuf { data: [0.0; 4096] }
    vpc_simulate_population(
        pk_model, &theta, params, dose,
        time_grid, n_time_points, n_sim_individuals,
        &!seed, &!sim_conc
    )

    // Extract percentiles at each time point
    t = 0
    while t < n_time_points {
        // Collect concentrations at this time point
        var vals: SortBuf = SortBuf { data: [0.0; 128] }
        let n_vals_f = nlme_min((n_sim_individuals as f64), 128.0)
        let n_vals = n_vals_f as i64
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n_vals {
            vals.data[i] = sim_conc.data[i * 128 + t]
            i = i + 1
        }
        sort_f64(&!vals, n_vals)

        // Percentile indices
        let idx_5  = ((n_vals as f64) * 0.05) as i64
        let idx_50 = ((n_vals as f64) * 0.50) as i64
        let idx_95 = ((n_vals as f64) * 0.95) as i64

        vpc.p5[t]  = vals.data[idx_5]
        vpc.p50[t] = vals.data[idx_50]
        vpc.p95[t] = vals.data[idx_95]
        t = t + 1
    }

    return vpc
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/regression/linear.sio ===
// stats::regression::linear — Epistemic Linear Regression
//
// Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression with:
// - Knowledge<LinearModel> return type
// - Full diagnostics (VIF, Cook's D, leverage, residual plots)
// - Assumption checks as BetaConfidence
// - GUM-compliant uncertainty propagation
//
// References:
// - Gauss (1809): Method of least squares
// - Cook (1977): Detection of influential observations
// - Belsley et al. (1980): Regression Diagnostics (VIF)
// - Durbin & Watson (1950): Testing for serial correlation

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
}

pub use stats::shared::*
use special::beta::{ibeta}

// ============================================================================
// CORE TYPES
// ============================================================================

/// Linear model coefficients and statistics.
///
/// # Builder Pattern
///
/// ```sio
/// let model = LinearRegression::new()
///     .with_data(&x, &y, n)
///     .fit();
///
/// // Or with method chaining:
/// let prediction = LinearRegression::new()
///     .with_data(&x, &y, n)
///     .fit()
///     .predict(5.0);
/// ```
pub struct LinearModel {
    pub coefficients: [f64; 10],      // β₀, β₁, ..., β_p
    pub std_errors: [f64; 10],         // SE(βⱼ)
    pub t_statistics: [f64; 10],       // t = βⱼ / SE(βⱼ)
    pub p_values: [f64; 10],           // Two-tailed p-values
    pub n_predictors: i64,             // Number of predictors (excluding intercept)
    pub n_obs: i64,                    // Sample size
    pub r_squared: f64,                // R²
    pub adj_r_squared: f64,            // Adjusted R²
    pub f_statistic: f64,              // Overall model F-test
    pub residual_se: f64,              // Residual standard error
    pub residuals: [f64; 100]          // Residuals eᵢ = yᵢ - ŷᵢ
}

// ============================================================================
// LinearRegression Builder
// ============================================================================

/// Builder for linear regression with method chaining.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```sio
/// let model = LinearRegression::builder()
///     .with_x(&x)
///     .with_y(&y)
///     .with_n(10)
///     .fit_simple();
///
/// // Predict new value
/// let y_pred = model.predict(5.0);
/// ```
pub struct LinearRegression {
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    fitted: bool,
    model: LinearModel,
}

impl LinearRegression {
    /// Create a new empty regression builder.
    pub fn builder() -> LinearRegression {
        LinearRegression {
            x: [0.0; 100],
            y: [0.0; 100],
            n: 0,
            fitted: false,
            model: LinearModel {
                coefficients: [0.0; 10],
                std_errors: [0.0; 10],
                t_statistics: [0.0; 10],
                p_values: [0.0; 10],
                n_predictors: 0,
                n_obs: 0,
                r_squared: 0.0,
                adj_r_squared: 0.0,
                f_statistic: 0.0,
                residual_se: 0.0,
                residuals: [0.0; 100],
            },
        }
    }

    /// Alias for builder() for convenience.
    pub fn new() -> LinearRegression {
        LinearRegression::builder()
    }

    /// Set predictor variable X.
    pub fn with_x(self, x: [f64; 100]) -> LinearRegression {
        var result = self
        result.x = x
        result
    }

    /// Set response variable Y.
    pub fn with_y(self, y: [f64; 100]) -> LinearRegression {
        var result = self
        result.y = y
        result
    }

    /// Set number of observations.
    pub fn with_n(self, n: i64) -> LinearRegression {
        var result = self
        result.n = n
        result
    }

    /// Set all data at once.
    pub fn with_data(self, x: [f64; 100], y: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> LinearRegression {
        var result = self
        result.x = x
        result.y = y
        result.n = n
        result
    }

    /// Fit simple linear regression (y = β₀ + β₁x).
    pub fn fit_simple(self) -> LinearModel {
        fit_simple_linear_regression(self.x, self.y, self.n)
    }

    /// Fit epistemic linear regression with full diagnostics.
    pub fn fit_epistemic(self) -> KnowledgeLinearModel {
        fit_linear_regression_epistemic(self.x, self.y, self.n)
    }
}

impl LinearModel {
    /// Predict y for a given x value.
    ///
    /// # Parameters
    /// - `x_val`: Predictor value
    ///
    /// # Return
    /// Predicted y value (ŷ = β₀ + β₁x)
    pub fn predict(&self, x_val: f64) -> f64 {
        self.coefficients[0] + self.coefficients[1] * x_val
    }

    /// Get intercept (β₀).
    pub fn intercept(&self) -> f64 {
        self.coefficients[0]
    }

    /// Get slope (β₁).
    pub fn slope(&self) -> f64 {
        self.coefficients[1]
    }

    /// Get standard error of slope.
    pub fn slope_se(&self) -> f64 {
        self.std_errors[1]
    }

    /// Get R² (coefficient of determination).
    pub fn r2(&self) -> f64 {
        self.r_squared
    }

    /// Get adjusted R².
    pub fn adj_r2(&self) -> f64 {
        self.adj_r_squared
    }

    /// Check if slope is significant at p < 0.05.
    pub fn is_slope_significant(&self) -> bool {
        self.p_values[1] < 0.05
    }

    /// Get confidence interval for slope.
    pub fn slope_ci(&self) -> (f64, f64) {
        // 95% CI: β₁ ± 1.96 * SE(β₁)
        let margin = 1.96 * self.std_errors[1]
        (self.coefficients[1] - margin, self.coefficients[1] + margin)
    }
}

// Regression diagnostics
pub struct ModelDiagnostics {
    pub vif: [f64; 10],
    pub cooks_distance: [f64; 100],
    pub leverage: [f64; 100],
    pub dffits: [f64; 100],
    pub normality_resid: BetaConfidence,
    pub homoscedasticity: BetaConfidence,
    pub no_autocorrelation: BetaConfidence,
    pub no_multicollinearity: BetaConfidence,
    pub influential_points: i64
}

pub struct RegressionAssumptions {
    pub linearity: BetaConfidence,
    pub normality_residuals: BetaConfidence,
    pub homoscedasticity: BetaConfidence,
    pub independence: BetaConfidence,
    pub no_multicollinearity: BetaConfidence
}

pub struct RegressionProvenance {
    pub method_code: i32,  // 0=OLS, 1=WeightedLS, 2=RobustLS
    pub n_obs: i64,
    pub n_predictors: i64,
    pub timestamp: i64,
    pub assumptions: RegressionAssumptions,
    pub diagnostics: ModelDiagnostics
}

pub struct KnowledgeLinearModel {
    pub value: LinearModel,
    pub variance: f64,
    pub confidence: BetaConfidence,
    pub provenance: RegressionProvenance
}

// ============================================================================
// MATRIX OPERATIONS (Simplified)
// ============================================================================

// Compute X'X (2x2 for simple regression: intercept + 1 predictor)
fn xtx_simple(x: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> (f64, f64, f64, f64) {
    var sum_1 = 0.0
    var sum_x = 0.0
    var sum_x2 = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        sum_1 = sum_1 + 1.0
        sum_x = sum_x + xi
        sum_x2 = sum_x2 + xi * xi
        i = i + 1
    }

    // X'X = [[n, Σx], [Σx, Σx²]]
    (sum_1, sum_x, sum_x, sum_x2)
}

// Compute X'y (2x1 for simple regression)
fn xty_simple(x: [f64; 100], y: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> (f64, f64) {
    var sum_y = 0.0
    var sum_xy = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        let yi = y[i as usize]
        sum_y = sum_y + yi
        sum_xy = sum_xy + xi * yi
        i = i + 1
    }

    (sum_y, sum_xy)
}

// Solve 2x2 system: (X'X)β = X'y
fn solve_2x2(a11: f64, a12: f64, a21: f64, a22: f64, b1: f64, b2: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
    let det = a11 * a22 - a12 * a21

    if abs_f64(det) < 1e-10 {
        // Singular matrix
        return (0.0, 0.0)
    }

    let beta0 = (a22 * b1 - a12 * b2) / det
    let beta1 = (a11 * b2 - a21 * b1) / det

    (beta0, beta1)
}

// Compute mean
fn mean(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

// Compute variance
fn variance(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    let m = mean(data, n)
    var sum_sq = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = data[i as usize] - m
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum_sq / ((n - 1) as f64)
}

// ============================================================================
// SIMPLE LINEAR REGRESSION (y = β₀ + β₁x)
// ============================================================================

pub fn fit_simple_linear_regression(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> LinearModel {
    // Compute X'X and X'y
    let (xx_11, xx_12, xx_21, xx_22) = xtx_simple(x, n)
    let (xy_1, xy_2) = xty_simple(x, y, n)

    // Solve for coefficients: β = (X'X)⁻¹ X'y
    let (beta0, beta1) = solve_2x2(xx_11, xx_12, xx_21, xx_22, xy_1, xy_2)

    // Compute fitted values and residuals
    var y_hat: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var residuals: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var rss = 0.0  // Residual sum of squares

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        let yi = y[i as usize]
        let pred = beta0 + beta1 * xi
        y_hat[i as usize] = pred
        residuals[i as usize] = yi - pred
        rss = rss + (yi - pred) * (yi - pred)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Degrees of freedom
    let df_resid = (n - 2) as f64  // n - p - 1 where p=1
    let residual_se = sqrt(rss / df_resid)

    // Total sum of squares
    let y_mean = mean(y, n)
    var tss = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = y[i as usize] - y_mean
        tss = tss + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }

    // R² = 1 - RSS/TSS
    let r_squared = if tss > 1e-10 { 1.0 - rss / tss } else { 0.0 }

    // Adjusted R²
    let n_f = n as f64
    let p = 1.0  // Number of predictors
    let adj_r_squared = 1.0 - (1.0 - r_squared) * (n_f - 1.0) / (n_f - p - 1.0)

    // F-statistic: F = (TSS - RSS) / p / (RSS / df_resid)
    let f_stat = if rss > 1e-10 {
        ((tss - rss) / p) / (rss / df_resid)
    } else {
        0.0
    }

    // Standard errors of coefficients
    // Var(β) = σ² (X'X)⁻¹
    let det = xx_11 * xx_22 - xx_12 * xx_21
    let var_beta0 = if abs_f64(det) > 1e-10 {
        (residual_se * residual_se) * xx_22 / det
    } else {
        0.0
    }
    let var_beta1 = if abs_f64(det) > 1e-10 {
        (residual_se * residual_se) * xx_11 / det
    } else {
        0.0
    }

    let se_beta0 = sqrt(var_beta0)
    let se_beta1 = sqrt(var_beta1)

    // t-statistics
    let t0 = if se_beta0 > 1e-10 { beta0 / se_beta0 } else { 0.0 }
    let t1 = if se_beta1 > 1e-10 { beta1 / se_beta1 } else { 0.0 }

    // p-values (approximation)
    let p0 = t_to_p_approx(t0, df_resid)
    let p1 = t_to_p_approx(t1, df_resid)

    // Construct result
    var coefficients: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    coefficients[0] = beta0
    coefficients[1] = beta1

    var std_errors: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    std_errors[0] = se_beta0
    std_errors[1] = se_beta1

    var t_stats: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    t_stats[0] = t0
    t_stats[1] = t1

    var p_vals: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    p_vals[0] = p0
    p_vals[1] = p1

    LinearModel {
        coefficients: coefficients,
        std_errors: std_errors,
        t_statistics: t_stats,
        p_values: p_vals,
        n_predictors: 1,
        n_obs: n,
        r_squared: r_squared,
        adj_r_squared: adj_r_squared,
        f_statistic: f_stat,
        residual_se: residual_se,
        residuals: residuals
    }
}

// p-value from t-distribution using regularized incomplete beta
// Two-tailed: p = 2 * I_{df/(df+t²)}(df/2, 1/2)
// References: Abramowitz & Stegun §26.7.1; Press et al. §6.4
fn t_to_p_approx(t: f64, df: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if df <= 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    let t2 = t * t
    let x = df / (df + t2)
    let p_one_tail = ibeta(df / 2.0, 0.5, x)
    // two-tailed: 2 * (1 - p_one_tail) but ibeta gives lower tail
    // For t-dist: p_two_tail = ibeta(df/2, 0.5, df/(df+t^2))
    // since p_one_tail here is already P(T >= |t|) = I_x(df/2, 0.5)
    let p = p_one_tail
    if p > 1.0 { return 1.0 }
    if p < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    p
}

// ============================================================================
// DIAGNOSTICS
// ============================================================================

// Compute leverage (hat matrix diagonals)
fn compute_leverage(x: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> [f64; 100] {
    let x_mean = mean(x, n)
    var sxx = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = x[i as usize] - x_mean
        sxx = sxx + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }

    var leverage: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = x[i as usize] - x_mean
        // hᵢᵢ = 1/n + (xᵢ - x̄)² / Σ(xⱼ - x̄)²
        let h = 1.0 / (n as f64) + (diff * diff) / sxx
        leverage[i as usize] = h
        i = i + 1
    }

    leverage
}

// Compute Cook's distance
fn compute_cooks_distance(
    model: &LinearModel,
    leverage: [f64; 100]
) -> [f64; 100] {
    var cooks_d: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    let p = (model.n_predictors + 1) as f64  // Including intercept
    let mse = model.residual_se * model.residual_se

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < model.n_obs {
        let e = model.residuals[i as usize]
        let h = leverage[i as usize]

        // D = (eᵢ² / (p * MSE)) * (hᵢᵢ / (1 - hᵢᵢ)²)
        if abs_f64(1.0 - h) > 1e-10 && mse > 1e-10 {
            let d = (e * e / (p * mse)) * (h / ((1.0 - h) * (1.0 - h)))
            cooks_d[i as usize] = d
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    cooks_d
}

// Compute VIF (for simple regression: VIF = 1 always)
fn compute_vif_simple() -> [f64; 10] {
    var vif: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    vif[0] = 1.0  // Intercept: not applicable
    vif[1] = 1.0  // Single predictor: VIF = 1
    vif
}

// Check normality of residuals
fn check_residual_normality(residuals: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
    // Use Shapiro-Wilk approximation from assumption checks
    // Simplified: check standardized range
    let resid_mean = mean(residuals, n)
    let resid_var = variance(residuals, n)
    let resid_sd = sqrt(resid_var)

    if resid_sd < 1e-10 {
        return beta_new(100.0, 1.0)
    }

    var min_r = residuals[0]
    var max_r = residuals[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        let r = residuals[i as usize]
        if r < min_r { min_r = r }
        if r > max_r { max_r = r }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let range = max_r - min_r
    let expected_range = resid_sd * (2.5 + 0.5 * sqrt(n as f64))
    let ratio = range / expected_range
    let deviation = abs_f64(ratio - 1.0)

    let p_conf = if deviation < 0.15 { 0.90 }
                 else if deviation < 0.30 { 0.70 }
                 else { 0.50 }

    let nf = n as f64
    let n_factor = if nf >= 30.0 { 1.0 } else { sqrt(nf / 30.0) }
    let concentration = nf * 0.5

    beta_new(p_conf * n_factor * concentration, (1.0 - p_conf * n_factor) * concentration)
}

// Check homoscedasticity (Breusch-Pagan approximation)
fn check_homoscedasticity(
    residuals: [f64; 100],
    x: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> BetaConfidence {
    // Simplified: check if |residuals| correlate with x
    // Full BP: regress e² on x

    var abs_resid: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        abs_resid[i as usize] = abs_f64(residuals[i as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute correlation between |e| and x
    let mean_abs_r = mean(abs_resid, n)
    let mean_x = mean(x, n)

    var cov = 0.0
    var var_abs_r = 0.0
    var var_x = 0.0

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let d_abs_r = abs_resid[i as usize] - mean_abs_r
        let d_x = x[i as usize] - mean_x
        cov = cov + d_abs_r * d_x
        var_abs_r = var_abs_r + d_abs_r * d_abs_r
        var_x = var_x + d_x * d_x
        i = i + 1
    }

    let denom = sqrt(var_abs_r * var_x)
    let corr = if denom > 1e-10 { cov / denom } else { 0.0 }

    // High |corr| → heteroscedasticity
    let abs_corr = abs_f64(corr)
    let p_conf = if abs_corr < 0.3 { 0.90 }
                 else if abs_corr < 0.5 { 0.70 }
                 else { 0.50 }

    let nf = n as f64
    beta_new(p_conf * nf * 0.3, (1.0 - p_conf) * nf * 0.3)
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC LINEAR REGRESSION
// ============================================================================

pub fn fit_linear_regression_epistemic(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> KnowledgeLinearModel {
    // Fit classical OLS
    let model = fit_simple_linear_regression(x, y, n)

    // Compute diagnostics
    let leverage = compute_leverage(x, n)
    let cooks_d = compute_cooks_distance(&model, leverage)
    let vif = compute_vif_simple()

    // Assumption checks
    let norm_resid = check_residual_normality(model.residuals, n)
    let homosked = check_homoscedasticity(model.residuals, x, n)

    // Independence: Durbin-Watson approximation
    // DW ≈ 2 → no autocorrelation
    var dw_num = 0.0
    var dw_denom = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        let diff = model.residuals[i as usize] - model.residuals[(i - 1) as usize]
        dw_num = dw_num + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let e = model.residuals[i as usize]
        dw_denom = dw_denom + e * e
        i = i + 1
    }
    let dw = if dw_denom > 1e-10 { dw_num / dw_denom } else { 2.0 }
    let dw_deviation = abs_f64(dw - 2.0)
    let indep_conf = if dw_deviation < 0.5 { 0.90 }
                     else if dw_deviation < 1.0 { 0.70 }
                     else { 0.50 }
    let independence = beta_new(indep_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - indep_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    // Multicollinearity: VIF check (for simple regression: always ok)
    let multicol = beta_new(100.0, 1.0)

    // Count influential points (Cook's D > 1)
    var influential = 0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if cooks_d[i as usize] > 1.0 {
            influential = influential + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let diagnostics = ModelDiagnostics {
        vif: vif,
        cooks_distance: cooks_d,
        leverage: leverage,
        dffits: [0.0; 100],  // Placeholder
        normality_resid: norm_resid,
        homoscedasticity: homosked,
        no_autocorrelation: independence,
        no_multicollinearity: multicol,
        influential_points: influential
    }

    let assumptions = RegressionAssumptions {
        linearity: beta_new(50.0, 10.0),  // Placeholder: would check residual patterns
        normality_residuals: norm_resid,
        homoscedasticity: homosked,
        independence: independence,
        no_multicollinearity: multicol
    }

    // Combine confidences
    let conf1 = beta_combine(&norm_resid, &homosked)
    let conf2 = beta_combine(&conf1, &independence)
    let overall_conf = conf2

    // Variance on coefficient estimates (already in model.std_errors)
    let coef_variance = model.std_errors[1] * model.std_errors[1]

    let prov = RegressionProvenance {
        method_code: 0,
        n_obs: n,
        n_predictors: 1,
        timestamp: 0,
        assumptions: assumptions,
        diagnostics: diagnostics
    }

    KnowledgeLinearModel {
        value: model,
        variance: coef_variance,
        confidence: overall_conf,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_simple_regression() -> bool {
    // y = 2 + 3x with small noise
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 10 {
        x[i as usize] = i as f64
        y[i as usize] = 2.0 + 3.0 * (i as f64) + 0.1  // Small noise
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fit_linear_regression_epistemic(x, y, 10)

    // Check β₀ ≈ 2.0, β₁ ≈ 3.0
    let beta0 = result.value.coefficients[0]
    let beta1 = result.value.coefficients[1]

    let beta0_ok = abs_f64(beta0 - 2.0) < 0.5
    let beta1_ok = abs_f64(beta1 - 3.0) < 0.5

    // Check R² is high
    let r2_ok = result.value.r_squared > 0.95

    beta0_ok && beta1_ok && r2_ok
}

// =============================================================================
// Top-level constructor (avoids cross-module static resolution issue)
// =============================================================================

/// Create a new empty LinearRegression builder.
/// Use instead of LinearRegression::new() when calling from other modules.
pub fn linear_regression_new() -> LinearRegression {
    LinearRegression {
        x: [0.0; 100],
        y: [0.0; 100],
        n: 0,
        fitted: false,
        model: LinearModel {
            coefficients: [0.0; 10],
            std_errors: [0.0; 10],
            t_statistics: [0.0; 10],
            p_values: [0.0; 10],
            n_predictors: 0,
            n_obs: 0,
            r_squared: 0.0,
            adj_r_squared: 0.0,
            f_statistic: 0.0,
            residual_se: 0.0,
            residuals: [0.0; 100],
        },
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/regression/logistic.sio ===
// stats::regression::logistic — Epistemic Logistic Regression
//
// Generalized linear model for binary outcomes with:
// - Maximum likelihood estimation via IRLS
// - Odds ratios as Knowledge<f64> with confidence
// - Dose-response modeling (ED50, ED90)
// - ROC/AUC curve analysis
// - Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit
//
// Returns Knowledge<LogisticModel> with full diagnostics
//
// References:
// - Cox (1958): "The regression analysis of binary sequences"
// - Hosmer & Lemeshow (2000): "Applied Logistic Regression"
// - McCullagh & Nelder (1989): "Generalized Linear Models"

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers (self-contained, following medical/ pattern)
// =============================================================================

struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

fn logit_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn logit_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn logit_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64
        k = k + 1
    }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn logit_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = x / ln2
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    } else {
        var i = 0
        while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    }
    result
}

fn logit_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn logit_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// =============================================================================
// Link Functions
// =============================================================================

// Logistic (sigmoid) function: p = 1 / (1 + exp(-z))
fn sigmoid(z: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if z > 20.0 { return 1.0 - 1.0e-10 }
    if z < -20.0 { return 1.0e-10 }
    1.0 / (1.0 + logit_exp(0.0 - z))
}

// Logit (inverse sigmoid): z = ln(p / (1 - p))
fn logit(p: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let clipped = logit_max(1.0e-10, logit_min(1.0 - 1.0e-10, p))
    logit_ln(clipped / (1.0 - clipped))
}

// =============================================================================
// Core Types
// =============================================================================

struct LogisticModel {
    beta: [f64; 10],          // Coefficients (β₀ = intercept)
    se: [f64; 10],            // Standard errors
    z_scores: [f64; 10],       // Wald z-scores (β/SE)
    p_values: [f64; 10],       // Two-tailed p-values
    odds_ratios: [f64; 10],    // exp(β) for each predictor
    or_ci_lower: [f64; 10],    // 95% CI lower for OR
    or_ci_upper: [f64; 10],    // 95% CI upper for OR
    n_predictors: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    n_events: i64,             // Number of y=1
    log_likelihood: f64,
    aic: f64,
    bic: f64,
    deviance: f64,
    null_deviance: f64,
    pseudo_r_squared: f64,     // McFadden's R²
    converged: bool,
    iterations: i64
}



// Diagnostics
struct LogisticDiagnostics {
    hosmer_lemeshow_stat: f64,  // Goodness-of-fit
    hosmer_lemeshow_p: f64,
    auc: f64,                    // Area under ROC curve
    concordance: f64,            // C-statistic
    separation_adequate: BetaConfidence,
    sample_events_adequate: BetaConfidence
}

// Provenance
struct LogisticProvenance {
    method_id: i64,  // 1 = IRLS_MLE
    n_obs: i64,
    n_events: i64,
    n_predictors: i64,
    iterations: i64,
    converged: bool,
    diagnostics: LogisticDiagnostics
}

// Knowledge wrapper
struct KnowledgeLogistic {
    value: LogisticModel,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: LogisticProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// Dose-Response Types
// =============================================================================

struct DoseResponseResult {
    ed50: f64,        // Dose producing 50% effect
    ed90: f64,        // Dose producing 90% effect
    ed50_ci_lower: f64,
    ed50_ci_upper: f64,
    slope: f64,        // Hill slope at ED50
    max_effect: f64
}

struct KnowledgeDoseResponse {
    value: DoseResponseResult,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence
}

// =============================================================================
// Simple Linear Regression (used internally)
// =============================================================================

fn mean_arr(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n { sum = sum + data[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// IRLS (Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares)
// =============================================================================

// Simple logistic regression: logit(p) = β₀ + β₁x
fn fit_logistic_simple(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],   // Binary: 0 or 1
    n: i64
) -> LogisticModel with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let max_iter = 25
    let tol = 1.0e-8

    // Count events
    var n_events: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if y[i as usize] > 0.5 { n_events = n_events + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Initialize β₀ = logit(p_bar), β₁ = 0
    let p_bar = (n_events as f64) / (n as f64)
    var beta0 = logit(p_bar)
    var beta1 = 0.0

    // Null log-likelihood (for pseudo-R²)
    var null_ll = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let yi = y[i as usize]
        if yi > 0.5 {
            null_ll = null_ll + logit_ln(p_bar)
        } else {
            null_ll = null_ll + logit_ln(1.0 - p_bar)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // IRLS iterations
    var converged = false
    var iter: i64 = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        // E-step: compute predicted probabilities
        var sum_w = 0.0
        var sum_wx = 0.0
        var sum_wxx = 0.0
        var sum_wz = 0.0
        var sum_wxz = 0.0

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            let xi = x[i as usize]
            let yi = y[i as usize]

            // Linear predictor
            let eta = beta0 + beta1 * xi

            // Predicted probability
            let pi = sigmoid(eta)

            // Weight: w = p(1-p)
            let w = pi * (1.0 - pi)
            if w < 1.0e-10 { i = i + 1; continue }

            // Working response: z = eta + (y - p) / w_raw
            let z = eta + (yi - pi) / w

            // Accumulate weighted normal equations
            sum_w = sum_w + w
            sum_wx = sum_wx + w * xi
            sum_wxx = sum_wxx + w * xi * xi
            sum_wz = sum_wz + w * z
            sum_wxz = sum_wxz + w * xi * z

            i = i + 1
        }

        // Solve 2x2 weighted normal equations
        let det = sum_w * sum_wxx - sum_wx * sum_wx
        if logit_abs(det) < 1.0e-10 { break }

        let new_beta0 = (sum_wxx * sum_wz - sum_wx * sum_wxz) / det
        let new_beta1 = (sum_w * sum_wxz - sum_wx * sum_wz) / det

        // Check convergence
        let delta0 = logit_abs(new_beta0 - beta0)
        let delta1 = logit_abs(new_beta1 - beta1)

        beta0 = new_beta0
        beta1 = new_beta1

        if delta0 < tol && delta1 < tol {
            converged = true
            break
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Compute final statistics
    var log_lik = 0.0
    var deviance = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        let yi = y[i as usize]
        let eta = beta0 + beta1 * xi
        let pi = sigmoid(eta)

        // Log-likelihood: Σ[y·ln(p) + (1-y)·ln(1-p)]
        if yi > 0.5 {
            log_lik = log_lik + logit_ln(logit_max(pi, 1.0e-10))
        } else {
            log_lik = log_lik + logit_ln(logit_max(1.0 - pi, 1.0e-10))
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    deviance = -2.0 * log_lik
    let null_deviance = -2.0 * null_ll

    // AIC = -2LL + 2k, BIC = -2LL + k·ln(n)
    let k = 2.0  // Number of parameters
    let aic = deviance + 2.0 * k
    let bic = deviance + k * logit_ln(n as f64)

    // McFadden's pseudo-R²
    let pseudo_r2 = 1.0 - log_lik / null_ll

    // Standard errors from Fisher Information (last IRLS weights)
    var sum_w = 0.0
    var sum_wx = 0.0
    var sum_wxx = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        let eta = beta0 + beta1 * xi
        let pi = sigmoid(eta)
        let w = pi * (1.0 - pi)
        sum_w = sum_w + w
        sum_wx = sum_wx + w * xi
        sum_wxx = sum_wxx + w * xi * xi
        i = i + 1
    }

    let det = sum_w * sum_wxx - sum_wx * sum_wx
    let se_beta0 = if logit_abs(det) > 1.0e-10 {
        logit_sqrt(sum_wxx / det)
    } else { 0.0 }
    let se_beta1 = if logit_abs(det) > 1.0e-10 {
        logit_sqrt(sum_w / det)
    } else { 0.0 }

    // Wald z-scores
    let z0 = if se_beta0 > 1.0e-10 { beta0 / se_beta0 } else { 0.0 }
    let z1 = if se_beta1 > 1.0e-10 { beta1 / se_beta1 } else { 0.0 }

    // Approximate p-values (normal)
    let p0 = 2.0 * (1.0 - sigmoid(logit_abs(z0)))
    let p1 = 2.0 * (1.0 - sigmoid(logit_abs(z1)))

    // Odds ratios: exp(β)
    let or0 = logit_exp(beta0)
    let or1 = logit_exp(beta1)

    // 95% CI for OR: exp(β ± 1.96·SE)
    let or1_lower = logit_exp(beta1 - 1.96 * se_beta1)
    let or1_upper = logit_exp(beta1 + 1.96 * se_beta1)

    // Construct result
    var betas: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    betas[0] = beta0
    betas[1] = beta1

    var ses: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    ses[0] = se_beta0
    ses[1] = se_beta1

    var zs: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    zs[0] = z0
    zs[1] = z1

    var ps: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    ps[0] = p0
    ps[1] = p1

    var ors: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    ors[0] = or0
    ors[1] = or1

    var or_lo: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    or_lo[1] = or1_lower

    var or_hi: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    or_hi[1] = or1_upper

    LogisticModel {
        beta: betas,
        se: ses,
        z_scores: zs,
        p_values: ps,
        odds_ratios: ors,
        or_ci_lower: or_lo,
        or_ci_upper: or_hi,
        n_predictors: 1,
        n_obs: n,
        n_events: n_events,
        log_likelihood: log_lik,
        aic: aic,
        bic: bic,
        deviance: deviance,
        null_deviance: null_deviance,
        pseudo_r_squared: pseudo_r2,
        converged: converged,
        iterations: iter
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// ROC / AUC
// =============================================================================

fn compute_auc(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    beta0: f64,
    beta1: f64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Compute AUC via Mann-Whitney U statistic
    // AUC = P(score(positive) > score(negative))

    // Compute predicted probabilities
    var probs: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        probs[i as usize] = sigmoid(beta0 + beta1 * x[i as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Count concordant pairs
    var concordant: i64 = 0
    var discordant: i64 = 0
    var tied: i64 = 0

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if y[i as usize] < 0.5 { i = i + 1; continue }  // Only positive cases

        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            if y[j as usize] > 0.5 { j = j + 1; continue }  // Only negative cases

            let pi = probs[i as usize]
            let pj = probs[j as usize]

            if pi > pj { concordant = concordant + 1 }
            else if pi < pj { discordant = discordant + 1 }
            else { tied = tied + 1 }

            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let total = concordant + discordant + tied
    if total == 0 { return 0.5 }

    (concordant as f64 + 0.5 * (tied as f64)) / (total as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// Epistemic Logistic Regression
// =============================================================================

fn fit_logistic_epistemic(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> KnowledgeLogistic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let model = fit_logistic_simple(x, y, n)

    // AUC
    let auc = compute_auc(x, y, n, model.beta[0], model.beta[1])

    // Assumption checks
    // 1. Sufficient events (rule of thumb: 10 events per predictor)
    let events_per_pred = model.n_events / (model.n_predictors + 1)
    let event_conf = if events_per_pred >= 10 { 0.95 }
                     else if events_per_pred >= 5 { 0.75 }
                     else { 0.50 }
    let event_beta = beta_new(
        event_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3,
        (1.0 - event_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3
    )

    // 2. Separation (complete separation → infinite β)
    let sep_conf = if model.converged { 0.90 } else { 0.40 }
    let sep_beta = beta_new(
        sep_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3,
        (1.0 - sep_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3
    )

    // Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test
    // Bins observations into 10 equal-width probability groups [0,0.1), [0.1,0.2), ..., [0.9,1.0]
    // HL = Σ_g [(O1g - E1g)² / E1g + (O0g - E0g)² / E0g]
    // Under H₀ (good fit): HL ~ χ²(8)
    // Reference: Hosmer & Lemeshow (2000), "Applied Logistic Regression", Ch. 5
    var hl_stat = 0.0
    var g: i64 = 0
    while g < 10 {
        let lo = (g as f64) * 0.1
        let hi = if g == 9 { 1.0001 } else { lo + 0.1 }
        var obs1 = 0.0   // observed events in bin
        var exp1 = 0.0   // expected events in bin
        var ng = 0.0     // total observations in bin
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            let p_j = 1.0 / (1.0 + logit_exp(0.0 - model.beta[0] - model.beta[1] * x[j as usize]))
            if p_j >= lo && p_j < hi {
                obs1 = obs1 + y[j as usize]
                exp1 = exp1 + p_j
                ng = ng + 1.0
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if ng > 0.0 && exp1 > 1.0e-8 && (ng - exp1) > 1.0e-8 {
            let obs0 = ng - obs1
            let exp0 = ng - exp1
            hl_stat = hl_stat + (obs1 - exp1) * (obs1 - exp1) / exp1
                    + (obs0 - exp0) * (obs0 - exp0) / exp0
        }
        g = g + 1
    }
    // p-value approximation for χ²(8): critical values 15.51 (p=0.05), 20.09 (p=0.01)
    let hl_p = if hl_stat > 20.09 { 0.01 }
               else if hl_stat > 15.51 { 0.05 }
               else if hl_stat > 13.36 { 0.10 }
               else { 0.50 }

    let diag = LogisticDiagnostics {
        hosmer_lemeshow_stat: hl_stat,
        hosmer_lemeshow_p: hl_p,
        auc: auc,
        concordance: auc,  // C-statistic = AUC for binary
        separation_adequate: sep_beta,
        sample_events_adequate: event_beta
    }

    let overall_conf = beta_combine(&event_beta, &sep_beta)

    let prov = LogisticProvenance {
        method_id: 1,
        n_obs: n,
        n_events: model.n_events,
        n_predictors: model.n_predictors,
        iterations: model.iterations,
        converged: model.converged,
        diagnostics: diag
    }

    KnowledgeLogistic {
        value: model,
        variance: model.se[1] * model.se[1],  // Variance of slope
        confidence: overall_conf,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Dose-Response Modeling
// =============================================================================

fn fit_dose_response(
    doses: [f64; 100],
    responses: [f64; 100],  // Binary: 0 or 1
    n: i64
) -> KnowledgeDoseResponse with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Fit logistic model: logit(P(response=1)) = β₀ + β₁·dose
    let model = fit_logistic_simple(doses, responses, n)

    let beta0 = model.beta[0]
    let beta1 = model.beta[1]

    // ED50: dose where P(response) = 0.5
    // logit(0.5) = 0 = β₀ + β₁·ED50
    // ED50 = -β₀/β₁
    let ed50 = if logit_abs(beta1) > 1.0e-10 {
        0.0 - beta0 / beta1
    } else { 0.0 }

    // ED90: dose where P(response) = 0.9
    // logit(0.9) = 2.197 = β₀ + β₁·ED90
    let logit_90 = logit_ln(0.9 / 0.1)
    let ed90 = if logit_abs(beta1) > 1.0e-10 {
        (logit_90 - beta0) / beta1
    } else { 0.0 }

    // CI for ED50 using delta method
    // Var(ED50) ≈ (1/β₁²)[Var(β₀) + ED50²·Var(β₁) + 2·ED50·Cov(β₀,β₁)]
    // Simplified (ignoring covariance):
    let se_beta0 = model.se[0]
    let se_beta1 = model.se[1]
    let var_ed50 = if logit_abs(beta1) > 1.0e-10 {
        (1.0 / (beta1 * beta1)) * (se_beta0 * se_beta0 + ed50 * ed50 * se_beta1 * se_beta1)
    } else { 0.0 }
    let se_ed50 = logit_sqrt(var_ed50)

    let ed50_lower = ed50 - 1.96 * se_ed50
    let ed50_upper = ed50 + 1.96 * se_ed50

    // Hill slope at ED50
    let slope = beta1 * 0.25  // p(1-p) = 0.25 at ED50

    let result = DoseResponseResult {
        ed50: ed50,
        ed90: ed90,
        ed50_ci_lower: ed50_lower,
        ed50_ci_upper: ed50_upper,
        slope: slope,
        max_effect: 1.0
    }

    // Confidence from model fit
    let auc = compute_auc(doses, responses, n, beta0, beta1)
    let conf_level = if auc > 0.80 { 0.90 }
                     else if auc > 0.70 { 0.70 }
                     else { 0.50 }

    KnowledgeDoseResponse {
        value: result,
        variance: var_ed50,
        confidence: beta_new(
            conf_level * (n as f64) * 0.3,
            (1.0 - conf_level) * (n as f64) * 0.3
        )
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_logistic_regression() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Dose-response data: higher dose → more response
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // Low doses: mostly 0
    x[0] = 1.0;  y[0] = 0.0
    x[1] = 2.0;  y[1] = 0.0
    x[2] = 3.0;  y[2] = 0.0
    x[3] = 4.0;  y[3] = 0.0
    // Medium doses: mixed
    x[4] = 5.0;  y[4] = 1.0
    x[5] = 6.0;  y[5] = 0.0
    x[6] = 7.0;  y[6] = 1.0
    // High doses: mostly 1
    x[7] = 8.0;  y[7] = 1.0
    x[8] = 9.0;  y[8] = 1.0
    x[9] = 10.0; y[9] = 1.0

    let result = fit_logistic_epistemic(x, y, 10)

    // β₁ should be positive (higher dose → more response)
    let slope_positive = result.value.beta[1] > 0.0

    // OR > 1 (each unit increase in dose increases odds)
    let or_positive = result.value.odds_ratios[1] > 1.0

    // Model should converge
    let did_converge = result.value.converged

    slope_positive && or_positive && did_converge
}

fn test_dose_response() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var doses: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var responses: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    doses[0] = 1.0;  responses[0] = 0.0
    doses[1] = 2.0;  responses[1] = 0.0
    doses[2] = 3.0;  responses[2] = 0.0
    doses[3] = 4.0;  responses[3] = 0.0
    doses[4] = 5.0;  responses[4] = 1.0
    doses[5] = 6.0;  responses[5] = 0.0
    doses[6] = 7.0;  responses[6] = 1.0
    doses[7] = 8.0;  responses[7] = 1.0
    doses[8] = 9.0;  responses[8] = 1.0
    doses[9] = 10.0; responses[9] = 1.0
