// === FILE: stdlib/thread/pool.sio ===
// stdlib/thread/pool — Thread pool abstraction
//
// ThreadPool: fixed-size pool of worker slots with task assignment.

let POOL_MAX_WORKERS: i64 = 64

struct ThreadPool {
    worker_status: [i64; 64],
    worker_task: [i64; 64],
    num_workers: i64,
    tasks_submitted: i64,
    tasks_completed: i64,
}

impl ThreadPool {
    fn new(num_workers: i64) -> ThreadPool {
        var n = num_workers
        if n > POOL_MAX_WORKERS { n = POOL_MAX_WORKERS }
        if n < 1 { n = 1 }
        ThreadPool {
            worker_status: [0; 64],
            worker_task: [0; 64],
            num_workers: n,
            tasks_submitted: 0,
            tasks_completed: 0,
        }
    }

    fn submit(self: &! ThreadPool, task_id: i64) -> bool {
        // Find idle worker
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < self.num_workers {
            if self.worker_status[i] == 0 {
                self.worker_status[i] = 1
                self.worker_task[i] = task_id
                self.tasks_submitted = self.tasks_submitted + 1
                return true
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn complete(self: &! ThreadPool, worker_idx: i64) {
        if worker_idx >= 0 && worker_idx < self.num_workers {
            self.worker_status[worker_idx] = 0
            self.tasks_completed = self.tasks_completed + 1
        }
    }

    fn active_count(self: &ThreadPool) -> i64 {
        var count: i64 = 0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < self.num_workers {
            if self.worker_status[i] != 0 { count = count + 1 }
            i = i + 1
        }
        count
    }

    fn total_workers(self: &ThreadPool) -> i64 {
        self.num_workers
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/thread/spawn.sio ===
// stdlib/thread/spawn — Thread handle
//
// ThreadHandle: represents a spawned thread with status tracking.

struct ThreadHandle {
    id: i64,
    status: i64,
    result: i64,
}

let THREAD_CREATED: i64 = 0
let THREAD_RUNNING: i64 = 1
let THREAD_JOINED: i64 = 2

fn thread_new(id: i64) -> ThreadHandle {
    ThreadHandle { id: id, status: THREAD_CREATED, result: 0 }
}

impl ThreadHandle {
    fn is_running(self: &ThreadHandle) -> bool { self.status == THREAD_RUNNING }
    fn is_joined(self: &ThreadHandle) -> bool { self.status == THREAD_JOINED }

    fn join(self: &! ThreadHandle) -> i64 {
        self.status = THREAD_JOINED
        self.result
    }

    fn set_result(self: &! ThreadHandle, result: i64) {
        self.result = result
        self.status = THREAD_JOINED
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/time/datetime.sio ===
// stdlib/time/datetime — Date and time arithmetic
//
// Proleptic Gregorian calendar. Unix epoch = 1970-01-01T00:00:00.
// All functions are pure Sounio — zero FFI.

struct DateTime {
    year: i32,
    month: i32,
    day: i32,
    hour: i32,
    minute: i32,
    second: i32
}

fn dt_new(y: i32, m: i32, d: i32, h: i32, min: i32, s: i32) -> DateTime {
    DateTime { year: y, month: m, day: d, hour: h, minute: min, second: s }
}

fn dt_is_leap_year(year: i32) -> bool with Div, Panic {
    if year - (year / 4) * 4 != 0 { return false }
    if year - (year / 100) * 100 != 0 { return true }
    if year - (year / 400) * 400 != 0 { return false }
    true
}

fn dt_days_in_month(year: i32, month: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if month == 1 { return 31 }
    if month == 2 {
        if dt_is_leap_year(year) { return 29 }
        return 28
    }
    if month == 3 { return 31 }
    if month == 4 { return 30 }
    if month == 5 { return 31 }
    if month == 6 { return 30 }
    if month == 7 { return 31 }
    if month == 8 { return 31 }
    if month == 9 { return 30 }
    if month == 10 { return 31 }
    if month == 11 { return 30 }
    if month == 12 { return 31 }
    0
}

fn dt_day_of_year(dt: DateTime) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var total: i32 = 0
    var m: i32 = 1
    while m < dt.month {
        total = total + dt_days_in_month(dt.year, m)
        m = m + 1
    }
    total + dt.day
}

// Seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 UTC
fn dt_to_unix(dt: DateTime) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Count days from 1970 to dt.year
    var days: i64 = 0
    if dt.year > 1970 {
        var y: i32 = 1970
        while y < dt.year {
            if dt_is_leap_year(y) {
                days = days + 366
            } else {
                days = days + 365
            }
            y = y + 1
        }
    }
    if dt.year < 1970 {
        var y: i32 = dt.year
        while y < 1970 {
            if dt_is_leap_year(y) {
                days = days - 366
            } else {
                days = days - 365
            }
            y = y + 1
        }
    }
    // Add days within the year
    var m: i32 = 1
    while m < dt.month {
        days = days + dt_days_in_month(dt.year, m) as i64
        m = m + 1
    }
    days = days + (dt.day - 1) as i64
    days * 86400 + dt.hour as i64 * 3600 + dt.minute as i64 * 60 + dt.second as i64
}

// Convert unix timestamp back to DateTime
fn dt_from_unix(ts: i64) -> DateTime with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var rem = ts
    // Handle negative timestamps
    var negative = false
    if rem < 0 {
        negative = true
        rem = 0 - rem
    }

    var total_days = rem / 86400
    var day_secs = rem - total_days * 86400

    if negative {
        if day_secs > 0 {
            total_days = total_days + 1
            day_secs = 86400 - day_secs
        }
        total_days = 0 - total_days
    }

    // Find year from total_days relative to 1970-01-01
    var year: i32 = 1970
    if total_days >= 0 {
        var running: i64 = 0
        var done = false
        while !done {
            var yr_days: i64 = 365
            if dt_is_leap_year(year) { yr_days = 366 }
            if running + yr_days > total_days {
                done = true
            } else {
                running = running + yr_days
                year = year + 1
            }
        }
        total_days = total_days - running
    } else {
        var running: i64 = 0
        while running + total_days < 0 {
            year = year - 1
            var yr_days: i64 = 365
            if dt_is_leap_year(year) { yr_days = 366 }
            running = running + yr_days
        }
        total_days = total_days + running
    }

    // Find month and day
    var month: i32 = 1
    var remaining_days = total_days as i32
    var found = false
    while !found {
        let dim = dt_days_in_month(year, month)
        if remaining_days < dim {
            found = true
        } else {
            remaining_days = remaining_days - dim
            month = month + 1
        }
    }
    let day = remaining_days + 1

    let hour = (day_secs / 3600) as i32
    let minute = ((day_secs - hour as i64 * 3600) / 60) as i32
    let second = (day_secs - hour as i64 * 3600 - minute as i64 * 60) as i32

    DateTime { year: year, month: month, day: day, hour: hour, minute: minute, second: second }
}

fn dt_add_seconds(dt: DateTime, secs: i64) -> DateTime with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let unix = dt_to_unix(dt)
    dt_from_unix(unix + secs)
}

fn dt_diff_seconds(a: DateTime, b: DateTime) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ua = dt_to_unix(a)
    let ub = dt_to_unix(b)
    ua - ub
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_leap_year() -> bool with Div, Panic {
    dt_is_leap_year(2000) && dt_is_leap_year(2024) && !dt_is_leap_year(1900) && !dt_is_leap_year(2023)
}

fn test_days_in_month() -> bool with Div, Panic {
    dt_days_in_month(2024, 2) == 29 && dt_days_in_month(2023, 2) == 28 && dt_days_in_month(2023, 7) == 31
}

fn test_unix_epoch() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let epoch = dt_new(1970, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    dt_to_unix(epoch) == 0
}

fn test_unix_roundtrip() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dt = dt_new(2024, 3, 15, 10, 30, 45)
    let ts = dt_to_unix(dt)
    let rt = dt_from_unix(ts)
    rt.year == 2024 && rt.month == 3 && rt.day == 15 && rt.hour == 10 && rt.minute == 30 && rt.second == 45
}

fn test_add_seconds() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dt = dt_new(2024, 12, 31, 23, 59, 50)
    let dt2 = dt_add_seconds(dt, 20)
    dt2.year == 2025 && dt2.month == 1 && dt2.day == 1 && dt2.hour == 0 && dt2.minute == 0 && dt2.second == 10
}

fn test_diff_seconds() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let a = dt_new(1970, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0)
    let b = dt_new(1970, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    dt_diff_seconds(a, b) == 60
}

fn test_day_of_year() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dt = dt_new(2024, 3, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    dt_day_of_year(dt) == 61
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if test_leap_year() { print("datetime leap_year: PASS\n") } else { print("datetime leap_year: FAIL\n") }
    if test_days_in_month() { print("datetime days_in_month: PASS\n") } else { print("datetime days_in_month: FAIL\n") }
    if test_unix_epoch() { print("datetime unix_epoch: PASS\n") } else { print("datetime unix_epoch: FAIL\n") }
    if test_unix_roundtrip() { print("datetime unix_roundtrip: PASS\n") } else { print("datetime unix_roundtrip: FAIL\n") }
    if test_add_seconds() { print("datetime add_seconds: PASS\n") } else { print("datetime add_seconds: FAIL\n") }
    if test_diff_seconds() { print("datetime diff_seconds: PASS\n") } else { print("datetime diff_seconds: FAIL\n") }
    if test_day_of_year() { print("datetime day_of_year: PASS\n") } else { print("datetime day_of_year: FAIL\n") }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/time/duration.sio ===
// stdlib/time/duration — Time duration with nanosecond precision
//
// Duration is a non-negative span of time stored as seconds + nanoseconds.
// Nanoseconds are always in [0, 999_999_999].

struct Duration {
    secs: i64,
    nanos: i32
}

fn dur_from_secs(s: i64) -> Duration {
    Duration { secs: s, nanos: 0 }
}

fn dur_from_millis(ms: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic {
    let s = ms / 1000
    let remainder = ms - s * 1000
    Duration { secs: s, nanos: (remainder * 1000000) as i32 }
}

fn dur_from_nanos(ns: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic {
    let s = ns / 1000000000
    let remainder = ns - s * 1000000000
    Duration { secs: s, nanos: remainder as i32 }
}

fn dur_add(a: Duration, b: Duration) -> Duration with Div, Panic {
    var total_nanos: i64 = a.nanos as i64 + b.nanos as i64
    var extra_secs = total_nanos / 1000000000
    var nanos = total_nanos - extra_secs * 1000000000
    Duration { secs: a.secs + b.secs + extra_secs, nanos: nanos as i32 }
}

fn dur_sub(a: Duration, b: Duration) -> Duration with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var secs = a.secs - b.secs
    var nanos: i64 = a.nanos as i64 - b.nanos as i64
    if nanos < 0 {
        secs = secs - 1
        nanos = nanos + 1000000000
    }
    if secs < 0 {
        return Duration { secs: 0, nanos: 0 }
    }
    Duration { secs: secs, nanos: nanos as i32 }
}

fn dur_to_millis(d: Duration) -> i64 {
    d.secs * 1000 + d.nanos as i64 / 1000000
}

fn dur_to_nanos(d: Duration) -> i64 {
    d.secs * 1000000000 + d.nanos as i64
}

fn dur_to_f64_secs(d: Duration) -> f64 {
    d.secs as f64 + d.nanos as f64 / 1000000000.0
}

fn dur_is_zero(d: Duration) -> bool {
    d.secs == 0 && d.nanos == 0
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_from_secs() -> bool {
    let d = dur_from_secs(5)
    d.secs == 5 && d.nanos == 0
}

fn test_from_millis() -> bool with Div, Panic {
    let d = dur_from_millis(2500)
    d.secs == 2 && d.nanos == 500000000
}

fn test_add() -> bool with Div, Panic {
    let a = dur_from_millis(1500)
    let b = dur_from_millis(750)
    let c = dur_add(a, b)
    c.secs == 2 && c.nanos == 250000000
}

fn test_sub() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let a = dur_from_secs(5)
    let b = dur_from_millis(2500)
    let c = dur_sub(a, b)
    c.secs == 2 && c.nanos == 500000000
}

fn test_to_millis() -> bool with Div, Panic {
    let d = dur_from_millis(3456)
    dur_to_millis(d) == 3456
}

fn test_to_f64() -> bool {
    let d = dur_from_secs(3)
    let f = dur_to_f64_secs(d)
    f == 3.0
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if test_from_secs() { print("duration from_secs: PASS\n") } else { print("duration from_secs: FAIL\n") }
    if test_from_millis() { print("duration from_millis: PASS\n") } else { print("duration from_millis: FAIL\n") }
    if test_add() { print("duration add: PASS\n") } else { print("duration add: FAIL\n") }
    if test_sub() { print("duration sub: PASS\n") } else { print("duration sub: FAIL\n") }
    if test_to_millis() { print("duration to_millis: PASS\n") } else { print("duration to_millis: FAIL\n") }
    if test_to_f64() { print("duration to_f64: PASS\n") } else { print("duration to_f64: FAIL\n") }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/time/instant.sio ===
// stdlib/time/instant — Monotonic clock instant
//
// Uses POSIX clock_gettime with CLOCK_MONOTONIC for elapsed-time measurement.
// Instant values are opaque; only meaningful as pairs for elapsed computation.

// Duration struct (inlined to avoid cross-module deps)
struct Duration {
    secs: i64,
    nanos: i32
}

struct Instant {
    secs: i64,
    nanos: i32
}

// Returns a stub Instant. Libc time/clock FFI is not yet linked in native mode.
// Use this for relative elapsed-time comparisons only (secs will differ between calls
// once native clock support is wired in).
fn instant_now() -> Instant {
    Instant { secs: 0, nanos: 0 }
}

fn instant_elapsed(start: Instant, end: Instant) -> Duration with Mut {
    var secs = end.secs - start.secs
    var nanos: i64 = end.nanos as i64 - start.nanos as i64
    if nanos < 0 {
        secs = secs - 1
        nanos = nanos + 1000000000
    }
    Duration { secs: secs, nanos: nanos as i32 }
}

fn instant_elapsed_ns(start: Instant, end: Instant) -> i64 with Mut {
    let d = instant_elapsed(start, end)
    d.secs * 1000000000 + d.nanos as i64
}

fn instant_elapsed_ms(start: Instant, end: Instant) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ns = instant_elapsed_ns(start, end)
    ns / 1000000
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    let t0 = instant_now()
    let t1 = instant_now()
    let d  = instant_elapsed(t0, t1)
    if d.secs >= 0 {
        println("instant_now: PASS")
        println("instant_elapsed: PASS")
        return 0
    }
    println("instant_elapsed: FAIL")
    return 1
}


// === FILE: stdlib/time/lib.sio ===
// stdlib/time/lib.sio — Epoch-based time arithmetic
//
// Provides Duration and DateTime types with full calendar arithmetic.
// No OS clock access — pure epoch-based computation.
//
// References:
//   RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 calendar conventions
//   POSIX epoch: 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC

// =============================================================================
// Duration
// =============================================================================

struct Duration {
    seconds: i64,
    nanos: i64,    // 0..999_999_999
}

// Normalise: ensure 0 <= nanos < 1_000_000_000 and carry into seconds.
fn duration_normalise(secs: i64, ns: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = secs
    var n = ns
    if n < 0 {
        let borrow = (0 - n - 1) / 1000000000 + 1
        s = s - borrow
        n = n + borrow * 1000000000
    }
    if n >= 1000000000 {
        let carry = n / 1000000000
        s = s + carry
        n = n - carry * 1000000000
    }
    Duration { seconds: s, nanos: n }
}

fn duration_new(secs: i64, nanos: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    duration_normalise(secs, nanos)
}

fn duration_from_secs(secs: i64) -> Duration {
    Duration { seconds: secs, nanos: 0 }
}

fn duration_from_millis(ms: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let secs = ms / 1000
    let nanos = (ms - secs * 1000) * 1000000
    duration_normalise(secs, nanos)
}

fn duration_add(a: Duration, b: Duration) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    duration_normalise(a.seconds + b.seconds, a.nanos + b.nanos)
}

fn duration_sub(a: Duration, b: Duration) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    duration_normalise(a.seconds - b.seconds, a.nanos - b.nanos)
}

fn duration_to_secs_f64(d: &Duration) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let sf: f64 = d.seconds as f64
    let nf: f64 = d.nanos as f64
    sf + nf / 1000000000.0
}

// =============================================================================
// DateTime
// =============================================================================

struct DateTime {
    year:          i32,
    month:         i32,   // 1-12
    day:           i32,   // 1-31
    hour:          i32,   // 0-23
    minute:        i32,   // 0-59
    second:        i32,   // 0-59
    epoch_seconds: i64,   // seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC
}

// =============================================================================
// Calendar helpers — must precede callers
// =============================================================================

fn is_leap_year(y: i32) -> bool with Div, Panic {
    if y % 400 == 0 { return true }
    if y % 100 == 0 { return false }
    if y % 4 == 0   { return true }
    false
}

fn days_in_month(y: i32, m: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if m == 1  { return 31 }
    if m == 2  {
        if is_leap_year(y) { return 29 }
        return 28
    }
    if m == 3  { return 31 }
    if m == 4  { return 30 }
    if m == 5  { return 31 }
    if m == 6  { return 30 }
    if m == 7  { return 31 }
    if m == 8  { return 31 }
    if m == 9  { return 30 }
    if m == 10 { return 31 }
    if m == 11 { return 30 }
    31
}

fn day_of_year(y: i32, m: i32, d: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var doy = 0
    var mo = 1
    while mo < m {
        doy = doy + days_in_month(y, mo)
        mo = mo + 1
    }
    doy + d
}

// Days from the POSIX epoch (1970-01-01) to the start of year y.
// Uses the Gregorian formula: every 4 years +1 leap, every 100 -1, every 400 +1.
fn days_from_epoch_to_year(y: i32) -> i64 with Div, Panic {
    let y0: i64 = y as i64 - 1
    let base: i64 = (y as i64 - 1970) * 365
    let leaps: i64 = y0 / 4 - y0 / 100 + y0 / 400
    let epoch_base: i64 = 1969 / 4 - 1969 / 100 + 1969 / 400
    base + leaps - epoch_base
}

// =============================================================================
// datetime_new — compute epoch_seconds from calendar components
// =============================================================================

fn datetime_new(y: i32, m: i32, d: i32, h: i32, min: i32, s: i32) -> DateTime with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let year_days: i64 = days_from_epoch_to_year(y)
    let month_days: i64 = day_of_year(y, m, d) as i64 - 1
    let total_days: i64 = year_days + month_days
    let epoch: i64 = total_days * 86400 + h as i64 * 3600 + min as i64 * 60 + s as i64
    DateTime {
        year: y, month: m, day: d,
        hour: h, minute: min, second: s,
        epoch_seconds: epoch,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// datetime_from_epoch — reverse: epoch → calendar fields
// =============================================================================

fn datetime_from_epoch(epoch: i64) -> DateTime with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var remaining: i64 = epoch

    // Extract time-of-day
    var day_secs: i64 = remaining % 86400
    var day_count: i64 = remaining / 86400
    if day_secs < 0 {
        day_secs = day_secs + 86400
        day_count = day_count - 1
    }
    let h: i32   = (day_secs / 3600) as i32
    let mn: i32  = ((day_secs % 3600) / 60) as i32
    let sec: i32 = (day_secs % 60) as i32

    // Walk forward/backward from 1970 to find the year
    var y: i32 = 1970
    if day_count >= 0 {
        while true {
            let dy: i64 = if is_leap_year(y) { 366 } else { 365 }
            if day_count < dy { break }
            day_count = day_count - dy
            y = y + 1
        }
    } else {
        while day_count < 0 {
            y = y - 1
            let dy: i64 = if is_leap_year(y) { 366 } else { 365 }
            day_count = day_count + dy
        }
    }

    // Walk months within the year
    var mo: i32 = 1
    while mo <= 12 {
        let dm: i64 = days_in_month(y, mo) as i64
        if day_count < dm { break }
        day_count = day_count - dm
        mo = mo + 1
    }
    let d: i32 = day_count as i32 + 1

    DateTime {
        year: y, month: mo, day: d,
        hour: h, minute: mn, second: sec,
        epoch_seconds: epoch,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// datetime_add_duration
// =============================================================================

fn datetime_add_duration(dt: DateTime, d: Duration) -> DateTime with Div, Panic, Mut {
    datetime_from_epoch(dt.epoch_seconds + d.seconds)
}

// =============================================================================
// datetime_diff — returns Duration representing a - b (may be negative seconds)
// =============================================================================

fn datetime_diff(a: &DateTime, b: &DateTime) -> Duration with Div, Panic {
    let diff_secs: i64 = a.epoch_seconds - b.epoch_seconds
    Duration { seconds: diff_secs, nanos: 0 }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/toml/mod.sio ===
//! stdlib/toml - TOML Parser
//!
//! Provides TOML format parsing and serialization.
//! Currently pending enum variant constructor and string support.

module toml

pub fn toml_module_ready() -> i32 { 1 }


// === FILE: stdlib/toml/parser.sio ===
// stdlib/toml/parser.sio — Minimal TOML parser
//
// Represents TOML as a flat key-value document (up to 32 entries).
// No heap allocation — all storage is fixed-size arrays.
// Supports flat key=value only (no tables, no arrays-of-tables).
// Value types: string, integer, float, bool.
// Handles: # comments, blank lines, whitespace around '='.
//
// JIT note: only &!Struct field mutations propagate to callers.
// Standalone &!array and &!scalar do NOT propagate in JIT mode.
// All helpers use struct-wrapping or by-value returns for correctness.
//
// # Limits
//   - Up to 32 key-value pairs per document
//   - Keys up to 63 bytes (null-terminated in 64-byte slot)
//   - String values up to 127 bytes (null-terminated in 128-byte slot)
//   - Parse input up to 4095 bytes

// ============================================================================
// TOML VALUE TYPES
// ============================================================================

pub fn TOML_STRING()  -> i32 { 0 }
pub fn TOML_INTEGER() -> i32 { 1 }
pub fn TOML_FLOAT()   -> i32 { 2 }
pub fn TOML_BOOL()    -> i32 { 3 }

// ============================================================================
// TomlDoc — flat key→value store, up to 32 entries
// ============================================================================

pub struct TomlDoc {
    pub keys:      [[u8; 64]; 32],
    pub key_lens:  [i32; 32],
    pub str_vals:  [[u8; 128]; 32],
    pub str_lens:  [i32; 32],
    pub num_vals:  [f64; 32],
    pub bool_vals: [i32; 32],
    pub types:     [i32; 32],
    pub count:     i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// Internal result types
// ============================================================================

// Result from parsing a quoted string body (after opening '"').
struct TStrResult {
    data:    [u8; 128],
    str_len: i32,
    new_pos: i32,   // -1 on error
}

// Result from parsing a number token.
struct TNumResult {
    value:   f64,
    new_pos: i32,
    is_int:  i32,   // 1 if no decimal point seen
}

// ============================================================================
// TomlDoc constructor
// ============================================================================

pub fn toml_doc_new() -> TomlDoc {
    TomlDoc {
        keys:      [[(0 as u8); 64]; 32],
        key_lens:  [0; 32],
        str_vals:  [[(0 as u8); 128]; 32],
        str_lens:  [0; 32],
        num_vals:  [0.0; 32],
        bool_vals: [0; 32],
        types:     [0; 32],
        count:     0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Internal helpers (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

// Skip spaces and tabs (but not newlines). Returns new position.
fn toml_skip_ws(input: &[u8; 4096], pos: i32, len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = pos
    while p < len {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        if c == (32 as u8) || c == (9 as u8) {
            p = p + 1
        } else {
            return p
        }
    }
    p
}

// Skip to end of current line (past '\n'). Returns new position.
fn toml_skip_line(input: &[u8; 4096], pos: i32, len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = pos
    while p < len {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        p = p + 1
        if c == (10 as u8) {
            return p
        }
    }
    p
}

// Parse a quoted TOML basic string body (after opening '"').
// Returns TStrResult; new_pos=-1 on error.
fn toml_parse_string(input: &[u8; 4096], start: i32, len: i32) -> TStrResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = TStrResult {
        data:    [0; 128],
        str_len: 0,
        new_pos: 0 - 1,
    }
    var p = start
    var wpos: i32 = 0
    var done: i32 = 0
    while p < len && done == 0 {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        if c == (34 as u8) {
            // closing '"'
            p = p + 1
            done = 1
        } else if c == (92 as u8) {
            // escape sequence
            p = p + 1
            if p >= len { return r }
            let esc = input[p as usize]
            if esc == (34 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = (34 as u8); wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == (92 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = (92 as u8); wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == (110 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = (10 as u8); wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == (116 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = (9 as u8); wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == (114 as u8) {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = (13 as u8); wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = esc; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            }
            p = p + 1
        } else if c == (10 as u8) || c == (13 as u8) {
            // unterminated string
            return r
        } else {
            if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = c; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            p = p + 1
        }
    }
    if done == 0 { return r }
    r.str_len = wpos
    r.new_pos = p
    r
}

// Parse a number starting at pos. Handles optional sign, digits, optional '.'.
// Returns TNumResult; is_int=1 when no decimal point seen.
fn toml_parse_number(input: &[u8; 4096], start: i32, len: i32) -> TNumResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = start
    var negative: i32 = 0
    if p < len && input[p as usize] == (45 as u8) {
        negative = 1
        p = p + 1
    }
    var int_part: f64 = 0.0
    var int_done: i32 = 0
    while p < len && int_done == 0 {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        if c >= (48 as u8) && c <= (57 as u8) {
            int_part = int_part * 10.0 + (c - (48 as u8)) as f64
            p = p + 1
        } else {
            int_done = 1
        }
    }
    var frac: f64 = 0.0
    var frac_div: f64 = 1.0
    var is_int: i32 = 1
    if p < len && input[p as usize] == (46 as u8) {
        is_int = 0
        p = p + 1
        var frac_done: i32 = 0
        while p < len && frac_done == 0 {
            let c = input[p as usize]
            if c >= (48 as u8) && c <= (57 as u8) {
                frac = frac * 10.0 + (c - (48 as u8)) as f64
                frac_div = frac_div * 10.0
                p = p + 1
            } else {
                frac_done = 1
            }
        }
    }
    var result = int_part + frac / frac_div
    if negative == 1 {
        result = 0.0 - result
    }
    TNumResult { value: result, new_pos: p, is_int: is_int }
}

// Compare a key slot in doc against a provided key. Returns 1 if equal.
fn toml_keys_equal(doc: &TomlDoc, slot: i32, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if doc.key_lens[slot as usize] != key_len { return 0 }
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < key_len {
        if doc.keys[slot as usize][i as usize] != key[i as usize] { return 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    1
}

// Find slot index for a key. Returns index or -1.
fn toml_find_key(doc: &TomlDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < doc.count {
        if toml_keys_equal(doc, i, key, key_len) == 1 {
            return i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0 - 1
}

// ============================================================================
// toml_parse — main parse entry point
// ============================================================================

// Parse a flat TOML document from input bytes.
// Handles: key = "string", key = 123, key = 3.14, key = true/false,
//          # comments, blank lines.
// Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
pub fn toml_parse(input: &[u8; 4096], len: i32, doc: &!TomlDoc) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = 0
    while p < len {
        // Skip leading whitespace on the line.
        p = toml_skip_ws(input, p, len)
        if p >= len { return 0 }

        let c0 = input[p as usize]

        // Blank line or comment — skip to next line.
        if c0 == (10 as u8) || c0 == (13 as u8) {
            p = p + 1
            // skip \r\n pair
            if c0 == (13 as u8) && p < len && input[p as usize] == (10 as u8) {
                p = p + 1
            }
            // Advance p (loop will handle)
        } else if c0 == (35 as u8) {
            // '#' comment
            p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
        } else if c0 == (91 as u8) {
            // '[' table header — skip entire line (no table support)
            p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
        } else {
            // Parse key (bare key: alphanumeric, '-', '_')
            var key64: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
            var klen: i32 = 0
            var key_done: i32 = 0
            while p < len && key_done == 0 {
                let kc = input[p as usize]
                // valid bare key chars
                if (kc >= (65 as u8) && kc <= (90 as u8)) ||   // A-Z
                   (kc >= (97 as u8) && kc <= (122 as u8)) ||  // a-z
                   (kc >= (48 as u8) && kc <= (57 as u8)) ||   // 0-9
                   kc == (45 as u8) || kc == (95 as u8) {       // '-', '_'
                    if klen < 63 {
                        key64[klen as usize] = kc
                        klen = klen + 1
                    }
                    p = p + 1
                } else {
                    key_done = 1
                }
            }
            if klen == 0 {
                // Not a valid key start — skip line
                p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
            } else {
                // Skip whitespace before '='
                p = toml_skip_ws(input, p, len)
                if p >= len { return 0 - 1 }
                if input[p as usize] != (61 as u8) {
                    // '=' expected
                    return 0 - 1
                }
                p = p + 1
                // Skip whitespace after '='
                p = toml_skip_ws(input, p, len)
                if p >= len { return 0 - 1 }

                let vc = input[p as usize]

                if doc.count < 32 {
                    let slot = doc.count
                    // Copy key into slot.
                    var ki: i32 = 0
                    while ki < klen {
                        doc.keys[slot as usize][ki as usize] = key64[ki as usize]
                        ki = ki + 1
                    }
                    doc.key_lens[slot as usize] = klen

                    if vc == (34 as u8) {
                        // Quoted string value.
                        p = p + 1
                        let sr = toml_parse_string(input, p, len)
                        if sr.new_pos < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
                        p = sr.new_pos
                        doc.types[slot as usize] = 0
                        doc.str_lens[slot as usize] = sr.str_len
                        var si: i32 = 0
                        while si < sr.str_len {
                            doc.str_vals[slot as usize][si as usize] = sr.data[si as usize]
                            si = si + 1
                        }
                        doc.count = doc.count + 1

                    } else if vc == (116 as u8) {
                        // 'true'
                        if p + 3 < len &&
                           input[(p+1) as usize] == (114 as u8) &&
                           input[(p+2) as usize] == (117 as u8) &&
                           input[(p+3) as usize] == (101 as u8) {
                            doc.types[slot as usize] = 3
                            doc.bool_vals[slot as usize] = 1
                            p = p + 4
                            doc.count = doc.count + 1
                        } else {
                            return 0 - 1
                        }

                    } else if vc == (102 as u8) {
                        // 'false'
                        if p + 4 < len &&
                           input[(p+1) as usize] == (97 as u8)  &&
                           input[(p+2) as usize] == (108 as u8) &&
                           input[(p+3) as usize] == (115 as u8) &&
                           input[(p+4) as usize] == (101 as u8) {
                            doc.types[slot as usize] = 3
                            doc.bool_vals[slot as usize] = 0
                            p = p + 5
                            doc.count = doc.count + 1
                        } else {
                            return 0 - 1
                        }

                    } else if (vc >= (48 as u8) && vc <= (57 as u8)) || vc == (45 as u8) {
                        // Number (integer or float).
                        let nr = toml_parse_number(input, p, len)
                        if nr.new_pos <= p { return 0 - 1 }
                        p = nr.new_pos
                        if nr.is_int == 1 {
                            doc.types[slot as usize] = 1
                        } else {
                            doc.types[slot as usize] = 2
                        }
                        doc.num_vals[slot as usize] = nr.value
                        doc.count = doc.count + 1

                    } else {
                        // Unrecognised value — skip line, don't add entry.
                        p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
                    }
                }

                // Skip trailing whitespace and comment on line.
                p = toml_skip_ws(input, p, len)
                if p < len {
                    let trail = input[p as usize]
                    if trail == (35 as u8) {
                        // inline comment
                        p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
                    } else if trail == (10 as u8) || trail == (13 as u8) {
                        p = p + 1
                        if trail == (13 as u8) && p < len && input[p as usize] == (10 as u8) {
                            p = p + 1
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    0
}

// ============================================================================
// Accessor functions
// ============================================================================

// Returns string length into out buffer, or -1 if key not found / not a string.
pub fn toml_get_string(doc: &TomlDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32, out: &![u8; 128]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = toml_find_key(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    if doc.types[idx as usize] != 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    let slen = doc.str_lens[idx as usize]
    // NOTE: &![u8;128] mutations do NOT propagate in JIT — caller must use
    // doc.str_vals[slot] directly after finding the slot via toml_find_key.
    // This function copies to out for API completeness; JIT callers see stale value.
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < slen {
        out[i as usize] = doc.str_vals[idx as usize][i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    slen
}

// Returns number value, or 0.0 if not found / not numeric.
pub fn toml_get_number(doc: &TomlDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = toml_find_key(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx < 0 { return 0.0 }
    let t = doc.types[idx as usize]
    if t == 1 || t == 2 {
        return doc.num_vals[idx as usize]
    }
    0.0
}

// Returns 0 or 1 for bool, -1 if not found / not a bool.
pub fn toml_get_bool(doc: &TomlDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = toml_find_key(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    if doc.types[idx as usize] != 3 { return 0 - 1 }
    doc.bool_vals[idx as usize]
}

// Returns total number of key-value pairs in document.
pub fn toml_doc_count(doc: &TomlDoc) -> i32 {
    doc.count
}

// ============================================================================
// Self-tests
// ============================================================================

pub fn toml_self_test() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail: i32 = 0

    // T1: empty doc
    var doc = toml_doc_new()
    if doc.count != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T2: parse integer
    var raw: [u8; 4096] = [0; 4096]
    // "version = 3\n"
    raw[0]  = (118 as u8)  // v
    raw[1]  = (101 as u8)  // e
    raw[2]  = (114 as u8)  // r
    raw[3]  = (115 as u8)  // s
    raw[4]  = (105 as u8)  // i
    raw[5]  = (111 as u8)  // o
    raw[6]  = (110 as u8)  // n
    raw[7]  = (32 as u8)   // space
    raw[8]  = (61 as u8)   // =
    raw[9]  = (32 as u8)   // space
    raw[10] = (51 as u8)   // 3
    raw[11] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    let r1 = toml_parse(&raw, 12, &!doc)
    if r1 != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.count != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.types[0] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    let vdiff = doc.num_vals[0] - 3.0
    let avdiff = if vdiff < 0.0 { 0.0 - vdiff } else { vdiff }
    if avdiff > 0.0001 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T3: parse bool
    var doc2 = toml_doc_new()
    var raw2: [u8; 4096] = [0; 4096]
    // "debug = true\n"
    raw2[0]  = (100 as u8)  // d
    raw2[1]  = (101 as u8)  // e
    raw2[2]  = (98 as u8)   // b
    raw2[3]  = (117 as u8)  // u
    raw2[4]  = (103 as u8)  // g
    raw2[5]  = (32 as u8)   // space
    raw2[6]  = (61 as u8)   // =
    raw2[7]  = (32 as u8)   // space
    raw2[8]  = (116 as u8)  // t
    raw2[9]  = (114 as u8)  // r
    raw2[10] = (117 as u8)  // u
    raw2[11] = (101 as u8)  // e
    raw2[12] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    let r2 = toml_parse(&raw2, 13, &!doc2)
    if r2 != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc2.count != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc2.types[0] != 3 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc2.bool_vals[0] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T4: doc.count (direct field access — avoids borrow conflict after &!doc)
    if doc.count != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }

    fail
}

// === FILE: stdlib/trace/mod.sio ===

    tracer_span_duration,

// === FILE: stdlib/trace/trace.sio ===
// trace/mod.sio — Lightweight Execution Tracing
//
// Structured span-based tracing for profiling and diagnostics.
// Fixed-capacity tracer (128 spans) with nanosecond timestamps.
//
// Inspired by: Tokio tracing, OpenTelemetry spans

// ============================================================================
// TRACER — parallel flat arrays (avoids runtime-indexed struct-array write bug)
// ============================================================================

pub struct Tracer {
    span_id:     [i64; 128],
    span_parent: [i64; 128],
    span_start:  [i64; 128],
    span_end:    [i64; 128],
    span_tag:    [i64; 128],
    count:       i32,
}

pub fn tracer_new() -> Tracer {
    Tracer {
        span_id:     [0; 128],
        span_parent: [0; 128],
        span_start:  [0; 128],
        span_end:    [0; 128],
        span_tag:    [0; 128],
        count:       0,
    }
}

// Begin a new span. Mutates tracer in place; returns new span ID (-1 if full).
pub fn tracer_begin(t: &!Tracer, parent: i64, tag: i64, now: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    if t.count >= 128 { return 0 - 1 }
    let idx = t.count as usize
    let new_id = (t.count as i64) + 1
    t.span_id[idx]     = new_id
    t.span_parent[idx] = parent
    t.span_start[idx]  = now
    t.span_end[idx]    = 0
    t.span_tag[idx]    = tag
    t.count = t.count + 1
    new_id
}

// End a span by setting its end timestamp. Mutates tracer in place.
pub fn tracer_end(t: &!Tracer, id: i64, now: i64) with Mut {
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < t.count {
        if t.span_id[i as usize] == id {
            t.span_end[i as usize] = now
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Get duration of a span in nanoseconds (0 if not ended or not found)
pub fn tracer_span_duration(t: &Tracer, id: i64) -> i64 {
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < t.count {
        if t.span_id[i as usize] == id {
            let s = t.span_start[i as usize]
            let e = t.span_end[i as usize]
            if e > s { return e - s }
            return 0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0
}

// ============================================================================
// INLINE TESTS
// ============================================================================

//@ run-pass
fn test_tracer_new() -> i32 {
    let t = tracer_new()
    if t.count != 0 { return 1 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_tracer_begin_end() -> i32 with Mut {
    var t = tracer_new()
    let id = tracer_begin(&!t, 0, 42, 1000)
    if id != 1 { return 1 }
    if t.count != 1 { return 2 }
    tracer_end(&!t, id, 2000)
    let dur = tracer_span_duration(&t, id)
    if dur != 1000 { return 3 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_tracer_multiple_spans() -> i32 with Mut {
    var t = tracer_new()
    let id1 = tracer_begin(&!t, 0, 1, 100)
    let id2 = tracer_begin(&!t, id1, 2, 200)
    if id2 != 2 { return 1 }
    tracer_end(&!t, id2, 300)
    tracer_end(&!t, id1, 400)
    let dur1 = tracer_span_duration(&t, 1)
    let dur2 = tracer_span_duration(&t, 2)
    if dur1 != 300 { return 2 }
    if dur2 != 100 { return 3 }
    0
}

// === FILE: stdlib/types/refinement.sio ===
// stdlib/types/refinement.sio — Refinement Types for Sounio
//
// Provides 8 concrete refinement types, each as a struct + typed functions.
// No generics, no traits — pure Sounio with explicit structs per type.
//
// Design: each type X has:
//   struct X { value: f64 }
//   struct XResult { ok: bool, value: X }
//   pub fn x_new(v: f64) -> X          -- panics on invalid (prints error, returns default)
//   pub fn x_try_new(v: f64) -> XResult -- returns ok=false on invalid
//   pub fn x_clamp(v: f64) -> X        -- clips to valid range
//   pub fn x_is_valid(v: f64) -> bool
//   pub fn x_value(x: X) -> f64

// ============================================================================
// 1. Probability — [0.0, 1.0]
// ============================================================================

struct Probability { value: f64 }
struct ProbabilityResult { ok: bool, value: Probability }

pub fn probability_is_valid(v: f64) -> bool {
    v >= 0.0 && v <= 1.0
}

pub fn probability_new(v: f64) -> Probability with IO {
    if probability_is_valid(v) {
        return Probability { value: v }
    }
    println("probability_new: value out of range [0.0, 1.0]: ", v)
    Probability { value: 0.0 }
}

pub fn probability_try_new(v: f64) -> ProbabilityResult {
    if probability_is_valid(v) {
        return ProbabilityResult { ok: true, value: Probability { value: v } }
    }
    ProbabilityResult { ok: false, value: Probability { value: 0.0 } }
}

pub fn probability_clamp(v: f64) -> Probability {
    if v < 0.0 { return Probability { value: 0.0 } }
    if v > 1.0 { return Probability { value: 1.0 } }
    Probability { value: v }
}

pub fn probability_value(x: Probability) -> f64 {
    x.value
}

// ============================================================================
// 2. Positive — (0.0, +inf)
// ============================================================================

struct Positive { value: f64 }
struct PositiveResult { ok: bool, value: Positive }

pub fn positive_is_valid(v: f64) -> bool {
    v > 0.0
}

pub fn positive_new(v: f64) -> Positive with IO {
    if positive_is_valid(v) {
        return Positive { value: v }
    }
    println("positive_new: value must be > 0.0, got: ", v)
    Positive { value: 1.0 }
}

pub fn positive_try_new(v: f64) -> PositiveResult {
    if positive_is_valid(v) {
        return PositiveResult { ok: true, value: Positive { value: v } }
    }
    PositiveResult { ok: false, value: Positive { value: 1.0 } }
}

pub fn positive_clamp(v: f64) -> Positive {
    if v <= 0.0 { return Positive { value: 1.0e-300 } }
    Positive { value: v }
}

pub fn positive_value(x: Positive) -> f64 {
    x.value
}

// ============================================================================
// 5. NonZero — |x| > 1e-15
// ============================================================================

struct NonZero { value: f64 }
struct NonZeroResult { ok: bool, value: NonZero }

fn abs_nz(v: f64) -> f64 {
    if v < 0.0 { 0.0 - v } else { v }
}

pub fn non_zero_is_valid(v: f64) -> bool {
    abs_nz(v) > 1.0e-15
}

pub fn non_zero_new(v: f64) -> NonZero with IO {
    if non_zero_is_valid(v) {
        return NonZero { value: v }
    }
    println("non_zero_new: |value| must be > 1e-15, got: ", v)
    NonZero { value: 1.0 }
}

pub fn non_zero_try_new(v: f64) -> NonZeroResult {
    if non_zero_is_valid(v) {
        return NonZeroResult { ok: true, value: NonZero { value: v } }
    }
    NonZeroResult { ok: false, value: NonZero { value: 1.0 } }
}

pub fn non_zero_value(x: NonZero) -> f64 {
    x.value
}

// Conversion helpers

/// probability_to_percentage: [0,1] → [0,100]
pub fn probability_to_percentage(p: Probability) -> Percentage {
    Percentage { value: p.value * 100.0 }
}

/// percentage_to_probability: [0,100] → [0,1]
pub fn percentage_to_probability(p: Percentage) -> Probability with Div, Panic {
    Probability { value: p.value / 100.0 }
}

/// probability_to_unit_interval: identity (both are [0,1])
pub fn probability_to_unit_interval(p: Probability) -> UnitInterval {
    UnitInterval { value: p.value }
}

/// positive_to_concentration: reinterpret Positive mol/L as Concentration
pub fn positive_to_concentration(p: Positive) -> Concentration {
    Concentration { value: p.value }
}

/// temperature_celsius_to_kelvin: C + 273.15 = K
pub fn temperature_celsius_to_kelvin(c: f64) -> f64 {
    c + 273.15
}

/// temperature_kelvin_to_celsius: K - 273.15 = C
pub fn temperature_kelvin_to_celsius(t: Temperature) -> f64 {
    t.value + (0.0 - 273.15)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/types/types.sio ===
// types/mod.sio — Type Metadata
//
// Runtime type information for reflection and serialization.
// Provides size, alignment, and kind metadata for primitive types.

// ============================================================================
// TYPE INFO
// ============================================================================

// Type kind constants
fn TYPE_KIND_BOOL() -> i32 { 0 }
fn TYPE_KIND_I32() -> i32 { 1 }
fn TYPE_KIND_I64() -> i32 { 2 }
fn TYPE_KIND_F64() -> i32 { 3 }
fn TYPE_KIND_ARRAY() -> i32 { 4 }
fn TYPE_KIND_STRUCT() -> i32 { 5 }

pub struct TypeInfo {
    kind: i32,       // TYPE_KIND_*
    size: i32,       // Size in bytes
    alignment: i32,  // Alignment requirement in bytes
}

pub fn TYPE_I32() -> TypeInfo {
    TypeInfo { kind: 1, size: 4, alignment: 4 }
}

pub fn TYPE_I64() -> TypeInfo {
    TypeInfo { kind: 2, size: 8, alignment: 8 }
}

pub fn TYPE_F64() -> TypeInfo {
    TypeInfo { kind: 3, size: 8, alignment: 8 }
}

pub fn TYPE_BOOL() -> TypeInfo {
    TypeInfo { kind: 0, size: 1, alignment: 1 }
}

pub fn TYPE_ARRAY() -> TypeInfo {
    // Generic array metadata (element type determined separately)
    TypeInfo { kind: 4, size: 0, alignment: 8 }
}

// Check if two TypeInfos represent the same type
pub fn type_eq(a: TypeInfo, b: TypeInfo) -> bool {
    a.kind == b.kind && a.size == b.size && a.alignment == b.alignment
}

// Is this a numeric type?
pub fn type_is_numeric(t: TypeInfo) -> bool {
    t.kind == 1 || t.kind == 2 || t.kind == 3
}

// Is this an integer type?
pub fn type_is_integer(t: TypeInfo) -> bool {
    t.kind == 1 || t.kind == 2
}

// ============================================================================
// INLINE TESTS
// ============================================================================

//@ run-pass
fn test_type_i32() -> i32 {
    let t = TYPE_I32()
    if t.kind != 1 { return 1 }
    if t.size != 4 { return 2 }
    if t.alignment != 4 { return 3 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_type_f64() -> i32 {
    let t = TYPE_F64()
    if t.kind != 3 { return 1 }
    if t.size != 8 { return 2 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_type_eq() -> i32 {
    let a = TYPE_I32()
    let b = TYPE_I32()
    if !type_eq(a, b) { return 1 }
    let c = TYPE_F64()
    if type_eq(a, c) { return 2 }
    0
}

//@ run-pass
fn test_type_is_numeric() -> i32 {
    if !type_is_numeric(TYPE_I32()) { return 1 }
    if !type_is_numeric(TYPE_F64()) { return 2 }
    if type_is_numeric(TYPE_BOOL()) { return 3 }
    0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ui/render.sio ===
// stdlib/ui/render.sio — Widget rendering and event dispatch

use display::canvas::{Canvas, canvas_fill_rect, canvas_draw_rect, canvas_draw_text}
use display::event::{Event, EV_MOUSE_PRESS, EV_MOUSE_RELEASE, EV_MOTION}
use ui::widget::{Widget, UiState, WIDGET_PANEL, WIDGET_BUTTON, WIDGET_LABEL,
                  ui_widget_hit, ui_hit_test}

// ============================================================
// Render one widget onto a canvas
// ============================================================

fn ui_render_widget(wid: Widget, state: &UiState, c: &!Canvas) with Mut, Div {
    // Determine background colour (buttons highlight on hover/press)
    var r = wid.bg_r
    var g = wid.bg_g
    var b = wid.bg_b

    if wid.kind == WIDGET_BUTTON {
        if wid.id == state.pressed_id {
            // Darken pressed button
            r = r * 6 / 10
            g = g * 6 / 10
            b = b * 6 / 10
        } else if wid.id == state.hovered_id {
            // Lighten hovered button
            let dr = (255 - r) / 4
            let dg = (255 - g) / 4
            let db = (255 - b) / 4
            r = r + dr
            g = g + dg
            b = b + db
        }
    }

    // Background fill
    canvas_fill_rect(c, wid.x, wid.y, wid.w, wid.h, r, g, b)

    // Border for buttons
    if wid.kind == WIDGET_BUTTON {
        canvas_draw_rect(c, wid.x, wid.y, wid.w, wid.h, 200, 200, 220)
    }

    // Text (centred vertically; left-padded by 4px for labels)
    if wid.text_len > 0 {
        let text_h = 8
        let ty = wid.y + (wid.h - text_h) / 2
        let tx = if wid.kind == WIDGET_BUTTON {
            let text_w = wid.text_len * 8
            wid.x + (wid.w - text_w) / 2
        } else {
            wid.x + 4
        }
        // Repack text into a [i8; 256] for canvas_draw_text
        var text_buf: [i8; 256] = [0; 256]
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < wid.text_len {
            text_buf[i as usize] = wid.text[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
        canvas_draw_text(c, &text_buf, wid.text_len, tx, ty,
                         wid.fg_r, wid.fg_g, wid.fg_b)
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Render all widgets in order (painter's algorithm)
// ============================================================

pub fn ui_render(widgets: &[Widget; 64], n: i64, state: &UiState, c: &!Canvas) with Mut, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        ui_render_widget(widgets[i as usize], state, c)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Handle one event and update UiState
// ============================================================

pub fn ui_handle_event(ev: Event, widgets: &[Widget; 64], n: i64, state: &!UiState) with Mut {
    // Reset per-frame click
    state.clicked_id = 0 - 1

    if ev.kind == EV_MOTION {
        state.mouse_x = ev.x
        state.mouse_y = ev.y
        let hit_idx = ui_hit_test(widgets, n, ev.x, ev.y)
        state.hovered_id = if hit_idx >= 0 {
            widgets[hit_idx as usize].id
        } else {
            0 - 1
        }
    } else if ev.kind == EV_MOUSE_PRESS {
        state.mouse_x = ev.x
        state.mouse_y = ev.y
        let hit_idx = ui_hit_test(widgets, n, ev.x, ev.y)
        if hit_idx >= 0 {
            state.pressed_id = widgets[hit_idx as usize].id
        }
    } else if ev.kind == EV_MOUSE_RELEASE {
        state.mouse_x = ev.x
        state.mouse_y = ev.y
        // A click completes if release is over the same widget
        let hit_idx = ui_hit_test(widgets, n, ev.x, ev.y)
        if hit_idx >= 0 {
            let hid = widgets[hit_idx as usize].id
            if hid == state.pressed_id {
                state.clicked_id = hid
            }
        }
        state.pressed_id = 0 - 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Query helpers
// ============================================================

pub fn ui_was_clicked(state: &UiState, id: i64) -> bool {
    state.clicked_id == id
}

pub fn ui_is_hovered(state: &UiState, id: i64) -> bool {
    state.hovered_id == id
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ui/widget.sio ===
// stdlib/ui/widget.sio — Widget definitions and hit testing

// ============================================================
// Widget kinds
// ============================================================

let WIDGET_PANEL:  i64 = 0
let WIDGET_BUTTON: i64 = 1
let WIDGET_LABEL:  i64 = 2
let WIDGET_INPUT:  i64 = 3

// ============================================================
// Widget struct
//
// Fixed-size text[64] avoids heap allocation per widget.
// bg_*/fg_* are 0-255 RGB components.
// ============================================================

pub struct Widget {
    pub id: i64,
    pub kind: i64,
    pub x: i64,
    pub y: i64,
    pub w: i64,
    pub h: i64,
    pub text: [i8; 64],
    pub text_len: i64,
    pub bg_r: i64, pub bg_g: i64, pub bg_b: i64,
    pub fg_r: i64, pub fg_g: i64, pub fg_b: i64,
}

// ============================================================
// UI interaction state (one per application)
// ============================================================

pub struct UiState {
    pub hovered_id: i64,   // id of widget under cursor, or -1
    pub pressed_id: i64,   // id of widget currently held, or -1
    pub clicked_id: i64,   // id of widget that received a click this frame, or -1
    pub focused_id: i64,   // id of text-input with keyboard focus, or -1
    pub mouse_x: i64,
    pub mouse_y: i64,
}

pub fn ui_state_new() -> UiState {
    UiState {
        hovered_id: 0 - 1,
        pressed_id: 0 - 1,
        clicked_id: 0 - 1,
        focused_id: 0 - 1,
        mouse_x: 0,
        mouse_y: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Hit testing
// ============================================================

pub fn ui_widget_hit(wid: Widget, x: i64, y: i64) -> bool {
    x >= wid.x && y >= wid.y && x < wid.x + wid.w && y < wid.y + wid.h
}

// Find the topmost widget at (x, y); returns index in widgets array or -1.
pub fn ui_hit_test(widgets: &[Widget; 64], n: i64, x: i64, y: i64) -> i64 {
    var idx = n - 1
    var result: i64 = 0 - 1
    var found = false
    while idx >= 0 && !found {
        if ui_widget_hit(widgets[idx as usize], x, y) {
            result = idx
            found = true
        }
        idx = idx - 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================
// Widget constructors (helpers for common kinds)
// ============================================================

pub fn widget_zero() -> Widget {
    Widget {
        id: 0, kind: 0, x: 0, y: 0, w: 0, h: 0,
        text: [0; 64], text_len: 0,
        bg_r: 0, bg_g: 0, bg_b: 0, fg_r: 0, fg_g: 0, fg_b: 0,
    }
}

pub fn widget_panel(id: i64, x: i64, y: i64, w: i64, h: i64, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) -> Widget {
    var wid = Widget {
        id: id,
        kind: WIDGET_PANEL,
        x: x, y: y, w: w, h: h,
        text: [0; 64],
        text_len: 0,
        bg_r: r, bg_g: g, bg_b: b,
        fg_r: 255, fg_g: 255, fg_b: 255,
    }
    wid
}

pub fn widget_label(
    id: i64,
    x: i64, y: i64, w: i64, h: i64,
    label: &[i8; 64], label_len: i64,
    bg_r: i64, bg_g: i64, bg_b: i64,
    fg_r: i64, fg_g: i64, fg_b: i64,
) -> Widget {
    var wid = Widget {
        id: id,
        kind: WIDGET_LABEL,
        x: x, y: y, w: w, h: h,
        text: [0; 64],
        text_len: label_len,
        bg_r: bg_r, bg_g: bg_g, bg_b: bg_b,
        fg_r: fg_r, fg_g: fg_g, fg_b: fg_b,
    }
    // Copy label text
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < label_len {
        wid.text[i as usize] = label[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    wid
}

pub fn widget_button(
    id: i64,
    x: i64, y: i64, w: i64, h: i64,
    label: &[i8; 64], label_len: i64,
) -> Widget {
    var wid = Widget {
        id: id,
        kind: WIDGET_BUTTON,
        x: x, y: y, w: w, h: h,
        text: [0; 64],
        text_len: label_len,
        bg_r: 60, bg_g: 100, bg_b: 160,
        fg_r: 255, fg_g: 255, fg_b: 255,
    }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < label_len {
        wid.text[i as usize] = label[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    wid
}

// Example: stellar distance ladder
fn astro_demo() -> i32 with IO {
    let dist_alpha_cen: ly  = 4.367    // distance to Alpha Centauri
    let dist_m31:       Mpc = 0.785    // distance to Andromeda galaxy
    let mass_sun:       Msun = 1.0

    let mass_kg:  f64 = mass_sgr_a * MSUN_TO_KG

// Unit system: Atomic and Nuclear
// Gen 19: dimensional analysis — eV, keV, MeV, GeV, u, amu preloaded
//@ run-pass

// ── Energy ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
unit eV;    // electron-volt        = 1.602e-19 J
unit keV;   // kilo-electron-volt   = 1.602e-16 J
unit MeV;   // mega-electron-volt   = 1.602e-13 J
unit GeV;   // giga-electron-volt   = 1.602e-10 J
unit TeV;   // tera-electron-volt   = 1.602e-7 J

unit u;     // unified atomic mass unit = 1.66054e-27 kg  (also: Da, amu)
unit amu;   // alias for u
unit me;    // electron mass = 9.10938e-31 kg

unit nm;    // nanometre    = 1e-9 m
unit pm;    // picometre    = 1e-12 m  (bond lengths)
unit fm;    // femtometre   = 1e-15 m  (nuclear radii; 1 fm = 1 fermi)

// ── Natural units (ℏ=c=1 system) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
// In the natural unit system all quantities reduce to powers of energy (eV).
// Length = 1/energy, time = 1/energy, mass = energy.
// We declare these as dimensionless since mixing natural and SI units is undefined.
unit hbar_eV; // reduced Planck constant in eV·s (= 6.582e-16 eV·s) [dimensionless]
unit c_nat;   // speed of light in natural units = 1 [dimensionless]

// ── Atomic physics ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

unit Hartree; // Hartree energy Eₕ = 27.211 eV (energy)

let KEV_TO_J:      f64 = 1.60217663e-16
let MEV_TO_J:      f64 = 1.60217663e-13
let GEV_TO_J:      f64 = 1.60217663e-10
let U_TO_KG:       f64 = 1.66053906660e-27
let ME_TO_KG:      f64 = 9.1093837015e-31
let NM_TO_M:       f64 = 1.0e-9
let PM_TO_M:       f64 = 1.0e-12
let FM_TO_M:       f64 = 1.0e-15
let BOHR_TO_M:     f64 = 5.29177210903e-11
let HARTREE_TO_EV: f64 = 27.211396132
let HARTREE_TO_J:  f64 = 4.3597447222071e-18
let ALPHA_FINE:    f64 = 7.2973525693e-3  // fine structure constant (dimensionless)
let HBAR_EV_S:     f64 = 6.582119569e-16  // ℏ in eV·s
let C_LIGHT:       f64 = 2.99792458e8     // m/s

// Example: nuclear binding energy
fn atomic_demo() -> i32 with IO {
    // He-4 binding energy
    let binding: MeV = 28.295673   // total binding energy
    let per_nucleon: f64 = binding / 4.0  // MeV per nucleon

// === FILE: stdlib/units/cgs.sio ===
// Unit system: CGS (Centimetre-Gram-Second)
// Gen 19: dimensional analysis — base units cm, g, s are preloaded
//@ run-pass

// ── CGS base ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
unit cm;    // centimetre (length^1)  = 0.01 m
unit g;     // gram (mass^1)          = 0.001 kg
unit s;     // second (time^1)        — same as SI

// ── CGS mechanical ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
unit dyn;   // dyne (force)           = 1e-5 N   = g·cm/s²
unit erg;   // erg (energy)           = 1e-7 J   = g·cm²/s²
unit P;     // poise (dynamic viscosity) = 0.1 Pa·s  = g/(cm·s)
unit St;    // stokes (kinematic viscosity) = 1e-4 m²/s = cm²/s
unit Gal;   // galileo (acceleration) = 0.01 m/s²  = cm/s²

// ── CGS electromagnetic (Gaussian) ───────────────────────────────────────────
// Note: Gaussian units unify E and B in one system; dimensionality differs from SI.
// These are declared as dimensionless at the type-system level since they cannot
// be safely combined with SI electromagnetic units.
unit Gs;    // gauss (magnetic flux density) = 1e-4 T  [dimensionless in type system]
unit Oe;    // oersted (magnetic field)       = 79.577 A/m [dimensionless in type system]
unit Mx;    // maxwell (magnetic flux)        = 1e-8 Wb [dimensionless in type system]
unit statC; // statcoulomb (charge)           = 3.336e-10 C [dimensionless in type system]

// Conversion constants
let DYN_TO_N:      f64 = 1.0e-5
let ERG_TO_J:      f64 = 1.0e-7
let CM_TO_M:       f64 = 0.01
let G_TO_KG:       f64 = 0.001
let GS_TO_T:       f64 = 1.0e-4     // gauss → tesla
let OE_TO_AM:      f64 = 79.5774715 // oersted → A/m

// Example: CGS mechanics
fn cgs_demo() -> i32 with IO {
    let force:  dyn = 1.0e6     // 10 N in dynes
    let energy: erg = 1.0e7     // 1 J in ergs
    let force_n:  f64 = force  * DYN_TO_N
    let energy_j: f64 = energy * ERG_TO_J
    println("10 N in dynes: 1e6 dyn")
    println("1 J in ergs:   1e7 erg")
    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    return cgs_demo()
}
