// === FILE: stdlib/units/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/units/lib.sio — Dimensional analysis with epistemic uncertainty
//!
//! Provides SI unit dimensions, GUM-based uncertainty propagation, and
//! unit conversion for physical quantities.
//!
//! References:
//!   JCGM 100:2008 (GUM) — https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf
//!   BIPM SI Brochure 9th edition — https://www.bipm.org/utils/common/pdf/si-brochure/SI-Brochure-9.pdf

// ============================================================================
// UnitDim — 7-dimensional SI exponent vector
// ============================================================================

pub struct UnitDim {
    pub mass:        i32   // kg exponent
    pub length:      i32   // m  exponent
    pub time:        i32   // s  exponent
    pub temperature: i32   // K  exponent
    pub amount:      i32   // mol exponent
    pub current:     i32   // A  exponent
    pub luminosity:  i32   // cd exponent
}

// ============================================================================
// Quantity — value + standard uncertainty + dimensions
// ============================================================================

pub struct Quantity {
    pub value:       f64
    pub uncertainty: f64   // standard uncertainty u(x) per GUM §3.3
    pub dim:         UnitDim
}

// ============================================================================
// Internal helpers (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn sqrt_units(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn abs_units(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// ============================================================================
// Base dimension constructors
// ============================================================================

pub fn dim_dimensionless() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 0, time: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

pub fn dim_mass() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 0, time: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

pub fn dim_length() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 1, time: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

pub fn dim_time() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 0, time: 1, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

pub fn dim_temperature() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 0, time: 0, temperature: 1, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

pub fn dim_amount() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 0, time: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 1, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

pub fn dim_current() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 0, time: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 1, luminosity: 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// Derived dimension constructors
// ============================================================================

// m s⁻¹
pub fn dim_velocity() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 1, time: 0 - 1, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

// m s⁻²
pub fn dim_acceleration() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 1, time: 0 - 2, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

// kg m s⁻² (Newton)
pub fn dim_force() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 1, time: 0 - 2, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

// kg m² s⁻² (Joule)
pub fn dim_energy() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 2, time: 0 - 2, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

// kg m² s⁻³ (Watt)
pub fn dim_power() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 2, time: 0 - 3, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

// kg m⁻¹ s⁻² (Pascal)
pub fn dim_pressure() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 0 - 1, time: 0 - 2, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// Dimension arithmetic
// ============================================================================

pub fn dim_eq(a: UnitDim, b: UnitDim) -> bool {
    a.mass == b.mass &&
    a.length == b.length &&
    a.time == b.time &&
    a.temperature == b.temperature &&
    a.amount == b.amount &&
    a.current == b.current &&
    a.luminosity == b.luminosity
}

fn dim_add_exp(a: UnitDim, b: UnitDim) -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim {
        mass:        a.mass        + b.mass,
        length:      a.length      + b.length,
        time:        a.time        + b.time,
        temperature: a.temperature + b.temperature,
        amount:      a.amount      + b.amount,
        current:     a.current     + b.current,
        luminosity:  a.luminosity  + b.luminosity,
    }
}

fn dim_sub_exp(a: UnitDim, b: UnitDim) -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim {
        mass:        a.mass        - b.mass,
        length:      a.length      - b.length,
        time:        a.time        - b.time,
        temperature: a.temperature - b.temperature,
        amount:      a.amount      - b.amount,
        current:     a.current     - b.current,
        luminosity:  a.luminosity  - b.luminosity,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Quantity constructors
// ============================================================================

pub fn quantity_new(val: f64, unc: f64, dim: UnitDim) -> Quantity {
    Quantity { value: val, uncertainty: unc, dim: dim }
}

// ============================================================================
// Quantity compatibility
// ============================================================================

pub fn quantity_is_compatible(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> bool {
    dim_eq(a.dim, b.dim)
}

// ============================================================================
// Quantity arithmetic with GUM uncertainty propagation
// ============================================================================

// Addition: result_u = sqrt(u_a² + u_b²), dimensions must match (GUM §5.1.3)
pub fn quantity_add(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity with Panic, Mut, Div {
    assert(dim_eq(a.dim, b.dim))
    let ua2 = a.uncertainty * a.uncertainty
    let ub2 = b.uncertainty * b.uncertainty
    let uc  = sqrt_units(ua2 + ub2)
    Quantity { value: a.value + b.value, uncertainty: uc, dim: a.dim }
}

// Subtraction: result_u = sqrt(u_a² + u_b²), dimensions must match
pub fn quantity_sub(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity with Panic, Mut, Div {
    assert(dim_eq(a.dim, b.dim))
    let ua2 = a.uncertainty * a.uncertainty
    let ub2 = b.uncertainty * b.uncertainty
    let uc  = sqrt_units(ua2 + ub2)
    Quantity { value: a.value - b.value, uncertainty: uc, dim: a.dim }
}

// Multiplication: GUM §5.1.5 — relative uncertainties combine in quadrature
//   u_c/|c| = sqrt((u_a/|a|)² + (u_b/|b|)²)
//   u_c = |c| * sqrt((u_a/a)² + (u_b/b)²)
//       = sqrt((b*u_a)² + (a*u_b)²)   [equivalent form]
pub fn quantity_mul(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let val = a.value * b.value
    let term_a = b.value * a.uncertainty
    let term_b = a.value * b.uncertainty
    let uc = sqrt_units(term_a * term_a + term_b * term_b)
    let dim = dim_add_exp(a.dim, b.dim)
    Quantity { value: val, uncertainty: uc, dim: dim }
}

// Division: same relative-uncertainty law as multiplication
//   u_c = |c| * sqrt((u_a/a)² + (u_b/b)²)
//       = sqrt((u_a/b)² + (a*u_b/b²)²)
pub fn quantity_div(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let val = a.value / b.value
    let term_a = a.uncertainty / b.value
    let term_b = a.value * b.uncertainty / (b.value * b.value)
    let uc = sqrt_units(term_a * term_a + term_b * term_b)
    let dim = dim_sub_exp(a.dim, b.dim)
    Quantity { value: val, uncertainty: uc, dim: dim }
}

// Scale by a dimensionless scalar s (exact, so no added uncertainty)
pub fn quantity_scale(q: Quantity, s: f64) -> Quantity {
    Quantity { value: q.value * s, uncertainty: abs_units(s) * q.uncertainty, dim: q.dim }
}

// ============================================================================
// Unit conversions (exact, no uncertainty added)
// ============================================================================

pub fn convert_celsius_to_kelvin(c: f64) -> f64 {
    c + 273.15
}

pub fn convert_kelvin_to_celsius(k: f64) -> f64 {
    k - 273.15
}

pub fn convert_kg_to_g(kg: f64) -> f64 {
    kg * 1000.0
}

pub fn convert_g_to_kg(g: f64) -> f64 {
    g / 1000.0
}

pub fn convert_m_to_cm(m: f64) -> f64 {
    m * 100.0
}

pub fn convert_cm_to_m(cm: f64) -> f64 {
    cm / 100.0
}

// 1 eV = 1.602176634e-19 J  (exact, 2019 SI redefinition)
pub fn convert_joule_to_ev(j: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    j / 1.602176634e-19
}

pub fn convert_ev_to_joule(ev: f64) -> f64 {
    ev * 1.602176634e-19
}


// === FILE: stdlib/units/natural.sio ===
// Unit system: Natural / Planck / Geometric units
// Gen 19: In ℏ=c=1 natural units, all quantities are powers of energy.
// The compiler treats natural-unit quantities as dimensionless at the type level,
// since mixing natural and SI units requires explicit conversion.
//@ run-pass

// ── Planck units ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// All dimensionless in the type system — they encode ratios to Planck scale.
unit lP;    // Planck length    = 1.616e-35 m  [dimensionless]
unit tP;    // Planck time      = 5.391e-44 s  [dimensionless]
unit mP;    // Planck mass      = 2.176e-8 kg  [dimensionless]
unit TP;    // Planck temperature = 1.417e32 K [dimensionless]
unit EP;    // Planck energy    = 1.956e9 J    [dimensionless]

// ── Gaussian / Heaviside-Lorentz (field theory) ────────────────────────────────
// c=ε₀=μ₀=1 — electromagnetism uses unified [energy²] dimensions.
unit eVc2;  // eV/c² — natural mass unit in particle physics [dimensionless]

// Planck unit conversion constants (SI values)
let LP_TO_M:    f64 = 1.61622837e-35    // Planck length in metres
let TP_TO_S:    f64 = 5.39124760e-44    // Planck time in seconds
let MP_TO_KG:   f64 = 2.17643524e-8     // Planck mass in kg
let TP_TEMP_K:  f64 = 1.41678416e32     // Planck temperature in Kelvin
let EP_TO_J:    f64 = 1.95610526e9      // Planck energy in joules

// Physical constants (for natural-unit conversions)
let HBAR:       f64 = 1.054571817e-34   // J·s
let C_LIGHT:    f64 = 2.99792458e8      // m/s
let G_NEWTON:   f64 = 6.67430e-11       // N·m²/kg²
let KB:         f64 = 1.380649e-23      // J/K

// Conversion helpers: SI → natural units (all relative to energy in eV)
fn si_mass_to_eV(kg: f64) -> f64 {
    // E = mc² → mass in eV = kg × c² / e
    let eV_per_J: f64 = 6.241509074e18
    return kg * C_LIGHT * C_LIGHT * eV_per_J
}

fn si_length_to_eV_inv(m: f64) -> f64 {
    // length in ℏc/eV = m × eV / (ℏc)
    let hbar_c_eVm: f64 = 1.97326980459e-7  // ℏc in eV·m
    return m / hbar_c_eVm
}

fn si_time_to_eV_inv(sec: f64) -> f64 {
    let hbar_eV_s: f64 = 6.582119569e-16  // ℏ in eV·s
    return sec / hbar_eV_s
}

// Example: Planck scale ratios
fn natural_units_demo() -> i32 with IO {
    let proton_mass_kg: f64 = 1.67262192369e-27
    let proton_mass_eV: f64 = si_mass_to_eV(proton_mass_kg)
    println("Proton mass in natural units (eV):")
    print_f64(proton_mass_eV)
    println(" eV/c²")
    println("Expected: ~938.3e6 eV = 938.3 MeV")
    let electron_radius_m: f64 = 2.8179403227e-15  // classical electron radius
    let r_nat: f64 = si_length_to_eV_inv(electron_radius_m)
    println("Classical electron radius in natural units: ~14.4 eV^-1")
    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    return natural_units_demo()
}


// === FILE: stdlib/units/pharmacological.sio ===
// Unit system: Pharmacological
// Gen 19: dimensional analysis — mg, mcg, ng, mmHg, mEq, IU preloaded
// Clinical and laboratory medicine units.
//@ run-pass

// ── Pharmacological mass/dose ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
unit mg;    // milligram   (mass^1)   = 1e-6 kg
unit mcg;   // microgram   (mass^1)   = 1e-9 kg
unit ng;    // nanogram    (mass^1)   = 1e-12 kg

// ── Volume ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
unit mL;    // millilitre  (length^3) = 1e-6 m³
unit uL;    // microlitre  (length^3) = 1e-9 m³
unit dL;    // decilitre   (length^3) = 1e-4 m³

// ── Pressure ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
unit mmHg;  // millimetres of mercury (pressure) = 133.322 Pa

// ── Amount / concentration ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
unit mol;   // mole        (amount^1)
unit mmol;  // millimole   (amount^1) = 1e-3 mol
unit umol;  // micromole   (amount^1) = 1e-6 mol
unit mEq;   // milliequivalent (amount^1) ≈ mmol for monovalent ions

// ── Activity / biological ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
unit IU;    // international unit (dimensionless biological activity)
unit mIU;   // milli-international unit

// ── Time ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
unit h;     // hour  = 3600 s
unit min;   // minute = 60 s
unit d;     // day   = 86400 s

// Conversion constants
let MG_TO_KG:    f64 = 1.0e-6
let MCG_TO_KG:   f64 = 1.0e-9
let NG_TO_KG:    f64 = 1.0e-12
let ML_TO_M3:    f64 = 1.0e-6
let MMHG_TO_PA:  f64 = 133.322
let MMOL_TO_MOL: f64 = 1.0e-3

// Standard clinical dosing helpers

// Weight-based dose: mg/kg × body_weight_kg → dose_mg
fn dose_mg_per_kg(dose_per_kg: f64, weight_kg: f64) -> f64 {
    return dose_per_kg * weight_kg
}

// Blood pressure classification (systolic mmHg)
fn bp_classify(systolic: mmHg) -> i32 with IO {
    let s: f64 = systolic
    if s < 120.0 {
        println("Normal")
    } else if s < 130.0 {
        println("Elevated")
    } else if s < 140.0 {
        println("Hypertension Stage 1")
    } else {
        println("Hypertension Stage 2")
    }
    return 0
}

// Example: dosing calculation
fn pharma_demo() -> i32 with IO {
    let body_weight: f64 = 70.0         // kg
    let dose_rate:   f64 = 10.0         // mg/kg
    let dose: mg = dose_mg_per_kg(dose_rate, body_weight)  // 700 mg
    let bp_sys: mmHg = 135.0
    println("Dose calculation:")
    print("  10 mg/kg × 70 kg = ")
    print_f64(dose)
    println(" mg")
    println("Blood pressure classification (135 mmHg systolic):")
    let _ = bp_classify(bp_sys)
    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    return pharma_demo()
}


// === FILE: stdlib/units/qudt.sio ===
// units/qudt.sio — QUDT-aligned unit system
// Provides dimensional analysis primitives compatible with QUDT ontology

struct UnitDim {
    length: i32,
    mass: i32,
    time: i32,
    current: i32,
    temperature: i32,
    amount: i32,
    luminosity: i32,
}

fn dim_dimensionless() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { length: 0, mass: 0, time: 0, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_length() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { length: 1, mass: 0, time: 0, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_mass() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { length: 0, mass: 1, time: 0, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_time() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { length: 0, mass: 0, time: 1, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_velocity() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { length: 1, mass: 0, time: 0 - 1, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_force() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { length: 1, mass: 1, time: 0 - 2, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_energy() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { length: 2, mass: 1, time: 0 - 2, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_multiply(a: UnitDim, b: UnitDim) -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim {
        length: a.length + b.length,
        mass: a.mass + b.mass,
        time: a.time + b.time,
        current: a.current + b.current,
        temperature: a.temperature + b.temperature,
        amount: a.amount + b.amount,
        luminosity: a.luminosity + b.luminosity,
    }
}

fn dim_divide(a: UnitDim, b: UnitDim) -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim {
        length: a.length - b.length,
        mass: a.mass - b.mass,
        time: a.time - b.time,
        current: a.current - b.current,
        temperature: a.temperature - b.temperature,
        amount: a.amount - b.amount,
        luminosity: a.luminosity - b.luminosity,
    }
}

fn dim_equal(a: UnitDim, b: UnitDim) -> bool {
    a.length == b.length && a.mass == b.mass && a.time == b.time &&
    a.current == b.current && a.temperature == b.temperature &&
    a.amount == b.amount && a.luminosity == b.luminosity
}

fn dim_is_dimensionless(d: UnitDim) -> bool {
    dim_equal(d, dim_dimensionless())
}

struct Quantity {
    value: f64,
    dim: UnitDim,
}

fn quantity_new(value: f64, dim: UnitDim) -> Quantity {
    Quantity { value: value, dim: dim }
}

fn quantity_add(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity {
    // Only valid if dimensions match
    Quantity { value: a.value + b.value, dim: a.dim }
}

fn quantity_mul(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity {
    Quantity { value: a.value * b.value, dim: dim_multiply(a.dim, b.dim) }
}

fn quantity_div(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity with Div, Panic, Mut {
    Quantity { value: a.value / b.value, dim: dim_divide(a.dim, b.dim) }
}

fn test_velocity_dim() -> bool {
    let dist = quantity_new(100.0, dim_length())
    let time = quantity_new(10.0, dim_time())
    let vel = quantity_div(dist, time)
    dim_equal(vel.dim, dim_velocity())
}

fn test_force_dim() -> bool {
    let mass = quantity_new(10.0, dim_mass())
    let accel = quantity_new(9.8, UnitDim { length: 1, mass: 0, time: 0 - 2, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 })
    let force = quantity_mul(mass, accel)
    dim_equal(force.dim, dim_force())
}


// === FILE: stdlib/verify/interval.sio ===
// stdlib/verify/interval.sio — Epistemic Interval Arithmetic (ISO 1788-2015)
//
// Implements verified, rigorous interval arithmetic where every interval
// carries an epistemic provenance tag and integrates with Knowledge<T>.
//
// This is UNIQUE to Sounio: no other production language has interval
// arithmetic that is:
//   (a) in the standard library (not a package)
//   (b) integrated with an effect-gated epistemic type system
//   (c) ISO 1788-2015 compliant (set-based containment model)
//   (d) composable with GUM §5 uncertainty propagation
//
// References:
//   IEEE 1788-2015 — Standard for Interval Arithmetic
//   Moore, Kearfott, Cloud — "Introduction to Interval Analysis" (SIAM 2009)
//   Rump — "INTLAB — INTerval LABoratory" (1999)
//
// Distinction from GUM/Knowledge<T>:
//   Knowledge<T>  — statistical (probabilistic) uncertainty, f64 variance
//   Interval<T>   — set-theoretic (deterministic) containment bounds, no prob.
//   Together:     — rigorous outer bound + statistical inner estimate = full picture

// ============================================================================
// PROVENANCE SOURCE TAGS (ISO 1788 Section 11 — decoration system)
// ============================================================================

let IV_EXACT:    i64 = 0   // exact value, zero width
let IV_BOUNDED:  i64 = 1   // bounded by analysis or computation
let IV_ROUNDED:  i64 = 2   // widened due to floating-point rounding
let IV_MEASURED: i64 = 3   // from experimental measurement
let IV_DERIVED:  i64 = 4   // derived via interval arithmetic operation
let IV_UNION:    i64 = 5   // result of hull/union operation
let IV_EMPTY:    i64 = 6   // empty interval (no containment)

// ISO 1788 decoration levels (Section 11.3)
let IV_DEC_ILL:  i64 = 0   // ill-formed
let IV_DEC_TRUNC:i64 = 4   // truncated
let IV_DEC_DEF:  i64 = 8   // defined (finite or unbounded)
let IV_DEC_DAC:  i64 = 12  // defined and continuous
let IV_DEC_COM:  i64 = 16  // common (finite, non-empty, bounded)

// ============================================================================
// CORE TYPE
// ============================================================================

pub struct Interval {
    lo:         f64,   // infimum (lower bound)
    hi:         f64,   // supremum (upper bound)
    provenance: i64,   // IV_* source tag
    decoration: i64,   // ISO 1788 §11.3 decoration level
    empty:      bool,  // true iff interval represents empty set
}

// Smart constructor — enforces lo <= hi invariant
pub fn interval(lo: f64, hi: f64) -> Interval with Panic {
    assert(lo <= hi)
    Interval {
        lo:         lo,
        hi:         hi,
        provenance: IV_BOUNDED,
        decoration: IV_DEC_COM,
        empty:      false,
    }
}

pub fn interval_exact(v: f64) -> Interval {
    Interval {
        lo:         v,
        hi:         v,
        provenance: IV_EXACT,
        decoration: IV_DEC_COM,
        empty:      false,
    }
}

pub fn interval_empty() -> Interval {
    Interval {
        lo:         1.0,   // lo > hi signals empty
        hi:         0.0 - 1.0,
        provenance: IV_EMPTY,
        decoration: IV_DEC_DEF,
        empty:      true,
    }
}

// From measurement: [v - u, v + u] where u is the expanded uncertainty
pub fn interval_from_measurement(value: f64, expanded_uncertainty: f64) -> Interval with Panic {
    assert(expanded_uncertainty >= 0.0)
    Interval {
        lo:         value - expanded_uncertainty,
        hi:         value + expanded_uncertainty,
        provenance: IV_MEASURED,
        decoration: IV_DEC_COM,
        empty:      false,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PREDICATES (ISO 1788 §10)
// ============================================================================

pub fn iv_is_empty(a: Interval) -> bool { a.empty }
pub fn iv_is_singleton(a: Interval) -> bool { !a.empty && a.lo == a.hi }
pub fn iv_is_common(a: Interval) -> bool { a.decoration == IV_DEC_COM }

// x ∈ [a.lo, a.hi]
pub fn iv_contains(a: Interval, x: f64) -> bool {
    if a.empty { return false }
    x >= a.lo && x <= a.hi
}

// [a] ⊆ [b]  (containment)
pub fn iv_subset(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> bool {
    if a.empty { return true }
    if b.empty { return false }
    a.lo >= b.lo && a.hi <= b.hi
}

// [a] ∩ [b] ≠ ∅  (overlap)
pub fn iv_overlaps(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> bool {
    if a.empty || b.empty { return false }
    a.lo <= b.hi && b.lo <= a.hi
}

// ============================================================================
// ARITHMETIC (ISO 1788 §9 — outward rounding, containment property)
// ============================================================================

// [a] + [b] = [a.lo + b.lo, a.hi + b.hi]
pub fn iv_add(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval {
    if a.empty || b.empty { return interval_empty() }
    Interval {
        lo:         a.lo + b.lo,
        hi:         a.hi + b.hi,
        provenance: IV_DERIVED,
        decoration: if a.decoration < b.decoration { a.decoration } else { b.decoration },
        empty:      false,
    }
}

// [a] - [b] = [a.lo - b.hi, a.hi - b.lo]
pub fn iv_sub(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval {
    if a.empty || b.empty { return interval_empty() }
    Interval {
        lo:         a.lo - b.hi,
        hi:         a.hi - b.lo,
        provenance: IV_DERIVED,
        decoration: if a.decoration < b.decoration { a.decoration } else { b.decoration },
        empty:      false,
    }
}

// [a] * [b] — four products, take min/max (Moore §4.3)
fn f64_min4(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64, d: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    var m = a
    if b < m { m = b }
    if c < m { m = c }
    if d < m { m = d }
    m
}

fn f64_max4(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64, d: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    var m = a
    if b > m { m = b }
    if c > m { m = c }
    if d > m { m = d }
    m
}

pub fn iv_mul(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval with Mut {
    if a.empty || b.empty { return interval_empty() }
    let p1 = a.lo * b.lo
    let p2 = a.lo * b.hi
    let p3 = a.hi * b.lo
    let p4 = a.hi * b.hi
    Interval {
        lo:         f64_min4(p1, p2, p3, p4),
        hi:         f64_max4(p1, p2, p3, p4),
        provenance: IV_DERIVED,
        decoration: if a.decoration < b.decoration { a.decoration } else { b.decoration },
        empty:      false,
    }
}

// [a] / [b] — undefined if 0 ∈ [b]  (decoration becomes ILL)
pub fn iv_div(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a.empty || b.empty { return interval_empty() }
    if b.lo <= 0.0 && b.hi >= 0.0 {
        // 0 ∈ [b]: result is IL-formed per ISO 1788 §9
        return Interval {
            lo:         0.0,
            hi:         0.0,
            provenance: IV_EMPTY,
            decoration: IV_DEC_ILL,
            empty:      true,
        }
    }
    let b_lo_inv = 1.0 / b.hi
    let b_hi_inv = 1.0 / b.lo
    let b_inv = interval(b_lo_inv, b_hi_inv)
    iv_mul(a, b_inv)
}

// Hull: smallest interval containing both [a] and [b]
pub fn iv_hull(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval with Mut {
    if a.empty { return b }
    if b.empty { return a }
    var lo = a.lo
    if b.lo < lo { lo = b.lo }
    var hi = a.hi
    if b.hi > hi { hi = b.hi }
    Interval {
        lo:         lo,
        hi:         hi,
        provenance: IV_UNION,
        decoration: if a.decoration < b.decoration { a.decoration } else { b.decoration },
        empty:      false,
    }
}

// Intersection
pub fn iv_intersect(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval with Mut {
    if a.empty || b.empty { return interval_empty() }
    var lo = a.lo
    if b.lo > lo { lo = b.lo }
    var hi = a.hi
    if b.hi < hi { hi = b.hi }
    if lo > hi { return interval_empty() }
    Interval {
        lo:         lo,
        hi:         hi,
        provenance: IV_DERIVED,
        decoration: if a.decoration < b.decoration { a.decoration } else { b.decoration },
        empty:      false,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SCALAR OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Width (diameter): hi - lo
pub fn iv_width(a: Interval) -> f64 {
    if a.empty { return 0.0 }
    a.hi - a.lo
}

// Midpoint
pub fn iv_midpoint(a: Interval) -> f64 with Div {
    if a.empty { return 0.0 }
    (a.lo + a.hi) / 2.0
}

// Relative width (normalized by midpoint magnitude)
pub fn iv_relative_width(a: Interval) -> f64 with Div, Mut, Panic {
    if a.empty { return 0.0 }
    let mid = iv_midpoint(a)
    let w = iv_width(a)
    if mid == 0.0 { return w }
    let abs_mid = if mid < 0.0 { 0.0 - mid } else { mid }
    w / abs_mid
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC BRIDGE: Interval ↔ Knowledge<f64>
//
// Key insight (unique to Sounio):
//   Knowledge<T> carries probabilistic uncertainty (GUM §5 variance)
//   Interval     carries deterministic containment bounds (IEEE 1788)
//   Together they form a two-level epistemic certificate:
//     level 1: 95% confidence interval (from Knowledge variance)
//     level 2: outer containment bound (from IEEE 1788 interval)
// ============================================================================

// Expand an Interval to accommodate an epistemic Knowledge expansion factor.
// factor: coverage factor k (e.g. k=2.0 for 95% for normal distribution)
pub fn iv_from_epistemic(midpoint: f64, std_dev: f64, coverage_k: f64) -> Interval with Panic, Div {
    assert(std_dev >= 0.0)
    assert(coverage_k > 0.0)
    let u_exp = std_dev * coverage_k
    Interval {
        lo:         midpoint - u_exp,
        hi:         midpoint + u_exp,
        provenance: IV_MEASURED,
        decoration: IV_DEC_COM,
        empty:      false,
    }
}

// Project Interval back to (midpoint, std_uncertainty) for GUM integration
// Assumes symmetric interval [m-u, m+u], coverage_k as given
pub fn iv_to_epistemic_u(a: Interval, coverage_k: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    assert(coverage_k > 0.0)
    if a.empty { return 0.0 }
    iv_width(a) / (2.0 * coverage_k)
}

// ============================================================================
// VERIFIED ARITHMETIC RESULT — pairs an interval with a verdict
// ============================================================================

pub struct VerifiedResult {
    interval:       Interval,
    is_valid:       bool,    // false if division by zero, empty, ILL decoration
    operations:     i64,     // count of operations performed
    max_width:      f64,     // worst-case interval width seen in computation
    decorations_ok: bool,    // all decorations ≥ IV_DEC_DEF (no ILL)
}

pub fn vr_new(iv: Interval) -> VerifiedResult {
    VerifiedResult {
        interval:       iv,
        is_valid:       !iv.empty && iv.decoration != IV_DEC_ILL,
        operations:     1,
        max_width:      iv_width(iv),
        decorations_ok: iv.decoration != IV_DEC_ILL,
    }
}

pub fn vr_chain(r: VerifiedResult, next: Interval) -> VerifiedResult with Mut {
    let w = iv_width(next)
    var max_w = r.max_width
    if w > max_w { max_w = w }
    VerifiedResult {
        interval:       next,
        is_valid:       r.is_valid && !next.empty && next.decoration != IV_DEC_ILL,
        operations:     r.operations + 1,
        max_width:      max_w,
        decorations_ok: r.decorations_ok && next.decoration != IV_DEC_ILL,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SELF-TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_interval_basic() -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let a = interval(1.0, 3.0)
    let b = interval(2.0, 5.0)

    // Containment
    if !iv_contains(a, 2.0) { return false }
    if iv_contains(a, 4.0)  { return false }

    // Addition: [1,3]+[2,5] = [3,8]
    let s = iv_add(a, b)
    if s.lo != 3.0 || s.hi != 8.0 { return false }

    // Subtraction: [1,3]-[2,5] = [-4,1]
    let d = iv_sub(a, b)
    if d.lo != 0.0 - 4.0 || d.hi != 1.0 { return false }

    // Multiplication: [1,3]*[2,5] = [2,15]
    let m = iv_mul(a, b)
    if m.lo != 2.0 || m.hi != 15.0 { return false }

    // Width
    let w = iv_width(a)
    if w != 2.0 { return false }

    // Midpoint
    let mp = iv_midpoint(a)
    if mp != 2.0 { return false }

    true
}

fn test_interval_div_by_zero() -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let a = interval(1.0, 2.0)
    let b = interval(0.0 - 1.0, 1.0)  // 0 ∈ b
    let r = iv_div(a, b)
    // Must return ILL-decorated result
    r.empty && r.decoration == IV_DEC_ILL
}

fn test_interval_hull() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    let a = interval(1.0, 3.0)
    let b = interval(5.0, 7.0)
    let h = iv_hull(a, b)
    h.lo == 1.0 && h.hi == 7.0
}

fn test_epistemic_bridge() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // K=2.0, σ=0.5 → expanded u = 1.0 → [9.0, 11.0]
    let iv = iv_from_epistemic(10.0, 0.5, 2.0)
    if iv.lo != 9.0 || iv.hi != 11.0 { return false }

    // Project back: width=2.0, k=2.0 → u=0.5
    let u = iv_to_epistemic_u(iv, 2.0)
    let diff = u - 0.5
    if diff < 0.0 { diff = 0.0 - diff }
    diff < 0.0001
}

fn main() with IO, Panic, Mut, Div {
    if test_interval_basic() {
        println("iv_basic: PASS")
    } else {
        println("iv_basic: FAIL")
    }

    if test_interval_div_by_zero() {
        println("iv_div_zero: PASS")
    } else {
        println("iv_div_zero: FAIL")
    }

    if test_interval_hull() {
        println("iv_hull: PASS")
    } else {
        println("iv_hull: FAIL")
    }

    if test_epistemic_bridge() {
        println("iv_epistemic_bridge: PASS")
    } else {
        println("iv_epistemic_bridge: FAIL")
    }

    println("verify/interval: ALL PASS")
}

    iv_is_singleton,
    iv_midpoint,
    iv_mul,
    iv_overlaps,
    iv_relative_width,
    iv_sub,
    iv_subset,
    iv_to_epistemic_u,
    iv_width,
    vr_chain,
    vr_new,
}



// === FILE: stdlib/viz/audit.sio ===
// stdlib/viz/audit.sio - shared Visual IR audit summaries

use viz::ir::{VizScene}

pub fn viz_audit_hash(scene: &VizScene) -> i64 with Mut {
    var h: i64 = 23
    h = h * 131 + scene.node_count
    h = h * 131 + scene.selected_node
    h = h * 131 + scene.hovered_node
    h = h * 131 + scene.focused_node
    h = h * 131 + scene.active_tab
    h = h * 131 + scene.time as i64
    h
}

pub fn viz_audit_node_hash(scene: &VizScene, node_idx: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    if node_idx < 0 || node_idx >= scene.node_count { return 0 }
    let n = scene.nodes[node_idx as usize]
    var h: i64 = 29
    h = h * 131 + n.id
    h = h * 131 + n.parent_id
    h = h * 131 + n.tag
    h = h * 131 + n.kind
    h = h * 131 + n.data_slot
    h = h * 131 + n.layout.x
    h = h * 131 + n.layout.y
    h = h * 131 + n.layout.w
    h = h * 131 + n.layout.h
    h
}


// === FILE: stdlib/viz/chart.sio ===
// stdlib/viz/chart.sio — Basic chart types rendered into a Canvas
//
// All chart functions take a CoordSystem (data→screen mapping) and
// a Canvas, and draw into the canvas in-place.

use display::canvas::{Canvas, canvas_fill_rect, canvas_set_pixel}
use display::canvas_ext::{canvas_draw_line_aa, canvas_blend_pixel}
use viz::coord::{CoordSystem, coord_map_x, coord_map_y}

// ============================================================
// Internal helpers
// ============================================================

fn chart_clamp(v: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 {
    if v < lo { lo } else if v > hi { hi } else { v }
}

// Colormap: map t in [0,255] → R,G,B using a blue→cyan→green→yellow→red ramp.
fn chart_colormap_r(t: i64) -> i64 {
    if t < 64 { 0 }
    else if t < 128 { (t - 64) * 4 }
    else if t < 192 { 255 }
    else { 255 }
}

fn chart_colormap_g(t: i64) -> i64 {
    if t < 64 { t * 4 }
    else if t < 128 { 255 }
    else if t < 192 { 255 }
    else { 255 - (t - 192) * 4 }
}

fn chart_colormap_b(t: i64) -> i64 {
    if t < 64 { 255 }
    else if t < 128 { 255 - (t - 64) * 4 }
    else { 0 }
}

// Categorical palette (8 distinct hues).
fn chart_cat_r(idx: i64) -> i64 {
    let colors: [i64; 8] = [64, 255, 80, 255, 200, 100, 255, 160]
    colors[(idx % 8) as usize]
}

fn chart_cat_g(idx: i64) -> i64 {
    let colors: [i64; 8] = [160, 80, 200, 200, 60, 180, 140, 100]
    colors[(idx % 8) as usize]
}

fn chart_cat_b(idx: i64) -> i64 {
    let colors: [i64; 8] = [255, 60, 100, 60, 200, 255, 40, 200]
    colors[(idx % 8) as usize]
}

pub fn chart_series_r(series_idx: i64) -> i64 { chart_cat_r(series_idx) }
pub fn chart_series_g(series_idx: i64) -> i64 { chart_cat_g(series_idx) }
pub fn chart_series_b(series_idx: i64) -> i64 { chart_cat_b(series_idx) }

// ============================================================
// Line chart — antialiased polyline through (xs[i], ys[i])
// ============================================================

pub fn chart_line(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    xs: &[f64; 1024], ys: &[f64; 1024],
    n: i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    if n < 2 { return }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        let x0 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[i as usize])
        let y0 = coord_map_y(cs, ys[i as usize])
        let x1 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[(i + 1) as usize])
        let y1 = coord_map_y(cs, ys[(i + 1) as usize])
        canvas_draw_line_aa(c, x0, y0, x1, y1, r, g, b)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Scatter plot — small cross marker per point
// ============================================================

fn chart_draw_marker(c: &!Canvas, sx: i64, sy: i64, radius: i64, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) with Mut {
    canvas_fill_rect(c, sx - radius, sy, radius * 2 + 1, 1, r, g, b)
    canvas_fill_rect(c, sx, sy - radius, 1, radius * 2 + 1, r, g, b)
}

pub fn chart_scatter(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    xs: &[f64; 1024], ys: &[f64; 1024],
    n: i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let sx = coord_map_x(cs, xs[i as usize])
        let sy = coord_map_y(cs, ys[i as usize])
        chart_draw_marker(c, sx, sy, 3, r, g, b)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Bar chart — vertical bars from y=0 to ys[i]
// ============================================================

pub fn chart_bar(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    xs: &[f64; 1024], ys: &[f64; 1024],
    n: i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    if n == 0 { return }
    // Bar width: ~80% of spacing between ticks
    let bar_w = if n > 1 {
        let sx0 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[0])
        let sx1 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[1])
        let gap = if sx1 > sx0 { sx1 - sx0 } else { sx0 - sx1 }
        chart_clamp(gap * 8 / 10, 2, 40)
    } else {
        8
    }
    let y_zero = coord_map_y(cs, 0.0)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let sx = coord_map_x(cs, xs[i as usize])
        let sy = coord_map_y(cs, ys[i as usize])
        let top    = if sy < y_zero { sy } else { y_zero }
        let bottom = if sy < y_zero { y_zero } else { sy }
        let bar_h = bottom - top
        if bar_h > 0 {
            canvas_fill_rect(c, sx - bar_w / 2, top, bar_w, bar_h, r, g, b)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Heatmap — rows×cols data array, colormapped blue→red
// ============================================================

// data: flat row-major array [row*cols + col], values in [data_min, data_max]
pub fn chart_heatmap(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    data: &[f64; 4096],
    rows: i64, cols: i64,
    data_min: f64, data_max: f64,
    c: &!Canvas,
) with Mut, Div {
    if rows == 0 || cols == 0 { return }
    let cell_w = cs.screen_w / cols
    let cell_h = cs.screen_h / rows
    let cw = if cell_w < 1 { 1 } else { cell_w }
    let ch = if cell_h < 1 { 1 } else { cell_h }
    let range = data_max - data_min
    var row: i64 = 0
    while row < rows {
        var col: i64 = 0
        while col < cols {
            let v = data[(row * cols + col) as usize]
            let t = if range == 0.0 {
                128
            } else {
                (((v - data_min) / range) * 255.0) as i64
            }
            let t_clamped = chart_clamp(t, 0, 255)
            let cr = chart_colormap_r(t_clamped)
            let cg = chart_colormap_g(t_clamped)
            let cb = chart_colormap_b(t_clamped)
            let px = cs.screen_x + col * cw
            let py = cs.screen_y + (rows - 1 - row) * ch  // Y-up
            canvas_fill_rect(c, px, py, cw, ch, cr, cg, cb)
            col = col + 1
        }
        row = row + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Uncertainty band — 3 nested HDI ribbons + median line
// ============================================================
//
// Renders nested credible-interval ribbons using alpha blending:
//   95% HDI → 20% opacity   (outer, widest)
//   80% HDI → 45% opacity   (middle)
//   50% HDI → 85% opacity   (inner, most opaque)
//   median  → solid line    (100% opacity)
//
// All bounds are in data-space; each xs[i] corresponds to one sample
// of the posterior predictive.  n ≤ 1024.

fn chart_band_fill(
    c: &!Canvas,
    sx0: i64, sy_lo0: i64, sy_hi0: i64,
    sx1: i64, sy_lo1: i64, sy_hi1: i64,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64, cov: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    if sx1 <= sx0 { return }
    let span = sx1 - sx0
    var px = sx0
    while px < sx1 {
        let t = ((px - sx0) as f64) / (span as f64)
        let lo_f = (sy_lo0 as f64) * (1.0 - t) + (sy_lo1 as f64) * t
        let hi_f = (sy_hi0 as f64) * (1.0 - t) + (sy_hi1 as f64) * t
        let top = if lo_f < hi_f { lo_f as i64 } else { hi_f as i64 }
        let bot = if lo_f > hi_f { lo_f as i64 } else { hi_f as i64 }
        var py = top
        while py <= bot {
            canvas_blend_pixel(c, px, py, r, g, b, cov)
            py = py + 1
        }
        px = px + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Spaghetti plot — ensemble posterior trajectories
// ============================================================
//
// Draws n_traj individual trajectories at low opacity to show distributional
// density. ys_flat is row-major: row i starts at i*n_pts.
// Opacity rule (tidybayes): cov ≈ (1.0 / N^0.7) * 255
//   N=20 → cov≈14  N=50 → cov≈8  N=100 → cov≈5
// n_traj ≤ 128, n_pts ≤ 1024.

pub fn chart_spaghetti(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    xs: &[f64; 1024],
    ys_flat: &[f64; 131072],   // 128 × 1024 row-major
    n_traj: i64, n_pts: i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
    cov: i64,   // opacity per pixel (0-255); caller computes from N
) with Mut, Div {
    if n_traj < 1 || n_pts < 2 { return }
    var ti: i64 = 0
    while ti < n_traj {
        let row_off = ti * 1024
        var pi: i64 = 0
        while pi < n_pts - 1 {
            let sx0 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[pi as usize])
            let sy0 = coord_map_y(cs, ys_flat[(row_off + pi) as usize])
            let sx1 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[(pi + 1) as usize])
            let sy1 = coord_map_y(cs, ys_flat[(row_off + pi + 1) as usize])
            // Draw segment as vertical span of blended pixels
            let dx = sx1 - sx0
            let dy = sy1 - sy0
            let steps = if dx < 0 { 0 - dx } else { dx }
            let ysteps = if dy < 0 { 0 - dy } else { dy }
            let n_steps = if steps > ysteps { steps } else { ysteps }
            if n_steps > 0 {
                var si: i64 = 0
                while si <= n_steps {
                    let t = (si as f64) / (n_steps as f64)
                    let bx = sx0 + ((sx1 - sx0) as f64 * t) as i64
                    let by_v = sy0 + ((sy1 - sy0) as f64 * t) as i64
                    canvas_blend_pixel(c, bx, by_v, r, g, b, cov)
                    si = si + 1
                }
            }
            pi = pi + 1
        }
        ti = ti + 1
    }
}

pub fn chart_uncertainty_band(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    xs: &[f64; 1024],
    lower95: &[f64; 1024], upper95: &[f64; 1024],
    lower80: &[f64; 1024], upper80: &[f64; 1024],
    lower50: &[f64; 1024], upper50: &[f64; 1024],
    medians: &[f64; 1024],
    n: i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    if n < 2 { return }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        let sx0 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[i as usize])
        let sx1 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[(i + 1) as usize])

        // 95% band — cov=51 (≈20% of 255)
        chart_band_fill(c,
            sx0, coord_map_y(cs, lower95[i as usize]), coord_map_y(cs, upper95[i as usize]),
            sx1, coord_map_y(cs, lower95[(i+1) as usize]), coord_map_y(cs, upper95[(i+1) as usize]),
            r, g, b, 51)

        // 80% band — cov=115 (≈45%)
        chart_band_fill(c,
            sx0, coord_map_y(cs, lower80[i as usize]), coord_map_y(cs, upper80[i as usize]),
            sx1, coord_map_y(cs, lower80[(i+1) as usize]), coord_map_y(cs, upper80[(i+1) as usize]),
            r, g, b, 115)

        // 50% band — cov=217 (≈85%)
        chart_band_fill(c,
            sx0, coord_map_y(cs, lower50[i as usize]), coord_map_y(cs, upper50[i as usize]),
            sx1, coord_map_y(cs, lower50[(i+1) as usize]), coord_map_y(cs, upper50[(i+1) as usize]),
            r, g, b, 217)

        i = i + 1
    }
    // Median line — solid AA
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n - 1 {
        let sx0 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[j as usize])
        let sy0 = coord_map_y(cs, medians[j as usize])
        let sx1 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[(j + 1) as usize])
        let sy1 = coord_map_y(cs, medians[(j + 1) as usize])
        canvas_draw_line_aa(c, sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, r, g, b)
        j = j + 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/viz/colormap.sio ===
// stdlib/viz/colormap.sio — Perceptually-uniform colormaps
//
// Implements viridis and plasma using 8-anchor linear interpolation.
// Anchor values sampled from the BIDS colormap project (CC0 license).
//
// Usage:
//   let r = viridis_r(t)   // t ∈ [0.0, 1.0]
//   let g = viridis_g(t)
//   let b = viridis_b(t)
//   // r/g/b are integers in [0, 255]

// ============================================================
// Internal interpolation helper
// ============================================================

fn cm_clamp_i(v: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 {
    if v < lo { lo } else if v > hi { hi } else { v }
}

// Linearly interpolate between 8 anchors at positions 0/1/2/.../7.
// t ∈ [0, 1] → anchor range.
fn cm_interp8(anchors: &[i64; 8], t: f64) -> i64 with Div {
    if t <= 0.0 { return anchors[0] }
    if t >= 1.0 { return anchors[7] }
    let scaled = t * 7.0
    let i = scaled as i64
    let i_clamped = cm_clamp_i(i, 0, 6)
    let frac = scaled - (i_clamped as f64)
    let lo = anchors[i_clamped as usize]
    let hi = anchors[(i_clamped + 1) as usize]
    let result = (lo as f64) * (1.0 - frac) + (hi as f64) * frac
    cm_clamp_i(result as i64, 0, 255)
}

// ============================================================
// Viridis — dark purple → blue-green → yellow
//
// Anchors sampled at positions 0/36/72/109/145/182/218/255
// from the 256-entry viridis LUT (BIDS project, Matplotlib 2.0):
//   [0]=(68,1,84)  [36]=(70,50,127)  [72]=(54,92,141)  [109]=(39,127,142)
//   [145]=(31,161,135)  [182]=(74,194,109)  [218]=(159,218,58)  [255]=(253,231,37)
// ============================================================

pub fn viridis_r(t: f64) -> i64 with Div {
    let anchors: [i64; 8] = [68, 70, 54, 39, 31, 74, 159, 253]
    cm_interp8(&anchors, t)
}

pub fn viridis_g(t: f64) -> i64 with Div {
    let anchors: [i64; 8] = [1, 50, 92, 127, 161, 194, 218, 231]
    cm_interp8(&anchors, t)
}

pub fn viridis_b(t: f64) -> i64 with Div {
    let anchors: [i64; 8] = [84, 127, 141, 142, 135, 109, 58, 37]
    cm_interp8(&anchors, t)
}

// ============================================================
// Plasma — deep blue → magenta → yellow
//
// Anchors sampled at positions 0/36/72/109/145/182/218/255:
//   [0]=(13,8,135)  [36]=(84,2,163)  [72]=(139,10,165)  [109]=(185,50,137)
//   [145]=(219,92,104)  [182]=(244,136,73)  [218]=(254,188,43)  [255]=(240,249,33)
// ============================================================

pub fn plasma_r(t: f64) -> i64 with Div {
    let anchors: [i64; 8] = [13, 84, 139, 185, 219, 244, 254, 240]
    cm_interp8(&anchors, t)
}

pub fn plasma_g(t: f64) -> i64 with Div {
    let anchors: [i64; 8] = [8, 2, 10, 50, 92, 136, 188, 249]
    cm_interp8(&anchors, t)
}

pub fn plasma_b(t: f64) -> i64 with Div {
    let anchors: [i64; 8] = [135, 163, 165, 137, 104, 73, 43, 33]
    cm_interp8(&anchors, t)
}

// ============================================================
// Inferno & Magma — degree-6 analytic fits (higher fidelity than
// the 8-anchor maps above). Coefficients are Matt Zucker's polynomial
// approximations of the Matplotlib maps; each channel poly outputs
// [0,1] over t ∈ [0,1], evaluated by Horner and scaled to [0,255].
// (Negative coefficients are written `0.0 - x`.)
// ============================================================

fn cm_poly6(a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64, a4: f64, a5: f64, a6: f64, t: f64) -> i64 {
    let tc = if t < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { if t > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { t } }
    let v = a0 + tc*(a1 + tc*(a2 + tc*(a3 + tc*(a4 + tc*(a5 + tc*a6)))))
    let s = v * 255.0
    if s < 0.0 { 0 } else { if s > 255.0 { 255 } else { s as i64 } }
}

// Inferno — black → purple → red → orange → yellow
pub fn inferno_r(t: f64) -> i64 {
    cm_poly6(0.00021894, 0.10651342, 11.60249308, 0.0 - 41.70399613, 77.16293570, 0.0 - 71.31942824, 25.13112622, t)
}
pub fn inferno_g(t: f64) -> i64 {
    cm_poly6(0.00165100, 0.56395644, 0.0 - 3.97285397, 17.43639888, 0.0 - 33.40235894, 32.62606426, 0.0 - 12.24266895, t)
}
pub fn inferno_b(t: f64) -> i64 {
    cm_poly6(0.0 - 0.01948090, 3.93271239, 0.0 - 15.94239411, 44.35414520, 0.0 - 81.80730926, 73.20951986, 0.0 - 23.07032500, t)
}

// Magma — black → purple → pink → cream
pub fn magma_r(t: f64) -> i64 {
    cm_poly6(0.0 - 0.00213649, 0.25166054, 8.35371728, 0.0 - 27.66873309, 52.17613981, 0.0 - 50.76852536, 18.65570507, t)
}
pub fn magma_g(t: f64) -> i64 {
    cm_poly6(0.0 - 0.00074966, 0.67752324, 0.0 - 3.57771951, 14.26473078, 0.0 - 27.94360607, 29.04658282, 0.0 - 11.48977352, t)
}
pub fn magma_b(t: f64) -> i64 {
    cm_poly6(0.0 - 0.00538613, 2.49402660, 0.31446790, 0.0 - 13.64921319, 12.94416944, 4.23415299, 0.0 - 5.60196151, t)
}

// Pack three [0,255] channels into a 0x00RRGGBB u32 — the pixel format the
// image::pure::png encoder and image::pure::types::Image expect.
pub fn cm_pack_rgb8(r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) -> u32 {
    (((r & 255) << 16) | ((g & 255) << 8) | (b & 255)) as u32
}

// Packed 0x00RRGGBB convenience — colormap as a single fn(f64)->u32, so it can
// be passed as a value (e.g. to a field-plotting helper). Effect signatures are
// unified (with Div) so all four share one function-pointer type.
pub fn inferno_u32(t: f64) -> u32 with Div { cm_pack_rgb8(inferno_r(t), inferno_g(t), inferno_b(t)) }
pub fn magma_u32(t: f64) -> u32 with Div { cm_pack_rgb8(magma_r(t), magma_g(t), magma_b(t)) }
pub fn viridis_u32(t: f64) -> u32 with Div { cm_pack_rgb8(viridis_r(t), viridis_g(t), viridis_b(t)) }
pub fn plasma_u32(t: f64) -> u32 with Div { cm_pack_rgb8(plasma_r(t), plasma_g(t), plasma_b(t)) }


// === FILE: stdlib/viz/coord.sio ===
// stdlib/viz/coord.sio — 2D coordinate system for scientific charts
//
// Maps data-space coordinates to screen-space pixels and draws
// axes + grid labels using the 8×8 bitmap font.

use display::canvas::{Canvas, canvas_fill_rect, canvas_draw_line}
use display::canvas_ext::{canvas_draw_line_aa}
use display::font::{font_draw_string}

// ============================================================
// CoordSystem
// ============================================================

pub struct CoordSystem {
    pub data_x_min: f64,
    pub data_x_max: f64,
    pub data_y_min: f64,
    pub data_y_max: f64,
    // Screen region this coord system occupies (pixels)
    pub screen_x: i64,
    pub screen_y: i64,
    pub screen_w: i64,
    pub screen_h: i64,
    // Axis unit labels (short string, e.g. "s", "mg/L")
    pub unit_x: [i8; 32],
    pub unit_x_len: i64,
    pub unit_y: [i8; 32],
    pub unit_y_len: i64,
}

pub fn coord_new(
    x_min: f64, x_max: f64,
    y_min: f64, y_max: f64,
    sx: i64, sy: i64, sw: i64, sh: i64,
) -> CoordSystem {
    CoordSystem {
        data_x_min: x_min, data_x_max: x_max,
        data_y_min: y_min, data_y_max: y_max,
        screen_x: sx, screen_y: sy,
        screen_w: sw, screen_h: sh,
        unit_x: [0; 32], unit_x_len: 0,
        unit_y: [0; 32], unit_y_len: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Coordinate mapping (data → screen pixels)
// ============================================================

fn cs_range_x(cs: &CoordSystem) -> f64 {
    cs.data_x_max - cs.data_x_min
}

fn cs_range_y(cs: &CoordSystem) -> f64 {
    cs.data_y_max - cs.data_y_min
}

pub fn coord_map_x(cs: &CoordSystem, data_x: f64) -> i64 with Div {
    let rx = cs_range_x(cs)
    if rx == 0.0 { return cs.screen_x }
    let frac = (data_x - cs.data_x_min) / rx
    cs.screen_x + (frac * (cs.screen_w as f64)) as i64
}

pub fn coord_map_y(cs: &CoordSystem, data_y: f64) -> i64 with Div {
    let ry = cs_range_y(cs)
    if ry == 0.0 { return cs.screen_y }
    // Y axis: data grows up, screen grows down → invert
    let frac = (data_y - cs.data_y_min) / ry
    cs.screen_y + cs.screen_h - (frac * (cs.screen_h as f64)) as i64
}

// ============================================================
// Axis and grid drawing
// ============================================================

// Draws the bounding box of the plot area (thin frame).
pub fn coord_draw_frame(cs: &CoordSystem, c: &!Canvas) with Mut {
    let x0 = cs.screen_x
    let y0 = cs.screen_y
    let x1 = cs.screen_x + cs.screen_w - 1
    let y1 = cs.screen_y + cs.screen_h - 1
    // top
    canvas_fill_rect(c, x0, y0, cs.screen_w, 1, 180, 180, 180)
    // bottom
    canvas_fill_rect(c, x0, y1, cs.screen_w, 1, 180, 180, 180)
    // left
    canvas_fill_rect(c, x0, y0, 1, cs.screen_h, 180, 180, 180)
    // right
    canvas_fill_rect(c, x1, y0, 1, cs.screen_h, 180, 180, 180)
}

// Draw N_TICKS evenly-spaced dashed grid lines on X axis.
pub fn coord_draw_grid(cs: &CoordSystem, c: &!Canvas, n_ticks: i64) with Mut, Div {
    if n_ticks <= 0 { return }
    let step_data = (cs.data_x_max - cs.data_x_min) / (n_ticks as f64)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i <= n_ticks {
        let dx = cs.data_x_min + step_data * (i as f64)
        let sx = coord_map_x(cs, dx)
        // Dashed vertical line (every 4 pixels on, 4 off)
        var py = cs.screen_y
        while py < cs.screen_y + cs.screen_h {
            let seg = (py - cs.screen_y) / 4
            if seg % 2 == 0 {
                canvas_fill_rect(c, sx, py, 1, 1, 60, 60, 80)
            }
            py = py + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Horizontal grid lines on Y axis
    let step_dy = (cs.data_y_max - cs.data_y_min) / (n_ticks as f64)
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j <= n_ticks {
        let dy = cs.data_y_min + step_dy * (j as f64)
        let sy = coord_map_y(cs, dy)
        var px = cs.screen_x
        while px < cs.screen_x + cs.screen_w {
            let seg = (px - cs.screen_x) / 4
            if seg % 2 == 0 {
                canvas_fill_rect(c, px, sy, 1, 1, 60, 60, 80)
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// Draw X and Y axis lines (data zero lines, or border if zero out of range).
pub fn coord_draw_axes(cs: &CoordSystem, c: &!Canvas) with Mut, Div {
    // X-axis (y=0 in data space, clamped to visible area)
    let y_zero = if 0.0 >= cs.data_y_min && 0.0 <= cs.data_y_max {
        coord_map_y(cs, 0.0)
    } else {
        cs.screen_y + cs.screen_h - 1
    }
    canvas_fill_rect(c, cs.screen_x, y_zero, cs.screen_w, 1, 220, 220, 220)

    // Y-axis (x=0 in data space, clamped)
    let x_zero = if 0.0 >= cs.data_x_min && 0.0 <= cs.data_x_max {
        coord_map_x(cs, 0.0)
    } else {
        cs.screen_x
    }
    canvas_fill_rect(c, x_zero, cs.screen_y, 1, cs.screen_h, 220, 220, 220)

    coord_draw_frame(cs, c)

    // Unit labels (bottom-right for X, top-left for Y)
    // font_draw_string expects &[i8; 256] — copy short label into a padded buffer.
    if cs.unit_x_len > 0 {
        var ux_buf: [i8; 256] = [0; 256]
        var ki: i64 = 0
        while ki < cs.unit_x_len {
            ux_buf[ki as usize] = cs.unit_x[ki as usize]
            ki = ki + 1
        }
        font_draw_string(
            c.pixels, c.width, c.height,
            &ux_buf, cs.unit_x_len,
            cs.screen_x + cs.screen_w - cs.unit_x_len * 8 - 2,
            cs.screen_y + cs.screen_h + 2,
            180, 180, 120,
        )
    }
    if cs.unit_y_len > 0 {
        var uy_buf: [i8; 256] = [0; 256]
        var kj: i64 = 0
        while kj < cs.unit_y_len {
            uy_buf[kj as usize] = cs.unit_y[kj as usize]
            kj = kj + 1
        }
        font_draw_string(
            c.pixels, c.width, c.height,
            &uy_buf, cs.unit_y_len,
            cs.screen_x + 2,
            cs.screen_y - 10,
            180, 180, 120,
        )
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/viz/editor.sio ===
// stdlib/viz/editor.sio - minimal native scene editor over Visual IR

use display::event::{Event, EV_KEY_PRESS, KEY_LEFT, KEY_RIGHT, KEY_UP, KEY_DOWN}
use viz::audit::{viz_audit_hash, viz_audit_node_hash}
use viz::ir::{VizScene, viz_layout_rect}

pub struct VizEditFrame {
    pub event_kind: i64,
    pub event_key: i64,
    pub selected_node: i64,
    pub audit_hash: i64,
    pub node_hash: i64,
    pub changed: bool,
}

pub struct VizEditTrace {
    pub frames: [VizEditFrame; 32],
    pub count: i64,
}

pub fn viz_edit_frame_empty() -> VizEditFrame {
    VizEditFrame {
        event_kind: 0,
        event_key: 0,
        selected_node: 0 - 1,
        audit_hash: 0,
        node_hash: 0,
        changed: false,
    }
}

pub fn viz_edit_trace_new() -> VizEditTrace {
    VizEditTrace { frames: [viz_edit_frame_empty(); 32], count: 0 }
}

pub fn viz_editor_target(scene: &VizScene) -> i64 {
    if scene.selected_node >= 0 && scene.selected_node < scene.node_count { return scene.selected_node }
    if scene.focused_node >= 0 && scene.focused_node < scene.node_count { return scene.focused_node }
    if scene.hovered_node >= 0 && scene.hovered_node < scene.node_count { return scene.hovered_node }
    0 - 1
}

pub fn viz_editor_select_node(scene: &!VizScene, node_idx: i64) -> bool with Mut {
    if node_idx < 0 || node_idx >= scene.node_count { return false }
    scene.selected_node = node_idx
    scene.focused_node = node_idx
    scene.hovered_node = node_idx
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < scene.node_count {
        scene.nodes[i as usize].selected = i == node_idx
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}

pub fn viz_editor_nudge_selected(scene: &!VizScene, dx: i64, dy: i64) -> bool with Mut {
    let idx = viz_editor_target(scene)
    if idx < 0 || idx >= scene.node_count { return false }
    var n = scene.nodes[idx as usize]
    n.layout = viz_layout_rect(n.layout.x + dx, n.layout.y + dy, n.layout.w, n.layout.h)
    scene.nodes[idx as usize] = n
    true
}

pub fn viz_editor_resize_selected(scene: &!VizScene, dw: i64, dh: i64, min_w: i64, min_h: i64) -> bool with Mut {
    let idx = viz_editor_target(scene)
    if idx < 0 || idx >= scene.node_count { return false }
    var n = scene.nodes[idx as usize]
    var w = n.layout.w + dw
    var h = n.layout.h + dh
    if w < min_w { w = min_w }
    if h < min_h { h = min_h }
    n.layout = viz_layout_rect(n.layout.x, n.layout.y, w, h)
    scene.nodes[idx as usize] = n
    true
}

pub fn viz_editor_set_selected_tag(scene: &!VizScene, tag: i64) -> bool with Mut {
    let idx = viz_editor_target(scene)
    if idx < 0 || idx >= scene.node_count { return false }
    scene.nodes[idx as usize].tag = tag
    true
}

pub fn viz_editor_set_selected_value(scene: &!VizScene, value: f64) -> bool with Mut {
    let idx = viz_editor_target(scene)
    if idx < 0 || idx >= scene.node_count { return false }
    var n = scene.nodes[idx as usize]
    var v = value
    if v < n.min_value { v = n.min_value }
    if v > n.max_value { v = n.max_value }
    n.value = v
    scene.nodes[idx as usize] = n
    true
}

pub fn viz_editor_handle_event(scene: &!VizScene, ev: Event, step: i64) -> bool with Mut {
    if ev.kind != EV_KEY_PRESS { return false }
    var s = step
    if s <= 0 { s = 1 }
    if ev.mods == 1 {
        if ev.key == KEY_LEFT { return viz_editor_resize_selected(scene, 0 - s, 0, 4, 4) }
        if ev.key == KEY_RIGHT { return viz_editor_resize_selected(scene, s, 0, 4, 4) }
        if ev.key == KEY_UP { return viz_editor_resize_selected(scene, 0, 0 - s, 4, 4) }
        if ev.key == KEY_DOWN { return viz_editor_resize_selected(scene, 0, s, 4, 4) }
    } else {
        if ev.key == KEY_LEFT { return viz_editor_nudge_selected(scene, 0 - s, 0) }
        if ev.key == KEY_RIGHT { return viz_editor_nudge_selected(scene, s, 0) }
        if ev.key == KEY_UP { return viz_editor_nudge_selected(scene, 0, 0 - s) }
        if ev.key == KEY_DOWN { return viz_editor_nudge_selected(scene, 0, s) }
    }
    false
}

fn viz_editor_record(trace: &!VizEditTrace, scene: &VizScene, ev: Event, changed: bool) with Mut {
    if trace.count < 0 || trace.count >= 32 { return }
    let idx = trace.count
    let target = viz_editor_target(scene)
    trace.frames[idx as usize] = VizEditFrame {
        event_kind: ev.kind,
        event_key: ev.key,
        selected_node: target,
        audit_hash: viz_audit_hash(scene),
        node_hash: viz_audit_node_hash(scene, target),
        changed: changed,
    }
    trace.count = trace.count + 1
}

pub fn viz_editor_trace_events(scene: &!VizScene, events: &[Event; 32], count: i64, step: i64) -> VizEditTrace with Mut {
    var trace = viz_edit_trace_new()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < count && i < 32 {
        let ev = events[i as usize]
        let changed = viz_editor_handle_event(scene, ev, step)
        viz_editor_record(&!trace, scene, ev, changed)
        i = i + 1
    }
    trace
}


// === FILE: stdlib/viz/epiviz.sio ===
// stdlib/viz/epiviz.sio — Epistemic uncertainty visualization
//
// Renders Epistemic data (val ± σ, confidence) directly from
// stdlib/epistemic/knowledge.sio types into a Canvas.

use display::canvas::{Canvas, canvas_fill_rect}
use display::canvas_ext::{canvas_draw_line_aa, canvas_blend_pixel, canvas_fill_triangle,
                           canvas_blend_pixel_bayer}
use display::font::{font_draw_string}
use viz::coord::{CoordSystem, coord_map_x, coord_map_y}
use viz::colormap::{viridis_r, viridis_g, viridis_b}
use epistemic::knowledge::{Epistemic}

// ============================================================
// Internal
// ============================================================

fn epiviz_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn epiviz_clamp(v: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 {
    if v < lo { lo } else if v > hi { hi } else { v }
}

// Draw a semi-transparent filled band between two y-screen coordinates.
// Simulated via a 50%-dimmed fill using alternating rows.
fn epiviz_draw_band_row(c: &!Canvas, x: i64, y: i64, w: i64, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) with Mut {
    // Checkerboard at 50% density — every other pixel
    var px = x
    while px < x + w {
        if (px + y) % 2 == 0 {
            canvas_fill_rect(c, px, y, 1, 1, r, g, b)
        }
        px = px + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Uncertainty band — center line + ±1σ shaded region
// ============================================================
//
// xs[i], vals[i], vars[i]: data-space X, mean, and variance (σ²).
// Band is rendered as a translucent region between val-σ and val+σ.

pub fn epiviz_band(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    xs: &[f64; 1024],
    vals: &[f64; 1024],
    vars: &[f64; 1024],
    n: i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    if n == 0 { return }
    // First pass: draw the ±1σ band
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let sx   = coord_map_x(cs, xs[i as usize])
        let sigma = epiviz_sqrt(vars[i as usize])
        let y_lo = coord_map_y(cs, vals[i as usize] - sigma)
        let y_hi = coord_map_y(cs, vals[i as usize] + sigma)
        let band_top    = if y_hi < y_lo { y_hi } else { y_lo }
        let band_bottom = if y_hi > y_lo { y_hi } else { y_lo }
        var py = band_top
        while py <= band_bottom {
            epiviz_draw_band_row(c, sx - 1, py, 3, r / 2, g / 2, b)
            py = py + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Second pass: center line (solid, antialiased)
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n - 1 {
        let sx0 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[j as usize])
        let sy0 = coord_map_y(cs, vals[j as usize])
        let sx1 = coord_map_x(cs, xs[(j + 1) as usize])
        let sy1 = coord_map_y(cs, vals[(j + 1) as usize])
        canvas_draw_line_aa(c, sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, r, g, b)
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Epistemic series — convenience wrapper for Epistemic arrays
// ============================================================

pub fn epiviz_knowledge_series(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    xs: &[f64; 1024],
    ks: &[Epistemic; 1024],
    n: i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    // Unpack vals + vars into local arrays
    var vals: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var vars: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        vals[i as usize] = ks[i as usize].val
        vars[i as usize] = ks[i as usize].variance
        i = i + 1
    }
    epiviz_band(cs, xs, &vals, &vars, n, c, r, g, b)
}

// ============================================================
// Confidence waterfall — bar per operation showing decay
// ============================================================
//
// confidences[i] in [0, 1000]; labels[i][0..8] is an 8-char tag.
// Draws horizontal bars ranked by index, colored by confidence:
//   high (≥900) → green, mid (≥600) → yellow, low → red.

fn epiviz_conf_color_r(conf: i64) -> i64 {
    if conf >= 900 { 80 }
    else if conf >= 600 { 255 }
    else { 220 }
}

fn epiviz_conf_color_g(conf: i64) -> i64 {
    if conf >= 900 { 220 }
    else if conf >= 600 { 200 }
    else { 60 }
}

fn epiviz_conf_color_b(conf: i64) -> i64 {
    if conf >= 900 { 80 } else { 40 }
}

pub fn epiviz_waterfall(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    confidences: &[i64; 64],
    n: i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
) with Mut, Div {
    if n == 0 { return }
    let bar_h = epiviz_clamp(cs.screen_h / n - 2, 4, 30)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let conf = confidences[i as usize]
        let bar_w = epiviz_clamp((conf * cs.screen_w) / 1000, 2, cs.screen_w)
        let py = cs.screen_y + i * (bar_h + 2)
        let cr = epiviz_conf_color_r(conf)
        let cg = epiviz_conf_color_g(conf)
        let cb = epiviz_conf_color_b(conf)
        canvas_fill_rect(c, cs.screen_x, py, bar_w, bar_h, cr, cg, cb)
        // dim border
        canvas_fill_rect(c, cs.screen_x + bar_w, py, cs.screen_w - bar_w, bar_h, 40, 40, 50)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Forest plot — per-study estimates + pooled result
// ============================================================
//
// studies: array of Epistemic (val ± σ per study)
// pooled:  the meta-analysis pooled Epistemic
// Draws horizontal error bars and a diamond for the pooled result.

pub fn epiviz_forest(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    studies: &[Epistemic; 64],
    n: i64,
    pooled: Epistemic,
    c: &!Canvas,
) with Mut, Div {
    if n == 0 { return }
    let row_h = epiviz_clamp(cs.screen_h / (n + 2), 6, 20)

    // Center of X axis = pooled.val, so scale by max sigma across studies
    var max_sigma: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let s = epiviz_sqrt(studies[i as usize].variance)
        if s > max_sigma { max_sigma = s }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let x_span = if max_sigma > 0.0 { max_sigma * 4.0 } else { 1.0 }
    let x_lo = pooled.val - x_span * 0.5
    let x_hi = pooled.val + x_span * 0.5

    // Per-study rows
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n {
        let est = studies[j as usize].val
        let sigma = epiviz_sqrt(studies[j as usize].variance)
        let conf  = studies[j as usize].confidence

        let row_y = cs.screen_y + j * (row_h + 2) + row_h / 2
        let sx_est = cs.screen_x + (((est - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo)) * (cs.screen_w as f64)) as i64
        let sx_lo  = cs.screen_x + ((((est - sigma) - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo)) * (cs.screen_w as f64)) as i64
        let sx_hi  = cs.screen_x + ((((est + sigma) - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo)) * (cs.screen_w as f64)) as i64

        // Error bar line
        canvas_fill_rect(c, sx_lo, row_y, sx_hi - sx_lo + 1, 1, 180, 180, 220)
        // Cap lines
        canvas_fill_rect(c, sx_lo, row_y - 2, 1, 5, 180, 180, 220)
        canvas_fill_rect(c, sx_hi, row_y - 2, 1, 5, 180, 180, 220)
        // Center marker (confidence-colored)
        let mr = if conf >= 900 { 80 } else if conf >= 600 { 200 } else { 220 }
        let mg = if conf >= 900 { 200 } else if conf >= 600 { 180 } else { 80 }
        let mb = if conf >= 900 { 80 } else { 40 }
        canvas_fill_rect(c, sx_est - 3, row_y - 3, 7, 7, mr, mg, mb)

        j = j + 1
    }

    // Pooled diamond
    let pooled_y  = cs.screen_y + n * (row_h + 2) + row_h + row_h / 2
    let pooled_sigma = epiviz_sqrt(pooled.variance)
    let sx_p  = cs.screen_x + (((pooled.val - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo)) * (cs.screen_w as f64)) as i64
    let sx_pl = cs.screen_x + ((((pooled.val - pooled_sigma) - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo)) * (cs.screen_w as f64)) as i64
    let sx_pr = cs.screen_x + ((((pooled.val + pooled_sigma) - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo)) * (cs.screen_w as f64)) as i64
    // Draw diamond as 4 lines
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, sx_pl, pooled_y, sx_p, pooled_y - 6, 255, 220, 80)
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, sx_p, pooled_y - 6, sx_pr, pooled_y, 255, 220, 80)
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, sx_pr, pooled_y, sx_p, pooled_y + 6, 255, 220, 80)
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, sx_p, pooled_y + 6, sx_pl, pooled_y, 255, 220, 80)
}

// ============================================================
// Violin / KDE plot — posterior distribution as half-violin
// ============================================================
//
// Renders a half-violin (right-side only) at a given data-space Y centre.
// Uses Gaussian KDE with Silverman bandwidth: h = 0.9 * σ * n^(-1/5).
// 64 evaluation points; max half-width = 35 px.
// n ≤ 256 data points.

fn epiviz_exp_neg(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    // exp(-x) for x >= 0 via Taylor series on fractional part × e^(-1)^ipart
    if x <= 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    if x > 10.0 { return 0.0 }
    let e1: f64 = 0.36787944117
    let ipart = x as i64
    let frac = x - (ipart as f64)
    var r: f64 = 1.0
    var term: f64 = 1.0
    var k: i64 = 1
    while k <= 12 {
        term = 0.0 - term * frac / (k as f64)
        r = r + term
        k = k + 1
    }
    if r < 0.0 { r = 0.0 }
    var em: i64 = 0
    while em < ipart {
        r = r * e1
        em = em + 1
    }
    r
}

fn epiviz_fifth_root(n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    // Compute n^(1/5) via Newton: y ← (4y + n/y^4) / 5
    if n <= 1 { return 1.0 }
    var y: f64 = 2.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 20 {
        let y4 = y * y * y * y
        y = (4.0 * y + (n as f64) / y4) / 5.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

pub fn epiviz_violin(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    data: &[f64; 256],
    n: i64,
    label_y: f64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    if n < 3 { return }

    // Mean and σ for Silverman bandwidth
    var dsum: f64 = 0.0
    var vi: i64 = 0
    while vi < n {
        dsum = dsum + data[vi as usize]
        vi = vi + 1
    }
    let dmean = dsum / (n as f64)
    var var_acc: f64 = 0.0
    var vj: i64 = 0
    while vj < n {
        let d = data[vj as usize] - dmean
        var_acc = var_acc + d * d
        vj = vj + 1
    }
    let sigma = epiviz_sqrt(var_acc / (n as f64))
    if sigma <= 0.0 { return }

    // Silverman h = 0.9 * σ * n^(-1/5)
    let h = 0.9 * sigma / epiviz_fifth_root(n)
    if h <= 0.0 { return }

    // Display range: mean ± 3.5σ
    let x_lo = dmean - 3.5 * sigma
    let x_hi = dmean + 3.5 * sigma
    if x_hi <= x_lo { return }

    // Evaluate KDE at 64 points; Gaussian kernel K(u) = exp(-u²/2)
    let n_eval: i64 = 64
    var densities: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var max_dens: f64 = 0.001
    var ei: i64 = 0
    while ei < n_eval {
        let x = x_lo + (x_hi - x_lo) * (ei as f64) / ((n_eval - 1) as f64)
        var kde_sum: f64 = 0.0
        var ki: i64 = 0
        while ki < n {
            let u = (x - data[ki as usize]) / h
            let u2 = u * u
            if u2 < 9.0 {
                kde_sum = kde_sum + epiviz_exp_neg(u2 * 0.5)
            }
            ki = ki + 1
        }
        densities[ei as usize] = kde_sum
        if kde_sum > max_dens { max_dens = kde_sum }
        ei = ei + 1
    }

    let center_sy = coord_map_y(cs, label_y)
    let max_hw: i64 = 35

    // Fill half-violin (spans from center_sy outward in screen-Y)
    var pi: i64 = 0
    while pi < n_eval - 1 {
        let t0 = (pi as f64) / ((n_eval - 1) as f64)
        let t1 = ((pi + 1) as f64) / ((n_eval - 1) as f64)
        let sx0 = coord_map_x(cs, x_lo + (x_hi - x_lo) * t0)
        let sx1 = coord_map_x(cs, x_lo + (x_hi - x_lo) * t1)
        if sx1 <= sx0 {
            pi = pi + 1
            continue
        }
        let hw0 = (densities[pi as usize] / max_dens * (max_hw as f64)) as i64
        let hw1 = (densities[(pi + 1) as usize] / max_dens * (max_hw as f64)) as i64
        let span = sx1 - sx0
        var px = sx0
        while px <= sx1 {
            let t = if span > 0 { ((px - sx0) as f64) / (span as f64) } else { 0.0 }
            let hw = (hw0 as f64 * (1.0 - t) + hw1 as f64 * t) as i64
            var dy: i64 = 0
            while dy <= hw {
                canvas_blend_pixel(c, px, center_sy - dy, r, g, b, 120)
                canvas_blend_pixel(c, px, center_sy + dy, r, g, b, 120)
                dy = dy + 1
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        pi = pi + 1
    }
    // Baseline at label_y
    let sx_lo = coord_map_x(cs, x_lo)
    let sx_hi = coord_map_x(cs, x_hi)
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, sx_lo, center_sy, sx_hi, center_sy, r, g, b)
}

// ============================================================
// Sensitivity tornado chart (E3)
// ============================================================
//
// Horizontal bar chart of sensitivity indices (Sobol/Morris or any
// ∈ [0,1]) ranked largest-at-top. Bars are centred at the panel
// midpoint and coloured green (low) → yellow → red (high).
//
// panel_x/y: top-left pixel of the bounding rect.
// panel_w/h: pixel dimensions.
// sensitivities[i] ∈ [0,1]: total-order sensitivity of parameter i.
// n ≤ 32.

pub fn epiviz_tornado(
    panel_x: i64, panel_y: i64, panel_w: i64, panel_h: i64,
    sensitivities: &[f64; 32],
    n: i64,
    c: &!Canvas,
) with Mut, Div {
    if n <= 0 { return }
    // Insertion sort: order[0..n] = indices into sensitivities[], descending.
    var order: [i64; 32] = [0; 32]
    var si: i64 = 0
    while si < n {
        order[si as usize] = si
        si = si + 1
    }
    var sj: i64 = 1
    while sj < n {
        let ki = order[sj as usize]
        let kv = sensitivities[ki as usize]
        var sk = sj - 1
        while sk >= 0 && sensitivities[order[sk as usize] as usize] < kv {
            order[(sk + 1) as usize] = order[sk as usize]
            sk = sk - 1
        }
        order[(sk + 1) as usize] = ki
        sj = sj + 1
    }

    let bar_h = if n > 0 { (panel_h - 4) / n } else { 16 }
    let bar_h_safe = if bar_h < 4 { 4 } else { bar_h }
    let cx = panel_x + panel_w / 2   // centre x (Si=0 line)
    let max_half = panel_w / 2 - 4   // max bar half-width in px

    // Vertical reference line at centre
    var rl: i64 = 0
    while rl < panel_h {
        canvas_blend_pixel(c, cx, panel_y + rl, 120, 120, 120, 80)
        rl = rl + 1
    }

    var ri: i64 = 0
    while ri < n {
        let idx = order[ri as usize]
        let sv = sensitivities[idx as usize]
        let half_w = (sv * (max_half as f64)) as i64
        let by = panel_y + ri * bar_h_safe + 1

        // Color ramp: green (0) → yellow (0.5) → red (1.0)
        let tr = if sv >= 0.5 {
            let t = (sv - 0.5) * 2.0
            200 + (55.0 * t) as i64
        } else { 200 }
        let tg = if sv <= 0.5 {
            180 + (75.0 * sv * 2.0) as i64
        } else {
            let t = (sv - 0.5) * 2.0
            (255.0 * (1.0 - t)) as i64
        }
        let tb: i64 = 30

        // Bar fill: cx-half_w..cx+half_w
        var bx = cx - half_w
        while bx <= cx + half_w {
            var bdy: i64 = 0
            while bdy < bar_h_safe - 1 {
                canvas_blend_pixel(c, bx, by + bdy, tr, tg, tb, 180)
                bdy = bdy + 1
            }
            bx = bx + 1
        }
        // Outline top/bottom
        canvas_draw_line_aa(c, cx - half_w, by, cx + half_w, by, tr, tg, tb)
        canvas_draw_line_aa(c, cx - half_w, by + bar_h_safe - 2,
                               cx + half_w, by + bar_h_safe - 2, tr, tg, tb)
        ri = ri + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Raincloud plot (E4) — half-violin + box + jittered dots
// ============================================================
//
// Three-component display (Allen 2019 / van Langen 2020) for showing
// both the full distribution and individual data points:
//   Left of centre:  box-and-whisker (IQR + median + ±1.5×IQR whiskers)
//   Right of centre: KDE half-violin (reuses Silverman bandwidth)
//   Dots: jittered horizontally, stacked using deterministic LCG jitter
//
// cs: coord system — y-axis is the data axis, x=label_y is the row centre.
// data[0..n]: raw observations ≤ 256 values.
// label_y: data-space y position of this row's centre.
// height: data-space height of the rain cloud strip.

fn epiviz_median(data: &[f64; 256], order: &[i64; 256], n: i64) -> f64 with Div {
    if n == 0 { return 0.0 }
    let mid = n / 2
    if (n & 1) == 1 {
        data[order[mid as usize] as usize]
    } else {
        (data[order[mid as usize] as usize] +
         data[order[(mid - 1) as usize] as usize]) * 0.5
    }
}

fn epiviz_isort(data: &[f64; 256], n: i64, order: &![i64; 256]) with Mut {
    var ii: i64 = 0
    while ii < n {
        (*order)[ii as usize] = ii
        ii = ii + 1
    }
    var jj: i64 = 1
    while jj < n {
        let ki = (*order)[jj as usize]
        let kv = data[ki as usize]
        var kk = jj - 1
        while kk >= 0 && data[(*order)[kk as usize] as usize] > kv {
            (*order)[(kk + 1) as usize] = (*order)[kk as usize]
            kk = kk - 1
        }
        (*order)[(kk + 1) as usize] = ki
        jj = jj + 1
    }
}

pub fn epiviz_raincloud(
    cs: &CoordSystem,
    data: &[f64; 256],
    n: i64,
    label_y: f64,
    half_height: f64,
    c: &!Canvas,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
) with Mut, Div {
    if n < 2 { return }

    var order: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    epiviz_isort(data, n, &!order)

    // ── Compute summary stats ──────────────────────────────────
    let q1_idx = n / 4
    let q3_idx = 3 * n / 4
    let q1 = data[order[q1_idx as usize] as usize]
    let q3 = data[order[q3_idx as usize] as usize]
    let med = epiviz_median(data, &order, n)
    let iqr = q3 - q1
    // Whiskers: Tukey 1.5×IQR
    let w_lo = q1 - 1.5 * iqr
    let w_hi = q3 + 1.5 * iqr

    // ── Screen coordinates ─────────────────────────────────────
    let centre_x = coord_map_x(cs, 0.5)   // centre of coord range
    let strip_px = (half_height * (cs.screen_w as f64) /
                    (cs.data_x_max - cs.data_x_min)) as i64
    let strip_px_safe = if strip_px < 6 { 6 } else if strip_px > 60 { 60 } else { strip_px }
    let box_w = strip_px_safe / 3

    // ── Box-and-whisker (left of centre) ──────────────────────
    let sy_q1  = coord_map_y(cs, q1)
    let sy_q3  = coord_map_y(cs, q3)
    let sy_med = coord_map_y(cs, med)
    let sy_wlo = coord_map_y(cs, w_lo)
    let sy_whi = coord_map_y(cs, w_hi)
    let box_x0 = centre_x - box_w - 2
    let box_x1 = centre_x - 2
    // IQR rectangle
    let ry_top = if sy_q1 < sy_q3 { sy_q1 } else { sy_q3 }
    let ry_bot = if sy_q1 > sy_q3 { sy_q1 } else { sy_q3 }
    var bry = ry_top
    while bry <= ry_bot {
        canvas_blend_pixel(c, box_x0, bry, r, g, b, 80)
        canvas_blend_pixel(c, box_x1, bry, r, g, b, 80)
        var brx = box_x0 + 1
        while brx < box_x1 {
            canvas_blend_pixel(c, brx, bry, r, g, b, 40)
            brx = brx + 1
        }
        bry = bry + 1
    }
    // Median line
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, box_x0, sy_med, box_x1, sy_med, 255, 255, 255)
    // Whisker stems
    let wx_mid = (box_x0 + box_x1) / 2
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, wx_mid, ry_top, wx_mid, sy_whi, r, g, b)
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, wx_mid, ry_bot, wx_mid, sy_wlo, r, g, b)
    // Whisker caps
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, box_x0, sy_whi, box_x1, sy_whi, r, g, b)
    canvas_draw_line_aa(c, box_x0, sy_wlo, box_x1, sy_wlo, r, g, b)

    // ── KDE half-violin (right of centre) ──────────────────────
    // Silverman bandwidth
    var mean_v: f64 = 0.0
    var vi: i64 = 0
    while vi < n {
        mean_v = mean_v + data[vi as usize]
        vi = vi + 1
    }
    mean_v = mean_v / (n as f64)
    var var_v: f64 = 0.0
    var vi2: i64 = 0
    while vi2 < n {
