//@ run-pass
// Door 4: real stdlib import — no more concatenation hack
use stdlib::epistemic::audit_runtime::*

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Audit {
    var log = audit_log_new()

    let e1 = audit_log_read(&!log, 12345, 0, 1024)
    let e2 = audit_log_transform(&!log, 1, e1, 0)
    let e3 = audit_log_test(&!log, 1, 2.45, 0.014, 0.52)

    let count = audit_log_count(&log)
    if count == 3 { println("T1 PASS: 3 entries logged") }
    else { println("T1 FAIL") }

    let entry0 = audit_get_entry(&log, 0)
    if entry0.entry_type == 0 { println("T2 PASS: first entry is data_read") }
    else { println("T2 FAIL") }

    let entry2 = audit_get_entry(&log, 2)
    if entry2.entry_type == 3 { println("T3 PASS: third entry is stat_test") }
    else { println("T3 FAIL") }

    // Keep the chained IDs live so the test also exercises return values.
    if e1 > 0 && e2 > e1 && e3 > e2 { println("T4 PASS: entity IDs chain") }
    else { println("T4 FAIL") }

    println("---")
    println("ALL PASS")
    0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/autodiff_forward.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Forward-Mode Automatic Differentiation Test Suite
//
// Self-contained implementation of forward-mode AD using dual numbers.
// A dual number (a + b*epsilon) where epsilon^2 = 0 carries both a value
// and its derivative through arithmetic operations automatically.
//
// All functions are inlined since tests cannot import.
//
// References:
//   Griewank & Walther, "Evaluating Derivatives" (2nd ed., SIAM, 2008)
//   Baydin et al., "Automatic Differentiation in Machine Learning: a Survey"
//       (JMLR 18, 2018)

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    abs_f64(a - b) < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL NUMBER STRUCT AND OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

// A dual number represents value + derivative*epsilon
// where epsilon is an infinitesimal with epsilon^2 = 0.
struct Dual {
    val: f64,   // primal value f(x)
    dot: f64,   // derivative f'(x) (tangent)
}

// Create a dual number representing a variable with derivative 1
fn dual_var(x: f64) -> Dual with Mut, Panic {
    Dual { val: x, dot: 1.0 }
}

// Create a dual number representing a constant (derivative 0)
fn dual_const(c: f64) -> Dual with Mut, Panic {
    Dual { val: c, dot: 0.0 }
}

// Addition: (a + b*eps) + (c + d*eps) = (a+c) + (b+d)*eps
fn dual_add(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic {
    Dual { val: a.val + b.val, dot: a.dot + b.dot }
}

// Subtraction: (a + b*eps) - (c + d*eps) = (a-c) + (b-d)*eps
fn dual_sub(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic {
    Dual { val: a.val - b.val, dot: a.dot - b.dot }
}

// Multiplication (product rule):
// (a + b*eps)(c + d*eps) = ac + (ad + bc)*eps  (eps^2 = 0)
fn dual_mul(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic {
    Dual {
        val: a.val * b.val,
        dot: a.val * b.dot + a.dot * b.val,
    }
}

// Division (quotient rule):
// (a + b*eps)/(c + d*eps) = a/c + (b*c - a*d)/(c^2) * eps
fn dual_div(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let val = a.val / b.val
    let dot = (a.dot * b.val - a.val * b.dot) / (b.val * b.val)
    Dual { val: val, dot: dot }
}

// Scale by a constant: c * (a + b*eps) = c*a + c*b*eps
fn dual_scale(c: f64, d: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic {
    Dual { val: c * d.val, dot: c * d.dot }
}

// Power by integer exponent (repeated multiplication)
fn dual_powi(base: Dual, n: i32) -> Dual with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if n == 0 {
        return dual_const(1.0)
    }
    if n == 1 {
        return base
    }
    var result = base
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        result = dual_mul(result, base)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// Reciprocal: 1/(a + b*eps) = 1/a + (-b/a^2)*eps
fn dual_recip(d: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let val = 1.0 / d.val
    let dot = (0.0 - d.dot) / (d.val * d.val)
    Dual { val: val, dot: dot }
}

// Negate: -(a + b*eps) = -a + (-b)*eps
fn dual_neg(d: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic {
    Dual { val: 0.0 - d.val, dot: 0.0 - d.dot }
}

// ============================================================================
// TRIGONOMETRIC FUNCTIONS ON DUALS (for extended tests)
// ============================================================================

fn floor_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let i = x as i32
    let f = i as f64
    if x < 0.0 && f != x { return f - 1.0 }
    return f
}

fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 6.283185307179586
    var t = x - floor_f64(x / two_pi) * two_pi
    if t > pi { t = t - two_pi }
    if t < 0.0 - pi { t = t + two_pi }
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var n = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        term = 0.0 - term * t * t / (((2 * n) as f64) * ((2 * n + 1) as f64))
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    return sum
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    return sin_f64(x + 1.5707963267948966)
}

// sin(a + b*eps) = sin(a) + b*cos(a)*eps
fn dual_sin(d: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic, Div {
    Dual { val: sin_f64(d.val), dot: d.dot * cos_f64(d.val) }
}

// cos(a + b*eps) = cos(a) - b*sin(a)*eps
fn dual_cos(d: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic, Div {
    Dual { val: cos_f64(d.val), dot: 0.0 - d.dot * sin_f64(d.val) }
}

// exp(a + b*eps) = exp(a) + b*exp(a)*eps
fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    let k_f = floor_f64(x / ln2 + 0.5)
    let k = k_f as i32
    let r = x - k_f * ln2
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n <= 25 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    var result = sum
    if k > 0 {
        var j = 0
        while j < k { result = result * 2.0; j = j + 1 }
    } else if k < 0 {
        var j = 0
        let neg_k = 0 - k
        while j < neg_k { result = result / 2.0; j = j + 1 }
    }
    return result
}

fn dual_exp(d: Dual) -> Dual with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let e = exp_f64(d.val)
    Dual { val: e, dot: d.dot * e }
}

// Test 1: d/dx(x^2) at x=3
// f(x) = x^2, f'(x) = 2x, f'(3) = 6
fn test_x_squared() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(3.0)
    let result = dual_mul(x, x)
    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, 9.0, tol)
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, 6.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 2: d/dx(x^3) at x=2
// f(x) = x^3, f'(x) = 3x^2, f'(2) = 12
fn test_x_cubed() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(2.0)
    let x2 = dual_mul(x, x)
    let result = dual_mul(x2, x)
    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, 8.0, tol)
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, 12.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 3: d/dx(1/x) at x=4
// f(x) = 1/x, f'(x) = -1/x^2, f'(4) = -1/16 = -0.0625
fn test_reciprocal() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(4.0)
    let one = dual_const(1.0)
    let result = dual_div(one, x)
    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, 0.25, tol)
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, 0.0 - 0.0625, tol)
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 4: Chain rule: d/dx(f(g(x))) where f(u)=u^2, g(x)=3x+1, at x=2
// g(2) = 7, f(7) = 49
// f'(g(x)) * g'(x) = 2*(3*2+1)*3 = 2*7*3 = 42
fn test_chain_rule() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(2.0)
    let three = dual_const(3.0)
    let one = dual_const(1.0)

    // g(x) = 3x + 1
    let g = dual_add(dual_mul(three, x), one)

    // f(g) = g^2
    let f = dual_mul(g, g)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(f.val, 49.0, tol)
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(f.dot, 42.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 5: Product rule: d/dx(x^2 * x^3) = d/dx(x^5) = 5x^4 at x=2
// f(x) = x^2 * x^3 = x^5, f'(2) = 5*16 = 80
fn test_product_rule() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(2.0)
    let x2 = dual_mul(x, x)           // x^2
    let x3 = dual_mul(x2, x)          // x^3 (using x as the same seed)
    let result = dual_mul(x2, x3)     // x^2 * x^3

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, 32.0, tol)   // 2^5 = 32
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, 80.0, tol)   // 5*2^4 = 80
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 6: Quotient rule: d/dx(x^2 / (x+1)) at x=3
// f(x) = x^2/(x+1), f'(x) = (2x(x+1) - x^2)/(x+1)^2 = (x^2 + 2x)/(x+1)^2
// f'(3) = (9 + 6)/(16) = 15/16 = 0.9375
fn test_quotient_rule() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(3.0)
    let one = dual_const(1.0)
    let numer = dual_mul(x, x)          // x^2
    let denom = dual_add(x, one)        // x+1
    let result = dual_div(numer, denom)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, 2.25, tol)       // 9/4 = 2.25
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, 0.9375, tol)     // 15/16
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 7: d/dx(constant) = 0
fn test_constant_derivative() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let c = dual_const(42.0)
    let tol = 1.0e-12
    let val_ok = approx_eq(c.val, 42.0, tol)
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(c.dot, 0.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 8: d/dx(x) = 1 (identity derivative)
fn test_identity_derivative() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(7.0)
    let tol = 1.0e-12
    let val_ok = approx_eq(x.val, 7.0, tol)
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(x.dot, 1.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 9: d/dx(sin(x)) = cos(x) at x=pi/4
// sin(pi/4) ~ 0.7071, cos(pi/4) ~ 0.7071
fn test_sin_derivative() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let pi_4 = 0.7853981633974483
    let x = dual_var(pi_4)
    let result = dual_sin(x)
    let expected_val = sin_f64(pi_4)
    let expected_dot = cos_f64(pi_4)
    let tol = 1.0e-8
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, expected_val, tol)
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, expected_dot, tol)
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 10: d/dx(exp(x)) = exp(x) at x=1
// exp(1) ~ 2.71828
fn test_exp_derivative() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(1.0)
    let result = dual_exp(x)
    let e = exp_f64(1.0)
    let tol = 1.0e-8
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, e, tol)
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, e, tol)  // d/dx(e^x) = e^x
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 11: Polynomial d/dx(3x^4 - 2x^2 + x - 5) at x=1
// f'(x) = 12x^3 - 4x + 1, f'(1) = 12 - 4 + 1 = 9
fn test_polynomial_derivative() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(1.0)
    let three = dual_const(3.0)
    let two = dual_const(2.0)
    let five = dual_const(5.0)

    let x2 = dual_mul(x, x)
    let x4 = dual_mul(x2, x2)

    // 3x^4
    let term1 = dual_mul(three, x4)
    // -2x^2
    let term2 = dual_neg(dual_mul(two, x2))
    // x
    let term3 = x
    // -5
    let term4 = dual_neg(five)

    let result = dual_add(dual_add(term1, term2), dual_add(term3, term4))

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    // f(1) = 3 - 2 + 1 - 5 = -3
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, 0.0 - 3.0, tol)
    // f'(1) = 12 - 4 + 1 = 9
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, 9.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 12: d/dx(sin(x)^2) = 2*sin(x)*cos(x) at x = pi/6
// sin(pi/6) = 0.5, cos(pi/6) ~ 0.866
// d/dx = 2 * 0.5 * 0.866 = 0.866
fn test_sin_squared() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let pi_6 = 0.5235987755982988
    let x = dual_var(pi_6)
    let sx = dual_sin(x)
    let result = dual_mul(sx, sx)  // sin(x)^2

    let s = sin_f64(pi_6)
    let c = cos_f64(pi_6)
    let expected_val = s * s
    let expected_dot = 2.0 * s * c

    let tol = 1.0e-8
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, expected_val, tol)
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, expected_dot, tol)
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 13: Composition d/dx(exp(sin(x))) at x = 0
// f(x) = exp(sin(x)), f'(x) = exp(sin(x)) * cos(x)
// f'(0) = exp(0) * cos(0) = 1 * 1 = 1
fn test_exp_sin_composition() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(0.0)
    let result = dual_exp(dual_sin(x))
    let tol = 1.0e-8
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, 1.0, tol)  // exp(sin(0)) = exp(0) = 1
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, 1.0, tol)  // exp(sin(0))*cos(0) = 1*1 = 1
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 14: d/dx(x / (1 + x^2)) at x = 1
// f(x) = x/(1+x^2), f'(x) = (1+x^2 - 2x^2)/(1+x^2)^2 = (1-x^2)/(1+x^2)^2
// f'(1) = (1-1)/(1+1)^2 = 0/4 = 0
fn test_lorentzian_derivative() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let x = dual_var(1.0)
    let one = dual_const(1.0)
    let numer = x
    let denom = dual_add(one, dual_mul(x, x))
    let result = dual_div(numer, denom)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, 0.5, tol)   // 1/(1+1) = 0.5
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, 0.0, tol)    // (1-1)/(2)^2 = 0
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

// Test 15: Higher-order: d^2/dx^2(x^3) at x=2, computed via nested duals
// We approximate by differentiating through a function that itself uses duals.
// d/dx(x^3) = 3x^2, d^2/dx^2(x^3) = 6x, so at x=2 => 12
// We verify by computing d/dx(3x^2) using a fresh dual pass.
fn test_second_derivative_via_composition() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // First pass: d/dx(x^3) at x=2 gives 3*4=12 (verified in test 2)
    // Second pass: compute d/dx(3x^2) at x=2
    //   3x^2 with x as dual_var(2): val=12, dot=12 (since d/dx(3x^2) = 6x = 12)
    let x = dual_var(2.0)
    let three = dual_const(3.0)
    let x2 = dual_mul(x, x)
    let result = dual_mul(three, x2)  // 3x^2

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(result.val, 12.0, tol)   // 3*4 = 12
    let dot_ok = approx_eq(result.dot, 12.0, tol)   // 6*2 = 12
    return val_ok && dot_ok
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("=== Forward-Mode Autodiff Tests ===")

    var passed = 0

    } else {
        println("FAIL")

    }

    print("Test  4: chain rule................ ")

    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  5: product rule (x^5)........ ")
    if test_product_rule() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  6: quotient rule............. ")
    if test_quotient_rule() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  7: constant derivative = 0... ")
    if test_constant_derivative() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  8: identity derivative = 1... ")
    if test_identity_derivative() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  9: d/dx(sin(x)) = cos(x).... ")
    if test_sin_derivative() {
        println("PASS")

    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1

    print("Test 10: d/dx(exp(x)) = exp(x).... ")
    if test_exp_derivative() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test 11: polynomial derivative..... ")
    if test_polynomial_derivative() {
        println("PASS")

    } else {
        println("FAIL")

    }

    print("Test 12: d/dx(sin(x)^2)........... ")

    if failed > 0 {

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/autodiff_forward_basic.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ description: Forward-mode autodiff via dual numbers — self-contained integration tests

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS (inlined from stdlib/autodiff/dual.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x > 20.0 { return exp_f64(x / 2.0) * exp_f64(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / exp_f64(0.0 - x) }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * x / 1.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 2.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 3.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 4.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 5.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 6.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 7.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 8.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 9.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 10.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 11.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 12.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 13.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 14.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 15.0; sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = y
    var term = y
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (2.0 * 3.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (4.0 * 5.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (6.0 * 7.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (8.0 * 9.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (10.0 * 11.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (12.0 * 13.0); sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (1.0 * 2.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (3.0 * 4.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (5.0 * 6.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (7.0 * 8.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (9.0 * 10.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (11.0 * 12.0); sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL NUMBER TYPE (inlined from stdlib/autodiff/dual.sio)
// ============================================================================

struct Dual {
    val: f64,
    dot: f64
}

fn dual_new(val: f64, dot: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: val, dot: dot }
}

fn dual_const(val: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: val, dot: 0.0 }
}

fn dual_add(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: a.val + b.val, dot: a.dot + b.dot }
}

fn dual_sub(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: a.val - b.val, dot: a.dot - b.dot }
}

fn dual_mul(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual {
        val: a.val * b.val,
        dot: a.dot * b.val + a.val * b.dot
    }
}

fn dual_exp(a: Dual) -> Dual with Mut {
    let e = exp_f64(a.val)
    return Dual { val: e, dot: a.dot * e }
}

fn dual_sin(a: Dual) -> Dual with Mut {
    return Dual { val: sin_f64(a.val), dot: a.dot * cos_f64(a.val) }
}

fn dual_cos(a: Dual) -> Dual with Mut {
    return Dual { val: cos_f64(a.val), dot: 0.0 - a.dot * sin_f64(a.val) }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic {
    var pass: i64 = 0
    var fail: i64 = 0

    // T1: d/dx(x²) at x=3 → 6
    // f(x) = x², f'(x) = 2x, f'(3) = 6
    let d1 = dual_new(3.0, 1.0)
    let r1 = dual_mul(d1, d1)
    if abs_f64(r1.dot - 6.0) < 0.001 {
        print("T1 PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("T1 FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // T2: d/dx(x³) at x=2 → 12
    // f(x) = x³, f'(x) = 3x², f'(2) = 12
    let d2 = dual_new(2.0, 1.0)
    let r2 = dual_mul(dual_mul(d2, d2), d2)
    if abs_f64(r2.dot - 12.0) < 0.001 {
        print("T2 PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("T2 FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // T3: d/dx(x² + 2x + 1) at x=1 → 4
    // f(x) = x² + 2x + 1, f'(x) = 2x + 2, f'(1) = 4
    let d3 = dual_new(1.0, 1.0)
    let two3 = dual_const(2.0)
    let one3 = dual_const(1.0)
    let x2_3 = dual_mul(d3, d3)
    let twox3 = dual_mul(two3, d3)
    let r3 = dual_add(dual_add(x2_3, twox3), one3)
    if abs_f64(r3.dot - 4.0) < 0.001 {
        print("T3 PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("T3 FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // T4: d/dx(exp(x)) at x=0 → 1.0
    // f(x) = exp(x), f'(x) = exp(x), f'(0) = 1
    let d4 = dual_new(0.0, 1.0)
    let r4 = dual_exp(d4)
    if abs_f64(r4.dot - 1.0) < 0.001 {
        print("T4 PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("T4 FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // T5: d/dx(sin(x)) at x=0 → 1.0 (cos(0) = 1)
    // f(x) = sin(x), f'(x) = cos(x), f'(0) = 1
    let d5 = dual_new(0.0, 1.0)
    let r5 = dual_sin(d5)
    if abs_f64(r5.dot - 1.0) < 0.001 {
        print("T5 PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("T5 FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // T6: Chain rule — d/dx(exp(x²)) at x=1 → 2*exp(1) ≈ 5.436
    // f(x) = exp(x²), f'(x) = 2x*exp(x²), f'(1) = 2*exp(1) ≈ 5.4366
    let d6 = dual_new(1.0, 1.0)
    let x2_6 = dual_mul(d6, d6)
    let r6 = dual_exp(x2_6)
    let expected6 = 2.0 * exp_f64(1.0)
    if abs_f64(r6.dot - expected6) < 0.01 {
        print("T6 PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("T6 FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail == 0 {
        print("autodiff_forward_basic: ALL PASS\n")
        return 0
    }
    print("autodiff_forward_basic: SOME FAIL\n")
    return 1 as i32
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/autodiff_reverse.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation Test Suite
//
// Self-contained implementation of reverse-mode AD using a Wengert tape.
// The tape records operations during the forward pass, then the backward pass
// propagates gradients (adjoints) from output to inputs.
//
// All functions are inlined since tests cannot import.
//
// References:
//   Wengert, "A simple automatic derivative evaluation program",
//       Comm. ACM 7:8 (1964), 463-464
//   Griewank & Walther, "Evaluating Derivatives" (2nd ed., SIAM, 2008)

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    abs_f64(a - b) < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// TAPE DATA STRUCTURE
// ============================================================================

// Operation codes for the tape
// 0 = INPUT (leaf variable)
// 1 = CONST (constant value)
// 2 = ADD
// 3 = MUL
// 4 = SUB
// 5 = DIV

// Fixed-size tape: up to 64 nodes
// Each node stores: op code, two argument indices, value, and adjoint (gradient)
struct Tape {
    op: [i32; 64],      // operation code
    arg1: [i32; 64],    // first argument index (-1 for leaves)
    arg2: [i32; 64],    // second argument index (-1 for leaves)
    val: [f64; 64],     // computed value (forward pass)
    adj: [f64; 64],     // adjoint / gradient (backward pass)
    len: i32,           // number of nodes on tape
}

// ============================================================================
// TAPE OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

fn tape_new() -> Tape with Mut, Panic {
    Tape {
        op: [0; 64],
        arg1: [-1; 64],
        arg2: [-1; 64],
        val: [0.0; 64],
        adj: [0.0; 64],
        len: 0,
    }
}

// Push an input variable onto the tape. Returns its index.
fn tape_input(tape: Tape, x: f64) -> Tape with Mut, Panic {
    var t = tape
    let idx = t.len
    t.op[idx] = 0      // INPUT
    t.arg1[idx] = -1
    t.arg2[idx] = -1
    t.val[idx] = x
    t.adj[idx] = 0.0
    t.len = idx + 1
    return t
}

// Push a constant onto the tape. Returns modified tape.
fn tape_const(tape: Tape, c: f64) -> Tape with Mut, Panic {
    var t = tape
    let idx = t.len
    t.op[idx] = 1      // CONST
    t.arg1[idx] = -1
    t.arg2[idx] = -1
    t.val[idx] = c
    t.adj[idx] = 0.0
    t.len = idx + 1
    return t
}

// Record addition: result = tape[a] + tape[b]
fn tape_add(tape: Tape, a: i32, b: i32) -> Tape with Mut, Panic {
    var t = tape
    let idx = t.len
    t.op[idx] = 2      // ADD
    t.arg1[idx] = a
    t.arg2[idx] = b
    t.val[idx] = t.val[a] + t.val[b]
    t.adj[idx] = 0.0
    t.len = idx + 1
    return t
}

// Record multiplication: result = tape[a] * tape[b]
fn tape_mul(tape: Tape, a: i32, b: i32) -> Tape with Mut, Panic {
    var t = tape
    let idx = t.len
    t.op[idx] = 3      // MUL
    t.arg1[idx] = a
    t.arg2[idx] = b
    t.val[idx] = t.val[a] * t.val[b]
    t.adj[idx] = 0.0
    t.len = idx + 1
    return t
}

// Record subtraction: result = tape[a] - tape[b]
fn tape_sub(tape: Tape, a: i32, b: i32) -> Tape with Mut, Panic {
    var t = tape
    let idx = t.len
    t.op[idx] = 4      // SUB
    t.arg1[idx] = a
    t.arg2[idx] = b
    t.val[idx] = t.val[a] - t.val[b]
    t.adj[idx] = 0.0
    t.len = idx + 1
    return t
}

// Record division: result = tape[a] / tape[b]
fn tape_div(tape: Tape, a: i32, b: i32) -> Tape with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape
    let idx = t.len
    t.op[idx] = 5      // DIV
    t.arg1[idx] = a
    t.arg2[idx] = b
    t.val[idx] = t.val[a] / t.val[b]
    t.adj[idx] = 0.0
    t.len = idx + 1
    return t
}

// ============================================================================
// BACKWARD PASS
// ============================================================================

// Propagate adjoints backward from the output node (last node on tape).
// Sets adj[output_idx] = 1.0, then walks tape in reverse.
fn tape_backward(tape: Tape, output_idx: i32) -> Tape with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape

    // Seed the output adjoint
    t.adj[output_idx] = 1.0

    // Walk tape in reverse
    var i = output_idx
    while i >= 0 {
        let op = t.op[i]
        let a1 = t.arg1[i]
        let a2 = t.arg2[i]
        let g = t.adj[i]

        if op == 2 {
            // ADD: d(a+b)/da = 1, d(a+b)/db = 1
            t.adj[a1] = t.adj[a1] + g
            t.adj[a2] = t.adj[a2] + g
        } else if op == 3 {
            // MUL: d(a*b)/da = b, d(a*b)/db = a
            t.adj[a1] = t.adj[a1] + g * t.val[a2]
            t.adj[a2] = t.adj[a2] + g * t.val[a1]
        } else if op == 4 {
            // SUB: d(a-b)/da = 1, d(a-b)/db = -1
            t.adj[a1] = t.adj[a1] + g
            t.adj[a2] = t.adj[a2] - g
        } else if op == 5 {
            // DIV: d(a/b)/da = 1/b, d(a/b)/db = -a/b^2
            t.adj[a1] = t.adj[a1] + g / t.val[a2]
            t.adj[a2] = t.adj[a2] - g * t.val[a1] / (t.val[a2] * t.val[a2])
        }
        // op == 0 (INPUT) or op == 1 (CONST): nothing to propagate

        i = i - 1
    }

    return t
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Test 1: f(x,y) = x*y at (3,4)
// df/dx = y = 4, df/dy = x = 3
fn test_mul_grad() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 3.0)     // node 0: x = 3
    t = tape_input(t, 4.0)     // node 1: y = 4
    t = tape_mul(t, 0, 1)      // node 2: x * y = 12

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[2], 12.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 4.0, tol)    // df/dx = y = 4
    let dy_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[1], 3.0, tol)    // df/dy = x = 3
    return val_ok && dx_ok && dy_ok
}

// Test 2: f(x) = x^2 at x=5
// Record as x*x, df/dx = 2x = 10
fn test_square_grad() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 5.0)     // node 0: x = 5
    t = tape_mul(t, 0, 0)      // node 1: x * x = 25

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[1], 25.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 10.0, tol)   // df/dx = 2*5 = 10
    return val_ok && dx_ok
}

// Test 3: f(x,y) = x^2 + x*y at (2,3)
// df/dx = 2x + y = 4 + 3 = 7, df/dy = x = 2
fn test_mixed_grad() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 2.0)     // node 0: x = 2
    t = tape_input(t, 3.0)     // node 1: y = 3
    t = tape_mul(t, 0, 0)      // node 2: x^2 = 4
    t = tape_mul(t, 0, 1)      // node 3: x*y = 6
    t = tape_add(t, 2, 3)      // node 4: x^2 + x*y = 10

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[4], 10.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 7.0, tol)     // df/dx = 2x + y = 7
    let dy_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[1], 2.0, tol)     // df/dy = x = 2
    return val_ok && dx_ok && dy_ok
}

// Test 4: f(x) = x + x at x=3
// This tests that the adjoint of a shared variable accumulates correctly.
// df/dx = 2
fn test_add_shared() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 3.0)     // node 0: x = 3
    t = tape_add(t, 0, 0)      // node 1: x + x = 6

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[1], 6.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 2.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dx_ok
}

// Test 5: f(x,y) = (x + y)^2 at (1,2)
// f(x,y) = (x+y)^2 = 9, df/dx = 2(x+y) = 6, df/dy = 2(x+y) = 6
fn test_sum_squared() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 1.0)     // node 0: x = 1
    t = tape_input(t, 2.0)     // node 1: y = 2
    t = tape_add(t, 0, 1)      // node 2: x + y = 3
    t = tape_mul(t, 2, 2)      // node 3: (x+y)^2 = 9

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[3], 9.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 6.0, tol)
    let dy_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[1], 6.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dx_ok && dy_ok
}

// Test 6: f(x,y) = x - y at (5,3)
// df/dx = 1, df/dy = -1
fn test_sub_grad() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 5.0)     // node 0: x = 5
    t = tape_input(t, 3.0)     // node 1: y = 3
    t = tape_sub(t, 0, 1)      // node 2: x - y = 2

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[2], 2.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 1.0, tol)
    let dy_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[1], 0.0 - 1.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dx_ok && dy_ok
}

// Test 7: f(x,y) = x / y at (6,3)
// df/dx = 1/y = 1/3, df/dy = -x/y^2 = -6/9 = -2/3
fn test_div_grad() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 6.0)     // node 0: x = 6
    t = tape_input(t, 3.0)     // node 1: y = 3
    t = tape_div(t, 0, 1)      // node 2: x / y = 2

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[2], 2.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 1.0 / 3.0, tol)
    let dy_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[1], 0.0 - 2.0 / 3.0, tol)
    return val_ok && dx_ok && dy_ok
}

// Test 8: Longer expression: f(x) = (x+1)*(x-1) at x=3
// f(x) = x^2 - 1 = 8, f'(x) = 2x = 6
fn test_difference_of_squares() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 3.0)     // node 0: x = 3
    t = tape_const(t, 1.0)     // node 1: const 1
    t = tape_add(t, 0, 1)      // node 2: x + 1 = 4
    t = tape_sub(t, 0, 1)      // node 3: x - 1 = 2
    t = tape_mul(t, 2, 3)      // node 4: (x+1)*(x-1) = 8

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[4], 8.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 6.0, tol)     // df/dx = 2x = 6
    // Constant should have zero gradient (it's not an input we differentiate)
    // But constants accumulate adjoints from the expression too -- they just aren't used.
    return val_ok && dx_ok
}

// Test 9: f(x,y,z) = x*y + y*z at (2,3,4)
// df/dx = y = 3, df/dy = x + z = 6, df/dz = y = 3
fn test_three_vars() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 2.0)     // node 0: x = 2
    t = tape_input(t, 3.0)     // node 1: y = 3
    t = tape_input(t, 4.0)     // node 2: z = 4
    t = tape_mul(t, 0, 1)      // node 3: x*y = 6
    t = tape_mul(t, 1, 2)      // node 4: y*z = 12
    t = tape_add(t, 3, 4)      // node 5: x*y + y*z = 18

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[5], 18.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 3.0, tol)     // df/dx = y = 3
    let dy_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[1], 6.0, tol)     // df/dy = x + z = 6
    let dz_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[2], 3.0, tol)     // df/dz = y = 3
    return val_ok && dx_ok && dy_ok && dz_ok
}

// Test 10: f(x) = x^3 via x*x*x at x=2
// f(2) = 8, f'(2) = 3*4 = 12
fn test_cube_via_tape() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 2.0)     // node 0: x = 2
    t = tape_mul(t, 0, 0)      // node 1: x^2 = 4
    t = tape_mul(t, 1, 0)      // node 2: x^2 * x = x^3 = 8

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[2], 8.0, tol)
    // The adjoint of x accumulates from: x^2*x = mul(x^2, x)
    //   adj[0] += adj[2] * val[1]  (from second arg of mul at node 2) = 1*4 = 4
    //   adj[1] += adj[2] * val[0]  (from first arg of mul at node 2)  = 1*2 = 2
    // Then from node 1: x*x = mul(x,x)
    //   adj[0] += adj[1] * val[0]  (from first arg) = 2*2 = 4
    //   adj[0] += adj[1] * val[0]  (from second arg) = 2*2 = 4
    // Total: adj[0] = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 12.0, tol)    // 3*x^2 = 3*4 = 12
    return val_ok && dx_ok
}

// Test 11: Gradient of constant function f(x) = 5 should be 0
fn test_constant_grad() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 3.0)     // node 0: x = 3 (unused in output)
    t = tape_const(t, 5.0)     // node 1: const 5

    // The output is just the constant
    t = tape_backward(t, 1)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[1], 5.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 0.0, tol)     // df/dx = 0
    return val_ok && dx_ok
}

// Test 12: f(x) = c*x where c=7, at x=4
// f(4) = 28, df/dx = c = 7
fn test_scale_grad() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var t = tape_new()
    t = tape_input(t, 4.0)     // node 0: x = 4
    t = tape_const(t, 7.0)     // node 1: c = 7
    t = tape_mul(t, 1, 0)      // node 2: c * x = 28

    let output_idx = t.len - 1
    t = tape_backward(t, output_idx)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    let val_ok = approx_eq(t.val[2], 28.0, tol)
    let dx_ok = approx_eq(t.adj[0], 7.0, tol)     // df/dx = c = 7
    return val_ok && dx_ok
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("=== Reverse-Mode Autodiff (Wengert Tape) Tests ===")
    println("")

    var passed = 0
    var failed = 0

    print("Test  1: f(x,y) = x*y grad........ ")
    if test_mul_grad() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  2: f(x) = x^2 grad.......... ")
    if test_square_grad() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  3: f(x,y) = x^2 + x*y....... ")
    if test_mixed_grad() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  4: f(x) = x + x shared...... ")
    if test_add_shared() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  5: f(x,y) = (x+y)^2......... ")
    if test_sum_squared() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  6: f(x,y) = x - y grad...... ")
    if test_sub_grad() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  7: f(x,y) = x / y grad...... ")
    if test_div_grad() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  8: (x+1)*(x-1) diff of sq... ")
    if test_difference_of_squares() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test  9: f(x,y,z) three vars....... ")
    if test_three_vars() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test 10: x^3 via tape.............. ")
    if test_cube_via_tape() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test 11: constant gradient = 0..... ")
    if test_constant_grad() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test 12: scale f(x) = c*x......... ")
    if test_scale_grad() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    println("")
    print("Passed: ")
    println(passed)
    print("Failed: ")
    println(failed)

    if failed > 0 {
        println("SOME TESTS FAILED")
        return 1
    }
    println("ALL 12 TESTS PASSED")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/autodiff_tape_basic.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ description: Reverse-mode autodiff via Wengert tape — self-contained integration tests
//
// NOTE: The full tape implementation in stdlib/autodiff/tape.sio is ~1050 lines
// (20 individually-named node fields, 20 tape_set_N functions, full backward pass).
// Inlining all of it would exceed the practical self-contained limit. Instead, we
// implement a minimal 4-node reverse-mode tape manually that covers the three
// required test cases. For the complete tape API, see stdlib/autodiff/tape.sio.

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// MINIMAL REVERSE-MODE TAPE (4 nodes, covers T1-T3)
//
// Design: flat arrays over a fixed 4-node graph.
//   node i has: value[i], adjoint[i], op[i], p1[i], p2[i]
// op codes: 0=var, 2=add, 4=mul
// Backward is done inline per test (no dynamic dispatch needed for 4 ops).
// ============================================================================

fn op_var_c() -> i64 { 0 }
fn op_add_c() -> i64 { 2 }
fn op_mul_c() -> i64 { 4 }

struct MiniTape {
    v0: f64, v1: f64, v2: f64, v3: f64,
    a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64,
    op0: i64, op1: i64, op2: i64, op3: i64,
    p10: i64, p11: i64, p12: i64, p13: i64,
    p20: i64, p21: i64, p22: i64, p23: i64,
    size: i64
}

fn mini_tape_new() -> MiniTape {
    return MiniTape {
        v0: 0.0, v1: 0.0, v2: 0.0, v3: 0.0,
        a0: 0.0, a1: 0.0, a2: 0.0, a3: 0.0,
        op0: 0, op1: 0, op2: 0, op3: 0,
        p10: 0 - 1, p11: 0 - 1, p12: 0 - 1, p13: 0 - 1,
        p20: 0 - 1, p21: 0 - 1, p22: 0 - 1, p23: 0 - 1,
        size: 0
    }
}

// Get value by index
fn mt_val(t: MiniTape, i: i64) -> f64 {
    if i == 0 { return t.v0 }
    if i == 1 { return t.v1 }
    if i == 2 { return t.v2 }
    return t.v3
}

// Get adjoint by index
fn mt_adj(t: MiniTape, i: i64) -> f64 {
    if i == 0 { return t.a0 }
    if i == 1 { return t.a1 }
    if i == 2 { return t.a2 }
    return t.a3
}

// Get op by index
fn mt_op(t: MiniTape, i: i64) -> i64 {
    if i == 0 { return t.op0 }
    if i == 1 { return t.op1 }
    if i == 2 { return t.op2 }
    return t.op3
}

// Get parent1 by index
fn mt_p1(t: MiniTape, i: i64) -> i64 {
    if i == 0 { return t.p10 }
    if i == 1 { return t.p11 }
    if i == 2 { return t.p12 }
    return t.p13
}

// Get parent2 by index
fn mt_p2(t: MiniTape, i: i64) -> i64 {
    if i == 0 { return t.p20 }
    if i == 1 { return t.p21 }
    if i == 2 { return t.p22 }
    return t.p23
}

// Set adjoint by index — returns new tape
fn mt_set_adj(t: MiniTape, i: i64, a: f64) -> MiniTape {
    if i == 0 {
        return MiniTape {
            v0: t.v0, v1: t.v1, v2: t.v2, v3: t.v3,
            a0: a,    a1: t.a1, a2: t.a2, a3: t.a3,
            op0: t.op0, op1: t.op1, op2: t.op2, op3: t.op3,
            p10: t.p10, p11: t.p11, p12: t.p12, p13: t.p13,
            p20: t.p20, p21: t.p21, p22: t.p22, p23: t.p23,
            size: t.size
        }
    }
    if i == 1 {
        return MiniTape {
            v0: t.v0, v1: t.v1, v2: t.v2, v3: t.v3,
            a0: t.a0, a1: a,    a2: t.a2, a3: t.a3,
            op0: t.op0, op1: t.op1, op2: t.op2, op3: t.op3,
            p10: t.p10, p11: t.p11, p12: t.p12, p13: t.p13,
            p20: t.p20, p21: t.p21, p22: t.p22, p23: t.p23,
            size: t.size
        }
    }
    if i == 2 {
        return MiniTape {
            v0: t.v0, v1: t.v1, v2: t.v2, v3: t.v3,
            a0: t.a0, a1: t.a1, a2: a,    a3: t.a3,
            op0: t.op0, op1: t.op1, op2: t.op2, op3: t.op3,
            p10: t.p10, p11: t.p11, p12: t.p12, p13: t.p13,
            p20: t.p20, p21: t.p21, p22: t.p22, p23: t.p23,
            size: t.size
        }
    }
    return MiniTape {
        v0: t.v0, v1: t.v1, v2: t.v2, v3: t.v3,
        a0: t.a0, a1: t.a1, a2: t.a2, a3: a,
        op0: t.op0, op1: t.op1, op2: t.op2, op3: t.op3,
        p10: t.p10, p11: t.p11, p12: t.p12, p13: t.p13,
        p20: t.p20, p21: t.p21, p22: t.p22, p23: t.p23,
        size: t.size
    }
}

// Add a variable node to the tape — returns (tape, node_index)
struct TapeAndIdx { tape: MiniTape, idx: i64 }

fn mt_add_var(t: MiniTape, val: f64) -> TapeAndIdx with Mut {
    let i = t.size
    var t2 = MiniTape {
        v0: t.v0, v1: t.v1, v2: t.v2, v3: t.v3,
        a0: t.a0, a1: t.a1, a2: t.a2, a3: t.a3,
        op0: t.op0, op1: t.op1, op2: t.op2, op3: t.op3,
        p10: t.p10, p11: t.p11, p12: t.p12, p13: t.p13,
        p20: t.p20, p21: t.p21, p22: t.p22, p23: t.p23,
        size: i + 1
    }
    // Set value at slot i
    if i == 0 { t2.v0 = val; t2.op0 = op_var_c(); t2.p10 = 0 - 1; t2.p20 = 0 - 1 }
    if i == 1 { t2.v1 = val; t2.op1 = op_var_c(); t2.p11 = 0 - 1; t2.p21 = 0 - 1 }
    if i == 2 { t2.v2 = val; t2.op2 = op_var_c(); t2.p12 = 0 - 1; t2.p22 = 0 - 1 }
    if i == 3 { t2.v3 = val; t2.op3 = op_var_c(); t2.p13 = 0 - 1; t2.p23 = 0 - 1 }
    return TapeAndIdx { tape: t2, idx: i }
}

fn mt_add_op(t: MiniTape, val: f64, op: i64, p1: i64, p2: i64) -> TapeAndIdx with Mut {
    let i = t.size
    var t2 = MiniTape {
        v0: t.v0, v1: t.v1, v2: t.v2, v3: t.v3,
        a0: t.a0, a1: t.a1, a2: t.a2, a3: t.a3,
        op0: t.op0, op1: t.op1, op2: t.op2, op3: t.op3,
        p10: t.p10, p11: t.p11, p12: t.p12, p13: t.p13,
        p20: t.p20, p21: t.p21, p22: t.p22, p23: t.p23,
        size: i + 1
    }
    if i == 0 { t2.v0 = val; t2.op0 = op; t2.p10 = p1; t2.p20 = p2 }
    if i == 1 { t2.v1 = val; t2.op1 = op; t2.p11 = p1; t2.p21 = p2 }
    if i == 2 { t2.v2 = val; t2.op2 = op; t2.p12 = p1; t2.p22 = p2 }
    if i == 3 { t2.v3 = val; t2.op3 = op; t2.p13 = p1; t2.p23 = p2 }
    return TapeAndIdx { tape: t2, idx: i }
}

// Backward pass for a 4-node tape — propagates adjoints from output (last node)
fn mt_backward(t: MiniTape, out_idx: i64) -> MiniTape with Mut {
    // Seed the output adjoint
    var tape = mt_set_adj(t, out_idx, 1.0)

    // Traverse in reverse order
    var i = out_idx
    while i >= 0 {
        let cur_adj = mt_adj(tape, i)
        let cur_op = mt_op(tape, i)
        let p1 = mt_p1(tape, i)
        let p2 = mt_p2(tape, i)

        if cur_op == op_add_c() {
            // add: grad flows equally to both parents
            if p1 >= 0 {
                let a = mt_adj(tape, p1) + cur_adj
                tape = mt_set_adj(tape, p1, a)
            }
            if p2 >= 0 {
                let a = mt_adj(tape, p2) + cur_adj
                tape = mt_set_adj(tape, p2, a)
            }
        }

        if cur_op == op_mul_c() {
            // mul: grad_p1 = cur_adj * v_p2, grad_p2 = cur_adj * v_p1
            if p1 >= 0 {
                let p2_val = mt_val(tape, p2)
                let a = mt_adj(tape, p1) + cur_adj * p2_val
                tape = mt_set_adj(tape, p1, a)
            }
            if p2 >= 0 {
                let p1_val = mt_val(tape, p1)
                let a = mt_adj(tape, p2) + cur_adj * p1_val
                tape = mt_set_adj(tape, p2, a)
            }
        }

        i = i - 1
    }

    return tape
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic {
    var pass: i64 = 0
    var fail: i64 = 0

    // T1: f(x) = x² at x=3 → grad=6
    // Graph: node0=x(3), node1=x*x (mul, p1=0, p2=0)
    var ti1 = mini_tape_new()
    let r1a = mt_add_var(ti1, 3.0)
    ti1 = r1a.tape
    let x1_idx = r1a.idx
    // x*x: p1=x_idx, p2=x_idx, val=9
    let r1b = mt_add_op(ti1, 9.0, op_mul_c(), x1_idx, x1_idx)
    ti1 = r1b.tape
    let y1_idx = r1b.idx
    let bt1 = mt_backward(ti1, y1_idx)
    let grad1 = mt_adj(bt1, x1_idx)
    if abs_f64(grad1 - 6.0) < 0.001 {
        print("T1 PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("T1 FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // T2: f(x,y) = x + y at (2,3) → grad_x=1, grad_y=1
    // Graph: node0=x(2), node1=y(3), node2=x+y (add, p1=0, p2=1)
    var ti2 = mini_tape_new()
    let r2a = mt_add_var(ti2, 2.0)
    ti2 = r2a.tape
    let x2_idx = r2a.idx
    let r2b = mt_add_var(ti2, 3.0)
    ti2 = r2b.tape
    let y2_idx = r2b.idx
    let r2c = mt_add_op(ti2, 5.0, op_add_c(), x2_idx, y2_idx)
    ti2 = r2c.tape
    let z2_idx = r2c.idx
    let bt2 = mt_backward(ti2, z2_idx)
    let gx2 = mt_adj(bt2, x2_idx)
    let gy2 = mt_adj(bt2, y2_idx)
    if abs_f64(gx2 - 1.0) < 0.001 && abs_f64(gy2 - 1.0) < 0.001 {
        print("T2 PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("T2 FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // T3: f(x,y) = x*y at (2,3) → grad_x=3 (df/dx=y), grad_y=2 (df/dy=x)
    // Graph: node0=x(2), node1=y(3), node2=x*y (mul, p1=0, p2=1)
    var ti3 = mini_tape_new()
    let r3a = mt_add_var(ti3, 2.0)
    ti3 = r3a.tape
    let x3_idx = r3a.idx
    let r3b = mt_add_var(ti3, 3.0)
    ti3 = r3b.tape
    let y3_idx = r3b.idx
    let r3c = mt_add_op(ti3, 6.0, op_mul_c(), x3_idx, y3_idx)
    ti3 = r3c.tape
    let z3_idx = r3c.idx
    let bt3 = mt_backward(ti3, z3_idx)
    let gx3 = mt_adj(bt3, x3_idx)
    let gy3 = mt_adj(bt3, y3_idx)
    if abs_f64(gx3 - 3.0) < 0.001 && abs_f64(gy3 - 2.0) < 0.001 {
        print("T3 PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("T3 FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail == 0 {
        print("autodiff_tape_basic: ALL PASS\n")
        return 0
    }
    print("autodiff_tape_basic: SOME FAIL\n")
    return 1 as i32
}

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/bayesian_observe.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Test: Bayesian observation narrows variance
//
// A thermometer reads 37.2°C with variance 0.25 (±0.5°C).
// Our prior belief: body temperature is 37.0°C with variance 0.04 (±0.2°C).
// After observation: posterior should be closer to 37.0 with smaller variance.

fn bayesian_mean(val: f64, mv: f64, pm: f64, pv: f64) -> f64 with Div {
    let total = pv + mv
    if total == 0.0 { return val }
    let a = pv * val
    let b = mv * pm
    let sum = a + b
    sum / total
}

fn bayesian_var(mv: f64, pv: f64) -> f64 with Div {
    let total = pv + mv
    if total == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let prod = pv * mv
    prod / total
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Observe, Div, Mut {
    // Measurement: 37.2 ± 0.5 (variance = 0.25)
    let meas_val: f64 = 37.2
    let meas_var: f64 = 0.25

    // Prior: 37.0 ± 0.2 (variance = 0.04)
    let prior_mean: f64 = 37.0
    let prior_var: f64 = 0.04

    // Bayesian posterior
    let post_mean = bayesian_mean(meas_val, meas_var, prior_mean, prior_var)
    let post_var = bayesian_var(meas_var, prior_var)

    // Expected:
    //   post_mean = (0.04*37.2 + 0.25*37.0) / (0.04+0.25) = (1.488+9.25)/0.29 = 37.028
    //   post_var = (0.04*0.25) / 0.29 = 0.01/0.29 = 0.0345

    println("Posterior mean:")
    println(post_mean)
    println("Posterior variance:")
    println(post_var)

    // Variance MUST be less than both prior and measurement
    // (observation always narrows in normal-normal model)
    if post_var < prior_var {
        println("PASS: variance narrowed from prior")
    } else {
        println("FAIL: variance did not narrow")
        return 1
    }

    if post_var < meas_var {
        println("PASS: variance narrower than measurement alone")
    } else {
        println("FAIL: variance not narrower than measurement")
        return 1
    }

    // Posterior mean should be between prior and measurement
    let low = if prior_mean < meas_val { prior_mean } else { meas_val }
    let high = if prior_mean > meas_val { prior_mean } else { meas_val }
    if post_mean >= low {
        if post_mean <= high {
            println("PASS: posterior mean between prior and measurement")
        } else {
            println("FAIL: posterior mean out of range")
            return 1
        }
    } else {
        println("FAIL: posterior mean below range")
        return 1
    }

    println("ALL PASS: observation narrows uncertainty")
    0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/bdf64_test.sio ===
//@ run-pass
fn bdf_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn bdf_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn bdf_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut { if x<=0.0{return 0.0} var y=x;var i=0;while i<20{y=0.5*(y+x/y);i=i+1}y }
fn bdf_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div {
    if x>700.0{return 1.0e200} if x<0.0-700.0{return 0.0}
    var kf=x/0.6931471805599453;var k:i64=0
    if kf>=0.0{k=kf as i64}else{k=(kf as i64)-1}
    let r=x-(k as f64)*0.6931471805599453
    var s=1.0;var term=1.0;var n:i64=1
    while n<25{term=term*r/(n as f64);s=s+term;n=n+1}
    var result=s
    if k>=0{var i:i64=0;while i<k{result=result*2.0;i=i+1}}
    else{var i:i64=0;while i<(0-k){result=result/2.0;i=i+1}}
    result
}
fn bdf_rhs(rhs_id: i64, y: &[f64; 64], n: i64, out: &![f64; 64]) with Mut {
    var k:i64=0
    if rhs_id==0{out[0]=0.0-1000.0*y[0];out[1]=0.0-1.0*y[1];k=2;while k<n{out[k]=0.0;k=k+1}return}
    if rhs_id==1{
        out[0]=0.0-0.04*y[0]+10000.0*y[1]*y[2]
        out[1]=0.04*y[0]-10000.0*y[1]*y[2]-30000000.0*y[1]*y[1]
        out[2]=30000000.0*y[1]*y[1]
        k=3;while k<n{out[k]=0.0;k=k+1}return
    }
    out[0]=0.0-0.5*y[0];out[1]=0.0-0.1*y[1];k=2;while k<n{out[k]=0.0;k=k+1}
}
var G_JAC:[f64;4096]=[0.0;4096]
var G_M:[f64;4096]=[0.0;4096]
var G_MC:[f64;4096]=[0.0;4096]
fn gsolve(a: &![f64;4096], b: &![f64;64], n: i64) with Mut, Div {
    var col:i64=0
    while col<n {
        let pivot=a[col*64+col]
        if bdf_abs(pivot)>1.0e-30 {
            var row=col+1
            while row<n {
                let fac=a[row*64+col]/pivot
                var k=col+1
                while k<n{a[row*64+k]=a[row*64+k]-fac*a[col*64+k];k=k+1}
                a[row*64+col]=0.0
                b[row]=b[row]-fac*b[col]
                row=row+1
            }
        }
        col=col+1
    }
    var i=n-1
    while i>=0 {
        var sum=b[i];var j=i+1
        while j<n{sum=sum-a[i*64+j]*b[j];j=j+1}
        let d=a[i*64+i]
        if bdf_abs(d)<1.0e-30{b[i]=0.0}else{b[i]=sum/d}
        i=i-1
    }
}
fn bdf1(rhs_id:i64, y:&![f64;64], n:i64, t_start:f64, t_end:f64, h:f64, vars:&![f64;64]) with Mut, Div {
    var t=t_start
    while t<t_end {
        var dt=h;if t+dt>t_end{dt=t_end-t}
        var y_n:[f64;64]=[0.0;64];var i:i64=0
        while i<n{y_n[i]=y[i];i=i+1}
        var f0:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]
        bdf_rhs(rhs_id,y,n,&!f0)
        let eps=1.0e-8;var j:i64=0
        while j<n {
            var yp:[f64;64]=[0.0;64];i=0;while i<n{yp[i]=y[i];i=i+1}
            let delta=bdf_max(eps*bdf_abs(y[j]),eps)
            yp[j]=y[j]+delta
            var fp:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]
            bdf_rhs(rhs_id,&yp,n,&!fp)
            i=0;while i<n{G_JAC[i*64+j]=(fp[i]-f0[i])/delta;i=i+1}
            j=j+1
        }
        i=0;while i<n{j=0;while j<n{
            if i==j{G_M[i*64+j]=1.0-dt*G_JAC[i*64+j]}else{G_M[i*64+j]=0.0-dt*G_JAC[i*64+j]}
            j=j+1};i=i+1}
        var iter:i64=0
        while iter<20 {
            var fk:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]
            bdf_rhs(rhs_id,y,n,&!fk)
            var ng:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]
            i=0;while i<n{ng[i]=0.0-(y[i]-y_n[i]-dt*fk[i]);i=i+1}
            var gnorm=0.0;i=0;while i<n{gnorm=gnorm+ng[i]*ng[i];i=i+1}
            gnorm=bdf_sqrt(gnorm)
            if gnorm<1.0e-10{iter=100}else{
                i=0;while i<n{j=0;while j<n{G_MC[i*64+j]=G_M[i*64+j];j=j+1};i=i+1}
                gsolve(&!G_MC,&!ng,n)
                i=0;while i<n{y[i]=y[i]+ng[i];i=i+1}
                iter=iter+1
            }
        }
        i=0;while i<n{
            let mii=1.0-dt*G_JAC[i*64+i]
            if bdf_abs(mii)<1.0e-30{vars[i]=vars[i]*1.0e10}else{vars[i]=vars[i]/(mii*mii)}
            i=i+1}
        t=t+dt
    }
}
fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var y1:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]; y1[0]=1.0;y1[1]=1.0
    var v1:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]
    bdf1(0,&!y1,2,0.0,0.01,0.001,&!v1)
    let e0=bdf_exp(0.0-10.0);let e1=bdf_exp(0.0-0.01)
    println(y1[0]);println(y1[1]);println(e0);println(e1)
    let t1=bdf_abs(y1[0]-e0)<1.0e-3&&bdf_abs(y1[1]-e1)<1.0e-3
    if t1{println("T1 PASS")}else{println("T1 FAIL")}

    var y2:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]; y2[0]=1.0
    var v2:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]
    bdf1(1,&!y2,3,0.0,0.001,1.0e-6,&!v2)
    let sy=y2[0]+y2[1]+y2[2]
    println(y2[0]);println(y2[1]);println(y2[2]);println(sy)
    let t2=bdf_abs(sy-1.0)<1.0e-3&&y2[0]<1.0&&y2[0]>=0.0-1.0e-6&&y2[1]>=0.0-1.0e-6&&y2[2]>=0.0-1.0e-6
    if t2{println("T2 PASS")}else{println("T2 FAIL")}

    var y3:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]; y3[0]=10.0;y3[1]=5.0
    var v3:[f64;64]=[0.0;64]; v3[0]=0.01;v3[1]=0.005
    bdf1(2,&!y3,2,0.0,1.0,0.01,&!v3)
    let yg0=10.0*bdf_exp(0.0-0.5);let yg1=5.0*bdf_exp(0.0-0.1)
    println(y3[0]);println(y3[1]);println(yg0);println(yg1)
    println(v3[0]);println(v3[1])
    let t3=bdf_abs(y3[0]-yg0)<0.5&&bdf_abs(y3[1]-yg1)<0.5&&v3[0]>1.0e-15&&v3[1]>1.0e-15
    if t3{println("T3 PASS")}else{println("T3 FAIL")}

    let np=(if t1{1}else{0})+(if t2{1}else{0})+(if t3{1}else{0})
    if np==3{return 0}else{return 1}
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/bdf_stiff.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// BDF Stiff ODE Solver Integration Tests
//
// Validates the BDF (Backward Differentiation Formula) implicit solver
// for stiff ordinary differential equations. BDF methods are the standard
// for stiff systems arising in chemical kinetics, PBPK models, and
// electrical circuits.
//
// References:
//   Hairer, Wanner (1996) "Solving ODEs II: Stiff Problems"
//   Robertson (1966) "The solution of a set of reaction rate equations"

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

// ============================================================================
// DATA STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

struct BDFState {
    y: [f64; 8],
    t: f64,
    dt: f64,
    dt_max: f64,
    n_eqs: i64,
    y_prev1: [f64; 8],
    y_prev2: [f64; 8],
    y_prev3: [f64; 8],
    n_history: i64,
    order: i64,
    max_order: i64,
    n_steps: i64,
    n_function_evals: i64,
    n_jac_evals: i64,
    atol: f64,
    rtol: f64,
    newton_tol: f64,
    max_newton_iter: i64,
    last_accepted: i64
}

struct BDFResult {
    t_final: f64,
    y_final: [f64; 8],
    n_steps: i64,
    n_accepted: i64,
    n_rejected: i64,
    n_function_evals: i64,
    n_jac_evals: i64,
    success: i64
}

struct BDFTrajectory {
    times: [f64; 256],
    states: [f64; 2048],
    n_points: i64,
    n_eqs: i64
}

struct NewtonResult {
    converged: i64,
    iters: i64,
    fevals: i64,
    jevals: i64,
    y: [f64; 8]
}

struct BDFStepResult {
    new_state: BDFState,
    accepted: i64
}

// ============================================================================
// RHS FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn rhs_exponential_decay(t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i64, dydt: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [f64; 8] = dydt
    out[0] = 0.0 - 1000.0 * y[0]
    var k: i64 = 1
    while k < 8 {
        out[k] = 0.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    return out
}

fn rhs_robertson(t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i64, dydt: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [f64; 8] = dydt
    out[0] = 0.0 - 0.04 * y[0] + 10000.0 * y[1] * y[2]
    out[1] = 0.04 * y[0] - 10000.0 * y[1] * y[2] - 30000000.0 * y[1] * y[1]
    out[2] = 30000000.0 * y[1] * y[1]
    var k: i64 = 3
    while k < 8 {
        out[k] = 0.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    return out
}

fn rhs_van_der_pol(t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i64, dydt: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [f64; 8] = dydt
    let mu = 1000.0
    out[0] = y[1]
    out[1] = mu * (1.0 - y[0] * y[0]) * y[1] - y[0]
    var k: i64 = 2
    while k < 8 {
        out[k] = 0.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    return out
}

fn rhs_linear_stiff(t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i64, dydt: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [f64; 8] = dydt
    out[0] = 0.0 - 1000.0 * y[0]
    out[1] = 0.0 - 1.0 * y[1]
    var k: i64 = 2
    while k < 8 {
        out[k] = 0.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    return out
}

fn eval_rhs(fn_id: i64, t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i64) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var dydt: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    if fn_id == 0 {
        return rhs_exponential_decay(t, y, n, dydt)
    }
    if fn_id == 1 {
        return rhs_robertson(t, y, n, dydt)
    }
    if fn_id == 2 {
        return rhs_van_der_pol(t, y, n, dydt)
    }
    if fn_id == 3 {
        return rhs_linear_stiff(t, y, n, dydt)
    }
    return dydt
}

// ============================================================================
// GAUSSIAN ELIMINATION
// ============================================================================

fn gauss_solve_8(a: [f64; 64], b: [f64; 8], n: i64) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var aa: [f64; 64] = a
    var bb: [f64; 8] = b
    var x: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]

    var col: i64 = 0
    while col < n {
        var max_val: f64 = abs_f64(aa[col * 8 + col])
        var max_row: i64 = col
        var row: i64 = col + 1
        while row < n {
            let val = abs_f64(aa[row * 8 + col])
            if val > max_val {
                max_val = val
                max_row = row
            }
            row = row + 1
        }

        if max_row != col {
            var k: i64 = 0
            while k < n {
                let tmp_a = aa[col * 8 + k]
                aa[col * 8 + k] = aa[max_row * 8 + k]
                aa[max_row * 8 + k] = tmp_a
                k = k + 1
            }
            let tmp_b = bb[col]
            bb[col] = bb[max_row]
            bb[max_row] = tmp_b
        }

        let pivot = aa[col * 8 + col]
        if abs_f64(pivot) < 1.0e-30 {
            return x
        }

        row = col + 1
        while row < n {
            let factor = aa[row * 8 + col] / pivot
            var k: i64 = col + 1
            while k < n {
                aa[row * 8 + k] = aa[row * 8 + k] - factor * aa[col * 8 + k]
                k = k + 1
            }
            aa[row * 8 + col] = 0.0
            bb[row] = bb[row] - factor * bb[col]
            row = row + 1
        }
        col = col + 1
    }

    var i: i64 = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum: f64 = bb[i]
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n {
            sum = sum - aa[i * 8 + j] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let diag = aa[i * 8 + i]
        if abs_f64(diag) < 1.0e-30 {
            x[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            x[i] = sum / diag
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// BDF PREDICTORS
// ============================================================================

fn bdf1_predict(state: BDFState) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < state.n_eqs {
        y_pred[i] = state.y[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y_pred
}

fn bdf2_predict(state: BDFState) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < state.n_eqs {
        y_pred[i] = 2.0 * state.y[i] - state.y_prev1[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y_pred
}

fn bdf3_predict(state: BDFState) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < state.n_eqs {
        y_pred[i] = 3.0 * state.y[i] - 3.0 * state.y_prev1[i] + state.y_prev2[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y_pred
}

fn bdf4_predict(state: BDFState) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < state.n_eqs {
        y_pred[i] = 4.0 * state.y[i] - 6.0 * state.y_prev1[i]
                     + 4.0 * state.y_prev2[i] - state.y_prev3[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y_pred
}

// ============================================================================
// BDF COEFFICIENTS
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_beta(order: i64) -> f64 with Panic {
    if order == 1 { return 1.0 }
    if order == 2 { return 2.0 / 3.0 }
    if order == 3 { return 6.0 / 11.0 }
    if order == 4 { return 12.0 / 25.0 }
    return 1.0
}

// Error constant for BDF-k (Gear's formula)
// BDF-1: 1/2, BDF-2: 2/9, BDF-3: 3/22, BDF-4: 12/125
fn bdf_error_constant(order: i64) -> f64 with Panic {
    if order == 1 { return 0.5 }
    if order == 2 { return 2.0 / 9.0 }
    if order == 3 { return 3.0 / 22.0 }
    if order == 4 { return 12.0 / 125.0 }
    return 0.5
}

fn bdf_history_sum(state: BDFState, order: i64) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i64 = 0

    if order == 1 {
        while i < state.n_eqs {
            s[i] = state.y[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else if order == 2 {
        while i < state.n_eqs {
            s[i] = (4.0 / 3.0) * state.y[i] - (1.0 / 3.0) * state.y_prev1[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else if order == 3 {
        while i < state.n_eqs {
            s[i] = (18.0 / 11.0) * state.y[i]
                 - (9.0 / 11.0) * state.y_prev1[i]
                 + (2.0 / 11.0) * state.y_prev2[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        while i < state.n_eqs {
            s[i] = (48.0 / 25.0) * state.y[i]
                 - (36.0 / 25.0) * state.y_prev1[i]
                 + (16.0 / 25.0) * state.y_prev2[i]
                 - (3.0 / 25.0) * state.y_prev3[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    return s
}

// ============================================================================
// JACOBIAN
// ============================================================================

fn compute_jacobian(fn_id: i64, t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i64, f0: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 64] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var jac: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    let eps = 1.0e-8

    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n {
        var y_pert: [f64; 8] = y
        let delta = eps * max_f64(abs_f64(y[j]), 1.0)
        y_pert[j] = y[j] + delta

        let f_pert = eval_rhs(fn_id, t, y_pert, n)

        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            jac[i * 8 + j] = (f_pert[i] - f0[i]) / delta
            i = i + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    return jac
}

// ============================================================================
// NEWTON SOLVE
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_newton_solve(
    fn_id: i64,
    t_new: f64,
    y_pred: [f64; 8],
    hist_sum: [f64; 8],
    beta_h: f64,
    n_eqs: i64,
    newton_tol: f64,
    max_iter: i64
) -> NewtonResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_k: [f64; 8] = y_pred
    var converged: i64 = 0
    var iters: i64 = 0
    var fevals: i64 = 0
    var jevals: i64 = 0

    let f_pred = eval_rhs(fn_id, t_new, y_pred, n_eqs)
    fevals = fevals + 1

    let jac = compute_jacobian(fn_id, t_new, y_pred, n_eqs, f_pred)
    fevals = fevals + n_eqs
    jevals = jevals + 1

    // Build iteration matrix M = I - beta*h*J
    var M: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_eqs {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n_eqs {
            let jac_val = jac[i * 8 + j]
            if i == j {
                M[i * 8 + j] = 1.0 - beta_h * jac_val
            } else {
                M[i * 8 + j] = 0.0 - beta_h * jac_val
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var iter: i64 = 0
    while iter < max_iter {
        let f_k = eval_rhs(fn_id, t_new, y_k, n_eqs)
        fevals = fevals + 1

        // Residual: G(y_k) = y_k - hist_sum - beta*h*f(t_new, y_k)
        // We want to solve G(y) = 0, so neg_G = -G(y_k)
        var neg_G: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
        i = 0
        while i < n_eqs {
            neg_G[i] = 0.0 - (y_k[i] - hist_sum[i] - beta_h * f_k[i])
            i = i + 1
        }

        var g_sq: f64 = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n_eqs {
            g_sq = g_sq + neg_G[i] * neg_G[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        // Compare squared norms to avoid sqrt precision issues for small values
        let tol_sq: f64 = newton_tol * newton_tol
        if g_sq < tol_sq {
            converged = 1
            iters = iter + 1
            return NewtonResult {
                converged: converged,
                iters: iters,
                fevals: fevals,
                jevals: jevals,
                y: y_k
            }
        }

        let delta = gauss_solve_8(M, neg_G, n_eqs)

        i = 0
        while i < n_eqs {
            y_k[i] = y_k[i] + delta[i]
            i = i + 1
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Check if final residual is small enough even if max_iter reached
    let f_final = eval_rhs(fn_id, t_new, y_k, n_eqs)
    fevals = fevals + 1
    var final_sq: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_eqs {
        let g_i = y_k[i] - hist_sum[i] - beta_h * f_final[i]
        final_sq = final_sq + g_i * g_i
        i = i + 1
    }
    let tol100_sq: f64 = newton_tol * newton_tol * 10000.0  // (tol*100)^2
    if final_sq < tol100_sq {
        converged = 1
    }

    iters = max_iter
    return NewtonResult {
        converged: converged,
        iters: iters,
        fevals: fevals,
        jevals: jevals,
        y: y_k
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ERROR NORM
// ============================================================================

fn error_norm_weighted(err: [f64; 8], y_old: [f64; 8], y_new: [f64; 8],
                       n: i64, atol: f64, rtol: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var scale = atol + rtol * max_f64(abs_f64(y_old[i]), abs_f64(y_new[i]))
        if scale < 1.0e-30 { scale = 1.0e-30 }
        let e = err[i] / scale
        sum = sum + e * e
        i = i + 1
    }
    if n > 0 {
        return sqrt_f64(sum / (n as f64))
    }
    return 0.0
}

// ============================================================================
// BDF STEP
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_step(state: BDFState, rhs_fn_id: i64) -> BDFState with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = state
    let n = s.n_eqs
    let h = s.dt
    let t_new = s.t + h

    // Determine effective order
    // Stay at BDF-1 during rapid step growth (variable step BDF-k>1
    // requires constant step size for accurate predictors)
    var eff_order: i64 = 1
    if s.order > 1 && s.n_history >= s.order - 1 {
        eff_order = s.order
    }
    if eff_order > s.n_history + 1 {
        eff_order = s.n_history + 1
    }
    if eff_order < 1 {
        eff_order = 1
    }
    if eff_order > s.max_order {
        eff_order = s.max_order
    }

    // Predictor
    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    if eff_order == 1 {
        y_pred = bdf1_predict(s)
    } else if eff_order == 2 {
        y_pred = bdf2_predict(s)
    } else if eff_order == 3 {
        y_pred = bdf3_predict(s)
    } else {
        y_pred = bdf4_predict(s)
    }

    // BDF coefficients
    let beta = bdf_beta(eff_order)
    let beta_h = beta * h
    let hist_sum = bdf_history_sum(s, eff_order)

    // Newton solve
    let newton = bdf_newton_solve(
        rhs_fn_id, t_new, y_pred, hist_sum,
        beta_h, n, s.newton_tol, s.max_newton_iter
    )

    s.n_function_evals = s.n_function_evals + newton.fevals
    s.n_jac_evals = s.n_jac_evals + newton.jevals

    if newton.converged == 0 {
        // Newton failed: reject step, shrink dt aggressively
        s.dt = s.dt * 0.25
        s.dt = max_f64(1.0e-14, s.dt)
        // Also reduce order on Newton failure
        if s.order > 1 {
            s.order = s.order - 1
        }
        s.last_accepted = 0; return s
    }

    // Error estimation using predictor-corrector difference with error constant
    // This is the standard LSODE/CVODE approach for all orders
    let err_const = bdf_error_constant(eff_order)

    var lte: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        lte[i] = err_const * (newton.y[i] - y_pred[i])
        i = i + 1
    }

    let err_n = error_norm_weighted(lte, s.y, newton.y, n, s.atol, s.rtol)

    let accepted: i64 = if err_n <= 1.0 { 1 } else { 0 }

    if accepted != 0 {
        // Shift history
        s.y_prev3 = s.y_prev2
        s.y_prev2 = s.y_prev1
        s.y_prev1 = s.y
        s.y = newton.y
        s.t = t_new
        s.n_steps = s.n_steps + 1

        if s.n_history < 3 {
            s.n_history = s.n_history + 1
        }

        // Conservative order control: only promote if error is comfortably small
        // and we have enough history and step size is at dt_max (stable)
        if s.n_history >= s.order && s.order < s.max_order && err_n < 0.1 {
            s.order = s.order + 1
        }

        // Step size control: conservative growth
        if err_n > 1.0e-10 {
            let order_p1 = (eff_order + 1) as f64
            let factor = 0.9 * exp(log(1.0 / err_n) / order_p1)
            let factor_lim = min_f64(1.5, max_f64(0.8, factor))
            s.dt = s.dt * factor_lim
        } else {
            s.dt = s.dt * 1.5
        }
    } else {
        // Rejected: shrink step and reduce order
        if s.order > 1 {
            s.order = s.order - 1
        }
        if err_n > 1.0e-10 {
            let order_p1 = (eff_order + 1) as f64
            let factor = 0.9 * exp(log(1.0 / err_n) / order_p1)
            let factor_lim = max_f64(0.1, min_f64(0.5, factor))
            s.dt = s.dt * factor_lim
        } else {
            s.dt = s.dt * 0.5
        }
    }

    s.dt = max_f64(1.0e-14, s.dt)
    s.dt = min_f64(s.dt, s.dt_max)

    s.last_accepted = accepted; return s
}

// ============================================================================
// INITIALIZATION
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_init(n_eqs: i64, y0: [f64; 8], t0: f64, dt: f64,
            dt_max: f64, atol: f64, rtol: f64) -> BDFState {
    return BDFState {
        y: y0,
        t: t0,
        dt: dt,
        dt_max: dt_max,
        n_eqs: n_eqs,
        y_prev1: [0.0; 8],
        y_prev2: [0.0; 8],
        y_prev3: [0.0; 8],
        n_history: 0,
        order: 1,
        max_order: 4,
        n_steps: 0,
        n_function_evals: 0,
        n_jac_evals: 0,
        atol: atol,
        rtol: rtol,
        newton_tol: 1.0e-10,
        max_newton_iter: 20,
        last_accepted: 0
    }
}

fn bdf_init_order(n_eqs: i64, y0: [f64; 8], t0: f64, dt: f64,
                  dt_max: f64, atol: f64, rtol: f64, max_order: i64) -> BDFState {
    return BDFState {
        y: y0,
        t: t0,
        dt: dt,
        dt_max: dt_max,
        n_eqs: n_eqs,
        y_prev1: [0.0; 8],
        y_prev2: [0.0; 8],
        y_prev3: [0.0; 8],
        n_history: 0,
        order: 1,
        max_order: max_order,
        n_steps: 0,
        n_function_evals: 0,
        n_jac_evals: 0,
        atol: atol,
        rtol: rtol,
        newton_tol: 1.0e-10,
        max_newton_iter: 20,
        last_accepted: 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// INTEGRATION DRIVER
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_integrate(state: BDFState, t_end: f64, rhs_fn_id: i64) -> BDFResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = state
    var n_accepted: i64 = 0
    var n_rejected: i64 = 0
    let max_total_steps: i64 = 50000

    var total_attempts: i64 = 0
    while s.t < t_end && total_attempts < max_total_steps {
        // Don't overshoot
        if s.t + s.dt > t_end {
            s.dt = t_end - s.t
        }
        if s.dt < 1.0e-15 {
            s.dt = 1.0e-15
        }

        s = bdf_step(s, rhs_fn_id)
        // s already updated by SRET

        if s.last_accepted != 0 {
            n_accepted = n_accepted + 1
        } else {
            n_rejected = n_rejected + 1
        }

        total_attempts = total_attempts + 1
    }

    let success: i64 = if s.t >= t_end - 1.0e-12 { 1 } else { 0 }

    return BDFResult {
        t_final: s.t,
        y_final: s.y,
        n_steps: s.n_steps,
        n_accepted: n_accepted,
        n_rejected: n_rejected,
        n_function_evals: s.n_function_evals,
        n_jac_evals: s.n_jac_evals,
        success: success
    }
}

fn bdf_integrate_trajectory(state: BDFState, t_end: f64, rhs_fn_id: i64) -> BDFTrajectory with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var traj = BDFTrajectory {
        times: [0.0; 256],
        states: [0.0; 2048],
        n_points: 0,
        n_eqs: state.n_eqs
    }

    var s = state

    traj.times[0] = s.t
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < s.n_eqs {
        traj.states[0 * 8 + k] = s.y[k]
        k = k + 1
    }
    traj.n_points = 1

    let max_total_steps: i64 = 50000
    var total_attempts: i64 = 0

    while s.t < t_end && total_attempts < max_total_steps && traj.n_points < 256 {
        if s.t + s.dt > t_end {
            s.dt = t_end - s.t
        }
        if s.dt < 1.0e-15 {
            s.dt = 1.0e-15
        }

        s = bdf_step(s, rhs_fn_id)
        // s already updated by SRET

        if s.last_accepted != 0 {
            let idx = traj.n_points
            traj.times[idx] = s.t
            k = 0
            while k < s.n_eqs {
                traj.states[idx * 8 + k] = s.y[k]
                k = k + 1
            }
            traj.n_points = traj.n_points + 1
        }

        total_attempts = total_attempts + 1
    }

    return traj
}
