fn t_factor_approx(dof: f64, confidence: f64) -> f64 {
    if dof > 1.0e10 {
        if confidence >= 0.99 { return 2.576 }
        if confidence >= 0.95 { return 1.960 }
        if confidence >= 0.90 { return 1.645 }
        return 1.0
    }
    if confidence >= 0.945 {
        if confidence < 0.955 {
            if dof < 2.0 { return 12.71 }
            if dof < 3.0 { return 4.303 }
            if dof < 4.0 { return 3.182 }
            if dof < 5.0 { return 2.776 }
            if dof < 6.0 { return 2.571 }
            if dof < 8.0 { return 2.447 }
            if dof < 10.0 { return 2.306 }
            if dof < 15.0 { return 2.228 }
            if dof < 20.0 { return 2.131 }
            if dof < 30.0 { return 2.086 }
            if dof < 50.0 { return 2.042 }
            if dof < 100.0 { return 2.009 }
            return 1.960
        }
    }
    if confidence >= 0.985 {
        if dof < 2.0 { return 63.66 }
        if dof < 3.0 { return 9.925 }
        if dof < 4.0 { return 5.841 }
        if dof < 5.0 { return 4.604 }
        if dof < 6.0 { return 4.032 }
        if dof < 8.0 { return 3.707 }
        if dof < 10.0 { return 3.355 }
        if dof < 15.0 { return 3.169 }
        if dof < 20.0 { return 2.947 }
        if dof < 30.0 { return 2.845 }
        if dof < 50.0 { return 2.756 }
        if dof < 100.0 { return 2.678 }
        return 2.576
    }
    if confidence >= 0.895 {
        if confidence < 0.945 {
            if dof < 2.0 { return 6.314 }
            if dof < 3.0 { return 2.920 }
            if dof < 4.0 { return 2.353 }
            if dof < 5.0 { return 2.132 }
            if dof < 6.0 { return 2.015 }
            if dof < 8.0 { return 1.943 }
            if dof < 10.0 { return 1.860 }
            if dof < 15.0 { return 1.812 }
            if dof < 20.0 { return 1.753 }
            if dof < 30.0 { return 1.725 }
            if dof < 50.0 { return 1.697 }
            if dof < 100.0 { return 1.676 }
            return 1.645
        }
    }
    if dof < 2.0 { return 12.71 }
    return 1.96 + 2.4 / dof
}

fn get_pct(budget: UncertaintyBudget, idx: i32) -> f64 {
    if budget.combined_variance < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0 }
    let entry = get_entry(budget, idx)
    return 100.0 * entry.contribution / budget.combined_variance
}

fn sensitivity_ranking(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> SensitivityRanking with Mut {
    var ranking = empty_ranking()
    ranking.n_entries = budget.entry_count
    if budget.entry_count == 0 { return ranking }

    var pct0 = get_pct(budget, 0)
    var pct1: f64 = 0.0
    var pct2: f64 = 0.0
    var pct3: f64 = 0.0
    if budget.entry_count > 1 { pct1 = get_pct(budget, 1) }
    if budget.entry_count > 2 { pct2 = get_pct(budget, 2) }
    if budget.entry_count > 3 { pct3 = get_pct(budget, 3) }

    var i0 = 0
    var i1 = 1
    var i2 = 2
    var i3 = 3
    var v0 = pct0
    var v1 = pct1
    var v2 = pct2
    var v3 = pct3

    // Selection sort pass 1: find largest
    if budget.entry_count > 1 {
        if v1 > v0 {
            var ti = i0
            i0 = i1
            i1 = ti
            var tv = v0
            v0 = v1
            v1 = tv
        }
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 2 {
        if v2 > v0 {
            var ti = i0
            i0 = i2
            i2 = ti
            var tv = v0
            v0 = v2
            v2 = tv
        }
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 3 {
        if v3 > v0 {
            var ti = i0
            i0 = i3
            i3 = ti
            var tv = v0
            v0 = v3
            v3 = tv
        }
    }

    // Pass 2: find second largest
    if budget.entry_count > 2 {
        if v2 > v1 {
            var ti = i1
            i1 = i2
            i2 = ti
            var tv = v1
            v1 = v2
            v2 = tv
        }
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 3 {
        if v3 > v1 {
            var ti = i1
            i1 = i3
            i3 = ti
            var tv = v1
            v1 = v3
            v3 = tv
        }
    }

    // Pass 3: find third largest
    if budget.entry_count > 3 {
        if v3 > v2 {
            var ti = i2
            i2 = i3
            i3 = ti
            var tv = v2
            v2 = v3
            v3 = tv
        }
    }

    ranking.idx0 = i0
    ranking.idx1 = i1
    ranking.idx2 = i2
    ranking.idx3 = i3
    ranking.c0 = v0
    ranking.c1 = v1
    ranking.c2 = v2
    ranking.c3 = v3

    return ranking
}

fn identify_dominant(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> i32 with Mut {
    if budget.entry_count == 0 { return 0 }
    var best_idx = 0
    var best_pct = get_pct(budget, 0)
    if budget.entry_count > 1 {
        let pct1 = get_pct(budget, 1)
        if pct1 > best_pct {
            best_idx = 1
            best_pct = pct1
        }
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 2 {
        let pct2 = get_pct(budget, 2)
        if pct2 > best_pct {
            best_idx = 2
            best_pct = pct2
        }
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 3 {
        let pct3 = get_pct(budget, 3)
        if pct3 > best_pct {
            best_idx = 3
            best_pct = pct3
        }
    }
    return best_idx
}

fn dominant_contribution_pct(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> f64 with Mut {
    let idx = identify_dominant(budget)
    return get_pct(budget, idx)
}

fn compute_expanded_uncertainty(combined_u: f64, dof: f64, confidence: f64) -> f64 {
    let k = t_factor_approx(dof, confidence)
    return k * combined_u
}

fn budget_validate(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> bool with Mut {
    if budget.entry_count == 0 { return true }
    if budget.combined_variance < 1.0e-15 { return true }
    var total_pct: f64 = 0.0
    var idx = 0
    while idx < budget.entry_count {
        total_pct = total_pct + get_pct(budget, idx)
        idx = idx + 1
    }
    let diff = abs_f64(total_pct - 100.0)
    if diff < 1.0 { return true }
    return false
}

// Recommendation codes:
//   1 = Reduce dominant source (>50%)
//   2 = Increase measurements (DoF < 10)
//   3 = Target highest sensitivity
//   4 = Well-balanced budget
//   5 = Reduce second-largest source
//   6 = Consider correlations
//   7 = Increase replicates
fn generate_rec_code_0(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> i32 with Mut {
    let dom_pct = dominant_contribution_pct(budget)
    if dom_pct > 50.0 { return 1 }
    if budget.effective_dof < 10.0 {
        if budget.effective_dof > 0.0 { return 2 }
    }
    return 3
}

fn generate_rec_code_1(budget: UncertaintyBudget) -> i32 with Mut {
    let dom_pct = dominant_contribution_pct(budget)
    if dom_pct > 50.0 {
        if budget.effective_dof < 10.0 {
            if budget.effective_dof > 0.0 { return 2 }
        }
        return 5
    }
    if budget.effective_dof < 10.0 {
        if budget.effective_dof > 0.0 { return 7 }
    }
    return 4
}

fn generate_report(budget: UncertaintyBudget, confidence: f64) -> GUMReport with Mut {
    var report = empty_gum_report()
    report.n_inputs = budget.entry_count
    report.result_value = budget.result_value
    report.combined_std_uncert = budget.combined_std_uncert
    report.effective_dof = budget.effective_dof
    report.confidence_level = confidence

    let k = t_factor_approx(budget.effective_dof, confidence)
    report.coverage_factor = k
    report.expanded_uncert = k * budget.combined_std_uncert

    if budget.entry_count > 0 {
        report.i0 = ReportInput {
            name_code: 0,
            estimate: budget.e0.estimate,
            std_uncert: budget.e0.std_uncert,
            dist_type: budget.e0.source_type,
            dof: budget.e0.dof,
            unit_code: 0
        }
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 1 {
        report.i1 = ReportInput {
            name_code: 1,
            estimate: budget.e1.estimate,
            std_uncert: budget.e1.std_uncert,
            dist_type: budget.e1.source_type,
            dof: budget.e1.dof,
            unit_code: 0
        }
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 2 {
        report.i2 = ReportInput {
            name_code: 2,
            estimate: budget.e2.estimate,
            std_uncert: budget.e2.std_uncert,
            dist_type: budget.e2.source_type,
            dof: budget.e2.dof,
            unit_code: 0
        }
    }
    if budget.entry_count > 3 {
        report.i3 = ReportInput {
            name_code: 3,
            estimate: budget.e3.estimate,
            std_uncert: budget.e3.std_uncert,
            dist_type: budget.e3.source_type,
            dof: budget.e3.dof,
            unit_code: 0
        }
    }

    report.dominant_source_idx = identify_dominant(budget)
    report.dominant_contribution_pct = dominant_contribution_pct(budget)

    report.r0 = generate_rec_code_0(budget)
    report.r1 = generate_rec_code_1(budget)
    report.r2 = 6
    report.r3 = 0

    var n_rec = 0
    if report.r0 != 0 { n_rec = n_rec + 1 }
    if report.r1 != 0 { n_rec = n_rec + 1 }
    if report.r2 != 0 { n_rec = n_rec + 1 }
    if report.r3 != 0 { n_rec = n_rec + 1 }
    report.n_recommendations = n_rec

    return report
}

fn report_is_valid(report: GUMReport) -> bool {
    if report.combined_std_uncert < 0.0 { return false }
    if report.coverage_factor <= 0.0 { return false }
    let expected_exp = report.coverage_factor * report.combined_std_uncert
    let diff = abs_f64(report.expanded_uncert - expected_exp)
    if diff > 0.001 {
        if expected_exp > 0.001 { return false }
    }
    if report.confidence_level <= 0.0 { return false }
    if report.confidence_level >= 1.0 { return false }
    if report.dominant_contribution_pct < 0.0 { return false }
    if report.dominant_contribution_pct > 100.01 { return false }
    if report.n_inputs < 0 { return false }
    if report.n_inputs > 8 { return false }
    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN — Test Suite
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic {
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  GUM Automated Reporting Test Suite")
    println("  JCGM 100:2008 Section 8 — Reporting Uncertainty")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("")

    var passed = 0
    var failed = 0

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 1: Cockcroft-Gault CrCl uncertainty budget
    //
    // CrCl = (140 - Age) * Weight / (72 * SCr)
    //
    // We build the budget with sensitivity coefficients:
    //   dCrCl/dAge    = -Weight / (72 * SCr)
    //   dCrCl/dWeight = (140 - Age) / (72 * SCr)
    //   dCrCl/dSCr    = -(140 - Age) * Weight / (72 * SCr^2)
    //
    // Age = 60 +/- 0.5 (n=10), Weight = 70 +/- 1.0 (Type B),
    // SCr = 1.2 +/- 0.15 (n=5)
    //
    // Expected: SCr dominates because of high sensitivity coefficient.
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 1: Cockcroft-Gault CrCl budget (SCr dominance)")

    let age_val = 60.0
    let wt_val = 70.0
    let scr_val = 1.2
    let crcl_val = (140.0 - age_val) * wt_val / (72.0 * scr_val)

    // Sensitivity coefficients
    let s_age = 0.0 - wt_val / (72.0 * scr_val)
    let s_wt = (140.0 - age_val) / (72.0 * scr_val)
    let s_scr = 0.0 - (140.0 - age_val) * wt_val / (72.0 * scr_val * scr_val)

    var budget1 = budget_new(crcl_val, 0.95)
    budget1 = add_type_a(budget1, age_val, 0.5, abs_f64(s_age), 10.0)
    budget1 = add_type_b(budget1, wt_val, 1.0, abs_f64(s_wt))
    budget1 = add_type_a(budget1, scr_val, 0.15, abs_f64(s_scr), 5.0)
    budget1 = finalize_budget(budget1)

    let dom_idx1 = identify_dominant(budget1)
    let dom_pct1 = dominant_contribution_pct(budget1)

    println("  CrCl value:")
    println(crcl_val)
    println("  Combined std uncertainty:")
    println(budget1.combined_std_uncert)
    println("  Dominant source index (expect 2 = SCr):")
    println(dom_idx1)
    println("  Dominant contribution %:")
    println(dom_pct1)

    // SCr should be the dominant source (index 2) with > 60%
    if dom_idx1 != 2 {
        println("FAIL: Expected SCr (index 2) as dominant source")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if dom_pct1 < 60.0 {
        println("FAIL: SCr should contribute >60% of total variance")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] SCr dominates CrCl budget")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 2: Simple 2-input equal-contribution addition
    //
    // y = x1 + x2, both with u=1.0, sensitivity=1.0
    // Each contributes 50% of total variance.
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 2: Equal contributions (two inputs)")

    var budget2 = budget_new(20.0, 0.95)
    budget2 = add_type_b(budget2, 10.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    budget2 = add_type_b(budget2, 10.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    budget2 = finalize_budget(budget2)

    let pct2_0 = percent_contribution(budget2, 0)
    let pct2_1 = percent_contribution(budget2, 1)

    println("  Source 0 contribution %:")
    println(pct2_0)
    println("  Source 1 contribution %:")
    println(pct2_1)

    if abs_f64(pct2_0 - 50.0) > 1.0 {
        println("FAIL: Source 0 should be ~50%")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if abs_f64(pct2_1 - 50.0) > 1.0 {
        println("FAIL: Source 1 should be ~50%")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Equal contributions verified")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 3: Budget validation — contributions sum to 100%
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 3: Budget validation (contributions sum to 100%)")

    let valid1 = budget_validate(budget1)
    let valid2 = budget_validate(budget2)

    println("  CrCl budget valid:")
    if valid1 { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }
    println("  Equal budget valid:")
    if valid2 { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }

    if valid1 == false {
        println("FAIL: CrCl budget should be valid")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if valid2 == false {
        println("FAIL: Equal budget should be valid")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Budget validation correct")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 4: Expanded uncertainty with known coverage factor
    //
    // For infinite DoF and 95% confidence, k = 1.96
    // u_c = 2.0 => U = 1.96 * 2.0 = 3.92
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 4: Expanded uncertainty (k * u_c)")

    let u_exp = compute_expanded_uncertainty(2.0, 1.0e30, 0.95)
    let expected_uexp = 1.960 * 2.0
    let err4 = abs_f64(u_exp - expected_uexp)

    println("  Combined u = 2.0, infinite DoF, 95% confidence")
    println("  Expanded uncertainty:")
    println(u_exp)
    println("  Expected:")
    println(expected_uexp)
    println("  Error:")
    println(err4)

    if err4 > 0.01 {
        println("FAIL: Expanded uncertainty incorrect")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Expanded uncertainty matches k * u_c")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 5: Sensitivity ranking — correct descending order
    //
    // 3-input budget: contributions 10%, 70%, 20%
    // Ranking should be: [1, 2, 0] with contributions [70%, 20%, 10%]
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 5: Sensitivity ranking (descending order)")

    // Build a budget where:
    //   e0: u=1, c=1 => contribution = 1  (10%)
    //   e1: u=1, c=sqrt(7) => contribution = 7  (70%)
    //   e2: u=1, c=sqrt(2) => contribution = 2  (20%)
    var budget5 = budget_new(50.0, 0.95)
    budget5 = add_type_b(budget5, 10.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    budget5 = add_type_b(budget5, 20.0, 1.0, sqrt_f64(7.0))
    budget5 = add_type_b(budget5, 20.0, 1.0, sqrt_f64(2.0))
    budget5 = finalize_budget(budget5)

    let ranking5 = sensitivity_ranking(budget5)

    println("  Ranking index 0 (should be 1 = 70% source):")
    println(ranking5.idx0)
    println("  Ranking contribution 0:")
    println(ranking5.c0)
    println("  Ranking index 1 (should be 2 = 20% source):")
    println(ranking5.idx1)
    println("  Ranking contribution 1:")
    println(ranking5.c1)
    println("  Ranking index 2 (should be 0 = 10% source):")
    println(ranking5.idx2)
    println("  Ranking contribution 2:")
    println(ranking5.c2)

    if ranking5.idx0 != 1 {
        println("FAIL: Highest contributor should be index 1")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if ranking5.idx1 != 2 {
        println("FAIL: Second contributor should be index 2")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if ranking5.idx2 != 0 {
        println("FAIL: Third contributor should be index 0")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if ranking5.c0 < ranking5.c1 {
        println("FAIL: Contributions not in descending order")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Sensitivity ranking correctly ordered")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 6: Dominant source identification
    //
    // Same budget as test 5: dominant should be index 1 (~70%)
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 6: Dominant source identification")

    let dom5 = identify_dominant(budget5)
    let dom5_pct = dominant_contribution_pct(budget5)

    println("  Dominant index:")
    println(dom5)
    println("  Dominant contribution %:")
    println(dom5_pct)

    if dom5 != 1 {
        println("FAIL: Dominant source should be index 1")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if abs_f64(dom5_pct - 70.0) > 2.0 {
        println("FAIL: Dominant contribution should be ~70%")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Dominant source correctly identified")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 7: Recommendation generation — dominant source case
    //
    // When one source > 50%, primary recommendation should be code 1
    // (reduce dominant source uncertainty).
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 7: Recommendations (dominant source)")

    let rec7 = generate_rec_code_0(budget5)
    println("  Primary recommendation code (expect 1 = reduce dominant):")
    println(rec7)

    if rec7 != 1 {
        println("FAIL: Should recommend reducing dominant source (code 1)")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Correct recommendation for dominant source")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 8: Recommendation generation — balanced case
    //
    // When no single source dominates (all ~equal), recommendation
    // should be code 3 (target highest sensitivity).
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 8: Recommendations (balanced case)")

    let rec8 = generate_rec_code_0(budget2)
    println("  Primary recommendation code (expect 3 = target sensitivity):")
    println(rec8)

    if rec8 != 3 {
        println("FAIL: Balanced budget should recommend targeting sensitivity (code 3)")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Correct recommendation for balanced budget")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 9: Full report generation and validation
    //
    // Generate a complete GUM report from the CrCl budget
    // and verify it passes integrity checks.
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 9: Full report generation")

    let report9 = generate_report(budget1, 0.95)
    let valid9 = report_is_valid(report9)

    println("  Report result value:")
    println(report9.result_value)
    println("  Report combined std uncert:")
    println(report9.combined_std_uncert)
    println("  Report coverage factor:")
    println(report9.coverage_factor)
    println("  Report expanded uncert:")
    println(report9.expanded_uncert)
    println("  Report dominant source idx:")
    println(report9.dominant_source_idx)
    println("  Report dominant contribution %:")
    println(report9.dominant_contribution_pct)
    println("  Report n_recommendations:")
    println(report9.n_recommendations)
    println("  Report is valid:")
    if valid9 { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }

    if valid9 == false {
        println("FAIL: Generated report should be valid")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if report9.n_inputs != 3 {
        println("FAIL: Report should have 3 inputs")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if report9.coverage_factor < 1.5 {
        println("FAIL: Coverage factor should be reasonable (>1.5)")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if report9.expanded_uncert <= 0.0 {
        println("FAIL: Expanded uncertainty should be positive")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Report generation and validation correct")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 10: Report integrity — expanded = k * u_c
    //
    // Verify that the expanded uncertainty in the report is
    // exactly k * combined_std_uncert.
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 10: Report integrity (U = k * u_c)")

    let expected_exp10 = report9.coverage_factor * report9.combined_std_uncert
    let err10 = abs_f64(report9.expanded_uncert - expected_exp10)

    println("  k * u_c:")
    println(expected_exp10)
    println("  Report expanded U:")
    println(report9.expanded_uncert)
    println("  Error:")
    println(err10)

    if err10 > 0.001 {
        println("FAIL: Expanded uncertainty != k * u_c")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Report integrity verified: U = k * u_c")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // SUMMARY
    // ================================================================
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  GUM AUTOMATED REPORTING — TEST SUMMARY")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  Passed:")
    println(passed)
    println("  Failed:")
    println(failed)

    if failed == 0 {
        println("  ALL 10 TESTS PASSED")
        println("  GUM reporting compliant with JCGM 100:2008 Section 8")
    } else {
        println("  SOME TESTS FAILED")
    }
    println("======================================================================")

    return failed
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/gum_supplement1_compliance.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// GUM Supplement 1 compliance tests
// Validates covariance propagation per JCGM 101:2008
//
// Tests:
// 1. Independent inputs (rho=0): covariance propagation = standard GUM RSS
// 2. Fully correlated (rho=1): uncertainties add linearly
// 3. Anti-correlated (rho=-1): uncertainties cancel
// 4. Partial correlation (rho=0.5): intermediate result
// 5. Product with correlation
// 6. 3D propagation with correlation
// 7. Cockcroft-Gault with correlated weight/SCr

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (self-contained, no imports)
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x / 2.0
    if guess < 0.001 { guess = 0.001 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 {
        guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    return guess
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

// =============================================================================
// CovarianceMatrix (inline, matches stdlib/epistemic/covariance.sio)
// =============================================================================

struct CovMat {
    n: i32,
    data: [f64; 300],
}

fn tri_idx(n: i32, i: i32, j: i32) -> i32 with Mut {
    var row = i
    var col = j
    if i > j {
        row = j
        col = i
    }
    return row * n - (row * (row - 1)) / 2 + (col - row)
}

fn cm_new(n: i32) -> CovMat {
    return CovMat { n: n, data: [0.0; 300] }
}

fn cm_set(m: &!CovMat, i: i32, j: i32, val: f64) with Mut {
    m.data[tri_idx(m.n, i, j)] = val
}

fn cm_get(m: &CovMat, i: i32, j: i32) -> f64 with Mut {
    return m.data[tri_idx(m.n, i, j)]
}

// =============================================================================
// GUMResult (inline, matches stdlib/epistemic/gum.sio)
// =============================================================================

struct GR {
    v: f64,
    u: f64,
}

fn gr_new(val: f64, unc: f64) -> GR {
    return GR { v: val, u: abs_f64(unc) }
}

// =============================================================================
// Correlated operations (matches gum_supplement1.sio)
// =============================================================================

// y = x1 + x2, Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 + 2*rho*u1*u2
fn add_correlated(a: GR, b: GR, rho: f64) -> GR with Mut {
    let val = a.v + b.v
    let var_y = a.u*a.u + b.u*b.u + 2.0 * rho * a.u * b.u
    return gr_new(val, sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y)))
}

// y = x1 - x2, Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 - 2*rho*u1*u2
fn sub_correlated(a: GR, b: GR, rho: f64) -> GR with Mut {
    let val = a.v - b.v
    let var_y = a.u*a.u + b.u*b.u - 2.0 * rho * a.u * b.u
    return gr_new(val, sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y)))
}

// y = x1 * x2, Var(y) = x2^2*u1^2 + x1^2*u2^2 + 2*x1*x2*rho*u1*u2
fn mul_correlated(a: GR, b: GR, rho: f64) -> GR with Mut {
    let val = a.v * b.v
    let var_y = b.v*b.v*a.u*a.u + a.v*a.v*b.u*b.u + 2.0*a.v*b.v*rho*a.u*b.u
    return gr_new(val, sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y)))
}

// y = x1 / x2
fn div_correlated(a: GR, b: GR, rho: f64) -> GR with Mut {
    let val = a.v / b.v
    let c1 = 1.0 / b.v
    let c2 = 0.0 - a.v / (b.v * b.v)
    let var_y = c1*c1*a.u*a.u + c2*c2*b.u*b.u + 2.0*c1*c2*rho*a.u*b.u
    return gr_new(val, sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y)))
}

// Scale by exact constant
fn scale(a: GR, c: f64) -> GR {
    return gr_new(a.v * c, abs_f64(c) * a.u)
}

// 2D covariance propagation via numerical Jacobian
fn propagate_2d(f_add: i32, x: [f64; 2], u: [f64; 2], rho: f64) -> GR with Mut {
    // Build 2x2 covariance matrix
    var cov = cm_new(2)
    cm_set(&!cov, 0, 0, u[0] * u[0])
    cm_set(&!cov, 1, 1, u[1] * u[1])
    cm_set(&!cov, 0, 1, rho * u[0] * u[1])

    // Numerical Jacobian via central differences
    let h = 1.0e-7

    let h0 = h * max_f64(abs_f64(x[0]), 1.0)
    let h1 = h * max_f64(abs_f64(x[1]), 1.0)

    // For f = x0 + x1 (f_add == 1) or f = x0 * x1 (f_add == 0)
    var fp0: f64 = 0.0
    var fm0: f64 = 0.0
    var fp1: f64 = 0.0
    var fm1: f64 = 0.0
    var fval: f64 = 0.0

    if f_add == 1 {
        fp0 = (x[0] + h0) + x[1]
        fm0 = (x[0] - h0) + x[1]
        fp1 = x[0] + (x[1] + h1)
        fm1 = x[0] + (x[1] - h1)
        fval = x[0] + x[1]
    } else {
        fp0 = (x[0] + h0) * x[1]
        fm0 = (x[0] - h0) * x[1]
        fp1 = x[0] * (x[1] + h1)
        fm1 = x[0] * (x[1] - h1)
        fval = x[0] * x[1]
    }

    let j0 = (fp0 - fm0) / (2.0 * h0)
    let j1 = (fp1 - fm1) / (2.0 * h1)

    // Var(y) = j0^2*s00 + 2*j0*j1*s01 + j1^2*s11
    let s00 = cm_get(&cov, 0, 0)
    let s01 = cm_get(&cov, 0, 1)
    let s11 = cm_get(&cov, 1, 1)

    let var_y = j0*j0*s00 + 2.0*j0*j1*s01 + j1*j1*s11
    return gr_new(fval, sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y)))
}

// =============================================================================
// Main: Test Suite
// =============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic {
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  GUM Supplement 1 Compliance Test Suite")
    println("  JCGM 101:2008 — Covariance Propagation")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 1: Independent inputs (rho = 0) should match standard GUM
    // For y = x1 + x2, uncorrelated:
    //   GUM:   u(y) = sqrt(u1^2 + u2^2)      (RSS)
    //   Sup 1: u(y) = sqrt(u1^2 + u2^2 + 0)  (same)
    // ================================================================

    let x1 = gr_new(10.0, 0.3)
    let x2 = gr_new(20.0, 0.4)

    // Standard GUM (RSS)
    let gum_u = sqrt_f64(0.3*0.3 + 0.4*0.4)   // = 0.5

    // Supplement 1 with rho = 0
    let s1_result = add_correlated(x1, x2, 0.0)

    let err1 = abs_f64(s1_result.u - gum_u)

    println("TEST 1: Independent inputs (rho=0) vs GUM RSS")
    println("  x1 = 10.0 +/- 0.3, x2 = 20.0 +/- 0.4")
    println("  GUM RSS uncertainty:")
    println(gum_u)
    println("  Supplement 1 uncertainty (rho=0):")
    println(s1_result.u)
    println("  Difference:")
    println(err1)

    if err1 > 0.001 {
        println("FAIL: Independent inputs should match GUM RSS")
        return 1
    }
    println("[PASS] Independent inputs match GUM RSS")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 2: Fully correlated (rho = 1)
    // For y = x1 + x2, rho = 1:
    //   Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 + 2*u1*u2 = (u1 + u2)^2
    //   u(y) = u1 + u2 = 0.3 + 0.4 = 0.7
    //
    // This is the worst case: uncertainties add linearly.
    // ================================================================

    let full_corr = add_correlated(x1, x2, 1.0)
    let expected_full = 0.3 + 0.4  // 0.7
    let err2 = abs_f64(full_corr.u - expected_full)

    println("TEST 2: Fully correlated (rho=1)")
    println("  Expected uncertainty (u1+u2):")
    println(expected_full)
    println("  Supplement 1 uncertainty:")
    println(full_corr.u)
    println("  Difference:")
    println(err2)

    if err2 > 0.001 {
        println("FAIL: Fully correlated should give u1+u2")
        return 2
    }
    println("[PASS] Fully correlated: u(y) = u1 + u2")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 3: Anti-correlated (rho = -1)
    // For y = x1 + x2, rho = -1:
    //   Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 - 2*u1*u2 = (u1 - u2)^2
    //   u(y) = |u1 - u2| = |0.3 - 0.4| = 0.1
    //
    // Anti-correlation causes uncertainty cancellation.
    // ================================================================

    let anti_corr = add_correlated(x1, x2, 0.0 - 1.0)
    let expected_anti = abs_f64(0.3 - 0.4)  // 0.1
    let err3 = abs_f64(anti_corr.u - expected_anti)

    println("TEST 3: Anti-correlated (rho=-1)")
    println("  Expected uncertainty |u1-u2|:")
    println(expected_anti)
    println("  Supplement 1 uncertainty:")
    println(anti_corr.u)
    println("  Difference:")
    println(err3)

    if err3 > 0.001 {
        println("FAIL: Anti-correlated should give |u1-u2|")
        return 3
    }
    println("[PASS] Anti-correlated: u(y) = |u1 - u2|")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 4: Partial correlation (rho = 0.5)
    // For y = x1 + x2, rho = 0.5:
    //   Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 + 2*0.5*u1*u2
    //          = 0.09 + 0.16 + 0.12 = 0.37
    //   u(y) = sqrt(0.37) ~ 0.60828
    //
    // Should be between RSS (0.5) and linear (0.7)
    // ================================================================

    let partial_corr = add_correlated(x1, x2, 0.5)
    let expected_partial = sqrt_f64(0.09 + 0.16 + 2.0 * 0.5 * 0.3 * 0.4)
    let err4 = abs_f64(partial_corr.u - expected_partial)

    println("TEST 4: Partial correlation (rho=0.5)")
    println("  Expected uncertainty sqrt(0.37):")
    println(expected_partial)
    println("  Supplement 1 uncertainty:")
    println(partial_corr.u)
    println("  Difference:")
    println(err4)

    // Verify it's between RSS and linear
    let rss_u = sqrt_f64(0.09 + 0.16)
    let lin_u = 0.3 + 0.4
    let between_rss = partial_corr.u > rss_u - 0.001
    let between_lin = partial_corr.u < lin_u + 0.001

    if err4 > 0.001 {
        println("FAIL: Partial correlation value incorrect")
        return 4
    }
    if between_rss == false {
        println("FAIL: Partial correlation should exceed RSS")
        return 4
    }
    if between_lin == false {
        println("FAIL: Partial correlation should be less than linear")
        return 4
    }
    println("[PASS] Partial correlation: RSS < u(y) < linear")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 5: Correlated product
    // y = x1 * x2, with rho = 0.5
    //
    // Var(y) = x2^2*u1^2 + x1^2*u2^2 + 2*x1*x2*rho*u1*u2
    //
    // x1 = 5.0 +/- 0.1, x2 = 8.0 +/- 0.2, rho = 0.5
    // Var(y) = 64*0.01 + 25*0.04 + 2*5*8*0.5*0.1*0.2
    //        = 0.64 + 1.00 + 0.80 = 2.44
    // u(y) = sqrt(2.44) ~ 1.5620
    // ================================================================

    let a5 = gr_new(5.0, 0.1)
    let b5 = gr_new(8.0, 0.2)
    let prod5 = mul_correlated(a5, b5, 0.5)

    let expected_var5 = 64.0*0.01 + 25.0*0.04 + 2.0*5.0*8.0*0.5*0.1*0.2
    let expected_u5 = sqrt_f64(expected_var5)
    let err5 = abs_f64(prod5.u - expected_u5)

    println("TEST 5: Correlated product (rho=0.5)")
    println("  a=5+/-0.1, b=8+/-0.2, rho=0.5")
    println("  Expected: sqrt(2.44) =")
    println(expected_u5)
    println("  Got:")
    println(prod5.u)
    println("  Value (should be 40):")
    println(prod5.v)
    println("  Difference:")
    println(err5)

    if err5 > 0.001 {
        println("FAIL: Correlated product uncertainty")
        return 5
    }
    println("[PASS] Correlated product matches analytic")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 6: 3D propagation — y = x1 + x2 + x3 with pairwise correlations
    //
    // For addition, the Jacobian is J = [1, 1, 1], so:
    //   Var(y) = s00 + s11 + s22 + 2*s01 + 2*s02 + 2*s12
    //
    // x1 = 1.0 +/- 0.1, x2 = 2.0 +/- 0.2, x3 = 3.0 +/- 0.3
    // rho_12 = 0.5, rho_13 = 0.0, rho_23 = -0.3
    //
    // s00 = 0.01, s11 = 0.04, s22 = 0.09
    // s01 = 0.5*0.1*0.2 = 0.01
    // s02 = 0.0*0.1*0.3 = 0.0
    // s12 = -0.3*0.2*0.3 = -0.018
    //
    // Var(y) = 0.01 + 0.04 + 0.09 + 2*0.01 + 0 + 2*(-0.018)
    //        = 0.14 + 0.02 - 0.036 = 0.124
    // u(y) = sqrt(0.124) ~ 0.3521
    // ================================================================

    let s00 = 0.01
    let s11 = 0.04
    let s22 = 0.09
    let s01 = 0.5 * 0.1 * 0.2    // 0.01
    let s02 = 0.0 * 0.1 * 0.3    // 0.0
    let s12 = 0.0 - 0.3 * 0.2 * 0.3  // -0.018

    let var_3d = s00 + s11 + s22 + 2.0*s01 + 2.0*s02 + 2.0*s12
    let expected_u_3d = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_3d))

    // Compute using Jacobian propagation formula directly.
    // (CovMat-based pass-by-reference propagation deferred until VM supports &! semantics.)
    // J = [1, 1, 1] for y = x1 + x2 + x3
    // Var(y) = J * Cov * J^T = sum over all i,j of J_i * Cov_ij * J_j
    let j0: f64 = 1.0
    let j1: f64 = 1.0
    let j2: f64 = 1.0

    // Var(y) = j0^2*s00 + j1^2*s11 + j2^2*s22 + 2*j0*j1*s01 + 2*j0*j2*s02 + 2*j1*j2*s12
    let diag_part = j0*j0*s00 + j1*j1*s11 + j2*j2*s22
    let cross_part = 2.0*j0*j1*s01 + 2.0*j0*j2*s02 + 2.0*j1*j2*s12
    let var_prop = diag_part + cross_part

    let u_prop = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_prop))
    let err6 = abs_f64(u_prop - expected_u_3d)

    println("TEST 6: 3D correlated addition")
    println("  x1=1+/-0.1, x2=2+/-0.2, x3=3+/-0.3")
    println("  rho_12=0.5, rho_13=0, rho_23=-0.3")
    println("  Expected uncertainty:")
    println(expected_u_3d)
    println("  Propagated uncertainty:")
    println(u_prop)
    println("  Difference:")
    println(err6)

    if err6 > 0.001 {
        println("FAIL: 3D propagation")
        return 6
    }
    println("[PASS] 3D correlated propagation matches analytic")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 7: Cockcroft-Gault with correlated weight/SCr
    //
    // CrCl = (140 - age) * weight / (72 * SCr)
    //
    // Clinical scenario: weight and SCr are positively correlated
    // (obese patients tend to have higher SCr from increased muscle mass)
    // rho(weight, SCr) = 0.3
    //
    // Age = 55 +/- 0.5 (uncorrelated with others)
    // Weight = 70 +/- 2.0 kg
    // SCr = 1.1 +/- 0.05 mg/dL
    // ================================================================

    let age = gr_new(55.0, 0.5)
    let wt = gr_new(70.0, 2.0)
    let scr = gr_new(1.1, 0.05)

    // Step 1: (140 - age)
    let age_factor = sub_correlated(gr_new(140.0, 0.0), age, 0.0)
    // v = 85.0, u = 0.5

    // Step 2: (140 - age) * weight
    // Age and weight are uncorrelated (rho = 0)
    let numerator = mul_correlated(age_factor, wt, 0.0)

    // Step 3: 72 * SCr
    let denom = scale(scr, 72.0)
    // v = 79.2, u = 3.6

    // Step 4: numerator / denominator
    // Weight is in numerator, SCr is in denominator
    // The correlation between numerator and denominator comes from
    // the weight/SCr correlation, propagated through the formula.
    //
    // For simplicity, propagate the weight/SCr correlation to the
    // numerator/denominator: since numerator ~ weight and denominator ~ SCr,
    // rho(num, denom) ~ rho(weight, SCr) = 0.3
    let crcl = div_correlated(numerator, denom, 0.3)

    let crcl_expected = (140.0 - 55.0) * 70.0 / (72.0 * 1.1)
    let err_val = abs_f64(crcl.v - crcl_expected)

    println("TEST 7: Cockcroft-Gault with correlated weight/SCr")
    println("  Age=55+/-0.5, Weight=70+/-2.0kg, SCr=1.1+/-0.05mg/dL")
    println("  rho(weight, SCr) = 0.3")
    println("  CrCl value (mL/min):")
    println(crcl.v)
    println("  CrCl uncertainty:")
    println(crcl.u)
    println("  Expected CrCl:")
    println(crcl_expected)

    if err_val > 0.1 {
        println("FAIL: CrCl value incorrect")
        return 7
    }

    // The uncertainty should be positive and clinically reasonable
    if crcl.u <= 0.0 {
        println("FAIL: CrCl uncertainty must be positive")
        return 7
    }

    // Compare with uncorrelated case to show correlation effect
    let crcl_uncorr = div_correlated(numerator, denom, 0.0)
    println("  CrCl uncertainty (uncorrelated):")
    println(crcl_uncorr.u)

    // With positive correlation between weight (numerator) and SCr (denominator),
    // division should yield LOWER uncertainty than uncorrelated case
    // because when weight goes up, SCr tends to go up too, partially cancelling
    // the ratio effect.
    println("  Correlation effect: correlated < uncorrelated =")
    let corr_reduces = crcl.u < crcl_uncorr.u + 0.001
    if corr_reduces {
        println("  YES (correlation reduces uncertainty in ratio)")
    } else {
        println("  NO (unexpected: correlation should reduce ratio uncertainty)")
    }

    println("[PASS] Cockcroft-Gault with correlated inputs")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 8: Subtraction with positive correlation (common-mode rejection)
    //
    // For y = x1 - x2 with rho = 1:
    //   Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 - 2*u1*u2 = (u1 - u2)^2
    //
    // With equal uncertainties (u1 = u2), perfect correlation gives
    // zero uncertainty — the ideal differential measurement.
    // ================================================================

    let s1 = gr_new(100.5, 0.3)
    let s2 = gr_new(100.0, 0.3)

    let diff_corr = sub_correlated(s1, s2, 1.0)
    // Var(y) = 0.09 + 0.09 - 2*0.09 = 0
    // u(y) = 0

    println("TEST 8: Subtraction with rho=1 (common-mode rejection)")
    println("  x1=100.5+/-0.3, x2=100.0+/-0.3, rho=1.0")
    println("  Difference value:")
    println(diff_corr.v)
    println("  Difference uncertainty (should be ~0):")
    println(diff_corr.u)

    if diff_corr.u > 0.001 {
        println("FAIL: Equal uncertainties with rho=1 should cancel in subtraction")
        return 8
    }
    println("[PASS] Common-mode rejection: u(x1-x2) -> 0 when rho=1, u1=u2")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 9: Cholesky-based positive definiteness check
    //
    // A valid covariance matrix must be positive semi-definite.
    // Verify that our test matrices satisfy |rho| <= 1.
    // ================================================================

    // Valid 2x2: rho = 0.5, det = s00*s11 - s01^2 > 0
    // Direct computation (avoids VM &! reference limitation)
    let cv_s00: f64 = 1.0
    let cv_s11: f64 = 1.0
    let cv_s01: f64 = 0.5

    let det_valid = cv_s00 * cv_s11 - cv_s01 * cv_s01

    println("TEST 9: Covariance matrix positive definiteness")
    println("  [[1.0, 0.5], [0.5, 1.0]]")
    println("  Determinant:")
    println(det_valid)

    if det_valid <= 0.0 {
        println("FAIL: Valid covariance matrix should have positive determinant")
        return 9
    }

    // Invalid 2x2: rho = 1.5, det < 0
    let ci_s00: f64 = 1.0
    let ci_s11: f64 = 1.0
    let ci_s01: f64 = 1.5

    let det_invalid = ci_s00 * ci_s11 - ci_s01 * ci_s01

    println("  [[1.0, 1.5], [1.5, 1.0]]")
    println("  Determinant:")
    println(det_invalid)

    if det_invalid >= 0.0 {
        println("FAIL: Invalid covariance matrix (|rho|>1) should have negative determinant")
        return 9
    }
    println("[PASS] Positive definiteness check works")
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // SUMMARY
    // ================================================================
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  GUM SUPPLEMENT 1 COMPLIANCE SUMMARY")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  [PASS] Test 1: Independent inputs match GUM RSS")
    println("  [PASS] Test 2: Fully correlated (rho=1): u = u1 + u2")
    println("  [PASS] Test 3: Anti-correlated (rho=-1): u = |u1 - u2|")
    println("  [PASS] Test 4: Partial correlation (rho=0.5): intermediate")
    println("  [PASS] Test 5: Correlated product")
    println("  [PASS] Test 6: 3D correlated propagation")
    println("  [PASS] Test 7: Cockcroft-Gault with correlated weight/SCr")
    println("  [PASS] Test 8: Common-mode rejection (subtraction, rho=1)")
    println("  [PASS] Test 9: Positive definiteness check")
    println("  All 9 tests validate JCGM 101:2008 covariance propagation")
    println("======================================================================")

    return 0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/gum_variance_shadow.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// End-to-end GUM variance shadow buffer test.
// Tests: seeding via Knowledge.value, additive + multiplicative propagation,
// and variance_of() introspection.

fn main() with IO, Mut, Epistemic {
    // Seed variance from Knowledge via .value extraction
    let k1: Knowledge<f64> = measure(100.0, uncertainty: 2.0)
    let k2: Knowledge<f64> = measure(50.0, uncertainty: 1.0)
    let a = k1.value   // BSS_VAR[a_slot] = 4.0 (2.0²)
    let b = k2.value   // BSS_VAR[b_slot] = 1.0 (1.0²)

    // Additive GUM: var(a + b) = var(a) + var(b) = 4.0 + 1.0 = 5.0
    let sum = a + b

    // Multiplicative GUM: var(a * b) = a²·var(b) + b²·var(a)
    //   = 100²·1.0 + 50²·4.0 = 10000 + 10000 = 20000
    let prod = a * b

    // Introspect the variances
    let va = variance_of(a)
    let vb = variance_of(b)

    // Print results
    print("a="); println(a)
    print("b="); println(b)
    print("var(a)="); println(va)
    print("var(b)="); println(vb)
    print("sum="); println(sum)
    print("prod="); println(prod)
    print("PASS\n")
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/halo_pgx_gate_pass.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: HALO PGX GATE PASS

// Dissertation contribution: compile-time PGx confidence gate — PASS path.
//
// `prescribe_haloperidol` is annotated `with Confidence(750)`. Per the compiler's
// EpistemicComplete gate, every expression inside the body must carry compile-time
// confidence ≥ 750/1000.
//
// `measure(40.0, uncertainty: 1.6)` yields confidence = 1 − 1.6/40.0 = 0.96
// = 960/1000, which EXCEEDS the 750 threshold. The compiler emits binary code.
//
// Clinical narrative: post-CYP2D6 genotyping with activity score confirms NM
// phenotype. The star-allele call (e.g., *1/*1) reduces CL uncertainty to ±4%
// (measurement CV), well above the Confidence(750) threshold. The program
// compiles — prescribing is authorised.

fn prescribe_haloperidol(cl_l_h: f64, dose_target_ng_ml: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Confidence(750) {
    let f_oral:  f64 = 0.65
    let tau_h:   f64 = 24.0
    let target_mg_l = dose_target_ng_ml * 1.0e-3
    target_mg_l * cl_l_h * tau_h / f_oral
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic, Confidence(750) {
    // Post-genotyping: NM phenotype confirmed (activity score = 1.0).
    // CL = 40 L/h ± 1.6 (CV = 4%) from pharmacogenomic-guided population estimate.
    // confidence = 1 − 1.6/40.0 = 0.96 = 960/1000 > 750.  COMPILE PASSES.
    let k_cl: Knowledge<f64> = measure(40.0, uncertainty: 1.6)
    let cl = k_cl.value
    let dose_mg = prescribe_haloperidol(cl, 5.0)
    print("dose_mg = ")
    print_f64(dose_mg)
    println("")
    println("HALO PGX GATE PASS")
}

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/heap_vec_basic.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Tests heap-allocated vectors using raw pointer pattern

fn test_heap_vec_pattern() -> i64 with IO, Alloc, Mut {
    var cap: i64 = 4
    var len: i64 = 0
    var ptr = heap_alloc(cap * 8)

    // Push values
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        if len >= cap {
            cap = cap * 2
            ptr = heap_realloc(ptr, cap * 8)
        }
        write_i64(ptr, len, i * 10)
        len = len + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Verify
    if len != 8 { return 0 }

    i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let v = read_i64(ptr, i)
        if v != i * 10 { return 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }

    heap_free(ptr)
    1
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Alloc, Mut {
    let r = test_heap_vec_pattern()

    if r == 1 {
        print("heap_vec_basic: PASS\n")
        return 0
    }
    print("heap_vec_basic: FAIL\n")
    1
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/heap_vec_growth.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ description: Test heap allocation growth pattern

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Alloc {
    // Start with small allocation
    var cap: i64 = 4
    var len: i64 = 0
    var ptr = heap_alloc(cap * 8)

    // Push 0..20 with growth
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 20 {
        if len >= cap {
            cap = cap * 2
            ptr = heap_realloc(ptr, cap * 8)
        }
        write_i64(ptr, len, i * 10)
        len = len + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Verify all values
    var ok: i64 = 1
    i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        let v = read_i64(ptr, i)
        if v != i * 10 { ok = 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Verify capacity grew
    if cap < 20 { ok = 0 }

    heap_free(ptr)

    if ok == 1 {
        print("heap_vec_growth: PASS\n")
        return 0
    } else {
        print("heap_vec_growth: FAIL\n")
        return 1
    }
}

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/heap_vec_pattern.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ description: growable vec pattern using heap_alloc + write_i64 + read_i64 + heap_realloc

fn main() with IO, Alloc {
    // Simulate a growable i64 vec: alloc, push, grow, push more, verify
    var cap: i64 = 4
    var len: i64 = 0
    var data = heap_alloc(cap * 8)

    // Push 0..7
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        if len >= cap {
            cap = cap * 2
            data = heap_realloc(data, cap * 8)
        }
        write_i64(data, len, i * 10)
        len = len + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Verify
    var ok: i64 = 1
    i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        let v = read_i64(data, i)
        if v != i * 10 { ok = 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if ok == 1 {
        print("heap_vec_pattern: PASS\n")
    } else {
        print("heap_vec_pattern: FAIL\n")
    }

    heap_free(data)
}

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/hof_mut_struct_min.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Minimal: fn-HOF with mutable struct ref

struct Box4 { v: [f64; 4], n: i64 }

fn writer(out: &!Box4) with Mut { out.v[0] = 42.0 }

fn runner(f: fn(&!Box4) -> (), b: &!Box4) with Mut { f(b) }

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut {
    var b = Box4 { v: [0.0; 4], n: 0 }
    runner(writer, &!b)
    println(b.v[0])
    if b.v[0] == 42.0 { println("PASS T1") } else { println("FAIL T1") }

    // T2: fn-HOF with f64 + struct ref (matching rhs_decay pattern)
    0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/hypothesis_registered.sio ===
//@ run-pass

study MyStudy {
    title: "Test"
    design: parallel_rct
    participants {
        sample_size: 30
        power: 0.80
    }
    outcomes {
        primary: endpoint_a
    }
    analysis {
        hypothesis H1 {
            outcome: endpoint_a
            direction: greater
            effect_size: 0.5
        }
        alpha: 0.05
        correction: bonferroni
    }
}

fn t_test_one_sample(outcome: i32, n: i32, mu0: i32) -> i32 {
    outcome + n + mu0
}

fn analyze() -> i32 with Hypothesis {
    let endpoint_a = 3
    t_test_one_sample(endpoint_a, 30, 0)
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Hypothesis {
    let r = analyze()
    println("registered analysis: clean")
    0
}

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/if_let_pattern.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ description: Phase 1.3 — if let pattern matching (Some/None/Ok/Err/enum/wildcard)
// NOTE: if-let is implemented in lean_single.sio source; activates on Gen 23 rebuild.

fn get_some() -> Option<i64> with IO {
    Some(42)
}

fn get_none() -> Option<i64> with IO {
    None
}

fn main() with IO {
    // --- if let Some(x) ---
    let v = get_some()
    if let Some(x) = v {
        if x == 42 {
            print("if_let Some: PASS\n")
        } else {
            print("if_let Some: FAIL (wrong value)\n")
        }
    } else {
        print("if_let Some: FAIL (branch not taken)\n")
    }

    // --- if let None (should not enter branch) ---
    let v2 = get_some()
    if let None = v2 {
        print("if_let None wrongly triggered: FAIL\n")
    } else {
        print("if_let None-else: PASS\n")
    }

    // --- if let None (should enter branch) ---
    let v3 = get_none()
    if let None = v3 {
        print("if_let None: PASS\n")
    } else {
        print("if_let None: FAIL\n")
    }

    // --- if let with wildcard _ (always matches) ---
    let v4 = get_some()
    if let _ = v4 {
        print("if_let wildcard: PASS\n")
    } else {
        print("if_let wildcard: FAIL\n")
    }
}

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/interpolation.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// interpolation.sio - Integration tests for interpolation algorithms
//
// Tests piecewise linear, natural cubic spline, Lagrange, and Akima
// interpolation methods. Validates exactness at data points, correct
// behavior between points, boundary clamping, derivative accuracy,
// and monotonicity preservation.

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// Binary search for interval i such that xs[i] <= x < xs[i+1].
fn binary_search_interval(xs: [f64; 256], n: i32, x: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if n < 2 { return 0 }
    if x <= xs[0] { return 0 }
    if x >= xs[n - 1] { return n - 2 }

    var lo: i32 = 0
    var hi: i32 = n - 1
    while hi - lo > 1 {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
        if xs[mid] <= x {
            lo = mid
        } else {
            hi = mid
        }
    }
    return lo
}

fn binary_search_interval_64(xs: [f64; 64], n: i32, x: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if n < 2 { return 0 }
    if x <= xs[0] { return 0 }
    if x >= xs[n - 1] { return n - 2 }

    var lo: i32 = 0
    var hi: i32 = n - 1
    while hi - lo > 1 {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
        if xs[mid] <= x {
            lo = mid
        } else {
            hi = mid
        }
    }
    return lo
}

// Thomas algorithm for tridiagonal systems.
fn tridiag_solve(
    lower: [f64; 256],
    diag: [f64; 256],
    upper: [f64; 256],
    rhs: [f64; 256],
    n: i32
) -> [f64; 256] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c_prime: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var d_prime: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var x_out: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]

    c_prime[0] = upper[0] / diag[0]
    d_prime[0] = rhs[0] / diag[0]

    var i: i32 = 1
    while i < n {
        let m = lower[i] / (diag[i] - lower[i] * c_prime[i - 1])
        c_prime[i] = upper[i] / (diag[i] - lower[i] * c_prime[i - 1])
        d_prime[i] = (rhs[i] - lower[i] * d_prime[i - 1]) / (diag[i] - lower[i] * c_prime[i - 1])
        i = i + 1
    }

    x_out[n - 1] = d_prime[n - 1]
    i = n - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        x_out[i] = d_prime[i] - c_prime[i] * x_out[i + 1]
        i = i - 1
    }

    return x_out
}

// ============================================================================
// DATA STRUCTURES (inlined since tests cannot import)
// ============================================================================

struct PiecewiseLinear {
    xs: [f64; 256],
    ys: [f64; 256],
    n: i32
}

struct NaturalSpline {
    xs: [f64; 256],
    a: [f64; 256],
    b: [f64; 256],
    c: [f64; 256],
    d: [f64; 256],
    n: i32
}

struct LagrangeInterp {
    xs: [f64; 64],
    ys: [f64; 64],
    n: i32
}

struct AkimaSpline {
    xs: [f64; 256],
    a: [f64; 256],
    b: [f64; 256],
    c: [f64; 256],
    d: [f64; 256],
    n: i32
}

// ============================================================================
// PIECEWISE LINEAR INTERPOLATION
// ============================================================================

fn piecewise_linear_new(xs: [f64; 256], ys: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> PiecewiseLinear {
    return PiecewiseLinear { xs: xs, ys: ys, n: n }
}

fn piecewise_linear_eval(interp: PiecewiseLinear, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if interp.n < 2 {
        if interp.n == 1 { return interp.ys[0] }
        return 0.0
    }
    if x <= interp.xs[0] { return interp.ys[0] }
    if x >= interp.xs[interp.n - 1] { return interp.ys[interp.n - 1] }

    let i = binary_search_interval(interp.xs, interp.n, x)
    let h = interp.xs[i + 1] - interp.xs[i]
    if abs_f64(h) < 1.0e-30 { return interp.ys[i] }
    let t = (x - interp.xs[i]) / h
    return interp.ys[i] + t * (interp.ys[i + 1] - interp.ys[i])
}

// ============================================================================
// NATURAL CUBIC SPLINE
// ============================================================================

fn cubic_spline_fit_into(out: &!NaturalSpline, xs: [f64; 256], ys: [f64; 256], n: i32) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    out.xs = xs
    out.a = ys
    out.n = n
    var zi: i32 = 0
    while zi < 256 {
        out.b[zi] = 0.0
        out.c[zi] = 0.0
        out.d[zi] = 0.0
        zi = zi + 1
    }

    if n < 2 { return }

    var h: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        h[i] = xs[i + 1] - xs[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    if n == 2 {
        if abs_f64(h[0]) > 1.0e-30 {
            out.b[0] = (ys[1] - ys[0]) / h[0]
        }
        return
    }

    let m = n - 2
    var lower: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var diag: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var upper: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var rhs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]

    i = 0
    while i < m {
        let idx = i + 1
        diag[i] = 2.0 * (h[idx - 1] + h[idx])
        if i > 0 {
            lower[i] = h[idx - 1]
        }
        if i < m - 1 {
            upper[i] = h[idx]
        }
        let slope_right = (ys[idx + 1] - ys[idx]) / h[idx]
        let slope_left = (ys[idx] - ys[idx - 1]) / h[idx - 1]
        rhs[i] = 3.0 * (slope_right - slope_left)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Thomas algorithm inlined — tridiag_solve() array return is zeroed by codegen
    var c_prime: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var d_prime: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var x_out: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    c_prime[0] = upper[0] / diag[0]
    d_prime[0] = rhs[0] / diag[0]
    i = 1
    while i < m {
        c_prime[i] = upper[i] / (diag[i] - lower[i] * c_prime[i - 1])
        d_prime[i] = (rhs[i] - lower[i] * d_prime[i - 1]) / (diag[i] - lower[i] * c_prime[i - 1])
        i = i + 1
    }
    x_out[m - 1] = d_prime[m - 1]
    i = m - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        x_out[i] = d_prime[i] - c_prime[i] * x_out[i + 1]
        i = i - 1
    }

    out.c[0] = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < m {
        out.c[i + 1] = x_out[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    out.c[n - 1] = 0.0

    i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        let hi = h[i]
        if abs_f64(hi) < 1.0e-30 {
            out.b[i] = 0.0
            out.d[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            out.b[i] = (ys[i + 1] - ys[i]) / hi - hi * (2.0 * out.c[i] + out.c[i + 1]) / 3.0
            out.d[i] = (out.c[i + 1] - out.c[i]) / (3.0 * hi)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn cubic_spline_eval(spline: NaturalSpline, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if spline.n < 2 {
        if spline.n == 1 { return spline.a[0] }
        return 0.0
    }

    var xc: f64 = x
    if xc < spline.xs[0] { xc = spline.xs[0] }
    if xc > spline.xs[spline.n - 1] { xc = spline.xs[spline.n - 1] }

    let i = binary_search_interval(spline.xs, spline.n, xc)
    let dx = xc - spline.xs[i]
    return spline.a[i] + dx * (spline.b[i] + dx * (spline.c[i] + dx * spline.d[i]))
}

fn cubic_spline_derivative(spline: NaturalSpline, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if spline.n < 2 { return 0.0 }

    var xc: f64 = x
    if xc < spline.xs[0] { xc = spline.xs[0] }
    if xc > spline.xs[spline.n - 1] { xc = spline.xs[spline.n - 1] }

    let i = binary_search_interval(spline.xs, spline.n, xc)
    let dx = xc - spline.xs[i]
    return spline.b[i] + dx * (2.0 * spline.c[i] + 3.0 * spline.d[i] * dx)
}

// ============================================================================
// LAGRANGE INTERPOLATION (Barycentric)
// ============================================================================

fn lagrange_new(xs: [f64; 64], ys: [f64; 64], n: i32) -> LagrangeInterp {
    return LagrangeInterp { xs: xs, ys: ys, n: n }
}

fn lagrange_eval(interp: LagrangeInterp, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = interp.n
    if n < 1 { return 0.0 }
    if n == 1 { return interp.ys[0] }

    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < n {
        if abs_f64(x - interp.xs[k]) < 1.0e-15 {
            return interp.ys[k]
        }
        k = k + 1
    }

    var weights: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        var prod: f64 = 1.0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < n {
            if j != i {
                prod = prod * (interp.xs[i] - interp.xs[j])
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if abs_f64(prod) < 1.0e-30 {
            weights[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            weights[i] = 1.0 / prod
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var numerator: f64 = 0.0
    var denominator: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = x - interp.xs[i]
        let term = weights[i] / diff
        numerator = numerator + term * interp.ys[i]
        denominator = denominator + term
        i = i + 1
    }

    if abs_f64(denominator) < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
    return numerator / denominator
}

// ============================================================================
// AKIMA INTERPOLATION
// ============================================================================

fn akima_fit(xs: [f64; 256], ys: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> AkimaSpline with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var spline = AkimaSpline {
        xs: xs,
        a: ys,
        b: [0.0; 256],
        c: [0.0; 256],
        d: [0.0; 256],
        n: n
    }

    if n < 2 { return spline }

    if n == 2 {
        let h = xs[1] - xs[0]
        if abs_f64(h) > 1.0e-30 {
            spline.b[0] = (ys[1] - ys[0]) / h
        }
        return spline
    }

    var dm: [f64; 260] = [0.0; 260]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        let h = xs[i + 1] - xs[i]
        if abs_f64(h) < 1.0e-30 {
            dm[i + 2] = 0.0
        } else {
            dm[i + 2] = (ys[i + 1] - ys[i]) / h
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if n >= 3 {
        dm[1] = 2.0 * dm[2] - dm[3]
        dm[0] = 2.0 * dm[1] - dm[2]
        dm[n + 1] = 2.0 * dm[n] - dm[n - 1]
        dm[n + 2] = 2.0 * dm[n + 1] - dm[n]
    } else {
        dm[1] = dm[2]
        dm[0] = dm[2]
        dm[3] = dm[2]
        dm[4] = dm[2]
    }

    var slopes: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let w1 = abs_f64(dm[i + 3] - dm[i + 2])
        let w2 = abs_f64(dm[i + 1] - dm[i])

        if w1 + w2 < 1.0e-30 {
            slopes[i] = (dm[i + 1] + dm[i + 2]) / 2.0
        } else {
            slopes[i] = (w1 * dm[i + 1] + w2 * dm[i + 2]) / (w1 + w2)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        let h = xs[i + 1] - xs[i]
        if abs_f64(h) < 1.0e-30 {
            spline.b[i] = slopes[i]
            spline.c[i] = 0.0
            spline.d[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            let mi = (ys[i + 1] - ys[i]) / h
            spline.b[i] = slopes[i]
            spline.c[i] = (3.0 * mi - 2.0 * slopes[i] - slopes[i + 1]) / h
            spline.d[i] = (slopes[i] + slopes[i + 1] - 2.0 * mi) / (h * h)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return spline
}

fn akima_eval(spline: AkimaSpline, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if spline.n < 2 {
        if spline.n == 1 { return spline.a[0] }
        return 0.0
    }

    var xc: f64 = x
    if xc < spline.xs[0] { xc = spline.xs[0] }
    if xc > spline.xs[spline.n - 1] { xc = spline.xs[spline.n - 1] }

    let i = binary_search_interval(spline.xs, spline.n, xc)
    let dx = xc - spline.xs[i]
    return spline.a[i] + dx * (spline.b[i] + dx * (spline.c[i] + dx * spline.d[i]))
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

// Test 1: Piecewise linear interpolation at data points returns exact values
fn test_piecewise_linear_exact() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 0.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 2.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 1.0
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 4.0
    xs[4] = 4.0; ys[4] = 3.0

    let interp = piecewise_linear_new(xs, ys, 5)

    var max_err: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 5 {
        let val = piecewise_linear_eval(interp, xs[i])
        let err = abs_f64(val - ys[i])
        if err > max_err { max_err = err }
        i = i + 1
    }

    print("  max_err=")
    println(max_err)
    return max_err < 1.0e-12
}

// Test 2: Piecewise linear interpolation at midpoints
fn test_piecewise_linear_midpoint() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 0.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 2.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 1.0
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 4.0

    let interp = piecewise_linear_new(xs, ys, 4)

    // Midpoint of [0,1]: expected (0+2)/2 = 1.0
    let v1 = piecewise_linear_eval(interp, 0.5)
    let e1 = abs_f64(v1 - 1.0)

    // Midpoint of [1,2]: expected (2+1)/2 = 1.5
    let v2 = piecewise_linear_eval(interp, 1.5)
    let e2 = abs_f64(v2 - 1.5)

    // Midpoint of [2,3]: expected (1+4)/2 = 2.5
    let v3 = piecewise_linear_eval(interp, 2.5)
    let e3 = abs_f64(v3 - 2.5)

    print("  e1=")
    println(e1)
    print("  e2=")
    println(e2)
    print("  e3=")
    println(e3)

    return e1 < 1.0e-12 && e2 < 1.0e-12 && e3 < 1.0e-12
}

// Test 3: Piecewise linear extrapolation clamps at boundaries
fn test_piecewise_linear_extrapolate() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 1.0; ys[0] = 10.0
    xs[1] = 2.0; ys[1] = 20.0
    xs[2] = 3.0; ys[2] = 30.0

    let interp = piecewise_linear_new(xs, ys, 3)

    // Below range: should clamp to ys[0] = 10.0
    let v_low = piecewise_linear_eval(interp, 0.0 - 5.0)
    let e_low = abs_f64(v_low - 10.0)

    // Above range: should clamp to ys[2] = 30.0
    let v_high = piecewise_linear_eval(interp, 100.0)
    let e_high = abs_f64(v_high - 30.0)

    print("  v_low=")
    println(v_low)
    print("  v_high=")
    println(v_high)

    return e_low < 1.0e-12 && e_high < 1.0e-12
}

// Test 4: Cubic spline passes through data points
fn test_cubic_spline_exact() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 0.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 1.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 0.0
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 1.0
    xs[4] = 4.0; ys[4] = 0.0

    var spline = NaturalSpline { xs: [0.0; 256], a: [0.0; 256], b: [0.0; 256], c: [0.0; 256], d: [0.0; 256], n: 0 }
    cubic_spline_fit_into(&!spline, xs, ys, 5)

    var max_err: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 5 {
        let val = cubic_spline_eval(spline, xs[i])
        let err = abs_f64(val - ys[i])
        if err > max_err { max_err = err }
        i = i + 1
    }

    print("  max_err=")
    println(max_err)
    return max_err < 1.0e-10
}

// Test 5: Cubic spline evaluates smoothly between points (no jumps)
fn test_cubic_spline_smooth() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 0.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 1.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 4.0
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 9.0
    xs[4] = 4.0; ys[4] = 16.0

    var spline = NaturalSpline { xs: [0.0; 256], a: [0.0; 256], b: [0.0; 256], c: [0.0; 256], d: [0.0; 256], n: 0 }
    cubic_spline_fit_into(&!spline, xs, ys, 5)

    // Evaluate at fine grid
    var max_jump: f64 = 0.0
    var prev_val: f64 = cubic_spline_eval(spline, 0.0)
    let step = 0.01
    var t: f64 = 0.01
    var count: i32 = 0
    while t <= 4.0 {
        let val = cubic_spline_eval(spline, t)
        let jump = abs_f64(val - prev_val)
        if jump > max_jump { max_jump = jump }
        prev_val = val
        t = t + step
        count = count + 1
    }

    print("  max_jump=")
    println(max_jump)
    print("  n_points=")
    println(count)

    // For step=0.01 on quadratic data, jumps should be small (no discontinuities)
    return max_jump < 0.5
}

// Test 6: Cubic spline fits quadratic data exactly (C2 continuity)
// For y = x^2, a natural cubic spline with enough points should reproduce it well.
fn test_cubic_spline_quadratic() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 0.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 1.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 4.0
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 9.0
    xs[4] = 4.0; ys[4] = 16.0

    var spline = NaturalSpline { xs: [0.0; 256], a: [0.0; 256], b: [0.0; 256], c: [0.0; 256], d: [0.0; 256], n: 0 }
    cubic_spline_fit_into(&!spline, xs, ys, 5)

    // Test at interior points where the spline should closely match x^2.
    // Natural cubic spline reproduces quadratics exactly on interior intervals
    // (only boundary intervals may deviate due to natural BC).
    var max_err: f64 = 0.0
    let v1 = cubic_spline_eval(spline, 1.5)
    let e1 = abs_f64(v1 - 2.25)
    if e1 > max_err { max_err = e1 }

    let v2 = cubic_spline_eval(spline, 2.5)
    let e2 = abs_f64(v2 - 6.25)
    if e2 > max_err { max_err = e2 }

    let v3 = cubic_spline_eval(spline, 2.0)
    let e3 = abs_f64(v3 - 4.0)
    if e3 > max_err { max_err = e3 }

    print("  v(1.5)=")
    println(v1)
    print("  v(2.5)=")
    println(v2)
    print("  max_err=")
    println(max_err)

    // Natural cubic spline reproduces quadratics exactly on interior intervals
    return max_err < 0.1
}

// Test 7: Derivative of cubic spline on quadratic data matches 2x
fn test_cubic_spline_derivative() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 0.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 1.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 4.0
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 9.0
    xs[4] = 4.0; ys[4] = 16.0

    var spline = NaturalSpline { xs: [0.0; 256], a: [0.0; 256], b: [0.0; 256], c: [0.0; 256], d: [0.0; 256], n: 0 }
    cubic_spline_fit_into(&!spline, xs, ys, 5)

    // For y=x^2, derivative should be 2x.
    // Test at interior points.
    let d1 = cubic_spline_derivative(spline, 1.5)
    let e1 = abs_f64(d1 - 3.0)

    let d2 = cubic_spline_derivative(spline, 2.0)
    let e2 = abs_f64(d2 - 4.0)

    let d3 = cubic_spline_derivative(spline, 2.5)
    let e3 = abs_f64(d3 - 5.0)

    print("  d(1.5)=")
    println(d1)
    print("  d(2.0)=")
    println(d2)
    print("  d(2.5)=")
    println(d3)

    var max_err: f64 = e1
    if e2 > max_err { max_err = e2 }
    if e3 > max_err { max_err = e3 }

    print("  max_err=")
    println(max_err)

    return max_err < 0.5
}

// Test 8: Lagrange interpolation at nodes returns exact values
fn test_lagrange_exact() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var ys: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 1.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 3.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 2.0
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 5.0

    let interp = lagrange_new(xs, ys, 4)

    var max_err: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 4 {
        let val = lagrange_eval(interp, xs[i])
        let err = abs_f64(val - ys[i])
        if err > max_err { max_err = err }
        i = i + 1
    }

    print("  max_err=")
    println(max_err)
    return max_err < 1.0e-10
}

// Test 9: Lagrange fits polynomial data exactly
// Data from y = x^2 - x + 1 at x=0,1,2,3 (degree-2 polynomial, 4 points is enough)
fn test_lagrange_polynomial() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var ys: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    // y = x^2 - x + 1: y(0)=1, y(1)=1, y(2)=3, y(3)=7
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 1.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 1.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 3.0
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 7.0

    let interp = lagrange_new(xs, ys, 4)

    // Test at non-node points
    // y(0.5) = 0.25 - 0.5 + 1 = 0.75
    let v1 = lagrange_eval(interp, 0.5)
    let e1 = abs_f64(v1 - 0.75)

    // y(1.5) = 2.25 - 1.5 + 1 = 1.75
    let v2 = lagrange_eval(interp, 1.5)
    let e2 = abs_f64(v2 - 1.75)

    // y(2.5) = 6.25 - 2.5 + 1 = 4.75
    let v3 = lagrange_eval(interp, 2.5)
    let e3 = abs_f64(v3 - 4.75)

    print("  v(0.5)=")
    println(v1)
    print("  v(1.5)=")
    println(v2)
    print("  v(2.5)=")
    println(v3)

    var max_err: f64 = e1
    if e2 > max_err { max_err = e2 }
    if e3 > max_err { max_err = e3 }

    print("  max_err=")
    println(max_err)

    return max_err < 1.0e-8
}

// Test 10: Akima interpolation passes through data points
fn test_akima_exact() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 0.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 1.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 0.5
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 2.0
    xs[4] = 4.0; ys[4] = 1.5
    xs[5] = 5.0; ys[5] = 3.0

    let spline = akima_fit(xs, ys, 6)

    var max_err: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 6 {
        let val = akima_eval(spline, xs[i])
        let err = abs_f64(val - ys[i])
        if err > max_err { max_err = err }
        i = i + 1
    }

    print("  max_err=")
    println(max_err)
    return max_err < 1.0e-10
}

// Test 11: Akima on monotone data produces monotone interpolant
fn test_akima_no_wiggle() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Strictly monotone increasing data
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs[0] = 0.0; ys[0] = 0.0
    xs[1] = 1.0; ys[1] = 1.0
    xs[2] = 2.0; ys[2] = 2.0
    xs[3] = 3.0; ys[3] = 3.0
    xs[4] = 4.0; ys[4] = 4.0
    xs[5] = 5.0; ys[5] = 5.0

    let spline = akima_fit(xs, ys, 6)

    // Check monotonicity at several points
    var prev_val: f64 = akima_eval(spline, 0.0)
    var monotone: bool = true
    var t: f64 = 0.1
    while t <= 5.0 {
        let val = akima_eval(spline, t)
        if val < prev_val - 1.0e-10 {
            monotone = false
        }
        prev_val = val
        t = t + 0.1
    }

    // Also test a specific non-trivial monotone dataset
    var xs2: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys2: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    xs2[0] = 0.0; ys2[0] = 0.0
    xs2[1] = 1.0; ys2[1] = 0.5
    xs2[2] = 2.0; ys2[2] = 2.0
    xs2[3] = 3.0; ys2[3] = 3.5
    xs2[4] = 4.0; ys2[4] = 5.0
    xs2[5] = 5.0; ys2[5] = 8.0

    let spline2 = akima_fit(xs2, ys2, 6)

    var prev_val2: f64 = akima_eval(spline2, 0.0)
    var t2: f64 = 0.25
    while t2 <= 5.0 {
        let val2 = akima_eval(spline2, t2)
        if val2 < prev_val2 - 1.0e-10 {
            monotone = false
        }
        prev_val2 = val2
        t2 = t2 + 0.25
    }

    if monotone {
        println("  monotone=true")
    } else {
        println("  monotone=false")
    }

    return monotone
}

    if test_piecewise_linear_extrapolate() {
        println("PASS")

    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // Test 4
    print("Test  4: Cubic spline exact......... ")
    if test_cubic_spline_exact() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // Test 5

        println("PASS")

        println("FAIL")

    }

    if test_cubic_spline_quadratic() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // Test 7
    print("Test  7: Cubic spline derivative.... ")
    if test_cubic_spline_derivative() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // Test 8
    print("Test  8: Lagrange exact............. ")
    if test_lagrange_exact() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // Test 9
    print("Test  9: Lagrange polynomial........ ")
    if test_lagrange_polynomial() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // Test 10
    print("Test 10: Akima exact................ ")
    if test_akima_exact() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // Test 11
    print("Test 11: Akima no wiggle............ ")
    if test_akima_no_wiggle() {
        println("PASS")

    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1

    print("Failed: ")
    println(failed)

    if failed == 0 {
        println("ALL 11 TESTS PASSED")
        return 0
    }
    println("SOME TESTS FAILED")
    return 1
}
