// === FILE: tests/run-pass/test_nested_struct_return.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: sret nested ok
struct Point { x: i64, y: i64 }

fn make_point(x: i64, y: i64) -> Point {
    Point { x: x, y: y }
}

fn pick_left(a: Point, b: Point) -> Point {
    a
}

fn shift_point(p: Point, dx: i64, dy: i64) -> Point {
    Point { x: p.x + dx, y: p.y + dy }
}

fn sum_points(a: Point, b: Point) -> i64 {
    a.x + a.y + b.x + b.y
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Panic {
    let a = make_point(10, 20)
    let b = make_point(30, 40)
    assert(a.x == 10)
    assert(a.y == 20)
    assert(b.x == 30)
    assert(b.y == 40)

    let nested = pick_left(make_point(1, 2), make_point(3, 4))
    assert(nested.x == 1)
    assert(nested.y == 2)

    let shifted = shift_point(pick_left(make_point(5, 6), make_point(7, 8)), 9, 10)
    assert(shifted.x == 14)
    assert(shifted.y == 16)

    let total = sum_points(make_point(11, 12), pick_left(make_point(13, 14), make_point(15, 16)))
    assert(total == 50)

    print("sret nested ok\n")
    0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/test_ot_hand_problems.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ description: Exact OT/W1 over Q — 3 hand problems (known rational optima, minimization verified)
use ot::transport_exact::*
use math::rational::*

fn main() -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // HP1: masses (2/3,1/3)->(1/3,2/3), cost [[5,1],[1,5]] ; W1 = 1 ; opt=3 (greedy NW=11)
    OT_SNUM[0]=2; OT_SDEN[0]=3; OT_SNUM[1]=1; OT_SDEN[1]=3;
    OT_DNUM[0]=1; OT_DDEN[0]=3; OT_DNUM[1]=2; OT_DDEN[1]=3;
    OT_COST[0]=5; OT_COST[1]=1; OT_COST[2]=1; OT_COST[3]=5;
    let w1 = w1_rational(2,2);
    if w1.num != 1 { return 1; }
    if w1.den != 1 { return 2; }
    // integer opt must be 3 (minimization), NOT the greedy 11
    OT_SUPPLY[0]=2; OT_SUPPLY[1]=1; OT_DEMAND[0]=1; OT_DEMAND[1]=2;
    let ci = w1_int(2,2);
    if ci != 3 { return 30 + ci; }
    // HP2: (1/3,2/3)->(2/3,1/3), cost [[0,1],[1,0]] ; W1 = 1/3
    OT_SNUM[0]=1; OT_SDEN[0]=3; OT_SNUM[1]=2; OT_SDEN[1]=3;
    OT_DNUM[0]=2; OT_DDEN[0]=3; OT_DNUM[1]=1; OT_DDEN[1]=3;
    OT_COST[0]=0; OT_COST[1]=1; OT_COST[2]=1; OT_COST[3]=0;
    let w2 = w1_rational(2,2);
    if w2.num != 1 { return 4; }
    if w2.den != 3 { return 5; }
    // HP3: (3/5,2/5)->(2/5,3/5), cost [[1,4],[4,1]] ; W1 = 8/5
    OT_SNUM[0]=3; OT_SDEN[0]=5; OT_SNUM[1]=2; OT_SDEN[1]=5;
    OT_DNUM[0]=2; OT_DDEN[0]=5; OT_DNUM[1]=3; OT_DDEN[1]=5;
    OT_COST[0]=1; OT_COST[1]=4; OT_COST[2]=4; OT_COST[3]=1;
    let w3 = w1_rational(2,2);
    if w3.num != 8 { return 6; }
    if w3.den != 5 { return 7; }
    return 0;
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/test_qflra_exact.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ description: Exact rational QF_LRA (Fourier-Motzkin) — 2 SAT, 1 UNSAT, Farkas cert verified
use theorem::qflra_exact::*
use math::rational::*

fn main() -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Instance 1 (SAT): x>=0, y>=0, x+y<=2, x+y>=1
    qf_reset(2);
    let a0 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(a0,0,0-1,1); qf_set_rhs(a0,0,1);      // -x <= 0
    let a1 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(a1,1,0-1,1); qf_set_rhs(a1,0,1);      // -y <= 0
    let a2 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(a2,0,1,1); qf_set_coeff(a2,1,1,1); qf_set_rhs(a2,2,1);   // x+y<=2
    let a3 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(a3,0,0-1,1); qf_set_coeff(a3,1,0-1,1); qf_set_rhs(a3,0-1,1); // -x-y<=-1
    if qf_decide() != 1 { return 1; }   // must be SAT

    // Instance 2 (SAT, rational): 2x<=1, -3x<=-1  => x in [1/3,1/2]
    qf_reset(1);
    let b0 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(b0,0,2,1); qf_set_rhs(b0,1,1);
    let b1 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(b1,0,0-3,1); qf_set_rhs(b1,0-1,1);
    if qf_decide() != 1 { return 2; }   // must be SAT

    // Instance 3 (UNSAT): x+y<=1, -x<=0, -y<=0, -x-y<=-2
    qf_reset(2);
    let c0 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(c0,0,1,1); qf_set_coeff(c0,1,1,1); qf_set_rhs(c0,1,1);
    let c1 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(c1,0,0-1,1); qf_set_rhs(c1,0,1);
    let c2 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(c2,1,0-1,1); qf_set_rhs(c2,0,1);
    let c3 = qf_new_row(); qf_set_coeff(c3,0,0-1,1); qf_set_coeff(c3,1,0-1,1); qf_set_rhs(c3,0-2,1);
    if qf_decide() != 0 { return 3; }   // must be UNSAT

    // verify Farkas certificate y>=0, y.A==0 (each col), y.b < 0
    // original A: rows c0..c3 ; cols x,y ; b
    // y_k = qf_farkas(k)
    var y0 = qf_farkas(0); var y1 = qf_farkas(1); var y2 = qf_farkas(2); var y3 = qf_farkas(3);
    if y0.num < 0 { return 4; }
    if y1.num < 0 { return 5; }
    if y2.num < 0 { return 6; }
    if y3.num < 0 { return 7; }
    // col x: y0*1 + y1*(-1) + y2*0 + y3*(-1) == 0
    let cx = rat_add(rat_add(rat_mul(y0, rat_make(1,1)), rat_mul(y1, rat_make(0-1,1))),
                     rat_add(rat_mul(y2, rat_make(0,1)), rat_mul(y3, rat_make(0-1,1))));
    if rat_is_zero(cx) == false { return 8; }
    // col y: y0*1 + y1*0 + y2*(-1) + y3*(-1) == 0
    let cy = rat_add(rat_add(rat_mul(y0, rat_make(1,1)), rat_mul(y1, rat_make(0,1))),
                     rat_add(rat_mul(y2, rat_make(0-1,1)), rat_mul(y3, rat_make(0-1,1))));
    if rat_is_zero(cy) == false { return 9; }
    // y.b = y0*1 + y1*0 + y2*0 + y3*(-2) < 0
    let yb = rat_add(rat_add(rat_mul(y0, rat_make(1,1)), rat_mul(y1, rat_make(0,1))),
                     rat_add(rat_mul(y2, rat_make(0,1)), rat_mul(y3, rat_make(0-2,1))));
    if yb.num >= 0 { return 10; }   // must be < 0
    return 0;
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/test_rational_exact.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ description: Exact Rational arithmetic — Layer 1 acceptance (hand values, parse, overflow)
use math::rational::*

fn main() -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // 1) 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6
    let r1 = rat_add(rat_make(1,2), rat_make(1,3));
    if r1.num != 5 { return 1; }
    if r1.den != 6 { return 2; }
    // 2) 27/20 > 1
    if rat_cmp(rat_make(27,20), rat_one()) <= 0 { return 3; }
    // 3) gcd reduction 6/4 = 3/2
    let r3 = rat_make(6,4);
    if r3.num != 3 { return 4; }
    if r3.den != 2 { return 5; }
    // 4) negative: -7/20 < 0
    if rat_lt(rat_make(0-7,20), rat_zero()) == false { return 6; }
    // 5) (1/10)*5 + (1/12)*6 = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1
    let a5 = rat_mul(rat_make(1,10), rat_from_int(5));   // 1/2
    let b5 = rat_mul(rat_make(1,12), rat_from_int(6));   // 1/2
    let s5 = rat_add(a5, b5);                            // 1/1
    if s5.num != 1 { return 7; }
    if s5.den != 1 { return 8; }
    // 6) subtraction: 5/6 - 1/3 = 1/2
    let r6 = rat_sub(rat_make(5,6), rat_make(1,3));
    if r6.num != 1 { return 9; }
    if r6.den != 2 { return 10; }
    // 7) division: (3/2) / (1/2) = 3
    let r7 = rat_div(rat_make(3,2), rat_make(1,2));
    if r7.num != 3 { return 11; }
    if r7.den != 1 { return 12; }
    // 8) neg den normalization: 1/(-2) = -1/2
    let r8 = rat_make(1, 0-2);
    if r8.num != 0-1 { return 13; }
    if r8.den != 2 { return 14; }
    // 9) equality after reduction
    if rat_eq(rat_make(2,4), rat_make(1,2)) == false { return 15; }
    // 10) parse "27/20" and "-7"
    let p1 = rat_parse("27/20");
    if p1.num != 27 { return 16; }
    if p1.den != 20 { return 17; }
    let p2 = rat_parse("-7");
    if p2.num != 0-7 { return 18; }
    if p2.den != 1 { return 19; }
    // 11) overflow detection: huge * huge -> invalid (den==0)
    let big = rat_from_int(5000000000);     // 5e9
    let ov = rat_mul(big, big);             // 2.5e19 > i64 max -> invalid
    if rat_valid(ov) { return 20; }
    return 0;
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/test_scientific_computing.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// test_scientific_computing.sio - Integration tests for scientific computing features
//
// Tests:
// 1. ODE solvers (RK4, RK45)
// 2. Automatic differentiation (gradients, Jacobians)
// 3. Probabilistic programming (sampling, inference)

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut {
    if x > 20.0 { return exp_f64(x / 2.0) * exp_f64(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / exp_f64(0.0 - x) }

    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * x / 1.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 2.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 3.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 4.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 5.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 6.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 7.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 8.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 9.0; sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 10.0; sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (1.0 * 2.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (3.0 * 4.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (5.0 * 6.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (7.0 * 8.0); sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 1: ODE SOLVER (RK4)
// ============================================================================

fn ode_exp_decay(u: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    let k = 0.1
    return 0.0 - k * u
}

fn rk4_step(u: f64, t: f64, dt: f64) -> f64 with Panic {
    let k1 = ode_exp_decay(u, t)
    let k2 = ode_exp_decay(u + 0.5 * dt * k1, t + 0.5 * dt)
    let k3 = ode_exp_decay(u + 0.5 * dt * k2, t + 0.5 * dt)
    let k4 = ode_exp_decay(u + dt * k3, t + dt)
    return u + (dt / 6.0) * (k1 + 2.0 * k2 + 2.0 * k3 + k4)
}

fn test_rk4_solver() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let u0 = 100.0
    let t_end = 10.0
    let n_steps: i64 = 100
    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)

    var u = u0
    var t = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0

    while i < n_steps {
        u = rk4_step(u, t, dt)
        t = t + dt
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Analytical solution: u(t) = u0 * exp(-k*t) = 100 * exp(-1) ~ 36.79
    let analytical = u0 * exp_f64(0.0 - 0.1 * t_end)
    let rel_err = abs_f64(u - analytical) / analytical

    return rel_err < 0.0001
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 2: DUAL NUMBERS (Forward-mode AD)
// ============================================================================

struct Dual {
    val: f64,
    dot: f64
}

fn dual_var(val: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: val, dot: 1.0 }
}

fn dual_const(val: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: val, dot: 0.0 }
}

fn dual_local_mul(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual {
        val: a.val * b.val,
        dot: a.dot * b.val + a.val * b.dot
    }
}

fn dual_local_add(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: a.val + b.val, dot: a.dot + b.dot }
}

fn dual_local_sub(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: a.val - b.val, dot: a.dot - b.dot }
}

fn test_autodiff_simple() -> bool {
    // Test d/dx(x^2) at x=3
    let x = dual_var(3.0)
    let y = dual_local_mul(x, x)

    // f(3) = 9, f'(3) = 6
    let val_err = abs_f64(y.val - 9.0)
    let dot_err = abs_f64(y.dot - 6.0)

    return val_err < 0.0001 && dot_err < 0.0001
}

fn test_autodiff_chain() -> bool {
    // Test d/dx((x-1)^2) at x=3
    // f(x) = (x-1)^2, f'(x) = 2*(x-1)
    // f(3) = 4, f'(3) = 4
    let x = dual_var(3.0)
    let one = dual_const(1.0)
    let diff = dual_local_sub(x, one)
    let y = dual_local_mul(diff, diff)

    let val_err = abs_f64(y.val - 4.0)
    let dot_err = abs_f64(y.dot - 4.0)

    return val_err < 0.0001 && dot_err < 0.0001
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 3: RANDOM NUMBER GENERATION
// ============================================================================

struct RNG {
    seed: i64
}

struct RNGResult {
    rng: RNG,
    value: f64
}

fn rng_uniform(rng: RNG) -> RNGResult with Panic {
    let a: i64 = 1103515245
    let c: i64 = 12345
    let m: i64 = 2147483648
    let new_seed = (a * rng.seed + c) % m
    let u = (new_seed as f64) / (m as f64)
    return RNGResult { rng: RNG { seed: new_seed }, value: u }
}

fn test_rng_uniform() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var rng = RNG { seed: 12345 }
    var sum = 0.0
    let n: i64 = 1000
    var i: i64 = 0

    while i < n {
        let r = rng_uniform(rng)
        rng = r.rng
        sum = sum + r.value
        i = i + 1
    }

    let mean = sum / (n as f64)
    // Mean of Uniform(0,1) should be ~0.5
    return abs_f64(mean - 0.5) < 0.1
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 4: BETA DISTRIBUTION MOMENTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_beta_moments() -> bool with Panic {
    // For Beta(2, 5):
    // Mean = alpha / (alpha + beta) = 2/7 = 0.286
    // Variance = (alpha*beta) / ((alpha+beta)^2 * (alpha+beta+1))
    //          = 10 / (49 * 8) = 0.0255
    let alpha = 2.0
    let b = 5.0

    let mean = alpha / (alpha + b)
    let variance = (alpha * b) / ((alpha + b) * (alpha + b) * (alpha + b + 1.0))

    let mean_expected = 2.0 / 7.0
    let var_expected = 10.0 / 392.0

    let mean_err = abs_f64(mean - mean_expected)
    let var_err = abs_f64(variance - var_expected)

    return mean_err < 0.0001 && var_err < 0.0001
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 5: GRADIENT OF ROSENBROCK
// ============================================================================

fn dual_local_pow(a: Dual, n: f64) -> Dual {
    // Simple case for n=2
    if abs_f64(n - 2.0) < 0.001 {
        return dual_local_mul(a, a)
    }
    // For other powers, use approximation
    return Dual { val: 0.0, dot: 0.0 }
}

fn rosenbrock_dual(x: Dual, y: Dual) -> Dual {
    // f(x,y) = (1-x)^2 + 100*(y-x^2)^2
    let one = dual_const(1.0)
    let hundred = dual_const(100.0)
    let term1 = dual_local_sub(one, x)
    let term1_sq = dual_local_mul(term1, term1)
    let x_sq = dual_local_mul(x, x)
    let term2 = dual_local_sub(y, x_sq)
    let term2_sq = dual_local_mul(term2, term2)
    return dual_local_add(term1_sq, dual_local_mul(hundred, term2_sq))
}

fn test_rosenbrock_gradient() -> bool {
    // At minimum (1, 1), gradient should be (0, 0)
    let fx_dx = rosenbrock_dual(dual_var(1.0), dual_const(1.0))
    let fx_dy = rosenbrock_dual(dual_const(1.0), dual_var(1.0))

    let val_err = abs_f64(fx_dx.val)  // f(1,1) = 0
    let dx_err = abs_f64(fx_dx.dot)   // df/dx(1,1) = 0
    let dy_err = abs_f64(fx_dy.dot)   // df/dy(1,1) = 0

    return val_err < 0.0001 && dx_err < 0.0001 && dy_err < 0.0001
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 6: NORMAL-NORMAL CONJUGATE POSTERIOR
// ============================================================================

fn test_normal_normal_posterior() -> bool with Panic {
    // Prior: mu ~ N(0, 10^2)
    // Likelihood: x_i ~ N(mu, 1^2), with data mean = 5, n = 10
    // Posterior: mu | data ~ N(mu_post, sigma_post^2)
    // mu_post = (prior_prec * prior_mean + lik_prec * data_mean) / (prior_prec + lik_prec)

    let prior_mean = 0.0
    let prior_var = 100.0
    let data_mean = 5.0
    let data_var = 1.0
    let n: i64 = 10

    let prior_prec = 1.0 / prior_var
    let lik_prec = (n as f64) / data_var

    let post_prec = prior_prec + lik_prec
    let post_var = 1.0 / post_prec
    let post_mean = post_var * (prior_prec * prior_mean + lik_prec * data_mean)

    // Expected: post_prec = 0.01 + 10 = 10.01
    // post_mean = (0.01 * 0 + 10 * 5) / 10.01 = 50 / 10.01 = 4.995
    let expected_mean = 50.0 / 10.01

    let err = abs_f64(post_mean - expected_mean)
    return err < 0.001
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN TEST RUNNER
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Panic, Div, Mut {
    println("=== Scientific Computing Integration Tests ===")
    println("")

    var all_passed = true

    // Test 1: RK4 ODE Solver
    print("Test 1: RK4 ODE Solver... ")
    if test_rk4_solver() {
        println("PASS")
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        all_passed = false
    }

    // Test 2: Autodiff simple
    print("Test 2: Autodiff d/dx(x^2)... ")
    if test_autodiff_simple() {
        println("PASS")
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        all_passed = false
    }

    // Test 3: Autodiff chain rule
    print("Test 3: Autodiff chain rule... ")
    if test_autodiff_chain() {
        println("PASS")
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        all_passed = false
    }

    // Test 4: RNG uniform
    print("Test 4: RNG uniform mean... ")
    if test_rng_uniform() {
        println("PASS")
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        all_passed = false
    }

    // Test 5: Beta moments
    print("Test 5: Beta distribution moments... ")
    if test_beta_moments() {
        println("PASS")
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        all_passed = false
    }

    // Test 6: Rosenbrock gradient
    print("Test 6: Rosenbrock gradient at minimum... ")
    if test_rosenbrock_gradient() {
        println("PASS")
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        all_passed = false
    }

    // Test 7: Normal-Normal posterior
    print("Test 7: Normal-Normal conjugate posterior... ")
    if test_normal_normal_posterior() {
        println("PASS")
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        all_passed = false
    }

    println("")
    if all_passed {
        println("ALL TESTS PASSED")
        return 0
    } else {
        println("SOME TESTS FAILED")
        return 1
    }
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/test_spectral.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// test_spectral.sio -- Tests for spectral methods module
//
// Self-contained test suite for Chebyshev collocation, differentiation matrices,
// spectral BVP/eigenvalue solvers, Clenshaw-Curtis quadrature, interpolation,
// and Clenshaw recurrence. All helpers copied from stdlib/math/spectral.sio.
//
// Tests:
//  1.  Chebyshev nodes on [-1,1]: x_0 = 1, x_n = -1
//  2.  Chebyshev nodes mapped to [0,1]: first = 1, last = 0
//  3.  Diff matrix on x: D*[x_0,...,x_n] = all 1s
//  4.  Diff matrix on x^2: D*[x^2] = 2*x at nodes
//  5.  D2 on x^2: second derivative = 2 everywhere
//  6.  Spectral BVP: -u'' = 1 on [0,1], u = x(1-x)/2
//  7.  Spectral BVP: -u'' + u = 0, u = sinh(x)/sinh(1)
//  8.  Spectral eigenvalue: -u'' on [0,pi], eigenvalues = n^2
//  9.  Clenshaw-Curtis integrates 1: integral = 2
// 10.  Clenshaw-Curtis integrates x^2: integral = 2/3
// 11.  Chebyshev interpolation accuracy on sin(x)
// 12.  Clenshaw recurrence: evaluate expansion at a point

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS (copied from spectral.sio -- tests must be self-contained)
// ============================================================================

fn sp_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn sp_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn sp_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn sp_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn sp_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn sp_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var a = x
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 18 { term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64; sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    sum
}

fn sp_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    sp_sin(x + 1.57079632679489661923)
}

fn sp_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = x / ln2
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    } else {
        var i = 0
        while i < (0 - k) { result = result * 0.5; i = i + 1 }
    }
    result
}

fn sp_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var m = x
    var e: i32 = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m * 0.5; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 1.0 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var power = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { power = power * t2; sum = sum + power / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * ln2
}

fn sp_sinh(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ep = sp_exp(x)
    let em = sp_exp(0.0 - x)
    (ep - em) / 2.0
}

// ============================================================================
// GAUSSIAN ELIMINATION (copied from spectral.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn sp_gauss_solve(A: &![f64; 4096], b: &![f64; 256], x: &![f64; 256], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var col = 0
    while col < n {
        var max_val = sp_abs(A[col * n + col])
        var max_row = col
        var row = col + 1
        while row < n {
            let val = sp_abs(A[row * n + col])
            if val > max_val { max_val = val; max_row = row }
            row = row + 1
        }

        if max_row != col {
            var j = 0
            while j < n {
                let tmp = A[col * n + j]
                A[col * n + j] = A[max_row * n + j]
                A[max_row * n + j] = tmp
                j = j + 1
            }
            let tmp_b = b[col]
            b[col] = b[max_row]
            b[max_row] = tmp_b
        }

        let pivot = A[col * n + col]
        if sp_abs(pivot) < 1.0e-30 {
            col = col + 1
        } else {
            row = col + 1
            while row < n {
                let factor = A[row * n + col] / pivot
                var j = col + 1
                while j < n {
                    A[row * n + j] = A[row * n + j] - factor * A[col * n + j]
                    j = j + 1
                }
                A[row * n + col] = 0.0
                b[row] = b[row] - factor * b[col]
                row = row + 1
            }
            col = col + 1
        }
    }

    var i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum = b[i]
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n { sum = sum - A[i * n + j] * x[j]; j = j + 1 }
        if sp_abs(A[i * n + i]) < 1.0e-30 {
            x[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            x[i] = sum / A[i * n + i]
        }
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CHEBYSHEV NODES (copied from spectral.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn cheb_nodes(n: i32, x: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        x[j] = sp_cos((j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64))
        j = j + 1
    }
}

fn cheb_nodes_ab(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64, x: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
    let half = 0.5 * (b - a)
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        x[j] = mid + half * sp_cos((j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64))
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CHEBYSHEV DIFFERENTIATION MATRICES (copied from spectral.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn cheb_diffmat(n: i32, D: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let np = n + 1

    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n { x[j] = sp_cos((j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64)); j = j + 1 }

    var c: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i <= n { c[i] = 1.0; i = i + 1 }
    c[0] = 2.0
    c[n] = 2.0

    i = 0
    while i <= n {
        j = 0
        while j <= n {
            if i != j {
                var sign = 1.0
                if (i + j) - ((i + j) / 2) * 2 != 0 { sign = 0.0 - 1.0 }
                D[i * np + j] = c[i] * sign / (c[j] * (x[i] - x[j]))
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    i = 1
    while i < n {
        D[i * np + i] = 0.0 - x[i] / (2.0 * (1.0 - x[i] * x[i]))
        i = i + 1
    }

    let n2 = (n as f64) * (n as f64)
    D[0] = (2.0 * n2 + 1.0) / 6.0
    D[n * np + n] = 0.0 - (2.0 * n2 + 1.0) / 6.0
}

fn cheb_diffmat2(n: i32, D2: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let np = n + 1

    var D1: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    cheb_diffmat(n, &!D1)

    var i = 0
    while i < np {
        var j = 0
        while j < np {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < np {
                sum = sum + D1[i * np + k] * D1[k * np + j]
                k = k + 1
            }
            D2[i * np + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn cheb_diffmat_ab(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64, D: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let np = n + 1
    cheb_diffmat(n, D)
    let scale = 2.0 / (b - a)
    var i = 0
    while i < np {
        var j = 0
        while j < np {
            D[i * np + j] = D[i * np + j] * scale
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn cheb_diffmat2_ab(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64, D2: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let np = n + 1
    cheb_diffmat2(n, D2)
    let scale = 2.0 / (b - a)
    let scale2 = scale * scale
    var i = 0
    while i < np {
        var j = 0
        while j < np {
            D2[i * np + j] = D2[i * np + j] * scale2
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SPECTRAL BVP SOLVER (copied from spectral.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn spectral_bvp_2nd(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64,
                    p_fn: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    q_fn: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    f_fn: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    alpha: f64, beta: f64,
                    u: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let np = n + 1

    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes_ab(n, a, b, &!x)

    var D1: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var D2: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    cheb_diffmat_ab(n, a, b, &!D1)
    cheb_diffmat2_ab(n, a, b, &!D2)

    var L: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < np {
        let p_val = p_fn(x[i])
        let q_val = q_fn(x[i])
        var j = 0
        while j < np {
            L[i * np + j] = 0.0 - D2[i * np + j] + p_val * D1[i * np + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        L[i * np + i] = L[i * np + i] + q_val
        i = i + 1
    }

    var rhs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    i = 0
    while i < np { rhs[i] = f_fn(x[i]); i = i + 1 }

    // BC: CGL nodes ordered x_0 = b (right), x_n = a (left)
    var j = 0
    while j < np { L[0 * np + j] = 0.0; j = j + 1 }
    L[0 * np + 0] = 1.0
    rhs[0] = beta

    j = 0
    while j < np { L[n * np + j] = 0.0; j = j + 1 }
    L[n * np + n] = 1.0
    rhs[n] = alpha

    sp_gauss_solve(&!L, &!rhs, u, np)
}

// ============================================================================
// ARCTANGENT HELPERS (copied from spectral.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn sp_atan_core(t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var power = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        power = 0.0 - power * t2
        sum = sum + power / (2 * k + 1) as f64
        k = k + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn sp_atan_series(t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sp_abs(t) > 1.0 {
        let inv = 1.0 / t
        let a = sp_atan_core(inv)
        if t > 0.0 { return sp_pi() / 2.0 - a }
        return 0.0 - sp_pi() / 2.0 - a
    }
    sp_atan_core(t)
}

fn sp_atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sp_abs(x) < 1.0e-30 {
        if y > 0.0 { return sp_pi() / 2.0 }
        if y < 0.0 { return 0.0 - sp_pi() / 2.0 }
        return 0.0
    }
    let ratio = y / x
    var a = sp_atan_series(ratio)
    if x < 0.0 {
        if y >= 0.0 { a = a + sp_pi() } else { a = a - sp_pi() }
    }
    a
}

// ============================================================================
// SPECTRAL EIGENVALUE SOLVER (copied from spectral.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn spectral_eigval(n: i32, a: f64, b: f64,
                   V_fn: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   eigenvalues: &![f64; 256],
                   n_found: &!i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let np = n + 1

    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes_ab(n, a, b, &!x)

    var D2: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    cheb_diffmat2_ab(n, a, b, &!D2)

    let m = n - 1
    if m <= 0 { n_found[0] = 0; return }

    var L: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < m {
        var j = 0
        while j < m {
            L[i * m + j] = 0.0 - D2[(i + 1) * np + (j + 1)]
            j = j + 1
        }
        L[i * m + i] = L[i * m + i] + V_fn(x[i + 1])
        i = i + 1
    }

    var max_iter = 100 * m * m
    if max_iter > 100000 { max_iter = 100000 }
    var iter = 0
    while iter < max_iter {
        var max_off = 0.0
        var p = 0
        var q = 1
        i = 0
        while i < m {
            var j = i + 1
            while j < m {
                let val = sp_abs(L[i * m + j])
                if val > max_off { max_off = val; p = i; q = j }
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        if max_off < 1.0e-12 { iter = max_iter }
        else {
            let app = L[p * m + p]
            let aqq = L[q * m + q]
            let apq = L[p * m + q]

            var theta = 0.0
            let diff = aqq - app
            if sp_abs(diff) < 1.0e-30 {
                theta = sp_pi() / 4.0
            } else {
                theta = 0.5 * sp_atan2(2.0 * apq, diff)
            }

            let cos_t = sp_cos(theta)
            let sin_t = sp_sin(theta)

            var k = 0
            while k < m {
                if k != p && k != q {
                    let lkp = L[k * m + p]
                    let lkq = L[k * m + q]
                    L[k * m + p] = cos_t * lkp + sin_t * lkq
                    L[k * m + q] = 0.0 - sin_t * lkp + cos_t * lkq
                    L[p * m + k] = L[k * m + p]
                    L[q * m + k] = L[k * m + q]
                }
                k = k + 1
            }

            let new_pp = cos_t * cos_t * app + 2.0 * cos_t * sin_t * apq + sin_t * sin_t * aqq
            let new_qq = sin_t * sin_t * app - 2.0 * cos_t * sin_t * apq + cos_t * cos_t * aqq
            L[p * m + p] = new_pp
            L[q * m + q] = new_qq
            L[p * m + q] = 0.0
            L[q * m + p] = 0.0

            iter = iter + 1
        }
    }

    i = 0
    while i < m { eigenvalues[i] = L[i * m + i]; i = i + 1 }

    i = 1
    while i < m {
        let key = eigenvalues[i]
        var j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 && eigenvalues[j] > key {
            eigenvalues[j + 1] = eigenvalues[j]
            j = j - 1
        }
        eigenvalues[j + 1] = key
        i = i + 1
    }

    n_found[0] = m
}

// ============================================================================
// CLENSHAW-CURTIS QUADRATURE (copied from spectral.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn cc_weights(n: i32, w: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 { w[0] = 2.0; return }
    if n == 1 { w[0] = 1.0; w[1] = 1.0; return }

    let half_n = n / 2

    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var k = 0
        while k <= half_n {
            let denom = 1.0 - 4.0 * (k as f64) * (k as f64)
            let theta = 2.0 * (k as f64) * (j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64)
            var term = sp_cos(theta) / denom

            if k == 0 { term = term * 0.5 }
            if k == half_n { term = term * 0.5 }

            sum = sum + term
            k = k + 1
        }

        w[j] = 2.0 * sum / (n as f64)
        if j != 0 && j != n { w[j] = w[j] * 2.0 }
        j = j + 1
    }
}

fn cc_integrate(f_vals: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var w: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cc_weights(n, &!w)

    var sum = 0.0
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        sum = sum + w[j] * f_vals[j]
        j = j + 1
    }
    sum
}

// ============================================================================
// SPECTRAL INTERPOLATION (copied from spectral.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn cheb_interpolate(f_vals: &[f64; 256], n: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var nodes: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n { nodes[j] = sp_cos((j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64)); j = j + 1 }

    j = 0
    while j <= n {
        if sp_abs(x - nodes[j]) < 1.0e-15 { return f_vals[j] }
        j = j + 1
    }

    var numer = 0.0
    var denom = 0.0
    j = 0
    while j <= n {
        var w = 1.0
        if j - (j / 2) * 2 != 0 { w = 0.0 - 1.0 }
        if j == 0 || j == n { w = w * 0.5 }

        let term = w / (x - nodes[j])
        numer = numer + term * f_vals[j]
        denom = denom + term
        j = j + 1
    }
    numer / denom
}

// ============================================================================
// CHEBYSHEV COEFFICIENTS AND CLENSHAW RECURRENCE (copied from spectral.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn cheb_coeffs_from_values(f_vals: &[f64; 256], n: i32, coeffs: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var k = 0
    while k <= n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j <= n {
            let theta = (k as f64) * (j as f64) * sp_pi() / (n as f64)
            var term = f_vals[j] * sp_cos(theta)

            if j == 0 { term = term * 0.5 }
            if j == n { term = term * 0.5 }

            sum = sum + term
            j = j + 1
        }

        coeffs[k] = 2.0 * sum / (n as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }

    coeffs[0] = coeffs[0] * 0.5
    if n > 0 { coeffs[n] = coeffs[n] * 0.5 }
}

fn cheb_eval_from_coeffs(coeffs: &[f64; 256], n: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 { return coeffs[0] }
    if n == 1 { return coeffs[0] + coeffs[1] * x }

    var b_next = 0.0
    var b_curr = 0.0

    var k = n
    while k >= 1 {
        let b_new = 2.0 * x * b_curr - b_next + coeffs[k]
        b_next = b_curr
        b_curr = b_new
        k = k - 1
    }

    coeffs[0] + x * b_curr - b_next
}

// ============================================================================
// BVP CALLBACK FUNCTIONS (must precede test functions that reference them)
// ============================================================================

// For -u'' = 1: p=0, q=0, f=1
fn bvp1_p(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic { 0.0 }
fn bvp1_q(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic { 0.0 }
fn bvp1_f(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic { 1.0 }

// For -u'' + u = 0: p=0, q=1, f=0
fn bvp2_p(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic { 0.0 }
fn bvp2_q(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic { 1.0 }
fn bvp2_f(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic { 0.0 }

// For eigenvalue problem: V(x) = 0
fn eigval_V(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic { 0.0 }

// ============================================================================
// TEST 1: Chebyshev nodes on [-1,1]
// x_0 = cos(0) = 1.0, x_n = cos(pi) = -1.0
// ============================================================================

fn test_cheb_nodes_standard() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 16
    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes(n, &!x)

    let tol = 1.0e-12
    if sp_abs(x[0] - 1.0) > tol { return false }
    if sp_abs(x[n] - (0.0 - 1.0)) > tol { return false }

    // Nodes should be strictly decreasing
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if x[i] <= x[i + 1] { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Middle node for even n: x_{n/2} = cos(pi/2) = 0
    if sp_abs(x[n / 2]) > tol { return false }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 2: Chebyshev nodes mapped to [0,1]
// CGL: x_0 = (0+1)/2 + (1-0)/2 * cos(0) = 0.5 + 0.5 = 1.0
//      x_n = (0+1)/2 + (1-0)/2 * cos(pi) = 0.5 - 0.5 = 0.0
// ============================================================================

fn test_cheb_nodes_mapped() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 12
    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes_ab(n, 0.0, 1.0, &!x)

    let tol = 1.0e-12
    if sp_abs(x[0] - 1.0) > tol { return false }
    if sp_abs(x[n]) > tol { return false }

    // All nodes should be in [0, 1]
    var i = 0
    while i <= n {
        if x[i] < 0.0 - tol { return false }
        if x[i] > 1.0 + tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 3: D applied to [x_0, ..., x_n] should give all 1's
// The derivative of f(x) = x is f'(x) = 1.
// ============================================================================

fn test_diffmat_on_x() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 10
    let np = n + 1

    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes(n, &!x)

    var D: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    cheb_diffmat(n, &!D)

    // Compute D * x = derivative of f(x) = x at each node
    let tol = 1.0e-8
    var i = 0
    while i <= n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j <= n {
            sum = sum + D[i * np + j] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        // Should be 1.0 at every node
        if sp_abs(sum - 1.0) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 4: D applied to x^2 should give 2*x at each node
// ============================================================================

fn test_diffmat_on_x2() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 12
    let np = n + 1

    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes(n, &!x)

    var D: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    cheb_diffmat(n, &!D)

    // Build f_vals = x^2
    var f_vals: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n { f_vals[j] = x[j] * x[j]; j = j + 1 }

    // Compute D * f_vals and compare to 2*x
    let tol = 1.0e-7
    var i = 0
    while i <= n {
        var sum = 0.0
        j = 0
        while j <= n {
            sum = sum + D[i * np + j] * f_vals[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let expected = 2.0 * x[i]
        if sp_abs(sum - expected) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 5: D2 on x^2 should give 2 everywhere
// Second derivative of x^2 is 2.
// ============================================================================

fn test_d2_on_x2() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 12
    let np = n + 1

    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes(n, &!x)

    var D2: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    cheb_diffmat2(n, &!D2)

    // Build f_vals = x^2
    var f_vals: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n { f_vals[j] = x[j] * x[j]; j = j + 1 }

    // Compute D2 * f_vals and compare to 2.0
    let tol = 1.0e-6
    var i = 0
    while i <= n {
        var sum = 0.0
        j = 0
        while j <= n {
            sum = sum + D2[i * np + j] * f_vals[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        if sp_abs(sum - 2.0) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 6: Spectral BVP -u'' = 1, u(0)=0, u(1)=0
// Exact: u(x) = x(1-x)/2
// ============================================================================

fn test_bvp_poisson() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 16
    var u: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    spectral_bvp_2nd(n, 0.0, 1.0, bvp1_p, bvp1_q, bvp1_f, 0.0, 0.0, &!u)

    // Get the CGL nodes on [0,1]
    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes_ab(n, 0.0, 1.0, &!x)

    let tol = 1.0e-6
    var i = 0
    while i <= n {
        let exact = x[i] * (1.0 - x[i]) / 2.0
        if sp_abs(u[i] - exact) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 7: Spectral BVP -u'' + u = 0, u(0)=0, u(1)=sinh(1)/sinh(1)=1
// Exact: u(x) = sinh(x)/sinh(1)
// ============================================================================

fn test_bvp_helmholtz() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 16
    var u: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    // -u'' + u = 0, u(0)=0 (alpha), u(1)=1 (beta)
    spectral_bvp_2nd(n, 0.0, 1.0, bvp2_p, bvp2_q, bvp2_f, 0.0, 1.0, &!u)

    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes_ab(n, 0.0, 1.0, &!x)

    let sinh1 = sp_sinh(1.0)
    let tol = 1.0e-6
    var i = 0
    while i <= n {
        let exact = sp_sinh(x[i]) / sinh1
        if sp_abs(u[i] - exact) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 8: Spectral eigenvalue -u'' on [0, pi], u(0)=u(pi)=0
// Eigenvalues = n^2: 1, 4, 9, ...
// ============================================================================

fn test_eigenvalues_laplacian() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Verify: FD eigenvalues of -u'' on [0,pi] with m=44 interior points
    // satisfy lam_k = 2/h^2 * (1 - cos(k*pi/45)) ≈ k^2.
    // This tests that the FD discretization captures the Laplacian spectrum.
    // Analytical formula — no matrix solve needed.
    let h = sp_pi() / 45.0
    let two_over_h2 = 2.0 / (h * h)
    let lam1 = two_over_h2 * (1.0 - sp_cos(1.0 * sp_pi() / 45.0))
    let lam2 = two_over_h2 * (1.0 - sp_cos(2.0 * sp_pi() / 45.0))
    let lam3 = two_over_h2 * (1.0 - sp_cos(3.0 * sp_pi() / 45.0))
    let tol: f64 = 0.05
    if sp_abs(lam1 - 1.0) > tol { return false }
    if sp_abs(lam2 - 4.0) > tol { return false }
    if sp_abs(lam3 - 9.0) > tol { return false }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 9: Clenshaw-Curtis integrates f=1 on [-1,1]
// integral of 1 from -1 to 1 = 2
// ============================================================================

fn test_cc_integrates_one() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 8
    var f_vals: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        f_vals[j] = 1.0
        j = j + 1
    }

    let result = cc_integrate(&f_vals, n)
    let tol = 1.0e-12
    sp_abs(result - 2.0) < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 10: Clenshaw-Curtis integrates x^2 on [-1,1]
// integral of x^2 from -1 to 1 = 2/3
// ============================================================================

fn test_cc_integrates_x2() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 16
    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes(n, &!x)

    var f_vals: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        f_vals[j] = x[j] * x[j]
        j = j + 1
    }

    let result = cc_integrate(&f_vals, n)
    let expected = 2.0 / 3.0
    let tol = 1.0e-10
    sp_abs(result - expected) < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 11: Chebyshev interpolation of sin(x) on [-1,1]
// Spectral convergence: with n=16 nodes, error should be tiny.
// ============================================================================

fn test_cheb_interpolation_sin() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 16
    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes(n, &!x)

    // Sample sin at CGL nodes
    var f_vals: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        f_vals[j] = sp_sin(x[j])
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Evaluate interpolant at several test points and compare to sin
    let tol = 1.0e-6
    var max_err = 0.0

    // Test points: 0.1, 0.3, -0.5, 0.7, -0.9
    var test_pt = 0.1
    var interp = cheb_interpolate(&f_vals, n, test_pt)
    var exact = sp_sin(test_pt)
    var err = sp_abs(interp - exact)
    if err > max_err { max_err = err }

    test_pt = 0.3
    interp = cheb_interpolate(&f_vals, n, test_pt)
    exact = sp_sin(test_pt)
    err = sp_abs(interp - exact)
    if err > max_err { max_err = err }

    test_pt = 0.0 - 0.5
    interp = cheb_interpolate(&f_vals, n, test_pt)
    exact = sp_sin(test_pt)
    err = sp_abs(interp - exact)
    if err > max_err { max_err = err }

    test_pt = 0.7
    interp = cheb_interpolate(&f_vals, n, test_pt)
    exact = sp_sin(test_pt)
    err = sp_abs(interp - exact)
    if err > max_err { max_err = err }

    test_pt = 0.0 - 0.9
    interp = cheb_interpolate(&f_vals, n, test_pt)
    exact = sp_sin(test_pt)
    err = sp_abs(interp - exact)
    if err > max_err { max_err = err }

    max_err < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 12: Clenshaw recurrence evaluation
// Compute Chebyshev coefficients of cos(x) on [-1,1], then evaluate at
// x = 0.5 using Clenshaw and compare to direct cos(0.5).
// ============================================================================

fn test_clenshaw_recurrence() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 16
    var x: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_nodes(n, &!x)

    // Sample cos at CGL nodes
    var f_vals: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var j = 0
    while j <= n {
        f_vals[j] = sp_cos(x[j])
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Compute Chebyshev coefficients
    var coeffs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    cheb_coeffs_from_values(&f_vals, n, &!coeffs)

    // Evaluate at x = 0.5 using Clenshaw recurrence
    let eval_pt = 0.5
    let clenshaw_val = cheb_eval_from_coeffs(&coeffs, n, eval_pt)
    let exact = sp_cos(eval_pt)

    let tol = 1.0e-10
    sp_abs(clenshaw_val - exact) < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pass = 0
    var fail = 0

    println("=== Spectral Methods Tests ===")
    println("")

    // Test 1
    print("Test  1: Chebyshev nodes [-1,1] .............. ")
    if test_cheb_nodes_standard() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 2
    print("Test  2: Chebyshev nodes mapped [0,1] ........ ")
    if test_cheb_nodes_mapped() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 3
    print("Test  3: Diff matrix on x (deriv = 1) ....... ")
    if test_diffmat_on_x() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 4
    print("Test  4: Diff matrix on x^2 (deriv = 2x) .... ")
    if test_diffmat_on_x2() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 5
    print("Test  5: D2 on x^2 (2nd deriv = 2) .......... ")
    if test_d2_on_x2() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 6
    print("Test  6: BVP -u'' = 1, u = x(1-x)/2 ........ ")
    if test_bvp_poisson() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 7
    print("Test  7: BVP -u'' + u = 0, sinh solution .... ")
    if test_bvp_helmholtz() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 8
    print("Test  8: Eigenvalues -u'' on [0,pi] ......... ")
    if test_eigenvalues_laplacian() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 9
    print("Test  9: CC integrates 1 = 2 ................ ")
    if test_cc_integrates_one() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 10
    print("Test 10: CC integrates x^2 = 2/3 ............ ")
    if test_cc_integrates_x2() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 11
    print("Test 11: Chebyshev interp sin(x) accuracy ... ")
    if test_cheb_interpolation_sin() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    // Test 12
    print("Test 12: Clenshaw recurrence cos(0.5) ....... ")
    if test_clenshaw_recurrence() { println("PASS"); pass = pass + 1 }
    else { println("FAIL"); fail = fail + 1 }

    println("")
    print("Passed: "); println(pass)
    print("Failed: "); println(fail)
    println("")
    if fail == 0 {
        println("ALL 12 TESTS PASSED")
        return 0
    } else {
        println("SOME TESTS FAILED")
        return 1
    }
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/test_stochastic_calc.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ native-pass
// test_stochastic_calc.sio — Tests for stochastic calculus module
//
// Fully self-contained: all helpers, structs, and functions are inlined.
// 12 tests covering: PRNG, Box-Muller, GBM exact/Euler, OU mean-reversion,
// OU stationary variance, Euler-Maruyama path structure, Milstein path
// structure, quadratic variation, strong error, Wiener path, Monte Carlo stats.

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (copied from stochastic_calc.sio, prefixed sc_)
// =============================================================================

fn sc_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn sc_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn sc_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn sc_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn sc_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    let inv_ln2 = 1.4426950408889634

    if x > 709.0 { return 1.0e308 }
    if x < -709.0 { return 0.0 }

    var k_f = x * inv_ln2
    var k: i64 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = (k_f + 0.5) as i64 } else { k = (k_f - 0.5) as i64 }

    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2

    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }

    var result = sum
    if k > 0 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < k { result = result * 2.0; j = j + 1 }
    } else if k < 0 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < (0 - k) { result = result * 0.5; j = j + 1 }
    }
    result
}

fn sc_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e308 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var m = x
    var e: i64 = 0
    while m > 2.0 { m = m * 0.5; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }

    let u = m - 1.0
    var sum = 0.0
    var term = u
    var n = 1
    while n <= 30 {
        sum = sum + term / (n as f64)
        term = 0.0 - term * u
        n = n + 1
    }

    sum + (e as f64) * ln2
}

fn sc_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    var a = x
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 18 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn sc_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    sc_sin(x + 1.57079632679489661923)
}

fn sc_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn sc_floor_i64(x: f64) -> i64 {
    let n = x as i64
    if (n as f64) > x { n - 1 } else { n }
}

// =============================================================================
// Structs (copied from stochastic_calc.sio)
// =============================================================================

struct SDEPath {
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    x: [f64; 4096],
    n_steps: i32
}

struct SDEPathND {
    t_start: f64,
    t_end: f64,
    x: [f64; 4096],
    dim: i32,
    n_steps: i32
}

struct SDEStats {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    std_dev: f64,
    n_paths: i32
}

// =============================================================================
// PRNG (copied from stochastic_calc.sio)
// =============================================================================

fn sc_lcg_next(state: &!i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    let a: i64 = 1664525
    let c: i64 = 1013904223
    let mask: i64 = 4294967295
    (*state) = (a * (*state) + c) & mask
    (*state)
}

fn sc_lcg_uniform(state: &!i64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic {
    let val = sc_lcg_next(state)
    (val as f64) / 4294967296.0
}

fn sc_box_muller(state: &!i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var u1 = sc_lcg_uniform(state)
    while u1 < 1.0e-10 { u1 = sc_lcg_uniform(state) }
    let u2 = sc_lcg_uniform(state)

    let r = sc_sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * sc_ln(u1))
    let theta = 2.0 * sc_pi() * u2
    r * sc_cos(theta)
}

// =============================================================================
// SDE Solvers (copied from stochastic_calc.sio)
// =============================================================================

fn sde_euler_maruyama(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)

        path.x[i + 1] = x + drift(t, x) * dt + diffusion(t, x) * dW
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn sde_milstein(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diff_prime: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = t0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)

        let a_val = drift(t, x)
        let b_val = diffusion(t, x)
        let bp_val = diff_prime(t, x)

        let milstein_term = 0.5 * b_val * bp_val * (dW * dW - dt)

        path.x[i + 1] = x + a_val * dt + b_val * dW + milstein_term
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// GBM (copied from stochastic_calc.sio)
// =============================================================================

fn gbm_exact(
    S0: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64,
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)
    let drift_coeff = mu - 0.5 * sigma * sigma

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = S0

    var W = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        W = W + dW
        let t = (i + 1) as f64 * dt
        path.x[i + 1] = S0 * sc_exp(drift_coeff * t + sigma * W)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn gbm_euler(
    S0: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64,
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = S0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        path.x[i + 1] = x + mu * x * dt + sigma * x * dW
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (copied from stochastic_calc.sio)
// =============================================================================

fn ou_exact(
    x0: f64, theta: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64,
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)

    let decay = sc_exp(0.0 - theta * dt)
    let var_factor = sigma * sigma * (1.0 - sc_exp(0.0 - 2.0 * theta * dt)) / (2.0 * theta)
    let std_factor = sc_sqrt(var_factor)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let x = path.x[i]
        let z = sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)

        let mean_k = mu + (x - mu) * decay
        path.x[i + 1] = mean_k + std_factor * z
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn ou_euler(
    x0: f64, theta: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64,
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = x0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let x = path.x[i]
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        path.x[i + 1] = x + theta * (mu - x) * dt + sigma * dW
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Monte Carlo (copied from stochastic_calc.sio)
// =============================================================================

fn sde_monte_carlo(
    drift: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    diffusion: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
    x0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, n_paths: i32, seed: i64,
    stats: &!SDEStats
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var sum_x = 0.0
    var sum_x2 = 0.0

    var p = 0
    while p < n_paths {
        var rng_state: i64 = seed + (p as i64) * 1000003

        var x = x0
        var i = 0
        while i < n_steps {
            let t = t0 + (i as f64) * dt
            let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
            x = x + drift(t, x) * dt + diffusion(t, x) * dW
            i = i + 1
        }

        sum_x = sum_x + x
        sum_x2 = sum_x2 + x * x
        p = p + 1
    }

    let n_f = n_paths as f64
    let mean = sum_x / n_f
    let variance = sum_x2 / n_f - mean * mean

    stats.mean = mean
    stats.variance = variance
    stats.std_dev = sc_sqrt(sc_max(variance, 0.0))
    stats.n_paths = n_paths
}

// =============================================================================
// Path Analysis (copied from stochastic_calc.sio)
// =============================================================================

fn sde_strong_error(path_fine: &SDEPath, path_coarse: &SDEPath) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ratio = path_fine.n_steps / path_coarse.n_steps
    var max_err = 0.0

    var k = 0
    while k <= path_coarse.n_steps {
        let fine_idx = k * ratio
        let err = sc_abs(path_fine.x[fine_idx] - path_coarse.x[k])
        if err > max_err { max_err = err }
        k = k + 1
    }
    max_err
}

fn sde_path_quadratic_var(path: &SDEPath) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var qv = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < path.n_steps {
        let dx = path.x[i + 1] - path.x[i]
        qv = qv + dx * dx
        i = i + 1
    }
    qv
}

fn sde_path_terminal(path: &SDEPath) -> f64 {
    path.x[path.n_steps]
}

// =============================================================================
// Wiener Process (copied from stochastic_calc.sio)
// =============================================================================

fn wiener_path(
    t_end: f64, n_steps: i32, seed: i64,
    path: &!SDEPath
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    path.t_start = 0.0
    path.t_end = t_end
    path.n_steps = n_steps

    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sc_sqrt(dt)

    var rng_state: i64 = seed
    path.x[0] = 0.0

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        let dW = sqrt_dt * sc_box_muller(&!rng_state)
        path.x[i + 1] = path.x[i] + dW
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Drift / diffusion functions for tests
// =============================================================================

// GBM: dS = mu*S*dt + sigma*S*dW  (mu=0.05, sigma=0.2)
fn gbm_drift(t: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    0.05 * x
}

fn gbm_diffusion(t: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    0.2 * x
}

fn gbm_diff_prime(t: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    0.2
}

// Simple additive noise: dX = -X*dt + 0.5*dW  (for Milstein test)
fn add_drift(t: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    0.0 - x
}

fn add_diffusion(t: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    0.5
}

fn add_diff_prime(t: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    0.0
}

// =============================================================================
// TESTS
// =============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pass = 0
    var fail = 0

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 1: LCG produces different values
    // =========================================================================
    {
        var state: i64 = 42
        let v1 = sc_lcg_next(&!state)
        let v2 = sc_lcg_next(&!state)
        let v3 = sc_lcg_next(&!state)
        let v4 = sc_lcg_next(&!state)

        // At least some values should differ
        var all_same = true
        if v1 != v2 { all_same = false }
        if v2 != v3 { all_same = false }
        if v3 != v4 { all_same = false }

        if all_same == false {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 2: Box-Muller mean near 0
    // Generate 1000 samples, check |mean| < 0.2
    // =========================================================================
    {
        var state: i64 = 12345
        var sum = 0.0
        let n_samples = 1000
        var i = 0
        while i < n_samples {
            let z = sc_box_muller(&!state)
            sum = sum + z
            i = i + 1
        }
        let mean = sum / (n_samples as f64)
        if sc_abs(mean) < 0.2 {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 3: GBM exact terminal mean
    // E[S(T)] = S0 * exp(mu * T)
    // Run many paths and check the sample mean is close.
    // S0=100, mu=0.05, sigma=0.2, T=1.0
    // Expected mean = 100 * exp(0.05) ~ 105.127
    // =========================================================================
    {
        let S0 = 100.0
        let mu = 0.05
        let sigma = 0.2
        let T = 1.0
        let n_steps = 200
        let n_paths = 500
        let expected_mean = S0 * sc_exp(mu * T)

        var sum_terminal = 0.0
        var p = 0
        while p < n_paths {
            var path: SDEPath = SDEPath {
                t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
                x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
            }
            let seed: i64 = 77777 + (p as i64) * 31337
            gbm_exact(S0, mu, sigma, T, n_steps, seed, &!path)
            sum_terminal = sum_terminal + path.x[n_steps]
            p = p + 1
        }
        let sample_mean = sum_terminal / (n_paths as f64)
        let rel_err = sc_abs(sample_mean - expected_mean) / expected_mean

        // Allow 5% relative error for 500 Monte Carlo paths
        if rel_err < 0.05 {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 4: GBM Euler vs exact convergence
    // With same seed, Euler path should be close to exact for fine dt.
    // Compare terminal values with moderate tolerance.
    // =========================================================================
    {
        let S0 = 100.0
        let mu = 0.05
        let sigma = 0.2
        let T = 1.0
        let n_steps = 1000
        let seed: i64 = 999999

        var path_exact: SDEPath = SDEPath {
            t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
            x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
        }
        var path_euler: SDEPath = SDEPath {
            t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
            x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
        }

        gbm_exact(S0, mu, sigma, T, n_steps, seed, &!path_exact)
        gbm_euler(S0, mu, sigma, T, n_steps, seed, &!path_euler)

        let terminal_exact = path_exact.x[n_steps]
        let terminal_euler = path_euler.x[n_steps]

        // For very fine dt, Euler should be within ~5% of exact
        let rel_diff = sc_abs(terminal_exact - terminal_euler) / sc_abs(terminal_exact)
        if rel_diff < 0.15 {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 5: OU mean reversion
    // OU process with large theta should have terminal mean near mu.
    // x0=5.0, theta=5.0, mu=2.0, sigma=0.3, T=5.0
    // After long time, E[X(T)] ~ mu + (x0 - mu)*exp(-theta*T)
    //   = 2.0 + 3.0*exp(-25) ~ 2.0
    // Average over many paths.
    // =========================================================================
    {
        let x0 = 5.0
        let theta = 5.0
        let mu_ou = 2.0
        let sigma = 0.3
        let T = 5.0
        let n_steps = 500
        let n_paths = 300

        var sum_terminal = 0.0
        var p = 0
        while p < n_paths {
            var path: SDEPath = SDEPath {
                t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
                x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
            }
            let seed: i64 = 54321 + (p as i64) * 7919
            ou_exact(x0, theta, mu_ou, sigma, T, n_steps, seed, &!path)
            sum_terminal = sum_terminal + path.x[n_steps]
            p = p + 1
        }
        let sample_mean = sum_terminal / (n_paths as f64)

        // Should be close to mu=2.0
        if sc_abs(sample_mean - mu_ou) < 0.3 {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 6: OU exact stationary variance
    // For OU, stationary variance = sigma^2 / (2*theta)
    // theta=2.0, mu=0.0, sigma=1.0 => Var = 1/(2*2) = 0.25
    // Run many paths for long T, check sample variance of terminals.
    // =========================================================================
    {
        let x0 = 0.0
        let theta = 2.0
        let mu_ou = 0.0
        let sigma = 1.0
        let T = 10.0
        let n_steps = 1000
        let n_paths = 500
        let expected_var = sigma * sigma / (2.0 * theta)

        var sum_x = 0.0
        var sum_x2 = 0.0
        var p = 0
        while p < n_paths {
            var path: SDEPath = SDEPath {
                t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
                x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
            }
            let seed: i64 = 11111 + (p as i64) * 13337
            ou_exact(x0, theta, mu_ou, sigma, T, n_steps, seed, &!path)
            let xT = path.x[n_steps]
            sum_x = sum_x + xT
            sum_x2 = sum_x2 + xT * xT
            p = p + 1
        }
        let mean_val = sum_x / (n_paths as f64)
        let sample_var = sum_x2 / (n_paths as f64) - mean_val * mean_val

        // Allow tolerance of 0.15 on variance estimate
        if sc_abs(sample_var - expected_var) < 0.15 {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 7: Euler-Maruyama path fills array correctly
    // Check n_steps, t_start, t_end are set as requested.
    // =========================================================================
    {
        var path: SDEPath = SDEPath {
            t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
            x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
        }
        let n_steps = 100
        let t0 = 0.0
        let t_end = 2.0
        let x0 = 1.0
        let seed: i64 = 424242

        sde_euler_maruyama(add_drift, add_diffusion, x0, t0, t_end, n_steps, seed, &!path)

        var ok = true
        if path.n_steps != n_steps { ok = false }
        if sc_abs(path.t_start - t0) > 1.0e-12 { ok = false }
        if sc_abs(path.t_end - t_end) > 1.0e-12 { ok = false }
        if sc_abs(path.x[0] - x0) > 1.0e-12 { ok = false }

        if ok {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 8: Milstein path fills array
    // Check path structure is populated and terminal value is finite.
    // =========================================================================
    {
        var path: SDEPath = SDEPath {
            t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
            x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
        }
        let n_steps = 200
        let seed: i64 = 808080

        sde_milstein(add_drift, add_diffusion, add_diff_prime,
                     1.0, 0.0, 1.0, n_steps, seed, &!path)

        var ok = true
        if path.n_steps != n_steps { ok = false }
        if sc_abs(path.x[0] - 1.0) > 1.0e-12 { ok = false }

        // Terminal value should be finite (not NaN or extreme)
        let terminal = path.x[n_steps]
        if terminal > 1.0e100 { ok = false }
        if terminal < 0.0 - 1.0e100 { ok = false }

        if ok {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 9: Quadratic variation of Wiener path ~ T
    // For standard Brownian motion, [W,W](T) -> T as n_steps -> inf.
    // With n_steps=2000 and T=1.0, QV should be close to 1.0.
    // =========================================================================
    {
        var path: SDEPath = SDEPath {
            t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
            x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
        }
        let T = 1.0
        let n_steps = 2000
        let seed: i64 = 314159

        wiener_path(T, n_steps, seed, &!path)
        let qv = sde_path_quadratic_var(&path)

        // QV should be near T=1.0, tolerance 0.3 for stochastic noise
        if sc_abs(qv - T) < 0.3 {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 10: SDE strong error — fine path has smaller max error vs coarse
    // Use Euler-Maruyama with additive noise. Same seed for consistency.
    // Fine: 400 steps, coarse: 100 steps (ratio 4).
    // Strong error (max pointwise diff) should be bounded.
    // =========================================================================
    {
        var path_fine: SDEPath = SDEPath {
            t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
            x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
        }
        var path_coarse: SDEPath = SDEPath {
            t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
            x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
        }
        let seed: i64 = 271828

        sde_euler_maruyama(add_drift, add_diffusion,
                           1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 400, seed, &!path_fine)
        sde_euler_maruyama(add_drift, add_diffusion,
                           1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 100, seed, &!path_coarse)

        let err = sde_strong_error(&path_fine, &path_coarse)

        // Strong error should be positive but bounded (< 2.0 for this SDE)
        if err > 0.0 {
            if err < 2.0 {
                pass = pass + 1
            } else {
                fail = fail + 1
            }
        } else {
            // err == 0 is extremely unlikely but technically OK
            pass = pass + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 11: Wiener path starts at 0
    // W(0) = 0 by definition.
    // =========================================================================
    {
        var path: SDEPath = SDEPath {
            t_start: 0.0, t_end: 0.0,
            x: [0.0; 4096], n_steps: 0
        }
        let seed: i64 = 161803

        wiener_path(1.0, 500, seed, &!path)

        if sc_abs(path.x[0]) < 1.0e-15 {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Test 12: Monte Carlo stats — n_paths matches, variance >= 0
    // Use GBM drift/diffusion. Check SDEStats fields are sensible.
    // =========================================================================
    {
        var stats: SDEStats = SDEStats {
            mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, std_dev: 0.0, n_paths: 0
        }
        let n_paths = 200
        let seed: i64 = 999000

        sde_monte_carlo(gbm_drift, gbm_diffusion,
                        100.0, 0.0, 1.0, 200, n_paths, seed, &!stats)

        var ok = true
        if stats.n_paths != n_paths { ok = false }
        if stats.variance < 0.0 { ok = false }
        if stats.std_dev < 0.0 { ok = false }

        // Mean should be positive (GBM with positive S0 and mu)
        if stats.mean <= 0.0 { ok = false }

        // std_dev should be consistent with variance
        let std_check = sc_abs(stats.std_dev * stats.std_dev - stats.variance)
        if std_check > 0.01 { ok = false }

        if ok {
            pass = pass + 1
        } else {
            fail = fail + 1
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Summary
    // =========================================================================
    if fail > 0 { return 1 }
    return 0
}
