// E2E: stdlib/collections/heap_vec.sio — HeapI64Vec and HeapF64Vec method API

use collections::heap_vec::*;

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Alloc {
    // HeapI64Vec method API
    var v = HeapI64Vec { ptr: 0 as *mut i64, len: 0, cap: 0 }

    // push multiple values
    v.push(10)
    v.push(20)
    v.push(30)
    v.push(40)
    v.push(50)

    // len
    if v.len() != 5 { print("FAIL: len\n"); return 1 }

    // get
    if v.get(0) != 10 { print("FAIL: get(0)\n"); return 1 }
    if v.get(2) != 30 { print("FAIL: get(2)\n"); return 1 }
    if v.get(4) != 50 { print("FAIL: get(4)\n"); return 1 }
    if v.get(99) != 0 { print("FAIL: get out-of-bounds\n"); return 1 }

    // set
    v.set(1, 99)
    if v.get(1) != 99 { print("FAIL: set\n"); return 1 }

    // contains
    if v.contains(30) == false { print("FAIL: contains(30)\n"); return 1 }
    if v.contains(77) == true  { print("FAIL: contains(77)\n"); return 1 }

    // pop
    let last = v.pop()
    if last != 50 { print("FAIL: pop value\n"); return 1 }
    if v.len() != 4 { print("FAIL: len after pop\n"); return 1 }

    // clear
    v.clear()
    if v.len() != 0 { print("FAIL: clear\n"); return 1 }

    // push after clear grows again
    v.push(7)
    v.push(8)
    if v.len() != 2 { print("FAIL: push after clear\n"); return 1 }
    if v.get(0) != 7 { print("FAIL: get after clear\n"); return 1 }

    v.free()

    // HeapF64Vec method API
    var f = HeapF64Vec { ptr: 0 as *mut f64, len: 0, cap: 0 }
    f.push(1.0)
    f.push(2.0)
    f.push(3.0)

    if f.len() != 3 { print("FAIL: f64 len\n"); return 1 }
    if f.get(1) != 2.0 { print("FAIL: f64 get\n"); return 1 }

    let s = f.sum()
    if s < 5.9 || s > 6.1 { print("FAIL: f64 sum\n"); return 1 }

    f.free()

    print("PASS\n")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/collections/test_intvec_e2e.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E: stdlib/collections/vec.sio — IntVec push/pop/get/set/len/contains/swap

use collections::vec::*;

fn run_tests(v: &! IntVec) -> i32 {
    // Test push and len
    v.push(10)
    v.push(20)
    v.push(30)
    if v.len() != 3 { return 1 }

    // Test get
    if v.get(0) != 10 { return 2 }
    if v.get(1) != 20 { return 3 }
    if v.get(2) != 30 { return 4 }

    // Test set
    v.set(1, 99)
    if v.get(1) != 99 { return 5 }

    // Test contains
    if !v.contains(10) { return 6 }
    if v.contains(42) { return 7 }

    // Test index_of
    if v.index_of(30) != 2 { return 8 }
    if v.index_of(999) != 0 - 1 { return 9 }

    // Test swap
    v.swap(0, 2)
    if v.get(0) != 30 { return 10 }
    if v.get(2) != 10 { return 11 }

    // Test pop
    let popped = v.pop()
    if popped != 10 { return 12 }
    if v.len() != 2 { return 13 }

    // Test sum/min/max
    v.clear()
    v.push(5)
    v.push(3)
    v.push(8)
    v.push(1)
    if v.sum() != 17 { return 14 }
    if v.min() != 1 { return 15 }
    if v.max() != 8 { return 16 }

    // Test first/last
    if v.first() != 5 { return 17 }
    if v.last() != 1 { return 18 }

    // Test reverse
    v.reverse()
    if v.get(0) != 1 { return 19 }
    if v.get(3) != 5 { return 20 }

    // Test is_empty after clear
    v.clear()
    if !v.is_empty() { return 21 }

    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 {
    var v = IntVec::new()
    return run_tests(&! v)
}

// ============================================================================
// SPAN AND TOKEN STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

struct Span {
    start: i64,
    end: i64,
}

struct Token {
    kind: i32,
    span: Span,
    text: [i8; 256],
    text_len: i64,
}

struct TokenStream {
    tokens: [Token; 16384],
    n_tokens: i64,
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPER: Create source from string literal bytes
// ============================================================================

fn make_source(bytes: [i8; 256], len: i64) -> ([i8; 1048576], i64) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div, Alloc {
    var source: [i8; 1048576] = [0; 1048576];
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < len && i < 256 {
        source[i as usize] = bytes[i as usize];
        i = i + 1;
    }
    (source, len)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 1: SOUNIO FUNCTION SIGNATURE
// ============================================================================

/// Test: "fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a + b }"
fn test_function_signature() -> bool  with Mut{
    var source: [i8; 1048576] = [0; 1048576];

    // "fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a + b }"
    // f=102, n=110, space=32
    source[0] = 102; source[1] = 110; source[2] = 32;
    // add
    source[3] = 97; source[4] = 100; source[5] = 100;
    source[6] = 40;  // (
    source[7] = 97;  // a
    source[8] = 58;  // :
    source[9] = 32;  // space
    source[10] = 105; source[11] = 51; source[12] = 50;  // i32
    source[13] = 44; source[14] = 32;  // , space
    source[15] = 98;  // b
    source[16] = 58; source[17] = 32;  // : space
    source[18] = 105; source[19] = 51; source[20] = 50;  // i32
    source[21] = 41;  // )
    source[22] = 32;  // space
    source[23] = 45; source[24] = 62;  // ->
    source[25] = 32;  // space
    source[26] = 105; source[27] = 51; source[28] = 50;  // i32
    source[29] = 32;  // space
    source[30] = 123; // {
    source[31] = 32;  // space
    source[32] = 97;  // a
    source[33] = 32;  // space
    source[34] = 43;  // +
    source[35] = 32;  // space
    source[36] = 98;  // b
    source[37] = 32;  // space
    source[38] = 125; // }
    let source_len: i64 = 39;

    // Expected tokens:
    // 0: fn (TK_FN)
    // 1: add (TK_IDENT)
    // 2: ( (TK_LPAREN)
    // 3: a (TK_IDENT)
    // 4: : (TK_COLON)
    // 5: i32 (TK_IDENT)
    // 6: , (TK_COMMA)
    // 7: b (TK_IDENT)
    // 8: : (TK_COLON)
    // 9: i32 (TK_IDENT)
    // 10: ) (TK_RPAREN)
    // 11: -> (TK_ARROW)
    // 12: i32 (TK_IDENT)
    // 13: { (TK_LBRACE)
    // 14: a (TK_IDENT)
    // 15: + (TK_PLUS)
    // 16: b (TK_IDENT)
    // 17: } (TK_RBRACE)
    // 18: EOF

    // Would call tokenize(source, source_len) and verify
    true
}

    // + (TK_PLUS)

/// Test: "/// Outer doc\n//! Inner doc\nfn foo() {}"
fn test_doc_comments() -> bool  with Mut{
    var source: [i8; 1048576] = [0; 1048576];

    // "/// Outer doc\n"
    source[0] = 47; source[1] = 47; source[2] = 47; source[3] = 32;  // /// space
    source[4] = 79; source[5] = 117; source[6] = 116; source[7] = 101; source[8] = 114;  // Outer
    source[9] = 32;  // space
    source[10] = 100; source[11] = 111; source[12] = 99;  // doc
    source[13] = 10;  // newline
    // "//! Inner doc\n"

    source[18] = 73; source[19] = 110; source[20] = 110; source[21] = 101; source[22] = 114;  // Inner
    source[23] = 32;  // space
    source[24] = 100; source[25] = 111; source[26] = 99;  // doc
    source[27] = 10;  // newline
    // "fn foo() {}"
    source[28] = 102; source[29] = 110; source[30] = 32;  // fn space
    source[31] = 102; source[32] = 111; source[33] = 111;  // foo
    source[34] = 40; source[35] = 41; source[36] = 32;  // () space
    source[37] = 123; source[38] = 125;  // {}
    let source_len: i64 = 39;

    // Expected:
    // TK_DOC_COMMENT_OUTER (310) - "/// Outer doc"
    // TK_DOC_COMMENT_INNER (311) - "//! Inner doc"
    // fn, foo, (, ), {, }, EOF
    true
}

/// Test: "kernel fn vec_add(a: &[f32], b: &![f32]) { }"
fn test_kernel_syntax() -> bool  with Mut{
    var source: [i8; 1048576] = [0; 1048576];

    // "kernel fn vec_add(a: &[f32], b: &![f32]) { }"
    // k=107, e=101, r=114, n=110, l=108
    source[0] = 107; source[1] = 101; source[2] = 114;
    source[3] = 110; source[4] = 101; source[5] = 108;  // kernel
    source[6] = 32;  // space
    source[7] = 102; source[8] = 110;  // fn
    source[9] = 32;  // space
    // vec_add
    source[10] = 118; source[11] = 101; source[12] = 99;  // vec
    source[13] = 95;  // _
    source[14] = 97; source[15] = 100; source[16] = 100;  // add
    source[17] = 40;  // (
    source[18] = 97; source[19] = 58; source[20] = 32;  // a: space
    source[21] = 38;  // &
    source[22] = 91;  // [
    source[23] = 102; source[24] = 51; source[25] = 50;  // f32
    source[26] = 93;  // ]
    source[27] = 44; source[28] = 32;  // , space
    source[29] = 98; source[30] = 58; source[31] = 32;  // b: space
    source[32] = 38; source[33] = 33;  // &!  (Sounio mutable reference!)
    source[34] = 91;  // [
    source[35] = 102; source[36] = 51; source[37] = 50;  // f32
    source[38] = 93;  // ]
    source[39] = 41;  // )
    source[40] = 32;  // space
    source[41] = 123; source[42] = 32; source[43] = 125;  // { }
    let source_len: i64 = 44;

    // Expected:
    // kernel (TK_KERNEL), fn, vec_add, (, a, :, & (TK_AMP), [, f32, ], ,
    // b, :, & (TK_AMP), ! (TK_BANG), [, f32, ], ), {, }, EOF
    // Note: &! is TWO tokens in Sounio (& followed by !) - the exclusive reference
    true
}

// === FILE: tests/stdlib/compiler/parser/test_minimal.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Minimal parser test

fn TK_EOF() -> i32 { 0 }
fn TK_INT() -> i32 { 201 }
fn TK_PLUS() -> i32 { 220 }

fn PREC_NONE() -> i32 { 0 }
fn PREC_ADD() -> i32 { 10 }

fn get_prec(kind: i32) -> i32 {
    if kind == TK_PLUS() {
        return PREC_ADD()
    }
    PREC_NONE()
}

struct Token {
    kind: i32,
    val: i64,
}

fn token_new() -> Token {
    Token { kind: TK_EOF(), val: 0 }
}

struct State {
    tokens: [Token; 16],
    n: i64,
    pos: i64,
}

fn state_new() -> State {
    State {
        tokens: [token_new(); 16],
        n: 0,
        pos: 0,
    }
}

fn peek(s: State) -> i32 {
    if s.pos < s.n {
        s.tokens[s.pos as usize].kind
    } else {
        TK_EOF()
    }
}

fn advance(s: State) -> State  with Mut{
    var new_s = s;
    if new_s.pos < new_s.n {
        new_s.pos = new_s.pos + 1;
    }
    new_s
}

struct Expr {
    is_binary: bool,
    val: i64,
}

fn expr_lit(v: i64) -> Expr {
    Expr { is_binary: false, val: v }
}

fn expr_bin() -> Expr {
    Expr { is_binary: true, val: 0 }
}

struct ParseResult {
    state: State,
    expr: Expr,
    ok: bool,
}

fn parse_ok(s: State, e: Expr) -> ParseResult {
    ParseResult { state: s, expr: e, ok: true }
}

fn parse_err(s: State) -> ParseResult {
    ParseResult { state: s, expr: expr_lit(0), ok: false }
}

fn parse_primary(s: State) -> ParseResult  with IO, Mut, Panic, Div{
    var st = s;
    let curr = peek(st);
    print("  parse_primary: kind=");
    if curr == TK_INT() {
        print("INT\n");
        let v = st.tokens[st.pos as usize].val;
        st = advance(st);
        return parse_ok(st, expr_lit(v))
    }
    if curr == TK_EOF() {
        print("EOF\n");
    } else {
        print("OTHER\n");
    }
    parse_err(st)
}

fn parse_expr_prec(s: State, min_prec: i32) -> ParseResult  with IO, Mut, Panic, Div{
    var st = s;

    let left = parse_primary(st);
    if !left.ok {
        return left
    }
    st = left.state;
    var left_expr = left.expr;

    while true {
        let op = peek(st);
        let prec = get_prec(op);

        if prec < min_prec {
            break
        }

        st = advance(st);

        let right = parse_expr_prec(st, prec + 1);
        if !right.ok {
            return right
        }
        st = right.state;

        left_expr = expr_bin();
    }

    parse_ok(st, left_expr)
}

fn parse_expr(s: State) -> ParseResult  with IO, Mut, Panic, Div{
    parse_expr_prec(s, 1)
}

fn make_int_token(v: i64) -> Token {
    Token { kind: TK_INT(), val: v }
}

fn make_plus_token() -> Token {
    Token { kind: TK_PLUS(), val: 0 }
}

fn test_simple() -> bool  with IO, Mut, Panic, Div{
    var st = state_new();
    // Construct tokens and assign whole struct
    st.tokens[0] = make_int_token(1);
    st.tokens[1] = make_plus_token();
    st.tokens[2] = make_int_token(2);
    st.n = 3;

    print("  setup: tokens[0].kind = ");
    if st.tokens[0].kind == TK_INT() {
        print("INT\n");
    } else {
        print("OTHER\n");
    }

    let result = parse_expr(st);

    if !result.ok {
        print("  Parse failed\n");
        return false
    }

    if !result.expr.is_binary {
        print("  Expected binary\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    print("Minimal parser test...\n");

    if test_simple() {
        print("PASS\n");
        0
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n");
        1
    }
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/complex/test_complex.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E test for stdlib/complex/lib — 10 tests covering arithmetic, special functions,
// epistemic uncertainty propagation, and polynomial roots.

use complex::lib::*

// Absolute-value helper for f64
fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn check_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    abs_f64(a - b) < tol
}

fn run_tests() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail = 0

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 1: Multiplication  (1+2i)*(3+4i) = (3-8) + (4+6)i = -5+10i
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let z1 = complex_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let z2 = complex_new(3.0, 4.0)
    let p  = complex_mul(z1, z2)
    if !check_near(p.re, 0.0 - 5.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(p.im, 10.0,       1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 2: Division  (1+2i)/(3+4i) = (3+8)/25 + (6-4)i/25 = 11/25 + 2/25·i
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let d = complex_div(z1, z2)
    if !check_near(d.re, 11.0 / 25.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(d.im,  2.0 / 25.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 3: Euler's identity  |e^(iπ) + 1| < 1e-10
    // π approximated to 15 significant figures
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let pi_val = 3.141592653589793
    let z_i_pi = complex_new(0.0, pi_val)
    let e_ipi  = complex_exp(z_i_pi)
    let euler  = complex_add(e_ipi, complex_one())
    let mag    = complex_abs(euler)
    if !check_near(mag, 0.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 4: exp(0) = 1 + 0i
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let exp0 = complex_exp(complex_zero())
    if !check_near(exp0.re, 1.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(exp0.im, 0.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 5: log(e) = 1 + 0i  (e ≈ 2.718281828459045)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let e_val  = 2.718281828459045
    let log_e  = complex_log(complex_new(e_val, 0.0))
    if !check_near(log_e.re, 1.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(log_e.im, 0.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 6: sqrt(-1) = i  (principal branch)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let minus_one = complex_new(0.0 - 1.0, 0.0)
    let sq_neg1   = complex_sqrt(minus_one)
    if !check_near(sq_neg1.re, 0.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(sq_neg1.im, 1.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 7: Quadratic roots of x² + 1 = 0  →  ±i
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let roots = complex_quadratic_roots(1.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    let root1 = roots.r1
    let root2 = roots.r2
    // root1 should be +i (principal)
    if !check_near(root1.re, 0.0,        1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(root1.im, 1.0,        1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    // root2 should be -i
    if !check_near(root2.re, 0.0,        1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(root2.im, 0.0 - 1.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 8: Epistemic add — uncertainties combine in quadrature
    // a = (1+0i, u_re=0.1, u_im=0.2)
    // b = (0+1i, u_re=0.3, u_im=0.4)
    // expected u_re = sqrt(0.01 + 0.09) = sqrt(0.1) ≈ 0.31623
    // expected u_im = sqrt(0.04 + 0.16) = sqrt(0.2) ≈ 0.44721
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let ea = ecomplex_new(1.0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.2)
    let eb = ecomplex_new(0.0, 1.0, 0.3, 0.4)
    let es = ecomplex_add(ea, eb)
    let exp_ru = 0.31622776601683794   // sqrt(0.1)
    let exp_iu = 0.4472135954999579    // sqrt(0.2)
    if !check_near(es.value.re, 1.0,     1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(es.value.im, 1.0,     1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(es.re_unc,   exp_ru,  1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(es.im_unc,   exp_iu,  1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 9: Epistemic mul — GUM first-order propagation
    // a = (2+0i, u_re=0.1, u_im=0.0)
    // b = (3+0i, u_re=0.2, u_im=0.0)
    // product = 6+0i
    // ∂re/∂ar=3, ∂re/∂br=2  →  u²(re)=(3·0.1)²+(2·0.2)²=0.09+0.16=0.25  u=0.5
    // ∂im/∂ai=3, ∂im/∂bi=2  →  same with zeros — u(im)=0
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let ea2 = ecomplex_new(2.0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.0)
    let eb2 = ecomplex_new(3.0, 0.0, 0.2, 0.0)
    let em  = ecomplex_mul(ea2, eb2)
    if !check_near(em.value.re, 6.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(em.value.im, 0.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(em.re_unc,   0.5, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(em.im_unc,   0.0, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 10: complex_sin(i) = i·sinh(1) ≈ 0 + 1.1752011936438014·i
    // sin(0 + 1·i) = sin(0)·cosh(1) + i·cos(0)·sinh(1) = 0 + i·sinh(1)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let z_i      = complex_new(0.0, 1.0)
    let sin_i    = complex_sin(z_i)
    let sinh_1   = 1.1752011936438014
    if !check_near(sin_i.re, 0.0,    1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !check_near(sin_i.im, sinh_1, 1e-10) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Report
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if fail > 0 { return 1 }
    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    return run_tests()
}

// tests/stdlib/compress/test_gzip_pure.sio — Pure (non-FFI) tests for compress::gzip
//
// Tests: level constants, GzipError/GzipResult predicates, error messages.
// These do not call compress/decompress/crc32 (which require PLT linking to
// libz — not available until the native backend gains GOT/PLT support).

use compress::gzip::{
    GzipError, GzipResult,
    gzip_compress, gzip_decompress,
    gzip_is_ok,
    gzip_error_message,
    gzip_default_level, gzip_best_speed, gzip_best_compression,

fn test_level_constants() with Panic {
    assert(gzip_default_level() == 6 as i32)
    assert(gzip_best_speed() == 1 as i32)
    assert(gzip_best_compression() == 9 as i32)
}

fn test_error_message_ok() with Panic {
    let e = GzipError { code: 0 }
    assert(gzip_error_message(e) == "ok")
}

fn test_error_message_buf_error() with Panic {
    let neg5: i32 = 0 - 5
    let e = GzipError { code: neg5 }
    assert(gzip_error_message(e) == "buf error")
}

fn test_error_message_data_error() with Panic {
    let neg3: i32 = 0 - 3
    let e = GzipError { code: neg3 }
    assert(gzip_error_message(e) == "data error")
}

fn test_error_message_unknown() with Panic {
    let e = GzipError { code: 99 }
    assert(gzip_error_message(e) == "unknown error")
}

fn test_gzip_is_ok_true() with Panic {
    let e = GzipError { code: 0 }
    let r = GzipResult { ok: true, size: 42, error: e }
    assert(gzip_is_ok(r))
}

fn test_gzip_is_ok_false() with Panic {
    let neg3: i32 = 0 - 3
    let e = GzipError { code: neg3 }
    let r = GzipResult { ok: false, size: 0, error: e }
    assert(!gzip_is_ok(r))
}

fn test_compress_returns_error() with Mut, Panic {
    // compress/decompress stubs return Z_BUF_ERROR (-5) until PLT support lands
    var dummy_src: [u8; 4] = [0; 4]
    var dummy_dst: [u8; 8] = [0; 8]
    let r = gzip_compress((&!dummy_src) as *mut u8, 4, (&!dummy_dst) as *mut u8, 8)
    assert(!gzip_is_ok(r))
    let neg5: i32 = 0 - 5
    assert(r.error.code == neg5)
}

    test_level_constants()
    test_error_message_ok()
    test_error_message_buf_error()
    test_error_message_data_error()
    test_error_message_unknown()
    test_gzip_is_ok_true()
    test_gzip_is_ok_false()
    test_compress_returns_error()
    println("PASS: compress/gzip — pure tests passed")
}

// === FILE: tests/stdlib/constants/test_constants.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Tests for stdlib/constants/lib.sio
// Validates mathematical and physical constants against known identities.
// Note: constants use a units-aware type; cast to f64 for comparison.

use constants::*

fn check_near(got: f64, expected: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = got - expected
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    return ad < tol
}

fn check_rel(got: f64, expected: f64, rel_tol: f64) -> bool with Div {
    let d = got - expected
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    let scale = if expected < 0.0 { 0.0 - expected } else { expected }
    if scale < 1.0e-300 { return ad < 1.0e-10 }
    return ad / scale < rel_tol
}

fn run_tests() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail: i32 = 0

    // ---- Mathematical constants ----

    // PI ≈ 3.14159265358979
    if !check_near(PI as f64, 3.141592653589793, 1.0e-13) {
        println("FAIL: PI")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // E ≈ 2.71828182845905
    if !check_near(E as f64, 2.718281828459045, 1.0e-13) {
        println("FAIL: E")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // LN_2 ≈ 0.693147
    if !check_near(LN_2 as f64, 0.6931471805599453, 1.0e-14) {
        println("FAIL: LN_2")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // LN_10 ≈ 2.302585
    if !check_near(LN_10 as f64, 2.302585092994046, 1.0e-13) {
        println("FAIL: LN_10")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // SQRT_2 ≈ 1.41421
    if !check_near(SQRT_2 as f64, 1.4142135623730951, 1.0e-13) {
        println("FAIL: SQRT_2")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // SQRT_3 ≈ 1.73205
    if !check_near(SQRT_3 as f64, 1.7320508075688772, 1.0e-13) {
        println("FAIL: SQRT_3")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // PHI = (1 + sqrt(5)) / 2 ≈ 1.61803
    if !check_near(PHI as f64, 1.618033988749895, 1.0e-13) {
        println("FAIL: PHI")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ---- Physical constants ----

    // C = speed of light = exactly 299792458.0 m/s
    let c_val: f64 = C as f64
    if c_val != 299792458.0 {
        println("FAIL: C")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // H (Planck) ≈ 6.62607015e-34 J·s
    if !check_rel(H as f64, 6.62607015e-34, 1.0e-10) {
        println("FAIL: H")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // HBAR = h / (2PI): verify identity
    let pi_val: f64 = PI as f64
    let h_val: f64 = H as f64
    let hbar_derived = h_val / (2.0 * pi_val)
    if !check_rel(HBAR as f64, hbar_derived, 1.0e-8) {
        println("FAIL: HBAR")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // K_B (Boltzmann) ≈ 1.380649e-23 J/K
    if !check_rel(K_B as f64, 1.380649e-23, 1.0e-10) {
        println("FAIL: K_B")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // N_A (Avogadro) ≈ 6.02214076e23 1/mol
    if !check_rel(N_A as f64, 6.02214076e23, 1.0e-10) {
        println("FAIL: N_A")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // R_GAS = K_B * N_A (molar gas constant identity)
    let kb_val: f64 = K_B as f64
    let na_val: f64 = N_A as f64
    let r_derived = kb_val * na_val
    if !check_rel(R_GAS as f64, r_derived, 1.0e-6) {
        println("FAIL: R_GAS identity")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // R_GAS ≈ 8.314462618
    if !check_near(R_GAS as f64, 8.314462618, 1.0e-7) {
        println("FAIL: R_GAS value")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // M_ELECTRON ≈ 9.1093837015e-31 kg
    if !check_rel(M_ELECTRON as f64, 9.1093837015e-31, 1.0e-10) {
        println("FAIL: M_ELECTRON")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // M_PROTON ≈ 1.67262192369e-27 kg
    if !check_rel(M_PROTON as f64, 1.67262192369e-27, 1.0e-10) {
        println("FAIL: M_PROTON")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // E_CHARGE ≈ 1.602176634e-19 C
    if !check_rel(E_CHARGE as f64, 1.602176634e-19, 1.0e-10) {
        println("FAIL: E_CHARGE")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // G (Gravitational) ≈ 6.67430e-11 m^3/(kg*s^2)
    if !check_rel(G as f64, 6.67430e-11, 1.0e-5) {
        println("FAIL: G")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // EPSILON_0 (Vacuum permittivity) ≈ 8.8541878128e-12 F/m
    if !check_rel(EPSILON_0 as f64, 8.8541878128e-12, 1.0e-10) {
        println("FAIL: EPSILON_0")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ---- Conversion factors ----

    // DEG_TO_RAD * 180 ≈ PI
    let dtr: f64 = DEG_TO_RAD as f64
    let rtd: f64 = RAD_TO_DEG as f64
    let pi_from_deg = dtr * 180.0
    if !check_near(pi_from_deg, pi_val, 1.0e-12) {
        println("FAIL: DEG_TO_RAD")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // RAD_TO_DEG * PI ≈ 180
    let deg_from_rad = rtd * pi_val
    if !check_near(deg_from_rad, 180.0, 1.0e-10) {
        println("FAIL: RAD_TO_DEG")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // DEG_TO_RAD * RAD_TO_DEG ≈ 1 (inverse relationship)
    let product = dtr * rtd
    if !check_near(product, 1.0, 1.0e-13) {
        println("FAIL: DEG/RAD inverse")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ATM_TO_PA = exactly 101325.0
    let atm: f64 = ATM_TO_PA as f64
    if atm != 101325.0 {
        println("FAIL: ATM_TO_PA")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // EV_TO_JOULE ≈ 1.602176634e-19 J (same as elementary charge in SI)
    if !check_rel(EV_TO_JOULE as f64, 1.602176634e-19, 1.0e-10) {
        println("FAIL: EV_TO_JOULE")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // EV_TO_JOULE = E_CHARGE (by definition)
    let echarge_val: f64 = E_CHARGE as f64
    if !check_rel(EV_TO_JOULE as f64, echarge_val, 1.0e-13) {
        println("FAIL: EV_TO_JOULE == E_CHARGE")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail > 0 { return 1 }
    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let result = run_tests()
    if result == 0 {
        println("constants: all tests PASSED")
    } else {
        println("constants: some tests FAILED")
    }
    return result
}

use core::option::*;

fn run_tests() -> i32 {
    // IntOption None
    let none = int_none()
    if int_option_is_some(&none) { return 1 }
    if !int_option_is_none(&none) { return 2 }
    if int_option_unwrap_or(&none, 42) != 42 { return 3 }

    // IntOption Some
    let some = int_some(99)
    if !int_option_is_some(&some) { return 4 }
    if int_option_is_none(&some) { return 5 }
    if int_option_unwrap(&some) != 99 { return 6 }
    if int_option_unwrap_or(&some, 0) != 99 { return 7 }

    // FloatOption
    let fnone = float_none()
    if float_option_is_some(&fnone) { return 8 }
    if float_option_unwrap_or(&fnone, 3.14) != 3.14 { return 9 }

    let fsome = float_some(2.718)
    if !float_option_is_some(&fsome) { return 10 }

    return 0
}

    return run_tests()
}

    }

        print("PASS\n"); pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n"); fail = fail + 1
    }

    } else {

    }

        print("PASS\n"); pass = pass + 1

        print("FAIL\n"); fail = fail + 1

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- IntResult

    } else {
        print("FAIL\n"); fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 11: int_ok — is_err false... ")
    if !int_result_is_err(&ok) {

        print("FAIL\n"); fail = fail + 1

    print("Test 13: int_err — is_err true... ")

    } else {
        print("FAIL\n"); fail = fail + 1

    }

        print("PASS\n"); pass = pass + 1

        print("FAIL\n"); fail = fail + 1
    }

    }

//@ run-pass
// E2E: stdlib/core/result.sio — IntResult/FloatResult

use core::result::*;

fn run_tests() -> i32 {
    // IntResult Ok
    let ok = int_ok(42)
    if !ok.is_ok() { return 1 }
    if ok.is_err() { return 2 }
    if int_result_unwrap(&ok) != 42 { return 3 }
    if int_result_unwrap_or(&ok, 0) != 42 { return 4 }

    // IntResult Err
    let err = int_err(404)
    if err.is_ok() { return 5 }
    if !err.is_err() { return 6 }
    if int_result_err(&err) != 404 { return 7 }
    if int_result_unwrap_or(&err, 0 - 1) != 0 - 1 { return 8 }

    // FloatResult
    let fok = float_ok(3.14)
    if !float_result_is_ok(&fok) { return 9 }

    let ferr = float_err(500)
    if float_result_is_ok(&ferr) { return 10 }
    if float_result_err(&ferr) != 500 { return 11 }

    return 0
}

    return run_tests()

// === FILE: tests/stdlib/crypto/test_sha256.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! tests/stdlib/crypto/test_sha256.sio
//!
//! NIST FIPS 180-4 test vectors for SHA-256 and RFC 2104 HMAC-SHA256.
//!
//! Test vectors:
//!   T1: SHA-256("") = e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
//!   T2: SHA-256("abc") = ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
//!   T3: HMAC-SHA256(key="key", msg="The quick brown fox...") — RFC 2104 example

use crypto::sha256::{
    SHA256State, SHA256Digest,
    sha256_init, sha256_update, sha256_finalize, sha256_hash,
    hmac_sha256,
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Build a [u8; 256] from a Sounio string literal stored as explicit bytes.
// Returns count of bytes filled.
fn make_buf_empty() -> [u8; 256] {
    let b: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    return b
}

// "abc" = 0x61, 0x62, 0x63
fn make_buf_abc() -> [u8; 256]  with Mut{
    var b: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    b[0] = 0x61 as u8
    b[1] = 0x62 as u8
    b[2] = 0x63 as u8
    return b
}

// "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" (43 bytes)
fn make_buf_fox() -> [u8; 256]  with Mut{
    var b: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    b[ 0] = 0x54 as u8   // T
    b[ 1] = 0x68 as u8   // h
    b[ 2] = 0x65 as u8   // e
    b[ 3] = 0x20 as u8   //
    b[ 4] = 0x71 as u8   // q
    b[ 5] = 0x75 as u8   // u
    b[ 6] = 0x69 as u8   // i
    b[ 7] = 0x63 as u8   // c
    b[ 8] = 0x6b as u8   // k
    b[ 9] = 0x20 as u8   //
    b[10] = 0x62 as u8   // b
    b[11] = 0x72 as u8   // r
    b[12] = 0x6f as u8   // o
    b[13] = 0x77 as u8   // w
    b[14] = 0x6e as u8   // n
    b[15] = 0x20 as u8   //
    b[16] = 0x66 as u8   // f
    b[17] = 0x6f as u8   // o
    b[18] = 0x78 as u8   // x
    b[19] = 0x20 as u8   //
    b[20] = 0x6a as u8   // j
    b[21] = 0x75 as u8   // u
    b[22] = 0x6d as u8   // m
    b[23] = 0x70 as u8   // p
    b[24] = 0x73 as u8   // s
    b[25] = 0x20 as u8   //
    b[26] = 0x6f as u8   // o
    b[27] = 0x76 as u8   // v
    b[28] = 0x65 as u8   // e
    b[29] = 0x72 as u8   // r
    b[30] = 0x20 as u8   //
    b[31] = 0x74 as u8   // t
    b[32] = 0x68 as u8   // h
    b[33] = 0x65 as u8   // e
    b[34] = 0x20 as u8   //
    b[35] = 0x6c as u8   // l
    b[36] = 0x61 as u8   // a
    b[37] = 0x7a as u8   // z
    b[38] = 0x79 as u8   // y
    b[39] = 0x20 as u8   //
    b[40] = 0x64 as u8   // d
    b[41] = 0x6f as u8   // o
    b[42] = 0x67 as u8   // g
    return b
}

// "key" = 0x6b, 0x65, 0x79
fn make_key_key() -> [u8; 256]  with Mut{
    var b: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    b[0] = 0x6b as u8   // k
    b[1] = 0x65 as u8   // e
    b[2] = 0x79 as u8   // y
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// T1: SHA-256("") — NIST FIPS 180-4 example
// Expected: e3b0c442 98fc1c14 9afbf4c8 996fb924 27ae41e4 649b934c a495991b 7852b855
// ============================================================================

fn test_sha256_empty() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let data = make_buf_empty()
    let d = sha256_hash(data, 0)

    // Check first 8 bytes of the digest.
    if d.bytes[0] != (0xe3 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[1] != (0xb0 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[2] != (0xc4 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[3] != (0x42 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[4] != (0x98 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[5] != (0xfc as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[6] != (0x1c as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[7] != (0x14 as u8) { return false }

    // Check last 8 bytes.
    if d.bytes[24] != (0xa4 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[25] != (0x95 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[26] != (0x99 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[27] != (0x1b as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[28] != (0x78 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[29] != (0x52 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[30] != (0xb8 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[31] != (0x55 as u8) { return false }

    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// T2: SHA-256("abc") — NIST FIPS 180-4 example
// Expected: ba7816bf 8f01cfea 414140de 5dae2223 b00361a3 96177a9c b410ff61 f20015ad
// ============================================================================

fn test_sha256_abc() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let data = make_buf_abc()
    let d = sha256_hash(data, 3)

    if d.bytes[0] != (0xba as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[1] != (0x78 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[2] != (0x16 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[3] != (0xbf as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[4] != (0x8f as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[5] != (0x01 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[6] != (0xcf as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[7] != (0xea as u8) { return false }

    if d.bytes[ 8] != (0x41 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[ 9] != (0x41 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[10] != (0x40 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[11] != (0xde as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[12] != (0x5d as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[13] != (0xae as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[14] != (0x22 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[15] != (0x23 as u8) { return false }

    if d.bytes[24] != (0xb4 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[25] != (0x10 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[26] != (0xff as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[27] != (0x61 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[28] != (0xf2 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[29] != (0x00 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[30] != (0x15 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[31] != (0xad as u8) { return false }

    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// T3: Streaming SHA-256("abc") using update/finalize
// Same expected digest as T2, but verifying the streaming API.
// ============================================================================

fn test_sha256_streaming() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = sha256_init()
    let data = make_buf_abc()
    s = sha256_update(s, data, 3)
    let d = sha256_finalize(s)

    if d.bytes[0] != (0xba as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[1] != (0x78 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[2] != (0x16 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[3] != (0xbf as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[31] != (0xad as u8) { return false }
    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// T4: HMAC-SHA256(key="key", msg="The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog")
// Expected: f7bc83f430538424b13298e6aa6fb143ef4d59a14946175997479dbc2d1a3cd8
// (RFC 2104 / Wikipedia test vector)
// ============================================================================

fn test_hmac_sha256_fox() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let key = make_key_key()
    let msg = make_buf_fox()
    let d = hmac_sha256(key, 3, msg, 43)

    if d.bytes[0] != (0xf7 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[1] != (0xbc as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[2] != (0x83 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[3] != (0xf4 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[4] != (0x30 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[5] != (0x53 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[6] != (0x84 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[7] != (0x24 as u8) { return false }

    if d.bytes[ 8] != (0xb1 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[ 9] != (0x32 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[10] != (0x98 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[11] != (0xe6 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[12] != (0xaa as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[13] != (0x6f as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[14] != (0xb1 as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[15] != (0x43 as u8) { return false }

    if d.bytes[28] != (0x2d as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[29] != (0x1a as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[30] != (0x3c as u8) { return false }
    if d.bytes[31] != (0xd8 as u8) { return false }

    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// RUNNER
// ============================================================================

fn main() with Mut, Panic, Div, IO {
    var passed: i32 = 0
    var failed: i32 = 0

    if test_sha256_empty() {
        print("T1 PASS: SHA-256(\"\") correct\n")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        print("T1 FAIL: SHA-256(\"\") mismatch\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    if test_sha256_abc() {
        print("T2 PASS: SHA-256(\"abc\") correct\n")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        print("T2 FAIL: SHA-256(\"abc\") mismatch\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    if test_sha256_streaming() {
        print("T3 PASS: streaming SHA-256(\"abc\") correct\n")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        print("T3 FAIL: streaming SHA-256(\"abc\") mismatch\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    if test_hmac_sha256_fox() {
        print("T4 PASS: HMAC-SHA256(key,fox) correct\n")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        print("T4 FAIL: HMAC-SHA256(key,fox) mismatch\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Results: ")
    print(passed)
    print(" passed, ")
    print(failed)
    print(" failed\n")

    assert(failed == 0)
}
