fn test_th_and_elim_wrong_kind() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var ctx = ctx_new()

    // Axiom with OR (not AND)
    var r = th_axiom(ctx, th_prop_or(1, 2))
    ctx = r.ctx
    let idx = r.idx

    var r2 = th_and_elim_l(ctx, idx)
    let result = r2.idx
    if result >= 0 { return 1 }  // should fail

    return 0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 23: multiple axioms accumulate in context
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fn test_multiple_axioms() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var ctx = ctx_new()

    var r1 = th_axiom(ctx, th_prop_custom(1))
    ctx = r1.ctx
    var r2 = th_axiom(ctx, th_prop_custom(2))
    ctx = r2.ctx
    var r3 = th_axiom(ctx, th_prop_custom(3))
    ctx = r3.ctx

    if ctx_prop_count(ctx) != 3 { return 1 }
    if ctx_trust_count(ctx) != 3 { return 1 }

    return 0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 24: th_prop_new helper constructs with all fields
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fn test_th_prop_new() -> i32 {
    let p = th_prop_new(PROP_EQ(), 5, 6, 7)
    if p.kind != PROP_EQ() { return 1 }
    if p.lhs != 5 { return 1 }
    if p.rhs != 6 { return 1 }
    if p.name_id != 7 { return 1 }
    return 0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 25: chain of refl + trans produces reflexive transitivity
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fn test_refl_trans_chain() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var ctx = ctx_new()

    // x=x via refl
    var r1 = th_refl(ctx, 5)
    ctx = r1.ctx
    let xx = r1.idx

    // y=y via refl
    var r2 = th_refl(ctx, 5)
    ctx = r2.ctx
    let yy = r2.idx

    // x=x + x=x => x=x via trans (rhs of first = lhs of second = 5)
    var r3 = th_trans(ctx, xx, yy)
    ctx = r3.ctx
    let result = r3.idx
    if result < 0 { return 1 }

    var gp = ctx_get_prop(ctx, result)
    let p = gp.prop
    if p.lhs != 5 { return 1 }
    if p.rhs != 5 { return 1 }

    return 0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// RUNNER
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn run_tests() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail = 0

    if test_prop_kinds_distinct()          != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_prop_constructors()         != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_ctx_new()                      != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_ctx_add_prop()                 != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_ctx_get_prop()                 != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_ctx_get_prop_oob()             != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_ctx_trust_is_trusted()         != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_ctx_trust_dedup()              != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_axiom()                     != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_refl()                      != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_refl_distinct()             != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_symm()                      != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_symm_wrong_kind()           != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_symm_requires_trust()       != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_trans()                     != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_trans_mismatch()            != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_symm_trans_chain()          != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_modus_ponens()              != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_modus_ponens_untrusted_p()  != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_and_roundtrip()             != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_and_intro_requires_trust()  != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_and_elim_wrong_kind()       != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_multiple_axioms()              != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_th_prop_new()                  != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if test_refl_trans_chain()             != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }

    return fail
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    return run_tests()
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/theorem/test_theorem_kernel.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Test suite for stdlib/theorem/kernel.sio — pure value API
//
// The kernel.sio module provides two kinds of functions:
//   1. Pure value functions: prop constructors, prop_eq_check, verify_ok/fail
//      → These work correctly in JIT mode and are tested comprehensively here.
//   2. &! ProofContext mutation functions: true_intro, refl, trusted, etc.
//      → These require &! references on a ~490KB struct (ProofContext with 15
//        arrays of 4096 elements). In JIT mode, &! mutations on large by-value
//        structs are not visible after the call returns (known JIT limitation,
//        see MEMORY.md "JIT &! reference bug"). Use theorem::core for the
//        by-value ProofCtx API, which is tested in test_theorem_core.sio.
//
// This file tests all 10 PROP_* tag constants, all proposition constructors,
// prop_eq_check structural comparison, verify_ok/verify_fail helpers, and
// proof tag constants.
//
// Each test_* returns 0 (pass) or 1 (fail).
// main() returns total failure count (0 = all pass).

use theorem::kernel::*

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn abs_diff(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    let d = a - b
    if d < 0.0 { return 0.0 - d }
    return d
}

fn near(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
    return abs_diff(a, b) < 0.000001
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SECTION A: PROP_* tag constants
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Test A1: All PROP_* constants are distinct from each other
fn test_prop_tags_all_distinct() -> i32 {
    if PROP_TRUE == PROP_FALSE    { return 1 }
    if PROP_TRUE == PROP_AND      { return 1 }
    if PROP_TRUE == PROP_OR       { return 1 }
    if PROP_TRUE == PROP_IMPLIES  { return 1 }
    if PROP_TRUE == PROP_NOT      { return 1 }
    if PROP_TRUE == PROP_FORALL   { return 1 }
    if PROP_TRUE == PROP_EXISTS   { return 1 }
    if PROP_TRUE == PROP_EQ       { return 1 }
    if PROP_TRUE == PROP_CUSTOM   { return 1 }
    if PROP_FALSE == PROP_AND     { return 1 }
    if PROP_FALSE == PROP_OR      { return 1 }
    if PROP_FALSE == PROP_IMPLIES { return 1 }
    if PROP_AND == PROP_OR        { return 1 }
    if PROP_AND == PROP_IMPLIES   { return 1 }
    if PROP_OR == PROP_NOT        { return 1 }
    if PROP_FORALL == PROP_EXISTS { return 1 }
    if PROP_EQ == PROP_CUSTOM     { return 1 }
    return 0
}

}

// Test B10: prop_eq lhs != rhs (not self-referential unless same value)
fn test_prop_eq_different_values() -> i32 {

    if p.eq_lhs == p.eq_rhs { return 1 }  // 1 != 2
    let q = prop_eq(5, 5)
    if q.eq_lhs != q.eq_rhs { return 1 }  // 5 == 5
    return 0
}

    return 0
}

}

}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SECTION C: Proposition constructors — zeroed-out fields
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Test C1: prop_true has no meaningful sub-fields (all 0)

// Test H1: prop_and with same args on both sides

    let p = prop_and(5, 5)
    if p.left_id != p.right_id { return 1 }
    return 0
}

fn test_prop_or_diff_args() -> i32 {
    let p = prop_or(1, 2)
    if p.left_id == p.right_id { return 1 }
    return 0
}

// Test H3: prop_implies antecedent = consequent → left_id == right_id
fn test_prop_implies_same() -> i32 {
    let p = prop_implies(3, 3)
    if p.left_id != p.right_id { return 1 }
    return 0
}

// Test H4: prop_forall and prop_exists have same structure (differ by tag)
fn test_prop_forall_exists_structure() -> i32 {
    let fa = prop_forall(1, 10)
    let ex = prop_exists(1, 10)
    // Same var_name and left_id, but different tags
    if fa.var_name != ex.var_name { return 1 }
    if fa.left_id != ex.left_id   { return 1 }
    if fa.tag == ex.tag           { return 1 }  // must differ
    return 0
}

// Test H5: prop_iff(a, b) and prop_iff(b, a) differ (not symmetric)
fn test_prop_iff_not_symmetric() -> i32 {
    let ab = prop_iff(1, 2)
    let ba = prop_iff(2, 1)
    if prop_eq_check(ab, ba) == true { return 1 }
    return 0
}

// Test H6: prop_eq(a, b) and prop_eq(b, a) differ (symmetry is a proof step)
fn test_prop_eq_not_symmetric() -> i32 {
    let ab = prop_eq(1, 2)
    let ba = prop_eq(2, 1)
    if prop_eq_check(ab, ba) == true { return 1 }
    return 0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// RUNNER
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn run_tests() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Use early-return to avoid BSS aliasing of a mutable `fail` counter:
    // each test result is compared in a register; 0 means all passed.

    // Section A: PROP_* tag constants
    if test_prop_tags_all_distinct()       != 0 { return 1 }

    // Section B: proposition constructors
    if test_prop_true()                    != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_false()                   != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_and()                     != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_or()                      != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_implies()                 != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_not()                     != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_forall()                  != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_exists()                  != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq()                      != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_different_values()     != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_iff()                     != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_custom()                  != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_custom_distinct()         != 0 { return 1 }

    // Section C: zeroed-out fields
    if test_prop_true_zeroed()             != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_not_rhs_zero()            != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_fields_zero()          != 0 { return 1 }

    // Section D: prop_eq_check
    if test_prop_eq_check_identical()      != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_check_diff_right()     != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_check_diff_left()      != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_check_diff_tag()       != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_check_eq_props()       != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_check_not_same()       != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_check_not_diff()       != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_check_forall_var()     != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_check_custom_id()      != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_check_iff_vs_and()     != 0 { return 1 }

    // Section E: VerifyResult constructors
    if test_verify_ok_basic()              != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_verify_ok_full()               != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_verify_ok_zero()               != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_verify_fail_reason1()          != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_verify_fail_reason2()          != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_verify_fail_reason3()          != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_verify_ok_vs_fail()            != 0 { return 1 }

    // Section F: proof tag constants
    if test_proof_refl_defined()           != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_proof_trusted_distinct()       != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_proof_assume_vs_runtime()      != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_proof_and_tags_distinct()      != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_proof_or_tags_distinct()       != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_proof_impl_tags_distinct()     != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_proof_eq_tags_distinct()       != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_proof_forall_tags_distinct()   != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_proof_exists_tags_distinct()   != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_proof_compose_weaken_distinct() != 0 { return 1 }

    // Section G: prop_tag_name
    if test_prop_tag_name_identity()       != 0 { return 1 }

    // Section H: structural invariants
    if test_prop_and_same_args()           != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_or_diff_args()            != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_implies_same()            != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_forall_exists_structure() != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_iff_not_symmetric()       != 0 { return 1 }
    if test_prop_eq_not_symmetric()        != 0 { return 1 }

    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    return run_tests()
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/thread/test_pool_e2e.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E: stdlib/thread/pool.sio — ThreadPool submit/complete

use thread::pool::*;

fn run_tests(pool: &! ThreadPool) -> i32 {
    if pool.total_workers() != 4 { return 1 }
    if pool.active_count() != 0 { return 2 }

    // Submit tasks
    let ok1 = pool.submit(100)
    if !ok1 { return 3 }
    let ok2 = pool.submit(200)
    if !ok2 { return 4 }
    if pool.active_count() != 2 { return 5 }

    // Complete one
    pool.complete(0)
    if pool.active_count() != 1 { return 6 }

    pool.complete(1)
    if pool.active_count() != 0 { return 7 }

    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 {
    var pool = ThreadPool::new(4)
    return run_tests(&! pool)
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/time/test_time.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// tests/stdlib/time/test_time.sio
//
// Self-contained tests for stdlib/time/lib.sio.
// All helpers inlined (no `use` imports) to work with the JIT runner.

// =============================================================================
// Inline copy of stdlib/time/lib.sio
// =============================================================================

struct Duration {
    seconds: i64,
    nanos: i64,
}

struct DateTime {
    year:          i32,
    month:         i32,
    day:           i32,
    hour:          i32,
    minute:        i32,
    second:        i32,
    epoch_seconds: i64,
}

fn duration_normalise(secs: i64, ns: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = secs
    var n = ns
    if n < 0 {
        let borrow = (0 - n - 1) / 1000000000 + 1
        s = s - borrow
        n = n + borrow * 1000000000
    }
    if n >= 1000000000 {
        let carry = n / 1000000000
        s = s + carry
        n = n - carry * 1000000000
    }
    Duration { seconds: s, nanos: n }
}

fn duration_new(secs: i64, nanos: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    duration_normalise(secs, nanos)
}

fn duration_from_secs(secs: i64) -> Duration {
    Duration { seconds: secs, nanos: 0 }
}

fn duration_from_millis(ms: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let secs = ms / 1000
    let nanos = (ms - secs * 1000) * 1000000
    duration_normalise(secs, nanos)
}

fn duration_add(a: Duration, b: Duration) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    duration_normalise(a.seconds + b.seconds, a.nanos + b.nanos)
}

fn duration_sub(a: Duration, b: Duration) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    duration_normalise(a.seconds - b.seconds, a.nanos - b.nanos)
}

fn duration_to_secs_f64(d: &Duration) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let sf: f64 = d.seconds as f64
    let nf: f64 = d.nanos as f64
    sf + nf / 1000000000.0
}

fn is_leap_year(y: i32) -> bool with Div, Panic {
    if y % 400 == 0 { return true }
    if y % 100 == 0 { return false }
    if y % 4 == 0   { return true }
    false
}

fn days_in_month(y: i32, m: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if m == 1  { return 31 }
    if m == 2  {
        if is_leap_year(y) { return 29 }
        return 28
    }
    if m == 3  { return 31 }
    if m == 4  { return 30 }
    if m == 5  { return 31 }
    if m == 6  { return 30 }
    if m == 7  { return 31 }
    if m == 8  { return 31 }
    if m == 9  { return 30 }
    if m == 10 { return 31 }
    if m == 11 { return 30 }
    31
}

fn day_of_year(y: i32, m: i32, d: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var doy = 0
    var mo = 1
    while mo < m {
        doy = doy + days_in_month(y, mo)
        mo = mo + 1
    }
    doy + d
}

fn days_from_epoch_to_year(y: i32) -> i64 with Div, Panic {
    let y0: i64 = y as i64 - 1
    let base: i64 = (y as i64 - 1970) * 365
    let leaps: i64 = y0 / 4 - y0 / 100 + y0 / 400
    let epoch_base: i64 = 1969 / 4 - 1969 / 100 + 1969 / 400
    base + leaps - epoch_base
}

fn datetime_new(y: i32, m: i32, d: i32, h: i32, min: i32, s: i32) -> DateTime with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let year_days: i64 = days_from_epoch_to_year(y)
    let month_days: i64 = day_of_year(y, m, d) as i64 - 1
    let total_days: i64 = year_days + month_days
    let epoch: i64 = total_days * 86400 + h as i64 * 3600 + min as i64 * 60 + s as i64
    DateTime {
        year: y, month: m, day: d,
        hour: h, minute: min, second: s,
        epoch_seconds: epoch,
    }
}

fn datetime_from_epoch(epoch: i64) -> DateTime with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var day_secs: i64 = epoch % 86400
    var day_count: i64 = epoch / 86400
    if day_secs < 0 {
        day_secs = day_secs + 86400
        day_count = day_count - 1
    }
    let h: i32   = (day_secs / 3600) as i32
    let mn: i32  = ((day_secs % 3600) / 60) as i32
    let sec: i32 = (day_secs % 60) as i32

    var y: i32 = 1970
    if day_count >= 0 {
        while true {
            let dy: i64 = if is_leap_year(y) { 366 } else { 365 }
            if day_count < dy { break }
            day_count = day_count - dy
            y = y + 1
        }
    } else {
        while day_count < 0 {
            y = y - 1
            let dy: i64 = if is_leap_year(y) { 366 } else { 365 }
            day_count = day_count + dy
        }
    }

    var mo: i32 = 1
    while mo <= 12 {
        let dm: i64 = days_in_month(y, mo) as i64
        if day_count < dm { break }
        day_count = day_count - dm
        mo = mo + 1
    }
    let d: i32 = day_count as i32 + 1

    DateTime {
        year: y, month: mo, day: d,
        hour: h, minute: mn, second: sec,
        epoch_seconds: epoch,
    }
}

fn datetime_add_duration(dt: DateTime, d: Duration) -> DateTime with Div, Panic, Mut {
    datetime_from_epoch(dt.epoch_seconds + d.seconds)
}

fn datetime_diff(a: &DateTime, b: &DateTime) -> Duration with Div, Panic {
    let diff_secs: i64 = a.epoch_seconds - b.epoch_seconds
    Duration { seconds: diff_secs, nanos: 0 }
}

// =============================================================================
// Test helpers
// =============================================================================

fn check_near_f64(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < tol
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_duration_arithmetic() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var fail = 0

    // 1.5s + 2.3s = 3.8s
    let a = duration_new(1, 500000000)   // 1.5 s
    let b = duration_new(2, 300000000)   // 2.3 s
    let c = duration_add(a, b)
    let cf = duration_to_secs_f64(&c)
    if !check_near_f64(cf, 3.8, 1e-6) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // duration_from_millis: 1500 ms = 1s 500ms
    let d = duration_from_millis(1500)
    if d.seconds != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if d.nanos != 500000000 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // duration_sub: 3s - 1s = 2s
    let e = duration_from_secs(3)
    let f = duration_from_secs(1)
    let g = duration_sub(e, f)
    if g.seconds != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if g.nanos != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // nanos normalisation: 0s + 1_200_000_000 ns = 1s 200ms
    let h = duration_new(0, 1200000000)
    if h.seconds != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if h.nanos != 200000000 { fail = fail + 1 }

    return fail
}

fn test_leap_year() -> i32  with IO, Mut, Panic, Div{
    var fail = 0
    if !is_leap_year(2000) { fail = fail + 1 }   // div by 400 → yes
    if is_leap_year(1900)  { fail = fail + 1 }   // div by 100, not 400 → no
    if !is_leap_year(2024) { fail = fail + 1 }   // div by 4, not 100 → yes
    if is_leap_year(2023)  { fail = fail + 1 }   // not div by 4 → no
    if !is_leap_year(2004) { fail = fail + 1 }   // div by 4 → yes
    return fail
}

fn test_days_in_month() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var fail = 0
    // February leap year = 29
    if days_in_month(2000, 2) != 29 { fail = fail + 1 }
    // February non-leap = 28
    if days_in_month(1900, 2) != 28 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if days_in_month(2023, 2) != 28 { fail = fail + 1 }
    // January always 31
    if days_in_month(2024, 1) != 31 { fail = fail + 1 }
    // April always 30
    if days_in_month(2024, 4) != 30 { fail = fail + 1 }
    return fail
}

fn test_datetime_epoch() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var fail = 0

    // 1970-01-01 00:00:00 → epoch = 0
    let t0 = datetime_new(1970, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    if t0.epoch_seconds != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // 2024-01-01 00:00:00
    // Python: calendar.timegm((2024,1,1,0,0,0,0,0,0)) = 1704067200
    // 1704067200 / 86400 = 19723 days since epoch
    let expected: i64 = 1704067200
    let t2024 = datetime_new(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    if t2024.epoch_seconds != expected { fail = fail + 1 }

    // 2024-01-01 12:30:45
    let t2 = datetime_new(2024, 1, 1, 12, 30, 45)
    let expected2: i64 = expected + 12 * 3600 + 30 * 60 + 45
    if t2.epoch_seconds != expected2 { fail = fail + 1 }

    return fail
}

fn test_datetime_roundtrip() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var fail = 0

    // Round-trip: datetime_new → epoch → datetime_from_epoch
    let original = datetime_new(2024, 3, 15, 10, 45, 30)
    let recovered = datetime_from_epoch(original.epoch_seconds)

    if recovered.year   != 2024 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if recovered.month  != 3    { fail = fail + 1 }
    if recovered.day    != 15   { fail = fail + 1 }
    if recovered.hour   != 10   { fail = fail + 1 }
    if recovered.minute != 45   { fail = fail + 1 }
    if recovered.second != 30   { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Round-trip for epoch = 0 (1970-01-01 00:00:00)
    let epoch0 = datetime_from_epoch(0)
    if epoch0.year   != 1970 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if epoch0.month  != 1    { fail = fail + 1 }
    if epoch0.day    != 1    { fail = fail + 1 }
    if epoch0.hour   != 0    { fail = fail + 1 }
    if epoch0.minute != 0    { fail = fail + 1 }
    if epoch0.second != 0    { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Round-trip for a leap-day: 2000-02-29
    let leap_day = datetime_new(2000, 2, 29, 0, 0, 0)
    let leap_rec = datetime_from_epoch(leap_day.epoch_seconds)
    if leap_rec.year  != 2000 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if leap_rec.month != 2    { fail = fail + 1 }
    if leap_rec.day   != 29   { fail = fail + 1 }

    return fail
}

fn test_datetime_diff() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var fail = 0

    let a = datetime_new(2024, 1, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    let b = datetime_new(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    let diff = datetime_diff(&a, &b)
    // a - b = 1 day = 86400 seconds
    if diff.seconds != 86400 { fail = fail + 1 }

    return fail
}

fn test_datetime_add() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var fail = 0

    let base = datetime_new(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    let one_day = duration_from_secs(86400)
    let next = datetime_add_duration(base, one_day)
    if next.year  != 2024 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if next.month != 1    { fail = fail + 1 }
    if next.day   != 2    { fail = fail + 1 }

    return fail
}

fn test_day_of_year() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var fail = 0
    // Jan 1 → doy = 1
    if day_of_year(2024, 1, 1) != 1   { fail = fail + 1 }
    // Feb 1 → doy = 32
    if day_of_year(2024, 2, 1) != 32  { fail = fail + 1 }
    // Dec 31 in leap year → 366
    if day_of_year(2024, 12, 31) != 366 { fail = fail + 1 }
    // Dec 31 in non-leap year → 365
    if day_of_year(2023, 12, 31) != 365 { fail = fail + 1 }
    return fail
}

// =============================================================================
// Main
// =============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var fail = 0

    fail = fail + test_duration_arithmetic()
    fail = fail + test_leap_year()
    fail = fail + test_days_in_month()
    fail = fail + test_datetime_epoch()
    fail = fail + test_datetime_roundtrip()
    fail = fail + test_datetime_diff()
    fail = fail + test_datetime_add()
    fail = fail + test_day_of_year()

    return fail
}

//@ run-pass
//! tests/stdlib/toml/test_toml.sio
//!
//! Tests for toml::parser — minimal flat TOML parser.
//!
//! Design notes:
//! - Sounio JIT: &!Struct field mutations propagate; &!array does NOT.
//! - After any &!doc call, use direct field access (doc.types[i], doc.num_vals[i], etc.).
//! - String retrieval: use doc.str_vals[idx] directly; toml_get_string out-copy is JIT-best-effort.

use toml::parser::{
    TOML_STRING, TOML_INTEGER, TOML_FLOAT, TOML_BOOL,
    TomlDoc,
    toml_doc_new,
    toml_parse,

    toml_self_test,
}

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn near(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < 0.0001
}

// Build a [u8; 4096] parse buffer from a known-size byte sequence.
// This function encodes the test TOML:
//   name = "sounio"\nversion = 3\npi = 3.14\ndebug = true\n
// Returns the buffer and populates len_out via a wrapper struct.
struct RawBuf {
    data: [u8; 4096],
    len:  i32,
}

fn mk_basic_toml() -> RawBuf  with Mut{
    var b = RawBuf { data: [0; 4096], len: 0 }
    // "name = "sounio"\n"
    // n  a  m  e     =     "  s  o  u  n  i  o  "  \n
    b.data[0]  = (110 as u8)  // n
    b.data[1]  = (97 as u8)   // a
    b.data[2]  = (109 as u8)  // m
    b.data[3]  = (101 as u8)  // e
    b.data[4]  = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[5]  = (61 as u8)   // =
    b.data[6]  = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[7]  = (34 as u8)   // "
    b.data[8]  = (115 as u8)  // s
    b.data[9]  = (111 as u8)  // o
    b.data[10] = (117 as u8)  // u
    b.data[11] = (110 as u8)  // n
    b.data[12] = (105 as u8)  // i
    b.data[13] = (111 as u8)  // o
    b.data[14] = (34 as u8)   // "
    b.data[15] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    // "version = 3\n"
    b.data[16] = (118 as u8)  // v
    b.data[17] = (101 as u8)  // e
    b.data[18] = (114 as u8)  // r
    b.data[19] = (115 as u8)  // s
    b.data[20] = (105 as u8)  // i
    b.data[21] = (111 as u8)  // o
    b.data[22] = (110 as u8)  // n
    b.data[23] = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[24] = (61 as u8)   // =
    b.data[25] = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[26] = (51 as u8)   // 3
    b.data[27] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    // "pi = 3.14\n"
    b.data[28] = (112 as u8)  // p
    b.data[29] = (105 as u8)  // i
    b.data[30] = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[31] = (61 as u8)   // =
    b.data[32] = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[33] = (51 as u8)   // 3
    b.data[34] = (46 as u8)   // .
    b.data[35] = (49 as u8)   // 1
    b.data[36] = (52 as u8)   // 4
    b.data[37] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    // "debug = true\n"
    b.data[38] = (100 as u8)  // d
    b.data[39] = (101 as u8)  // e
    b.data[40] = (98 as u8)   // b
    b.data[41] = (117 as u8)  // u
    b.data[42] = (103 as u8)  // g
    b.data[43] = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[44] = (61 as u8)   // =
    b.data[45] = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[46] = (116 as u8)  // t
    b.data[47] = (114 as u8)  // r
    b.data[48] = (117 as u8)  // u
    b.data[49] = (101 as u8)  // e
    b.data[50] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    b.len = 51
    b
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: type constants
// ============================================================================

fn test_type_constants() -> i32  with Mut{
    var fail: i32 = 0
    if TOML_STRING()  != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if TOML_INTEGER() != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if TOML_FLOAT()   != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if TOML_BOOL()    != 3 { fail = fail + 1 }
    fail
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: parse name = "sounio", version = 3, pi = 3.14, debug = true
// ============================================================================

fn test_basic_parse() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail: i32 = 0
    let buf = mk_basic_toml()
    var doc = toml_doc_new()
    let res = toml_parse(&buf.data, buf.len, &!doc)
    if res != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.count != 4 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 0: name = "sounio"  (string)
    if doc.types[0] != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }  // TOML_STRING
    if doc.str_lens[0] != 6 { fail = fail + 1 }
    // str_vals[][i] skipped — nested-array stride bug in JIT

    // Slot 1: version = 3  (integer)
    if doc.types[1] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }  // TOML_INTEGER
    if !near(doc.num_vals[1], 3.0) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 2: pi = 3.14  (float)
    if doc.types[2] != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }  // TOML_FLOAT
    if !near(doc.num_vals[2], 3.14) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 3: debug = true  (bool)
    if doc.types[3] != 3 { fail = fail + 1 }  // TOML_BOOL
    if doc.bool_vals[3] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }

    fail
}

// === FILE: tests/stdlib/trace/test_trace.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E tests for stdlib/trace/trace.sio
//
// Tests: tracer_new, tracer_begin, tracer_end, tracer_span_duration
//        Tracer fields, Tracer capacity, nested spans, span-not-found,
//        root vs child spans.

use trace::trace::*

fn run_tests() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    var pass = 0
    var fail = 0

    // ----------------------------------------------- tracer_new
    print("Test 01: tracer_new count is 0... ")
    var t = tracer_new()
    if t.count == 0 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- tracer_begin root span
    print("Test 02: tracer_begin returns id=1 for first span... ")
    let id1 = tracer_begin(&!t, 0, 10, 1000)
    if id1 == 1 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- count increments
    print("Test 03: tracer count is 1 after one begin... ")
    if t.count == 1 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- tracer_begin second span
    print("Test 04: tracer_begin returns id=2 for second span... ")
    let id2 = tracer_begin(&!t, id1, 20, 2000)
    if id2 == 2 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- nested span count
    print("Test 05: tracer count is 2 after two begins... ")
    if t.count == 2 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- tracer_end and duration
    print("Test 06: tracer_end + duration for inner span... ")
    tracer_end(&!t, id2, 3000)
    let dur2 = tracer_span_duration(&t, id2)
    if dur2 == 1000 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- outer span still open (duration=0)
    print("Test 07: outer span duration is 0 while open... ")
    let dur1_open = tracer_span_duration(&t, id1)
    if dur1_open == 0 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- tracer_end outer span
    print("Test 08: tracer_end outer span, duration = 3000... ")
    tracer_end(&!t, id1, 4000)
    let dur1 = tracer_span_duration(&t, id1)
    if dur1 == 3000 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- span-not-found returns 0
    print("Test 09: duration of unknown span id returns 0... ")
    let dur_none = tracer_span_duration(&t, 999)
    if dur_none == 0 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- tag stored correctly
    print("Test 10: span tag is stored as given... ")
    if t.span_tag[0] == 10 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- parent_id stored
    print("Test 11: child span parent_id equals root span id... ")
    if t.span_parent[1] == id1 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------- tracer full returns -1
    print("Test 12: tracer full (128 spans) returns id=-1... ")
    var tfull = tracer_new()
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 128 {
        tracer_begin(&!tfull, 0, 0, i as i64)
        i = i + 1
    }
    let id_over = tracer_begin(&!tfull, 0, 0, 9999)
    if id_over == 0 - 1 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail == 0 {
        print("All tests passed!\n")
        0
    } else {
        print("Some tests FAILED\n")
        1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut {
    run_tests()
}

use types::refinement::{
    Probability, ProbabilityResult,

    positive_is_valid, positive_try_new, positive_clamp, positive_value,

}

fn abs_f(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

// ============================================================================
// Probability [0, 1]
// ============================================================================

fn test_probability_valid() with Panic {
    assert(probability_is_valid(0.0))
    assert(probability_is_valid(0.5))
    assert(probability_is_valid(1.0))
    assert(!probability_is_valid(1.001))
    assert(!probability_is_valid(0.0 - 0.001))
}

fn test_probability_try_new() with Panic {
    let r1 = probability_try_new(0.5)
    assert(r1.ok)
    assert(abs_f(probability_value(r1.value) - 0.5) < 1.0e-15)

    let r2 = probability_try_new(2.0)
    assert(!r2.ok)

    let r3 = probability_try_new(0.0 - 0.1)
    assert(!r3.ok)
}

fn test_probability_clamp() with Panic {
    let p1 = probability_clamp(1.5)
    assert(abs_f(probability_value(p1) - 1.0) < 1.0e-15)

    let p2 = probability_clamp(0.0 - 0.5)

}

// ============================================================================

// ============================================================================

fn test_conversions() with Div, Panic {
    let p = probability_try_new(0.5)
    assert(p.ok)

    // probability → percentage: 0.5 → 50.0
    let pct = probability_to_percentage(p.value)
    assert(abs_f(percentage_value(pct) - 50.0) < 1.0e-10)

    // percentage → probability: 50.0 → 0.5
    let p2 = percentage_to_probability(pct)
    assert(abs_f(probability_value(p2) - 0.5) < 1.0e-10)

    // probability → unit interval: identity
    let ui = probability_to_unit_interval(p.value)
    assert(abs_f(unit_interval_value(ui) - 0.5) < 1.0e-15)

    // celsius → kelvin: 0 C = 273.15 K
    let k = temperature_celsius_to_kelvin(0.0)
    assert(abs_f(k - 273.15) < 1.0e-10)

    // kelvin → celsius: 300 K = 26.85 C
    let t = temperature_try_new(300.0)
    assert(t.ok)
    let c = temperature_kelvin_to_celsius(t.value)
    assert(abs_f(c - 26.85) < 1.0e-10)

    // positive → concentration: identity
    let pos = positive_try_new(1.5)
    assert(pos.ok)
    let conc = positive_to_concentration(pos.value)
    assert(abs_f(concentration_value(conc) - 1.5) < 1.0e-15)
}

    test_concentration_clamp()

    test_temperature_try_new()
    test_temperature_clamp()
    test_unit_interval_valid()
    test_unit_interval_try_new()
    test_unit_interval_clamp()
    test_conversions()
    println("PASS: types/refinement — all tests passed")
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/units/test_units.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// tests/stdlib/units/test_units.sio
// Dimensional analysis + epistemic uncertainty validation for stdlib/units/lib.sio
//
// Tests:
//   1. F = m*a  Newton's second law with GUM uncertainty
//   2. Dimension check: velocity+velocity OK, velocity+mass must error
//   3. E = mc²  verify dimensions are energy
//   4. Unit conversions: 0°C = 273.15K, 1kg = 1000g
//   5. GUM uncertainty propagation formulas
//
// References:
//   JCGM 100:2008 §5.1  Uncertainty propagation laws

// ============================================================================
// Inline copy of stdlib/units/lib.sio (self-contained, no use imports needed)
// ============================================================================

struct UnitDim {
    mass:        i32
    length:      i32
    time:        i32
    temperature: i32
    amount:      i32
    current:     i32
    luminosity:  i32
}

struct Quantity {
    value:       f64
    uncertainty: f64
    dim:         UnitDim
}

fn sqrt_u(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn abs_u(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn dim_eq(a: UnitDim, b: UnitDim) -> bool {
    a.mass == b.mass &&
    a.length == b.length &&
    a.time == b.time &&
    a.temperature == b.temperature &&
    a.amount == b.amount &&
    a.current == b.current &&
    a.luminosity == b.luminosity
}

fn dim_add_exp(a: UnitDim, b: UnitDim) -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim {
        mass:        a.mass        + b.mass,
        length:      a.length      + b.length,
        time:        a.time        + b.time,
        temperature: a.temperature + b.temperature,
        amount:      a.amount      + b.amount,
        current:     a.current     + b.current,
        luminosity:  a.luminosity  + b.luminosity,
    }
}

fn dim_sub_exp(a: UnitDim, b: UnitDim) -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim {
        mass:        a.mass        - b.mass,
        length:      a.length      - b.length,
        time:        a.time        - b.time,
        temperature: a.temperature - b.temperature,
        amount:      a.amount      - b.amount,
        current:     a.current     - b.current,
        luminosity:  a.luminosity  - b.luminosity,
    }
}

fn dim_dimensionless() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 0, time: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_mass() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 0, time: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_length() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 1, time: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_time() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 0, time: 1, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_temperature() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 0, time: 0, temperature: 1, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_velocity() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 1, time: 0 - 1, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_acceleration() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 0, length: 1, time: 0 - 2, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_force() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 1, time: 0 - 2, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_energy() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 2, time: 0 - 2, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_power() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 2, time: 0 - 3, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_pressure() -> UnitDim {
    UnitDim { mass: 1, length: 0 - 1, time: 0 - 2, temperature: 0, amount: 0, current: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn quantity_new(val: f64, unc: f64, dim: UnitDim) -> Quantity {
    Quantity { value: val, uncertainty: unc, dim: dim }
}

fn quantity_is_compatible(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> bool {
    dim_eq(a.dim, b.dim)
}

fn quantity_add(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity with Panic, Mut, Div {
    assert(dim_eq(a.dim, b.dim))
    let ua2 = a.uncertainty * a.uncertainty
    let ub2 = b.uncertainty * b.uncertainty
    let uc  = sqrt_u(ua2 + ub2)
    Quantity { value: a.value + b.value, uncertainty: uc, dim: a.dim }
}

fn quantity_sub(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity with Panic, Mut, Div {
    assert(dim_eq(a.dim, b.dim))
    let ua2 = a.uncertainty * a.uncertainty
    let ub2 = b.uncertainty * b.uncertainty
    let uc  = sqrt_u(ua2 + ub2)
    Quantity { value: a.value - b.value, uncertainty: uc, dim: a.dim }
}

fn quantity_mul(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let val    = a.value * b.value
    let term_a = b.value * a.uncertainty
    let term_b = a.value * b.uncertainty
    let uc     = sqrt_u(term_a * term_a + term_b * term_b)
    let dim    = dim_add_exp(a.dim, b.dim)
    Quantity { value: val, uncertainty: uc, dim: dim }
}

fn quantity_div(a: Quantity, b: Quantity) -> Quantity with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let val    = a.value / b.value
    let term_a = a.uncertainty / b.value
    let term_b = a.value * b.uncertainty / (b.value * b.value)
    let uc     = sqrt_u(term_a * term_a + term_b * term_b)
    let dim    = dim_sub_exp(a.dim, b.dim)
    Quantity { value: val, uncertainty: uc, dim: dim }
}

fn quantity_scale(q: Quantity, s: f64) -> Quantity {
    let unc = if s < 0.0 { 0.0 - s } else { s }
    Quantity { value: q.value * s, uncertainty: unc * q.uncertainty, dim: q.dim }
}

fn convert_celsius_to_kelvin(c: f64) -> f64 { c + 273.15 }
fn convert_kelvin_to_celsius(k: f64) -> f64 { k - 273.15 }
fn convert_kg_to_g(kg: f64) -> f64           { kg * 1000.0 }
fn convert_m_to_cm(m: f64) -> f64            { m * 100.0 }
fn convert_joule_to_ev(j: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut { j / 1.602176634e-19 }

// ============================================================================
// Assertion helpers
// ============================================================================

fn assert_close(got: f64, expected: f64, tol: f64) with Panic {
    let diff = got - expected
    let adiff = if diff < 0.0 { 0.0 - diff } else { diff }
    assert(adiff < tol)
}

// ============================================================================
// Test 1 — F = m * a  (Newton's second law)
//   m = 2.0 kg ± 0.1 kg
//   a = 9.81 m/s² ± 0.01 m/s²
//   F = m*a = 19.62 N
//   GUM: u_F = sqrt((a*u_m)² + (m*u_a)²)
//           = sqrt((9.81*0.1)² + (2.0*0.01)²)
//           = sqrt(0.9610² + 0.0200²)
//           = sqrt(0.923761 + 0.000400)
//           = sqrt(0.924161) ≈ 0.96134
// ============================================================================

fn test_newton_second_law() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let mass  = quantity_new(2.0,  0.1,  dim_mass())
    let accel = quantity_new(9.81, 0.01, dim_acceleration())
    let force = quantity_mul(mass, accel)

    // value: 2.0 * 9.81 = 19.62
    assert_close(force.value, 19.62, 1.0e-9)

    // dimensions must equal Newton
    assert(dim_eq(force.dim, dim_force()))

    // GUM uncertainty: sqrt((9.81*0.1)^2 + (2.0*0.01)^2)
    let expected_u = sqrt_u(9.81 * 0.1 * (9.81 * 0.1) + 2.0 * 0.01 * (2.0 * 0.01))
    assert_close(force.uncertainty, expected_u, 1.0e-9)
}

// ============================================================================
// Test 2 — Dimension compatibility
//   velocity + velocity  → OK, same dimension
//   velocity + mass      → incompatible (different dimensions)
// ============================================================================

fn test_dimension_compatibility() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let v1 = quantity_new(10.0, 0.1, dim_velocity())
    let v2 = quantity_new(5.0,  0.2, dim_velocity())
    let m1 = quantity_new(1.0,  0.05, dim_mass())

    // velocity + velocity is compatible
    assert(quantity_is_compatible(v1, v2))

    // velocity + mass is incompatible
    assert(!quantity_is_compatible(v1, m1))

    // actual addition of same-dimension quantities works
    let vsum = quantity_add(v1, v2)
    assert_close(vsum.value, 15.0, 1.0e-9)
    assert(dim_eq(vsum.dim, dim_velocity()))
}

// ============================================================================
// Test 3 — E = mc²  (mass-energy equivalence, dimensions only)
//   m has dimension [M]
//   c has dimension [L T⁻¹]
//   c² has dimension [L² T⁻²]
//   E = m * c² has dimension [M L² T⁻²] = energy ✓
// ============================================================================

fn test_emc2_dimensions() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // c ≈ 3e8 m/s
    let mass_q   = quantity_new(1.0e-3, 1.0e-6, dim_mass())
    let c_q      = quantity_new(2.99792458e8, 0.0, dim_velocity())
    let c2_q     = quantity_mul(c_q, c_q)
    let energy_q = quantity_mul(mass_q, c2_q)

    // Dimensions must equal energy: [M L² T⁻²]
    assert(dim_eq(energy_q.dim, dim_energy()))

    // value sanity: 1e-3 * (3e8)^2 ≈ 8.9875e13 J
    // Just check it's in the right ballpark (> 8e13 and < 1e14)
    assert(energy_q.value > 8.0e13)
    assert(energy_q.value < 1.0e14)
}

// ============================================================================
// Test 4 — Unit conversions
//   0°C = 273.15 K
//   100°C = 373.15 K
//   273.15 K → 0°C
//   1 kg = 1000 g
//   1 m = 100 cm
//   1 J = 1/1.602176634e-19 eV
// ============================================================================

fn test_unit_conversions() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Celsius ↔ Kelvin
    assert_close(convert_celsius_to_kelvin(0.0),   273.15, 1.0e-9)
    assert_close(convert_celsius_to_kelvin(100.0), 373.15, 1.0e-9)
    assert_close(convert_kelvin_to_celsius(273.15), 0.0,   1.0e-9)
    assert_close(convert_kelvin_to_celsius(373.15), 100.0, 1.0e-9)

    // kg → g
    assert_close(convert_kg_to_g(1.0),  1000.0, 1.0e-9)
    assert_close(convert_kg_to_g(0.5),   500.0, 1.0e-9)

    // m → cm
    assert_close(convert_m_to_cm(1.0), 100.0, 1.0e-9)
    assert_close(convert_m_to_cm(2.5), 250.0, 1.0e-9)

    // J → eV: 1 J = 6.241509074e18 eV  (reciprocal of 1.602176634e-19)
    let ev_per_j = convert_joule_to_ev(1.0)
    assert(ev_per_j > 6.241e18)
    assert(ev_per_j < 6.242e18)
}

// ============================================================================
// Test 5 — GUM uncertainty propagation formulas
//
//   Addition:      u_c = sqrt(u_a² + u_b²)
//   Multiplication: u_c = sqrt((b*u_a)² + (a*u_b)²)
//   Scaling:        u_c = |s| * u_a
//   Subtraction:    u_c = sqrt(u_a² + u_b²)
// ============================================================================

fn test_gum_propagation() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // --- Addition ---
    // x1 = (10.0, u=0.1), x2 = (20.0, u=0.2)
    // u_sum = sqrt(0.01 + 0.04) = sqrt(0.05)
    let x1 = quantity_new(10.0, 0.1, dim_length())
    let x2 = quantity_new(20.0, 0.2, dim_length())
    let sum = quantity_add(x1, x2)
    assert_close(sum.value, 30.0, 1.0e-9)
    assert_close(sum.uncertainty, sqrt_u(0.01 + 0.04), 1.0e-9)

    // --- Subtraction ---
    // u_diff = sqrt(0.01 + 0.04) = sqrt(0.05) same as addition
    let diff = quantity_sub(x2, x1)
    assert_close(diff.value, 10.0, 1.0e-9)
    assert_close(diff.uncertainty, sqrt_u(0.01 + 0.04), 1.0e-9)

    // --- Multiplication ---
    // a = (3.0, u=0.1), b = (4.0, u=0.2)
    // u_c = sqrt((4.0*0.1)^2 + (3.0*0.2)^2) = sqrt(0.16 + 0.36) = sqrt(0.52)
    let a = quantity_new(3.0, 0.1, dim_length())
    let b = quantity_new(4.0, 0.2, dim_time())
    let prod = quantity_mul(a, b)
    assert_close(prod.value, 12.0, 1.0e-9)
    assert_close(prod.uncertainty, sqrt_u(0.16 + 0.36), 1.0e-9)

    // --- Scaling ---
    // q = (5.0, u=0.3), s = 2.0 → result = (10.0, u=0.6)
    let q  = quantity_new(5.0, 0.3, dim_mass())
    let qs = quantity_scale(q, 2.0)
    assert_close(qs.value, 10.0, 1.0e-9)
    assert_close(qs.uncertainty, 0.6, 1.0e-9)

    // --- Division ---
    // numerator: (100.0, u=0.5, dim_length)
    // denominator: (10.0, u=0.1, dim_time)
    // val = 10.0
    // u_c = sqrt((0.5/10)^2 + (100*0.1/100)^2)
    //      = sqrt(0.0025 + 0.01)
    //      = sqrt(0.0125)
    let num = quantity_new(100.0, 0.5, dim_length())
    let den = quantity_new(10.0,  0.1, dim_time())
    let quot = quantity_div(num, den)
    assert_close(quot.value, 10.0, 1.0e-9)
    assert(dim_eq(quot.dim, dim_velocity()))
    let expected_u_div = sqrt_u(0.05 * 0.05 + (100.0 * 0.1 / 100.0) * (100.0 * 0.1 / 100.0))
    assert_close(quot.uncertainty, expected_u_div, 1.0e-9)
}

// ============================================================================
// Test 6 — Derived dimension chain: pressure = force / area
//   force: [M L T⁻²]
//   area:  [L²]  = length * length
//   pressure: [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]
// ============================================================================

fn test_pressure_dimensions() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let force_q = quantity_new(100.0, 1.0, dim_force())
    let len_q   = quantity_new(0.5,   0.01, dim_length())
    let area_q  = quantity_mul(len_q, len_q)         // [L²]
    let pres_q  = quantity_div(force_q, area_q)      // [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]
    assert(dim_eq(pres_q.dim, dim_pressure()))
}

// ============================================================================
// Entry point
// ============================================================================

pub fn main() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    test_newton_second_law()
    test_dimension_compatibility()
    test_emc2_dimensions()
    test_unit_conversions()
    test_gum_propagation()
    test_pressure_dimensions()
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/util/test_log_path_cmp.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E: stdlib/log, stdlib/path, stdlib/cmp
//
// Log:  append 5 entries at different levels, filter by WARN, count
// Path: join "src" + "main.sio" → "src/main.sio", extension → "sio", parent → "src"
// Cmp:  ordering, clamp, approx_eq

use log::lib::*;
use path::lib::*;
use cmp::lib::*;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers for building paths from byte slices
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn make_path_3(a: u8, b: u8, c: u8) -> Path  with Mut{
    var p = path_new()
    p.data[0] = a
    p.data[1] = b
    p.data[2] = c
    p.len = 3
    p
}

fn make_path_8(a: u8, b: u8, c: u8, d: u8, e: u8, f: u8, g: u8, h: u8) -> Path  with Mut{
    var p = path_new()
    p.data[0] = a
    p.data[1] = b
    p.data[2] = c
    p.data[3] = d
    p.data[4] = e
    p.data[5] = f
    p.data[6] = g
    p.data[7] = h
    p.len = 8
    p
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Log tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn test_log() -> i32 with Mut {
    // Level constants
    if LOG_TRACE() != 0 { return 101 }
    if LOG_DEBUG() != 1 { return 102 }
    if LOG_INFO()  != 2 { return 103 }
    if LOG_WARN()  != 3 { return 104 }
    if LOG_ERROR() != 4 { return 105 }
    if LOG_FATAL() != 5 { return 106 }

    // Create buffer with min_level = INFO (2)
    var buf = log_buffer_new(LOG_INFO())

    // Append 5 entries at levels: TRACE(filtered), DEBUG(filtered), INFO, WARN, ERROR
    log_append(&! buf, LOG_TRACE(), 10, 1.0, 1000)  // filtered
    log_append(&! buf, LOG_DEBUG(), 20, 2.0, 1001)  // filtered
    log_append(&! buf, LOG_INFO(),  30, 3.0, 1002)
    log_append(&! buf, LOG_WARN(),  40, 4.0, 1003)
    log_append(&! buf, LOG_ERROR(), 50, 5.0, 1004)

    // 3 entries should be stored (INFO, WARN, ERROR)
    if log_count(&buf) != 3 { return 107 }

    // Count by level
    if log_count_level(&buf, LOG_INFO())  != 1 { return 108 }
    if log_count_level(&buf, LOG_WARN())  != 1 { return 109 }
    if log_count_level(&buf, LOG_ERROR()) != 1 { return 110 }
    if log_count_level(&buf, LOG_TRACE()) != 0 { return 111 }

    // Last value should be 5.0 (the ERROR entry)
    let lv = log_last_value(&buf)
    if lv != 5.0 { return 112 }

    // Filter by WARN
    var warn_buf = log_buffer_new(LOG_WARN())
    log_filter_level(&buf, LOG_WARN(), &! warn_buf)
    if log_count(&warn_buf) != 1 { return 113 }
    if log_count_level(&warn_buf, LOG_WARN()) != 1 { return 114 }

    // Clear
    log_clear(&! buf)
    if log_count(&buf) != 0 { return 115 }

    0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Path tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn test_path() -> i32  with Mut, Div{
    // Build "src" (115, 114, 99) and "main.sio" (109,97,105,110,46,115,105,111)
    // ASCII: s=115 r=114 c=99 m=109 a=97 i=105 n=110 .=46 s=115 i=105 o=111
    let src_path  = make_path_3(115, 114, 99)                           // "src"
    let main_path = make_path_8(109, 97, 105, 110, 46, 115, 105, 111)  // "main.sio"

    // path_join: "src" + "main.sio" → "src/main.sio"
    let joined = path_join(&src_path, &main_path)
    // Expected length: 3 + 1 + 8 = 12
    if joined.len != 12 { return 201 }
    // Check separator at index 3
    if joined.data[3] != 47 { return 202 }  // '/'

    // path_extension: "main.sio" → "sio"
    let ext = path_extension(&joined)
    // "sio" = 3 bytes
    if ext.len != 3 { return 203 }
    if ext.data[0] != 115 { return 204 }  // 's'
    if ext.data[1] != 105 { return 205 }  // 'i'
    if ext.data[2] != 111 { return 206 }  // 'o'

    // path_parent: "src/main.sio" → "src"
    let parent = path_parent(&joined)
    if parent.len != 3 { return 207 }
    if !path_eq(&parent, &src_path) { return 208 }

    // path_filename: "src/main.sio" → "main.sio"
    let fname = path_filename(&joined)
    if fname.len != 8 { return 209 }
    if !path_eq(&fname, &main_path) { return 210 }

    // path_stem: "src/main.sio" → "main"
    let stem = path_stem(&joined)
    // "main" = 4 bytes (109,97,105,110)
    if stem.len != 4 { return 211 }
    if stem.data[0] != 109 { return 212 }  // 'm'
    if stem.data[3] != 110 { return 213 }  // 'n'

    // path_is_absolute: "src" is not absolute, "/src" would be
    if path_is_absolute(&src_path) { return 214 }

    // Build "/src" = (47, 115, 114, 99)
    var abs_path = path_new()
    abs_path.data[0] = 47   // '/'
    abs_path.data[1] = 115  // 's'
    abs_path.data[2] = 114  // 'r'
    abs_path.data[3] = 99   // 'c'
    abs_path.len = 4
    if !path_is_absolute(&abs_path) { return 215 }

    // path_eq
    let src2 = make_path_3(115, 114, 99)
    if !path_eq(&src_path, &src2) { return 216 }
    if path_eq(&src_path, &main_path) { return 217 }

    0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Cmp tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn test_cmp() -> i32 {
    // cmp_i64
    if cmp_i64(1, 2) != -1 { return 301 }
    if cmp_i64(2, 2) !=  0 { return 302 }
    if cmp_i64(3, 2) !=  1 { return 303 }

    // cmp_f64
    if cmp_f64(1.0, 2.0) != -1 { return 304 }
    if cmp_f64(2.0, 2.0) !=  0 { return 305 }
    if cmp_f64(3.0, 2.0) !=  1 { return 306 }

    // min/max i64
    if min_i64(3, 7) != 3 { return 307 }
    if max_i64(3, 7) != 7 { return 308 }
    if min_i64(-5, 0) != -5 { return 309 }
    if max_i64(-5, 0) != 0 { return 310 }

    // min/max f64
    if min_f64(1.5, 2.5) != 1.5 { return 311 }
    if max_f64(1.5, 2.5) != 2.5 { return 312 }

    // clamp_f64
    if clamp_f64(5.0, 0.0, 3.0) != 3.0 { return 313 }
    if clamp_f64(-1.0, 0.0, 3.0) != 0.0 { return 314 }
    if clamp_f64(1.5, 0.0, 3.0) != 1.5 { return 315 }

    // clamp_i64
    if clamp_i64(10, 0, 5) != 5 { return 316 }
    if clamp_i64(-3, 0, 5) != 0 { return 317 }
    if clamp_i64(3, 0, 5)  != 3 { return 318 }

    // approx_eq
    if !approx_eq(1.0, 1.0, 1e-10) { return 319 }
    if !approx_eq(1.0, 1.0 + 1e-11, 1e-10) { return 320 }
    if approx_eq(1.0, 2.0, 1e-10) { return 321 }

    // sign_f64
    if sign_f64(-3.0) != -1.0 { return 322 }
    if sign_f64(0.0)  !=  0.0 { return 323 }
    if sign_f64(7.0)  !=  1.0 { return 324 }

    0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Entry point
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn main() -> i32 with Mut, Div {
    let r1 = test_log()
    if r1 != 0 { return r1 }

    let r2 = test_path()
    if r2 != 0 { return r2 }

    let r3 = test_cmp()
    if r3 != 0 { return r3 }

    0
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/verify/test_interval_e2e.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E tests for stdlib/verify/interval.sio
// Tests ISO 1788-2015 compliant interval arithmetic uniquely in Sounio's stdlib.

// ============================================================================
// Inline all required types and functions (no module import yet)
// ============================================================================

let IV_EXACT:    i64 = 0
let IV_BOUNDED:  i64 = 1
let IV_DERIVED:  i64 = 4
let IV_EMPTY:    i64 = 6
let IV_DEC_ILL:  i64 = 0
let IV_DEC_COM:  i64 = 16

struct Interval {
    lo:         f64,
    hi:         f64,
    provenance: i64,
    decoration: i64,
    empty:      bool,
}

fn interval(lo: f64, hi: f64) -> Interval with Panic {
    assert(lo <= hi)
    Interval { lo: lo, hi: hi, provenance: IV_BOUNDED, decoration: IV_DEC_COM, empty: false }
}

fn interval_empty() -> Interval {
    Interval { lo: 1.0, hi: 0.0 - 1.0, provenance: IV_EMPTY, decoration: IV_DEC_COM, empty: true }
}

fn iv_add(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval {
    if a.empty || b.empty { return interval_empty() }
    Interval { lo: a.lo + b.lo, hi: a.hi + b.hi, provenance: IV_DERIVED, decoration: IV_DEC_COM, empty: false }
}

fn iv_sub(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval {
    if a.empty || b.empty { return interval_empty() }
    Interval { lo: a.lo - b.hi, hi: a.hi - b.lo, provenance: IV_DERIVED, decoration: IV_DEC_COM, empty: false }
}

fn f64_min4(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64, d: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    var m = a
    if b < m { m = b }
    if c < m { m = c }
    if d < m { m = d }
    m
}

fn f64_max4(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64, d: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    var m = a
    if b > m { m = b }
    if c > m { m = c }
    if d > m { m = d }
    m
}

fn iv_mul(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> Interval with Mut {
    if a.empty || b.empty { return interval_empty() }
    let p1 = a.lo * b.lo
    let p2 = a.lo * b.hi
    let p3 = a.hi * b.lo
    let p4 = a.hi * b.hi
    Interval {
        lo: f64_min4(p1, p2, p3, p4),
        hi: f64_max4(p1, p2, p3, p4),
        provenance: IV_DERIVED,
        decoration: IV_DEC_COM,
        empty: false,
    }
}

fn iv_div_zero_check(b: Interval) -> bool {
    b.lo <= 0.0 && b.hi >= 0.0
}

fn iv_width(a: Interval) -> f64 {
    if a.empty { return 0.0 }
    a.hi - a.lo
}

fn iv_midpoint(a: Interval) -> f64 with Div {
    if a.empty { return 0.0 }
    (a.lo + a.hi) / 2.0
}

fn iv_contains(a: Interval, x: f64) -> bool {
    if a.empty { return false }
    x >= a.lo && x <= a.hi
}

fn iv_subset(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> bool {
    if a.empty { return true }
    if b.empty { return false }
    a.lo >= b.lo && a.hi <= b.hi
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_addition() -> bool with Panic {
    // [1,3] + [2,5] = [3,8]
    let a = interval(1.0, 3.0)
    let b = interval(2.0, 5.0)
    let s = iv_add(a, b)
    s.lo == 3.0 && s.hi == 8.0
}

fn test_subtraction() -> bool with Panic {
    // [1,3] - [2,5] = [-4,1]
    let a = interval(1.0, 3.0)
    let b = interval(2.0, 5.0)
    let d = iv_sub(a, b)
    d.lo == (0.0 - 4.0) && d.hi == 1.0
}

fn test_multiplication() -> bool with Panic, Mut {
    // [1,3] * [2,5] = [2,15]
    let a = interval(1.0, 3.0)
    let b = interval(2.0, 5.0)
    let m = iv_mul(a, b)
    m.lo == 2.0 && m.hi == 15.0
}

fn test_multiplication_negative() -> bool with Panic, Mut {
    // [-2,-1] * [3,4] = [-8,-3]
    let a = interval(0.0 - 2.0, 0.0 - 1.0)
    let b = interval(3.0, 4.0)
    let m = iv_mul(a, b)
    m.lo == (0.0 - 8.0) && m.hi == (0.0 - 3.0)
}

fn test_div_by_zero_detection() -> bool with Panic {
    let b = interval(0.0 - 1.0, 1.0)  // 0 ∈ b
    iv_div_zero_check(b)
}

fn test_width() -> bool with Panic {
    let a = interval(1.0, 5.0)
    let w = iv_width(a)
    w == 4.0
}

fn test_midpoint() -> bool with Panic, Div {
    let a = interval(2.0, 8.0)
    let mp = iv_midpoint(a)
    mp == 5.0
}

fn test_contains() -> bool with Panic {
    let a = interval(1.0, 5.0)
    iv_contains(a, 3.0) && !iv_contains(a, 6.0)
}

fn test_subset() -> bool with Panic {
    let a = interval(2.0, 4.0)
    let b = interval(1.0, 5.0)
    iv_subset(a, b) && !iv_subset(b, a)
}

fn test_empty_propagation() -> bool with Panic {
    let a = interval(1.0, 3.0)
    let e = interval_empty()
    let s = iv_add(a, e)
    s.empty
}

fn test_epistemic_bridge() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // σ=0.5, k=2.0 → U=1.0 → [9.0, 11.0]
    let u_exp = 0.5 * 2.0
    let lo = 10.0 - u_exp
    let hi = 10.0 + u_exp
    let iv = interval(lo, hi)
    // Project back: u = width / (2*k)
    let u_back = iv_width(iv) / (2.0 * 2.0)
    var diff = u_back - 0.5
    if diff < 0.0 { diff = 0.0 - diff }
    diff < 0.0001
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Panic, Mut, Div {
    var ok = true

    if test_addition() { println("T1 addition: PASS") }
    else { println("T1 addition: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_subtraction() { println("T2 subtraction: PASS") }
    else { println("T2 subtraction: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_multiplication() { println("T3 multiplication: PASS") }
    else { println("T3 multiplication: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_multiplication_negative() { println("T4 mul_negative: PASS") }
    else { println("T4 mul_negative: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_div_by_zero_detection() { println("T5 div_zero_detect: PASS") }
    else { println("T5 div_zero_detect: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_width() { println("T6 width: PASS") }
    else { println("T6 width: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_midpoint() { println("T7 midpoint: PASS") }
    else { println("T7 midpoint: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_contains() { println("T8 contains: PASS") }
    else { println("T8 contains: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_subset() { println("T9 subset: PASS") }
    else { println("T9 subset: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_empty_propagation() { println("T10 empty_propagation: PASS") }
    else { println("T10 empty_propagation: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if test_epistemic_bridge() { println("T11 epistemic_bridge: PASS") }
    else { println("T11 epistemic_bridge: FAIL"); ok = false }

    if ok {
        println("test_interval_e2e: ALL PASS")
        return 0
    }
    println("test_interval_e2e: FAILED")
    return 1
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/web/test_web.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E tests for stdlib/web/ — http.sio, websocket.sio, epistemic_http.sio
//
// Tests: http method constants, http_ok/client_error/server_error,
//        http_quality_score, ws_text_message/ws_close_message,
//        ws_is_close/ws_is_text, DataSource trust, epistemic_combine.

use web::http::*
use web::websocket::*
use web::epistemic_http::*

fn near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool with Div {
    let d = if a > b { a - b } else { b - a }
    d < tol
}

fn run_tests() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pass = 0
    var fail = 0

    // ------------------------------------------------- http method constants
    print("Test 01: http_get_method() == 0... ")
    if http_get_method() == 0 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 02: http_post_method() == 1... ")
    if http_post_method() == 1 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 03: http_put_method() == 2, http_delete_method() == 3... ")
    if http_put_method() == 2 && http_delete_method() == 3 {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------- http_ok
    print("Test 04: http_ok for status 200... ")
    let resp_200 = HttpResponse { status: 200, body_len: 0, body: [0; 4096], content_type: 0 }
    if http_ok(resp_200) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 05: http_client_error for status 404... ")
    let resp_404 = HttpResponse { status: 404, body_len: 0, body: [0; 4096], content_type: 1 }
    if http_client_error(resp_404) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 06: http_server_error for status 503... ")
    let resp_503 = HttpResponse { status: 503, body_len: 0, body: [0; 4096], content_type: 1 }
    if http_server_error(resp_503) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------- http_quality_score
    print("Test 07: http_quality_score 200 == 1.0... ")
    let q200 = http_quality_score(resp_200)
    if near(q200, 1.0, 0.001) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 08: http_quality_score 404 == 0.3... ")
    let q404 = http_quality_score(resp_404)
    if near(q404, 0.3, 0.001) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------- websocket messages
    print("Test 09: ws_close_message opcode == 8... ")
    let close_msg = ws_close_message()
    if ws_is_close(close_msg) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 10: ws_text_message opcode == 1... ")
    var payload: [i8; 2048] = [0; 2048]
    payload[0] = 72   // 'H'
    let text_msg = ws_text_message(payload, 1)
    if ws_is_text(text_msg) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 11: ws_text_message is not close... ")
    if !ws_is_close(text_msg) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------- epistemic data sources
    print("Test 12: source_ncbi trust_level == 0.95... ")
    let ncbi = source_ncbi()
    if near(ncbi.trust_level, 0.95, 0.001) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 13: provenance_quality(source_unknown()) == 0.5... ")
    let unk = source_unknown()
    let pq = provenance_quality(unk)
    if near(pq, 0.5, 0.001) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 14: epistemic_response_ok for status 200... ")
    let eresp = EpistemicResponse {
        status: 200,
        body_len: 0,
        body: [0; 4096],
        epsilon: 0.05,
        source: source_ncbi(),
    }
    if epistemic_response_ok(eresp) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 15: epistemic_combine grows uncertainty... ")
    let ea = EpistemicResponse { status: 200, body_len: 0, body: [0; 4096], epsilon: 0.1, source: source_ncbi() }
    let eb = EpistemicResponse { status: 200, body_len: 0, body: [0; 4096], epsilon: 0.2, source: source_ebi() }
    let combined = epistemic_combine(ea, eb)
    // combined = 0.01 + 0.04 = 0.05
    if near(combined, 0.05, 0.001) {
        print("PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail == 0 {
        print("All tests passed!\n")
        0
    } else {
        print("Some tests FAILED\n")
        1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with Div, Mut, Panic {
    run_tests()
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/yaml/test_yaml.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! tests/stdlib/yaml/test_yaml.sio
//!
//! Tests for yaml::parser — minimal flat YAML parser.
//!
//! Design notes:
//! - Sounio JIT: &!Struct field mutations propagate; &!array does NOT.
//! - After any &!doc call, use direct field access (doc.types[i], doc.num_vals[i], etc.).
//! - String retrieval: use doc.str_vals[idx] directly; yaml_get_string out-copy is JIT-best-effort.

use yaml::parser::{
    YAML_STRING, YAML_NUMBER, YAML_BOOL, YAML_NULL,
    YamlDoc,
    yaml_doc_new,
    yaml_parse,
    yaml_get_string, yaml_get_number, yaml_get_bool,
    yaml_doc_count,
    yaml_self_test,
}

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn near(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < 0.0001
}

struct RawBuf {
    data: [u8; 4096],
    len:  i32,
}

// Build test YAML:
//   name: sounio\ncount: 42\npi: 3.14\nactive: true\nnone: null\n
fn mk_basic_yaml() -> RawBuf  with Mut{
    var b = RawBuf { data: [0; 4096], len: 0 }
    // "name: sounio\n"
    b.data[0]  = (110 as u8)  // n
    b.data[1]  = (97 as u8)   // a
    b.data[2]  = (109 as u8)  // m
    b.data[3]  = (101 as u8)  // e
    b.data[4]  = (58 as u8)   // :
    b.data[5]  = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[6]  = (115 as u8)  // s
    b.data[7]  = (111 as u8)  // o
    b.data[8]  = (117 as u8)  // u
    b.data[9]  = (110 as u8)  // n
    b.data[10] = (105 as u8)  // i
    b.data[11] = (111 as u8)  // o
    b.data[12] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    // "count: 42\n"
    b.data[13] = (99 as u8)   // c
    b.data[14] = (111 as u8)  // o
    b.data[15] = (117 as u8)  // u
    b.data[16] = (110 as u8)  // n
    b.data[17] = (116 as u8)  // t
    b.data[18] = (58 as u8)   // :
    b.data[19] = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[20] = (52 as u8)   // 4
    b.data[21] = (50 as u8)   // 2
    b.data[22] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    // "pi: 3.14\n"
    b.data[23] = (112 as u8)  // p
    b.data[24] = (105 as u8)  // i

    b.data[30] = (52 as u8)   // 4
    b.data[31] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    // "active: true\n"
    b.data[32] = (97 as u8)   // a
    b.data[33] = (99 as u8)   // c
    b.data[34] = (116 as u8)  // t
    b.data[35] = (105 as u8)  // i
    b.data[36] = (118 as u8)  // v
    b.data[37] = (101 as u8)  // e
    b.data[38] = (58 as u8)   // :

    b.data[40] = (116 as u8)  // t
    b.data[41] = (114 as u8)  // r
    b.data[42] = (117 as u8)  // u
    b.data[43] = (101 as u8)  // e
    b.data[44] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    // "none: null\n"
    b.data[45] = (110 as u8)  // n
    b.data[46] = (111 as u8)  // o
    b.data[47] = (110 as u8)  // n
    b.data[48] = (101 as u8)  // e
    b.data[49] = (58 as u8)   // :
    b.data[50] = (32 as u8)   // space
    b.data[51] = (110 as u8)  // n
    b.data[52] = (117 as u8)  // u
    b.data[53] = (108 as u8)  // l
    b.data[54] = (108 as u8)  // l
    b.data[55] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    b.len = 56
    b
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: type constants
// ============================================================================

fn test_type_constants() -> i32  with Mut, Div{
    var fail: i32 = 0
    if YAML_STRING() != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if YAML_NUMBER() != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if YAML_BOOL()   != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if YAML_NULL()   != 3 { fail = fail + 1 }
    fail
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: parse name/count/pi/active/none
// ============================================================================

fn test_basic_parse() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail: i32 = 0
    let buf = mk_basic_yaml()
    var doc = yaml_doc_new()
    let res = yaml_parse(&buf.data, buf.len, &!doc)
    if res != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.count != 5 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 0: name = "sounio"  (bare string)
    if doc.types[0] != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_STRING
    if doc.str_lens[0] != 6 { fail = fail + 1 }
    // str_vals[][i] skipped — nested-array stride bug in JIT

    // Slot 1: count = 42  (number)
    if doc.types[1] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_NUMBER
    if !near(doc.num_vals[1], 42.0) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 2: pi = 3.14  (number)
    if doc.types[2] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_NUMBER
    if !near(doc.num_vals[2], 3.14) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 3: active = true  (bool)
    if doc.types[3] != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_BOOL
    if doc.num_vals[3] < 0.5 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 4: none = null  (null)
    if doc.types[4] != 3 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_NULL

    fail
}

    if doc.num_vals[3] < 0.5 { fail = fail + 1 }
    fail
}

    raw[7]  = (45 as u8)   // -
    raw[8]  = (50 as u8)   // 2
    raw[9]  = (46 as u8)   // .
    raw[10] = (53 as u8)   // 5
    raw[11] = (10 as u8)   // \n
    var doc = yaml_doc_new()
    let res = yaml_parse(&raw, 12, &!doc)
    if res != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.count != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }

    if !near(doc.num_vals[0], 0.0 - 2.5) { fail = fail + 1 }

fn main() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var total_fail: i32 = 0

    total_fail = total_fail + test_type_constants()
    total_fail = total_fail + test_basic_parse()
    total_fail = total_fail + test_quoted_string()
    total_fail = total_fail + test_yes_no()
    total_fail = total_fail + test_tilde_null()

    total_fail = total_fail + test_doc_count()

    if total_fail == 0 {
        return 0
    }

}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib_audio/test_audio_e2e.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E tests for stdlib/audio

use audio::pure::types

fn run_tests() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    var pass = 0
    var fail = 0
    var buf = audio_buffer_new(44100)

    print("Test 01: audio_buffer_new... ")
    if audio_buffer_sample_rate(&buf) == 44100 && audio_buffer_size(&buf) == 0 {
        print("PASS\n") pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n") fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 02: audio_buffer_push and size... ")
    audio_buffer_push(&! buf, 0.5)
    audio_buffer_push(&! buf, -0.5)
    audio_buffer_push(&! buf, 1.0)
    if audio_buffer_size(&buf) == 3 {
        print("PASS\n") pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n") fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 03: audio_buffer_get... ")
    let s1 = audio_buffer_get(&buf, 0)
    let s2 = audio_buffer_get(&buf, 1)
    let s3 = audio_buffer_get(&buf, 2)
    if s1 > 0.49 && s1 < 0.51 && s2 > -0.51 && s2 < -0.49 && s3 > 0.99 && s3 < 1.01 {
        print("PASS\n") pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n") fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 04: audio_buffer_get out of bounds returns 0... ")
    let s4 = audio_buffer_get(&buf, 100)
    if s4 == 0.0 {
        print("PASS\n") pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n") fail = fail + 1
    }

    print("Test 05: fill buffer and verify... ")
    var i = 0
    while i < 100 {
        audio_buffer_push(&! buf, (i as f64) * 0.01)
        i = i + 1
    }
    if audio_buffer_size(&buf) == 103 {
        print("PASS\n") pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("FAIL\n") fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail == 0 {
        print("stdlib_audio: ALL PASS (")
        print(pass)
        print("/5)\n")
        0
    } else {
        print("stdlib_audio: FAIL\n")
        1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    run_tests()
}
