struct EpistemicObjective {
    function: String,
    domain: String,
}

fn create_epistemic_objective() -> EpistemicObjective {
    EpistemicObjective {
        function: "f(x) = (x-2)² + sin(x)".to_string(),
        domain: "x ∈ [0, 10]".to_string(),
    }
}

struct OptimizationResultEpistemic {
    final_params: Vec<f64>,
    optimal_value: f64,
    optimal_uncertainty: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn epistemic_gradient_descent(
    objective: &EpistemicObjective,
    initial_params: Vec<f64>,
    learning_rate: f64,
    iterations: usize,
) -> OptimizationResultEpistemic {
    // Simular gradient descent epistêmico
    var params = initial_params;

    for _ in 0..iterations {
        // Gradiente com incerteza
        let gradient = compute_epistemic_gradient(&params);
        let step_size = learning_rate * gradient.confidence;
        let epistemic_step = step_size * gradient.uncertainty;

        // Atualizar parâmetros
        var idx = 0
        for param in params {
            if idx < gradient.values.len() {
                let grad = gradient.values[idx]
                param -= grad * epistemic_step
            }
            idx += 1
        }
    }

    // Resultado final
    let optimal_value = 0.123;  // Valor ótimo simulado
    let optimal_uncertainty = 0.045;  // Incerteza no ótimo
    let confidence = 0.89;

    OptimizationResultEpistemic {
        final_params: params,
        optimal_value,
        optimal_uncertainty,
        confidence,
    }
}

struct EpistemicGradient {
    values: Vec<f64>,
    uncertainty: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn compute_epistemic_gradient(params: &[f64]) -> EpistemicGradient {
    // Calcular gradiente com incerteza
    EpistemicGradient {
        values: vec![-0.5, 0.3],  // Gradiente simulado
        uncertainty: 0.02,
        confidence: 0.92,
    }
}

struct EpistemicDecision {
    recommended_action: String,
    risk_assessment: String,
    decision_confidence: f64,
}

fn make_epistemic_decision(result: &OptimizationResultEpistemic) -> EpistemicDecision {
    // Tomar decisão baseada em confiança epistêmica
    if result.confidence > 0.85 {
        EpistemicDecision {
            recommended_action: "Implementar solução otimizada".to_string(),
            risk_assessment: "Baixo risco - alta confiança".to_string(),
            decision_confidence: 0.91,
        }
    } else {
        EpistemicDecision {
            recommended_action: "Mais testes necessários".to_string(),
            risk_assessment: "Risco moderado - confiança insuficiente".to_string(),
            decision_confidence: 0.67,
        }
    }
}

// Função auxiliar para ativação ReLU
fn activation_relu(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 {
        x
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

// Função auxiliar para exponencial
fn exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Aproximação simples de exp(x)
    1.0 + x + (x * x) / 2.0 + (x * x * x) / 6.0
}

// === FILE: examples/algebra_demo.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// algebra_demo.sio — How a mathematician uses Sounio
//
// "I want to work in the octonions. Show me the associator structure."
// "Now switch to sedenions. Do zero divisors appear?"
// "What's T_k for k=3,4,5?"

// Inline the CD algebra (self-contained demo)
fn cd_sigma(a: i32, b: i32, bits: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if a == 0 || b == 0 { return 1 }
    if bits <= 1 { return -1 }
    let half = 1 << (bits - 1)
    let a_hi = if a >= half { 1 } else { 0 }
    let b_hi = if b >= half { 1 } else { 0 }
    let a_lo = a & (half - 1)
    let b_lo = b & (half - 1)
    if a_hi == 0 && b_hi == 0 { return cd_sigma(a_lo, b_lo, bits - 1) }
    if a_hi == 0 && b_hi == 1 { return cd_sigma(b_lo, a_lo, bits - 1) }
    if a_hi == 1 && b_hi == 0 {
        if b_lo == 0 { return cd_sigma(a_lo, 0, bits - 1) }
        return 0 - cd_sigma(a_lo, b_lo, bits - 1)
    }
    if b_lo == 0 { return 0 - cd_sigma(0, a_lo, bits - 1) }
    cd_sigma(b_lo, a_lo, bits - 1)
}

struct CD {
    c: [f64; 64],
    bits: i32,
}

fn cd_zero(k: i32) -> CD with Mut, Panic { CD { c: [0.0; 64], bits: k } }

fn cd_basis(k: i32, idx: i32) -> CD with Mut, Panic {
    var r = cd_zero(k)
    r.c[idx as usize] = 1.0
    r
}

fn cd_mul(a: CD, b: CD) -> CD with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var r = cd_zero(a.bits)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        if a.c[i as usize] != 0.0 {
            var j: i32 = 0
            while j < n {
                if b.c[j as usize] != 0.0 {
                    let idx = i ^ j
                    let sign = cd_sigma(i, j, a.bits)
                    r.c[idx as usize] = r.c[idx as usize]
                        + (sign as f64) * a.c[i as usize] * b.c[j as usize]
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

fn cd_norm_sq(a: CD) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n { s = s + a.c[i as usize] * a.c[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

fn cd_sub(a: CD, b: CD) -> CD with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var r = cd_zero(a.bits)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n { r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize] - b.c[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn cd_add(a: CD, b: CD) -> CD with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 1 << a.bits
    var r = cd_zero(a.bits)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n { r.c[i as usize] = a.c[i as usize] + b.c[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    r
}

fn abs_f(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn main() -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div, IO {
    println("================================================================")
    println("  SOUNIO ALGEBRA DEMO — Cayley-Dickson Tower")
    println("  Choose your algebra. Compute. Explore.")
    println("================================================================")

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    // QUATERNIONS (k=2, dim 4): associative, non-commutative
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    println("")
    println("=== QUATERNIONS (k=2, dim 4) ===")
    let k = 2
    let i_q = cd_basis(k, 1)   // i
    let j_q = cd_basis(k, 2)   // j
    let k_q = cd_basis(k, 3)   // k

    let ij = cd_mul(i_q, j_q)  // i*j = k
    let ji = cd_mul(j_q, i_q)  // j*i = -k

    // Check: i*j = -j*i (anti-commutative)
    let sum = cd_add(ij, ji)
    let anticomm = cd_norm_sq(sum) < 0.001
    println("  i*j + j*i = 0 (anti-commutative): ")
    if anticomm { println("  YES") } else { println("  NO") }

    // Check associativity: (i*j)*k = i*(j*k)
    let left = cd_mul(cd_mul(i_q, j_q), k_q)
    let right = cd_mul(i_q, cd_mul(j_q, k_q))
    let assoc = cd_sub(left, right)
    let is_assoc = cd_norm_sq(assoc) < 0.001
    println("  (i*j)*k = i*(j*k) (associative): ")
    if is_assoc { println("  YES — quaternions are associative") } else { println("  NO") }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    // OCTONIONS (k=3, dim 8): non-associative, alternative
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    println("")
    println("=== OCTONIONS (k=3, dim 8) ===")
    let k3 = 3
    let e1 = cd_basis(k3, 1)
    let e2 = cd_basis(k3, 2)
    let e4 = cd_basis(k3, 4)

    // Find an associative and a non-associative triple in the BINARY labeling
    // (Note: the binary labeling's Fano lines differ from the standard labeling)
    let e3 = cd_basis(k3, 3)
    let e5 = cd_basis(k3, 5)

    // Test (1,2,3): 1 XOR 2 = 3 → these share a "line" in Z_2^3
    let left2 = cd_mul(cd_mul(e1, e2), e3)
    let right2 = cd_mul(e1, cd_mul(e2, e3))
    let assoc2 = cd_sub(left2, right2)
    let nsq2 = cd_norm_sq(assoc2)
    println("  [e1, e2, e3]: ||assoc||^2 = ")
    println(nsq2)
    if abs_f(nsq2) < 0.001 {
        println("  → ASSOCIATIVE")
    } else {
        println("  → NON-ASSOCIATIVE (norm = 2)")
    }

    // Test (1,2,5)
    let left3 = cd_mul(cd_mul(e1, e2), e5)
    let right3 = cd_mul(e1, cd_mul(e2, e5))
    let assoc3 = cd_sub(left3, right3)
    let nsq3 = cd_norm_sq(assoc3)
    println("  [e1, e2, e5]: ||assoc||^2 = ")
    println(nsq3)
    if abs_f(nsq3) < 0.001 {
        println("  → ASSOCIATIVE")
    } else {
        println("  → NON-ASSOCIATIVE (norm = 2)")
    }

    println("  (Binary labeling: Fano lines differ from standard labeling)")

    // Count T_3
    var t3: i32 = 0
    var ii: i32 = 1
    while ii <= 7 {
        var jj: i32 = 1
        while jj <= 7 {
            var kk: i32 = 1
            while kk <= 7 {
                let a = cd_sigma(ii, jj, 3) * cd_sigma(ii ^ jj, kk, 3)
                let b = cd_sigma(jj, kk, 3) * cd_sigma(ii, jj ^ kk, 3)
                if a != b { t3 = t3 + 1 }
                kk = kk + 1
            }
            jj = jj + 1
        }
        ii = ii + 1
    }
    println("  T_3 = ")
    println(t3)
    println("  (= 168 = |PSL(2,7)|)")

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    // SEDENIONS (k=4, dim 16): zero divisors appear!
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    println("")
    println("=== SEDENIONS (k=4, dim 16) ===")
    let k4 = 4

    // Known zero divisor: (e3 + e10)(e6 - e15) = 0
    let zd_a = cd_add(cd_basis(k4, 3), cd_basis(k4, 10))
    let zd_b = cd_sub(cd_basis(k4, 6), cd_basis(k4, 15))
    let zd_prod = cd_mul(zd_a, zd_b)

    println("  (e3 + e10)(e6 - e15) norm^2 = ")
    println(cd_norm_sq(zd_prod))
    println("  → 0 = ZERO DIVISOR (both factors nonzero, product = 0)")

    println("  ||e3 + e10||^2 = ")
    println(cd_norm_sq(zd_a))
    println("  ||e6 - e15||^2 = ")
    println(cd_norm_sq(zd_b))
    println("  Both nonzero → division algebra BROKEN at sedenions")

    // Count T_4
    var t4: i32 = 0
    ii = 1
    while ii <= 15 {
        var jj2: i32 = 1
        while jj2 <= 15 {
            var kk2: i32 = 1
            while kk2 <= 15 {
                let a = cd_sigma(ii, jj2, 4) * cd_sigma(ii ^ jj2, kk2, 4)
                let b = cd_sigma(jj2, kk2, 4) * cd_sigma(ii, jj2 ^ kk2, 4)
                if a != b { t4 = t4 + 1 }
                kk2 = kk2 + 1
            }
            jj2 = jj2 + 1
        }
        ii = ii + 1
    }
    println("  T_4 = ")
    println(t4)
    println("  (= 1848 = 11 × 168)")

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    // SUMMARY
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    println("")
    println("================================================================")
    println("  TOWER SUMMARY")
    println("================================================================")
    println("  k=1 (C):   commutative, associative, division")
    println("  k=2 (H):   non-commutative, associative, division")
    println("  k=3 (O):   non-commutative, NON-ASSOCIATIVE, division, T=168")
    println("  k=4 (S):   non-commutative, non-associative, ZERO DIVISORS, T=1848")
    println("")
    println("  At each step, a property is lost.")
    println("  The 168 quantum is preserved: T_k is always a multiple of 168.")
    println("  ||[a,b,c]|| in {0, 2} for ALL k (proven).")
    println("")
    println("  To explore higher algebras:")
    println("    let k = 5  // trigintaduonions, dim 32")
    println("    let a = cd_basis(k, 1)")
    println("    let b = cd_basis(k, 17)")
    println("    let c = cd_mul(a, b)")

    0
}


// === FILE: examples/algo/graph_demo.sio ===
//! Graph Algorithms Demonstration
//!
//! Demonstrates Dijkstra's shortest path, DFS, and BFS algorithms
//! on a sample weighted directed graph.

extern "C" {
    fn printf(fmt: *const u8, ...) -> i32;
    fn malloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn free(ptr: *mut u8);
}

struct Edge {
    to: usize,
    weight: f64,
}

const INFINITY: f64 = 1.0e308

// Dijkstra's algorithm for shortest paths
fn dijkstra(adj: &[*const Edge], edge_counts: &[usize], n: usize, source: usize) -> *mut f64 with Alloc, Panic {
    // Allocate distance and visited arrays
    let dist = malloc(n * 8) as *mut f64
    let visited = malloc(n) as *mut bool

    // Initialize distances
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        dist[i] = INFINITY
        visited[i] = false
        i = i + 1
    }

    dist[source] = 0.0

    var remaining = n

    while remaining > 0 {
        // Find unvisited node with minimum distance
        var min_dist = INFINITY
        var min_node: i64 = -1

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            if !visited[i] && dist[i] < min_dist {
                min_dist = dist[i]
                min_node = i as i64
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        if min_node == -1 {
            break
        }

        let u = min_node as usize
        visited[u] = true
        remaining = remaining - 1

        // Relax edges from u
        let edges = adj[u]
        let count = edge_counts[u]
        var j: usize = 0
        while j < count {
            let edge = &edges[j]
            let v = edge.to
            let new_dist = dist[u] + edge.weight

            if new_dist < dist[v] {
                dist[v] = new_dist
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }

    free(visited as *mut u8)
    return dist
}

// Breadth-first search
fn bfs(adj: &[*const Edge], edge_counts: &[usize], n: usize, source: usize) -> *mut i64 with Alloc, Panic {
    let distances = malloc(n * 8) as *mut i64

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        distances[i] = -1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Simple queue using array
    let queue = malloc(n * 8) as *mut usize
    var head: usize = 0
    var tail: usize = 0

    distances[source] = 0
    queue[tail] = source
    tail = tail + 1

    while head < tail {
        let u = queue[head]
        head = head + 1

        let edges = adj[u]
        let count = edge_counts[u]
        var j: usize = 0
        while j < count {
            let v = edges[j].to
            if distances[v] == -1 {
                distances[v] = distances[u] + 1
                queue[tail] = v
                tail = tail + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }

    free(queue as *mut u8)
    return distances
}

// Depth-first search
fn dfs_visit(adj: &[*const Edge], edge_counts: &[usize], u: usize, visited: &!*mut bool) with Panic {
    visited[u] = true

    let edges = adj[u]
    let count = edge_counts[u]
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < count {
        let v = edges[i].to
        if !visited[v] {
            dfs_visit(adj, edge_counts, v, visited)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn dfs(adj: &[*const Edge], edge_counts: &[usize], n: usize, source: usize) -> *mut bool with Alloc, Panic {
    let visited = malloc(n) as *mut bool

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        visited[i] = false
        i = i + 1
    }

    dfs_visit(adj, edge_counts, source, &!visited)

    return visited
}

fn main() -> i32 with Alloc, Panic {
    printf("Graph Algorithms Demonstration\n".as_ptr())
    printf("===============================\n\n".as_ptr())

    // Build sample graph: 6 nodes (0-5)
    // Graph structure:
    //   0 -> 1 (2.0), 0 -> 2 (4.0)
    //   1 -> 2 (1.0), 1 -> 3 (7.0)
    //   2 -> 4 (3.0)
    //   3 -> 5 (1.0)
    //   4 -> 3 (2.0), 4 -> 5 (5.0)

    let n: usize = 6

    // Allocate edge arrays for each node
    let edges0 = malloc(2 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges0[0] = Edge { to: 1, weight: 2.0 }
    edges0[1] = Edge { to: 2, weight: 4.0 }

    let edges1 = malloc(2 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges1[0] = Edge { to: 2, weight: 1.0 }
    edges1[1] = Edge { to: 3, weight: 7.0 }

    let edges2 = malloc(1 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges2[0] = Edge { to: 4, weight: 3.0 }

    let edges3 = malloc(1 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges3[0] = Edge { to: 5, weight: 1.0 }

    let edges4 = malloc(2 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges4[0] = Edge { to: 3, weight: 2.0 }
    edges4[1] = Edge { to: 5, weight: 5.0 }

    let edges5 = malloc(0) as *mut Edge

    // Build adjacency list
    let adj = [edges0 as *const Edge, edges1 as *const Edge, edges2 as *const Edge,
               edges3 as *const Edge, edges4 as *const Edge, edges5 as *const Edge]
    let edge_counts: [usize; 6] = [2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 0]

    printf("Graph structure (6 nodes, weighted edges):\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  0 -> 1 (2.0), 2 (4.0)\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  1 -> 2 (1.0), 3 (7.0)\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  2 -> 4 (3.0)\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  3 -> 5 (1.0)\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  4 -> 3 (2.0), 5 (5.0)\n\n".as_ptr())

    // Run Dijkstra from node 0
    printf("1. Dijkstra's Shortest Paths (from node 0):\n".as_ptr())
    let dist = dijkstra(&adj, &edge_counts, n, 0)

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        if dist[i] < INFINITY {
            printf("   Distance to node %zu: %.1f\n".as_ptr(), i, dist[i])
        } else {
            printf("   Distance to node %zu: ∞ (unreachable)\n".as_ptr(), i)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    printf("\n".as_ptr())

    // Run BFS from node 0
    printf("2. Breadth-First Search (from node 0):\n".as_ptr())
    let bfs_dist = bfs(&adj, &edge_counts, n, 0)

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if bfs_dist[i] >= 0 {
            printf("   BFS distance to node %zu: %lld hops\n".as_ptr(), i, bfs_dist[i])
        } else {
            printf("   Node %zu: unreachable\n".as_ptr(), i)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    printf("\n".as_ptr())

    // Run DFS from node 0
    printf("3. Depth-First Search (from node 0):\n".as_ptr())
    let visited = dfs(&adj, &edge_counts, n, 0)

    printf("   Visited nodes: ".as_ptr())
    i = 0
    var first = true
    while i < n {
        if visited[i] {
            if !first {
                printf(", ".as_ptr())
            }
            printf("%zu".as_ptr(), i)
            first = false
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    printf("\n\n".as_ptr())

    // Verify shortest path to node 5
    printf("Shortest path from 0 to 5:\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  Dijkstra distance: %.1f\n".as_ptr(), dist[5])
    printf("  Path: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 3 -> 5\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  (2.0 + 1.0 + 3.0 + 2.0 + 1.0 = 9.0)\n".as_ptr())

    // Clean up
    free(dist as *mut u8)
    free(bfs_dist as *mut u8)
    free(visited as *mut u8)
    free(edges0 as *mut u8)
    free(edges1 as *mut u8)
    free(edges2 as *mut u8)
    free(edges3 as *mut u8)
    free(edges4 as *mut u8)

    printf("\nGraph algorithms completed successfully!\n".as_ptr())
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/algo/sorting_demo.sio ===
//! Sorting Algorithms Demonstration
//!
//! Compares quicksort, mergesort, and heapsort on the same dataset.
//! Shows algorithm correctness and sorting verification.

extern "C" {
    fn printf(fmt: *const u8, ...) -> i32;
    fn malloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn free(ptr: *mut u8);
}

// Quicksort implementation
fn quicksort_i64(arr: &![i64], len: usize) with Panic, Div {
    if len <= 1 {
        return
    }
    quicksort_range(&!arr, 0, len - 1)
}

fn quicksort_range(arr: &![i64], low: usize, high: usize) with Panic, Div {
    if low < high {
        let pivot_idx = partition(&!arr, low, high)

        if pivot_idx > 0 {
            quicksort_range(&!arr, low, pivot_idx - 1)
        }

        if pivot_idx < high {
            quicksort_range(&!arr, pivot_idx + 1, high)
        }
    }
}

fn partition(arr: &![i64], low: usize, high: usize) -> usize with Panic, Div {
    let mid = low + (high - low) / 2
    let pivot = arr[mid]

    var i = low
    var j = high

    while true {
        while arr[i] < pivot {
            i = i + 1
        }

        while arr[j] > pivot {
            j = j - 1
        }

        if i >= j {
            return j
        }

        let temp = arr[i]
        arr[i] = arr[j]
        arr[j] = temp

        i = i + 1
        j = j - 1
    }

    return j
}

// Mergesort implementation
fn mergesort_i64(arr: &![i64], len: usize) with Alloc, Panic, Div {
    if len <= 1 {
        return
    }

    let size_bytes = len * 8
    let temp = malloc(size_bytes) as *mut i64

    mergesort_recursive(&!arr, temp, 0, len - 1)

    free(temp as *mut u8)
}

fn mergesort_recursive(arr: &![i64], temp: *mut i64, left: usize, right: usize) with Panic, Div {
    if left >= right {
        return
    }

    let mid = left + (right - left) / 2

    mergesort_recursive(&!arr, temp, left, mid)
    mergesort_recursive(&!arr, temp, mid + 1, right)
    merge(&!arr, temp, left, mid, right)
}

fn merge(arr: &![i64], temp: *mut i64, left: usize, mid: usize, right: usize) with Panic, Div {
    var i = left
    while i <= right {
        temp[i] = arr[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    var i1 = left
    var i2 = mid + 1
    var curr = left

    while i1 <= mid && i2 <= right {
        if temp[i1] <= temp[i2] {
            arr[curr] = temp[i1]
            i1 = i1 + 1
        } else {
            arr[curr] = temp[i2]
            i2 = i2 + 1
        }
        curr = curr + 1
    }

    while i1 <= mid {
        arr[curr] = temp[i1]
        i1 = i1 + 1
        curr = curr + 1
    }
}

// Heapsort implementation
fn heapsort_i64(arr: &![i64], len: usize) with Panic, Div {
    if len <= 1 {
        return
    }

    var i = len / 2
    while i > 0 {
        i = i - 1
        heapify(&!arr, len, i)
    }

    var end = len - 1
    while end > 0 {
        let temp = arr[0]
        arr[0] = arr[end]
        arr[end] = temp

        heapify(&!arr, end, 0)

        end = end - 1
    }
}

fn heapify(arr: &![i64], heap_size: usize, root: usize) with Panic {
    var largest = root
    let left = 2 * root + 1
    let right = 2 * root + 2

    if left < heap_size && arr[left] > arr[largest] {
        largest = left
    }

    if right < heap_size && arr[right] > arr[largest] {
        largest = right
    }

    if largest != root {
        let temp = arr[root]
        arr[root] = arr[largest]
        arr[largest] = temp

        heapify(&!arr, heap_size, largest)
    }
}

// Check if array is sorted
fn is_sorted(arr: &[i64], len: usize) -> bool with Panic, Div {
    if len <= 1 {
        return true
    }

    var i = 0
    while i < len - 1 {
        if arr[i] > arr[i + 1] {
            return false
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return true
}

// Print array helper
fn print_array(arr: &[i64], len: usize) with Panic {
    printf("  [".as_ptr())
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len {
        if i > 0 {
            printf(", ".as_ptr())
        }
        printf("%lld".as_ptr(), arr[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    printf("]\n".as_ptr())
}

// Copy array helper
fn copy_array(dest: &![i64], src: &[i64], len: usize) with Panic {
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len {
        dest[i] = src[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with Alloc, Panic, Div {
    printf("Sorting Algorithms Comparison\n".as_ptr())
    printf("=============================\n\n".as_ptr())

    // Sample dataset
    let original = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90, 88, 45, 50, 23, 36]
    let len: usize = 12

    printf("Original array:\n".as_ptr())
    print_array(&original, len)
    printf("\n".as_ptr())

    // Test Quicksort
    printf("1. Quicksort (in-place, unstable)\n".as_ptr())
    var arr_quick = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90, 88, 45, 50, 23, 36]
    quicksort_i64(&!arr_quick, len)
    printf("   Sorted: ".as_ptr())
    print_array(&arr_quick, len)
    printf("   Verified: %s\n\n".as_ptr(),
           if is_sorted(&arr_quick, len) { "✓ Correct" } else { "✗ Failed" }.as_ptr())

    // Test Mergesort
    printf("2. Mergesort (stable, O(n) space)\n".as_ptr())
    var arr_merge = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90, 88, 45, 50, 23, 36]
    mergesort_i64(&!arr_merge, len)
    printf("   Sorted: ".as_ptr())
    print_array(&arr_merge, len)
    printf("   Verified: %s\n\n".as_ptr(),
           if is_sorted(&arr_merge, len) { "✓ Correct" } else { "✗ Failed" }.as_ptr())

    // Test Heapsort
    printf("3. Heapsort (in-place, unstable)\n".as_ptr())
    var arr_heap = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90, 88, 45, 50, 23, 36]
    heapsort_i64(&!arr_heap, len)
    printf("   Sorted: ".as_ptr())
    print_array(&arr_heap, len)
    printf("   Verified: %s\n\n".as_ptr(),
           if is_sorted(&arr_heap, len) { "✓ Correct" } else { "✗ Failed" }.as_ptr())

    // Verify all algorithms produce same result
    printf("Comparing results:\n".as_ptr())
    var all_match = true
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len {
        if arr_quick[i] != arr_merge[i] || arr_merge[i] != arr_heap[i] {
            all_match = false
            break
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    printf("  All algorithms agree: %s\n".as_ptr(),
           if all_match { "✓ Yes" } else { "✗ No" }.as_ptr())

    printf("\nSorting demo completed successfully!\n".as_ptr())
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/complex_native_demo.sio ===
// COMPLEX DEMO: Quicksort + Sieve + GCD + Fibonacci + Collatz
// Tests: recursion, 8 functions, 2 global arrays, all operators

var DATA: [i64; 10000]
var PRIMES: [i64; 1300]

fn swap(i: i64, j: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    var tmp = DATA[i]
    DATA[i] = DATA[j]
    DATA[j] = tmp
}

fn partition(lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var pivot = DATA[hi]
    var i = lo - 1
    var j = lo
    while j < hi {
        if DATA[j] <= pivot {
            i = i + 1
            swap(i, j)
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    swap(i + 1, hi)
    return i + 1
}

fn qsort(lo: i64, hi: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    if lo < hi {
        var p = partition(lo, hi)
        qsort(lo, p - 1)
        qsort(p + 1, hi)
    }
}

fn gcd(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 with Div {
    if b == 0 { return a }
    return gcd(b, a % b)
}

fn fib(n: i64) -> i64 {
    if n <= 1 { return n }
    return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
}

fn collatz_steps(n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var steps = 0
    var x = n
    while x != 1 {
        if (x % 2) == 0 {
            x = x / 2
        } else {
            x = x * 3 + 1
        }
        steps = steps + 1
    }
    return steps
}

fn sieve_primes(limit: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    // Use DATA as sieve (0=composite, 1=prime) up to limit
    var i = 2
    while i <= limit {
        DATA[i] = 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 2
    while (i * i) <= limit {
        if DATA[i] == 1 {
            var j = i * i
            while j <= limit {
                DATA[j] = 0
                j = j + i
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Collect primes into PRIMES array
    var count = 0
    i = 2
    while i <= limit {
        if DATA[i] == 1 {
            PRIMES[count] = i
            count = count + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return count
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pass = 0
    var total = 0

    // TEST 1: Fibonacci
    print("=== TEST 1: Fibonacci ===\n")
    var f20 = fib(20)
    print("fib(20) = ")
    print_int(f20)
    print("\n")
    total = total + 1
    if f20 == 6765 { pass = pass + 1; print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }

    // TEST 2: GCD
    print("\n=== TEST 2: GCD ===\n")
    var g1 = gcd(48, 18)
    var g2 = gcd(1071, 462)
    print("gcd(48,18) = ")
    print_int(g1)
    print("\ngcd(1071,462) = ")
    print_int(g2)
    print("\n")
    total = total + 1
    if g1 == 6 { pass = pass + 1; print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }
    total = total + 1
    if g2 == 21 { pass = pass + 1; print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }

    // TEST 3: Collatz
    print("\n=== TEST 3: Collatz ===\n")
    var c27 = collatz_steps(27)
    var c1000 = collatz_steps(1000)
    print("collatz(27) = ")
    print_int(c27)
    print(" steps\ncollatz(1000) = ")
    print_int(c1000)
    print(" steps\n")
    total = total + 1
    if c27 == 111 { pass = pass + 1; print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }
    total = total + 1
    if c1000 == 111 { pass = pass + 1; print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }

    // TEST 4: Sieve of Eratosthenes (primes up to 10000)
    print("\n=== TEST 4: Sieve (primes to 10000) ===\n")
    var nprimes = sieve_primes(9999)
    print("Primes found: ")
    print_int(nprimes)
    print("\nFirst 5: ")
    print_int(PRIMES[0])
    print(", ")
    print_int(PRIMES[1])
    print(", ")
    print_int(PRIMES[2])
    print(", ")
    print_int(PRIMES[3])
    print(", ")
    print_int(PRIMES[4])
    print("\nLast: ")
    print_int(PRIMES[nprimes - 1])
    print("\n")
    total = total + 1
    if nprimes == 1229 { pass = pass + 1; print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }

    // TEST 5: Quicksort 10000
    print("\n=== TEST 5: Quicksort 10,000 ===\n")
    var seed = 42
    var i = 0
    while i < 10000 {
        seed = ((seed * 1103515245) + 12345)
        DATA[i] = seed
        i = i + 1
    }
    qsort(0, 9999)
    var sorted = 1
    i = 1
    while i < 10000 {
        if DATA[i] < DATA[i - 1] { sorted = 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    total = total + 1
    if sorted == 1 {
        print("Quicksort 10,000: PASS\n")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        print("Quicksort 10,000: FAIL\n")
    }

    // SUMMARY
    print("\n=============================\n")
    print_int(pass)
    print(" / ")
    print_int(total)
    print(" tests passed\n")
    if pass == total { print("ALL PASS\n") } else { print("SOME FAILED\n") }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/mandelbrot.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! Mandelbrot Set: ASCII render at 80×40 resolution
//!
//! Demonstrates: f64 arithmetic, nested loops, complex iteration,
//! character output — zero external dependencies.
//!
//! Outputs a text-art rendering of the Mandelbrot set.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/mandelbrot.sio

const WIDTH: i64 = 78
const HEIGHT: i64 = 36
const MAX_ITER: i64 = 64

// Compute Mandelbrot escape count for point (cx, cy)
fn mandelbrot(cx: f64, cy: f64) -> i64 {
    var zx: f64 = 0.0
    var zy: f64 = 0.0
    var iter: i64 = 0
    while iter < MAX_ITER {
        let zx2 = zx * zx
        let zy2 = zy * zy
        if zx2 + zy2 > 4.0 {
            return iter
        }
        let new_zx = zx2 - zy2 + cx
        zy = 2.0 * zx * zy + cy
        zx = new_zx
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    MAX_ITER
}

// Map escape count to ASCII character
fn iter_to_char(n: i64) -> i64 {
    if n == MAX_ITER { return 64 }   // '@' = 64
    if n > 48 { return 35 }          // '#' = 35
    if n > 32 { return 43 }          // '+' = 43
    if n > 16 { return 46 }          // '.' = 46
    if n > 8  { return 58 }          // ':' = 58
    32                                // ' ' = 32
}

fn print_char(c: i64) with IO {
    if c == 64 { print("@") }
    else if c == 35 { print("#") }
    else if c == 43 { print("+") }
    else if c == 46 { print(".") }
    else if c == 58 { print(":") }
    else { print(" ") }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    print("Mandelbrot Set (")
    print_int(WIDTH)
    print("x")
    print_int(HEIGHT)
    print(", max_iter=")
    print_int(MAX_ITER)
    print(")\n")
    print("Region: x in [-2.5, 1.0], y in [-1.2, 1.2]\n\n")

    let x_min: f64 = -2.5
    let x_max: f64 =  1.0
    let y_min: f64 = -1.2
    let y_max: f64 =  1.2

    var row: i64 = 0
    while row < HEIGHT {
        let cy = y_max - (y_max - y_min) * (row as f64) / (HEIGHT as f64)
        var col: i64 = 0
        while col < WIDTH {
            let cx = x_min + (x_max - x_min) * (col as f64) / (WIDTH as f64)
            let n = mandelbrot(cx, cy)
            print_char(iter_to_char(n))
            col = col + 1
        }
        print("\n")
        row = row + 1
    }

    // Count pixels in the set (escape == MAX_ITER)
    var in_set: i64 = 0
    row = 0
    while row < HEIGHT {
        let cy = y_max - (y_max - y_min) * (row as f64) / (HEIGHT as f64)
        var col: i64 = 0
        while col < WIDTH {
            let cx = x_min + (x_max - x_min) * (col as f64) / (WIDTH as f64)
            if mandelbrot(cx, cy) == MAX_ITER { in_set = in_set + 1 }
            col = col + 1
        }
        row = row + 1
    }

    print("\nPixels in Mandelbrot set: ")
    println(in_set)
    print("Total pixels: ")
    println(WIDTH * HEIGHT)

    0
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/matrix_mul.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! Dense Matrix Multiplication: 64×64 matrices (262,144 multiply-add ops)
//!
//! Demonstrates: high-throughput f64 computation, struct arrays, O(n³) loop,
//! numerical verification — zero external dependencies.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/matrix_mul.sio

const DIM: i64 = 64   // matrix dimension (DIM × DIM)

struct Matrix {
    m: [f64; 4096],    // DIM * DIM = 64 * 64 = 4096
}

fn mat_get(mat: &! Matrix, row: i64, col: i64) -> f64 with Mut {
    mat.m[row * DIM + col]
}

fn mat_set(mat: &! Matrix, row: i64, col: i64, val: f64) with Mut {
    mat.m[row * DIM + col] = val
}

// Initialize: A[i][j] = (i + j + 1) as f64 / DIM
fn mat_init_a(mat: &! Matrix) with Mut, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < DIM {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < DIM {
            let v = (i + j + 1) as f64 / (DIM as f64)
            mat_set(mat, i, j, v)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Initialize: B[i][j] = (i * j + 1) as f64 / (DIM * DIM)
fn mat_init_b(mat: &! Matrix) with Mut, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < DIM {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < DIM {
            let v = (i * j + 1) as f64 / (DIM * DIM) as f64
            mat_set(mat, i, j, v)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// C = A × B  (standard O(n³) multiply)
fn mat_mul(a: &! Matrix, b: &! Matrix, c: &! Matrix) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < DIM {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < DIM {
            var sum: f64 = 0.0
            var k: i64 = 0
            while k < DIM {
                sum = sum + mat_get(a, i, k) * mat_get(b, k, j)
                k = k + 1
            }
            mat_set(c, i, j, sum)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Frobenius norm: sqrt(sum of squares) — we return sum-of-squares to avoid FFI
fn frobenius_sq(mat: &! Matrix) -> f64 with Mut {
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < DIM * DIM {
        s = s + mat.m[i] * mat.m[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    s
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div {
    var a = Matrix { m: [0.0; 4096] }
    var b = Matrix { m: [0.0; 4096] }
    var c = Matrix { m: [0.0; 4096] }

    mat_init_a(&! a)
    mat_init_b(&! b)
    mat_mul(&! a, &! b, &! c)

    // Spot-check: C[0][0] = sum_k A[0][k] * B[k][0]
    //   A[0][k] = (0 + k + 1) / 64 = (k+1)/64
    //   B[k][0] = (k * 0 + 1) / 4096 = 1/4096
    //   C[0][0] = sum_{k=0}^{63} (k+1)/64 * 1/4096
    //           = (1/64)(1/4096) * sum_{k=0}^{63}(k+1)
    //           = (1/262144) * (64*65/2) = 2080/262144 = 0.007934570...
    let c00 = mat_get(&! c, 0, 0)

    // C[1][1] spot-check
    let c11 = mat_get(&! c, 1, 1)

    // Frobenius norm squared
    let fnorm_sq = frobenius_sq(&! c)

    print("Matrix multiplication ")
    print_int(DIM)
    print("x")
    print_int(DIM)
    print(": done\n")
    print("  Operations: ")
    println(DIM * DIM * DIM)
    print("  C[0][0] = ")
    println(c00)
    print("  C[1][1] = ")
    println(c11)
    print("  ||C||^2 = ")
    println(fnorm_sq)

    // Verify C[0][0] ≈ 0.007934 (check it's positive and reasonable)
    let ok = c00 > 0.007 && c00 < 0.009 && c11 > 0.0 && fnorm_sq > 0.0
    if ok {
        print("Verification: PASS\n")
        0
    } else {
        print("Verification: FAIL\n")
        1
    }
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/quicksort.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! Quicksort: in-place sort of 10,000 integers
//!
//! Demonstrates: real algorithms, mutable struct refs, LCG pseudo-random data,
//! verification pass, O(n log n) on 10K elements.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/quicksort.sio

struct SortBuf {
    data: [i64; 10000],
}

fn swap(arr: &! SortBuf, i: i64, j: i64) with Mut {
    let tmp = arr.data[i]
    arr.data[i] = arr.data[j]
    arr.data[j] = tmp
}

// Lomuto partition — median-of-three pivot for better performance
fn median3(arr: &! SortBuf, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
    // Sort lo, mid, hi and use mid as pivot
    if arr.data[lo] > arr.data[mid] { swap(arr, lo, mid) }
    if arr.data[lo] > arr.data[hi]  { swap(arr, lo, hi)  }
    if arr.data[mid] > arr.data[hi] { swap(arr, mid, hi) }
    mid
}

fn partition(arr: &! SortBuf, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    let pivot_idx = median3(arr, lo, hi)
    let pivot = arr.data[pivot_idx]
    // Move pivot to end
    swap(arr, pivot_idx, hi)
    var i = lo - 1
    var j = lo
    while j < hi {
        if arr.data[j] <= pivot {
            i = i + 1
            swap(arr, i, j)
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    swap(arr, i + 1, hi)
    i + 1
}

fn qsort(arr: &! SortBuf, lo: i64, hi: i64) with Mut {
    if lo < hi {
        let p = partition(arr, lo, hi)
        qsort(arr, lo, p - 1)
        qsort(arr, p + 1, hi)
    }
}

fn abs64(x: i64) -> i64 {
    if x < 0 { 0 - x } else { x }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    var buf = SortBuf { data: [0; 10000] }
    let n: i64 = 10000

    // Fill with LCG pseudo-random values (Knuth multiplicative)
    var seed: i64 = 6364136223846793005
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        seed = seed * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
        buf.data[i] = seed
        i = i + 1
    }

    let first_before = buf.data[0]

    qsort(&! buf, 0, n - 1)

    // Verify sorted
    var sorted = true
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        if buf.data[i] < buf.data[i - 1] { sorted = false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if sorted {
        print("Quicksort (10,000 integers): PASS\n")
        print("  min = ")
        println(buf.data[0])
        print("  max = ")
        println(buf.data[n - 1])
        print("  unsorted[0] was: ")
        println(first_before)
        0
    } else {
        print("FAIL: sort verification failed\n")
        1
    }
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/radix_sort.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! Radix Sort (LSD, base-256) on 100,000 integers
//!
//! Demonstrates: O(kn) linear sorting, large buffers (1.6MB struct),
//! multi-pass counting sort, data structure manipulation at scale.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/radix_sort.sio

const N: i64 = 100000

struct RadixBufs {
    data:   [i64; 100000],
    output: [i64; 100000],
    count:  [i64; 256],
}

// Counting sort on one byte extracted by dividing by `divisor`
// divisor: 1 (byte0), 256 (byte1), 65536 (byte2), 16777216 (byte3)
fn counting_sort(b: &! RadixBufs, divisor: i64, n: i64) with Mut, Div {
    // Clear counts
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 256 {
        b.count[k] = 0
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Count occurrences of each byte value
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let byte_val = (b.data[i] / divisor) & 255
        b.count[byte_val] = b.count[byte_val] + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Prefix sums (cumulative counts → starting positions)
    var prev: i64 = 0
    k = 0
    while k < 256 {
        let c = b.count[k]
        b.count[k] = prev
        prev = prev + c
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Place elements in output
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let byte_val = (b.data[i] / divisor) & 255
        let pos = b.count[byte_val]
        b.output[pos] = b.data[i]
        b.count[byte_val] = pos + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Copy output back to data
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        b.data[i] = b.output[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn radix_sort(b: &! RadixBufs, n: i64) with Mut, Div {
    // 4 passes: bytes 0,1,2,3 of the lower 32 bits
    counting_sort(b, 1,        n)   // byte 0: value & 255
    counting_sort(b, 256,      n)   // byte 1: (value / 256) & 255
    counting_sort(b, 65536,    n)   // byte 2: (value / 65536) & 255
    counting_sort(b, 16777216, n)   // byte 3: (value / 16777216) & 255
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div {
    var bufs = RadixBufs {
        data:   [0; 100000],
        output: [0; 100000],
        count:  [0; 256],
    }

    // Fill with positive pseudo-random values in [0, 2^31 - 1]
    var seed: i64 = 987654321
    var i: i64 = 0
    var checksum_before: i64 = 0
    while i < N {
        seed = seed * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
        // Keep positive: take abs and mask to 31 bits
        var v = seed
        if v < 0 { v = 0 - v }
        v = v & 2147483647   // mask to [0, 2^31-1]
        bufs.data[i] = v
        checksum_before = checksum_before + v
        i = i + 1
    }

    let first_unsorted = bufs.data[0]
    let second_unsorted = bufs.data[1]

    radix_sort(&! bufs, N)

    // Verify sorted
    var ok = true
    i = 1
    while i < N {
        if bufs.data[i] < bufs.data[i - 1] { ok = false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Verify checksum preserved
    var checksum_after: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < N {
        checksum_after = checksum_after + bufs.data[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    if ok && checksum_before == checksum_after {
        print("Radix sort (100,000 integers): PASS\n")
        print("  Input[0,1]: ")
        println(first_unsorted)
        println(second_unsorted)
        print("  Sorted min: ")
        println(bufs.data[0])
        print("  Sorted max: ")
        println(bufs.data[N - 1])
        print("  Checksum:   ")
        println(checksum_after)
        0
    } else if ok == false {
        print("FAIL: sort order wrong\n")
        1
    } else {
        print("FAIL: checksum mismatch\n")
        2
    }
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/sieve.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! Sieve of Eratosthenes: find all primes up to 100,000
//!
//! Demonstrates: O(n log log n) algorithm, large arrays, nested loops,
//! counting and searching.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/sieve.sio

struct SieveBuf {
    is_prime: [i32; 100001],
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    var s = SieveBuf { is_prime: [1; 100001] }
    let limit: i64 = 100000

    // 0 and 1 are not prime
    s.is_prime[0] = 0
    s.is_prime[1] = 0

    // Sieve: mark composites
    var i: i64 = 2
    while i * i <= limit {
        if s.is_prime[i] == 1 {
            var j = i * i
            while j <= limit {
                s.is_prime[j] = 0
                j = j + i
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Count primes and find largest
    var count: i64 = 0
    var largest: i64 = 0
    i = 2
    while i <= limit {
        if s.is_prime[i] == 1 {
            count = count + 1
            largest = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Print first 10 primes
    print("First 10 primes: ")
    var printed: i64 = 0
    i = 2
    while i <= limit && printed < 10 {
        if s.is_prime[i] == 1 {
            if printed > 0 { print(", ") }
            print_int(i)
            printed = printed + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    print("\n")

    print("Primes up to 100,000: ")
    println(count)
    print("Largest prime: ")
    println(largest)

    // Verify known count (9592 primes up to 100000)
    if count == 9592 {
        print("Count verified: PASS\n")
        0
    } else {
        print("Count mismatch: FAIL\n")
        1
    }
}


// === FILE: examples/alpha_geo_zero.sio ===
/*
Aspirational example preserved below.
To restore, remove this stub and uncomment the original content.

// AlphaGeoZero: Epistemic Geometry Theorem Proving in Sounio
//
// This example demonstrates the full self-play loop for geometry theorem proving
// with epistemic MCTS, variance-driven curriculum, and IMO-AG-30 benchmark evaluation.
//
// Key innovations:
// 1. Beta-distributed Q-values for principled uncertainty quantification
// 2. PUCT with epistemic ignorance bonus (explore what you don't know)
// 3. Variance penalty in training loss (honest confidence predictions)
// 4. Solve rate as Beta posterior (quantified trust in performance)

// =============================================================================
// Core Types with Epistemic Semantics
// =============================================================================

/// A geometric point with epistemic coordinates
struct Point {
    name: string,
    x: Knowledge<f64>,  // x-coordinate with confidence
    y: Knowledge<f64>,  // y-coordinate with confidence
}

/// Geometric predicates with full epistemic tracking
enum PredicateKind {
    Collinear,      // Points A, B, C lie on a line
    Parallel,       // Lines AB || CD
    Perpendicular,  // Lines AB ⊥ CD
    EqualLength,    // |AB| = |CD|
    Midpoint,       // M is midpoint of AB
    OnCircle,       // Point P lies on circle with center O
    Congruent,      // Triangles ABC ≅ DEF
    Similar,        // Triangles ABC ~ DEF
    Cyclic,         // Points lie on a circle
}

/// A predicate is Knowledge<fact> - carries mean, variance, provenance
struct Predicate {
    kind: PredicateKind,
    args: [string],
    epistemic: EpistemicStatus,  // Beta confidence + Merkle provenance
}

/// Proof state: all known predicates with epistemic status
struct ProofState {
    points: Map<string, Point>,
    predicates: Map<string, Predicate>,
    goal: Option<Predicate>,
    constructions: [Construction],
}

// =============================================================================
// Epistemic MCTS for Proof Search
// =============================================================================

/// MCTS node with Beta-distributed value estimation
struct EpistemicMCTSNode {
    state: ProofState,
    action: Option<GeoAction>,
    parent: Option<NodeId>,
    children: [NodeId],

    // Epistemic value estimation
    prior: f64,                    // Neural network prior π(a|s)
    value_beta: BetaConfidence,    // Value as Beta(α, β) distribution
    visits: u32,
    total_value: f64,

    // Provenance
    provenance_hash: u64,
}

impl EpistemicMCTSNode {
    /// PUCT score with epistemic ignorance bonus
    ///
    /// UCB(s, a) = Q(s,a) + c_puct * P(a|s) * sqrt(N(s)) / (1 + N(s,a))
    ///           + c_ignorance * sqrt(Var(Q))
    ///
    /// High variance = "I don't know" → explore more (active inference)
    fn puct_score(self, parent_visits: u32, config: &MCTSConfig) -> f64 {
        let q = self.q_value()
        let exploration = config.c_puct * self.prior * sqrt(parent_visits as f64)
                        / (1.0 + self.visits as f64)

        // Epistemic ignorance bonus - KEY INNOVATION
        let ignorance_bonus = if config.use_variance_bonus {
            config.c_ignorance * sqrt(self.value_beta.variance())
        } else {
            0.0
        }

        q + exploration + ignorance_bonus
    }

    /// Update value with Bayesian posterior
    fn update_value(self: &!Self, value: f64) {
        self.visits += 1
        self.total_value += value

        // Conjugate Beta update
        let alpha_update = max(0.0, min(1.0, value))
        let beta_update = max(0.0, min(1.0, 1.0 - value))

        self.value_beta = BetaConfidence::new(
            self.value_beta.alpha + alpha_update,
            self.value_beta.beta + beta_update
        )
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Geometry Actions
// =============================================================================

/// Actions in the geometry proof game
enum GeoAction {
    /// Run symbolic deduction (forward chaining)
    DeductionStep,

    /// Add auxiliary construction (neural-suggested)
    Construct(Construction),

    /// Request neural suggestion (triggers NeSy effect)
    RequestNeural,

    /// Terminate search
    Terminate,
}

/// Auxiliary constructions (the "magic" of geometry proofs)
enum Construction {
    Midpoint { p1: string, p2: string },
    Perpendicular { point: string, line_p1: string, line_p2: string },
    Circumcircle { p1: string, p2: string, p3: string },
    AngleBisector { p1: string, vertex: string, p2: string },
    LineIntersection { l1_p1: string, l1_p2: string, l2_p1: string, l2_p2: string },
}

// =============================================================================
// Self-Play Training Loop
// =============================================================================

/// Training configuration with variance penalty
struct TrainingConfig {
    learning_rate: f64,
    batch_size: usize,
    policy_weight: f64,
    value_weight: f64,
    variance_penalty: f64,  // λ in loss - penalize overconfident wrong predictions
}

/// Training step with variance penalty loss
///
/// Loss = L_policy + L_value + λ * Var(value)
///
/// The variance penalty encourages honest predictions:
/// - If you're wrong, better to be uncertain than confidently wrong
/// - Network learns to output high variance when it doesn't know
fn train_step(
    network: &!NeuralNetwork,
    examples: [TrainingExample],
    config: TrainingConfig
) -> TrainingResult with Neural, Grad {
    var total_policy_loss = 0.0
    var total_value_loss = 0.0
    var total_variance_penalty = 0.0

    for example in examples {
        // Forward pass
        let (pred_policy, pred_value) = network.forward(example.features)

        // Policy cross-entropy loss
        let policy_loss = cross_entropy(pred_policy, example.target_policy)

        // Value MSE loss
        let value_loss = mse(pred_value, example.target_value)

        // Variance penalty - KEY INNOVATION
        // High variance when wrong is acceptable; high variance when right is suboptimal
        let variance_penalty = example.value_variance * config.variance_penalty

        total_policy_loss += policy_loss * example.weight
        total_value_loss += value_loss * example.weight
        total_variance_penalty += variance_penalty
    }

    let total_loss = config.policy_weight * total_policy_loss
                   + config.value_weight * total_value_loss
                   + total_variance_penalty

    // Backprop
    network.backward(total_loss)
    network.step(config.learning_rate)

    TrainingResult {
        total_loss,
        policy_loss: total_policy_loss,
        value_loss: total_value_loss,
        variance_penalty: total_variance_penalty
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// IMO-AG-30 Benchmark

/// An IMO geometry problem
struct IMOProblem {
    id: string,
    name: string,
    year: u32,
    problem_num: u32,
    initial_state: ProofState,
    goal: Predicate,
    difficulty: f64,  // 0-1 estimated difficulty
}

/// Benchmark result with epistemic posterior
struct BenchmarkResult {
    problem_id: string,
    solved: bool,
    time_taken: Duration,
    constructions: usize,
    confidence: Option<BetaConfidence>,  // How confident in the proof
    proof_text: Option<string>,
}

/// Aggregate statistics with Beta posterior on solve rate
struct BenchmarkStats {
    total_problems: usize,
    solved: usize,

    // Solve rate as Beta posterior - KEY INNOVATION
    // Not just "73% solved" but "73% ± 8% with 95% credible interval"
    solve_rate_posterior: BetaConfidence,

    avg_time: Duration,
    avg_constructions: f64,
    results: [BenchmarkResult],
}

/// Run the IMO-AG-30 benchmark with epistemic tracking
fn run_imo_benchmark(
    network: &NeuralNetwork,
    config: BenchmarkConfig
) -> BenchmarkStats with IO, Neural {
    let problems = imo_ag_30()  // Load all 30 problems
    var stats = BenchmarkStats::new()

    // Prior: Start with uniform Beta(1,1) = "I know nothing"
    var solve_rate_beta = BetaConfidence::uniform_prior()

    for problem in problems {
        print(f"Attempting: {problem.id} ({problem.name})...")

        let start = now()
        let result = solve_problem(problem, network, config)
        let elapsed = now() - start

        // Bayesian update of solve rate posterior
        if result.solved {
            solve_rate_beta = solve_rate_beta.observe_success()
            print(f"  [SOLVED] in {elapsed}s")
        } else {
            solve_rate_beta = solve_rate_beta.observe_failure()
            print(f"  [FAILED] in {elapsed}s")
        }

        stats.add_result(result)
    }

    stats.solve_rate_posterior = solve_rate_beta

    // Print epistemic summary
    let mean = solve_rate_beta.mean()
    let std = sqrt(solve_rate_beta.variance())
    let (lo, hi) = solve_rate_beta.credible_interval(0.95)

    print(f"\n=== IMO-AG-30 Results ===")
    print(f"Solved: {stats.solved}/{stats.total_problems}")
    print(f"Solve rate: {mean*100:.1}% ± {std*100:.1}%")
    print(f"95% credible interval: [{lo*100:.1}%, {hi*100:.1}%]")
    print(f"AlphaGeometry baseline: 83% (25/30)")

    if mean > 0.83 {
        print("Status: EXCEEDS AlphaGeometry!")
    } else if hi > 0.83 {
        print("Status: Competitive (baseline within credible interval)")
    } else {
        print("Status: Below baseline (more training needed)")
    }

    stats
}

// =============================================================================
// Variance-Priority Replay Buffer
// =============================================================================

/// Replay buffer that prioritizes high-variance (uncertain) examples
///
/// Curriculum learning based on epistemic uncertainty:
/// - Problems where model is uncertain get more training
/// - Natural progression from easy → hard problems
struct VariancePriorityBuffer {
    episodes: [ProofGameEpisode],
    priorities: [f64],
    max_size: usize,
    alpha: f64,  // Priority exponent (higher = more focus on high variance)
}

impl VariancePriorityBuffer {
    /// Add episode with variance-based priority
    fn add(self: &!Self, episode: ProofGameEpisode) {
        // Priority = average variance (higher variance = more priority)
        let avg_variance = episode.total_variance / max(1, episode.length) as f64
        let priority = pow(avg_variance + 0.01, self.alpha)

        if self.episodes.len() >= self.max_size {
            // Remove lowest priority episode
            let min_idx = self.priorities.argmin()
            self.episodes.remove(min_idx)
            self.priorities.remove(min_idx)
        }

        self.episodes.push(episode)
        self.priorities.push(priority)
    }

    /// Sample batch with priority weighting
    fn sample(self, batch_size: usize) -> [(ProofGameEpisode, f64)] {
        let total_priority = self.priorities.sum()
        var samples = []

        for _ in 0..min(batch_size, self.episodes.len()) {
            // Weighted random sampling
            let threshold = random() * total_priority
            var cumsum = 0.0

            for (i, p) in self.priorities.enumerate() {
                cumsum += p
                if cumsum >= threshold {
                    // Importance sampling weight
                    let prob = p / total_priority
                    let weight = pow(1.0 / (self.episodes.len() as f64 * prob), self.beta)
                    samples.push((self.episodes[i], weight))
                    break
                }
            }
        }

        samples
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Full Self-Play Loop
// =============================================================================

/// The complete AlphaGeoZero training loop
fn alpha_geo_zero_loop(
    network: &!NeuralNetwork,
    config: LoopConfig
) -> LoopStats with IO, Neural, Grad {
    var buffer = VariancePriorityBuffer::new(config.buffer_size)
    var curriculum = ProblemCurriculum::new(imo_ag_30())
    var stats = LoopStats::new()

    for iteration in 0..config.total_iterations {
        // ========== Self-Play Phase ==========
        for _ in 0..config.games_per_iteration {
            // Sample problem based on difficulty/variance curriculum
            let problem = curriculum.sample()

            // Generate proof game episode with MCTS
            let episode = generate_proof_game(
                problem.initial_state,
                problem.goal,
                network,
                config.mcts_config
            )

            // Update curriculum difficulty based on result
            let variance = episode.total_variance / max(1, episode.length) as f64
            curriculum.update(problem.id, variance, episode.proved)

            // Add to variance-priority buffer
            buffer.add(episode)

            stats.record_episode(episode)
        }

        // ========== Training Phase ==========
        for _ in 0..config.training_steps_per_iteration {
            let batch = buffer.sample(config.batch_size)
            let result = train_step(network, batch, config.training_config)
            stats.record_training(result)
        }

        // ========== Evaluation Phase ==========
        if iteration % config.eval_interval == 0 {
            let benchmark = run_imo_benchmark(network, config.benchmark_config)
            stats.record_benchmark(benchmark)

            print(f"Iteration {iteration}: {benchmark.solve_rate_posterior.mean()*100:.1}% solve rate")
        }

        // ========== Checkpoint ==========
        if iteration % config.checkpoint_interval == 0 {
            network.save(f"checkpoints/alpha_geo_zero_{iteration}.pt")
        }
    }

    stats
}

/// Prove: If M is midpoint of AB and N is midpoint of AC, then MN || BC
fn prove_midpoint_theorem() -> ProofGameEpisode with Geometry, Neural {
    // Setup
    var state = ProofState::new()
    state.add_points(["A", "B", "C", "M", "N"])
    state.add_axiom(Predicate::midpoint("M", "A", "B"))
    state.add_axiom(Predicate::midpoint("N", "A", "C"))

    let goal = Predicate::parallel("M", "N", "B", "C")

    // Create proof game
    let game = GeoProofGame::for_goal(state, goal, 0.9)

    // Run MCTS search with epistemic exploration
    let config = MCTSConfig {
        num_simulations: 800,
        c_puct: 1.5,
        c_ignorance: 0.5,  // Epistemic bonus
        use_variance_bonus: true,
        temperature: 1.0,
    }

    var tree = EpistemicMCTSTree::new(game, config)
    tree.search(UniformNetwork::new())  // Or trained network

    // Extract best proof
    let action = tree.select_action()
    let value_posterior = tree.root_value()  // Beta distribution

    print(f"Proof value: {value_posterior.mean():.3} ± {sqrt(value_posterior.variance()):.3}")

    // ... continue until terminal
}

struct Sample {
    value: i64
}

fn scale(item: Sample, factor: i64) -> Sample {
    return Sample { value: item.value * factor }
}

fn checksum(values: [i64]) -> i64 {
    var sum: i64 = 0
    for v in values {
        sum = sum + v
    }
    return sum
}

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Exp 3: Subject-stratified mixed-effects re-analysis of α
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
//
// Data: 7 CHB-MIT subjects. Metric: h_sep = ||h_II − h_IC|| (S-SSM, α sweep).
// Generated by scripts/research/alpha_hierarchical_analysis.py.
//
// ── What Door III claimed ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
//   α=0.20 is the interior population optimum (from MSE ratio on chb03).
//
// ── What this analysis finds ─────────────────────────────────────────────
//   Individual optima (α* = argmax_α h_sep per subject):
//     chb01: α*=0.05  chb02: α*=0.05  chb03: α*=0.50
//     chb05: α*=0.30  chb06: α*=0.80  chb08: α*=0.80  chb11: α*=0.80
//
//   Population model:  α*_i ~ Normal(μ, σ²)  (hierarchical random slopes)
//   Posterior (conjugate):  μ̂=0.471  σ̂=0.344  95% CI=[0.153, 0.789]
//   P(μ ∈ [0.18, 0.22]) = 0.0175   (α=0.20 is unlikely as population mean)
//
//   ZERO subjects have α*=0.20 as their individual optimum.
//   SD of individual optima: 0.344 — strongly heterogeneous.
//
// ── Corrections required ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
//   1. "α=0.20 is the population optimum" → RETRACT.
//      The MSE ratio and h_sep disagree on chb03 itself (h_sep peaks at 0.50).
//      The pooled h_sep optimum is 0.80, not 0.20.
//   2. "α should be fixed at 0.20" → REPLACE with: α is patient-specific.
//      Deploy with per-subject α tuning or treat as a nuisance parameter.
//   3. The individual landscape is BIMODAL:
//      - Small-α group (chb01, chb02): flat landscape, α ≤ 0.05 marginally best
//      - Large-α group (chb06, chb08, chb11): monotone increasing, α=0.80 best
//      - Medium-α (chb03, chb05): interior peaks at 0.50 / 0.30
//      This bimodality may reflect seizure type, not model sensitivity.

// ─── Per-subject h_sep data ───────────────────────────────────────────────
// Columns: hsep at α = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, 0.80
// Row 0=chb01, 1=chb02, 2=chb03, 3=chb05, 4=chb06, 5=chb08, 6=chb11

var HSEP: [f64; 49] = [0.0; 49]   // 7 subjects × 7 alpha values
var ALPHA_OPT: [f64; 7] = [0.0; 7]  // per-subject argmax alpha

fn load_data() with Mut {
    // chb01: α*=0.05
    HSEP[ 0]=0.820472; HSEP[ 1]=0.816917; HSEP[ 2]=0.815108; HSEP[ 3]=0.812488

// Alpha grid values
fn alpha_at(j: i64) -> f64 {
    if j==0 { 0.05 } else if j==1 { 0.10 } else if j==2 { 0.15 }
    else if j==3 { 0.20 } else if j==4 { 0.30 } else if j==5 { 0.50 }
    else { 0.80 }
}

// Posterior statistics (from generator output)
fn MU_HAT()       -> f64 { 0.4714 }
fn SIGMA_HAT()    -> f64 { 0.3438 }
fn CI_LO()        -> f64 { 0.1534 }
fn CI_HI()        -> f64 { 0.7894 }
fn P_AT_020()     -> f64 { 0.0175 }   // P(μ ∈ [0.18,0.22])

// ─── Math helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn abs_f(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn print_i(v: i64) with IO, Mut {
    if v < 0 { print("-"); print_i(0 - v); return }
    if v >= 10 { print_i(v / 10) }
    let d = v % 10
    if d==0{print("0")}if d==1{print("1")}if d==2{print("2")}if d==3{print("3")}
    if d==4{print("4")}if d==5{print("5")}if d==6{print("6")}if d==7{print("7")}
    if d==8{print("8")}if d==9{print("9")}
}

fn print_f3(v: f64) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if v < 0.0 { print("-"); print_f3(0.0 - v); return }
    let iv: i64 = v as i64
    print_i(iv); print(".")
    let d1: i64 = ((v - (iv as f64)) * 10.0) as i64
    let d2: i64 = ((v - (iv as f64)) * 100.0) as i64 % 10
    let d3: i64 = ((v - (iv as f64)) * 1000.0) as i64 % 10
    print_i(d1); print_i(d2); print_i(d3)
}

// ─── Assertions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    load_data()
    let N_SUBJ: i64 = 7

    print("=== Exp 3: Subject-stratified α re-analysis ===\n\n")

    // ── Print per-subject optimal α ───────────────────────────────────────
    print("Individual optima (α* = argmax h_sep):\n")
    let subj_names: [string; 7] = ["chb01","chb02","chb03","chb05","chb06","chb08","chb11"]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < N_SUBJ {
        print("  "); print(subj_names[i as usize])
        print(": α*="); print_f3(ALPHA_OPT[i as usize])
        print("\n")
        i = i + 1
    }

    // ── T1: No subject has α*=0.20 ────────────────────────────────────────
    print("\nT1 No subject has α*=0.20 (the Door III claim):\n")
    var n_at_020: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < N_SUBJ {
        let diff = abs_f(ALPHA_OPT[i as usize] - 0.20)
        if diff < 0.001 { n_at_020 = n_at_020 + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    print("  Subjects with α*=0.20: "); print_i(n_at_020); print("/7\n")
    assert(n_at_020 == 0)   // RETRACTION: α=0.20 is nobody's individual optimum

    // ── T2: Strong heterogeneity σ̂ > 0.25 ────────────────────────────────
    print("T2 Individual optima are heterogeneous (σ̂ > 0.25):\n")
    print("  σ̂ = "); print_f3(SIGMA_HAT()); print("\n")
    assert(SIGMA_HAT() > 0.25)   // heterogeneous — α is patient-specific

    // ── T3: Population mean μ̂ ≠ 0.20 ─────────────────────────────────────
    print("T3 Population mean μ̂ far from 0.20:\n")
    print("  μ̂ = "); print_f3(MU_HAT())
    print("  (claim was 0.20, diff="); print_f3(abs_f(MU_HAT() - 0.20)); print(")\n")
    assert(abs_f(MU_HAT() - 0.20) > 0.20)   // μ̂=0.471, more than 0.20 away

    // ── T4: P(μ ∈ [0.18,0.22]) is very small ─────────────────────────────
    print("T4 P(μ ∈ [0.18,0.22]) very small (Door III's claim region):\n")
    print("  P = "); print_f3(P_AT_020()); print("  (< 0.05)\n")
    assert(P_AT_020() < 0.05)   // Door III's specific claim poorly supported

    // ── T5: Bimodal structure — small-α and large-α clusters ─────────────
    // Count subjects with α* ≤ 0.15 (small group) and α* ≥ 0.50 (large group)
    print("T5 Bimodal distribution — two subgroups:\n")
    var n_small: i64 = 0   // chb01, chb02 (α*=0.05)
    var n_medium: i64 = 0  // chb03, chb05 (α*=0.30, 0.50)
    var n_large: i64 = 0   // chb06, chb08, chb11 (α*=0.80)
    i = 0
    while i < N_SUBJ {
        let a = ALPHA_OPT[i as usize]
        if a <= 0.15 { n_small = n_small + 1 }
        else if a <= 0.40 { n_medium = n_medium + 1 }
        else { n_large = n_large + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    print("  Small-α (≤0.15):   "); print_i(n_small); print(" subjects (flat landscape)\n")
    print("  Medium-α (0.20-0.40): "); print_i(n_medium); print(" subjects\n")
    print("  Large-α (≥0.50):   "); print_i(n_large); print(" subjects (monotone rising)\n")
    // Two dominant clusters: small (2) and large (3), medium (2)
    assert(n_small >= 2)
    assert(n_large >= 3)
    // No single cluster dominates — heterogeneous landscape confirmed
    assert(n_small + n_medium + n_large == 7)

    // ── T6: 95% CI for μ includes 0.20 but barely ─────────────────────────
    print("T6 95% CI for μ: ["); print_f3(CI_LO()); print(", "); print_f3(CI_HI())
    print("]\n")
    print("  Includes 0.20: ")
    let ci_includes_020 = CI_LO() <= 0.20 && 0.20 <= CI_HI()
    if ci_includes_020 { print("yes (barely — tail of distribution)\n") }
    else { print("no\n") }
    // 0.20 is within the wide CI (σ̂=0.34 makes CI very wide)
    // but this does NOT mean 0.20 is a good individual prescription
    assert(ci_includes_020)   // consistent but not individually prescriptive

    // ── T7: Pooled optimum is NOT 0.20 ────────────────────────────────────
    // Pooled h_sep at each α (mean across subjects)
    print("T7 Pooled h_sep: ")
    var pooled: [f64; 7] = [0.0; 7]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < 7 {
        var sum: f64 = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < N_SUBJ {
            sum = sum + HSEP[i * 7 + j]
            i = i + 1
        }
        pooled[j as usize] = sum / 7.0
        print_f3(pooled[j as usize]); print(" ")
        j = j + 1
    }
    print("\n")
    // Find pooled argmax
    var pooled_best_j: i64 = 0
    var pooled_best_v: f64 = pooled[0]
    j = 1
    while j < 7 {
        if pooled[j as usize] > pooled_best_v {
            pooled_best_v = pooled[j as usize]
            pooled_best_j = j
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    let pooled_best_alpha = alpha_at(pooled_best_j)
    print("  Pooled optimal α: "); print_f3(pooled_best_alpha); print("\n")
    // Pooled optimum is 0.80 (driven by chb06/08/11), not 0.20
    assert(abs_f(pooled_best_alpha - 0.20) > 0.10)

    print("\n=== Corrections ===\n")
    print("1. RETRACT: alpha=0.20 as population optimum\n")
    print("   0/7 subjects have alpha*=0.20; pooled opt=0.80\n")
    print("2. REPLACE: alpha is patient-specific (sigma=0.344)\n")
    print("3. BIMODAL: small-alpha (flat) vs large-alpha (rising) subgroups\n")
    print("   May reflect seizure type — needs clinical stratification\n")
    print("4. Door III metric (MSE ratio) vs h_sep disagree on chb03 itself\n")
    print("   Future work: report both metrics, clarify which drives the claim\n")

    print("\nALL PASS\n")
}

/*

// AlphaSounio: Self-Learning MCTS with Neural Effects
// Features:
//   - Neural policy/value network (simulated with linear approximation)
//   - Epistemic PUCT with confidence tracking
//   - Beta posterior updates for Bayesian value estimates
//   - Self-play training loop
//   - Uncertainty propagation across model updates
//
// Architecture following AlphaZero:
