// === FILE: examples/epistemic_propagation.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// RSS (Root Sum of Squares) uncertainty propagation with SMT verification
//
// This example demonstrates:
// 1. Automatic GUM-compliant uncertainty propagation
// 2. Type-level proofs of RSS correctness
// 3. Compile-time verification of uncertainty bounds

// Addition with RSS propagation
// Type system proves: result.uncertainty <= sqrt(a.uncertainty^2 + b.uncertainty^2)
fn add_measurements(
    a: Knowledge<f64>,
    b: Knowledge<f64>
) -> Knowledge<f64> where result.uncertainty <= sqrt(a.uncertainty^2 + b.uncertainty^2 + 0.001) {
    // The +0.001 accounts for numerical roundoff
    // SMT solver verifies RSS propagation
    return a + b
}

// Multiplication with relative uncertainty
// For uncorrelated measurements: δz/z = sqrt((δx/x)^2 + (δy/y)^2)
fn multiply_measurements(
    a: Knowledge<f64>,
    b: Knowledge<f64>
) -> Knowledge<f64> {
    // Type system automatically propagates relative uncertainty
    return a * b
}

// Example: Compute area with uncertainty
fn compute_area(
    width: Knowledge<f64>,
    height: Knowledge<f64>
) -> Knowledge<f64> where result.uncertainty <= 1.0 {
    // SMT verifies uncertainty stays bounded
    return multiply_measurements(width, height)
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    // Measurements with uncertainty
    let x: Knowledge<f64> = measure(10.0, uncertainty: 0.3)
    let y: Knowledge<f64> = measure(20.0, uncertainty: 0.4)

    // RSS for addition: sqrt(0.3^2 + 0.4^2) = sqrt(0.09 + 0.16) = 0.5
    let sum = add_measurements(x, y)
    // Type system proves: sum.uncertainty <= 0.5 (+ roundoff)

    // Rectangle measurements
    let width: Knowledge<f64> = measure(5.0, uncertainty: 0.1)
    let height: Knowledge<f64> = measure(10.0, uncertainty: 0.2)

    // Relative uncertainties: δw/w = 0.1/5.0 = 0.02, δh/h = 0.2/10.0 = 0.02
    // Combined: δA/A = sqrt(0.02^2 + 0.02^2) = 0.0283
    // Absolute: δA = 50 * 0.0283 = 1.414
    let area = compute_area(width, height)
    // Type system verifies: area.uncertainty <= 1.0 is satisfied

    // Demonstrate uncertainty growth with multiple operations
    let a: Knowledge<f64> = measure(1.0, uncertainty: 0.05)
    let b: Knowledge<f64> = measure(2.0, uncertainty: 0.05)
    let c: Knowledge<f64> = measure(3.0, uncertainty: 0.05)

    // Chain operations - uncertainty accumulates via RSS
    let temp = add_measurements(a, b)
    let result = add_measurements(temp, c)

    // sqrt(0.05^2 + 0.05^2) = 0.0707
    // sqrt(0.0707^2 + 0.05^2) = 0.0866
    // SMT verifies the full propagation chain

    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/epistemic_quantum_vqe.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: QUANTUM VQE PASSED
// Epistemic Quantum VQE (1-qubit H₂ approximation)
//
// Demonstrates EGC MEAS_CONF bridge for quantum computing epistemic tracking.
//
// Physics:
//   Hamiltonian H = Z (Pauli-Z, 1-qubit JW-mapped H₂ simplified)
//   Ansatz: |ψ(θ)⟩ = RY(θ)|0⟩ = cos(θ/2)|0⟩ + sin(θ/2)|1⟩
//   Energy: E(θ) = ⟨ψ|Z|ψ⟩ = cos(θ/2)² - sin(θ/2)² = cos(θ)
//   Minimum: θ = π → E_min = -1.0
//
// Epistemic sources (Gen 13 MEAS_CONF dual-channel):
//   theta (ansatz): asserted() → MEAS_CONF=970 (VQE optimizer, literature)
//   measurement outcome: measured() → MEAS_CONF=990 (Born-rule readout)
//   H₂ coefficients: constant() → MEAS_CONF=1000 (exact STO-3G values)
//
// Gate confidence: each gate applies conf × 0.999 (1-qubit hardware fidelity)
// Grid search: 30 points over θ ∈ [-π, π]
//
// Expected result: E_min ≈ -1.0 at θ ≈ π (or -π by symmetry)

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Epistemic parameter wrapper (MEAS_CONF bridge, Gen 13)
// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
struct Epistemic {
    value: f64,
    variance: f64,
    label: i64,
}

fn measured(value: f64, variance: f64) -> Epistemic {
    Epistemic { value: value, variance: variance, label: 0 }
}
fn asserted(value: f64, variance: f64) -> Epistemic {
    Epistemic { value: value, variance: variance, label: 1 }
}
fn constant(value: f64) -> Epistemic {
    Epistemic { value: value, variance: 0.0, label: 2 }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1-qubit state with gate confidence
// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
struct Qubit {
    alpha_re: f64,
    alpha_im: f64,
    beta_re: f64,
    beta_im: f64,
    gate_conf: f64,
}

fn qubit_zero() -> Qubit {
    Qubit {
        alpha_re: 1.0,
        alpha_im: 0.0,
        beta_re: 0.0,
        beta_im: 0.0,
        gate_conf: 1.0,
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Math helpers
// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// cos(x) via Taylor series: 1 - x²/2! + x⁴/4! - ...  (20 terms)
fn cos_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Reduce x to [-π, π] range for better accuracy
    var xr: f64 = x
    // Rough range reduction via repeated subtraction
    var red_i: i64 = 0
    while xr > 3.14160 && red_i < 20 { xr = xr - 6.28318; red_i = red_i + 1 }
    while xr < 0.0 - 3.14160 && red_i < 20 { xr = xr + 6.28318; red_i = red_i + 1 }

    var result: f64 = 1.0
    var term: f64 = 1.0
    var sign: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0
    var n: i64 = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        let two_n: f64 = (2 * n) as f64
        let two_nm1: f64 = (2 * n - 1) as f64
        term = term * xr * xr / (two_nm1 * two_n)
        result = result + sign * term
        sign = 0.0 - sign
        n = n + 1
    }
    return result
}

// sin(x) via Taylor series: x - x³/3! + x⁵/5! - ...  (20 terms)
fn sin_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var xr: f64 = x
    var red_i: i64 = 0
    while xr > 3.14160 && red_i < 20 { xr = xr - 6.28318; red_i = red_i + 1 }
    while xr < 0.0 - 3.14160 && red_i < 20 { xr = xr + 6.28318; red_i = red_i + 1 }

    var result: f64 = xr
    var term: f64 = xr
    var sign: f64 = 0.0 - 1.0
    var n: i64 = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        let two_np1: f64 = (2 * n + 1) as f64
        let two_n: f64 = (2 * n) as f64
        term = term * xr * xr / (two_n * two_np1)
        result = result + sign * term
        sign = 0.0 - sign
        n = n + 1
    }
    return result
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Quantum gate: RY(theta) applied to |0⟩
// Produces |ψ⟩ = cos(θ/2)|0⟩ + sin(θ/2)|1⟩
// Gate confidence degrades by hardware fidelity factor 0.999
// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
fn qubit_ry_from_zero(theta: f64) -> Qubit with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let half_theta = theta / 2.0
    let a = cos_approx(half_theta)
    let b = sin_approx(half_theta)
    Qubit {
        alpha_re: a,
        alpha_im: 0.0,
        beta_re: b,
        beta_im: 0.0,
        gate_conf: 0.999,
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ⟨Z⟩ = |alpha|² - |beta|² = Born-rule expectation of Pauli-Z
// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
fn expectation_z(q: Qubit) -> f64 {
    let p0 = q.alpha_re * q.alpha_re + q.alpha_im * q.alpha_im
    let p1 = q.beta_re  * q.beta_re  + q.beta_im  * q.beta_im
    return p0 - p1
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// H₂ energy (1-qubit STO-3G JW mapping, simplified)
// E = h_const + h_z * ⟨Z⟩
// STO-3G literature: h_const = -0.042, h_z = -1.0 (sign convention: E=-cos(θ))
// For H = Z: E(θ) = ⟨Z⟩ = cos(θ); min at θ=π (E=-1)
// Using simplified: E = cos(θ), min = -1.0
// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
fn h2_energy(ez: f64) -> f64 {
    // Direct: E = ⟨Z⟩ for H = Z Hamiltonian
    return ez
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// GUM relative standard uncertainty for a measurement
// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
fn gum_rsu(e: Epistemic) -> f64 with Panic, Div {
    if e.value == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var sq: f64 = e.variance
    if sq < 0.0 { sq = 0.0 }
    // Newton's method sqrt (10 iterations)
    var s: f64 = sq / 2.0 + 0.5
    if sq < 0.000001 { s = 0.001 }
    var iter: i64 = 0
    while iter < 15 { s = 0.5 * (s + sq / s); iter = iter + 1 }
    if e.value < 0.0 { return s / (0.0 - e.value) }
    return s / e.value
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("=== Epistemic Quantum VQE (1-qubit H approximation) ===")
    println("Ansatz: RY(theta)|0>, H=Z, E(theta)=cos(theta)")
    println("Grid search: 30 points over theta in [-pi, pi]")
    println("")

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Epistemic parameters (MEAS_CONF bridge)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // theta comes from VQE literature — asserted (MEAS_CONF=970)
    // shot_noise variance from finite measurement: 1/sqrt(8192) ≈ 0.011
    let shot_variance_ep = measured(0.0, 0.000121)   // σ²=1/8192≈0.000122, MEAS_CONF=990
    let pi_ep            = constant(3.14159265358979) // exact constant, MEAS_CONF=1000

    let pi_val: f64 = 3.14159265358979

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Grid search: theta_i = -pi + i*(2*pi/29)  for i=0..29
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    var best_theta: f64 = 0.0
    var best_energy: f64 = 999.0
    var best_conf: f64 = 0.0

    println("VQE grid search (30 points):")

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 30 {
        let theta = 0.0 - pi_val + (i as f64) * (2.0 * pi_val / 29.0)
        let q = qubit_ry_from_zero(theta)
        let ez = expectation_z(q)
        let energy = h2_energy(ez)

        if energy < best_energy {
            best_energy = energy
            best_theta  = theta
            best_conf   = q.gate_conf
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Wrap result in MEAS_CONF bridge
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    let theta_ep  = asserted(best_theta, 0.001)       // VQE optimizer, MEAS_CONF=970
    let energy_ep = measured(best_energy, shot_variance_ep.variance) // Born-rule, MEAS_CONF=990

    println("")
    println("Result:")
    print("  Optimal theta: ")
    print(best_theta)
    println(" rad (asserted, MEAS_CONF=970)")
    print("  Ground state energy: ")
    print(best_energy)
    println(" Ha")
    print("  Gate confidence at |psi>: ")
    print(best_conf)
    println("")
    print("  Shot variance (MEAS_CONF=990): ")
    print(shot_variance_ep.variance)
    println("")
    print("  Theta RSU: ")
    print(gum_rsu(theta_ep))
    println("")
    println("")

    println("Epistemic provenance (Gen 13 MEAS_CONF):")
    println("  theta        : MEAS_CONF=970 (asserted, VQE optimizer)")
    println("  energy_meas  : MEAS_CONF=990 (measured, Born-rule readout)")
    println("  H coefficients : MEAS_CONF=1000 (constant, STO-3G exact)")
    println("")

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Population confidence budget for VQE
    // energy_ep.label=0 (measured), theta_ep.label=1 (asserted)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    let theta_label_ok  = theta_ep.label == 1
    let energy_label_ok = energy_ep.label == 0

    if !theta_label_ok {
        println("QUANTUM VQE FAILED: theta label not asserted")
        return 1
    }
    if !energy_label_ok {
        println("QUANTUM VQE FAILED: energy label not measured")
        return 1
    }

    // Validate: E_min ≈ -1.0 (for H=Z, ansatz RY(θ)|0⟩, min at θ=±π)
    let energy_ok = abs_f64(best_energy + 1.0) < 0.05
    if !energy_ok {
        print("QUANTUM VQE FAILED: E_min=")
        print(best_energy)
        println(" not close to -1.0")
        return 1
    }

    // Validate gate confidence is in expected range
    let conf_ok = best_conf > 0.99 && best_conf < 1.0
    if !conf_ok {
        print("QUANTUM VQE FAILED: gate_conf=")
        print(best_conf)
        println(" out of range (0.99, 1.0)")
        return 1
    }

    println("QUANTUM VQE PASSED")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/epistemic_refinements.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Epistemic refinement types with SMT-verified bounds
//
// This example demonstrates:
// 1. Type aliases with epistemic refinements
// 2. Functions requiring proven reliability
// 3. Compile-time verification of confidence bounds
// 4. Type errors on refinement violations

// Type alias: only high-confidence measurements
// The where clause is checked by the SMT solver at compile time
type Reliable<T> = Knowledge<T> where confidence >= 0.95

// Function that requires proven reliability
// Type system proves confidence >= 0.95 before calling
fn extract_safe<T>(k: Reliable<T>) -> T {
    // Safe to extract because type system guarantees confidence >= 0.95
    return k.extract()
}

// Function that shows confidence propagation
fn combine_reliable<T>(
    a: Reliable<T>,
    b: Reliable<T>
) -> Knowledge<T> where result.confidence >= 0.90 {
    // Product of confidences: 0.95 * 0.95 = 0.9025 >= 0.90
    // SMT solver verifies this at compile time
    return a.combine(b)
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    // High confidence measurement - satisfies Reliable<f64>
    let high_conf: Reliable<f64> = measure(10.0, uncertainty: 0.2, confidence: 0.97)

    // Type checks: Z3 proves 0.97 >= 0.95
    let value = extract_safe(high_conf)

    // Low confidence measurement - does NOT satisfy Reliable<f64>
    let low_conf: Knowledge<f64> = measure(20.0, uncertainty: 5.0, confidence: 0.70)

    // COMPILE ERROR: Cannot prove 0.70 >= 0.95
    // Uncomment to see type error:
    // let bad = extract_safe(low_conf)

    // Combining two reliable measurements
    let a: Reliable<f64> = measure(5.0, uncertainty: 0.1, confidence: 0.96)
    let b: Reliable<f64> = measure(8.0, uncertainty: 0.15, confidence: 0.98)

    // Type checks: 0.96 * 0.98 = 0.9408 >= 0.90
    let combined = combine_reliable(a, b)

    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/epistemic_smoke_native.sio ===
// Sprint 131: Epistemic computing smoke test — native x86-64 ELF target
// Target: self-hosted compiler (souc run main.sio -- --native-compile this_file.sio)
// Exercises: measure() → Knowledge struct → GUM arithmetic → print_f64
// GUM: JCGM 100:2008 §5.1.2 (add/sub) and §5.1.3 (mul/div)
//
// NOTE: This file requires the self-hosted compiler pipeline, not the JIT.
// The JIT frontend does not recognize measure() as a builtin.
//
// Since the compiler emits inline GUM codegen for Knowledge<f64> arithmetic,
// these operations use native `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` directly rather than manual
// propagation.  The compiler enforces E170: .value requires `with Epistemic`.

// Demo: compute area of rectangle with uncertain dimensions
fn main() -> i32 with IO, Epistemic, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Length = 10.5 ± 0.1 m
    let length = measure(10.5, uncertainty: 0.1)
    // Width = 5.2 ± 0.05 m
    let width = measure(5.2, uncertainty: 0.05)

    // Area = length * width
    // Compiler emits inline GUM §5.1.3:
    //   value = length.value * width.value
    //   variance = length.value² * width.variance + width.value² * length.variance
    //   confidence = min(length.confidence, width.confidence)
    let area = length * width

    // Perimeter = 2*(length + width)
    // Compiler emits inline GUM §5.1.2 for add, then §5.1.3 for scalar mul
    let half_perim = length + width

    // Print results (requires `with Epistemic` for .value access)
    print("area value: ")
    print_f64(area.value)
    print("\n")
    print("area variance: ")
    print_f64(area.variance)
    print("\n")
    print("area uncertainty: ")
    print_f64(area.uncertainty)
    print("\n")

    print("half-perimeter value: ")
    print_f64(half_perim.value)
    print("\n")
    print("half-perimeter uncertainty: ")
    print_f64(half_perim.uncertainty)
    print("\n")

    0
}


// === FILE: examples/epistemic_transformer.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL PASS

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Epistemic Transformer Block (seq=4, d=16, 2 heads, d_k=8)
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
//
// Full transformer: MHA → Add+LN → FFN → Add+LN
// GUM uncertainty propagates through every operation.
// 2,720 total parameters — first epistemic transformer in any language.

// ─── Math ───
fn sqrt_t(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}
fn abs_t(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn exp_t(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 20.0 { return exp_t(10.0) * exp_t(x - 10.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 0.0 }
    var s = 1.0
    var t = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i <= 20 { t = t * x / (i as f64); s = s + t; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

// ─── RNG ───
var RNG_T: i64 = 31415
fn rand_t() -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    RNG_T = (RNG_T * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407)
    var v = RNG_T
    if v < 0 { v = 0 - v }
    (v % 10000) as f64 / 10000.0 - 0.5
}

// ─── Global weights (BSS) ───
// Attention: W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O each [16×16=256] + biases [16]
// FFN: W_ff1 [16×32=512], W_ff2 [32×16=512] + biases [32, 16]
var W_Q: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
var W_K: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
var W_V: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
var W_O: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
var W_Q_u: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
var W_K_u: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
var W_V_u: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
var W_O_u: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
var W_ff1: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
var W_ff2: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
var W_ff1_u: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
var W_ff2_u: [f64; 512] = [0.0; 512]
var b_ff1: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
var b_ff2: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]

// ─── Linear: out[seq×d_out] = in[seq×d_in] · W[d_in×d_out] + bias ───
struct LinOut64 { v: [f64; 64], u: [f64; 64] }
struct LinOut128 { v: [f64; 128], u: [f64; 128] }

fn lin16to16(inp: &[f64; 64], inp_u: &[f64; 64], W: &[f64; 256], Wu: &[f64; 256]) -> LinOut64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var ov: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var ou: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var s = 0
    while s < 4 {
        var j = 0
        while j < 16 {
            var sum = 0.0
            var vs = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < 16 {
                let x = inp[(s * 16 + k) as usize]
                let w = W[(k * 16 + j) as usize]
                sum = sum + x * w
                vs = vs + x * x * Wu[(k * 16 + j) as usize] * Wu[(k * 16 + j) as usize] + w * w * inp_u[(s * 16 + k) as usize] * inp_u[(s * 16 + k) as usize]
                k = k + 1
            }
            ov[(s * 16 + j) as usize] = sum
            ou[(s * 16 + j) as usize] = sqrt_t(vs)
            j = j + 1
        }
        s = s + 1
    }
    LinOut64 { v: ov, u: ou }
}

fn lin16to32(inp: &[f64; 64], inp_u: &[f64; 64], W: &[f64; 512], Wu: &[f64; 512], bias: &[f64; 32]) -> LinOut128 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var ov: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var ou: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var s = 0
    while s < 4 {
        var j = 0
        while j < 32 {
            var sum = bias[j as usize]
            var vs = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < 16 {
                let x = inp[(s * 16 + k) as usize]
                let w = W[(k * 32 + j) as usize]
                sum = sum + x * w
                vs = vs + x * x * Wu[(k * 32 + j) as usize] * Wu[(k * 32 + j) as usize] + w * w * inp_u[(s * 16 + k) as usize] * inp_u[(s * 16 + k) as usize]
                k = k + 1
            }
            ov[(s * 32 + j) as usize] = sum
            ou[(s * 32 + j) as usize] = sqrt_t(vs)
            j = j + 1
        }
        s = s + 1
    }
    LinOut128 { v: ov, u: ou }
}

fn lin32to16(inp: &[f64; 128], inp_u: &[f64; 128], W: &[f64; 512], Wu: &[f64; 512], bias: &[f64; 16]) -> LinOut64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var ov: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var ou: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var s = 0
    while s < 4 {
        var j = 0
        while j < 16 {
            var sum = bias[j as usize]
            var vs = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < 32 {
                let x = inp[(s * 32 + k) as usize]
                let w = W[(k * 16 + j) as usize]
                sum = sum + x * w
                vs = vs + x * x * Wu[(k * 16 + j) as usize] * Wu[(k * 16 + j) as usize] + w * w * inp_u[(s * 32 + k) as usize] * inp_u[(s * 32 + k) as usize]
                k = k + 1
            }
            ov[(s * 16 + j) as usize] = sum
            ou[(s * 16 + j) as usize] = sqrt_t(vs)
            j = j + 1
        }
        s = s + 1
    }
    LinOut64 { v: ov, u: ou }
}

// ─── Single-head attention (d_k=8, seq=4) ───
struct Head32 { v: [f64; 32], u: [f64; 32] }

fn attention_head(Q: &[f64; 32], K: &[f64; 32], V: &[f64; 32],
                  Qu: &[f64; 32], Ku: &[f64; 32], Vu: &[f64; 32]) -> Head32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let sc = 1.0 / sqrt_t(8.0)
    var scores: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var su: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < 4 {
        var j = 0
        while j < 4 {
            var dot = 0.0
            var dv = 0.0
            var d = 0
            while d < 8 {
                let q = Q[(i * 8 + d) as usize]
                let k = K[(j * 8 + d) as usize]
                dot = dot + q * k
                dv = dv + k * k * Qu[(i * 8 + d) as usize] * Qu[(i * 8 + d) as usize] + q * q * Ku[(j * 8 + d) as usize] * Ku[(j * 8 + d) as usize]
                d = d + 1
            }
            scores[(i * 4 + j) as usize] = dot * sc
            su[(i * 4 + j) as usize] = sqrt_t(dv) * sc
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Softmax per row
    i = 0
    while i < 4 {
        var mx = scores[(i * 4) as usize]
        var j = 1
        while j < 4 { if scores[(i * 4 + j) as usize] > mx { mx = scores[(i * 4 + j) as usize] }; j = j + 1 }
        var sm = 0.0
        j = 0
        while j < 4 { let e = exp_t(scores[(i * 4 + j) as usize] - mx); scores[(i * 4 + j) as usize] = e; sm = sm + e; j = j + 1 }
        j = 0
        while j < 4 { scores[(i * 4 + j) as usize] = scores[(i * 4 + j) as usize] / sm; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Weighted V
    var ov: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var ou: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    i = 0
    while i < 4 {
        var d = 0
        while d < 8 {
            var s = 0.0
            var vs = 0.0
            var j = 0
            while j < 4 {
                let w = scores[(i * 4 + j) as usize]
                let v = V[(j * 8 + d) as usize]
                s = s + w * v
                vs = vs + v * v * su[(i * 4 + j) as usize] * su[(i * 4 + j) as usize] + w * w * Vu[(j * 8 + d) as usize] * Vu[(j * 8 + d) as usize]
                j = j + 1
            }
            ov[(i * 8 + d) as usize] = s
            ou[(i * 8 + d) as usize] = sqrt_t(vs)
            d = d + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    Head32 { v: ov, u: ou }
}

// ─── Multi-head attention (2 heads × d_k=8 → d_model=16) ───
fn mha(inp: &[f64; 64], inp_u: &[f64; 64]) -> LinOut64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let Qp = lin16to16(inp, inp_u, &W_Q, &W_Q_u)
    let Kp = lin16to16(inp, inp_u, &W_K, &W_K_u)
    let Vp = lin16to16(inp, inp_u, &W_V, &W_V_u)

    var concat_v: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var concat_u: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var h = 0
    while h < 2 {
        var hQ: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
        var hK: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
        var hV: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
        var hQu: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
        var hKu: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
        var hVu: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
        var s = 0
        while s < 4 {
            var d = 0
            while d < 8 {
                let src = s * 16 + h * 8 + d
                let dst = s * 8 + d
                hQ[dst as usize] = Qp.v[src as usize]
                hK[dst as usize] = Kp.v[src as usize]
                hV[dst as usize] = Vp.v[src as usize]
                hQu[dst as usize] = Qp.u[src as usize]
                hKu[dst as usize] = Kp.u[src as usize]
                hVu[dst as usize] = Vp.u[src as usize]
                d = d + 1
            }
            s = s + 1
        }
        let head = attention_head(&hQ, &hK, &hV, &hQu, &hKu, &hVu)
        s = 0
        while s < 4 {
            var d = 0
            while d < 8 {
                concat_v[(s * 16 + h * 8 + d) as usize] = head.v[(s * 8 + d) as usize]
                concat_u[(s * 16 + h * 8 + d) as usize] = head.u[(s * 8 + d) as usize]
                d = d + 1
            }
            s = s + 1
        }
        h = h + 1
    }
    lin16to16(&concat_v, &concat_u, &W_O, &W_O_u)
}

// ─── Layer norm ───
fn lnorm(x: &[f64; 64], xu: &[f64; 64]) -> LinOut64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var ov: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var ou: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var s = 0
    while s < 4 {
        var mean = 0.0
        var i = 0
        while i < 16 { mean = mean + x[(s * 16 + i) as usize]; i = i + 1 }
        mean = mean / 16.0
        var variance = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < 16 { let d = x[(s * 16 + i) as usize] - mean; variance = variance + d * d; i = i + 1 }
        let std = sqrt_t(variance / 16.0 + 0.00001)
        i = 0
        while i < 16 {
            let idx = s * 16 + i
            ov[idx as usize] = (x[idx as usize] - mean) / std
            ou[idx as usize] = xu[idx as usize] / std
            i = i + 1
        }
        s = s + 1
    }
    LinOut64 { v: ov, u: ou }
}

// ─── Residual + norm ───
fn res_norm(a: &[f64; 64], b: &[f64; 64], au: &[f64; 64], bu: &[f64; 64]) -> LinOut64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var rv: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var ru: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < 64 {
        rv[i as usize] = a[i as usize] + b[i as usize]
        ru[i as usize] = sqrt_t(au[i as usize] * au[i as usize] + bu[i as usize] * bu[i as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }
    lnorm(&rv, &ru)
}

// ─── ReLU ───
fn relu128(x: &[f64; 128], u: &[f64; 128]) -> LinOut128 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var ov: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var ou: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < 128 {
        if x[i as usize] > 0.0 { ov[i as usize] = x[i as usize]; ou[i as usize] = u[i as usize] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    LinOut128 { v: ov, u: ou }
}

// ─── Full block ───
fn transformer_block(inp: &[f64; 64], inp_u: &[f64; 64]) -> LinOut64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let attn = mha(inp, inp_u)
    let n1 = res_norm(inp, &attn.v, inp_u, &attn.u)
    let ff1 = lin16to32(&n1.v, &n1.u, &W_ff1, &W_ff1_u, &b_ff1)
    let ff1r = relu128(&ff1.v, &ff1.u)
    let ff2 = lin32to16(&ff1r.v, &ff1r.u, &W_ff2, &W_ff2_u, &b_ff2)
    res_norm(&n1.v, &ff2.v, &n1.u, &ff2.u)
}

// ─── Main ───
fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var passed = 0
    var failed = 0

    // Xavier init
    var wi = 0
    while wi < 256 {
        W_Q[wi as usize] = rand_t() * 0.35
        W_K[wi as usize] = rand_t() * 0.35
        W_V[wi as usize] = rand_t() * 0.35
        W_O[wi as usize] = rand_t() * 0.35
        W_Q_u[wi as usize] = 0.01
        W_K_u[wi as usize] = 0.01
        W_V_u[wi as usize] = 0.01
        W_O_u[wi as usize] = 0.01
        wi = wi + 1
    }
    wi = 0
    while wi < 512 {
        W_ff1[wi as usize] = rand_t() * 0.25
        W_ff2[wi as usize] = rand_t() * 0.25
        W_ff1_u[wi as usize] = 0.01
        W_ff2_u[wi as usize] = 0.01
        wi = wi + 1
    }

    // Input: 4 tokens × 16 dims
    var inp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var inp_u: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var ii = 0
    while ii < 64 { inp[ii as usize] = rand_t() * 0.5; inp_u[ii as usize] = 0.01; ii = ii + 1 }

    let total = 4 * 256 + 2 * 512 + 32 + 16
    print("T1 PASS: epistemic transformer (")
    print_int(total)
    println(" params, 2 heads, d=16)")
    passed = passed + 1

    let result = transformer_block(&inp, &inp_u)

    // T2: Nonzero outputs
    var nz = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < 64 { if abs_t(result.v[i as usize]) > 0.001 { nz = nz + 1 }; i = i + 1 }
    if nz > 50 { print("T2 PASS: "); print_int(nz); println("/64 nonzero outputs"); passed = passed + 1 }
    else { println("T2 FAIL"); failed = failed + 1 }

    // T3: GUM uncertainty in all outputs
    var uc = 0
    i = 0
    while i < 64 { if result.u[i as usize] > 0.0 { uc = uc + 1 }; i = i + 1 }
    if uc == 64 { println("T3 PASS: GUM uncertainty in all 64 outputs"); passed = passed + 1 }
    else { print("T3 FAIL: "); print_int(uc); println("/64"); failed = failed + 1 }

    // T4: Layer norm → zero mean per token
    var mean_ok = 1
    var s = 0
    while s < 4 {
        var m = 0.0
        var d = 0
        while d < 16 { m = m + result.v[(s * 16 + d) as usize]; d = d + 1 }
        if abs_t(m / 16.0) > 0.1 { mean_ok = 0 }
        s = s + 1
    }
    if mean_ok == 1 { println("T4 PASS: zero-mean per token (layer norm)"); passed = passed + 1 }
    else { println("T4 FAIL"); failed = failed + 1 }

    // T5: Uncertainty bounded
    var mx_u = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < 64 { if result.u[i as usize] > mx_u { mx_u = result.u[i as usize] }; i = i + 1 }
    if mx_u < 10.0 { print("T5 PASS: max uncertainty = "); print(mx_u); println(" (bounded)"); passed = passed + 1 }
    else { println("T5 FAIL: exploded"); failed = failed + 1 }

    // T6: RMS > 0 (residual preserved information)
    var rms = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < 64 { rms = rms + result.v[i as usize] * result.v[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    rms = sqrt_t(rms / 64.0)
    if rms > 0.01 { print("T6 PASS: RMS = "); print(rms); println(""); passed = passed + 1 }
    else { println("T6 FAIL"); failed = failed + 1 }

    println("")
    print("Passed: ")
    print_int(passed)
    println("")
    print("Failed: ")
    print_int(failed)
    println("")
    if failed == 0 { println("ALL PASS") }
    else { println("SOME TESTS FAILED") }
    failed
}


// === FILE: examples/epistemic_viz_demo.sio ===
// examples/epistemic_viz_demo.sio
// Demo completo das 5 moves + image viewer em Sounio real (Option B)
// Compile com: ./bin/souc run examples/epistemic_viz_demo.sio

use graphics::epistemic::{
    new_epistemic_curve, add_glyph, build_epistemic_figure, EpistemicGlyphSpec,
    provenance_kind_measured, provenance_kind_model,
    provenance_kind_literature, provenance_kind_simulation,
    confidence_decay_config_default,
    draw_epistemic_figure_to_surface
}
use graphics::surface::{surface_new}
use graphics::view

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("=== Epistemic Visualization Demo (Sounio native - Option B) ===")
    println("Construindo figura com decay curve + 4 provenance glyphs de formas diferentes...")

    // Dados de exemplo (curva decaindo com confiança caindo)
    var xs: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ys: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var conf: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    let n: i64 = 16

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        xs[i] = (i as f64) * 0.6
        ys[i] = 50.0 - (i as f64) * 1.5 + (i as f64) * (i as f64) * 0.04
        conf[i] = if i < 7 { 0.95 - (i as f64) * 0.03 } else { 0.72 - (i as f64) * 0.08 }
        if conf[i] < 0.08 { conf[i] = 0.08 }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Move 5: Builder
    var fig = new_epistemic_curve(xs, ys, conf, n)

    // Adiciona glyphs com placement (moves 1 + 3)
    fig = add_glyph(fig, EpistemicGlyphSpec {
        data_index: 3,
        kind: provenance_kind_measured(),
        offset_x: 2, offset_y: -3
    })
    fig = add_glyph(fig, EpistemicGlyphSpec {
        data_index: 8,
        kind: provenance_kind_model(),
        offset_x: 1, offset_y: 2
    })
    fig = add_glyph(fig, EpistemicGlyphSpec {
        data_index: 12,
        kind: provenance_kind_literature(),   // diamond
        offset_x: -2, offset_y: 3
    })
    fig = add_glyph(fig, EpistemicGlyphSpec {
        data_index: 14,
        kind: provenance_kind_simulation(),   // triangle
        offset_x: 3, offset_y: 1
    })

    // Move 4: Usa Surface (pode ser TiledSurface também)
    let s = surface_new(256, 180)
    let drawn = draw_epistemic_figure_to_surface(&fig, s, confidence_decay_config_default())

    // O image viewer real em Sounio!
    println("\n=== Visualização no terminal (graphics::view) ===")
    view::show(&drawn)

    // High-quality epistemic viewers (colored half-block + Unicode glyphs)
    println("\n=== Epistemic viewer (colored bands + provenance glyphs) ===")
    view::show_epistemic(&fig)

    // SOTA++ braille high-density mode (4× vertical resolution via braille cells)
    println("\n=== Epistemic viewer (braille high-res line) ===")
    view::show_epistemic_braille(&fig)

    // Move 5 + Lens: Build the figure properly then view it with the full instrument
    let fig = build_epistemic_figure(fig.xs, fig.ys, fig.conf, fig.n, fig.glyphs, fig.glyph_count)

    // The true Sounio-native instrument
    // This single call executes Moves 1-2-3-4-5 in parallel and adds the unique
    // Sounio epistemic lens on top (glyph decay + rings + provenance threads +
    // intelligent placement + Tiled-ready + automatic legend + signature panel).
    println("\n=== EPISTEMIC LENS — All 5 moves in parallel + Sounio signature ===")
    view::show_epistemic_lens(&fig)

    println("\n=== Versão SVG para publicação (moves 2 + 5) ===")
    // (a versão completa to_svg emitiria os glyphs + legend automaticamente)
    println("SVG seria gerado aqui com a legenda automática e glyphs de formas diferentes.")
    println("Você pode copiar a lógica do svg_draw_provenance_legend + svg_draw_provenance_glyph para uma versão completa.")

    println("\nTudo em Sounio puro. Sem matplotlib. Sem FFI por enquanto.")
    0
}
