            LEARNT[0] = 0 - vc(u, c)
            LEARNT[1] = 0 - vc(w, c)
            let _ = db_add(&LEARNT, 2)
            c = c + 1
        }
        e = e + 1
    }
}
fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("=== de Grey -> chi(R^2)>=5  (fast CDCL: 2-watched + VSIDS + restarts) ===\n")
    print("vertices=1581 edges=7877\n")
    ginit_all()
    let okg = validate_geometry()
    print("[geometry] unit-distance edges: ")  print_dec(okg as i64)  print(" / 7877\n")
    build_coloring()
    let orig_nc = nclauses
    n_orig = orig_nc
    print("[cnf] vars=")  print_dec(nvars as i64)  print(" clauses=")  print_dec(orig_nc as i64)  print("\n")
    print("[solve] starting (2-watched CDCL)...\n")
    let r = solve()
    print("[solve] code=")  print_dec(r as i64)  print(" conflicts=")  print_dec(n_conflicts)
    print(" decisions=")  print_dec(n_decisions)  print(" restarts=")  print_dec(n_restarts)
    print(" reduces=")  print_dec(n_reduces)  print(" deleted=")  print_dec(n_deleted)
    print(" lemmas=")  print_dec(P_n as i64)  print("\n")
    if r == 0 {
        print("[RESULT] UNSAT: de Grey graph is NOT 4-colorable => chi(R^2) >= 5\n")
        print("[proof] DRUP lemmas=")  print_dec(P_n as i64)  print("\n")
        if (P_n as i64) < 3000000 {
            print("%%DIMACS%%\n")  emit_dimacs(orig_nc)
            print("%%DRAT%%\n")  emit_drat()  print("%%END%%\n")
        } else {
            print("[proof] (too large to stream; solved -- verify via on-node drat-trim)\n")
        }
    } else if r == 1 {
        print("[RESULT] SAT (unexpected for de Grey)\n")
    } else {
        print("[RESULT] WALL/CAP code=")  print_dec(r as i64)  print("\n")
    }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/erdos/degrey_fieldtower.sio ===
// examples/erdos/degrey_fieldtower.sio
//
// EXACT ARITHMETIC over Q(√3, √5, √7, √11) — the degree-16 field of de Grey's
// FULL 1581-vertex 5-chromatic graph (Erdős #508).
//
// Resolved field tower (Polymath16 wiki; de Grey 2018, arXiv:1804.02385):
// de Grey's graph G derives from N = Z[ω_1, ω_3, ω_4, ω_16], with
// ω_t = exp(i·arccos(1 − 1/2t)),  sin(ω_t) = √(4t−1)/(2t):
//   ω_1  → √3/2     (60°)
//   ω_3  → √11/6    (arccos 5/6)
//   ω_4  → √15/8    (arccos 7/8)   ⟹ needs √5  (√15 = √3·√5)
//   ω_16 → √63/32   (arccos 31/32) ⟹ needs √7  (√63 = 3√7)
// So the full χ≥5 certificate lives in Q(√3,√5,√7,√11). This file extends the
// Q(√3,√11) spindle kernel to that whole tower.
//
// REPRESENTATION (generalises the 4-tuple Q(√3,√11)). The 2^4 = 16 monomials
// √(∏ S), for S ⊆ {3,5,7,11}, form a Q-basis. Index a basis element by a 4-bit
// mask: bit0=√3, bit1=√5, bit2=√7, bit3=√11. A field element is an integer
// 16-tuple. The multiplication table is pure XOR with a rational coefficient:
//   √(∏S) · √(∏T) = (∏_{p∈S∩T} p) · √(∏(S△T)),
// i.e. basis i times basis j lands in basis (i XOR j) with coefficient =
// product of the primes selected by (i AND j). (Same XOR algebra as the
// Cayley–Dickson e_a·e_b = ±e_{a^b}, here with positive square-root coeffs.)
//
// Self-contained.

struct Q16 { c: [i64; 16] }

// product of primes selected by mask bits (bit0=3,bit1=5,bit2=7,bit3=11)
fn bcoeff(mask: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var p = 1
    if (mask & 1) != 0 { p = p * 3 }
    if (mask & 2) != 0 { p = p * 5 }
    if (mask & 4) != 0 { p = p * 7 }
    if (mask & 8) != 0 { p = p * 11 }
    return p
}

fn q16_zero() -> Q16 { return Q16 { c: [0; 16] } }

fn q16_rat(v: i64) -> Q16 with Mut, Panic {
    var r = Q16 { c: [0; 16] }
    r.c[0] = v
    return r
}

// single basis monomial: coefficient v on basis index idx
fn q16_mono(idx: i64, v: i64) -> Q16 with Mut, Panic {
    var r = Q16 { c: [0; 16] }
    r.c[idx as usize] = v
    return r
}

fn q16_add(x: Q16, y: Q16) -> Q16 with Mut, Panic {
    var r = Q16 { c: [0; 16] }
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        r.c[i as usize] = x.c[i as usize] + y.c[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return r
}

fn q16_sub(x: Q16, y: Q16) -> Q16 with Mut, Panic {
    var r = Q16 { c: [0; 16] }
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        r.c[i as usize] = x.c[i as usize] - y.c[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return r
}

// (∏S)·(∏T): result basis i^j, coefficient ∏ primes in i&j. O(16²).
fn q16_mul(x: Q16, y: Q16) -> Q16 with Mut, Panic {
    var r = Q16 { c: [0; 16] }
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        var j = 0
        while j < 16 {
            let coeff = bcoeff(i & j)
            let idx = (i ^ j) as usize
            r.c[idx] = r.c[idx] + x.c[i as usize] * y.c[j as usize] * coeff
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return r
}

fn q16_sq(x: Q16) -> Q16 with Mut, Panic { return q16_mul(x, x) }

// is x exactly the rational v (all surd components zero)?
fn q16_is_rat(x: Q16, v: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    if x.c[0 as usize] != v { return 0 }
    var i = 1
    while i < 16 {
        if x.c[i as usize] != 0 { return 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 1
}

fn print_q16(x: Q16) with IO, Mut, Panic {
    // labels for the 16 basis monomials
    print_int(x.c[0 as usize])
    var i = 1
    while i < 16 {
        let v = x.c[i as usize]
        if v != 0 {
            print(" + "); print_int(v); print("*b"); print_int(i)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    print("\n")
}

// squared distance between (px,py) and (qx,qy), all Q16
fn dist2(px: Q16, py: Q16, qx: Q16, qy: Q16) -> Q16 with Mut, Panic {
    let dx = q16_sub(px, qx)
    let dy = q16_sub(py, qy)
    return q16_add(q16_sq(dx), q16_sq(dy))
}

fn check(name_ok: i64) -> i64 { return name_ok }

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic {
    print("=== Exact arithmetic over Q(√3,√5,√7,√11) — de Grey's degree-16 field ===\n")
    print("basis index bits: bit0=√3 bit1=√5 bit2=√7 bit3=√11; b3=√15 b5=√21 b6=√35 b12=√77 ...\n\n")

    var pass = 0
    var total = 0

    // --- arithmetic self-tests ---
    print("Arithmetic self-tests:\n")

    // (√15)² = 15  : √15 = b3 (bits 0,1)
    let t1 = q16_sq(q16_mono(3, 1))
    total = total + 1
    print("  (√15)² = "); print_q16(t1)
    if q16_is_rat(t1, 15) == 1 { pass = pass + 1; print("    [OK == 15]\n") } else { print("    [FAIL]\n") }

    // √15 · √35 = 5√21  : √15=b3(0,1), √35=b6(1,2) -> i^j=b5(0,2)=√21, coeff(i&j=b1=√5)=5
    let t2 = q16_mul(q16_mono(3, 1), q16_mono(6, 1))
    total = total + 1
    print("  √15 · √35 = "); print_q16(t2)
    // expect 5 on b5
    var t2ok = 1
    if t2.c[5 as usize] != 5 { t2ok = 0 }
    var k = 0
    while k < 16 { if k != 5 { if t2.c[k as usize] != 0 { t2ok = 0 } }  k = k + 1 }
    if t2ok == 1 { pass = pass + 1; print("    [OK == 5√21 (5 on b5)]\n") } else { print("    [FAIL]\n") }

    // (√3 + √5)² = 8 + 2√15
    let t3 = q16_sq(q16_add(q16_mono(1, 1), q16_mono(2, 1)))
    total = total + 1
    print("  (√3 + √5)² = "); print_q16(t3)
    var t3ok = 1
    if t3.c[0 as usize] != 8 { t3ok = 0 }
    if t3.c[3 as usize] != 2 { t3ok = 0 }
    k = 0
    while k < 16 { if k != 0 { if k != 3 { if t3.c[k as usize] != 0 { t3ok = 0 } } }  k = k + 1 }
    if t3ok == 1 { pass = pass + 1; print("    [OK == 8 + 2√15]\n") } else { print("    [FAIL]\n") }

    print("\nRotation realizations de Grey's full graph needs:\n")

    // ω_4 isosceles triangle (sides 2, base 1, apex arccos 7/8), scale ×4 (unit² = 16).
    // O=(0,0); P1=(8,0); P2=(7, √15).  Base |P1−P2|² must equal 16, using √5 (via √15).
    let ox = q16_zero();  let oy = q16_zero()
    let p1x = q16_rat(8); let p1y = q16_zero()
    let p2x = q16_rat(7); let p2y = q16_mono(3, 1)   // √15
    let d_base4 = dist2(p1x, p1y, p2x, p2y)
    total = total + 1
    print("  ω_4 base (needs √5): dist² = "); print_q16(d_base4)
    if q16_is_rat(d_base4, 16) == 1 { pass = pass + 1; print("    [OK == 16 = (unit·4)²; √15 cancels]\n") } else { print("    [FAIL]\n") }

    // ω_16 isosceles triangle (sides 4, base 1, apex arccos 31/32), scale ×8 (unit² = 64).
    // O=(0,0); P1=(32,0); P2=(31, 3√7).  Base must equal 64, using √7.
    let q1x = q16_rat(32); let q1y = q16_zero()
    let q2x = q16_rat(31); let q2y = q16_mono(4, 3)   // 3√7  (√7 = b4)
    let d_base16 = dist2(q1x, q1y, q2x, q2y)
    total = total + 1
    print("  ω_16 base (needs √7): dist² = "); print_q16(d_base16)
    if q16_is_rat(d_base16, 64) == 1 { pass = pass + 1; print("    [OK == 64 = (unit·8)²; √63 cancels]\n") } else { print("    [FAIL]\n") }

    print("\n");  print_int(pass);  print(" / ");  print_int(total);  print(" checks passed\n")
    if pass == total {
        print("Q(√3,√5,√7,√11) kernel OPERATIONAL: the exact arithmetic foundation for\n")
        print("de Grey's full 5-chromatic graph (Z[ω_1,ω_3,ω_4,ω_16]) now exists in Sounio.\n")
        print("Next: realize de Grey's minimized graphs (G_2/G_3 ⊂ Z[ω_1,ω_3,ω_4]) and\n")
        print("certify χ≥5 with the native SAT solver (cap already raised to 256 vars).\n")
    }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/erdos/degrey_fragment_q3q11.sio ===
// examples/erdos/degrey_fragment_q3q11.sio
//
// FIELD-CLOSURE under de Grey-style gluing (Erdős #508) — answers the xai
// math-review flag (2026-05-28) on the single-spindle artifact: "gluing spindles
// at non-Moser vertices may introduce an auxiliary surd; unverified."
//
// The Moser spindle itself requires exactly two rotations, both in Q(√3,√11):
//   R_60  (cos 60° = 1/2,  sin 60° = √3/2)        — hexagonal / Eisenstein, in Q(√3)
//   R_φ   (cos φ = 5/6,     sin φ = √11/6)         — the spindle twist, in Q(√11)
// Since Q(√3,√11) is a field (closed under +,−,×,÷), ANY finite composition of
// these rotations maps a point with Q(√3,√11) coordinates to another such point.
// So for graphs GENERATED BY R_60 and R_φ (plus translations) NO auxiliary surd
// can appear: every vertex stays in Q(√3,√11) and every pairwise squared distance
// is an exact element of the field. This file PROVES that computationally: it
// glues a second spindle onto the first by a 60° rotation about the shared apex
// and verifies every coordinate is exact and every unit edge has squared distance
// exactly 1 (all √3/√11/√33 parts cancel).
//
// SCOPE — RESOLVED (Polymath16 wiki; de Grey 2018, arXiv:1804.02385):
// graphs embed in rings Z[ω_{t1},…] with ω_t = exp(i·arccos(1−1/2t)),
// sin(ω_t) = √(4t−1)/(2t). The Moser spindle is Z[ω_1,ω_3], whose real
// coordinates are EXACTLY Q(√3,√11) (ω_1: √3/2; ω_3: √11/6) — so this kernel is
// exactly right for the spindle and the ω_1,ω_3 family (Golomb, V, G_21, G_43,
// and G_49 ⊂ Q(√3,√11)²). BUT de Grey's full 1581-vertex graph G derives from
// N = Z[ω_1,ω_3,ω_4,ω_16], which ALSO uses ω_4 (sin = √15/8 ⟹ √5) and
// ω_16 (sin = √63/32 = 3√7/32 ⟹ √7). So the full 5-chromatic graph needs
// Q(√3,√5,√7,√11) (degree 16) — the auxiliary surds the math-review flagged are
// real: √5 and √7. Scaling this kernel to the full χ≥5 certificate means
// extending the 4-tuple representation to that field tower. The spindle gluing
// demonstrated here is the Q(√3,√11) base of that tower.
//
// Representation: a+b√3+c√11+d√33 as integer 4-tuple (a,b,c,d). The base spindle
// is built at scale ×12 (as in degrey_q3q11_spindle.sio); the glued graph is
// carried at GLOBAL scale ×24 so the 60° rotation's 1/2 factor stays integral.
// Unit distance² target at scale 24 is 24² = 576.
//
// The glued graph's chromatic number is then certified by Sounio's NATIVE CDCL
// solver (theorem::smt): 3-coloring UNSAT, 4-coloring SAT — no external solver.

use theorem::smt::*

struct Qf { a: i64, b: i64, c: i64, d: i64 }

fn qadd(x: Qf, y: Qf) -> Qf {
    return Qf { a: x.a + y.a, b: x.b + y.b, c: x.c + y.c, d: x.d + y.d }
}
fn qsub(x: Qf, y: Qf) -> Qf {
    return Qf { a: x.a - y.a, b: x.b - y.b, c: x.c - y.c, d: x.d - y.d }
}
fn qmul(x: Qf, y: Qf) -> Qf {
    let ra  = x.a*y.a + 3*x.b*y.b + 11*x.c*y.c + 33*x.d*y.d
    let r3  = x.a*y.b + y.a*x.b + 11*(x.c*y.d + y.c*x.d)
    let r11 = x.a*y.c + y.a*x.c + 3*(x.b*y.d + y.b*x.d)
    let r33 = x.a*y.d + y.a*x.d + x.b*y.c + y.b*x.c
    return Qf { a: ra, b: r3, c: r11, d: r33 }
}
fn qsq(x: Qf) -> Qf { return qmul(x, x) }
fn qeq(x: Qf, y: Qf) -> i64 {
    if x.a == y.a && x.b == y.b && x.c == y.c && x.d == y.d { return 1 }
    return 0
}
// multiply a field element by √3 = (0,1,0,0): closure generator for R_60 / R_120.
fn qmul_s3(x: Qf) -> Qf { return qmul(x, Qf { a: 0, b: 1, c: 0, d: 0 }) }
fn qscale(x: Qf, k: i64) -> Qf { return Qf { a: x.a*k, b: x.b*k, c: x.c*k, d: x.d*k } }

// Base Moser spindle, ×12 scaled (see degrey_q3q11_spindle.sio for derivation).
var BXA: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]
var BXB: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]
var BXC: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]
var BXD: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]
var BYA: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]
var BYB: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]
var BYC: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]
var BYD: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]

fn setup_base() with Mut, Panic {
    BXA[0] = 0  BXB[0] = 0       BXC[0] = 0       BXD[0] = 0
    BYA[0] = 0  BYB[0] = 0       BYC[0] = 0       BYD[0] = 0
    BXA[1] = 0  BXB[1] = 6       BXC[1] = 0       BXD[1] = 0
    BYA[1] = 6  BYB[1] = 0       BYC[1] = 0       BYD[1] = 0
    BXA[2] = 0  BXB[2] = 12      BXC[2] = 0       BXD[2] = 0
    BYA[2] = 0  BYB[2] = 0       BYC[2] = 0       BYD[2] = 0
    BXA[3] = 0  BXB[3] = 6       BXC[3] = 0       BXD[3] = 0
    BYA[3] = 0 - 6  BYB[3] = 0   BYC[3] = 0       BYD[3] = 0
    BXA[4] = 0  BXB[4] = 5       BXC[4] = 0 - 1   BXD[4] = 0
    BYA[4] = 5  BYB[4] = 0       BYC[4] = 0       BYD[4] = 1
    BXA[5] = 0  BXB[5] = 10      BXC[5] = 0       BXD[5] = 0
    BYA[5] = 0  BYB[5] = 0       BYC[5] = 0       BYD[5] = 2
    BXA[6] = 0  BXB[6] = 5       BXC[6] = 1       BXD[6] = 0
    BYA[6] = 0 - 5  BYB[6] = 0   BYC[6] = 0       BYD[6] = 1
}

fn base_x(i: i64) -> Qf with Panic {
    return Qf { a: BXA[i as usize], b: BXB[i as usize], c: BXC[i as usize], d: BXD[i as usize] }
}
fn base_y(i: i64) -> Qf with Panic {
    return Qf { a: BYA[i as usize], b: BYB[i as usize], c: BYC[i as usize], d: BYD[i as usize] }
}

// Fragment vertices, carried at global scale ×24. Up to 16 (we use 13).
var FX_A: [i64; 16] = [0; 16]
var FX_B: [i64; 16] = [0; 16]
var FX_C: [i64; 16] = [0; 16]
var FX_D: [i64; 16] = [0; 16]
var FY_A: [i64; 16] = [0; 16]
var FY_B: [i64; 16] = [0; 16]
var FY_C: [i64; 16] = [0; 16]
var FY_D: [i64; 16] = [0; 16]
var NF: i64 = 0

var FADJ: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]   // 16*16

fn frag_x(i: i64) -> Qf with Panic {
    return Qf { a: FX_A[i as usize], b: FX_B[i as usize], c: FX_C[i as usize], d: FX_D[i as usize] }
}
fn frag_y(i: i64) -> Qf with Panic {
    return Qf { a: FY_A[i as usize], b: FY_B[i as usize], c: FY_C[i as usize], d: FY_D[i as usize] }
}

// Add a vertex (px,py) at scale 24 if not already present; return its index.
fn frag_add(px: Qf, py: Qf) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < NF {
        if qeq(frag_x(i), px) == 1 && qeq(frag_y(i), py) == 1 { return i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let k = NF
    FX_A[k as usize] = px.a  FX_B[k as usize] = px.b  FX_C[k as usize] = px.c  FX_D[k as usize] = px.d
    FY_A[k as usize] = py.a  FY_B[k as usize] = py.b  FY_C[k as usize] = py.c  FY_D[k as usize] = py.d
    NF = NF + 1
    return k
}

// Add the base spindle rotated by rot60 ∈ {0,1,2} (i.e. 0°, 60°, 120°) about the
// apex A=origin, carried at scale 24. rot60=0 is the identity (just ×2).
// All three rotations have matrix entries in Q(√3,√11), so outputs stay exact.
fn add_rotated_spindle(rot60: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < 7 {
        let px12 = base_x(i)
        let py12 = base_y(i)
        var nx = Qf { a: 0, b: 0, c: 0, d: 0 }
        var ny = Qf { a: 0, b: 0, c: 0, d: 0 }
        if rot60 == 0 {
            // identity at scale 24 = ×2
            nx = qscale(px12, 2)
            ny = qscale(py12, 2)
        }
        if rot60 == 1 {
            // R_60 at scale 24:  x' = px - py√3 ;  y' = px√3 + py
            nx = qsub(px12, qmul_s3(py12))
            ny = qadd(qmul_s3(px12), py12)
        }
        if rot60 == 2 {
            // R_120 at scale 24: x' = -px - py√3 ;  y' = px√3 - py
            nx = qsub(qsub(Qf { a: 0, b: 0, c: 0, d: 0 }, px12), qmul_s3(py12))
            ny = qsub(qmul_s3(px12), py12)
        }
        let _ = frag_add(nx, ny)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn frag_dist2(i: i64, j: i64) -> Qf with Panic {
    let dx = qsub(frag_x(i), frag_x(j))
    let dy = qsub(frag_y(i), frag_y(j))
    return qadd(qsq(dx), qsq(dy))
}

// Unit edge at scale 24 ⟺ dist² exactly 576 (rational; irrational parts 0).
fn frag_is_unit(d: Qf) -> i64 {
    if d.a == 576 && d.b == 0 && d.c == 0 && d.d == 0 { return 1 }
    return 0
}

// Count pairs whose squared distance carries a nonzero surd part. Every such
// distance is STILL an exact Q(√3,√11) element (no auxiliary surd) — this is
// purely informational, confirming distances live in the field as 4-tuples.
fn count_surd_distances() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var n = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < NF {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < NF {
            let d = frag_dist2(i, j)
            if d.b != 0 || d.c != 0 || d.d != 0 { n = n + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return n
}

fn build_frag_edges() with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < 256 { FADJ[i as usize] = 0  i = i + 1 }
    i = 0
    while i < NF {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < NF {
            if frag_is_unit(frag_dist2(i, j)) == 1 {
                FADJ[(i*16 + j) as usize] = 1
                FADJ[(j*16 + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn frag_count_edges() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var c = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < NF {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < NF {
            if FADJ[(i*16 + j) as usize] == 1 { c = c + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return c
}

// Native CDCL k-colorability of the fragment (NF vertices). 1=SAT, 0=UNSAT.
fn sat_kcolorable(k: i64) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var ctx = smt_new()
    var v: i64 = 0
    while v < NF {
        var lits: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
        var c: i64 = 0
        while c < k {
            lits[c as usize] = ((v*k + c + 1)*2 + 1) as i32
            c = c + 1
        }
        smt_add_clause(&! ctx, &lits, k as i32)
        v = v + 1
    }
    v = 0
    while v < NF {
        var c1: i64 = 0
        while c1 < k {
            var c2: i64 = c1 + 1
            while c2 < k {
                var lp: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
                lp[0] = ((v*k + c1 + 1)*2) as i32
                lp[1] = ((v*k + c2 + 1)*2) as i32
                smt_add_clause(&! ctx, &lp, 2)
                c2 = c2 + 1
            }
            c1 = c1 + 1
        }
        v = v + 1
    }
    var u: i64 = 0
    while u < NF {
        var w: i64 = u + 1
        while w < NF {
            if FADJ[(u*16 + w) as usize] == 1 {
                var c: i64 = 0
                while c < k {
                    var le: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
                    le[0] = ((u*k + c + 1)*2) as i32
                    le[1] = ((w*k + c + 1)*2) as i32
                    smt_add_clause(&! ctx, &le, 2)
                    c = c + 1
                }
            }
            w = w + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    smt_set_score_mode(&! ctx, 3)
    smt_set_no_ple(&! ctx, 1)
    return smt_solve(&! ctx)
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("=== Erdős #508 — field closure of de Grey-style spindle gluing ===\n")
    print("(two spindles glued at the apex by a 60° rotation; exact Q(√3,√11), scale ×24)\n\n")

    setup_base()
    NF = 0
    add_rotated_spindle(0)   // base spindle (identity, scale ×2)
    add_rotated_spindle(1)   // second spindle = base rotated 60° about apex A

    print("fragment vertices (after dedup of shared apex): "); print_int(NF); print("\n")
    build_frag_edges()
    let e = frag_count_edges()
    print("unit edges (dist² = 576 exactly, all √-parts 0): "); print_int(e); print("\n")
    let ns = count_surd_distances()
    print("pairs whose dist² carries a surd (still exact in-field, informational): ")
    print_int(ns); print("\n\n")

    print("FIELD CLOSURE: every vertex is an exact Q(√3,√11) 4-tuple and every unit\n")
    print("edge has dist² = 576 with zero √3/√11/√33 components. The 60° rotation\n")
    print("introduced NO auxiliary surd — gluing stays inside Q(√3,√11). (R_60 and\n")
    print("R_φ both have entries in the field, so any composition does too.)\n\n")

    let s3 = sat_kcolorable(3)
    let s4 = sat_kcolorable(4)
    print("native SAT: 3-coloring = ")
    if s3 == 1 { print("SAT") } else { print("UNSAT") }
    print("  4-coloring = ")
    if s4 == 1 { print("SAT") } else { print("UNSAT") }
    print("\n")
    if s3 == 0 {
        print("=> glued graph still contains a 4-chromatic spindle (3-col UNSAT),\n")
        print("   certified natively. Field-closed exact gluing + native χ certificate:\n")
        print("   the de Grey assembly path, end-to-end inside Sounio.\n")
    }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/erdos/degrey_geometry.sio ===
// examples/erdos/degrey_geometry.sio
//
// PART B of the chi(R^2) >= 5 flagship: EXACT unit-distance certification.
//
// Reads the exact algebraic coordinates of Heule's 529-vertex de Grey core
// (data/degrey_529.vtx, Mathematica points over Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11)) and its
// edge list (data/degrey_529.edge), and certifies that EVERY edge has squared
// distance exactly 1 -- with no floating point. Together with Part A
// (souc_sat.sio: G_529 is not 4-colourable, drat-trim s VERIFIED) this proves
// G_529 is a unit-distance graph with chromatic number >= 5, hence chi(R^2) >= 5.
//
// FIELD. The coordinates live in Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt11): a degree-8 field with
// Q-basis  b[mask] = sqrt(prod of primes selected by mask),  mask in 0..7 over
// {3,5,11}.  We embed it in the existing degree-16 basis of degrey_fieldtower.sio
// (bit0=sqrt3, bit1=sqrt5, bit2=sqrt7, bit3=sqrt11) so sqrt7 simply never occurs.
// Multiplication is XOR on masks with a rational coefficient = product of shared
// primes:  sqrt(prod S) * sqrt(prod T) = (prod_{p in S&T} p) * sqrt(prod (S^T)).
// A field element is an integer 16-tuple c[] over a common positive denominator d.
//
// All denominators in the .vtx involve only sqrt3 (e.g. 1/(16*Sqrt[3])) or are
// rational, and 1/sqrt3 = sqrt3/3, so division never needs a general inverse.
//
// Self-contained.  Run:  $SOUC run examples/erdos/degrey_geometry.sio
// (set SOUNIO_SOUC_BIN to the native self-hosted ELF first).

struct QF { c: [i64; 16], d: i64 }

// ---- integer helpers ----
fn igcd(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x = a  var y = b
    if x < 0 { x = 0 - x }
    if y < 0 { y = 0 - y }
    while y != 0 { let t = x % y  x = y  y = t }
    return x
}

// product of primes selected by mask bits (bit0=3,bit1=5,bit2=7,bit3=11)
fn bcoeff(mask: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var p = 1
    if (mask & 1) != 0 { p = p * 3 }
    if (mask & 2) != 0 { p = p * 5 }
    if (mask & 4) != 0 { p = p * 7 }
    if (mask & 8) != 0 { p = p * 11 }
    return p
}

// ---- field constructors ----
fn qf_zero() -> QF with Mut, Panic { return QF { c: [0; 16], d: 1 } }
fn qf_rat(v: i64) -> QF with Mut, Panic { var r = QF { c: [0; 16], d: 1 }  r.c[0] = v  return r }
fn qf_mono(idx: i64, v: i64) -> QF with Mut, Panic { var r = QF { c: [0; 16], d: 1 }  r.c[idx as usize] = v  return r }

// gcd-reduce all numerators with the denominator; keep d > 0.
fn qf_reduce(x: QF) -> QF with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = x
    if r.d < 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < 16 { r.c[i as usize] = 0 - r.c[i as usize]  i = i + 1 }
        r.d = 0 - r.d
    }
    var g = r.d
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { g = igcd(g, r.c[i as usize])  i = i + 1 }
    if g > 1 {
        i = 0
        while i < 16 { r.c[i as usize] = r.c[i as usize] / g  i = i + 1 }
        r.d = r.d / g
    }
    return r
}

fn qf_neg(x: QF) -> QF with Mut, Panic {
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { r.c[i as usize] = 0 - r.c[i as usize]  i = i + 1 }
    return r
}

fn qf_add(x: QF, y: QF) -> QF with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = QF { c: [0; 16], d: x.d * y.d }
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        r.c[i as usize] = x.c[i as usize] * y.d + y.c[i as usize] * x.d
        i = i + 1
    }
    return qf_reduce(r)
}

fn qf_sub(x: QF, y: QF) -> QF with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = QF { c: [0; 16], d: x.d * y.d }
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        r.c[i as usize] = x.c[i as usize] * y.d - y.c[i as usize] * x.d
        i = i + 1
    }
    return qf_reduce(r)
}

// (prod S)*(prod T): result basis i^j, coeff = product of shared primes. O(16^2).
fn qf_mul(x: QF, y: QF) -> QF with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = QF { c: [0; 16], d: x.d * y.d }
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        if x.c[i as usize] != 0 {
            var j = 0
            while j < 16 {
                if y.c[j as usize] != 0 {
                    let coeff = bcoeff(i & j)
                    let idx = (i ^ j) as usize
                    r.c[idx] = r.c[idx] + x.c[i as usize] * y.c[j as usize] * coeff
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return qf_reduce(r)
}

fn qf_scal_mul(x: QF, k: i64) -> QF with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { r.c[i as usize] = r.c[i as usize] * k  i = i + 1 }
    return qf_reduce(r)
}

fn qf_scal_div(x: QF, k: i64) -> QF with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = x
    var kk = k
    if kk < 0 { r = qf_neg(r)  kk = 0 - kk }
    r.d = r.d * kk
    return qf_reduce(r)
}

// number of nonzero surd components beyond the rational part
fn qf_only_index(x: QF) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    // returns -1 if more than one nonzero component, else the single nonzero index
    var found: i64 = 0 - 1
    var cnt = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 {
        if x.c[i as usize] != 0 { cnt = cnt + 1  found = i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if cnt == 0 { return 0 }      // zero -> treat as rational index 0
    if cnt == 1 { return found }
    return 0 - 2                  // multi-term: needs general inverse (not in data)
}

// Divide V by F where F is rational (index 0) or a pure multiple of sqrt3 (index 1).
// rational a/F.d:  V / (a/F.d) = V * F.d / a.
// b*sqrt3/F.d:     V / (b*sqrt3/F.d) = V * F.d * sqrt3 / (3b)   (since 1/sqrt3 = sqrt3/3).
var DIV_ERR: i32 = 0
fn qf_div(v: QF, f: QF) -> QF with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let fr = qf_reduce(f)
    let oi = qf_only_index(fr)
    if oi == 0 {
        let a = fr.c[0]
        return qf_scal_div(qf_scal_mul(v, fr.d), a)
    }
    if oi == 1 {
        let b = fr.c[1]
        let v3 = qf_mul(v, qf_mono(1, 1))     // V * sqrt3
        return qf_scal_div(qf_scal_mul(v3, fr.d), 3 * b)
    }
    DIV_ERR = 1
    return v
}

fn qf_is_one(x: QF) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = qf_reduce(x)
    if r.c[0] != r.d { return 0 }
    var i = 1
    while i < 16 { if r.c[i as usize] != 0 { return 0 }  i = i + 1 }
    return 1
}

// sqrt of the rational p/q, returned as a field element. sqrt(p/q)=sqrt(p*q)/q;
// pull square factors out of p*q, then map the squarefree radical onto {3,5,11}.
var SQRT_ERR: i32 = 0
fn sqrt_of_rational(p: i64, q: i64) -> QF with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var val = p * q
    var s: i64 = 1
    var f: i64 = 2
    while f * f <= val {
        while val % (f * f) == 0 { val = val / (f * f)  s = s * f }
        f = f + 1
    }
    var mask: i64 = 0
    if val % 3 == 0 { mask = mask | 1   val = val / 3 }
    if val % 5 == 0 { mask = mask | 2   val = val / 5 }
    if val % 11 == 0 { mask = mask | 8  val = val / 11 }
    if val != 1 { SQRT_ERR = 1 }          // radical outside Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11)
    return qf_scal_div(qf_mono(mask, s), q)
}

// ===== file reader (syscalls) =====
var RB: [i8; 1048576] = [0; 1048576]
var RBlen: i64 = 0
var PPOS: i64 = 0

fn read_file(path: string) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic {
    let fd = syscall6(2, path, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)        // open O_RDONLY
    if fd < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    let n = syscall6(0, fd, &! RB, 1048576, 0, 0, 0) // read
    let _ = syscall6(3, fd, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)           // close
    RBlen = n
    PPOS = 0
    return n
}

fn cur() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    if PPOS >= RBlen { return 0 - 1 }
    return RB[PPOS as usize] as i64
}
fn skip_spaces() with Mut, Panic {
    while PPOS < RBlen { let c = RB[PPOS as usize] as i64  if c == 32 { PPOS = PPOS + 1 } else { break } }
}
fn parse_uint() -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    skip_spaces()
    var v: i64 = 0
    while PPOS < RBlen {
        let c = RB[PPOS as usize] as i64
        if c < 48 { break }
        if c > 57 { break }
        v = v * 10 + (c - 48)
        PPOS = PPOS + 1
    }
    return v
}

// ===== recursive-descent expression parser over Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11) =====
// Helpers must precede callers; forward recursion is via a hand-rolled split:
// parse_factor calls parse_expr through a trampoline flag is impossible, so we
// inline the grammar with the standard expr->term->factor chain, and let
// parse_factor handle '(' by calling parse_expr (defined after) — Sounio needs
// definition-before-use, so we order factor last and pre-declare via mutual
// structure: we implement a single parse_expr that contains nested loops.

fn parse_sqrt() -> QF with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    while cur() != 91 { PPOS = PPOS + 1 }    // skip "Sqrt", stop at '['
    PPOS = PPOS + 1                          // consume '['
    let p = parse_uint()
    var q: i64 = 1
    if cur() == 47 { PPOS = PPOS + 1  q = parse_uint() }   // '/'
    while cur() != 93 { PPOS = PPOS + 1 }    // stop at ']'
    PPOS = PPOS + 1                          // consume ']'
    return sqrt_of_rational(p, q)
}

// Evaluate the expression starting at PPOS until a top-level ',' '}' ')' or EOF.
// Implements +,-,*,/, unary minus, integers, Sqrt[...], and '(' ... ')'.
fn parse_expr() -> QF with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Shunting-yard-lite over the field: we accumulate sum of terms; each term is
    // a product/quotient of factors. Parens recurse by counting depth manually.
    var acc = qf_zero()         // running sum
    var term = qf_rat(1)        // running product for the current term
    var have_term: i32 = 0      // whether term has a real factor yet
    var add_sign: i64 = 1       // +1 / -1 to apply when flushing the term into acc
    var pend_div: i32 = 0       // next factor is a divisor
    var fneg: i32 = 0           // unary minus pending on the next factor
    var go: i32 = 1
    while go == 1 {
        skip_spaces()
        let c = cur()
        if c < 0 { go = 0 }
        else if c == 44 { go = 0 }            // ','
        else if c == 125 { go = 0 }           // '}'
        else if c == 41 { go = 0 }            // ')'
        else if c == 43 {                     // '+'
            if have_term == 1 { acc = qf_add(acc, qf_scal_mul(term, add_sign)) }
            term = qf_rat(1)  have_term = 0  add_sign = 1  pend_div = 0  fneg = 0
            PPOS = PPOS + 1
        }
        else if c == 45 {                     // '-'
            if have_term == 1 {
                acc = qf_add(acc, qf_scal_mul(term, add_sign))
                term = qf_rat(1)  have_term = 0  add_sign = 1  pend_div = 0  fneg = 0
                add_sign = 0 - 1
            } else {
                // unary minus on the forthcoming factor
                fneg = 1 - fneg
            }
            PPOS = PPOS + 1
        }
        else if c == 42 {                     // '*'
            pend_div = 0  PPOS = PPOS + 1
        }
        else if c == 47 {                     // '/'
            pend_div = 1  PPOS = PPOS + 1
        }
        else {
            // a factor: integer, Sqrt[...], or '(' expr ')'
            var fac = qf_zero()
            if c == 40 {                      // '('
                PPOS = PPOS + 1
                fac = parse_expr()
                skip_spaces()
                if cur() == 41 { PPOS = PPOS + 1 }   // consume ')'
            } else if c == 83 {               // 'S' (Sqrt)
                fac = parse_sqrt()
            } else {
                fac = qf_rat(parse_uint())
            }
            if fneg == 1 { fac = qf_neg(fac)  fneg = 0 }
            if have_term == 0 { term = fac  have_term = 1 }
            else if pend_div == 1 { term = qf_div(term, fac)  pend_div = 0 }
            else { term = qf_mul(term, fac) }
        }
    }
    if have_term == 1 { acc = qf_add(acc, qf_scal_mul(term, add_sign)) }
    return acc
}

// ===== vertex / edge storage =====
var NV: i64 = 0
var XC: [i64; 9600] = [0; 9600]    // 600 * 16
var XD: [i64; 600] = [0; 600]
var YC: [i64; 9600] = [0; 9600]
var YD: [i64; 600] = [0; 600]

fn store_xy(v: i64, x: QF, y: QF) with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { XC[(v * 16 + i) as usize] = x.c[i as usize]  YC[(v * 16 + i) as usize] = y.c[i as usize]  i = i + 1 }
    XD[v as usize] = x.d
    YD[v as usize] = y.d
}
fn load_x(v: i64) -> QF with Mut, Panic {
    var r = QF { c: [0; 16], d: XD[v as usize] }
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { r.c[i as usize] = XC[(v * 16 + i) as usize]  i = i + 1 }
    return r
}
fn load_y(v: i64) -> QF with Mut, Panic {
    var r = QF { c: [0; 16], d: YD[v as usize] }
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { r.c[i as usize] = YC[(v * 16 + i) as usize]  i = i + 1 }
    return r
}

// Parse the whole .vtx buffer: a sequence of "{ x , y }" lines.
fn load_vtx() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    NV = 0
    var go: i32 = 1
    while go == 1 {
        // advance to next '{'
        while PPOS < RBlen { if RB[PPOS as usize] as i64 == 123 { break }  PPOS = PPOS + 1 }
        if PPOS >= RBlen { go = 0 }
        else {
            PPOS = PPOS + 1                 // consume '{'
            let x = parse_expr()
            skip_spaces()
            if cur() == 44 { PPOS = PPOS + 1 }   // ','
            let y = parse_expr()
            skip_spaces()
            if cur() == 125 { PPOS = PPOS + 1 }  // '}'
            if NV < 600 { store_xy(NV, x, y)  NV = NV + 1 }
        }
    }
    return NV
}

fn gnext_int() -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    while PPOS < RBlen {
        let c = RB[PPOS as usize] as i64
        if c >= 48 { if c <= 57 { break } }
        PPOS = PPOS + 1
    }
    if PPOS >= RBlen { return 0 - 1 }
    var v: i64 = 0
    while PPOS < RBlen {
        let c = RB[PPOS as usize] as i64
        if c < 48 { break }
        if c > 57 { break }
        v = v * 10 + (c - 48)
        PPOS = PPOS + 1
    }
    return v
}

fn print_dec(n: i64) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    if n == 0 { print("0")  return }
    var x = n
    if x < 0 { print("-")  x = 0 - x }
    var tmp: [i64; 24] = [0; 24]
    var len: i32 = 0
    while x > 0 { tmp[len as usize] = x % 10  x = x / 10  len = len + 1 }
    var i = len - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        let d = tmp[i as usize]
        if d == 0 { print("0") } else if d == 1 { print("1") } else if d == 2 { print("2") }
        else if d == 3 { print("3") } else if d == 4 { print("4") } else if d == 5 { print("5") }
        else if d == 6 { print("6") } else if d == 7 { print("7") } else if d == 8 { print("8") }
        else { print("9") }
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// Emit the parsed coordinates + edge list as Lean data defs (Array QF over the
// degree-16 basis, denominator kept). A static Lean kernel+theorem wraps this so
// `lean` re-checks dist^2=1 for every edge by native_decide. The Sounio parse is the
// single source of truth for the coordinates. Uses the QF/VPair abbrevs from the
// static header to avoid the unicode product symbol in emitted text.
fn emit_arr(isX: i32, nv: i64) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var v: i64 = 0
    while v < nv {
        print("([")
        var i = 0
        while i < 16 {
            if isX == 1 { print_dec(XC[(v * 16 + i) as usize]) } else { print_dec(YC[(v * 16 + i) as usize]) }
            if i < 15 { print(",") }
            i = i + 1
        }
        print("],")
        if isX == 1 { print_dec(XD[v as usize]) } else { print_dec(YD[v as usize]) }
        print("),\n")
        v = v + 1
    }
}

fn emit_lean_full() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if read_file("examples/erdos/data/degrey_529.vtx") < 0 { print("-- cannot read vtx\n")  return }
    let nv = load_vtx()
    print("def X : Array QF := #[\n")
    emit_arr(1, nv)
    print("]\n\n")
    print("def Y : Array QF := #[\n")
    emit_arr(0, nv)
    print("]\n\n")
    if read_file("examples/erdos/data/degrey_529.edge") < 0 { print("-- cannot read edge\n")  return }
    let gN = gnext_int()
    let gM = gnext_int()
    print("def edges : Array VPair := #[\n")
    var e: i64 = 0
    while e < gM {
        let u = gnext_int()
        let w = gnext_int()
        if u < 1 { break }
        print("(")  print_dec(u - 1)  print(",")  print_dec(w - 1)  print("),\n")
        e = e + 1
    }
    print("]\n")
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if arg_count() >= 1 { emit_lean_full()  return 0 }
    print("=== Part B: exact unit-distance certification of G_529 over Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11) ===\n")

    if read_file("examples/erdos/data/degrey_529.vtx") < 0 {
        print("cannot read degrey_529.vtx\n")  return 1
    }
    let nv = load_vtx()
    print("vertices parsed: ")  print_dec(nv)  print("\n")
    if SQRT_ERR == 1 { print("[FATAL] a Sqrt fell outside Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11)\n")  return 1 }
    if DIV_ERR == 1 { print("[FATAL] a division needed a general field inverse\n")  return 1 }

    // self-test: vertex 0 = (0,0), vertex 1 = (1,0): dist^2 must be exactly 1
    let d01 = qf_add(qf_mul(qf_sub(load_x(0), load_x(1)), qf_sub(load_x(0), load_x(1))),
                     qf_mul(qf_sub(load_y(0), load_y(1)), qf_sub(load_y(0), load_y(1))))
    print("self-test dist^2(v0,v1) is 1: ")  print_dec(qf_is_one(d01))  print("\n")

    if read_file("examples/erdos/data/degrey_529.edge") < 0 {
        print("cannot read degrey_529.edge\n")  return 1
    }
    let gN = gnext_int()
    let gM = gnext_int()
    print("edge header: N=")  print_dec(gN)  print(" M=")  print_dec(gM)  print("\n")

    var pass: i64 = 0
    var fail: i64 = 0
    var e: i64 = 0
    while e < gM {
        let u = gnext_int()
        let w = gnext_int()
        if u < 1 { break }
        let a = u - 1
        let b = w - 1
        let dx = qf_sub(load_x(a), load_x(b))
        let dy = qf_sub(load_y(a), load_y(b))
        let d2 = qf_add(qf_mul(dx, dx), qf_mul(dy, dy))
        if qf_is_one(d2) == 1 { pass = pass + 1 }
        else {
            fail = fail + 1
            if fail <= 5 {
                print("  [FAIL] edge ")  print_dec(u)  print("-")  print_dec(w)
                print(" dist^2 not 1\n")
            }
        }
        e = e + 1
    }

    print("\nedges checked: ")  print_dec(pass + fail)
    print("   dist^2 == 1: ")  print_dec(pass)
    print("   FAIL: ")  print_dec(fail)  print("\n")
    if fail == 0 {
        print("PROVEN (exact, no floats): G_529 is a unit-distance graph.\n")
        print("With Part A (chi(G_529) >= 5, drat-trim VERIFIED): chi(R^2) >= 5.\n")
    }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/erdos/degrey_q3q11_spindle.sio ===
// examples/erdos/degrey_q3q11_spindle.sio
//
// BOLD LINE on Erdős #508 (chromatic number of the plane, currently 5 ≤ χ ≤ 7).
//
// The prior Sounio attack caged itself in INTEGER coordinates Z^16, where
// "dist² == 1" forces bipartiteness (χ ≤ 2) by a Hamming-parity 2-coloring —
// a self-imposed ceiling. The honest reviewer finding (xai math-review,
// 2026-05-28) is that exactness for unit-distance work does NOT live in Z; it
// lives in a real NUMBER FIELD. The hard graphs (Moser spindle, de Grey's
// 5-chromatic graph) are realized exactly over Q(√3, √11).
//
// de Grey's 1581-vertex 5-chromatic graph is ASSEMBLED FROM Moser spindles.
// This file builds the atomic piece — the Moser spindle — with EXACT arithmetic
// in Q(√3, √11). NOTE (xai math-review, 2026-05-28): the spindle and the 60° /
// arccos(5/6) rotations provably stay in Q(√3,√11), but it is NOT yet verified
// that gluing spindles at non-Moser vertices keeps the full de Grey graph inside
// this field (an auxiliary surd may appear). That field check is the first task
// when scaling. What is established here:
//   (1) every unit edge has squared distance exactly 1 (a rational; the √3, √11,
//       √33 components cancel to zero — verified, not approximated);
//   (2) the chromatic number χ = 4 is computed by exact brute force (no floats,
//       native_decide-able), refuting the prior plan's claim that the spindle's
//       irrational coordinates "break exactness".
//
// FIELD REPRESENTATION. A number a + b√3 + c√11 + d√33 (note √33 = √3·√11) is the
// integer 4-tuple (a, b, c, d). Multiplication table:
//   √3·√3=3  √11·√11=11  √33·√33=33  √3·√11=√33  √3·√33=3√11  √11·√33=11√3
//
// SPINDLE CONSTRUCTION (two unit rhombi sharing apex A, rotated by φ with
// cos φ = 5/6, sin φ = √11/6 so the far vertices C,F land at unit distance).
// All coordinates scaled by 12 to clear denominators ⇒ unit distance = 12,
// unit squared-distance target = 144. Vertices A,B,C,D (rhombus 1) and
// A,E,F,G (rhombus 2 = rhombus 1 rotated by φ), with the edge C–F closing it.
//
// Native SAT/UNSAT: the chromatic certificate is produced INSIDE Sounio (no
// external SAT solver, no third-party DRAT). χ=4 is certified two independent
// ways: (a) exact base-k brute force, and (b) the native CDCL solver
// theorem::smt — 3-coloring is UNSAT, 4-coloring is SAT. Route (b) is the
// scalable mechanism that templates directly to de Grey's graph (the only limit
// today is the solver's 64-variable cap; de Grey scale needs that grown, but the
// path stays native and self-certifying).

use theorem::smt::*

struct Qf { a: i64, b: i64, c: i64, d: i64 }

fn qadd(x: Qf, y: Qf) -> Qf {
    return Qf { a: x.a + y.a, b: x.b + y.b, c: x.c + y.c, d: x.d + y.d }
}

fn qsub(x: Qf, y: Qf) -> Qf {
    return Qf { a: x.a - y.a, b: x.b - y.b, c: x.c - y.c, d: x.d - y.d }
}

// (a+b√3+c√11+d√33)(a'+b'√3+c'√11+d'√33), reduced via the table above.
fn qmul(x: Qf, y: Qf) -> Qf {
    let ra  = x.a*y.a + 3*x.b*y.b + 11*x.c*y.c + 33*x.d*y.d
    let r3  = x.a*y.b + y.a*x.b + 11*(x.c*y.d + y.c*x.d)
    let r11 = x.a*y.c + y.a*x.c + 3*(x.b*y.d + y.b*x.d)
    let r33 = x.a*y.d + y.a*x.d + x.b*y.c + y.b*x.c
    return Qf { a: ra, b: r3, c: r11, d: r33 }
}

fn qsq(x: Qf) -> Qf { return qmul(x, x) }

// ============================================================================
// The 7 spindle vertices, scaled ×12, as exact Q(√3,√11) coordinates.
// Index: A=0 B=1 C=2 D=3 E=4 F=5 G=6.
// ============================================================================

var XA: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]   // x: rational part
var XB: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]   // x: √3 part
var XC: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]   // x: √11 part
var XD: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]   // x: √33 part
var YA: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]   // y: rational part
var YB: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]   // y: √3 part
var YC: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]   // y: √11 part
var YD: [i64; 7] = [0; 7]   // y: √33 part

var ADJ:    [i64; 49] = [0; 49]
var COLORS: [i64; 7]  = [0; 7]

fn setup_points() with Mut, Panic {
    // A = (0, 0)
    XA[0] = 0  XB[0] = 0       XC[0] = 0       XD[0] = 0
    YA[0] = 0  YB[0] = 0       YC[0] = 0       YD[0] = 0
    // B = (√3/2, 1/2)  ×12 → (6√3, 6)
    XA[1] = 0  XB[1] = 6       XC[1] = 0       XD[1] = 0
    YA[1] = 6  YB[1] = 0       YC[1] = 0       YD[1] = 0
    // C = (√3, 0)  ×12 → (12√3, 0)
    XA[2] = 0  XB[2] = 12      XC[2] = 0       XD[2] = 0
    YA[2] = 0  YB[2] = 0       YC[2] = 0       YD[2] = 0
    // D = (√3/2, -1/2)  ×12 → (6√3, -6)
    XA[3] = 0  XB[3] = 6       XC[3] = 0       XD[3] = 0
    YA[3] = 0 - 6  YB[3] = 0   YC[3] = 0       YD[3] = 0
    // E = Rφ·B = (5√3/12 - √11/12, √33/12 + 5/12)  ×12 → (5√3 - √11, 5 + √33)
    XA[4] = 0  XB[4] = 5       XC[4] = 0 - 1   XD[4] = 0
    YA[4] = 5  YB[4] = 0       YC[4] = 0       YD[4] = 1
    // F = Rφ·C = (5√3/6, √33/6)  ×12 → (10√3, 2√33)
    XA[5] = 0  XB[5] = 10      XC[5] = 0       XD[5] = 0
    YA[5] = 0  YB[5] = 0       YC[5] = 0       YD[5] = 2
    // G = Rφ·D = (5√3/12 + √11/12, √33/12 - 5/12)  ×12 → (5√3 + √11, √33 - 5)
    XA[6] = 0  XB[6] = 5       XC[6] = 1       XD[6] = 0
    YA[6] = 0 - 5  YB[6] = 0   YC[6] = 0       YD[6] = 1
}

fn get_x(i: i64) -> Qf with Panic {
    return Qf { a: XA[i as usize], b: XB[i as usize], c: XC[i as usize], d: XD[i as usize] }
}

fn get_y(i: i64) -> Qf with Panic {
    return Qf { a: YA[i as usize], b: YB[i as usize], c: YC[i as usize], d: YD[i as usize] }
}

// Squared Euclidean distance as an exact Q(√3,√11) element.
fn dist2(i: i64, j: i64) -> Qf with Panic {
    let dx = qsub(get_x(i), get_x(j))
    let dy = qsub(get_y(i), get_y(j))
    return qadd(qsq(dx), qsq(dy))
}

// Unit edge ⟺ dist² is EXACTLY the rational 1 (scaled 144); the irrational
// √3/√11/√33 components must all vanish.
fn is_unit(d: Qf) -> i64 {
    if d.a == 144 && d.b == 0 && d.c == 0 && d.d == 0 { return 1 }
    return 0
}

fn build_edges() with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < 7 {
        var j = 0
        while j < 7 {
            ADJ[(i*7 + j) as usize] = 0
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < 7 {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < 7 {
            if is_unit(dist2(i, j)) == 1 {
                ADJ[(i*7 + j) as usize] = 1
                ADJ[(j*7 + i) as usize] = 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn count_edges() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var c = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < 7 {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < 7 {
            if ADJ[(i*7 + j) as usize] == 1 { c = c + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return c
}

// Proper k-colorability of ADJ (7 vertices) by exact base-k odometer brute force.
fn colorable(k: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < 7 { COLORS[i as usize] = 0  i = i + 1 }
    var done = 0
    while done == 0 {
        var ok = 1
        var a = 0
        while a < 7 {
            var b = a + 1
            while b < 7 {
                if ADJ[(a*7 + b) as usize] == 1 {
                    if COLORS[a as usize] == COLORS[b as usize] { ok = 0 }
                }
                b = b + 1
            }
            a = a + 1
        }
        if ok == 1 { return 1 }
        var pos = 0
        var carry = 1
        while pos < 7 && carry == 1 {
            COLORS[pos as usize] = COLORS[pos as usize] + 1
            if COLORS[pos as usize] >= k {
                COLORS[pos as usize] = 0
                pos = pos + 1
            } else {
                carry = 0
            }
        }
        if carry == 1 { done = 1 }
    }
    return 0
}

fn chromatic_number() -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var k = 1
    while k <= 7 {
        if colorable(k) == 1 { return k }
        k = k + 1
    }
    return 7
}

// Native CDCL k-colorability of ADJ (7 vertices). Returns smt_solve: 1=SAT, 0=UNSAT.
// 1-indexed vars: var(v,c) = v*k + c + 1 ; positive lit = var*2+1, negative = var*2.
// This is the SAME encoding de Grey's graph needs — only bigger (k*V vars).
fn sat_kcolorable(k: i64) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var ctx = smt_new()
    // at-least-one color per vertex
    var v: i64 = 0
    while v < 7 {
        var lits: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
        var c: i64 = 0
        while c < k {
            lits[c as usize] = ((v*k + c + 1)*2 + 1) as i32
            c = c + 1
        }
        smt_add_clause(&! ctx, &lits, k as i32)
        v = v + 1
    }
    // at-most-one color per vertex (pairwise negative clauses)
    v = 0
    while v < 7 {
        var c1: i64 = 0
        while c1 < k {
            var c2: i64 = c1 + 1
            while c2 < k {
                var lp: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
                lp[0] = ((v*k + c1 + 1)*2) as i32
                lp[1] = ((v*k + c2 + 1)*2) as i32
                smt_add_clause(&! ctx, &lp, 2)
                c2 = c2 + 1
            }
            c1 = c1 + 1
        }
        v = v + 1
    }
    // edge constraints: adjacent vertices cannot share a color
    var u: i64 = 0
    while u < 7 {
        var w: i64 = u + 1
        while w < 7 {
            if ADJ[(u*7 + w) as usize] == 1 {
                var c: i64 = 0
                while c < k {
                    var le: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
                    le[0] = ((u*k + c + 1)*2) as i32
                    le[1] = ((w*k + c + 1)*2) as i32
                    smt_add_clause(&! ctx, &le, 2)
                    c = c + 1
                }
            }
            w = w + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    smt_set_score_mode(&! ctx, 3)
    smt_set_no_ple(&! ctx, 1)
    return smt_solve(&! ctx)
}

fn print_edge(i: i64, j: i64) with IO, Panic {
    let d = dist2(i, j)
    print("  edge (")
    print_int(i); print(","); print_int(j)
    print(")  dist2 = ")
    print_int(d.a); print(" + "); print_int(d.b); print("*r3 + ")
    print_int(d.c); print("*r11 + "); print_int(d.d); print("*r33\n")
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic {
    print("=== Erdős #508 — exact Moser spindle over Q(√3, √11) ===\n")
    print("(scaled ×12; unit distance² target = 144; de Grey's atomic building block)\n\n")

    setup_points()
    build_edges()

    let e = count_edges()
    print("vertices: 7   unit edges: "); print_int(e)
    print("  (expected 11 = Moser spindle)\n\n")

    print("Exact unit edges — note every √3/√11/√33 component is 0 (rational 144):\n")
    var i = 0
    while i < 7 {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < 7 {
            if ADJ[(i*7 + j) as usize] == 1 { print_edge(i, j) }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    print("\nSanity (non-edges keep irrational parts / wrong rational):\n")
    print_edge(0, 2)   // A–C: the √3 long diagonal, dist² = 432 = 144·3
    print_edge(0, 5)   // A–F: rotated long diagonal, dist² = 432

    let chi = chromatic_number()
    print("\nchi(spindle) = "); print_int(chi); print("  (route a: exact brute force over 4^7)\n")

    // Route (b): native CDCL SAT/UNSAT — the de Grey-scale mechanism, no external solver.
    let s3 = sat_kcolorable(3)
    let s4 = sat_kcolorable(4)
    print("native SAT: 3-coloring = ")
    if s3 == 1 { print("SAT") } else { print("UNSAT") }
    print("  4-coloring = ")
    if s4 == 1 { print("SAT") } else { print("UNSAT") }
    print("\n")
    if s3 == 0 && s4 == 1 {
        print("=> chi=4 CERTIFIED natively: 3-col UNSAT (no 4th color avoidable) + 4-col SAT.\n")
        print("   The UNSAT certificate is produced INSIDE Sounio. This is exactly the\n")
        print("   de Grey mechanism: realize the graph exactly, then certify χ≥5 by a\n")
        print("   native 4-coloring UNSAT. Today's only gap is the solver's 64-var cap.\n")
    }

    if chi == 4 {
        print("RESULT: χ = 4 proved over EXACT Q(√3,√11) coordinates — the prior plan's\n")
        print("claim that the spindle's irrationals 'break native exactness' is REFUTED.\n")
        print("The cage was Z, not the problem. The spindle and its 60°/arccos(5/6)\n")
        print("rotations stay in Q(√3,√11); scaling toward de Grey's 5-chromatic graph\n")
        print("needs a check that gluing spindles at non-Moser vertices introduces no\n")
        print("auxiliary surd (xai math-review 2026-05-28 flagged this as unverified).\n")
    }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/erdos/dpll_scale_wall.sio ===
// examples/erdos/dpll_scale_wall.sio
//
// SCALING ENVELOPE of the native DPLL->DRUP certifier (the Erdős #508 χ≥5 path).
//
// Honest finding behind this file: a 3-coloring UNSAT certificate for ANY graph
// that CONTAINS a Moser spindle is refuted by the 7-vertex spindle alone, so it
// stays tiny no matter how large the host graph is (it is a LOCAL contradiction).
// The chromatic regime that actually matters for χ(ℝ²) ≥ 5 is a *4-coloring
// UNSAT* on de Grey's ~510-vertex graph — an instance whose unsatisfiability needs
// the WHOLE graph, not a local core.
//
// This file measures how far the chronological-backtracking DPLL->DRUP emitter
// scales on a HARD, fully global UNSAT family: k-coloring the complete graph K_n
// with k = n-1 colors. That CNF is exactly the pigeonhole principle PHP(n, n-1),
// for which resolution (hence any tree-resolution DPLL refutation) has a proven
// EXPONENTIAL lower bound (Haken 1985). So the emitted DRUP proof size must blow
// up — empirically pinning the wall and proving WHY clause learning (CDCL) is
// required to reach the de Grey scale.
//
// Each completed certificate is checked by our native RUP checker; one is also
// emitted as DIMACS+DRAT for external drat-trim. A node budget bails gracefully
// at the wall (reported as WALL, not a crash).
//
// All integer arithmetic. Flat GLOBAL arrays (no large struct returns).

let NODE_LIMIT: i64 = 3000000
let LEMMA_CAP: i32 = 500000

// ---- clause DB (the formula; lemmas are appended during checking) ----
var G_nvars: i32 = 0
var G_nclauses: i32 = 0
var G_cstart: [i32; 524288] = [0; 524288]
var G_clen: [i32; 524288] = [0; 524288]
var G_lits: [i64; 1048576] = [0; 1048576]
var G_assign: [i32; 1024] = [0; 1024]

// ---- DRUP proof ----
var P_n: i32 = 0
var P_start: [i32; 524288] = [0; 524288]
var P_len: [i32; 524288] = [0; 524288]
var P_lits: [i64; 1048576] = [0; 1048576]

// ---- search scratch ----
var DEC: [i64; 1024] = [0; 1024]
var NODE_COUNT: i64 = 0
var BAILED: i32 = 0

fn lit_var(l: i64) -> i32 with Panic {
    if l < 0 { return (0 - l) as i32 }
    return l as i32
}

fn g_add_clause(arr: &[i64; 16], n: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    if G_nclauses >= 524288 { return }
    let idx = G_nclauses
    var start: i32 = 0
    if idx > 0 { start = G_cstart[idx - 1] + G_clen[idx - 1] }
    if (start as i64) + (n as i64) > 1048576 { return }
    G_cstart[idx] = start
    G_clen[idx] = n
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        G_lits[start + i] = arr[i]
        let v = lit_var(arr[i])
        if v > G_nvars { G_nvars = v }
        i = i + 1
    }
    G_nclauses = idx + 1
}

fn propagate() -> i32 with Mut, Panic {
    var changed: i32 = 1
    while changed == 1 {
        changed = 0
        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < G_nclauses {
            let st = G_cstart[c]
            let ln = G_clen[c]
            var sat: i32 = 0
            var unassigned: i32 = 0
            var last_lit: i64 = 0
            var k: i32 = 0
            while k < ln {
                let l = G_lits[st + k]
                let v = lit_var(l)
                var a = G_assign[v]
                if l < 0 { a = 0 - a }
                if a == 1 { sat = 1 }
                if a == 0 { unassigned = unassigned + 1  last_lit = l }
                k = k + 1
            }
            if sat == 0 {
                if unassigned == 0 { return 1 }
                if unassigned == 1 {
                    let v = lit_var(last_lit)
                    if last_lit < 0 { G_assign[v] = 0 - 1 } else { G_assign[v] = 1 }
                    changed = 1
                }
            }
            c = c + 1
        }
    }
    return 0
}

fn reset_assign() with Mut, Panic {
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i <= G_nvars { G_assign[i] = 0  i = i + 1 }
}

fn emit_neg(dec_len: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    if P_n >= LEMMA_CAP { BAILED = 1  return }
    let idx = P_n
    var start: i32 = 0
    if idx > 0 { start = P_start[idx - 1] + P_len[idx - 1] }
    if (start as i64) + (dec_len as i64) > 1048576 { BAILED = 1  return }
    P_start[idx] = start
    P_len[idx] = dec_len
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < dec_len {
        P_lits[start + i] = 0 - DEC[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    P_n = idx + 1
}

fn solve_rec(dec_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic {
    if BAILED == 1 { return 0 }
    NODE_COUNT = NODE_COUNT + 1
    if NODE_COUNT > NODE_LIMIT { BAILED = 1  return 0 }

    let cf = propagate()
    if cf == 1 {
        emit_neg(dec_len)
        return 0
    }
    var x: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 1
    while i <= G_nvars {
        if G_assign[i] == 0 { x = i  i = G_nvars + 1 } else { i = i + 1 }
    }
    if x == 0 { return 1 }

    var snap: [i32; 1024] = [0; 1024]
    var s: i32 = 0
    while s <= G_nvars { snap[s] = G_assign[s]  s = s + 1 }

    G_assign[x] = 1
    DEC[dec_len] = x as i64
    let r1 = solve_rec(dec_len + 1)
    if r1 == 1 { return 1 }

    s = 0
    while s <= G_nvars { G_assign[s] = snap[s]  s = s + 1 }

    if BAILED == 1 { return 0 }

    G_assign[x] = 0 - 1
    DEC[dec_len] = 0 - (x as i64)
    let r2 = solve_rec(dec_len + 1)
    if r2 == 1 { return 1 }

    s = 0
    while s <= G_nvars { G_assign[s] = snap[s]  s = s + 1 }

    if BAILED == 1 { return 0 }
    emit_neg(dec_len)
    return 0
}

fn add_lemma_to_db(pst: i32, pln: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    if G_nclauses >= 524288 { return }
    let idx = G_nclauses
    var start: i32 = 0
    if idx > 0 { start = G_cstart[idx - 1] + G_clen[idx - 1] }
    if (start as i64) + (pln as i64) > 1048576 { return }
    G_cstart[idx] = start
    G_clen[idx] = pln
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < pln { G_lits[start + i] = P_lits[pst + i]  i = i + 1 }
    G_nclauses = idx + 1
}

fn verify(orig_nc: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic {
    G_nclauses = orig_nc
    var pi: i32 = 0
    while pi < P_n {
        let pst = P_start[pi]
        let pln = P_len[pi]
        reset_assign()
        var taut: i32 = 0
        var k: i32 = 0
        while k < pln {
            let l = P_lits[pst + k]
            let v = lit_var(l)
            var want: i32 = 0 - 1
            if l < 0 { want = 1 }
            if G_assign[v] != 0 {
                if G_assign[v] != want { taut = 1 }
            }
            G_assign[v] = want
            k = k + 1
        }
        var ok: i32 = 0
        if taut == 1 { ok = 1 } else {
            let cf = propagate()
            if cf == 1 { ok = 1 }
        }
        if ok == 0 { return 0 - 1 }
        if pln == 0 { return 1 }
        add_lemma_to_db(pst, pln)
        pi = pi + 1
    }
    return 0
}

fn print_digit(d: i64) with IO {
    if d == 0 { print("0") } else if d == 1 { print("1") } else if d == 2 { print("2") }
    else if d == 3 { print("3") } else if d == 4 { print("4") } else if d == 5 { print("5") }
    else if d == 6 { print("6") } else if d == 7 { print("7") } else if d == 8 { print("8") }
    else { print("9") }
}
fn print_dec(n: i64) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 { print("0") return }
    var x = n
    if x < 0 { print("-") x = 0 - x }
    var buf: [i64; 24] = [0; 24]
    var len: i32 = 0
    while x > 0 { buf[len] = x % 10  x = x / 10  len = len + 1 }
    var i: i32 = len - 1
    while i >= 0 { print_digit(buf[i])  i = i - 1 }
}
fn emit_dimacs(orig_nc: i32) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("p cnf ")  print_dec(G_nvars as i64)  print(" ")  print_dec(orig_nc as i64)  print("\n")
    var c: i32 = 0
    while c < orig_nc {
        let st = G_cstart[c]
        let ln = G_clen[c]
        var k: i32 = 0
        while k < ln { print_dec(G_lits[st + k])  print(" ")  k = k + 1 }
        print("0\n")
        c = c + 1
    }
}
fn emit_drat() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pi: i32 = 0
    while pi < P_n {
        let pst = P_start[pi]
        let pln = P_len[pi]
        var k: i32 = 0
        while k < pln { print_dec(P_lits[pst + k])  print(" ")  k = k + 1 }
        print("0\n")
        pi = pi + 1
    }
}

fn reset_all() with Mut, Panic {
    reset_assign()
    G_nvars = 0
    G_nclauses = 0
    P_n = 0
    NODE_COUNT = 0
    BAILED = 0
}

// K_n with k colors: ALO per vertex + edge inequality for every pair (complete).
fn build_clique_coloring(n: i64, k: i64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var arr: [i64; 16] = [0; 16]
    var v: i64 = 0
    while v < n {
        var c: i64 = 0
        while c < k { arr[c as usize] = v*k + c + 1  c = c + 1 }
        g_add_clause(&arr, k as i32)
        v = v + 1
    }
    var a: i64 = 0
    while a < n {
        var b: i64 = a + 1
        while b < n {
            var c: i64 = 0
            while c < k {
                arr[0] = 0 - (a*k + c + 1)
                arr[1] = 0 - (b*k + c + 1)
                g_add_clause(&arr, 2)
                c = c + 1
            }
            b = b + 1
        }
        a = a + 1
    }
}

// One row of the scaling table: K_n with (n-1) colors = PHP(n, n-1), UNSAT.
fn run_case(n: i64) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    reset_all()
    build_clique_coloring(n, n - 1)
    let orig_nc = G_nclauses
    print("K_")  print_int(n)  print(" / ")  print_int(n - 1)  print("-col  vars=")
    print_int(G_nvars)  print("  clauses=")  print_int(orig_nc)
    let sat = solve_rec(0)
    if BAILED == 1 {
        print("  nodes>")  print_int(NODE_LIMIT)  print("  => WALL (proof too large for tree-resolution DPLL)\n")
        return
    }
    if sat == 1 {
        print("  SAT (UNEXPECTED — pigeonhole should be UNSAT)\n")
        return
    }
    reset_assign()
    let vr = verify(orig_nc)
    print("  nodes=")  print_int(NODE_COUNT)  print("  DRUP-lemmas=")  print_int(P_n)
    if vr == 1 { print("  native RUP: VERIFIED\n") } else { print("  native RUP: FAILED\n") }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("=== DPLL->DRUP scaling wall: pigeonhole K_n / (n-1)-coloring ===\n")
    print("(resolution has an exponential lower bound here — Haken 1985)\n\n")

    run_case(4)
    run_case(5)
    run_case(6)
    run_case(7)
    run_case(8)
    run_case(9)

    // Emit a mid-size certificate for external drat-trim (K_6 / 5-coloring).
    print("\n-- certificate for external drat-trim: K_6 / 5-coloring --\n")
    reset_all()
    build_clique_coloring(6, 5)
    let onc = G_nclauses
    let s = solve_rec(0)
    if BAILED == 0 {
        if s == 0 {
            G_nclauses = onc
            print("%%DIMACS%%\n")
            emit_dimacs(onc)
            print("%%DRAT%%\n")
            emit_drat()
            print("%%END%%\n")
        }
    }

    print("\nReading: 3-coloring of a spindle-containing graph stays a ~30-lemma LOCAL\n")
    print("refutation at any host size; but a GLOBAL hard UNSAT (the χ≥5 regime) blows\n")
    print("up here. Reaching de Grey's 510-vertex 4-coloring UNSAT needs (1) the graph\n")
    print("data (not in this repo) and (2) CDCL clause learning — chronological DPLL\n")
    print("tree-resolution provably cannot produce a sub-exponential proof.\n")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/erdos/erdos90_cubic_tower_base.sio ===
// examples/erdos/erdos90_cubic_tower_base.sio
//
// EXPLICIT, EXACT-ARITHMETIC certification of the NUMBER-FIELD BASE LAYER of the
// OpenAI (2026) disproof of Erdős's planar unit-distance conjecture
// (Erdős #90; Lean: github.com/logical-intelligence/erdos-unit-distance).
//
// Their proof is existential and conditional. Two of its load-bearing Lean
// theorems are arithmetic facts about the totally-real cubic subfield
// L ⊂ ℚ(ζ_r) used as the base of the Golod–Shafarevich pro-3 tower:
//
//   `cubic_subfield_prime_ramification_data` :  for prime r ≡ 1 (mod 3),
//        r is TOTALLY ramified in L (e=3, f=1, g=1) and EVERY other prime
//        q ≠ r is unramified in L.
//   `differentIdeal_cubic_subfield_eq_prime_sq` :  differentIdeal ℤ 𝓞_L = P²
//        (tame ramification, e−1 = 2), hence  disc(L) = N(P²) = r².
//
// Lean states these for ALL such r as abstract ideal-theoretic facts. Here we
// make them CONCRETE and machine-checkable: we GENERATE the cubic field from
// scratch via Gauss periods, then certify the ramification data as exact
// integers. This is the explicit witness the infinitary proof never writes down.
//
//   Gauss: for prime r ≡ 1 (mod 3), write 4r = L² + 27·M² with L ≡ 1 (mod 3).
//   The period polynomial of the cubic subfield is
//        f(x) = x³ + x² − ((r−1)/3)·x − (r·(L+3) − 1)/27.
//
//   Polynomial vs FIELD discriminant: disc(f) = disc(L) · s², where s = [𝓞_L : ℤ[α]]
//   is the index of the period order. Since L is cyclic cubic of conductor r,
//   disc(L) = r² (conductor–discriminant formula), hence disc(f) = (r·s)².
//   Certificate 1:  disc(f)/r² is a PERFECT SQUARE s²  ⇒  disc(L) = disc(f)/s² = r²,
//                   i.e. r is the unique ramified prime (every q ≠ r unramified).
//   Certificate 2:  f(x) ≡ (x − k)³  (mod r)  (with r ∤ s, Dedekind)  ⇒  r totally ramified.
//
// All i64 integer arithmetic, no floats, no external libraries.

fn isqrt(n: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    var r = 0
    while (r + 1) * (r + 1) <= n { r = r + 1 }
    return r
}

fn pmod(x: i64, m: i64) -> i64 with Div {
    return ((x % m) + m) % m
}

// Discriminant of monic cubic x³ + A·x² + B·x + C.
fn cubic_disc(a: i64, b: i64, c: i64) -> i64 {
    return 18 * a * b * c - 4 * a * a * a * c + a * a * b * b - 4 * b * b * b - 27 * c * c
}

// Certify the cubic subfield L ⊂ ℚ(ζ_r) for a prime r ≡ 1 (mod 3).
fn certify(r: i64) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if pmod(r, 3) != 1 {
        print("  r="); print_int(r); print("  SKIP (r not ≡ 1 mod 3)\n")
        return 0
    }

    // Solve 4r = L² + 27·M² (Gauss); the period polynomial needs L ≡ 1 (mod 3).
    let four_r = 4 * r
    var m = 1
    var mfound = 0
    var labs = 0 - 1
    while 27 * m * m < four_r {
        let rem = four_r - 27 * m * m
        let s = isqrt(rem)
        if s * s == rem { labs = s  mfound = m  m = four_r }   // found; force loop exit
        m = m + 1
    }
    if labs < 0 {
        print("  r="); print_int(r); print("  FAIL (no 4r = L²+27M²)\n")
        return 0
    }
    var lval = labs
    if pmod(lval, 3) != 1 { lval = 0 - lval }

    // Period polynomial f(x) = x³ + A·x² + B·x + C, with A = 1.
    let a = 1
    let b = 0 - (r - 1) / 3
    let c = 0 - (r * (lval + 3) - 1) / 27

    // Certificate 1: disc(f) = (r·s)², i.e. disc(f)/r² is a perfect square s².
    // Then the FIELD discriminant is disc(f)/s² = r² (s = period-order index).
    let disc = cubic_disc(a, b, c)
    let r2 = r * r
    var pass1 = 0
    var sidx = 0
    if disc > 0 {
        if disc % r2 == 0 {
            let quo = disc / r2
            let s = isqrt(quo)
            if s * s == quo { pass1 = 1  sidx = s }
        }
    }

    // Certificate 2: f(x) ≡ (x − k)³ (mod r), i.e. r totally ramified.
    // (x − k)³ = x³ − 3k·x² + 3k²·x − k³.  Match A,B,C mod r.
    // From −3k ≡ A = 1 (mod r): for r ≡ 1 (mod 3), inv(3) = (2r+1)/3, k = r − inv3.
    let inv3 = (2 * r + 1) / 3
    let k = pmod(0 - inv3, r)
    let mA = pmod(0 - 3 * k, r)              // expect ≡ A = 1
    let mB = pmod(3 * k * k, r)              // expect ≡ B
    let mC = pmod(0 - k * k % r * k, r)      // expect ≡ C
    var pass2 = 0
    if mA == pmod(a, r) {
        if mB == pmod(b, r) {
            if mC == pmod(c, r) { pass2 = 1 }
        }
    }

    print("  r="); print_int(r)
    print("  4r=L²+27M²: L="); print_int(lval); print(" M="); print_int(mfound)
    print("  | f = x^3 + x^2 + ("); print_int(b); print(")x + ("); print_int(c); print(")\n")
    print("        disc(f)="); print_int(disc)
    print("  = r^2 * "); print_int(sidx); print("^2   (index s="); print_int(sidx)
    print(", field disc = disc/s^2 = r^2 = "); print_int(r2); print(")")
    if pass1 == 1 { print("  [field disc=r^2 OK]") } else { print("  [disc NOT r^2*square]") }
    if pass2 == 1 { print("  [f≡(x-k)^3 mod r: r totally ramified OK]\n") }
    else { print("  [total-ramification CHECK FAILED]\n") }

    if pass1 == 1 {
        if pass2 == 1 { return 1 }
    }
    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("=== Cubic tower-base certifier for the OpenAI 2026 Erdős #90 disproof ===\n")
    print("Explicit witness for Lean theorems `cubic_subfield_prime_ramification_data`\n")
    print("and `differentIdeal_cubic_subfield_eq_prime_sq` (disc = r^2), per prime r ≡ 1 (mod 3).\n\n")

    var primes: [i64; 11] = [0; 11]
    primes[0 as usize] = 7
    primes[1 as usize] = 13
    primes[2 as usize] = 19
    primes[3 as usize] = 31
    primes[4 as usize] = 37
    primes[5 as usize] = 43
    primes[6 as usize] = 61
    primes[7 as usize] = 67
    primes[8 as usize] = 73
    primes[9 as usize] = 79
    primes[10 as usize] = 97

    var passed = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < 11 {
        let ok = certify(primes[i as usize])
        passed = passed + ok
        i = i + 1
    }

    print("\nCertified ")
    print_int(passed)
    print(" / 11 cubic base fields (disc = r^2 AND r totally ramified).\n")
    print("\nWhat this is: the explicit, exact-arithmetic shadow of the abstract ramification\n")
    print("Lean lemmas. What it is NOT: the tower's infinitude (Golod–Shafarevich, d^2 < 4r)\n")
    print("or the geometric exponent γ > 0 — those need genuine class field theory, not\n")
    print("finite computation. Sounio certifies here exactly the layer that IS computable.\n")

    if passed == 11 { return 0 }
    return 1
}


// === FILE: examples/erdos/erdos90_repcount_engine.sio ===
// examples/erdos/erdos90_repcount_engine.sio
//
// Independent EXACT-arithmetic sanity check of the COMBINATORIAL CORE behind the
// OpenAI (2026) disproof of Erdős's planar unit-distance conjecture
// (Erdős #90; Lean formalization: github.com/logical-intelligence/erdos-unit-distance).
//
// We do NOT verify the disproof (its engine is class field theory: infinite
// Golod–Shafarevich pro-3 towers, far outside finite computation). We verify the
// elementary, classical fact the construction lifts to number-field towers.
//
// In the Lean `AdmissibleDatum`, the field is K = L(i) (the plane) and the t chosen
// rational primes satisfy `q_mod4 : q b % 4 = 1` and split completely. The exponent
// excess is `γ = t·log 2 − log H > 0`: each split prime q ≡ 1 (mod 4) DOUBLES the
// number of algebraic elements of a given norm (factor 2), while the class number
// (the loss) is bounded by H^f. In the base plane K = ℚ(i) = ℤ[i] this is exactly
// Gauss's sum-of-two-squares count:
//
//     for squarefree N = q_1 · … · q_t with each q_i prime ≡ 1 (mod 4):
//         r₂(N) := #{ (a,b) ∈ ℤ² : a² + b² = N } = 4 · 2^t.
//
// The 4 is the Gaussian units {±1,±i}; the 2^t is the "t·log 2" engine of γ.
// A single prime ≡ 3 (mod 4) factor sends r₂ to 0 — which is precisely why the
// construction REQUIRES q ≡ 1 (mod 4). All integer arithmetic, no floats.

fn isqrt(n: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var r = 0
    while (r + 1) * (r + 1) <= n { r = r + 1 }
    return r
}

// r₂(N) = number of ordered, signed integer pairs (a,b) with a² + b² = N.
fn r2(n: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    let s = isqrt(n)
    var cnt = 0
    var a = 0 - s
    while a <= s {
        var b = 0 - s
        while b <= s {
            if a * a + b * b == n { cnt = cnt + 1 }
            b = b + 1
        }
        a = a + 1
    }
    return cnt
}

// 4 · 2^t
fn expected(t: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var p = 4
    var i = 0
    while i < t { p = p * 2  i = i + 1 }
    return p
}

fn report(label_n: i64, n: i64, t: i64) with IO, Mut {
    let got = r2(n)
    let exp = expected(t)
    print("  N="); print_int(n); print("  r2="); print_int(got)
    print("  (4*2^"); print_int(t); print("="); print_int(exp); print(") ")
    if got == exp { print("[OK]\n") } else { print("[*]\n") }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    print("=== r2(N) doubling engine for primes q ≡ 1 (mod 4) — Erdős #90 core ===\n\n")

    print("Single primes ≡ 1 (mod 4): r2 = 8 = 4·2^1\n")
    report(0, 5, 1)        // 5
    report(0, 13, 1)       // 13
    report(0, 17, 1)       // 17
    report(0, 29, 1)       // 29

    print("\nProducts of distinct primes ≡ 1 (mod 4): r2 doubles per prime (= t·log2)\n")
    report(0, 5, 1)                       // 5            t=1 -> 8
    report(0, 5 * 13, 2)                  // 65           t=2 -> 16
    report(0, 5 * 13 * 17, 3)             // 1105         t=3 -> 32
    report(0, 5 * 13 * 17 * 29, 4)        // 32045        t=4 -> 64

    print("\nWhy q ≡ 1 (mod 4) is REQUIRED: a prime ≡ 3 (mod 4) factor kills r2\n")
    print("  r2(3)  = "); print_int(r2(3));  print("  (3 ≡ 3 mod 4)\n")
    print("  r2(7)  = "); print_int(r2(7));  print("  (7 ≡ 3 mod 4)\n")
    print("  r2(15) = "); print_int(r2(3 * 5)); print("  (3·5: the 3 kills the 5's reps)\n")
    print("  r2(21) = "); print_int(r2(3 * 7)); print("\n")

    print("\nInterpretation: γ = t·log2 − log H. The exact 2^t growth above is the\n")
    print("t·log2 engine. OpenAI's construction keeps it alive across an INFINITE\n")
    print("class field tower (K_j = L_j(i), deg → ∞) with class number ≤ H^f, so when\n")
    print("t·log2 > log H the unit-distance count beats n^(1+o(1)): νn(n) ≥ n^(1+δ).\n")
    print("This file verifies only the finite arithmetic core, not the tower.\n")
    return 0
}

// === FILE: examples/erdos/native_sat_scale_demo.sio ===
// examples/erdos/native_sat_scale_demo.sio
//
// Demonstrates the native CDCL solver (theorem::smt) AFTER raising the BOOLEAN
// VARIABLE cap 256→1024 (clause budget kept at 4096 clauses / 16384 literals — see
// the BLOCKER note below for why clause_data was NOT enlarged further).
//
// All instances have rigorously known chromatic numbers, validating soundness at
// scale across the FULL sequence (the bug we hit was execution-order dependent, so
// stability of the whole run matters, not just isolated cases):
//   - K_18,  4-coloring → UNSAT (72 vars).  K_n needs n colors.
//   - C_80,  2-coloring → SAT   (160 vars). χ(even cycle)=2.
//   - C_81,  2-coloring → UNSAT (162 vars). χ(odd cycle)=3.
//   --- past the old 256-var cap (new 1024 cap) ---
//   - C_400, 2-coloring → SAT   (800 vars).  χ(even cycle)=2.
//   - C_500, 2-coloring → SAT   (1000 vars). χ(even cycle)=2.
//   - C_511, 2-coloring → UNSAT (1022 vars, near the 1024 cap). χ(odd cycle)=3.
//
// Only SPARSE graphs (cycles: n edges) reach high var counts within the 4096-clause
// budget. Dense graphs (e.g. K_70 4-col ≈ 10k clauses) overflow it. Enlarging
// clause_data to ~512 KB (SmtContext ~800 KB) once produced a spurious UNSAT on a
// known-SAT cycle in one build, but this was NOT reliably reproducible — see the
// OPEN ISSUE in examples/erdos/README.md and docs/audit/sret_large_struct_smtcontext/.
// Pending a reproducible diagnosis the clause budget stays at the proven-stable size.
//
// This is the de Grey-scale mechanism in miniature: the native UNSAT certificate
// scales with the variable cap — no external SAT solver, no third-party DRAT.

use theorem::smt::*

var ADJ: [i64; 262144] = [0; 262144]   // flat n*n, supports up to n=512
var NV: i64 = 0

fn clear_graph(n: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    NV = n
    var i = 0
    while i < n*n { ADJ[i as usize] = 0  i = i + 1 }
}

fn add_edge(u: i64, w: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    ADJ[(u*NV + w) as usize] = 1
    ADJ[(w*NV + u) as usize] = 1
}

fn build_complete(n: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_graph(n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n { add_edge(i, j)  j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn build_cycle(n: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    clear_graph(n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        add_edge(i, (i + 1) - ((i + 1) / n) * n)   // (i+1) mod n without %
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Native CDCL k-colorability of ADJ (NV vertices). 1=SAT, 0=UNSAT.
fn sat_kcolorable(k: i64) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var ctx = smt_new()
    var v: i64 = 0
    while v < NV {
        var lits: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
        var c: i64 = 0
        while c < k {
            lits[c as usize] = ((v*k + c + 1)*2 + 1) as i32
            c = c + 1
        }
        smt_add_clause(&! ctx, &lits, k as i32)
        v = v + 1
    }
    v = 0
    while v < NV {
        var c1: i64 = 0
        while c1 < k {
            var c2: i64 = c1 + 1
            while c2 < k {
                var lp: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
                lp[0] = ((v*k + c1 + 1)*2) as i32
                lp[1] = ((v*k + c2 + 1)*2) as i32
                smt_add_clause(&! ctx, &lp, 2)
                c2 = c2 + 1
            }
            c1 = c1 + 1
        }
        v = v + 1
    }
    var u: i64 = 0
    while u < NV {
        var w: i64 = u + 1
        while w < NV {
            if ADJ[(u*NV + w) as usize] == 1 {
                var c: i64 = 0
                while c < k {
                    var le: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
                    le[0] = ((u*k + c + 1)*2) as i32
                    le[1] = ((w*k + c + 1)*2) as i32
                    smt_add_clause(&! ctx, &le, 2)
                    c = c + 1
                }
            }
            w = w + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    smt_set_score_mode(&! ctx, 3)
    smt_set_no_ple(&! ctx, 1)
    return smt_solve(&! ctx)
}

fn report(name: i64, n: i64, k: i64, expect_sat: i64) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = sat_kcolorable(k)
    print("  n="); print_int(n); print(" vertices, k="); print_int(k)
    print(" colors => "); print_int(n*k); print(" vars: ")
    if r == 1 { print("SAT") } else { print("UNSAT") }
    print("  (expected "); if expect_sat == 1 { print("SAT") } else { print("UNSAT") }
    print(")")
    let ok = if r == expect_sat { 1 } else { 0 }
    if ok == 1 { print("  [OK]\n") } else { print("  [MISMATCH]\n") }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("=== native SAT/UNSAT at scale (var cap 256->1024; clause budget 4096/16384) ===\n\n")

    print("K_18, 4-coloring (K_n needs n colors):\n")
    build_complete(18)
    report(0, 18, 4, 0)        // UNSAT, 72 vars

    print("even cycle C_80, 2-coloring (chi=2):\n")
    build_cycle(80)
    report(0, 80, 2, 1)        // SAT, 160 vars

    print("odd cycle C_81, 2-coloring (chi=3):\n")
    build_cycle(81)
    report(0, 81, 2, 0)        // UNSAT, 162 vars

    print("\n--- past the old 256-var cap (sparse graphs within the clause budget) ---\n")

    print("even cycle C_400, 2-coloring (chi=2):\n")
    build_cycle(400)
    report(0, 400, 2, 1)       // SAT, 800 vars

    print("even cycle C_500, 2-coloring (chi=2):\n")
    build_cycle(500)
    report(0, 500, 2, 1)       // SAT, 1000 vars

    print("odd cycle C_511, 2-coloring (chi=3) — 1022 vars, near the 1024 cap:\n")
    build_cycle(511)
    report(0, 511, 2, 0)       // UNSAT, 1022 vars

    print("\nAll six correct across the full run (order-stable). The variable cap now\n")
    print("reaches >1000 vars for sparse graphs. de Grey's ~510-vtx graphs are DENSE\n")
    print("(4-col ≈ 2040 vars + ~10k clauses): they need both a larger clause budget AND\n")
    print("the large-struct return fix noted in the header. That is the remaining gate.\n")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/erdos/nsat_smoke.sio ===
// examples/erdos/nsat_smoke.sio
//
// Smoke: verify module-level LCG + near-threshold 3-SAT baseline before
// committing to the full 84-sweep redesign.
//
// Tests idx = 0 (e=6), 46 (e=9), 57 (e=9) with three background densities:
//   A: 10 cls / 21 vars = ratio 0.48  (far below threshold, easy SAT base)
//   B: 40 cls / 21 vars = ratio 1.90  (below threshold, SAT base)
//   C: 70 cls / 21 vars = ratio 3.33  (near threshold after adding coloring)
//
// Goal: find the density where confl/hardness discriminates e=6 vs e=9.
// If all three show flat hardness, the signal is in d, not clauses, and
// we need a different encoding.

use hypercomplex_graph::erdos_unit_distance::*
use theorem::smt::*

// Module-level LCG state — reset to fixed seed at each twist.
var lcg_state: i64 = 0

fn lcg_next() -> i64 with Mut {
    lcg_state = (lcg_state * 1664525 + 1013904223) & 0x7FFFFFFF
    return lcg_state
}

fn lrand(n: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    return lcg_next() % n
}

fn pri(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0 { print("-"); pri(0 - x); return }
    if x == 0 { print("0"); return }
    if x >= 10 { pri(x / 10) }
    let d = x - (x / 10) * 10
    if d == 0 { print("0") }
    if d == 1 { print("1") }
    if d == 2 { print("2") }
    if d == 3 { print("3") }
    if d == 4 { print("4") }
    if d == 5 { print("5") }
    if d == 6 { print("6") }
    if d == 7 { print("7") }
    if d == 8 { print("8") }
    if d == 9 { print("9") }
}

fn prf(x: f64) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 { print("-"); prf(0.0 - x); return }
    let ip = x as i32
    pri(ip)
    print(".")
    let f0 = (x - (ip as f64)) * 10.0
    let d0 = f0 as i32
    let f1 = (f0 - (d0 as f64)) * 10.0
    let d1 = f1 as i32
    pri(d0)
    pri(d1)
}

fn add2(ctx: &!SmtContext, a: i32, b: i32) with Mut, Div {
    var lits: [i32; 8] = [0; 8]
    lits[0] = a
    lits[1] = b
