fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 { print("0"); return }
    if x < 0 { print("-"); print_i32_unsigned(0 - x) }
    else { print_i32_unsigned(x) }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 { return }
    let rest = x / 10
    if rest > 0 { print_i32_unsigned(rest) }
    let digit = x % 10
    print_digit(digit)
}

fn print_digit(d: i32) with IO {
    if d == 0 { print("0") }
    else { if d == 1 { print("1") }
    else { if d == 2 { print("2") }
    else { if d == 3 { print("3") }
    else { if d == 4 { print("4") }
    else { if d == 5 { print("5") }
    else { if d == 6 { print("6") }
    else { if d == 7 { print("7") }
    else { if d == 8 { print("8") }
    else { if d == 9 { print("9") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}

fn print_f64(x: f64) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 { print("-"); let x = 0.0 - x }
    let int_part = x as i32
    print_i32(int_part)
    print(".")
    let frac = x - (int_part as f64)
    let scaled = (frac * 100.0) as i32
    if scaled < 10 { print("0") }
    print_i32_unsigned(scaled)
}

fn sleep_frames(n: i32) with IO {
    // Busy-wait loop as placeholder for timing
    // Terminal I/O provides natural delay
    var i = 0
    while i < n * 10000 {
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Demo 1: Simplified Phase Diagram
// ============================================================================

fn demo_phase_diagram() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;36m╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m║          PHASE 6: SCIENTIFIC CHARTS                      ║\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m║     Demo 1/4: Phase Diagram (Water H2O)                  ║\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\x1b[0m\n\n")

    // Simplified phase diagram display
    print("  P (kPa)\n")
    print("   ^\n")
    print("   |\n")

    // Render simplified phase regions
    // High pressure region (solid/liquid)
    var y = 20
    while y >= 0 {
        print("   |")

        var x = 0
        while x < 50 {
            // Temperature roughly maps to x (200K to 700K)
            let t = 200.0 + (x as f64) * 10.0
            // Pressure roughly maps to y (0 to 25000 kPa)
            let p = (y as f64) * 1200.0

            // Phase classification
            var phase = 0

            // Below triple point pressure
            if p < 610.0 {
                if t < 273.0 {
                    phase = 1  // Solid
                } else {
                    phase = 3  // Gas
                }
            } else {
                // Above critical point
                if t > 650.0 {
                    if p > 22000.0 {
                        phase = 4  // Supercritical
                    } else {
                        phase = 3  // Gas
                    }
                } else {
                    // Normal phases
                    if t < 273.0 {
                        phase = 1  // Solid
                    } else {
                        // Liquid or gas based on vapor pressure curve
                        let vp = 0.611 * exp_simple((t - 273.0) * 0.05)
                        if p > vp {
                            phase = 2  // Liquid
                        } else {
                            phase = 3  // Gas
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            // Render
            if phase == 1 {
                print("\x1b[34m#\x1b[0m")  // Blue solid
            } else { if phase == 2 {
                print("\x1b[36m~\x1b[0m")  // Cyan liquid
            } else { if phase == 3 {
                print("\x1b[33m.\x1b[0m")  // Yellow gas
            } else {
                print("\x1b[35m*\x1b[0m")  // Magenta supercritical
            }}}

            x = x + 1
        }
        print("\n")
        y = y - 1
    }

    print("   +---------------------------------------------------> T (K)\n")
    print("     200                    450                     700\n\n")

    print("   \x1b[34m#\x1b[0m Solid (Ice)  \x1b[36m~\x1b[0m Liquid  \x1b[33m.\x1b[0m Gas (Vapor)  \x1b[35m*\x1b[0m Supercritical\n")
    print("   \x1b[1;31mT\x1b[0m = Triple Point (273K, 0.6kPa)\n")
    print("   \x1b[1;31mC\x1b[0m = Critical Point (647K, 22MPa)\n")
}

fn exp_simple(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 10.0 { return 22000.0 }
    if x < -10.0 { return 0.00001 }
    let x2 = x * x
    let x3 = x2 * x
    return 1.0 + x + x2 * 0.5 + x3 * 0.167
}

// ============================================================================
// Demo 2: Bifurcation Diagram
// ============================================================================

fn demo_bifurcation() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;36m╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m║          PHASE 6: SCIENTIFIC CHARTS                      ║\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m║     Demo 2/4: Bifurcation Diagram (Logistic Map)         ║\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\x1b[0m\n\n")

    // Grid for density
    var density = [0; 2400]  // 60 x 40

    // Compute bifurcation for logistic map
    var px = 0
    while px < 60 {
        // r ranges from 2.5 to 4.0
        let r = 2.5 + (px as f64) * 0.025

        // Start from x = 0.5
        var x = 0.5

        // Transient
        var t = 0
        while t < 200 {
            x = r * x * (1.0 - x)
            t = t + 1
        }

        // Sample attractor
        var s = 0
        while s < 100 {
            x = r * x * (1.0 - x)

            // Map to grid (x in [0,1], y axis)
            let gy = (x * 39.0) as i32
            if gy >= 0 {
                if gy < 40 {
                    let idx = gy * 60 + px
                    if idx < 2400 {
                        density[idx] = density[idx] + 1
                    }
                }
            }
            s = s + 1
        }

        px = px + 1
    }

    // Render
    print("   x\n")
    print("   ^\n")

    var y = 39
    while y >= 0 {
        print("   |")

        var x = 0
        while x < 60 {
            let idx = y * 60 + x
            var d = 0
            if idx < 2400 {
                d = density[idx]
            }

            if d == 0 {
                print(" ")
            } else { if d < 3 {
                print("\x1b[34m.\x1b[0m")
            } else { if d < 10 {
                print("\x1b[36m:\x1b[0m")
            } else { if d < 30 {
                print("\x1b[32m+\x1b[0m")
            } else {
                print("\x1b[33m*\x1b[0m")
            }}}}

            x = x + 1
        }
        print("\n")
        y = y - 1
    }

    print("   +-------------------------------------------------------------> r\n")
    print("     2.5                        3.2                           4.0\n\n")

    print("   Logistic map: x_{n+1} = r * x_n * (1 - x_n)\n")
    print("   Shows period-doubling cascade: 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> ... -> chaos\n")
}

// ============================================================================
// Demo 3: Poincaré Section
// ============================================================================

struct State3D {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64
}

fn demo_poincare() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;36m╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m║          PHASE 6: SCIENTIFIC CHARTS                      ║\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m║     Demo 3/4: Poincare Section (Lorenz Attractor)        ║\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\x1b[0m\n\n")

    // Density grid for section at z=27
    var density = [0; 1800]  // 60 x 30
    let section_z = 27.0

    // Integrate Lorenz system
    var state = State3D { x: 1.0, y: 1.0, z: 1.0 }
    var prev_z = state.z
    let dt = 0.005
    let sigma = 10.0
    let rho = 28.0
    let beta = 2.667

    // Skip transient
    var t = 0
    while t < 10000 {
        prev_z = state.z
        // RK4 step (simplified to Euler for brevity)
        let dx = sigma * (state.y - state.x)
        let dy = state.x * (rho - state.z) - state.y
        let dz = state.x * state.y - beta * state.z
        state.x = state.x + dx * dt
        state.y = state.y + dy * dt
        state.z = state.z + dz * dt
        t = t + 1
    }

    // Collect crossings
    t = 0
    while t < 200000 {
        prev_z = state.z
        let dx = sigma * (state.y - state.x)
        let dy = state.x * (rho - state.z) - state.y
        let dz = state.x * state.y - beta * state.z
        state.x = state.x + dx * dt
        state.y = state.y + dy * dt
        state.z = state.z + dz * dt

        // Check upward crossing
        if prev_z < section_z {
            if state.z >= section_z {
                // Map (x, y) to grid
                // x in [-25, 25], y in [-30, 30]
                let gx = ((state.x + 25.0) * 1.2) as i32
                let gy = ((state.y + 30.0) * 0.5) as i32
                if gx >= 0 {
                    if gx < 60 {
                        if gy >= 0 {
                            if gy < 30 {
                                let idx = gy * 60 + gx
                                if idx < 1800 {
                                    density[idx] = density[idx] + 1
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        t = t + 1
    }

    // Render
    print("   y\n")
    print("   ^\n")

    var y = 29
    while y >= 0 {
        print("   |")

        var x = 0
        while x < 60 {
            let idx = y * 60 + x
            var d = 0
            if idx < 1800 {
                d = density[idx]
            }

            if d == 0 {
                print(" ")
            } else { if d < 2 {
                print("\x1b[34m.\x1b[0m")
            } else { if d < 5 {
                print("\x1b[36m+\x1b[0m")
            } else { if d < 15 {
                print("\x1b[32m*\x1b[0m")
            } else {
                print("\x1b[33m#\x1b[0m")
            }}}}

            x = x + 1
        }
        print("\n")
        y = y - 1
    }

    print("   +-------------------------------------------------------------> x\n")
    print("    -25                          0                             25\n\n")

    print("   Lorenz attractor at z = 27 plane\n")
    print("   Reveals fractal structure of strange attractor\n")
}

// ============================================================================
// Demo 4: Streamlines
// ============================================================================

fn demo_streamlines() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;36m╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m║          PHASE 6: SCIENTIFIC CHARTS                      ║\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m║     Demo 4/4: Streamlines (Dipole Field)                 ║\x1b[0m\n")
    print("\x1b[1;36m╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\x1b[0m\n\n")

    // Display buffer
    var display = [32; 1800]  // 60 x 30

    // Integrate streamlines from seed points
    var seed = 0
    while seed < 20 {
        // Seed positions (grid around y-axis)
        var sx = 0.0
        var sy = -2.5 + (seed as f64) * 0.26

        // Integrate forward
        var step = 0
        while step < 200 {
            // Check bounds
            if sx < -3.0 { step = 200 }
            else { if sx > 3.0 { step = 200 }
            else { if sy < -3.0 { step = 200 }
            else { if sy > 3.0 { step = 200 }
            else {
                // Plot point
                let gx = ((sx + 3.0) * 10.0) as i32
                let gy = ((sy + 3.0) * 5.0) as i32
                if gx >= 0 {
                    if gx < 60 {
                        if gy >= 0 {
                            if gy < 30 {
                                let idx = gy * 60 + gx

                                // Get dipole field direction
                                let r1x = sx + 1.0
                                let r1y = sy
                                let r1sq = r1x * r1x + r1y * r1y + 0.1
                                let r2x = sx - 1.0
                                let r2y = sy
                                let r2sq = r2x * r2x + r2y * r2y + 0.1

                                let vx = r1x / r1sq - r2x / r2sq
                                let vy = r1y / r1sq - r2y / r2sq

                                // Direction character
                                var ch = 45  // '-'
                                let abs_vx = vx
                                let abs_vy = vy
                                if abs_vx < 0.0 { let abs_vx = 0.0 - abs_vx }
                                if abs_vy < 0.0 { let abs_vy = 0.0 - abs_vy }

                                if abs_vy > abs_vx * 2.0 {
                                    ch = 124  // '|'
                                } else { if abs_vx > abs_vy * 2.0 {
                                    ch = 45  // '-'
                                } else {
                                    if vx * vy > 0.0 {
                                        ch = 92  // '\'
                                    } else {
                                        ch = 47  // '/'
                                    }
                                }}

                                if idx < 1800 {
                                    display[idx] = ch
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }

                // Euler step
                let r1x = sx + 1.0
                let r1y = sy
                let r1sq = r1x * r1x + r1y * r1y + 0.1
                let r2x = sx - 1.0
                let r2y = sy
                let r2sq = r2x * r2x + r2y * r2y + 0.1

                let vx = r1x / r1sq - r2x / r2sq
                let vy = r1y / r1sq - r2y / r2sq

                let vlen = sqrt_simple(vx * vx + vy * vy)
                if vlen > 0.01 {
                    sx = sx + vx * 0.03 / vlen
                    sy = sy + vy * 0.03 / vlen
                } else {
                    step = 200
                }
            }}}}

            step = step + 1
        }

        seed = seed + 1
    }

    // Mark source and sink
    let src_x = ((0.0 - 1.0 + 3.0) * 10.0) as i32
    let src_y = ((0.0 + 3.0) * 5.0) as i32
    let sink_x = ((1.0 + 3.0) * 10.0) as i32
    let sink_y = ((0.0 + 3.0) * 5.0) as i32

    if src_x >= 0 {
        if src_x < 60 {
            if src_y >= 0 {
                if src_y < 30 {
                    display[src_y * 60 + src_x] = 43  // '+'
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if sink_x >= 0 {
        if sink_x < 60 {
            if sink_y >= 0 {
                if sink_y < 30 {
                    display[sink_y * 60 + sink_x] = 45  // '-' for sink
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Render
    print("   y\n")
    print("   ^\n")

    var y = 29
    while y >= 0 {
        print("   |")

        var x = 0
        while x < 60 {
            let idx = y * 60 + x
            var ch = 32
            if idx < 1800 {
                ch = display[idx]
            }

            // Color streamlines cyan, special points red
            if ch == 43 {
                print("\x1b[1;31m+\x1b[0m")  // Source
            } else { if ch == 45 {
                if x == sink_x {
                    if y == sink_y {
                        print("\x1b[1;31m-\x1b[0m")  // Sink
                    } else {
                        print("\x1b[36m-\x1b[0m")
                    }
                } else {
                    print("\x1b[36m-\x1b[0m")
                }
            } else { if ch == 32 {
                print(" ")
            } else {
                print("\x1b[36m")
                print_char_code(ch)
                print("\x1b[0m")
            }}}

            x = x + 1
        }
        print("\n")
        y = y - 1
    }

    print("   +-------------------------------------------------------------> x\n")
    print("    -3                           0                              3\n\n")

    print("   Electric dipole field: \x1b[1;31m+\x1b[0m source at (-1,0), \x1b[1;31m-\x1b[0m sink at (1,0)\n")
    print("   Field lines flow from positive to negative charge\n")
}

fn sqrt_simple(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var g = x * 0.5
    if g < 1.0 { g = 1.0 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        g = 0.5 * (g + x / g)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return g
}

fn print_char_code(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 32 { print(" ") }
    else { if code == 45 { print("-") }
    else { if code == 47 { print("/") }
    else { if code == 92 { print("\\") }
    else { if code == 124 { print("|") }
    else { print(".") }
    }}}}
}

// === FILE: examples/graphics/demos/phase7_showcase.sio ===
// phase7_showcase.sio - Network/Graph Visualization Demonstration
//
// Showcases all Phase 7 graphics library capabilities:
// 1. Graph data structures and operations
// 2. Force-directed layout (Fruchterman-Reingold)
// 3. Tree layouts (binary, radial)
// 4. Graph rendering with colors and animation
//
// Run: ./bin/souc run examples/graphics/demos/phase7_showcase.sio

// ============================================================================
// Data Structures (simplified inline versions)
// ============================================================================

struct Node {
    id: i32,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    label: i32,
    color: i32,
    fixed: i32
}

struct Edge {
    from_id: i32,
    to_id: i32,
    weight: f64,
    directed: i32
}

struct Force {
    fx: f64,
    fy: f64
}

// ============================================================================
// Demo 1: Social Network Graph
// ============================================================================

fn demo_social_network() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;36m=== Demo 1: Social Network Graph ===\x1b[0m\n\n")

    // Create nodes (6 people)
    var nodes: [Node; 20] = [Node {
        id: 0, x: 0.0, y: 0.0, label: 65, color: 37, fixed: 0
    }; 20]

    var edges: [Edge; 50] = [Edge {
        from_id: 0, to_id: 0, weight: 1.0, directed: 0
    }; 50]

    // Initialize positions and labels
    let n_nodes = 6
    var i = 0
    while i < n_nodes {
        nodes[i].id = i
        nodes[i].label = 65 + i
        nodes[i].x = ((i % 3) as f64) * 10.0 - 10.0
        nodes[i].y = ((i / 3) as f64) * 8.0 - 4.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Create friendships
    let n_edges = 8
    edges[0] = Edge { from_id: 0, to_id: 1, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // A-B
    edges[1] = Edge { from_id: 0, to_id: 2, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // A-C
    edges[2] = Edge { from_id: 1, to_id: 2, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // B-C
    edges[3] = Edge { from_id: 1, to_id: 3, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // B-D
    edges[4] = Edge { from_id: 2, to_id: 4, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // C-E
    edges[5] = Edge { from_id: 3, to_id: 4, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // D-E
    edges[6] = Edge { from_id: 3, to_id: 5, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // D-F
    edges[7] = Edge { from_id: 4, to_id: 5, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // E-F

    print("Social network with ")
    print_i32(n_nodes)
    print(" people and ")
    print_i32(n_edges)
    print(" friendships\n\n")

    // Apply force-directed layout
    print("Applying Fruchterman-Reingold layout...\n\n")

    var forces: [Force; 20] = [Force { fx: 0.0, fy: 0.0 }; 20]
    let k = 8.0  // Optimal distance
    var temperature = 10.0

    var iter = 0
    while iter < 50 {
        // Reset forces
        var f = 0
        while f < n_nodes {
            forces[f].fx = 0.0
            forces[f].fy = 0.0
            f = f + 1
        }

        // Repulsive forces
        i = 0
        while i < n_nodes {
            var j = 0
            while j < n_nodes {
                if i != j {
                    let dx = nodes[i].x - nodes[j].x
                    let dy = nodes[i].y - nodes[j].y
                    let dist = sqrt_approx(dx * dx + dy * dy) + 0.1
                    let force = (k * k) / dist
                    forces[i].fx = forces[i].fx + (dx / dist) * force
                    forces[i].fy = forces[i].fy + (dy / dist) * force
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Attractive forces
        var e = 0
        while e < n_edges {
            let from = edges[e].from_id
            let to = edges[e].to_id
            let dx = nodes[to].x - nodes[from].x
            let dy = nodes[to].y - nodes[from].y
            let dist = sqrt_approx(dx * dx + dy * dy) + 0.1
            let force = (dist * dist) / k

            forces[from].fx = forces[from].fx + (dx / dist) * force
            forces[from].fy = forces[from].fy + (dy / dist) * force
            forces[to].fx = forces[to].fx - (dx / dist) * force
            forces[to].fy = forces[to].fy - (dy / dist) * force

            e = e + 1
        }

        // Apply forces with temperature limiting
        i = 0
        while i < n_nodes {
            let mag = sqrt_approx(forces[i].fx * forces[i].fx + forces[i].fy * forces[i].fy)
            if mag > temperature {
                forces[i].fx = forces[i].fx * temperature / mag
                forces[i].fy = forces[i].fy * temperature / mag
            }
            nodes[i].x = nodes[i].x + forces[i].fx
            nodes[i].y = nodes[i].y + forces[i].fy
            i = i + 1
        }

        temperature = temperature * 0.95
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Display result
    print("Layout complete. Final positions:\n")
    i = 0
    while i < n_nodes {
        print("  ")
        print_node_label(nodes[i].label)
        print(": (")
        print_f64(nodes[i].x)
        print(", ")
        print_f64(nodes[i].y)
        print(")\n")
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Render ASCII visualization
    print("\n")
    render_graph_ascii(&nodes, n_nodes, &edges, n_edges, 50, 15)

    print("\nPress Enter for next demo...")
    wait_for_input()
}

// ============================================================================
// Demo 2: Binary Tree Layout
// ============================================================================

fn demo_binary_tree() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;36m=== Demo 2: Binary Tree Layout ===\x1b[0m\n\n")

    var nodes: [Node; 20] = [Node {
        id: 0, x: 0.0, y: 0.0, label: 65, color: 37, fixed: 0
    }; 20]

    var edges: [Edge; 50] = [Edge {
        from_id: 0, to_id: 0, weight: 1.0, directed: 0
    }; 50]

    // Create binary tree: 15 nodes (depth 4)
    let n_nodes = 15

    // Initialize labels
    var i = 0
    while i < n_nodes {
        nodes[i].id = i
        nodes[i].label = 65 + i
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Create edges (parent to children)
    let n_edges = 14
    i = 0
    while i < 7 {  // Internal nodes
        let left = 2 * i + 1
        let right = 2 * i + 2
        edges[2 * i] = Edge { from_id: i, to_id: left, weight: 1.0, directed: 1 }
        edges[2 * i + 1] = Edge { from_id: i, to_id: right, weight: 1.0, directed: 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }

    print("Binary tree with ")
    print_i32(n_nodes)
    print(" nodes (depth 4)\n\n")

    // Apply hierarchical layout
    print("Applying hierarchical layout...\n\n")

    let level_height = 3.0
    let node_sep = 2.5

    // Position nodes by level
    // Level 0: 1 node at center
    nodes[0].x = 0.0
    nodes[0].y = 0.0

    // Level 1: 2 nodes
    nodes[1].x = -8.0
    nodes[1].y = level_height
    nodes[2].x = 8.0
    nodes[2].y = level_height

    // Level 2: 4 nodes
    nodes[3].x = -12.0
    nodes[3].y = 2.0 * level_height
    nodes[4].x = -4.0
    nodes[4].y = 2.0 * level_height
    nodes[5].x = 4.0
    nodes[5].y = 2.0 * level_height
    nodes[6].x = 12.0
    nodes[6].y = 2.0 * level_height

    // Level 3: 8 nodes
    var leaf_start = 7
    var leaf_x = -14.0
    i = 0
    while i < 8 {
        nodes[leaf_start + i].x = leaf_x
        nodes[leaf_start + i].y = 3.0 * level_height
        leaf_x = leaf_x + 4.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Display structure
    print("Tree structure:\n")
    print("  Level 0 (root): A\n")
    print("  Level 1:        B, C\n")
    print("  Level 2:        D, E, F, G\n")
    print("  Level 3 (leaves): H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O\n\n")

    // Render
    render_tree_ascii(&nodes, n_nodes, &edges, n_edges, 50, 12)

    print("\nPress Enter for next demo...")
    wait_for_input()
}

// ============================================================================
// Demo 3: Radial Tree Layout
// ============================================================================

fn demo_radial_tree() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;36m=== Demo 3: Radial Tree Layout ===\x1b[0m\n\n")

    var nodes: [Node; 20] = [Node {
        id: 0, x: 0.0, y: 0.0, label: 65, color: 37, fixed: 0
    }; 20]

    var edges: [Edge; 50] = [Edge {
        from_id: 0, to_id: 0, weight: 1.0, directed: 0
    }; 50]

    // Create tree with root and 6 children, each with 2 grandchildren
    let n_nodes = 13  // 1 root + 4 children + 8 grandchildren

    // Initialize
    var i = 0
    while i < n_nodes {
        nodes[i].id = i
        nodes[i].label = 65 + i
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Edges: root to children, children to grandchildren
    let n_edges = 12
    // Root to children (0 -> 1,2,3,4)
    edges[0] = Edge { from_id: 0, to_id: 1, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[1] = Edge { from_id: 0, to_id: 2, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[2] = Edge { from_id: 0, to_id: 3, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[3] = Edge { from_id: 0, to_id: 4, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }

    // Children to grandchildren
    edges[4] = Edge { from_id: 1, to_id: 5, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[5] = Edge { from_id: 1, to_id: 6, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[6] = Edge { from_id: 2, to_id: 7, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[7] = Edge { from_id: 2, to_id: 8, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[8] = Edge { from_id: 3, to_id: 9, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[9] = Edge { from_id: 3, to_id: 10, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[10] = Edge { from_id: 4, to_id: 11, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }
    edges[11] = Edge { from_id: 4, to_id: 12, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }

    print("Radial tree with ")
    print_i32(n_nodes)
    print(" nodes (3 levels)\n\n")

    // Apply radial layout
    print("Applying radial layout...\n\n")

    // Root at center
    nodes[0].x = 0.0
    nodes[0].y = 0.0

    // Level 1: 4 children in circle
    let r1 = 5.0
    i = 0
    while i < 4 {
        let angle = (i as f64) * 1.5708  // 90 degrees apart
        nodes[1 + i].x = cos_approx(angle) * r1
        nodes[1 + i].y = sin_approx(angle) * r1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Level 2: 2 grandchildren per child
    let r2 = 10.0
    i = 0
    while i < 4 {
        let base_angle = (i as f64) * 1.5708
        let spread = 0.5

        let gc1 = 5 + i * 2
        let gc2 = 5 + i * 2 + 1

        nodes[gc1].x = cos_approx(base_angle - spread) * r2
        nodes[gc1].y = sin_approx(base_angle - spread) * r2
        nodes[gc2].x = cos_approx(base_angle + spread) * r2
        nodes[gc2].y = sin_approx(base_angle + spread) * r2

        i = i + 1
    }

    // Render
    render_radial_ascii(&nodes, n_nodes, &edges, n_edges, 50, 20)

    print("\nPress Enter for next demo...")
    wait_for_input()
}

// ============================================================================
// Demo 4: Graph Traversal Animation
// ============================================================================

fn demo_graph_traversal() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;36m=== Demo 4: BFS Graph Traversal ===\x1b[0m\n\n")

    // Simple graph for BFS demo
    var nodes: [Node; 10] = [Node {
        id: 0, x: 0.0, y: 0.0, label: 65, color: 37, fixed: 0
    }; 10]

    let n_nodes = 7

    // Arrange in a pattern
    nodes[0].x = 0.0; nodes[0].y = 0.0; nodes[0].label = 65  // A (start)
    nodes[1].x = -6.0; nodes[1].y = 4.0; nodes[1].label = 66  // B
    nodes[2].x = 6.0; nodes[2].y = 4.0; nodes[2].label = 67  // C
    nodes[3].x = -9.0; nodes[3].y = 8.0; nodes[3].label = 68  // D
    nodes[4].x = -3.0; nodes[4].y = 8.0; nodes[4].label = 69  // E
    nodes[5].x = 3.0; nodes[5].y = 8.0; nodes[5].label = 70  // F
    nodes[6].x = 9.0; nodes[6].y = 8.0; nodes[6].label = 71  // G

    // Edges
    var edges: [Edge; 20] = [Edge {
        from_id: 0, to_id: 0, weight: 1.0, directed: 0
    }; 20]

    let n_edges = 8
    edges[0] = Edge { from_id: 0, to_id: 1, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // A-B
    edges[1] = Edge { from_id: 0, to_id: 2, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // A-C
    edges[2] = Edge { from_id: 1, to_id: 3, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // B-D
    edges[3] = Edge { from_id: 1, to_id: 4, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // B-E
    edges[4] = Edge { from_id: 2, to_id: 5, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // C-F
    edges[5] = Edge { from_id: 2, to_id: 6, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // C-G
    edges[6] = Edge { from_id: 4, to_id: 5, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // E-F (cross edge)
    edges[7] = Edge { from_id: 3, to_id: 4, weight: 1.0, directed: 0 }  // D-E

    print("BFS traversal starting from node A\n\n")

    // Build adjacency for BFS
    var adj: [i32; 50] = [0; 50]
    var adj_offset: [i32; 10] = [0; 10]

    // Count degrees
    var degrees: [i32; 10] = [0; 10]
    var e = 0
    while e < n_edges {
        degrees[edges[e].from_id] = degrees[edges[e].from_id] + 1
        degrees[edges[e].to_id] = degrees[edges[e].to_id] + 1
        e = e + 1
    }

    // Build offsets
    adj_offset[0] = 0
    var n = 0
    while n < n_nodes {
        adj_offset[n + 1] = adj_offset[n] + degrees[n]
        degrees[n] = 0  // Reset for filling
        n = n + 1
    }

    // Fill adjacency
    e = 0
    while e < n_edges {
        let from = edges[e].from_id
        let to = edges[e].to_id

        adj[adj_offset[from] + degrees[from]] = to
        degrees[from] = degrees[from] + 1

        adj[adj_offset[to] + degrees[to]] = from
        degrees[to] = degrees[to] + 1

        e = e + 1
    }

    // BFS traversal
    var visited: [i32; 10] = [0; 10]
    var queue: [i32; 20] = [0; 20]
    var q_front = 0
    var q_back = 0

    // Start from A
    queue[q_back] = 0
    q_back = q_back + 1

    print("Traversal order: ")

    var step = 0
    while q_front < q_back {
        let current = queue[q_front]
        q_front = q_front + 1

        if visited[current] == 0 {
            visited[current] = 1

            // Print current node
            if step > 0 { print(" -> ") }
            print_node_label(nodes[current].label)
            step = step + 1

            // Enqueue neighbors
            var i = adj_offset[current]
            while i < adj_offset[current + 1] {
                let neighbor = adj[i]
                if visited[neighbor] == 0 {
                    queue[q_back] = neighbor
                    q_back = q_back + 1
                }
                i = i + 1
            }
        }
    }

    print("\n\nLevel-order exploration:\n")
    print("  Level 0: A (start)\n")
    print("  Level 1: B, C (neighbors of A)\n")
    print("  Level 2: D, E, F, G (neighbors of B and C)\n\n")

    // Show graph structure
    render_bfs_ascii(&nodes, n_nodes, &edges, n_edges, 40, 12)

    print("\nPress Enter to finish...")
    wait_for_input()
}

// ============================================================================
// ASCII Rendering Functions
// ============================================================================

fn render_graph_ascii(
    nodes: &[Node], n_nodes: i32,
    edges: &[Edge], n_edges: i32,
    width: i32, height: i32
) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Find bounds
    var min_x = nodes[0].x
    var max_x = nodes[0].x
    var min_y = nodes[0].y
    var max_y = nodes[0].y

    var i = 1
    while i < n_nodes {
        if nodes[i].x < min_x { min_x = nodes[i].x }
        if nodes[i].x > max_x { max_x = nodes[i].x }
        if nodes[i].y < min_y { min_y = nodes[i].y }
        if nodes[i].y > max_y { max_y = nodes[i].y }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Add margin
    min_x = min_x - 2.0
    max_x = max_x + 2.0
    min_y = min_y - 1.0
    max_y = max_y + 1.0

    // Create buffer
    var buffer: [i32; 1000] = [32; 1000]  // Space

    // Draw edges
    var e = 0
    while e < n_edges {
        let from = edges[e].from_id
        let to = edges[e].to_id

        let x0 = scale_x(nodes[from].x, min_x, max_x, width)
        let y0 = scale_y(nodes[from].y, min_y, max_y, height)
        let x1 = scale_x(nodes[to].x, min_x, max_x, width)
        let y1 = scale_y(nodes[to].y, min_y, max_y, height)

        draw_line_buffer(&!buffer, width, height, x0, y0, x1, y1, 45)  // '-'
        e = e + 1
    }

    // Draw nodes
    i = 0
    while i < n_nodes {
        let x = scale_x(nodes[i].x, min_x, max_x, width)
        let y = scale_y(nodes[i].y, min_y, max_y, height)
        let idx = y * width + x
        if idx >= 0 {
            if idx < 1000 {
                buffer[idx] = nodes[i].label
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Print buffer
    var y = 0
    while y < height {
        var x = 0
        while x < width {
            let idx = y * width + x
            let ch = buffer[idx]
            if ch >= 65 {
                if ch <= 90 {
                    print("\x1b[1;36m")  // Cyan bold for nodes
                }
            }
            print_char_simple(ch)
            print("\x1b[0m")
            x = x + 1
        }
        print("\n")
        y = y + 1
    }
}

fn render_tree_ascii(
    nodes: &[Node], n_nodes: i32,
    edges: &[Edge], n_edges: i32,
    width: i32, height: i32
) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var buffer: [i32; 1000] = [32; 1000]

    let min_x = -16.0
    let max_x = 16.0
    let min_y = -1.0
    let max_y = 10.0

    // Draw edges as vertical lines where possible
    var e = 0
    while e < n_edges {
        let from = edges[e].from_id
        let to = edges[e].to_id

        let x0 = scale_x(nodes[from].x, min_x, max_x, width)
        let y0 = scale_y(nodes[from].y, min_y, max_y, height)
        let x1 = scale_x(nodes[to].x, min_x, max_x, width)
        let y1 = scale_y(nodes[to].y, min_y, max_y, height)

        draw_line_buffer(&!buffer, width, height, x0, y0, x1, y1, 124)  // '|'
        e = e + 1
    }

    // Draw nodes
    var i = 0
    while i < n_nodes {
        let x = scale_x(nodes[i].x, min_x, max_x, width)
        let y = scale_y(nodes[i].y, min_y, max_y, height)
        let idx = y * width + x
        if idx >= 0 {
            if idx < 1000 {
                buffer[idx] = nodes[i].label
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Print
    var y = 0
    while y < height {
        var x = 0
        while x < width {
            let idx = y * width + x
            let ch = buffer[idx]
            if ch >= 65 {
                if ch <= 90 {
                    print("\x1b[1;32m")  // Green for tree nodes
                }
            } else { if ch == 124 {
                print("\x1b[33m")  // Yellow for edges
            }}
            print_char_simple(ch)
            print("\x1b[0m")
            x = x + 1
        }
        print("\n")
        y = y + 1
    }
}

fn render_radial_ascii(
    nodes: &[Node], n_nodes: i32,
    edges: &[Edge], n_edges: i32,

fn render_bfs_ascii(
    nodes: &[Node], n_nodes: i32,
    edges: &[Edge], n_edges: i32,
    width: i32, height: i32
) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var buffer: [i32; 600] = [32; 600]

    let min_x = -12.0
    let max_x = 12.0
    let min_y = -2.0
    let max_y = 10.0

    // Draw edges
    var e = 0
    while e < n_edges {
        let from = edges[e].from_id
        let to = edges[e].to_id

        let x0 = scale_x(nodes[from].x, min_x, max_x, width)
        let y0 = scale_y(nodes[from].y, min_y, max_y, height)
        let x1 = scale_x(nodes[to].x, min_x, max_x, width)
        let y1 = scale_y(nodes[to].y, min_y, max_y, height)

        draw_line_buffer(&!buffer, width, height, x0, y0, x1, y1, 46)  // '.'
        e = e + 1
    }

    // Draw nodes
    var i = 0
    while i < n_nodes {
        let x = scale_x(nodes[i].x, min_x, max_x, width)
        let y = scale_y(nodes[i].y, min_y, max_y, height)
        let idx = y * width + x
        if idx >= 0 {
            if idx < 600 {
                buffer[idx] = nodes[i].label
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Print
    var y = 0
    while y < height {
        var x = 0
        while x < width {
            let idx = y * width + x
            let ch = buffer[idx]
            if ch >= 65 {
                if ch <= 90 {
                    print("\x1b[1;33m")  // Yellow for BFS nodes
                }
            }
            print_char_simple(ch)
            print("\x1b[0m")
            x = x + 1
        }
        print("\n")
        y = y + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Drawing Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn scale_x(x: f64, min: f64, max: f64, width: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    let range = max - min
    if range <= 0.0 { return 0 }
    let t = (x - min) / range
    return (t * ((width - 1) as f64)) as i32
}

fn scale_y(y: f64, min: f64, max: f64, height: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    let range = max - min
    if range <= 0.0 { return 0 }
    let t = (y - min) / range
    return ((1.0 - t) * ((height - 1) as f64)) as i32  // Flip Y
}

fn draw_line_buffer(
    buffer: &![i32],
    width: i32, height: i32,
    x0: i32, y0: i32,
    x1: i32, y1: i32,
    ch: i32
) with Mut {
    var dx = x1 - x0
    var dy = y1 - y0
    var abs_dx = dx
    var abs_dy = dy
    if dx < 0 { abs_dx = 0 - dx }
    if dy < 0 { abs_dy = 0 - dy }

    var sx = 1
    var sy = 1
    if dx < 0 { sx = -1 }
    if dy < 0 { sy = -1 }

    var err = abs_dx - abs_dy
    var x = x0
    var y = y0

    var steps = 0
    let max_steps = abs_dx + abs_dy + 1

    while steps < max_steps {
        if x >= 0 {
            if x < width {
                if y >= 0 {
                    if y < height {
                        let idx = y * width + x
                        if idx < 1200 {
                            if buffer[idx] == 32 {  // Only draw on empty
                                buffer[idx] = ch
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if x == x1 {
            if y == y1 {
                return
            }
        }

        let e2 = 2 * err
        if e2 > 0 - abs_dy {
            err = err - abs_dy
            x = x + sx
        }
        if e2 < abs_dx {
            err = err + abs_dx
            y = y + sy
        }

        steps = steps + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Math and Print Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x * 0.5
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        guess = (guess + x / guess) * 0.5
        i = i + 1
    }
    return guess
}

fn sin_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var xx = x
    while xx > 3.14159 { xx = xx - 6.28318 }
    while xx < -3.14159 { xx = xx + 6.28318 }
    let x2 = xx * xx
    let x3 = x2 * xx
    let x5 = x3 * x2
    return xx - x3 * 0.16667 + x5 * 0.00833
}

fn cos_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return sin_approx(x + 1.5708)
}

fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 { print("0"); return }
    if x < 0 { print("-"); print_i32_unsigned(0 - x) }
    else { print_i32_unsigned(x) }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 { return }
    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10
    if rest > 0 { print_i32_unsigned(rest) }
    print_digit(digit)
}

fn print_digit(d: i32) with IO {
    if d == 0 { print("0") }
    else { if d == 1 { print("1") }
    else { if d == 2 { print("2") }
    else { if d == 3 { print("3") }
    else { if d == 4 { print("4") }
    else { if d == 5 { print("5") }
    else { if d == 6 { print("6") }
    else { if d == 7 { print("7") }
    else { if d == 8 { print("8") }
    else { if d == 9 { print("9") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}

fn print_f64(x: f64) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 { print("-"); print_f64_pos(0.0 - x) }
    else { print_f64_pos(x) }
}

fn print_f64_pos(x: f64) with IO, Div, Panic {
    let int_part = x as i32
    print_i32(int_part)
    print(".")
    let frac = x - (int_part as f64)
    var frac_scaled = (frac * 100.0) as i32
    if frac_scaled < 0 { frac_scaled = 0 }
    if frac_scaled < 10 { print("0") }
    print_i32_unsigned(frac_scaled)
}

fn print_node_label(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 65 { print("A") }
    else { if code == 66 { print("B") }
    else { if code == 67 { print("C") }
    else { if code == 68 { print("D") }
    else { if code == 69 { print("E") }
    else { if code == 70 { print("F") }
    else { if code == 71 { print("G") }
    else { if code == 72 { print("H") }
    else { if code == 73 { print("I") }
    else { if code == 74 { print("J") }
    else { if code == 75 { print("K") }
    else { if code == 76 { print("L") }
    else { if code == 77 { print("M") }
    else { if code == 78 { print("N") }
    else { if code == 79 { print("O") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}}}}}}}
}

fn print_char_simple(ch: i32) with IO {
    if ch == 32 { print(" ") }
    else { if ch == 42 { print("*") }
    else { if ch == 45 { print("-") }
    else { if ch == 46 { print(".") }
    else { if ch == 124 { print("|") }
    else { if ch >= 65 {
        if ch <= 90 {
            print_node_label(ch)
        } else {
            print(" ")
        }
    } else {
        print(" ")
    }}}}}}
}

fn wait_for_input() with IO {
    // Busy wait simulation (no actual input in Sounio yet)
    var i = 0
    while i < 50000000 {
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;35m")
    print("╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
    print("║      Phase 7: Network/Graph Visualization Showcase       ║\n")
    print("║                                                          ║\n")
    print("║  Demonstrating graph structures, layouts, and rendering  ║\n")

    print("\x1b[0m\n")

    print("This showcase demonstrates:\n\n")
    print("  1. \x1b[36mSocial Network\x1b[0m - Force-directed layout (Fruchterman-Reingold)\n")
    print("  2. \x1b[32mBinary Tree\x1b[0m - Hierarchical layout with levels\n")
    print("  3. \x1b[35mRadial Tree\x1b[0m - Circular layout from center\n")

    print("\n")

    print("Press Enter to begin...")
    wait_for_input()

    demo_social_network()
    demo_binary_tree()
    demo_radial_tree()
    demo_graph_traversal()

    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")
    print("\x1b[1;32m")

    print("╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n")

// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/00_canvas.sio ===
// Canvas Abstraction - In-memory framebuffer for terminal graphics
//
// Provides a character grid with color attributes that can be manipulated
// before rendering to the terminal. Enables double buffering and complex
// compositions.

// Cell represents a single character cell with color and styling
struct Cell {
    ch: i32,        // Unicode character (as int codepoint)
    fg_color: i32,  // Foreground color code (0-15 for ANSI)
    bg_color: i32,  // Background color code (0-15)
    bold: i32,      // 0 or 1
    dim: i32        // 0 or 1
}

// Canvas is an in-memory framebuffer of character cells
struct Canvas {
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    cells: [Cell; 2400]  // 80×30 default
}

// Helper: Create a blank cell with space character
fn cell_blank() -> Cell {
    return Cell {
        ch: 32,        // Space character
        fg_color: 7,   // White
        bg_color: 0,   // Black
        bold: 0,
        dim: 0
    }
}

// Initialize a new canvas with given dimensions
fn canvas_new(width: i32, height: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var canvas = Canvas {
        width: width,
        height: height,
        cells: [cell_blank(); 2400]
    }

    // Initialize all cells to blank
    var i = 0
    while i < width * height {
        canvas.cells[i] = cell_blank()
        i = i + 1
    }

    return canvas
}

// Clear canvas (reset all cells to blank) - functional style
fn canvas_clear_func(canvas: Canvas) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var new_canvas = canvas
    var i = 0
    let total = new_canvas.width * new_canvas.height
    while i < total {
        new_canvas.cells[i] = cell_blank()
        i = i + 1
    }
    return new_canvas
}

// Set a cell at (x, y) position - functional style
fn canvas_set_func(canvas: Canvas, x: i32, y: i32, ch: i32, fg: i32, bg: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic {
    // Bounds check
    if x < 0 { return canvas }
    if y < 0 { return canvas }
    if x >= canvas.width { return canvas }
    if y >= canvas.height { return canvas }

    var new_canvas = canvas
    let index = y * canvas.width + x
    new_canvas.cells[index] = Cell {
        ch: ch,
        fg_color: fg,
        bg_color: bg,
        bold: 0,
        dim: 0
    }
    return new_canvas
}

// Get a cell at (x, y) position
fn canvas_get(canvas: &Canvas, x: i32, y: i32) -> Cell with Panic {
    // Bounds check - return blank cell if out of bounds
    if x < 0 { return cell_blank() }
    if y < 0 { return cell_blank() }
    if x >= canvas.width { return cell_blank() }
    if y >= canvas.height { return cell_blank() }

    let index = y * canvas.width + x
    return canvas.cells[index]
}

// Helper: Convert color code to ANSI foreground sequence
fn color_code_to_fg_ansi(color: i32) -> i32 {
    // Map color codes 0-15 to ANSI codes
    // 0-7: normal colors (30-37)
    // 8-15: bright colors (90-97)
    if color < 8 {
        return 30 + color
    } else {
        return 90 + (color - 8)
    }
}

// Helper: Convert color code to ANSI background sequence
fn color_code_to_bg_ansi(color: i32) -> i32 {
    // Map color codes 0-15 to ANSI codes
    // 0-7: normal colors (40-47)
    // 8-15: bright colors (100-107)
    if color < 8 {
        return 40 + color
    } else {
        return 100 + (color - 8)
    }
}

// Helper: Print ANSI escape sequence for foreground color
fn print_fg_color(color: i32) with IO {
    print("\x1b[")

    // Convert color code to ANSI
    let ansi_code = color_code_to_fg_ansi(color)

    // Print the number (need to convert i32 to output)
    // Simple approach: use conditionals for 30-37, 90-97
    if ansi_code == 30 { print("30") }
    if ansi_code == 31 { print("31") }
    if ansi_code == 32 { print("32") }
    if ansi_code == 33 { print("33") }
    if ansi_code == 34 { print("34") }
    if ansi_code == 35 { print("35") }
    if ansi_code == 36 { print("36") }
    if ansi_code == 37 { print("37") }
    if ansi_code == 90 { print("90") }
    if ansi_code == 91 { print("91") }
    if ansi_code == 92 { print("92") }
    if ansi_code == 93 { print("93") }
    if ansi_code == 94 { print("94") }
    if ansi_code == 95 { print("95") }
    if ansi_code == 96 { print("96") }
    if ansi_code == 97 { print("97") }

    print("m")
}

// Helper: Print ANSI escape sequence for background color
fn print_bg_color(color: i32) with IO {
    print("\x1b[")

    // Convert color code to ANSI
    let ansi_code = color_code_to_bg_ansi(color)

    // Print the number
    if ansi_code == 40 { print("40") }
    if ansi_code == 41 { print("41") }
    if ansi_code == 42 { print("42") }
    if ansi_code == 43 { print("43") }
    if ansi_code == 44 { print("44") }
    if ansi_code == 45 { print("45") }
    if ansi_code == 46 { print("46") }
    if ansi_code == 47 { print("47") }
    if ansi_code == 100 { print("100") }
    if ansi_code == 101 { print("101") }
    if ansi_code == 102 { print("102") }
    if ansi_code == 103 { print("103") }
    if ansi_code == 104 { print("104") }
    if ansi_code == 105 { print("105") }
    if ansi_code == 106 { print("106") }
    if ansi_code == 107 { print("107") }

    print("m")
}

// Helper: Print character from code point
fn print_char_code(code: i32) with IO {
    // Map common character codes to their characters
    // For ASCII printable: 32-126
    if code == 32 { print(" ") }
    if code == 33 { print("!") }
    if code == 35 { print("#") }
    if code == 42 { print("*") }
    if code == 43 { print("+") }
    if code == 45 { print("-") }
    if code == 46 { print(".") }
    if code == 61 { print("=") }
    if code == 72 { print("H") }
    if code == 88 { print("X") }
    if code == 101 { print("e") }
    if code == 108 { print("l") }
    if code == 111 { print("o") }
    if code == 124 { print("|") }

    // Unicode box drawing characters
    if code == 9473 { print("-") }  // Horizontal line (simplified)
    if code == 9474 { print("|") }  // Vertical line (simplified)

    // Unicode block characters
    if code == 9608 { print("█") }  // Full block
    if code == 9617 { print("░") }  // Light shade
    if code == 9618 { print("▒") }  // Medium shade
    if code == 9619 { print("▓") }  // Dark shade
    if code == 9632 { print("■") }  // Black square

    // Fallback: print space for unknown characters
    // TODO: Add more character mappings as needed
}

// Render canvas to terminal
fn canvas_render(canvas: &Canvas) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Save cursor position and clear screen
    print("\x1b[H")  // Home cursor

    var y = 0
    while y < canvas.height {
        var x = 0

        // Track current styling to avoid redundant ANSI codes
        var current_fg = -1
        var current_bg = -1
        var current_bold = 0
        var current_dim = 0

        while x < canvas.width {
            let cell = canvas_get(canvas, x, y)

            // Update foreground color if changed
            if cell.fg_color != current_fg {
                print_fg_color(cell.fg_color)
                current_fg = cell.fg_color
            }

            // Update background color if changed
            if cell.bg_color != current_bg {
                print_bg_color(cell.bg_color)
                current_bg = cell.bg_color
            }

            // Update bold if changed
            if cell.bold != current_bold {
                if cell.bold == 1 {
                    print("\x1b[1m")
                } else {
                    print("\x1b[22m")  // Normal intensity
                }
                current_bold = cell.bold
            }

            // Update dim if changed
            if cell.dim != current_dim {
                if cell.dim == 1 {
                    print("\x1b[2m")
                } else {
                    print("\x1b[22m")  // Normal intensity
                }
                current_dim = cell.dim
            }

            // Print character
            print_char_code(cell.ch)

            x = x + 1
        }

        // Reset styles at end of line
        print("\x1b[0m")
        print("\n")

        y = y + 1
    }

    // Final reset
    print("\x1b[0m")
}

// Main function - simple test
fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Create a small canvas
    var canvas = canvas_new(40, 10)

    // Draw a border - functional style
    var x = 0
    while x < 40 {
        canvas = canvas_set_func(canvas, x, 0, 9473, 2, 0)  // Top border (green)
        canvas = canvas_set_func(canvas, x, 9, 9473, 2, 0)  // Bottom border
        x = x + 1
    }

    var y = 0
    while y < 10 {
        canvas = canvas_set_func(canvas, 0, y, 9474, 2, 0)   // Left border
        canvas = canvas_set_func(canvas, 39, y, 9474, 2, 0)  // Right border
        y = y + 1
    }

    // Draw some text
    canvas = canvas_set_func(canvas, 10, 5, 72, 3, 0)   // 'H' in yellow
    canvas = canvas_set_func(canvas, 11, 5, 101, 3, 0)  // 'e'
    canvas = canvas_set_func(canvas, 12, 5, 108, 3, 0)  // 'l'
    canvas = canvas_set_func(canvas, 13, 5, 108, 3, 0)  // 'l'
    canvas = canvas_set_func(canvas, 14, 5, 111, 3, 0)  // 'o'

    // Render to terminal
    canvas_render(&canvas)

    return 0
}

// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/01_colors.sio ===
// Color Management - ANSI 16-color palette with semantic mappings
//
// Provides standard ANSI color constants and helper functions for
// semantic color selection (uncertainty levels, temperature gradients, etc.)

// ============================================================================
// Standard ANSI 16-color palette (color codes 0-15)
// ============================================================================

// Normal colors (0-7)
fn COLOR_BLACK() -> i32 { return 0 }
fn COLOR_RED() -> i32 { return 1 }
fn COLOR_GREEN() -> i32 { return 2 }
fn COLOR_YELLOW() -> i32 { return 3 }
fn COLOR_BLUE() -> i32 { return 4 }
fn COLOR_MAGENTA() -> i32 { return 5 }
fn COLOR_CYAN() -> i32 { return 6 }
fn COLOR_WHITE() -> i32 { return 7 }

// Bright colors (8-15)
fn COLOR_BRIGHT_BLACK() -> i32 { return 8 }   // Gray
fn COLOR_BRIGHT_RED() -> i32 { return 9 }
fn COLOR_BRIGHT_GREEN() -> i32 { return 10 }
fn COLOR_BRIGHT_YELLOW() -> i32 { return 11 }
fn COLOR_BRIGHT_BLUE() -> i32 { return 12 }
fn COLOR_BRIGHT_MAGENTA() -> i32 { return 13 }
fn COLOR_BRIGHT_CYAN() -> i32 { return 14 }
fn COLOR_BRIGHT_WHITE() -> i32 { return 15 }

// ============================================================================
// Semantic color mappings for scientific visualization
// ============================================================================

// Map uncertainty level (0.0-1.0) to traffic light colors
// 0.0-0.3: Green (high confidence)
// 0.3-0.6: Yellow (medium confidence)
// 0.6-1.0: Red (low confidence)
fn uncertainty_to_color(normalized: f64) -> i32 {
    if normalized < 0.3 {
        return COLOR_GREEN()
    }
    if normalized < 0.6 {
        return COLOR_YELLOW()
    }
    return COLOR_RED()
}

// Map temperature value to heat map colors
// Uses blue → cyan → green → yellow → red gradient
fn temperature_to_color(temp: f64, min_temp: f64, max_temp: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Normalize to 0.0-1.0 range
    var normalized = (temp - min_temp) / (max_temp - min_temp)

    // Clamp to 0-1
    if normalized < 0.0 { normalized = 0.0 }
    if normalized > 1.0 { normalized = 1.0 }

    // Map to 5-step gradient
    if normalized < 0.2 {
        return COLOR_BLUE()       // Coldest
    }
    if normalized < 0.4 {
        return COLOR_CYAN()       // Cold
    }
    if normalized < 0.6 {
        return COLOR_GREEN()      // Medium
    }
    if normalized < 0.8 {
        return COLOR_YELLOW()     // Hot
    }
    return COLOR_RED()            // Hottest
}

// Map value to grayscale (black → white)
fn value_to_grayscale(value: f64, min_val: f64, max_val: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Normalize to 0.0-1.0
    var normalized = (value - min_val) / (max_val - min_val)

    // Clamp
    if normalized < 0.0 { normalized = 0.0 }
    if normalized > 1.0 { normalized = 1.0 }

    // Map to 4-step grayscale (black → gray → white → bright white)
    if normalized < 0.25 {
        return COLOR_BLACK()
    }
    if normalized < 0.5 {
        return COLOR_BRIGHT_BLACK()  // Gray
    }
    if normalized < 0.75 {
        return COLOR_WHITE()
    }
    return COLOR_BRIGHT_WHITE()
}

// Categorical colors for distinct data series (up to 8 series)
fn category_color(index: i32) -> i32 with Panic {
    let color_idx = index % 8  // Wrap around for >8 categories

    if color_idx == 0 { return COLOR_RED() }
    if color_idx == 1 { return COLOR_GREEN() }
    if color_idx == 2 { return COLOR_BLUE() }
    if color_idx == 3 { return COLOR_YELLOW() }
    if color_idx == 4 { return COLOR_MAGENTA() }
    if color_idx == 5 { return COLOR_CYAN() }
    if color_idx == 6 { return COLOR_WHITE() }
    return COLOR_BRIGHT_WHITE()
}

// Phase-coded colors for time series (absorption → distribution → elimination)
fn phase_color(phase_idx: i32) -> i32 {
    if phase_idx == 0 { return COLOR_GREEN() }   // Early phase
    if phase_idx == 1 { return COLOR_YELLOW() }  // Middle phase
    if phase_idx == 2 { return COLOR_RED() }     // Late phase
    return COLOR_WHITE()  // Unknown phase
}

// Status colors for pass/fail/warning indicators
fn status_pass_color() -> i32 { return COLOR_GREEN() }
fn status_fail_color() -> i32 { return COLOR_RED() }
fn status_warning_color() -> i32 { return COLOR_YELLOW() }
fn status_info_color() -> i32 { return COLOR_BLUE() }

// Scientific domain color schemes
fn octonion_basis_color(basis_idx: i32) -> i32 {
    // Color map for octonion basis elements (0-7)
    if basis_idx == 0 { return COLOR_WHITE() }    // Real part
    if basis_idx == 1 { return COLOR_RED() }      // i
    if basis_idx == 2 { return COLOR_GREEN() }    // j
    if basis_idx == 3 { return COLOR_BLUE() }     // k
    if basis_idx == 4 { return COLOR_YELLOW() }   // l
    if basis_idx == 5 { return COLOR_MAGENTA() }  // il
    if basis_idx == 6 { return COLOR_CYAN() }     // jl
    return COLOR_BRIGHT_WHITE()                   // kl
}

// Epidemic model compartments
fn sir_susceptible_color() -> i32 { return COLOR_BLUE() }
fn sir_infectious_color() -> i32 { return COLOR_RED() }
fn sir_recovered_color() -> i32 { return COLOR_GREEN() }

// ============================================================================
// Intensity/brightness modulation
// ============================================================================

// Get bright version of a normal color (0-7 → 8-15)
fn color_brighten(color: i32) -> i32 {
    if color >= 0 && color < 8 {
        return color + 8
    }
    return color  // Already bright or out of range
}

// Get normal version of a bright color (8-15 → 0-7)
fn color_dim(color: i32) -> i32 {
    if color >= 8 && color < 16 {
        return color - 8
    }
    return color  // Already normal or out of range
}

// ============================================================================
// Color blending/mixing (discrete approximation)
// ============================================================================

// Mix two colors (simple nearest-neighbor approximation)
// Returns the color closer to the midpoint
fn color_mix(color1: i32, color2: i32) -> i32 with Panic, Div {
    // Simple heuristic: if both are bright or both normal, average
    // Otherwise return the brighter one

    let both_bright = (color1 >= 8 && color2 >= 8)
    let both_normal = (color1 < 8 && color2 < 8)

    if both_bright || both_normal {
        // Average and clamp to valid range
        let avg = (color1 + color2) / 2
        if avg < 0 { return 0 }
        if avg > 15 { return 15 }
        return avg
    }

    // Return the brighter one
    if color1 >= 8 { return color1 }
    return color2
}

// ============================================================================
// Color name lookup (for display/debugging)
// ============================================================================

// Get human-readable color name
fn color_name(color: i32) -> i32 {
    // Returns a code representing the name (could be extended to return strings)
    // For now, just return the color code itself
    // TODO: When string manipulation is available, return actual names
    return color
}

// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/02_drawing.sio ===
// Drawing Primitives - Bresenham lines, circles, rectangles, and fills
//
// Implements efficient raster drawing algorithms for terminal graphics.
// All functions use functional style to avoid borrow checker issues.

// NOTE: This file needs Canvas type from 00_canvas.sio
// For now, we duplicate the necessary types until module system is ready

// Cell represents a single character cell
struct Cell {
    ch: i32,
    fg_color: i32,
    bg_color: i32,
    bold: i32,
    dim: i32
}

// Canvas framebuffer
struct Canvas {
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    cells: [Cell; 2400]
}

// Helper to set a single pixel on canvas (functional style)
fn canvas_set_pixel(canvas: Canvas, x: i32, y: i32, ch: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic {
    // Bounds check
    if x < 0 { return canvas }
    if y < 0 { return canvas }
    if x >= canvas.width { return canvas }
    if y >= canvas.height { return canvas }

    var new_canvas = canvas
    let index = y * canvas.width + x
    new_canvas.cells[index] = Cell {
        ch: ch,
        fg_color: color,
        bg_color: 0,
        bold: 0,
        dim: 0
    }
    return new_canvas
}

// ============================================================================
// Line Drawing - Bresenham's Algorithm
// ============================================================================

// Draw a line from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) using Bresenham's algorithm
fn draw_line(canvas: Canvas, x0: i32, y0: i32, x1: i32, y1: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    // Calculate deltas
    let dx = if x1 > x0 { x1 - x0 } else { x0 - x1 }
    let dy = if y1 > y0 { y1 - y0 } else { y0 - y1 }

    // Determine step directions
    let sx = if x0 < x1 { 1 } else { -1 }
    let sy = if y0 < y1 { 1 } else { -1 }

    var err = dx - dy
    var x = x0
    var y = y0

    // Bresenham's loop
    var done = 0
    while done == 0 {
        // Plot current point
        result = canvas_set_pixel(result, x, y, 9608, color)  // Full block █

        // Check if we've reached the end
        if x == x1 && y == y1 {
            done = 1
        } else {
            let e2 = 2 * err

            if e2 > -dy {
                err = err - dy
                x = x + sx
            }

            if e2 < dx {
                err = err + dx
                y = y + sy
            }
        }
    }

    return result
}

// Draw a horizontal line (optimized)
fn draw_hline(canvas: Canvas, x0: i32, x1: i32, y: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    let start_x = if x0 < x1 { x0 } else { x1 }
    let end_x = if x0 < x1 { x1 } else { x0 }

    var x = start_x
    while x <= end_x {
        result = canvas_set_pixel(result, x, y, 9608, color)
        x = x + 1
    }

    return result
}

// Draw a vertical line (optimized)
fn draw_vline(canvas: Canvas, x: i32, y0: i32, y1: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    let start_y = if y0 < y1 { y0 } else { y1 }
    let end_y = if y0 < y1 { y1 } else { y0 }

    var y = start_y
    while y <= end_y {
        result = canvas_set_pixel(result, x, y, 9608, color)
        y = y + 1
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// Circle Drawing - Midpoint Circle Algorithm
// ============================================================================

// Helper: Draw 8-way symmetric circle points
fn draw_circle_points(canvas: Canvas, cx: i32, cy: i32, x: i32, y: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic {
    var result = canvas

    // 8 symmetric points
    result = canvas_set_pixel(result, cx + x, cy + y, 9679, color)  // ○
    result = canvas_set_pixel(result, cx - x, cy + y, 9679, color)
    result = canvas_set_pixel(result, cx + x, cy - y, 9679, color)
    result = canvas_set_pixel(result, cx - x, cy - y, 9679, color)
    result = canvas_set_pixel(result, cx + y, cy + x, 9679, color)
    result = canvas_set_pixel(result, cx - y, cy + x, 9679, color)
    result = canvas_set_pixel(result, cx + y, cy - x, 9679, color)
    result = canvas_set_pixel(result, cx - y, cy - x, 9679, color)

    return result
}

// Draw a circle outline using midpoint algorithm
fn draw_circle(canvas: Canvas, cx: i32, cy: i32, radius: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    var x = 0
    var y = radius
    var d = 1 - radius  // Decision parameter

    // Draw initial point
    result = draw_circle_points(result, cx, cy, x, y, color)

    while x < y {
        x = x + 1

        // Update decision parameter
        if d < 0 {
            d = d + 2 * x + 1
        } else {
            y = y - 1
            d = d + 2 * (x - y) + 1
        }

        result = draw_circle_points(result, cx, cy, x, y, color)
    }

    return result
}

// Draw a filled circle
fn draw_circle_filled(canvas: Canvas, cx: i32, cy: i32, radius: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    var y = -radius
    while y <= radius {
        var x = -radius
        while x <= radius {
            // Check if point is inside circle
            let dist_sq = x * x + y * y
            if dist_sq <= radius * radius {
                result = canvas_set_pixel(result, cx + x, cy + y, 9608, color)
            }
            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// Rectangle Drawing
// ============================================================================

// Draw a rectangle outline
fn draw_rect(canvas: Canvas, x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    // Top and bottom edges
    result = draw_hline(result, x, x + width - 1, y, color)
    result = draw_hline(result, x, x + width - 1, y + height - 1, color)

    // Left and right edges
    result = draw_vline(result, x, y, y + height - 1, color)
    result = draw_vline(result, x + width - 1, y, y + height - 1, color)

    return result
}

// Draw a filled rectangle
fn fill_rect(canvas: Canvas, x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    var row = 0
    while row < height {
        result = draw_hline(result, x, x + width - 1, y + row, color)
        row = row + 1
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// Triangle Drawing
// ============================================================================

// Draw a triangle outline
fn draw_triangle(
    canvas: Canvas,
    x0: i32,
    y0: i32,
    x1: i32,
    y1: i32,
    x2: i32,
    y2: i32,
    color: i32
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    result = draw_line(result, x0, y0, x1, y1, color)
    result = draw_line(result, x1, y1, x2, y2, color)
    result = draw_line(result, x2, y2, x0, y0, color)

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// Polygon Drawing (general N-sided)
// ============================================================================

// Draw a polygon from an array of points
// NOTE: Simplified version without Point2D struct for now
fn draw_polygon_4(
    canvas: Canvas,
    x0: i32,
    y0: i32,
    x1: i32,
    y1: i32,
    x2: i32,
    y2: i32,
    x3: i32,
    y3: i32,
    color: i32
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    result = draw_line(result, x0, y0, x1, y1, color)
    result = draw_line(result, x1, y1, x2, y2, color)
    result = draw_line(result, x2, y2, x3, y3, color)
    result = draw_line(result, x3, y3, x0, y0, color)

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// Plotting Single Points
// ============================================================================

// Draw a single point with specific marker
fn draw_point(canvas: Canvas, x: i32, y: i32, marker: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic {
    return canvas_set_pixel(canvas, x, y, marker, color)
}

// Draw a point with default marker (small dot)
fn draw_dot(canvas: Canvas, x: i32, y: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic {
    return canvas_set_pixel(canvas, x, y, 9679, color)  // ○
}

// ============================================================================
// Grid Drawing
// ============================================================================

// Draw a rectangular grid
fn draw_grid(canvas: Canvas, x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32, spacing: i32, color: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    // Vertical lines
    var vx = x
    while vx <= x + width {
        result = draw_vline(result, vx, y, y + height, color)
        vx = vx + spacing
    }

    // Horizontal lines
    var hy = y
    while hy <= y + height {
        result = draw_hline(result, x, x + width, hy, color)
        hy = hy + spacing
    }

    return result
}

// Helper: Create blank cell
fn cell_blank() -> Cell {
    return Cell {
        ch: 32,
        fg_color: 7,
        bg_color: 0,
        bold: 0,
        dim: 0
    }
}

// Helper: Initialize canvas
fn canvas_new(width: i32, height: i32) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var canvas = Canvas {
        width: width,
        height: height,
        cells: [cell_blank(); 2400]
    }

    var i = 0
    while i < width * height {
        canvas.cells[i] = cell_blank()
        i = i + 1
    }

    return canvas
}

    // Create a test canvas
    var canvas = canvas_new(60, 30)

    // Test 1: Horizontal line
    print("Drawing horizontal line (y=5)...\n")
    canvas = draw_hline(canvas, 5, 25, 5, 2)  // Green line

    // Test 2: Vertical line
    print("Drawing vertical line (x=10)...\n")
    canvas = draw_vline(canvas, 10, 8, 20, 4)  // Blue line

    // Test 3: Diagonal line (Bresenham)
    print("Drawing diagonal line...\n")
    canvas = draw_line(canvas, 15, 10, 40, 20, 1)  // Red line

    // Test 4: Rectangle
    print("Drawing rectangle...\n")
    canvas = draw_rect(canvas, 25, 5, 10, 8, 3)  // Yellow rectangle

    // Test 5: Filled rectangle
    print("Drawing filled rectangle...\n")
    canvas = fill_rect(canvas, 30, 15, 8, 5, 5)  // Magenta filled

    // Test 6: Circle
    print("Drawing circle...\n")
    canvas = draw_circle(canvas, 50, 15, 7, 6)  // Cyan circle

    // Test 7: Triangle
    print("Drawing triangle...\n")
    canvas = draw_triangle(canvas, 5, 22, 10, 28, 15, 22, 2)  // Green triangle

    // Test 8: Dots
    print("Drawing scattered dots...\n")
    canvas = draw_dot(canvas, 45, 5, 1)
    canvas = draw_dot(canvas, 47, 6, 1)
    canvas = draw_dot(canvas, 49, 7, 1)

    print("\n=== All drawing primitives tested! ===\n")
    print("(Canvas created with various shapes, but not rendered to avoid ANSI complexity)\n")

    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/03_text.sio ===
// Text Rendering - Arbitrary positioning with alignment and styling
//
// Provides text rendering capabilities for terminal graphics with support
// for different alignments, colors, bold, and dim styling.

// Duplicate necessary types (until module system is ready)
struct Cell {
    ch: i32,
    fg_color: i32,
    bg_color: i32,
    bold: i32,
    dim: i32
}

struct Canvas {
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    cells: [Cell; 2400]
}

// Text styling options
struct TextStyle {
    fg_color: i32,
    bg_color: i32,
    bold: i32,      // 0 or 1
    dim: i32        // 0 or 1
}

// Default text style (white on black, normal intensity)
fn text_style_default() -> TextStyle {
    return TextStyle {
        fg_color: 7,    // White
        bg_color: 0,    // Black
        bold: 0,
        dim: 0
    }
}

// Create a styled text config
fn text_style_new(fg: i32, bg: i32, bold: i32, dim: i32) -> TextStyle {
    return TextStyle {
        fg_color: fg,
        bg_color: bg,
        bold: bold,
        dim: dim
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Character Rendering
// ============================================================================

// Helper: Set a character with style
fn canvas_set_char(canvas: Canvas, x: i32, y: i32, ch: i32, style: TextStyle) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic {
    // Bounds check
    if x < 0 { return canvas }
    if y < 0 { return canvas }
    if x >= canvas.width { return canvas }
    if y >= canvas.height { return canvas }

    var new_canvas = canvas
    let index = y * canvas.width + x
    new_canvas.cells[index] = Cell {
        ch: ch,
        fg_color: style.fg_color,
        bg_color: style.bg_color,
        bold: style.bold,
        dim: style.dim
    }
    return new_canvas
}

// ============================================================================
// String Length Calculation (character codes)
// ============================================================================

// Calculate length of a string represented as character codes
// For simplicity, we'll use fixed-length arrays and a sentinel value
// Sentinel: -1 marks end of string
fn string_length(chars: &[i32], max_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var len = 0
    while len < max_len {
        if chars[len] == -1 {
            return len
        }
        len = len + 1
    }
    return len
}

// ============================================================================
// Left-aligned Text
// ============================================================================

// Draw text left-aligned from (x, y)
// Text is array of character codes ending with -1 sentinel
fn draw_text_left(
    canvas: Canvas,
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    text: &[i32],
    max_len: i32,
    style: TextStyle
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas
    var i = 0
    var cur_x = x

    while i < max_len {
        let ch = text[i]
        if ch == -1 {
            return result  // End of string
        }

        result = canvas_set_char(result, cur_x, y, ch, style)
        cur_x = cur_x + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// Right-aligned Text
// ============================================================================

// Draw text right-aligned ending at (x, y)
fn draw_text_right(
    canvas: Canvas,
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    text: &[i32],
    max_len: i32,
    style: TextStyle
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let text_len = string_length(text, max_len)
    let start_x = x - text_len + 1

    return draw_text_left(canvas, start_x, y, text, max_len, style)
}

// ============================================================================
// Center-aligned Text
// ============================================================================

// Draw text centered at (x, y)
fn draw_text_center(
    canvas: Canvas,
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    text: &[i32],
    max_len: i32,
    style: TextStyle
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let text_len = string_length(text, max_len)
    let start_x = x - (text_len / 2)

    return draw_text_left(canvas, start_x, y, text, max_len, style)
}

// ============================================================================
// Multiline Text (automatic wrapping)
// ============================================================================

// Draw text with wrapping at specified width
// Returns the canvas and the number of lines used
fn draw_text_wrapped(
    canvas: Canvas,
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    text: &[i32],
    max_len: i32,
    wrap_width: i32,
    style: TextStyle
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas
    var i = 0
    var cur_x = x
    var cur_y = y
    var chars_in_line = 0

    while i < max_len {
        let ch = text[i]
        if ch == -1 {
            return result  // End of string
        }

        // Check if we need to wrap
        if chars_in_line >= wrap_width {
            cur_x = x
            cur_y = cur_y + 1
            chars_in_line = 0
        }

        result = canvas_set_char(result, cur_x, cur_y, ch, style)
        cur_x = cur_x + 1
        chars_in_line = chars_in_line + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// Number Formatting (for labels, axes, etc.)
// ============================================================================

// Convert digit (0-9) to ASCII character code
fn digit_to_char(digit: i32) -> i32 {
    return 48 + digit  // ASCII '0' = 48
}

// Format an integer as string (character codes)
// Stores result in output array, returns length
// NOTE: Simplified - only handles positive integers up to 99999
fn format_int(value: i32, output: &![i32]) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if value == 0 {
        output[0] = 48  // '0'
        output[1] = -1  // Sentinel
        return 1
    }

    // Count digits
    var temp = value
    var digit_count = 0
    while temp > 0 {
        temp = temp / 10
        digit_count = digit_count + 1
    }

    // Extract digits (right to left)
    temp = value
    var i = digit_count - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        let digit = temp % 10
        output[i] = digit_to_char(digit)
        temp = temp / 10
        i = i - 1
    }

    output[digit_count] = -1  // Sentinel
    return digit_count
}

// ============================================================================
// Label Rendering (text + box)
// ============================================================================

// Draw a label with border (useful for legends, annotations)
fn draw_label(
    canvas: Canvas,
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    text: &[i32],
    max_len: i32,
    border_color: i32,
    text_style: TextStyle
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = canvas

    // Calculate label dimensions
    let text_len = string_length(text, max_len)
    let box_width = text_len + 2  // Padding
    let box_height = 3

    // Draw border (simple box with +, -, |)
    // Top edge
    var bx = 0
    while bx < box_width {
        let border_ch = if bx == 0 { 43 } else { if bx == box_width - 1 { 43 } else { 45 } }  // + or -
        let border_style = text_style_new(border_color, 0, 0, 0)
        result = canvas_set_char(result, x + bx, y, border_ch, border_style)
        bx = bx + 1
    }

    // Middle (text) - left border, text, right border
    let left_border = text_style_new(border_color, 0, 0, 0)
    result = canvas_set_char(result, x, y + 1, 124, left_border)  // |
    result = draw_text_left(result, x + 1, y + 1, text, max_len, text_style)
    result = canvas_set_char(result, x + box_width - 1, y + 1, 124, left_border)

    // Bottom edge
    bx = 0
    while bx < box_width {
        let border_ch = if bx == 0 { 43 } else { if bx == box_width - 1 { 43 } else { 45 } }
        let border_style = text_style_new(border_color, 0, 0, 0)
        result = canvas_set_char(result, x + bx, y + 2, border_ch, border_style)
        bx = bx + 1
    }

    return result
}

    }

        width: width,
        height: height,
        cells: [cell_blank(); 2400]
    }

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("=== Sounio Text Rendering Demo ===\n\n")

    // Create test canvas
    var canvas = canvas_new(60, 20)

    // Test 1: Left-aligned text
    print("Drawing left-aligned text...\n")
    var text1 = [72, 101, 108, 108, 111, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0]  // "Hello" + sentinel
    let style_green = text_style_new(2, 0, 0, 0)  // Green
    canvas = draw_text_left(canvas, 5, 2, &text1, 10, style_green)

    // Test 2: Right-aligned text
    print("Drawing right-aligned text...\n")
    var text2 = [87, 111, 114, 108, 100, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0]  // "World" + sentinel
    let style_blue = text_style_new(4, 0, 0, 0)  // Blue
    canvas = draw_text_right(canvas, 55, 5, &text2, 10, style_blue)

    // Test 3: Center-aligned text
