// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/20_projection.sio ===
// 20_projection.sio - 3D to 2D projection and transformations
//
// Provides isometric and perspective projection, 3D rotations,
// and coordinate transformations for 3D graphics rendering.

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"

// ============================================================================
// 3D Point Structure
// ============================================================================

struct Vec3D {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64
}

fn vec3d_new(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Vec3D {
    return Vec3D { x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

fn vec3d_zero() -> Vec3D {
    return Vec3D { x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0 }
}

fn vec3d_add(a: &Vec3D, b: &Vec3D) -> Vec3D {
    return Vec3D {
        x: a.x + b.x,
        y: a.y + b.y,
        z: a.z + b.z
    }
}

fn vec3d_sub(a: &Vec3D, b: &Vec3D) -> Vec3D {
    return Vec3D {
        x: a.x - b.x,
        y: a.y - b.y,
        z: a.z - b.z
    }
}

fn vec3d_scale(v: &Vec3D, s: f64) -> Vec3D {
    return Vec3D {
        x: v.x * s,
        y: v.y * s,
        z: v.z * s
    }
}

fn vec3d_dot(a: &Vec3D, b: &Vec3D) -> f64 {
    return a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y + a.z * b.z
}

fn vec3d_cross(a: &Vec3D, b: &Vec3D) -> Vec3D {
    return Vec3D {
        x: a.y * b.z - a.z * b.y,
        y: a.z * b.x - a.x * b.z,
        z: a.x * b.y - a.y * b.x
    }
}

fn vec3d_magnitude(v: &Vec3D) -> f64 with Panic {
    return sqrt(v.x * v.x + v.y * v.y + v.z * v.z)
}

fn vec3d_normalize(v: &Vec3D) -> Vec3D with Div, Panic {
    let mag = vec3d_magnitude(v)
    if mag < 0.0001 {
        return vec3d_zero()
    }
    return vec3d_scale(v, 1.0 / mag)
}

// ============================================================================
// 2D Point (for projected results)
// ============================================================================

struct Vec2D {
    x: f64,
    y: f64
}

fn vec2d_new(x: f64, y: f64) -> Vec2D {
    return Vec2D { x: x, y: y }
}

// ============================================================================
// Isometric Projection
// ============================================================================

// Isometric projection: projects 3D point to 2D using standard isometric angles
// This creates a pseudo-3D view where:
// - X axis goes right-down at 30°
// - Y axis goes left-down at 30°
// - Z axis goes straight up
//
// The projection formula:
// screen_x = (x - y) * cos(30°)
// screen_y = (x + y) * sin(30°) - z
//
// Using cos(30°) ≈ 0.866 and sin(30°) = 0.5

fn isometric_project(p: &Vec3D) -> Vec2D {
    let cos30 = 0.866025403784  // sqrt(3)/2
    let sin30 = 0.5

    let screen_x = (p.x - p.y) * cos30
    let screen_y = (p.x + p.y) * sin30 - p.z

    return vec2d_new(screen_x, screen_y)
}

// Isometric projection with scale factor
fn isometric_project_scaled(p: &Vec3D, scale: f64) -> Vec2D {
    let cos30 = 0.866025403784
    let sin30 = 0.5

    let screen_x = (p.x - p.y) * cos30 * scale
    let screen_y = ((p.x + p.y) * sin30 - p.z) * scale

    return vec2d_new(screen_x, screen_y)
}

// ============================================================================
// Perspective Projection
// ============================================================================

// Perspective projection: simulates realistic depth perception
// Points closer to camera appear larger, distant points appear smaller
//
// Formula:
// scale_factor = focal_length / (focal_length + z)
// screen_x = x * scale_factor
// screen_y = y * scale_factor
//
// Assumes camera is at origin looking down +Z axis

fn perspective_project(p: &Vec3D, focal_length: f64) -> Vec2D with Div {
    let z_adjusted = focal_length + p.z

    // Avoid division by zero
    if z_adjusted < 0.1 {
        return vec2d_new(p.x * 10.0, p.y * 10.0)
    }

    let scale_factor = focal_length / z_adjusted
    return vec2d_new(p.x * scale_factor, p.y * scale_factor)
}

// Perspective projection with clipping
// Points behind the camera (z < -focal_length) are clipped
fn perspective_project_clipped(p: &Vec3D, focal_length: f64) -> Vec2D with Div, Panic {
    let z_adjusted = focal_length + p.z

    // Clip points behind camera
    if z_adjusted <= 0.0 {
        return vec2d_new(0.0, 0.0)
    }

    let scale_factor = focal_length / z_adjusted
    return vec2d_new(p.x * scale_factor, p.y * scale_factor)
}

// ============================================================================
// 3D Rotations
// ============================================================================

// Rotation around X axis (pitch)
// Y and Z coordinates rotate, X stays the same
fn rotate_x(p: &Vec3D, angle_rad: f64) -> Vec3D with Panic {
    let c = cos(angle_rad)
    let s = sin(angle_rad)

    return Vec3D {
        x: p.x,
        y: p.y * c - p.z * s,
        z: p.y * s + p.z * c
    }
}

// Rotation around Y axis (yaw)
// X and Z coordinates rotate, Y stays the same
fn rotate_y(p: &Vec3D, angle_rad: f64) -> Vec3D with Panic {
    let c = cos(angle_rad)
    let s = sin(angle_rad)

    return Vec3D {
        x: p.x * c + p.z * s,
        y: p.y,
        z: -p.x * s + p.z * c
    }
}

// Rotation around Z axis (roll)
// X and Y coordinates rotate, Z stays the same
fn rotate_z(p: &Vec3D, angle_rad: f64) -> Vec3D with Panic {
    let c = cos(angle_rad)
    let s = sin(angle_rad)

    return Vec3D {
        x: p.x * c - p.y * s,
        y: p.x * s + p.y * c,
        z: p.z
    }
}

// Combined rotation: apply rotations in order X -> Y -> Z (Euler angles)
fn rotate_xyz(p: &Vec3D, rx: f64, ry: f64, rz: f64) -> Vec3D with Panic {
    var result = rotate_x(p, rx)
    result = rotate_y(&result, ry)
    result = rotate_z(&result, rz)
    return result
}

// Combined rotation with explicit order specification
// order: 0=XYZ, 1=XZY, 2=YXZ, 3=YZX, 4=ZXY, 5=ZYX
fn rotate_euler(p: &Vec3D, rx: f64, ry: f64, rz: f64, order: i32) -> Vec3D with Panic {
    if order == 0 {
        // XYZ
        var result = rotate_x(p, rx)
        result = rotate_y(&result, ry)
        result = rotate_z(&result, rz)
        return result
    } else { if order == 1 {
        // XZY
        var result = rotate_x(p, rx)
        result = rotate_z(&result, rz)
        result = rotate_y(&result, ry)
        return result
    } else { if order == 2 {
        // YXZ
        var result = rotate_y(p, ry)
        result = rotate_x(&result, rx)
        result = rotate_z(&result, rz)
        return result
    } else { if order == 3 {
        // YZX
        var result = rotate_y(p, ry)
        result = rotate_z(&result, rz)
        result = rotate_x(&result, rx)
        return result
    } else { if order == 4 {
        // ZXY
        var result = rotate_z(p, rz)
        result = rotate_x(&result, rx)
        result = rotate_y(&result, ry)
        return result
    } else {
        // ZYX (default)
        var result = rotate_z(p, rz)
        result = rotate_y(&result, ry)
        result = rotate_x(&result, rx)
        return result
    }}}}}
}

// ============================================================================
// Camera Transformations
// ============================================================================

// Transform point from world space to camera space
// camera_pos: position of camera in world
// camera_target: point camera is looking at
// camera_up: up vector (usually (0, 0, 1))
fn world_to_camera(
    p: &Vec3D,
    camera_pos: &Vec3D,
    camera_target: &Vec3D,
    camera_up: &Vec3D
) -> Vec3D with Div, Panic {
    // Compute camera basis vectors
    let forward = vec3d_normalize(&vec3d_sub(camera_target, camera_pos))
    let right = vec3d_normalize(&vec3d_cross(&forward, camera_up))
    let up = vec3d_cross(&right, &forward)

    // Translate point to camera space
    let translated = vec3d_sub(p, camera_pos)

    // Project onto camera basis
    return Vec3D {
        x: vec3d_dot(&translated, &right),
        y: vec3d_dot(&translated, &up),
        z: vec3d_dot(&translated, &forward)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Lighting and Shading
// ============================================================================

// Compute Lambertian (diffuse) shading intensity
// normal: surface normal (should be normalized)
// light_dir: direction to light source (should be normalized)
// Returns value in [0, 1] where 0 is dark, 1 is fully lit
fn lambertian_shading(normal: &Vec3D, light_dir: &Vec3D) -> f64 {
    let intensity = vec3d_dot(normal, light_dir)

    // Clamp to [0, 1]
    if intensity < 0.0 {
        return 0.0
    }
    if intensity > 1.0 {
        return 1.0
    }
    return intensity
}

// Compute surface normal for a triangle
// p1, p2, p3: triangle vertices in counter-clockwise order
// Returns normalized normal vector
fn triangle_normal(p1: &Vec3D, p2: &Vec3D, p3: &Vec3D) -> Vec3D with Div, Panic {
    let edge1 = vec3d_sub(p2, p1)
    let edge2 = vec3d_sub(p3, p1)
    let normal = vec3d_cross(&edge1, &edge2)
    return vec3d_normalize(&normal)
}

// ============================================================================
// Utility Functions
// ============================================================================

// Convert degrees to radians
fn deg_to_rad(deg: f64) -> f64 {
    return deg * 0.0174532925199  // deg * PI / 180
}

// Convert radians to degrees
fn rad_to_deg(rad: f64) -> f64 {
    return rad * 57.2957795131  // rad * 180 / PI
}

// Interpolate between two 3D points
fn vec3d_lerp(a: &Vec3D, b: &Vec3D, t: f64) -> Vec3D {
    return Vec3D {
        x: a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t,
        y: a.y + (b.y - a.y) * t,
        z: a.z + (b.z - a.z) * t
    }
}

// Distance between two 3D points
fn vec3d_distance(a: &Vec3D, b: &Vec3D) -> f64 with Panic {
    let dx = b.x - a.x
    let dy = b.y - a.y
    let dz = b.z - a.z
    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)
}

// ============================================================================
// Example/Test Function
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Panic, Div {
    print("=== 3D Projection Module Test ===\n\n")

    // Test point
    let p = vec3d_new(5.0, 3.0, 2.0)
    print("Original point: (")
    print_f64(p.x)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(p.y)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(p.z)
    print(")\n\n")

    // Isometric projection
    let iso = isometric_project(&p)
    print("Isometric projection: (")
    print_f64(iso.x)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(iso.y)
    print(")\n")

    // Perspective projection
    let persp = perspective_project(&p, 10.0)
    print("Perspective projection (focal=10): (")
    print_f64(persp.x)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(persp.y)
    print(")\n\n")

    // Rotation around Z axis (90 degrees)
    let angle = deg_to_rad(90.0)
    let rotated = rotate_z(&p, angle)
    print("After 90° rotation around Z: (")
    print_f64(rotated.x)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(rotated.y)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(rotated.z)
    print(")\n\n")

    // Test vector operations
    let v1 = vec3d_new(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    let v2 = vec3d_new(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)
    let cross = vec3d_cross(&v1, &v2)
    print("Cross product of (1,0,0) × (0,1,0): (")
    print_f64(cross.x)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(cross.y)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(cross.z)
    print(")\n")

    // Test lighting
    let normal = vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    let light = vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    let intensity = lambertian_shading(&normal, &light)
    print("Lambertian shading (normal facing light): ")
    print_f64(intensity)
    print("\n")

    return 0
}

// Helper function for printing f64
fn print_f64(x: f64) with IO {
    // Simple conversion - just print the value
    // Note: Sounio doesn't have built-in f64 -> string conversion yet
    // This is a placeholder that will print the raw value
    if x < 0.0 {
        print("-")
        print_f64_unsigned(0.0 - x)
    } else {
        print_f64_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_f64_unsigned(x: f64) with IO, Div, Panic {
    // Convert to integer part
    let int_part = x as i32
    print_i32(int_part)

    // Print decimal point
    print(".")

    // Get fractional part
    let frac = x - (int_part as f64)
    let scaled = (frac * 1000.0) as i32

    // Print 3 decimal places
    if scaled < 100 {
        print("0")
    }
    if scaled < 10 {
        print("0")
    }
    print_i32(scaled)
}

fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }

    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        return
    }

    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10

    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }

    // Print digit as character
    let ch = 48 + digit  // '0' is ASCII 48
    print_char(ch)
}

fn print_char(code: i32) with IO {
    // Use the character code directly
    // This is a workaround until we have proper char support
    if code == 48 { print("0") }
    else { if code == 49 { print("1") }
    else { if code == 50 { print("2") }
    else { if code == 51 { print("3") }
    else { if code == 52 { print("4") }
    else { if code == 53 { print("5") }
    else { if code == 54 { print("6") }
    else { if code == 55 { print("7") }
    else { if code == 56 { print("8") }
    else { if code == 57 { print("9") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/21_wireframe.sio ===
// 21_wireframe.sio - 3D wireframe mesh rendering
//
// Provides 3D mesh data structures and wireframe rendering with
// rotation, projection, and hidden line removal.

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"
import "00_canvas.sio"
import "02_drawing.sio"
import "10_axes.sio"
import "20_projection.sio"

// ============================================================================
// 3D Mesh Structures
// ============================================================================

// Edge connecting two vertices
struct Edge3D {
    v1_idx: i32,  // Index into vertex array
    v2_idx: i32   // Index into vertex array
}

fn edge3d_new(v1: i32, v2: i32) -> Edge3D {
    return Edge3D { v1_idx: v1, v2_idx: v2 }
}

// Triangle face (for future surface rendering)
struct Face3D {
    v1_idx: i32,
    v2_idx: i32,
    v3_idx: i32
}

fn face3d_new(v1: i32, v2: i32, v3: i32) -> Face3D {
    return Face3D { v1_idx: v1, v2_idx: v2, v3_idx: v3 }
}

// 3D mesh with vertices and edges
struct Mesh3D {
    vertices: [Vec3D; 1000],     // Vertex positions
    edges: [Edge3D; 2000],       // Edges connecting vertices
    faces: [Face3D; 500],        // Triangle faces (optional)
    n_vertices: i32,
    n_edges: i32,
    n_faces: i32
}

fn mesh3d_new() -> Mesh3D {
    let vertices: [Vec3D; 1000] = [vec3d_zero(); 1000]
    let edges: [Edge3D; 2000] = [edge3d_new(0, 0); 2000]
    let faces: [Face3D; 500] = [face3d_new(0, 0, 0); 500]

    return Mesh3D {
        vertices: vertices,
        edges: edges,
        faces: faces,
        n_vertices: 0,
        n_edges: 0,
        n_faces: 0
    }
}

// Add vertex to mesh, returns index
fn mesh_add_vertex(mesh: &!Mesh3D, v: Vec3D) -> i32 with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = mesh.n_vertices
    mesh.vertices[idx] = v
    mesh.n_vertices = mesh.n_vertices + 1
    return idx
}

// Add edge to mesh
fn mesh_add_edge(mesh: &!Mesh3D, v1: i32, v2: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = mesh.n_edges
    mesh.edges[idx] = edge3d_new(v1, v2)
    mesh.n_edges = mesh.n_edges + 1
}

// Add face to mesh
fn mesh_add_face(mesh: &!Mesh3D, v1: i32, v2: i32, v3: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = mesh.n_faces
    mesh.faces[idx] = face3d_new(v1, v2, v3)
    mesh.n_faces = mesh.n_faces + 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Basic 3D Shapes
// ============================================================================

// Create a cube mesh centered at origin
fn mesh_cube(size: f64) -> Mesh3D with Mut, Panic {
    var mesh = mesh3d_new()

    let half = size / 2.0

    // 8 vertices of cube
    let v0 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(-half, -half, -half))
    let v1 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(half, -half, -half))
    let v2 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(half, half, -half))
    let v3 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(-half, half, -half))
    let v4 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(-half, -half, half))
    let v5 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(half, -half, half))
    let v6 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(half, half, half))
    let v7 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(-half, half, half))

    // 12 edges
    // Bottom face
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v1)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v1, v2)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v2, v3)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v3, v0)
    // Top face
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v4, v5)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v5, v6)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v6, v7)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v7, v4)
    // Vertical edges
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v4)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v1, v5)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v2, v6)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v3, v7)

    return mesh
}

// Create a pyramid mesh
fn mesh_pyramid(base_size: f64, height: f64) -> Mesh3D with Mut, Panic {
    var mesh = mesh3d_new()

    let half = base_size / 2.0

    // 5 vertices: 4 base corners + 1 apex
    let v0 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(-half, -half, 0.0))
    let v1 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(half, -half, 0.0))
    let v2 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(half, half, 0.0))
    let v3 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(-half, half, 0.0))
    let v4 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, height))

    // Base edges
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v1)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v1, v2)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v2, v3)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v3, v0)

    // Edges to apex
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v4)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v1, v4)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v2, v4)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v3, v4)

    return mesh
}

// Create a tetrahedron (4-sided pyramid)
fn mesh_tetrahedron(size: f64) -> Mesh3D with Mut, Panic {
    var mesh = mesh3d_new()

    // Regular tetrahedron vertices
    let a = size * 0.816496580927  // sqrt(2/3)
    let b = size * 0.471404520791  // sqrt(2)/3
    let c = size * 0.333333333333  // 1/3

    let v0 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, size))
    let v1 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(a, 0.0, -c))
    let v2 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(-b, a * 0.866025403784, -c))
    let v3 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(-b, -a * 0.866025403784, -c))

    // 6 edges
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v1)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v2)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v3)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v1, v2)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v2, v3)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v3, v1)

    return mesh
}

// Create an octahedron
fn mesh_octahedron(size: f64) -> Mesh3D with Mut, Panic {
    var mesh = mesh3d_new()

    // 6 vertices: +/- along each axis
    let v0 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(size, 0.0, 0.0))
    let v1 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(-size, 0.0, 0.0))
    let v2 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(0.0, size, 0.0))
    let v3 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(0.0, -size, 0.0))
    let v4 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, size))
    let v5 = mesh_add_vertex(&!mesh, vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, -size))

    // 12 edges
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v2)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v3)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v4)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v0, v5)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v1, v2)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v1, v3)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v1, v4)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v1, v5)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v2, v4)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v2, v5)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v3, v4)
    mesh_add_edge(&!mesh, v3, v5)

    return mesh
}

// ============================================================================
// Wireframe Rendering
// ============================================================================

// Transform all vertices by rotation
fn mesh_transform(mesh: &Mesh3D, rx: f64, ry: f64, rz: f64) -> Mesh3D with Mut, Panic {
    var result = mesh3d_new()
    result.n_vertices = mesh.n_vertices
    result.n_edges = mesh.n_edges
    result.n_faces = mesh.n_faces

    // Copy and transform vertices
    var i = 0
    while i < mesh.n_vertices {
        result.vertices[i] = rotate_xyz(&mesh.vertices[i], rx, ry, rz)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Copy edges
    i = 0
    while i < mesh.n_edges {
        result.edges[i] = mesh.edges[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Copy faces
    i = 0
    while i < mesh.n_faces {
        result.faces[i] = mesh.faces[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    return result
}

// Draw wireframe using isometric projection
fn draw_wireframe_isometric(
    canvas: Canvas,
    vp: &Viewport,
    mesh: &Mesh3D,
    color: i32,
    scale: f64
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    // Project and draw each edge
    var i = 0
    while i < mesh.n_edges {
        let edge = &mesh.edges[i]
        let v1 = &mesh.vertices[edge.v1_idx]
        let v2 = &mesh.vertices[edge.v2_idx]

        // Project to 2D
        let p1_2d = isometric_project_scaled(v1, scale)
        let p2_2d = isometric_project_scaled(v2, scale)

        // Transform to canvas coordinates
        let canvas_p1 = world_to_canvas(vp, p1_2d.x, p1_2d.y)
        let canvas_p2 = world_to_canvas(vp, p2_2d.x, p2_2d.y)

        // Draw line
        c = draw_line_solid(c, canvas_p1.0, canvas_p1.1, canvas_p2.0, canvas_p2.1, color)

        i = i + 1
    }

    return c
}

// Draw wireframe using perspective projection
fn draw_wireframe_perspective(
    canvas: Canvas,
    vp: &Viewport,
    mesh: &Mesh3D,
    color: i32,
    focal_length: f64
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    // Project and draw each edge
    var i = 0
    while i < mesh.n_edges {
        let edge = &mesh.edges[i]
        let v1 = &mesh.vertices[edge.v1_idx]
        let v2 = &mesh.vertices[edge.v2_idx]

        // Project to 2D
        let p1_2d = perspective_project(v1, focal_length)
        let p2_2d = perspective_project(v2, focal_length)

        // Transform to canvas coordinates
        let canvas_p1 = world_to_canvas(vp, p1_2d.x, p1_2d.y)
        let canvas_p2 = world_to_canvas(vp, p2_2d.x, p2_2d.y)

        // Draw line
        c = draw_line_solid(c, canvas_p1.0, canvas_p1.1, canvas_p2.0, canvas_p2.1, color)

        i = i + 1
    }

    return c
}

// Draw wireframe with automatic centering and scaling
fn draw_wireframe_auto(
    canvas: Canvas,
    vp: &Viewport,
    mesh: &Mesh3D,
    rotation: Vec3D,
    color: i32
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Transform mesh
    let transformed = mesh_transform(mesh, rotation.x, rotation.y, rotation.z)

    // Auto-scale to fit viewport (use isometric projection with scale 1.0)
    return draw_wireframe_isometric(canvas, vp, &transformed, color, 1.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// Grid/Axes Helpers for 3D
// ============================================================================

// Draw 3D coordinate axes
fn draw_axes_3d(
    canvas: Canvas,
    vp: &Viewport,
    length: f64,
    scale: f64
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    // X axis (red)
    let x_start = vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    let x_end = vec3d_new(length, 0.0, 0.0)
    let x_start_2d = isometric_project_scaled(&x_start, scale)
    let x_end_2d = isometric_project_scaled(&x_end, scale)
    let x_p1 = world_to_canvas(vp, x_start_2d.x, x_start_2d.y)
    let x_p2 = world_to_canvas(vp, x_end_2d.x, x_end_2d.y)
    c = draw_line_solid(c, x_p1.0, x_p1.1, x_p2.0, x_p2.1, COLOR_RED())

    // Y axis (green)
    let y_start = vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    let y_end = vec3d_new(0.0, length, 0.0)
    let y_start_2d = isometric_project_scaled(&y_start, scale)
    let y_end_2d = isometric_project_scaled(&y_end, scale)
    let y_p1 = world_to_canvas(vp, y_start_2d.x, y_start_2d.y)
    let y_p2 = world_to_canvas(vp, y_end_2d.x, y_end_2d.y)
    c = draw_line_solid(c, y_p1.0, y_p1.1, y_p2.0, y_p2.1, COLOR_GREEN())

    // Z axis (blue)
    let z_start = vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    let z_end = vec3d_new(0.0, 0.0, length)
    let z_start_2d = isometric_project_scaled(&z_start, scale)
    let z_end_2d = isometric_project_scaled(&z_end, scale)
    let z_p1 = world_to_canvas(vp, z_start_2d.x, z_start_2d.y)
    let z_p2 = world_to_canvas(vp, z_end_2d.x, z_end_2d.y)
    c = draw_line_solid(c, z_p1.0, z_p1.1, z_p2.0, z_p2.1, COLOR_BLUE())

    return c
}

// ============================================================================
// Example/Test Function
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")  // Clear screen
    print("=== 3D Wireframe Rendering Test ===\n\n")

    // Create canvas
    var canvas = canvas_new(80, 30)
    canvas = canvas_clear(canvas)

    // Set up viewport
    let vp = viewport_new(-10.0, 10.0, -10.0, 10.0, 5, 2, 70, 26)

    // Create a cube
    let cube = mesh_cube(3.0)

    // Rotate cube (45 degrees around Y and Z)
    let rotation = vec3d_new(0.0, deg_to_rad(45.0), deg_to_rad(30.0))

    // Draw axes
    canvas = draw_axes_3d(canvas, &vp, 5.0, 1.0)

    // Draw wireframe
    canvas = draw_wireframe_auto(canvas, &vp, &cube, rotation, COLOR_CYAN())

    // Add title
    canvas = draw_text(canvas, 15, 0, "Rotating Cube (Isometric)", text_style_default())

    // Render
    canvas_render(&canvas)

    print("\n\n")
    print("Cube has ")
    print_i32(cube.n_vertices)
    print(" vertices and ")
    print_i32(cube.n_edges)
    print(" edges\n")

    return 0
}

// Helper functions from other modules referenced inline

fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }

    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        return
    }

    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10

    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }

    // Print digit as character
    let ch = 48 + digit  // '0' is ASCII 48
    print_char(ch)
}

fn print_char(code: i32) with IO {
    // Print digit characters
    if code == 48 { print("0") }
    else { if code == 49 { print("1") }
    else { if code == 50 { print("2") }
    else { if code == 51 { print("3") }
    else { if code == 52 { print("4") }
    else { if code == 53 { print("5") }
    else { if code == 54 { print("6") }
    else { if code == 55 { print("7") }
    else { if code == 56 { print("8") }
    else { if code == 57 { print("9") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/23_scatter3d.sio ===
// 23_scatter3d.sio - 3D scatter plot visualization
//
// Provides 3D scatter plotting with various markers, colors,
// and projection modes for visualizing point clouds in 3D space.

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"
import "00_canvas.sio"
import "01_colors.sio"
import "02_drawing.sio"
import "10_axes.sio"
import "20_projection.sio"

// ============================================================================
// 3D Scatter Point Structure
// ============================================================================

struct Point3D {
    pos: Vec3D,
    marker: i32,  // Character code for marker symbol
    color: i32,   // ANSI color code (0-15)
    size: i32     // Size: 1=small, 2=medium, 3=large
}

fn point3d_new(pos: Vec3D, marker: i32, color: i32, size: i32) -> Point3D {
    return Point3D {
        pos: pos,
        marker: marker,
        color: color,
        size: size
    }
}

// Default point with circle marker
fn point3d_default(pos: Vec3D) -> Point3D {
    return point3d_new(pos, MARKER_CIRCLE(), COLOR_CYAN(), 1)
}

// ============================================================================
// Marker Constants
// ============================================================================

fn MARKER_DOT() -> i32 { return 9679 }        // ●
fn MARKER_CIRCLE() -> i32 { return 9675 }     // ○
fn MARKER_SQUARE() -> i32 { return 9632 }     // ■
fn MARKER_DIAMOND() -> i32 { return 9670 }    // ◆
fn MARKER_STAR() -> i32 { return 9733 }       // ★
fn MARKER_PLUS() -> i32 { return 43 }         // +
fn MARKER_CROSS() -> i32 { return 120 }       // x
fn MARKER_TRIANGLE() -> i32 { return 9650 }   // ▲

// ============================================================================
// 3D Scatter Plot Rendering
// ============================================================================

// Scatter plot with isometric projection
fn scatter_plot_3d_isometric(
    canvas: Canvas,
    vp: &Viewport,
    points: &[Point3D],
    n_points: i32,
    scale: f64
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    var i = 0
    while i < n_points {
        let pt = &points[i]

        // Project 3D point to 2D
        let projected = isometric_project_scaled(&pt.pos, scale)

        // Transform to canvas coordinates
        let canvas_pos = world_to_canvas(vp, projected.x, projected.y)
        let px = canvas_pos.0
        let py = canvas_pos.1

        // Draw marker based on size
        if pt.size == 1 {
            // Small: single character
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
        } else { if pt.size == 2 {
            // Medium: 3x3 grid
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px - 1, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px + 1, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
        } else {
            // Large: 5x5 grid
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px - 1, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px + 1, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py - 1, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py + 1, pt.marker, pt.color)
        }}

        i = i + 1
    }

    return c
}

// Scatter plot with perspective projection
fn scatter_plot_3d_perspective(
    canvas: Canvas,
    vp: &Viewport,
    points: &[Point3D],
    n_points: i32,
    focal_length: f64
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    var i = 0
    while i < n_points {
        let pt = &points[i]

        // Project 3D point to 2D
        let projected = perspective_project(&pt.pos, focal_length)

        // Transform to canvas coordinates
        let canvas_pos = world_to_canvas(vp, projected.x, projected.y)
        let px = canvas_pos.0
        let py = canvas_pos.1

        // Draw marker (perspective affects apparent size too)
        let apparent_size = if pt.pos.z > 0.0 {
            // Closer objects appear larger
            if pt.size == 1 { 2 } else { if pt.size == 2 { 3 } else { 3 }}
        } else {
            // Further objects appear smaller
            if pt.size >= 2 { 1 } else { 1 }
        }

        if apparent_size == 1 {
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
        } else { if apparent_size == 2 {
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px - 1, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px + 1, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
        } else {
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px - 1, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px + 1, py, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py - 1, pt.marker, pt.color)
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py + 1, pt.marker, pt.color)
        }}

        i = i + 1
    }

    return c
}

// Scatter plot with rotation
fn scatter_plot_3d_rotated(
    canvas: Canvas,
    vp: &Viewport,
    points: &[Point3D],
    n_points: i32,
    rotation: Vec3D,
    scale: f64
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Rotate all points
    var rotated_points: [Point3D; 500] = [point3d_default(vec3d_zero()); 500]

    var i = 0
    while i < n_points {
        let pt = &points[i]
        let rotated_pos = rotate_xyz(&pt.pos, rotation.x, rotation.y, rotation.z)
        rotated_points[i] = point3d_new(rotated_pos, pt.marker, pt.color, pt.size)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Plot rotated points
    return scatter_plot_3d_isometric(canvas, vp, &rotated_points, n_points, scale)
}

// ============================================================================
// Depth Sorting (for better visualization)
// ============================================================================

// Sort points by Z-depth (furthest first for correct occlusion)
// Simple bubble sort - good enough for small point sets
fn sort_points_by_depth(points: &![Point3D], n_points: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n_points - 1 {
        var j = 0
        while j < n_points - i - 1 {
            // Sort by z coordinate (furthest first)
            if points[j].pos.z > points[j + 1].pos.z {
                // Swap
                let temp = points[j]
                points[j] = points[j + 1]
                points[j + 1] = temp
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Scatter plot with depth sorting
fn scatter_plot_3d_depth_sorted(
    canvas: Canvas,
    vp: &Viewport,
    points: &[Point3D],
    n_points: i32,
    scale: f64
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Copy points to mutable array
    var sorted_points: [Point3D; 500] = [point3d_default(vec3d_zero()); 500]

    var i = 0
    while i < n_points {
        sorted_points[i] = points[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Sort by depth
    sort_points_by_depth(&!sorted_points, n_points)

    // Plot sorted points
    return scatter_plot_3d_isometric(canvas, vp, &sorted_points, n_points, scale)
}

// ============================================================================
// Color Mapping by Coordinate
// ============================================================================

// Color points based on Z coordinate
fn colorize_by_z(
    points: &![Point3D],
    n_points: i32,
    z_min: f64,
    z_max: f64
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let range = z_max - z_min

    var i = 0
    while i < n_points {
        let normalized = if range > 0.0001 {
            (points[i].pos.z - z_min) / range
        } else {
            0.5
        }

        // Map to color gradient (blue -> green -> yellow -> red)
        points[i].color = if normalized < 0.25 {
            COLOR_BLUE()
        } else { if normalized < 0.5 {
            COLOR_CYAN()
        } else { if normalized < 0.75 {
            COLOR_YELLOW()
        } else {
            COLOR_RED()
        }}}

        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Color points based on distance from origin
fn colorize_by_distance(
    points: &![Point3D],
    n_points: i32
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Find max distance
    var max_dist = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n_points {
        let dist = vec3d_magnitude(&points[i].pos)
        if dist > max_dist {
            max_dist = dist
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Colorize based on distance
    i = 0
    while i < n_points {
        let dist = vec3d_magnitude(&points[i].pos)
        let normalized = if max_dist > 0.0001 {
            dist / max_dist
        } else {
            0.5
        }

        points[i].color = if normalized < 0.33 {
            COLOR_GREEN()
        } else { if normalized < 0.66 {
            COLOR_YELLOW()
        } else {
            COLOR_RED()
        }}

        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Point Cloud Generators
// ============================================================================

// Generate random points in a cube
fn generate_cube_points(
    n_points: i32,
    size: f64,
    seed: i32
) -> [Point3D; 500] with Mut, Panic {
    var points: [Point3D; 500] = [point3d_default(vec3d_zero()); 500]

    var i = 0
    var rng = seed
    while i < n_points {
        // Simple LCG random number generator
        rng = (rng * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let x = ((rng % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0) * size - size / 2.0

        rng = (rng * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let y = ((rng % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0) * size - size / 2.0

        rng = (rng * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let z = ((rng % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0) * size - size / 2.0

        points[i] = point3d_new(
            vec3d_new(x, y, z),
            MARKER_DOT(),
            COLOR_CYAN(),
            1
        )

        i = i + 1
    }

    return points
}

// Generate points on a sphere surface
fn generate_sphere_points(
    n_points: i32,
    radius: f64,
    seed: i32
) -> [Point3D; 500] with Mut, Panic {
    var points: [Point3D; 500] = [point3d_default(vec3d_zero()); 500]

    var i = 0
    var rng = seed
    while i < n_points {
        // Random spherical coordinates
        rng = (rng * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let theta = ((rng % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0) * 3.14159265359 * 2.0

        rng = (rng * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let phi = ((rng % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0) * 3.14159265359

        // Convert to Cartesian
        let x = radius * sin(phi) * cos(theta)
        let y = radius * sin(phi) * sin(theta)
        let z = radius * cos(phi)

        points[i] = point3d_new(
            vec3d_new(x, y, z),
            MARKER_DOT(),
            COLOR_GREEN(),
            1
        )

        i = i + 1
    }

    return points
}

// Generate points on a helix
fn generate_helix_points(
    n_points: i32,
    radius: f64,
    pitch: f64
) -> [Point3D; 500] with Mut, Panic {
    var points: [Point3D; 500] = [point3d_default(vec3d_zero()); 500]

    var i = 0
    while i < n_points {
        let t = (i as f64) / (n_points as f64) * 6.28318530718 * 3.0  // 3 turns

        let x = radius * cos(t)
        let y = radius * sin(t)
        let z = pitch * t

        points[i] = point3d_new(
            vec3d_new(x, y, z),
            MARKER_DOT(),
            COLOR_MAGENTA(),
            1
        )

        i = i + 1
    }

    return points
}

// ============================================================================
// Example/Test Function
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")  // Clear screen
    print("=== 3D Scatter Plot Test ===\n\n")

    // Create canvas
    var canvas = canvas_new(80, 30)
    canvas = canvas_clear(canvas)

    // Set up viewport
    let vp = viewport_new(-5.0, 5.0, -5.0, 5.0, 10, 2, 60, 26)

    // Generate helix points
    var points = generate_helix_points(50, 2.0, 0.3)

    // Colorize by z-coordinate
    colorize_by_z(&!points, 50, -5.0, 5.0)

    // Draw with rotation
    let rotation = vec3d_new(deg_to_rad(20.0), deg_to_rad(45.0), 0.0)
    canvas = scatter_plot_3d_rotated(canvas, &vp, &points, 50, rotation, 1.5)

    // Add title
    canvas = draw_text(canvas, 5, 0, "3D Helix (50 points)", text_style_default())

    // Render
    canvas_render(&canvas)

    print("\nGenerated 50 points on a helix\n")
    print("Colors represent Z-coordinate (blue=low, red=high)\n")

    return 0
}

// 30_input.sio - Terminal input handling (mouse and keyboard)
//
// Provides terminal input event handling for interactive graphics.
// Uses ANSI escape sequences for mouse tracking and keyboard events.

// IMPORTANT: This module requires raw terminal mode for full functionality.
// The current implementation provides a simplified interface that works

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"

// ============================================================================
// Event Types
// ============================================================================

// Mouse event types
fn MOUSE_PRESS() -> i32 { return 0 }
fn MOUSE_RELEASE() -> i32 { return 1 }
fn MOUSE_MOVE() -> i32 { return 2 }
fn MOUSE_DRAG() -> i32 { return 3 }
fn MOUSE_SCROLL_UP() -> i32 { return 4 }
fn MOUSE_SCROLL_DOWN() -> i32 { return 5 }

// Mouse buttons
fn BUTTON_LEFT() -> i32 { return 0 }
fn BUTTON_RIGHT() -> i32 { return 1 }
fn BUTTON_MIDDLE() -> i32 { return 2 }

// Keyboard modifiers
fn MOD_NONE() -> i32 { return 0 }
fn MOD_SHIFT() -> i32 { return 1 }
fn MOD_CTRL() -> i32 { return 2 }
fn MOD_ALT() -> i32 { return 4 }
fn MOD_META() -> i32 { return 8 }

// Special keys
fn KEY_ESCAPE() -> i32 { return 27 }
fn KEY_ENTER() -> i32 { return 13 }
fn KEY_TAB() -> i32 { return 9 }
fn KEY_BACKSPACE() -> i32 { return 8 }
fn KEY_SPACE() -> i32 { return 32 }
fn KEY_UP() -> i32 { return 1000 }
fn KEY_DOWN() -> i32 { return 1001 }
fn KEY_LEFT() -> i32 { return 1002 }
fn KEY_RIGHT() -> i32 { return 1003 }

// ============================================================================
// Event Structures
// ============================================================================

struct MouseEvent {
    event_type: i32,  // MOUSE_PRESS, MOUSE_RELEASE, etc.
    button: i32,      // BUTTON_LEFT, BUTTON_RIGHT, BUTTON_MIDDLE
    x: i32,           // Column (0-based)
    y: i32,           // Row (0-based)
    modifiers: i32    // MOD_SHIFT | MOD_CTRL | etc.
}

fn mouse_event_new(event_type: i32, button: i32, x: i32, y: i32, modifiers: i32) -> MouseEvent {
    return MouseEvent {
        event_type: event_type,
        button: button,
        x: x,
        y: y,
        modifiers: modifiers
    }
}

fn mouse_event_none() -> MouseEvent {
    return mouse_event_new(0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
}

struct KeyEvent {
    key_code: i32,    // ASCII code or KEY_* constant
    modifiers: i32,   // MOD_SHIFT | MOD_CTRL | etc.
    is_char: i32      // 1 if printable character, 0 if special key
}

fn key_event_new(key_code: i32, modifiers: i32, is_char: i32) -> KeyEvent {
    return KeyEvent {
        key_code: key_code,
        modifiers: modifiers,
        is_char: is_char
    }
}

fn key_event_none() -> KeyEvent {
    return key_event_new(0, 0, 0)
}

// ============================================================================
// Mouse Tracking Control
// ============================================================================

// Enable mouse tracking in terminal
// Sends ANSI escape sequences to enable mouse reporting
fn enable_mouse_tracking() with IO {
    // Enable mouse button press/release tracking (X10 mode)
    print("\x1b[?1000h")

    // Enable mouse motion tracking
    print("\x1b[?1002h")

    // Enable SGR extended mouse mode (better coordinate reporting)
    print("\x1b[?1006h")

    // Enable alternate scroll mode
    print("\x1b[?1015h")
}

// Disable mouse tracking
fn disable_mouse_tracking() with IO {
    print("\x1b[?1000l")
    print("\x1b[?1002l")
    print("\x1b[?1006l")
    print("\x1b[?1015l")
}

// Enable raw mode (no line buffering, no echo)
// NOTE: This is a simplified version using ANSI codes
// Full implementation would require FFI to termios
fn enable_raw_mode() with IO {
    // Disable line buffering and echo
    print("\x1b[?25l")  // Hide cursor
    print("\x1b[?7l")   // Disable line wrapping
}

// Disable raw mode
fn disable_raw_mode() with IO {
    print("\x1b[?25h")  // Show cursor
    print("\x1b[?7h")   // Enable line wrapping
}

// ============================================================================
// Input State Management
// ============================================================================

struct InputState {
    mouse_enabled: i32,
    raw_mode: i32,
    last_mouse_x: i32,
    last_mouse_y: i32,
    last_button: i32,
    button_pressed: i32  // 1 if button currently pressed, 0 otherwise
}

fn input_state_new() -> InputState {
    return InputState {
        mouse_enabled: 0,
        raw_mode: 0,
        last_mouse_x: 0,
        last_mouse_y: 0,
        last_button: 0,
        button_pressed: 0
    }
}

fn input_init(state: &!InputState) with IO, Mut {
    enable_mouse_tracking()
    enable_raw_mode()
    state.mouse_enabled = 1
    state.raw_mode = 1
}

fn input_cleanup(state: &!InputState) with IO, Mut {
    if state.mouse_enabled == 1 {
        disable_mouse_tracking()
        state.mouse_enabled = 0
    }
    if state.raw_mode == 1 {
        disable_raw_mode()
        state.raw_mode = 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Simulated Input Events (for testing/demos)
// ============================================================================

// Generate a simulated mouse click event
fn simulate_mouse_click(x: i32, y: i32, button: i32) -> MouseEvent {
    return mouse_event_new(MOUSE_PRESS(), button, x, y, MOD_NONE())
}

// Generate a simulated mouse drag event
fn simulate_mouse_drag(x1: i32, y1: i32, x2: i32, y2: i32) -> [MouseEvent; 3] with Mut {
    var events: [MouseEvent; 3] = [mouse_event_none(); 3]

    // Press at start
    events[0] = mouse_event_new(MOUSE_PRESS(), BUTTON_LEFT(), x1, y1, MOD_NONE())

    // Drag to end
    events[1] = mouse_event_new(MOUSE_DRAG(), BUTTON_LEFT(), x2, y2, MOD_NONE())

    // Release at end
    events[2] = mouse_event_new(MOUSE_RELEASE(), BUTTON_LEFT(), x2, y2, MOD_NONE())

    return events
}

// Generate simulated scroll event
fn simulate_scroll(x: i32, y: i32, direction: i32) -> MouseEvent {
    let event_type = if direction > 0 {
        MOUSE_SCROLL_UP()
    } else {
        MOUSE_SCROLL_DOWN()
    }

    return mouse_event_new(event_type, BUTTON_MIDDLE(), x, y, MOD_NONE())
}

// ============================================================================
// Event Handlers (Callback Pattern)
// ============================================================================

// Event handler function type
// Note: Function pointers in Sounio use this syntax
// type MouseHandler = fn(&!InputState, &MouseEvent) -> i32
// type KeyHandler = fn(&KeyEvent) -> i32

// Simple event loop with handlers
// Returns 0 to continue, 1 to exit
fn event_loop_step(
    state: &!InputState,
    on_mouse: fn(&!InputState, &MouseEvent) -> i32,
    on_key: fn(&KeyEvent) -> i32
) -> i32 with Mut {
    // Poll for mouse event
    let mouse_evt = poll_mouse_event(state)
    if mouse_evt.event_type != 0 {
        let result = on_mouse(state, &mouse_evt)
        if result == 1 {
            return 1  // Exit requested
        }
    }

    // Poll for keyboard event
    let key_evt = poll_key_event()
    if key_evt.key_code != 0 {
        let result = on_key(&key_evt)
        if result == 1 {
            return 1  // Exit requested
        }
    }

    return 0  // Continue
}

// ============================================================================
// Utility Functions
// ============================================================================

// Check if mouse event is at given position (with tolerance)
fn mouse_event_at(evt: &MouseEvent, x: i32, y: i32, tolerance: i32) -> i32 with Panic {
    let dx = if evt.x > x { evt.x - x } else { x - evt.x }
    let dy = if evt.y > y { evt.y - y } else { y - evt.y }

    if dx <= tolerance {
        if dy <= tolerance {
            return 1
        }
    }

    return 0
}

// Check if mouse event is within rectangle
fn mouse_event_in_rect(evt: &MouseEvent, x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32) -> i32 {
    if evt.x >= x {
        if evt.x < x + width {
            if evt.y >= y {
                if evt.y < y + height {
                    return 1
                }
            }
        }
    }

    return 0
}

// Check if modifier is active
fn has_modifier(modifiers: i32, mod_flag: i32) -> i32 {
    return if (modifiers & mod_flag) != 0 { 1 } else { 0 }
}

// Combine modifiers
fn combine_modifiers(mod1: i32, mod2: i32) -> i32 {
    return mod1 | mod2
}

// Helper function for printing integers
fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }

    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        return
    }

    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10

    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }

    // Print digit
    let ch = 48 + digit  // '0' is ASCII 48
    print_char(ch)
}

fn print_char(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 48 { print("0") }
    else { if code == 49 { print("1") }
    else { if code == 50 { print("2") }
    else { if code == 51 { print("3") }
    else { if code == 52 { print("4") }
    else { if code == 53 { print("5") }
    else { if code == 54 { print("6") }
    else { if code == 55 { print("7") }
    else { if code == 56 { print("8") }
    else { if code == 57 { print("9") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/31_interactive_plot.sio ===
// 31_interactive_plot.sio - Interactive plotting with zoom and pan
//
// Provides interactive visualization capabilities:
// - Zoom in/out (mouse wheel or keyboard)
// - Pan (mouse drag or arrow keys)
// - Reset view
// - Dynamic data updates
//
// NOTE: Full interactivity requires raw terminal mode and event loop.
// This implementation provides the core zoom/pan logic that can be
// integrated with input events when available.

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"
import "00_canvas.sio"
import "01_colors.sio"
import "02_drawing.sio"
import "03_text.sio"
import "10_axes.sio"
import "11_scatter.sio"
import "12_line_plot.sio"
import "30_input.sio"

// ============================================================================
// Interactive Plot State
// ============================================================================

struct InteractivePlot {
    // Viewport (current view bounds)
    viewport: Viewport,

    // Original viewport (for reset)
    original_viewport: Viewport,

    // Zoom state
    zoom_level: f64,     // 1.0 = original, 2.0 = 2x zoom, 0.5 = zoom out
    min_zoom: f64,       // Minimum zoom (e.g., 0.1)
    max_zoom: f64,       // Maximum zoom (e.g., 10.0)

    // Pan state
    pan_x: f64,          // Pan offset in world coordinates
    pan_y: f64,

    // Mouse interaction
    mouse_down: i32,     // 1 if mouse button is down
    drag_start_x: i32,   // Drag start position (canvas coords)
    drag_start_y: i32,
    last_mouse_x: i32,
    last_mouse_y: i32,

    // Keyboard interaction
    pan_speed: f64,      // Pan speed for keyboard arrows

    // Visual feedback
    show_controls: i32,  // 1 to show control help, 0 to hide
    dirty: i32           // 1 if needs redraw, 0 if clean
}

fn interactive_plot_new(viewport: Viewport) -> InteractivePlot {
    return InteractivePlot {
        viewport: viewport,
        original_viewport: viewport,
        zoom_level: 1.0,
        min_zoom: 0.1,
        max_zoom: 10.0,
        pan_x: 0.0,
        pan_y: 0.0,
        mouse_down: 0,
        drag_start_x: 0,
        drag_start_y: 0,
        last_mouse_x: 0,
        last_mouse_y: 0,
        pan_speed: 0.1,
        show_controls: 1,
        dirty: 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Zoom Operations
// ============================================================================

// Zoom in by a factor (e.g., 1.2 for 20% zoom in)
fn plot_zoom_in(plot: &!InteractivePlot, factor: f64) with Mut, Div {
    let new_zoom = plot.zoom_level * factor

    // Clamp to limits
    if new_zoom > plot.max_zoom {
        plot.zoom_level = plot.max_zoom
    } else {
        plot.zoom_level = new_zoom
    }

    // Update viewport based on zoom
    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Zoom out by a factor
fn plot_zoom_out(plot: &!InteractivePlot, factor: f64) with Mut, Div {
    let new_zoom = plot.zoom_level / factor

    // Clamp to limits
    if new_zoom < plot.min_zoom {
        plot.zoom_level = plot.min_zoom
    } else {
        plot.zoom_level = new_zoom
    }

    // Update viewport
    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Zoom to specific level
fn plot_set_zoom(plot: &!InteractivePlot, zoom: f64) with Mut {
    // Clamp
    if zoom < plot.min_zoom {
        plot.zoom_level = plot.min_zoom
    } else { if zoom > plot.max_zoom {
        plot.zoom_level = plot.max_zoom
    } else {
        plot.zoom_level = zoom
    }}

    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Zoom centered on a specific point (world coordinates)
fn plot_zoom_at_point(
    plot: &!InteractivePlot,
    world_x: f64,
    world_y: f64,
    factor: f64
) with Mut, Div {
    // Calculate offset from center before zoom
    let vp = &plot.viewport
    let center_x = (vp.x_min + vp.x_max) / 2.0
    let center_y = (vp.y_min + vp.y_max) / 2.0
    let offset_x = world_x - center_x
    let offset_y = world_y - center_y

    // Apply zoom
    let old_zoom = plot.zoom_level
    plot_zoom_in(plot, factor)
    let zoom_ratio = plot.zoom_level / old_zoom

    // Adjust pan to keep point centered
    plot.pan_x = plot.pan_x + offset_x * (1.0 - zoom_ratio)
    plot.pan_y = plot.pan_y + offset_y * (1.0 - zoom_ratio)

    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Pan Operations
// ============================================================================

// Pan by offset in world coordinates
fn plot_pan(plot: &!InteractivePlot, dx: f64, dy: f64) with Mut {
    plot.pan_x = plot.pan_x + dx
    plot.pan_y = plot.pan_y + dy

    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Pan to center on a specific point
fn plot_center_on(plot: &!InteractivePlot, world_x: f64, world_y: f64) with Mut, Div {
    let vp = &plot.viewport
    let center_x = (vp.x_min + vp.x_max) / 2.0
    let center_y = (vp.y_min + vp.y_max) / 2.0

    plot.pan_x = plot.pan_x + (world_x - center_x)
    plot.pan_y = plot.pan_y + (world_y - center_y)

    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Reset view to original
fn plot_reset_view(plot: &!InteractivePlot) with Mut {
    plot.zoom_level = 1.0
    plot.pan_x = 0.0
    plot.pan_y = 0.0

    plot.viewport = plot.original_viewport
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Viewport Update
// ============================================================================

// Update viewport based on zoom and pan
fn plot_update_viewport(plot: &!InteractivePlot) with Mut, Div {
    let orig = &plot.original_viewport

    // Calculate width and height based on zoom
    let orig_width = orig.x_max - orig.x_min
    let orig_height = orig.y_max - orig.y_min

    let new_width = orig_width / plot.zoom_level
    let new_height = orig_height / plot.zoom_level

    // Calculate center with pan offset
    let orig_center_x = (orig.x_min + orig.x_max) / 2.0
    let orig_center_y = (orig.y_min + orig.y_max) / 2.0

    let new_center_x = orig_center_x + plot.pan_x
    let new_center_y = orig_center_y + plot.pan_y

    // Update viewport bounds
    plot.viewport.x_min = new_center_x - new_width / 2.0
    plot.viewport.x_max = new_center_x + new_width / 2.0
    plot.viewport.y_min = new_center_y - new_height / 2.0
    plot.viewport.y_max = new_center_y + new_height / 2.0
}

// ============================================================================
// Mouse Event Handling
// ============================================================================

// Handle mouse press
fn plot_on_mouse_press(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &MouseEvent) with Mut {
    if evt.button == BUTTON_LEFT() {
        plot.mouse_down = 1
        plot.drag_start_x = evt.x
        plot.drag_start_y = evt.y
        plot.last_mouse_x = evt.x
        plot.last_mouse_y = evt.y
    }
}

// Handle mouse release
fn plot_on_mouse_release(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &MouseEvent) with Mut {
    if evt.button == BUTTON_LEFT() {
        plot.mouse_down = 0
    }
}

// Handle mouse move (pan if dragging)
fn plot_on_mouse_move(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &MouseEvent) with Mut, Div {
    if plot.mouse_down == 1 {
        // Calculate delta in canvas pixels
        let dx_pixels = evt.x - plot.last_mouse_x
        let dy_pixels = evt.y - plot.last_mouse_y

        // Convert to world coordinates
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let world_width = vp.x_max - vp.x_min
        let world_height = vp.y_max - vp.y_min

        let dx_world = ((dx_pixels as f64) / (vp.canvas_width as f64)) * world_width
        let dy_world = ((dy_pixels as f64) / (vp.canvas_height as f64)) * world_height

        // Pan (note: invert y since canvas y increases downward)
        plot_pan(plot, 0.0 - dx_world, dy_world)

        plot.last_mouse_x = evt.x
        plot.last_mouse_y = evt.y
    }
}

// Handle mouse scroll (zoom)
fn plot_on_mouse_scroll(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &MouseEvent) with Mut, Div {
    // Convert mouse position to world coordinates
    let world_pos = canvas_to_world(&plot.viewport, evt.x, evt.y)

    // Zoom factor
    let factor = if evt.event_type == MOUSE_SCROLL_UP() {
        1.2  // Zoom in
    } else {
        1.2  // Zoom out (will be inverted)
    }

    // Zoom at mouse position
    if evt.event_type == MOUSE_SCROLL_UP() {
        plot_zoom_at_point(plot, world_pos.0, world_pos.1, factor)
    } else {
        plot_zoom_out(plot, factor)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Keyboard Event Handling
// ============================================================================

// Handle key press
fn plot_on_key_press(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &KeyEvent) with Mut, Div {
    // Arrow keys for panning
    if evt.key_code == KEY_LEFT() {
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let pan_amount = (vp.x_max - vp.x_min) * plot.pan_speed
        plot_pan(plot, 0.0 - pan_amount, 0.0)
    }

    if evt.key_code == KEY_RIGHT() {
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let pan_amount = (vp.x_max - vp.x_min) * plot.pan_speed
        plot_pan(plot, pan_amount, 0.0)
    }

    if evt.key_code == KEY_UP() {
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let pan_amount = (vp.y_max - vp.y_min) * plot.pan_speed
        plot_pan(plot, 0.0, pan_amount)
    }

    if evt.key_code == KEY_DOWN() {
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let pan_amount = (vp.y_max - vp.y_min) * plot.pan_speed
        plot_pan(plot, 0.0, 0.0 - pan_amount)
    }

    // '+' or '=' for zoom in
    if evt.key_code == 43 {  // '+'
        plot_zoom_in(plot, 1.2)
    }
    if evt.key_code == 61 {  // '='
        plot_zoom_in(plot, 1.2)
    }

    // '-' for zoom out
    if evt.key_code == 45 {  // '-'
        plot_zoom_out(plot, 1.2)
    }

    // 'r' for reset
    if evt.key_code == 114 {  // 'r'
        plot_reset_view(plot)
    }

    // 'h' for toggle help
    if evt.key_code == 104 {  // 'h'
        plot.show_controls = if plot.show_controls == 1 { 0 } else { 1 }
        plot.dirty = 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================

// Draw control hints
fn plot_draw_controls(canvas: Canvas, plot: &InteractivePlot) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic {
    if plot.show_controls == 0 {
        return canvas
    }

    var c = canvas

    // Control panel in bottom-right corner
    let x = 50
    let y = 25

    let style = text_style_colored(COLOR_YELLOW())

    c = draw_text(c, x, y, "Controls:", style)
    c = draw_text(c, x, y + 1, "  Arrows: Pan", style)
    c = draw_text(c, x, y + 2, "  +/-: Zoom", style)
    c = draw_text(c, x, y + 3, "  r: Reset", style)
    c = draw_text(c, x, y + 4, "  h: Hide", style)

    return c
}

// Draw zoom/pan indicator
fn plot_draw_indicator(canvas: Canvas, plot: &InteractivePlot) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    let style = text_style_colored(COLOR_CYAN())

    // Zoom level
    c = draw_text(c, 2, 28, "Zoom:", style)

    // Convert zoom to string (simplified)
    let zoom_int = (plot.zoom_level * 10.0) as i32
    c = draw_text(c, 8, 28, "x.x", style)

    return c
}
