// Helper functions

fn print_f64(x: f64) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 {
        print("-")
        print_f64_unsigned(0.0 - x)
    } else {
        print_f64_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_f64_unsigned(x: f64) with IO, Div, Panic {
    let int_part = x as i32
    print_i32(int_part)
    print(".")

    let frac = x - (int_part as f64)
    let scaled = (frac * 100.0) as i32
    if scaled < 10 {
        print("0")
    }
    print_i32(scaled)
}

fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }

    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        return
    }

    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10

    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }

    let ch = 48 + digit
    print_char(ch)
}

fn print_char(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 48 { print("0") }
    else { if code == 49 { print("1") }
    else { if code == 50 { print("2") }
    else { if code == 51 { print("3") }
    else { if code == 52 { print("4") }
    else { if code == 53 { print("5") }
    else { if code == 54 { print("6") }
    else { if code == 55 { print("7") }
    else { if code == 56 { print("8") }
    else { if code == 57 { print("9") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/40_animation.sio ===
// 40_animation.sio - Animation framework with double buffering
//
// Provides terminal animation capabilities:
// - Frame management and timing
// - Double buffering (in-place updates)
// - FPS control (limited by terminal I/O speed)
// - Animation state tracking
//
// NOTE: Sleep/delay functionality requires FFI to platform timing.
// Current implementation relies on terminal I/O as the bottleneck.

// No imports needed - standalone module

// ============================================================================
// Animation State
// ============================================================================

struct AnimationState {
    frame: i32,           // Current frame number
    max_frames: i32,      // Total frames (0 = infinite loop)
    frame_delay_ms: i32,  // Target delay between frames
    running: i32,         // 1 if running, 0 if stopped
    loop_mode: i32,       // 0=once, 1=loop, 2=bounce
    fps_target: i32,      // Target frames per second
    elapsed_frames: i32   // Total frames elapsed (for statistics)
}

fn animation_state_new(max_frames: i32, fps: i32) -> AnimationState with Panic, Div {
    let frame_delay = if fps > 0 {
        1000 / fps
    } else {
        33  // Default ~30 FPS
    }

    return AnimationState {
        frame: 0,
        max_frames: max_frames,
        frame_delay_ms: frame_delay,
        running: 1,
        loop_mode: 0,
        fps_target: fps,
        elapsed_frames: 0
    }
}

fn animation_state_infinite(fps: i32) -> AnimationState with Panic, Div {
    return animation_state_new(0, fps)
}

fn animation_state_looping(max_frames: i32, fps: i32) -> AnimationState with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var state = animation_state_new(max_frames, fps)
    state.loop_mode = 1
    return state
}

// ============================================================================
// Animation Control
// ============================================================================

// Initialize animation (clear screen, hide cursor)
fn animation_init() with IO {
    print("\x1b[2J")      // Clear screen
    print("\x1b[H")       // Home cursor
    print("\x1b[?25l")    // Hide cursor
}

// Cleanup animation (show cursor, reset colors)
fn animation_cleanup() with IO {
    print("\x1b[?25h")    // Show cursor
    print("\x1b[0m")      // Reset colors
    print("\n")
}

// Begin a new frame (clear and home cursor)
fn animation_begin_frame() with IO {
    print("\x1b[H")       // Home cursor (don't clear to avoid flicker)
}

// End frame and update state
fn animation_end_frame(state: &!AnimationState) with Mut {
    state.frame = state.frame + 1
    state.elapsed_frames = state.elapsed_frames + 1

    // Check if animation should stop
    if state.max_frames > 0 {
        if state.frame >= state.max_frames {
            if state.loop_mode == 0 {
                // Stop after max frames
                state.running = 0
            } else { if state.loop_mode == 1 {
                // Loop mode: restart
                state.frame = 0
            } else {
                // Bounce mode: reverse (not implemented yet)
                state.running = 0
            }}
        }
    }

    // TODO: Sleep for frame_delay_ms
    // This requires FFI to platform sleep function
    // For now, terminal I/O provides natural throttling
}

// Check if animation should continue
fn animation_should_continue(state: &AnimationState) -> i32 {
    return state.running
}

// Stop animation
fn animation_stop(state: &!AnimationState) with Mut {
    state.running = 0
}

// Restart animation
fn animation_restart(state: &!AnimationState) with Mut {
    state.frame = 0
    state.running = 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Frame Utilities
// ============================================================================

// Get normalized time (0.0 to 1.0) within animation
fn animation_get_t(state: &AnimationState) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if state.max_frames <= 0 {
        return 0.0
    }

    return (state.frame as f64) / (state.max_frames as f64)
}

// Get frame progress percentage (0-100)
fn animation_get_progress(state: &AnimationState) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if state.max_frames <= 0 {
        return 0
    }

    return (state.frame * 100) / state.max_frames
}

// Oscillate between 0.0 and 1.0 (smooth back-and-forth)
fn animation_oscillate(state: &AnimationState) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let t = animation_get_t(state)
    // sin((t * 2π)) maps to [-1, 1], we want [0, 1]
    // So use: (1 + sin(2π * t - π/2)) / 2
    // Simplified: (1 - cos(2π * t)) / 2

    // For now, use triangle wave approximation
    if t < 0.5 {
        return t * 2.0
    } else {
        return 2.0 - t * 2.0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Animation Loop Pattern
// ============================================================================
//
// NOTE: Animation loops that use Canvas are implemented in demo files
// where Canvas is available. This module provides only the core state
// management, timing, and easing functions.

// ============================================================================
// Easing Functions (for smooth animations)
// ============================================================================

// Linear interpolation: out = a + t * (b - a)
// Note: A lerp function may exist in math stdlib, but we define our own for standalone use
fn anim_lerp(a: f64, b: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    return a + t * (b - a)
}

// Ease in (quadratic): starts slow, accelerates
fn ease_in(t: f64) -> f64 {
    return t * t
}

// Ease out (quadratic): starts fast, decelerates
fn ease_out(t: f64) -> f64 {
    return t * (2.0 - t)
}

// Ease in-out (quadratic): slow start and end, fast middle
fn ease_in_out(t: f64) -> f64 {
    if t < 0.5 {
        return 2.0 * t * t
    } else {
        let s = t - 0.5
        return 0.5 + 2.0 * s * (1.0 - s)
    }
}

// Bounce easing (simulates elastic bounce)
fn ease_bounce(t: f64) -> f64 {
    if t < 0.5 {
        return 8.0 * t * t * t * t
    } else {
        let s = t - 1.0
        return 1.0 - 8.0 * s * s * s * s
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Helper Functions
// ============================================================================

fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }

    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        return
    }

    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10

    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }

    let ch = 48 + digit
    print_char(ch)
}

fn print_char(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 48 { print("0") }
    else { if code == 49 { print("1") }
    else { if code == 50 { print("2") }
    else { if code == 51 { print("3") }
    else { if code == 52 { print("4") }
    else { if code == 53 { print("5") }
    else { if code == 54 { print("6") }
    else { if code == 55 { print("7") }
    else { if code == 56 { print("8") }
    else { if code == 57 { print("9") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}
}

// ============================================================================
// Example/Test Function
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")  // Clear screen
    print("=== Animation Framework Test ===\n\n")

    // Create animation state
    var state = animation_state_new(10, 30)

    print("Animation state created:\n")
    print("  Max frames: ")
    print_i32(state.max_frames)
    print("\n")
    print("  FPS target: ")
    print_i32(state.fps_target)
    print("\n")
    print("  Frame delay: ")
    print_i32(state.frame_delay_ms)
    print("ms\n\n")

    print("Frame progression test:\n")

    var i = 0
    while i < 12 {
        print("  Frame ")
        print_i32(state.frame)
        print(": t=")

        let t = animation_get_t(&state)
        let t_int = (t * 100.0) as i32
        print_i32(t_int / 100)
        print(".")
        let frac = t_int % 100
        if frac < 10 {
            print("0")
        }
        print_i32(frac)

        print(", progress=")
        print_i32(animation_get_progress(&state))
        print("%, running=")
        print_i32(state.running)
        print("\n")

        animation_end_frame(&!state)
        i = i + 1
    }

    print("\nEasing functions test (t=0.0 to 1.0):\n")

    var j = 0
    while j <= 10 {
        let t = (j as f64) / 10.0

        print("  t=")
        let t_int = (t * 10.0) as i32
        print_i32(t_int / 10)
        print(".")
        print_i32(t_int % 10)

        print(": ease_in=")
        let ei = (ease_in(t) * 100.0) as i32
        print_i32(ei)

        print(", ease_out=")
        let eo = (ease_out(t) * 100.0) as i32
        print_i32(eo)

        print(", ease_in_out=")
        let eio = (ease_in_out(t) * 100.0) as i32
        print_i32(eio)
        print("\n")

        j = j + 1
    }

    print("\n=== Animation Framework Ready ===\n")
    print("Use animation_loop() or animation_loop_time() for canvas animation\n")

    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/41_particle_system.sio ===
// 41_particle_system.sio - Particle physics simulation
//
// Provides particle system for visual effects:
// - 2D/3D particle simulation with physics
// - Forces: gravity, drag, wind
// - Particle lifecycle management (birth, death)
// - Emitters with various patterns
// - Visual rendering with markers and trails

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"
import "00_canvas.sio"
import "01_colors.sio"
import "02_drawing.sio"
import "10_axes.sio"
import "20_projection.sio"

// ============================================================================
// Particle Structure
// ============================================================================

struct Particle {
    pos: Vec3D,        // Position (x, y, z)
    vel: Vec3D,        // Velocity (dx/dt, dy/dt, dz/dt)
    acc: Vec3D,        // Acceleration (forces applied)
    color: i32,        // Particle color (0-15)
    marker: i32,       // Character marker
    size: i32,         // Particle size (1-3)
    life: f64,         // Remaining lifetime (seconds)
    max_life: f64,     // Initial lifetime
    mass: f64,         // Particle mass (affects forces)
    alive: i32         // 1 if active, 0 if dead
}

fn particle_new(
    pos: Vec3D,
    vel: Vec3D,
    color: i32,
    marker: i32,
    life: f64,
    mass: f64
) -> Particle {
    return Particle {
        pos: pos,
        vel: vel,
        acc: vec3d_zero(),
        color: color,
        marker: marker,
        size: 1,
        life: life,
        max_life: life,
        mass: mass,
        alive: 1
    }
}

fn particle_dead() -> Particle {
    return Particle {
        pos: vec3d_zero(),
        vel: vec3d_zero(),
        acc: vec3d_zero(),
        color: 0,
        marker: 32,  // Space
        size: 1,
        life: 0.0,
        max_life: 1.0,
        mass: 1.0,
        alive: 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Particle System
// ============================================================================

struct ParticleSystem {
    particles: [Particle; 500],
    n_particles: i32,
    max_particles: i32,

    // Global forces
    gravity: Vec3D,
    wind: Vec3D,
    drag: f64,          // Air resistance coefficient

    // Emitter settings
    emit_pos: Vec3D,
    emit_rate: i32,     // Particles per frame
    emit_velocity: f64, // Initial speed
    emit_spread: f64,   // Angle spread (radians)

    // Particle lifecycle
    particle_lifetime: f64,
    particle_mass: f64,

    // Rendering
    trail_length: i32,  // 0 = no trails
    fade_with_age: i32  // 1 = fade color as particle ages
}

fn particle_system_new(max_particles: i32) -> ParticleSystem {
    return ParticleSystem {
        particles: [particle_dead(); 500],
        n_particles: 0,
        max_particles: max_particles,
        gravity: vec3d_new(0.0, -9.8, 0.0),
        wind: vec3d_zero(),
        drag: 0.01,
        emit_pos: vec3d_zero(),
        emit_rate: 5,
        emit_velocity: 10.0,
        emit_spread: 0.5,
        particle_lifetime: 3.0,
        particle_mass: 1.0,
        trail_length: 0,
        fade_with_age: 1
    }
}

fn particle_system_fountain(max_particles: i32) -> ParticleSystem {
    var sys = particle_system_new(max_particles)
    sys.emit_pos = vec3d_new(0.0, -5.0, 0.0)
    sys.emit_velocity = 15.0
    sys.emit_spread = 0.8
    sys.emit_rate = 10
    sys.particle_lifetime = 2.5
    sys.gravity = vec3d_new(0.0, -15.0, 0.0)
    sys.drag = 0.02
    return sys
}

fn particle_system_explosion(max_particles: i32) -> ParticleSystem {
    var sys = particle_system_new(max_particles)
    sys.emit_pos = vec3d_zero()
    sys.emit_velocity = 20.0
    sys.emit_spread = 3.14159265359  // Full sphere
    sys.emit_rate = 50
    sys.particle_lifetime = 1.5
    sys.gravity = vec3d_new(0.0, -5.0, 0.0)
    sys.drag = 0.05
    return sys
}

// ============================================================================
// Particle Emission
// ============================================================================

// Emit a single particle
fn emit_particle(
    sys: &!ParticleSystem,
    direction: Vec3D,
    velocity: f64,
    color: i32,
    marker: i32
) with Mut, Panic {
    // Find dead particle slot
    var i = 0
    while i < sys.max_particles {
        if sys.particles[i].alive == 0 {
            let dir_norm = vec3d_normalize(&direction)
            let vel = vec3d_scale(&dir_norm, velocity)

            sys.particles[i] = particle_new(
                sys.emit_pos,
                vel,
                color,
                marker,
                sys.particle_lifetime,
                sys.particle_mass
            )

            sys.n_particles = sys.n_particles + 1
            return
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Emit particles from emitter (called each frame)
fn emit_particles(sys: &!ParticleSystem, rng_seed: &!i32) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i = 0
    while i < sys.emit_rate {
        // Generate random direction within spread cone
        // Simple pseudo-random using LCG
        rng_seed.val = (rng_seed.val * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let theta = ((rng_seed.val % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0) * sys.emit_spread

        rng_seed.val = (rng_seed.val * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let phi = ((rng_seed.val % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0) * 6.28318530718

        // Spherical to Cartesian
        let x = sin(theta) * cos(phi)
        let y = cos(theta)
        let z = sin(theta) * sin(phi)

        let direction = vec3d_new(x, y, z)

        // Random color
        rng_seed.val = (rng_seed.val * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let color = (rng_seed.val % 6) + 2  // Colors 2-7 (avoid black/white)

        emit_particle(sys, direction, sys.emit_velocity, color as i32, 9679)  // ●
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Particle Physics Update
// ============================================================================

// Apply forces to particle
fn apply_forces(particle: &!Particle, gravity: Vec3D, wind: Vec3D, drag: f64) with Mut {
    // Reset acceleration
    particle.acc = vec3d_zero()

    // Gravity (F = m * g)
    let gravity_force = vec3d_scale(&gravity, particle.mass)
    particle.acc = vec3d_add(&particle.acc, &gravity_force)

    // Wind (constant force)
    particle.acc = vec3d_add(&particle.acc, &wind)

    // Drag (F = -drag * v)
    let drag_force = vec3d_scale(&particle.vel, 0.0 - drag)
    particle.acc = vec3d_add(&particle.acc, &drag_force)
}

// Update single particle (Euler integration)
fn update_particle(
    particle: &!Particle,
    dt: f64,
    gravity: Vec3D,
    wind: Vec3D,
    drag: f64
) with Mut {
    if particle.alive == 0 {
        return
    }

    // Apply forces
    apply_forces(particle, gravity, wind, drag)

    // Update velocity: v = v + a * dt
    let dv = vec3d_scale(&particle.acc, dt)
    particle.vel = vec3d_add(&particle.vel, &dv)

    // Update position: p = p + v * dt
    let dp = vec3d_scale(&particle.vel, dt)
    particle.pos = vec3d_add(&particle.pos, &dp)

    // Update lifetime
    particle.life = particle.life - dt
    if particle.life <= 0.0 {
        particle.alive = 0
    }
}

// Update entire particle system
fn particle_system_update(sys: &!ParticleSystem, dt: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    var alive_count = 0

    while i < sys.max_particles {
        if sys.particles[i].alive == 1 {
            update_particle(
                &!sys.particles[i],
                dt,
                sys.gravity,
                sys.wind,
                sys.drag
            )

            if sys.particles[i].alive == 1 {
                alive_count = alive_count + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    sys.n_particles = alive_count
}

// ============================================================================
// Particle Rendering
// ============================================================================

// Render particle system (2D projection)
fn particle_system_render_2d(
    canvas: Canvas,
    sys: &ParticleSystem,
    vp: &Viewport
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    var i = 0
    while i < sys.max_particles {
        let p = &sys.particles[i]

        if p.alive == 1 {
            // Project 3D position to 2D (use x, y, ignore z for now)
            let px = world_to_canvas_x(vp, p.pos.x)
            let py = world_to_canvas_y(vp, p.pos.y)

            // Fade color with age if enabled
            let color = if sys.fade_with_age == 1 {
                let age_ratio = p.life / p.max_life
                if age_ratio < 0.33 {
                    8  // Dark gray (fading out)
                } else {
                    p.color
                }
            } else {
                p.color
            }

            // Draw particle
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, p.marker, color)
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    return c
}

// Render particle system (3D with isometric projection)
fn particle_system_render_3d(
    canvas: Canvas,
    sys: &ParticleSystem,
    vp: &Viewport,
    scale: f64
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    var i = 0
    while i < sys.max_particles {
        let p = &sys.particles[i]

        if p.alive == 1 {
            // Isometric projection
            let projected = isometric_project_scaled(&p.pos, scale)

            let px = world_to_canvas_x(vp, projected.x)
            let py = world_to_canvas_y(vp, projected.y)

            // Fade color with age
            let color = if sys.fade_with_age == 1 {
                let age_ratio = p.life / p.max_life
                if age_ratio < 0.25 {
                    8  // Dark gray
                } else { if age_ratio < 0.5 {
                    p.color + 8  // Bright version
                } else {
                    p.color
                }}
            } else {
                p.color
            }

            // Draw particle
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, p.marker, color)
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    return c
}

// Particle Effects Presets

// Create fountain effect

    sys.emit_pos = vec3d_new(0.0, -5.0, 0.0)

    sys.emit_spread = 0.5
    sys.emit_rate = 8

    print_i32(int_part)

}

// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/42_fluid_sim.sio ===
// 42_fluid_sim.sio - Fluid dynamics simulation
//
// Provides 2D fluid simulation using Navier-Stokes equations:
// - Incompressible fluid flow
// - Velocity field (u, v)
// - Density/dye visualization
// - Vorticity confinement (optional)
// - Semi-Lagrangian advection
//
// Based on Jos Stam's "Stable Fluids" (SIGGRAPH 1999)
// Simplified for terminal visualization

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"
import "00_canvas.sio"
import "01_colors.sio"
import "15_heatmap.sio"

// ============================================================================
// Fluid Grid Structure
// ============================================================================

struct FluidGrid {
    width: i32,
    height: i32,

    // Velocity field
    u: [f64; 2500],      // X-velocity at each cell
    v: [f64; 2500],      // Y-velocity at each cell
    u_prev: [f64; 2500], // Previous X-velocity
    v_prev: [f64; 2500], // Previous Y-velocity

    // Density/dye field
    density: [f64; 2500],
    density_prev: [f64; 2500],

    // Simulation parameters
    diffusion: f64,      // Viscosity coefficient
    viscosity: f64,      // Kinematic viscosity
    dt: f64              // Time step
}

fn fluid_grid_new(width: i32, height: i32, diffusion: f64, viscosity: f64) -> FluidGrid {
    return FluidGrid {
        width: width,
        height: height,
        u: [0.0; 2500],
        v: [0.0; 2500],
        u_prev: [0.0; 2500],
        v_prev: [0.0; 2500],
        density: [0.0; 2500],
        density_prev: [0.0; 2500],
        diffusion: diffusion,
        viscosity: viscosity,
        dt: 0.016  // ~60 FPS
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Grid Access Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn ix(x: i32, y: i32, width: i32) -> i32 with Panic {
    return y * width + x
}

fn get_cell(grid: &[f64], x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32) -> f64 with Panic {
    if x < 0 || x >= width || y < 0 || y >= height {
        return 0.0
    }
    return grid[ix(x, y, width)]
}

fn set_cell(grid: &![f64], x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32, value: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < width && y >= 0 && y < height {
        grid[ix(x, y, width)] = value
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Boundary Conditions
// ============================================================================

// Apply boundary conditions to scalar field
fn set_bounds_scalar(field: &![f64], width: i32, height: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    // Left and right edges
    var y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        field[ix(0, y, width)] = field[ix(1, y, width)]
        field[ix(width - 1, y, width)] = field[ix(width - 2, y, width)]
        y = y + 1
    }

    // Top and bottom edges
    var x = 1
    while x < width - 1 {
        field[ix(x, 0, width)] = field[ix(x, 1, width)]
        field[ix(x, height - 1, width)] = field[ix(x, height - 2, width)]
        x = x + 1
    }

    // Corners
    field[ix(0, 0, width)] = (field[ix(1, 0, width)] + field[ix(0, 1, width)]) / 2.0
    field[ix(width - 1, 0, width)] = (field[ix(width - 2, 0, width)] + field[ix(width - 1, 1, width)]) / 2.0
    field[ix(0, height - 1, width)] = (field[ix(1, height - 1, width)] + field[ix(0, height - 2, width)]) / 2.0
    field[ix(width - 1, height - 1, width)] = (field[ix(width - 2, height - 1, width)] + field[ix(width - 1, height - 2, width)]) / 2.0
}

// Apply boundary conditions to velocity field
fn set_bounds_velocity(u: &![f64], v: &![f64], width: i32, height: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    // U velocity (horizontal): reverse at left/right walls
    var y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        u[ix(0, y, width)] = 0.0 - u[ix(1, y, width)]
        u[ix(width - 1, y, width)] = 0.0 - u[ix(width - 2, y, width)]
        y = y + 1
    }

    // V velocity (vertical): reverse at top/bottom walls
    var x = 1
    while x < width - 1 {
        v[ix(x, 0, width)] = 0.0 - v[ix(x, 1, width)]
        v[ix(x, height - 1, width)] = 0.0 - v[ix(x, height - 2, width)]
        x = x + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Diffusion (Implicit Method)
// ============================================================================

// Gauss-Seidel relaxation for diffusion
fn diffuse(
    current: &![f64],
    prev: &[f64],
    diff_coeff: f64,
    dt: f64,
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    iterations: i32
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let a = dt * diff_coeff * ((width - 2) * (height - 2)) as f64

    var iter = 0
    while iter < iterations {
        var y = 1
        while y < height - 1 {
            var x = 1
            while x < width - 1 {
                let idx = ix(x, y, width)

                let neighbors =
                    current[ix(x - 1, y, width)] +
                    current[ix(x + 1, y, width)] +
                    current[ix(x, y - 1, width)] +
                    current[ix(x, y + 1, width)]

                current[idx] = (prev[idx] + a * neighbors) / (1.0 + 4.0 * a)

                x = x + 1
            }
            y = y + 1
        }

        set_bounds_scalar(current, width, height)
        iter = iter + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Advection (Semi-Lagrangian)
// ============================================================================

// Advect scalar field by velocity field
fn advect(
    current: &![f64],
    prev: &[f64],
    u: &[f64],
    v: &[f64],
    dt: f64,
    width: i32,
    height: i32
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let dt_x = dt * (width - 2) as f64
    let dt_y = dt * (height - 2) as f64

    var y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        var x = 1
        while x < width - 1 {
            let idx = ix(x, y, width)

            // Backtrack position
            let x_back = (x as f64) - dt_x * u[idx]
            let y_back = (y as f64) - dt_y * v[idx]

            // Clamp to grid bounds
            let x_clamp = if x_back < 0.5 {
                0.5
            } else { if x_back > (width as f64) - 1.5 {
                (width as f64) - 1.5
            } else {
                x_back
            }}

            let y_clamp = if y_back < 0.5 {
                0.5
            } else { if y_back > (height as f64) - 1.5 {
                (height as f64) - 1.5
            } else {
                y_back
            }}

            // Bilinear interpolation
            let i0 = x_clamp as i32
            let i1 = i0 + 1
            let j0 = y_clamp as i32
            let j1 = j0 + 1

            let s1 = x_clamp - (i0 as f64)
            let s0 = 1.0 - s1
            let t1 = y_clamp - (j0 as f64)
            let t0 = 1.0 - t1

            current[idx] =
                s0 * (t0 * prev[ix(i0, j0, width)] + t1 * prev[ix(i0, j1, width)]) +
                s1 * (t0 * prev[ix(i1, j0, width)] + t1 * prev[ix(i1, j1, width)])

            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }

    set_bounds_scalar(current, width, height)
}

// ============================================================================
// Projection (Incompressibility)
// ============================================================================

// Project velocity field to be divergence-free
fn project(
    u: &![f64],
    v: &![f64],
    p: &![f64],    // Pressure
    div: &![f64],  // Divergence
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    iterations: i32
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Compute divergence
    var y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        var x = 1
        while x < width - 1 {
            let idx = ix(x, y, width)

            div[idx] = -0.5 * (
                u[ix(x + 1, y, width)] - u[ix(x - 1, y, width)] +
                v[ix(x, y + 1, width)] - v[ix(x, y - 1, width)]
            ) / (width as f64)

            p[idx] = 0.0

            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }

    set_bounds_scalar(div, width, height)
    set_bounds_scalar(p, width, height)

    // Solve for pressure (Gauss-Seidel)
    var iter = 0
    while iter < iterations {
        y = 1
        while y < height - 1 {
            x = 1
            while x < width - 1 {
                let idx = ix(x, y, width)

                p[idx] = (
                    div[idx] +
                    p[ix(x - 1, y, width)] +
                    p[ix(x + 1, y, width)] +
                    p[ix(x, y - 1, width)] +
                    p[ix(x, y + 1, width)]
                ) / 4.0

                x = x + 1
            }
            y = y + 1
        }

        set_bounds_scalar(p, width, height)
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Subtract pressure gradient from velocity
    y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        x = 1
        while x < width - 1 {
            let idx = ix(x, y, width)

            u[idx] = u[idx] - 0.5 * (width as f64) * (p[ix(x + 1, y, width)] - p[ix(x - 1, y, width)])
            v[idx] = v[idx] - 0.5 * (height as f64) * (p[ix(x, y + 1, width)] - p[ix(x, y - 1, width)])

            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }

    set_bounds_velocity(u, v, width, height)
}

// ============================================================================
// Fluid Simulation Step
// ============================================================================

fn fluid_step(fluid: &!FluidGrid) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let width = fluid.width
    let height = fluid.height
    let dt = fluid.dt
    let visc = fluid.viscosity
    let diff = fluid.diffusion

    // Temporary arrays for projection
    var p: [f64; 2500] = [0.0; 2500]
    var div: [f64; 2500] = [0.0; 2500]

    // ========================================================================
    // Velocity Step
    // ========================================================================

    // Diffusion (viscosity)
    if visc > 0.0001 {
        diffuse(&!fluid.u, &fluid.u_prev, visc, dt, width, height, 4)
        diffuse(&!fluid.v, &fluid.v_prev, visc, dt, width, height, 4)
    }

    // Projection (incompressibility)
    project(&!fluid.u, &!fluid.v, &!p, &!div, width, height, 4)

    // Save for advection
    fluid.u_prev = fluid.u
    fluid.v_prev = fluid.v

    // Advection (self-advection of velocity)
    advect(&!fluid.u, &fluid.u_prev, &fluid.u_prev, &fluid.v_prev, dt, width, height)
    advect(&!fluid.v, &fluid.v_prev, &fluid.u_prev, &fluid.v_prev, dt, width, height)

    // Final projection
    project(&!fluid.u, &!fluid.v, &!p, &!div, width, height, 4)

    // ========================================================================
    // Density Step
    // ========================================================================

    // Diffusion
    if diff > 0.0001 {
        diffuse(&!fluid.density, &fluid.density_prev, diff, dt, width, height, 4)
        fluid.density_prev = fluid.density
    }

    // Advection
    advect(&!fluid.density, &fluid.density_prev, &fluid.u, &fluid.v, dt, width, height)
}

// ============================================================================
// User Interaction Helpers
// ============================================================================

// Add density at position
fn add_density(fluid: &!FluidGrid, x: i32, y: i32, amount: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < fluid.width && y >= 0 && y < fluid.height {
        let idx = ix(x, y, fluid.width)
        fluid.density[idx] = fluid.density[idx] + amount
    }
}

// Add velocity at position
fn add_velocity(fluid: &!FluidGrid, x: i32, y: i32, vx: f64, vy: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < fluid.width && y >= 0 && y < fluid.height {
        let idx = ix(x, y, fluid.width)
        fluid.u[idx] = fluid.u[idx] + vx
        fluid.v[idx] = fluid.v[idx] + vy
    }
}

// Clear density field
fn clear_density(fluid: &!FluidGrid) with Mut {
    fluid.density = [0.0; 2500]
}

// Fade density over time
fn fade_density(fluid: &!FluidGrid, fade_rate: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < fluid.width * fluid.height {
        fluid.density[i] = fluid.density[i] * fade_rate
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Rendering
// ============================================================================

// Render fluid density as heatmap
fn fluid_render(
    canvas: Canvas,
    fluid: &FluidGrid,
    vp: &Viewport,
    colormap: i32
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Find max density for normalization
    var max_density = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < fluid.width * fluid.height {
        if fluid.density[i] > max_density {
            max_density = fluid.density[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Render using heatmap
    return heatmap(
        canvas,
        vp,
        &fluid.density,
        fluid.width,
        fluid.height,
        0.0,
        max_density,
        colormap
    )
}

// ============================================================================
// Example/Test Function
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")  // Clear screen
    print("=== Fluid Simulation Test ===\n\n")

    // Create fluid grid
    var fluid = fluid_grid_new(30, 30, 0.0, 0.0001)

    print("Fluid grid created:\n")
    print("  Size: ")
    print_i32(fluid.width)
    print(" x ")
    print_i32(fluid.height)
    print("\n")
    print("  Viscosity: ")
    print_f64(fluid.viscosity)
    print("\n")
    print("  Diffusion: ")
    print_f64(fluid.diffusion)
    print("\n\n")

    // Add some initial density and velocity
    add_density(&!fluid, 15, 15, 100.0)
    add_velocity(&!fluid, 15, 15, 5.0, 3.0)

    print("Initial conditions:\n")
    print("  Density at (15, 15): ")
    print_f64(fluid.density[ix(15, 15, fluid.width)])
    print("\n")
    print("  Velocity at (15, 15): (")
    print_f64(fluid.u[ix(15, 15, fluid.width)])
    print(", ")
    print_f64(fluid.v[ix(15, 15, fluid.width)])
    print(")\n\n")

    // Simulate a few steps
    print("Simulation steps:\n")

    var step = 0
    while step < 5 {
        fluid_step(&!fluid)

        print("  Step ")
        print_i32(step)
        print(": density at (15, 15) = ")
        print_f64(fluid.density[ix(15, 15, fluid.width)])
        print("\n")

        step = step + 1
    }

    print("\n=== Fluid Simulation Ready ===\n")
    print("Methods:\n")
    print("  • add_density(x, y, amount) - Add dye\n")
    print("  • add_velocity(x, y, vx, vy) - Add force\n")
    print("  • fluid_step() - Advance simulation\n")
    print("  • fluid_render() - Visualize density field\n")

    return 0
}

// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/50_phase_diagram.sio ===
// 50_phase_diagram.sio - Phase diagram visualization for scientific computing
//
// Phase diagrams show regions of different system states based on two
// control parameters (e.g., temperature vs pressure, composition vs temperature).
// Essential for materials science, thermodynamics, and dynamical systems.
//
// Features:
// - Multiple phase regions with distinct colors
// - Phase boundaries (coexistence curves)
// - Critical points and triple points
// - Tie lines for two-phase regions
// - Labeled axes with scientific units

// ============================================================================
// Phase Region Types
// ============================================================================

struct PhaseRegion {
    id: i32,              // Region identifier
    color: i32,           // ANSI color code
    marker: i32,          // Character code for filling
    name_code: i32        // First character of phase name (S=83, L=76, G=71, etc.)
}

struct PhaseBoundary {
    phase1: i32,          // ID of first phase
    phase2: i32,          // ID of second phase
    // Boundary is defined by points
    x_points: [f64; 100],
    y_points: [f64; 100],
    num_points: i32
}

struct CriticalPoint {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    marker: i32           // Character to display
}

struct TriplePoint {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    marker: i32
}

struct PhaseDiagram {
    // Viewport bounds
    x_min: f64,
    x_max: f64,
    y_min: f64,
    y_max: f64,

    // Grid dimensions for rendering
    width: i32,
    height: i32,

    // Phase regions (up to 8)
    regions: [PhaseRegion; 8],
    num_regions: i32,

    // Boundaries (up to 16)
    boundaries: [PhaseBoundary; 16],
    num_boundaries: i32,

    // Special points
    critical_points: [CriticalPoint; 4],
    num_critical: i32,
    triple_points: [TriplePoint; 4],
    num_triple: i32,

    // Phase field (stores which phase each grid cell belongs to)
    phase_field: [i32; 4096],  // Up to 64x64 grid

    // Axis labels (as character codes)
    x_label: i32,  // First char of x-axis label
    y_label: i32   // First char of y-axis label
}

// ============================================================================
// Initialization
// ============================================================================

fn phase_diagram_new(
    x_min: f64, x_max: f64,
    y_min: f64, y_max: f64,
    width: i32, height: i32
) -> PhaseDiagram {
    let empty_region = PhaseRegion {
        id: 0,
        color: 0,
        marker: 32,  // Space
        name_code: 32
    }

    let empty_boundary = PhaseBoundary {
        phase1: 0,
        phase2: 0,
        x_points: [0.0; 100],
        y_points: [0.0; 100],
        num_points: 0
    }

    let empty_critical = CriticalPoint {
        x: 0.0,
        y: 0.0,
        marker: 67  // 'C'
    }

    let empty_triple = TriplePoint {
        x: 0.0,
        y: 0.0,
        marker: 84  // 'T'
    }

    return PhaseDiagram {
        x_min: x_min,
        x_max: x_max,
        y_min: y_min,
        y_max: y_max,
        width: width,
        height: height,
        regions: [empty_region; 8],
        num_regions: 0,
        boundaries: [empty_boundary; 16],
        num_boundaries: 0,
        critical_points: [empty_critical; 4],
        num_critical: 0,
        triple_points: [empty_triple; 4],
        num_triple: 0,
        phase_field: [0; 4096],
        x_label: 84,  // 'T' for temperature
        y_label: 80   // 'P' for pressure
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Phase Region Management
// ============================================================================

fn phase_diagram_add_region(
    diagram: &!PhaseDiagram,
    id: i32,
    color: i32,
    marker: i32,
    name_code: i32
) with Mut {
    if diagram.num_regions < 8 {
        let idx = diagram.num_regions
        diagram.regions[idx] = PhaseRegion {
            id: id,
            color: color,
            marker: marker,
            name_code: name_code
        }
        diagram.num_regions = diagram.num_regions + 1
    }
}

// Standard phases for materials
fn phase_diagram_add_solid(diagram: &!PhaseDiagram) with Mut {
    phase_diagram_add_region(diagram, 1, 34, 35, 83)  // Blue, '#', 'S'
}

fn phase_diagram_add_liquid(diagram: &!PhaseDiagram) with Mut {
    phase_diagram_add_region(diagram, 2, 36, 126, 76)  // Cyan, '~', 'L'
}

fn phase_diagram_add_gas(diagram: &!PhaseDiagram) with Mut {
    phase_diagram_add_region(diagram, 3, 33, 46, 71)  // Yellow, '.', 'G'
}

fn phase_diagram_add_supercritical(diagram: &!PhaseDiagram) with Mut {
    phase_diagram_add_region(diagram, 4, 35, 42, 88)  // Magenta, '*', 'X'
}

// ============================================================================
// Phase Field Computation
// ============================================================================

// Set phase for a grid cell
fn phase_field_set(diagram: &!PhaseDiagram, x: i32, y: i32, phase: i32) with Mut {
    if x >= 0 {
        if x < diagram.width {
            if y >= 0 {
                if y < diagram.height {
                    let idx = y * diagram.width + x
                    if idx < 4096 {
                        diagram.phase_field[idx] = phase
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

// Get phase for a grid cell
fn phase_field_get(diagram: &PhaseDiagram, x: i32, y: i32) -> i32 {
    if x >= 0 {
        if x < diagram.width {
            if y >= 0 {
                if y < diagram.height {
                    let idx = y * diagram.width + x
                    if idx < 4096 {
                        return diagram.phase_field[idx]
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return 0
}

// Convert grid coordinates to data coordinates
fn grid_to_data_x(diagram: &PhaseDiagram, gx: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let t = (gx as f64) / ((diagram.width - 1) as f64)
    return diagram.x_min + t * (diagram.x_max - diagram.x_min)
}

fn grid_to_data_y(diagram: &PhaseDiagram, gy: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let t = (gy as f64) / ((diagram.height - 1) as f64)
    return diagram.y_min + t * (diagram.y_max - diagram.y_min)
}

// Fill phase field using a classifier function
// classifier: given (x, y) returns phase id
fn phase_diagram_compute_field(
    diagram: &!PhaseDiagram,
    classifier: fn(f64, f64) -> i32
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var y = 0
    while y < diagram.height {
        var x = 0
        while x < diagram.width {
            let data_x = grid_to_data_x(diagram, x)
            let data_y = grid_to_data_y(diagram, y)
            let phase = classifier(data_x, data_y)
            phase_field_set(diagram, x, y, phase)
            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Special Points
// ============================================================================

fn phase_diagram_add_critical_point(
    diagram: &!PhaseDiagram,
    x: f64,
    y: f64
) with Mut {
    if diagram.num_critical < 4 {
        let idx = diagram.num_critical
        diagram.critical_points[idx] = CriticalPoint {
            x: x,
            y: y,
            marker: 67  // 'C'
        }
        diagram.num_critical = diagram.num_critical + 1
    }
}

fn phase_diagram_add_triple_point(
    diagram: &!PhaseDiagram,
    x: f64,
    y: f64
) with Mut {
    if diagram.num_triple < 4 {
        let idx = diagram.num_triple
        diagram.triple_points[idx] = TriplePoint {
            x: x,
            y: y,
            marker: 84  // 'T'
        }
        diagram.num_triple = diagram.num_triple + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Rendering Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn print_char_code(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 32 { print(" ") }
    else { if code == 35 { print("#") }
    else { if code == 42 { print("*") }
    else { if code == 46 { print(".") }
    else { if code == 67 { print("C") }
    else { if code == 71 { print("G") }
    else { if code == 76 { print("L") }
    else { if code == 80 { print("P") }
    else { if code == 83 { print("S") }
    else { if code == 84 { print("T") }
    else { if code == 88 { print("X") }
    else { if code == 124 { print("|") }
    else { if code == 126 { print("~") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}}}}}
}

fn get_region_by_id(diagram: &PhaseDiagram, id: i32) -> PhaseRegion {
    var i = 0
    while i < diagram.num_regions {
        if diagram.regions[i].id == id {
            return diagram.regions[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Return default
    return PhaseRegion {
        id: 0,
        color: 37,  // White
        marker: 32,
        name_code: 32
    }
}

// Check if a cell is on a phase boundary
fn is_boundary_cell(diagram: &PhaseDiagram, x: i32, y: i32) -> i32 {
    let phase = phase_field_get(diagram, x, y)

    // Check neighbors
    if x > 0 {
        if phase_field_get(diagram, x - 1, y) != phase {
            return 1
        }
    }
    if x < diagram.width - 1 {
        if phase_field_get(diagram, x + 1, y) != phase {
            return 1
        }
    }
    if y > 0 {
        if phase_field_get(diagram, x, y - 1) != phase {
            return 1
        }
    }
    if y < diagram.height - 1 {
        if phase_field_get(diagram, x, y + 1) != phase {
            return 1
        }
    }

    return 0
}

// ============================================================================
// Main Rendering
// ============================================================================

fn phase_diagram_render(diagram: &PhaseDiagram) with IO, Div, Panic {
    // Clear screen and position cursor
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")

    // Title
    print("\x1b[1m=== Phase Diagram ===\x1b[0m\n\n")

    // Y-axis label
    print("  ")
    print_char_code(diagram.y_label)
    print("\n")
    print("  ^\n")

    // Render from top to bottom (high y first)
    var y = diagram.height - 1
    while y >= 0 {
        // Y-axis
        print("  |")

        var x = 0
        while x < diagram.width {
            let phase = phase_field_get(diagram, x, y)
            let region = get_region_by_id(diagram, phase)

            // Check for special points
            let data_x = grid_to_data_x(diagram, x)
            let data_y = grid_to_data_y(diagram, y)
            var is_special = 0
            var special_marker = 0

            // Check critical points
            var ci = 0
            while ci < diagram.num_critical {
                let cp = diagram.critical_points[ci]
                let dx = data_x - cp.x
                let dy = data_y - cp.y
                if dx < 0.0 { let dx = 0.0 - dx }
                if dy < 0.0 { let dy = 0.0 - dy }
                let range_x = (diagram.x_max - diagram.x_min) / (diagram.width as f64)
                let range_y = (diagram.y_max - diagram.y_min) / (diagram.height as f64)
                if dx < range_x {
                    if dy < range_y {
                        is_special = 1
                        special_marker = cp.marker
                    }
                }
                ci = ci + 1
            }

            // Check triple points
            var ti = 0
            while ti < diagram.num_triple {
                let tp = diagram.triple_points[ti]
                let dx = data_x - tp.x
                let dy = data_y - tp.y
                if dx < 0.0 { let dx = 0.0 - dx }
                if dy < 0.0 { let dy = 0.0 - dy }
                let range_x = (diagram.x_max - diagram.x_min) / (diagram.width as f64)
                let range_y = (diagram.y_max - diagram.y_min) / (diagram.height as f64)
                if dx < range_x {
                    if dy < range_y {
                        is_special = 1
                        special_marker = tp.marker
                    }
                }
                ti = ti + 1
            }

            // Render cell
            if is_special == 1 {
                print("\x1b[1;31m")  // Bold red for special points
                print_char_code(special_marker)
                print("\x1b[0m")
            } else { if is_boundary_cell(diagram, x, y) == 1 {
                print("\x1b[1;37m")  // Bold white for boundaries
                print("|")
                print("\x1b[0m")
            } else {
                // Normal phase cell
                print("\x1b[")
                print_i32(region.color)
                print("m")
                print_char_code(region.marker)
                print("\x1b[0m")
            }}

            x = x + 1
        }

        print("\n")
        y = y - 1
    }

    // X-axis
    print("  +")
    var xi = 0
    while xi < diagram.width {
        print("-")
        xi = xi + 1
    }
    print("> ")
    print_char_code(diagram.x_label)
    print("\n\n")

    // Legend
    print("Legend: ")
    var ri = 0
    while ri < diagram.num_regions {
        let region = diagram.regions[ri]
        print("\x1b[")
        print_i32(region.color)
        print("m")
        print_char_code(region.marker)
        print("\x1b[0m=")
        print_char_code(region.name_code)
        print(" ")
        ri = ri + 1
    }

    if diagram.num_critical > 0 {
        print(" \x1b[1;31mC\x1b[0m=Critical")
    }
    if diagram.num_triple > 0 {
        print(" \x1b[1;31mT\x1b[0m=Triple")
    }
    print("\n")
}

// ============================================================================
// Helper: Print integer
// ============================================================================

fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }

    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        return
    }

    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10

    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }

    print_digit(digit)
}

fn print_digit(d: i32) with IO {
    if d == 0 { print("0") }
    else { if d == 1 { print("1") }
    else { if d == 2 { print("2") }
    else { if d == 3 { print("3") }
    else { if d == 4 { print("4") }
    else { if d == 5 { print("5") }
    else { if d == 6 { print("6") }
    else { if d == 7 { print("7") }
    else { if d == 8 { print("8") }
    else { if d == 9 { print("9") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}

// ============================================================================
// Example: Water Phase Diagram Classifier
// ============================================================================

// Simple water phase classifier (T in Kelvin, P in kPa)
fn water_phase_classifier(t: f64, p: f64) -> i32 {
    // Very simplified model
    // Triple point: ~273.16 K, 0.611 kPa
    // Critical point: ~647 K, 22064 kPa

    // Below triple point pressure: sublimation
    if p < 0.611 {
        if t < 273.16 {
            return 1  // Solid (ice)
        } else {
            return 3  // Gas (vapor)
        }
    }

    // Above critical point: supercritical
    if t > 647.0 {
        if p > 22064.0 {
            return 4  // Supercritical
        }
    }

    // Melting curve (solid-liquid boundary)
    // Simplified: nearly vertical at 273 K
    if t < 273.15 {
        return 1  // Solid
    }

    // Vapor pressure curve (liquid-gas boundary)
    // Clausius-Clapeyron approximation
    // ln(P/P0) = -L/R * (1/T - 1/T0)
    // Simplified exponential fit
    let vapor_pressure = 0.611 * exp_approx((t - 273.15) * 0.05)

    if p < vapor_pressure {
        return 3  // Gas
    } else {
        return 2  // Liquid
    }
}

// Simple exponential approximation
fn exp_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Taylor series: 1 + x + x^2/2 + x^3/6 + x^4/24
    if x > 10.0 {
        return 22000.0  // Cap for large values
    }
    if x < -10.0 {
        return 0.00001
    }

    let x2 = x * x
    let x3 = x2 * x
    let x4 = x3 * x

    return 1.0 + x + x2 * 0.5 + x3 * 0.1667 + x4 * 0.0417
}

// ============================================================================
// Main Demo
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Create a water phase diagram
    // T: 200-700 K, P: 0.1-25000 kPa (log scale would be better but simplified here)
    var diagram = phase_diagram_new(200.0, 700.0, 0.0, 25000.0, 50, 25)

    // Add phases
    phase_diagram_add_solid(&!diagram)
    phase_diagram_add_liquid(&!diagram)
    phase_diagram_add_gas(&!diagram)
    phase_diagram_add_supercritical(&!diagram)

    // Add special points
    phase_diagram_add_triple_point(&!diagram, 273.16, 0.611)
    phase_diagram_add_critical_point(&!diagram, 647.0, 22064.0)

    // Compute phase field
    phase_diagram_compute_field(&!diagram, water_phase_classifier)

    // Render
    phase_diagram_render(&diagram)

    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/51_bifurcation.sio ===
// 51_bifurcation.sio - Bifurcation diagram visualization
//
// Bifurcation diagrams show how the long-term behavior of a dynamical system
// changes as a control parameter is varied. Key for understanding:
// - Period-doubling cascades
// - Routes to chaos
// - Stability analysis
// - Attractors and their basins
//
// Classic example: Logistic map x_{n+1} = r * x_n * (1 - x_n)

// ============================================================================
// Bifurcation Diagram Structure
// ============================================================================

struct BifurcationDiagram {
    // Parameter range (horizontal axis)
    param_min: f64,
    param_max: f64,

    // State variable range (vertical axis)
    state_min: f64,
    state_max: f64,

    // Grid dimensions
    width: i32,
    height: i32,

    // Density field (counts hits per pixel)
    // Higher values = more frequently visited states
    density: [i32; 8192],  // Up to 128x64

    // Iteration parameters
    transient_iters: i32,   // Iterations to skip (reach attractor)
    sample_iters: i32,      // Iterations to plot

    // Maximum density for normalization
    max_density: i32
}

// ============================================================================
// Initialization
// ============================================================================

fn bifurcation_new(
    param_min: f64, param_max: f64,
    state_min: f64, state_max: f64,
    width: i32, height: i32
) -> BifurcationDiagram {
    return BifurcationDiagram {
        param_min: param_min,
        param_max: param_max,
        state_min: state_min,
        state_max: state_max,
        width: width,
        height: height,
        density: [0; 8192],
        transient_iters: 200,
        sample_iters: 100,
        max_density: 1
    }
}

fn bifurcation_set_iterations(
    diagram: &!BifurcationDiagram,
    transient: i32,
    sample: i32
) with Mut {
    diagram.transient_iters = transient
    diagram.sample_iters = sample
}

// ============================================================================
// Density Field Operations
// ============================================================================

fn density_index(diagram: &BifurcationDiagram, x: i32, y: i32) -> i32 {
    return y * diagram.width + x
}

fn density_get(diagram: &BifurcationDiagram, x: i32, y: i32) -> i32 {
    if x >= 0 {
        if x < diagram.width {
            if y >= 0 {
                if y < diagram.height {
                    let idx = density_index(diagram, x, y)
                    if idx < 8192 {
                        return diagram.density[idx]
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return 0
}

fn density_increment(diagram: &!BifurcationDiagram, x: i32, y: i32) with Mut {
    if x >= 0 {
        if x < diagram.width {
            if y >= 0 {
                if y < diagram.height {
                    let idx = density_index(diagram, x, y)
                    if idx < 8192 {
                        diagram.density[idx] = diagram.density[idx] + 1
                        if diagram.density[idx] > diagram.max_density {
                            diagram.max_density = diagram.density[idx]
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

fn density_clear(diagram: &!BifurcationDiagram) with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < 8192 {
        diagram.density[i] = 0
        i = i + 1
    }
    diagram.max_density = 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Coordinate Conversion
// ============================================================================

fn param_to_grid(diagram: &BifurcationDiagram, param: f64) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    let range = diagram.param_max - diagram.param_min
    if range <= 0.0 {
        return 0
    }
    let t = (param - diagram.param_min) / range
    let x = (t * ((diagram.width - 1) as f64)) as i32
    return x
}

fn state_to_grid(diagram: &BifurcationDiagram, state: f64) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    let range = diagram.state_max - diagram.state_min
    if range <= 0.0 {
        return 0
    }
    let t = (state - diagram.state_min) / range
    let y = (t * ((diagram.height - 1) as f64)) as i32
    return y
}

fn grid_to_param(diagram: &BifurcationDiagram, x: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let t = (x as f64) / ((diagram.width - 1) as f64)
    return diagram.param_min + t * (diagram.param_max - diagram.param_min)
}

// ============================================================================
// Map Functions
// ============================================================================

// Logistic map: x_{n+1} = r * x_n * (1 - x_n)
fn logistic_map(x: f64, r: f64) -> f64 {
    return r * x * (1.0 - x)
}

// Sine map: x_{n+1} = r * sin(pi * x)
fn sine_map(x: f64, r: f64) -> f64 {
    // Approximate sin(pi * x) using Taylor series
    let pi_x = 3.14159265 * x
    return r * sin_approx(pi_x)
}

// Tent map: x_{n+1} = r * min(x, 1-x)
fn tent_map(x: f64, r: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.5 {
        return r * x * 2.0
    } else {
        return r * (1.0 - x) * 2.0
    }
}

// Cubic map: x_{n+1} = r * x - x^3
fn cubic_map(x: f64, r: f64) -> f64 {
    return r * x - x * x * x
}

// Helper: sin approximation
fn sin_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Reduce to [0, 2*pi]
    var xx = x
    while xx > 6.28318 {
        xx = xx - 6.28318
    }
    while xx < 0.0 {
        xx = xx + 6.28318
    }

    // Taylor series around 0
    let x2 = xx * xx
    let x3 = x2 * xx
    let x5 = x3 * x2
    let x7 = x5 * x2

    return xx - x3 * 0.16667 + x5 * 0.00833 - x7 * 0.0001984
}

// ============================================================================
// Bifurcation Computation
// ============================================================================

// Compute bifurcation diagram for a generic 1D map
fn bifurcation_compute(
    diagram: &!BifurcationDiagram,
    map_fn: fn(f64, f64) -> f64,
    initial_state: f64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    density_clear(diagram)

    // For each parameter value (column)
    var px = 0
    while px < diagram.width {
        let param = grid_to_param(diagram, px)

        // Start from initial condition
        var state = initial_state

        // Skip transient
        var t = 0
        while t < diagram.transient_iters {
            state = map_fn(state, param)

            // Bound check
            if state < -1000.0 {
                state = 0.5
            }
            if state > 1000.0 {
                state = 0.5
            }

            t = t + 1
        }

        // Sample the attractor
        var s = 0
        while s < diagram.sample_iters {
            state = map_fn(state, param)

            // Bound check
            if state < -1000.0 {
                state = 0.5
            }
            if state > 1000.0 {
                state = 0.5
            }

            // Map to grid and increment
            let gy = state_to_grid(diagram, state)
            density_increment(diagram, px, gy)

            s = s + 1
        }

        px = px + 1
    }
}

// Convenience function for logistic map
fn bifurcation_compute_logistic(diagram: &!BifurcationDiagram) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    bifurcation_compute(diagram, logistic_map, 0.5)
}

// ============================================================================
// Rendering
// ============================================================================

fn density_to_char(density: i32, max_density: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if density == 0 {
        return 32  // Space
    }

    // Normalize to 0-7 scale
    let ratio = (density * 8) / (max_density + 1)

    if ratio == 0 { return 46 }       // '.'
    else { if ratio == 1 { return 58 }  // ':'
    else { if ratio == 2 { return 43 }  // '+'
    else { if ratio == 3 { return 42 }  // '*'
    else { if ratio == 4 { return 35 }  // '#'
    else { if ratio == 5 { return 37 }  // '%'
    else { if ratio == 6 { return 64 }  // '@'
    else { return 64 }  // '@'
    }}}}}}}
}

fn density_to_color(density: i32, max_density: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if density == 0 {
        return 30  // Black
    }

    let ratio = (density * 6) / (max_density + 1)

    if ratio == 0 { return 34 }       // Blue
    else { if ratio == 1 { return 36 }  // Cyan
    else { if ratio == 2 { return 32 }  // Green
    else { if ratio == 3 { return 33 }  // Yellow
    else { if ratio == 4 { return 31 }  // Red
    else { return 35 }  // Magenta
    }}}}}
}

fn bifurcation_render(diagram: &BifurcationDiagram) with IO, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")

    print("\x1b[1m=== Bifurcation Diagram ===\x1b[0m\n\n")

    // State axis label
    print("  x\n")
    print("  ^\n")

    // Render from top to bottom
    var y = diagram.height - 1
    while y >= 0 {
        print("  |")

        var x = 0
        while x < diagram.width {
            let d = density_get(diagram, x, y)
            let ch = density_to_char(d, diagram.max_density)
            let color = density_to_color(d, diagram.max_density)

            print("\x1b[")
            print_i32(color)
            print("m")
            print_char_code(ch)
            print("\x1b[0m")

            x = x + 1
        }

        print("\n")
        y = y - 1
    }

    // X-axis
    print("  +")
    var xi = 0
    while xi < diagram.width {
        print("-")
        xi = xi + 1
    }
    print("> r\n\n")

    // Parameter range
    print("  r: ")
    print_f64(diagram.param_min)
    print(" to ")
    print_f64(diagram.param_max)
    print("\n")

    // State range
    print("  x: ")
    print_f64(diagram.state_min)
    print(" to ")
    print_f64(diagram.state_max)
    print("\n")
}

// ============================================================================
// Helper Functions
// ============================================================================

fn print_char_code(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 32 { print(" ") }
    else { if code == 35 { print("#") }
    else { if code == 37 { print("%") }
    else { if code == 42 { print("*") }
    else { if code == 43 { print("+") }
    else { if code == 46 { print(".") }
    else { if code == 58 { print(":") }
    else { if code == 64 { print("@") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}
}

fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }
    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 { return }
    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10
    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }
    print_digit(digit)
}

fn print_digit(d: i32) with IO {
    if d == 0 { print("0") }
    else { if d == 1 { print("1") }
    else { if d == 2 { print("2") }
    else { if d == 3 { print("3") }
    else { if d == 4 { print("4") }
    else { if d == 5 { print("5") }
    else { if d == 6 { print("6") }
    else { if d == 7 { print("7") }
    else { if d == 8 { print("8") }
    else { if d == 9 { print("9") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}

fn print_f64(x: f64) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 {
        print("-")
        let x = 0.0 - x
    }

    let int_part = x as i32
    print_i32(int_part)
    print(".")

    let frac = x - (int_part as f64)
    let frac_scaled = (frac * 100.0) as i32
    if frac_scaled < 10 {
        print("0")
    }
    print_i32_unsigned(frac_scaled)
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Create bifurcation diagram for logistic map
    // r ranges from 2.5 to 4.0 (period-doubling region)
    // x ranges from 0 to 1
    var diagram = bifurcation_new(2.5, 4.0, 0.0, 1.0, 80, 30)

    // Set iteration parameters
    bifurcation_set_iterations(&!diagram, 500, 200)

    // Compute the diagram
    print("Computing bifurcation diagram...\n")
    bifurcation_compute_logistic(&!diagram)

    // Render
    bifurcation_render(&diagram)

    print("\nLogistic map: x_{n+1} = r * x_n * (1 - x_n)\n")
    print("Shows period-doubling route to chaos as r increases\n")

    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/52_poincare.sio ===
// 52_poincare.sio - Poincaré section visualization
//
// A Poincaré section reduces a continuous-time dynamical system to a discrete
// map by recording where trajectories cross a chosen surface (section).
// Essential for analyzing:
// - Periodic orbits (appear as fixed points)
// - Quasiperiodic motion (appears as curves)
// - Chaos (appears as scattered points with structure)
//
// This module supports 3D systems with a z=const section plane.

// ============================================================================
// Poincaré Section Structure
// ============================================================================

struct PoincareSection {
    // Section plane: z = section_z (crossing from below)
    section_z: f64,
    crossing_direction: i32,  // 1 = upward, -1 = downward, 0 = both

    // View bounds (x, y coordinates on the section)
    x_min: f64,
    x_max: f64,
    y_min: f64,
    y_max: f64,

    // Display grid
    width: i32,
    height: i32,

    // Points storage (up to 2000 crossing points)
    points_x: [f64; 2000],
    points_y: [f64; 2000],
    num_points: i32,

    // Density grid for visualization
    density: [i32; 4096],
    max_density: i32,

    // Integration parameters
    dt: f64,
    max_time: f64
}

// ============================================================================
// State Vector for 3D Systems
// ============================================================================

struct State3D {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64
}

fn state3d_new(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> State3D {
    return State3D { x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

// ============================================================================
// Initialization
// ============================================================================

fn poincare_new(
    section_z: f64,
    x_min: f64, x_max: f64,
    y_min: f64, y_max: f64,
    width: i32, height: i32
) -> PoincareSection {
    return PoincareSection {
        section_z: section_z,
        crossing_direction: 1,  // Default: upward crossings
        x_min: x_min,
        x_max: x_max,
        y_min: y_min,
        y_max: y_max,
        width: width,
        height: height,
        points_x: [0.0; 2000],
        points_y: [0.0; 2000],
        num_points: 0,
        density: [0; 4096],
        max_density: 1,
        dt: 0.01,
        max_time: 1000.0
    }
}

fn poincare_set_integration(
    section: &!PoincareSection,
    dt: f64,
    max_time: f64
) with Mut {
    section.dt = dt
    section.max_time = max_time
}

fn poincare_set_direction(section: &!PoincareSection, direction: i32) with Mut {
    section.crossing_direction = direction
}

fn poincare_clear(section: &!PoincareSection) with Mut {
    section.num_points = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < 4096 {
        section.density[i] = 0
        i = i + 1
    }
    section.max_density = 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Coordinate Mapping
// ============================================================================

fn x_to_grid(section: &PoincareSection, x: f64) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    let range = section.x_max - section.x_min
    if range <= 0.0 { return 0 }
    let t = (x - section.x_min) / range
    return (t * ((section.width - 1) as f64)) as i32
}

fn y_to_grid(section: &PoincareSection, y: f64) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    let range = section.y_max - section.y_min
    if range <= 0.0 { return 0 }
    let t = (y - section.y_min) / range
    return (t * ((section.height - 1) as f64)) as i32
}

// ============================================================================
// Point Recording
// ============================================================================

fn record_crossing(
    section: &!PoincareSection,
    x: f64,
    y: f64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Store point
    if section.num_points < 2000 {
        section.points_x[section.num_points] = x
        section.points_y[section.num_points] = y
        section.num_points = section.num_points + 1
    }

    // Update density grid
    let gx = x_to_grid(section, x)
    let gy = y_to_grid(section, y)

    if gx >= 0 {
        if gx < section.width {
            if gy >= 0 {
                if gy < section.height {
                    let idx = gy * section.width + gx
                    if idx < 4096 {
                        section.density[idx] = section.density[idx] + 1
                        if section.density[idx] > section.max_density {
                            section.max_density = section.density[idx]
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ODE Integration (RK4)
// ============================================================================

fn rk4_step(
    state: State3D,
    dt: f64,
    deriv_fn: fn(State3D) -> State3D
) -> State3D {
    let k1 = deriv_fn(state)

    let s2 = State3D {
        x: state.x + k1.x * dt * 0.5,
        y: state.y + k1.y * dt * 0.5,
        z: state.z + k1.z * dt * 0.5
    }
    let k2 = deriv_fn(s2)

    let s3 = State3D {
        x: state.x + k2.x * dt * 0.5,
        y: state.y + k2.y * dt * 0.5,
        z: state.z + k2.z * dt * 0.5
    }
    let k3 = deriv_fn(s3)

    let s4 = State3D {
        x: state.x + k3.x * dt,
        y: state.y + k3.y * dt,
        z: state.z + k3.z * dt
    }
    let k4 = deriv_fn(s4)

    return State3D {
        x: state.x + (k1.x + 2.0 * k2.x + 2.0 * k3.x + k4.x) * dt / 6.0,
        y: state.y + (k1.y + 2.0 * k2.y + 2.0 * k3.y + k4.y) * dt / 6.0,
        z: state.z + (k1.z + 2.0 * k2.z + 2.0 * k3.z + k4.z) * dt / 6.0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Section Computation
// ============================================================================

fn poincare_compute(
    section: &!PoincareSection,
    initial: State3D,
    deriv_fn: fn(State3D) -> State3D
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = initial
    var prev_state = state
    var t = 0.0
    let dt = section.dt
    let max_t = section.max_time

    // Skip initial transient (first 10% of time)
    let transient_time = max_t * 0.1
    while t < transient_time {
        prev_state = state
        state = rk4_step(state, dt, deriv_fn)
        t = t + dt
    }

    // Record crossings
    while t < max_t {
        prev_state = state
        state = rk4_step(state, dt, deriv_fn)

        // Check for crossing
        let crossed = check_crossing(section, prev_state.z, state.z)

        if crossed == 1 {
            // Linear interpolation to find crossing point
            let dz = state.z - prev_state.z
            if dz != 0.0 {
                let alpha = (section.section_z - prev_state.z) / dz
                let cross_x = prev_state.x + alpha * (state.x - prev_state.x)
                let cross_y = prev_state.y + alpha * (state.y - prev_state.y)
                record_crossing(section, cross_x, cross_y)
            }
        }

        t = t + dt
    }
}

fn check_crossing(section: &PoincareSection, z_prev: f64, z_curr: f64) -> i32 {
    let z_sec = section.section_z
    let dir = section.crossing_direction

    // Upward crossing
    if dir >= 0 {
        if z_prev < z_sec {
            if z_curr >= z_sec {
                return 1
            }
        }
    }

    // Downward crossing
    if dir <= 0 {
        if z_prev > z_sec {
            if z_curr <= z_sec {
                return 1
            }
        }
    }

    return 0
}

// ============================================================================
// Example Systems
// ============================================================================

// Lorenz system: classic chaotic attractor
// Parameters: sigma=10, rho=28, beta=8/3
fn lorenz_deriv(s: State3D) -> State3D {
    let sigma = 10.0
    let rho = 28.0
    let beta = 2.667

    return State3D {
        x: sigma * (s.y - s.x),
        y: s.x * (rho - s.z) - s.y,
        z: s.x * s.y - beta * s.z
    }
}

// Rössler system: simpler chaotic attractor
// Parameters: a=0.2, b=0.2, c=5.7
fn rossler_deriv(s: State3D) -> State3D {
    let a = 0.2
    let b = 0.2
    let c = 5.7

    return State3D {
        x: 0.0 - s.y - s.z,
        y: s.x + a * s.y,
        z: b + s.z * (s.x - c)
    }
}

// Driven damped pendulum (in 3D: theta, omega, time)
// theta' = omega
// omega' = -gamma*omega - sin(theta) + A*cos(omega_d * t)
fn driven_pendulum_deriv(s: State3D) -> State3D {
    let gamma = 0.1    // Damping
    let A = 1.5        // Driving amplitude
    let omega_d = 0.67 // Driving frequency

    let theta = s.x
    let omega = s.y
    let t = s.z

    return State3D {
        x: omega,
        y: 0.0 - gamma * omega - sin_approx(theta) + A * cos_approx(omega_d * t),
        z: 1.0  // dt/dt = 1
    }
}

fn sin_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var xx = x
    while xx > 3.14159 { xx = xx - 6.28318 }
    while xx < -3.14159 { xx = xx + 6.28318 }
    let x2 = xx * xx
    let x3 = x2 * xx
    let x5 = x3 * x2
    return xx - x3 * 0.16667 + x5 * 0.00833
}

fn cos_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return sin_approx(x + 1.5708)
}

// ============================================================================
// Rendering
// ============================================================================

fn density_to_char(d: i32, max_d: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if d == 0 { return 32 }
    let ratio = (d * 5) / (max_d + 1)
    if ratio == 0 { return 46 }      // '.'
    else { if ratio == 1 { return 43 }  // '+'
    else { if ratio == 2 { return 42 }  // '*'
    else { if ratio == 3 { return 35 }  // '#'
    else { return 64 }}}}}               // '@'
}

fn density_to_color(d: i32, max_d: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if d == 0 { return 30 }
    let ratio = (d * 5) / (max_d + 1)
    if ratio == 0 { return 34 }      // Blue
    else { if ratio == 1 { return 36 }  // Cyan
    else { if ratio == 2 { return 32 }  // Green
    else { if ratio == 3 { return 33 }  // Yellow
    else { return 31 }}}}}               // Red
}

fn poincare_render(section: &PoincareSection) with IO, Div, Panic {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")

    print("\x1b[1m=== Poincare Section ===\x1b[0m\n")
    print("z = ")
    print_f64(section.section_z)
    print(", points: ")
    print_i32(section.num_points)
    print("\n\n")

    // Y-axis label
    print("  y\n")
    print("  ^\n")

    // Render from top to bottom
    var y = section.height - 1
    while y >= 0 {
        print("  |")

        var x = 0
        while x < section.width {
            let idx = y * section.width + x
            var d = 0
            if idx < 4096 {
                d = section.density[idx]
            }

            let ch = density_to_char(d, section.max_density)
            let color = density_to_color(d, section.max_density)

            print("\x1b[")
            print_i32(color)
            print("m")
            print_char_code(ch)
            print("\x1b[0m")

            x = x + 1
        }

        print("\n")
        y = y - 1
    }

    // X-axis
    print("  +")
    var xi = 0
    while xi < section.width {
        print("-")
        xi = xi + 1
    }
    print("> x\n\n")

    // Bounds info
    print("  x: [")
    print_f64(section.x_min)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(section.x_max)
    print("]  y: [")
    print_f64(section.y_min)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(section.y_max)
    print("]\n")
}

// ============================================================================
// Helper Functions
