//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 076: Longest Palindromic Substring
//
// Find the longest palindromic substring using expand-around-center approach.
// For each position, try expanding outward while characters match.
// Check both odd-length (single center) and even-length (double center)
// palindromes. Returns the start index and length of the longest palindrome.
// Input is a byte array with its length.

struct PalinResult { start: i64, length: i64 }

fn expand(arr: [i64; 256], n: i64, left: i64, right: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var lo = left
    var hi = right
    while lo >= 0 && hi < n && arr[lo] == arr[hi] {
        lo = lo - 1
        hi = hi + 1
    }
    // length = hi - lo - 1
    hi - lo - 1
}

fn longest_palindrome(arr: [i64; 256], n: i64) -> PalinResult with Mut, Panic {
    if n == 0 { return PalinResult { start: 0, length: 0 } }

    var best_start: i64 = 0
    var best_len: i64 = 1

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        // Odd-length palindrome centered at i
        let odd_len = expand(arr, n, i, i)
        if odd_len > best_len {
            best_len = odd_len
            best_start = i - (odd_len - 1) / 2
        }

        // Even-length palindrome centered between i and i+1
        if i + 1 < n {
            let even_len = expand(arr, n, i, i + 1)
            if even_len > best_len {
                best_len = even_len
                best_start = i - (even_len - 2) / 2
            }
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    PalinResult { start: best_start, length: best_len }
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: "babad" -> "bab" or "aba" (length 3)
    // b=98, a=97, b=98, a=97, d=100
    var a1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a1[0] = 98
    a1[1] = 97
    a1[2] = 98
    a1[3] = 97
    a1[4] = 100
    let r1 = longest_palindrome(a1, 5)
    assert(r1.length == 3)

    // Test 2: "cbbd" -> "bb" (length 2)
    // c=99, b=98, b=98, d=100
    var a2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a2[0] = 99
    a2[1] = 98
    a2[2] = 98
    a2[3] = 100
    let r2 = longest_palindrome(a2, 4)
    assert(r2.length == 2)
    assert(r2.start == 1)

    // Test 3: "a" -> "a" (length 1)
    var a3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a3[0] = 97
    let r3 = longest_palindrome(a3, 1)
    assert(r3.length == 1)
    assert(r3.start == 0)

    // Test 4: "racecar" -> "racecar" (length 7)
    // r=114, a=97, c=99, e=101, c=99, a=97, r=114
    var a4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a4[0] = 114
    a4[1] = 97
    a4[2] = 99
    a4[3] = 101
    a4[4] = 99
    a4[5] = 97
    a4[6] = 114
    let r4 = longest_palindrome(a4, 7)
    assert(r4.length == 7)
    assert(r4.start == 0)

    // Test 5: "abcba" -> "abcba" (length 5)
    var a5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a5[0] = 97
    a5[1] = 98
    a5[2] = 99
    a5[3] = 98
    a5[4] = 97
    let r5 = longest_palindrome(a5, 5)
    assert(r5.length == 5)
    assert(r5.start == 0)

    // Test 6: "abcd" -> any single char (length 1)
    var a6: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a6[0] = 97
    a6[1] = 98
    a6[2] = 99
    a6[3] = 100
    let r6 = longest_palindrome(a6, 4)
    assert(r6.length == 1)

    // Test 7: empty -> length 0
    var a7: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    let r7 = longest_palindrome(a7, 0)
    assert(r7.length == 0)

    println("076_longest_palindrome_substring: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/077_count_and_say.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 077: Count and Say
//
// Generate the nth term of the count-and-say sequence.
// Term 1: "1" -> [1]
// Term 2: "11" (one 1) -> [1, 1]
// Term 3: "21" (two 1s) -> [2, 1]
// Term 4: "1211" (one 2, one 1) -> [1, 2, 1, 1]
// Term 5: "111221" (one 1, one 2, two 1s) -> [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1]
// Operates on digit arrays (values 1-9, not ASCII).

struct Seq { data: [i64; 1024] }

fn count_and_say(n: i64, out: &!Seq) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    // Start with [1]
    var curr = Seq { data: [0; 1024] }
    curr.data[0] = 1
    var curr_len: i64 = 1

    var step: i64 = 1
    while step < n {
        var next = Seq { data: [0; 1024] }
        var next_len: i64 = 0

        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < curr_len {
            let digit = curr.data[i]
            var count: i64 = 1
            while i + count < curr_len && curr.data[i + count] == digit {
                count = count + 1
            }
            // Append count, then digit
            next.data[next_len] = count
            next_len = next_len + 1
            next.data[next_len] = digit
            next_len = next_len + 1
            i = i + count
        }

        // Copy next to curr
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < next_len {
            curr.data[k] = next.data[k]
            k = k + 1
        }
        curr_len = next_len
        step = step + 1
    }

    // Copy result to output
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < curr_len {
        out.data[j] = curr.data[j]
        j = j + 1
    }
    curr_len
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: n=1 -> [1]
    var out1 = Seq { data: [0; 1024] }
    let len1 = count_and_say(1, &!out1)
    assert(len1 == 1)
    assert(out1.data[0] == 1)

    // Test 2: n=2 -> [1, 1] (one 1)
    var out2 = Seq { data: [0; 1024] }
    let len2 = count_and_say(2, &!out2)
    assert(len2 == 2)
    assert(out2.data[0] == 1)
    assert(out2.data[1] == 1)

    // Test 3: n=3 -> [2, 1] (two 1s)
    var out3 = Seq { data: [0; 1024] }
    let len3 = count_and_say(3, &!out3)
    assert(len3 == 2)
    assert(out3.data[0] == 2)
    assert(out3.data[1] == 1)

    // Test 4: n=4 -> [1, 2, 1, 1] (one 2, one 1)
    var out4 = Seq { data: [0; 1024] }
    let len4 = count_and_say(4, &!out4)
    assert(len4 == 4)
    assert(out4.data[0] == 1)
    assert(out4.data[1] == 2)
    assert(out4.data[2] == 1)
    assert(out4.data[3] == 1)

    // Test 5: n=5 -> [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1]
    var out5 = Seq { data: [0; 1024] }
    let len5 = count_and_say(5, &!out5)
    assert(len5 == 6)
    assert(out5.data[0] == 1)
    assert(out5.data[1] == 1)
    assert(out5.data[2] == 1)
    assert(out5.data[3] == 2)
    assert(out5.data[4] == 2)
    assert(out5.data[5] == 1)

    // Test 6: n=6 -> [3, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1] (three 1s, two 2s, one 1)
    var out6 = Seq { data: [0; 1024] }
    let len6 = count_and_say(6, &!out6)
    assert(len6 == 6)
    assert(out6.data[0] == 3)
    assert(out6.data[1] == 1)
    assert(out6.data[2] == 2)
    assert(out6.data[3] == 2)
    assert(out6.data[4] == 1)
    assert(out6.data[5] == 1)

    println("077_count_and_say: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/078_spiral_order.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 078: Spiral Order
//
// Read a matrix (rows x cols, stored flat row-major) in spiral order
// into an output array. Traversal: right along top, down right side,
// left along bottom, up left side, then shrink boundaries and repeat.

struct Matrix { data: [i64; 256] }
struct Output { data: [i64; 256] }

fn spiral_order(mat: [i64; 256], rows: i64, cols: i64, out: &!Output) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    if rows == 0 || cols == 0 { return 0 }

    var top: i64 = 0
    var bottom: i64 = rows - 1
    var left: i64 = 0
    var right: i64 = cols - 1
    var idx: i64 = 0

    while top <= bottom && left <= right {
        // Right across top row
        var c = left
        while c <= right {
            out.data[idx] = mat[top * cols + c]
            idx = idx + 1
            c = c + 1
        }
        top = top + 1

        // Down right column
        var r = top
        while r <= bottom {
            out.data[idx] = mat[r * cols + right]
            idx = idx + 1
            r = r + 1
        }
        right = right - 1

        // Left across bottom row
        if top <= bottom {
            var c2 = right
            while c2 >= left {
                out.data[idx] = mat[bottom * cols + c2]
                idx = idx + 1
                c2 = c2 - 1
            }
            bottom = bottom - 1
        }

        // Up left column
        if left <= right {
            var r2 = bottom
            while r2 >= top {
                out.data[idx] = mat[r2 * cols + left]
                idx = idx + 1
                r2 = r2 - 1
            }
            left = left + 1
        }
    }

    idx
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: 3x3 matrix
    // [1, 2, 3]
    // [4, 5, 6]
    // [7, 8, 9]
    // Spiral: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 8, 7, 4, 5
    var m1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    m1[0] = 1
    m1[1] = 2
    m1[2] = 3
    m1[3] = 4
    m1[4] = 5
    m1[5] = 6
    m1[6] = 7
    m1[7] = 8
    m1[8] = 9
    var o1 = Output { data: [0; 256] }
    let n1 = spiral_order(m1, 3, 3, &!o1)
    assert(n1 == 9)
    assert(o1.data[0] == 1)
    assert(o1.data[1] == 2)
    assert(o1.data[2] == 3)
    assert(o1.data[3] == 6)
    assert(o1.data[4] == 9)
    assert(o1.data[5] == 8)
    assert(o1.data[6] == 7)
    assert(o1.data[7] == 4)
    assert(o1.data[8] == 5)

    // Test 2: 2x3 matrix
    // [1, 2, 3]
    // [4, 5, 6]
    // Spiral: 1, 2, 3, 6, 5, 4
    var m2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    m2[0] = 1
    m2[1] = 2
    m2[2] = 3
    m2[3] = 4
    m2[4] = 5
    m2[5] = 6
    var o2 = Output { data: [0; 256] }
    let n2 = spiral_order(m2, 2, 3, &!o2)
    assert(n2 == 6)
    assert(o2.data[0] == 1)
    assert(o2.data[1] == 2)
    assert(o2.data[2] == 3)
    assert(o2.data[3] == 6)
    assert(o2.data[4] == 5)
    assert(o2.data[5] == 4)

    // Test 3: 1x4 row vector
    // [1, 2, 3, 4]
    var m3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    m3[0] = 1
    m3[1] = 2
    m3[2] = 3
    m3[3] = 4
    var o3 = Output { data: [0; 256] }
    let n3 = spiral_order(m3, 1, 4, &!o3)
    assert(n3 == 4)
    assert(o3.data[0] == 1)
    assert(o3.data[1] == 2)
    assert(o3.data[2] == 3)
    assert(o3.data[3] == 4)

    // Test 4: 4x1 column vector
    // [1], [2], [3], [4]
    var m4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    m4[0] = 1
    m4[1] = 2
    m4[2] = 3
    m4[3] = 4
    var o4 = Output { data: [0; 256] }
    let n4 = spiral_order(m4, 4, 1, &!o4)
    assert(n4 == 4)
    assert(o4.data[0] == 1)
    assert(o4.data[1] == 2)
    assert(o4.data[2] == 3)
    assert(o4.data[3] == 4)

    // Test 5: 1x1
    var m5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    m5[0] = 42
    var o5 = Output { data: [0; 256] }
    let n5 = spiral_order(m5, 1, 1, &!o5)
    assert(n5 == 1)
    assert(o5.data[0] == 42)

    println("078_spiral_order: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/079_set_matrix_zeroes.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 079: Set Matrix Zeroes
//
// Given an MxN matrix (flat row-major), if an element is 0, set its entire
// row and column to 0. Uses O(M+N) extra space: two marker arrays to record
// which rows and columns need zeroing.

struct Matrix { data: [i64; 256] }
struct Markers { data: [i64; 16] }

fn set_zeroes(mat: &!Matrix, rows: i64, cols: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    // Mark which rows and columns contain a zero
    var zero_row = Markers { data: [0; 16] }
    var zero_col = Markers { data: [0; 16] }

    var r: i64 = 0
    while r < rows {
        var c: i64 = 0
        while c < cols {
            if mat.data[r * cols + c] == 0 {
                zero_row.data[r] = 1
                zero_col.data[c] = 1
            }
            c = c + 1
        }
        r = r + 1
    }

    // Zero out marked rows and columns
    var r2: i64 = 0
    while r2 < rows {
        var c2: i64 = 0
        while c2 < cols {
            if zero_row.data[r2] == 1 || zero_col.data[c2] == 1 {
                mat.data[r2 * cols + c2] = 0
            }
            c2 = c2 + 1
        }
        r2 = r2 + 1
    }
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: 3x3 with one zero
    // [1, 1, 1]    [1, 0, 1]
    // [1, 0, 1] -> [0, 0, 0]
    // [1, 1, 1]    [1, 0, 1]
    var m1 = Matrix { data: [0; 256] }
    m1.data[0] = 1
    m1.data[1] = 1
    m1.data[2] = 1
    m1.data[3] = 1
    m1.data[4] = 0
    m1.data[5] = 1
    m1.data[6] = 1
    m1.data[7] = 1
    m1.data[8] = 1
    set_zeroes(&!m1, 3, 3)
    assert(m1.data[0] == 1)
    assert(m1.data[1] == 0)
    assert(m1.data[2] == 1)
    assert(m1.data[3] == 0)
    assert(m1.data[4] == 0)
    assert(m1.data[5] == 0)
    assert(m1.data[6] == 1)
    assert(m1.data[7] == 0)
    assert(m1.data[8] == 1)

    // Test 2: 3x4 with two zeroes
    // [0, 1, 2, 0]    [0, 0, 0, 0]
    // [3, 4, 5, 2] -> [0, 4, 5, 0]
    // [1, 3, 1, 5]    [0, 3, 1, 0]
    var m2 = Matrix { data: [0; 256] }
    m2.data[0] = 0
    m2.data[1] = 1
    m2.data[2] = 2
    m2.data[3] = 0
    m2.data[4] = 3
    m2.data[5] = 4
    m2.data[6] = 5
    m2.data[7] = 2
    m2.data[8] = 1
    m2.data[9] = 3
    m2.data[10] = 1
    m2.data[11] = 5
    set_zeroes(&!m2, 3, 4)
    assert(m2.data[0] == 0)
    assert(m2.data[1] == 0)
    assert(m2.data[2] == 0)
    assert(m2.data[3] == 0)
    assert(m2.data[4] == 0)
    assert(m2.data[5] == 4)
    assert(m2.data[6] == 5)
    assert(m2.data[7] == 0)
    assert(m2.data[8] == 0)
    assert(m2.data[9] == 3)
    assert(m2.data[10] == 1)
    assert(m2.data[11] == 0)

    // Test 3: no zeroes -> unchanged
    var m3 = Matrix { data: [0; 256] }
    m3.data[0] = 1
    m3.data[1] = 2
    m3.data[2] = 3
    m3.data[3] = 4
    set_zeroes(&!m3, 2, 2)
    assert(m3.data[0] == 1)
    assert(m3.data[1] == 2)
    assert(m3.data[2] == 3)
    assert(m3.data[3] == 4)

    // Test 4: all zeroes -> all zeroes
    var m4 = Matrix { data: [0; 256] }
    set_zeroes(&!m4, 2, 2)
    assert(m4.data[0] == 0)
    assert(m4.data[1] == 0)
    assert(m4.data[2] == 0)
    assert(m4.data[3] == 0)

    println("079_set_matrix_zeroes: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/080_search_rotated.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 080: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
//
// Search for a target in a sorted array that has been rotated at some pivot.
// For example, [4,5,6,7,0,1,2] is [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] rotated at pivot 4.
// Uses modified binary search in O(log n). Returns the index or -1 if not found.

fn search_rotated(arr: [i64; 256], n: i64, target: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var lo: i64 = 0
    var hi: i64 = n - 1

    while lo <= hi {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
        if arr[mid] == target {
            return mid
        }

        // Determine which half is sorted
        if arr[lo] <= arr[mid] {
            // Left half is sorted
            if target >= arr[lo] && target < arr[mid] {
                hi = mid - 1
            } else {
                lo = mid + 1
            }
        } else {
            // Right half is sorted
            if target > arr[mid] && target <= arr[hi] {
                lo = mid + 1
            } else {
                hi = mid - 1
            }
        }
    }

    0 - 1
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: [4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2], target=0 -> index 4
    var a1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a1[0] = 4
    a1[1] = 5
    a1[2] = 6
    a1[3] = 7
    a1[4] = 0
    a1[5] = 1
    a1[6] = 2
    assert(search_rotated(a1, 7, 0) == 4)

    // Test 2: [4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2], target=3 -> -1
    assert(search_rotated(a1, 7, 3) == 0 - 1)

    // Test 3: [4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2], target=5 -> 1
    assert(search_rotated(a1, 7, 5) == 1)

    // Test 4: not rotated [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], target=3 -> 2
    var a4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a4[0] = 1
    a4[1] = 2
    a4[2] = 3
    a4[3] = 4
    a4[4] = 5
    assert(search_rotated(a4, 5, 3) == 2)

    // Test 5: single element [1], target=1 -> 0
    var a5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a5[0] = 1
    assert(search_rotated(a5, 1, 1) == 0)

    // Test 6: single element [1], target=0 -> -1
    assert(search_rotated(a5, 1, 0) == 0 - 1)

    // Test 7: [2, 1], target=1 -> 1
    var a7: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a7[0] = 2
    a7[1] = 1
    assert(search_rotated(a7, 2, 1) == 1)

    // Test 8: find first element
    assert(search_rotated(a1, 7, 4) == 0)

    // Test 9: find last element
    assert(search_rotated(a1, 7, 2) == 6)

    println("080_search_rotated: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/081_find_peak.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 081: Find Peak Element
//
// A peak element is one that is strictly greater than its neighbors.
// arr[-1] and arr[n] are treated as negative infinity.
// Uses binary search: if arr[mid] < arr[mid+1], peak is to the right;
// otherwise peak is to the left (including mid). O(log n).
// Returns any valid peak index.

fn find_peak(arr: [i64; 256], n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    if n == 1 { return 0 }

    // Check edges first
    if arr[0] > arr[1] { return 0 }
    if arr[n - 1] > arr[n - 2] { return n - 1 }

    var lo: i64 = 1
    var hi: i64 = n - 2

    while lo <= hi {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
        if arr[mid] > arr[mid - 1] && arr[mid] > arr[mid + 1] {
            return mid
        }
        if arr[mid] < arr[mid + 1] {
            lo = mid + 1
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1
        }
    }

    lo
}

fn is_peak(arr: [i64; 256], n: i64, idx: i64) -> i64 with Panic {
    // Check that idx is a valid peak
    let left_ok = if idx == 0 { 1 } else { if arr[idx] > arr[idx - 1] { 1 } else { 0 } }
    let right_ok = if idx == n - 1 { 1 } else { if arr[idx] > arr[idx + 1] { 1 } else { 0 } }
    if left_ok == 1 && right_ok == 1 { 1 } else { 0 }
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: [1, 2, 3, 1] -> peak at 2 (value 3)
    var a1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a1[0] = 1
    a1[1] = 2
    a1[2] = 3
    a1[3] = 1
    let p1 = find_peak(a1, 4)
    assert(is_peak(a1, 4, p1) == 1)

    // Test 2: [1, 2, 1, 3, 5, 6, 4] -> peak at 1 or 5
    var a2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a2[0] = 1
    a2[1] = 2
    a2[2] = 1
    a2[3] = 3
    a2[4] = 5
    a2[5] = 6
    a2[6] = 4
    let p2 = find_peak(a2, 7)
    assert(is_peak(a2, 7, p2) == 1)

    // Test 3: strictly increasing [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] -> peak at 4
    var a3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a3[0] = 1
    a3[1] = 2
    a3[2] = 3
    a3[3] = 4
    a3[4] = 5
    let p3 = find_peak(a3, 5)
    assert(is_peak(a3, 5, p3) == 1)

    // Test 4: strictly decreasing [5, 4, 3, 2, 1] -> peak at 0
    var a4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a4[0] = 5
    a4[1] = 4
    a4[2] = 3
    a4[3] = 2
    a4[4] = 1
    let p4 = find_peak(a4, 5)
    assert(is_peak(a4, 5, p4) == 1)

    // Test 5: single element [42] -> peak at 0
    var a5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a5[0] = 42
    let p5 = find_peak(a5, 1)
    assert(p5 == 0)

    // Test 6: two elements [1, 2] -> peak at 1
    var a6: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a6[0] = 1
    a6[1] = 2
    let p6 = find_peak(a6, 2)
    assert(is_peak(a6, 2, p6) == 1)

    println("081_find_peak: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/082_sqrt_int.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 082: Integer Square Root
//
// Compute floor(sqrt(x)) for non-negative integer x using binary search.
// Find the largest integer r such that r*r <= x. O(log x).

fn isqrt(x: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 1 { return x }

    var lo: i64 = 1
    var hi: i64 = x
    // Clamp hi to avoid overflow: sqrt(x) <= 46340 for 32-bit,
    // but we use i64 so clamp to x/2+1 for safety
    if hi > x / 2 + 1 {
        hi = x / 2 + 1
    }

    var result: i64 = 1
    while lo <= hi {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
        if mid <= x / mid {
            // mid*mid <= x (using division to avoid overflow)
            result = mid
            lo = mid + 1
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1
        }
    }

    result
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: sqrt(0) = 0
    assert(isqrt(0) == 0)

    // Test 2: sqrt(1) = 1
    assert(isqrt(1) == 1)

    // Test 3: sqrt(4) = 2
    assert(isqrt(4) == 2)

    // Test 4: sqrt(8) = 2 (floor)
    assert(isqrt(8) == 2)

    // Test 5: sqrt(9) = 3
    assert(isqrt(9) == 3)

    // Test 6: sqrt(16) = 4
    assert(isqrt(16) == 4)

    // Test 7: sqrt(100) = 10
    assert(isqrt(100) == 10)

    // Test 8: sqrt(99) = 9
    assert(isqrt(99) == 9)

    // Test 9: sqrt(101) = 10
    assert(isqrt(101) == 10)

    // Test 10: sqrt(10000) = 100
    assert(isqrt(10000) == 100)

    // Test 11: sqrt(2) = 1
    assert(isqrt(2) == 1)

    // Test 12: sqrt(3) = 1
    assert(isqrt(3) == 1)

    // Test 13: sqrt(25) = 5
    assert(isqrt(25) == 5)

    // Test 14: sqrt(1000000) = 1000
    assert(isqrt(1000000) == 1000)

    println("082_sqrt_int: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/083_pow_double.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 083: Power (Floating Point)
//
// Compute x^n for f64 base and i64 exponent using fast exponentiation
// (exponentiation by squaring). Handles negative exponents via 1/(x^|n|).
// O(log |n|) multiplications.

fn abs_i64(x: i64) -> i64 {
    if x < 0 { 0 - x } else { x }
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn pow_double(x: f64, n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 { return 1.0 }

    var base = x
    var exp = abs_i64(n)
    var result: f64 = 1.0

    while exp > 0 {
        if exp % 2 == 1 {
            result = result * base
        }
        base = base * base
        exp = exp / 2
    }

    if n < 0 {
        1.0 / result
    } else {
        result
    }
}

fn near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> i64 {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    if ad < tol { 1 } else { 0 }
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: 2.0^10 = 1024.0
    assert(near(pow_double(2.0, 10), 1024.0, 0.001) == 1)

    // Test 2: 2.0^0 = 1.0
    assert(near(pow_double(2.0, 0), 1.0, 0.001) == 1)

    // Test 3: 2.0^(-2) = 0.25
    assert(near(pow_double(2.0, 0 - 2), 0.25, 0.001) == 1)

    // Test 4: 3.0^3 = 27.0
    assert(near(pow_double(3.0, 3), 27.0, 0.001) == 1)

    // Test 5: 0.5^3 = 0.125
    assert(near(pow_double(0.5, 3), 0.125, 0.001) == 1)

    // Test 6: 1.0^1000 = 1.0
    assert(near(pow_double(1.0, 1000), 1.0, 0.001) == 1)

    // Test 7: 10.0^(-1) = 0.1
    assert(near(pow_double(10.0, 0 - 1), 0.1, 0.001) == 1)

    // Test 8: 5.0^1 = 5.0
    assert(near(pow_double(5.0, 1), 5.0, 0.001) == 1)

    // Test 9: 2.0^20 = 1048576.0
    assert(near(pow_double(2.0, 20), 1048576.0, 0.1) == 1)

    // Test 10: 0.0^5 = 0.0
    assert(near(pow_double(0.0, 5), 0.0, 0.001) == 1)

    println("083_pow_double: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/084_atoi.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 084: String to Integer (atoi) with Overflow Handling
//
// Parse a byte array as a signed integer. Rules:
// 1. Skip leading whitespace (space = 32)
// 2. Optional sign ('+' = 43, '-' = 45)
// 3. Parse digits until non-digit or end
// 4. Clamp to [INT_MIN, INT_MAX] range on overflow
// Returns parsed value. INT_MAX = 2147483647, INT_MIN = -2147483648.

struct AtoiResult { value: i64, ok: i64 }

fn is_digit(ch: i64) -> i64 {
    if ch >= 48 && ch <= 57 { 1 } else { 0 }
}

fn my_atoi(bytes: [i64; 256], n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let INT_MAX: i64 = 2147483647
    let INT_MIN: i64 = 0 - 2147483648

    if n == 0 { return 0 }

    var i: i64 = 0

    // Skip whitespace
    while i < n && bytes[i] == 32 {
        i = i + 1
    }
    if i >= n { return 0 }

    // Check sign
    var sign: i64 = 1
    if bytes[i] == 45 {
        sign = 0 - 1
        i = i + 1
    } else if bytes[i] == 43 {
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Parse digits with overflow check
    var result: i64 = 0
    while i < n && is_digit(bytes[i]) == 1 {
        let digit = bytes[i] - 48

        // Check overflow before multiplying
        if result > (INT_MAX - digit) / 10 {
            if sign == 1 { return INT_MAX }
            return INT_MIN
        }

        result = result * 10 + digit
        i = i + 1
    }

    result * sign
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // '0'=48, '1'=49, ..., '9'=57, ' '=32, '+'=43, '-'=45
    // 'w'=119, 'o'=111, 'r'=114, 'd'=100, 's'=115

    // Test 1: "42" -> 42
    var b1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b1[0] = 52
    b1[1] = 50
    assert(my_atoi(b1, 2) == 42)

    // Test 2: "   -42" -> -42
    var b2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b2[0] = 32
    b2[1] = 32
    b2[2] = 32
    b2[3] = 45
    b2[4] = 52
    b2[5] = 50
    assert(my_atoi(b2, 6) == 0 - 42)

    // Test 3: "4193 with words" -> 4193
    // '4'=52, '1'=49, '9'=57, '3'=51, ' '=32, 'w'=119
    var b3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b3[0] = 52
    b3[1] = 49
    b3[2] = 57
    b3[3] = 51
    b3[4] = 32
    b3[5] = 119
    assert(my_atoi(b3, 6) == 4193)

    // Test 4: empty -> 0
    var b4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    assert(my_atoi(b4, 0) == 0)

    // Test 5: "+" alone -> 0 (no digits)
    var b5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b5[0] = 43
    assert(my_atoi(b5, 1) == 0)

    // Test 6: "0" -> 0
    var b6: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b6[0] = 48
    assert(my_atoi(b6, 1) == 0)

    // Test 7: "+123" -> 123
    var b7: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b7[0] = 43
    b7[1] = 49
    b7[2] = 50
    b7[3] = 51
    assert(my_atoi(b7, 4) == 123)

    // Test 8: "   " -> 0 (only whitespace)
    var b8: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b8[0] = 32
    b8[1] = 32
    b8[2] = 32
    assert(my_atoi(b8, 3) == 0)

    println("084_atoi: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/085_add_binary.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 085: Add Binary
//
// Add two binary numbers represented as byte arrays of 0s and 1s
// (least significant bit first). Returns the sum in the same format.
// Example: [1,0,1] (5) + [1,1] (3) = [0,0,0,1] (8).

struct Buf { data: [i64; 256] }

fn add_binary(a: [i64; 256], a_len: i64, b: [i64; 256], b_len: i64, out: &!Buf) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var carry: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    var out_len: i64 = 0

    // Find the longer length
    var max_len = a_len
    if b_len > max_len { max_len = b_len }

    while i < max_len || carry > 0 {
        var sum = carry
        if i < a_len {
            sum = sum + a[i]
        }
        if i < b_len {
            sum = sum + b[i]
        }

        out.data[out_len] = sum % 2
        carry = sum / 2
        out_len = out_len + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    out_len
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: [1,0,1] (5) + [1,1] (3) = [0,0,0,1] (8)
    var a1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a1[0] = 1
    a1[1] = 0
    a1[2] = 1
    var b1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b1[0] = 1
    b1[1] = 1
    var o1 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n1 = add_binary(a1, 3, b1, 2, &!o1)
    assert(n1 == 4)
    assert(o1.data[0] == 0)
    assert(o1.data[1] == 0)
    assert(o1.data[2] == 0)
    assert(o1.data[3] == 1)

    // Test 2: [1,1] (3) + [1] (1) = [0,0,1] (4)
    var a2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a2[0] = 1
    a2[1] = 1
    var b2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b2[0] = 1
    var o2 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n2 = add_binary(a2, 2, b2, 1, &!o2)
    assert(n2 == 3)
    assert(o2.data[0] == 0)
    assert(o2.data[1] == 0)
    assert(o2.data[2] == 1)

    // Test 3: [0] + [0] = [0]
    var a3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    var b3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    var o3 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n3 = add_binary(a3, 1, b3, 1, &!o3)
    assert(n3 == 1)
    assert(o3.data[0] == 0)

    // Test 4: [1,1,1] (7) + [1,1,1] (7) = [0,1,1,1] (14)
    var a4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a4[0] = 1
    a4[1] = 1
    a4[2] = 1
    var b4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b4[0] = 1
    b4[1] = 1
    b4[2] = 1
    var o4 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n4 = add_binary(a4, 3, b4, 3, &!o4)
    assert(n4 == 4)
    assert(o4.data[0] == 0)
    assert(o4.data[1] == 1)
    assert(o4.data[2] == 1)
    assert(o4.data[3] == 1)

    // Test 5: [1] + [1] = [0, 1] (2)
    var a5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a5[0] = 1
    var b5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b5[0] = 1
    var o5 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n5 = add_binary(a5, 1, b5, 1, &!o5)
    assert(n5 == 2)
    assert(o5.data[0] == 0)
    assert(o5.data[1] == 1)

    // Test 6: [0] + [1] = [1]
    var a6: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    var b6: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b6[0] = 1
    var o6 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n6 = add_binary(a6, 1, b6, 1, &!o6)
    assert(n6 == 1)
    assert(o6.data[0] == 1)

    println("085_add_binary: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/086_multiply_strings.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 086: Multiply Strings
//
// Multiply two non-negative integers represented as digit arrays
// (most significant digit first, values 0-9). Uses grade-school
// long multiplication. Returns product as digit array.
// Example: [1, 2, 3] * [4, 5, 6] = [5, 6, 0, 8, 8]

struct Buf { data: [i64; 512] }

fn multiply_strings(a: [i64; 256], a_len: i64, b: [i64; 256], b_len: i64, out: &!Buf) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if a_len == 0 || b_len == 0 { return 0 }

    // Product has at most a_len + b_len digits
    let prod_len = a_len + b_len
    var prod = Buf { data: [0; 512] }

    // Multiply each digit of a with each digit of b
    var i: i64 = a_len - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var j: i64 = b_len - 1
        while j >= 0 {
            let mul = a[i] * b[j]
            let pos1 = i + j
            let pos2 = i + j + 1
            let sum = mul + prod.data[pos2]

            prod.data[pos2] = sum % 10
            prod.data[pos1] = prod.data[pos1] + sum / 10
            j = j - 1
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    // Skip leading zeros
    var start: i64 = 0
    while start < prod_len - 1 && prod.data[start] == 0 {
        start = start + 1
    }

    // Copy result
    var out_len: i64 = 0
    var k = start
    while k < prod_len {
        out.data[out_len] = prod.data[k]
        out_len = out_len + 1
        k = k + 1
    }

    out_len
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: [1, 2, 3] * [4, 5, 6] = 123 * 456 = 56088 -> [5, 6, 0, 8, 8]
    var a1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a1[0] = 1
    a1[1] = 2
    a1[2] = 3
    var b1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b1[0] = 4
    b1[1] = 5
    b1[2] = 6
    var o1 = Buf { data: [0; 512] }
    let n1 = multiply_strings(a1, 3, b1, 3, &!o1)
    assert(n1 == 5)
    assert(o1.data[0] == 5)
    assert(o1.data[1] == 6)
    assert(o1.data[2] == 0)
    assert(o1.data[3] == 8)
    assert(o1.data[4] == 8)

    // Test 2: [2] * [3] = 6 -> [6]
    var a2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a2[0] = 2
    var b2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b2[0] = 3
    var o2 = Buf { data: [0; 512] }
    let n2 = multiply_strings(a2, 1, b2, 1, &!o2)
    assert(n2 == 1)
    assert(o2.data[0] == 6)

    // Test 3: [9, 9] * [9, 9] = 99 * 99 = 9801 -> [9, 8, 0, 1]
    var a3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a3[0] = 9
    a3[1] = 9
    var b3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b3[0] = 9
    b3[1] = 9
    var o3 = Buf { data: [0; 512] }
    let n3 = multiply_strings(a3, 2, b3, 2, &!o3)
    assert(n3 == 4)
    assert(o3.data[0] == 9)
    assert(o3.data[1] == 8)
    assert(o3.data[2] == 0)
    assert(o3.data[3] == 1)

    // Test 4: [0] * [5, 6] = 0 -> [0]
    var a4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    var b4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b4[0] = 5
    b4[1] = 6
    var o4 = Buf { data: [0; 512] }
    let n4 = multiply_strings(a4, 1, b4, 2, &!o4)
    assert(n4 == 1)
    assert(o4.data[0] == 0)

    // Test 5: [1, 0, 0] * [1, 0] = 100 * 10 = 1000 -> [1, 0, 0, 0]
    var a5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a5[0] = 1
    var b5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    b5[0] = 1
    b5[1] = 0
    var o5 = Buf { data: [0; 512] }
    let n5 = multiply_strings(a5, 3, b5, 2, &!o5)
    assert(n5 == 4)
    assert(o5.data[0] == 1)
    assert(o5.data[1] == 0)
    assert(o5.data[2] == 0)
    assert(o5.data[3] == 0)

    println("086_multiply_strings: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/087_zigzag_conversion.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 087: Zigzag Conversion
//
// Rearrange characters in a zigzag pattern with a given number of rows,
// then read off row by row. For "PAYPALISHIRING" with 3 rows:
//   P   A   H   N
//   A P L S I I G
//   Y   I   R
// Result: "PAHNAPLSIIGYIR"
// Input/output as byte arrays.

struct Buf { data: [i64; 256] }

fn zigzag(input: [i64; 256], n: i64, num_rows: i64, out: &!Buf) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if num_rows <= 1 || num_rows >= n {
        // Just copy
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < n {
            out.data[k] = input[k]
            k = k + 1
        }
        return n
    }

    // Cycle length = 2 * (num_rows - 1)
    let cycle = 2 * (num_rows - 1)
    var out_idx: i64 = 0

    var row: i64 = 0
    while row < num_rows {
        var i: i64 = row
        while i < n {
            out.data[out_idx] = input[i]
            out_idx = out_idx + 1

            // For non-first and non-last rows, there is a mid-cycle char
            if row > 0 && row < num_rows - 1 {
                let mid = i + cycle - 2 * row
                if mid < n {
                    out.data[out_idx] = input[mid]
                    out_idx = out_idx + 1
                }
            }

            i = i + cycle
        }
        row = row + 1
    }

    out_idx
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: "PAYPALISHIRING" (3 rows) -> "PAHNAPLSIIGYIR"

    var s1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]

// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/088_pascal_triangle.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 088: Pascal's Triangle
//
// Generate the first n rows of Pascal's triangle. Each element is the
// sum of the two elements above it. Row k has k+1 elements.
// Stored as flat array: row r starts at index r*(r+1)/2.
// C(r,c) = C(r-1,c-1) + C(r-1,c), with C(r,0) = C(r,r) = 1.

struct Triangle { data: [i64; 1024] }

fn row_start(r: i64) -> i64 with Div {
    r * (r + 1) / 2
}

fn pascal(n: i64, out: &!Triangle) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if n <= 0 { return 0 }

    var r: i64 = 0
    while r < n {
        let base = row_start(r)
        out.data[base] = 1
        out.data[base + r] = 1

        var c: i64 = 1
        while c < r {
            let prev_base = row_start(r - 1)
            out.data[base + c] = out.data[prev_base + c - 1] + out.data[prev_base + c]
            c = c + 1
        }
        r = r + 1
    }

    // Total elements = n*(n+1)/2
    row_start(n)
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: n=1 -> [1]
    var t1 = Triangle { data: [0; 1024] }
    let total1 = pascal(1, &!t1)
    assert(total1 == 1)
    assert(t1.data[0] == 1)

    // Test 2: n=2 -> [1], [1,1]
    var t2 = Triangle { data: [0; 1024] }
    let total2 = pascal(2, &!t2)
    assert(total2 == 3)
    assert(t2.data[0] == 1)
    assert(t2.data[1] == 1)
    assert(t2.data[2] == 1)

    // Test 3: n=5 -> row 0: [1], row 1: [1,1], row 2: [1,2,1],
    //                 row 3: [1,3,3,1], row 4: [1,4,6,4,1]
    var t3 = Triangle { data: [0; 1024] }
    let total3 = pascal(5, &!t3)
    assert(total3 == 15)
    // Row 0 at idx 0: [1]
    assert(t3.data[0] == 1)
    // Row 1 at idx 1: [1, 1]
    assert(t3.data[1] == 1)
    assert(t3.data[2] == 1)
    // Row 2 at idx 3: [1, 2, 1]
    assert(t3.data[3] == 1)
    assert(t3.data[4] == 2)
    assert(t3.data[5] == 1)
    // Row 3 at idx 6: [1, 3, 3, 1]
    assert(t3.data[6] == 1)
    assert(t3.data[7] == 3)
    assert(t3.data[8] == 3)
    assert(t3.data[9] == 1)
    // Row 4 at idx 10: [1, 4, 6, 4, 1]
    assert(t3.data[10] == 1)
    assert(t3.data[11] == 4)
    assert(t3.data[12] == 6)
    assert(t3.data[13] == 4)
    assert(t3.data[14] == 1)

    // Test 4: n=0 -> 0 elements
    var t4 = Triangle { data: [0; 1024] }
    let total4 = pascal(0, &!t4)
    assert(total4 == 0)

    // Test 5: n=7, check row 6: [1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1]
    var t5 = Triangle { data: [0; 1024] }
    pascal(7, &!t5)
    let r6_base = row_start(6)
    assert(t5.data[r6_base] == 1)
    assert(t5.data[r6_base + 1] == 6)
    assert(t5.data[r6_base + 2] == 15)
    assert(t5.data[r6_base + 3] == 20)
    assert(t5.data[r6_base + 4] == 15)
    assert(t5.data[r6_base + 5] == 6)
    assert(t5.data[r6_base + 6] == 1)

    println("088_pascal_triangle: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/089_roman_to_integer.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 089: Roman Numeral to Integer (Full Range)
//
// Convert a Roman numeral byte array to its integer value.
// Supports I(1) V(5) X(10) L(50) C(100) D(500) M(1000)
// and subtractive forms: IV(4) IX(9) XL(40) XC(90) CD(400) CM(900).
// Valid range: 1 to 3999 (I to MMMCMXCIX).
// ASCII: I=73, V=86, X=88, L=76, C=67, D=68, M=77

fn roman_val(ch: i64) -> i64 {
    if ch == 73 { return 1 }
    if ch == 86 { return 5 }
    if ch == 88 { return 10 }
    if ch == 76 { return 50 }
    if ch == 67 { return 100 }
    if ch == 68 { return 500 }
    if ch == 77 { return 1000 }
    0
}

fn roman_to_integer(bytes: [i64; 256], n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    if n == 0 { return 0 }

    var result: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0

    while i < n {
        let curr = roman_val(bytes[i])
        if i + 1 < n {
            let next = roman_val(bytes[i + 1])
            if curr < next {
                result = result + next - curr
                i = i + 2
            } else {
                result = result + curr
                i = i + 1
            }
        } else {
            result = result + curr
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    result
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // I=73, V=86, X=88, L=76, C=67, D=68, M=77

    // Test 1: I = 1
    var r1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r1[0] = 73
    assert(roman_to_integer(r1, 1) == 1)

    // Test 2: IV = 4
    var r2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r2[0] = 73
    r2[1] = 86
    assert(roman_to_integer(r2, 2) == 4)

    // Test 3: IX = 9
    var r3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r3[0] = 73
    r3[1] = 88
    assert(roman_to_integer(r3, 2) == 9)

    // Test 4: XLII = 42
    var r4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r4[0] = 88
    r4[1] = 76
    r4[2] = 73
    r4[3] = 73
    assert(roman_to_integer(r4, 4) == 42)

    // Test 5: MCMXCIV = 1994
    var r5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r5[0] = 77
    r5[1] = 67
    r5[2] = 77
    r5[3] = 88
    r5[4] = 67
    r5[5] = 73
    r5[6] = 86
    assert(roman_to_integer(r5, 7) == 1994)

    // Test 6: MMMCMXCIX = 3999
    var r6: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r6[0] = 77
    r6[1] = 77
    r6[2] = 77
    r6[3] = 67
    r6[4] = 77
    r6[5] = 88
    r6[6] = 67
    r6[7] = 73
    r6[8] = 88
    assert(roman_to_integer(r6, 9) == 3999)

    // Test 7: DCCCXLV = 845
    var r7: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r7[0] = 68
    r7[1] = 67
    r7[2] = 67
    r7[3] = 67
    r7[4] = 88
    r7[5] = 76
    r7[6] = 86
    assert(roman_to_integer(r7, 7) == 845)

    // Test 8: LVIII = 58
    var r8: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r8[0] = 76
    r8[1] = 86
    r8[2] = 73
    r8[3] = 73
    r8[4] = 73
    assert(roman_to_integer(r8, 5) == 58)

    // Test 9: CD = 400
    var r9: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r9[0] = 67
    r9[1] = 68
    assert(roman_to_integer(r9, 2) == 400)

    // Test 10: CM = 900
    var r10: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    r10[0] = 67
    r10[1] = 77
    assert(roman_to_integer(r10, 2) == 900)

    println("089_roman_to_integer: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/090_integer_to_roman.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 090: Integer to Roman Numeral
//
// Convert an integer (1-3999) to a Roman numeral byte array.
// Uses a greedy approach with value-symbol pairs including subtractive forms.
// Values: 1000=M, 900=CM, 500=D, 400=CD, 100=C, 90=XC, 50=L, 40=XL,
//         10=X, 9=IX, 5=V, 4=IV, 1=I
// ASCII: I=73, V=86, X=88, L=76, C=67, D=68, M=77

struct Buf { data: [i64; 256] }

fn int_to_roman(num: i64, out: &!Buf) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // 13 value-symbol pairs (values and corresponding byte sequences)
    var values: [i64; 13] = [1000, 900, 500, 400, 100, 90, 50, 40, 10, 9, 5, 4, 1]

    // Symbol bytes: pairs of (byte1, byte2) where byte2=0 means single char
    // M=77, CM=(67,77), D=68, CD=(67,68), C=67, XC=(88,67), L=76, XL=(88,76),
    // X=88, IX=(73,88), V=86, IV=(73,86), I=73
    var sym1: [i64; 13] = [77, 67, 68, 67, 67, 88, 76, 88, 88, 73, 86, 73, 73]
    var sym2: [i64; 13] = [0, 77, 0, 68, 0, 67, 0, 76, 0, 88, 0, 86, 0]

    var n = num
    var out_len: i64 = 0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 13 {
        while n >= values[i] {
            out.data[out_len] = sym1[i]
            out_len = out_len + 1
            if sym2[i] != 0 {
                out.data[out_len] = sym2[i]
                out_len = out_len + 1
            }
            n = n - values[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    out_len
}

fn check_bytes(buf: &Buf, expected: [i64; 256], n: i64) -> i64 with Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if buf.data[i] != expected[i] { return 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    1
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // I=73, V=86, X=88, L=76, C=67, D=68, M=77

    // Test 1: 3 -> "III"
    var o1 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n1 = int_to_roman(3, &!o1)
    assert(n1 == 3)
    assert(o1.data[0] == 73)
    assert(o1.data[1] == 73)
    assert(o1.data[2] == 73)

    // Test 2: 4 -> "IV"
    var o2 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n2 = int_to_roman(4, &!o2)
    assert(n2 == 2)
    assert(o2.data[0] == 73)
    assert(o2.data[1] == 86)

    // Test 3: 9 -> "IX"
    var o3 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n3 = int_to_roman(9, &!o3)
    assert(n3 == 2)
    assert(o3.data[0] == 73)
    assert(o3.data[1] == 88)

    // Test 4: 58 -> "LVIII"
    var o4 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n4 = int_to_roman(58, &!o4)
    assert(n4 == 5)
    assert(o4.data[0] == 76)
    assert(o4.data[1] == 86)
    assert(o4.data[2] == 73)
    assert(o4.data[3] == 73)
    assert(o4.data[4] == 73)

    // Test 5: 1994 -> "MCMXCIV"
    var o5 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n5 = int_to_roman(1994, &!o5)
    assert(n5 == 7)
    assert(o5.data[0] == 77)
    assert(o5.data[1] == 67)
    assert(o5.data[2] == 77)
    assert(o5.data[3] == 88)
    assert(o5.data[4] == 67)
    assert(o5.data[5] == 73)
    assert(o5.data[6] == 86)

    // Test 6: 3999 -> "MMMCMXCIX"
    var o6 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n6 = int_to_roman(3999, &!o6)
    assert(n6 == 9)
    assert(o6.data[0] == 77)
    assert(o6.data[1] == 77)
    assert(o6.data[2] == 77)
    assert(o6.data[3] == 67)
    assert(o6.data[4] == 77)
    assert(o6.data[5] == 88)
    assert(o6.data[6] == 67)
    assert(o6.data[7] == 73)
    assert(o6.data[8] == 88)

    // Test 7: 1 -> "I"
    var o7 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n7 = int_to_roman(1, &!o7)
    assert(n7 == 1)
    assert(o7.data[0] == 73)

    // Test 8: 1000 -> "M"
    var o8 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n8 = int_to_roman(1000, &!o8)
    assert(n8 == 1)
    assert(o8.data[0] == 77)

    println("090_integer_to_roman: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/091_hamming_distance.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 091: Hamming Distance
//
// Count the number of positions at which the corresponding bits differ
// between two non-negative integers. Uses XOR to find differing bits,
// then counts set bits in the result.

fn hamming_distance(x: i64, y: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div {
    var xor = x ^ y
    var count: i64 = 0
    while xor > 0 {
        count = count + (xor & 1)
        xor = xor >> 1
        count = count
    }
    count
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: hamming(1, 4) = 2
    // 1 = 001, 4 = 100 -> XOR = 101 -> 2 bits
    assert(hamming_distance(1, 4) == 2)

    // Test 2: hamming(0, 0) = 0
    assert(hamming_distance(0, 0) == 0)

    // Test 3: hamming(3, 1) = 1
    // 3 = 11, 1 = 01 -> XOR = 10 -> 1 bit
    assert(hamming_distance(3, 1) == 1)

    // Test 4: hamming(7, 0) = 3
    // 7 = 111, 0 = 000 -> XOR = 111 -> 3 bits
    assert(hamming_distance(7, 0) == 3)

    // Test 5: hamming(15, 15) = 0
    assert(hamming_distance(15, 15) == 0)

    // Test 6: hamming(255, 0) = 8
    assert(hamming_distance(255, 0) == 8)

    // Test 7: hamming(10, 5) = 4
    // 10 = 1010, 5 = 0101 -> XOR = 1111 -> 4 bits
    assert(hamming_distance(10, 5) == 4)

    // Test 8: hamming(14, 1) = 3
    // 14 = 1110, 1 = 0001 -> XOR = 1111 -> 4 bits
    assert(hamming_distance(14, 1) == 4)

    // Test 9: hamming(0, 1) = 1
    assert(hamming_distance(0, 1) == 1)

    // Test 10: hamming(1023, 0) = 10 (1023 = 0b1111111111)
    assert(hamming_distance(1023, 0) == 10)

    println("091_hamming_distance: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/092_popcount.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 092: Population Count (Popcount)
//
// Count the number of set bits (1-bits) in a non-negative integer.
// Uses Brian Kernighan's algorithm: repeatedly clear the lowest set bit
// with n & (n - 1). Each iteration removes exactly one set bit. O(k)
// where k is the number of set bits.

fn popcount(n: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var x = n
    var count: i64 = 0
    while x > 0 {
        x = x & (x - 1)
        count = count + 1
    }
    count
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: popcount(0) = 0
    assert(popcount(0) == 0)

    // Test 2: popcount(1) = 1
    assert(popcount(1) == 1)

    // Test 3: popcount(2) = 1 (10)
    assert(popcount(2) == 1)

    // Test 4: popcount(3) = 2 (11)
    assert(popcount(3) == 2)

    // Test 5: popcount(7) = 3 (111)
    assert(popcount(7) == 3)

    // Test 6: popcount(8) = 1 (1000)
    assert(popcount(8) == 1)

    // Test 7: popcount(15) = 4 (1111)
    assert(popcount(15) == 4)

    // Test 8: popcount(16) = 1 (10000)
    assert(popcount(16) == 1)

    // Test 9: popcount(255) = 8 (11111111)
    assert(popcount(255) == 8)

    // Test 10: popcount(1023) = 10 (1111111111)
    assert(popcount(1023) == 10)

    // Test 11: popcount(256) = 1 (100000000)
    assert(popcount(256) == 1)

    // Test 12: popcount(1024) = 1
    assert(popcount(1024) == 1)

    // Test 13: popcount(65535) = 16
    assert(popcount(65535) == 16)

    // Test 14: popcount(42) = 3 (101010)
    assert(popcount(42) == 3)

    println("092_popcount: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/093_reverse_bits.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 093: Reverse Bits
//
// Reverse the bits of a 32-bit unsigned integer. For example,
// 43261596 (00000010100101000001111010011100) becomes
// 964176192 (00111001011110000010100101000000).
// Iterates 32 times, shifting bits from input to output.

fn reverse_bits(n: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var result: i64 = 0
    var x = n
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 {
        result = (result << 1) | (x & 1)
        x = x >> 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: reverse_bits(0) = 0
    assert(reverse_bits(0) == 0)

    // Test 2: reverse_bits(1) = 2147483648 (bit 0 -> bit 31)
    assert(reverse_bits(1) == 2147483648)

    // Test 3: reverse_bits(2147483648) = 1 (bit 31 -> bit 0)
    assert(reverse_bits(2147483648) == 1)

    // Test 4: reverse_bits(43261596) = 964176192
    // 43261596  = 00000010 10010100 00011110 10011100
    // reversed  = 00111001 01111000 00101001 01000000 = 964176192
    assert(reverse_bits(43261596) == 964176192)

    // Test 5: reverse_bits(4294967295) = 4294967295 (all 1s)
    assert(reverse_bits(4294967295) == 4294967295)

    // Test 6: reverse_bits(2) = 1073741824
    // 2 = ...10, reversed = 01000...0 = 2^30
    assert(reverse_bits(2) == 1073741824)

    // Test 7: reverse_bits(4) = 536870912
    // 4 = ...100, reversed = 001000...0 = 2^29
    assert(reverse_bits(4) == 536870912)

    // Test 8: reverse_bits(255) = 4278190080
    // 255 = 00000000...11111111
    // reversed = 11111111 00000000 00000000 00000000 = 0xFF000000
    assert(reverse_bits(255) == 4278190080)

    println("093_reverse_bits: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/094_single_number.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 094: Single Number
//
// Given an array where every element appears twice except for one,
// find the element that appears only once. Uses XOR: a ^ a = 0 and
// a ^ 0 = a, so XOR of all elements cancels pairs and leaves the unique one.
// O(n) time, O(1) space.

fn single_number(arr: [i64; 256], n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var result: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        result = result ^ arr[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: [2, 2, 1] -> 1
    var a1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a1[0] = 2
    a1[1] = 2
    a1[2] = 1
    assert(single_number(a1, 3) == 1)

    // Test 2: [4, 1, 2, 1, 2] -> 4
    var a2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a2[0] = 4
    a2[1] = 1
    a2[2] = 2
    a2[3] = 1
    a2[4] = 2
    assert(single_number(a2, 5) == 4)

    // Test 3: [1] -> 1
    var a3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a3[0] = 1
    assert(single_number(a3, 1) == 1)

    // Test 4: [7, 3, 5, 3, 7] -> 5
    var a4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a4[0] = 7
    a4[1] = 3
    a4[2] = 5
    a4[3] = 3
    a4[4] = 7
    assert(single_number(a4, 5) == 5)

    // Test 5: [0, 1, 0] -> 1
    var a5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a5[0] = 0
    a5[1] = 1
    a5[2] = 0
    assert(single_number(a5, 3) == 1)

    // Test 6: [100, 200, 100, 300, 200, 400, 300] -> 400
    var a6: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a6[0] = 100
    a6[1] = 200
    a6[2] = 100
    a6[3] = 300
    a6[4] = 200
    a6[5] = 400
    a6[6] = 300
    assert(single_number(a6, 7) == 400)

    // Test 7: [42] -> 42
    var a7: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a7[0] = 42
    assert(single_number(a7, 1) == 42)

    // Test 8: [10, 20, 10, 30, 20, 30, 99] -> 99
    var a8: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a8[0] = 10
    a8[1] = 20
    a8[2] = 10
    a8[3] = 30
    a8[4] = 20
    a8[5] = 30
    a8[6] = 99
    assert(single_number(a8, 7) == 99)

    println("094_single_number: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/095_bitwise_and_range.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 095: Bitwise AND of Range
//
// Given two non-negative integers m and n (m <= n), compute the bitwise
// AND of all integers in range [m, n]. Key insight: the result is the
// common prefix of m and n in binary, with trailing bits zeroed.
// Shift both numbers right until they are equal (finding the common prefix),
// then shift back left by the same amount. O(log n).

fn range_and(m: i64, n: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var a = m
    var b = n
    var shift: i64 = 0

    while a != b {
        a = a >> 1
        b = b >> 1
        shift = shift + 1
    }

    a << shift as u8
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: range_and(5, 7) = 4
    // 5=101, 6=110, 7=111 -> AND = 100 = 4
    assert(range_and(5, 7) == 4)

    // Test 2: range_and(0, 0) = 0
    assert(range_and(0, 0) == 0)

    // Test 3: range_and(1, 1) = 1
    assert(range_and(1, 1) == 1)

    // Test 4: range_and(0, 1) = 0
    // 0 & 1 = 0
    assert(range_and(0, 1) == 0)

    // Test 5: range_and(5, 5) = 5
    assert(range_and(5, 5) == 5)

    // Test 6: range_and(4, 7) = 4
    // 4=100, 5=101, 6=110, 7=111 -> AND = 100 = 4
    assert(range_and(4, 7) == 4)

    // Test 7: range_and(1, 2147483647) = 0
    // Wide range -> no common bits
    assert(range_and(1, 2147483647) == 0)

    // Test 8: range_and(12, 15) = 12
    // 12=1100, 13=1101, 14=1110, 15=1111 -> AND = 1100 = 12
    assert(range_and(12, 15) == 12)

    // Test 9: range_and(8, 10) = 8
    // 8=1000, 9=1001, 10=1010 -> AND = 1000 = 8
    assert(range_and(8, 10) == 8)

    // Test 10: range_and(6, 7) = 6
    // 6=110, 7=111 -> AND = 110 = 6
    assert(range_and(6, 7) == 6)

    println("095_bitwise_and_range: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/096_gray_code.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 096: Gray Code
//
// Generate the n-bit Gray code sequence. Gray code is a binary numeral
// system where two successive values differ in only one bit.
// Formula: gray(i) = i ^ (i >> 1). For n bits, generate 2^n values.
// Maximum n=8 (256 values).

struct Buf { data: [i64; 256] }

fn gray_code(n: i64, out: &!Buf) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    // Number of codes = 2^n
    var total: i64 = 1
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n {
        total = total * 2
        k = k + 1
    }

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < total {
        out.data[i] = i ^ (i >> 1)
        i = i + 1
    }

    total
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: n=1 -> [0, 1]
    var o1 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n1 = gray_code(1, &!o1)
    assert(n1 == 2)
    assert(o1.data[0] == 0)
    assert(o1.data[1] == 1)

    // Test 2: n=2 -> [0, 1, 3, 2]
    var o2 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n2 = gray_code(2, &!o2)
    assert(n2 == 4)
    assert(o2.data[0] == 0)
    assert(o2.data[1] == 1)
    assert(o2.data[2] == 3)
    assert(o2.data[3] == 2)

    // Test 3: n=3 -> [0, 1, 3, 2, 6, 7, 5, 4]
    var o3 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n3 = gray_code(3, &!o3)
    assert(n3 == 8)
    assert(o3.data[0] == 0)
    assert(o3.data[1] == 1)
    assert(o3.data[2] == 3)
    assert(o3.data[3] == 2)
    assert(o3.data[4] == 6)
    assert(o3.data[5] == 7)
    assert(o3.data[6] == 5)
    assert(o3.data[7] == 4)

    // Test 4: n=0 -> [0] (one code: the empty bit string)
    var o4 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n4 = gray_code(0, &!o4)
    assert(n4 == 1)
    assert(o4.data[0] == 0)

    // Test 5: Verify adjacent codes differ by exactly 1 bit (n=4)
    var o5 = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    let n5 = gray_code(4, &!o5)
    assert(n5 == 16)
    // Check first few and adjacency
    assert(o5.data[0] == 0)
    assert(o5.data[1] == 1)
    assert(o5.data[15] == 8)
    // Verify all adjacent pairs differ by 1 bit
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n5 - 1 {
        let diff = o5.data[i] ^ o5.data[i + 1]
        // diff must be a power of 2 (exactly one bit set)
        assert(diff > 0)
        assert((diff & (diff - 1)) == 0)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Test 6: n=4 starts at 0 and has 16 distinct values
    // (They cover all of 0..15)
    var seen: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n5 {
        seen[o5.data[j]] = seen[o5.data[j]] + 1
        j = j + 1
    }
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 16 {
        assert(seen[k] == 1)
        k = k + 1
    }

    println("096_gray_code: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/097_subsets.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 097: Subsets (Power Set)
//
// Generate all subsets of an array using bitmask iteration.
// For n elements, iterate masks from 0 to 2^n - 1. Each bit in the
// mask indicates whether the corresponding element is included.
// Subsets are written into a flat output array; each subset is followed
// by a -1 sentinel. Returns the number of subsets (2^n).

struct Buf { data: [i64; 4096] }

fn subsets(arr: [i64; 256], n: i64, out: &!Buf) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    // 2^n subsets
    var total: i64 = 1
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n {
        total = total * 2
        k = k + 1
    }

    var out_idx: i64 = 0
    var mask: i64 = 0
    while mask < total {
        // For each bit in mask, include that element
        var bit: i64 = 0
        while bit < n {
            if (mask >> bit as u8) & 1 == 1 {
                out.data[out_idx] = arr[bit]
                out_idx = out_idx + 1
            }
            bit = bit + 1
        }
        // Sentinel for end of this subset
        out.data[out_idx] = 0 - 1
        out_idx = out_idx + 1
        mask = mask + 1
    }

    total
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: subsets of [1, 2, 3] -> 8 subsets
    var a1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a1[0] = 1
    a1[1] = 2
    a1[2] = 3
    var o1 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n1 = subsets(a1, 3, &!o1)
    assert(n1 == 8)
    // Subset 0 (mask=0): {} -> sentinel at [0]
    assert(o1.data[0] == 0 - 1)
    // Subset 1 (mask=1): {1} -> [1, -1]
    assert(o1.data[1] == 1)
    assert(o1.data[2] == 0 - 1)
    // Subset 2 (mask=2): {2} -> [2, -1]
    assert(o1.data[3] == 2)
    assert(o1.data[4] == 0 - 1)
    // Subset 3 (mask=3): {1, 2} -> [1, 2, -1]
    assert(o1.data[5] == 1)
    assert(o1.data[6] == 2)
    assert(o1.data[7] == 0 - 1)

    // Test 2: subsets of empty -> 1 subset (the empty set)
    var a2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    var o2 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n2 = subsets(a2, 0, &!o2)
    assert(n2 == 1)
    assert(o2.data[0] == 0 - 1)

    // Test 3: subsets of [5] -> 2 subsets: {}, {5}
    var a3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a3[0] = 5
    var o3 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n3 = subsets(a3, 1, &!o3)
    assert(n3 == 2)
    assert(o3.data[0] == 0 - 1)
    assert(o3.data[1] == 5)
    assert(o3.data[2] == 0 - 1)

    // Test 4: subsets of [10, 20] -> 4 subsets
    var a4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a4[0] = 10
    a4[1] = 20
    var o4 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n4 = subsets(a4, 2, &!o4)
    assert(n4 == 4)
    // mask=0: {} -> [-1]
    assert(o4.data[0] == 0 - 1)
    // mask=1: {10} -> [10, -1]
    assert(o4.data[1] == 10)
    assert(o4.data[2] == 0 - 1)
    // mask=2: {20} -> [20, -1]
    assert(o4.data[3] == 20)
    assert(o4.data[4] == 0 - 1)
    // mask=3: {10, 20} -> [10, 20, -1]
    assert(o4.data[5] == 10)
    assert(o4.data[6] == 20)
    assert(o4.data[7] == 0 - 1)

    // Test 5: 4 elements -> 16 subsets
    var a5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a5[0] = 1
    a5[1] = 2
    a5[2] = 3
    a5[3] = 4
    var o5 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n5 = subsets(a5, 4, &!o5)
    assert(n5 == 16)

    println("097_subsets: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/098_permutations.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 098: Permutations (Iterative)
//
// Generate all permutations of an array using the iterative
// "next permutation" algorithm. Start with sorted input, then repeatedly
// compute the next lexicographic permutation until we cycle back.
// For n elements, produces n! permutations. Each permutation is stored
// consecutively in the output array. Maximum n=6 (720 permutations).

struct Buf { data: [i64; 256] }
struct PermOut { data: [i64; 4096] }

fn swap_buf(buf: &!Buf, i: i64, j: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    let tmp = buf.data[i]
    buf.data[i] = buf.data[j]
    buf.data[j] = tmp
}

fn reverse_range(buf: &!Buf, start: i64, end: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    var lo = start
    var hi = end
    while lo < hi {
        swap_buf(buf, lo, hi)
        lo = lo + 1
        hi = hi - 1
    }
}

fn next_perm(buf: &!Buf, n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    // Returns 1 if next permutation exists, 0 if wrapped
    if n <= 1 { return 0 }

    var pivot: i64 = 0 - 1
    var i: i64 = n - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        if buf.data[i] < buf.data[i + 1] {
            pivot = i
            break
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    if pivot == 0 - 1 {
        // Wrapped back to sorted order
        reverse_range(buf, 0, n - 1)
        return 0
    }

    var j: i64 = n - 1
    while j > pivot {
        if buf.data[j] > buf.data[pivot] { break }
        j = j - 1
    }

    swap_buf(buf, pivot, j)
    reverse_range(buf, pivot + 1, n - 1)
    1
}

fn factorial(n: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 2
    while i <= n {
        result = result * i
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn permutations(arr: [i64; 256], n: i64, out: &!PermOut) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    var buf = Buf { data: [0; 256] }
    // Copy and sort input (assume already sorted for simplicity)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        buf.data[i] = arr[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    let total = factorial(n)
    var count: i64 = 0
    var out_idx: i64 = 0

    // Store first permutation
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n {
        out.data[out_idx] = buf.data[k]
        out_idx = out_idx + 1
        k = k + 1
    }
    count = 1

    // Generate remaining permutations
    while count < total {
        let has_next = next_perm(&!buf, n)
        if has_next == 0 { break }
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            out.data[out_idx] = buf.data[j]
            out_idx = out_idx + 1
            j = j + 1
        }
        count = count + 1
    }

    count
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: permutations of [1, 2, 3] -> 6 permutations
    var a1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a1[0] = 1
    a1[1] = 2
    a1[2] = 3
    var o1 = PermOut { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n1 = permutations(a1, 3, &!o1)
    assert(n1 == 6)
    // First perm: [1, 2, 3]
    assert(o1.data[0] == 1)
    assert(o1.data[1] == 2)
    assert(o1.data[2] == 3)
    // Second perm: [1, 3, 2]
    assert(o1.data[3] == 1)
    assert(o1.data[4] == 3)
    assert(o1.data[5] == 2)
    // Third perm: [2, 1, 3]
    assert(o1.data[6] == 2)
    assert(o1.data[7] == 1)
    assert(o1.data[8] == 3)
    // Last perm: [3, 2, 1]
    assert(o1.data[15] == 3)
    assert(o1.data[16] == 2)
    assert(o1.data[17] == 1)

    // Test 2: permutations of [1] -> 1 permutation
    var a2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a2[0] = 1
    var o2 = PermOut { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n2 = permutations(a2, 1, &!o2)
    assert(n2 == 1)
    assert(o2.data[0] == 1)

    // Test 3: permutations of [1, 2] -> 2 permutations
    var a3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a3[0] = 1
    a3[1] = 2
    var o3 = PermOut { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n3 = permutations(a3, 2, &!o3)
    assert(n3 == 2)
    assert(o3.data[0] == 1)
    assert(o3.data[1] == 2)
    assert(o3.data[2] == 2)
    assert(o3.data[3] == 1)

    // Test 4: permutations of [1, 2, 3, 4] -> 24 permutations
    var a4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    a4[0] = 1
    a4[1] = 2
    a4[2] = 3
    a4[3] = 4
    var o4 = PermOut { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n4 = permutations(a4, 4, &!o4)
    assert(n4 == 24)

    println("098_permutations: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/099_combination_sum.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 099: Combination Sum (Simplified)
//
// Given an array of distinct positive integers (candidates) and a target,
// find all unique combinations where the candidates sum to target.
// Each candidate may be used unlimited times. Uses iterative backtracking
// with an explicit stack. Combinations are stored in a flat output array
// separated by -1 sentinels. Returns the number of valid combinations.
// Candidates must be sorted. Maximum candidates=8, target<=100.

struct Buf { data: [i64; 4096] }

// Stack frame for iterative backtracking
struct Stack { data: [i64; 256] }

fn combination_sum(cands: [i64; 256], num_cands: i64, target: i64, out: &!Buf) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    // Working combination buffer
    var combo: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]
    var combo_len: i64 = 0
    var out_idx: i64 = 0
    var count: i64 = 0

    // Iterative DFS using explicit stack
    // Each stack entry: (candidate_index, remaining_sum)
    // We use a different approach: iterate with backtracking positions
    var start_idx: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]
    var depth: i64 = 0
    var remaining = target

    // Initialize: start searching from candidate 0
    start_idx[0] = 0

    // Use a while loop to simulate recursion
    var running: i64 = 1
    while running == 1 {
        if remaining == 0 {
            // Found a valid combination - copy to output
            var k: i64 = 0
            while k < combo_len {
                out.data[out_idx] = combo[k]
                out_idx = out_idx + 1
                k = k + 1
            }
            out.data[out_idx] = 0 - 1
            out_idx = out_idx + 1
            count = count + 1

            // Backtrack
            if combo_len == 0 {
                running = 0
            } else {
                combo_len = combo_len - 1
                remaining = remaining + combo[combo_len]
                depth = depth - 1
                start_idx[depth] = start_idx[depth] + 1
            }
        } else {
            // Try candidates starting from start_idx[depth]
            var found: i64 = 0
            var ci = start_idx[depth]
            while ci < num_cands && found == 0 {
                if cands[ci] <= remaining {
                    // Choose this candidate
                    combo[combo_len] = cands[ci]
                    combo_len = combo_len + 1
                    remaining = remaining - cands[ci]
                    start_idx[depth] = ci
                    depth = depth + 1
                    start_idx[depth] = ci
                    found = 1
                } else {
                    ci = ci + 1
                }
            }
            if found == 0 {
                // No valid candidate: backtrack
                if combo_len == 0 {
                    running = 0
                } else {
                    combo_len = combo_len - 1
                    remaining = remaining + combo[combo_len]
                    depth = depth - 1
                    start_idx[depth] = start_idx[depth] + 1
                }
            }
        }
    }

    count
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: candidates=[2, 3, 6, 7], target=7
    // Solutions: [2,2,3], [7]
    var c1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    c1[0] = 2
    c1[1] = 3
    c1[2] = 6
    c1[3] = 7
    var o1 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n1 = combination_sum(c1, 4, 7, &!o1)
    assert(n1 == 2)
    // First combo: [2, 2, 3, -1]
    assert(o1.data[0] == 2)
    assert(o1.data[1] == 2)
    assert(o1.data[2] == 3)
    assert(o1.data[3] == 0 - 1)
    // Second combo: [7, -1]
    assert(o1.data[4] == 7)
    assert(o1.data[5] == 0 - 1)

    // Test 2: candidates=[2, 3, 5], target=8
    // Solutions: [2,2,2,2], [2,3,3], [3,5]
    var c2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    c2[0] = 2
    c2[1] = 3
    c2[2] = 5
    var o2 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n2 = combination_sum(c2, 3, 8, &!o2)
    assert(n2 == 3)

    // Test 3: candidates=[2], target=1 -> no solution
    var c3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    c3[0] = 2
    var o3 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n3 = combination_sum(c3, 1, 1, &!o3)
    assert(n3 == 0)

    // Test 4: candidates=[1], target=3 -> [1,1,1]
    var c4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    c4[0] = 1
    var o4 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n4 = combination_sum(c4, 1, 3, &!o4)
    assert(n4 == 1)
    assert(o4.data[0] == 1)
    assert(o4.data[1] == 1)
    assert(o4.data[2] == 1)
    assert(o4.data[3] == 0 - 1)

    // Test 5: candidates=[3, 5], target=6 -> [3,3]
    var c5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    c5[0] = 3
    c5[1] = 5
    var o5 = Buf { data: [0; 4096] }
    let n5 = combination_sum(c5, 2, 6, &!o5)
    assert(n5 == 1)
    assert(o5.data[0] == 3)
    assert(o5.data[1] == 3)
    assert(o5.data[2] == 0 - 1)

    println("099_combination_sum: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/humaneval_sounio/100_matrix_chain.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// HumanEval 100: Matrix Chain Multiplication
//
// Given a sequence of matrices, find the most efficient order to multiply
// them (minimizing total scalar multiplications). Matrix i has dimensions
// dims[i] x dims[i+1]. Uses bottom-up DP.
// dp[i][j] = minimum cost to multiply matrices i..j.
// dp[i][j] = min over k of dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + dims[i]*dims[k+1]*dims[j+1]
// Stored as flat array: dp[i*MAX + j]. Returns minimum cost.

struct DpTable { data: [i64; 4096] }

fn matrix_chain(dims: [i64; 256], n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic {
    // n = number of matrices, dims has n+1 elements
    if n <= 1 { return 0 }

    let MAX: i64 = 64
    var dp = DpTable { data: [0; 4096] }

    // chain_len is the number of matrices in the sub-chain
    var chain_len: i64 = 2
    while chain_len <= n {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i <= n - chain_len {
            let j = i + chain_len - 1
            dp.data[i * MAX + j] = 999999999

            var k = i
            while k < j {
                let cost = dp.data[i * MAX + k] + dp.data[(k + 1) * MAX + j] + dims[i] * dims[k + 1] * dims[j + 1]
                if cost < dp.data[i * MAX + j] {
                    dp.data[i * MAX + j] = cost
                }
                k = k + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        chain_len = chain_len + 1
    }

    dp.data[0 * MAX + (n - 1)]
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: dims=[10, 30, 5, 60], 3 matrices (10x30, 30x5, 5x60)
    // Optimal: (A1*A2)*A3 = 10*30*5 + 10*5*60 = 1500 + 3000 = 4500
    // vs A1*(A2*A3) = 30*5*60 + 10*30*60 = 9000 + 18000 = 27000
    var d1: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    d1[0] = 10
    d1[1] = 30
    d1[2] = 5
    d1[3] = 60
    assert(matrix_chain(d1, 3) == 4500)

    // Test 2: dims=[40, 20, 30, 10, 30], 4 matrices
    // Optimal cost = 26000
    var d2: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    d2[0] = 40
    d2[1] = 20
    d2[2] = 30
    d2[3] = 10
    d2[4] = 30
    assert(matrix_chain(d2, 4) == 26000)

    // Test 3: single matrix -> cost 0
    var d3: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    d3[0] = 10
    d3[1] = 20
    assert(matrix_chain(d3, 1) == 0)

    // Test 4: two matrices [10, 20, 30] -> 10*20*30 = 6000
    var d4: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    d4[0] = 10
    d4[1] = 20
    d4[2] = 30
    assert(matrix_chain(d4, 2) == 6000)

    // Test 5: dims=[1, 2, 3, 4], 3 matrices (1x2, 2x3, 3x4)
    // (A1*A2)*A3 = 1*2*3 + 1*3*4 = 6 + 12 = 18
    // A1*(A2*A3) = 2*3*4 + 1*2*4 = 24 + 8 = 32
    // Optimal = 18
    var d5: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    d5[0] = 1
    d5[1] = 2
    d5[2] = 3
    d5[3] = 4
    assert(matrix_chain(d5, 3) == 18)

    // Test 6: dims=[5, 10, 3, 12, 5, 50, 6], 6 matrices
    // Known optimal: 2010
    var d6: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    d6[0] = 5
    d6[1] = 10
    d6[2] = 3
    d6[3] = 12
    d6[4] = 5
    d6[5] = 50
    d6[6] = 6
    assert(matrix_chain(d6, 6) == 2010)

    // Test 7: all same dimension [10, 10, 10, 10] -> 2000
    // (A1*A2)*A3 = 10*10*10 + 10*10*10 = 1000 + 1000 = 2000
    var d7: [i64; 256] = [0; 256]
    d7[0] = 10
    d7[1] = 10
    d7[2] = 10
    d7[3] = 10
    assert(matrix_chain(d7, 3) == 2000)

    println("100_matrix_chain: ALL TESTS PASSED")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/particle_physics/bench_cross_section.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// bench_cross_section: Tree-level e+e- -> mu+mu- cross-section benchmark.
// Validates 1/s scaling and parity-relevant energy points.

use particle_physics::amplitude::*;
use particle_physics::cross_section::*;
use particle_physics::sm_params::*;

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn check_near_rel(a: f64, b: f64, rtol: f64) -> bool {
    if b == 0.0 { return abs_f64(a) < rtol }
    abs_f64(a - b) / abs_f64(b) < rtol
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail = 0
    let alpha = alpha_em().val()
    let pi = 3.141592653589793

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Benchmark: σ(e+e- -> mu+mu-) at reference energies
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let energies: [f64; 5] = [10.0, 50.0, 91.2, 200.0, 500.0]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 5 {
        let s = energies[i] * energies[i]
        let sigma = eemm_qed_total_cross_section(s)
        let sigma_pb = eemm_qed_total_cross_section_pb(s)
        let expected = 4.0 * pi * alpha * alpha / (3.0 * s)
        let expected_pb = expected * 0.389379e9

        if !check_near_rel(sigma, expected, 1e-6) {
            println("FAIL: QED cross-section consistency")
            fail = fail + 1
        }

        // Reference: ~870 pb at 10 GeV
        if energies[i] == 10.0 {
            if !check_near_rel(sigma_pb, 870.0, 0.1) {
                println("FAIL: sigma_pb at 10 GeV")
                fail = fail + 1
            } else {
                println("BENCH|gate=eemm_10GeV_pb|value=")
                // Note: cannot format numbers in println, just emit marker
            }
        }

        // 1/s scaling: sigma(2E) / sigma(E) ≈ 1/4
        if i > 0 {
            let s_prev = energies[i - 1] * energies[i - 1]
            let sigma_prev = eemm_qed_total_cross_section(s_prev)
            let ratio = sigma / sigma_prev
            let expected_ratio = s_prev / s
            if !check_near_rel(ratio, expected_ratio, 1e-6) {
                println("FAIL: 1/s scaling")
                fail = fail + 1
            }
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Benchmark: R-ratio energies
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let r10 = r_ratio(100.0)
    if !check_near_rel(r10, 11.0 / 3.0, 1e-6) {
        println("FAIL: R-ratio at 10 GeV")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail == 0 {
        println("BENCH|name=cross_section|status=PASS")
    } else {
        println("BENCH|name=cross_section|status=FAIL")
    }
    return fail
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/particle_physics/bench_decay_widths.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// bench_decay_widths: Z and Higgs decay width benchmark.
// Validates total widths against PDG reference values.

use particle_physics::amplitude::*;
use particle_physics::sm_params::*;
use particle_physics::decay::*;

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn check_near_rel(a: f64, b: f64, rtol: f64) -> bool {
    if b == 0.0 { return abs_f64(a) < rtol }
    abs_f64(a - b) / abs_f64(b) < rtol
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail = 0

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Z boson partial widths
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let g_ee = z_decay_width_ee()
    let g_mumu = z_decay_width_mumu()
    let g_had = z_decay_width_hadrons()
    let g_tot = z_total_width()

    // lepton universality: Γ_ee ≈ Γ_μμ
    if !check_near_rel(g_ee, g_mumu, 0.01) {
        println("FAIL: Z lepton universality")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // PDG: Γ_Z(total) ≈ 2.495 GeV (tree-level within ~15%)
    if !check_near_rel(g_tot, 2.495, 0.15) {
        println("FAIL: Z total width")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Sum of known partials should not exceed total
    let g_sum = g_ee + g_mumu + g_had
    if g_sum > g_tot * 1.2 {
        println("FAIL: partial widths exceed total")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Branching ratios
    let br_ee = branching_ratio(g_ee, g_tot)
    let br_had = branching_ratio(g_had, g_tot)
    if br_ee < 0.03 || br_ee > 0.04 {
        println("FAIL: BR(Z->ee)")
        fail = fail + 1
    }
    if br_had < 0.65 || br_had > 0.75 {
        println("FAIL: BR(Z->had)")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Higgs boson partial widths
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let mh = mass_h().val()
    let gamma_h_bb = h_decay_width_ff(mh, mass_bottom().val(), 3.0)
    let gamma_h_tautau = h_decay_width_ff(mh, mass_tau().val(), 1.0)
    let gamma_h_gg = h_decay_width_gg(mh)
    let gamma_h_gamgam = h_decay_width_gammagamma(mh)
    let gamma_h_tot = h_total_width()

    // b-bbar dominates
    if gamma_h_bb <= gamma_h_tautau {
        println("FAIL: H->bb not dominant")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Total width ≈ 4.1 MeV (tree-level within factor 2)
    if !check_near_rel(gamma_h_tot, 0.0041, 1.0) {
        println("FAIL: H total width")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Sum of explicit channels <= total (within reason)
    let gamma_h_sum = gamma_h_bb + gamma_h_tautau + gamma_h_gg + gamma_h_gamgam
    if gamma_h_sum > gamma_h_tot * 2.0 {
        println("FAIL: Higgs partial sum exceeds total")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail == 0 {
        println("BENCH|name=decay_widths|status=PASS")
    } else {
        println("BENCH|name=decay_widths|status=FAIL")
    }
    return fail
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/particle_physics/bench_rge_running.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// bench_rge_running: QCD coupling running benchmark.
// Validates monotonicity and flavor-threshold behavior.

use particle_physics::rge::*;
use particle_physics::sm_params::*;

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn check_near_rel(a: f64, b: f64, rtol: f64) -> bool {
    if b == 0.0 { return abs_f64(a) < rtol }
    abs_f64(a - b) / abs_f64(b) < rtol
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail = 0
    let alpha_mz = alpha_s_mz().val()
    let mz = mass_z().val()

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Monotonicity: α_s increases as μ decreases
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let scales: [f64; 6] = [200.0, 91.19, 50.0, 10.0, 5.0, 2.0]
    var prev_alpha: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 6 {
        let mu = scales[i]
        let alpha_ep = alpha_s_running(mu, alpha_mz, mz)
        let alpha = alpha_ep.val()

        if i > 0 && alpha <= prev_alpha {
            println("FAIL: alpha_s not monotonically increasing")
            fail = fail + 1
        }
        prev_alpha = alpha
        i = i + 1
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Reference: α_s(10 GeV) ≈ 0.179 (within 5%)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let alpha_10_ep = alpha_s_running(10.0, alpha_mz, mz)
    let alpha_10 = alpha_10_ep.val()
    if !check_near_rel(alpha_10, 0.179, 0.05) {
        println("FAIL: alpha_s at 10 GeV")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Flavor thresholds
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let nf_200 = active_flavors(200.0)
    let nf_10 = active_flavors(10.0)
    let nf_2 = active_flavors(2.0)

    // u,d,s = 3 base; +c above m_c, +b above m_b, +t above m_t
    if nf_200 != 6 {
        println("FAIL: active flavors at 200 GeV")
        fail = fail + 1
    }
    if nf_10 != 5 {
        println("FAIL: active flavors at 10 GeV")
        fail = fail + 1
    }
    if nf_2 != 4 {
        println("FAIL: active flavors at 2 GeV")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // QED running: α_EM should decrease as μ decreases
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    let alpha_em_mz = alpha_em().val()
    let alpha_em_10_ep = alpha_em_running(10.0, alpha_em_mz, mz)
    let alpha_em_10 = alpha_em_10_ep.val()
    let alpha_em_200_ep = alpha_em_running(200.0, alpha_em_mz, mz)
    let alpha_em_200 = alpha_em_200_ep.val()

    if alpha_em_10 <= alpha_em_200 {
        println("FAIL: alpha_EM running direction")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail == 0 {
        println("BENCH|name=rge_running|status=PASS")
    } else {
        println("BENCH|name=rge_running|status=FAIL")
    }
    return fail
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/pbpk/causal_intervention.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// PBPK Causal Intervention Benchmark
//
// Paper: "Causal Programming with do-Calculus Types" (PLDI/UAI 2027)
//
// Demonstrates:
// 1. Causal DAG encoding for pharmacokinetic model
// 2. Compile-time identifiability verification via type system
// 3. Epistemic uncertainty propagation through causal estimates
// 4. Rejection of non-identifiable queries at compile time
//
// Model: 2-compartment PBPK with genotype-dependent metabolism
//
//   Causal Graph:
//     Dose ──→ Plasma ──→ Effect
//                ↑
//     Genotype → Metabolism
//
//   Question: What is P(Effect | do(Dose = 100mg))?
//   Answer: Identifiable via backdoor adjustment on {Genotype, Metabolism}

// ============================================================================
// SECTION 1: PBPK Model Parameters
// ============================================================================

struct DrugParams {
    ka: f64,         // Absorption rate (1/h)
    ke: f64,         // Elimination rate (1/h)
    vd: f64,         // Volume of distribution (L)
    fu: f64,         // Fraction unbound
    bp_ratio: f64    // Blood-to-plasma ratio
}

struct PatientParams {
    weight: f64,     // Body weight (kg)
    age: f64,        // Age (years)
    genotype: i32,   // CYP2D6 metabolizer status (0=poor, 1=extensive, 2=ultra)
    metabolism: f64   // Metabolic clearance multiplier
}

struct PBPKState {
    gut: f64,        // Drug in GI tract (mg)
    central: f64,    // Drug in central compartment (mg)
    t: f64           // Time (h)
}

struct SimResult {
    concentration: f64,   // Final plasma concentration (mg/L)
    auc: f64,             // Area under curve (mg*h/L)
    cmax: f64,            // Peak concentration (mg/L)
